en: The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter One: The World-Purifying Eye.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was at the site of the terrace of enlightenment in the kingdom of Magadha, having newly attained perfect awakening.

That ground was composed of vajra, perfectly adorned and pure, decorated with various jewels and diverse flowers; it was filled with supreme and wondrous jewel wheels, complete and stainless, with infinite exquisite colors and manifold ornaments, shining with radiance like the jeweled banners, flags, and canopies of the great ocean.

Exquisite fragrant flowers and garlands encircle it on all sides, while nets of the seven precious gems cover it above. An inexhaustible rain of jewels falls, manifesting sovereign power; various jewel trees with flowers and leaves of radiant luxuriance flourish there by the Buddha’s spiritual power.
This ground is made vast, majestic, and pure, universally illumined by light, and piled high with all manner of extraordinary and wondrous jewels.

Adorned with immeasurable roots of goodness, the site of enlightenment was magnificent; its Bodhi tree was lofty and extraordinary, with a trunk of pure lapis lazuli and branches adorned with exquisite jewels, while its precious leaves hung down like heavy clouds.

Various colored jewel flowers were interspersed among them, with wish-fulfilling *maṇi* gems as their fruit. The light from these trees shone universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions, manifesting various transformations to perform Buddha-deeds without end; they everywhere revealed the Mahāyāna path of the Bodhisattvas through the spiritual power of the Buddha.
They constantly produced all manner of exquisite sounds, extolling the immeasurable and inconceivable merits of the Tathāgata.

The lion thrones were like the great ocean, adorned with various wonderful jewel flowers; flowing light was like clouds, universally illuminating the ocean-like treasuries of innumerable Bodhisattvas, while a great sound reverberated afar in an inconceivable manner.
The Tathāgata’s radiance surpasses that of the noble maṇi jewel, completely covering all above; through various transformations, he performs buddha-works, which all behold without any obstruction;
in a single thought-moment, all manifested emanations fill the entire dharma-realm.

The Tathāgata’s wondrous treasury reaches everywhere without exception, adorned with a jeweled pavilion of immeasurable treasures; the Tathāgata dwells upon this precious lion throne and has attained supreme perfect enlightenment regarding all dharmas.

Having realized the body of wisdom of the equal dharma of the three periods of time, they universally enter the bodies of all worlds; their wondrous voices reach all realms without end, like space, being the sphere of activity for the wisdom of the mark of equality of dharmas;
like space, they accord with all sentient beings with an impartial mind.

His body sits pervasively in all places of enlightenment; he fully knows the conduct of all sentient beings; the sun of his wisdom shines to dispel all darkness; and he is able to manifest all buddha-lands.

Universally emitting the light of the ocean of wisdom of the three periods of time to illuminate pure realms, immeasurable lights fill the ten directions, and indestructible clouds of Dharma cover all things.

By means of the powers and fearlessnesses, they manifest the light of immeasurable sovereign power; opening the gates of expedient means, they teach and transform sentient beings, being able to universally appear before all assemblies.
It is like space, without coming or going.
One thoroughly realizes that all things lack intrinsic nature and accords with the mark of the equality of all phenomena.

All radiance universally manifests the practices of the Buddhas of the three periods of time and their Buddha-worlds, which are like a great ocean, inconceivable, and capable of responding to all sounds and languages.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-worlds,
whose names were: Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Samantaguṇaprabha Bodhisattva, Samantābhāsasiṃha Bodhisattva,
Samantajayaratnaprabha Bodhisattva, Samantaguṇasāgaradhvaja Bodhisattva, and Samantamati-prabhāsa Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Universal Jewel Flower Banner, the Bodhisattva Universal Supreme Soft Voice, the Bodhisattva Universal Pure Virtue Flame,
the Bodhisattva Universal Mark Radiance, the Bodhisattva Great Light Ocean Moon, the Bodhisattva Cloud Sound Ocean Treasury, the Bodhisattva Virtue Jewel Supreme Moon,
the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Pure Wisdom Light Flame, and the Transcendent...
The Bodhisattva Flower Radiance, the Bodhisattva Immeasurable Wisdom Cloud Sunlight, the Bodhisattva Great Power Diligence Vajra,
the Bodhisattva Fragrant Flame Light Banner, the Bodhisattva Moon Virtue Wondrous Sound, and the Bodhisattva Radiant Honored Virtue—
these and other such bodhisattvas were all together with him; they were all emanations of Vairocana Buddha.
They were virtuous friends from past lives;

they were a great ocean of all accomplished merits, with the perfections fully perfected and universally illuminating, their wisdom-eye pure, observing the three periods of time with equanimity, and possessing the complete clarity and purity of all samādhis;
their ocean of eloquence was profound, vast, and inexhaustible, universally manifesting the radiant glory of the merits of all Buddhas.
He thoroughly knows the mental activities of all sentient beings and tames them as is appropriate, illuminating all spheres with vajra-wisdom.

Being of one and the same dharma-nature, his awakened wisdom is vast and his profound sphere of knowledge is such that nothing remains unpenetrated. Abiding in the first stage, he universally encompasses the merits of all stages; his unsurpassed wisdom and vows are all fully perfected. He is endowed with the profound, extensive, and secret teachings of the Tathāgatas and has attained all the dharmas shared by all Buddhas. Sharing the same ground of practice, power, and virtue as the Tathāgatas, he attains mastery over all oceans of samādhi-doors and manifests appropriately within the ocean of sentient beings, skillfully establishing them according to their respective conduct.
They skillfully enter the ocean of all dharmas; their bodies are filled by the ocean of the Tathāgata’s ocean of merit and dharmas, which they revolve through as dhāraṇīs.

They travel everywhere throughout the ocean of all Buddha-worlds, giving rise to the ocean of vows for all pure lands, and fully attain the skillful wisdom of all Buddhas that reaches to the limits of the future.

To all Tathāgatas seated at the site of enlightenment, they are able to go everywhere to pay homage, serve, and make offerings. Having fully attained the ocean of all Samantabhadra’s vows, they bring fulfillment to the body of wisdom for all sentient beings.
Furthermore, there were Vajrapāṇis as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-world, whose names were:

Vajrapāṇi of Firm Radiance, Vajrapāṇi of Solar Radiance, Vajrapāṇi of Sumeru Flowers, Vajrapāṇi of Pure Cloud Sounds, Vajrapāṇi of Asura Power, Vajrapāṇi of Supreme Light, Vajrapāṇi of Tree Resonances, Vajrapāṇi of the Lion King, Vajrapāṇi of the Treasury of Thick Light, and Vajrapāṇi of Jewel Topknot Flower Light. Together with these and other such Vajrapāṇis, they had all made great vows over incalculable kalpas to serve and protect the Buddhas.

The Buddha has fully perfected all spheres of aspiration and practice; his immeasurable merits are entirely pure. He traverses the profound and vast realms of samādhi and possesses immeasurable spiritual powers. There is no place where the Buddha travels that he does not reach. He is able to traverse the inconceivable realm of liberation; dwelling among all assemblies, his body is so extraordinary that none can obscure it. According to those among sentient beings who are ready to be delivered, he can manifest his body and transform them as appropriate.
Furthermore, there were as many field-protector deities (maṇḍala-devatās) as there are atoms in a buddha-world, their names being:

Pure Adornment Deity, Jewel Accumulation Radiance Deity, Roaring Sound Deity, Rain of Various Flowers Deity, Adorned Jewel Light Deity, Skillfully Transcending Fragrance Deity, Golden Cloud Deity, Joyful Flower Tree Deity, and Adorned Light Deity. Together with these and other field-protector deities, they had all previously established vows and practices under former buddhas.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by as many nāgas and devas as there are atoms in a Buddha-world. Their names were:

Maṇiprabha Nāga, Vicitravyūha Nāga, Ratnaprabhāsa Nāga, Śuddhakāyaprabha Nāga, Gandhavyūha Nāga, and Ratnanetra Nāga. All of these, throughout inconceivable asaṃkhyeya kalpas in the past, had constantly served to adorn the Dharma-hall of the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by as many earth-deities as there are atoms in a Buddha-world. Their names were:

Earth-Deity Pure Flower Radiance, Earth-Deity Good Thought Radiance, Earth-Deity Adorned with Various Flowers, Earth-Deity Scattering Jewel Flames, Earth-Deity Delightful to Behold According to the Season, Earth-Deity Supreme Golden Eye, Earth-Deity Scattering Fragrance from the Pores, and Earth-Deity Harmonious Sound Responding to the Occasion. All of these shared the same roots of virtue and had universally cultivated vows and practices in the presence of past Buddhas.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by an inconceivable number of tree spirits (*vṛkṣadevatā*), whose names were:

Cloud of Miscellaneous Flowers, Various Kinds of Light, Pure Supreme Light, Hanging Adornments, Adorned Light, Delight in Harmonious Sound, Universally Victorious Equality, and Flavor of Flowers and Fruits. All of these had fully accomplished the great joy that shines everywhere.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by boundless medicinal herb spirits, whose names were:

Flame-Spirit, Sandalwood Fragrance-Spirit, Pure Light-Spirit, Universal Renown-Spirit, Universal Power-Spirit, Universal Purity-Spirit, Universal Radiance-Spirit, Beloved Fragrance-Spirit, and Supreme Manifestation-Spirit. All such beings as these had fully accomplished the universal illumination of great compassion.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable deities of grain, whose names were:

the Deity of Supreme Flavor, the Deity of Pure Flowers, the Deity of Good Power, the Deity of Potent Flavor, the Deity of Roots and Fruits, the Deity of Pure Flowers, the Deity of Joyful Purity, and the Deity of Pure Light; all such as these had fully accomplished great joy.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable river deities, whose names were:

the Universal Flow Deity, the Victorious Whirlpool Deity, the Torrent Sound Deity, the Water-Nourishing Deity, the Pure Ocean Radiance Deity, the Universal Love Deity, the Wondrous Banner Deity, the Victorious Water Deity, and the Ocean-Endowed Radiance Deity. All such beings as these were constantly able to apply themselves with diligence to benefiting sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by an inconceivable number of ocean deities, whose names were:

the deity Jewel-Victorious Radiance, the deity Vajra-Wisdom, the deity Universally Surging Waves, the deity Variegated Flower Dragon-Victor, the deity Jewel-Flower Radiance, the deity Sumeru Adornment, and the deity Ocean Sound; all such beings as these were themselves filled with the ocean of the Buddha’s immeasurable merits.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable asankhyeyas of fire deities, whose names were:

the Deity of the Treasury of Blazing Light, the Deity of the Wheel of Blazing Light, the Deity of Vast Radiance, the Deity of the Inexhaustible, the Deity of Supreme Miscellaneous Jewels, the Deity Who Illuminates and Dispels All Darkness, and the Deity of the Radiance of Flame Clouds. All such beings as these entirely illuminate and dispel the darkness for the sake of sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable wind deities (*vāyu-devatā*), whose names were:

Unobstructed Illumination of Space Deity, Universally Transcending Excellence Deity, Scattering Mount Sumeru Deity, Pure Flavor of Flames Deity, Purifying Flavor Deity, Producing Great Sound Deity, Tree-Peak Flower Forest Deity, and Sustaining the World Deity. All such beings as these are able to harmonize sentient beings, ensuring they do not become scattered.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by boundless space deities, whose names were:

the Deity Universal Radiance Pure Excellence, the Deity Boundless Profundity and Vastness, the Deity Arising Wind, the Deity Free from All Obstructions, the Deity Vast Transcendence, the Deity Unrivaled Flame, the Deity Supreme Power of Non-obstruction, the Deity Most Excellent Sublime Sound, and the Deity Manifesting the Ten Directions. All such beings as these had minds entirely free of defilement, being firm, pure, and wondrous.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable Lords of the Directions, whose names were:

Lord of Good Abiding, Lord of Pervasive Fulfillment, Lord of Immeasurable Manifesting Light, Lord of Radiant Adornment, Lord of Universal Turning and Gradual Progression, Lord of Unconfused Turning, Lord of Pure Roaming in Space, Lord of Universal Travel through the World, and Lord of Profound Conduct. All such beings as these were able to skillfully illuminate all sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable night goddesses, whose names were:

Goddess of Sublime Light, Goddess of Pure Light, Goddess Who Skillfully Observes Sentient Beings, Goddess of Firmness in Stillness, Goddess Endowed with Supreme Expedient Means, Goddess Who Produces All Tree Fruits, Goddess of Inexhaustible Retinue, Goddess Who Governs the Knowledge of Pure Play in Joy, Goddess Who Harmonizes Disputes, and Goddess Endowed with Pure Merit. All of these deeply cherished and delighted in the dharmas that assist the path.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable Lords of the Day-Gods (*divāpati*), whose names were:

the God Who Manifests Palaces, the God Who Skillfully Establishes Battlefields, the God of Universal Victory Who Delights in Adornments, the God of Joyful Flower Fragrance, the God of Universally Assembled Superior Medicines, the God Who Delights in Seeing Kings, the God of Pure Eyes, Lofty and Universally Victorious, the God of Great Compassionate Radiance, the God of Light Who Shines Well, and the God of Universally Victorious Hanging Flowers. All such beings as these were entirely devoted to and delighted in the adornment of the True Dharma.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable asura deities, whose names were:

King Rāhula, King Vemacitrin, King Śumbha, King Candraprabha, King Vajradṛḍhavatrasaṃjñaka, King Mahājñānabala, and Queen Jayasamudgatadevī; all of these were capable of subduing pride and negligence.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable *garuḍa* kings, whose names were:

King of Great Courageous Power, King of Fearless Jewel-Crest, King of Courageous Pure Eyes, King of Non-Retrogressive Adornment, King Who Holds the Light of the Great Ocean, King Who Holds the Dharma with Firmness, King of Supreme Faculty Radiance, King of Pervasive Manifestation, King Who Roams Universally in All Directions, and King of Universal Vision Observing Equally. All such as these had accomplished skillful means and extensively moistened sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable Kinnara kings, whose names were:

King Good Wisdom, King Good Banner, King Variegated Flower Conduct, King Free from the Sound of Love and Pride, King Jewel Tree Radiance, King Manifesting Good Affection, King Adorned Light, King Good Flower Banner, King Victorious Ground, and King Victorious Wisdom. All of these beings diligently exhorted and inspired sentient beings everywhere, enabling them to delight in the Dharma.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable mahoraga kings, whose names were:

King Good Wisdom, King Pure and Majestic Sound, King Multitude of Sublime Wisdom, King Lamp Banner, King Fierce Light, King Incense of Lion Fragrance, King Sound of Variegated Necklaces, and King Firm Joyous Radiance. All of these universally dispelled the net of doubts for all sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable kings of the kumbhāṇḍas, whose names were:

King Vairocana, King Well-Cultivated Banner, King Level Feet Pure White, King Able to Remove Fear, King Pure Sumeru Forest, King Immeasurable Pure Eye, and King Immeasurable Gate of Eyes. All such as these had fully cultivated the dharma-gate of non-obstruction.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable kings of the ghost realm, whose names were:

King Vaiśravaṇa, King Great Sound, King Pure Ground, King Great Lord, King Blazing Eye, King Firm Eye, King Adorned Victorious Army, King Great Wealth Pure Body, and King Sumeru Power. All such as these were universally able to diligently protect all sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable sons of gods of the lunar body, their names being:

Moon Devaputra, Radiant Flower Devaputra, Victorious Flow Adornment Devaputra, Delighting in All Worldly Pleasures Devaputra, Eye-Light Devaputra, Pure Light Devaputra, Universally Roaming Pure Light Devaputra, Constellation King Devaputra, Pure Awakening Devaputra, and Upright and Majestic Good Light Devaputra. All such beings as these diligently used wisdom to universally inspire in sentient beings the unsurpassed jewel-mind.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable sons of the Sun Devas (*Sūryadevaputra*), whose names were:

Sūryadevaputra, Netrajvālāprabha Devaputra, Meruprabhāgra Devaputra, Vimalaratnanetra Devaputra, Vikrāntāvinivartana Devaputra, Sukusumamālāprabha Devaputra, Ratnabodhi Devaputra, Vimalanetra Devaputra, Jitasunanda Devaputra, and Samantavijayaprabha Devaputra. All of these had fully accomplished pure roots of goodness and constantly desired to benefit all sentient beings.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, whose names were:

Śakra-devendra-rāja, Samantakīrti-pūrṇa-rāja, Cūḍākṣa-rāja, Ratnaprabhāsa-kīrti-rāja, Nandana-rāja, Priyamanas-rāja, Jayaghoṣa-rāja, and Viśuddhapuṣpa-rāja. All of these were fully endowed with pure and wholesome karma, capable of causing sentient beings to be born in pure and wondrous realms.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable kings of the Yāma Heaven, whose names were:

King Sucīra, King Akṣayajñāna, King Susaṃskāra, King Rati-ratijvāla, King Sumeruprabha, King Acintyaprajña, King Nābhi-cakra, King Acintya, King Candrānanābha, and King Samantavyūha. All of these had diligently cultivated the arising of joy, and they possessed faith, delight, and contentment.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable kings of the Tuṣita Heaven, whose names were:

King Good Joy, King Oceanic Bliss, King Supreme Virtue, King Hundred Radiance, King Good Eyes, King Jewel Mountain Moon, King Transcendent Valor Moon, King Vajra Good Splendor, and King Joyful Transcendence. All of these had fully accomplished the *nien-fo samādhi* (samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha).
Furthermore, he was accompanied by an inconceivable number of kings of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations (*Nirmāṇarati*), whose names were:

King of Skillful Emanation, King of Pure Light, King of Supreme Cloud-Sound, King Adorned with Exquisite Colors, King Who Delights in Wisdom, King of Flower-Light Moon, and King Illuminating the Directions. All of these had fully accomplished the gateways to the dharma of tranquility and brought sentient beings under their influence.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, their names being:

King Sovereign Transformation, King Good Eye, King Variegated Jewel Crown, King Vigorous Wisdom, King Multitude Flower Sound, King Joyful Radiance, King Abode of Tranquility, King Variegated Wheel, King Sublime Light of Wisdom, and King Great Powerful Light. All of these universally and diligently cultivated the sovereign True Dharma.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by an inconceivable number of Great Brahmās, whose names were:

Śikhin Great Brahmā, Jñānaprabha Great Brahmā, Suprabha Great Brahmā, Samantaghoṣa Great Brahmā, Lokasvaraghoṣa Great Brahmā, Śāntopāyavaraprabha Great Brahmā, Viśuddhanetra Great Brahmā, and Mṛdusvara Great Brahmā. All of these were fully endowed with great compassion; they liberated sentient beings, illuminating and dispelling their feverish afflictions so that they might become cool and supple.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable sons of the Heaven of Radiant Sound (*Ābhāsvara*), whose names were:

Son of Heaven Delightful Light, Son of Heaven Pure Light, Son of Heaven Great Sound, Son of Heaven Delightful Pure Sound, Son of Heaven Virtuous Thought Sound, Son of Heaven Liberation Sound, Son of Heaven Profound and Sublime Sound, Son of Heaven Stainless Light, and Son of Heaven Supreme Pure Light. All such as these dwelt securely in the dharma-gate of the tranquility of joyful light.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by asankhyas of Śuddhāvāsa devas, whose names were:

King of Pure Wisdom Deva, Manifesting Excellence Deva, Tranquil Excellence Deva, Sumeru-Time Deva, Pure-Mind Eye Deva, Unsurpassed Affectionate Light Deva, Worldly Wisdom Sound Deva, Blazing Wisdom Deva, Mind Delighting in the Transformation of Dharma Deva, and High Transformation Deva. All such beings constantly cause sentient beings to dwell securely in vast joy.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable sons of devas of the Fruit-bearing Heaven (*Phala-deva*), whose names were:

Dharma-puṣpa-prabhāsa-deva, Viśuddha-dṛḍha-deva, Prajñā-prabhāsa-deva, Jñānarāja-deva, Samantamukha-jñānacakṣus-deva, Anivartya-prema-deva, Vimala-śāntaprabhā-deva, and Viśuddha-arcis-deva. All of these were perfectly established in the gateway of the tranquil mind.
Furthermore, he was accompanied by immeasurable devas from the Śuddhāvāsa (Pure Abode) heavens, such as Maheśvara, including those named:

Sunlight Deva, Great Lord Deva, Great Renown Light Deva, Virtue-Pure Eye Deva, Great Wisdom Light Deva, Immovable Light-Sound Deva, Good Bestower of Sight Deva, Joyful Mahāyāna Deva, Universal Sound Deva, and Joyful Renown Light Deva. All of these had already cultivated the signless and equal Dharma-realm, and were all present within the ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata.
He practices equanimity toward all sentient beings and has fully accomplished immeasurable, wondrous forms;
he is well-established within the ten powers and remains unshakable amidst all assemblies; wherever he goes, none can destroy him, and that upon which the Tathāgata rides is ever present before him.

Having been freed from the hindrance of afflictions, his mind was pure; all the mountains of fetters had already been shattered and extinguished. Beholding the Buddha’s countenance, immeasurable and wondrous colors and radiance shone everywhere.

Why is this? Because in the past, throughout immeasurable kalpas while practicing the bodhisattva path, the Tathāgata skillfully gathered in sentient beings through the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*).

He accumulated roots of goodness under all Tathāgatas; through various causes, conditions, and expedient means, he taught and transformed them so that they might establish themselves on the path of the Tathāgata. He deeply planted immeasurable roots of goodness of the Tathāgata in them, causing them all to be securely established in the path of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
They have attained immeasurable power of merit and have fully accomplished the ocean of the Tathāgata’s vows.
The conduct of these bodhisattvas is perfectly pure; each follows their original practice and attains the path of transcendence, all because they are illuminated by the light of the Tathāgata.
Riding upon the power of liberation, they enter the ocean of the Tathāgata and attain complete mastery over all the gates of the Buddha-dharma.
The Deva Sāgarabhadra attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Radiance of Skillful Means for the Tranquility of the Dharmadhātu and Space;
the Deva Maheśvara-Abhigata-prabhā attained mastery in the Dharma-door of Universal Roaming through All Dharmas;
and the Deva Guṇaviśuddhanetra attained mastery in the Dharma-door of Skillful Means regarding the Non-arising and Non-ceasing of All Dharmas.
The Deva Mahāprabhā attained mastery in the Dharma-door of Radiant Play within the Ocean of Expedient Wisdom regarding all phenomena;
the Deva Śāntaprabhasvara attained mastery in the Dharma-door of Universally Arising Immeasurable Joy and Bliss through All Meditations;
and the Deva Kṣemalocanadatta attained mastery in the Dharma-door of Roaming in Stillness by Turning Away from Delusion and Fear.
The Celestial King Inconceivable attained mastery over the dharma-door of non-arising within immeasurable realms;
the Celestial King Delighting in the Mahāyāna attained mastery over the dharma-door of all phenomena being neither coming nor going and having no place of dependence or abiding;
the Celestial King Universal Mixture of Sounds attained mastery over the dharma-door of the tranquility of the Buddha-realm.
The gods of the Heaven of Delighting in Praise and Light attained mastery over the dharma-gate of immeasurable realms.
At that time, the Great Sovereign God Ocean of Good Radiance, through the spiritual power of the Tathāgata, surveyed the entire assembly of sovereign gods and spoke in verse:
"The inexhaustible, equal, and wondrous Dharma-realm Is entirely filled with the body of the Tathāgata."
Without grasping and without arising, eternally quiescent, he has appeared in the world as the refuge for all.
The Dharma-King of the Buddhas has appeared in the world and is able to establish the unsurpassed, true teaching.
The realm of the Tathāgata is boundless; he is the Sovereign of the World, acclaimed as supreme.
The Buddha is inconceivable and without peer; His marks and signs, and his radiance, illuminate the ten directions.
The Great Sage, the World-Honored One’s path of true teaching, Is like clear eyes beholding a bright pearl.
All classes of sentient beings in the world cannot conceive of the Buddha’s merit;
he has extinguished all darkness of ignorance and ascended to the terrace of unsurpassed wisdom.
The merit of the Tathāgata is inconceivable; those sentient beings who behold him have their afflictions extinguished.
Upon seeing the Immovable and Sovereign Honored One, they are able to give rise to a heart of immeasurable joy.
For the great ocean of sentient beings whose minds are shrouded by ignorance, you manifest the tranquil and subtle Dharma;
you are able to kindle the lamp of unsurpassed wisdom—this is the true, pure eye of skillful means.
The Tathāgata’s pure and wondrous form-body Is able to manifest throughout the ten directions;
This body is neither existent nor has it any basis— To see the Buddha thus is the true contemplation.
The Tathāgata’s voice is without obstruction; there is no one among those ready for transformation who does not hear it.
It is serene and unmoving, without coming or going; this is called the Dharma-gate of the Joy of Excellent Wisdom.

All the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions, The Lords of Gods and Men of the gate of the tranquil Dharma— The Tathāgata’s radiance shines everywhere; This is the wondrous Dharma-gate of the Banner of Adornment.
Throughout boundless oceans of kalpas, the Buddha constantly seeks perfect enlightenment to awaken sentient beings;
through immeasurable skillful means he transforms all, and thus is seen as one of pure and vast renown.
Furthermore, there was the Celestial King Light of Joyful Karma, who attained mastery over the Dharma-door of the Cloud of Dharma that observes the faculties of all sentient beings;
the Celestial King Pure Solidity, who attained mastery over the Dharma-door of contemplating the skillful means of the wondrous forms of all Buddhas;
and the Celestial King Joy of Joys, who attained mastery over the Dharma-door of perceiving the inconceivable realms of the Buddha-lands within a single pore.
The Celestial King Universal Gate Wisdom-Eye attained mastery in the dharma-door of entering the universal gate to observe the dharma-realm;
the Celestial King Non-Retrogressive Love attained mastery in the dharma-door of causing all sentient beings to take birth in various places;
the Celestial King Good Wisdom Light attained mastery in the dharma-door of entering the inconceivable realms of all worlds.
The Celestial King Vimalaprabha attained mastery over the dharma-door of the essential method for deliverance among all sentient beings and all phenomena;
the Celestial King Vimalaprabhāsa attained mastery over the dharma-door that enables those to be transformed to enter the realm of the Buddha.
At that time, the Celestial King Light of Joyful Action, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of the Fruit-Bearing Heaven deities and spoke in verse:
“The realm of all Buddhas is profoundly deep and inconceivable;
No other class of sentient beings is able to fathom it.”
The Tathāgata skillfully guides and instructs immeasurable multitudes of sentient beings,
enabling them all to aspire with joy and resolve to seek the unsurpassed path.
By means of his supernormal powers, the Buddha remains in the world to universally enlighten and transform all.
All classes of sentient beings, each according to what they have heard,
forever eliminate the obstacles of delusion; their life of wisdom becomes pure and free from defilement,
enabling them to behold all Tathāgatas and the ocean of the various wondrous, pure Dharmas.
The true nature of all phenomena is quiescent and without dependence;
through the power of skillful means, the Tathāgata is able to manifest it for the sake of sentient beings.
Regarding all phenomena, the Tathāgata has no intrinsic nature and nothing upon which to depend.
Yet they are able to manifest myriad forms, their appearances as clear as bright lamps.
Through various analogies and parables, employing skillful means according to what beings delight in,
they manifest for them the wisdom and supernormal powers of all Tathāgatas.
Because the gateways to awakening differ, they are immeasurable and inconceivable;
to erect the banner of the True Dharma, they cause beings to enter the ocean of merit.
By the Tathāgata’s power of spiritual transformations, he can, within a single pore, [accomplish all this].
Each expounds for the multitude the unsurpassed dharma of tranquil extinction.
Each and every Tathāgata, for his own retinue,
reveals immeasurable gateways of the Dharma— an ocean of merit.
All of them let out the lion’s roar, expounding the teachings of all Buddhas;
this is the Greatly Wise Honored One’s unsurpassed power of skillful means.
Throughout the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, among all classes of living beings—
He is able to manifest for them the true Dharma of the Tathāgata.
The Tathāgata has never had any distinction between coming and going;
he causes all beings to rejoice and never retreat from the realm of wisdom.
For the sake of sentient beings, the Tathāgata universally manifests the signs of karmic retribution,
just as the light of the sun shines upon all such forms so that none fail to appear.
Furthermore, for those sentient beings, he expounds the Dharma of quiescent extinction.
Causing them to see the truth, the realm of profound wisdom;
the Tathāgata, having personally contemplated the profound and subtle meaning,
rains down the nectar-like Dharma everywhere according to the faculties of sentient beings.
To open the gateways of all dharmas, Immeasurable and inconceivable,
All lead back to entry into quiescence, The equal and true contemplation.
Throughout countless and immeasurable kalpas, He extensively cultivated great compassion.
Upon attaining equal and perfect enlightenment, you deliver all classes of sentient beings.
You rain down the nectar of the Dharma everywhere, filling all according to their capacities;
like a dragon raising auspicious clouds, you rain equally upon all.
Furthermore, there was the Celestial King Pure Wisdom, who had attained mastery over the dharma-door of observing the roots of goodness in sentient beings;
the Celestial King Manifesting the Sublime, who had attained mastery over the dharma-door of awakening and illuminating all that exists;
and the Celestial King Supreme Sublimity, who had attained mastery over the dharma-door of dhāraṇīs and eloquence.
The Celestial King Universal Lamp attained mastery in the dharma-door of delighting in the appearance of Buddhas in the world and in liberation;
the Celestial King Wisdom Flame attained mastery in the dharma-door of being able to give rise to joy regarding the profound dharmas of all sentient beings;
the Celestial King Delighting in Transformation attained mastery in the dharma-door of entering inexhaustibility through the complete perfection of the merits of transforming bodhisattvas.

The Celestial King Leaping Transformation attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Wisdom of Compassion that Universally Observes and Fully Fulfills the Suffering and Distress of Immeasurable Sentient Beings.
At that time, the Celestial King Pure Wisdom, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of the Universal Purity Heaven and spoke in verse:
“The True Dharma of all Buddhas is without obstruction, Pervading and filling the immeasurable realms of the ten directions.”
The manifested realm of the Buddha is inconceivable, An immeasurable ocean of stainless Dharma-gates.
The Tathāgata dwells in the world without dependence; The Dharmakāya is pure, without arising or ceasing.
Yet he can illuminate and manifest immeasurable lands, So that all may behold the God among Gods.
Having cultivated skillful means for an ocean of immeasurable eons, His radiance universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions;
Abiding in the pure dharma-realm as it truly is, It is tranquil, subtle, and most unsurpassed.
Sentient beings are deluded, their eyes and minds blinded; Lacking sight, they wander through birth and death.
The Tathāgata guides them with the pure path, Revealing the unsurpassed and most excellent gate.
The unsurpassed path upon which the Tathāgata rides cannot be conceived by any sentient being;
the Buddha manifests all gates of wondrous forms, which those with virtuous thoughts and pure vision behold with joy.
The Buddha has taught the subtle and wondrous gateways of dhāraṇī, as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields;
for the sake of taming all sentient beings, his pure eye of wisdom is able to perceive them clearly.
The appearance of a Tathāgata in the world is extremely rare to encounter; only once in immeasurable billions of kalpas does one meet him.
Having left behind all places of hardship and gathered this assembly, only the Buddha, the World-Honored One, can respond to the needs of the time.
All sentient beings are difficult to conceive; the Buddha can fully manifest the pure and wondrous Dharma.
Beholding the Tathāgata’s immeasurable virtues is like seeing all forms through clear illumination.
The Dharma attained by all Buddhas of the three periods of time, Which teaches and transforms sentient beings in ways inconceivable—
Having fully contemplated these merits, They rejoice with great exultation, delighting in the Dharma.
Sentient beings are submerged in the ocean of afflictions, In great terror of ignorance, evil, and turbidity;
The Buddha, through his ultimate compassion, delivers them, Revealing the pure realm like a celestial banner.

The Buddha emits immeasurable great rays of light; within each ray of light are immeasurable Buddhas, all appearing through countless skillful means to transform and deliver all classes of sentient beings.
Furthermore, the Devaputra Priyadarśana attained mastery over the Dharma-door of delighting in tranquility and extinguishing the suffering of sentient beings;
the Devaputra Citrābhāsa attained mastery over the Dharma-door of purifying the minds of all sentient beings, removing their defilements, and extensively cultivating an ocean of merit;
the Devaputra Svairaghoṣa attained mastery over the Dharma-door of generating within a single thought-moment the merits cultivated by all sentient beings throughout an entire eon.
The Deva Supreme Mindfulness and Wisdom attained mastery over the dharma-gates of various pure merits regarding the birth, abiding, and cessation within the world;
the Deva Pure Joyful Sound attained mastery over the dharma-gate of extensively expounding the methods of making offerings for all Bodhisattvas in the Tuṣita Heaven;

the Deva Sound of Excellent Thought attained mastery over the dharma-gate of being able to receive and retain the teachings on the meaning of the stages (*bhūmi*) throughout an entire eon by means of a single thought-moment.
The Deva Vimuktiprabhasvara attained mastery in the dharma-door of the Arrayed Site of Enlightenment;
the Deva Gambhīraśabda attained mastery in the dharma-door of the ocean of meritorious qualities of inexhaustible supernormal powers;
the Deva Vimalaghoṣa attained mastery in the dharma-door of the sphere of the ocean of all Buddhas' meritorious qualities.
Emerging from the Heaven of Pure Light, he attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Treasury of the Power of Joyful Merit Sustained by the Vow-Power of Past Buddhas.
At that time, the Devaputra of the Heaven of Light-Sound, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the assembly of the Heaven of Light-Sound and spoke in verse:
“I recall the Tathāgata’s past conduct, And I also remember my own practice of making offerings.”
Just as the pure joy originally cultivated, Is now fully seen through the Buddha’s radiance;
The Tathāgata’s stainless, adorned body Increases the pure minds of sentient beings.
Abiding in loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity— This is called the Dharma-gate of Adorned Purity.
The Tathāgata’s vast and skillful methods, Accumulated through oceans of immeasurable eons,
Reveal the suchness of those phenomena of arising and ceasing— The gateway of skillful means through the voice of the Lord of Dharma.
The Tathāgata’s supernatural power pervades the ten directions, universally illuminating immeasurable Buddha-fields;
the Buddhas of the ten directions all appear therein, and through supreme mindfulness and skillful means, they extinguish ignorance.

Making offerings to and revering Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable oceans of lands, thereby giving rise to joy, they are able to sever the darkness of all living beings; this is called the supreme realm of Wondrous Sound.
The ocean of immeasurable kalpas is most vast and wide; you preach the peerless stages of skillful means.
The wondrous Dharma you expound is inexhaustible; you have attained mastery in the gateway of mental skillful means.
The Tathāgata’s immeasurable power of mastery Is universally manifested in every thought-moment;
His descent into the womb, his attainment of enlightenment, and his skillful means are infinite— This is what is called the wondrous Dharma-gate.
The Buddha’s mastery is profound and vast, beyond compare; his manifestations of supernormal power are immeasurable.
He is able to cause all faculties to become utterly pure, enabling them to dwell upon the most profound and subtle stage.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom is boundless; his conduct is pure, peerless, and unimpeded.
He universally beholds all Honored Ones among Two-Legged Beings, possessing supreme, stainless skillful means.
In past lives as a bodhisattva, you made offerings to oceans of immeasurable Buddhas;
having established inconceivable great vows, you have thus attained unsurpassed wisdom.
Furthermore, there was the Great Brahmā Śikhin, who attained mastery in the dharma-door of manifesting all phenomena through illumination and entering the inconceivable;
the Brahmā Jñānaprabha, who attained mastery in the dharma-door of skillfully abiding in the tranquility of all meditative concentrations and equal contemplations;
and the Brahmā Jñānaprabhacitta, who attained mastery in the dharma-door of illuminating all phenomena and entering the skillful means of the inconceivable.
The Brahma Universal Sound Cloud attained mastery in the dharma-gate of entering with equanimity into the ocean of the sublime voices of all Buddhas;
the Brahma Timely Sound attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the most excellent methods for gathering and subduing sentient beings;
the Brahma Tranquil Light attained mastery in the dharma-gate of being able to give rise to, abide in, and discern all phenomena within all lands.
The Brahma Joyful Light attained mastery in the dharma-gate of transforming sentient beings through immeasurable skillful means;
the Brahma Firmly Established attained mastery in the dharma-gate of abiding in the practice of tranquility regarding the pure marks of all phenomena;
the Brahma Eye of Delight attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the courageous [realization] that all existence is without coming, without going, and without any basis of reliance.
The Brahmā Mṛdusvara attained mastery in the Dharma-door of universally illuminating by following the inexhaustible Dharma.
At that time, the Great Brahmā Śikhin, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed all the hosts of great Brahmās and spoke in verse:
“The Buddha’s body is pure and eternally tranquil, Universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions.”
Quiescent, signless, and without manifestation, The Buddha’s physical form is seen like floating clouds.
No sentient beings can fathom it; The Tathāgata’s Dharma-body and the realm of dhyāna, With immeasurable skillful means, are inconceivable— This is the Dharma-gate of the illumination of wisdom.
The ocean of all dharmas, as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field, is expounded in its entirety by a single voice;
though one were to speak for aeons as many as those atoms, it would never be exhausted—this is called the Dharma-door of the Illuminating Mind.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous voice is profoundly fulfilled; Sentient beings, according to their kind, all attain understanding.
Everyone says it is identical to their own speech; This Brahma-voice reaches everywhere, most unsurpassed.
Whatever has been attained by the Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, and all the skillful means and practices of the bodhisattvas,
are all manifested within the body of the Tathāgata, yet within that Buddha-body there is no discrimination.
The Buddha’s body is like space, inexhaustible; Formless and unimpeded, it manifests everywhere.
Its responsive manifestations are like illusions and transformations; Its spiritual transformations and pure sounds reach everywhere.
The Buddha’s body is boundless like space; his light of wisdom and pure voice are likewise.
The Buddha has no obstructions regarding all phenomena, just as moonlight illuminates everything.
The Dharma King dwells in the Hall of Sublime Dharma; The radiance of his Dharma-body shines everywhere.
The nature of phenomena is as it truly is, without any distinction; This is called the Dharma-door of the Ocean of Joyful Sounds.
Furthermore, there was the Celestial King Vaśavartin, who had attained mastery in the dharma-door of teaching and transforming the treasury of immeasurable sentient beings;
the Deva Sun-Eye, who had attained mastery in the dharma-door of causing all sentient beings to obtain the dharma of supreme bliss;
and the Deva Variegated Jewel-Crown, who had attained mastery in the dharma-door of skillful means for understanding the immeasurable dispositions and desires of sentient beings.
The Deva Vīryasubuddhi attained mastery in the dharma-gate of discerning the meanings for sentient beings;
the Deva Suvicitraghoṣa attained mastery in the dharma-gate of observing all sentient beings with compassionate mindfulness;
the Deva Prabhāśvararatnaketu attained mastery in the dharma-gate of transcending demonic activities for all sentient beings.
The gods of the Pure Realm attain mastery over the dharma-gate of contemplating the transformation of all sentient beings;
the gods of the Multicolored Wheel attain mastery over the dharma-gate of recollecting the Buddhas of the ten directions to fill them completely;
and the gods of the Wondrous Light of Wisdom-Flowers attain mastery over the dharma-gate of spontaneously awakening to the Buddha’s virtues and following them with a mind full of mindfulness.
The Deva of Great Power Light attained mastery over the Dharma-door of the realm transcending the world.
At that time, the Heavenly King Sovereign, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed all the hosts of the Sovereign Heavens and spoke in verse:
“The Dharma-body of the Tathāgata is equal to the Dharma-realm; It universally responds to sentient beings, manifesting before them all.”
The Tathāgata, the Dharma King, transforms sentient beings, Subduing them all in accordance with the nature of phenomena.
Of all the supreme and wondrous pleasures in the world, The noble joy of cessation is the most excellent.
The stainless, wondrous Dharma is the chamber of the Tathāgata; With the pure, supreme eye, one sees according to reality.
The Tathāgata universally illumines all worlds, raining down the Dharma rain upon the withered forests of the ground of doubt;
sentient beings receive its moisture and their net of doubts is removed—this is the wondrous Dharma-gate of the Jewel-Crown Banner.
The Tathāgata utters a single sublime sound, Expounding the vast ocean of Dharma without exception;
With one voice, the Buddha pervades the ten directions— This is called the Dharma-gate of Supreme Valor.
All the Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions Do not fill even a single pore of the Buddha;
The Buddha’s great compassion is like space— This is called the Dharma-door of Pure Wisdom.
The high mountains of pride of all sentient beings, The Buddha shatters them utterly with his ten powers;
The Buddha’s compassionate radiance illuminates the ten directions— This is called the wondrous Dharma-gate of the Light Banner.
Having beheld the Tathāgata, one extinguishes delusion and confusion; pure vision and wisdom become fully perfected.
One is forever freed from the terrors of the evil realms; this is called the wondrous Dharma-gate of the tranquil realm.
The Tathāgata’s pores all emit light, Causing each to hear the Dharma according to their needs;
Universally guiding sentient beings to the happy realms— This is called the wondrous Dharma-door of the Good Banner.
All the Buddha-works of the ten directions, this entire assembly beholds them all;
the Tathāgata’s dharma-realm fills all of space—this is called the sublime Dharma-gate of Pure Flowers.
The oceans of Buddha-lands throughout immeasurable eons are all the realm of supreme wisdom;
the Tathāgata has no sense of superiority therein—this is the wondrous Dharma-gate of the Banner of Great Power.
Furthermore, there was the Celestial King Skillful Transformation, who had attained mastery in the dharma-door of discerning and transforming all phenomena;
the Celestial King Tranquil Radiance, who had attained mastery in the dharma-door of contemplating the reality of all existence and the self;
and the Celestial King Light of Transformative Power, who had attained mastery in the dharma-door of fulfilling the wisdom that liberates all sentient beings from delusion.
The Deva Duṣpradharṣa attained mastery over the dharma-gate of giving rise to all joy and valor through the voices of all Buddhas;
the Deva Smṛtiprabha attained mastery over the dharma-gate of the inexhaustible perfection of the marks and signs of all Buddhas;
and the Deva Meghasvaravikrīḍita attained mastery over the dharma-gate of recollecting, through pure wisdom, the successive events of immeasurable eons in the past.
The Deva Supreme Pure Light attained mastery over the dharma-gate of nurturing all kinds of merit and wisdom for all sentient beings;
the Deva Joyful Light Topknot attained mastery over the dharma-gate of sitting cross-legged without obstruction throughout the entire realm of space;
the Deva Joyful Wisdom attained mastery over the dharma-gate of inexhaustible power within the sphere of all skillful means.
The Deva Flower-Light Topknot has attained mastery over the dharma-gate of contemplating the karmic actions, suffering, and happiness of all sentient beings.
At that time, the Celestial King Skillful Transformation, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations and spoke in verse:
“The Dharma-body is inconceivable within the world; The Tathāgata universally manifests in response to sentient beings.”
The nature of conditions is uncreated and not real; yet the adornment of karma manifests in the world.
Seeking the Buddha through skillful means, nothing is found; grasping for it throughout the ten directions, it cannot be obtained.
The Dharma-body appears as a manifestation without reality; such is the vision of the arising of mastery.
Having cultivated all practices throughout an ocean of immeasurable eons, He has severed the darkness of ignorance in sentient beings;
The Tathāgata’s wisdom is exceedingly pure— This is called the Buddha-wisdom power that eliminates delusion.
The exquisite sounds of all worlds Can never equal the voice of the Tathāgata;
A single sound resonates afar throughout the ten directions— This is called the sublime Dharma-gate of the Supreme Sound.
The various merits of all sentient beings do not equal the merit of a single mark of the Tathāgata;
the Buddha’s virtue is like space, without limit or boundary—this is called the wondrous Dharma-gate of Producing Light.

The events throughout immeasurable kalpas of the three periods of time, and the various signs of the formation and destruction of worlds—all can be manifested within a single pore; this is called the pure, unsurpassed wisdom.
One might still find the limit of empty space, But a single pore of the Buddha is without bound;
The Buddha’s virtues are thus inconceivable— This is called the Tathāgata’s pure knowledge and vision.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas in past lives, the Buddha fulfilled all the pāramitās;
he practiced with diligent vigor without weariness or indolence—this is called the Dharma-gate of the Pure Realm of Delightful Vision.
The causes and conditions of karmic actions are inconceivable; the Buddha has explained them for sentient beings without exception.
He universally manifests all phenomena as pure and undefiled; this is called the unsurpassed, profound Dharma-gate.
Beholding a single pore of the Tathāgata, All sentient beings enter therein;
Yet these beings have no thought of coming or going— This is called the Dharma-gate of Illuminating All Directions.
Furthermore, there was the Tushita Heavenly King, who had attained mastery over the dharma-gate of accomplishing the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Buddhas;
the Joyful Jewel-Crested Deva, who had attained mastery over the dharma-gate of pure light within the realm of space;
and the Victorious Banner Deva, who had attained mastery over the dharma-gate of entering the ocean of vast vows to bring peace to all sentient beings.
The Celestial King Hundred Radiant Lights attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the contemplative practice of the immeasurable and signless nature of all phenomena;
the Celestial King Moon-Leaping Attainment attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the power of awakening that leaps beyond the realm of the Buddhas;
and the Celestial King Supreme Eye-Light attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the indestructible bodhicitta cultivated through joyful practice.
The Celestial King Adorned from Past Lives attained mastery over the skillful means of the Buddhas of the ten directions for taming sentient beings;

the Celestial King Delighting in Tranquil Subtlety attained mastery over the dharma-door of dedicating every thought within the boundless ocean of the mind to manifest universally according to the capacities of beings.
At that time, the Deva King Tuṣita, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of the Tuṣita heavens and spoke in verse:
“The Tathāgata pervades everywhere, equal to the Dharma-realm; He appears in the world for the sake of defiled sentient beings.
According to their various desires, he preaches the Dharma; He is named the Unsurpassed and Supreme Dharma King.”
The Tathāgata’s immeasurable practices in past lives Have fully perfected the ocean of pure vows;
All dharmas are entirely complete therein— This is called the supreme merit of skillful means.
The Dharma-body of the Tathāgata is inconceivable; so too are the eloquence of the Dharma-realm and the Dharma-nature.
Its radiance universally illumines all phenomena, and within that tranquility, all dharmas are fully manifested.
Sentient beings are bound by the karmic obstacles of ignorance and darkness; with haughty minds and heedlessness, they race toward sensory realms.
The Tathāgata preaches for them the Dharma of quiescent extinction, so that they may all see it with joyful and virtuous delight.
The supreme refuge for all the world, He protects all beings and removes their manifold sufferings;
All beings joyfully behold the Unsurpassed Honored One, Like the full moon appearing upon a high mountain.
The realm of all Buddhas is inconceivable; so too is the entire dharma-realm.
Having reached the ultimate consummation in all dharmas, they have fully accomplished meditative concentration, wisdom, and skillful means.

The ocean of merit of the pure realm: all sentient beings who possess the karmic affinity, hearing of the Buddha’s merits, shall resolve for Bodhicitta; having eliminated defilements and dust, they shall become most supreme.
As numerous as the atoms within oceans of worlds, all the sons of the Buddhas have gathered here;
they make offerings to the Tathāgata to hear and receive the Dharma, and all behold the King of Skillful Means, the Banner of Dharma.
Furthermore, there was the King of the Yāma Heaven, who had attained mastery over the Dharma-door of turning roots of goodness away from the sorrows of sentient beings;
the Deva Joyful Light, who had attained mastery over the Dharma-door of all objective realms;
and the Deva Inexhaustible Wisdom, who had attained mastery over the Dharma-door of being free from all afflictions and possessing great compassion.
The Deva Pure Adornment attained mastery over the dharma-gate of discerning all faculties;
the Deva Sustaining Mount Sumeru attained mastery over the dharma-gate of illuminating immeasurable dhāraṇīs;
and the Deva Inconceivable Wisdom attained mastery over the dharma-gate of the inconceivable reality of karmic actions within all realms.
The Celestial King Navel-Wheel attained mastery in the dharma-gate of taming sentient beings by turning the wheel of Dharma;
the Celestial King Inconceivable Light attained mastery in the dharma-gate of universally observing the realms of sentient beings with the supreme eye;
the Celestial King Moon-like Countenance attained mastery in the dharma-gate of universally manifesting the reality of all phenomena.
The Celestial King Universal Sound, having attained mastery over the Dharma-gate of purifying the minds of all celestial hosts through universal observation,
then, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of the Yāma Heaven and spoke in verse:
“Throughout an ocean of immeasurable great eons, The Buddha has forever exhausted birth-and-death and afflictions.
Able to teach sentient beings the path of purity, the Buddha is the lamp of all wisdom.
The Tathāgata’s Dharma-body is exceedingly vast, pervading the ten directions without limit;
the light of his wisdom and his power of skillful means, as well as the bliss of his tranquil extinction and meditative concentration, are likewise boundless.
Birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, and suffering— Poisonous harms press upon and afflict sentient beings;
For the sake of such as these, you give rise to compassion, And with inexhaustible wisdom, you reveal enlightenment.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom follows and awakens accordingly; He thoroughly understands the three periods of time without obstruction.
He fully knows all virtuous practices; This is called the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Joyful Transformation.
Immeasurable dhāraṇīs are boundless, and the ocean of the Tathāgata’s eloquence is inexhaustible;
able to turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma—this is called the Sumeru Dhāraṇī Gate.
The unsurpassed, great sage’s single wondrous body, Manifests through transformation throughout all worlds, Appearing before all sentient beings; This is called the supreme realm of excellent light.
When sentient beings behold the body of the Tathāgata even once, they are able to sever all afflictions and remain far removed from all demonic activities; this is called the pure and wondrous realm.
The Buddha, amidst the ocean-like assembly of all beings, Abides here illuminating this gathering in its entirety;
Universally raining down the rain of Dharma for all sentient beings— This is called the Dharma-door of the Universal Sound’s Praise.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume One;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Part Two of the First Chapter, "The Pure Eye of the World.

Furthermore, there was Śakra-devānām-indra, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Great Wisdom of Certainty regarding the arising, abiding, and ceasing of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and who rejoiced in the Dharma;

he had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the purity of the power of all merits of the physical forms of sentient beings and the form-bodies of the Tathāgatas, which universally resounds throughout the heavens.
The deva Maitreya-locana attained mastery in the dharma-door of the canopy of the clouds of impartial compassion;
the deva Ratna-prabha-samudgata attained mastery in the dharma-door of the universal power of mindfulness of the Buddha through the perfection of all radiant colors;
the deva Priya-moda-cūḍa attained mastery in the dharma-door of observing the karmic retributions of sentient beings.
The Deva of Delightful Mindfulness of Purity attained mastery over the dharma-gate of possessing pure qualities in all buddha-lands;
the Deva of Supreme Sound of Mount Sumeru attained mastery over the dharma-gate of observing the arising and ceasing of phenomena in the world;

and the Deva of Mindfulness of Wisdom attained mastery over the dharma-gate of transcending thought through the causes for transforming sentient beings by initiating the various practices of future bodhisattvas.
The Celestial King Pure Flower Radiance attained mastery over the dharma-gate of all celestial modes of enjoyment;
the Celestial King Wisdom Sun Eye attained mastery over the dharma-gate of teaching and circulating roots of goodness throughout all celestial realms.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa gods and spoke in verse:
“If one recollects all Buddhas of the three periods of time, And is able extensively to observe the realms of the Buddhas—
The matters of the formation and destruction of all Buddha-lands, One sees them all through the Buddha’s spiritual power.”
The Buddha’s body is pure, filling the ten directions; Its wondrous form is peerless, responding to all.
Its radiance shines most exceptionally; Thus one beholds it, endowed with vast renown.
Having originally cultivated the ocean of great compassion through skillful means, It fills all sentient beings.
He is able to subdue all beings, opening the pure eye to see the infinite;
because he contemplates the immeasurable merit of the Buddha, he gives rise to a heart of vast joy.
In the world, none is equal to the Tathāgata; King Vimalakīrti dwells in this Dharma-gate.
The ocean of pure karma fulfills all sentient beings, such that everyone perceives it without exception;
through various causes, profound and vast merit arises, and this sublime vision is like the full moon.
The Buddhas fill and pervade the ten directions, so that there are no sentient beings who do not see them.
Having seen them, they are all thoroughly subdued; All attain the supreme mindfulness of skillful means.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom-body and clear, pure eye Pervade all lands throughout the ten directions, Causing all sentient beings to behold it;
With wondrous sounds he proclaims the transformation, Such that none fail to understand.
From a single pore of the Buddha, he manifests myriad practices; having seen this, the sons of the Buddha cultivate them fully.

Endowed with the accomplishment of immeasurable virtues, their excellent wisdom is like the full moon, bringing joy and delight to all sentient beings—all of which arises through the Tathāgata’s spiritual power.
Because the Tathāgata possesses immeasurable merit, this is called the Gate of the Stainless Variegated Flowers.

If one can bring the Tathāgata to mind for even a moment, then by the power of that merit of even a single thought, one shall forever remain far removed from all evil realms; the sunlight of wisdom shall extinguish the darkness of delusion.

Furthermore, there was the Sunlight Deva King, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Adorned Abiding in Rightness throughout the bodies of all sentient beings in the ten directions until the end of the future;
the Eye-Flame Light Deva, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Unsurpassed Ocean of Wisdom that Illumines All Forms;
and the Sumeru Light Deva, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of Arousing the Increasingly Superior and Pure Merits of Sentient Beings.
The Deva Pure Jewel Moon attained mastery in the dharma-door of the joyful practice of transcending all suffering;
the Deva Valiant and Non-regressing attained mastery in the dharma-door of unobstructed universal illumination;
and the Deva Sublime Flower Light attained mastery in the dharma-door of purifying the bodies of sentient beings with the light of the sun.
The Deva Jyotiṣprabha attained mastery over the dharma-door of the accumulation of merit that illuminates the world;
the Deva Ratnaśikhin attained mastery over the dharma-door of manifesting various colored realms within the ocean of jewels;
the Deva Vimalanetra attained mastery over the dharma-door of opening the pure eye in all realms of existence to contemplate the treasury of the dharma-realm.
The Celestial King Jyotiṣprabha has attained mastery over the Dharma-gates of the pure vehicle for all sentient beings.
At that time, the Sun God (Sūryadevaputra), empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire host of sun deities and spoke in verse:
“The light of the Buddha’s wisdom is boundless, Universally illuminating immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions.”
Causing all assemblies to behold the Buddha face-to-face, He transforms sentient beings through various skillful means.
The great ocean of sentient beings is vast and immeasurable; He is able to fully know their minds in their entirety.
He opens up the ocean of wisdom for all beings— Such is the vision of the Light of Supreme Excellence.
The Tathāgata appears universally in the world, Illuminating the ten directions entirely without exception;
The Dharma-body of the Tathāgata is peerless, Expounding the Dharma through unsurpassed wisdom.
Throughout oceans of incalculable eons within the realms of existence, you have practiced difficult austerities for the sake of sentient beings;
therefore, your pure light is like space, and your wondrous body appears like the full moon.
The Buddha proclaims wondrous sounds without obstruction, pervading the ten directions without exception;
he analyzes and extensively expounds all dharmas, teaching with the full complement of causes, conditions, and skillful means.
Emitting great, inconceivable light, The worlds of the ten directions are all made bright and pure;
Causing people to rejoice and resolve upon the Way— This is called the sublime Dharma-gate of Adornment.
All the lights of the entire world cannot equal the light from a single pore of the Buddha’s body;
the Buddha’s light is subtle and wondrous, beyond conception, for the Most Victorious One can manifest such spiritual transformations.

The Dharma of all Buddhas is thus: each sits beneath the Bodhi tree in the ten directions, distinguishing for the multitudes what is the Path and what is not the Path; with such pure and wondrous eyes, they see in this way.
Sentient beings are shrouded in the darkness of ignorance and blind without eyes;
for the sake of these suffering multitudes, you open the pure eye, and for their sake, you manifest the lamp of wisdom, so that they may behold the Tathāgata’s pure body.
Mastery in skillful means and freedom from delusion, Fully worthy of receiving all offerings,
Gradually teaching and revealing the path to liberation— This is called the Stage of Skillful Means of the Pure Eye.

Within a single Dharma-door, one speaks boundlessly; throughout countless eons, one extensively expounds it, analyzing its profound and pure meanings—this is called the universally pervasive, wondrous Dharma-door.
Furthermore, there was the Moon Deva-son, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of universally illuminating the Dharma-realm to subdue sentient beings;
the Radiant Flower Deva, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the realm of universally observing and encompassing all dharmas;
and the Victorious Light Adornment Deva, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of causing the ocean-like realms of the minds of all sentient beings to turn toward the Dharma.
The Celestial King Variegated Music attained mastery over the dharma-door that gives rise to all inconceivable delights;
the Celestial King Eye-Light attained mastery over the dharma-door that causes sentient beings to see reality;
and the Celestial King Manifesting Pure Light attained mastery over the dharma-door of great compassion that rescues and protects all suffering beings.
The Universal Roaming Tranquil Light Heaven attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the Pure Moon of Non-delusion;
the Subtle Adornment Heaven attained mastery in the Dharma-door of observing all phenomena as being like illusions, like transformations, empty, and non-existent;
and the Pure Bodhi Heaven attained mastery in the Dharma-door of skillfully understanding how all karmic actions arise.
The Celestial King Great Radiant Flame attained mastery in the Dharma-door of illuminating and delivering all devas by extinguishing their doubts.
At that time, the Moon Deva-son, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire assembly of Moon Devas and spoke in verse:
“Universally emitting great light upon all sentient beings, The Tathāgata is seen throughout the lands of the ten directions.”
Illuminating and dispelling all darkness of ignorance, He clearly understands the inconceivable Dharma.
The Buddha-realm is boundless and inexhaustible; Throughout immeasurable eons he has accumulated merit.
Through various skillful means and wondrous Dharma-gates, He tames and transforms all classes of sentient beings.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom is profoundly deep and far-reaching;
Knowing the immeasurable oceans of others’ minds, he turns the pure wheel of Dharma in accordance with them, Causing the birth of immeasurable hearts of joy.
Sentient beings are far removed from the joy of the noble ones, Sunk in the immeasurable sufferings of the world;
The Buddha bestows upon them this pure Dharma, So that their minds may find delight and dwell in peace.
The Tathāgata universally radiates great light, Discerning the various characteristics of all phenomena in the world;
The retribution of sins and merits never perishes— Thus does the Pure Light Heaven perceive it.

The Buddha is the ground for all sentient beings; He can sustain immeasurable fruits of goodness, Causing all beings to leave the paths of error, And skillfully establishing them on the ground of expedient means.
The great clouds of compassion leave nothing uncovered; the Buddha’s inconceivable body is equal to all sentient beings.
Universally raining down the rain of Dharma to moisten all, this is the Buddha’s foremost and supreme skillful means.
The nature of all that exists and does not exist is like space;
the Buddha is the great light for sentient beings, constantly and diligently employing skillful means to benefit all. Thus should one see the most supreme purity.
Furthermore, there was the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who had attained mastery in the dharma-gate of skillful means for gathering all sentient beings through entertainment;
the Gandharva Drum-light (Vṛkṣaprabha), who had attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the adornment of the Buddha’s merits;
and the Gandharva Arisen Pure Eye (Viśuddhanetra), who had attained mastery in the dharma-gate of causing sentient beings to be free from sorrow and joy.
The Gandharva Puṣpavṛkṣa attained mastery in the dharma-gate of extinguishing the fetters and afflictions;
the Gandharva Priyavicāra attained mastery in the dharma-gate of subduing aspirations;
the Gandharva Sunetra attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the right abiding of the treasury of light of all joy and delight.
The Gandharva Siṃhadhvaja attained mastery over the dharma-door of raining down jewels upon all directions;
the Gandharva Ratnaprabha attained mastery over the dharma-door of manifesting all wondrous bodies and vast wisdom;
the Gandharva Vajradruma attained mastery over the dharma-door of the joyful light that nurtures all trees.

They attained mastery in the dharma-gate of manifesting gandharvas adorned with all manner of ornaments, causing all sentient beings to experience the joy of the Dharma throughout the spheres and activities of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire assembly of gandharvas and spoke in verse:
"The realms of the Tathāgata have immeasurable gateways; No sentient beings are able to conceive of them.
The World-Honored One is as pure as space; He reveals to all beings the path of the True Way."
The Tathāgata’s ocean of immeasurable merit—within every single pore it is fully seen;
he causes all beings to find joy according to their wishes, seeing him thus with pure delight.
The immeasurable ocean of sorrow and suffering of sentient beings, the Buddha is able to extinguish entirely without remainder;
through great compassion and manifold skillful means, the Buddha can open the pure eyes of sentient beings.

The oceans of Buddha-fields fill the ten directions; The Tathāgata’s radiance shines everywhere, Able to remove the defilements of sentient beings’ afflictions, Proclaiming the profound and pure Dharma.
Throughout oceans of immeasurable kalpas, the Buddha has extensively cultivated pure lands through skillful means;
with the supreme voice of all-knowledge, he brings comfort to boundless multitudes of sentient beings.
The Tathāgata Joyful to Behold is universally pure; May all sentient beings attain inexhaustible bliss.
Following this, they can give rise to the causes of liberation; Attaining the crown of liberation, their hearts are filled with joy.
The obstacles and hindrances of ignorance are exceedingly firm; sentient beings revolve within the ocean of birth and death.
The Tathāgata manifests the vast Dharma, proclaiming the pure teaching and erecting the banner of the Dharma.
For all sentient beings through immeasurable gateways, the Tathāgata manifests various forms;
with many doors of skillful means he illuminates sentient beings—thus does the Tathāgata Priyaghoṣa manifest.
The Tathāgata’s skillful means are boundless; the Sugata, fully endowed with them, extensively reveals and manifests them.
Entering the practice of skillful means on the most supreme path, he attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Vajra tree.
Taking immeasurable eons as a single thought-instant, the Buddha’s power can manifest them without accumulation;
he is able to bestow all happiness upon sentient beings—this is called the "Gate of Skillful Means for Delightful Vision."
Furthermore, there was the Kumbhāṇḍa King Virūḍhaka, who had attained mastery over the dharma-gate of extinguishing all strife and contention;
the Kumbhāṇḍa Dīrghapradīpāloka, who had attained mastery over the dharma-gate of manifesting all practices before one;
and the Kumbhāṇḍa Sukṛtadhvaja, who had attained mastery over the dharma-gate of correctly directing all realms of existence.
The Kumbhāṇḍa Benefactor of All Conditioned Phenomena attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the equal purity of good and evil;
the Kumbhāṇḍa Remover of Fear attained mastery in the Dharma-door of fearless, peaceful, and secure adornment for all sentient beings;
and the Kumbhāṇḍa Purifier of the Śāla Forest attained mastery in the Dharma-door of extinguishing the blazing ocean of craving of immeasurable sentient beings.
The Kumbhāṇḍa Sumeru-udgata attained mastery in the dharma-door of the Cloud of Illumination in All Realms of Existence;
the Kumbhāṇḍa Nityodyukta attained mastery in the dharma-door of Universal Radiance;
and the Kumbhāṇḍa Ananta-viśuddha-cakṣus attained mastery in the dharma-door of Arising the Treasury of Non-retrogressive Great Compassion.
The Kumbhāṇḍa of Immeasurable Gates has attained mastery over the dharma-gate of performing all activities for the sake of all realms of existence.
At that time, the Kumbhāṇḍa King Virūḍhaka, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of Kumbhāṇḍas and spoke in verse:
“The Tathāgata has perfected the power of patience; For immeasurable eons, he practiced for the sake of sentient beings.”
Free from negligence, pride, and all afflictions, The Buddha’s body is pure, illuminating the ten directions.
In the past, he practiced the ocean of bodhisattva deeds, Taming immeasurable multitudes throughout the ten directions.
Through various skillful means, he opened the gates of compassion, Causing sentient beings to attain all-encompassing wisdom.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom rescues all living beings; He discerns and knows the minds of all sentient beings.
With immeasurable mastery, he disciplines sentient beings; All who behold him are filled with joy.
The realm of the Buddha’s spiritual power is inconceivable;
throughout all kalpas of the future, he turns the true wheel of Dharma like space, so that immeasurable sentient beings attain the pure eye.
Sentient beings have the defilement of ignorance obscuring the eye of their minds; the Tathāgata illuminates and removes it so they may see the true path.
He rescues and delivers them so they forever leave behind immeasurable suffering, causing them to be free from fear and attain pure wisdom.
Sentient beings are submerged in the ocean of the suffering of craving; the Tathāgata’s wisdom shines upon them, extinguishing it without remainder.
Free from desire and undefiled, they behold the Buddha-body, which is as utterly pure as a jewel tree.
The Buddha’s body responds universally, nowhere unseen; Through various skillful means, he transforms sentient beings.
His voice thunders like a roll of thunder, raining down the rain of Dharma; This is called the "Wisdom Dharma Door of the Mountain King."
The Buddha’s light is stainless and most pure; It illuminates and dispels the mountain of sentient beings’ delusion and darkness.
It manifests the immeasurable virtues of the Tathāgata; Through skillful means free from delusion, one beholds the Buddha-body.
Having cultivated the gate of great compassion for immeasurable eons, you bestow upon all sentient beings sovereign bliss;
through various skillful means, you extinguish all sufferings, becoming stainless and pure like a blossoming flower.
The Supreme One’s manifested body pervades all, Without coming or going throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
The Great Sage, through self-awakening, manifests everything— This is what the Buddha can perceive through his immeasurable gateways.
Furthermore, there was the Naga King Vairocana, who attained mastery over the dharma-door of extinguishing all burning terrors within the realm of nagas and providing relief;
the Naga King Sāgara, who attained mastery over the dharma-door of being able, in a single thought-moment, to transform all inconceivable naga bodies;
and the Naga King Meghasvararāja-sudhvaja, who attained mastery over the dharma-door of turning the wheel of purity and hearing sounds throughout all realms of existence.
The Naga King Universal Banner of Mount Sumeru attained mastery in the dharma-door of manifesting the ocean of great merit for all sentient beings;
the Naga King Takshaka attained mastery in the dharma-door of purity free from fear;
and the Naga King Immeasurable Steps attained mastery in the dharma-door of manifesting immeasurable clouds for all sentient beings, transcending immeasurable eons, and abiding in longevity.
The dragon Jvālākṣa-susthita attained mastery in the dharma-door of manifesting the skillful means for distinguishing the immeasurable Buddha-dharmas throughout all established worlds;
the dragon Vimalavega-varṇa attained mastery in the dharma-door of entering the skillful means of stainlessness, joy, and contentment for all sentient beings;
the dragon Samantacāra-vipula-ārya attained mastery in the dharma-door of the equal contemplation that fulfills all sounds, whether good or evil.
The Nāga King Anavatapta has attained mastery in the Dharma-door of using the canopy of great compassion clouds to cover all sentient beings and free them from suffering.
At that time, the Nāga King Virūpākṣa, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of nāgas and spoke in verse:
“Beholding all the most supreme Dharmas, He rescues and delivers the multitudes of beings throughout the ten directions.”
Sentient beings in the evil realms are constantly transmigrating, yet through the power of great compassion, he is able to rescue and deliver them.
According to the forms favored by each sentient being, the Buddha manifests within every single pore;
the realm of his supernormal powers is immeasurable, as the ocean of the Buddha’s merit appears with perfect purity.
The most supreme and wondrous Dharma is immeasurable, like the great ocean deep and bottomless;
according to what beings delight in, they are enabled to hear it, as a wondrous voice, soft yet resonant, issues forth like the sound of thunder.
All sentient beings harbor hearts of anger, Enveloped by the veils and shrouds of the ocean of ignorance;
The Tathāgata, with supreme great compassion, Liberates them through the power of his spiritual feet.
Within a single pore of the Tathāgata’s body, the merits of all sentient beings are fully manifested;
entering the deep and immeasurable ocean of merit, the Meru-mountain-banner merit appears.
The various fears and sufferings of sentient beings, the Dharma King’s light of wisdom rescues them all;
from his most supreme pore he emanates wondrous sounds, opening the pure eyes of immeasurable beings.
