The Tathāgatas of the ten directions and three periods of time manifest their physical forms within the Buddha’s body;
having purified Buddha-lands throughout immeasurable eons, this is called the Ground of the Supreme Great Dragon.

Within a single hair-pore of the Buddha, all are clearly manifested: immeasurable supernatural transformations adorning the lands, with the Buddha seated surrounded by his retinue, preaching the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
When the Buddha was a bodhisattva seeking the Way, he reverently made offerings to oceans of Buddhas;
through various and immeasurable gates of skillful means, he delivered and liberated oceans of all sentient beings.
When the Tathāgata expounds the True Dharma, he fills all sentient beings with joy;
the Buddha’s voice can arouse hearts of delight, causing all beings everywhere to attain the bliss of the Dharma.
Furthermore, there was the Yakṣa King Vaiśravaṇa, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of the skillful means of equanimous contemplation that abandons all evil and benefits sentient beings;
the Yakṣa Ghoṣeśvara, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of universal supremacy;
and the Yakṣa Dharaṇīdhara, who had attained mastery in the Dharma-door of being able to eliminate the vital energy stolen from sentient beings and to nourish all life-sustaining energies.
The yakṣa Sarvanetrapati attained mastery in the dharma-door of contemplating all the holy qualities;
the yakṣa Viśiṣṭanetra attained mastery in the dharma-door of contemplating the wisdom of all sentient beings;
the yakṣa Dṛḍhavajranetra attained mastery in the dharma-door of bestowing peace and happiness upon all sentient beings.
The yakṣa Life-Protector attained mastery in the dharma-door of the method for rescuing through the power of upholding;
the yakṣa Able-to-Shatter-Sumeru attained mastery in the dharma-door of the method for generating accordance with the Buddha’s power.
At that time, the Yakṣa King Vaiśravaṇa, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the assembly of yakṣas and spoke in verse:
“The afflictions and defilements of sentient beings are exceedingly deep and heavy; for hundreds of thousands of kalpas they have not seen a Buddha.
Wandering through birth and death, they undergo manifold sufferings; it is to deliver such as these that the Buddha has appeared in the world.”
For the sake of rescuing and relieving all beings, the Buddha appears before the multitudes in the ten directions;
he extracts them from the wheel of suffering in the various realms of existence, for he is the Lord of Causes and Conditions, whose skillful means are supreme.
The heavy sins and karmic obstacles of sentient beings, the Buddha completely eliminates through skillful means;
he establishes sentient beings within the True Dharma—this is called the vision of the skillful means for departing from delusion.
When the Buddha practiced for immeasurable eons in the past, He praised all the Buddhas of the ten directions;
Therefore, he possesses a lofty and great reputation, Which is heard everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions.
The Buddha’s wisdom is boundless, equal to space; The Tathāgata’s Dharma-body is inconceivable.
Thus he can manifest and illuminate the ten directions, This sublime Dharma-gate of the King of Luminous Pure Eyes.
All sentient beings have entered upon wrong paths; the Buddha reveals the inconceivable right path.
Seeing that all sentient beings are capable of being transformed, he employs various skillful means to bring them under discipline.
The various merits of all sentient beings do not equal the blessing of a single ray of light from the Tathāgata;
the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom is inconceivable—this is what is seen by the King of Jewels.
Throughout inconceivable numbers of immeasurable eons, the Buddha cultivated the ten powers therein;
therefore, the World-Honored One is fully endowed with these powers, and none in all the worlds can destroy them.
Furthermore, the Malla Vajranetra-avabhāsa attained mastery in the dharma-gate of manifesting the infinite forms and images of the Tathāgata;
the Malla Vimalasūryodgata attained mastery in the dharma-gate of the infinite colors of all Buddhas;
and the Malla Sumerukusumaprabha attained mastery in the dharma-gate of various manifestations through stainless sovereignty.
The Malla Śuddhameghasvara attained mastery over the immeasurable dharma-gate of the Tathāgata’s boundless pure voice;
the Malla Asurarājendra attained mastery over the dharma-gate of manifesting all manner of things;
and the Malla Vajraprabhasukha attained mastery over the dharma-gate of entering all Buddha-dharmas without exception.
The Malla Thunderous Sound attained mastery over the dharma-door of being able to lift all the dharmas of the devas;
the Malla Lion-Dignified King attained mastery over the dharma-door of the broad illumination of the Tathāgata’s merits;
and the Malla Supreme Radiance attained mastery over the dharma-door of eliminating the evil minds of sentient beings and establishing them in the realm of the Buddha.
The Malla Jewel-Crest Flower-Radiance attained mastery in the dharma-gate of manifesting the raining of jewels upon all worlds for bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Malla Vajra-Eye Illumination, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire assembly of Mallas and spoke in verse:
“For the sake of all beings throughout the three realms, He acts as the Dharma King among all phenomena.”
Endowed with immeasurable and wondrous forms, they illuminate the ten directions so that nothing remains unlit.
From every single pore of the Buddha’s body, inconceivable rays of light are universally emitted;
they eclipse the brilliance of all the suns, shining everywhere throughout the ten directions without exception.
The Tathāgata’s great, holy power of mastery fills all dharma-realms;
the Dharma-body manifests without limit, appearing before all sentient beings.
The Buddha’s voice is pure, profound, and wondrous, Resounding throughout all worlds in the ten directions;
With its supple, subtle, harmonious, and elegant tones, It extinguishes the defilements of sentient beings and fulfills their aspirations.
In all the palaces of the triple world throughout the ten directions, the most supreme [Buddhas] appear seated therein;
at each and every Buddha’s abode, amidst immeasurable multitudes, the Guide sits in their midst and preaches the Dharma.
The ocean of Dharma is immeasurable and boundless; All gates of skillful means enter therein.
Discerning all realms of phenomena, The Most Victorious One manifests them without end.
The great ocean of sentient beings is without limit; The most supreme, pure-eyed one can deliver them all.
The Tathāgata’s radiance shines upon all beings, So that everyone may behold the Great Teacher.
All pay respectful homage and present offerings to the Buddhas of immeasurable oceans of lands;
their merits are as boundless as space, and all behold the Great Teacher.
The Tathāgata’s spiritual power is indestructible, manifesting all Buddha-lands;
the Tathāgata sits serenely within the pure site of enlightenment, visible before the eyes of all sentient beings.
Light shines universally like rising clouds; Adorned with myriad wonders, its radiance is perfect and full.
It illuminates all realms of phenomena, Revealing the profound and wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva had accomplished an ocean of inconceivable gates of skillful means and was able to enter the ocean of the Tathāgata’s immeasurable merits.
That is to say:
the dharma-gate of giving birth to and ultimately purifying all Buddha-lands to discipline sentient beings;
and the dharma-gate of approaching the presence of all Buddhas to give rise to all fully perfected merits.
The Dharma-door of the vows and practices of the various stages of the Bodhisattvas;
the Dharma-door of universally manifesting clouds of bodies as numerous as the atoms within the dharma-realm;
and the Dharma-door of upholding the inconceivable wheels of skillful means of all Buddha-lands.
The dharma gate of manifesting the infinite and boundless realms of Bodhisattvas with sovereign mastery amidst all assemblies;
the dharma gate of knowing the arising and ceasing of kalpas throughout the three periods of time within a single thought-moment;
and the dharma gate of discerning and manifesting the ocean-like realms of the faculties of all Bodhisattvas.
The dharma-gate of the sovereign body filling the immeasurable and boundless Dharma-realm;
and the dharma-gate of the skillful means of all Bodhisattvas’ various expedients for extensively discerning phenomena and entering the skillful means of omniscience.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva surveyed the entire assembly and spoke in verse:
"Most supreme and pure are the countless Buddha-fields, With immeasurable pure forms and profound merit."
Truly pure and free from defilement, the sons of the Buddha fill [the world], constantly hearing the wondrous Dharma and its inconceivable sounds.
Seeing the Buddha here upon this lion throne, it is likewise so within all atoms of dust.
Yet the body of the Tathāgata does not go there; rather, it universally manifests throughout the buddha-fields and the realms of merit. It fully enters into the infinite skillful means of all stages.
The Buddha reveals all the practices of the bodhisattvas and explains these various skillful means.
Inconceivable! Causing all the sons of the Buddhas to enter the pure Dharma-realm, with stainless and pure eyes, they abide in the profound nature of phenomena.
Without limit or boundary, equal in number to motes of dust, the bodies of these emanation Buddhas teach and guide immeasurable multitudes of sentient beings.
In all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, the World-Honored One provides equal protection for them all.
Through skillful means, the Buddha has attained complete purity, taming sentient beings and causing them to eliminate their defilements.
Throughout all lands as numerous as atoms, the Tathāgata manifests infinite mastery.
With a harmonious and elegant Brahma-voice that pervades every site of enlightenment, he expounds the supreme and fundamental practices of the Bodhisattvas.
Throughout all three periods of time, All kalpas that exist, Within every single thought-moment,
He perceives them all without exception.
Inconceivable is the World-Protector’s ability to see The immeasurable multitudes.
Their number is inexhaustible;
all these dharma-gates are immeasurable and boundless, beyond the scope of the sons of the Buddha.
The Tathāgata Vimalaprabha is like empty space: pure and unattached, equal to the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
He manifests infinite emanations that are inexhaustible; all sit beneath the tree of enlightenment and attain perfect awakening.
With a single word, the Buddha expounds all stages; the characteristics of all phenomena are entirely exhausted therein.
Through immeasurable skillful means, within each and every gateway, he elucidates all dharmas, leaving nothing remaining.

At that time, from within every single ornament—such as the lion throne of the Buddha, the exquisite flowers, the mani-jewel wheels, the high platforms, and the multi-storied pavilions—an assembly of great bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-world emerged one by one. Their names were as follows:

The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-viśeṣa, the Bodhisattva Amitasiṃhanāda, the Bodhisattva Sarvaratnaprabhāketu, the Bodhisattva Jñānasūryaviśeṣamati, the Bodhisattva Acintyaguṇajñānasaṃbhava, the Bodhisattva Upāyaśāntisumanoṣṇīṣa, the Bodhisattva Suvarṇakārciḥ, the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātusvaraviśuddha, the Bodhisattva Vimalameghacandradhvaja, and the Bodhisattva Viśuddhaprabhāviśeṣa—these and other great bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within each buddha-world, prepared various offerings. They scattered myriad exquisite flowers that filled the void, burned diverse incenses whose fragrance surpassed rising clouds, and manifested everywhere the circular halos of all manner of jewels.

Furthermore, they emitted the pure light of immeasurable suns and produced the subtle sounds of various musical performances. From the branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits of diverse jewel-trees, all manner of radiance arose like clouds, raining down immeasurable treasures. Each of these offering implements of every single bodhisattva was equal in number to the atoms within a buddha-world;

each individual article of offering was likewise equal in number to the atoms within a buddha-world. All were filled with great joy as they made offerings to the World-Honored One. After circumambulating him hundreds of thousands of times, they made offerings to the great assembly according to their respective capacities, continuing without interruption like falling rain. Following the direction from which they emerged, they manifested lion thrones of precious lotus-treasures and sat cross-legged in reverent homage toward the Buddha.

Those Bodhisattvas have all attained the Dharma-door of Universal Radiance, the Immeasurable Ocean of Pure Dharmas; they encounter no obstacles within the realm of the Buddhas and have fully entered the ocean of all eloquence.

Furthermore, they have attained the inconceivable Dharma-door of Illumination, dwelling correctly in the universal gateway realm of the Tathāgatas; they have already entered the ground of wisdom of the three periods of time and are fully accomplished in the great power of Dharma-love. Their immeasurable merits are pure and perfect; they constantly practice the ultimate emptiness of the dharma-realm and have fully completed offerings to all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvasāgarabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñārājan spoke in verse:
“The Buddha awakens to all phenomena as equal and true,
Unobstructed and pure like space.”
Universally illuminating the worlds of the ten directions, dwelling among all beings, most supreme and extraordinary;
self-awakened, immeasurable and boundless, filling the realms of sentient beings throughout the ten directions.
All sit beneath the King of Bodhi Trees, surrounded by the lords of all sentient beings.
In a single thought-moment, they manifest infinite bodies, causing all sentient beings everywhere to—
Having eradicated all defilements, the realm of the Tathāgata is without limit; throughout oceans of immeasurable eons, he has fully perfected his practice.
The Tathāgata, dwelling within the ocean of all existence, employs various skillful means to subdue sentient beings.
They all receive and practice the most supreme True Dharma; the assembly is freed from defilement and universally attains purity.
Possessing the most supreme and wondrous marks, fully adorned with all ornaments, he dwells upon a precious lion throne within a lotus treasury,
amidst every kind of jewel and all manner of decorative embellishments.
All emit immeasurable, subtle, and exquisite fragrances, while flower garlands of variegated colors hang and spread throughout space.
Immeasurable multitudes of jewels stream forth wondrous light; their radiant flames are pure and serene.
Radiant throughout the ten directions,
he brings forth pure and subtle, secret Brahma-sounds, proclaiming the most excellent,
unsurpassed True Dharma.
A vajra serves as its base, standing firm and solid; it is adorned with the wish-fulfilling treasury jewel.
The Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin constantly guards it.
The World-Honored One, here universally manifests illumination.
The Celestial Honored One dwells upon the precious lion throne, shining throughout the three periods of time, the Teacher of all.
"Immeasurable transformation Buddhas fill the ten directions, proclaiming the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the Tathāgata.
At that time, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, the Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean shook in six ways and eighteen manners.
That is to say:
it shakes, shakes everywhere, and shakes equally everywhere;
it rises, rises everywhere, and rises equally everywhere.
Awakening, fully awakening, and equally fully awakening;
shaking, fully shaking, and equally fully shaking;
roaring, fully roaring, and equally fully roaring.
It surged, surged everywhere, and surged equally everywhere.
Furthermore, it caused all the kings of every world-system to each rain down inconceivable articles of offering to worship the ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata;
that is to say:

They rained down clouds of all kinds of fragrant flowers, clouds of various wonderful jewels, clouds of multicolored jewel lotuses, clouds of *mandāra* flowers of immeasurable colors, clouds of liberation-jewels, clouds of powdered sandalwood incense, clouds of pure and gentle sounds, and clouds of jewel-nets like the sun; each, according to its power, rained down these manifold offerings. Thus, the kings of every single world-system established inconceivable clouds of offerings, universally making offerings to the great assemblies of all Tathāgatas;
as it was in this world, so it was in all the Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions.

In this world, the Buddha sits at the site of enlightenment; the kings of all worlds, each according to their own preferred realm, samādhi, and various gates of skillful means, have attained joy, renunciation, and detachment, and have mastered the courageous dharmas of all directions. They have already crossed over into the Tathāgata’s realm entered by spiritual power and the gates of the immeasurable ocean of dharmas of all Buddhas;
as it is in this world, so it is in all worlds throughout the ten directions.
Chapter Two: Vairocana Buddha. At that time, the assembly of bodhisattvas and all the kings of the worlds all had this thought:
"What is the ground of all buddhas?"
The Buddha’s realm? The Buddha’s sustaining power?
The Buddha’s conduct?
The Buddha’s power?
The Buddha’s fearlessness?
The Buddha’s samādhi?
Is it the Buddha’s sovereignty?
Is it the Buddha’s manifestation of supreme dharmas as awakening?
Or is it the Buddha’s faculties of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind?
The Buddha’s light, his voice,
his ocean of wisdom,
or his ocean of worlds?
The ocean of sentient beings?
The ocean of skillful means of the Dharma-realm?
The ocean of Buddhas?
The ocean of pāramitās?
The ocean of dharma-gates?
The ocean of transformation bodies?
The ocean of the names of Buddhas?
The ocean of the lifespans of Buddhas?
The ocean of all the practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas?
How does one give rise to the mind of the Mahāyāna and produce the treasury of vows and wisdom that gives birth to all the pāramitās?
I only pray that the Tathāgata, through his compassionate skillful means, will inspire my mind and enable me to attain understanding and liberation.
At that time, by the supernatural power of the bodhisattvas, a spontaneous sound issued from all the articles of offering, and they spoke these verses:
“The Tathāgata practiced through immeasurable and vast eons; Spontaneously awakened to perfect enlightenment in the world.
Throughout immeasurable eons in the future, His body shall respond to all beings like a great cloud.”
Severing the doubts of sentient beings forever without remainder, Giving birth to supreme power and attaining liberation,
Extinguishing the immeasurable sufferings of the world, Causing all to attain the bliss of perfect enlightenment.
Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable lands, with single-minded palms joined, gaze upon the Most Victorious One;
according to their respective aspirations and realms, they sever doubts and open the gates of the Dharma.
What is the ground of all Buddhas, the realm of the Great Sage, and the various dhāraṇīs of the Buddha?
The supreme power of wisdom and fearlessness of the Buddha—may you, for the sake of the sons of the Buddha, reveal these with impartiality.
The immeasurable and authentic samādhis, the profound and wondrous dharmas of all pure practices,
and the boundless supernatural power of the Great Sage— these raise great thunderclouds to rain down upon sentient beings.
May they all enter the true path of the Dharma King, Never regressing from the most supreme state;
And regarding the immeasurable virtues of the Buddhas, I pray that through the arising of compassion, all may behold them.
The Tathāgata’s faculty of the eye is immeasurable; so too are his faculties of ear, nose, tongue, and body.
The Buddha’s mind is true to reality and difficult to conceive; may he cause all sentient beings to fully know and see it.

The oceans of Buddha-lands and the oceans of sentient beings, The oceans of all dharmas and the oceans of those to be tamed— The oceans of Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless; May the sons of the Buddha perceive them all with equanimity.

The ocean of pāramitās is inconceivable; the ocean of the unsurpassed dharma-gates of skillful means, the ocean of immeasurable and boundless dharma-gates—may you fully expound them at this site of enlightenment.

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas, immediately emitted from his face and from between each of his teeth rays of light as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-world.

They are as follows: the light called Jewel Banner Illumination; the light called Adornment of the Sublime Sound of the Dharma Realm; the light called Clouds Hanging Down to Grant Joy; the light called Purifying the Site of Enlightenment with the Ten Powers of a Buddha; the light called Clouds of All Jewel Flames; the light called Pure and Unobstructed Pervading the Dharma Realm; the light called Able to Accomplish All Worlds; the light called Pure Jewel Vajra Sun Banner;

the light called Approaching the Great Assembly of Bodhisattvas; and the light called Manifesting the Wheel of Speech of All Buddhas. Each of these lights has as many attendant lights as there are atoms in a Buddha-world.
Each individual ray of light illumines as many lands as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields;
when those bodhisattvas behold these lights, they are able to see the Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean.
By the Buddha’s spiritual power, a verse is spoken within the light:
Having cultivated merit for oceans of immeasurable eons, Making offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions,
And transforming an ocean of boundless sentient beings, The Buddha Vairocana attained perfect enlightenment.
Emitting great radiance that illuminates the ten directions, From every pore, clouds of transformation bodies emerge;
According to the capacities of sentient beings, they bring them to enlightenment, Causing them to attain the path of skillful means and purity.
Throughout the cycle of birth and death in the distant past, the Buddha tamed all living beings;
in a single thought-moment, he brought them all to liberation, for the Hero of the World has attained infinite mastery.
Adorned everywhere by profound resolve and pure faith, having fulfilled the pāramitās through past cultivation,
they dwell with steadfast stability in all powers, as numerous as the atoms within oceans of lands.
He utters subtle sounds that pervade the ten directions; Possessing perfect true wisdom, he fulfills the hearts of all beings.
With immeasurable skillful means, he transforms sentient beings; This is the lion’s roar of the dharma of tranquility.
The Honored One among Men possesses such immeasurable virtues; One should go to him to make offerings and listen to the Dharma.
As numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields, the most excellent sons of the Victor approached the Tathāgata;
each rained down every kind of offering, and with single-minded reverence, they gazed upon the Teacher.
Within a single word spoken by the Tathāgata, he brings forth an ocean of boundless sūtras;
raining down nectar upon all beings, I approach with reverence the Honored One among Two-legged Beings.
The unsurpassed vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time were expounded in detail by the Great Sage at the site of enlightenment;
they are not gathered within a single thought-moment, so you should quickly go to behold the Most Victorious One.
The great ocean of Vairocana’s wisdom Shines its radiance everywhere without measure;
Observing the dharma of ultimate truth as it truly is, It universally illuminates all gates of dharma.
At that time, to the east of the Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, there was another world-ocean named Pure Lotus Supreme Light Adornment.
Within it was a buddha-field named Multitude of Jewels Vajra Treasury, where the Buddha was named Dharma-Water Awakened Space Dharma-King.

In the midst of that Tathāgata’s ocean-like great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named King of Contemplating the Supreme Dharma of Sublime Purity. Having been awakened by the Buddha’s light, he came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of a world-ocean, filling all the voids of the ten directions.

They produced ten kinds of clouds of jewel-colored light-flower mists, which completely covered and filled all of space; ten kinds of clouds of exquisite jewel Sumeru mountains, ten kinds of clouds of solar discs, ten kinds of clouds of precious flowers, ten kinds of clouds of exquisite jewel pavilions, ten kinds of clouds of flowering trees, ten kinds of clouds of exquisite incense manifesting various colors, and ten kinds of clouds of all manner of sublime sounds—all these completely covered and filled all of space. Having approached the place where the Buddha was, they made offerings, paid homage, and prostrated themselves. Then, in the east, upon a lion throne of variegated flower-light treasury, they sat cross-legged.
To the south of this world-ocean, there is another world-ocean named Treasury Adorned with the Moonlight of Various Jewels;
within it is a buddha-field named Array of Immeasurable Light, where the Buddha is named Supreme Sumeru King of Universal Wisdom-Light.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva named Pure Ocean-Wisdom, who, having been inspired by the Buddha’s radiance, came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
They raised ten kinds of clouds of kings of all manner of wonderful adornment treasuries made of various jewels, which completely covered and filled the void;
ten kinds of clouds of universally adorned jewel-kings; ten kinds of clouds of jewel-kings from wonderful treasure-treasuries that blazed with light and extolled the Buddha’s virtues;
and ten kinds of clouds of jewel-kings whose wonderful sounds filled the air in praise.
Clouds of ten kinds of jewel-kings adorning the site of enlightenment with bodhi-trees;
clouds of ten kinds of jewel-kings of the Buddha’s transformations manifesting universal gateways of light; clouds of ten kinds of jewel-kings manifesting indestructible multitudes of light;
clouds of ten kinds of jewel-kings filling all lands with the illumination of fragrant lamps; and ten kinds of inconceivable...

Clouds of jewel-kings manifesting the palaces of all Buddha-fields, and clouds of jewel-kings of the light of the dharma-bodies of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time— all these completely covered and filled the void,
coming to the place where the Buddha was; having paid homage, made offerings, and prostrated, they remained in the south, [of] a blue color.
Upon a lotus lion throne, he sat in the full lotus posture.
To the west of this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Jewel Light Joy;
within it is a buddha-field named All-Excelling Vision, where the Buddha is named King of Fragrant Light, Adorned with the Jewels of Merit.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva named Fragrant Flame Equally Adorned Moonlight. Having been awakened by the Buddha’s radiance, he approached the presence of the Buddha, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
He manifested ten kinds of clouds of pavilions made of all manner of miscellaneous jewel-scented flowers, which completely covered and filled the void of space;
[and likewise] ten kinds of clouds of pavilions adorned with all colors of jewel-kings, ten kinds of...
Clouds of pavilions like fragrant flames from precious banners; ten kinds of clouds of pavilions adorned with all forms of liberation;
ten kinds of clouds of all precious flower garlands; ten kinds of clouds of precious pavilions adorned with all kinds of precious wreaths;
ten kinds of clouds of pavilions that illuminate all adornments from the treasury of universal light.
Clouds of pavilions manifesting all kinds of jewel adornments and infinite arrays, ten kinds of pavilion clouds of universal and perfect adornment,
and ten kinds of clouds of immeasurable flowers and music— all completely covering and filling the void—
approached the place where the Buddha was; having made offerings, paid respect, and prostrated, they remained there.
In the west, upon a magically manifested lion throne adorned with golden lotuses and various jewels,
he sat cross-legged.
To the north of this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Treasury Filled with Lapis Lazuli Jewel Light.
Within it was a buddha-field named Adorned with Manifested Blue Lotuses; the Buddha there was named King of Infinite Wisdom Sound.

Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva named Lion Light Adornment, who, having been awakened by the Buddha’s radiance, came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.

He manifested ten kinds of clouds of all manner of incense, which completely covered and filled the void; ten kinds of clouds of all manner of blue flowers, ten kinds of clouds of all manner of exquisite jewel trees, ten kinds of clouds of all manner of various flowers, ten kinds of clouds of all manner of jewel adornments, ten kinds of clouds of all manner of jewel thunder-sounds, and ten kinds of clouds of all manner of exquisite sounds—all such as these completely covered and filled the void. Having approached the place where the Buddha was, and having made offerings, paid homage, and prostrated, he sat cross-legged upon the Lion Throne of Great Lamp Transformation in the northern quarter.
To the southeast of this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Jāmbūnada-vaidūrya-varṇa-dhvaja;
within it is a buddha-field named Ratnavyūhagarbha, where the Buddha is named Sarvadharma-pradīpa-avibhīta.

Within that Tathāgata’s great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named Akṣaya-jaya-pradīpa-guṇa-dharmagarbha, who, having been awakened by the Buddha’s radiance, comes toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
He manifested ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of immeasurable-colored lotuses, which completely covered and filled all of space;
ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones adorned with every kind of ornament; ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones of radiant lamps;
and ten kinds of [clouds] capable of producing [light] throughout the ten directions.
Clouds of lion thrones made of all kinds of jewels; clouds of lion thrones with ten kinds of all manner of fragrant garlands;
clouds of lion thrones manifesting ten kinds of all Buddhas’ adornments;
clouds of lion thrones adorned with ten kinds of all precious platforms and railings; clouds of lion thrones adorned with ten kinds of all precious trees.
Clouds of lion thrones adorned with ten kinds of suns, all completely covering and filling the void,
came to where the Buddha was; having made offerings, paid homage, and prostrated,
they sat cross-legged upon lion throne-clouds of nocturnal light-bannered jewel-treasuries in the southeastern quarter.
To the southwest of this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Universal Radiance Adornment;
within it is a buddha-field named Fragrant, Victorious, and Stainless Light, where the Buddha is named King Who Universally Delights All Sentient Beings.

Within that Tathāgata’s great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Lamp of Wisdom of Universal Knowledge Radiance, who, having been awakened by the Buddha’s light, came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of an ocean of worlds.

They manifested ten kinds of clouds of wish-fulfilling jewel-kings, which completely covered and filled the void; ten kinds of blue jewel clouds, ten kinds of clouds of all fragrances, ten kinds of clouds of all banners, and ten kinds of clouds of exquisite colored ornaments—all completely covering and filling the void. Having approached the Buddha’s presence to make offerings, pay respect, and prostrate, they sat cross-legged upon lion thrones made of various jewels in the southwest direction.
To the northwest of this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Good Radiance;
within it is a buddha-field named Entering the Mind, where the Buddha is named Pure Sound of Universal Gate Wisdom Entering the Mind.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva named Infinite Flower Radiance Hanging Topknot, who, having been awakened by the Buddha’s light, came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of an ocean of worlds.

They manifested ten kinds of clouds of wheels and canopies made of all manner of mixed jewels, which completely covered and filled the void; ten kinds of clouds of flower canopies, ten kinds of clouds of liberation canopies, ten kinds of clouds of jewel-king canopies, ten kinds of clouds of mixed-jewel canopies, ten kinds of clouds of universal-jewel canopies, ten kinds of clouds of lapis lazuli jewel-king canopies, and ten kinds of clouds of all-scented canopies—all of which completely covered and filled the void. Having approached the Buddha’s presence to make offerings, pay respect, and prostrate, they sat cross-legged upon lion thrones called "Banner of the Light of All Virtues" in the northwest direction.
To the northeast of this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Jewel-Illuminating Radiance Treasury;
within it is a buddha-field named Fragrant Adornment Joyful Supreme Treasury, where the Buddha is named Infinite Ocean of Merit.

Within that Tathāgata’s great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named King of Inexhaustible Pure Radiance, who, having been inspired by the Buddha’s light, came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.

They raised ten kinds of clouds of all-jeweled light-wheels, which completely covered and filled the void; ten kinds of clouds of light-wheels, ten kinds of clouds of flowers, ten kinds of clouds of Tathāgata-transformation wheels, ten kinds of clouds of all-Buddha-sphere wheels, ten kinds of clouds of all-merit jewels, ten kinds of clouds of inexhaustible manifestations for the joy of all sentient beings, and ten kinds of clouds of manifestations of the vows of all Buddhas—all of these completely covered and filled the void. Having approached the place where the Buddha was, they made offerings, paid respect, and prostrated, then sat cross-legged upon lion thrones of inexhaustible pure radiance in the northeast.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Two;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Three.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Part Two of the Second Chapter on Vairocana Buddha.
Beneath this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Lotus Exquisite Fragrance Supreme Treasury;
within it is a buddha-field named Jewel Lion Light, where the Buddha is named Illuminating the Dharma Realm.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva named Light Illuminating the Differentiation of the Dharma Realm. Having been inspired by the Buddha’s radiance, he approached the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.

He manifested ten kinds of clouds of light from all manner of jewels, which completely covered and filled the void; ten kinds of clouds of light from all manner of fragrances; ten kinds of clouds of the lion’s roar of all Buddhas; ten kinds of clouds of the meritorious adornments of all Buddha-fields; and ten kinds of clouds of flowered pavilions and ten kinds of clouds of seat-adornments—all of which completely covered and filled the void. Arriving at the Buddha’s presence, he sat cross-legged upon a treasure-store lion throne in the region below.
Above this ocean of worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Adorned by the Sea of Variegated Jewel Radiance.
Within it is a buddha-field named Pure Realm of Joyful Practice, where the Buddha is named King of Unobstructed Merit and Renown Who Dispels Darkness with Light.

In the midst of that Tathāgata’s great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Unobstructed Power, Diligence, and Wisdom. Having been inspired by the Buddha’s radiance, he came toward the Buddha’s presence, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
He manifested ten kinds of clouds of all-infinite, wondrously colored jewel-illumination that completely covered and filled the void;
ten kinds of clouds of infinite light universally shining; ten kinds of clouds of illumination of all adornments;
ten kinds of clouds of fragrant flames; ten kinds of clouds of all adornments; and ten kinds of Buddha-rays.
Flame-clouds, ten kinds of jewel-tree flower-flame clouds, ten kinds of all-jewel-tree firm radiance clouds,
ten kinds of all-supreme radiance clouds, ten kinds of all-bodhisattva-practice manifestation clouds,
and ten kinds of all-liberation radiance clouds completely overspread and filled [the space].

Filling the entirety of space, they came to where the Buddha was; having made offerings, paid respects, and prostrated, they sat cross-legged upon lion thrones of exquisite sound and supreme lotus-treasury in the upper direction.

From as many world-oceans as there are atoms in ten billion buddha-fields, there came great bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields. Each of these bodhisattvas was accompanied by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a single buddha-field. Each bodhisattva brought forth clouds of exquisite adornments as numerous as the atoms in a single buddha-field, which completely covered and filled the void. Arriving from their respective directions, they sat cross-legged.

Once those bodhisattvas had sat down in succession, from every single pore there issued forth clouds of pure light made of all manner of exquisite jewels, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-worlds. From within each ray of light, there emerged bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-worlds; each of these bodhisattvas filled all the paths as numerous as the atoms in the ocean of skillful means throughout the entire dharma-realm.
Within each atom, there were buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-worlds;
and within each of those buddha-lands, all the buddhas of the three periods of time were clearly manifest.
In every thought-moment, within each and every world, they transform as many sentient beings as there are atoms in a Buddha-field,
teaching them through the dharma-gate of manifesting mastery over dreams, the dharma-gate of the miraculous birth of all devas,
the dharma-gate of the sounds of the spheres of action of all bodhisattvas, and by shaking all Buddha-fields.
The teaching through the dharma-door of establishing all Buddha-dharmas; the teaching through the dharma-door of the ocean of all vows;
the teaching through the dharma-door of entering the Buddha’s voice by means of the speech of all sentient beings; the teaching through the dharma-door of the rain-clouds of all Buddha-dharmas;
the teaching through the dharma-door of the light of sovereignty over the dharma-realm; and the establishment of all greatness.
The Ocean of Multitudes is taught within the Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; by means of all such Dharma-gates,
he teaches them according to their inclinations, and in a single thought-moment,
he can extinguish the sufferings of the evil realms for as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru within every world.
May as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru be led to leave behind false certainty and be established in the assembly of right certainty;
may as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru be established on the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas;
and may as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru be established in the Unsurpassed Way.
May as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru each establish themselves upon the ground of inexhaustible merit and wisdom;
may as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru each be established within the ocean of the vow-nature of Vairocana Buddha.
At that time, from within the radiance of all the bodhisattvas, verses were uttered:
“From every light issues a wondrous sound, Proclaiming the complete practices of all bodhisattvas;
The merits of the Buddha-sons are fully perfected, Pervading everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions.”
Having practiced the path for an ocean of immeasurable eons, desiring to cause all sentient beings to leave suffering behind, they do not calculate their own suffering of birth and death;
these sons of the Buddha skillfully enter great expedient means.
Immeasurable, boundless, and without remainder, Exhausting all kalpas as vast as the great oceans,
Pervading all gateways of the Dharma, He skillfully expounds the subtle and tranquil Dharma.
The vows of all Buddhas of the three times have all been attained in pure and complete fulfillment;
these sons of the Buddha benefit all sentient beings and are able to personally practice the path of purity.
All are able to go to the abodes of the Buddhas; The pure Dharma-body illuminates the ten directions.
The sons of the Buddha possess oceans of wisdom without bound or bottom, Universally contemplating the mark of quiescence in all phenomena.
Within a single ray of light there are immeasurables; The unsurpassed great compassion is inconceivable.
With the pure eye of wisdom, they illumine all phenomena; This is the wondrous realm of the Buddha’s heirs.
Within a single hair-pore they receive all Buddha-fields, And are further able to shake all lands;
They can cause sentient beings to be free from thoughts of fear— This is called the Stage of Pure Skillful Means.
Within each and every atom are infinite bodies, And they further manifest infinitely adorned lands;
To see all of these within a single thought-moment— This is the pure dharma-gate of non-obstruction.
All kalpas throughout the three periods of time can be fully manifested within a single thought-moment;
like illusions and transformations, they have no inherent existence—this is called the unimpeded dharma of all Buddhas.
Samantabhadra is fully endowed with all practices, Able to cause all sentient beings to become completely pure;
The Sons of the Buddhas possess the dharma of mastery, And from every single pore they let out the lion’s roar.

At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to cause the entire assembly of bodhisattvas to know the Dharma-gate of the sovereign power of the Buddha’s immeasurable and boundless realm, emitted from the tuft of white hair between his eyebrows a cloud-light of lamp-illumination in all jewel colors, named "The Wisdom-Light of All Bodhisattvas Observing and Illuminating the Treasury of the Ten Directions."
This light pervaded all Buddha-fields, illuminating the entire Dharma-realm universally in a single thought-moment;

throughout all worlds, it rained down clouds of the great vows of all Buddhas, manifesting Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to the great assembly, after which he returned and entered back into the wheel-mark upon his foot.
Furthermore, there arose a great lotus flower with a stem made of various jewels, its treasury adorned by all kinds of jewel-kings; its petals completely covered the entire dharma-realm;
its filaments were adorned with every kind of precious incense, and its pericarp was made of Jāmbūnada gold.

Once this flower had appeared, a great bodhisattva emerged from between the Tathāgata’s eyebrows, named Sarvadharmavijayasvara (Victorious Sound of All Dharmas). Accompanied by a multitude of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, he respectfully circumambulated the World-Honored One immeasurable times, then withdrew to sit upon the lotus pedestal, while his retinue of bodhisattvas sat upon the filaments of the lotus.

The Bodhisattva Sarvadharmavaranirghoṣa has accomplished immeasurable joy within the dharma-realm; following the profound wisdom of the Buddhas' sphere of activity, he traverses the inconceivable light of the oceans of Buddhas and is able to go before all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvadharmasvararāja praised in verse:
“The Buddha’s body fills all dharma-realms, Appearing universally before all sentient beings;
Filling every vessel capable of being transformed, The Buddha therefore dwells here beneath this bodhi tree.”
Within as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms, that many Buddhas sit within a single pore;
each is surrounded by an infinite assembly of Bodhisattvas, who all expound the practices of Samantabhadra in their entirety.
Infinite oceans of lands reside within a single hair; All sit upon the lotus thrones of enlightenment, Pervading all realms of phenomena, Manifesting with sovereign ease from every pore.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Siṃhārcis-tejorāja-pracanda-ghoṣa spoke in verse:
“Vairocana Tathāgata turns the pure wheel of Dharma;
The skillful means of all dharmas are the Tathāgata-clouds that universally cover.”
Within the lands of the ten directions, throughout all oceans of worlds,
by the sovereign power of the Buddhas' vows, they universally manifest and turn the wheel of Dharma.
Within all Buddha-lands, amidst immeasurable oceans of assemblies,
Though their names and titles differ, they turn the pure wheel of Dharma.
By the spiritual power of Vairocana Buddha, the wheel of Dharma is turned within all lands;
the vow-voice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva pervades the entirety of the ocean of worlds.
The Dharma-body fills all lands, universally raining down the rain of all dharmas;
the characteristics of phenomena neither arise nor cease, illuminating all worlds throughout.
Throughout immeasurable and countless billions of kalpas, across paths as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields,
the wondrous voice of Vairocana Buddha fully expounds the deeds he performed in the past.
As numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, Great nets of light illuminate the ten directions;
Within each ray of light are Buddhas, Who transform sentient beings through the Unsurpassed Way.
The Dharma-body is firm and indestructible, Pervading all realms of phenomena;
It can universally manifest various form-bodies, Guiding and transforming all sentient beings according to their needs.
Throughout the infinite Buddha-fields of the three periods of time, All the Teachers therein,
their every voice and name— By the sovereign power of the Buddhas, all are universally seen.
Of the past, the future, and the present— of all such Guides,
those Sages cause everyone to hear the inconceivable Wheel of the True Dharma.

Thus, upon the sites of enlightenment in these four continents, they beheld the Buddha’s supernatural power and the vast assembly of all bodhisattvas gathered like clouds; it was likewise so throughout all oceans of worlds.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva sat upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury before the Tathāgata. He immediately entered the samādhi of the pure treasury of all Tathāgatas, universally illuminating the bodies of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire dharma-realm without obstruction, free from defilement and perfectly fulfilled, like empty space.
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra entered into samādhi in this world, and it was likewise so in all Buddha-lands throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
Once Samantabhadra Bodhisattva had entered this samādhi, the Buddhas of all the oceans of worlds in the ten directions appeared before him, and each of those Tathāgatas praised him, saying:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
Excellent, son of good family!
That you are able to enter this samādhi-samāpatti is entirely due to the power of the original vows of Vairocana Buddha.
Furthermore, by the power of your pure conduct and vows before all Buddhas— namely,
to turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas and to open the ocean of wisdom of all Tathāgatas— ...
Because they exhaustively deliver all dharmas through skillful means, leaving nothing remaining throughout the oceans of the ten directions;
because they eliminate the afflictions of all sentient beings and cause them to attain purity;
and because they are able to reach all buddha-lands without obstruction.
Because they enter the realm of all Buddhas without obstruction;
because they fulfill the merits of the universal gate of all Buddhas;
and because they enter the skillful means of all dharmas and deeply delight in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
"Because they skillfully observe all worldly phenomena;
because they know the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings.
At that time, all Buddhas and Samantabhadra Bodhisattva entered the power of omniscience.
They grant the wisdom that enters the immeasurable and boundless realm of phenomena;
they grant the wisdom that can reach the abodes of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they grant the wisdom regarding the formation and dissolution of all oceans of worlds.
Bestowing the wisdom that enters the realm of immeasurable sentient beings;
bestowing the wisdom of the Buddhas' profound Dharma gates;
bestowing the wisdom that abides in all indestructible samādhis;
Bestow the wisdom of entering the ocean of the faculties of all bodhisattvas;
bestow the wisdom of eloquence for turning the wheel of Dharma through the ocean of the languages of all sentient beings;
bestow the wisdom of a single body pervading all worlds.
One attains the wisdom of the vocal sounds of all Buddhas.
Why is this? Because one has attained this dharma of samādhi.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions each extended their right hands and stroked the crown of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s head.

When all the bodhisattvas saw the Buddhas of the ten directions each extend their right hands and stroke the crown of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s head, those bodhisattvas observed Samantabhadra Bodhisattva with single-minded reverence and immediately spoke in unison with these verses:
“The wholesome dharmas cultivated in the presence of all Buddhas, Fulfilling the power of all great vows.”
Born from the pure and wondrous Dharma-body, It is as real, level, and equal as space.
Throughout all the Buddha-lands, The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra always dwells therein.
In the worlds of the ten directions, there is nowhere he is not seen— He is an ocean of immeasurable merit and wisdom.
I see all the Buddhas of the ten directions, oceans of merit from their pure physical conduct;
within every single atom-path, they universally manifest in all lands.
Throughout all Buddha-worlds in the ten directions, for as many eons as there are atoms in the immeasurable [worlds],
they constantly behold the true sons of the Buddha, Samantabhadra, and their immeasurable practices of samādhi and skillful means.

The Dharma-body fills all dharma-realms; throughout all Buddha-lands in the ten directions, it wanders everywhere across the ocean of sentient beings, abiding securely in the profound, wondrous, and pure Dharma.
Forever traversing immeasurable dharma-realms, Free from all afflictions and indestructible,
His body pervades and fills all of space, Extensively expounding the infinite teachings of the Buddhas.
Born from the ocean of all merits, Universally emitting light like great clouds,
They establish the pure conduct of sentient beings with steadfastness, And with subtle, wondrous voices, they proclaim the realm of the Buddhas.
Throughout immeasurable and countless great kalpas, They have cultivated the profound practices of Samantabhadra;
With clouds of infinite and boundless dharmas, The thunder resounds, proclaiming the supreme realm of reality.
The true nature of all buddha-fields, The pure adornments cultivated by the Ten Powers—
Entering universally into the ocean of all sentient beings, They preach the pure Dharma according to what is appropriate.
The boundless and infinite ocean-like assembly, with single-minded reverence, beholds Samantabhadra;
may he turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma within his immeasurable, profound, and vast ocean of wisdom.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed all oceans of worlds, all oceans of sentient beings, the ocean of karma within the dharma-realm, the oceans of the inclinations, desires, and faculties of all sentient beings, and the oceans of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; having done so, he addressed the vast ocean of the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!

The wisdom of all Buddhas regarding the formation and destruction of all oceans of worlds and their purity; the inconceivable wisdom that arises regarding all realms of sentient beings; the wisdom that observes the dharma-realm; the wisdom of the sovereign mastery of all Tathāgatas; the wisdom of turning the wheel of Dharma through pure vows; the wisdom of the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique qualities; the wisdom of radiant praise and vocal resonance; the wisdom of the three types of means for teaching and transforming sentient beings; the indestructible wisdom of immeasurable samādhis and dharma-gates; and the various kinds of sovereign mastery of the Tathāgatas—all such things as these are entirely inconceivable. Relying upon the Buddha’s spiritual power, I shall fully expound them, desiring to lead all sentient beings into the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva arose from that samādhi; he arose from samādhis as numerous as the atoms of worlds; he arose from samādhis of the indestructible wisdom of skillful means throughout every thought-moment across all three periods of time.

At that moment, each and every one of that entire assembly of bodhisattvas attained samādhis as numerous as the atoms of worlds, oceans of dharma-methods of skillful means as numerous as the atoms of worlds, oceans of eloquence of skillful means, and oceans of various practices and vows. Just as the merit obtained by the bodhisattvas in this assembly was such, so too was the merit obtained by the assemblies of bodhisattvas in all oceans of worlds and all oceans of Tathāgatas.

At that time, all worlds shook in six ways; all sentient beings were peaceful, secure, and joyful; and all manner of precious jewels provided various adornments. Within the ocean-like assemblies of all Tathāgatas, ten kinds of clouds of jewel-kings rained down, namely:

clouds of the supreme golden banner jewel-king, clouds of the jewel-king illuminated by the Buddha’s radiance, clouds of the golden lotus jewel-king, clouds of the jewel-king of the bodhisattvas’ eloquence and radiance, clouds of the jewel-king of all wondrous sounds, clouds of the jewel-king of the adorned sites of enlightenment in Buddha-lands, and clouds of the jewel-king of the wondrous sounds of the immeasurable wheels of merit and radiance of all bodhisattvas.
From the pores and the various radiances of all Tathāgatas, [a voice] spoke in verse:
“Samantabhadra is present everywhere in all Buddha-fields, seated upon lion thrones of precious lotus flowers.”
Manifesting in this way throughout all realms, universally entering into infinite and boundless activities,
they are able to manifest immeasurable kinds of bodies, filling the worlds of the ten directions through their transformations.
With a wondrous voice, harmonious and elegant, he preaches the Dharma without obstruction;
in all samādhis, his skillful means are sovereign; in all Buddha-lands, at the abodes of all Tathāgatas, he has attained mastery over every samādhi.
They are able to fully comprehend the most supreme realm, manifesting the infinite sovereignty of Samantabhadra.
Just as in all lands, before all Tathāgatas, and within all atoms of all world-systems, the sovereign mastery of Samantabhadra is likewise so.
Because the fundamental vows have reached their ultimate fulfillment throughout the realm of Vairocana, the physical form of Samantabhadra is like empty space.
Manifesting in infinite forms, he universally responds to sentient beings, according to the various types of living creatures.
For the sake of manifesting emanations,
they are able to display all worlds and immeasurable Buddha-lands, entering into all dharma-gates.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, fully endowed with pure vows, possesses such qualities as these, along with immeasurable mastery.
Throughout all the oceans of sentient beings, infinite and boundless, he manifests purity within each and every buddha-field.
"All such things appear entirely within the body; according to their arising and ceasing, one knows them all in a single thought.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to cause the great assembly to rejoice once more, spoke in verse:
"The ocean of merit and profound wisdom of all Buddhas fills immeasurable and boundless lands."
Through skillful means, according to what each being should see, Vairocana Buddha turns the wheel of Dharma.
Within inconceivable oceans of buddha-fields, he has purified them throughout immeasurable eons;
this most excellent guide illuminates all, and is able to subdue the ocean of sentient beings.
The great ocean of sentient beings is difficult to fathom; the realm of the Buddhas is inconceivable.
Sentient beings delight in evil and are attached to the various realms of existence; they are unable to understand the Unsurpassed Way.
With a mind nurtured by the ocean of merit and Dharma, They are always able to draw near to spiritual friends;
Constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas, Such as these are able to cross over and attain supreme wisdom.
Free from all deceit and crookedness, their minds are pure;
Their vast compassion is boundless, and their deep-seated faith is insatiable. Upon hearing this Dharma, they experience immeasurable joy.
The vows for the various stages of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva— Who dwells securely and abides well, able to practice them in accordance;
Whose mind roams through the Dharma-realm like space— Only such a person knows the realm of the Buddha.
All Bodhisattvas attain excellent benefit, Able to behold the Sovereign, the Most Victorious Honored One;
Not known through the spheres of others, Samantabhadra’s skillful means allow all to enter.
Immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, Protected and mindful of by all Tathāgatas,
Turning the wheel of Dharma in all places— This is the power of the realm of Vairocana Buddha.
All lands and all Buddhas, without obstruction, are within my body;
from every one of my pores, I clearly observe the manifestation of the Buddha-realm.
The vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Infinite and boundless, are all fully perfected;
With a pure body within the realm of the Universal Eye, I shall now expound them; O Benevolent One, listen attentively.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of matters concerning the oceans of worlds, which have been expounded by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present. They are as follows:"

He spoke of the oceans of worlds: the oceans of worlds arising through causes and conditions, the oceans of worlds abiding, the oceans of worlds in form, the oceans of worlds in substance, the oceans of worlds in adornment, the oceans of worlds in purity, the oceans of worlds where Tathāgatas appear in the world, the oceans of kalpas, and the oceans of worlds through the skillful means of destruction.
O Sons of the Buddha!
Within the oceans of worlds, there are these ten kinds of matters as primary examples, up to and including as many kinds of matters as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
O Sons of the Buddha!

One should know that all oceans of worlds are formed through the presence of causes and conditions as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds; they have been formed, are being formed, and will be formed. These are: by the spiritual power of the Tathāgatas; because such is the nature of the Dharma; by the karma of sentient beings;

because all Bodhisattvas shall attain the Unsurpassed Way; by the roots of goodness of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; by the mastery of vows, practices, and liberation for purifying the Buddha-lands of the Bodhisattvas; by the fruit of reliance upon the unsurpassed roots of goodness of the Tathāgatas; and by the sovereign power of the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Through the presence of such causes and conditions as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, all oceans of worlds are formed.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
“The realm of the Buddha’s wisdom is inconceivable; so too is his sovereign and perfect abiding.”
Throughout immeasurable and boundless oceans of worlds, Vairocana Buddha is able to adorn and purify them all.
According to what is appropriate for their transformation and deliverance, the infinite oceans of vows of all bodhisattvas are likewise entirely purified.
In the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, all sentient beings are awakened by means of the inconceivable.
Through the gateway of skillful means that leads to all-knowledge, everything is brought forth.
An ocean of immeasurable vows,
universally practicing all the virtuous deeds of bodhisattvas, they enter the Buddha-realm,
which is immeasurable and boundless.
In each and every buddha-field, practicing for immeasurable eons, the mental states and objects of sentient beings are inconceivable.
Because of the defilements of sentient beings, the lands are not pure; their karmic actions are immeasurable.
The worlds are diverse;
they are adorned with various jewels free from defilement, nurturing the ocean of great vows that is stainless.
If there is a bodhisattva who cultivates the conduct of Samantabhadra and is always able to practice it,
they will purify the dharma-realm.
They can emerge from the infinite oceans of Tathāgata lands within a single thought-moment.
Pervading all throughout the ten directions,
profoundly deep and pure, like empty space; those who are equal to the realm of space possess such mastery.
Sitting upon a precious lotus flower, manifesting myriad wondrous colors,
within his body he contains all lands.
Entering into skillful means, he gives rise to oceans of lands throughout the realms of the three periods of time.
Manifesting the attainment of Buddhahood,
Vairocana Buddha resides in this land, which is pure and perfected with myriad jewels, without limit or boundary.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
The bases upon which each world-ocean rests are as numerous as the atoms within those worlds; they are as follows:

They abide supported by all manner of adornments, or they abide supported by space, or they abide supported by all jewels, or they abide supported by the light of the Buddhas, or they abide supported by illusory karma, or they abide supported within the palms of the Mahānāga Vajrapāṇis, or they abide supported by the power of the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"In infinite and boundless oceans of Buddha-lands, Adorned with stainless, wondrous jewels,
The pure radiance of the sovereign maṇi-kings Is seen by none who lack the most supreme majestic power."
The pure oceans of lands abide in space; The light from the wondrous treasury of jewel-kings shines everywhere.
They emit immeasurable, subtle, and wonderful sounds, Proclaiming the Buddha-way so that all rejoice.
Various flower-radiances bring sublime joy, adorned with wish-fulfilling jewels;
immeasurable nets of light cover it from above, while clouds of diverse fragrances fill it everywhere.
Immeasurable and boundless wondrous lotuses, with pedestals made of blue lapis lazuli gems;
the pure land is most marvelous, for it is adorned by all Buddhas.
There are some Buddha-lands that are pure, Abiding securely through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power;
One sees stainless, pure, and wondrous jewels, Completely filled with immeasurable bodhisattvas.
There are some pure buddha-fields of various Buddhas, Abiding within the palms of the Vajrapāṇi;
The World Hero of Ten Powers, Vairocana, Constantly turns the wheel of Dharma for all.
Some rest upon level ground beneath jewel trees; others likewise rest upon clouds of fragrant flames.
Some rest firmly upon the water-circle, while others rest upon seats of diamond oceans.
Some dwell upon supreme and wondrous diamond banners, covered above by various kinds of precious flowers.
In infinite sovereignty throughout all places, Vairocana Buddha causes the multitudes to behold him.
With various and diverse colors and long-reaching radiance, he flows universally through all Buddha-worlds;
they all see the treasury of manifold adornments, stainless, subtle, and exceedingly pure.
By the power of the ocean of all vows, they dwell upon infinite and diverse supports;
clouds of Tathāgatas completely fill them, as they always abide within the pure void.
In some Buddha-fields situated above, resting upon the pure celestial crowns of Bodhisattvas, they manifest the infinite sovereignty of Buddhas;
these sons of the Buddha are transformations produced by the pure karma of sublime sounds.
The various dharma-realms and Buddha-lands are like flashes of lightning and like illusions;
vast and pure like sapphire-blue lapis lazuli, they all arise from stainless and pure karma.
Universally manifesting various treasuries of adornments, Abiding peacefully, supported by empty space;
The realms of his deeds and spheres of action are inconceivable, As the Buddha causes all sentient beings to behold them everywhere.
All Buddha-fields, as numerous as atoms, are conceived in a single thought-moment by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
through practices over immeasurable eons, he transforms sentient beings, pervading the Dharma-realm and manifesting sovereign mastery.
Within each and every atom, oceans of Buddha-lands dwell in peace;
clouds of Buddhas pervade and protect with mindfulness, encompassing and covering all.
Within a single atom, a Buddha manifests the power of sovereign mastery.
"Within every single atom, spiritual transformations are likewise;
all Buddhas and their supernormal powers are manifested by Vairocana.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
“O Son of the Buddha!

The oceans of worlds have various forms: some are square, some are circular, some are neither square nor circular, some are like swirling eddies of water, some are shaped like flowers, and some take the forms of various sentient beings.”
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"The oceans of lands are immeasurable, With diverse forms and various adornments;
In the oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions, One beholds all manner of manifold appearances."
Some are circular, some are square, and others are neither square nor round;
with three dimensions and eight corners, their forms resemble mani jewels.
Because the oceans of all karmas are of various distinct kinds, [they appear thus].
Like a vajra-palm, it is adorned, level, and upright;
with the color of refined pure gold and a pure, wondrous form, he enters the gate of the immeasurable True Dharma.
The oceans of Buddha-fields, with their various treasuries, are like great clouds suspended in the void.
That ground of jewel-wheels is wondrously pure and distinct; Vairocana Buddha’s radiance illuminates it all.
The lands of all Buddhas arise from the karma of the mind, adorned with immeasurable varieties of forms.
Within the ocean of the Tathāgata’s realms, infinite manifestations appear; some are pure, and some are defiled.
Suffering and pleasure differ;
phenomena constantly flow and transform in such a manner that the entire ocean of karma is inconceivable.
Within a single pore, immeasurable Buddha-fields, adorned and pure, abide in vast tranquility.
In every one of those places, Vairocana Buddha, amidst oceans of assemblies, expounds the True Dharma.
Within a single atom, there are subtle lands; as many as all atoms, they all abide therein.
All worlds, with their various forms, are within them, where the supreme Wheel of Dharma is turned.
By the power of this sovereign force of great vows, within every single atom, all lands are manifested;
they are like magical illusions and like empty space, adorned by the power of the various mental activities.
Within each and every atom, there are clouds of emanation Buddhas, as numerous as all sentient beings, possessing sovereign spiritual powers.
Within a single minute atom, they dwell well within Buddha-fields; such is the manifestation of the Dharma by Rocana Buddha.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
You should know that the oceans of worlds possess various kinds of essences, namely:
It has a body adorned with all kinds of jewels, or a body of a single jewel, or a body of a vajra-solid ground, or a body of various fragrances, or a body of a solar-jewel disc.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"There are world-oceans, Composed of various jewels,
Firm and indestructible, Resting upon precious lotus flowers."
Some arise as supreme radiance, pure and brilliant with blazing light,
adorning lands with myriad wonders and dwelling supported by space.
Some lands of light dwell supported by light.
Adorned with clouds of radiant light, these are the palaces of the various bodhisattvas.
There are some oceans of buddha-fields that abide like flashes of lightning;
though one seeks them, they cannot be grasped, for they arise through the power of vows.
In some lands there are mani-jewels, Illuminated by the treasury of solar radiance;
With wheels of pearls strung upon the ground, Bodhisattvas fill them all.
In some jewel-flame lands, Clouds of light provide a covering shade.
Adorned with all manner of jewels, they are entirely subject to transformation.
Some possess bodies of manifold marks, adorned with subtle and wondrous features;
interspersed with various jeweled crowns, they are all emanations of the Buddhas.
The ocean of mind arises from karma, and lands dwell according to one's inclinations;
like illusions, they have no fixed location, for all are born of deluded thought.
The radiance of the Tathāgata’s body dwells within the maṇi-land.
The clouds of Perfect Enlightenment spread everywhere, and all Buddhas exercise their sovereign mastery.
Some are the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, manifesting oceans of Buddha-lands adorned with every kind of jewel, magnificently embellished by the power of their vows.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
You should know that the oceans of worlds possess adornments as numerous as the atoms within those oceans of worlds; namely:

There were adornments consisting of clouds of various kinds of all objective realms; adornments of the karmic activities of sentient beings in all worlds; and adornments of the power of the vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra—adornments such as these, numbering as many as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
“Equal in number to the atoms of oceans of worlds, The inconceivable fruits of karma and retribution—
Throughout all the oceans of worlds in the ten directions, Various adornments, pure and vast, are boundless.”
Immeasurable pure forms universally adorn it, And it is ever filled with supreme, wondrous merit;
Clouds of variegated light radiate Brahma-sounds, Which are heard throughout all Buddha-fields.
The Bodhisattva’s ocean of immeasurable merit, With wondrous sounds pervading all lands,
Adorned with clouds of various vows, Its resonance shakes the oceans of worlds in the ten directions.
The ocean of sentient beings' karma is vast and boundless; from clouds of pure adornment, wondrous sounds emerge.
Karmic retribution manifests like jewels according to conditions, and through the power of all Buddhas, it completely fills all places.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, Freely manifest throughout immeasurable lands;
In every single realm, all Buddhas Are seen adorning the ocean of lands.
Throughout the kalpas of the past, future, and present, In all worlds throughout the ten directions,
Adorned with pure splendor across immeasurable eons— I see every single Buddha-field in their entirety.
Clouds of Buddhas fill all realms, their number equaling that of sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
the Buddhas manifest sovereign conduct to make it known to the masses—this is called the Tathāgata’s adornment of the land.
Flows of various fragrant flames and flows of flowers, Flows of all manner of precious maṇi-jewels,
And clouds of various exquisite adornments— All of these embellish the buddha-fields.
In all the sites of enlightenment throughout the worlds of the ten directions, with every kind of wondrous adornment,
there is none that does not behold this ocean of lands, appearing like flashes of lightning in the sky.
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and the sons of the Buddha, Who are all able to adorn the buddha-fields,
And the ocean of pure practices throughout kalpas equal in number to sentient beings— All these appear within this world.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha,
you should know that within the oceans of worlds there are as many pure worlds as there are atoms in a world-system, namely:

The Bodhisattva draws near to spiritual friends, accomplishes all roots of goodness, benefits all sentient beings, purifies and fulfills all the pāramitās, and dwells securely in all stages of practice; such pure qualities are as numerous as the atoms within worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"The adornments of all Buddha-fields Are produced through the skillful means of oceans of countless vows;
The pure forms of all Buddha-fields Are cultivated and gathered through oceans of immeasurable practices."
Having long approached spiritual friends, And performed all pure and wondrous deeds,
With compassion flowing universally to moisten sentient beings, The oceans of Buddha-fields are thus purified.
The ground of samādhi of all dharma-gates, The ocean of pure virtues from all Buddhas’ abodes,
The ground of purity through the skillful means of the dhyāna-gates— Therefore, they adorn and purify the oceans of Buddha-fields.
Able to give rise to immeasurable pure minds, Their faith in the Buddha is firm and indestructible;
Through the skillful means of patience, they are pure and stainless, Adorning the ocean of lands with subtle and wondrous colors.
Raising clouds of merit that fill the void, they benefit all who practice pure conduct;
sentient beings everywhere obtain immeasurable virtue, and thus they adorn and purify the ocean of Buddha-fields.
The skillful means of the oceans of lands are as infinite as they are equal; They have completely purified all the perfections without exception.
By cultivating the perfection of inexhaustible vows, They thus adorn and purify the oceans of Buddha-lands.
The manifestations of illusory deeds arise immeasurably; all phenomena are vast and pure.
Through various skillful means, they purify sentient beings, giving rise to this delightful ocean of Buddha-fields.
Through skillful means, they purify all stages and fulfill the ocean of all Buddhas' merits;
causing all sentient beings to exhaust the source of suffering, they thus purify the ocean of Buddha-fields.
Cultivating an ocean of pure power beyond compare, Able to purify the faculties of all sentient beings,
Respectfully making offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, Therefore, they adorn and purify oceans of Buddha-fields.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
You should know that in each and every world-ocean, there appear as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a world-ocean, namely:

There are Buddhas appearing in the world, manifesting form-bodies that pervade the entire Dharma-realm; some have short lifespans, while others endure for immeasurable eons. In this manner, within each and every ocean of worlds, there appear as many Buddhas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"By means of immeasurable gates of skillful expedience, The Buddha is able to give rise to oceans of all buddha-fields;
In accordance with the desires and inclinations of sentient beings, The Dharma Kings of all Buddhas appear in the world."
The Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata is inconceivable, Without form, without marks, and without peer;
He manifests a rūpakāya for the sake of sentient beings, So that those receiving transformation throughout the ten directions may all behold him.
Sometimes manifesting short lifespans for the sake of sentient beings, Or manifesting immeasurable kalpas of long life;
The Dharma-body appears through many gates throughout the ten directions, Constantly serving as a sublime field of merit for the world.
Some are able to cause inconceivable oceans of lands in the ten directions to be entirely purified;
some are able to purify a single buddha-field—these are established through their skillful means and vows.
Some speak of the inconceivable vehicle; the Buddha universally manifests according to what beings delight in.
Some Tathāgatas speak of the One Vehicle; such skillful means of the Buddha are immeasurable.
Spontaneously attaining perfect enlightenment without a teacher, some may deliver but a few sentient beings,
while others are able, within a single thought-moment, to transform and liberate an ocean of immeasurable sentient beings.
Or there may be, from within a single pore, inconceivable clouds of emanated Buddhas emerging,
filling all the worlds of the ten directions, transforming sentient beings through immeasurable skillful means.
Or the Buddha’s voice vibrates throughout the ten directions, according to the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings;
for immeasurable billions of kalpas it never ceases, delivering an infinite ocean of sentient beings.
There are some lands of immeasurable adornment, where the pure great assembly sits in circumambulation;
they fill all oceans of worlds, and the Buddhas pervade the multitude like clouds in the sky.
This Buddha’s inconceivable skillful means fills the ocean of compassion throughout all things;
entering the gates of various adorned skillful means, he manifests before all sentient beings.
