At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
You should know that world-oceans have durations of existence equal to the atoms within a world-ocean of kalpas, namely:
In oceans of Buddha-fields, they may abide for incalculable eons, or they may abide for calculable eons; there are such eons of abiding as numerous as the atoms within these oceans of worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, wishing to analyze and reveal this matter, addressed the entire assembly, saying:
"O Children of the Buddha!

You should know that this Lotus Treasury World-Ocean was purified by Rocana Buddha during his original cultivation of the bodhisattva path over as many incalculable eons as there are atoms in a world. In each and every eon, he reverently made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a world; at the abode of each and every Buddha, he purely cultivated vows and practices as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds."
O Son of the Buddha!
You should know that there are wind-circles as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru which support this Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean:
the lowest wind-circle is named "Equanimity," and it supports the ground of all jewel-luminosity.
Above that is the wind-circle named Adorned with Various Jewels, which supports the Jewel Ground of Pure Radiance;
above that is the wind-circle named Power of Merit, which supports the Secret Jewel Ground;
above that is the wind-circle named Jewel Flame, which supports the Indestructible Jewel Ground of the Sun.
Above that is a wind-circle named Universal Adornment, which supports the Ground of Abundant Jewel Radiance;
above that is a wind-circle named Stainless Pure Equanimity, which supports the Ground of Jewel Flower Flames;
above that is a wind-circle named Rectilinear Movement, which supports the Ground of All Pearls.
Above that is the wind-circle named All-Ages (*sarvavatsara*), which sustains all times: the day, the half-month, the month, and the year.
Above that is the wind-circle named Universal Sustainer of Power (*samantadhāraṇavega*), which sustains all the mountains of Mount Sumeru.

Above that is the wind-circle named Adorned Radiance (*vyūhaprabhāsa*), which is able to sustain all existences; in this manner, there are successively above it wind-circles as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru.
The supreme wind-circle is named Victorious Treasury (*Jin-gang-zàng*), which sustains all fragrant water-oceans.
Within those fragrant water-oceans is a great lotus named Fragrant Banner Radiance Adornment (*Xiang-chuang guang-ming zhuang-yang*), which sustains this Lotus-Treasury Adorned World-Ocean.
On the periphery of this world-ocean, there is a diamond mountain that encircles it on all sides.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"In this Lotus Treasury, Within the ocean of adorned worlds,
All manner of wondrous jewel treasuries Radiate various pure lights."
Equal in number to all atoms, these are the abodes where past Buddhas dwelt.
Having long ago departed from defilement within the ocean of existence, they became utterly pure;
now, like clouds of immeasurable great compassion, they fill all sentient beings.
Having relinquished their own bodies, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields,
they constantly cultivate the ocean of immeasurable practices until they are purified;
therefore, the world-ocean of the Lotus Treasury is thus adorned.
Throughout the entire realm of space, Radiant light pervades and fills it all;
Abiding immovably, It is constantly supported by a supreme wind-circle.
Adorned with every kind of jewel, Sublime winds flow everywhere.
The vast vows of Rocana cause the lands to be adorned and purified;
wish-fulfilling jewels are spread everywhere, and various wondrous flowers bloom.
By the power of his original vows, he dwells within the void.
Firmly and well-established, adorned with all manner of jewels,
throughout all realms of the ten directions, they emit clouds of pure light;
from within those various maṇi jewels, emerge infinite clouds of bodhisattvas.
Wandering through the lands of the ten directions, their radiance is most fiercely brilliant;
with precious flowers of exquisite color,
they adorn wheels of light that fill the entire dharma-realm, pervading everywhere throughout the ten directions.
All the pure jewels of the assembly emit clouds of radiant light,
which completely fill all worlds throughout the ten directions;
they extinguish all suffering and establish beings in the unsurpassed path.
Sublime forms shine everywhere throughout all oceans of worlds;
within this Lotus Treasury ocean of worlds,
inside every single atom, one beholds the entirety of the Dharma-realm.
The clouds of all Buddhas emit precious radiance,
illuminating this realm of Vairocana, which possesses infinite sovereignty.
All sentient beings alike [are born] as Buddhas within lotus flowers.
He raises various and immeasurable clouds of sovereign transformations;
Śakra, Brahmā, and the hosts of devas, as well as the wheel-turning sage kings and all classes of sentient beings, all find secure dwelling therein.
They manifest transformations and radiate light, entirely equal to the Dharma-realm;
from within all these lights, the wondrous voices of the Buddhas emerge.
They know the minds of all sentient beings, perceiving every single thought without exception.
Through countless gates of expedient means, they tame the various classes of sentient beings.
Free from all inversions, they dwell eternally in tranquility;
their clouds of immeasurable light are entirely equal to the Dharma-realm.
"The wisdom practiced by Samantabhadra, The unsurpassed, supreme, and wondrous stage— Within this array of light, All have heard it in its entirety.
O Son of the Buddha! "
It should be known that this Lotus Treasury World-Ocean has its diamond perimeter mountains resting upon a ground of lotus-sun jewel-kings.

Within it are all fragrant water-oceans, and all manner of precious jewels are spread across its ground. This thick diamond ground is indestructible; it produces all varieties of precious jewels and is also able to clearly illuminate all worlds.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"In all oceans of worlds, There are infinite adornments;
Jeweled wheels of boundless colors Are produced by the Tathāgata’s spiritual power."
Adorned with *cakravāḍa* mountains, jewel wheels, and incense wheels,
resting upon pearl wheels and various precious gems;
firm and adorned with jewels, it is a pure treasury of Jāmbūnada gold.
Fragrant light fills the ten directions, illuminating the Cakravāḍa mountains;
Held by means of firm adamantine jewels, adorned with indestructible vajra-ornaments,
Adorned with the marks of various kinds of myriad treasures— All adornments are the pure Dharma.
Fragrant waters flow everywhere in infinite colors; scattered flowers, mani-jewels, and sandalwood incense fill the air.
Celestial robes cover all, adorned with blossoms; myriad precious gems and fragrant flowers perfume the boundless realm.
Pure jewel-trees form a magnificent canopy, universally illuminating all bodies.
The wondrous clouds of light are fully perfected; sitting serenely beneath the trees, there is nowhere they do not illuminate.
With various flowers, incense, banners, and canopies, all Bodhisattvas fill the Dharma-realm.
Able to expound the ocean of all languages—this is Vairocana turning the Wheel of Dharma.
In those places there are banners of rare jewels, and all the jewel-trees emit radiance;
the body of Vairocana Buddha is pure, and within that adornment, everything is seen.
Within all manner of adornments are countless bodies; the Tathāgata’s manifested forms are infinite, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions, subduing sentient beings beyond measure.
All adornments emit wondrous sounds; within the wheel of vows of Vairocana Buddha, according to each pure ocean of buddha-fields, all hear them through the Buddha’s power of mastery.

Within that world-ocean inside the Great Cakravāḍa Mountains, there is a sovereign king of indestructible mani-jewels that reflects the bodies of all sentient beings; the great earth is adorned with lotus flowers made of various jewels, filled everywhere with clouds of all manner of exquisite ornaments, perfumed by every kind of wonderful fragrance, and further embellished by the adornments of the Buddha-fields of the three periods of time.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"The ground is level, upright, pure, and perfect; Within the Cakravāḍa mountains, it is indestructible.
It abides in equanimity and is exceedingly pure, Adorned with various kinds of diverse jewels."
The ground of vajra-jewels is delightful, covered above by jeweled wheels and lattices;
it is adorned with various precious flowers and diverse, exquisite wheels of jewel-garments.
Spreading throughout all lands in succession, the bodhisattvas’ celestial crowns and precious necklaces—
adorned with stainless ornaments and radiating light— are completely filled with exquisite fragrances and crushed jewels.
Adorned with multitudes of radiant jewel-flowers, they radiate universally throughout the ten directions;
these jewel-flowers cover all lands, fully nourishing the merits of the Buddhas.
Raising clouds of all things that fill the void, their radiance shines everywhere without end;
this light completely pervades all lands, fully proclaiming the nectar-like flavor of the Buddha-dharma.
Entering fully into the vows of all Buddhas, they are always able to see extensively the dharmas of the three periods of time;
following the conduct of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, they perceive it all throughout this great earth.
This pure ground, adorned with jewels, receives all Buddha-fields;
within every single atom of this ground, all Buddha-fields likewise enter.
A treasury adorned with exquisite flowers of various jewels, where Bodhisattvas from the ten directions constantly come and go;
there they always hear of all the vows of the Bodhisattvas, as well as their sovereign virtues.
Adorned with the marks of jewel-like radiance, Stainless, pure, and emitting light,
They manifest all the teachings of the Buddhas, Pervading the Dharma-realm like space.
Those who attain the vows of Samantabhadra, The immeasurable wisdom of the realm of all Buddhas,
They shall obtain infinite and supreme mastery, And be able to enter the ocean of boundless Buddha-fields.

Upon that great earth there are fragrant oceans as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably many Buddha-fields, adorned with various jewels. The shores are formed of all kinds of fragrant *maṇi* jewel-kings, and nets of jewel-kings cover them above. Waters of various jewel colors fill them, in which all manner of flowers are in full bloom; they are perfumed by fine sandalwood powder, and the sublime voices of the Tathāgatas constantly resound from them without ceasing.
Successive clouds of fragrance permeate the ten directions, while stairways of mixed jewels and railings of pearls surround them.

Waves of various jewels produce wondrous sounds, and pavilions of jewel-flowers, as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields in the Ganges sands, encircle them on all sides. Beyond these, cities of various jewel-flowers, as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable Buddha-fields, stand in their outer perimeter.

There were flowers as numerous as the atoms in ten great trichiliocosms; each lotus was ten yojanas in size, blooming with fresh vigor and covering the surface of the water, their fragrance universally perfuming all worlds;
and they were adorned with fragrant trees as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-lands.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"In that place of the adorned and pure great earth, Adorned by seas of fragrant water and jewels,
Abiding eternally upon a pure jeweled ground, Firm as vajra and indestructible."
With the king of many fragrant jewels forming its banks, The radiance of jewel-clouds shines like the sun;
With exquisite necklaces of genuine jewel-flowers, It is universally adorned with stainless purity.
Pure scented water fills it to the brim, with swirling currents of light from myriad jewel-flowers;
wondrous sounds of joy never cease, heard everywhere throughout the Buddha-worlds at will.
The pure stairways and paths were adorned with various treasures; the ground was magnificently decorated with jewels and remained steadfast and unmoving.
Pearl-like exquisite gems formed the railings, and the radiant jewel-flowers were most delightful.
Jewel trees grow in rows along the sides of the path; Maṇi-jewels and precious ornaments shine with brilliant luster.
They produce immeasurable, harmonious sounds, Adorned with pure tones praising the Triple Gem.
Fragrant waters, soft and serene, fill it to the brim; Puṇḍarīka lotuses surround it on all sides.
All the fragrant flowers emit radiance, Pure and complete, forming a magnificent adornment.
Within the jeweled banners there is radiance, adorned with hanging jeweled flags and pennants;
from the mani-jewel nets emerge wondrous sounds, hearing which enables one to enter all-knowledge.
The city of myriad jewel flowers is most subtle and wondrous;
with the pure radiance of immeasurable jewel colors, it illuminates every world in the ten directions, all fully adorned with glorious light.
Encircled on all sides by surrounding walls, adorned with various kinds of diverse jewels,
sustained by the mutual support of pure jewel-flames, and fully endowed with oceans of precious incense as adornments.
The past practices of Vairocana Buddha have caused the ocean of Buddha-fields to become exceedingly pure;
countless, immeasurable, and boundless, he exercises sovereign mastery throughout them all.
"Each and every fragrant water ocean is surrounded by fragrant water rivers as numerous as the atoms in the four continents, with various jewel flowers covering their surfaces;
those fragrant water rivers issue forth from the white tuft between the Buddha’s eyebrows, where king-mani jewels float upon them, following the current."
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
“Stainless, pure streams of fragrant water flow, Covered everywhere by vajra-jewel flowers;
The ground of various jewel wheels is strewn with golden sand, Universally adorned with immeasurable rare treasures.”
The pure and wondrous stairways are formed of the seven treasures;
upon the various balustrades, lotus flowers are planted, with true-jewel flower-blossoms perpetually in full bloom, adorned by hanging garlands of diverse flowers.
The subtle colors of all jewel-lights, with pure fragrant waters flowing with various gems,
have waves of diverse precious flowers, while myriad harmonious sounds proclaim the voice of the Buddha.
Sandalwood jewel-powder blends with clear currents, And immeasurable miscellaneous jewels form swirling eddies;
Various fragrant flames of light emerge everywhere, Constantly flowing throughout all worlds of the ten directions.
From all the fragrant rivers emerge immeasurable, diverse, wondrous, and supreme treasures;
these various jewels are gathered together to form flower canopies, their radiance universally illuminating the rivers of fragrant water.
Throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions, the Buddha’s radiance illuminates the jewel-king;
at the Tathāgata’s site of enlightenment, the ground is a precious wheel, and rivers of various jewels and incense flow in full abundance.
The various jeweled nets strike and rub against one another, Proclaiming the Buddha’s voice, which never ceases;
All the teachings of the Buddhas for all Bodhisattvas Are what the Great Being Samantabhadra practices.
The vow-voices of all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are constantly heard upon that jeweled shore;
the past deeds of all Tathāgatas are heard everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions.
All the swirling currents of the rivers of fragrance, and all the clouds of merit of the Bodhisattvas,
gradually fill and pervade all realms of phenomena, reaching every single land without exception.
All those rivers of fragrant water are completely covered by clouds of pure jewel-kings;
from the Buddha’s white tuft-mark (ūrṇā-kośa) emerge jewel-kings, whose radiant light is equal to that of the Tathāgata.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Three.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Four.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Two, Part Three: The Chapter on Vairocana Buddha.

"The space between those fragrant rivers is entirely level and even, adorned with various exquisite jewel trees. Various kinds of jeweled canopies cover them from above; they are adorned by the power of the vows of all Bodhisattvas, protected by the Buddhas, and graced with the adornments of the three periods of time."
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
“Vairocana Buddha pervades the ten directions, Manifesting all manner of adorned transformation bodies;
They neither come nor go, Yet through the power of the Buddha’s vows, they are seen by all.”
Within the atoms of all Buddha-fields, immeasurable sons of the Buddha cultivate various practices;
they all receive the prediction of pure lands, beholding adorned and purified realms in accordance with their original vows.
“O Son of the Buddha!
You should know that within this Lotus Treasury World-Ocean, each and every realm possesses as many pure adornments as there are atoms in a world-ocean.”
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Upon this Sea of Fragrant Water dwell world-systems as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields. Some world-systems rest upon lotus flowers; some rest upon lotus flowers of immeasurable colors; some rely on jewels of true pearls; some rely on various jeweled nets; some rely on the bodies of various sentient beings; and some rely on the king of Buddha-maṇi jewels.

They take the form of Mount Sumeru, or the form of rivers, or the form of revolutions, or the form of swirling currents, or the form of wheels, or the form of trees, or the form of towers and pavilions, or the form of clouds, or the form of nets."
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"The firm and pure buddha-fields, Treasure-repositories of radiant light, free from defilement and liberation,
Some abide supported by oceans of mani jewels, And some abide supported by oceans of fragrance."
Some abide by means of various skillful methods; some abide by means of various adorned colors;
others abide in the circular forms of Mount Sumeru and trees; they abide in Buddha-fields through various diverse gateways.
In some, bodies of light and various flower-treasuries, jewel clouds universally radiate pure brilliance;
this light fills the supreme worlds, and the jewel-ground ocean-treasury is indestructible.
Some purify Buddha-fields with immeasurable colors, with clouds of radiant flames in all manner of hues;
others possess wondrous sounds throughout all worlds, with spontaneous and eternal sounds beyond conception.
The body of manifold aspirations and delights, the body of clouds of sovereign conduct and sound,
the immeasurable body of virtuous renown for sentient beings, and the most supreme body of all virtuous renown.
Entering all Buddha-fields through various gateways, Gradually reaching the inexhaustible and inconceivable;
Countless [realms] filling all directions, Inexhaustible, immeasurable, and universally sovereign.
In all directions, the lands of the Tathāgatas— Through vast skillful means, they enter the Buddha-realm;
They see the lands of the ten directions, arriving in succession, Yet the realms neither increase nor decrease.
A single land fills the ten directions, And the ten directions enter one without remainder;
The original characteristics of the worlds are not destroyed, For such is possible through incomparable merit.
Within every atom of all Buddha-fields, one beholds the sovereign power of Vairocana;
with the ocean-like resonance of his great vows, he tames all classes of sentient beings.
The Buddha’s body fills all lands, and countless bodhisattvas are likewise;
they transform and guide sentient beings without limit, as the Buddha manifests sovereign power beyond compare.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Within those oceans of fragrant water, there is one ocean of fragrant water named Joyful Radiance, which contains lotus flowers adorned with all kinds of fragrant mani-jewel kings."
Above is a world named Pure Jewel Net Radiance; the Buddha there is named Stainless Pure Eye Pervasively Entering.

Above that world, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, is a buddha-land named Exquisite Adornment of Various Fragrant Lotuses, which rests upon a jewel net and is shaped like a lion throne; the Buddha there is named Lion Throne Radiance Supreme Illumination.

Above that world, past as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there is a buddha-land named Universal Radiance of Jewel Adornments, which rests upon various flowers and is shaped like a solar disc cloud; the Buddha there is named Supreme Wisdom of Vast Radiance.

Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields from that world above, there is a buddha-field named Variegated Light Lotus, where the Buddha is named Universal Vigor of Vajra Radiance Well-Arisen.

Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields above that world, there is a buddha-land named Fearless Adorned Purity; the Buddha there is named King of the Banner of Equal Adornment and Wondrous Sound.

Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields from that world, there is a buddha-land named Pure Flame of Blossoming Flowers; the Buddha there is named King Renowned for the Merits of the Ocean of Love.
Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field above that world, there is a buddha-field named Saṃdhāraṇī; the Buddha there is named Viśuddhajñānasāgara.
Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field above that world, there is a buddha-field named Vimuktighoṣa; the Buddha there is named Sukhalakṣaṇadhvaja.
Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field from that world, there is a buddha-land named Victorious Arising; the Buddha there is named Lotus Treasury Light.
Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field from that world, there is a buddha-land named Well-Established Vajra Indestructible; the Buddha there is named Nārāyaṇa Indestructible.

Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields above that world, there is a buddha-field named Flower Grove Red Lotus; the Buddha there is named King of Wisdom of Various Jewel Flower Garlands.

Beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields above that world, there is a buddha-land named Pure Light Supreme Lightning Tathāgatagarbha; the Buddha there is named Able to Arouse All Merit of Vows.
Above that world, there is a sea of fragrant water named Pure Radiant Flame-Arising; within it is a world-system named Well-Abiding.
Above that, there is another sea of fragrant water named Vajra-Eye Radiance; within it is a world-system named Arising Equal to the Dharma-Domain.
Above that, there is another sea of fragrant water named Lotus Level and Upright; within it is a world-system named Manifestation of Transformation Bodies Throughout the Ten Directions.
Above that, there is another sea of fragrant water named Radiance of Jewel-Ground Adornments; within it is a world-system named Adorned with Jewel Branches.
Above that, there is another sea of fragrant water named Transformed Fragrance Flame; within it is a world-system named Pure Transformation.
Above that, there is another sea of fragrant water named Jewel Banner; within it is a world-system named Buddha’s Protective Recollection.
Above that, there is another world-system named Universal Light of All Colors.

In this manner, above that, there are world-oceans of fragrant water and world-systems as numerous as atoms of dust; as it is in one direction, so it is in all ten directions—these are the places where Rocana Buddha constantly turns the wheel of Dharma.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
"The Dharma-realm is indestructible; The Lotus World-Ocean, Pure and vast in its adornments, Abides within empty space."
Within this ocean of worlds, the nature of the lands is inconceivable;
they abide well without confusion, each entirely sovereign.
They dwell in majestic arrays, established upon various colors.
In the ocean-like worlds of the Tathāgatas, the Buddha-fields are in mutual accord.
With various bodies and voices, all Buddhas exercise their sovereign power;
they universally behold all worlds, adorned with diverse karmic manifestations.
The mountain-city net of Sumeru, the circular form of the revolving water-wheel,
and the lotuses of pure color— all these surround one another.
The banner of śīla in the shape of a basin, and the forms of colors that revolve accordingly.
Thus inconceivable are the forms of the Buddha-lands;
these inconceivable worlds rest upon lotuses and emit great nets of light that universally illuminate all things.
In each and every Tathāgata’s land, He emits nets of various radiances,
Illuminating all Buddha-fields, Filling the oceans of the ten directions.
In all the Buddha-lands of all Buddhas, And in all gateways of their realms,
Through all skillful means they enter, and behold entirely the infinite,
inconceivable Buddha-fields— indestructible and inexhaustible,
adorned with immeasurable purity— by the majestic spiritual power of the Great Sages.
At the summit of that Tathāgata’s realm, in this inconceivable world,
there is both formation and dissolution; yet it neither arises nor perishes,
just as in a forest of trees, flowers and leaves may sprout or fall.
So too are these Buddha-fields, their formation and destruction being likewise;
just as various fruits grow depending on various trees,
so too do various sentient beings dwell within various fields.
Due to the differences in seeds, the fruits that grow are not the same;
because karmic actions are manifold, the Buddha-fields are variously distinct.
They are like a wish-fulfilling gem, which manifests all manner of colors according to one's wishes.
Because all deluded thoughts are eliminated, one sees entirely pure lands;
just as clouds in the sky can be manifested by the power of the dragon kings,
so too do all Buddha-fields arise through the power of the Buddhas' vows.
Just as a skilled illusionist can manifest various multitudes,
so too are the karmas of sentient beings and the inconceivable Buddha-fields;
like seeing a painted image, one knows it was created by a painter.
Thus one sees these Buddha-fields, Produced by the mind as their painter.
As the minds of sentient beings differ, They give rise to various delusive conceptions;
Thus all these Buddha-fields Are entirely like magical transformations.
Just as one sees a guide appearing in various and immeasurable forms according to the mental activities of sentient beings, so too does one see the Buddha-fields.
Immeasurable pearls and flowers completely cover all the Buddha-fields.
Forms appear each distinct, manifesting as stainless adornments.
Within those lotus nets, Buddha-fields manifest as networks,
adorned with various wondrous ornaments, serving as the dwelling place for sentient beings.
There are some Buddha-fields whose lands are defiled and uneven;
because of the afflictions of sentient beings, such Buddha-fields arise.
Whether pure or impure, these Buddha-fields are inconceivable.
The aspirations that arise in sentient beings are what the Bodhisattvas sustain.
Whether pure or impure, the infinite Buddha-fields arise from the causes and conditions of the ocean of karma; these are what the Bodhisattvas transform.
Some emit pure light, with bodies composed of stainless various jewels, adorned with all manner of wondrous ornaments; the Buddhas cause them to be purified.
Within all lands, the calamity of fire is beyond conception.
They manifest as impure, yet their lands are ever firm and stable;
some rest upon wind-circles, while others rest upon water-circles.
The formation and destruction of immeasurable lands occur due to the karmic actions of sentient beings.
I see immeasurable Buddha-fields, some being formed and others perishing;
yet they have no formation, nor do they have any perishing.
Within each and every thought-moment, immeasurable Buddha-fields arise.
Because they are sustained by all Buddhas, their lands are pure and free from defilement.
Yet there are some Buddha-fields that arise as muddy and impure,
devoid of light and perpetually shrouded in darkness, where sinful beings dwell.
There are some lands of mud, where afflictions bring great terror;
there is little joy and much sorrow and suffering, the dwelling place of those with meager merit.
There are worlds of iron, or nations of red copper.
Various rocky mountains and foul impurities arise due to the karma of sentient beings.
There are also buddha-fields of mud where sentient beings are constantly afflicted by suffering;
dwelling in eternal darkness and deprived of light, they are illuminated by the Ocean of Radiance.
Within the various realms of animals, they assume immeasurable kinds of bodies;
because of their past karma, they endure immeasurable suffering for a long time.
Within the realm of King Yama, they are constantly oppressed by the sufferings of hunger and thirst.
Ascending the great volcanic mountain, one undergoes immeasurable suffering for a long time.
Yet there may be buddha-fields of the seven treasures, level, upright, and adorned;
arisen through the power of pure karma, they are subtle, wondrous, and profoundly peaceful.
Within that Buddha-field, one perceives only the realms of humans and devas;
having perfected the fruits of merit, they constantly experience all manner of bliss.
Within each and every pore, there are inconceivable billions of lands.
Adorned with immeasurable forms, they arise from various karmas.
Arising according to their own karma, the realms of sentient beings are difficult to fathom;
having assumed various appearances, some experience pleasure and others experience suffering.
Some lands have immeasurable light, with all manner of jewels for their ground,
covered everywhere with vajra-flowers, adorned with stainless purity.
Some lands have light as their very substance, abiding within circles of radiance.
Golden sandalwood incense, with clouds of radiance constantly shining;
some lands have the sun’s orb as their substance, draped with robes of various fragrant jewels;
or within a single lotus flower, bodhisattvas completely fill it.
Some have immeasurable colors, The Buddha-fields of stainless jewels,
with nets of sapphire light, Whose nets of light flash like lightning.
Some Buddha-fields have Diamond flowers as their substance.
Some spread various jeweled flowers, observing them with great purity.
Through the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the pure lands he has attained—
the adorned realms of the three periods of time— are all manifested within this place.
O Sons of the Buddha, observe: the sovereign mastery of the Buddha-worlds, all future lands, are seen entirely as if in a dream.
All lands in the ten directions, the oceans of past Buddha-fields—
Within a single world, one sees all lands as like illusions; within a single world,
one sees all Buddhas of the three periods of time, along with all their Buddha-fields— the Buddhas and their lands of the three periods of time.
Contemplating the lands upon a single atom, all the sovereign powers of the Buddhas and their immeasurable,
wondrous adornments are seen to be entirely like flashes of lightning.
Or there are immeasurable Buddha-fields, whose shapes are like the great ocean.
There are worlds as inconceivable as Mount Sumeru;
there are lands like strings of pearls, resting upon nets of deep-blue jewels,
or adorned by trees, all filled with Buddhas.
Some rest upon mani-wheels, others rely upon lotuses;
adorned with eight corners and various ornaments, they are free from defilement and possess manifold colors.
Some are like lion thrones, while some lands are like gold.
Some have the form of various jewels; some are like the abodes of the Brahma world;
some have the shape of the Lord of Gods or the moon; others again are shaped like the sun.
Some are like mani-gems, adorned with the fragrance of sandalwood.
Some are like revolving incense wreaths, with Buddha-worlds abiding therein;
some are like wheels of light, adorned with various colors.
Some have a lifespan of one kalpa, while others have a lifespan of a hundred kalpas.
Or again, there may be a lifespan equal to the atoms within a Buddha-field;
or within a single eon, one sees the arising of immeasurable fields,
and the destruction of immeasurable, incalculable, and inconceivable fields.
In some lands there is no Buddha; in some lands there is a Buddha;
in some lands there is a single Buddha; or there may be immeasurable Buddhas.
If in a land there is no Buddha, [he appears] in another direction, in a different world-system.
There are emanated Buddhas who come, manifesting the teachings of sovereign mastery.
Descending from Tuṣita to relinquish their life-span, they enter the womb and are born;
they subdue Māra and attain perfect enlightenment, turning the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
According to the inclinations of sentient beings, He manifests in various forms;
At all times unchanging, He turns the pure wheel of Dharma.
If sentient beings are not vessels, It is not that the Buddha causes them not to see.
Obstructed by afflictions, they do not perceive the Tathāgata’s intent;
in some lands that are extremely turbid and evil, they constantly hear foul and wicked sounds,
harsh and coarse voices, and terrifying noises that inspire no love.
Those in the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts suffer;
this is a turbid and evil buddha-field, an ocean of sorrow and affliction for sentient beings.
Yet in some lands there is the sound of nectar, where one constantly hears gentle and supple voices.
The sound of the path of pure karma is heard throughout all lands;
in some Buddha-fields it is heard as the voice of Śakra-devānām-indra,
the wondrous voice of Brahmā-deva-rāja, or the voices of the lords of the various worlds.
The sounds of revolving light and voices, the infinite emanations of Buddhas,
and the voices of all Bodhisattvas— these are constantly heard throughout oceans of Buddha-fields or inconceivable lands;
one hears the sound of the turning of the Wheel of Dharma.
The sound of inexhaustible vows, the voice of the practices one cultivates,
hearing the names of all Buddhas of the three periods of time in their full glory,
and the arising of Buddha-fields according to conditions— their voices are inexhaustible.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

In the distant past, beyond world-ocean-microdust numbers of kalpas, and even further than that number, there was at that time a world-ocean named Pure Light Universal Eye. Within it was a world-system named Supreme Wondrous Sound, which rested upon a sea of mani-flower nets; it was pure and stainless, with world-systems as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru serving as its retinue.

Its ground was adorned with three hundred layers of immeasurable jewels, and it was surrounded on all sides by mountains of various precious gems, lofty, vast, and pure. This world-system was shaped like the celestial palace of Mount Sumeru and was adorned; its sustenance was mindfulness."
Within that world-system, there is a sea of fragrant water named Pure Radiance.
In that sea of fragrance, there is a Mount Sumeru named Banner Adorned with Great Blazing Flowers, surrounded by ten kinds of precious railings.

On that Mount Sumeru there is a grove named Jewel Flower Branch, adorned with immeasurable pavilions of flowers, immeasurable pavilions of jewel banners, immeasurable nets of dark-blue jewels, and flowers of various colors; immeasurable clouds of fragrance overspread it from above, and it is surrounded on all sides by ten billion hundred thousand cities.

To the east of that forest, there is a great city named Jvālāprabha, composed entirely of fragrance, measuring one thousand yojanas on each side, and surrounded by a perimeter wall made of the seven precious gems.
The towers and pavilions of the city are adorned with various jewels and covered with diverse flowers and nets of gems; when stirred by a gentle breeze, they produce exquisite sounds.

The city has twelve thousand gates, each adorned with pillars of various jewels, and it is encircled by ten billion gardens and groves. All the sentient beings within the city have fully perfected their karmic rewards and possess supernormal powers equal to those of the gods; whatever they desire arrives instantly upon their thought.
To the south of that forest, there is a celestial city named Tree-Flower Adornment;
next, a nāga city named Ultimate;
and next, a yakṣa city named Supreme and Wondrously Adorned Victory Banner of Vajra.
Next there was a gandharva city named Stainless Excellence;
next there was an asura city named Jewel Wheel Ground;
next there was a garuḍa city named Well-Adorned with Various Jewels and Auspicious Light.
Next there was a city of kinnaras named Amusement Adornment;
next there was a city of mahoragas named Jewel-Vajra Banner.
At that time, within that forest, there was a site of enlightenment named Jewel-Flower Adornment.

Before his place of enlightenment, there was a great lotus flower named Fully Endowed with Floral Radiance, measuring ten billion yojanas in length and breadth, surrounded by a retinue of one billion lotus flowers.

At that time, after a hundred years had passed in that world, a Buddha appeared in the world; in this manner, ten Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, successively arose in the world.
The first of these Buddhas was named Sarvaguṇamūlavijayasumerumegha.

At that time, the Buddha sat upon that great lotus flower and emitted from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows a great radiance called "Awakening of All Meritorious Virtues," which had as its retinue as many rays of light as there are atoms in ten buddha-worlds.

That light eliminates the veils and hindrances of affliction for all sentient beings, causing them to attain a pure mind, give rise to an ocean of merit, forever leave behind the three evil realms, the eight difficulties, and all states of existence, and resolve their minds upon Bodhicitta.
“O Sons of the Buddha!

At that time, in the city of Jvālāprabha, there was a king named Priyadarśanasubuddhi. That king ruled over ten trillion cities and had thirty-seven thousand queens and court ladies, as well as twenty-five thousand sons;
his eldest son was named Guṇajaya, and the next was named Samantavyūha-kumāra.”

At that time, because of the causes and conditions of the Buddha’s immeasurable sovereign merit and roots of goodness, the boy immediately attained ten kinds of samādhis, namely: the Samādhi of the Buddhas’ Endowment with Merit; the Samādhi of Universal Gate Expedients; the Samādhi of the Pure Cloud of Expedients; the Samādhi of Teaching and Transforming Sentient Beings; the Samādhi of All Sounds Pervading Everywhere; the Samādhi of Immeasurable Merit and Sincere Aspiration; the Samādhi of Realizing All Dharmas as They Truly Are; the Samādhi of the Ocean of Extensive Ground Expedients; the Samādhi of Supreme Liberation; and the Samādhi of the Light of All-Knowledge.
At that time, the youth Samantavyūha spoke in verse:
"Just as when a thousand suns arise, There is no part of space they do not illuminate;
So too is the radiance of him who sits upon the site of enlightenment, Free from all defilement."
Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, a Teacher difficult to encounter has appeared in the world; all behold this Most Victorious One.
Observing the Buddha’s radiance, it is like a cloud beyond conception.
He is seen in all places, as if appearing right before one's eyes.
From his pores he emits radiance, inexhaustible like clouds;
according to the voices of all sentient beings, he praises the Buddha’s immeasurable virtues.
Sentient beings who encounter the Buddha’s light Are freed from suffering and enter eternal quiescence;
All find peace, security, and happiness, Filled everywhere with joy.
Beholding all the bodhisattvas, Who fill the realms of the ten directions,
They emit clouds of mani-jewels, praising all the Most Victorious Ones.
Constantly at the site of enlightenment, they hear an ocean of profound and wondrous sounds that extinguish the suffering of all sentient beings and manifest the Buddha’s power of mastery.
"Everyone shall arouse reverence, with immeasurable hearts of joy,
go to the presence of the Dharma King, gaze upon him, pay homage,
and make offerings. At that time, the sound of the verses spoken by the youth was heard everywhere throughout that world.
At that time, King Priyadarśana-Buddhi, having heard these verses being spoken, was filled with immeasurable joy and recited in verse:
"It is fitting to proclaim this everywhere at once to all the kings and great ministers,
so that they may know of these auspicious signs and all hasten to the Most Victorious One."
Adorn all the cities and cause them to be entirely pure;
erect various exquisite banners and streamers, decorated with all kinds of jewels.
Set up canopies of many wonderful gems, spreading them out to cover everything above.
Raising clouds of music from celestial maidens, let them fill the entirety of space.
Sweep clean all the streets and alleys, and let a rain of various jewels descend.
Adorned with many precious chariots, we shall go to behold the Most Victorious One.
Within each of those pavilions, rains of various clouds fall;
clouds of all manner of adornments flow through the midst of space.
Clouds of fragrant lotus-light and inconceivable flower-canopies descend.
Necklaces and crescent-moon clouds rain down myriad exquisite jeweled robes;
Mount Sumeru and fragrant waters are adorned with mani jewels and various pure,
diverse gems, all manifesting within the void of space.
Garlands of mani-jewel flowers, Stainless garlands of various jewels,
And clouds of mani-jewel lamps, Coalesce in radiance, suspended in the void. Gazing upon them,
all contemplate the Buddha, Giving rise to immeasurable joy.
"Together with your wife, children, and retinue, you should go to see the Most Victorious One.
At that time, King Priyadarśana-buddhi, accompanied by a retinue of seventy-seven billion nayutas, went to the presence of the Buddha Sarvaguṇamūla-vijitaparvata-megha.

Having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and sat to one side. Immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others also went to the Buddha’s presence, prostrated with their heads at his feet, and stood to one side.

At that time, for the sake of teaching and transforming all sentient beings, the Tathāgata preached a sutra named *The Assembly of All Buddhas of the Three Times Manifested* within that ocean-like assembly; it had as its retinue as many sūtras as there are atoms in a world-system, according to what each sentient being was capable of understanding.

At that time, having heard this sutra, the youth Samantavyūha, by virtue of the causes and conditions of his merit from past lives, attained the samādhi of the Fulfillment of All Dharmas, the samādhi of the Entry and Abiding of All Dharmas in the Bodhicitta, the samādhi of the Expedient Means of the Lion’s Light of the Dharma Realm, and the samādhi of the Purity of the Dharma Eye.
At that time, the youth spoke in verse:
"I have heard the most supreme Dharma, And my pure eye of wisdom has opened;
I am now able to see all Buddhas And the ocean of their past merits."
I see all beings as they truly are, complete with their original forms;
according to their original names and physical actions, I make offerings to all Buddhas.
In the presence of all past Buddhas, I have practiced for oceans of immeasurable eons.
I behold oceans of Buddhas and oceans of pure Buddha-fields.
Within the ocean of birth and death, I have relinquished my own bodies innumerable times;
practicing the supreme conduct of a Bodhisattva, I adorn and purify oceans of Buddha-fields.
He gave away immeasurable ears and noses, heads, eyes, hands, and feet;
the bodies of kings and the bodies of great ministers, fully cultivating a pure land.
Within each and every Buddha-field, for inconceivable billions of kalpas, he practiced.
Practicing the bodhisattva path, one purifies the oceans of buddha-fields.
Through the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, one cultivates an ocean of all practices,
so that within all oceans of lands, the buddha-lands are made pure.
Just as the light of the sun is pure, And all forms are seen in their fullness,
So when the light of the Buddha’s wisdom shines, One sees my original practice.
One sees immeasurable Buddhas In stainless and pure lands.
The sound of attaining equal and perfect enlightenment fills the entire dharma-realm.
Just as they cultivate purity and fully possess oceans of buddha-fields, one should,
through the spiritual power of all Buddhas, practice the bodhisattva path accordingly.
When this verse was spoken, sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru all resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed path.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke these verses for the sake of this youth:
“Excellent, Universal Adornment, Treasury of Virtue, Great Renown!”
For the sake of sentient beings, you courageously seek bodhi;
You can emit the light of wisdom, filling the entire dharma-realm.
With the cloud of unsurpassed virtue and conduct, you shall attain the ocean of wisdom.
Practicing within a single land for as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system,
one shall attain this wisdom just as I have attained it.
Those who are indolent cannot understand this ocean of profound skillful means.
Through the accomplishment of the power of diligence, one can purify Buddha-worlds.
Having cultivated myriad practices throughout oceans of eons as numerous as all atoms,
they attain such purity as that of my own ocean of Buddha-fields.
For the sake of each and every sentient being, They undergo ascetic practices for immeasurable eons;
Without wearying of the perils of birth and death, They are able to become great guides.
With immeasurable and boundless vows, They are the ocean of all Buddhas.
Able to cross over to the unsurpassed path, Fully endowed with an ocean of skillful means;
Having reverently made offerings to me, The Buddha of Universal Adornment and Great Power,
Who excels Mount Sumeru, He shall bring your unsurpassed path to fulfillment.
Samantabhadra is ever courageous, Possessing great renown,
Filling the entirety of the dharma-realm, Purifying the oceans of all Buddha-fields.
At that time, the Tathāgata Supreme Sumeru Cloud, the Source of All Merits, lived for five billion years.
After that Buddha had passed into parinirvāṇa, another Buddha appeared in the world named Sarvatrātarajñānavimalanetra-rāja Tathāgata.

Upon seeing this Tathāgata, the youth Samantavyūha immediately attained the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*, the *samantamukhasāgaragarbha-samādhi*, the *apramāṇajñānadhāraṇīdharmacakra-pravartana-samādhi*, and the *gambhīradharmarati-samādhi*.
At that time, the Buddha preached a sutra titled "The Adornment of the Stainless Nature of All Dharmadhātus," which had as many associated scriptures as there are atoms in a world-system.

Upon hearing this sutra, the youth Samantavyūha immediately attained two samādhis: the samādhi named "The Universal Gate Joy-Treasury of All Dharmas" and the samādhi named "Entering the Ocean of Expedient Means of All Dharmas."
Chapter Three: The Names of the Tathāgata. In the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*, Chapter Three: The Names of the Tathāgata.
The Buddha was at the site of enlightenment in the kingdom of Magadha; having first attained Buddhahood, he sat upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury in the Hall of Universal Radiance.
His wisdom was perfectly awakened and free from dualistic thought, and he had thoroughly realized all things.
Abiding in the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), dwelling where the Buddhas dwell, equal to all Tathāgatas, having reached the unimpeded state,
possessing the qualities of non-retrogression and an indestructible realm, they abide in the inconceivable and equally penetrate the three periods of time.
Together with a multitude of great Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-lands— all of whom are in their final birth before Buddhahood— they have all come from other world-systems.
Having gathered here, they have realized the nature of sentient beings and entered deeply into the Dharma-realm;

they constantly and skillfully contemplate the world and nirvana, clearly understand karmic retributions and the mental activities of sentient beings, and are fully able to comprehend the meanings and flavors of all phenomena.
They observe worldly and world-transcending dharmas, ultimately discerning their conditioned and unconditioned natures, and depart.
...and the present, there is nothing they have not thoroughly mastered.
At that time, all the bodhisattvas thought to themselves:

"We pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion for us, will manifest buddha-fields according to our aspirations, manifest where Buddhas dwell, manifest the adornments of buddha-lands, manifest the teachings of all Buddhas, manifest the purity of buddha-fields, manifest the Dharma taught by Buddhas, manifest the essence of buddha-fields, manifest the power of a Buddha's merits, manifest the arising of [Buddhas] in accordance with their buddha-fields, and manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment, thereby revealing to the bodhisattvas distinguished by all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions."

The ten abodes, the ten practices, the ten dedications, the ten treasuries, the ten stages, the ten vows, the ten concentrations, the ten masteries, and the bodhisattvas of the ten summits with their hearts of sympathetic joy; the uninterrupted nature of the Tathāgata; the salvation of sentient beings; the extinction of afflictions; the knowledge of all activities; the understanding of all dharmas; the departure from defilement; the uprooting of all hardships; the severing of the net of doubt; the exhaustion of craving and desire; the unsurpassed stage of the Buddha; the realm of the Buddha; the lifespan of the Buddha’s dwelling; the conduct of the Buddha; the powers of the Buddha; the fearlessnesses of the Buddha; the meditative concentrations of the Buddha; the supernormal powers of the Buddha; the supreme dharmas of the Buddha; the immovability of the Buddha; the six faculties of the Buddha; the light of the Buddha; the wisdom of the Buddha; and the unsurpassed merits of the Buddha—all these are fully perfected. May such matters as these be manifested for me.
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas, immediately manifested supernatural powers in accordance with their mental images.

Having manifested these powers, from the east, beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, there was a world named Golden Color. There, a Buddha named Immovable Wisdom resided, and a bodhisattva named Mañjuśrī, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, came to the place where the Buddha was. They paid respectful offerings and prostrated at his feet with their heads. Then, in the eastern direction, they magically created lion thrones of the Lotus Treasury and sat upon them in the full lotus posture.

To the south, beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, there is a world named Delightful Color. There, a Buddha named Wisdom Fire resides, and a bodhisattva named Chief of Enlightenment, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, came to the place where the Buddha was. Having paid respectful homage and made offerings, bowing their heads at his feet, they immediately manifested in the southern direction lion thrones of lotus-treasury and sat upon them cross-legged.

To the west, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, there is a world named Flower Color. The Buddha there is named Practice Wisdom, and the bodhisattva is named Wealth Chief. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, he came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet. Thereupon, in the western direction, he manifested a lion throne of the Lotus Treasury and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.

To the north, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, there is a world named Campaka Flower Color. The Buddha there is named Conduct Wisdom, and the bodhisattva is named Jewel Head. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, they came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating at his feet with their heads. Then, in the northern direction, they manifested a lion throne of lotus-treasury and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.

To the northeast, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, there is a world named Blue Lotus Color. The Buddha there is named Clear Wisdom, and the Bodhisattva is named Virtue Chief. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-lands, they came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating their heads at his feet. Then, in the northeastern quarter, they manifested a lion throne of lotus-treasury and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.

To the southeast, past as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, there is a world named Golden Color. The Buddha there is named Ultimate Wisdom, and the bodhisattva is named Eyes Chief. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, he came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet. He then manifested, in the southeastern direction, a lion throne of the Lotus Treasury and sat upon it cross-legged.

To the southwest, beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, there is a world named Jewel Color. Its Buddha is named Supreme Wisdom, and the bodhisattva there is named Foremost Progress. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, he came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet. Then, in the southwest, he manifested a lion throne of lotus-treasury and sat upon it cross-legged.

To the northwest, beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, there is a world named Vajra-Color. The Buddha there is named Sovereign Wisdom, and the bodhisattva is named Dharma-Crown. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, he came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet. Then, in the northwest, he magically manifested a lion throne of the Lotus Treasury and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.

Ten Buddha-lands beyond the number of atoms, passing downward, there is a world named Crystal Color; the Buddha there is named Brahma-Wisdom, and the Bodhisattva is named Wisdom Chief. Together with Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-lands, he came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet. He then manifested, in the region below, a lion throne of Lotus Treasury and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.

Above, passing through as many worlds as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, there is a world named True Color. The Buddha there is named Subduer of Enmity Wisdom, and the bodhisattva is named Worthy Head. Together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields, he came to the place where the Buddha was, paying respectful offerings and prostrating his head at the Buddha’s feet. He then manifested a lion throne of lotus-treasury in the space above and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the great assembly and exclaimed:
"How wonderful! This gathering of bodhisattvas today is truly unprecedented."
O Sons of the Buddha!

You should know that the buddha-fields are inconceivable; the dwelling of the Buddhas, the buddha-lands, the buddha-dharma, the purity of the buddha-fields, the Buddhas’ preaching of the Dharma, the appearance of the Buddhas in the world, the arising of the buddha-fields, and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* of all Buddhas—all these are inconceivable.

Why is this? The Buddhas of the ten directions preach the Dharma, knowing the mental activities of those beings and transforming them accordingly; they are equal to empty space and the dharma-realm. Why is this?

In this Sahā world-system, throughout all the four continents, there are beings who are taught in various ways—beings with diverse bodies, diverse names, locations, forms and colors, heights and lengths, lifespans, attainments, sense bases, origins of their faculties, and karmic retributions. Such beings are diverse in these many respects, and what they perceive is likewise different.
Why is this? O Sons of the Buddha!

In these four continents, the names of the Buddhas differ: some are called Siddhārtha, some Pūrṇacandra, some Siṃhanāda, some Śākyamuni, some Ṛṣi, some Vairocana, some Gautama, some Mahāśramaṇa, some Jina, and some Tāraṇa.
These and others are the names by which the Buddhas are called; their number is ten thousand. "O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the eastern direction, there is a world-system of four continents called Suvigupta. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Vajra, some call him Jinaśreṣṭha, some call him Mahājñāna, some call him Abhedyaka, some call him Megharāja, some call him Araṇa, some call him Samatā, some call him Nandana, some call him Anupama, and some call him Tūṣṇīmbhūta. These and others are the names by which the Buddhas are called; their number is ten thousand."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the southern direction, there is a world-system of four continents called Duskara (Difficult to Sustain). There, they call the Tathāgata by such names as Amṛtavarṣin (Ambrosial Shower), or Yaśaskīrti (Famous Renown), or Vimala (Stainless), or Satyavādin (Teacher of Truth), or Vinetā (Tamer), or Prajñārāma (Delighting in Wisdom), or Mahāghoṣa (Great Sound), or Saṃbhava (Benefactor of the Multitude), or Amita (Immeasurable), or Jñānavara (Supreme Wisdom)—there are ten thousand such names by which the Buddha is known."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the western direction, there is a world-system of four continents named Buddhaprajñā. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: sometimes Buddhaprajña, sometimes Priyadarśana, sometimes Anuttararāja, sometimes Abhaya, sometimes Satyajñāna, sometimes Nityavikrāmin, sometimes Santuṣṭa, sometimes Dharmaprajña, sometimes Niṣṭhāgata, and sometimes Kṣāntivādin; such are the names by which the Buddha is known, numbering ten thousand."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the north, there is a world-system of four continents called Siṃhavādin. There, they call the Tathāgata by names such as Mahāmuni, Tapasvin, Bhagavat, Puṇyakṣetra, Sarvajña, Kalyāṇamati, Viśuddha, Airāvaṇa, Vijayāvatī, or Pūrṇapraṇidhānacaryā; such names for the Buddha number ten thousand."
“O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the northeast, there is a world-system of four continents called Peaceful (An-ning). There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Dharma King, some call him Equal Arising, some call him Tranquility, some call him Wondrous Heaven, some call him Free from Desire, some call him Supreme Wisdom, some call him Equal Mind, some call him Indestructible, some call him Sound of Wisdom, and some call him Far-Come. Such names for the Buddha number ten thousand.”
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the southeast, there is a world-system of four continents called Joyful Delight (Nandana). Therein, the names by which the Buddhas are known are as follows: some are called Tathāgata, some Lotus, some Wisdom-Fire, some Knower of Men, some Secret Teaching, some Liberation, some Spontaneously Abiding, some Accomplishment of Sublime Conduct, some King of the Pure Eye, some Supreme Valor, and some Power of Diligence; such names for the Buddhas number ten thousand."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the southwest direction, there is a world-system of four continents called Sthira. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Acala, some Prajñārāja, some Pūrṇaprajña, some Akṣobhyaprajña, some Nityakaruṇa, some Mūrdharāja, some Jayasvara, some Sarvadatta, some Ṛṣidhara, and some Vijayasumeru. Such names for the Buddha number ten thousand."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next to this, in the northwest, there is a world-system of four continents named Subhūti. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Universal Wisdom (Samantaprajñā), some call him Accomplishment of Radiance (Prabhāsasiddha), some call him Jewel Topknot (Ratnaśikhin), some call him Worthy of Reverent Recollection (Smaraṇīya), some call him Unsurpassed Meaning (Anuttarārtha), some call him Joyful Delight (Nandana), some call him Innately Pure (Svabhāva-viśuddha), some call him Full of Radiance (Pūrṇaprabha), some call him Long Arms (Dīrghabhuja), and some call him Fundamentally Well-Abiding (Mūlasusthita). Such names for the Buddha number ten thousand."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Next below this, in the direction of the nadir, there is a world-system of four continents called Jvālāmārga (Flaming Path). There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Kuśalamūla-vardhana (Increasing the Roots of Virtue), some call him Siṃhavarṇa (Lion-Colored), some call him Prajñāmati (Wisdom-Minded), some call him Suvarṇajvālā (Golden Flame), some call him Viśvapriya (Universally Loved), some call him Brahmaghoṣa (Brahma-Voice), some call him Upakāraka (Benefactor), some call him Anuttarāgata (Supremely Arrived), some call him Satyadeva (True Heaven), and some call him Samadāna (Equal Giving). Such are the names by which the Buddha is designated; their number is ten thousand."
“O Sons of the Buddha!

Above this world-system, there is another world of four continents called *Dharanīdhara*. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him *Vikrāntamati* (Fierce Wisdom), some call him *Anantaviśuddha* (Immeasurable Purity), some call him *Bodhimati* (Awakened Wisdom), some call him *Śūramukha* (Heroic Head), some call him *Sudarśana* (Sublime Adornment), some call him *Prāmodyasamudgata* (Arisen from Joy), some call him *Manorathaparipūrṇa* (Fulfillment of Wishes), some call him *Jyotis* (Flame of Light), some call him *Vīrya* (Diligence), and some call him *Ekayāna* (The One Vehicle).”
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Thus, within the four continents known as Jambudvīpa, there are ten thousand such names of Buddhas.
In this Sahā world, there are likewise ten billion sets of four continents; the names by which the Tathāgatas therein are called are each different, numbering ten billion million."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the east of this Sahā world, there is another land called Guhyaviniścaya. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Samatā, some call him Paramavīra, some call him Āśvāsaka, some call him Vinītamanas, some call him Śrutamati, some call him Sarvatyāga, some call him Vaśavartin, some call him Dṛḍhakāya, some call him Mahātikrama, and some call him Asamasajñāna."
"O Sons of the Buddha!
In this manner, there are ten billion million lands within the Secret Instruction [world-system] that bear the names of Buddhas.
O Sons of the Buddha!"

To the south of this world, there is a land called Most Valiant (*Suvīra*). There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him the Self-Existent Pure One (*Svayambhū-viśuddha*), some call him the One Who Reaches the Intention (*Manogata*), some call him the Capable Sage (*Śākyamuni*), some call him the King of Liberation (*Vimukti-rāja*), some call him the King of Wisdom (*Jñāna-rāja*), some call him the One Perfected in Knowledge and Conduct (*Vidyācaraṇa-saṃpanna*), some call him the Well-Vowed One (*Svastika*), some call him the Capable of Quiescence (*Samatha-kara*), some call him Great Loving-kindness (*Mahāmaitrī*), and some call him Great Compassion (*Mahākaruṇā*). Such names for the Buddha number ten billion million.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the west of this world, there is a land called Vimalā. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Samantavajracitta (Endowed with Upright Mind), some call him Vibhaktamārga (Discerning the Path), some call him Sudhara (Well-Sustained), some call him Vimuktasambhrama (Liberated from All Confusion), some call him Śāstrin (Teacher), some call him Vibhaktaratna (Discerning All Jewels), some call him Anuttarābhāsa (Supreme Manifestation), some call him Āgatavikurvaṇa (Come to Transform), some call him Sarvaduṣkaracaryā (All Austerities), and some call him Balopeta (Endowed with Power). Such names for the Buddha are ten billion million in number."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the north of this world, there is a land called Ratnaviṣaya. There, the Tathāgatas are addressed by such names as Campakapuṣpavarṇa, or Sūryagarbha, or Vīryasthita, or Samudgatāyus, or Abhyudgatarāja, or Prajñāditya, or Anāvaraṇa, or Candrodaya, or Prajñāgnitejas, or Viśuddhakāya; there are ten billion million such names of Buddhas."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the northeast of this world, there is a land called Hani. There, they call the Tathāgata by various names: some call him Free from Suffering, some call him All-Liberated, some call him Endowed with Causes and Conditions, some call him Wisdom of Liberation, some call him Treasury of the Past, some call him Jewel Light, some call him Detached from the World, some call him Reached the Ground of Bodylessness, some call him Treasury of Majestic Beauty, and some call him Free from the Mind of Hatred. Such names for the Buddha number ten billion."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the southeast of this world, there is another land called Abhirati (Beneficial). There, the Tathāgata is addressed by such names as Hetu-pratyaya (Cause and Condition), Kṣaya-jñāna (Knowledge of Exhaustion), Manojña-svara (Beautiful Voice), Indriya-viśiṣṭa (Superior Faculties), Vyūha-chattra (Adorned Canopy), Viśuddhendriya (Pure Faculties), Viśeṣa (Exquisite), Pāramitā-vibhakti-gata (Attained through the Analysis of Perfections), Vimala-samādhi (Supreme Concentration), Maitreya-pitṛ (Loving Father), or Jñāna-sāgara (Ocean of Wisdom). Such names for the Buddha number ten billion."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the southwest of this world, there is another land called Few. There, the Tathāgata is addressed by such names as Lord of Sages, Joyful Jewel, Non-dual Contemplation, Knower of Wisdom, Humble Mind, Seen by Those with Karmic Connection, Lord of Faculties, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Established Deed, or Diamond Flower; indeed, there are ten billion million such names by which the Buddha is known."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

To the northwest of this world, there is a land called Saṃtuṣita. There, the Tathāgata is addressed by various names: some call him Puṣpasaṃcaya, some call him Candanacchatra, some call him Padmagarbha, some call him Sarvadharmasamatikrānta, some call him Dharmavyakta, some call him Anupūrvodaya, some call him Suviśuddhacchatra, some call him Vimalakuśalamūla, some call him Suvākya, some call him Ekāgradharmasmṛti, and some call him Pañcadharmakośa. Such names for the Buddha number ten billion."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Beneath this world, there is another land called Free from Solid Food. There, the Tathāgata is addressed by various names: some call him Pearl Flame, some Universal Transformation, some Lord of the Life of Dharma, some Unconditioned, some Root of Awakening, some Free from Dust, some Wind Unobstructed, some Delighting in Giving, some Discerning the Path, and some Erecting the Banner. Such names for the Buddha number ten billion."
"Sons of the Buddha!

Beyond this world-system, there is a land named Sound of Liberation. There, the Tathāgata is known by various names: some call him Fierce Banner, some Immeasurable Jewel, some Joy in Great Giving, some Celestial Light, some Auspicious Arising, some Departed from the Land of Death, some Most Victorious, some Non-retrogressive Wheel, some Free from Unrighteousness, and some Cultivator of All-Knowledge."
"O Sons of the Buddha!
In this world-system called Sound of Liberation, there are ten billion times ten million Buddhas bearing their respective names, just as there are in the Sahā world and the ten worlds.
Likewise, in the eastern direction, there are hundreds of thousands of billions, immeasurable, and incalculable [worlds]..."
In worlds as numerous as the incalculable, the inconceivable, the incomparable, the unequaled, the boundless, the limitless, the ineffable,
the space-like, and the dharma-realm, sentient beings call upon the names of Buddhas,
each being different; this is also true for the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.
Furthermore, it is thus: all these were employed by the Tathāgata while he was a bodhisattva;

for those with the necessary causes and conditions, in order to deliver them, he used various skillful means—verbal actions, vocal sounds, karmic deeds, retributions, dharma-gates, provisional paths, and the inclinations of the various faculties—to cause all sentient beings to know the Dharma of the Tathāgata.
Chapter Four: The Four Truths, Part One. At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!

That which is called the Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is sometimes called unobstructed, sometimes called stainless purity, sometimes called tranquility, sometimes called signless, sometimes called deathless, sometimes called non-existence, sometimes called the severance of causes and conditions, sometimes called cessation, sometimes called reality, and sometimes called abiding by its own nature.

That which is called the Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering is sometimes called the One Vehicle; sometimes called the approach to tranquility; sometimes called guidance; sometimes called the ultimate hope; sometimes called never being separated [from the goal]; sometimes called the ability to lay down the burden; sometimes called reaching the non-destination; sometimes called the conduct followed by the noble ones; sometimes called the path of the sages; and sometimes called the ten treasuries.
"Sons of the Buddha!
In this Sahā world, there are four hundred billion nayutas of such names for the Four Noble Truths; they are spoken in this way according to what is necessary to discipline sentient beings."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

What is called the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) in the Sahā world is, in the Guhyadēśanā world, called either Seeking the Root (*mūlaparyeṣaṇā*), or Inability to Escape (*aniḥsaraṇa*), or Unbound Root (*abaddhamūla*), or Doing What Should Not Be Done (*akāryakaraṇa*), or All Is Unreal (*asarvatattva*), or Weakness of Discrimination (*vikalpadaurbalya*), or Accomplishment of Location (*sthānasiddhi*), or Supreme Harm (*paramopaghāta*), or Movement (*calana*), or Bodily Affairs (*kāyakṛtya*)."""

That which is called the Truth of the Origin of Suffering is also termed "feeling," "branch," "burning," "solidity," "root-ruination," "continuity," "harmful conduct," "forgetfulness," "source of birth," or "division."

That which is called the Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is also termed Righteous Meaning, or Firmness, or Praise, or Tranquility, or the Happy Destination, or Subduing, or the Single Path, or Freedom from Affliction, or Non-confusion, or the Ultimate.

That which is called the Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering is also named the Fierce General, or the Non-submerged, or the Transcendent, or the Diligent Expedient, or the Universal Eye, or the One Free from Extremes, or Awakening, or Attainment of the Sublime, or the Unsurpassed Eye, or the Observer of Directions.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

In that world, Guhyadṛśa, there are four hundred billion nayutas of such names for the Four Noble Truths; they are spoken in this way according to what is necessary to discipline various sentient beings."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

That which is called the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) in the Sahā world is, in the world-system Most Valiant (*Suvīra*), known by various names: sometimes it is called Terror, sometimes the Severance of Merit, sometimes that Which Should Be Reprimanded, sometimes Constant Provision, sometimes Roughness, sometimes Constant Enmity, sometimes Deprived of Excellence, sometimes Robbed of Benefit, sometimes Difficult to Deal With, sometimes Falsehood, and sometimes Power."

That which is called the Truth of the Origin of Suffering is sometimes termed the causal condition, sometimes the root of delusion, sometimes the forest of enmity, sometimes the branch of blades, sometimes the taste of extinction, sometimes the adversary, sometimes attachment to flavor, sometimes the guide, sometimes the increase of darkness, and sometimes the harm to benefit.

That which is called the Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is also termed the Great Meaning, the Beneficial Portion, the Meaning within Meanings, the Immeasurable, the Vision, the Severance of Falsity, the Most Excellent, the Permanent, the Abiding, or the Unconditioned.

That which is called the Noble Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering is also termed the Extinguishing of Fire, the Supreme Branch, the Definitive Discernment, the Non-retrogression, the Profound Expedient Means, the Emergence, the Most Excellent, the Arrival at the Non-destination, Liberation, and that which enables liberation.
“O Sons of the Buddha!
In that world Most Valiant, there are four hundred billion nayutas of such names for the Four Noble Truths, spoken in this way according to what is necessary to discipline sentient beings.”
"O Sons of the Buddha!

Just as that which is called the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) is taught in the Sahā world, in the Vimala world it is called regret, or waiting for provisions, or discrimination, or saṃsāra, or the precursor, or the single flavor, or non-dharma, or the manifest ground, or the most perverse, or wrong view, or the unbearable."

That which is called the Truth of the Origin of Suffering is also termed the "empty vessel," the "portion," "endurance," "place of birth," "grasping," "rejection," "increase," "burden," "that which gives rise [to suffering]," or "firm bondage."

That which is called the Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is also named "the Equal," "the Empty," "the Stainless," "the Supreme Faculty," "the Supreme Equality," "the Unconditioned," "the Extinction of Latent Tendencies," "the Most Excellent," "the Ultimate," or "the Seal of Destruction."

"O Sons of the Buddha!

That which is called the Truth of the Origin of Suffering is sometimes termed craving (*tṛṣṇā*), sometimes termed sinking, sometimes termed inexhaustible, sometimes termed division, sometimes termed wrong course, sometimes termed a ford, sometimes termed an object, sometimes termed an obstruction, sometimes termed a vessel, and sometimes termed movement.

What is called the Truth of the Origin of Suffering (duḥkhasamudayasatya) is also termed "outflow" (āsrava), "disturbance" (saṃkleśa), "affliction" (kleśa), "weakness" (daurbalya), "drifting and sinking," "contradiction," "non-liberation," "that which is produced," "grasping" (upādāna), or "falsity."

That which is called the Truth of the Path Leading to the Cessation of Suffering is also named the realization of non-existence, the cause of all, the root of goodness, the arrival of clarity, the non-reverting dharma, that which has an end, the Great Path, the ability to subdue, tranquility, or the non-cyclic flow.

Chapter Four: The Four Noble Truths, Part Two.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

There are forty billion hundred thousand nayutas of such names for the Four Noble Truths that benefit the world; they are spoken in this way according to what is necessary to discipline various sentient beings."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

That which is called the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) in the Sahā world is, in the world-systems of Fewness, known by various names: sometimes it is called 'the mind of malice,' sometimes 'the lack of growing wisdom,' sometimes 'erroneous thought,' sometimes 'transmigration,' sometimes 'shamelessness and lack of remorse,' sometimes 'the root of greed,' sometimes 'blazing fire,' sometimes 'thorns and brambles,' sometimes 'a mountain of fire,' and sometimes 'grief and affliction.'"

"O Sons of the Buddha!

That which is called the Truth of Suffering (*duḥkha-satya*) in the Sahā world is, in the world-system called Sound of Liberation (*Vimukti-ghoṣa*), called either 'Concealed Fault,' or 'Sentient Being,' or 'Dependent on Branches,' or 'Destruction of Excellence,' or 'Obstruction,' or 'Swift Current,' or 'Remote,' or 'Treasury,' or 'Reception,' or 'Branch of Suffering.'"

In the world-system called Sound of Liberation, there are four hundred billion nayutas of such names for the Four Noble Truths; they are spoken in this way according to what is necessary to discipline various sentient beings."
