During the intense heat of midsummer, one should wish that all sentient beings be free from the fever of afflictions and attain the coolness of meditative concentration.
When the cold deepens and the ice freezes, may all sentient beings attain ultimate liberation and unsurpassed coolness.
When reciting the scriptures, may all sentient beings attain the gate of *dhāraṇī* and encompass all dharmas.
If one sees the Tathāgata, one should wish that all sentient beings may fully attain the Buddha-eye and behold all who are most supreme.
Contemplating the Tathāgata with clarity, one should wish that all sentient beings may see throughout the ten directions,
as upright and majestic as the Buddha.
Upon seeing a Buddha stupa or temple, one should wish that all beings be as revered as a stupa and receive the respect of devas and humans.
While observing a stupa with a respectful mind, one should wish that all beings be as honored as the Buddha and be venerated by devas and humans.
Prostrating before a Buddha stupa, one should wish that all sentient beings attain the Way like the Buddha,
such that no one can see the crown of their head.
Circumambulating the stupa and temple to the right, one should wish that all sentient beings tread the true path and fully realize the intent of the Way.
Circumambulating the stupa three times, one should wish that all beings attain a single-minded resolve and diligently seek the Buddha-way.
Praising and chanting the praises of the Tathāgata, one should wish that all beings reach the shore of merit and their eulogies be inexhaustible.
When praising the Buddha’s marks and signs, one should wish that all beings possess radiant spiritual power and virtue, equal to the Dharma-body of the Buddha.
When washing the feet, one should wish that all beings attain the four bases of supernatural power and achieve ultimate liberation.
When sleeping at night, may all beings rest from all conditioned activities,
their minds pure and free from defilement.
When awakening at dawn, may all beings awaken to all-knowledge, never abandoning the ten directions.
“O Son of the Buddha!

This is how the physical, verbal, and mental actions of a bodhisattva are able to attain all supreme and wondrous merits, such that they cannot be shaken by devas, māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, humans, non-humans, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas.”

Chapter Eight: The Bodhisattva Śrīghoṣa (Part One) At that time, Mañjuśrī, with verses, questioned the Bodhisattva Śrīghoṣa—who had attained profound understanding of the meaning and possessed pure virtues—saying:
“O Son of the Buddha, I have already explained The pure conduct of the bodhisattvas, Which all the World-Honored Ones In unison praise and extol.”
"Furthermore, you, O Benevolent One, should expound upon the profound and subtle practices,
the vast significance of merit, and the assembly of all great beings.
Bodhisattva Worthy Head replied:
The various merits of the Bodhisattvas are immeasurable and boundless;
I shall speak of them according to my ability. Yet the few merits of the Bodhisattvas that I have here expounded are like a single drop in the ocean.
When a bodhisattva, within the cycle of birth and death, first gives rise to the thought of enlightenment,
they seek only awakening with a resolve so firm it cannot be shaken.
The merit of that single moment of thought is profound, vast, and without limit.
Even if the Tathāgata were to explain them in detail, they would not be exhausted even after an entire kalpa;
how much less so in immeasurable, countless, and boundless kalpas?
Having fully cultivated the various perfections and the meritorious practices of the stages.
Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all the Tathāgatas,
even if they were to speak of those clouds of merit, could not reach their ultimate end.
Now I shall describe but a small fraction of the merits of these Bodhisattvas.
Like a bird traversing the void, or like a single atom upon the earth—
this is not without cause, nor is it without conditions;
when a Bodhisattva first resolves their mind, it is the great merit of the straightforward heart.
Toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, they give rise to deep and pure faith;
because of their faith and reverence for the Triple Gem, they are able to resolve upon bodhicitta.
They do not seek the pleasures of the five desires, nor precious goods or various worldly profits.
Seeking neither personal peace nor worldly fame,
but to eliminate the suffering of sentient beings until none remains,
the Bodhisattva makes the initial resolve to deliver all such beings. This is the Bodhisattva’s first generation of the mind of enlightenment.
Constantly wishing to cause all sentient beings to leave suffering behind and dwell forever in peace and joy;
to adorn and purify all buddha-fields and make offerings to immeasurable Buddhas;
to delight in establishing the True Dharma of the Buddhas and desire to attain the Unsurpassed Way.
Purifying all-encompassing wisdom, the Bodhisattva first gives rise to the mind of enlightenment.
With a profound mind and pure faith that cannot be destroyed, they reverently make offerings to all Buddhas, honoring the True Dharma and the Noble Sangha;
it is for the sake of faith and reverence toward the Triple Gem that they give rise to this mind.
With deep faith in all Buddhas and the True Dharma, And likewise faith in the path practiced by Bodhisattvas,
With a correct mind directed toward the Bodhi of the Buddhas— It is because of this that a Bodhisattva first resolves their mind [on enlightenment].
Faith is the source of the Path and the mother of all merit;
it increases all wholesome dharmas, eliminates all doubts and delusions, and reveals and develops the unsurpassed Way.
Pure faith removes defilement and makes the mind firm; it eradicates pride and is the root of reverence.
Faith is the foremost treasure among all dharmas; it serves as the pure hand that receives all practices.
Faith can cause one to abandon all defiled attachments; faith understands the subtle and profound Dharma.
Faith can transform and excel, accomplishing manifold virtues; ultimately, it leads inevitably to the abode of the Tathāgata.
Pure and sharp are all wholesome roots; the power of faith is firm and indestructible.
Faith forever eradicates all evils; faith can attain the treasure of the teacherless.
Faith is unobstructed within the gates of the Dharma; by abandoning the eight difficulties, one attains freedom from hardship.
Faith can transcend the realms of all Māras, Manifesting the unsurpassed path of liberation.
The indestructible seed of all merit, It gives birth to the unsurpassed Bodhi tree;
Nurturing the gateways of supreme wisdom, Faith can manifest all Buddhas.
Therefore, I shall explain the stages of practice: faith and joy are most supreme and exceedingly difficult to find.
Like the auspicious *udumbara* flower, or like a wondrous wish-fulfilling jewel—if one has faith and reverence for all Buddhas, then one upholds the pure precepts and accords with the true teaching.
If one maintains pure precepts in accordance with the sublime teaching, they will be praised by all Buddhas and noble sages;
since the precepts are the foundation of unsurpassed bodhi, one should maintain them fully and purely.
If one can fully maintain the pure precepts, praised by all Tathāgatas,
and if one has faith in and reveres all Buddhas, then one can perform extraordinary offerings to the Most Victorious One.
If one can offer extraordinary worship to the Most Victorious One, that mind of faith in the Buddha is inconceivable;
if one has faith in the Tathāgata’s true and correct Dharma, then one will always delight in hearing it without ever becoming weary.
If one delights in hearing the Dharma without weariness, rejoices in the inconceivable Dharma,
and has faith and reverence for the pure Saṅgha, then that faith will be firm and indestructible.
If one’s faith is firm and indestructible, that person’s power of faith cannot be shaken;
if faith is firm and unshakable, the faculties will be sharp and entirely purified.
If one's faculties are sharp and clear, and entirely pure, Then one will leave behind all evil associates;
If one can distance oneself from evil associates, Then one will be able to draw near to virtuous friends.
If one can draw near to virtuous friends, then one cultivates immeasurable merits;
if one can extensively cultivate all merits, then one can skillfully understand all causes and effects.
If one can skillfully understand all causes and effects, Then one will achieve the most excellent and wondrous liberation;
If one achieves the most excellent and wondrous liberation, Then one will be protected by all Buddhas.
If one is protected by all Buddhas, then one gives rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta;
if one gives rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta, then one is able to diligently cultivate the merits of the Buddha.
If one can diligently cultivate the virtues of the Buddha, one will be able to be born into the family of all Buddhas;
if one can be born into the family of all Buddhas, one will have no attachments to any phenomena.
If one is without attachment to any phenomena, Then one attains the wondrous purity of the profound mind;
If one attains the wondrous purity of the profound mind, Then one attains the supreme and unsurpassed mind.
If one attains the unsurpassed and most excellent mind, one then cultivates all the pāramitās;
if one cultivates all the pāramitās, one is then able to fulfill the Mahāyāna.
If one can fully possess the Mahāyāna, then one makes a Dharma-offering to all Buddhas;
if one makes a Dharma-offering to all Buddhas, then the concentration of mindfulness of the Buddha shall be indestructible.
If the concentration of mindfulness of the Buddha is indestructible, then one will constantly behold the Buddhas of the ten directions;
if one constantly beholds the Buddhas of the ten directions, then one knows that the Tathāgata dwells eternally in peace.
If one knows that the Tathāgata dwells eternally at peace, then the Dharma will abide forever within that person;
if the Dharma abides forever within that person, then they shall attain inexhaustible eloquence.
If one attains inexhaustible eloquence, one can then expound immeasurable teachings;
if one can expound immeasurable teachings, one can then deliver all sentient beings.
If one can deliver all sentient beings, then one attains a firm great compassionate heart;
if one attains a firm great compassionate heart, then one will always delight in the profound Dharma.
If one can take joy in the profound Dharma, then one can abandon the faults of the conditioned;
if one can abandon the faults of the conditioned, then one leaves behind the arrogance and all forms of heedlessness.
If one is free from self-conceit and all forms of heedlessness, Then one can benefit all sentient beings;
If one can benefit all sentient beings, Then one dwells in birth and death without sorrow or grief.
If one dwells within birth-and-death without sorrow or grief, then one can be supremely diligent;
if one can be supremely diligent, then one attains all supernatural powers.
If one attains all supernatural powers, one then understands the conduct of all sentient beings;
if one understands the conduct of all sentient beings, one is then able to bring all sentient beings to fulfillment.
If one can bring all sentient beings to fulfillment, then one attains the wisdom that fulfills sentient beings;
if one attains the wisdom that fulfills sentient beings, then one is able to be fully endowed with the four means of integration.
If one can fully possess the four means of integration, then one brings immeasurable benefit to sentient beings;
if one brings immeasurable benefit to sentient beings, then one can fully possess the wisdom of skillful means.
If one can be fully endowed with skillful means and wisdom, Then one can abide securely in the unsurpassed path;
If one can abide securely in the unsurpassed path, Then all Māras shall be unable to destroy them.
If one cannot be destroyed by any māras, then one can transcend the paths of the four māras;
if one can transcend the paths of the four māras, then one reaches the firm and unshakable stage.
When one reaches the stage of firmness and immovability, one then attains the profound dharma-patience of non-arising;
having attained the profound dharma-patience of non-arising, one receives the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas.
If one receives the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas, Then one will constantly appear before all Buddhas;
If one constantly appears before all Buddhas, Then one will understand the subtle and secret teachings of all Buddhas.
If one understands the subtle and secret teachings of all Buddhas, Then one will be constantly protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas;
If one is constantly protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas, One will adorn oneself with the merits of the Buddhas.
If one adorns oneself with the virtues of a Buddha, Then one attains a body of immeasurable merit;
Having attained a body of immeasurable merit, That body shines resplendently like a mountain of gold.
If the body is radiant like a mountain of gold, endowed with the thirty-two marks;
if one possesses the thirty-two marks, adorned by the eighty secondary characteristics.
Adorned by the eighty minor marks, his body possesses immeasurable radiance;
since the radiance of his body is immeasurable, that radiant adornment is inconceivable.
If the adornment of light is inconceivable, then immeasurable precious lotus flowers emerge;
if immeasurable precious lotus flowers emerge, then upon each flower sits an immeasurable Buddha.
Universally manifesting throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, He teaches and delivers all sentient beings;
If one can deliver all sentient beings, Then one attains immeasurable power of mastery.
If one attains immeasurable power of mastery, Then one can adorn and purify all Buddha-fields,
Explaining the profound and subtle Dharma, Causing inconceivable multitudes to rejoice.
If one preaches the subtle and profound Dharma, Which brings inconceivable joy to the multitude,
Then one will be fully endowed with the power of the four analytical knowledges, And will be able to liberate all beings with sovereign ease.
If one can be fully endowed with the power of the four analytical knowledges, One will be able to liberate all beings with mastery;
That person’s wisdom will always be foremost, And their actions of body, speech, and mind will be free from error.
If that wisdom is always foremost, such that the actions of body, speech, and mind are free from error,
that person attains mastery through the power of their vows, manifesting their body according to what is appropriate for sentient beings.
If they attain mastery through the power of their vows, manifesting their bodies according to what is appropriate for beings,
when they preach the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, their voices are subtle and wondrous, beyond conception.
When preaching the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, their voice is subtle and wondrous, beyond conception;
within a single thought-moment, they fully know the minds of all classes of sentient beings.
If one can, within a single thought-moment, fully know the minds of all classes of sentient beings,
that person will forever be free from birth and death without remainder, and all afflictions and sufferings will be extinguished in quiescence.
If a person’s birth and death are forever extinguished without remainder, All afflictions and sufferings are stilled in nirvana;
Endowed with the merits and wisdom of the Dharma-body, They deeply comprehend the reality of all phenomena.
If one is endowed with the merit and wisdom of the body, And deeply understands the reality of all phenomena,
Then the ten stages and the ten kinds of sovereign powers Will all lead to the ultimate, supreme liberation.
If one attains mastery over the seeds of the ten stages, One achieves liberation in its ultimate perfection;
The adornments of the prophecy are fully complete, And one gains sovereignty over immeasurable Dharma gates.
If they are recorded as being fully endowed with all adornments, having attained mastery over immeasurable Dharma gates,
and have served all the Buddhas of the ten directions, they shall all receive their prediction of enlightenment without exception.
If for the sake of all Buddhas of the ten directions, They have all been granted predictions without exception,
And the nectar-water of the Dharma has been poured upon their crowns— Then the Buddhas of the ten directions have completed their bestowal of predictions.
If the water of ambrosia is poured upon their crowns, and the Buddhas of the ten directions have completed their bestowal of prophecy,
their Dharma-body fills the entirety of space, abiding immovably throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
If his body fills and pervades all of space, abiding unmoving throughout the realms of the ten directions,
then all devas and worldly beings— none within the peerless realm can know him.
Whatever was practiced in the past bears fruit; for those who see or hear [this], it is never in vain.
This is the unsurpassed field of supreme merit; for those who make offerings and give, there is a great reward.
Through the majestic spiritual power of that son of noble family, the True Dharma abides eternally and shall never perish;
the merits of the ten wholesome paths and all wondrous practices are the most supreme among the immeasurable treasures of the Dharma.
The ocean of his majestic spiritual power and Buddha-dharma, With the Dharma-treasure as firm and solid as a diamond,
His wisdom is fully perfected and inexhaustible— Such is the immeasurable ocean of merit.
In some lands where there is no Buddha, he manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment;
in some realms where there is no Dharma, he manifests the teaching of the treasury of the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva has severed all hopes and desires; in a single thought-moment, they traverse the ten directions.
Appearing in the ten directions like the full moon, they transform sentient beings through immeasurable skillful means.
Throughout those worlds in the ten directions, In every thought-moment he manifests the attainment of Buddhahood;
He turns the wheel of the sublime Dharma and enters nirvana, Manifesting the distribution of relics for the sake of sentient beings.
Sometimes manifesting the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, They display the universal adornment of attaining Buddhahood;
Appearing for immeasurable kalpas to deliver sentient beings, They extensively transform and guide them through the gates of the three vehicles.
Sometimes manifesting in various forms as men or women, as devas, humans, nāgas, spirits, or asuras;
assuming bodies corresponding to the diverse needs of sentient beings, they produce the infinite sounds of their various karmic deeds.
All manifestations appear without exception, By the power of the Ocean-Seal Samādhi;
In inconceivable adorned lands, They reverently make offerings to all Buddhas.
The adornment of light is inconceivable; The transformation of sentient beings is immeasurable.
Wisdom is sovereign and beyond discussion; In preaching the Dharma and transforming others, one attains mastery.
Generosity, precepts, patience, diligence, meditation, Skillful means, wisdom, and all such merits—
All these sovereign and inconceivable powers Are due to the force of the Flower Adornment Samādhi.
Entering into samādhis as numerous as atoms, from a single samādhi arise as many concentrations as there are atoms;
within a single atom appear infinite lands, yet that minute atom does not increase in size.
Within a single atom, there are lands where Buddhas currently appear; some lands currently have no Buddhas;
some lands currently appear as pure or impure; some appear as great, medium, or small;
some lands are submerged or aligned; some are like mirages, or square.
There may be lands like celestial nets, wherein the formation and destruction of worlds are all manifested.
As is shown within a single atom, so it is within all atoms;
this is called the sovereign power of samādhi, and also the immeasurable power of liberation.
If one wishes to make offerings to all Buddhas, To give birth to immeasurable gates of samādhi,
And with a single hand can cover the trichiliocosm, One may thereby make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Exquisite flowers from the lands of the ten directions, priceless jewels, and extraordinary fragrances—
all emerge spontaneously from their hands as offerings to the Most Victorious Ones beneath the Bodhi tree.
Priceless precious robes mixed with exquisite incense, Adorned with jeweled banners, pennants, and canopies;
Golden flowers and jeweled curtains, most wonderfully embellished— All these supreme offerings from the ten directions emerge spontaneously from his hands,
As he makes offerings to the Most Victorious Ones beneath the Bodhi tree.
All the various musical performances throughout the ten directions, With infinite, harmonious, and wondrous sounds,
And diverse kinds of sublime verses, Praising the true merits of all Buddhas—
These sounds pervade the realms of the ten directions, All emerging spontaneously from within their palms.

Through immeasurable and pure deeds, The light emitted from his right hand Sprinkles fragrant water throughout the lands of the ten directions, Making offerings to all Lamps that Illuminate the World.
They emit great rays of light of wondrous adornment, Producing immeasurable jewel lotuses;
Within those lotuses are immeasurable Buddhas, Self-adorned with the full array of marks and signs.
They emit pure light adorned with flowers, using exquisite blossoms to form canopies;
scattering various flowers throughout the ten directions, they make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
Emitting pure light adorned with incense, With exquisite fragrances arrayed as canopies,
Scattering various blended perfumes throughout the ten directions, They make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
They release pure light from fine powdered incense, adorning it with canopies of powdered incense;
scattering various powders throughout the ten directions, they make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
They release robes of pure, radiant light, using adorned precious garments as canopies;
scattering these various jeweled robes throughout the ten directions, they make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
They emit pure light adorned with jewels, With exquisite gems fashioned into canopies;
Scattering various wonderful jewels throughout the ten directions, They make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
They emit the pure radiance of wondrous lotus flowers, Using myriad exquisite lotuses as canopies;
Scattering these lotuses throughout the ten directions, They make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
They release the pure radiance of various necklaces, using exquisite necklaces as canopies;
scattering various necklaces throughout the ten directions, they make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
They emit pure light from banners of adornment; those banners are blue, yellow, red, and white, adorned with immeasurable varieties, and they embellish all the buddha-fields with these banners.
Holding a canopy adorned with various jewels, with streamers of many precious silks hanging down,
and with jewel bells producing the most excellent sounds— this I offer to all the Tathāgatas.
From their hands emerge inconceivable offerings; thus they make offerings to a single Teacher, and likewise to all Buddhas— such is the power of mastery in the samādhi of the Great Sages.
Desiring to bring peace to all classes of sentient beings, they give rise to the supreme samādhi of mastery;
through all the merits of their various practices and immeasurable skillful means, they deliver sentient beings across.
Some manifest the gateway of making offerings to the Tathāgatas; some manifest the gateway of all forms of giving;

some manifest the gateway of perfecting ethical discipline; some manifest the gateway of inexhaustible patience, the gateway of immeasurable ascetic diligence, and the gateway of meditative concentration, tranquility, and samādhi.
The gate of immeasurable great eloquence and wisdom; The gate of all skillful means in practice;
The gate manifesting the four immeasurables and spiritual powers; The gate of great kindness, great compassion, and the four methods of attraction;
The gate of immeasurable merit and wisdom; The gate of liberation through all dependent origination.
The Dharma-gate of the power of the pure faculties may manifest as the gate of the Śrāvaka Hīnayāna,
or manifest as the gate of the Pratyekabuddha Madhyayāna, or manifest as the gate of the unsurpassed Mahāyāna;
it may manifest as the gate of impermanence and manifold suffering, or manifest as the gate of non-self and sentient beings.
Sometimes they manifest the gateway of impurity for the sake of detachment from desire, or the gateway of the samādhi of tranquil cessation;
according to the various illnesses arising among sentient beings, they employ all the gateways of dharmas as remedies.
In accordance with the nature of those beings' afflictions, they preach the Dharma as appropriate, extensively opening the way to transformation.
All such gateways to the Dharma, they deliver according to their inherent nature;
that all devas and humans cannot fathom them is the power of this sovereign, supreme samādhi.
Born into the supreme samādhi of following joy, they discern and understand the minds of sentient beings;
they teach and transform all living creatures in accordance with their needs, causing them to leave behind sorrow and affliction and attain great gladness.
During times of calamity and famine within an eon, Providing all necessities of life and every means of comfort,
Distributing them universally according to each person's needs— This is what it means to be a great benefactor.
Delicacies of exquisite fragrance and superior flavors, Adorned with precious garments according to their desires, He gives away his own body and the treasures of his land;
Sentient beings who delight in giving are all transformed by him.
Adorning their bodies with the primary and secondary marks, With exquisite garments and various flowers,
And anointing their bodies with diverse powdered incenses, They manifest these ornaments to deliver sentient beings.
Whatever delights the entire world, Those various, supreme, pure, and wondrous forms—
He manifests them all according to what is appropriate, Causing those who delight in form to attain liberation.

With a supple and beautiful voice like that of a mourning pheasant, and with subtle sounds such as those of the *kucilinda* bird, he possesses the eight qualities of the Brahma-voice; according to what beings delight in, he preaches the Dharma for them.
The eighty-four thousand Dharma gates—by these all Buddhas deliver sentient beings;
distinguishing the immeasurable gates of all dharmas, they transform and guide them according to the natures of sentient beings.

Regarding the suffering and happiness, benefit and lack of benefit of sentient beings, and all the practices performed throughout the world, he is able to universally respond by participating in those very affairs; through this method of gathering, he delivers sentient beings.
The immeasurable and boundless great ocean of suffering, for the sake of sentient beings, he is able to endure it all;
sharing their same activities, he does not dwell on the pain, benefiting sentient beings and causing them to find peace and happiness.
If there are those who do not understand the dharma of renunciation, who delight in and cling to birth and death without seeking liberation,
for this reason the Bodhisattva abandons his kingdom and wealth, always delighting in renunciation to seek tranquility.

Bound by the five desires, they do not leave their homes; yet, wishing to bring sentient beings to liberation, he manifests a lack of delight in dwelling amidst sensual pleasures, and thus departs from home to seek deliverance.

Desiring to bring the ten kinds of practices to fulfillment— those which the Buddha-Tathāgata originally cultivated and which the Bodhisattvas practice without exception— one should cultivate these dharmas to deliver sentient beings.
There are sentient beings whose lifespan is immeasurable, Whose afflictions are subtle and who delight in the world;
For the sake of all such classes of beings, I manifest the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death.
Some possess greed, hatred, and delusion, with the fierce fires of affliction constantly blazing;
for them, he manifests the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, in order to transform and deliver all sentient beings.
The Tathāgata’s ten powers and fearlessnesses, As well as the Buddha’s eighteen unique qualities—
By means of these most supreme and immeasurable virtues, He delivers sentient beings through this wondrous Dharma.
Teaching the Dharma through instruction and the supernormal powers, Abiding in the sovereign power of spiritual penetrations—
The Bodhisattva manifests these merits To deliver and liberate all living beings.
Such skillful means are immeasurable; following along with the world to deliver sentient beings, they remain unattached to the world like a lotus flower, able to cause all beings to rejoice greatly.
A king of eloquence who has mastered extensive knowledge, whose literary verses and discourses transcend the world,
he manifests all the various arts and crafts of the world, just as a magician displays a multitude of forms.
Sometimes he becomes an elder or a leader of a village; sometimes he becomes a guide for merchants and traders;
sometimes he becomes a king or a high minister; sometimes he becomes a skilled physician to heal all ailments;
sometimes he becomes a great tree in the wilderness; and sometimes he becomes an inexhaustible treasury of fine medicines.
Sometimes he becomes a wish-fulfilling jewel that grants whatever is sought; for sentient beings who have lost their way, he shows the correct path.

When he sees the world first being established and sentient beings do not yet know the means of livelihood, at that time the Bodhisattva acts as a craftsman and manifests various types of work for them.
One should not perform evil deeds or create instruments for harming living beings;
wishing to bring longevity and peace to all sentient beings, one studies incantations, medicinal herbs, and various treatises—all of which are praised by the Buddhas.
Sometimes he manifests the extraordinary conduct of a seer, beloved by all living beings;
he displays the practice of austerities and profound dharmas, manifesting whatever is appropriate for each being.
Sometimes he becomes a renunciant of non-Buddhist paths, or again manifests the practice of fire-worship;
sometimes he appears naked and without clothing, able to act as a teacher and elder for those people.
Seeing those with various modes of wrong livelihood, who practice unrighteousness as if it were supreme,
he is able to transform and deliver all such Brahmins through their manifold ascetic penances.
Scorching his body with the five fires while turning with the sun, or observing the precepts of cattle, deer, and other animals,
wearing robes of grass and serving the fire— for the sake of transforming such as these, he acts as their guide.
Manifesting joy, he wandered through the temples of the devas; He threw himself into the Ganges seeking liberation.
Eating fruit, practicing breath-control, and drinking only water, He contemplated the True Dharma without negligence.
Sometimes they appear kneeling with one foot raised, or lying upon thorns, spikes, ash, or soil;
or they lie upon pestles and stones seeking liberation, acting as teachers and guides to transform and instruct others.
Regarding such various types of non-Buddhists, the Bodhisattva observed their intentions and manifested accordingly;
his ascetic practices were peerless, and through these means, the non-Buddhists attained liberation.
If they see that the world lacks right view and constantly dwells in all manner of false views,
they employ skillful means to preach the profound Dharma, causing all to attain understanding of the true reality.
Sometimes using the dialects of spirits or those from remote borderlands, he teaches the Four Truths to such beings;
sometimes using the refined language of the correct tongue, he teaches the Four Truths; sometimes using the languages of humans and devas, he teaches the Four Truths;
sometimes using the analytical power of dharma (*dharmapratibhāna*), he teaches the Four Truths; and sometimes using the analytical power of meaning (*arthapratibhāna*), he teaches the Four Truths.
Some preach the Four Truths through eloquent rhetoric; some preach the Four Truths with inexhaustible eloquence;
some preach the Four Truths in the voices of the eight classes of beings; and some preach the Four Truths in all possible sounds.
According to the languages and sounds they understand, he preaches the Four Noble Truths to bring them liberation;
knowing that all speech is inconceivable—this is called the power of the Samādhi of Preaching the Dharma.
The supreme samādhi that brings peace and security to sentient beings, for the sake of delivering all beings, emits inconceivable great radiance;
by means of this light, it rescues the multitudes of living beings.

The light he emits is named "Excellent Manifestation"; if any sentient beings encounter this light, they shall obtain immeasurable rewards and, by means of this, ultimately attain the unsurpassed path.
Because he manifests all the Tathāgatas, And likewise manifests the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and the Path,
As well as manifesting the forms of the most supreme stūpas, He therefore obtained the light named "Excellent Manifestation."
Again, he emits a light named "Pure," which eclipses the radiance of all devas and humans,
extinguishes all darkness and gloom, and shines universally throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions.
That light awakens all beings; holding up lamps as an offering to the Buddha, by making such lamp-offerings to all Buddhas, one becomes the most supreme lamp of the world.
Yet by means of various fragrant oils and ghee lamps, or using bamboo and wood as torches for illumination—
by being able to kindle these various lamps and lights— one attains this pure and wondrous radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Deliverance," which awakens all sentient beings;
they shall resolve to attain unsurpassed bodhicitta and deliver all living beings from the sea of desire.
If one generates the unsurpassed bodhicitta to deliver all sentient beings from the ocean of desire,
they will be able to cross all four currents and show the way to the fearless state of liberation.
He constructed immeasurable bridges and causeways, or provided boats and ships to ferry sentient beings across;
by disparaging the conditioned and praising tranquility, he thereby attained the Radiance of Deliverance.
Again, he emits a light named "Remover of Craving," which awakens all beings;
they abandon the thirsting cravings for the five desires and come to delight in contemplating the nectar-water of liberation.
If one can distance oneself from the thirst for the five desires, And contemplate with joy the nectar-water of liberation,
Then by means of the Buddha’s rain of the nectar of liberation, One shall extinguish all the cravings of sentient beings.
He bestowed gifts such as ponds, wells, and various springs, seeking the unsurpassed Bodhi of the Buddha;
he reviled the five desires and praised the various dhyānas, thereby attaining the Light that Extinguishes Craving.
Again, he emits a light named "Joy," which awakens all beings;
they come to love and delight in the Buddha’s bodhi, resolving their minds to seek the Teacherless Jewel.
Having fashioned an image of the Tathāgata’s great compassion, complete with all the marks and signs, seated upon a lotus flower,
and praising his most supreme merits, one thereby attains the light of joy.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Six;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Eight: The Two Worthy Leaders, Part Two Furthermore,
he emits a light named "Loving Joy," which awakens all sentient beings so that their minds always delight in the Tathāgatas, the unsurpassed Dharma-jewel, and the pure Saṃgha.
Constantly appearing before the Buddhas of the ten directions, They attain the supreme and profound *dharmakṣānti*.
They transform and guide immeasurable classes of sentient beings, Their minds always mindful of the Buddhas' profound and wondrous Dharma;
They awaken the *bodhicitta* in all beings, And by this cause, they achieve the Light of Affectionate Joy.
Again, he emits a light named "Accumulation of Virtue," which awakens all beings.
They universally practice various kinds of immeasurable giving, seeking the unsurpassed path through these vows.
Whatever they seek is fully satisfied, and all their assemblies of giving become utterly pure.
Because he bestows gifts according to their requests, he thereby achieves the light of the mass of virtues.
Again, he emits a light named Profound Wisdom; that light awakens all beings so that, within a single thought-moment regarding one Dharma-gate, they fully understand immeasurable Dharma-gates.
Discriminating all phenomena to transform sentient beings, And [discerning] the true meaning of the characteristics of all phenomena,
Because they are fully endowed with the teaching of the Dharma and its meaning, They thereby attain the light of profound wisdom.
Again, he emits a light named "Lamp of Wisdom," which awakens all beings to the fact that all phenomena are empty and quiescent,
without arising or ceasing; they are understood to be neither existent nor non-existent,
like a mirage, the moon reflected in water, or like an illusion, a dream, or an image in a mirror.
All phenomena are without master, entirely empty and quiescent; By means of this, the lamp of wisdom is brought to fulfillment.
Again, he emits a light named "Sovereignty of Dharma," Which awakens all sentient beings.
The treasury of dhāraṇīs is inexhaustible; It can uphold all the teachings of the Tathāgata.
Reverently making offerings to those who uphold the Dharma, Protecting and guarding all the worthy sages,
Bestowing the immeasurable Dharma upon sentient beings— By these causes, one attains the Light of Sovereignty.
Again, he emits a light named "Non-avarice"; that light awakens beings to eliminate greed and attachment.
Understanding that wealth and treasures are impermanent, they are able to relinquish them all without clinging.
It can subdue the difficult-to-restrain mind of avarice, for it understands that wealth is like a dream or a floating cloud.
Always able to joyfully delight in giving, By this cause, he attains the light named "Non-avarice. Again,
he emits a light named "Coolness," That light awakens those who have violated the precepts,
Establishing sentient beings within pure morality, Guiding them so they may attain the Teacherless Jewel.

The tracks of the ten wholesome karmas are entirely pure; Exhorting and transforming sentient beings to uphold the pure precepts, Awakening sentient beings to seek the Buddha-way, By this cause, one attains the light of cool serenity.

Again, he emits a light named "Adornment of Forbearance"; this light awakens those who harbor anger, causing them to abandon malice and overweening pride, and to always delight in the dharmas of gentleness and patience.
Toward sentient beings of evil nature who are difficult to endure, they are all able to practice forbearance as they seek the Buddha-way.
He is always able to praise the dharma of patience, And by this cause, he attains the light of adornment. Again,
he emits a light named "Supremely Victorious," That light awakens those who are indolent,
Causing them to constantly and diligently cultivate the three types of action, Respectfully making offerings to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
If one can diligently cultivate the three types of action, Respectfully making offerings to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha,
One will be able to transcend the realms of the four māras And swiftly attain the unsurpassed Bodhi of a Buddha.
Exhorting and transforming sentient beings to be diligent, Reverently making offerings to the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha,
And being able to protect and uphold the Buddha-Dharma when it is about to perish— By these causes, one attains the attainment of Transcendent Victorious Light.
Again, he emits a light named "Quiescence"; that light awakens those with distracted minds, causing them to abandon greed, hatred, and delusion.
They dwell correctly in profound samādhis, stay far away from evil associates and unwholesome conduct, and further distance themselves from the ten kinds of improper speech.
Praising the practice of meditation in secluded places, By this cause, one attains the light of tranquility.
Again, a light is emitted named "Adornment of Wisdom"; That light awakens those who are deluded and ignorant.
Skillfully knowing dependent origination, they attain liberation; Wisdom shines forth, clearly illuminating all the faculties.

If one knows dependent origination, one attains liberation; with wisdom clearly illuminating all faculties, one attains noble wisdom and various samādhis, reaching equal and perfect enlightenment to illuminate the world.
Renouncing kingdom, wealth, and his beloved body, he diligently sought the Dharma for the sake of the Buddha-way;
with single-minded devotion, he preached the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, and by this cause, he attained the light of wisdom.
Again, he emits a light named "Buddha-Wisdom," Which awakens all sentient beings,
Causing them to see inconceivable and immeasurable Buddhas, Each seated upon a precious lotus flower,
Praising the liberation of all Buddhas And speaking of the Buddhas' immeasurable sovereignty.
Extensively expounding the Buddha’s powers and spiritual penetrations, By means of this, one attains the light of the Buddha’s wisdom.
Again, he emits a light named Fearlessness; That light comforts those who are terrified.
All poison and harm inflicted by non-human beings, And immeasurable terrors, are entirely extinguished.
Universally bestowing fearlessness upon all sentient beings, With a mind always compassionate and patient, free from affliction and harm,
Rescuing those in peril and distress who have no savior— By these causes, one attains the light of fearlessness.
Again, he emits a light named "Peaceful Security"; those who are touched by that light have all their illnesses and pains extinguished.

They all attain the bliss of right concentration (*samādhi*), and he bestows excellent medicines to heal their various ailments, rubbing them with precious jewels and anointing their bodies with fragrant unguents.
Or by giving ghee, milk, or rock honey, one thereby attains the Light of Peace and Security.

Again, he emits a light named "Beholding the Buddha"; that light awakens those whose lives have ended, so that through the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* they will surely see the Buddha; after their death, they are reborn before the Buddha.
Seeing them at the point of death, he exhorted them to practice Buddha-recollection;
he further displayed sacred images for them to behold with reverence, and again urged them to take refuge in the Buddha. By these means, they were able to attain the vision of the Buddha’s light.
Again, he emits a light named "Delight in the Dharma," which awakens all beings to listen to,
expound, and transcribe the teachings; they shall always cherish and delight in the True Dharma,
being able to protect and uphold it when the Buddha-Dharma is about to perish, and causing those who seek the Dharma to have their aspirations fulfilled.
Diligently practicing the Buddha’s true Dharma, One thereby attains the light of delighting in the Dharma.
Again, he emits a light named "Wondrous Sound," Which awakens all the sons of the Buddhas;
All sounds existing throughout every world, Upon being heard, are all the voice of the Tathāgata.
With great sounds they praise all Tathāgatas, Offering music, bells, and gongs to the Buddhas;
Furthermore, they constantly extol the Buddha’s voice, And by this cause, they attain the light of wondrous sound.
Again, he emits a light named "Bestowing Ambrosia," which awakens all sentient beings, causing them to distance themselves from all heedless conduct.
They come to fully possess all virtues and discern the immeasurable ocean of great suffering: that conditioned things are precarious and fragile, and not secure.
Proclaiming and praising the bliss of nirvāṇa, By this, he attained the Light of Ambrosia.
Again, he emitted a light named "Exquisite," Which awakened all sentient beings.
From the Tathāgata they heard the supreme precepts, The sublime samādhi, and the supreme wisdom.
Constantly praising the supreme and wondrous precepts of all Buddhas, The supreme samādhi and supreme wisdom,
Cultivating them with a single mind to seek Bodhi— By this cause, one attains supreme radiance.
Again, he emits a light named Jewel Adornment; that light awakens all beings so they may obtain inexhaustible, supreme treasuries of jewels.
With these they make offerings to all World-Honored Ones, presenting jewels to the Buddhas and their shrines, while also bestowing them upon all who are poor and destitute.
By offering various rare and wondrous treasures to the Most Victorious One, one thereby achieves the light of jewel-adornment.
Again, he emits a light named "Exquisite Fragrance"; that light awakens all beings, and any sentient beings who smell this fragrance fully attain all the merits of a Buddha.
By anointing the ground with the perfumes of humans and devas, making offerings to all Tathāgatas,
and fashioning images, stūpas, and temples from incense, one thereby attains the light of sublime fragrance.
Again, he emits a light named "Various Adornments," which is embellished with banners, streamers, and canopies;
with the harmonious and elegant sounds of music and the subtle tones of song, it scatters myriad precious flowers throughout the ten directions.
Originally through the subtle tones of music and song, blended with powdered incense and various miscellaneous flowers, [it fills all realms].
By offering banners, canopies, pennants, and curtains to the Buddhas, one attains the light of majestic adornment.
Again, he emits a light named "Exquisite Adornment," which causes the lands of the ten directions to become as level as the palm of a hand;
by sweeping monasteries and the stupas of the Great Sages, one attains this light of exquisite adornment.
Again, they emit a light named Great Cloud; that light can rain down exquisite fragrant water, which sprinkles upon stupas and monasteries.
Because of this, it attains the name of the Light of the Great Cloud.
Again, he emits a light named "Adornment of Robes," which causes those who are naked to obtain fine garments;
by bestowing these adorned robes upon sentient beings, he thereby accomplishes the light of "Adornment of Robes.
Again, he emits a light named "Supreme Flavor," which causes those who are hungry to obtain delicious meals.
Because I gave various kinds of food of supreme flavor, I have attained the light named Supreme Flavor.
Furthermore, I emit a light called Manifesting Jewels, which causes all who are destitute to obtain treasuries of jewels;
by giving inexhaustible treasuries to the Triple Gem, I have attained the light named Manifesting Jewels.
Again, he emits a light named "Pure Eyes," Which enables the blind to see all forms;
Because they offered lamps to the Buddha and his shrines, They thereby attain the pure light of the eyes.
Furthermore, it emits a light named "Purification of the Ear," Which enables the deaf to hear all manner of sounds.
By making offerings of music to the Buddhas and their shrines, One thereby attains this light of the purified ear.
Again, he emits a light named "Purification of the Nose Faculty," which causes all that is heard or not yet heard to be heard;
by offering various fragrances to the Buddhas and their shrines and temples, one attains this light of purified nose faculty through these causes.
Again, he emits a light named "Purification of the Tongue Root," praising all Buddhas with gentle sounds;
having forever abandoned coarse and unwholesome speech, through this cause he attains the light of the pure tongue.
Again, he emits a light named "Purification of the Body Faculty," which restores all impaired faculties to full perfection;
by prostrating before the Buddhas and their stūpas and temples, one thereby attains the pure light of the body.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of the Mental Faculty," which causes those who have lost their minds to regain right mindfulness;
by practicing the power of samādhi and dhyāna, they thereby achieve the light of mental purity.
Again, he emits a light named Purity of Form; beholding inconceivable Buddhas, he adorns stupas with various exquisite forms, and by this cause, he attains the light of purity of form.
Again, he emits a light named "Pure Sound," which understands that sound and non-sound are entirely empty and quiescent;
it transforms sentient beings so they know sound is like an echo, and by this cause, the light of Pure Sound is attained.
Again, he emits a light named "Pure Fragrance," which transforms all foul odors into exquisite scents;
by washing the stupas and the Bodhi tree with fragrant water, he thereby attains the light of pure fragrance.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of Taste," which completely eliminates all poisons within flavors;
by making offerings to the Buddha, the Sangha, and one's parents, one thereby attains the accomplishment of this Light of Pure Taste.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of Touch," by which all that is hard, coarse, or rough becomes soft;
even the rain of swords, wheels, halberds, and various sharp blades is entirely transformed into precious flower garlands.
Soft and exquisite robes were spread upon the streets; when the Most Victorious One walked, his feet trod upon them.
By giving away fragrant flowers and superior garments, he attained the Pure Light of Touch.
Again, he emits a light named "Dharma-Purity," from each and every pore of which emerge immeasurable Buddhas;
each proclaims the wondrous Dharma, inconceivable in its depth, causing all sentient beings to attain joy.
That which arises from causes and conditions has no nature of birth; The Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata is not a body.
It is serene and eternally abiding like space; Through this, he guides and transforms others, forming the light of the Dharma.
Such gateways of light as these, immeasurable and boundless in number as the sands of the Ganges,
all emerge from the pores of the Great Sage, and the fruits of all karmic actions are fully manifested therein.
The light emitted from a single pore is immeasurable and boundless, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
all pores are likewise so—this is the power of the Great Sage’s mastery over meditative concentration.

Attaining radiance according to their original practices, those with whom they shared karmic affinities in past lives receive light as it is appropriate for them; this is called the Great Sage’s mastery of wisdom.
Those whose practiced deeds are similar, and who share in the merit of sympathetic joy,
having heard and seen the pure conduct of the Bodhisattvas— those people shall behold this radiance.
If one cultivates immeasurable merits, Respectfully makes offerings to countless Buddhas,
And the mind always delights in seeking the unsurpassed path, That person shall awaken to this radiance.
For example, though one born blind does not see the sun, it is not that the sun has not risen in the world;
all those with eyes behold it, each according to their own pursuits, performing their respective tasks.
The radiance of the Great Sage is likewise: some sentient beings see it while others do not;
those with false views and malicious intent do not behold it, but only those of supreme wisdom are able to see it.

The palanquins and vehicles atop the mani-jewel palace, Adorned with various jewels, fragrances, and perfumes, Are spontaneously provided for those possessed of merit; They cannot be obtained by those lacking virtue.
The radiance of the Great Sage is likewise: whether it is seen or not depends upon one's own karma.
Those who hear of these various radiances and apply themselves with diligence, reverence, and faith shall behold them.
Eliminating all doubts and delusions, Swiftly accomplishing the banner of unsurpassed merit,
Giving birth to subtle and sublime supreme samādhi, The great adornment of the Buddhas' retinue.
Having attained mastery over spiritual powers herein, they are able to manifest and show to sentient beings the wondrous adornments of the trichiliocosm;
transforming it into a single lotus flower that fills the world,
they sit cross-legged, completely filling it— this is called the power of the Samādhi of Mastery.
The lands as numerous as motes of dust throughout the worlds of the ten directions are transformed into great lotus flowers made of the seven treasures;
surrounded by the assembly of Buddha-sons, this is called the Sovereign and Supreme Samādhi.
Having accomplished virtuous causes and conditions in past lives, they have fully perfected their merits while seeking the Buddha-way;
those sentient beings surround the Bodhisattva, all with palms joined, gazing at him without weariness.

Such is the nature of that Great Seer’s Dharma: through the power of profound right concentration and samādhi, the Bodhisattva dwells amidst that pure assembly, shining alone with brilliance like the moon among the stars.
As it is manifested in this one direction, with the sons of the Buddhas as their retinue, so it is in all the ten directions; thus they manifest the sovereign power of samādhi.
Because there are those with whom they have a karmic connection throughout the worlds of the ten directions, they come and go, entering and emerging to deliver sentient beings.
Some see the Bodhisattva entering right concentration; some see the Bodhisattva arising from meditative absorption.
Some see him enter right concentration in the eastern direction, while others see him arise from samādhi in the western direction.
Sometimes they see him entering meditative absorption in the west, and sometimes they see him arising from samādhi in the east;

thus he enters and emerges throughout the ten directions. Sometimes they see him entering absorption in one direction, and sometimes they see him arising from samādhi in another; this is the power of the Great Sage’s mastery over concentration.
Throughout the eastern worlds without exception, The Buddha-fields and Tathāgatas are inconceivable;
A bodhisattva constantly appears before those Buddhas— This is called the power of the Samādhi of Tranquility.
Before all Buddhas of the eastern direction, he is always seen dwelling in meditative absorption;
before all Buddhas of the western direction, he is always seen making offerings to the Buddhas as a Bodhisattva.
Throughout the entirety of the western worlds, there are inconceivable Buddha-fields and Tathāgatas.
Before all those Buddhas, he constantly beholds Bodhisattvas entering meditative absorption (*samādhi*).
Seeing them enter absorption in the western direction, he likewise sees them in every Buddha-field of the eastern direction without exception.
Rising from that samādhi before those Buddhas, he reverently makes offerings to all the Buddhas.
Thus, before the Buddhas of the ten directions, they enter and emerge from samādhi without exception;
some are seen as bodhisattvas entering right concentration, while others are seen reverently making offerings to the Buddhas.
Entering meditative absorption within the faculty of the eye, he arises from samādhi within the realm of forms;
manifesting inconceivable dharmas of form, none among all devas and humans can know them.
Entering meditative absorption within the realm of forms, he arises from concentration within the eye with mindfulness undisturbed.
Contemplating that the eye is unborn and devoid of self-nature, he proclaims it as empty, quiescent, and non-existent.
Entering into meditative absorption within the faculty of the ear, he arises from samādhi amidst the phenomena of sound;
though he discerns all various voices, neither gods nor worldly beings can comprehend this.
Entering meditative absorption within the phenomena of sound, He emerges from concentration regarding the ear with undistracted mindfulness;
Contemplating that the ear is unarisen and lacks intrinsic nature, He proclaims it as empty, quiescent, extinguished, and non-existent.
Entering meditative absorption within the faculty of the nose, He emerges from samādhi within the phenomena of fragrance.
He discerns all dharmas of fragrance, which neither gods nor worldly beings can know;
entering meditative absorption within the dharmas of fragrance, he emerges from concentration with his mindfulness undisturbed.
Contemplating that the nose is unarisen and lacks intrinsic nature, he proclaims it to be empty, quiescent, extinguished, and non-existent.
Entering meditative absorption within the faculty of the tongue, he arises from samādhi amidst the phenomena of taste;
discerning all various flavors, neither gods nor worldly beings can comprehend him.
Entering meditative absorption amidst the phenomena of taste, he gives rise to concentration upon the tongue with undisturbed mindfulness.
Contemplating that the tongue is unborn and lacks intrinsic nature, he proclaims it as empty, quiescent, and non-existent;
entering right concentration within the faculty of the body, he arises from samādhi amidst the phenomena of touch.
Discerning all such phenomena of touch, neither gods nor worldly beings are able to know it.
Entering meditative absorption amidst the phenomena of contact, he emerges from concentration within the body with undistracted mindfulness;
observing that the body is unborn and lacks intrinsic nature, he proclaims it as empty, quiescent, extinguished, and non-existent.
Entering meditative absorption within the faculty of mind, Arising from samādhi amidst all phenomena,
Discerning the characteristics of all dharmas— Neither gods nor worldly beings can know it.
Entering meditative absorption amidst all phenomena, He gives rise to concentration in the mind, his mindfulness undisturbed.
Contemplating that the mind is unborn and lacks intrinsic nature, he speaks of emptiness, quiescence, and non-existence.
Manifesting in the body of a youth, he enters meditative absorption; from the body of a young man, he arises from samādhi.
Manifesting in the body of a young man, he enters meditative absorption; from the body of an old man, he arises from samādhi.
Manifesting the body of an elderly person, he enters meditative absorption; Arising from the samādhi of a virtuous woman, He manifests as a virtuous woman and enters meditative absorption;
Arising from the samādhi of a virtuous man, He manifests as a virtuous man and enters meditative absorption;
Arising from the samādhi of the body of a bhikṣuṇī, He manifests as a bhikṣuṇī and enters meditative absorption.
Entering meditative absorption with the body of a bhikṣuṇī, she arises from samādhi with the body of a bhikṣu;
manifesting the body of a bhikṣu, she enters meditative absorption and arises from samādhi with the bodies of those in training and those beyond training;
manifesting as one in training or beyond training, she enters meditative absorption and arises from samādhi with the body of a pratyekabuddha.
Manifesting the body of a pratyekabuddha, they enter meditative absorption; from the samādhi of the Tathāgata’s body, they arise.
Manifesting the body of a Tathāgata, they enter meditative absorption; from the samādhi of the bodies of devas, they arise.
Manifesting the body of a deva, they enter meditative absorption; from the samādhi of the bodies of nāgas and spirits, they arise.
Manifesting as the body of a nāga deity, he enters meditative absorption; from this samādhi of the great ghost-deities, he arises.
Manifesting as a great ghost-deity, he enters meditative absorption; from this samādhi of all ghost-deities, he arises.
From this samādhi of all ghost-deities, he arises within a single pore.
Entering meditative absorption within a single pore, One arises from samādhi in all pores;
Entering meditative absorption in all pores, One arises from samādhi at the tip of a single hair;
Entering meditative absorption at the tip of a single hair, One arises from samādhi at the tips of all hairs.
Entering meditative absorption upon every tip of a hair, one arises from samādhi within a single mote of dust;
Entering meditative absorption within a single mote of dust, one arises from samādhi within all motes of dust;
Entering meditative absorption within all motes of dust, one arises from samādhi upon the adamantine ground.
Entering meditative absorption in the Diamond Ground, he arises in the Samādhi of the Maṇi Jewel Tree;
Entering meditative absorption in the Maṇi Jewel Tree, he arises in the Samādhi of the Radiance of All Buddhas;
Entering meditative absorption in the Radiance of All Buddhas, he arises in the Samādhi of the Great Ocean Waters.
Manifesting the great ocean water, he enters meditative absorption; from that state, he arises in the samādhi of the great blazing fire.
Manifesting the great blazing fire, he enters meditative absorption; from that state, he arises in the concentration of wind, his mind undisturbed.
Manifesting the element of wind, he enters meditative absorption; from that state, he arises in the samādhi of the element of earth.
Manifesting in the great halls of the earth, they enter right concentration;
emerging from samādhi in celestial palaces, manifesting in celestial palaces, they enter right concentration; emerging from samādhi in the midst of empty space.
This is called one of immeasurable merit, whose mastery of samādhi is inconceivable;
all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions could not exhaustively describe it even in inconceivable eons.
All Buddhas together proclaim that the karmic retribution of sentient beings is inconceivable;
the supernatural transformations of the nāgas and the sovereign power of the Buddhas, as well as dhyāna and samādhi, are likewise beyond thought.
Now, I speak of the sovereign power of the śrāvakas, for which no analogy can be made.
Only those with clear wisdom and profound discernment can understand this most profound meaning.

Having attained the eight liberations and mastery over the mind, they can manifest infinite bodies from a single body, and manifest a single body from infinite bodies; they enter the fire-samādhi within the midst of empty space.
Water flows from his upper body while fire issues from his lower; Fire issues from his upper body while water flows from his lower.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining within the void, He transforms with sovereign mastery in a single thought-moment.

Though they lack great compassion and do not seek the Buddha-way for the sake of sentient beings, they are still able to manifest inconceivable feats; how much more so with the sovereign power of great benefit!
They manifest as the sun and moon traveling through space, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions.
Sometimes they become rivers, ponds, wells, or springs; Sometimes they become the great ocean or vessels of myriad jewels.
Such manifestations as these are inconceivable, Appearing universally throughout all worlds in the ten directions.
Profoundly penetrating samādhis and all liberations— Only the Buddhas can realize and know them.
Just as the images of the fourfold army appear in clear water,
each distinct and clearly manifest— swords, wheels, halberds, and various other weapons—
all such armaments appear therein according to their original forms, all appearing within that clear water.
The reflections of the fourfold army in water harbor neither hatred nor love;
this is called the Great Sage’s mastery of meditative concentration. In the ocean there is a deity named Wondrous Sound;
among the various kinds of sentient beings therein, he understands all their diverse voices and causes them all to attain great joy.
Though they possess desire, hatred, and delusion, they are still able to discern all sounds;
how much more so, then, could those with the sovereign power of dhāraṇī not bring joy to sentient beings?
There was a woman named Pratibhānā, born through her parents' prayers to the gods;
free from all unwholesome dharmas, she delighted in the truth, and was able to enable sentient beings to attain eloquence.
Even those possessed of greed, hatred, and delusion can still grant supreme eloquence to the assembly and cause them to rejoice;
how much more so, then, can the immeasurable wisdom of a Bodhisattva?
Just as a master illusionist skilled in the arts of magic can manifest all manner of infinite forms,
displaying days and nights within a mere moment, or making a single moment appear as a hundred years.
He possesses desire, hatred, and delusion, yet through the sovereign power of illusion he delights the world;
how much more so, then, with the meditative absorptions, liberations, and supernormal powers—how could they not cause sentient beings to rejoice?
When the devas and asuras fought in battle, the hosts of asuras immediately retreated and dispersed;
with hearts filled with great terror, they fled, and their fourfold armies all entered the pores of a lotus fiber.
If those who possess greed, hatred, and delusion can exercise sovereign and inconceivable power,
how much more so for one who dwells in the dharma of sovereignty and fearlessness— how could such a one not manifest miraculous transformations?
Śakra Devānām-indra has an elephant king; when he knows that Śakra intends to travel,
he manifests thirty-three heads, each with six tusks,
and upon every tusk are seven bathing pools, filled to the brim with pure, fragrant water.
Within each of the pure ponds, there are seven lotus flowers as adornments.
Upon each of these adorned lotuses dwell seven celestial jade maidens;
together they play subtle and wondrous music, providing entertainment for Śakra, Lord of Devas.

Sometimes casting off that body of a dragon-elephant, he transforms into a celestial maiden of supreme adornment, whose majestic deportment and skillful grace are peerless; this is called the sovereign power of the dragon-elephant.
If those who possess greed, hatred, and delusion can perform such miraculous transformations,
how much more so for one who is fully endowed with the wisdom of skillful means— how could they not be masterful in all meditative absorptions?
Just as when an asura manifests a transformed body, planting his feet upon the ground of diamond,
the ocean waters— though exceedingly deep— reach him only to mid-body, while his head is as vast as Mount Sumeru.
If even those possessed of greed, hatred, and delusion can manifest such great supernormal powers,
how much more so the Lamp that Illumines the World, who has subdued the enmity of Māra— could he not manifest great miraculous transformations?
When the devas and asuras wage war together, Śakra, the Sovereign, is inconceivable in his power;
according to the number of the asura hosts, he manifests bodies equal to theirs to engage in battle.
The various asuras gave rise to this thought:
"Śakra Devānām Indra is coming toward me; he will surely bind my body with the fivefold bonds.
Śakra has manifested his body with a thousand eyes, and in his hands he holds the vajra from which flames issue forth."
Donning armor and grasping a staff, he adorns himself; upon seeing him, the asuras immediately retreat and scatter.
If one with such a minor power of merit can yet crush and destroy great enemies, how much more so for the Savior of All, who possesses immeasurable merit and sovereign power?
In order to transform and guide the various devas of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, he has attained this wondrous voice as a karmic reward;
because the devas engage in heedless conduct, this sound spontaneously issues forth from the sky:
"All five desires are entirely impermanent; they are false and unreal, like foam upon the water."
Like a phantom, a mirage, or the moon reflected in water, conditioned things are like dreams and like floating clouds.
All negligence brings grief and strife; it is not the path to the Deathless, but the track of birth and death.
Those who practice various forms of negligence enter the mouth of the Makara of saṃsāra.
That which I possess is the root of all suffering, detested by all the noble sages;
the qualities of the five desires are subject to decay, so I always delight in pure and true practice.
When the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three heard this sound, they all assembled in the Hall of Good Dharma;
there Śakra preached the subtle and wondrous Dharma, which accords with the practice of detachment and tranquility.
That sound is formless and invisible, yet it can still benefit the hosts of devas;
how much more so the manifested bodies for sentient beings—how could they not bring great benefit to all the world?
When the devas and asuras fought together, the hosts of devas were filled with great terror;
yet by the power of the devas' merit, a voice resounded from the sky saying, "Do not fear!"
When the devas heard these words of consolation, they immediately cast off their fear and gave rise to great strength;
at that time, the heart of the asura trembled with dread, and the troops he had led all retreated and dispersed.
How much more so his nectar-like, wondrous voice, Which can extinguish all the terrors of sentient beings;
Endowed with great compassion, he subdues the hosts of Māra, And with his tranquil, sublime sound, he removes all afflictions.
Śakra universally responded to all the celestial maidens, ninety-two nayutas in number;
each maiden thought to herself, "The Heavenly King is sporting with me alone."
Manifesting his body, he assembles in the Hall of Good Dharma, preaching the Dharma for the devas to bring them joy;
Śakra is able, within a single thought-moment, to manifest all these great supernatural transformations.
The Buddha, though possessing desire, hatred, and delusion, is able to cause his entire retinue to rejoice;
how much more so, having cultivated spiritual powers for immeasurable eons, could he not cause all beings to be delighted?
The six celestial kings of Paranirmita-vaśavartin Attain sovereignty within the realm of desire;
With karma and afflictions as their net, They bind all ordinary beings.
If he possesses greed, hatred, and delusion, yet can subdue all the beings of the desire realm,
how much more so when he is endowed with the ten kinds of sovereign power— how could he not cause the multitudes to follow his conduct?
The Great Brahmā King of the three-thousandfold world system, wherever all the Brahmās dwell,
can manifest his body and sit therein, proclaiming the subtle and wondrous Brahmā voice.
He has attained mastery over the four Brahma-abodes in the world and the five supernormal powers through meditative concentration;
how much more so, then, could he not attain mastery over meditative concentrations and liberations that transcend all worlds?
Maheśvara, sovereign in wisdom, when the great ocean dragon king sends down rain,
is able to distinguish and count every single drop, understanding them all clearly within a single thought-moment.
Having diligently practiced and studied for immeasurable billions of eons, you have attained this supreme wisdom of Bodhi;
how could you, within a single thought-moment, fail to know the minds of all sentient beings?

The karmic retributions of sentient beings are inconceivable: By means of the great wind-circle, worlds arise, Along with vast oceans, various mountains, celestial palaces, And myriad species of things glowing with precious jewels.
It can also raise clouds and bring down heavy rains, And it can likewise disperse and extinguish all vapors and mists.
It can ripen all grains and greatly benefit the various classes of sentient beings.
Even the wind cannot learn the *pāramitās*, nor can it learn the various merits of the Buddhas, yet it still accomplishes inconceivable deeds;
how much more so for one who is fully endowed with all vows?
Men, women, and all various beings, as well as the great roar of oceanic dragons and thunder—
[the Bodhisattva] fully understands them all to be like echoes; having attained unobstructed and inexhaustible eloquence,
he preaches the sublime Dharma for all multitudes, so that all who hear it are filled with joy.
Like the ocean, wondrous and unprecedented, it reflects the images of all things;
a great-bodied being and a treasury of sublime jewels, into which all streams flow without increase or decrease.

Such is the seal of equality for all sentient beings; through inexhaustible merit, meditative concentration, and liberation, all wisdom and every virtue increase, never tiring of cultivating manifold goodness.

When the Dragon King manifests his sovereign power, from the adamantine foundation up to the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations, he raises clouds that fill the four continents; those clouds are adorned with all manner of colors.
The sixth, the Heaven of Control over Others' Emanations, has clouds the color of gold;
in the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, the clouds are crimson; in Tuṣita Heaven, they are the color of white jewels;
in the Yāma Heaven, they are the color of lapis lazuli; and in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, they are the color of agate.
On the heavens of the Four Kings, it is the color of crystal; Upon the great ocean, it is the color of diamond;
Among the kiṃnaras, it is the color of exquisite fragrance; In the abodes of the nāgas, it is the color of the lotus;
In the Guhyaka heaven, it is the color of a white goose; Among the asuras, its form is like a mountain.
In Uttarakuru, it is like a golden mirage; in the realm of Jambudvīpa, it is the color of a cloud;
in the other two continents, it is of various colors—appearing in accordance with what beings delight in.
Furthermore, in the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations, it shines like lightning amidst the clouds, as brilliant as the sun;
in the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, it is like the light of the moon; in the Tuṣita Heaven, it is the color of Jambūnada gold;
in the Yāma Heaven, it has the hue of white jewels; and in the abode of Śakra, it is like golden clouds shimmering like a mirage.
The most exquisite color in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, The color of red jewels upon the great ocean,
The color of blue lapis lazuli among the kiṃnaras, The color of precious treasures in the abodes of the nāgas,
The color of crystal in the Guhyaka heaven, And the color of agate among the asuras.
The realm of Uttarakuru has the color of fire-jewels; the realm of Jambudvīpa has the color of blue jewels;
the other two continents are adorned with various ornaments—each responding according to the inclinations of its inhabitants.
The thunderous roar of Paranirmita-vaśavartin is like the Brahma-voice;
The exquisite sounds of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, The music of the Tuṣita Heaven, And the voices of the celestial maidens in the Yāma Heaven;
Furthermore, among the various heavens of the Trāyastriṃśa, There are the exquisite sounds of the Kinnara maidens.
The sound of *gandharvas* in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, The sound of flutes and pipes among the *kiṃnaras*,
Like the sound of two mountains crashing together within all those great oceans,
The *kalaviṅka* song in the abodes of the nāgas, And the voices of nāga maidens in the Guhyaka heaven—
Among the asuras, there is the sound of celestial drums; among humans, there is the sound of the ocean tide.
Furthermore, in the Heaven of Controlling Others' Emanations, a rain of exquisite fragrant flowers serves as an adornment;
in the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, there are campaka flowers, mandārava flowers, and fragrant ointments.
The maṇi jewels of Tuṣita Heaven, Various unsurpassed ornaments and treasures, A bright,
pure crest-jewel like the light of the moon, Exquisite fine garments of refined gold,
Yāma-deva banners, parasols, and pennants as adornments, Flower garlands and ointments as supreme adornments.
Red pearl robes and golden sashes, various subtle and exquisite celestial music,
the wish-fulfilling jewels of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, solid and wondrous sandalwood incense,
and various *uragasāra* saffron and heavenly flowers— raining down a mixture of pure flowers and fragrant water.
The Four Heavenly Kings rain down food of supreme flavor, complete with every taste and generating vital strength.
Furthermore, they rain down inconceivable jewels; the Dragon Kings descend these various rains, and moreover, within that great ocean, each drop of rain is as large as a chariot axle.
Immeasurable multitudes of jewels are inexhaustible, And again, various kinds of adorned jewels rain down;
Kinnaras rain flowers and blue jewel-garments, With exquisite *mālatī* flowers and fine powdered incense;
All manner of musical performances are fully provided— Such are the immeasurable and wondrous adornments.
In the abodes of the nāgas it is red pearl; in the subtle and secret heavens, it is the fire-jewel;
among the asuras, it rains down weapons, subduing all enemies and adversaries.

In Uttarakuru, there are priceless jewel necklaces; in the two continents of Pūrvavideha and Aparagoyānī, there are vārṣika and campaka flowers, as well as pure, wondrous jewels and liberation-flowers.
In Jambudvīpa, pure water rains down—soft, lustrous, and always falling in season.
He nurtures trees of various fruits, fragrances, and flowers, maturing them in due season to benefit sentient beings;
thus, in ways immeasurable and inconceivable, he raises clouds and thunders, sending down manifold rains,
yet remains unmoved within his palace, able to manifest such sovereign and inconceivable power.
When acting as the sovereign lord within that ocean, you manifest inconceivable supernatural transformations;
how much more so when entering the ocean of Dharma to its very source and bottom—how could you not perform great spiritual miracles?
The various parables I have spoken are for the sake of Bodhisattvas of profound wisdom—
fearless Great Beings without peer, who have attained mastery over all liberations,
subtle and immeasurable sages of supreme intelligence, who are able to expound such doors of liberation.
All the various unprecedented and marvelous dharmas cannot repay one's debt of gratitude;
yet to hear this profound and supreme liberation, to believe, understand, uphold, and explain it to others—
among all the ordinary people in the world, those who have faith in this Dharma are exceedingly rare.
Contemplating immeasurable wholesome dharmas, one is able to have faith by virtue of the power of original causes.
Among all the multitudes of sentient beings in every world, few desire to seek the path of the śrāvaka;
those who seek the state of a pratyekabuddha are even fewer still; and those who seek the Mahāyāna are exceedingly rare.
To seek the Mahāyāna is still easy; to be able to believe in this Dharma is extremely difficult.
