Therefore, whatever the Bodhisattva consumes, it is entirely for the sake of all the worms within, desiring to bring them peace and happiness, and not out of greed for its flavor.
The Bodhisattva further reflects:
"Throughout the long night, I have greedily sought food and drink for the sake of this body; I shall now apply myself with diligent vigor to quickly leave this body behind."
This is the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the dharma of giving.
What is the bodhisattva’s final dharma of difficult giving?

Suppose this bodhisattva obtains various superior flavors of food and drink, incense, flowers, clothing, and articles of livelihood; if he were to enjoy these himself, he would be happy and long-lived, but if he were to give them all away to others, he would suffer poverty and meet an early death.
At that time, there was a beggar who sought everything.
The Bodhisattva thought to himself:

"Since the beginningless past, I have lost my body countless times, yet never before have I sacrificed myself to benefit even a single sentient being so as to cause them to obtain great benefit. This is a rare and auspicious occasion; I shall now relinquish my life and abandon everything to benefit sentient beings, fulfilling the ultimate great gift. This is the final dharma of the difficult-to-practice giving of a Bodhisattva."
"What is the bodhisattva’s internal gift of the Dharma?
This bodhisattva, in his youth, possesses a dignified and majestic physique and an exceptionally distinguished countenance;

having bathed until pure, he wears exquisite garments and ornaments, and receives the consecration of the rank of a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*), endowed with the seven treasures and ruling over the four continents."
At that time, a beggar came to the king's presence and addressed him, saying: "Great King!

You should know that I am now old and decrepit, afflicted by a grave illness; I am solitary and beset by suffering, with no one to provide for or rescue me. My path of life is exhausted, and I am certain to go to the land of death."

If you obtain the body of a king, whatever may be required for use—whether hands and feet, or flesh and blood, or head and eyes, or marrow and brain—if Your Majesty, out of compassion and kindness, takes pity on the poor and the aged, and relinquishes this greedy body to save me, I shall surely receive your divine bounty and my life will be preserved.
The Bodhisattva then thought to himself:
"Now this body of mine shall likewise be like that; it must inevitably return to death and offers no benefit whatsoever. It is fitting that I should sacrifice my body at this time to save his life."
Having thought thus, he gives with joy to those sentient beings; this is the bodhisattva’s internal giving (*adhyātma-dāna*).
What is the bodhisattva’s external giving (*bāhya-dāna*)?

This bodhisattva, in his youth, possesses a dignified and majestic form and an exceptionally handsome countenance. Having bathed until pure, he wears exquisite garments and ornaments. He has received the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) to the rank of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*), possessing the seven treasures and ruling over the four continents.
At that time, a beggar came to the king's presence and spoke these words: "Great King!

You should know that I am now aged and infirm, afflicted by illness, with but little life remaining. I must end my existence in this state of poverty and suffering, while you, O King, possess every form of happiness."
"Excellent, Great King!
We pray that you relinquish the celestial throne and compassionately bestow it upon us; we shall then govern the world and enjoy the king’s blessings and pleasures.
The Bodhisattva then thought to himself:

"Prosperity and nobility are impermanent; they must inevitably return to poverty and lowliness. If one remains in poverty and lowliness, there is no benefit to be had, nor can one fulfill the aspirations of sentient beings.
Therefore, it is now appropriate for me to relinquish my position at this time, so as to bring joy to their hearts."
Having thought this, he rejoiced and immediately gave it away; this is the bodhisattva’s method of external giving.
What is the bodhisattva’s method of internal and external giving?

In his youth, this bodhisattva possessed a dignified and majestic form and an exceptionally radiant complexion. Having bathed until he was pure and clad in exquisite garments and ornaments, he received the consecration of the position of a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) and, endowed with the seven treasures, ruled over the four continents.
At that time, a beggar came before the king and spoke these words: "Great King!
You should know that I am now advanced in years and my body is afflicted by illness; yet, despite my decrepit and lowly condition, I have ventured to hope for a noble title."
"Excellent, Great King!

I pray that you bestow upon me your royal person, the seven treasures, the entire world, and the rank of a Wheel-Turning Monarch, so that I may be fully endowed with them and enjoy the sovereign felicity."
The Bodhisattva then thought:
"My body and my wealth are both not solid; they are impermanent, fragile, and subject to decay."
I am now in the prime of my vigor and possess the wealth of the world; with a beggar appearing before me, these three conditions are fulfilled.
Therefore, within these unstable phenomena, I must seek that which is stable.

Having formed this thought, he was filled with redoubled joy and immediately relinquished both internal and external things to give them away; this is the bodhisattva’s method of giving internally and externally.
What is the bodhisattva’s method of universal giving?

In his youth, this bodhisattva possessed a dignified and majestic form with exceptionally handsome features. Having bathed in fragrant waters and donned exquisite garments and ornaments, he received the consecration of the position of a Wheel-Turning King (*cakravartin*), endowed with the seven treasures and ruling over the four continents.
At that time, a beggar came to the king's presence and spoke these words:
"Great King! You should know that your fame is heard throughout the ten directions. I am from that very country, having come from afar to serve under your command; I have come with a request."
"Excellent, Great King!
May you fulfill my wishes according to your desire.
At that time, the beggars might have requested the kingdom or city, wife, children, kinsmen, limbs, blood, flesh, head, eyes, marrow, or brain.
At that time, the Bodhisattva reflected thus:
"All forms of affection must inevitably end in separation; they provide no lasting benefit and cannot fulfill the various aspirations of sentient beings."
"I should now abandon the conduct of poverty born of greed and swiftly relinquish everything to benefit sentient beings.
Having formed this thought, he experienced even greater joy and gave away all his possessions as gifts to sentient beings; this is the bodhisattva’s practice of universal giving.
"What is the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the dharma of past giving?
This bodhisattva hears of the complete merits practiced by the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the past;
having heard them, they do not become attached, but realize that these things do not exist, giving rise to no delusive thoughts, and feeling neither craving nor relish."

Observing all phenomena, the mind has no point of reliance; all phenomena are like dreams and possess no solidity. Regarding all roots of goodness, they do not give rise to the notion of existence, and the mind remains unattached. Yet, solely for the sake of transforming sentient beings, they manifest their bodies and extensively proclaim the teachings of the Way, desiring to cause sentient beings to achieve the Buddha-dharma.
Furthermore, he observes that all past phenomena, when sought throughout the ten directions, are entirely unobtainable.
Having observed thus, the bodhisattva further reflects:
"All past phenomena have been completely relinquished."
This is the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the practice of giving in the past.
What is the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the practice of giving in the future?
It is when this bodhisattva hears of the roots of goodness and the complete merits practiced by the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of future ages.

Having heard this, they do not grasp at signs; their minds are without anything possessed. They do not seek rebirth in that Buddha-field, nor do they harbor thoughts of seeking; they do not give rise to vows of practice. They collect the mind so it is not scattered, neither relishing nor loathing it. They do not dedicate their roots of goodness toward that realm, nor do they cultivate roots of goodness exclusively for the sake of being born there, yet they do not abandon them either.
Rather, they use those realms to teach and transform sentient beings, desiring to cause them to be fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma and to observe reality.
This true Dharma has no location, nor is it without location; it is neither internal nor external, neither distant nor near.
Furthermore, one should reflect:
"If a phenomenon does not exist, it cannot be that it is not relinquished."
This is the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the practice of giving for the future.
What is the bodhisattva’s cultivation of the practice of giving for the present?

This bodhisattva hears of the Four Heavenly Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, the Brahmā Heaven, the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Brahmapārṣadya Heaven, the Mahābrahmā Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven, the Puṇyaprasava Heaven, the Parītta-puṇya Heaven, the Apramāṇapuṇya Heaven, the Puṇyaprasava Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; he also hears of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas who possess complete merit.

Having heard this, his mind is not deluded or distracted; he maintains right mindfulness without forgetfulness, remains diligent and undaunted, and feels no sorrow or distress; his mind is tranquil and extinguished, free from all grasping.
The Bodhisattva reflects only thus:
"All conditioned phenomena are entirely like dreams; all that is practiced is not real. Because sentient beings do not know this, they wander through the evil realms."

The Bodhisattva extensively expounds the Dharma for them, leading them to distance themselves from all evils, to accomplish the Buddha-dharmas, and to cultivate the Bodhisattva path with a mind free from delusion and confusion; this is the Bodhisattva’s cultivation of the practice of giving in the present.
"What is the bodhisattva’s ultimate dharma of giving?
It is when immeasurable sentient beings of various forms and types approach this bodhisattva-mahāsattva and say: 'We have needs;
we pray that you will provide for us completely. Once our own intentions are satisfied, may your own vows also be fulfilled.'"
Upon hearing these words, the Bodhisattva was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he bestowed upon them whatever they sought, satisfying them completely.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva then observed within himself:
from the initial entry into the womb, through the impure and minute form, the fetal stages, the development of the sense organs, and on through birth, old age, sickness, and death.
Furthermore, one contemplates this body as follows:

it possesses no reality, has no inherent characteristics, and is devoid of shame or modesty; it is cast aside by the noble sages, a foul-smelling place of impurities, like a corpse held together by its joints of bone, smeared with the mud of blood and flesh, and from its nine apertures, impurity constantly flows.
The bodhisattva perceives the immeasurable faults and afflictions of the body, such that not even a single thought of greed or attachment toward this body arises; he further reflects:
"This body is precarious and fragile; how could I, having seen its immeasurable faults and afflictions, give rise to greedy attachment?"
I should relinquish these things and bestow them upon those sentient beings to fulfill their aspirations.
Within these non-substantial phenomena, I shall seek the substantial Dharma, so that all sentient beings may have every wish fulfilled according to their desires;
I shall awaken and guide them, causing them all to attain the pure Dharmakāya, to abide in non-abiding, and to be free from the marks of body and mind.
This is the sixth inexhaustible treasury of giving of the bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the inexhaustible treasury of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva?"

This bodhisattva knows form as suffering as it truly is, knows the origin of form as it truly is, knows the cessation of form as it truly is, and knows the path to the cessation of form as it truly is; he knows feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness as suffering as they truly are, knows the origin of consciousness as it truly is, knows the cessation of consciousness as it truly is, and knows the path to the cessation of consciousness as it truly is;
he knows ignorance as suffering, knows the origin of ignorance, knows the cessation of ignorance, and knows the path to the cessation of ignorance;
he knows craving as suffering, knows the origin of craving, knows the cessation of craving, and knows the path to the cessation of craving.
He knows the śrāvaka, he knows the dharma of the śrāvaka, he knows the origination of the śrāvaka, and he knows the nirvāṇa of the śrāvaka;
he knows the pratyekabuddha, he knows the dharma of the pratyekabuddha, he knows the origination of the pratyekabuddha, and he knows the nirvāṇa of the pratyekabuddha;
he knows the bodhisattva, he knows the dharma of the bodhisattva, he knows the origination of the bodhisattva, and he knows the nirvāṇa of the bodhisattva.
How does one know this?

One knows that all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) are produced through the causes and conditions of karmic retribution; they are not-self, not solid, without reality, empty, and non-existent. One does not grasp at the mark of solidity in phenomena, nor does one grasp at the mark of existence in phenomena. Knowing that all dharmas are entirely non-existent, one extensively expounds the true Dharma for the sake of sentient beings.
How is it explained?
It is explained that all phenomena are indestructible. What is indestructible?

Form is indestructible; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are indestructible; ignorance is indestructible; and the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas are indestructible.

Why is this? All dharmas are not self-made and not made by others; they transcend the path of language, are detached from all locations, and are without birth, arising, giving, or receiving, and are devoid of mind and consciousness.

When a bodhisattva accomplishes such an inexhaustible treasury of wisdom, they are able, through slight expedient means, to attain all the skillful and sublime expedients of all dharmas; they naturally achieve clear penetration, awakening without depending on others.
This treasury of wisdom has ten kinds of inexhaustibility.
What are these ten? The inexhaustibility of extensive learning and skillful means; [and so forth].
Associating with spiritual friends is inexhaustible;
expounding even a single phrase of the Dharma is inexhaustible;
entering the profound realm of reality (dharmadhātu) is inexhaustible.
Entering the inexhaustible adornment of immeasurable wisdom;
giving birth to and nurturing the treasury of all merits with a mind free from sorrow or weariness, which is inexhaustible;
and entering all dharani-gates, which is inexhaustible.
The inexhaustible discernment and understanding of the languages and sounds of all sentient beings;
the attainment of universally causing all sentient beings to be free from all doubts and delusions, which is inexhaustible;
and the attainment of the accomplishment of all practices through the sovereign manifestations of all Buddhas to teach and transform sentient beings, which is inexhaustible.
These are the ten kinds of inexhaustible dharmas.
This is the seventh inexhaustible treasury of wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
Abiding in this inexhaustible treasury of wisdom, the bodhisattva swiftly attains unsurpassed, equal, and perfect enlightenment.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the inexhaustible treasury of mindfulness of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas?

This Bodhisattva abandons the darkness of delusion and recollects one past life, ten lives, a hundred lives, a thousand lives, ten thousand lives, even up to incalculable, inconceivable, limitless, and ineffable billions of nayutas of lives; the eon of formation, the eon of destruction, the eon of both formation and destruction, not just a single eon of formation, not just a single eon of destruction, not just a single eon of formation and destruction, but hundreds of eons, thousands of eons, hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of eons, even up to incalculable, inconceivable, limitless, and ineffable billions of nayutas of eons.”
They mindfully know the name of one Buddha, up to the names of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
they mindfully know the bestowing of the prediction of enlightenment by one Buddha, up to the bestowing of predictions by unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
they mindfully know the appearance of one Buddha in the world, up to the appearance of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas in the world.
He recollects and knows that from one Buddha he received one *sūtra*, up to receiving unspeakably unspeakable numbers of *sūtras* from unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
the same applies to *geya*, *vyākaraṇa*, *gāthā*, *nidāna*, *udāna*, *itivṛttaka*, *jātaka*, *vaipulya*, *adbhutadharma*, *avadāna*, and *upadeśa*.
He recollects and knows the teachings given by a single assembly at one time, up to the teachings given by unspeakably unspeakable numbers of assemblies at unspeakably unspeakable times.
He mindfully knows one faculty, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of faculties;
he mindfully knows one affliction, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of afflictions;
he mindfully knows one samādhi, up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of samādhis.
The bodhisattva forms such thoughts:

sublime thought, pure thought, unclouded thought, universally pure thought, thought free from dust, thought free from various kinds of dust, stainless thought, radiant thought, joyful thought, and unobstructed thought.

When this bodhisattva dwells in these thoughts, no world can disturb or confuse them; their faculties are purified, and they are no longer stained by or attached to any world. They cannot be defeated by any māras or non-Buddhists; they maintain the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas with certainty and clarity, never falling into confusion.
This is the eighth inexhaustible treasury of mindfulness of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the inexhaustible treasury of hearing and retention of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas?"
This bodhisattva, in the presence of the Buddhas, hears and retains a single sūtra, up to hearing and retaining unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sūtras, never forgetting a single word or phrase;
throughout a single lifetime they do not forget them, nor even through unspeakably unspeakable lifetimes do they ever forget a single word or phrase;
they hear and retain the name of a single Buddha, up to hearing and retaining the names of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas.
They hear and retain the names of one world, up to hearing and retaining the names of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds;
they hear and retain the names of one eon, up to hearing and retaining the names of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of eons;
they hear and retain the predictions of one Tathāgata, up to hearing and retaining the predictions of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Tathāgatas.
They hear and retain one sutra, up to hearing and retaining unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sutras;
they hear and retain the names of one assembly, up to hearing and retaining the names of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of assemblies;
they hear and retain the Dharma taught at one time, up to hearing and retaining the Dharma taught during unspeakably unspeakable numbers of times.
They hear and retain one faculty, up to hearing and retaining unspeakably unspeakable numbers of faculties;
they hear and retain one affliction, up to hearing and retaining unspeakably unspeakable numbers of afflictions;
they hear and retain one samādhi, up to hearing and retaining unspeakably unspeakable numbers of samādhis.
This is the ninth profound and inexhaustible treasury of hearing and retention of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
This treasury of hearing and retention is the domain of the Buddhas alone; none others can equal it.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the inexhaustible treasury of eloquence of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?

This Bodhisattva achieves profound wisdom and extensively expounds all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings, never contradicting the sūtras of any of the Buddhas; he may expound a single chapter of the Dharma, or even expound chapters of the Dharma beyond the countable, the uncountable, and the ineffably ineffable.”
One may speak the name of a single Buddha, or even speak the names of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;

one may speak the name of a single world, speak of a single Buddha’s prediction, speak of a single sūtra, speak of a single assembly, speak of a single time, speak of the Dharma, speak of a single faculty, speak of a single affliction, or speak of a single samādhi, up to speaking of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of samādhis.

Or, one might speak a single phrase of a single flavor of the Dharma for a single day without end, or even for unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas, such that while all kalpas might be exhausted, the speaking of a single phrase of a single flavor of the Dharma remains inexhaustible.
Why is this? Because these bodhisattvas have accomplished ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries.
By accomplishing these treasuries, they attain the mastery of all dharmas, and the gates of dhāraṇī manifest before them, with one million asaṃkhyeya dhāraṇīs as their retinue.
Once this Bodhisattva has accomplished a retinue of a million *asaṃkhyeya* dhāraṇīs, he extensively expounds the profound Dharma for sentient beings through the eloquence of the light of Dharma;

with a broad and long tongue, he emits wondrous sounds that fill all worlds throughout the ten directions, conforming to their various faculties, extinguishing their afflictions, and causing them all to rejoice.

They skillfully enter all sounds and attain uninterrupted eloquence in the entry into all syllables; they universally illuminate the Dharma-gate by teaching that the seed of the Tathāgata within all sentient beings must never be severed; thus, they do not abandon any of the bodhisattva practices, their minds free from sorrow or weariness.
Why is this? Because this bodhisattva has accomplished and filled the dharma-realm of space with the pure dharma-body.
This is the tenth inexhaustible treasury of eloquence of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.

This treasury is immeasurable, without limit, uninterrupted, indestructible, unceasing, and cannot be severed; it is non-retrogressive, profoundly deep, and bottomless, entering all Buddha-dharmas through all dharma-gates.
“O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten inexhaustible treasuries of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, which cause all sentient beings to ultimately achieve unsurpassed bodhi.”
This treasury contains ten kinds of inexhaustible, profound dharmas.
What are these ten? They are:
benefiting all sentient beings through skillful dedication;
They do not sever their original vows, because they practice throughout all eons;
their minds are immeasurable and boundless, because they observe all things with equanimity like space;
they dedicate themselves to the conditioned, because they do not cling to the unconditioned.
All dharmas are inexhaustible, because one knows their spheres in every moment of thought;
great vows are indestructible, because one has perfected the practice of the *dhāraṇī* of all powers;
and they are protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas, because one enters into all dharmas as being like illusions and transformations.
These are the ten kinds of inexhaustible dharmas that enable all worlds to attain an inexhaustible treasury.
*The Flower Ornament Scripture of the Buddha*, Fascicle Twelve;
*The Flower Ornament Scripture of the Buddha*, Fascicle Thirteen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Nineteen: The Tathāgata Ascends to the Palace of Tuṣita Heaven and All the Jewel Halls.

At that time, through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, throughout all worlds in the ten directions, across all four continents, and in every single Jambudvīpa, there was a Tathāgata sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, appearing clearly to all without exception.
Those bodhisattvas, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, expounded various teachings, each of whom considered themselves to be in the presence of the Buddha.

At that time, through his sovereign spiritual power, the Tathāgata—without departing from his seat at the Bodhi tree or from the Sublime Victory Palace atop Mount Sumeru—ascended to the Jewel-Adorned Palace in the Yāma Heaven and proceeded to the Palace of All-Jewel Adornments in the Tuṣita Heaven.

At that time, the celestial king saw the Buddha approaching from afar; he immediately prepared a lion throne of the wish-fulfilling jewel-treasury within his palace, adorning it with various kinds of celestial jewels.

It is obtained through the cultivation of roots of goodness in the past; it is sustained by the majestic spiritual power of all Tathāgatas; it is born from incalculable *nayuta-asamkhyeya* roots of goodness; it arises from the pure dharmas of all Buddhas; it is a collective adornment for all sentient beings; and it is accomplished through immeasurable merit.

Free from all evil, it is the retribution of pure karma; it is a vision of universal beauty, never tiring of it. It arises from the transcendence of all worldly phenomena, pure and undefiled; it arises from the causes and conditions of the entire world, such that all sentient beings can never exhaust their perception of it.
They were adorned with immeasurable ornaments, namely:

a hundred trillion railings; a hundred trillion jeweled nets spread over them; a hundred trillion flower canopies stretched above them; and a hundred trillion flower garlands hanging down on all four sides;
a hundred trillion incense canopies perfuming the ten directions; and a hundred trillion jewel canopies stretched above them.
A hundred trillion flower canopies were held aloft by the devas;
a hundred trillion flower-garland canopies and a hundred trillion jewel canopies covered it from above;
and a hundred trillion precious robes were spread upon it.
There were one hundred trillion exquisite jewel pavilions, covered above by nets of one hundred trillion sovereign wish-fulfilling jewels;
one hundred trillion nets of various supreme marvels, and one hundred trillion necklaces of many jewels interspersed and hanging down;
one hundred trillion varieties of exquisite miscellaneous jewels, and one hundred trillion net-canopies covering them from above.
There were a hundred trillion nets of various jewels for clothing, and a hundred trillion exquisite jewel lotuses blooming with radiant light;
a hundred trillion nets of insatiable incense universally perfumed the ten directions;
and a hundred trillion great jewel canopies and nets covered them from above.
A hundred trillion jeweled bells, slightly stirred, produced harmonious and elegant sounds;
a hundred trillion sandalwood and jewel canopies perfumed the ten directions;
and a hundred trillion exquisite flowers of various jewels were scattered upon them.
A hundred trillion robes of various colored jewels covered its summit;

a hundred trillion great canopies of bodhisattvas, a hundred trillion canopies of various precious gems, a hundred trillion canopies of pure gold, a hundred trillion canopies of pure lapis lazuli, a hundred trillion canopies of various jewel treasuries, and a hundred trillion canopies of all kinds of jewels covered its summit;
and a hundred trillion exquisite flowers of various jewels surrounded it on all sides.
There were a hundred trillion canopies of precious images, a hundred trillion garlands of various exquisite jewels, and a hundred trillion fragrant garlands that perfumed the ten directions;
a hundred trillion celestial *mandārava* flowers and sandalwood, complete with color and fragrance, that perfumed the ten directions;

a hundred trillion celestial ornaments, a hundred trillion garlands of exquisite jewel-flowers, a hundred trillion supreme and wonderful jewel-treasuries, a hundred trillion garlands of supreme jewel-treasuries, a hundred trillion pure jewel-garlands, a hundred trillion garlands of ocean-jewel-treasuries, a hundred trillion exquisite *indra-vajra* jewels, and a hundred trillion exquisite jewel-silks, used as hanging streamers.
There were a hundred trillion immeasurable sovereign wonderful jewels and a hundred trillion treasuries of true gold, pure and subtle;
a hundred trillion vaiḍūrya jewels that shed brilliant light;
and a hundred trillion indranīla jewels interspersed with various other gems for adornment.
A hundred trillion Śūradhvaja jewels radiated brilliant, pure light;
a hundred trillion fire-jewels emitted great radiance, universally illuminating the ten directions;
and a hundred trillion celestial *dṛḍha* jewels formed the windows and casements.
There were one hundred trillion jewels of pure merit with immeasurable exquisite colors;
one hundred trillion multi-colored jeweled balconies, pure and wondrous treasuries;
one hundred trillion ocean-moon jewels, one hundred trillion stainless-treasury jewels, and one hundred trillion heart-king jewels, bringing immeasurable joy.

A hundred trillion lion-faced jewels, a hundred trillion Jāmbūnada gold jewels, a hundred trillion jewels of the pure treasury of all worlds, a hundred trillion jewels of Indra’s banner of all worlds, a hundred trillion jewels of the royal treasury, a hundred trillion jewels of the supreme banner of Mount Sumeru King, a hundred trillion exquisite jewels of liberation, and a hundred trillion lapis lazuli nets hung down on all sides;

There were a hundred trillion crimson jewel garlands; a hundred trillion *rati-maṇi* jewels; a hundred trillion pure *rati* jewels; a hundred trillion treasuries of various miscellaneous jewels; a hundred trillion exquisite red jewels beautiful to behold as they grant liberation; a hundred trillion jewel garlands of immeasurable colors; a hundred trillion incomparable jewel garlands; and a hundred trillion jewels of pure radiance that universally illumine all that is sublime.
There were a hundred trillion images of *maṇi* jewels; a hundred trillion *indra-nīla* jewels; and a hundred trillion black aloeswood incense that universally perfumes the ten directions.
There were a hundred trillion inconceivable varieties of exquisite incenses that universally perfume all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
A hundred trillion exquisite fragrances from the ten directions universally perfumed the worlds;
a hundred trillion most supreme fragrances universally perfumed the ten directions;
a hundred trillion fragrant images had their scents penetrating the ten directions.
One hundred trillion fragrances, according to their inclinations, universally permeate the ten directions;
one hundred trillion fragrances of pure radiance universally permeate all sentient beings;
and one hundred trillion fragrances of various colors universally permeate the Buddha-fields.

There were clouds of non-retrogressive incense, hundreds of billions of unguents, hundreds of billions of sandalwood unguents, hundreds of billions of perfumed incenses, and hundreds of billions of lotus-treasury black agarwood clouds filling the ten directions;
clouds of smoke from hundreds of billions of pellet incenses filled the ten directions;
and hundreds of billions of incenses of wondrous radiance constantly perfumed the air without ceasing.
A hundred trillion fragrances of wondrous sounds can transform the minds of the multitude;
a hundred trillion fragrances of radiant signs universally permeate all flavors;
a hundred trillion fragrances capable of awakening distance themselves from anger, quiet the sensory faculties, and fill the ten directions.
A hundred trillion kings of incense perfumed the ten directions universally.
There rained down clouds of a hundred trillion celestial flowers, clouds of a hundred trillion celestial incenses,
clouds of a hundred trillion celestial powdered incenses, clouds of a hundred trillion celestial exquisite lotus flowers, and clouds of a hundred trillion celestial...
Cloud-rains of various precious flowers; continuous cloud-rains of hundreds of billions of celestial blue lotuses;
cloud-rains of hundreds of billions of celestial jewel flowers; cloud-rains of hundreds of billions of celestial *puṇḍarīka* flowers;
cloud-rains of hundreds of billions of celestial *māndārava* flowers; and cloud-rains of hundreds of billions of celestial flowers of all varieties.
...a rain of hundreds of billions of clouds of various celestial garments; a rain of hundreds of billions of clouds of various celestial jewels that universally illuminate the ten directions;
a rain of hundreds of billions of clouds of various celestial canopies; a rain of hundreds of billions of clouds of celestial banners of immeasurable colors;
a rain of hundreds of billions of celestial crowns; and a rain of hundreds of billions of celestial ornaments of every kind...
Rains of clouds of majestic celestial crowns; rains of clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial ornaments;
rains of clouds of hundreds of billions of multicolored celestial garlands; rains of clouds of hundreds of billions of various great celestial ornamental garlands;
rains of clouds of hundreds of billions of celestial sandalwood of various colors; and rains of clouds of celestial aloeswood incense.
There were a hundred trillion celestial jewel banners, a hundred trillion celestial variegated pennants, and a hundred trillion celestial sashes hanging down;
a hundred trillion celestial harmonious incenses universally perfumed the ten directions.
A hundred trillion celestial garlands of exquisite merit and jewels hung down;
a hundred trillion celestial *tāla* trees made of jewels were suspended and radiated light;
and a hundred trillion celestial whisks were held by attendants standing in service.
A hundred trillion nets of celestial golden bells, stirred by a gentle breeze, produced wondrous sounds;
a hundred trillion celestial jewel balustrades surrounded it on all sides; a hundred trillion celestial *tāla* jewel walls encircled it on every side;
and a hundred trillion celestial trees of various jewels provided a protective canopy around it.
Within it were a hundred trillion celestial pavilions made of various jewels, adorned with a hundred trillion celestial gates of supreme precious gems;
a hundred trillion celestial bells of pure gold emitted harmonious and elegant sounds when stirred by a gentle breeze;
and a hundred trillion pure celestial garlands were arranged and hung down.
There were one hundred trillion celestial *suvāsti* jewels with various marks of liberation;
one hundred trillion celestial vajra-treasury necklaces of exquisite beauty; and one hundred trillion celestial canopies of various jewels, all held aloft by the devas;
as well as one hundred trillion celestial nets of various jewels and one hundred trillion celestial treasuries of various jewels, whose radiance was exceptionally sublime.
A hundred trillion celestial pure lights universally illumine the ten directions;
a hundred trillion great radiances shine everywhere;
a hundred trillion sun-treasury lights universally illuminate all things.
There were a hundred trillion multicolored moonlights, a hundred trillion pure fragrances free from delusion;
a hundred trillion celestial treasuries of exquisite blossoms, blooming and lush;
and a hundred trillion treasuries of jewel nets, a hundred trillion flower nets, and a hundred trillion fragrance nets covering them above.
A hundred trillion celestial garments of various jewels were spread upon it; a hundred trillion celestial robes of various jewels were placed everywhere;

a hundred trillion celestial blue garments, a hundred trillion celestial garments of various yellows, a hundred trillion celestial garments of various reds, a hundred trillion celestial garments of various colors, a hundred trillion celestial garments of various jewels, a hundred trillion garments of various perfumes, and a hundred trillion garments of supreme jewels—garments capable of causing sentient beings to give rise to a heart of joy—such as these were spread upon it;
and a hundred trillion pure, white, and exquisite garments covered it from above.
A hundred trillion celestial banner-jewels emitted subtle and wondrous sounds;
a hundred trillion pure white jewel banners produced exquisite melodies as they were stirred by a gentle breeze;
and a hundred trillion celestial silk banners and a hundred trillion incense banners released nets of various fragrances.
There were a hundred trillion flower-bannered canopies raining down all manner of flowers;

a hundred trillion celestial banners of exquisite garments, a hundred trillion banners of mani-jewels, a hundred trillion banners of all celestial ornaments, and a hundred trillion banners of celestial garlands, arranged in rows on all four sides, along with a hundred trillion celestial parasol banners.

All the jeweled bells produced wondrous sounds; a hundred trillion celestial conchs produced wondrous sounds; a hundred trillion celestial drums produced great sounds; a hundred trillion celestial lutes produced subtle and exquisite sounds; a hundred trillion celestial *mudrā* drums produced great sounds; and a hundred trillion celestial musical instruments and a hundred trillion celestial melodies filled all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions. A hundred trillion emanated voices resounded throughout the ten directions, and all sentient beings who heard them understood them to be like echoes.

A hundred trillion celestial maidens played musical instruments all at once; a hundred trillion divine beings produced harmonious sounds through their supernatural powers; and a hundred trillion implements for the entertainment of all the devas emitted exquisite melodies.
A hundred trillion voices of exquisite melody praised the Tathāgata; a hundred trillion voices of supreme and wonderful joy praised the Tathāgata;
a hundred trillion voices of profound resonance praised the Tathāgata; a hundred trillion voices of various kinds extolled the karmic fruition of the Buddha;
and a hundred trillion subtle voices proclaimed and praised the emergence of the Three [Vehicles].
Regarding the dharmas of the realms, a hundred trillion voices of tranquil resonance praised the original practices cultivated by the Tathāgata;
a hundred trillion sounds praised the Tathāgata for being forever free from anger throughout a hundred trillion kalpas;
they praised his hundred trillion offerings made to past Buddhas; and a hundred trillion dharma-gates praised the Tathāgata.
With a hundred trillion voices, they praise the merits of all bodhisattvas, which are inexhaustible;
with a hundred trillion voices, they praise the bodhisattvas’ perfection of the merits of all the stages (*bhūmi*);
with a hundred trillion voices, they praise the Buddhas without ever becoming weary; and with a hundred trillion voices, they extol and praise the vision of the Buddhas.
He performed a hundred trillion sounds of praise for the profound Dharma; those who heard these sounds attained deep wisdom without any obstruction.
A hundred trillion sublime sounds filled all worlds throughout the ten directions.
A hundred trillion exquisite voices praise all sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice according to their aspirations;
a hundred trillion voices praise all worlds, such that those who hear these sounds understand the true nature of all phenomena;
a hundred trillion voices praise the Tathāgata, such that those who hear these sounds are able to revere all Tathāgatas.
A hundred trillion voices extolled the Buddha’s realm and all its merits;

a hundred trillion voices extolled the various *dhāraṇīs* and skillful means, the thorough knowledge and discernment of all phenomena, and the hearing and retention of the teachings of all Tathāgatas;
a hundred trillion voices praised the profound and complete fulfillment of all dharmas.
A hundred trillion voices praised the bodhisattvas who have resolved their minds on enlightenment for cultivating and nurturing all-knowledge;
a hundred trillion voices praised the bodhisattvas on the stage of "preparing the ground," their hearts filled with joy;
and a hundred trillion voices praised the bodhisattvas on the stage of "practice," their liberation being pure.
A hundred trillion voices praised the Bodhisattva Jātigarbha, and his mind attained stable abiding;
a hundred trillion voices extolled the Bodhisattva Upāyasaṃpanna, who had reached ultimate certainty in the Mahāyāna;
a hundred trillion voices praised the Bodhisattva Subhūti, who was fully endowed with all the practices of a bodhisattva.
A hundred trillion voices praised the non-retrogressive bodhisattvas, whose practice of all stages (*bhūmi*) was entirely pure;
a hundred trillion voices praised the youthful (*kumāra-bhūta*) bodhisattvas, whose radiance universally illumined all ten directions;
a hundred trillion voices praised the prince (*rāja-putra*) bodhisattvas, who skillfully enter the profound and inconceivable realm of the Buddhas.
A hundred trillion voices extolled the Bodhisattvas of Consecration, who are able to manifest the powers of all Tathāgatas.

There were a hundred trillion sovereign spiritual powers, a hundred trillion pure liberations, a hundred trillion births of pure liberation, a hundred trillion cultivations of the dharma of great joy, a hundred trillion abidings in indestructible faith, a hundred trillion cultivations of the power of valor, and a hundred trillion cultivations of the dharma of renown;
there were a hundred trillion distinctions of the meaning of dharmas, extensively expounding on meditative concentration and wisdom.
From a hundred trillion pure and undisturbed states of right mindfulness, there arise a hundred trillion concentrations and wisdoms, and a hundred trillion dhāraṇīs.
They are fully able to receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas; they give rise to a hundred trillion vast wisdoms;
they give rise to a hundred trillion profound minds, with faith in the Buddha and the faculty of faith becoming firm and solid.
They give birth to hundreds of billions of pure dāna-pāramitās;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of śīla-pāramitās;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of kṣānti-pāramitās, giving rise to no mind of anger and fully perfecting the kṣānti-pāramitās of all Buddhas.
They give birth to hundreds of billions of *vīrya-pāramitās*, ultimately fulfilling immeasurable *vīrya-pāramitās*;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of *dhyāna-pāramitās*, wherein immeasurable meditative concentrations are tranquil and illuminating;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of *prajñā-pāramitās*, which illuminate all phenomena.
They give birth to hundreds of billions of pure great vows;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of lamps of wisdom for all profound Dharma gates;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of profound and wondrous Dharma gates of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
They give birth to a hundred trillion states free from delusion, manifesting sublime and skillful means;

they give birth to a hundred trillion practices of all dharmas, universally entering a hundred trillion buddha-fields; with a hundred trillion pure dharma-bodies, they travel to all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions;
and they give birth to a hundred trillion subtle and wondrous voices of the Tathāgatas.
They give birth to hundreds of billions of excellent skillful means of all-knowledge;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of dharma-gates that are fully perfected;
they give birth to hundreds of billions of right views of the true Dharma, seeing the true reality of all Buddhas as clearly as a precious banner.
He gives birth to hundreds of billions of wisdoms and manifests the realm of the Tathāgata without any obstruction.
Hundreds of billions of celestial kings pay him respectful homage;
hundreds of billions of dragon kings gaze upon him with single-minded attention, never wearying of it.
A hundred trillion yakṣa kings stood respectfully with palms joined;
a hundred trillion gandharva kings paid homage with single-minded devotion, their eyes never for a moment departing from him;
and a hundred trillion asura kings, having severed all arrogance, stood in attendance with reverent hearts.
A hundred trillion jewel-king garuḍas held silk ribbons in their beaks;
a hundred trillion kinnara kings stood in attendance with joy;
and a hundred trillion mahoraga kings leaped for joy, gazing intently with single-minded devotion.
A hundred trillion Brahmin kings paid him respectful homage;
a hundred trillion kings of all the worlds paid him reverent prostrations;
and a hundred trillion Śakra-devānām-indras honored and revered him, gazing upon him with single-minded attention.
A hundred trillion kings of the Yāma Heaven leaped for joy and praised him with loud voices;
a hundred trillion kings of the Tuṣita Heaven paid him reverent homage;
and a hundred trillion kings of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven offered reverent praise.
A hundred trillion kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven stood in attendance with palms joined in reverence;
a hundred trillion Brahmā kings observed with single-minded attention;
and a hundred trillion Maheśvara kings offered respectful praise.
A hundred trillion bodhisattvas paid homage and offered praise;
a hundred trillion celestial maidens paid homage and made offerings;
a hundred trillion vow-devas prostrated with reverent hearts.
A hundred trillion devas who had previously associated with spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) offered praise with sublime voices;
a hundred trillion Brahmakāyika devas prostrated by extending their bodies;
and a hundred trillion Brahmapurohita devas paid homage with reverent prostrations.
He was surrounded and guarded by a retinue of a hundred trillion Brahma-devas;
a hundred trillion Great Brahma Kings praised and extolled his immeasurable merits;
and a hundred trillion Ābhāsvara-devas prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground.
One hundred trillion Parīttābhadevas proclaimed and praised how difficult it is to encounter a Buddha in the world;
one hundred trillion Apramāṇābhadevas offered praise and prostrations;
and one hundred trillion Ābhāsvaradevas praised how difficult it is to meet and behold the Tathāgata.
One hundred trillion Śuddhāvāsa devas paid homage with respectful prostrations;
one hundred trillion Avrha devas paid homage with respectful prostrations;
and one hundred trillion Atapa devas, desiring to behold the Buddha, cast themselves down from the midst of the void.
One hundred trillion Śuddhāvāsa devas stood with palms joined in reverence;
one hundred trillion Guhyakadeva devas recalled their original merits, extolling and praising them;
and one hundred trillion Aparaguhyaka devas conceived the perception of the Tathāgata, single-mindedly seeking a vision of him.
One hundred trillion *Anantaguhyarūpa* devas, through their pure and virtuous karma, paid homage with reverent prostrations;
one hundred trillion *Guhyaphala* devas spread their bodies in respectful salutation; one hundred trillion *Avṛha* devas attained firm faith and paid homage with reverence;
one hundred trillion *Atapa* devas joined their palms in contemplation, their hearts never wearying of it.
One hundred trillion Śuddhāvāsa devas paid homage with reverence;
one hundred trillion Sudarśana devas recollected the immeasurable buddhas, paying them reverent offerings with minds that never grew weary;
and one hundred trillion Akaniṣṭha devas paid homage with reverence.
A hundred trillion various devas were all greatly delighted, paying homage and offering praise;
a hundred trillion devas adorned it with various forms of sublime wisdom;
and a hundred trillion great bodhisattvas received and upheld it upon their crowns.
One hundred trillion Puṣpahasta Bodhisattvas rained down all kinds of flowers;
one hundred trillion Gandhahasta Bodhisattvas rained down all kinds of incense;
one hundred trillion Mālāhasta Bodhisattvas rained down all kinds of garlands.
The Bodhisattva Hundred Million Trillion Incense-Powder Hands rained down all kinds of incense powder;
the Bodhisattva Hundred Million Trillion Robe Hands rained down all kinds of precious robes;
the Bodhisattva Hundred Million Trillion Banner Hands rained down all kinds of banners.
The Bodhisattva Hundred Thousand Myriad Banners-Hand rained down all manner of banners;
the Bodhisattva Hundred Thousand Myriad Jewels-Hand rained down all manner of jewels;
the Bodhisattva Hundred Thousand Myriad Adornments-Hand universally rained down all kinds of ornamental implements.
A hundred trillion devas adorned it with various celestial palaces of manifold adornments;
the Devaputra Pramudita adorned it with a hundred trillion celestial palaces of manifold adornments;
and the Dharma-bodies of a hundred trillion Jyotirpala-devaputras pervaded it everywhere.

A hundred trillion crown-princes (*abhiṣikta-devaputra*) supported the seat with their entire bodies; they brought forth a hundred trillion pure great vows of bodhisattvas, brought forth a hundred trillion initial pure minds of bodhisattvas, and brought forth a hundred trillion supple and sharp faculties of bodhisattvas. A hundred trillion treasuries of dhyāna were all completely purified;
there were a hundred trillion pure liberations of bodhisattvas, and they adorned and refined a hundred trillion pure karmas of bodhisattvas.
They brought forth a hundred trillion bodhisattvas abiding in the stage of noble birth, and brought forth a hundred [bodhisattvas]...
The ten trillion Dharma-gates universally illumine all things; they bring to fruition the hundred trillion stages of the bodhisattvas, and instruct and subdue the hundred trillion great assemblies.

They arise from the hundred trillion roots of goodness, are sustained by the hundred trillion Buddhas, are accomplished through the hundred trillion merits, and consist of the hundred trillion minds of straightforwardness.
Adorned and purified, adorned and purified by hundreds of billions of great vows; arisen from hundreds of billions of virtuous deeds;
filled with hundreds of billions of dharmas; accomplished through hundreds of billions of sovereign spiritual powers;
arisen from hundreds of billions of merits; and praised with hundreds of billions of praises of the Dharma.
He marveled at this:
as in this world, where lion thrones of the maṇi-jewel treasury were spread for the Tathāgata in the palaces of the Tuṣita Heaven and in all the jewel-adorned halls throughout the four continents;

so too it was in all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, in all their four continents, in the palaces of the Tuṣita Heavens, and in all their jewel-adorned halls, where lion thrones of the maṇi-jewel treasury were likewise spread for the Tathāgata.

At that time, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, having finished arranging the high seat for the Tathāgata, together with incalculable asaṃkhyeya sons of the Tuṣita Heaven, went out to welcome the Tathāgata. They rained down asaṃkhyeya varieties of colors and exquisite flowers as offerings to the Tathāgata;

they rained down inconceivable fragrances, rained down garlands of immeasurable colors, rained down exquisite sandalwood, rained down immeasurable varieties of jeweled canopies, rained down fine celestial garments, and rained down immeasurable miscellaneous jewels as offerings to the Tathāgata;
and with hearts full of joy, they rained down all manner of exquisite celestial ornaments.
They burned various kinds of incense, the fragrance of which pervaded the worlds of the ten directions;
they rained down powdered sandalwood incense, powdered aloeswood incense, and powdered *sāra* incense as offerings to the Tathāgata.
From each of their bodies, immeasurable sons of gods produced countless and innumerable further bodies of sons of gods;
the asankhyeya sons of gods from Tuṣita and the hosts of sons of gods who had come from other directions were all filled with great joy and paid homage with reverence;
the asankhyeya hosts of celestial maidens rejoiced immeasurably, and with single-minded tranquility, they gazed intently upon the Tathāgata.

Incalculable and inexpressible numbers of great bodhisattvas, all coming from the Tuṣita heavens of other directions, remained in the air and made offerings to the Tathāgata with inconceivable articles of worship that surpassed all the offerings of the devas. They praised the Tathāgata with incalculably sublime voices due to the Buddha’s supernatural power, the roots of goodness cultivated by past buddhas, and the Tathāgata’s inconceivable and sovereign spiritual power.
All the sons of the Tuṣita Heaven and the celestial maidens paid homage with single-minded reverence; they gazed upon the Buddha in silent stillness, each thinking to themselves:

"The appearance of a Tathāgata in the world is extremely rare to encounter. He is fully endowed with merit, possesses unimpeded wisdom, and has attained equal and perfect enlightenment—now we have been granted the sight of him."
Having formed this thought, they were all filled with great joy.

Incalculable nayutas of Tushita devaputras came to the place where the Buddha was; each took various jewels upon their celestial robes, as well as various incenses, all kinds of precious garments, and various ornaments—namely, sandalwood powder, aloeswood powder, exquisite celestial jewel powder, and the fragrant flowers of the devas, including celestial mandārava flowers—and scattered them throughout the ten directions as an offering to the Tathāgata.
Countless hundreds of millions of nayutas of devaputras adorned the void with various kinds of supreme and exquisite offerings;
they burned manifold famous incenses, the fragrances forming clouds that filled the ten directions and all of space, because their minds were focused on the realm of wisdom;
they rained down clouds of celestial flowers, adorning the void, because they had given rise to a heart of joy toward the Tathāgata.
They rained down clouds of all celestial canopies, adorning the void and filling the ten directions, because they had attained a mind of reverence for the Buddha;
they rained down clouds of all celestial garlands, adorning the void and filling the ten directions, as an offering to the Buddha;

and with an incalculable number (*asaṃkhyeya*) of pure white jewel nets, they filled the entire void as an adornment, interspersing them with many golden bells that moved gently of their own accord, producing wondrous sounds that awaken those of the three vehicles and cause them to attain liberation.
Countless jeweled canopies adorned the void, covering the ten directions, because they had attained deep faith in the Tathāgata;
they universally rained down clouds of all manner of exquisite jewel garlands, never ceasing for an instant.

They adorned the void with incalculable celestial palaces, as all manner of heavenly music produced subtle and wondrous sounds that filled the ten directions, because they were moved by the utmost sincerity and joy in their reverence for the Buddha;
they adorned the void with incalculable varieties of exquisite robes, because they felt that the appearance of a Buddha in the world was difficult to encounter;
they rained down incalculable celestial jeweled crowns, adorning the void, because they conceived a heart of joyful reverence toward the Tathāgata.

They rained down incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) supreme and exquisite jewels as well as celestial jewel-garlands, adorning the void; countless billions of *nayuta* sons of gods each produced from their own bodies incalculable flowers of various colors, making offerings to the Tathāgata without end because of their joy and reverence for the Tathāgata;
they offered countless varieties of fragrances according to their preferences to the Tathāgata because of their joy and reverence for the Tathāgata;
and they offered incalculable quantities of sandalwood powder to the Tathāgata because of their incomparable joy toward the Tathāgata.
They made offerings to the Tathāgata with various jeweled canopies in order to nurture the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*;
they spread countless varieties of exquisite and sublime jeweled robes along the road as an offering to the Tathāgata, out of joy and reverence for the Tathāgata;
and they made offerings to the Tathāgata with immeasurable and innumerable jeweled banners of diverse colors, giving rise to a heart of immeasurable joy toward the Tathāgata.
They made offerings to the Tathāgata with incalculable banners of various colors made of precious jewels, because they attained joy and reverence toward the Tathāgata;

they made offerings to the Tathāgata with countless celestial musical instruments producing subtle and wondrous sounds, their minds always remaining in meditative concentration, never becoming distracted.

Inconceivable billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas, within the Tuṣita Heaven palace, having set aside all offerings belonging to the three realms, give rise from the true Dharma to a heart of great compassion free from all afflictions. This fills the ten directions without obstruction; it is endowed with skillful means and all profound dharmas that only Buddhas can fathom, while others are unable to reach them.

It is nurtured by firm and pure faith, born of inconceivable roots of goodness, and arises through the power of countless transformations. It is the seal of the dharma of non-action, born of the true Dharma-transformation of all Tathāgatas.
All jeweled canopies universally cover the Dharma-realm to make offerings to the Tathāgata, surpassing all the offerings made by the devas;

all flower curtains arising from all the pāramitās universally cover the Dharma-realm, exceeding the offerings of the devas, making offerings to the Tathāgata who is pure liberation, filling the spheres of all Buddhas;
all jeweled robes universally cover and adorn the entire Dharma-realm, surpassing the offerings of the devas, making offerings to the Tathāgata.

A network of various jewel bells arising from the patience toward the non-arising of phenomena universally covers and adorns the entire Dharma-realm; surpassing all offerings made by the devas, it makes offerings to the Tathāgata and enters unimpeded wisdom.

Adorning the Dharma-realm with all solid fragrances, surpassing all offerings made by the devas, it makes offerings to the Tathāgata and understands that all phenomena are like illusions and transformations.
Arranging and placing thrones of all exquisite jewels to adorn the Dharma-realm, surpassing all offerings made by the devas, it makes offerings to the Tathāgata.
The sphere of their minds is equal to that of the Tathāgata, and the sphere of their seats is likewise identical to that of the Tathāgata;

they establish all jeweled banners to adorn the Dharma-realm, surpassing all offerings made by the devas as they make offerings to the Tathāgata, skillfully understanding how to offer at the appropriate time;
they adorn the Dharma-realm with all jeweled palaces, surpassing all offerings made by the devas as they make offerings to the Tathāgata, understanding that all phenomena are like dreams.
Adorned with various precious flowers, surpassing all offerings made by the devas, they were offered to the Tathāgata; born of unattached roots of goodness, they filled the entire dharma-realm.

From the bodies of these immeasurable bodhisattvas there issued forth clouds of all kinds of solid fragrances, clouds of flowers of every color, clouds of garments of every color, clouds of sandalwood incense, clouds of all manner of precious canopies for adornment, clouds of various types of perfumes, clouds of flower garlands, and clouds of pure ornaments—all surpassing the offerings of the devas—as they made offerings to the Tathāgata.

Immeasurable bodhisattvas praise the true merits of the Tathāgata; forever free from inversion, they dwell securely in the True Dharma and possess all powers. They are able to cause sentient beings to leave behind all evils and calamities, revealing the path of goodness. Within a single sound, they expound immeasurable teachings; from all dhāraṇīs, they give rise to a treasury of eloquence that is inexhaustible. Endowed with fearlessness, their minds are always joyful.

With such immeasurable and wondrous dharmas as these, the Bodhisattva praised the Tathāgata, whose Dharma-body fills the void of the Dharma-realm and whose mind is equal to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.

At that time, the entire assembly of devas, the multitude of sons of gods from other directions, and all the bodhisattvas from incalculable buddha-fields beheld the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the inconceivable hero among men;
his body was immeasurable and beyond reckoning, manifesting inconceivable supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*) that caused all sentient beings to rejoice greatly, pervading and filling all of space;
and he adorned the entire dharma-realm with the merits of the Buddhas, causing all sentient beings to dwell securely in all roots of goodness.
Having accomplished spiritual powers that transcend all paths of speech;
being reverently honored and made offerings to by all bodhisattvas; manifesting bodies to save and deliver beings according to their needs for transformation;
being fully endowed with all pure roots of goodness; manifesting the unsurpassed merits of the Tathāgata; and possessing a realm of wisdom that is inexhaustible.

Born from the peerless samādhi, the Dharma-body reaches universally to all sentient beings without limit or boundary, causing all sentient beings to rejoice greatly and ensuring that the seeds of omniscience are never severed.

Abiding where the Buddhas abide, one is born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; all inexhaustible sentient beings are brought to purity, and one is able to give birth to the pure wisdom of all bodhisattvas, activating all the faculties of bodhisattvas, and with clouds of all dharmas, universally covering the Dharma-realm.
Through the Tathāgata’s teaching, there is ultimate completion without remainder, fulfilling all according to their vows.
Establishing pure, equal, and correct wisdom, he transcends all sentient beings and attains omniscience;
with the eye of perfect enlightenment, he surveys the world universally and is able to manifest himself in accordance with the roots of goodness cultivated by them in previous lives.
Universally giving rise to the great resolve, they are beloved by all sentient beings; their wisdom is securely established such that none can destroy it.

Skillfully knowing sentient beings and discerning all lands, they give birth to the indestructible nature of phenomena within the non-retrogressive wholesome dharmas. Discerning the dharma-realm, they manifest the bodies of Tathāgatas—immeasurable and innumerable—remaining far removed from delusion and falsehood, and dwelling securely in reality. All sentient beings praise them without end. They teach and transform all beings, causing them to cultivate the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*, filling the entire dharma-realm and delivering sentient beings.

Boundless and limitless, they fulfill all that was originally requested, being able to transform and deliver them all according to what is appropriate. Bestowing the Dharma through various skillful means, they subdue sentient beings and cause them all to become pure according to their inclinations and natures. They manifest form-bodies that are inconceivable.
Observing all sentient beings with a mind free from attachment, they abide in unimpeded dwelling, seeing all things without obstruction;
they skillfully understand all the powers of the Tathāgata, their minds are always tranquil and concentrated, never becoming distracted;

abiding in omniscience, they are well able to expound the true meaning of the collection of phrases and the collection of syllables, fully penetrating the immeasurable ocean of wisdom and giving rise to an immeasurable treasury of merit and insight.
When the Tathāgata, the rising sun, universally illumines the Dharma-realm, the power of the vows of sentient beings remains eternally present without setting;

abiding where the Buddhas abide, firm and indestructible, they have no attachment to the mind of "self" or "mine. All dharmas they practice are forever detached from the world, remaining unstained by any worldly realm. Within the great assemblies, they erect the banner of wisdom; their wisdom transcends all worlds, free from all defilement and attachment.

With a heart of great compassion, they rescue and deliver beings from all suffering, establishing them in profound and wondrous wisdom. Their merit in benefiting sentient beings is inexhaustible; they skillfully discern the wisdom of bodhisattvas, lead others to have faith in the Buddha-way, and bring them to the realization of supreme perfect enlightenment.

Emerging from great kindness and manifesting great compassion, their Buddha-bodies are adorned with immeasurable dharmas; through various sounds, they expound immeasurable teachings, fulfilling the aspirations of beings according to what is appropriate for each.
With a mind that is eternally pure regarding the past, future, and present, they cause all living beings to remain unattached to sensory realms;

they are able to bestow predictions of enlightenment upon all bodhisattvas, causing them to be born into the family of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; their wisdom is universally unimpeded throughout the ten directions, reaching everywhere yet remaining without attachment;

they thoroughly comprehend the reality of all Buddha-worlds and are skillfully able to distinguish the supramundane merits of all sentient beings; they serve as universal lamps for all worlds, such that the defilements and afflictions of birth and death can never stain them.

The moon of the Buddha’s wisdom shines universally upon the Dharma-realm; having thoroughly realized that all phenomena lack any true inherent nature, his immeasurable and profound wisdom observes all things with equanimity. His mind of wisdom is luminous and pure, shining throughout the ten directions.

Understanding that all phenomena are like dreams and transformations, he manifests reality according to what is appropriate for the minds of all worldly beings, the minds of all Buddhas, and their various karmic retributions.
In accordance with the faculties of sentient beings, he manifests the body of a Buddha; the realm of the Tathāgata is capable of fully containing all living beings.

Universally knowing all phenomena practiced by sentient beings, they understand that their characteristics lack intrinsic nature; they know that all worlds are of a single nature—non-nature—yet they manifest the existence of nature in accordance with sentient beings.

Desiring to cause sentient beings to transcend the triple world and to proceed resolutely and correctly toward unsurpassed bodhi, they rescue and protect all beings, never falsely grasping at worldly signs. They extinguish all afflictions, correctly contemplate the world, and ensure that the driving of the Great Vehicle’s reins is never disordered.

They have accomplished all the excellent benefits of all dharmas; they are fully able to discern the roots of goodness in sentient beings, their karmic retributions are pure, and their wisdom is clear and lucid. They enter equally into the three periods of time and are forever detached from all worldly falsehoods.

They emit networks of light that universally illumine the ten directions, causing all beings everywhere to see the Tathāgata; they discern all Buddha-lands in the ten directions, which are complete with the primary and secondary marks, and they behold them with joy never wearying.

These are the merits and wisdom arising from the practices of Bodhisattvas; they are skillfully able to discern the faculties and realms of beings, and they carry out the Buddha-work at its proper time without fail.

They have accomplished the immeasurable skillful means of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; their compassion universally covers all sentient beings, raining down dhāraṇīs everywhere so that all may accomplish the merits of the Buddhas. Their Buddha-bodies are adorned with immeasurable wondrous colors, which no sentient being in the ten directions fails to behold.
They eliminate all obstacles of the world, discern all phenomena, understand the true meaning, and achieve the sovereign state of a Dharma King of merit.

King Sun of Merit universally illumines all worlds; he is the supreme field of merit, born from the conditions of all-encompassing wisdom. His transformation bodies fill all worlds, and each transformation body radiates immeasurable light of wisdom. This Dharma King wears a celestial silk crown upon his head; his merit is immeasurable, and he is able to skillfully discern and accord with all worlds. As the unsurpassed guide who transforms and enlightens all beings, he possesses the wisdom of the Tathāgata—the vehicle of fearlessness for all worlds.

The unsurpassed King of Physicians for all the world, he thoroughly understands the lightness or gravity of the illnesses of sentient beings; forever free from the darkness of delusion, firm and non-retrogressive, he possesses the treasury of the pure eye of wisdom.

He is skillfully able to discern all worlds and reveals to sentient beings all their karmic retributions; he can completely eliminate the sickness and suffering of all beings, delivering them through immeasurable skillful means, always acting at the appropriate time according to what is required.

Observing all sentient beings equally, he remains far removed from all evils and manifests the retribution of karma as being like a magical illusion. According to what is appropriate for each, he manifests the body of a Buddha, causing all sentient beings everywhere to see the Teacher. He discerns all phenomena of the world, inspiring joy and reverence for the Buddha, nurturing their roots of goodness, and enabling them to attain non-retrogression. He thoroughly understands and distinguishes all the karmic actions of those beings.

All sentient beings sleep long within birth and death; the Tathāgata, appearing in the world, is able to awaken them, bringing comfort to the world so that they may be free from fear. With minds unattached and indestructible by any force, he dwells securely in wisdom and is fully endowed with skillful means; thus the Tathāgata most excellently adorns and purifies sentient beings.

The King of Wisdom Mountains opens the gate of the pure Dharma, manifesting either as a Buddha or as a Bodhisattva to guide sentient beings, leading them away from all evils and establishing them in the ground of goodness. Adorned with immeasurable merit, his Buddha-body is formed by karmic actions; he manifests all worldly wisdom and reaches the other shore. When he attains Buddhahood, he causes all things to be completely purified.

He can fulfill every wish of the world and reveals himself as a steadfast and virtuous friend to the world. His radiance is pure and illuminates the ten directions; he universally manifests his body for the sake of sentient beings, extinguishing the stains of greed in immeasurable beings and causing the roots of goodness in all beings to be purified. According to their respective wishes, they all attain fulfillment.

Observing sentient beings equally—whether superior, middling, or inferior—they gather roots of goodness, give rise to pure karma, subdue all demons, eliminate afflictions, and bring forth immeasurable, unimpeded power.

The King of Pure Radiance of All Worlds, the Sun of Unobstructed Wisdom, illuminates and dispels the darkness of ignorance. He constantly bestows the gift of Dharma upon all sentient beings; his immeasurable and boundless treasury of Tathāgata-wisdom is luminously pure and shines universally throughout the ten directions. He causes all sentient beings to remain far removed from enmity and fulfills their aspirations in their entirety. As the most supreme field of merit, there is none who does not take refuge in him. His retribution is immeasurable and perfectly pure; by cultivating even a small root of goodness, one obtains great merit. He establishes sentient beings on the ground of inexhaustible wisdom. All roots of goodness arise from the mind; through these immeasurable, joyful, and pure merits, he is able to eliminate the various hardships of the evil realms for sentient beings.

Thus one correctly recollects the Tathāgata; thus one contemplates the Perfectly Awakened One; thus one enters the abyss of wisdom; thus one enters the ocean of merit; thus one reaches the wisdom of space; thus one knows the field of blessings for sentient beings; thus one correctly knows the Tathāgata; thus one contemplates the marks and signs of pure karma; thus one correctly knows the Dharma-body universally illuminating the ten directions; thus one knows the Buddha’s manifestation of all inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers.

At that time, the devas beheld the body of the Tathāgata, from each and every pore of which issued incalculable billions of nayutas of light rays. Within each light ray were incalculable wondrous colors, incalculable pure illuminations, incalculable Buddha-fields, incalculable sentient beings, incalculable nurturings of joy, incalculable purities of the courageous diligence of Buddhas, incalculable samādhis of quiescence, incalculable coolness and softness of the sense faculties, and incalculable acts of reverence toward the Tathāgata.

At that time, the devas again beheld the Buddha’s body emitting inconceivable wheels of multicolored light; each wheel of light possessed inconceivable colors and inconceivable illumination, universally shining throughout the infinite and boundless Dharma-realms of the ten directions, manifesting the Tathāgata’s immeasurable and innumerable sovereign spiritual powers.

All sentient beings hear this pure and wondrous sound, and from it there naturally issue inconceivable verses that proclaim and expound the supramundane Dharma. These bring about the full accomplishment of world-transcending roots of goodness and manifest an incalculable number of billions of nayutas of inconceivable, supreme, and sublime adornments, as well as an inconceivable eon’s worth of praises upon its radiance, which can never be exhausted.

Born from the inexhaustible sovereignty of the Tathāgata, they universally illuminate and manifest inconceivable lands; as the Buddhas appear in the world, they establish sentient beings in the gateway of wisdom and lead them into the meaning of reality. They manifest the inconceivable transformation bodies of the Tathāgatas, universally illuminating immeasurable and innumerable, inconceivable Buddha-worlds, all the dharma-realms of the ten directions, the ultimate dharma-realm, and the realm of empty space;
they arise for the sake of sustaining all worlds and universally cause sentient beings to attain pure equality, being born from the dwelling place of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded omniscience.

Furthermore, from within the Buddha’s body emerge immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable rays of light from wondrous jewels. Because he cultivated merit at the abodes of immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable Tathāgatas in the past, he has attained these lights;
they arise from pure great vows and roots of goodness, and are born of the cultivation of pure and heedful practices under immeasurable Buddhas, seeking exclusively for unsurpassed Bodhi.

Having attained this light, they give rise to immeasurable and unimpeded roots of goodness, causing all sentient beings everywhere to eliminate their doubts and delusions in the presence of the Tathāgata and to behold the Tathāgata;

furthermore, witnessing his sovereign spiritual powers, they establish immeasurable sentient beings in the gates of supreme roots of goodness, ferrying across the ocean of sentient beings, and expounding for all bodhisattvas throughout all buddha-fields the inconceivable Dharma of all Buddhas.

At that time, the Tathāgata, with great compassion universally covering all, manifested the adornment of all wisdom, desiring to cause all sentient beings in the infinite, boundless, and inconceivable Buddha-worlds who had not yet developed faith to believe, and those who already believed to increase their roots of goodness;
for those whose roots had increased, he caused them to become pure;
and for those who were already pure, he caused them to reach maturity.
Those who have already reached maturity, he causes to attain liberation;
they obtain the profound Dharma, become endowed with immeasurable light of wisdom, fulfill their vows, and their mind of omniscience becomes firm and unshakable.
They do not deviate from the indestructible nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and upon hearing of the true limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), they are not startled.
Fearless, they fully comprehend and master the true Dharma of the Tathāgata; they fulfill all the pāramitās; they achieve pure supramundane roots of goodness;
they fully cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra; they accomplish the immeasurable sovereignty of the Tathāgata;
they distance themselves from the realm of Māra and enter the Buddha-realm; and they understand the most profound Dharma.
Having attained inconceivable wisdom, their great vehicle vows become firm and irreversible;

they constantly behold all Buddhas and attain immeasurable wisdom and the power of an immeasurable, boundless treasury of merit. They give rise to the supreme, wondrous mind and leave behind the ground of the net of doubt;
extinguishing evil and becoming pure, they always rely upon the Tathāgata, remaining firm and unshakable in the true Dharma.
They attain entry into the assembly of all Bodhisattvas and constantly abide within the family of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.

The Tathāgata manifests such immeasurable and innumerable categories of pure roots of goodness to subdue sentient beings, desiring that they all come to know the merits of the Buddha and illuminate the treasury of all unimpeded wisdom.

The Tathāgata possesses inconceivable and great supernormal powers, manifesting sovereignly throughout all realms of existence.
