With such immeasurable offerings, throughout inconceivable kalpas,
they reverently made offerings to the Teacher, their hearts always joyful and never weary.
With single-minded focus, I observe all the Most Victorious Ones, the great luminous lamps of all worlds;
I behold every Buddha currently present throughout the ten directions as if they were before my very eyes.
For inconceivable and immeasurable kalpas, they practiced generosity without weariness;
for inconceivable and immeasurable kalpas, they cultivated all roots of goodness without satiety.
Skillfully discerning and knowing all thoughts and perceptions, Observing them as they truly are, without delusion,
Fully knowing all faculties without exception, He is always able to benefit all sentient beings.
With hearts filled with immeasurable great joy, their faith pure and full of reverence,
they remain in the world through inconceivable eons, benefiting and delivering all sentient beings.
After all Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa, one makes offerings to their śarīras without ever feeling weary,
using infinite varieties of wondrous jewels to erect as many stūpas and temples as there are sands in the Ganges.
He fashioned countless forms of the Honored One, adorned with pure gold from a treasure-trove;
towering and immense like the king of mountains, their number was immeasurable and inconceivable.
Cultivating and accumulating all merits, Supreme, wondrous, firm, and indestructible,
The Bodhisattva skillfully knows how to dedicate their practice, Discerning that it is neither existent nor non-existent.
If one can practice dedication in this way, The merit will be immeasurable and inexhaustible;
With supreme and wondrous wisdom observing all phenomena, One is able to fully comprehend that they are all unarisen.
Cultivating skillful means to purify the mind, one becomes equal to all Tathāgatas;
through inexhaustible skillful means, one dedicates [merit] to the inexhaustible Tathāgatagarbha.
Having resolved upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment, Without dependence on anything in all the worlds,
Reaching everywhere throughout the realms of the ten directions, Their minds are unimpeded toward all sentient beings.
Through skillful means, they guide the minds of sentient beings, causing them all to give birth to the Bodhi of the Buddhas;
observing the minds of sentient beings with equanimity, they seek the ultimate reality but find it unobtainable.
All phenomena, without exception, are understood to be devoid of intrinsic nature;
dedicating this toward the unattached, pure eye, one is forever freed from all worldly suffering.
Wishing to bring all states of existence to complete purity, The mind does not falsely grasp at the characteristics of phenomena;
By discerning both existence and non-existence, It is able to purify the mind and bring forth great joy.
Without attachment to a single buddha-field, they realize that all buddha-lands lack solidity;
they do not grasp at any conditioned phenomena, nor are they stained by the intrinsic nature of dharmas.
Skillfully dedicating toward omniscience, Adorning oneself with unsurpassed wisdom,
Causing all Buddhas everywhere to rejoice— This is the bodhisattva’s work of dedication.
The Bodhisattva single-mindedly contemplates all Buddhas, their unsurpassed wisdom and skillful means;
just as all Tathāgatas are free from attachment, may I fully attain these merits.
Constantly desiring to rescue and protect all beings, They remain far removed from immeasurable evil karmas;
Always practicing a mind that benefits sentient beings, Their altruistic mind is free from falsehood.
According to the dharmas protected by each respective stage, They manifest nirvāṇa while in truth never ceasing;
The dharma of all Tathāgatas is non-dual— May my dedication also be thus.
Within all realms of existence across all worlds, the bodhisattva has no attachment to conditioned phenomena;
they do not rely on the path of verbal expression, nor are they stained by or attached to the absence of verbal expression.
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions Comprehend all phenomena without exception;
They take birth while remaining detached from all realms of existence, And in that detachment from birth, there is no falsehood.
Adorning all with a single adornment, yet not discriminating among these phenomena;
realizing that the world is entirely illusory, they find nothing substantial in any of their actions.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Ten-Four;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Fifteen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Part Two of the Twenty-first Chapter, "The Ten Dedications," of the *Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva*:
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the third dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, which is equal to that of all Buddhas?"
This bodhisattva mahāsattva follows and trains in the dedication of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
When this bodhisattva practices the conduct of a bodhisattva, upon seeing beautiful or ugly forms, his mind remains pure, free from hatred or attachment;
he is joyful and delighted, giving rise to an indestructible mind, and is free from all sorrow and affliction.
Having attained an upright mind, their body and mind become supple, and their faculties are cooled.
When this bodhisattva experiences such bliss, they dedicate it to all Buddhas and form this thought:

"Although all Buddhas possess unsurpassed, pure, and wondrous happiness, I further pray that all Buddhas may be endowed with the inconceivable bliss in which Buddhas dwell; may they fully embrace the immeasurable bliss of the Buddha-samādhis; may they achieve the bliss of immeasurable great compassion; may they fully achieve the incalculable bliss of Buddha-liberation; and may they fully embrace the bliss of the Buddhas' sovereign supernormal powers—the unsurpassed, honored, and most wondrous bliss."

The Tathāgata universally covers all, constantly causing them to be fully endowed with the immeasurable power and bliss of all Buddhas; he is forever free from all conditioned pleasures of awakening, possessing the unsurpassed, quiescent, and immutable bliss;
he is fully endowed with the unimpeded Dharma-gates, his mind is always tranquil and concentrated without distraction, and he possesses the indestructible bliss of the Buddha’s non-dual conduct.

"Having thus dedicated these roots of goodness to all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further dedicates them to all Bodhisattvas, so that those whose vows are not yet fulfilled may have them all fulfilled;
those whose upright mind is not yet purified may have their upright mind purified;
and those who have not yet perfected the various pāramitās may have them all brought to fulfillment, thereby abiding in the adamantine mind of bodhi."

They attain non-retrogression regarding all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), do not abandon their great adornments, and protect the gates of enlightenment (*bodhimukha*) as well as all roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*).
They are able to cause all sentient beings to abandon negligence and resolve upon the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*).

Their vows are fulfilled; they dwell securely in all the abodes of bodhisattvas, obtain the sharp and keen faculties of all bodhisattvas, cultivate roots of goodness, and realize omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
"In this way, after the bodhisattva-mahāsattva has dedicated their various roots of goodness toward the bodhisattva path, they further dedicate them toward all sentient beings:
dedicating that all sentient beings may see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and approach the Sangha with a heart of reverence;
dedicating that they may be fully endowed with single-minded mindfulness of the Buddha; and dedicating that they may be fully endowed with pure mindfulness."
The sublime Dharma: dedicating toward mindfulness of the Sangha with reverence and respect;
dedicating toward never being separated from seeing the Buddhas; dedicating toward the accomplishment of all pure minds; dedicating toward the discernment of the teachings of all Tathāgatas;
dedicating toward the accomplishment of immeasurable merit; dedicating toward the purification of the roots of goodness of all supernormal powers; dedicating toward their removal...
Having extinguished all doubts and delusions, just as the Buddha dedicates his merit to transform and enlighten all sentient beings—
śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas— so too does the bodhisattva dedicate their roots of goodness to all sentient beings;
it is exactly like this.
May all sentient beings forever leave behind the hells, the hungry ghosts, the animals, and the realm of King Yama, as well as all evil destinies and immeasurable multitudes of hardships.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva causes all those sentient beings to universally resolve upon unsurpassed bodhicitta, to nurture that unsurpassed bodhicitta, to single-mindedly and exclusively seek all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), to abandon the slandering of the true Dharma of the Buddhas, and to always delight in being fully endowed with the ground of omniscience;
he causes all sentient beings to attain ultimate purity and to realize all-knowledge.

The roots of goodness practiced by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—whether they be practices gathered through various great vows, accumulations gathered, or nurtures nurtured—are all entirely vast, complete, and full.

When a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva is living as a householder together with his wife and children, he never for a moment departs from the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*). With right mindfulness, he contemplates the realm of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), seeking to deliver himself and others. With a straightforward and impartial mind, he manifests the appearance of a wife, children, and retinue through skillful means (*upāya*).
The Bodhisattva has fully accomplished all skillful means and wisdom, attaining ultimate liberation; though he dwells together with others, his mind is free from attachment.

Because of his original great compassion, he remains among his family and kin, and because of his great kindness, he accords with his wife and children, remaining unobstructed on the pure path of the Bodhisattva.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is living as a householder, they should dedicate their roots of goodness with such a mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), as follows:

whether putting on clothes, drinking or eating, taking medicinal decoctions, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; whether in the actions of body, speech, or mind, they remain fully pure, with all faculties subdued and entirely composed. Whether bathing or anointing the body, walking calmly and quietly, turning around or looking about, lifting or lowering the feet, whether sleeping or waking, they do not lose their dignified deportment; they skillfully restrain the faculties and never become distracted.
By means of all such practices, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva never departs from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*);
he dedicates his roots of goodness for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings;
he fully accomplishes immeasurable vows; he gathers immeasurable and vast roots of goodness; and he cultivates these roots of goodness to provide protection and refuge.
To eliminate all negligence and arrogance; to maintain single-minded right mindfulness of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*);
to desire to awaken to the bodhi of all Buddhas; to abandon afflictions (*kleśa*) and the factors conducive to affliction;
to cultivate all that is studied by Bodhisattvas; to be without obstruction on the path to omniscience; and to delight therein.
Cultivating the stages of wisdom and all roots of goodness, always delighting in kind speech, increasing these roots of goodness,
causing all sentient beings to forever leave behind suffering and affliction, remaining unattached to their own conduct, and single-mindedly upholding the Buddha’s teachings—
this is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwelling among householders while gathering roots of goodness.
They single-mindedly dedicate [their merit] toward unsurpassed bodhi.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"Even down to small dogs and other animals, I shall cause them all to fully practice the conduct of heedfulness, so that they may leave the realm of animals, attain beneficial happiness, achieve ultimate liberation, and forever cross over the immeasurable and boundless ocean of all sufferings—namely, the suffering of birth, the suffering of sensation, the suffering of the aggregates, the suffering of perception, the great suffering of increase, the suffering of activity, the suffering of the treasury, the suffering of the root, and the suffering of the abode."

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, desiring to cause all sentient beings to completely eliminate [afflictions], dedicates their pure roots of goodness toward unexcelled bodhi; he teaches all sentient beings to dedicate [their merit] toward such a realm, taking the correct mindfulness and contemplation of those various roots of goodness as the foremost.
That is to say:

dedicating toward all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), generating the bodhicitta, encompassing the bodhicitta, distancing oneself from birth and death, cultivating roots of goodness, emerging from the abyss of saṃsāra, and attaining the unimpeded bliss of all Tathāgatas.
They cultivate the Tathāgata’s loving-kindness, filling the ten directions, and through great compassion, they benefit all sentient beings;

they cause all to universally attain pure happiness, protect all supreme roots of goodness, lead all sentient beings to the ultimate realization of the Buddha-dharma, and cause them to remain far removed from all realms of Māra. They enter the profound realm of the Tathāgatas, are able to universally uproot all worldly existence, become fully endowed with all roots of goodness of the Tathāgatas, and abide within the equal Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
In this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness—those being accumulated now, those already accumulated, and those yet to be accumulated.
Furthermore, he reflects:

"Just as those bodhisattvas of the past practiced, reverently making offerings to all Buddhas, liberating sentient beings, protecting all, cultivating various roots of goodness, and dedicating them toward enlightenment without attachment; [so shall I do]."

Not relying on form, not clinging to sensation, not having perverted perception, not forming volitional formations, and not grasping at consciousness; being free from the six sense bases, not dwelling in worldly dharmas, and delighting in supramundane dharmas; knowing that dharmas are like space, ultimately reaching the further shore of non-destination; illuminating the understanding that all dharmas are neither born nor extinguished, have no real characteristics, and are without attachment; that all dharmas are without falsehood, have no place of resort, and are indestructible; abiding securely in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), because they lack intrinsic nature and are free from all natures.

In a single thought-moment, they realize that the nature of all phenomena is the absence of intrinsic nature; they constantly and joyfully practice the roots of goodness of the universal gate, fully possessing the perfect merits of the Tathāgata, and manifesting them all.
"Just as all the Tathāgatas of the past dedicated their roots of goodness, so too do I.
Delighting in such a Dharma, realizing such a Dharma, and thus generating the mind of enlightenment, one cultivates all phenomena without violating the characteristics of dharmas.

All arising phenomena are like illusions, flashes of lightning, the moon reflected in water, or images in a mirror; through the conjunction of causes and conditions, these dharmas are provisionally maintained. One discerns that they all arise from karmic causes, and that only the stage of the Tathāgata is the ultimate destination.
In this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva follows and learns the dedication practiced by the Buddhas of the past; it is likewise for those of the future and the present.
Having learned the dedication to all roots of goodness practiced by the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:
"Just as those Buddhas know the dedication of a bodhisattva, I too dedicate in this same manner:”

The first dedication, the superior dedication, the most excellent dedication, the highest dedication, the unsurpassed dedication, the unequaled dedication, the dedication equal to the unequaled, the incomparable dedication, the peerless dedication, the venerable dedication, the sublime dedication, the impartial dedication, the upright dedication, the dedication of great merit, the dedication of great vows, the luminous and pure dedication, the virtuous dedication, the pure dedication, the dedication free from evil, and the dedication that does not follow evil.

Thus, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva has correctly dedicated all roots of goodness, they accomplish pure actions of body, speech, and mind; all their deeds are entirely pure. Abiding in the bodhisattva-dwelling and remaining free from all evil dwellings, they cultivate roots of goodness, abandon the evil karma of body and speech, and with a mind free from discrimination, they cultivate *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge).

Abiding in immeasurable dwellings, they enter into all phenomena, which are empty and without self-mastery. They cultivate supramundane dharmas and remain without defiled attachment to worldly dharmas. Discerning and fully understanding immeasurable karmas, they achieve skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), dedicating all dharmas while their minds rest upon nothing.
“O Son of the Buddha! This is the third dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, which is equal to that of all Buddhas.

Once a Bodhisattva is established in this dedication, they enter deeply into the activities of all Tathāgatas and proceed toward the supreme and wondrous merits of all Tathāgatas. They enter the realm of profound and pure wisdom, never departing from the activities of all Bodhisattvas. They are skillfully able to discern the skillful means of artistry and enter the skillful means of the profound Dharma-realm. They successively accomplish the roots of goodness of a Bodhisattva and enter the nature of all Tathāgatas. By means of skillful means, they discern and understand all infinite and boundless phenomena.”
Although they manifest birth within worlds, their minds have no attachment to any world.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas that is equal to that of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas Cultivate the methods of dedication of the Buddhas of the past,
And likewise study the practices of the immeasurable Guides Of the future and the present worlds.”
All manner of subtle and wondrous joys, praised by all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas,
who have achieved the clear and pure, supreme Dharma-eye— may these be dedicated to all the Teachers.
The various pleasures of the bodhisattva’s body-faculty, and the various supreme, wondrous, and immeasurable pleasures of the eye,
ear, nose, tongue, and all other sense-faculties— these he dedicates to all the Most Victorious Ones.
All roots of goodness in all worlds, And those accomplished by all Tathāgatas—
I gather them all therein without exception, Rejoicing and dedicating them for the benefit of sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva’s rejoicing is immeasurable, and he also dedicates it to all beings;
may all sentient beings fully possess whatever happiness belongs to the Lions among Men.
That which all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, know and see— the pure bliss of all sentient beings—
desiring that all beings may fully attain it, the bliss experienced by the Lamps of the World.
The various kinds of bliss attained by the Bodhisattva, he dedicates to all Buddhas for the sake of sentient beings;
desiring that sentient beings always abide in peace and security, he remains unattached even toward that dedication.
When the Bodhisattva cultivates this dedication, He gives rise to immeasurable great compassion;
May I fully possess and accomplish all The merits of dedication as known by the Buddha.
Just as the Most Victorious Ones know and see, The subtle and wondrous bliss of the vehicle of omniscience,
And just as I have practiced throughout my time in the world, So too is the immeasurable bliss of all bodhisattvas.
All the manifold joys within every realm of existence, The bliss of taming the faculties with gentleness—
I dedicate them all for the sake of sentient beings, To cause them universally to achieve supreme wisdom.
With body, speech, and mind pure, free from all evils, With skillful means and an impartial heart,
I dedicate this to all classes of sentient beings, To cause them all to achieve unsurpassed wisdom.
The various deeds cultivated by Bodhisattvas, Accumulating immeasurable pure merits,
Following the Tathāgata to be born into the Buddha-family, Are serenely and undisturbedly dedicated with right dedication.
Throughout the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions, I gather in all classes of sentient beings;
I dedicate all their immeasurable roots of goodness, Universally causing all beings to attain peace and happiness.
Not seeking happiness for oneself alone, but desiring that all beings be entirely at peace;
having distanced oneself from all deluded minds, one fully understands that all phenomena are empty and without self.
To all the most victorious ones throughout the ten directions, And to all true sons of the Buddha whom they behold,
I dedicate these various merits to them, So that they may swiftly reach the ultimate, unsurpassed path.
All classes of sentient beings in every world, I shall embrace with an impartial mind, leaving none behind;
By means of all pure deeds I have performed, May those sentient beings swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Immeasurable and boundless pure vows, Expounded by the Peerless and Most Victorious One,
Are all entirely pure and free from all defilements, Causing the sons of the Buddha everywhere to reach ultimate fulfillment.
Dedicating all merits in their entirety, May all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions Be adorned with every kind of pure and wondrous excellence; Thus do Bodhisattvas train in dedication.
The mind does not weigh dualistic phenomena; having realized and awakened to the non-duality of all dharmas, one knows that all dharmas are neither dual nor non-dual.
One who does not engage in false conceptualization is a child of the Buddha.
All conceptualizations existing in all worlds, he has ultimately transcended them all without exception;
yet he neither destroys conceptualization nor non-conceptualization, for he definitively knows the conceptualizations of sentient beings.
Once those bodhisattvas have purified their bodies, their minds will likewise be pure and free from defilement;
once their verbal karma is purified and free from distraction, you should know that their minds are pure and without attachment.
With single-minded right mindfulness, one contemplates the Buddhas of the past; One discerns all the Teachers of the future;
And the Honored Ones among devas and humans in the ten directions of the present— The Bodhisattva studies the teachings of them all.
The infinite and most victorious ones of the three periods of time, Whose minds of wisdom are clear, penetrating, and unobstructed,
Practice immeasurable deeds seeking enlightenment, And dedicate them for the benefit of all worlds.
That supreme and wondrous wisdom, vast wisdom, the wisdom of the Four Noble Truths, the wisdom free from inversion,
the wisdom of equal reality, and pure wisdom— all such incomparable wisdoms are dedicated for the sake of others.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the fourth dedication of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, known as ‘Dedicating so as to Reach All Places’?
When these Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas cultivate all roots of goodness, they dedicate those roots of goodness in this manner:”
May the power of these roots of goodness and merit reach all places—just as the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) reaches everywhere without exception;

reaching all worlds, all states of existence, all sentient beings, all lands, all phenomena, all space, all three periods of time, all conditioned and unconditioned dharmas, and all languages and sounds. May these roots of goodness of mine likewise pervade the abodes of all Tathāgatas, making offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may the vows of the Buddhas of the past be entirely fulfilled.
The Buddhas of the future shall be endowed with the adornments of a Buddha;
within worlds as vast as space and the dharma-realm, they shall all make offerings to the present Buddhas and their immeasurable assemblies, who likewise constitute their adornment.
Just as the devas, in a single thought-moment, are able to completely fill all infinite and boundless worlds with vast merit and unimpeded wisdom, because they have dedicated their roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further reflects:
"By means of these roots of goodness, throughout all worlds equal to space and the Dharma-realm—worlds arising from the various karmas of the nature of worlds;

unspeakable worlds and unspeakable Buddha-fields in the ten directions; the realms of all Buddhas; boundless worlds; worlds turned upside down, overturned, prostrate, or rotated—all such worlds without exception—in which the present Buddhas manifest immeasurable and sovereign spiritual powers."

Therein are bodhisattvas who understand all dharmas, such as space and the dharma-realm; for the sake of all sentient beings, they manifest throughout all worlds as Tathāgatas appearing in the world, demonstrating the wisdom that reaches all places, the infinite and boundless dharma-body of sovereign birth, which pervades the indestructible dharma-realm, enters it universally with equanimity, and is identical to the treasury of the Buddha’s body—neither arising nor ceasing.
Universally responding to all skillful means, they appear in the world;
arising from the true nature of reality, they are firm and unchanging, sustained by non-obstruction, and born from the unimpeded merits of all Buddhas.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, in the presence of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, plant various roots of goodness by making offerings with diverse flowers, manifold incenses, garlands, canopies, banners, pennants, precious jewels, and lamps—using such excellent articles of worship as these—to venerate the honored images and the various stūpas and temples.”
One dedicates all these roots of goodness with a single-minded, undistracted, immovable, reverent, anger-free, non-abiding, unattached, selfless, guileless, harm-free, and tranquil mind.
Again, he forms this thought:

"Throughout all kalpas equal to space and the dharma-realm, the Buddhas of the past, future, and present are adorned by themselves with the perfection of the primary and secondary marks, and they adorn themselves with the adornment of the wondrous dharma-realm."
The retinue of that Buddha fills all worlds, equal to the expanse of space and the Dharma-realm; appearing in the world at the appropriate times, they never miss their appointed hour.

I dedicate my roots of goodness to make offerings to all Buddhas, using immeasurable incense canopies, immeasurable incense banners, immeasurable incense pennants, immeasurable incense palaces, immeasurable incense nets, immeasurable incense images, immeasurable incense lights, immeasurable incense flames, immeasurable incense clouds, immeasurable incense seats, immeasurable incense wheels, immeasurable incense abodes, immeasurable incense Buddha-worlds, immeasurable incense Sumeru Kings, immeasurable incense oceans, immeasurable incense rivers, immeasurable incense trees, immeasurable incense garments, and immeasurable incense lotuses. With such infinite and innumerable varieties of incense as adornments, I thus perform these offerings.
With immeasurable flower canopies—as extensively described above—up to being adorned with immeasurable and innumerable multitudes of flowers, they made offerings;
with innumerable garland canopies, up to being adorned with innumerable multitudes of garlands, they made offerings;
and with inconceivable ointment canopies, up to being adorned with inconceivable ointments, they made offerings.
They made offerings with incense-powder canopies beyond measure, up to incense-powder adornments beyond measure;
they made offerings with exquisite robe-canopies without limit, up to exquisite robe-adornments without limit;
and they made offerings with jewel-canopies without bound, up to adornments of myriad jewels without bound.
They made offerings with canopies of immeasurable lamps, up to canopies adorned with immeasurable multitudes of lamps;
they made offerings with canopies of unspeakable numbers of ornaments, up to unspeakable multitudes of ornaments.

With unspeakably unspeakable numbers of mani-jewel canopies, as well as mani-jewel banners, mani-jewel pennants, mani-jewel curtains, mani-jewel nets, mani-jewel garlands, mani-jewel lights, mani-jewel flames, mani-jewel clouds, mani-jewel thrones, mani-jewel wheels, mani-jewel palaces, mani-jewel worlds, mani-jewel Sumeru Kings, mani-jewel oceans, mani-jewel rivers, mani-jewel trees, mani-jewel garments, and mani-jewel lotuses—using such unspeakably unspeakable mani-jewel adornments, they made offerings.

Within each and every realm, there are incalculable railings, incalculable ornaments, incalculable palaces, incalculable towers, incalculable side-towers, incalculable crescent-shaped ornaments, incalculable inner curtains, incalculable windows, incalculable pure jewels, and incalculable jewels of all kinds, adorning and purifying all worlds without exception.

Adorned in this way, they cause all sentient beings to transcend birth and death, to achieve the stage of the ten powers of the Tathāgata, and to attain unimpeded illumination of the Dharma within all phenomena;

they dedicate all roots of goodness for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings, subduing the immeasurable minds of sentient beings so that they fill all Buddha-lands equal to space and the Dharma-realm, wherein phenomena have no destination;

they give rise to immeasurable roots of goodness throughout the three periods of time, causing all sentient beings to behold immeasurable Buddhas, to dwell securely within all roots of goodness, to achieve the Great Vehicle which is unattached to all phenomena, to be fully endowed with all roots of goodness, to perfect infinite practices, and to universally enter the dedication of roots of goodness within all infinite and boundless Dharma-realms.
Entering into the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas, may all sentient beings, by virtue of these roots of goodness, attain *sarvajñā* and realize the Unsurpassed Way.
Just as the non-self is not separate from all phenomena, so too are my roots of goodness:
because they encompass all Buddhas through respectful offering and service;
and because they encompass all dharmas by being free from obstacles.
They embrace all bodhisattvas because they ultimately share the same roots of goodness;
they embrace all bodhisattva practices because they fulfill all vows;
they embrace all bodhisattva illuminations of the Dharma because they are definitively unimpeded.
They embrace all the sovereign spiritual powers of the Buddhas, because they have accomplished immeasurable roots of goodness;
they embrace all the powers and fearlessnesses of the Buddhas, because they give rise to immeasurable resolve to fulfill all things;
they embrace all the samādhis, eloquence, and dhāraṇī-doors of the Bodhisattvas, because they understand the non-dual nature of worldly phenomena.
They encompass all the skillful means of the Buddhas, because they manifest the great supernormal powers of the Tathāgatas;

they encompass all Buddhas of the three periods of time, because they bring forth their attainment of the Way, their turning of the pure wheel of Dharma, their manifestation of nirvana, and their arousal of offerings to transform sentient beings;
they encompass all worlds, because of the adornment of the unsurpassed Buddha-fields.
They encompass all kalpas in order to never interrupt any bodhisattva practice;
they encompass all realms of existence in order to manifest birth therein;
and they encompass all sentient beings in order to fulfill the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
They embrace all sentient beings in order to purify the habitual tendencies of afflictions;
they embrace the faculties of all sentient beings in order to transform and deliver immeasurable numbers of them;
they embrace the various desires of all sentient beings in order to purify their afflictions.
They embrace all sentient beings, taming and bringing them to maturity by manifesting their own bodies according to what is appropriate for each;
they embrace all sentient beings, causing them to understand that sentient beings are like magical transformations;
and they embrace the nature of all Tathāgatas, guarding and upholding all Buddha-dharmas.

“Thus, when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate these roots of goodness, they realize that nothing exists at all; within karma, they do not grasp at false retribution, and within retribution, they do not grasp at false karma.
Free from all falsehoods, they enter the profound Dharma-realm, and their minds always abide peacefully in supreme and wondrous roots of goodness;
they remain far removed from distracted thoughts and cultivate wholesome dharmas.”

Lacking faith, one does not enter into any phenomena; one does not perceive any phenomenon as being established by way of its own nature (*svabhāva*), for neither an agent nor a destroyer can be found.
One knows that all phenomena are entirely devoid of sovereignty, and understands the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) such that there is no seer and no knower.

In this way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva becomes fully perfected and endowed with the complete understanding of all phenomena. He attains the ground of the manifold causes and conditions of all phenomena and perceives the body of all phenomena. Having transcended desire and reached the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), he contemplates all phenomena with equanimity. He understands that the world is like a magical transformation;
he clearly realizes that all sentient beings are a single dharma, distinguished yet non-dual.

Without abandoning the skillful means regarding the spheres of various karmic activities, they emerge from the conditioned realm into the unconditioned realm, yet do not destroy the nature of the conditioned;
they emerge from the unconditioned realm into the conditioned realm, yet do not destroy the nature of the unconditioned.

In this way, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva contemplates the mark of quiescence in all phenomena, giving rise to all pure roots of goodness and dedicating them entirely to the rescue and protection of sentient beings;
they diligently practice the dharma that transcends delusion, deeply penetrating and clearly understanding the ocean of all dharmas;
and by dedicating all roots of goodness equal to space, they become fully endowed with supreme and steadfast merit.
Having attained liberation from the darkness of delusion and gained the clear, pure Dharma-eye, they skillfully know the expedient means for dedicating merit.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this way, they cause all sentient beings to purify all lands, attain the sovereign mastery of Buddhas, and teach and transform sentient beings; they uphold the teachings of all Buddhas and become the supreme field of merit for all worlds;
they act as guides for all sentient beings to gather the jewels [of the Dharma].

For the sake of all worlds, they emerge as bright and pure suns; with each and every root of goodness, they fill the Dharma-realm, dedicating these roots of goodness to rescue and protect sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to fully accomplish pure merit and virtue.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this way, they protect and uphold the nature of all Tathāgatas; they teach, transform, and bring to maturity the nature of all sentient beings; they adorn and purify the nature of all Buddha-fields; they do not destroy the nature of karma; they discern the nature of phenomena; they contemplate the non-dual nature with equanimity; they travel everywhere throughout the ten directions; they extensively expound the nature of detachment from desire; they are fully endowed with the nature of liberation; and they universally illumine the nature of all faculties.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s fourth dedication, ‘Reaching All Places.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells securely in this dedication, they are able to dedicate all roots of goodness as follows:”

They attain bodily action that reaches all places, because they are skillfully able to manifest appropriately in all worlds; they attain verbal action that reaches all places, because their sublime voices fill all worlds throughout the ten directions;
they attain mental action that reaches all places, because they are fully able to receive and uphold all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas;
they attain supernormal power that reaches all places, because they are skillfully able to accord with the conduct of all worldly realms.
They attain the dharma that reaches all places, because they accord with all dharmas;
they attain the *dhāraṇī* and eloquence of the dharma that accords with all places, because they cause all sentient beings to be completely joyful;
they attain the entry into the dharma-realm that conforms to all places, because they are able to universally enter all worlds within a single hair-pore.
One attains a body that reaches all places, because one causes the bodies of all sentient beings to enter into the body of a single sentient being;
one attains kalpas that reach all places, because within all kalpas one constantly beholds all Buddhas;
one attains moments that reach all places, because within a single moment one manifests the appearance of all Buddhas arising in the world.
"O Son of the Buddha!
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains the dedication of roots of goodness that reaches all places, and is thus able to dedicate all roots of goodness.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"In all worlds, both internal and external, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is without attachment;
yet he does not abandon the work of benefiting sentient beings—such is the wondrous wisdom of the supreme among men."
Not clinging to any worlds, not grasping at the solid nature of the ten directions,
not grasping at the signs of sentient beings or their life-span, nor falsely grasping at any mundane realms.
Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they gather in sentient beings without exception;
observing existence and non-existence with mastery, they skillfully dedicate [merit] to reach every place.
Grasping both conditioned and unconditioned dharmas, the mind does not falsely grasp at any world;
seeing that all worldly phenomena are without distinction, the Lamp Illuminating the World awakens thus.
All karmic actions performed throughout one's conduct, Whether superior, middling, or inferior,
each distinct— The wise dedicate all such deeds To all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
The Bodhisattva dedicates merit to reach the other shore, Fully accomplishing all that is learned from the Tathāgata;
Discerning the most profound and subtle wisdom, They are endowed with the most supreme and extraordinary Dharma.
Dedicating all pure roots of goodness, may they always be able to benefit all living beings,
causing every single being throughout the ten directions to achieve the unsurpassed lamp that illuminates the world.
Never falsely grasping at sentient beings, nor falsely conceptualizing any phenomena;
unstained by and unattached to all worlds, yet never abandoning any sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva always delights in the dharma of quiescence, Following it until they reach the realm of quiescence;
Yet they do not abandon the path of sentient beings, Attaining such subtle and wondrous wisdom as this.
One does not give rise to false conceptualizations regarding various karmas, nor does one cling to any retributive fruits;
all worlds arise from conditions, and one perceives all phenomena as inseparable from causes and conditions.
Thus, following these realms as they arise, one remains far removed from all false conceptualizations;
as a teacher who tames all sentient beings, one is fully endowed with clear understanding and skillful dedication.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the fifth inexhaustible treasury of merit dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva cultivates roots of goodness through repentance and becomes free from all karmic obstructions.”
I rejoice in all the roots of goodness of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as in all the roots of goodness of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time.
I rejoice in the roots of goodness arising from honoring, revering, prostrating to, and making offerings to the Tathāgatas;
and in the roots of goodness arising from entreating the Buddhas [to teach].
The roots of goodness from hearing, retaining, and recollecting the Dharma taught by the Buddha and practicing it as instructed, thereby entering the inconceivable realm;
the inexhaustible roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
and the roots of goodness cultivated by all Bodhisattvas.
When the Buddhas of the three periods of time attain enlightenment, they possess unsurpassed roots of goodness;
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas rejoice in all these roots of goodness.
Having rejoiced, they abide in those roots of goodness.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time turn the pure wheel of Dharma to deliver immeasurable sentient beings;
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas rejoice in all the roots of goodness obtained by those sentient beings.

I rejoice in all the roots of goodness obtained by the Buddhas of the three periods of time—from their initial generation of the mind, through their cultivation of the bodhisattva practices, up until their attainment of Buddhahood and their manifestation of parinirvāṇa—during the entire interval between these events.
After those Tathāgatas have entered parinirvāṇa, [he] upholds and protects the true Dharma of all Buddhas until its extinction; the roots of goodness cultivated therein;
the roots of goodness cultivated by contemplating the realm of the Buddhas;
and the roots of goodness cultivated within his own realm.
Up to the roots of goodness within the realm of unsurpassed bodhi;
the bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates all these roots of goodness.
The bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:

"These roots of goodness—whether cultivated, studied, accumulated, understood, rejoiced in, perfected, accomplished, practiced, attained, correctly recollected, upheld, or made firm and indestructible—such roots of goodness have existed throughout all past eons; they are the adornments of all Buddhas' worlds, arisen from immeasurable deeds and practices, known by the wisdom of Buddhas, recognized by Bodhisattvas, arising in response to sentient beings, purified according to their inclinations, sustained by Tathāgatas, accomplished through the pure karma of the appearance of Tathāgatas in the world, and originated from the pure karma of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

In those worlds, if there are sentient beings who attain the unsurpassed path and manifest sovereign power, they shall purify Buddha-fields with various jewel adornments—just as all future Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas purify their Buddha-fields through wisdom—within all worlds equal to the Dharma-realm and the infinite, boundless void of space, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, for all those Buddhas.

The adornment of all unsurpassed fragrances that never weary; the adornment of rains of all flowers; the adornment of clouds of all garments; the adornment of the treasury of all merits; the adornment of the sustaining wisdom of all Tathāgatas; the adornment of all Buddha-fields; the unspeakable adornments; the adornment of the cultivation of inconceivable merits; and the adornment of the pure majestic power of the Tathāgatas’ equal and perfect enlightenment.
These are the adornments of the Buddha-fields of all future Buddhas, which cannot be seen by any in the world, but are perceived by the pure eyes of Bodhisattvas.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate supreme roots of goodness, fully entering all pure dharmas and upholding all pure dharmas as if they were transformations.

They universally practice the various pure deeds of bodhisattvas, enter the inconceivable sovereign samādhi of bodhisattvas, and the radiance of the Buddha’s wisdom shines universally upon the world.”
Just as the Buddha-fields of future Buddhas are adorned and purified, so too are the worlds of present Buddhas.

Adorned with various purities and endowed with perfect merit, they are universally covered by immeasurable wondrous colors, inconceivable fragrances, immeasurable diverse jewels, immeasurable jewel-trees, incalculable adornments, incalculable palaces, and incalculable sublime sounds. Following virtuous friends, they manifest immeasurable all-encompassing merits and supreme adornments that are inexhaustible.

Adorned with all kinds of incense, all kinds of garlands, all kinds of flowers, all kinds of powdered incense, all kinds of jewels, all kinds of robes, all kinds of banners, all kinds of pennants, all kinds of silken streamers, and all kinds of jeweled railings; adorned with incalculable nets of white jewels covering everywhere; adorned with incalculable rivers and incalculable clouds and rains;

and adorned with incalculable spontaneous, wondrous sounds that are heard everywhere—with such infinite and boundless ornaments, they adorn the infinite, boundless, and inconceivable worlds of the Buddhas.

In those various worlds, there are the adornments of buddha-fields, the purity of buddha-fields, the equality of buddha-fields, the excellence of buddha-fields, the merits of buddha-fields, the superiority of buddha-fields, the bliss of buddha-fields, the indestructibility of buddha-fields, the inexhaustibility of buddha-fields, the immeasurable and inexhaustible merits of buddha-fields, the non-retrogression of buddha-fields, the fearlessness of buddha-fields, the radiance of buddha-fields, the happiness of buddha-fields, the insatiability of buddha-fields, the universal illumination of buddha-fields, the illuminating clarity of buddha-fields, the rectitude of buddha-fields, the preeminence of buddha-fields, the victory of buddha-fields, the supreme victory of buddha-fields, the subtlety of buddha-fields, the incomparability of buddha-fields, the peerlessness of buddha-fields, the supremacy of buddha-fields, the unsurpassedness of buddha-fields, and the equality-with-the-unequaled of buddha-fields.
In this way, all the Buddhas of the three periods of time and the adornments of their Buddha-fields are likewise.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates all these roots of goodness so that all Buddha-fields may be universally purified and adorned.
Such adornments, within a single world-system, consist of the complete purity and pervasive accumulation of all the adorned Buddha-fields of the three periods of time;
they are fully endowed with equal arising adornments, and are entirely complete in their sustained maintenance of adornment.

Just as in a single world, so too in worlds as immeasurable and boundless as space and the dharma-realm, all are adorned with the adornments of the buddha-fields of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;

they are fully endowed with the merits of the buddha-fields, the insatiable contemplation of the buddha-fields, the immeasurability of the buddha-fields, the vastness of the buddha-fields, the incalculability of the buddha-fields, the inconceivability of the buddha-fields, the unsurpassed nature of the buddha-fields, the ineffability of the buddha-fields, and the boundlessness of the buddha-fields.
Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates in this way:
"May all the buddha-fields that I cultivate be entirely filled with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas."
These bodhisattvas are fully endowed with all pure merits and have perfected wisdom;
they are skillfully able to discern all world-realms and realms of sentient beings, entering the profound dharma-realm and abandoning ignorance;
they enter the realm of emptiness and stillness, and achieve mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the inconceivable Dharma, and mindfulness of the pure Sangha.

They have perfected mindfulness and equanimity; the sun of Dharma is full, its light of wisdom shines everywhere, and their profound knowledge is unimpeded. They arise from the dharma of non-existence and cessation, giving birth to immeasurable, pure Buddha-dharmas.
They have accomplished extraordinary, supreme, excellent, pure, most excellent, and superior roots of goodness;
they have established the mind of unsurpassed bodhi, skillfully accord with it, and enter the powers of the Tathāgata.
With a mind constantly resolved to seek all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), they purify all demonic activities and comprehend the nature of sentient beings;
knowing that phenomena are empty and quiescent, they abandon inversions, eliminate ignorance, cultivate all roots of goodness, and fulfill their great vows.

Having accomplished such immeasurable and boundless merits, Bodhisattvas fill that land; all are born from immeasurable Dharma-gates and dwell securely in all such merits. They accomplish peerless and supreme roots of goodness, constantly performing the work of Buddhas through skillful means;

they attain the radiance of Bodhi and are fully endowed with the wisdom of the non-deluded Dharma-realm. With a single body they pervade the entire Dharma-realm, manifesting sovereign power and accomplishing the realm of great wisdom and omniscience through skillful means.

They give birth to wisdom and discern the immeasurable dharma-realm; they travel throughout all lands without attachment, their minds as pure as space, able to distinguish every dharma-realm. Regarding the inconceivable samādhis and meditative attainments of the bodhisattvas, they are skillfully able to enter and emerge through their mastery of expedient means.

They proceed toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), dwell in the buddha-fields, are well able to comprehend the majestic spiritual power of all buddhas, and are well able to discern incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) profound and wondrous dharmas, remaining free from all fear.

They accord with the roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and universally illumine the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas. They are able to receive and uphold all the True Dharma preached by all Buddhas; they are skilled in producing inconceivable, pure sounds and are adept at discerning the methods of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) languages.

Having attained the Unsurpassed Way and the stage of the Buddha’s sovereign mastery, they are able to pervade all worlds without obstruction. They fully encompass all dharmas free from contention; their minds are without falsehood and are unstained by attachment.

They cultivate and expand the bodhicitta, possess excellent understanding of wisdom, respond to and transform beings according to the times, and employ skillful means without fixed method. Having realized the true meaning, they expound it fully, accomplishing such immeasurable merits as these.
The great bodhisattvas adorn the world and fill the world;
with various kinds of adornments, they proceed to abide in peace, having skillfully cultivated and refined themselves until they are pure and unmixed, universally purified, and serenely tranquil.

In even a small portion of a single buddha-field, there are immeasurable bodhisattvas, innumerable bodhisattvas, inconceivable bodhisattvas, incomparable bodhisattvas, unfathomable bodhisattvas, peerless bodhisattvas, bodhisattvas beyond the ultimate, bodhisattvas without limit, ineffable bodhisattvas, and ineffable-ineffable bodhisattvas;
as it is in one buddha-field, so it is in every small portion thereof—there are such great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Likewise, throughout all worlds, equal to space and the dharma-realm, they are entirely filled with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate their various roots of goodness through skillful means:

dedicating them to all Buddha-fields, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all Tathāgatas, all unsurpassed enlightenment, all great vows, all means of deliverance, and all sentient beings; purifying all worlds; constantly beholding the Tathāgatas; [ensuring] the lifespan of the Tathāgatas is immeasurable; and turning the irreversible wheel of Dharma, equal in extent to the dharma-realm.”
In this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness:
to cause all buddha-fields to be purified;
and to cause all realms of sentient beings to be purified.
To cause all bodhisattvas to be purified;
to cause all Buddhas to fill the dharma-realm;
and to cause the Tathāgata’s pure dharma-body to fill all buddha-fields.
By means of such peerless dedications, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva proceeds toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); his mind is as pure as space and as immovable as the great earth.

He enters into inconceivable dedication, joyfully contemplating that all karmic retributions are entirely quiescent, and he dedicates inexhaustible merit in equanimity, in accordance with the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

“After the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has performed such a dedication, he does not falsely grasp at a self or what belongs to a self; he does not falsely grasp at the Buddha or the qualities of the Buddhas; he does not falsely grasp at the Buddha-fields or the purification of those fields; he does not falsely grasp at sentient beings or the taming of sentient beings; he does not falsely grasp at various karmas or the retribution of karma. He is not attached to mental karma or the fruits of karma; he does not destroy cause and effect; he does not grasp at existent dharmas nor does he destroy existent dharmas. Birth and death are not chaotic, and nirvāṇa is not quiescent. The path of the Tathāgata’s realm is not created by others, and there is no dharma with which it coexists.”
In this way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to various roots of goodness, decisively dedicating them so that they reach full maturity;

he contemplates them with equanimity while grasping their characteristics, skillfully apprehending their objects, discerning and weighing them, remaining free from all falsehoods, and being without attachment.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have thus dedicated these roots of goodness, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
by constantly mindful of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, they attain all inexhaustible roots of goodness;
and by delivering immeasurable bodhisattvas, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
Purifying all Buddha-fields, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
purifying the realms of sentient beings, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
entering the profound Dharma-realm, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
Cultivating the immeasurable minds, pure as space, one attains inexhaustible roots of goodness;
understanding all the realms of the Buddhas, one attains inexhaustible roots of goodness;
practicing all the pure deeds of Bodhisattvas, one attains inexhaustible roots of goodness.
Thoroughly comprehending the three periods of time, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
By dedicating such roots of goodness, they are able to deliver all sentient beings;
yet, entering the realm of sentient beings, they do not perceive any sentient beings in their dedication.
The dedication that understands all phenomena to be devoid of a life-span;
the dedication that knows all phenomena to be real and devoid of a sovereign self;
the dedication that all dharmas are devoid of a *pudgala*.
Contemplating all phenomena as being free from all anger and contention, one dedicates [merit];
dedicating with the realization that all phenomena arise from causes and conditions and possess no solidity;
dedicating with the knowledge of the true nature of all phenomena and remaining without attachment.
Dedication without attachment to any buddha-field;
dedication that does not grasp at the solid characteristics of bodhisattva practices;
and dedication through the discerning realization that all realms are empty and non-existent.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate in this manner, their eyes ultimately never see impure Buddha-fields, nor do they see sentient beings with disparate characteristics;
they practice the Dharma without seeing a dharma, and enter into wisdom without anything entered;
they comprehend all things as being like empty space.

Within the body of the Tathāgata, one attains all dharmas, fully accomplishes immeasurable powers of merit, and is endowed with roots of goodness that reach all places, bringing peace and happiness to sentient beings.

In every moment of thought, these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain unspeakably unspeakable stages of the ten powers, fully possessing all kinds of pure roots of goodness, and are able to gather in and sustain all sentient beings.

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished a treasury of jewels of sovereign merit; wherever they travel, they are able to purify all buddha-fields and cause unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to dwell securely and acquire the power of all merits.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, by the power of this dedication, all their practices become peerless; they cannot be destroyed by anything in all the worlds; they awe and subdue all māras such that none can gaze upon them; they fully accomplish non-retrogressive merit, and all their immeasurable great vows are completely fulfilled.
Their minds become increasingly vast, equaling all-knowledge; within a single thought-moment, they are able to pervade immeasurable Buddha-fields;
they attain immeasurable power of wisdom, fully comprehending the realms of all Buddhas;
they constantly delight in receiving and upholding all Buddha-dharmas, abiding securely in immeasurable and boundless great wisdom.
The power of the Bodhisattva’s initial resolve for enlightenment is entirely equal to space and the dharma-realm.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the fifth inexhaustible treasury of merit dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva."
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this dedication of the inexhaustible treasury of merit, they further attain ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries of merit.
What are these ten?
First, constantly beholding the inexhaustible treasury of merits of all Buddhas, seeing immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* Buddhas within each and every pore;
second, entering the inexhaustible treasury of the merit of the Dharma, whereby through the wisdom of the Tathāgata one equally contemplates all phenomena as being a single phenomenon;
third, receiving and upholding the inexhaustible treasury of the merit of right mindfulness, hearing the true Dharma spoken by all Buddhas and retaining it upon hearing without forgetting.
Fourth, they attain the treasury of merit of inexhaustible wisdom, being well able to sequentially understand the meanings of the phrases in all the sutras and teachings spoken by the Tathāgatas;
fifth, they attain the treasury of merit of the inexhaustible inclinations of phenomena, being well able to discern the inclinations of all dharmas;
sixth, they attain the treasury of merit of the inexhaustible vows of the Buddhas, their wisdom being like space, filling all dharmas throughout the three periods of time.
Seventh is the inexhaustible treasury of meritorious qualities, which fulfills the intentions of all sentient beings and remains inexhaustible;
eighth is the inexhaustible treasury of the merit of wisdom, which can completely eliminate the obscurations of ignorance and delusion for all sentient beings;
ninth is the inexhaustible treasury of the merit of eloquence, which causes all sentient beings to fully understand all Buddha-dharmas as equal and non-dual.

Tenth, they possess the inexhaustible treasury of the ten powers and four fearlessnesses; having fully cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva, they assume the office of the Dharma King and attain all-knowledge.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s attainment of the ten inexhaustible treasuries of merit;
by means of these inexhaustible treasuries of merit, they dedicate them all toward every form of virtue.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The Bodhisattva achieves the power of the straight mind, Attaining mastery over all phenomena.
Rejoicing in all merits thus obtained, They skillfully dedicate them through unimpeded means."
All the Most Victorious Ones of the three periods of time, Adorning and purifying buddha-fields and worlds,
Endowed with all supreme merits— I dedicate [my merit] toward the purification of buddha-fields in the same way.
All the most supreme dharmas of the three periods of time, the Bodhisattvas are able to discern with perfect clarity;
with a pure mind they embrace all dharmas, thus adorning all Buddha-fields.
Though one exhausts immeasurable kalpas across the three periods of time praising all the merits of a single buddha-field,
the kalpas of the three periods may come to an end, yet the merits of the buddha-field are without limit.
Just as all these Buddha-fields, All most excellent ones, are completely adorned and purified,
So too do Bodhisattvas adorn and purify all fields, Making them no different from those of the Guides.
Those true sons of the Buddha have pure minds; All are born through transformation from the Tathāgata’s Dharma.
Their minds are adorned with all merits, Pervading and filling all buddha-fields.
Those bodhisattvas are all fully endowed with bodies adorned by immeasurable marks and signs;
they have perfected every form of eloquence, inexhaustible like the great ocean.
Observing all realms with an equanimous mind, Abiding securely in all gateways of samādhi,
They achieve a pure and peerless state of mind, Whose radiance shines universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
In this way, all Buddha-fields without exception are entirely filled with these bodhisattvas;
they never conceive thoughts of the Śrāvaka vehicle, nor do they seek the path of the Pratyekabuddha.
When a bodhisattva’s mind is thus purified, they dedicate their roots of goodness to all living beings,
universally causing all beings to achieve perfect enlightenment and fully possess the dharmas of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
All the Māra kings of the ten directions are completely subdued by the Bodhisattva’s majestic virtue;
dwelling with courageous steadfastness, they cannot be destroyed, as he resolutely practices the ultimate Dharma.

The Bodhisattva is fully endowed with the power of all vows; Dedicating merit without obstruction, they enter deeply into the inexhaustible treasury of merit, Wherein the retributions of the three periods of time are never-ending.
Skillfully observing all phenomena, they thoroughly understand that their nature is not independent;
having already discerned emptiness and selflessness, they therefore do not falsely grasp at karmic retribution.
There are no dharmas with form nor those without form; there is neither perception nor non-perception;
there are neither existent dharmas nor non-existent dharmas; all dharmas are utterly non-existent.
Neither existent nor non-existent, neither caused nor causeless—
within all those conditions, the mind thoroughly understands them to be free from defilement and delusion.
All the linguistic conventions of all sentient beings, he fully understands without attachment;
he thoroughly knows all the conventional designations of the world, and is certain that all phenomena are devoid of a self.
Equally observing all classes of sentient beings, Thoroughly understanding that all phenomena lack dual characteristics,
Universally seeing the three periods of time as undifferentiated, The various karmas of Buddha-fields are likewise so.
The Bodhisattva thus understands dedication, As the merit arises from their various deeds;
They clearly penetrate the true nature of all Buddhas And comprehend the profound and wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas.
When a bodhisattva thus performs pure dedication, their mind is able to discern and reflect skillfully;
realizing that all intrinsic natures are in fact no-nature, they remain unattached to any phenomena.
Gathering all spheres of experience, they dedicate them to all classes of sentient beings;
dispelling all darkness of ignorance, they awaken to the suchness of true reality.
The Bodhisattva has extinguished and discarded all false views without remainder;
having distanced himself from the fever of worldly afflictions, he has attained the state of ultimate coolness.
Not destroying the nature of all phenomena, Clearly realizing that they are truly unarisen;
Understanding all phenomena to be like echoes, They remain entirely unattached to anything.
Fully knowing the classes of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, all of whom arise from the conjunction of causes and conditions;
skillfully understanding the various habitual tendencies of afflictions, yet not destroying the true nature of all phenomena.
Thoroughly realizing that the nature of karma is not karma, yet without destroying the nature of various karmas,
and likewise without destroying the retribution of karma, he proclaims and praises the Dharma of dependent origination.
Sentient beings have no birth in their arising, nor do they transmigrate within the cycle of birth and death;
though they speak of sentient beings, they do not cling to them, skillfully conforming to all worlds.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifteen;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Sixteen.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Third Part of the Twenty-first Chapter on the Ten Dedications of the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja:
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s sixth dedication, which accords with all firm roots of goodness?

When this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva acts as a king, he obtains a superior realm that is secure, peaceful, and prosperous; he subdues his enemies and governs by the Right Path, teaching and transforming others in accordance with the Dharma. His merit covers all under heaven and his virtue overspreads the ten directions; the myriad nations submit and obey, none daring to disobey his commands. Weapons are not used, for there is natural peace and stability. He skillfully gathers and sustains sentient beings through the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), and as a Wheel-Turning Sage King (*cakravartin*), he achieves the seven treasures.

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva firmly abides in sovereign merit; his retinue is harmonious and cannot be broken apart. He is foremost in physical excellence, such that those who behold him never tire of looking.

Free from all evils, he is fully endowed with merit; his primary marks and secondary signs are perfected, and his countenance is extraordinary. His body and limbs are perfectly formed and majestic, pure and radiant, bringing joy to all who see him.
His physical strength is firm and indestructible, as he has assumed the body of Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Devas.
Free from all karmic obstructions, they attain pure karma and fully practice all forms of giving:

whether it be food and drink, various delicacies, vehicles, clothing, exquisite flower garlands, blended incenses, ointments, couches, dwellings, houses, lamps, medicinal decoctions, precious vessels, adorned jeweled chariots, elephant and horse kings, exquisite jeweled thrones, parasols, banners, and flags, various miscellaneous jewels, wonderful ornaments, pure celestial crowns, or the bright pearls within their topknots;

or when seeing prisoners undergoing various tortures, they give rise to great compassion, relinquishing their treasuries, wives, children, and retinues, and even placing themselves in prison to rescue suffering sentient beings.
Seeing a prisoner being led toward the place of execution, he sacrificed his own body to take their life;

if someone begged for his skin and hair from his head, the bright pearl within his topknot, his eyes, ears, nose, teeth, tongue, head, hands, or feet, or requested that he maim his body and shed blood, or asked for his marrow, flesh, heart, intestines, kidneys, liver, lungs, joints, various bones, thick or thin skin, or even his fingers and nails along with the flesh;
for the sake of seeking the True Dharma, he threw himself into a pit of fire, and for the sake of the Dharma, he underwent immeasurable sufferings with his entire body.

Because the Dharma is difficult to encounter, they are able to renounce the great earth, the territories of the four seas, cities large and small, villages, towns, and hamlets—lands of abundant joy with flourishing populations, groves and bathing pools where flowers and fruits grow in profusion, adorned with immeasurable splendor, and a world at peace, free from all enemies; as well as their stores of gold and silver, their wives, children, and retinues, and their sovereignty as Dharma-kings. They sever all evil karma of slaughter and bestow fearlessness upon all.

If they see anyone who has mutilated the bodies of animals or humans by destroying their vital organs, they give rise to great compassion to rescue and deliver them, proclaiming the name of the Buddha with a great voice so that all may hear it.
Some give away the great earth to erect Buddha halls and construct monastic dwellings, providing a secure abode for the Bodhisattvas and the holy assembly—the field of merit;
some build honored temples to respond appropriately to all needs;
some give servants and attendants to provide for the Triple Gem, their parents, and their spiritual friends—all fields of merit—offering even their own bodies as gifts to serve all.
Furthermore, they universally cover all Buddhas with their own bodies, bestow their own bodies upon all sentient beings, and constantly offer their own persons to serve the Buddhas;

they give away their kingdoms and royal capitals, as well as grand cities adorned with splendor; they also give precious women, attendants, retinues, wives, concubines, sons, and daughters; or they give houses, various ornaments, and pleasure gardens; or they establish countless great assemblies for giving, remaining far removed from all evils for the sake of purifying sentient beings, relinquishing all means of livelihood without mental attachment or seeking of karmic rewards, being able to renounce everything entirely.

If all sentient beings—humans and non-humans, the poor and the noble, the good and the evil—all kinds of fields of merit from distant and near regions were to come, whether seeking it themselves or not seeking it at all, one would give everything to them without any stinginess or parsimony.

He forms this thought: "I shall dedicate the gathering of all firm roots of goodness that accord with them; I shall dedicate the gathering of excellent form that accords with all firm roots of goodness; I shall dedicate the gathering of excellent feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness that accords with all firm roots of goodness; I shall dedicate the gathering of buddha-fields that accords with all firm roots of goodness; I shall dedicate the gathering of superior persons that accords with all firm roots of goodness; I shall dedicate the gathering of retinues that accords with all firm roots of goodness; I shall dedicate the gathering of wealth and profit that accords with all firm roots of goodness; and I shall dedicate the gathering of all acts of giving that accords with all firm roots of goodness."
After the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has thus dedicated these roots of goodness, he forms this thought:
"The giving I practice is without greed, without attachment, and is liberated from defilement; my mind is truly upright and free from any stinginess.

By the power of the merit of this gift, may all sentient beings attain great wisdom with unobstructed minds; may they know food and see food without any greedy attachment, but by means of the food of Dharma, forever leave behind solid food (kavaḍīkāra-āhāra), their wisdom being fully perfected as they embrace the roots of goodness, the Dharma-body, and the Wisdom-body, wandering in purity. Yet, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, they manifest the acceptance of solid food."
“When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives a drink, they dedicate the merit in this way:

‘By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings drink the nectar of the Dharma, accomplish the path of a Bodhisattva, eliminate thirst and craving, always delight in the Mahāyāna, leave behind the love for the five desires, attain pure love for the Dharma, have a supple Dharma-body, harmonize the mind through samādhi, never become distracted, enter the ocean of wisdom, raise great clouds of the Dharma, and rain down the nectar of the Dharma.’”
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives drinks.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives various flavors—namely, pungent, sour, salty, bland, sweet, and bitter—and such immeasurable varieties of food and drink with exquisite fragrances and tastes that one never tires of eating; which can make the four great elements supple and bring peace and happiness, filling the body, strengthening the vital energy, giving rise to a heart of joy, clarifying and purifying the sense faculties, maintaining the internal body, fostering suppleness, making the complexion radiant and lustrous, rendering it invulnerable to all poisons and harms, eliminating myriad illnesses, and attaining the state of being free from affliction.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva bestows such immeasurable and innumerable varieties of exquisite flavors, they dedicate the merit as follows:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain the marks of supreme flavor, filled with ambrosia;
may the minds of all sentient beings abide securely in the profound wisdom of the flavor of Dharma, and fully understand the karmic causes of all flavors."

May all sentient beings fully obtain the measureless, profound, and wondrous flavor of the Dharma, realize the wisdom of the Dharma-realm, abide securely in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), and reach the city of the Dharma;
may all sentient beings cause the clouds of Dharma to rain everywhere, filling the Dharma-realm, and be able to universally tame and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
may all sentient beings obtain the flavor of supreme wisdom, and through their unsurpassed love for the Dharma, have their bodies and minds become supple and serene.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of supreme flavor, remaining unattached to various tastes while cultivating all vows of the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings be well-harmonized, attaining the Dharma of a single flavor and giving birth to the non-dual Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the unimpeded flavor and achieve non-retrogression in the vehicle of omniscience.
May all sentient beings attain the undifferentiated flavor of the Dharma of all Buddhas and be skillfully able to discern all faculties;
may all sentient beings be filled with the flavor of the Dharma and fully abide in the unobstructed Buddha-dharmas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows various flavors, causing all sentient beings to fully attain the body of unimpeded wisdom.
“When a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives a vehicle, they dedicate the merit in this way:

‘By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of omniscience, becoming fully endowed with the Great Vehicle, the indestructible vehicle, the supreme vehicle, the excellent vehicle, the swift vehicle, the vehicle of great power, the vehicle of the accomplishment of merit, and the supramundane vehicle; may they give birth to the immeasurable vehicles of all bodhisattvas and bring their merits to fulfillment.’”
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives vehicles.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives clothing, they dedicate in this way:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain the robes of shame and remorse to cover their bodies; may they be freed from all unsightly forms, becoming upright, dignified, and exquisite; may their countenances be fresh and radiant, their skin and limbs soft and supple; may they attain the bliss of the body and the bliss of all Buddhas; and may they attain the immeasurable Dharma-body that universally responds to all, and the unsurpassed, pure, all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*)."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives clothing.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives various flowers—exquisite and fragrant flowers, flowers of manifold colors, flowers of immeasurable joy, well-manifested flowers, flowers that bring inexhaustible delight, flowers of all seasons, celestial flowers, human flowers, flowers cherished by the world, and unsurpassed fragrant flowers—a bodhisattva-mahāsattva offers all such immeasurable varieties of flowers to all the Buddhas currently residing throughout the ten directions, as well as to their stupas and shrines after their parinirvāṇa; furthermore, they offer them to those who bestow the gift of Dharma, to the Sangha of bhikṣus, to all bodhisattvas, to spiritual friends, to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, to parents and kinsmen, even unto oneself, and down to the poor and lowly.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives flowers, they dedicate the merit in this way:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain the pure blossoming of the flowers of the samādhis of all Buddhas, and may the manifold flowers of the sublime Dharma emerge from their hearts;
may all sentient beings never tire of beholding them, and may they attain love for the Buddha-dharma."
May all sentient beings always behold exquisite forms, their physical marks upright and majestic, such that those who see them never grow weary;
may all sentient beings never be distracted, fully accomplishing all pure deeds and practices;
may all sentient beings constantly mind their spiritual friends, their minds remaining unchanging.
May all sentient beings be like agada medicine, completely eliminating the manifold poisons of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings fulfill their great vows and resolutely abide in the sovereign king of unsurpassed wisdom;
