may all sentient beings give rise to the sun of wisdom, extinguishing all the darkness of ignorance.
May all sentient beings be like the pure, full moon, increasing the moon of Bodhi and causing the flowers of merit to bloom;
may all sentient beings enter the great ocean of jewels, behold spiritual friends, and fully accomplish all roots of goodness.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give flowers, causing all sentient beings to fully attain unimpeded, pure, and wondrous wisdom.
"When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives a garland, he dedicates the merit in this way:

'By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be pleasing to behold; may there be none who do not rejoice upon seeing them; may they be immediately drawn to them with intimacy and kindness; may there be none who do not love them upon seeing them; may they be freed from sorrow and affliction upon seeing them; and may they surely see all Buddhas and attain all pure wisdom.'"
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives garlands.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives incense, they dedicate it in this way:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be endowed with the fragrance of morality; may they attain indestructible morality, unadulterated morality, stainless morality, morality free from doubt, morality free from entanglements, cool and refreshing morality, non-transgressing morality, immeasurable morality, unsurpassed morality, world-transcending morality, and the ultimate morality of bodhisattvas that reaches the other shore; may all sentient beings fully achieve the moral body of all Buddhas."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give incense, so as to cause all sentient beings to fully accomplish the body of unimpeded precepts.
"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives powdered incense, they dedicate the merit in this way:
'By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings give incense that universally perfumes, and may they relinquish all that they possess;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of the precepts, and may they attain the pure precepts of a Buddha.'"
May the fragrance of patience pervade all sentient beings, causing them to abandon harmful intentions;
may the fragrance of diligence pervade all sentient beings, causing them to fully cultivate the Mahāyāna and adorn themselves with great vows;
may the fragrance of meditative concentration pervade all sentient beings, causing them to attain the samādhi of the presence of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of wisdom, attaining the King of Supreme Knowledge in a single thought-moment;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of the Dharma, accomplishing the supreme and fearless Dharma;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of virtue, accomplishing all merit and wisdom.
May all sentient beings be universally permeated by the sublime fragrance of unsurpassed bodhi, attaining the ten powers of a Buddha and reaching the ultimate further shore;
may all sentient beings be fully and universally permeated by the fragrance of pure white dharmas, severing and eliminating all unwholesome states.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives powdered incense.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives couches and seats, he dedicates them in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain celestial jewel thrones and be established securely upon the seat of wisdom."
May all sentient beings attain the seat of the noble ones, abandon the mind of ordinary worldlings, and cultivate the bodhicitta;
may all sentient beings attain the seat of peace and happiness, and be free from the suffering of birth and death;
may all sentient beings attain the supreme seat, and behold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings attain the seat of equanimity, with an impartial mind universally illuminating all phenomena;
may all sentient beings attain the most supreme seat, achieve unsurpassed karma, and forever leave the mundane world behind;
may all sentient beings attain the seat of peace and stability, personally realizing all profound and wondrous dharmas.
May all sentient beings attain the seat of purity, cultivating the realm of the Tathāgata’s pure wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain the seat of stable abiding, being constantly followed, protected, and shielded by spiritual friends;
may all sentient beings attain the lion throne, fully endowed with the fearless seat of the Tathāgata.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives beds and seats, causing all sentient beings to cultivate mindfulness and wisdom and to subdue their sense faculties.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives a dwelling place, they dedicate the merit in this way:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings fully attain the adorned and purified Buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas; may they cultivate the merits that adorn the Buddha-fields and dwell securely in the realm of profound samādhi; may they be without attachment to those dwelling places, skillfully discerning all abodes, dwelling apart from the world, and dwelling in the dwelling of the Buddhas; may they embrace the ultimate Great Way in which all Buddhas dwell, peacefully and securely abide while cultivating immeasurable pure roots of goodness, never abandoning the unsurpassed dwelling of the Buddhas."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives dwellings, so as to bring peace, benefit, and protection to all sentient beings.
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives a dwelling, they dedicate the merit in this way:
'By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be benefited and brought peace and happiness, and may they dwell in right mindfulness and reflection;

may all sentient beings dwell in reliance upon the Tathāgata, dwell in reliance upon great wisdom, dwell in reliance upon spiritual friends, dwell in reliance upon those worthy of respect, dwell in reliance upon virtuous conduct, dwell in reliance upon great loving-kindness, dwell in reliance upon great compassion, dwell in reliance upon the six pāramitās, dwell in reliance upon the immeasurable bodhicitta, and dwell in reliance upon the path of all bodhisattvas.'"

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives dwellings, so as to cause all sentient beings to fully accomplish pure wisdom and the merits of the various supernormal powers.
"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow lamps as gifts—

namely, lamps of ghee, lamps of oil, jewel lamps, maṇi lamps, lacquer lamps, fire lamps, lamps of agallochum incense, lamps of sandalwood incense, lamps of all-fragrant kings, and lamps of immeasurable colored flames— and when they give such immeasurable lamps and lights, they dedicate them in this way: 'By these roots of goodness,
may I benefit all sentient beings and gather in all sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to attain immeasurable light that universally illumines the Dharma of all Tathāgatas.'"
May all sentient beings attain the light of clarity and purity, universally illuminating all subtle forms;
may all sentient beings attain the light of freedom from delusion, skillfully understanding the realm of non-sentient beings;
may all sentient beings attain the immeasurable light of the Dharma-body and its pure radiance, universally illuminating all things.
May all sentient beings attain universal radiance and achieve non-retrogression in all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain the light of the Buddhas, universally illuminating all infinite Buddha-lands;
may all sentient beings attain unimpeded light, able to universally and pervasively illuminate the entire Dharma-realm with a single ray of light.
May all sentient beings attain immeasurable light that universally illumines Buddha-fields with an uninterrupted radiance;
may all sentient beings attain the Lamp of the Wisdom Banner of the King of Radiant Banners, universally illuminating the world;
may all sentient beings attain light of infinite colors, emitting the light of mastery to illuminate all lands.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives lamps: it is able to benefit all sentient beings and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings; it accords with roots of goodness and gathers in the roots of goodness of sentient beings; it is the root of goodness of impartially bestowing upon all sentient beings, the root of goodness of compassionate pity for sentient beings through impartial giving, the root of goodness of universally covering sentient beings through mindful compassion, the root of goodness of universally sheltering sentient beings through giving, the root of goodness of fulfilling sentient beings so they may universally enter into all things, the root of goodness of equality in the sphere of experience, and the root of goodness of wisdom that regards all sentient beings with equality—thus distinguishing all things.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the gift of lamps: to cause all sentient beings to attain unimpeded dedication and to abide securely in all pure and luminous roots of goodness.
"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives medicinal decoctions, he dedicates the merit in this way:
'By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be free from all obstacles;
may all sentient beings cast off their diseased bodies and all attain the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata.'"
May all sentient beings attain the nature of medicine, so that they may completely eliminate the diseases of unwholesomeness in all beings;
may all sentient beings become agada-medicine, abiding securely in the Bodhisattva stage of non-retrogression;
may all sentient beings become the medicine of the Tathāgata, extracting the poisonous thorns of all afflictions.
May all sentient beings associate with the noble and holy ones, eliminate their afflictions, and attain pure conduct;
may all sentient beings attain the mind of the Medicine King, never becoming weary of or turning away from any wholesome dharmas;
may all sentient beings fully accomplish the indestructible medicinal tree that counteracts all diseases of unwholesomeness.
May all sentient beings have the thorns of all diseases removed and fully attain the light of all-encompassing wisdom;
may all sentient beings understand the various remedial dharmas of the world and, according to the needs of beings, apply these remedies to cure their manifold ailments.

When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has thus dedicated the roots of goodness from giving medicine, by means of these roots of goodness, he causes all sentient beings to abandon all illnesses, to be secure and free from affliction, to be fully endowed with purity, and to attain the illness-free Dharma of all Tathāgatas;

he causes all sentient beings to emerge from the thorns of disease, to obtain an inexhaustible body that cannot be destroyed even by the Iron Ring Mountains, to be fully endowed with all firm powers, to fulfill the unsurpassed Dharma-bliss of all Buddhas, and to attain the sovereign Dharma-body of a Buddha’s spiritual power.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows medicinal decoctions.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able to generously give all kinds of vessels; namely:

There were vessels of pure gold filled with various jewels; vessels of white silver filled with various jewels; vessels of lapis lazuli filled with various jewels; vessels of crystal filled with various kinds of jewel ornaments; vessels of giant clam shell filled with red pearls; and vessels of agate filled with coral, moonstone, and other myriad treasures. Furthermore, there were stone vessels filled with exquisite delicacies;

sandalwood vessels filled with various precious garments; and vajra vessels filled with all manner of fragrances. In this way, there were immeasurable and innumerable such wonderful jewel vessels, each containing immeasurable and innumerable exquisite treasures.
Or they give to the Buddhas, because they believe that the Buddha-field is inconceivable;
or they give to the Bodhisattva-jewels, because spiritual friends who inspire the aspiration for enlightenment are difficult to encounter;
or they give to the Sangha, because it nurtures and sustains the Buddha-dharma.
Or one may give to individuals (*pudgala*), śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas out of love for the noble Dharma;
or one may give to one's parents out of respect;
or one may give to teachers and elders so that they may instruct one in the practice of merit according to the Dharma.
Even when practicing inferior and mundane acts of giving, it is because one views sentient beings with a mind of great loving-kindness, great compassion, and eyes of affection;
because one does not abandon the fulfillment of the *dāna-pāramitā* by all bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time;
and because one seeks exclusively and single-mindedly for unsurpassed enlightenment.
They relinquish all that they possess, both internal and external, because they do not abandon any class of sentient beings;
they do not cling to fields of merit or material wealth.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give by filling such immeasurable precious vessels with immeasurable varieties of jewels, they dedicate the merit in this way:

By means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings become vast and great receptacles; may they develop roots of mindfulness as expansive as space, so that they are able to receive and uphold all mundane and supramundane scriptures without ever forgetting them;
may they become pure vessels, so that they are universally able to receive and uphold the profound Dharma of the Buddhas;
may they become unsurpassed jewel vessels, so that they are able to receive and uphold all the teachings of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

May all sentient beings universally become supreme vessels for the Dharma-treasure of the Tathāgatas, so that they may fully receive and uphold the indestructible Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may all sentient beings become adorned vessels, so that they may receive and uphold the boundless bodhicitta;
may all sentient beings fully become vessels of all merit, as they aspire to and delight in the immeasurable pure wisdom of the Tathāgata.
To cause all sentient beings to become vessels for the internal dharma of omniscience, so that they may ultimately attain the Tathāgata’s unimpeded liberation and omniscience;

to cause all sentient beings to become vessels for the practices of all bodhisattvas throughout the kalpas of the future limit, so that all sentient beings may firmly abide in the power of omniscience;

and to cause all sentient beings to become supreme and wondrous vessels for the Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, so that they may fully receive and uphold the teachings spoken by all Buddhas in their Brahma-voices.

May all sentient beings become internal vessels, their bodies capable of containing all worlds, the realm of empty space, and the dharma-realm, because they are able to receive the exhortations of the Buddhas' retinues to turn the great wheel of Dharma.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows gifts upon those who are vessels, so as to cause all sentient beings to become vessels of the Dharma, all capable of upholding all the vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas offer various immeasurable and manifold adorned jeweled chariots to the Buddhas and bodhisattvas, to spiritual friends, to the great assemblies of Tathāgatas, to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and to all fields of merit;

they offer them to various sentient beings who come from other regions—whether they have come because they heard the bodhisattva’s reputation, or because of their connection with the bodhisattva, or because they heard of the bodhisattva’s vow to practice giving, or because they were invited by the bodhisattva’s mental aspiration.”

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas may give various kinds of magnificent jeweled golden chariots, covered with nets of golden bells that produce harmonious and elegant sounds when slightly moved; adorned with hanging precious necklaces and various ornaments;
or they may give pure lapis lazuli chariots, decorated with immeasurable rare and wonderful treasures;
or again, they may give chariots of many exquisite jewels, adorned with white silver and covered with white nets.
Or again, he bestowed divine horse-jeweled chariots, adorned with immeasurable billions of jewels;
or again, he bestowed great elephant-jeweled chariots, adorned with immeasurable billions of jewels, their surfaces entwined with nets of every kind of gem;

or again, he bestowed sandalwood-scented chariots, adorned with wheels of various jewels, with precious lion-thrones spread upon them, and within them attended by hundreds of thousands of court ladies who were perfect in human form and exquisite in countenance, while precious jeweled canopies covered them from above, and a hundred thousand strong men pulled and guided them.

Or again, they may give crystal chariots, adorned with immeasurable varieties of exquisite jewels, carrying countless beautiful and graceful women, covered above by canopies of diverse precious gems, and surrounded on all sides by ornaments of jeweled silk banners and streamers;

or again, they may give carnelian chariots, decorated with various jewels, perfumed with diverse incenses, rubbed with ointments, and strewn with wonderful flowers, while hundreds of thousands of women holding golden necklaces proceed with balanced composure and a speed as swift as the wind.

Or again, they may give a sturdy fragrant chariot, spread with various soft precious garments and covered above by nets of exquisite jewels; it is perfumed with pure, wondrous incense whose extraordinary fragrance delights the human heart, wafting afar even against the wind so that those who hear it never tire of it, while the sons of the gods lead and drive it before them.

Or again, they may give a chariot made of all kinds of jewels, adorned with various colors and decorated with intricate patterns, covered above by nets of exquisite jewels and draped all around with various jeweled bands; it is spread with precious cloths and sprinkled with powdered incense, and their beloved sons and daughters are seated within it.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give such various wondrous jeweled chariots to the Buddhas, they dedicate the merit as follows:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings joyfully seek the unsurpassed field of merit, and with deep faith believe that giving to the Buddha yields immeasurable retribution;
may all sentient beings turn their minds single-mindedly toward the Buddha and attain immeasurable, pure karmic fruits."
May all sentient beings be free from stinginess and possessiveness toward all Buddhas, fully accomplishing great generosity without any sense of attachment or regret;

may all sentient beings cultivate the supreme field of merit in the presence of all Buddhas, abandon the aspirations of the two vehicles, and attain the unimpeded liberation and the knowledge of all modes of the Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings plant inexhaustible roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas and attain the immeasurable merit and wisdom of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings grasp profound wisdom and be fully endowed with the pure, unsurpassed King of Wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain sovereign mastery in their movements and acquire the unimpeded spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas that reach all places;
may all sentient beings embrace the Mahāyāna, attain immeasurable kinds of knowledge, and abide immovably therein.
May all sentient beings fully accomplish the foremost field of merit, such that they are all able to give birth to the ground of omniscience;
may all sentient beings harbor no feelings of resentment toward any Buddha, planting various roots of goodness and joyfully seeking the wisdom of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings, through minimal expedient means, travel to all adorned Buddha-fields, penetrating deeply into the Dharma-realm in a single thought-moment without weariness.
May all sentient beings enter the bodhisattva supernormal powers equal to space, so that they may reach the abodes of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain incomparable bodies, able to travel throughout the worlds of the ten directions without ever experiencing fatigue;
may all sentient beings achieve vast bodies and attain the power to act according to their will.

May all sentient beings attain the adornment of the spiritual powers of all Buddhas and reach the ultimate further shore; may they manifest within a single thought-moment the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgatas, pervading the entire realm of empty space;
may all sentient beings cultivate practices of peace and stability, remaining in accord with the practices of all Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings proceed swiftly and without obstruction, reaching the ultimate further shore of the wisdom of the ten powers.
May all sentient beings attain the perfection of power to transform all worlds and universally enter the indestructible dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings practice the conduct of Samantabhadra, reach the other shore, and attain non-retrogressive omniscience;
may all sentient beings mount the peerless vehicle of wisdom, accord with and practice throughout the entire dharma-realm, and perceive true reality.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas offer various precious vehicles to the Buddhas currently residing in the world, as well as to the stūpas and shrines containing their relics after their parinirvāṇa, so that all sentient beings may ultimately attain the unimpeded Mahāyāna of all Buddhas.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows the pure vehicle upon other bodhisattvas and spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings never abandon the bodhisattvas and their spiritual friends, and may they recognize kindness and repay it;
may all sentient beings share the same purpose as spiritual friends, because they embrace roots of goodness that are of the same nature."
May all sentient beings draw near to and revere spiritual friends, honoring and making offerings to them, relinquishing everything to follow and embrace spiritual friends;
may all sentient beings attain an upright mind, following spiritual friends without ever being separated from them;
may all sentient beings constantly see spiritual friends and never contravene their instructions.
May all sentient beings attain an upright mind, never forsake spiritual friends, be free from all defilements, and possess an indestructible heart;
may all sentient beings, for the sake of spiritual friends, not begrudge their own bodies or lives, relinquish everything, and never disobey their instructions;
may all sentient beings be taken into the care of spiritual friends, cultivate great compassion, and remain far removed from all evils.
May all sentient beings follow spiritual friends and, upon hearing the Buddha’s true Dharma, be able to receive and uphold it in its entirety;
may all sentient beings share in the roots of goodness, karma, and retributions of spiritual friends, so that their bodhisattva practices and vows reach ultimate purity, equality, and fulfillment;
may all sentient beings give birth to the true Dharma, skillfully know the realms of all samādhis, be fully endowed with wisdom, and possess mastery over supernormal powers.
May all sentient beings be led far away from all realms of existence, uphold all dharmas, and ultimately reach the other shore;
may all sentient beings mount the Great Vehicle and, until they finally attain all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), remain free from indolence throughout the interval;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of wisdom and reach the place of peace and security, never to regress.
May all sentient beings know the practice of True Suchness (tathatā), remain far removed from ignorance, and hear and uphold the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be gathered by all Buddhas, attain unimpeded wisdom, and reach the ultimate realization of all dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain the deathless supernormal power (ṛddhipāda) that is wondrous, swift, and unimpeded.
May all sentient beings wander with sovereign ease, taming other beings and accomplishing the Mahāyāna;
may all sentient beings’ actions be non-vain and reach ultimate fulfillment, so that they obtain the vehicle of wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain the unimpeded vehicle, reaching all places through unimpeded knowledge.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when bestowing various vehicles upon spiritual friends; it causes all sentient beings to be fully endowed with merit, becoming equal to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas without distinction, and being able to please and satisfy all worthies and sages.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows various precious vehicles upon the assembly of Tathāgatas, they have well trained in the mind of giving, the mind of wise discernment, the mind of pure merit, the mind of compliant giving, the mind that the Jewel of the Saṃgha is difficult to encounter, the mind of deep faith in the Jewel of the Saṃgha, the mind of embracing the true teaching, and the mind of abiding in uprightness. They are well able to bring the great assembly of giving to ultimate completion, generating immeasurable and boundless merit; their faith in the Buddha’s true teaching is pure and cannot be thwarted or destroyed."
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives various vehicles as a gift to the Sangha Jewel, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings turn toward the Buddha’s true Dharma and embrace the correct teaching;
may all sentient beings focus their minds on internal contemplation, eliminate false teachings, and achieve the state of the noble ones."
May all sentient beings attain the stage of the noble ones (ārya-bhūmi), instructing one another through the Dharma of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings be honored and revered by the world, their words always trusted and accepted;
and may all sentient beings enter into all dharmas, skillfully discerning the non-dual realm of reality (advaya-dharmadhātu).
May all sentient beings be surrounded by the Jewel of Humanity, born from the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom;
may all sentient beings abide in the stainless Dharma, able to eliminate all defilements of affliction;
may all sentient beings be born from the unsurpassed Jewel of the Saṅgha, transcending the ways of ordinary worldlings and attaining the stage of the Noble Saṅgha.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the noble Dharma and cultivate unimpeded wisdom;
may all sentient beings become leaders of great assemblies, adorned with wisdom and untainted by the mundane world;
may all sentient beings, through skillful means, turn the wheel of the Dharma of wisdom.
May all sentient beings attain the spiritual power of a single thought-moment, such that they are able to pervade unspeakably, unspeakably many worlds;
may all sentient beings ride upon bodies of empty space, possessing unimpeded wisdom regarding all worlds;
may all sentient beings proceed to the assemblies of Tathāgatas, which are equal to space and the dharma-realm.
May all sentient beings attain a body of lightness and elevation, and through supreme, wondrous wisdom, be able to travel everywhere throughout all Buddha-worlds;
may all sentient beings attain unimpeded spiritual powers (*ṛddhipāda*), being able to manifest their bodies universally in all lands;
may all sentient beings reach the other shore of great sovereign spiritual powers, such that without rising from a single seat, they may universally appear in response within all worlds.
May all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-body, remaining unattached to any world, manifesting spiritual powers that move as swiftly as lightning;
may all sentient beings manifest the inconceivable realm of supernormal feats, skillfully following and transforming others to tame all sentient beings according to what is appropriate;

may all sentient beings attain wondrous supernormal powers, traveling throughout the worlds of the ten directions in a single thought-moment and transcending the entire Dharma-realm in a single thought-moment, without any hindrance.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows various vehicles upon the assembly of Tathāgatas, so that all sentient beings may universally ride the pure, unsurpassed vehicle of wisdom, and turn the unimpeded wheel of Dharma and the wheel of wisdom in all worlds.

"Furthermore, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows various vehicles upon śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, they give rise to a mind of reverence, a mind of respect, a mind regarding them as fields of merit, a mind regarding them as an ocean of merit, a mind that gives birth to merit and wisdom, a mind of deep faith in the merits of the Tathāgata, a mind that cultivates immeasurable billions of nayutas of pure roots of goodness, a mind that cultivates the pure practices of a bodhisattva for unspeakable eons, a mind liberated from all fetters of Māra, and a mind that crushes and destroys all the hosts of Māra’s armies."

With immeasurable, luminous, and pure wisdom, they are well able to discern all phenomena, causing all sentient beings to become the foremost field of merit worthy of trust, and to be fully endowed with the unsurpassed *dāna-pāramitā*;
causing all sentient beings to abandon useless speech, delighting in solitary seclusion, and maintaining a mind free from dualistic thoughts;
causing all sentient beings to become the most supreme, pure, and foremost field of merit, cultivating meritorious virtues, and gathering in all beings.
May all sentient beings become pools of wisdom, able to bestow upon them countless fruits of goodness;
may all sentient beings reach the most supreme field of merit—the realm of non-obstruction—pure and perfect;
may the minds of all sentient beings abide peacefully in the samādhi of non-contention, realizing that the nature of all phenomena is the absence of inherent nature.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with and nurture immeasurable merit, always encountering the most supreme and foremost field of blessings;
may all sentient beings manifest immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers, accordingly gathering in pure fields of blessings;
may all sentient beings accomplish inexhaustible fields of blessings of merit, capable of bestowing upon all the fruits of the vehicle of the ten powers.
May all sentient beings become true fields of merit, fully possessing the inexhaustible treasury of merit and ultimately attaining omniscience;
may all sentient beings extinguish all unwholesome dharmas and, upon hearing the Buddha’s true Dharma—both its phrasing and its flavor—be able to receive and uphold it entirely;
may all sentient beings universally hear the Buddha-Dharma and, according to what they hear, understand that its virtues are not in vain.

May all sentient beings hear the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma and reach the other shore; may they be able to expound the Buddha-dharma they have heard in accordance with the needs of sentient beings;
may all sentient beings always delight in the Dharma of the Tathāgata’s true teaching and eliminate all ninety-six kinds of heterodox views of external paths;
may all sentient beings constantly behold the worthy and holy ones and nurture all supreme roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings always behold those who delight in the perfection of knowledge and conduct, dwell together with them, and abide forever in peace and happiness;
may all sentient beings ensure that what they hear is not in vain, understand sounds to be like echoes, and witness the manifestation of Buddhas;
may all sentient beings skillfully discern and know the true teachings of all Buddhas, and be able to fully protect and uphold those who maintain the Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings always joyfully incline their minds toward hearing and upholding the Buddha-dharma, and be able to illuminate and manifest the teachings of the Tathāgata;

may all sentient beings, with deep resolve, believe in and understand all the merits of the Tathāgata’s true teaching, bringing joy to the Buddhas, skillfully understanding the ultimate truth, relinquishing both internal and external things, and perfecting the great giving.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when bestowing various vehicles upon Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas: to cause all sentient beings to attain supreme wisdom, purify all supernormal powers, practice with diligent effort free from indolence, and ultimately realize the Buddha-wisdom, the powers, and the fearlessnesses.

“If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas encounter all fields of merit coming from every direction—whether they come because they have heard the bodhisattva’s reputation, or because of a karmic connection with the bodhisattva, or because they have heard of the bodhisattva’s original vows, or because they have been invited by the bodhisattva’s mental aspiration—the bodhisattva shall joyfully bestow gifts upon them all without weariness.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva felt remorse toward those who had come seeking his help and spoke these words:
"All you people should know that I ought to go to them to pay homage, make offerings, and bestow various gifts;
yet now they have come from afar for my sake."

The Bodhisattva immediately paid homage and repented his transgressions, speaking with loving words to console and encourage him for having humbled himself to come from afar. He ensured that he was free from fatigue and established him in comfort, providing all that was required;
he might give a mani-jewel chariot carrying the foremost woman-treasure (*strī-ratna*) within Jambudvīpa, or he might give a golden chariot carrying the most excellent jewel-woman of his own kingdom.
Some gave pure lapis lazuli chariots carrying female attendants;
some gave musical chariots carrying young maidens whose countenances were like those of celestial beings;
and some gave immeasurable and innumerable chariots adorned with jewels, carrying precious women arrayed in various ornaments.
Some gave sandalwood chariots for the Bodhisattvas to ride;

others gave crystal jeweled chariots carrying precious women who were exceptionally beautiful and peerless in countenance, endowed with perfect deportment and composed in their movements, their bodies adorned with divine pearls and famous jewels as necklaces, and who delighted in practicing wholesome dharmas;
or some gave agate jeweled chariots carrying the crown princes.
Some gave solid, fragrant chariots carrying sons and daughters;
others gave chariots adorned with various jewels, carrying beloved and inseparable kinsmen and retinues.
With various precious chariots such as these, he bestows them all according to their requests, fulfilling their wishes and bringing them immeasurable joy.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practices the giving of vehicles, he dedicates the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings mount the non-retrogressive Mahāyāna vehicle and proceed to the inconceivable foot of the Bodhi tree."
May all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of great wisdom, so that throughout all kalpas of the future, they may cultivate and practice all the dharmas traversed by bodhisattvas;

may all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of non-existence, such that their minds have no attachment to any phenomena, they abandon all that is false and illusory, and they fully cultivate the path to omniscience;
may all sentient beings ride upon the stainless and tranquil vehicle, and through unimpeded spiritual power, travel to the buddha-fields of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings be firmly established in the vehicle of omniscience, constantly delighting themselves with the Dharma-pleasures of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the pure practices of Bodhisattvas, give birth to the tenfold path of Bodhisattvas, and joyfully cultivate all Bodhisattva samādhis;

may all sentient beings mount the four-wheeled vehicle—abiding in the wheel of the true realm, relying on the wheel of the true person, the wheel of fundamental merit, and the wheel of impartial vows—so that the pure conduct of Bodhisattvas may thereby be fulfilled.
May all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of the luminous Dharma, traveling throughout the ten directions to cultivate the power of a Buddha’s wisdom;
may all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of the Buddha-Dharma, reaching the ultimate further shore of all phenomena;
may all sentient beings ride upon the inconceivable vehicle of all meritorious roots and virtuous qualities, manifesting the path of peace and security for all beings in the ten directions.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of universal giving and sever the defilement of stinginess;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the pure *śīla-pāramitā* and be fully endowed with all pure precepts equal to the infinite and boundless *dharmadhātu*;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the *kṣānti-pāramitā*, abandon the mind of anger, and never give rise to malice or harm toward any sentient being.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the irreversible *vīrya-pāramitā*, fulfill the bodhisattva practices, and proceed to the site of enlightenment;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the *dhyāna-pāramitā* and swiftly hasten to the site of enlightenment;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the *prajñā-pāramitā* and manifest transformation bodies that fill all dharma realms and the spheres of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the Dharma King and accomplish the subtle Dharma of omniscience through the gift of fearlessness;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of non-attached wisdom and vows, able to enter universally into all directions while remaining non-entering within the true nature of phenomena;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the Buddhas' teachings, manifesting birth in all lands without ever destroying the Mahāyāna.
To cause all sentient beings to mount the vehicle of omniscience, fulfilling the bodhisattvas' impartial great vows without weariness or fatigue.

This is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s giving of various vehicles, universally bestowing immeasurable fields of merit upon sentient beings; by dedicating the roots of goodness with a joyful mind, they cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with immeasurable types of wisdom and to mount the vehicle of all-accomplishing knowledge.
“The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away the elephant-treasure:

its seven limbs are complete, its six humps are fully developed, its six tusks are like snow, and its mouth is as pure as a flower. Its body is level and upright, its coat is brilliant white, and it is adorned with rare, exquisite, and marvelous ornaments. A pure and wondrous net of jewels covers its back, and its head is embellished with various miscellaneous gems. Its radiance is dazzling, its bearing is calm and elegant, and in a mere instant it strides ten thousand *li*; its fierce spirit surges forth without ever tiring.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away precious horses:

their forms are exquisite, their coats are lustrous, and they possess all the characteristics of a horse, like the divine *aśvājāneya* steeds. Their bodies are adorned with immeasurable rare ornaments, with divine "bright moon" pearls providing radiance, and golden bells and jeweled nets covering them. They do not gallop recklessly, yet their speed surpasses that of a swift wind; they travel great distances without fatigue, providing comfort and security to those who ride them, and as they travel through the four quarters, they never fail to follow the master's intent.

With this precious vehicle, he gives as he wishes: whether bestowing it upon fields of merit, offering it to those worthy of respect, sending it to spiritual friends, presenting it to his parents, or providing for the poor and destitute; to all who have need, he gives everything. With a vast mind, he practices generosity without stinginess; his heart is always joyful and free from regret. Filled with great compassion, he is able to perform great acts of giving, single-mindedly and exclusively seeking the supreme birthplace of the bodhisattva’s merits, with a straightforward and pure mind.
They dedicate these roots of goodness with such a mind as follows:
"May all sentient beings achieve the treasure of humanity, give birth to the merits of a bodhisattva, and adorn the Mahāyāna;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of wholesome dharmas and, in accordance with it, reach all Buddha-dharmas."
May all sentient beings always delight in the Mahāyāna, attaining the Buddha’s vehicle of unimpeded wisdom-power and its light that shines everywhere;
may all sentient beings ride upon the courageous Mahāyāna, fulfilling all their aspirations;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the vehicle of the equal pāramitās, accomplishing and bringing to fulfillment all roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings achieve the precious vehicle and give birth to the jewel of the unsurpassed wisdom of the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings discern the adorned practices of Bodhisattvas, attain this wondrous vehicle, transcend the triple world, and fully open the flowers of all Bodhisattva samādhis;
may all sentient beings, for immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, purely cultivate the conduct of Bodhisattvas, mount the immeasurable vehicle, and swiftly understand all dharmas.
May all sentient beings be granted the precious Mahāyāna vehicle, and through skillful means, may they fulfill the stages of a bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings achieve the most supreme, vast, peaceful, and secure Mahāyāna, capable of transporting all beings to the unsurpassed path.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness from the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s giving of elephant and horse treasures throughout immeasurable, incalculable, and nayuta kalpas, which causes all sentient beings to mount the vehicle of unimpeded wisdom and reach the ultimate precious vehicle of the Tathāgata.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give various kinds of seats:
they may give the lion-throne of a noble cakravartin king, with feet made of lapis lazuli and a soft,
exquisite cloth woven of gold thread spread upon it, perfumed with all manner of enduring fragrances, and established in various ways.”
A most sublime jeweled banner, adorned with immeasurable billions of jewels, was covered above by a pure white jeweled net;
nets of golden bells emitted exquisite sounds, and hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of pure and wondrous jeweled images surrounded it on all sides.
That seat was lofty and vast, pure and magnificently decorated, [extending for] immeasurable *arhat*s...
Countless sentient beings gaze upon him with delight, never wearying; his merit surpasses that of all under heaven. This is the place where the Sovereign Great King sits;
seated upon that throne, he governs the kingdom with righteousness, such that none dare to oppose him.
His body is adorned with various exquisite jewels: the sovereign king of blue gems, the sovereign king of great blue gems, and the jewel of supreme treasury.
Adorned with such majesty, he was as bright and pure as the sun and as cool as the moon;
he was graced by a multitude of stars and possessed the supreme jewels of the ocean and the firm banners of the sea.
Stainless and radiant, his head was crowned with a fillet of exquisite Jāmbūnada gold and precious silks; he was a mighty consecrated king within all of Jambudvīpa.
The Dharma is used to consecrate his crown; possessing the power of merit as a Lord of Great Compassion, he subdues enemies so that none dare disobey his commands.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva thus becomes an immeasurable and incalculable Wheel-Turning King, attaining mastery over the Dharma and governing the country with righteousness, he uses such various seats adorned with many jewels to make offerings—whether to the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, spiritual friends, and the assembly of noble sages, or out of joy upon hearing the Dharma, to bestow them upon Dharma teachers, to support his parents and those worthy of respect, to the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all Bodhisattvas, even down to those who have first resolved to attain the Mahāyāna, and to all the stūpas and temples of the Buddhas—or he may give them to the countless poor and lowly, providing whatever they require or desire.
When giving a seat, one should dedicate the merit as follows:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain the seat of Bodhi and spontaneously awaken to the True Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the seat of mastery, fully accomplishing mastery over all dharmas, remaining indestructible by any adamantine mountains, and being able to subdue all māras."
May all sentient beings attain the sovereign lion-throne of the Buddhas, which all beings delight in beholding without weariness;
may all sentient beings attain unspeakably unspeakable thrones of pure adornment and exquisite beauty, attaining mastery over the Dharma and universally transforming sentient beings;
may all sentient beings attain the supreme throne, indestructible by the three worlds, wherein their vast roots of goodness and the perfection of those roots are entirely purified.

May all sentient beings attain high and vast seats that fill unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, such that even the Buddhas and Tathāgatas could not exhaustively praise them throughout incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*);
may all sentient beings occupy the seat of those of great wisdom, with a single body filling the entire Dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings attain seats adorned with inconceivable jewels, whereby they extensively provide the gift of Dharma to the sentient beings invited according to their original vows.
May all sentient beings attain the pure and wondrous Dharma-throne, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata throughout unspeakable worlds;

may all sentient beings sit upon thrones of all jewels, thrones of all fragrances, thrones of all flowers, thrones of all garments, thrones of all garlands, thrones of all mani-jewels, inconceivable thrones of pure lapis lazuli, thrones of immeasurable and unspeakable worlds, thrones adorned by the purification of all sentient beings, and the throne of freedom from strife; and while dwelling upon these thrones, may they awaken to the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes and manifest the spheres of merit of all Buddhas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives various kinds of seats, so that all sentient beings may attain the seat of unattached awakening and spontaneously realize all Buddha-dharmas.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha of Great Extensive Meaning, Scroll Sixteen;
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha of Great Extensive Meaning, Scroll Seventeen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master from India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Fourth Part of the Twenty-first Chapter, "The Ten Dedications" of the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja:
"The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva bestows various canopies, namely:
canopies for honoring and respecting others, adorned with various exquisite jewels, which are the foremost among immeasurable and boundless decorated canopies;..."

With poles made of various jewels, covered by nets of gold, and with necklaces of assorted gems hanging all around, it was hung with many jeweled bells; pure lapis lazuli beads moved slightly against one another, producing harmonious and elegant sounds, while pure white jewel-nets were interlaced and entwined about them. Hundreds of thousands of pure and diverse jewel-nets covered its top, adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of miscellaneous jewels, and perfumed with the solid fragrance of immeasurable billions of *nāyuta* measures of aloeswood and sandalwood, all beautifully decorated with pure Jāmbūnada gold.
With immeasurable, incalculable, and nayuta numbers of such canopies, they practice giving with a mind free from ill-will, a vast mind, and a mind of relinquishment;
they do so either by making offerings to the Buddhas currently living, or by making offerings to stupas and shrines after their parinirvāṇa.

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, they offer gifts to Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends, or to Dharma teachers, or to their parents, or to the Saṃgha; or they offer gifts to all the teachings of the Buddha, or to various individuals who are fields of merit, or to teachers, elders, and those worthy of respect; or they give to those who have first resolved upon Bodhicitta, or to all who are poor and lowly—granting whatever is requested by all such beings.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives a parasol, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be covered by roots of goodness and protected by the shade of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be shielded by wisdom and merit, and may they eliminate the defilements of all worldly afflictions."
May all sentient beings be covered by the pure Dharma, so that all the heat and affliction of their defilements are extinguished;
may all sentient beings fully attain the internal treasury of wisdom of the Tathāgata, such that all beings gaze upon it with joy without weariness;
may all sentient beings cover themselves with the serene white Dharma, so that they all attain the ultimate, indestructible Buddha-Dharma.
May all sentient beings obtain a well-covered body, ultimately attaining the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings act as a covering for all, with the wisdom of the ten powers universally covering the world;
may all sentient beings attain the wisdom that accords with their aspirations, transcending all worlds, pure, clear, and penetrating, without any defilement or attachment.
May all sentient beings obtain the parasol of being worthy of offerings, becoming supreme fields of merit that receive all offerings;
may all sentient beings obtain the most supreme parasol, spontaneously awakening to the parasol of unsurpassed wisdom.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas offer canopies, causing all sentient beings to uphold the canopy of mastery over the Dharma; to universally cover all worlds throughout the entire Dharma-realm and space-realm with a single canopy of merit; to manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas; to adorn the Dharma-realm with a single canopy of merit and make offerings to all Buddhas; to have wondrous banners, standards, and canopies universally cover all Tathāgatas of the ten directions;
to cause all Buddha-lands to be adorned with various precious canopies;
and to cause all sentient beings to joyfully seek unexcelled Bodhi, universally covering all beings with the canopy of the Unexcelled.
May all sentient beings offer exquisite canopies adorned with unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all kinds of jewels to a single Buddha, and likewise offer them to all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings spontaneously awaken to the attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment and obtain canopies of lofty, vast, subtle, and wondrous merit that universally cover all Buddhas;
and may all sentient beings offer various jeweled canopies to all Buddhas throughout the Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and all other worlds.

May all sentient beings, with various mani-jewel canopies adorned on all sides by hanging jewel necklaces, and with canopies of all solid fragrances adorned with pure miscellaneous jewels—extremely vast, high, and wide, covered above by nets of white pure jewels and surrounded by nets of golden bells that spontaneously produce subtle and wondrous sounds—make offerings of such immeasurable and incalculable canopies to all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain the canopy of unobstructed wisdom, universally covering all Buddhas of the ten directions;
may all sentient beings obtain the canopy of supreme wisdom, universally covering all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings obtain the precious canopy adorned with the merits of the Buddhas, universally covering all beings;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with pure great vows and the merits of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the jewel of inconceivable, pure mind.
May all sentient beings be brought to fulfillment in the wisdom of mastery over all dharmas;
may all sentient beings universally cover all beings with their roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings obtain the canopy of supreme wisdom and universally cover all beings.
May all sentient beings obtain the canopy of the ten powers to universally cover all beings;
may all sentient beings be able to universally cover the entire dharma-realm with a single buddha-field;
and may all sentient beings attain mastery over all dharmas.
May all sentient beings attain mastery over their minds;
may all sentient beings possess wisdom that is supreme and vast;
may all sentient beings, through immeasurable merit, be able to universally shelter all other sentient beings.
May all sentient beings have their minds covered by all manner of meritorious virtues;
may all sentient beings universally cover all things with a mind of equanimity;
may all sentient beings equally cover all things with great wisdom.
May all sentient beings be endowed with great dedication;
may all sentient beings fulfill their pure and upright minds;
and may the mental faculties of all sentient beings be purified.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives various canopies, causing all sentient beings to fully accomplish the greatest dedication, universally covering and gathering in all sentient beings.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give various kinds of pure banners and streamers:”

It had immeasurable miscellaneous jewels for its shafts, with various precious silks forming hanging banners and diverse colored fabrics draped all around. A pure white jewel net covered it from above, adorned with nets of golden bells that produced harmonious and elegant sounds when stirred by a gentle breeze. It was accompanied by an immeasurable and countless number of billions of nayutas of exquisite pennants and streamers, decorated with hanging silk ribbons of various jewels. Jeweled images of half-moons made of Jambūnada gold emitted great radiance, shining everywhere like the sun; these ornate jewel banners filled the entire earth, adorned according to the karmic rewards of joy throughout all worlds, and were established within all the Tathāgata-fields of space and the Dharma-realm.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, throughout all worlds, universally bestows sublime banners according to the inclinations of beings, causing them to give rise to the upright mind of bodhi. He may bestow them upon all present Buddhas, or bestow them upon stupas and temples, or bestow them upon the Jewel of the Dharma, or bestow them upon the Jewel of the Sangha, or bestow them upon spiritual friends, or bestow them upon Bodhisattvas, or bestow them upon Śrāvakas, or bestow them upon Pratyekabuddhas, or bestow them upon the great assemblies, or bestow them upon individuals (pudgala), or bestow them upon the poor; to all who come seeking, he gives universally without exception.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives banners and streamers, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings establish the banners and streamers of all roots of goodness and merits so that they cannot be destroyed;
may all sentient beings establish the banners of sovereignty over all dharmas and protect the True Dharma."
May all sentient beings protect the precious Dharma and uphold the profound teachings of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings establish lofty and manifest jeweled victory banners of merit, kindle the lamp of wisdom, and universally illumine all beings;
may all sentient beings become indestructible banners and streamers, subduing all demons and evil karmas.
May all sentient beings establish the banner and pennant of the power of wisdom, which cannot be destroyed by any demons;
may all sentient beings obtain the supreme banner and pennant of the great wisdom of Nārāyaṇa, crushing and destroying all worldly banners and pennants;
may all sentient beings erect the sun-banner of the perfect light of liberating wisdom, fully endowed with insight to universally illumine the Dharma-realm.

May all sentient beings obtain the jeweled banners and streamers adorned with wisdom, filling all Buddha-worlds, erecting unspeakably many supreme and wondrous banners and streamers to make offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions;
may all sentient beings obtain the banner of the Tathāgata, destroying and extinguishing all ninety-six kinds of banners of false views.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives banners and streamers: to cause all sentient beings to erect the high, vast, and profound banner of bodhisattva practice; to erect the banner of the sovereign practices of all bodhisattvas; and to attain the path of purity.
"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva opens the treasuries of various jewels and practices giving, they dedicate the merit in this way:
'By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings always behold the Jewel of the Buddha, abandon ignorance, and practice right mindfulness;
may all sentient beings attain the illumination of the Jewel of the Dharma and uphold the Dharma-treasuries of all Buddhas.'"
May all sentient beings embrace the Jewel of the Sangha, abandon stinginess, practice generosity, and fulfill their aspirations;
may all sentient beings attain the jewel of the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), never regressing from the pure bodhicitta;
and may all sentient beings cross over the jewel of wisdom, forever leave behind ignorance, and reach the ultimate realization of the Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings accomplish the jewel-treasures of all bodhisattva merits and expound the wondrous jewel-treasure of immeasurable wisdom;
may all sentient beings praise the jewel-treasure of immeasurable merit, cultivate the wisdom of the ten powers, and attain the jewel of perfect enlightenment;
may all sentient beings obtain the sixteen jewel-treasures of wisdom, enter the correct reception of samādhi, and ultimately expand and broaden the jewel-treasure of wisdom.
May all sentient beings achieve the jewel of the foremost field of merit, awakening to the Tathāgata’s jewel of unsurpassed wisdom;
may all sentient beings become supreme jewels, inexhaustible treasuries of eloquence, expounding the jewel of the Dharma.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow various jewels, so as to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the jewel of ultimate, unsurpassed wisdom and to attain the Buddha’s unimpeded, pure eye-jewel.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give away their ornaments as gifts to sentient beings, namely:

all ornaments for the body, ornaments for the limbs and joints, ornaments that purify the body, ornaments of insatiable splendor, and ornaments of various precious interwoven decorations. Having bestowed such various and immeasurable billions of nayutas of ornaments, they dedicate all roots of goodness [with this aspiration]:

‘May the bodies of all sentient beings be adorned with purity; may they regard all equally as if they were an only child; may they transcend the world and attain the bliss of Buddha-wisdom; may they subdue sentient beings, causing them to delight in the profound Dharma and abide securely within all the teachings of the Buddhas.’”
May all sentient beings be adorned as celestial and human beings, all of them self-adorned with pure wisdom;
may all sentient beings have bodies purified and adorned, fully endowed with the gates of merit and marks;
may all sentient beings have their bodies adorned with sublime marks, self-adorned with the excellence of a hundred blessings.
May all sentient beings be endowed with perfect physical forms, adorning themselves with the various marks and signs;
may all sentient beings have their speech adorned, fully possessing an inexhaustible treasury of eloquence;
may all sentient beings adorn their voices with all manner of merits, their Brahma-voices being pure, subtle, and complete.
May all sentient beings be inspired with a resolute aspiration for the adornment of the Buddha-dharma, hearing and receiving the True Dharma so that all Buddhas rejoice;
may all sentient beings adorn themselves with the adornment of the mind, attaining the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* and seeing all Buddhas everywhere;
may all sentient beings adorn themselves with the adornment of various *dhāraṇīs*, attaining the illumination of the Buddha-dharma and perceiving all the teachings of the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings adorn their minds with the wisdom of equanimity and adorn their Dharma-bodies with the wisdom of the Tathāgata.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow all ornaments, so that all sentient beings may become fully perfected in the adornments of the immeasurable merits, wisdom, and qualities of the Buddha-dharma, and so that all sentient beings may abandon self-importance, arrogance, and negligence.

“The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva acts as a consecrated great king, possessing sovereign power and majesty. He bestows celestial crowns and the bright pearls from within their topknots, providing for all and gathering in sentient beings. He nurtures the mind of giving, perfumes the mind with giving, and turns toward superior giving. Through giving he cultivates wisdom; through giving he cultivates the faculty of equanimity; through giving he cultivates vast awakening.”
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away the bright jewel from his topknot, he dedicates the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be well-empowered by the consecration of the Dharma-King of All-Knowledge;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the mark of the crown-protrusion (*uṣṇīṣa*), attain the summit of supreme wisdom, and reach the other shore."
May all sentient beings attain the jewel of supreme wisdom and reach the ultimate pinnacle of all merits;
may all sentient beings fully abide upon the crest-jewel of wisdom, becoming worthy of receiving the prostrations of all with reverent hearts;
may all sentient beings be crowned with the celestial tiara of wisdom, attaining sovereign mastery over all phenomena.
May all sentient beings bind the bright jewel of wisdom upon their crowns, such that no one in any world can see the top of their heads;
may all sentient beings be worthy of receiving reverent prostrations, possessing the crown of wisdom that illuminates the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings achieve the crown of the ten powers to adorn their heads, with the ocean-treasury of the jewels of knowledge pure and complete.

May all sentient beings abide securely as sovereign lords of the supreme great earth, crush the crowns of all Māras, attain supreme perfect enlightenment, and ultimately be fully endowed with the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings become victorious crest-kings and obtain the most supreme light of the crown of omniscience.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when relinquishing their celestial crowns and luminous pearls: to cause the supreme and wondrous wisdom of all sentient beings to be entirely pure, so that they may obtain the maṇi-jewel crown of pure wisdom.
"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas see sentient beings in prisons undergoing various forms of torment—

whether bound, beaten, confined in darkness, shackled with cangues and manacles, subjected to torture until blood flows, suffering unbearable hunger and thirst, naked and emaciated, with disheveled hair covering their bodies—

they endure immeasurable suffering with no one to save them. Having seen such suffering beings, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas may relinquish wealth, treasures, wives, children, and kinsmen, or even sacrifice their own bodies, to rescue those suffering beings within the prisons, just as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Compassion (Mahākāruṇika) and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva King Good Eyes (Sudarśana-rāja) did."
Having rescued sentient beings from within those hells, he bestows upon them whatever they require.

He may provide medical treatments or incantations to bring them peace and security; first causing them to rejoice, he then preaches the Dharma to them, establishing them all in the roots of goodness of heedfulness so that their minds do not regress from the teaching of the Perfectly Awakened One.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva rescues those in prison, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be liberated from the bonds of craving;
may all sentient beings sever the stream of birth and death and reach the further shore of wisdom."
May all sentient beings extinguish the darkness of ignorance and attain clear, pure wisdom; may they uproot the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) and be free from all defilements;
may all sentient beings sever the bonds of the triple world and attain omniscience (*sarvajñā*);
may all sentient beings forever extinguish the fetters and outflows (*āsrava*), attain the stage beyond afflictions, bring their unimpeded wisdom to ultimate perfection, and reach the other shore.
To cause all sentient beings to be free from the bonds of craving and pride, ultimately achieving the wisdom that is free from craving and pride;
to cause all sentient beings to be liberated from the bonds of all desires, forever departing from all worldly greed and attachment, dwelling in all worlds without being defiled or attached;
to cause all sentient beings to attain a pure and profound mind, constantly protected by all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain a mind free from attachment and bondage, as vast as the Dharma-realm and ultimate as space;
may all sentient beings attain the spiritual powers of a bodhisattva, traveling throughout all lands to tame sentient beings, renounce the world, and dwell securely in the Mahāyāna.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas to rescue suffering sentient beings, so as to cause all sentient beings to ultimately reach the stage of Tathāgata wisdom.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas see those condemned prisoners being led to the place of execution, bound by the fivefold fetters, their hearts pierced by grief and distress, their lives hanging by a thread, surrounded by a multitude of people; they abandon all the pleasures of Jambudvīpa and are forever separated from their loved ones as they gradually proceed to the place of death.

Some are impaled on wooden stakes atop high pillars, some are cut with knives, some are burned with fire, and some have their bodies wrapped in oil-soaked cloth and set ablaze—undergoing such immeasurable sufferings as these.”

Having seen this, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva sacrifices his own body and life to rescue them from their suffering and distress, just as the bodhisattvas such as Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Jayottara-rāja, and other great bodhisattvas, sacrificed their own bodies and endured all manner of agonizing torments to save sentient beings, saying:
"I shall sacrifice my body to take the place of their lives; even if the pain exceeds theirs immeasurably, I will endure it all on their behalf so that they may attain liberation."
Again, he thought: "To see such suffering and not take it upon oneself is to lose a great benefit. Why is this?"

For the sake of sentient beings, and for the purpose of protecting and rescuing them, I have resolved upon the bodhicitta of omniscience; therefore, I sacrifice my own body to take their lives in its stead.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva rescues suffering beings, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain inexhaustible bodies and lives, forever departing from the burning afflictions of grief and sorrow;
may all sentient beings abide by the Buddhas and receive the prediction of enlightenment through the power of all-knowledge."
May all sentient beings rescue themselves from all fears and forever leave the evil realms behind;
may all sentient beings attain the life of all things and forever enter the realm of deathless wisdom;
may all sentient beings remain far removed from enemies and adversaries, and be constantly gathered under the protection of Buddhas and spiritual friends.
May all sentient beings abandon weapons and staves, and cultivate pure karma;
may all sentient beings be freed from all terrors, sit beneath the Bodhi tree, and subdue the armies of Māra;
may all sentient beings be free from fear of great assemblies, and attain the pure, fearless Great Lion’s Roar within the unsurpassed Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded lion-like wisdom and practice pure deeds;
may all sentient beings reach the state of fearlessness and rescue and protect all beings suffering from affliction.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas sacrifice their own bodies and lives to save those condemned to death, so as to cause all sentient beings to leave behind the suffering of birth and death and ultimately attain the bliss of Buddhahood.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for the hair of his head, including the skin, as well as the bright jewel from his topknot, the Bodhisattva joyfully bestows it upon them, just like the great Bodhisattvas such as Cūḍāmaṇi-rāja and Jayagati.

When someone begs for the hair of his head, including the skin, and the bright jewel, he contemplates with right mind, not thinking of other activities; detached from all worldly things, he delights exclusively in tranquility, maintains pure right mindfulness, and cultivates a straightforward mind toward omniscience."

At that time, the Bodhisattva took a sharp blade in his hand and immediately cut off his skin and hair, including the jewel from his topknot. With his right knee touching the ground, he joined his palms in reverence and, with right mindfulness of the practices performed by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, gave rise to great joy. His mind was upright and pure;
all true dharmas filled his mental faculty, and his heart felt no sense of suffering—for what is called suffering is a phenomenon of arising and ceasing, a phenomenon of impermanence.
Having formed this thought, he extinguished all suffering and joyfully practiced giving, dedicating the roots of goodness as follows:
"May all sentient beings attain the mark of the invisible crown of the head (*anavalokitamūrdhatā*), achieving the *uṣṇīṣa* as a venerable stūpa;
may all sentient beings attain hair of deep blue-black color, hair like a diamond, and hair that is soft and supple, so that they may completely eliminate the afflictions of all defilements."
May all sentient beings obtain hair that is not disheveled and hair that is lustrous;
may all sentient beings obtain hair that is soft, curling, and spiral;
may all sentient beings obtain hair that curls to the right.
May all sentient beings obtain the hair of a Buddha’s marks, with all afflictions, fetters, and habitual tendencies completely extinguished;
may all sentient beings’ hair emit great radiance, universally illuminating the ten directions;
may all sentient beings obtain the pure and unconfused hair of a Buddha.
May all sentient beings obtain hair for the reliquary stūpas of those worthy of offerings, thereby eliminating their evil minds and beholding the hair of the Tathāgata;
may the hair of all sentient beings be free from all dust and defilement, so that they all attain the unstained hair of the Tathāgata.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving away their top-knot hair and the bright jewel from their topknots: to cause all sentient beings to fully attain all dhāraṇīs, all gates of samādhi, all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), and the ten powers of a Buddha.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away his eyes, he cultivates the mind of giving eyes just as the Bodhisattva Pramuditā, the Bodhisattva Pūrṇacandrarāja, and countless other great Bodhisattvas cultivated when they gave their eyes; he cultivates the mind of the wisdom-eye, attains the mind of the Buddha-Dharma-eye, directs his mind toward the Unsurpassed Way, perfects the minds of all supernormal powers, and single-mindedly seeks the mind of wisdom, cultivating the mind of wise giving equal to that of the Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
Toward those who beg for his eyes, he looks with eyes of love and gives them his eyes with an indestructible mind of faith;
thereby he gives rise to the Buddha-eye, expands the Mahāyāna mind of Bodhi, and through great kindness and great compassion, subdues the six sense faculties."

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates such a mind, they practice giving with their eyes; they always delight in bestowing them, establish the True Dharma, abandon worldly pleasures and negligence, grow weary of the five desires, and take joy in the bodhicitta. According to whatever others seek, they fulfill all their wishes, nurturing an impartial and non-dual generosity. Whatever is required, they are able to give it all, dedicating these roots of goodness thus:
"May all sentient beings attain clear vision, becoming eyes for the world;
may all sentient beings obtain unobstructed eyes, opening wide the treasury of wisdom."
May all sentient beings attain the pure fleshly eye, which none in any world can destroy;
may all sentient beings attain the pure celestial eye, seeing all beings die here and be born there;
may all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-eye, being able to accord with and enter the realm of the Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings attain the pure eye of wisdom, discerning and understanding all worlds;
may all sentient beings attain the pure Buddha-eye, being able to awaken to all dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain the universally pure eye, reaching the ultimate realm without any obstruction.
May all sentient beings eliminate the cataracts of ignorance and attain the pure eye, realizing that the realm of sentient beings is empty and devoid of intrinsic existence;
may all sentient beings attain the unobstructed eye and reach the supreme state of the Tathāgata’s ten powers.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives their eyes, causing all sentient beings to attain the eye of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives their ears, they do so as the Bodhisattva Jayarāja and the Bodhisattva Jayānāmaitrī gave their ears when practicing the bodhisattva path, being born into the family of the Tathāgatas, and cultivating the giving practiced by all Buddhas. They maintain right mindfulness of all the pure practices of bodhisattvas, accord with the enlightenment of all Buddhas, and give rise to the merit of the wisdom of the pure faculties. They observe that nothing in the world is solid or enduring;
they cause all sentient beings to constantly see all Buddhas and bodhisattvas, remain free from attachment to their own bodies, and accord with right mindfulness of all Buddha-dharmas.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away his ears, his mind is tranquil and he subdues all the sense faculties. He rescues sentient beings from perilous wildernesses, generates the merit of the lamp of wisdom, and accomplishes the ocean of *dānapāramitā*. His resolve for giving becomes fulfilled; he understands meaning and knows the Dharma, clearly discerning all paths and attaining the practice of wisdom. He gains mastery over all phenomena and exchanges this non-solid body for a solid body.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away their ears, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain unimpeded ears, so that they may universally hear immeasurable sounds of the Dharma and realize them without obstruction;
may all sentient beings attain unimpeded ears, discerning and fully understanding immeasurable sounds."
May all sentient beings attain the unobstructed ear and the pure ear of a Buddha;
may all sentient beings attain the purified ear and understand that the faculty of hearing is empty and non-existent;
may all sentient beings attain the vast ear, wherein all consciousnesses are utterly tranquil and do not arise.
May all sentient beings attain ears equal to the Dharma-realm, so that they may skillfully hear and retain all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain unattached ears, so that they may discern all dharmas without obstruction;
may all sentient beings attain indestructible ears, such that no heterodox arguments can destroy them.
May all sentient beings attain universally pervasive ears, vast and pure;
may all sentient beings attain the divine ear and the Buddha-ear.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away their ears, so that all sentient beings may attain pure ears.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away his nose, he dedicates this merit with such purity:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain the nose-mark of a Tathāgata; may they obtain a nose of excellent features, a nose that inspires love and joy, a pure nose, a harmonious nose, a high and beautiful nose, a nose that subdues enemies, and the nose of a Tathāgata.

May all sentient beings obtain a handsome face; may they obtain the gateway to all dharmas, the unobstructed gateway, the gateway of excellent manifestation, the gateway of insatiability, the pure gateway, the gateway free from evil, the perfect face-gateway of all Tathāgatas, the gateway of all things, and the gateway of excellent, joyful, and immeasurable qualities."
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives their nose, so as to cause all sentient beings to ultimately enter into the teachings of all Buddhas;
to cause all sentient beings to embrace the true Dharma of all Buddhas of the ten directions;
and to cause all sentient beings to discern and deeply understand the wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings reach the further shore of all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings constantly behold all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the immeasurable Dharma-gates of all Tathāgatas.
To cause all sentient beings to attain ultimate purity;
to cause all sentient beings to attain the illumination of the Buddha-dharma, universally shining upon all phenomena;
and to cause all sentient beings to attain the adornment and purification of Buddha-fields.
May all sentient beings attain the Buddha’s firm and indestructible body.
