This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives away their nose.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in the stage of the Sovereign Great King, they are able to give their own teeth to sentient beings. Just as when the Bodhisattva Flower-Toothed King and the Bodhisattva Six-Tusked White Elephant King gave their teeth, they attained a mind difficult to obtain: a pure mind of giving like the *udumbara* flower; an inexhaustible mind of giving; an unclouded mind of giving; an unattached mind of giving; an immeasurable mind of giving; a mind that tames and relinquishes the sense faculties; a mind of universal giving; a mind aspiring for all-knowledge; a mind that brings peace and security to sentient beings; a perfected mind of giving; a great mind of giving; and a supreme mind of giving."

Of the essential parts of the body, the teeth are the most vital; they are what one holds most dear and what others most deeply cherish. Yet, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to bestow them as a gift upon all who beg for them.
When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this Dharma and gives away his teeth, he dedicates the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain pure white fangs, become supreme reliquaries, and receive offerings from devas and humans."
May all sentient beings obtain the Buddha’s mark of teeth that are even, closely set, and without gaps;
may all sentient beings practice the subduing of the mind and advance toward the various pāramitās of the bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings have pure mouths and teeth, appearing bright and clear.
May all sentient beings attain the adornment of the mouth through mindfulness, with the marks of the teeth fully perfected, opening forth in fresh and pure brilliance;
may all sentient beings possess forty teeth that constantly emit immeasurable, pure, and wondrous fragrances;
may all sentient beings attain the adornment of the color and form of the whorled-tooth-flower, abiding securely therein, and be able to subdue their minds.
May all sentient beings obtain pure tusks, capable of emitting immeasurable billions of rays of light—fresh, clean, and perfect—which universally illuminate the ten directions;

may all sentient beings obtain slow-chewing tusks, such that when food enters the mouth, every grain is crushed as it turns, so that they have no attachment to flavors and become supreme fields of merit;
may all sentient beings obtain supremely wondrous tusks, emitting light of immeasurable colors and receiving the prediction of Bodhi.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his teeth, so as to cause all sentient beings to attain the unimpeded, adorned, and pure wisdom of all dharmas.
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva encounters someone who comes to beg for their tongue, they address the petitioner with gentle words,
affectionate words, and words born of a heart of compassion, giving rise to a mind of consolation,
just as the Bodhisattva King Fine Mouth, the Bodhisattva Non-Retrogression, and other immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas did."
When undergoing immeasurable births throughout the various realms of existence, if there is a beggar for a tongue, one first establishes that beggar upon a lion throne;
then, at the time of relinquishing one’s own tongue, one does so with a joyful mind, an uncorrupted mind,
a mind free from resentment, a great mind, a mind born into the family of the Buddhas, a mind established in the lineage of the Bodhisattvas, and an unturbid mind.
With a mind of courageous diligence, a mind unattached to his own person, and a mind free from enmity,
he knelt with his right knee on the ground, extended his tongue to show it, and spoke words that were gentle,
affectionate, and imbued with compassion, saying to the beggar:
"Take my tongue and use it as you wish; let it satisfy your desires.
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away his tongue, he dedicates the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain the mark of the broad and long tongue, and be able to produce all perfect sounds."
May all sentient beings attain the mark of a tongue that covers the face, such that their speech is non-dual and entirely truthful;
may all sentient beings have tongues capable of covering all Buddha-fields, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas;
and may all sentient beings attain soft and thin tongues, proclaiming and conveying the foremost, supreme, pure flavors.
May all sentient beings attain the tongue of right speech, such that all who hear their words rejoice and the net of doubt is entirely removed;
may all sentient beings attain the tongue of pure light, capable of emitting unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of rays of light;
may all sentient beings attain definitive speech, skillfully able to discern the inexhaustible treasury of the Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain pure and superior tongues, becoming skilled in all vocal sounds and ultimately accomplishing the work of teaching and transforming others;
may all sentient beings attain the wisdom of sound, becoming skillfully able to accord with and enter the ocean of languages;
may all sentient beings be skillfully able to expound all dharmas, giving rise to wisdom regarding all languages and reaching the other shore.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives away their tongue, so that all sentient beings may attain unimpeded wisdom and have all their vows fulfilled.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva encounters sentient beings who come to beg for their heads, they do so like the unsurpassed wise Bodhisattva, the noble son King Kāśyapa, and other such immeasurable great Bodhisattvas who, when giving their heads, desire to obtain the head of all wondrous wisdom;
desire to obtain the head of unsurpassed bodhi to rescue and protect sentient beings;
and desire to behold the head of all wondrous dharmas."
Desiring to see the head of all pure wisdom;
desiring to be endowed with the head of all unimpeded dharmas;
desiring to see the ground of the most supreme and wondrous head.
If you wish to attain the head of supreme wisdom, which all sentient beings love and cherish;
if you wish to possess the head of the treasury of the true Dharma of wisdom, which cannot be beheld by any sentient being;
if you wish to become a king of great wisdom endowed with the ten powers; and if you wish to attain the head of mastery over all dharmas in their full perfection;
That which cannot be destroyed by any world.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this abiding in the Dharma, they study all that the Buddhas have studied, place deep faith in all Buddhas, and nurture their roots of goodness. To those who come seeking, they fulfill their desires and cause them all to rejoice; with a pure mind, the Bodhisattva gives with joy.

Cherishing the Buddha-Dharma, they attain pure clarity, abide securely in Bodhi, and their minds do not regress. They are able to practice great renunciation, their faculties are joyful and glad, they increase the wondrous Dharma, and with an upright and virtuous mind, they are able to give extensively.
When a bodhisattva gives away their head, they dedicate the merit in this way:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain the head of a Tathāgata—a crown that no one in any world can see, which cannot be destroyed in any place, which transcends all worlds, and which is endowed with the mark of the uṣṇīṣa, adorned with coiled hair, unprecedented in all the world, obtaining the foremost mark of a Buddha, magnificent, supreme, and extraordinary;
and may all sentient beings obtain the head of wisdom, the most excellent head, the pure head, and the head endowed with wisdom."

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives his head, so as to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the supreme Dharma and to attain the head of unsurpassed, great wisdom.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas bestow their hands and feet upon sentient beings, such as the Bodhisattva Viryendra-rāja (King of Valour) and the Bodhisattva Abhaya (Fearless), and other such immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Throughout immeasurable births within the various realms of existence, they give away their hands and feet; they cultivate the hand of faith, constantly practice the True Dharma, and benefit sentient beings. Their deportment is dignified and orderly, with the ‘Precious Hand’ foremost among them; they possess the hand that gives without attachment. The conduct of these bodhisattvas is true and not in vain; their intention to give is vast, they establish roots of goodness, remain far removed from stinginess and greed, and fulfill the bodhisattva practices. Toward the Tathāgata, they attain indestructible faith, eliminate the evil destinies, and achieve awakening.”

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give their hands and feet, they do so with an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind, opening the gates of the pure Dharma, entering the ocean of all Buddhas, and beholding all Buddhas. They perfect the giving of hands, fulfilling the intentions of sentient beings, and are able to fully uphold all vows for the Bodhi of All-Knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*). Cultivating a pure mind, they are freed from the entanglements of afflictions (*kleśa*), attaining the wisdom-body (*jñānakāya*) and the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*), which are uninterrupted, indestructible, and imperishable. No demonic activities can shake them; they draw near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) and practice the sites of all Bodhisattva generosity, giving birth to the realm of all-knowledge of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
When giving hands and feet, one should dedicate the merit in this way:

"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings obtain precious hands and be endowed with supernatural powers. Having attained precious hands, may they respect one another, conceive the mind of a field of merit, and mutually provide offerings with various kinds of jewels;
furthermore, adorning them with manifold jewels, may they make offerings to all Buddhas, raising clouds of exquisite jewels that pervade all Buddha-fields."

May all sentient beings cultivate loving-kindness and compassion, refraining from harming one another; may they travel through the buddha-fields and dwell securely in fearlessness. Through minimal effort, may they perfect the divine powers (*ṛddhipāda*). With jewel-hands, incense-hands, robe-hands, parasol-hands, garland-hands, flower-hands, powdered-incense-hands, ornament-hands, immeasurable-flower-hands, immeasurable-incense-hands, and universal-hands, may they go to the various buddha-fields by means of their supernormal powers to make offerings to the Buddhas.
May they be able to stroke all buddha-worlds with a single hand;
may they, with hands of sovereign divine power, support all sentient beings, and with perfected hand-marks, emit immeasurable light.
To be able to universally cover all sentient beings with a single hand, thereby attaining the Buddha’s mark of webbed hands and feet—
this is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s Great Dedication-Hand that universally covers all sentient beings;
it causes all sentient beings to constantly and joyfully aspire to seek unsurpassed bodhi.
May all sentient beings give birth to an immeasurable great ocean of merit and attain the mind of forbearance;
may they feel great joy upon seeing those who come to seek their help, never tiring of observing them, enter the deep ocean of the Dharma, and attain the roots of goodness shared by all Buddhas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give their hands and feet.

Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who sever their own bodies to draw blood and give it to sentient beings—such as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmahasta, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pramuditacittarāja, and countless other Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas—sever their bodies and draw blood to give as gifts to those who beg for it throughout immeasurable births within the various realms of existence.

They give with the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*); they give with joy in the bodhicitta; they give with a mind that delights in cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva; they give with a mind that does not calculate suffering or pain; they give with a mind free from resentment toward those who come to beg; they give with a mind directed toward all bodhisattvas; they give with a mind that nurtures all bodhisattvas; they give with a mind that expands the wholesome mind of a bodhisattva; they give with a mind of non-retrogression; they give with a tireless mind; and they give with a mind that does not begrudge themselves.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives a gift by breaking their own body and shedding blood, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the Dharma-body and the Wisdom-body of a bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings achieve the subtle, secret, adamantine body."
May all sentient beings attain an inexhaustible body, pure and indestructible;
may all sentient beings attain manifest transformation bodies that pervade all worlds throughout the ten directions;
may all sentient beings attain a delightful body, luminous, pure, and fresh, which cannot be impaired or destroyed.
May all sentient beings attain a body born of the Dharma-realm, remaining unstained by and unattached to the body of a Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings attain a body of jewel-light, which none can destroy;
may all sentient beings attain a body that is a treasury of wisdom, attaining mastery over the deathless Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain a body like a jewel ocean, such that their appearance to all beings is never in vain;
may all sentient beings attain a body equal to space, remaining unstained by and unattached to any world.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, having broken his own body and shed his blood as an act of giving, dedicates them with a Mahāyāna mind, a pure mind, a great mind, a joyful mind, a mind of great joy, a tireless mind, a mind of peace and happiness, and a mind that is not turbid.
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for their marrow and flesh, they speak with joyful and gentle words to the beggar, saying:
'Take my marrow and flesh as you please.'"

Just as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Ānāthapiṇḍada and Sarvadarśin-rāja, throughout immeasurable births in the various realms of existence, gave away their marrow and flesh with great joy; their resolve to give was so profound and vast that it could not be measured.

The mind cultivated by all bodhisattvas; the mind of the unsurpassed Great Vehicle’s wondrous roots of goodness; the upright and supreme mind that has abandoned defilements and dust; the inexhaustible mind in bestowing upon those who come seeking; the mind capable of relinquishing one's own cherished body and life; the mind covered by the jewels of immeasurable roots of goodness and sublime merit sought with single-minded devotion; the tireless mind in the conduct of a bodhisattva; the mind of great generosity; the mind free from doubt and confusion; the mind that feels no regret regarding the objects bestowed upon beggars; the mind that practices discernment in giving without seeking recompense; and the impartial mind in giving that makes no distinctions.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give their marrow and flesh, they conceive toward all Buddhas the mind of a most venerable father; they cause all sentient beings to dwell in purity within all the adorned and purified Buddha-fields of the present worlds; great compassion manifests before them to rescue and protect sentient beings; the ten powers manifest before them as clear contemplation for the sake of Bodhi; the roots of goodness of Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time manifest before them in fulfillment; fearlessness manifests before them as the Great Lion’s Roar; wisdom manifests before them as equality throughout the three periods of time; they manifest before them the cultivation of Bodhisattva vows for all worlds until the end of the future; and they manifest before them without sorrow the practice of the countless deeds of all Bodhisattvas.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives marrow and flesh, they dedicate the merit in this way:
"By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain an indestructible body like the Vajra-treasury;
may all sentient beings attain a subtle and secret body, free from any gaps or flaws."
May all sentient beings attain the Buddha’s pure, adorned, and wish-fulfilling Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings attain a body of a hundred merits, adorned by the thirty-two marks;
may all sentient beings attain a body beautifully adorned with the eighty secondary characteristics, endowed with the ten powers, and indestructible.
May all sentient beings attain the Tathāgata’s wondrous body of eternal abiding, which is immeasurable;
may all sentient beings attain the most supreme body, which cannot be destroyed by any māras;
may all sentient beings fully attain the single body, equal to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
May all sentient beings attain an unimpeded body, subtle, wondrous, and pure, filling the realm of empty space;
may all sentient beings attain the bodhisattva-treasury body, capable of containing and sustaining all sentient beings.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas through the mind that takes the realm of omniscience as its object when giving marrow and flesh, so that all sentient beings may attain the eternally abiding, immeasurable Dharma-body of a Buddha.

“When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas see sentient beings coming to beg for their hearts, they give with joy—just as the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī (No-Regret), the Bodhisattva Acalarāja (Immovable King), and other such immeasurable Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas do when seeing someone come to beg for their heart. They train in the mind of uninterrupted giving, the mind of inexhaustible giving, the mind of the great *dānapāramitā*, and the mind that reaches the further shore of the *dānapāramitā*. They train in the mind of practicing the giving of all Bodhisattvas; they attain an inexhaustible mind regarding all giving; they cultivate the mind of all great giving; they establish the mind of all Bodhisattva giving; they manifest the mind of giving while maintaining right mindfulness of all Buddhas; and they fulfill the mind of giving to all who come seeking.”

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives with a mind of generosity, they give with a pure mind; they give with a mind intent on liberating all sentient beings; they give with a mind directed toward the realm of the ten powers of enlightenment; they give with a mind intent on fulfilling great vows; they give with a mind intent on practicing the bodhisattva deeds; they give with a mind intent on attaining *sarvajñā* (omniscience); and they give with a mind that does not abandon their original vow.

With these roots of goodness, they dedicate them to sentient beings, saying: "May all sentient beings attain the Vajra-Treasury Mind, which cannot be destroyed by any of the mountains of the Vajra Enclosure."

They have attained the mind adorned with vajra; the mind free from fear; the invincible mind; the mind that cannot be exhausted by any world; the mind that is a treasury of wisdom, a courageous and supreme banner; the mind of the great Nārāyaṇa, a lofty and victorious banner; the inexhaustible mind regarding the great ocean of sentient beings; the indestructible mind that is a treasury of Nārāyaṇa; the mind capable of utterly destroying all Māras, the works of Māra, and the hosts of Māra’s armies; the mind of a majestic, courageous, and heroic Great Being; the fearless mind; the supremely firm mind adorned with great vows; the most excellent Bodhisattva-mind; the mind adorned with enlightenment, endowed with all Buddha-dharmas; the mind of perfect awakening through all-aspect knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), which, seated at the foot of the Bodhi tree, accomplishes the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas and is free from all delusion; and the mind endowed with the ten powers (*daśabala*).

This is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s dedication of the roots of goodness from the mind of giving to sentient beings, so as to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the unattached mind of the ten powers.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for their intestines, kidneys, liver, or lungs—just as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Duryodhana and Akṣayamati-nirghāta-rāja, and other immeasurable Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, upon seeing someone come to beg for their intestines, kidneys, liver, or lungs, feel joy; they look upon them with eyes of affection, give rise to the love of Bodhi, and in accordance with what the supplicant desires, fulfill their wishes entirely. They give with joy, without regret in their hearts, and with right mindfulness they observe that from this non-solid body they take a solid body, thinking: 'This foul body of mine will be eaten by tigers, wolves, foxes, dogs, and various beasts; this body is impermanent and a thing to be cast away.'"
When the bodhisattva-mahāsattva has contemplated in this way, he gazes with a reverent mind at those who come to beg;
he further reflects:
"If I do not practice giving, I shall not attain that which is most firm among the firm, that which is permanent among the impermanent, and that which is pure within the impure."

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva maintains such right mindfulness, they are able to develop a pure and straightforward mind, understand the true Dharma, and regard those who come to beg as spiritual friends, thinking, "They are able to teach and transform me, extracting what is solid from within the insubstantial."
Having formed this thought, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness to all sentient beings:
"May all sentient beings attain a body that is a treasury of inner and outer pure wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain a belly that is a treasury of wisdom, fully able to receive and uphold all vows for omniscience."
May all sentient beings attain a pure body that those who behold it never tire of seeing; may they emit and radiate firm, wondrous fragrant light that universally perfumes the ten directions;
may all sentient beings achieve the Tathāgata’s mark of a non-protruding abdomen, with body and limbs in harmonious proportion and all members fully complete;
may all sentient beings obtain the food of the flavor of Dharma to nourish their bodies of wisdom, and be filled with the softness and fullness of love for the Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings attain an inexhaustible body and abide securely in the Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the inner treasury of pure dhāraṇīs, possessing all-encompassing eloquence and clarity that universally illumines all phenomena;
may all sentient beings attain a pure body, with both the internal and external being entirely cleansed.
May all sentient beings attain the body of practice cultivated through the wisdom of the Tathāgata, universally raining down the nectar-like Dharma rain of wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain internal purity and tranquility of body, and externally serve as the sovereign banner of wisdom for all beings, illuminating everything.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving their intestines, kidneys, liver, and lungs to sentient beings: to cause all sentient beings to fully attain bodies that are pure both internally and externally, and to abide in firm, unobstructed wisdom.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for their limbs and bones, they give them away—just as the Bodhisattva Dharmaguhya, the Bodhisattva Rātnaprabha, and other such immeasurable Bodhisattvas-Mahāsattvas gave their limbs and bones. Upon seeing the seeker, they give rise to a heart of great joy, a clear and pure heart, a tranquil heart, a heart of loving-kindness, a heart of peace and happiness, a heart free from attachment, and a pure heart; toward the one who comes begging, they give rise to a heart that fulfills their wishes."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness gathered by giving his own limbs and joints to all sentient beings:
"May all sentient beings attain bodies like emanations, forever free from the worldly body of bone, blood, and flesh;
may all sentient beings attain bodies of vajra-strength, which cannot be destroyed and cannot be surpassed."
May all sentient beings attain the body of dharma endowed with the power of sarvajñā (all-knowledge), born from the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) that is neither bound nor attached;
may all sentient beings attain the body of wisdom-power, with faculties firm and indestructible;
may all sentient beings attain the body of dharma-power, possessing sovereign mastery over the power of wisdom and reaching the further shore.
May all sentient beings attain a firm and solid body that cannot be destroyed or dispersed;
may all sentient beings attain a body of transformation according to need, skillfully taming and bringing sentient beings to maturity;
may all sentient beings attain a body perfumed by wisdom, adorned with limbs as strong as those of Nārāyaṇa.
May all sentient beings attain a body of steadfast continuity that is never interrupted, forever and ultimately free from all fatigue;
may all sentient beings attain a body of power established in peace, fully endowed with courageous diligence;
may all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-body, capable of discerning all sentient beings and entering the realm of the immeasurable wisdom-body.
May all sentient beings attain a body of merit-power, which eradicates all evils and is not seen in vain;
may all sentient beings attain an unimpeded body, fully perfected in wisdom free from defilement and attachment;
may all sentient beings attain a body embraced by the Buddhas, constantly protected by all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain a body that universally benefits all beings, capable of entering all realms of existence;

may all sentient beings attain a perfectly responsive body, such that all beings throughout the ten directions behold its face, never turning their backs on the Buddha-dharma, pure and illuminating, ever manifest before them;
may all sentient beings attain a body of perfected diligence, cultivating the ultimate wisdom of the Mahāyāna.
May all sentient beings abandon bodies characterized by self-conceit, arrogance, and heedlessness, and attain pure bodies with wisdom firmly established and unshakable;
may all sentient beings attain bodies that steadfastly uphold the precepts and accomplish the deeds of omniscience of the Mahāyāna;
may all sentient beings be born into the family of the Buddhas and forever leave behind the defiled bodies of worldly birth and death.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness from a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s giving of limbs, joints, and bones, which causes all sentient beings to become entirely pure and attain sarvajñā.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone approaching, holding a sharp knife and begging for his thick or thin skin, he gazes upon them with eyes of love, and with joy and reverence, prepares a seat for them. He then thinks:
"A field of merit is difficult to encounter, yet it has come to me of its own accord; it fulfills my original vow and shall bring me to the definitive realization of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā)."
He spoke these words:
"Take the skin of my body; use it as you wish.
When such pure-treasury bodhisattvas, Vajrapārśva-deer-king bodhisattvas, and other immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give their thick or thin skin to beggars, they dedicate the merit in this way:
By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings attain the Tathāgata’s mark of thin skin, pure and golden;
may all sentient beings attain thin skin that is as firm and indestructible as a diamond;
may all sentient beings attain golden skin, like a treasury of Jambūnada gold.
May all sentient beings obtain skin of immeasurable colors, manifesting forms according to their needs, and may these all be rendered pure;
may all sentient beings obtain bright and clear skin that does not receive dust or grime, like the pure color of a śramaṇa or a Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings obtain the foremost skin-color, naturally pure.
May all sentient beings attain the pure skin of a Tathāgata, adorned by subtle and wondrous marks and signs;
may all sentient beings obtain a clear and pure skin that emits great radiance, universally covering all things;
may all sentient beings obtain a skin like a net of light, fully endowed with immeasurable radiance, universally covering the world.
May all sentient beings obtain supple skin of pure and radiant colors.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away their own thick or thin skin, so as to cause all sentient beings to attain unsurpassed and most supreme enlightenment, fully endowed with all the merits of a Tathāgata.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Seventeen;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Eighteen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Fifth Part of the Twenty-first Chapter on the Ten Dedications of the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja:

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for their fingers and toes, they act like the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as Dṛḍhavīrya and Jambudvīpeśvararāja Suvarṇaprabhāsa, who, when giving their fingers and toes, feel great joy in their hearts, their countenance remains unchanged, and they practice the gift of the Mahāyāna. They do not give seeking the five desires, nor seeking fame and reputation; rather, they establish the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), practicing the gift with a great heart of generosity, a gift free from the stain of stinginess, a gift free from envy, and a gift that accords with the Buddhas. By means of the roots of goodness encompassed by this giving of fingers and toes, they dedicate them to all sentient beings, saying:
'May all sentient beings attain the mark of long fingers of a Buddha.'"
May all sentient beings attain the mark of closely set fingers—rounded, smooth, slender, and straight;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of copper-colored nails—tubular, closely set, and pure;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of the great man’s fingers, being fully able to grasp and uphold all dharmas.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of fingers adorned with the ten powers;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of the fingers of a Great Man, being slender, tapered, and closely set;
may all sentient beings have the tips of their fingers and toes adorned with wheel-marks, with finger-joints that are level and full, and the lines upon them clearly manifest.
May all sentient beings obtain fingers the color of lotuses, adorned with the marks and signs resulting from the karmic retribution of the ten powers;
may all sentient beings obtain fingers of radiant light, emitting nets of light that universally illuminate the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions;
may all sentient beings obtain pure and wondrous fingers, fully adorned with all the marks and signs.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva mahāsattva when giving his fingers to sentient beings, causing the minds of all sentient beings to become pure.
Furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva requests the Dharma, if someone should say:
"If you can give me your fingernails along with the flesh, I shall give you the Dharma."
The Bodhisattva replied:
"Simply grant me the Dharma; whatever you require, take and use it as you please.

Just as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Dharmarājaparyeṣin and Akṣaya, for the sake of seeking the Dharma and desiring to cause all sentient beings to be endowed with the True Dharma, dedicate these roots of goodness to sentient beings:
May all sentient beings obtain fingernails with the marks of the Red-Copper Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings obtain glossy fingernails;
may all sentient beings obtain the Buddha’s perfectly pure and radiant fingernails.
May all sentient beings attain the complete claws of great beings’ universal wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain incomparable claws, remaining unstained by and unattached to any world;
may all sentient beings attain adorned claws that universally illumine all beings.
May all sentient beings obtain fine and exquisite nails, subtle, secret, pure, and indestructible;
may all sentient beings obtain the Buddha’s complete marks and signs of skillful means, with great wisdom and purity;
may all sentient beings obtain well-born nails, purified by the Bodhisattva’s pure karmic fruits and retributions.
May all sentient beings obtain the excellent skillful means-claws of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), emitting a treasury of wondrous light of immeasurable colors.

This is the dedication of the roots of goodness from the giving of claws and flesh by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas to sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may obtain the claws of omniscience, fully adorn the Dharma-body of the Tathāgata, and become entirely fulfilled with unimpeded power.
"For the sake of seeking the Dharma, and because the Dharma is difficult to obtain, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva may say to one who is able to bestow the Dharma:
'If you can cast yourself into a fire-pit seven fathoms deep, I shall give you the Dharma.'"
Upon hearing this, the Bodhisattva was filled with immeasurable joy and reflected:

"For the sake of the Dharma, I would endure immeasurable suffering even within the Avīci Hell and all other evil realms; how much more so, then, would I enter a tiny fire-pit among humans to hear the Dharma?"
"How marvelous!
The True Dharma is so easily obtained that one may avoid the immeasurable agonies of hell by hearing the True Dharma while entering a pit of fire.
You simply preach the Dharma; I shall enter the pit of fire."
"Just as the Bodhisattva Seeking the Dharma King and the Bodhisattva Vajra Contemplation, out of joy for the Dharma, entered the fire and dedicated their roots of goodness to sentient beings, saying:
'May all sentient beings attain the Dharma of all-knowledge in which the Buddhas abide, remaining firm and non-retrogressive in the unsurpassed path;
may all sentient beings completely extinguish the fiery pits of the evil realms and experience the bliss of the Tathāgata.'"
May all sentient beings attain a mind free from fear and be liberated from all terrors;
may all sentient beings always delight in seeking the Dharma, attaining universal joy and being adorned by the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings leave behind all evil realms and be able to extinguish the blazing fires of the three poisons.
May all sentient beings attain happiness and achieve the most supreme and wondrous bliss of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings attain the bodhicitta and be able to extinguish the fires of greed, anger, and delusion;
may all sentient beings attain the bliss of all bodhisattva samādhis, universally behold all Buddhas, and experience great joy in their hearts.
May all sentient beings constantly hear the true Dharma, ultimately perfecting the path of the Buddha without ever forgetting it;
may all sentient beings fully attain the bliss of the bodhisattvas' sovereign supernormal powers, ultimately becoming complete in the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñā-jñāna*).

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, dedicates the roots of goodness from entering fire to all sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may be endowed with the fire of wisdom and remain far removed from all unwholesome karma.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, undergo immeasurable sufferings with their entire bodies;

for the sake of the True Dharma, for the sake of extensively expounding the True Dharma, for the sake of establishing the Bodhisattva path, for the sake of opening up unsurpassed bodhi, for the sake of perfecting unsurpassed wisdom, for the sake of cultivating the ten powers, for the sake of expanding the mind of omniscience, for the sake of attaining unimpeded wisdom, for the sake of purifying all sentient beings, for the sake of entering the realm of all bodhisattvas, and for the sake of protecting the Mahāyāna Buddha-bodhi.

Just as the Bodhisattva Seeking the True Dharma, the Bodhisattva King Courageous and Valiant, and other such immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, undergo immeasurable suffering.”

Even for those who slander the true Dharma, the most wicked persons, those hindered by evil karma, and those who uphold the works of Māra—for the sake of the true Dharma—he undergoes all sufferings on behalf of those evil people.
For the sake of seeking the Dharma, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva undergoes suffering on behalf of all sentient beings and dedicates their roots of goodness to them:
to cause all sentient beings to be free from all suffering and to attain the path of peace, happiness, and benefit;
and to cause all sentient beings to be free from all forms of suffering and to experience the attainment of wondrous bliss.
May all sentient beings forever extinguish the aggregate of suffering and attain the joy like a flash of lightning;
may all sentient beings transcend the prison of suffering and be fully endowed with the practice of ultimate wisdom;
may all sentient beings behold the path of peace and security, departing from the realm of affliction and distress.
May all sentient beings attain the joy of the Dharma, becoming fully endowed with it and ultimately pacifying all sufferings;
may all sentient beings give rise to great compassion, desiring to rescue and deliver all from the ocean of suffering;
may all sentient beings attain the bliss of the Buddhas and sever the suffering of birth and death.
May all sentient beings attain incomparable pure bliss, their bodies forever free from all painful sensations;
may all sentient beings attain all supreme joys, ultimately becoming fully endowed with the unimpeded bliss of the Buddhas.

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of seeking the Dharma, dedicates all roots of goodness from undergoing every kind of suffering to rescue and protect sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to dwell securely in omniscience and unimpeded liberation.

"For the sake of seeking the Dharma and because the Dharma is difficult to obtain, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is able to relinquish the great earth, the four seas, and their kingdoms; cities large and small, villages, hamlets, and settlements; lands of abundant prosperity and teeming populations; gardens, groves, and bathing pools; and such various immeasurable adornments as flourishing flowers and fruits. He is likewise able to relinquish universal peace where no enemies exist, as well as gold, silver, precious treasuries, wives, children, and retinues."

Within that which is not firm, they seek the dharma of firmness for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, so as to cause all sentient beings to attain the path of the Buddha’s unimpeded, pure liberation and *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge).

Like the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Mañjuśrī, Jayagati-rāja, and others of such infinite number, for the sake of seeking the true Dharma—even for a single phrase or a single flavor—they prostrate themselves with their five limbs touching the ground, reverently bowing and receiving it upon their heads; with right mindfulness toward the Buddhas of the three periods of time, they diligently seek the true Dharma. Within the true Dharma, their minds are always joyful and delighted; they cultivate various vows and seek the dharma of detachment from craving, renouncing the sovereign methods of worldly kings and emperors, and joyfully seeking the supreme, sovereign, and victorious Dharma of the Unsurpassed Dharma King.

Without recollecting or clinging to anything in the world, they nurture their own minds by remaining detached from worldly dharmas; they stay far removed from all evil speech of the world and dwell in the tranquility of the abode where all Buddhas reside.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, seeking the True Dharma, dedicates the roots of goodness encompassed by the gift of the great earth and the lands of the four continents to all sentient beings:
so that all sentient beings may be able to relinquish everything internal and external;
and so that all sentient beings may be able to renounce all things without any regret in their hearts.
May all sentient beings not begrudge their bodies or lives, nor their means of subsistence, as they constantly seek the True Dharma;
may all sentient beings fully obtain the benefits of the Dharma and sever the doubts of immeasurable beings;
may all sentient beings always delight in the True Dharma and attain deep love for the teachings of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings be able to relinquish body and life, seeking the Buddha-dharma with mastery over worldly pleasures, and cultivate supreme enlightenment with a great mind;
may all sentient beings reverently honor the True Dharma of all Buddhas, being able to relinquish body and life for the sake of the ultimate True Dharma;
may all sentient beings protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma, and practice the Dharma that is difficult even for Tathāgatas to hear.
May all sentient beings fully attain the luminous illumination of the Bodhi of all Buddhas, complete the bodhisattva practices, and realize awakening without depending on others;
may all sentient beings attain mastery over all Buddha-dharmas, extract the thorns of doubt, and maintain a mind that is always pure.

This is how a bodhisattva mahāsattva, for the sake of seeking the Dharma that is difficult to obtain, dedicates the roots of goodness from giving away their kingdom so that all sentient beings may attain fulfillment in knowledge and vision.

"Furthermore, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the sovereignty of the Dharma, he instructs all those within the cities, towns, and villages of Jambudvīpa to cease the slaughter of two-legged and four-legged beings, universally bestowing fearlessness upon them. Free from the mind of enmity, they cultivate the Bodhisattva practice and govern the country with righteousness, extinguishing all the sufferings and hardships of sentient beings. They give rise to the jewel of the mind of peace and security for all beings and fulfill the jewel of the upright, supreme, and wondrous mind. Being able to personally fulfill the three kinds of precepts, they also cause sentient beings to fulfill these three kinds of precepts."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from the five precepts, such as non-killing and so forth, to all sentient beings:
"May all sentient beings attain long life and wisdom, possess the bodhicitta, and have immeasurable life-force;
may all sentient beings attain immeasurable lifespan and reverently make offerings to all Buddhas."
May all sentient beings fully cultivate and practice so as to transcend the laws of old age and death, such that no calamities whatsoever can harm their lives;
may all sentient beings attain immeasurable bodies free from the suffering of illness, with mastery over the life-faculty, able to abide for as long as they wish;
may all sentient beings obtain inexhaustible life, and throughout all future kalpas, fully cultivate and practice the conduct of Bodhisattvas, taming and transforming all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings attain the gateway of pure livelihood, so that the roots of goodness of the ten powers may all enter within them;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with roots of goodness, possess immeasurable lifespans, and have all their vows fulfilled;
may all sentient beings behold all Buddhas and cultivate inexhaustible roots of goodness for long life.
May all sentient beings learn all that is to be learned within the family of the Tathāgata, fully accomplish an inexhaustible life-force, and attain a heart of joy within the noble Dharma;
may all sentient beings obtain a life-force free from aging, illness, and death, possess inexhaustible vigor, and abide securely in the Buddha-wisdom.

This is how a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from the five precepts, such as abstaining from killing, to sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may dwell securely in the Tathāgata’s three kinds of pure precepts and ultimately attain the wisdom of the ten powers.

"If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees sentient beings—whether human or animal—who are cruel and unrighteous, having their male organs destroyed, their bodies mutilated, and undergoing various agonizing torments;
having seen this suffering, he gives rise to great compassion and delivers them, causing them all to be fully endowed with honor, joy, and rare treasures."
The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva says to the evil person:
"For what benefit do you create these evil karmas?

Whatever you require, I shall provide it all to you. You should now abandon these evil karmas; it is impossible for one who lacks right mindfulness to indulge in greed, harming both others and oneself while seeking personal pleasure."
"Such evil conduct and all unwholesome dharmas are not praised by any Tathāgata.

The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva is able to relinquish all that he possesses so as to prevent those sentient beings from committing evil deeds; furthermore, he preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma to them, saying:
"The Dharma of tranquility nurtures pure conduct, eliminates the unwholesome, cultivates a mind of loving-kindness, and does not afflict sentient beings."
At that time, having heard these words of the Dharma, those evil persons immediately abandoned their wicked conduct and cultivated pure deeds.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from his compassionate rescue to sentient beings:
"May all sentient beings attain the Buddha’s mark of the great man’s concealed organ."
May all sentient beings be endowed with male form, attain the mind of a great man, and practice pure Brahma-conduct;
may all sentient beings achieve the desireless body of a great man, ride upon unimpeded wisdom, and ultimately never regress;
may all sentient beings attain the body of a Great Man, forever leave behind the mind of desire, and remain free from all defilement and attachment.
May all sentient beings fully accomplish the qualities of a true son of noble family, being praised by all Buddhas and endowed with perfect wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain the strength of a great man, fully accomplishing the roots of goodness of the ten powers;
may all sentient beings always achieve the male form, remaining firm and securely established in the unprecedented Dharma.

May all sentient beings be without attachment or bondage amidst the five desires, attaining liberation of mind, becoming weary of and renouncing the triple world, and cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings achieve the status of the foremost wise ones, be universally trusted and submitted to, and receive the transformation of the Way;
may all sentient beings accomplish the profound wisdom of the bodhisattva hero and ultimately reach the destination of the Great Vehicle of the Buddhas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas for the sake of rescuing those whose forms are impaired: to cause all sentient beings to rescue and protect all good sons, so that they may be born into the families of sages and saints, be fully endowed with wisdom, cultivate and practice the supreme knowledge of men, skillfully manifest the seven destinies of great men, be complete in the unsurpassed true Dharma of great men, and constantly be able to transform and deliver all sentient beings through the dedication of roots of goodness, so that all sentient beings may attain the pure and supreme Dharma of the Buddha as a great man.
"Furthermore, if a Tathāgata appears in the world, he proclaims to all with a great voice:
'A Tathāgata has appeared in the world!'"
"The Tathāgata has appeared in the world!
Thus he causes all sentient beings to hear the Buddha's voice;

having heard the Buddha's voice, they abandon self-conceit, arrogance, and heedlessness, and come to see the Buddhas. They become firmly established in the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* (samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha), cultivate the realm of the Buddhas without ever forgetting it, and respectfully make offerings to all Buddhas. Because they always delight in seeing the Buddhas—and because a Buddha is difficult to encounter even in hundreds of thousands of kalpas—they extensively explain to sentient beings the difficulty of encountering a Buddha.
Having heard this, sentient beings will constantly desire to see all Buddhas; their hearts will be filled with great joy as they reverently make offerings, honor, and praise them.
Having heard the names of the Buddhas from the Tathāgata, they will plant various roots of goodness under immeasurable Buddhas, cultivating and increasing them.
Because of the Tathāgata, immeasurable sentient beings all become completely pure;
because of the Tathāgata, immeasurable sentient beings are all thoroughly tamed and subdued.
Those sentient beings conceive the thought of regarding the Bodhisattva as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).

Because of the Bodhisattva, all sentient beings fully possess the Buddha-dharma; the roots of goodness cultivated by those sentient beings throughout immeasurable eons all constitute the work of a Buddha.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from praising the Buddha to all sentient beings, saying:
"May all sentient beings constantly see the Buddhas, never missing the proper time, receiving transformation according to their needs, and bringing joy to the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings always delight in seeing the Buddhas, never forgetting them."
May all sentient beings cultivate wisdom so that they are able to uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings never be separated from the Buddha-dharma, practicing the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons and constantly hearing the true Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain non-forgetfulness, fully upholding the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings not dwell upon divergent karmas, but maintain right mindfulness of all Buddhas and cultivate the ten powers;
may all sentient beings, wherever they look, behold the Buddhas, so that throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space, they may all reverently see all Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings attain mastery over the Buddha-body, manifesting the realization of the Buddha-way in all worlds.
May all sentient beings, in the presence of spiritual friends, hear the true Dharma of the Buddhas and attain indestructible faith in all Tathāgatas;

may all sentient beings praise the appearance of the Buddhas in the world, knowing that their efforts in transforming and delivering sentient beings are entirely not in vain, and may they cause all beings to be universally purified.

This is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s dedication of roots of goodness by extolling the appearance of Buddhas in the world, causing all sentient beings to see all Buddhas and receive transformation accordingly in the Unsurpassed Way, so that all Buddha-dharmas may reach ultimate purity.
"Furthermore, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva may give away the great earth; or give it to a Buddha to erect a hall and pavilion;
or give it to bodhisattvas and spiritual friends for their use as they wish;
or give it to the noble Saṃgha to construct monasteries."
Some offer it to their parents to build houses;
some give it to others—whether Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, all fields of merit, or those who beg;
or they give it to the fourfold assembly to use as they please, ensuring they lack for nothing.
Or they may honor the Tathāgata by constructing stupas and temples;
through such acts of giving, as they receive and enjoy these benefits, they shall be entirely freed from all enmity and every form of fear.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from bestowing the great earth [upon others] as follows:
May all sentient beings attain the pure Buddha-ground of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), ultimately reaching the further shore of the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings attain the *dhāraṇī* of the Great Ground, be free from delusion through right mindfulness, and be fully able to receive and uphold the wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings uphold all dharmas and protect the Buddha-Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain a mind equal to the great earth, being pure and upright toward all beings and never giving rise to evil thoughts;
may all sentient beings uphold the lineage of the Buddhas, ensuring that the seed of the Buddhas is not severed, and gradually establish the roots of goodness of all the bodhisattva stages;
may all sentient beings universally serve as a refuge of peace and security for all, bringing them all to subdual and achieving purity.
May all sentient beings benefit living beings equally with the Tathāgatas, establishing them in the powers of a Buddha;
may all sentient beings be beloved by all, dwelling securely in the state cherished by all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings be firmly established within the dharmas of the Tathāgata’s powers and fearlessnesses.
May all sentient beings attain the stage of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) and achieve ultimate mastery over all Buddha-dharmas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness through the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s gift of the great earth, so as to cause the realm of all sentient beings to ultimately reach the pure stage of the Tathāgata’s path.

"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives servants and attendants, whether to offer them to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, or spiritual friends, for the sake of increasing the Dharma of the Tathāgata;
or he gives to the Sangha Jewel, or offers them to his parents and other venerable fields of merit;
or again, he provides for those who are sick and emaciated to fully preserve their lives, giving to all those who are impoverished and seeking alms."
Or he may give to stūpas and temples, providing for their sweeping and cleaning;

or if there are those who can transcribe Buddhist scriptures, for the sake of protecting the Dharma, he provides them with immeasurable billions of servants and attendants. He causes these attendants to be all thoroughly proficient, clear-minded and wise, gentle and disciplined, always diligent and energetic, never indolent, and to have attained a mind that is upright, beneficial, peaceful, compassionate, and free from enmity. These servants, with such a mind, serve that bodhisattva-mahāsattva; according to what is appropriate for the customs and local conditions of the recipient, and according to his talents and skills, he gives these servants as a gift—all of which arise from the pure karma of the bodhisattva, capable of making the servants please the recipient's heart.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from serving servants and attendants as follows:
"May all sentient beings attain a disciplined mind to serve and attend upon all Buddhas, cultivating roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings accord with and serve all Buddhas, becoming fully capable of hearing and retaining everything spoken by the Buddhas."
May all sentient beings advance with sovereign mastery at will to manifest as Tathāgatas, constantly cultivating right mindfulness and remaining free from any further evil thoughts;
may all sentient beings succeed to the lineage of the Buddhas, following and conforming to the roots of goodness embraced by the Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings serve the Tathāgatas without ever failing in their timely devotion, so that every Buddha they behold shall never be in vain.
May all sentient beings fully grasp the sublime meanings of all Buddhas, possess pure speech, and wander with fearlessness;
may all sentient beings behold all Buddhas, delighting in the sight of them without weariness, and regarding all Tathāgatas without sparing their own bodies or lives;
may all sentient beings see all Buddhas, their minds free from defiled attachment, having departed from worldly dependencies.
May all sentient beings rely upon the Buddhas and remain far removed from all worldly auspiciousness;
may all sentient beings follow the path of the Buddhas and single-mindedly seek supreme enlightenment.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness from a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s giving of servants and attendants, which causes all sentient beings to forever leave behind defilement and attain the Tathāgata’s dharma-body of the Buddha’s pure ground, sovereign and unimpeded.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his body as an offering to serve others, he abandons arrogance and cultivates a humble mind, a mind of service, a mind like the great earth, a mind that endures all suffering, a mind that provides for all without weariness, and a mind free from indolence. He possesses a mind of all roots of goodness toward all poor and lowly sentient beings; a mind of respectful service and offering toward all those who are honored, noble, wealthy, and happy, even down to the ignorant and the young. Firmly established in the most supreme dharma-gate, he cultivates all roots of goodness with right mindfulness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from the gift of his own body, [vowing]:

"May all sentient beings never lack servants or attendants; may they cultivate the bodhisattva practices with a non-regressive mind, never failing or losing the true meaning of the bodhisattvas; may they single-mindedly and exclusively seek the path of the bodhisattvas, thoroughly comprehend the equal and correct Dharma of the bodhisattvas, and be numbered among the lineage of the Tathāgatas;

may they cultivate the true and real Dharma, increase their bodhisattva practices, and cause all worlds to attain the pure Buddha-Dharma, achieve liberation through their profound resolve, and reach ultimate bodhi."
May all sentient beings increase their pure, supreme, and great roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings turn toward great merit and ultimately attain omniscience.
“Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:

‘By means of the roots of goodness gathered through providing for others with my own body, may all sentient beings be well able to serve and attend upon all Buddhas; may their minds be harmonious and supple; may they constantly hear the True Dharma, receive and uphold the Dharma, protect the Dharma, not forget the Dharma, not destroy the Dharma, not discriminate within the Dharma, not depart from the Dharma, and be well-disciplined in the Dharma; may they be well able to discipline those who are undisciplined and attain the Dharma of disciplined quiescence;
and may those sentient beings, in the presence of all Buddhas, be well able to accord with them through the merit of such accordance.’”
May all sentient beings become the foremost stupas, fully capable of receiving the offerings of all beings;
may all sentient beings become the foremost fields of merit, spontaneously awakening to unsurpassed bodhi;
may all sentient beings become the most supreme fields of merit, universally able to benefit all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings become treasuries of supreme merit and meaning, able to exhaustively fathom the very source and bottom of all roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings become pure and wondrous fields of merit, able to produce immeasurable fruits of retribution;
may all sentient beings attain the supreme path of transcendence, able to completely surpass all worlds.
May all sentient beings become supreme taming-masters, able to provide guidance and instruction according to what is appropriate for each;
may all sentient beings attain the most excellent dhāraṇī, able to receive and uphold the teachings of all Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings reach the immeasurable, most excellent realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), fully endowed with the unimpeded right path that is like space.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness from a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s gift of his own body, which causes all sentient beings to attain the Tathāgata’s body of wisdom worthy of offerings.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas fully attain the love for the Dharma and a mind of pure joy; they are able to cover all Buddhas with their own bodies and constantly delight in cultivating the unsurpassed treasure of the Dharma. Toward all Buddhas, they give rise to the heart of a parent;

desiring to attain the ultimate, unobstructed path of the Dharma, they accomplish countless nayutas of the wondrous jewels of wisdom and the gates of all roots of goodness. Regarding the immeasurable Dharma-gates of all Tathāgatas, they maintain right mindfulness without forgetting and deeply understand the meaning of the Tathāgatas’ various spheres of activity.

They are able to universally rain down the Dharma-rain of all Buddhas with the subtle and secret Brahma-voice of the Tathāgata; the Dharma-clouds of the Tathāgata cover everything everywhere, and they remain free from fear.”

They are able to analytically explain the stages of the Omniscient One, are fully endowed with the vehicle of ultimate *sarvajñatā*, and have perfected all their faculties through immeasurable and boundless great dharmas.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas hear the profound Dharma from the various Buddhas, they experience immeasurable joy and cultivate the Right Path. They are able to personally eliminate all doubts and delusions, and further cause sentient beings to experience immeasurable joy, with their nets of doubt entirely removed. Their merits become fully perfected and their roots of goodness complete; they cultivate immeasurable Dharma-gates, universally practice great vows, and benefit sentient beings. Abiding immovably in the wisdom of the Vajra-treasury, they single-mindedly seek unsurpassed Bodhi with a correct mind, being able to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields and reverently draw near to immeasurable Tathāgatas.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this Dharma, they universally cover all Buddhas with their own bodies and dedicate these roots of goodness to sentient beings, saying:
"May all sentient beings be fully endowed with sublime bodies, such that they are all able to universally cover all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings dwell in reliance upon the Tathāgata, constantly seeing all Buddhas and never being separated from them."
May all sentient beings attain the most supreme body, fully endowed with all merit and wisdom;
may all sentient beings practice the Brahma-conduct that transcends existence, thereby causing all Buddhas to rejoice;
may all sentient beings attain a body free from the notion of "mine," such that their minds have no attachment to "self" or "what belongs to self."
May all sentient beings be able to manifest bodies everywhere throughout all lands, yet remain without coming or going among those worlds;
may all sentient beings attain a body of mastery, free from the notions of "self" and "mine," and travel freely in all directions;
may all sentient beings give birth to the Buddha-body and dwell within the supreme household of the Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings attain the body of the power of Dharma, abide securely upon the seat of Dharma through the power of patience, and achieve a mind that cannot be destroyed;
may all sentient beings attain the incomparable body, fully endowed with the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings attain a body of supramundane merit, born within the empty realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu).

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, who—encompassed by the Buddha’s own protection—dedicates them to sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may accomplish the supreme and wondrous merits of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives his own body as a gift to all sentient beings, he forms this thought:
'May all sentient beings accomplish roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings constantly keep roots of goodness in mind.'"
May all sentient beings be able to serve as bright lamps;
may all sentient beings dwell in peace and happiness;
may all sentient beings obtain the belly of the Dharma-treasury, capable of containing and sustaining all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings become lights for the world, extinguishing all darkness;

may all sentient beings become the causes and conditions for all roots of goodness, acting as spiritual friends who mutually support one another, revealing the right path and attaining unsurpassed bliss;
may all sentient beings become bright and pure suns.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates to all sentient beings the roots of goodness encompassed by the giving of his own body, saying:
"May all sentient beings ultimately reach the ground of the path of the wisdom of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings follow the true path and cause all to ultimately attain unsurpassed bodhi."
May all sentient beings always dwell in the assemblies of Buddhas and fully receive their correct transformation;
may all sentient beings be complete in dignified deportment and achieve the pure deportment of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain nirvana and deeply understand the meaning of the Dharma.
May all sentient beings fully attain the supreme Dharma without ever feeling satiated, constantly encountering the supreme Dharma and being born into the family of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings abandon worldly hopes and attain the true hope of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings sit beneath the Bodhi tree and give birth to immeasurable, pure roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings destroy all enemies that are their afflictions and give rise to a mind free from harm;
may all sentient beings attain the dharma of fearlessness and be able to fully protect and uphold all Buddha-dharmas.

This is the dedication of the roots of goodness from a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s gift of their own body, which brings benefit, peace, and security to all sentient beings, so that they may attain the unsurpassed Dharma.
“The bodhisattva-mahāsattva personally serves all Buddhas with his own body, giving rise to a mind of gratitude and a mind as toward one’s parents toward all Tathāgatas;
he gives rise to a pure and profound mind toward the Buddhas;

with a bright and clear mind, he upholds bodhi, attains the Buddha-dharmas, abandons worldly dharmas, is born into the family of the Tathāgatas, accords with all Buddhas, guards his own dharma, remains far removed from all realms of Māra, cultivates the realm of the Buddhas, and by means of his own body, accomplishes the vessel for all Buddha-dharmas.”
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates such a dharma-body for himself, dedicating the roots of goodness gathered through serving all Buddhas to sentient beings:
to cause all sentient beings to abide in a pure mind and adorn themselves with the jewel of omniscience;
and to cause all sentient beings to attain the means of taming beings and engage in their common affairs, remaining far removed from all unwholesome karma.
May all sentient beings obtain indestructible retinues and be able to uphold the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings become pure disciples of the Tathāgatas and achieve the stage of consecrated Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings be gathered and protected by all Buddhas and remain far removed from all evil associates.
May all sentient beings accord with all Buddhas and cultivate the bodhisattva practices of the most supreme place of birth;
may all sentient beings enter the realm of the Buddhas and all receive the prediction of omniscience;
may all sentient beings become equal to the Tathāgatas and attain mastery over all Buddha-dharmas.
May all sentient beings be entirely embraced by all Buddhas and practice the karma of non-attachment;
may all sentient beings become the foremost attendants of all Buddhas, endowed with perfect wisdom, and bring joy to all Buddhas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who personally serves the Buddhas toward unexcelled enlightenment; dedication toward the rescue and protection of all sentient beings; dedication toward the transcendence of the triple world by sentient beings; dedication toward making one’s own mind entirely pure; dedication toward immeasurable and vast enlightenment; dedication toward the illuminating wisdom of all Buddhas; dedication toward one’s own body being taken into the care of the Buddhas; dedication toward upholding all Buddha-dharmas; dedication toward the joyful seeking of all Buddha-dharmas; dedication toward roots of goodness being equal to those of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; and dedication toward attaining a cool and tranquil mind that realizes all Buddha-dharmas.

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives away a kingdom, he relinquishes the sovereign mind of a worldly monarch; being without attachment or bondage, he does not seek power for himself, remains far removed from evil karma, and universally gives rise to a mind of benefit and peace toward all sentient beings."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from giving away his kingdom, saying:
"May all sentient beings be far removed from ignorance and clearly understand karmic retribution;
may all sentient beings take no pleasure in worldly dharmas."
May all sentient beings not be attached to any place of birth within the world;
may all sentient beings not grasp at the characteristics of solidity in the world;
may the minds of all sentient beings not be defiled by or attached to the aggregates, elements, and sense bases.
May all sentient beings have minds that are unstained by and unattached to the dharmas of "self" and "what belongs to self";
may all sentient beings have minds that never forget or lose the practices of all bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings never abandon or distance themselves from spiritual friends.
May all sentient beings be able to fully receive and uphold the vows and practices of bodhisattvas;
may all spiritual friends of all sentient beings be filled with joy.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness from giving away their kingdoms as follows:
May all sentient beings attain the station of the Dharma King, reaching the further shore of the sovereign Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain the Dharma of the Dharma King, subduing all enemies who are the kings of the fetters;
may all sentient beings dwell together with the Dharma King, praising the Buddha-Dharma and the wisdom of the Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings dwell in the realm of the Buddhas, the household of the Dharma Kings, and be able to freely turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma;
may all sentient beings give birth to the skillful means of the Tathāgatas, attain mastery over the Dharma, protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma so that it never ceases;
and may all sentient beings protect and uphold the true Dharma of the immeasurable Dharma Kings, all fully accomplishing the state of supreme great Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings become Dharma Kings within the pure Dharma-realm, appearing in the world in uninterrupted succession;
may all sentient beings act as kings of wisdom throughout all worlds, taming and bringing to maturity all sentient beings;

may all sentient beings universally serve as patrons of the Dharma for the beings of the Dharma-realm, the realm of space, and all other worlds, establishing the realms of all sentient beings in the Mahāyāna.
May all sentient beings attain the Dharma of the Dharma-King, equalizing their roots of goodness with those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness from a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s giving away of a royal throne, so that all sentient beings may reach the state of ultimate peace and security.
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for the royal capital or a grand,
adorned city, they give with a joyful mind, with an undistracted mind, with a mind single-mindedly seeking bodhicitta,
with a mind of immeasurable vows, with a mind of great loving-kindness, with a mind of great compassion, and with a mind of cool clarity."
Giving for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings; giving to establish oneself in the Mahāyāna;
giving with a mind of equality toward all Buddha-dharmas; giving with a mind that practices wholesome dharmas; giving with a mind desiring the sovereignty of omniscience;
giving because of seeking the sovereign will of the Dharma King; giving with a mind desiring superior wisdom; desiring...
The practice of giving with a mind of all-pure merit; giving with a firm and vast mind; giving for the sake of nurturing all roots of goodness;
giving for the sake of remaining far removed from the terrors of all Māras and attaining the perfection of Buddha-wisdom;
giving by dwelling securely in the power of the Bodhisattva-mind; this is the conduct of a Bodhisattva regarding all objects and all-knowledge.
Furthermore, they give for the sake of their great vows.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give away royal capitals and grand, adorned cities, they dedicate the roots of goodness therein to sentient beings, saying:
"May all sentient beings purify all buddha-fields and offer them to the Buddhas so that they may dwell therein."
May all sentient beings always delight in aranya dwellings and abide in tranquility;
may all sentient beings not be attached to any lands, capitals, villages, or cities large or small, ultimately becoming free from desire and attaining supreme stillness;
may the minds of all sentient beings not draw near to anything worldly, forever departing from all worldly speech.
May all sentient beings attain a mind free from desire and give away all they possess without regret;
may all sentient beings not be attached to household affairs and attain a pure and upright mind;
may all sentient beings relinquish everything, remain unbound by attachments, and achieve the perfection of skillful giving.
May all sentient beings not be attached to dwelling places, and may they abandon all craving for domestic life;
may all sentient beings relinquish all suffering and affliction, and eliminate all fear, anxiety, and grief;
may all sentient beings take all worlds as adorned and purified buddha-fields and offer them to all Buddhas.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving away royal capitals and grand, adorned cities, so as to cause all sentient beings to purify the abodes of the Buddhas.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give away precious women, attendants, and retinues who are fully equipped with technical skills, possessed of clever talents, adept at witty conversation, and endowed with perfect deportment. They serve with reverence and obedience, capable of moving the hearts of others; they possess every worldly merit without exception, being adorned with such exquisite beauty that they captivate both gods and humans. Their voices are harmonious and elegant, free from coarseness or vulgarity; they serve their masters with utmost propriety, never failing to grasp their intentions, and their countenances are so exceptionally wonderful that those who behold them never grow weary.”

Worth a thousand billion in value, these precious women were provided as attendants; all of this was the karmic fruit of the Bodhisattva’s pure deeds, which he gave away as alms. He gave with a mind free from attachment, with a mind free from delusion, with a mind unbound by any desires, with a mind that clings to no forms, with a mind that does not crave sensual pleasure, with a mind free from the conceptualizations of desire, and with a mind that does not give rise to perceptions of the precious women’s physical beauty.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate the roots of goodness from giving away precious women and their retinues, they dedicate them so that all sentient beings may transcend birth and death; they dedicate them so that all may obtain the joy and bliss of all Buddhas; they dedicate them to attain firmness within that which is not firm; they dedicate them to the indestructible mind of the wisdom of the Vajra-realm; they dedicate them to the Tathāgata’s perfect assembly; they dedicate them to grasping the firm and true; they dedicate them to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi; they dedicate them to the wisdom that discriminates all dharmas; they dedicate them to the production of all roots of goodness; and they dedicate them to never contravening the teachings of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in such dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas, give birth to the path of all-knowledge, and enter deeply into all the wisdom-activities of Bodhisattvas. They cast off all worldly dust and defilement, tame the precious mind, and bring their merits to perfection. As unsurpassed fields of merit, they extensively expound the sublime Dharma, establishing sentient beings and causing them all to practice with complete purity, thereby gathering in all roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness comprised by the gift of precious women and retinues to all sentient beings, saying:
"May all sentient beings attain immeasurable retinues of samādhis, and further attain the indestructible samādhi of a bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings enter the samādhi of the adornments of all Buddhas, and always joyfully behold the Buddhas."
May all sentient beings practice the inconceivable samādhi of the bodhisattva’s sovereign play and dwell securely in immeasurable samādhis of mastery;
may all sentient beings enter the samādhi of suchness and never allow their minds to be disturbed;
may all sentient beings fully attain the profound samādhis of the bodhisattvas and achieve mastery over all samādhis.
May all sentient beings fully accomplish the retinue of samādhis and attain liberation of mind;
may all sentient beings be skillfully able to discern various samādhis and be fully capable of correctly grasping the characteristics of all samādhis;
may all sentient beings attain the samādhi of supreme wisdom and cultivate all gateways of samādhi.
May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded samādhi, enabling them to decisively enter indestructible meditative absorption;
may all sentient beings attain the non-attached samādhi, with minds constantly mindful of practicing the samādhi of non-duality;
may all sentient beings attain indestructible, pure retinues and bodhisattva retinues.
May all sentient beings universally give rise to the pure mind of bodhi and fulfill the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings attain the purity and fulfillment of the power of sarvajñā (omniscience) and obtain supreme wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain compliant retinues and dwell in harmony with the intentions of all beings.
May all sentient beings fully attain omniscience, accomplishing all supreme and wondrous roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings obtain true kinsmen and accomplish the pure Dharma-body of the Tathāgata;
