may all sentient beings accomplish all forms of eloquence, being neither bound nor attached, and extensively expound the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings each act as a virtuous friend for all others, bringing to fulfillment all supreme and wondrous roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings fulfill their pure karma and accomplish all dharmas of purity;
may all sentient beings satisfy the pure and wondrous Dharma-gates of all Buddhas, adorning the world with all pure dharmas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving away precious women and their retinues.

Furthermore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give away their wives, concubines, sons, and daughters—just as Prince Sudāna, the Bodhisattva King Prabhūtaratna, and other such immeasurable Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas did. Riding upon the vehicle of *sarvajñatā* (omniscience), they practice all-encompassing giving, fully perfecting the *dānapāramitā*, purifying the Bodhisattva path of generosity, nurturing a pure mind of giving free from regret, and entering the jewel-like mind of *sarvajñatā* through all-encompassing giving.

May all sentient beings become entirely pure and possess a straightforward mind; having attained this pure and straightforward mind, may they fulfill all aspects of enlightenment, constantly and joyfully seek the pure path of a bodhisattva, uphold the vows of the gateways to the enlightenment of all Buddhas, and cultivate the mind of the family of all Tathāgatas.
In this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva achieves mastery of mental power and seeks the state of a Tathāgata;

knowing his own body to be dependent upon all others and lacking self-mastery, he follows their commands and serves them, practicing universal giving toward all sentient beings and causing those who are not yet fulfilled to be fully satisfied.
To protect and comfort all sentient beings; to desire that one’s own person universally become the foremost stūpa for the world, causing all sentient beings to be entirely filled with joy;
to desire to maintain a mind of equanimity toward all;
and to desire to act as a pool of cool refreshment for the world.
They desire to act as lords who bestow gifts and happiness upon the world;
they desire to be great donors for all beings, with wisdom as their foremost priority, practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva and cultivating it according to the teachings;
they desire to perfect all-knowledge, adorned by their great vows.

One should constantly and single-mindedly seek the field of merit that is wisdom; one should universally invite all sentient beings to nurture their roots of goodness, establish oneself, and reverently follow the True Teaching. One should universally act as a lamp of wisdom for all, maintain right mindfulness of the Bodhisattva’s mind of universal giving, and ensure that all Buddhas are ever present before one.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, with a mind free from attachment, bondage, and liberation, dedicates the roots of goodness gathered through the giving of wife, concubines, sons, and daughters to all sentient beings:

"May all sentient beings universally manifest immeasurable bodies of transformation, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions, turning the wheel of the non-retrogressive Dharma, and establishing all sentient beings in the unsurpassed path;
may all sentient beings not be greedily attached to their bodies, fulfill all their vows, and travel to the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions."
May all sentient beings attain freedom from the mind of attachment and aversion, and sever the fetters of craving and anger;
may all sentient beings become true children of the Buddha, practicing within the family of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings, in the presence of all Buddhas, give rise to the thought of them as their own selves, such that it cannot be destroyed.
May all sentient beings always be children of the Buddha, born through transformation from the Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain right aspiration and realize sarvajñā (all-knowledge);
may all sentient beings cultivate roots of goodness and ultimately fulfill unsurpassed bodhi.
May all sentient beings achieve the bodhi and liberation of all Buddhas and bestow the unsurpassed Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain the mind of non-arising and not destroy the law of causes and conditions;

may all sentient beings sit beneath the Bodhi tree, attain supreme perfect enlightenment, accomplish the unsurpassed path, and transform and give birth to immeasurable sons and daughters of the True Dharma.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving away their wives, concubines, sons, and daughters, so as to cause all sentient beings to attain unattached liberation and unimpeded wisdom.
"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg from his household, he adorns the house with all its ornaments and gives it as a gift, cultivating majestic deportment;

he remains unattached to the home, stays far removed from all discursive thoughts regarding domestic life, and feels weary of household affairs and the necessities of living. He does not give rise to greed for the precious and exquisite objects of pleasure in the home, nor does he find any relish in them. Regarding the various implements of the household, his mind is free from defiled attachment; understanding that the home is subject to decay and changes in an instant, he leaves the home to seek the Way, attains the ultimate Buddha-dharma, and dwells securely as a Bodhisattva. Abiding in the adornments of the Buddha-dharma, his mind is able to relinquish everything without regret, and he is constantly praised by all Buddhas."
Regarding material requisites and all dwelling places, his mind is free from attachment; seeing those who come to seek them, he rejoices immeasurably and is able to give with certainty.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness gathered through the giving of his home to sentient beings in this way:
"May all sentient beings abandon wives and children and always delight in leaving the household life;
may all sentient beings have faith that the household is not the home, leave their homes to seek the Way, and purely cultivate the holy life within the Buddha-dharma."
May all sentient beings delight in all forms of giving, with minds that never regress, and abide securely in freedom from stinginess;
may all sentient beings forever leave behind the ways of householders, possessing few desires and knowing contentment, without any hoarding or accumulation;
may all sentient beings take no pleasure in worldly households, but always delight in the household of the Buddha.
May all sentient beings forever be free from obstructive dharmas and eliminate all paths of obstruction;
may all sentient beings remain unstained by family ties, their minds free from attachment even while living as householders;
may all sentient beings skillfully transform others, preaching the wisdom of perfect enlightenment even while living as householders.
May all sentient beings manifest as householders while dwelling in the abode of the Buddhas, their minds always in accord with the wisdom of the Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings, while remaining at home, be able to gladden all beings and dwell in the abode of the Buddhas.

This is the dedication of the roots of goodness from the donor’s household by the bodhisattva mahāsattva, which causes all sentient beings to practice all the various conducts of a bodhisattva, fulfilling all their aspirations and attaining mastery over wisdom.
"When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives away parks and gardens as adornments for play, they form this thought:
'I shall act as a forest of the Dharma that brings joy to all sentient beings;
I shall manifest places of delight for all sentient beings.'"
I shall bestow immeasurable joy upon all sentient beings;
I shall open the gates of the pure Dharma for all sentient beings so that they may transcend the triple world;
I shall grant supreme bodhi to all sentient beings and fulfill all their aspirations.
I shall act as a compassionate father for all sentient beings, observing the entire triple world with wisdom;
I shall bestow upon all sentient beings the necessities of life so that they lack for nothing;
I shall act as a compassionate mother for all sentient beings, giving birth to roots of goodness and fulfilling all their aspirations.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s dedication of roots of goodness is characterized by a mind that never tires; it is a dedication that distances oneself from all the evils of sentient beings, a dedication to a correct mind, and a dedication to bringing peace and security to all sentient beings;
it is a dedication that does not seek gratitude in return, nor does it seek the gain and offerings of sentient beings.
Dedicating without seeking praise;
dedicating to eliminate the immeasurable suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings;
dedicating so that the minds of all sentient beings become pure like space.
Taking all roots of goodness as the foremost, they dedicate by contemplating the reality of all phenomena;
they dedicate so that all sentient beings may adorn themselves with great adornments and forever leave behind the aggregate of suffering;
and they dedicate to never being satiated in their vows for the Mahāyāna, to forever leave behind false views, and to fully cultivate the practices of bodhisattvas and all great vows.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates to sentient beings the roots of goodness gathered through sporting in gardens adorned with giving:
to cause all sentient beings to attain ever-surpassing roots of goodness and ultimately achieve the mind of the garden of unsurpassed bodhi;
and to cause all sentient beings to attain the unshakable Dharma, universally behold all Buddhas, and be filled with joy.
May all sentient beings always delight in the forest of Dharma, attaining Buddha-fields and enjoying their groves;
may all sentient beings attain a pure and wondrous mind, constantly beholding the forest of the Tathāgata’s great supernormal powers;
may all sentient beings take joy in the Tathāgata’s sovereign mastery and the sovereign wisdom of his playful sport, traveling throughout the ten directions.
May all sentient beings practice the play of the Dharma, visiting the buddha-fields to inquire about and receive the transformative teachings of the Way;
may all sentient beings delight in the play of the bodhisattvas, practicing the bodhisattva conduct throughout all future kalpas with minds free from weariness, dwelling securely in liberation;
may all sentient beings behold all Buddhas filling the dharma-realm, delighting in the great mind of the Buddhas within pure gardens and groves.
May all sentient beings travel to the buddha-fields with hearts full of joy, making offerings to the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings delight in the mind of detachment from desire, purifying and adorning all buddha-fields.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas through the adornment of gardens and groves for the purpose of giving, so that all sentient beings may sport in the gardens and groves of all Buddhas and behold all Buddhas.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, the Great Vaipulya, Scroll Eighteen;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, the Great Vaipulya, Scroll Nineteen.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Sixth [Section] of the Chapter on the Twenty-First Ten Dedications of Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva, Part Six:
"Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva performs immeasurable billions of nayutas of asaṃkhyeyas of great assemblies for giving, which are free from evil, pure, and praised by all Buddhas."
Universally purifying all sentient beings so they forever leave behind all evils, he purifies the traces of the three karmas and gives birth to sarvajñā (all-knowledge);
all immeasurable realms are entirely pure, and he bestows as gifts immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of articles for giving, all magnificently adorned.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness gathered through great assemblies of giving to all sentient beings, saying:
"May all sentient beings fully attain the mind of unsurpassed bodhi, practice immeasurable giving, and be entirely pure;
may all sentient beings reach the ultimate, immeasurable, and boundless path of purity."
May all sentient beings practice immeasurable loving-kindness, satisfying everyone according to their needs;
may all sentient beings practice immeasurable compassion, being able to rescue and protect all living beings;
may all sentient beings follow the true teachings of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, bringing joy to the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings, in the presence of all Buddhas, practice giving with minds free from regret;
may all sentient beings fully nurture the supreme and wondrous faculty of faith, practicing and increasing immeasurable giving in every thought-moment;
may all sentient beings attain the mind of Mahāyāna and fully accomplish the great assembly of Mahāyāna giving.

May all sentient beings achieve the great assembly of giving, ultimate giving, excellent giving, supreme giving, wish-fulfilling giving, foremost giving, superior giving, unsurpassed giving, peerless giving, world-transcending giving, and the giving praised by all Buddhas;

may all sentient beings become the foremost donors, uprooting beings from all evil realms and establishing them on the path of unimpeded, pure wisdom, cultivating impartial vows and true roots of goodness, and attaining the unequaled wisdom of the Tathāgata.

May all sentient beings abide securely in the wisdom of tranquil meditative concentrations, enter the path to the deathless, and ultimately perfect all supernormal powers, clarities, and wisdom; may they be courageous and diligent, fulfill all the stages (*bhūmi*), adorn the Buddha-dharma, reach the ultimate further shore, and never regress.

May all sentient beings attain the assembly of the non-regressive Mahāyāna, provide for and bestow upon others without ceasing, and ultimately realize the unsurpassed knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
May all sentient beings plant various roots of goodness and all arrive at the further shore of immeasurable merit.

May all sentient beings be praised by all Buddhas, universally acting as great donors for all, fully endowed with merit that fills the Dharma-realm, and universally illuminating the ten directions to bestow unsurpassed bliss;
may all sentient beings become masters of impartial and great giving, perfecting their roots of goodness and equally gathering in all beings;
may all sentient beings become supreme donors, establishing everyone in the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
May all sentient beings become donors who give at the proper time, entirely free from untimely giving, and ultimately reach the assembly of the right moment;
may all sentient beings become excellent donors, possessing the dharma of the great person’s giving, and arrive at the other shore;
may all sentient beings become donors who purify through adornment, reaching the state of the *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge) of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings become pure donors for the sake of all, giving rise to and accumulating merits equal to the dharma-realm;

may all sentient beings become donors who transcend all others, fulfilling great vows, liberating sentient beings, and abiding in the Tathāgata’s power of knowing what is possible and what is impossible.

This is the dedication of the roots of goodness from the great giving of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, which causes all sentient beings to practice supreme relinquishment: the ultimate giving of a Buddha, the accomplishment of virtuous giving, the indestructible giving, the giving of the Dharma of all Buddhas, the giving of a heart with eyes of love, the giving that rescues sentient beings, the giving of omniscience (*sarvajñā*), the giving of seeing all Buddhas, the giving endowed with dignified conduct, and the giving of the Buddha-wisdom that fulfills the merits practiced by Bodhisattvas.
"Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva completely relinquishes all requisites for life, with a mind free from greedy attachment and seeking no karmic reward;
having no expectations for worldly wealth or pleasure, they abandon ignorance and deeply understand all dharmas;
they benefit and establish all sentient beings."

With a mind of true reality, they understand all phenomena; through various adornments, the necessities of life, and immeasurable realms, they provide various ornaments and the requisites for livelihood to benefit sentient beings.

They practice ultimate giving, universal giving, and the giving of both internal and external things, increasing their straightforward mind and causing all sentient beings to possess a mind that is a jewel of merit. They are well able to benefit immeasurable sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to achieve the precious mind.
May all sentient beings possess pure roots of goodness equal to those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time and be endowed with all-encompassing wisdom.
With the roots of goodness gathered through the gift of the necessities of life, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates them to sentient beings:
may all sentient beings be purified and disciplined.
May all sentient beings thoroughly adorn and purify all Buddha-lands and extinguish their afflictions;
may all sentient beings, with pure minds, fill the Dharma-realm in every thought-moment;
may all sentient beings have wisdom that fills the void and the Dharma-realm.
May all sentient beings attain all-knowledge and thoroughly comprehend the three periods of time, turning the non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma at all times;
may all sentient beings manifest all-encompassing wisdom through skillful and subtle means to benefit all beings;
may all sentient beings awaken to the path of all Tathāgatas, extensively expounding the Buddha-dharma in all lands throughout all future kalpas without ever resting.
May all sentient beings cultivate the bodhisattva practices throughout immeasurable eons with minds free from weariness;

may all sentient beings, in all worlds— pure worlds, impure worlds, small worlds, medium worlds, great worlds, subtle worlds, vast worlds, inverted worlds, and prostrate worlds— thoroughly purify and adorn every such world.

The Bodhisattvas are fully perfected and practice the Mahāyāna path, causing all sentient beings, in every moment of thought, to perform all the Buddha-deeds of the three periods of time, thereby taming sentient beings and establishing them in sarvajñā (omniscience).
This bodhisattva-mahāsattva, through such immeasurable and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, benefits sentient beings so as to ensure that the Buddha-dharma is never interrupted;
with a heart of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), he protects sentient beings, cultivates great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), and fulfills the bodhisattva practices;
he establishes the treatises of all Tathāgatas, ensuring that all sentient beings never sever their roots of goodness in the Buddhas.

Whenever there are those who come seeking anything, he fulfills their wishes entirely without weariness or aversion. He is able to give all things with a heart free from regret, relinquishing all possessions and the necessities of life. Toward every direction from which seekers arrive, he is never anything but joyful; regarding all sentient beings as his only child, he feels great delight upon seeing those who come to beg, thinking to himself:
"These are my spiritual friends."
"At that time, the Bodhisattva nurtured a mind of great compassion, a mind of joy, an indestructible mind, and a mind of great generosity;

whenever the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva saw a seeker come, he provided them with whatever they required, fully satisfying their wishes so that none lacked anything, making them all rejoice, severing their poverty and suffering, and endowing them with wealth and happiness, whereupon they would praise him in unison, extolling his virtue before returning home."
At that time, the Bodhisattva’s heart was filled with great joy; for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas, even the pleasures of Śakra could not equal it.
The joys experienced by the kings of Suyāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas could not equal it.

Even the bliss of the Brahmā kings, up to the immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable kalpas of meditative concentration and happiness enjoyed by the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, could not reach it.
Even the bliss of being a wheel-turning monarch for immeasurable, incalculable, ineffable, and asaṃkhyeya kalpas cannot equal it.

For the bodhisattva mahāsattva, such great joy is immeasurable; their faith increases, their straightforward mind becomes pure, their faculties become supple, their concentrated mind expands, and they give rise to a firm and unshakable resolve for bodhicitta.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness so that all sentient beings may be free from harmful intent; so that all sentient beings may dwell in peace and happiness; so that all sentient beings may attain the true meaning; so that all sentient beings may fully attain pure, unsurpassed bodhi; so that all sentient beings may attain equanimity; so that all sentient beings may attain a virtuous and wholesome mind; so that all sentient beings may reach the virtuous and wholesome Mahāyāna mind; so that all actions performed by all sentient beings are entirely wholesome; so that all sentient beings may be endowed with the vows and practices cultivated by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; and so that all sentient beings may awaken to the vehicle of the Ten Powers.

"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness, they dedicate them with liberation through non-attachment and non-binding in the actions of body, speech, and mind; they dedicate them without the notion of a sentient being."

Without the notion of a life-force, the notion of a person, the notion of a *pudgala*, the notion of a man, the notion of a youth, the notion of a *śrotriya*, the notion of an agent, the notion of a recipient, the notion of existence, the notion of non-existence, the notion of this world or the next world, the notion of dying here and being born there, the notion of permanence, the notion of impermanence, the notion of the three realms of existence, the notion of the absence of the three realms of existence, the notion of neither-perception-nor-non-perception—there is the dedication of a mind that is unbound, unattached, and liberated; the dedication of no-karma; the dedication of no-karmic retribution; the dedication of no-falsity; the dedication of no-reality; the dedication of no-thought; the dedication of no-thought-retribution; the dedication of no-mind; and the dedication of no-no-mind.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they do not cling to the internal, nor do they cling to the external;
they do not cling to conditions, nor do they cling to objective spheres;
they do not cling to causes, nor do they cling to the conjunction of causes.
He does not cling to dharmas, nor does he cling to non-dharmas;
he does not cling to volition, nor does he cling to the fruit of volition;
he does not cling to form, nor does he cling to the grasping of form, nor does he cling to the cessation of form.

One does not cling to feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness; one does not cling to the grasping of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness; and one does not cling to the cessation of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not become attached to these dharmas within this teaching, they will not be bound by form, nor bound by the grasping of form, nor bound by the cessation of form;

they will not be bound by feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor bound by the grasping of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness, nor bound by the cessation of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness.
If one is not bound by these phenomena, then there is likewise no liberation from all phenomena. Why is this? Because all phenomena are neither born nor extinguished;

they lack intrinsic nature; they are neither one nor two, neither many nor few, neither measurable nor immeasurable, neither good nor evil, neither deep nor shallow, neither still nor distracted, neither attached nor detached, neither dharma nor non-dharma, neither existence nor non-existence, and because they are neither being nor non-being.
When a bodhisattva perceives phenomena in this way, they are in fact non-phenomena (*adharma*), because the path of verbal expression has been severed.
They take what is non-dharmic as dharma, yet they do not destroy the traces of any karmic activity.

Fully cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva, they do not retreat from omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). Understanding that karmic conditions are like dreams, echoes, and reflections in a mirror, and that all phenomena are like illusions, they nevertheless do not contravene the retribution of causes, conditions, and karma.
They enter into profound karma, understanding the reality of dharmas as being without activity or fabrication, yet they do not contravene the path of karmic conduct.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate all roots of goodness in this way:
"May all-knowledge universally traverse the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings."
What is the meaning of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*)?
It is called dedication because it eternally carries one across the world to the further shore of birth and death;
it is called dedication because it carries one across the further shore of the aggregates (*skandha*).
Because they have crossed to the other shore of the path of language, they are said to dedicate;
because they have crossed to the other shore of the mark of sentient beings, they are said to dedicate;
because they have crossed to the other shore of the view of a self-identity, they are said to dedicate.
One speaks of dedication because of crossing to the further shore of what is not firm;
one speaks of dedication because of crossing to the further shore of all conditioned formations (*saṃskāra*);
one speaks of dedication because of crossing to the further shore of all states of existence (*bhava*).
Because it crosses over to the further shore of all grasping, it is called dedication;
because it crosses over to the further shore of all worldly dharmas, it is called dedication.

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva can dedicate these roots of goodness in this way, then they will all accord with all Buddhas, accord with the Dharma, accord with wisdom, accord with enlightenment, accord with meaning, accord with dedication, accord with practice, accord with reality, and accord with purity.
When the bodhisattva-mahāsattva has thus dedicated [the merit], they cause all sentient beings to attain the Dharma of the Tathāgata;

all Buddhas rejoice, there is no Buddha they do not encounter, and no Dharma they do not understand. Regarding all phenomena, they neither contradict nor err; they are able to discern all Buddha-dharmas, never abandoning the True Dharma, and never violating the principle of causes and conditions. With respect to all internal and external phenomena, their power of the Dharma is fully perfected and never ceases.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the sixth dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, which accords with all firm roots of goodness.
When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abide in this dedication, immeasurable Buddhas all protect them; they attain the firm Dharma and cultivate all-knowledge.

They understand the meaning of accordance and understand all phenomena, acceding with the true nature; they attain all phenomena, acceding to firm roots of goodness and acceding to the fulfillment of all vows.
They attain accordance with the firm Dharma, which cannot be destroyed by any vajra; they attain accordance with firm vows, thereby attaining mastery over all phenomena.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions, observed the entire great assembly, and contemplated the dharma-realm. He deeply penetrated the meanings of the phrases and flavors of all dharmas, cultivated immeasurable minds, and universally covered all sentient beings with great compassion. He awakened to the family-dharmas of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, entered into the merits of all Buddhas, and attained the sovereign bodies of all Buddhas. Discerning the minds of all sentient beings, according to the roots of goodness they had planted and the time when they were ready for transformation, he manifested a form-body in accordance with the dharma-body, and spoke in verse:
"The great kings of all worlds— The Bodhisattva manifests his body among them."
Occupying that position of a noble and eminent great king, he is fully able to subdue all living beings.
His mind is supple and ever pure; he attains mastery over all beings.
He always governs the world with the True Dharma, employing skillful means to accord with and bring joy to the world.
The Bodhisattva is born into a pure royal family, Always able to turn the wheel of Dharma as appropriate;
Remaining far removed from all evils while governing the realm with righteousness, The sentient beings of the ten directions do not oppose his teachings.
The Bodhisattva’s physical marks and merits are perfected; Possessing profound and wondrous wisdom, Firmly established in non-retrogression, He is able to subdue all Māras.
Always able to fully maintain the pure precepts, Resolutely abiding in the power of patience,
Eliminating all the poison of anger, They are always able to cultivate the most supreme Dharma.
The Bodhisattva fully practices the Dharma of giving: food and drink, flower garlands, vehicles, clothing, scented ointments, dwellings, and bright, pure lamps—such acts of giving are immeasurable.
The Bodhisattva’s giving benefits sentient beings; He is always able to develop a vast and great mind.
With a pure intention and great joy, He bestows upon those who are noble and supreme, as well as upon the world.
The Bodhisattva is able to relinquish all things, both internal and external, in measureless abundance;
in the practice of giving, they are always joyful, never for a moment harboring a heart of regret.
The Bodhisattva is able to give away his head and eyes, His hands, feet, flesh, muscles, and even his marrow;
He bestows every part of his body as a gift, And his mind never once gives rise to regret.
The Bodhisattva, dwelling in the position of a great king, pure and noble among the most honored of men, gives his tongue to all living beings out of great compassion;
though subjected to immeasurable torture and agony, he never feels regret.
The Bodhisattva’s pure roots of goodness from giving his tongue Dedicates to all living beings,
Causing every such class of sentient beings To fully achieve the broad and long tongue.
The Bodhisattva joyfully gives away his wife and children, yet his mind never gives rise to sorrow or regret;
furthermore, he delights in giving away his kingdom, and is likewise able to relinquish his own body without any stinginess.
He gives everything they seek according to their desires; he bestows gifts at the proper time without resentment.
Able to relinquish all that he possesses, he brings complete satisfaction to all who come seeking.
For the sake of the Dharma, he has sacrificed his body countless times; practicing various ascetic austerities, he sought Bodhi.
Furthermore, for the sake of sentient beings, he underwent all manner of sufferings, seeking supreme wisdom without ever retreating.
Because they hear and receive the True Dharma of the Tathāgata, they offer their bodies in almsgiving without weariness;
their inner joy is immeasurable, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings.
Having seen all the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, with hearts of loving-kindness and reverence, present offerings;
fully endowed with benefit and joy, they are able to hear and uphold all the Buddha-dharmas.
Dedicating this to all classes of sentient beings, may they all attain peace and happiness in the world;
may you universally protect and succor all multitudes, forever enabling them to achieve ultimate liberation.

The Bodhisattva is endowed with a full retinue; their physical forms are dignified and compliant with his instructions, adorned with exquisite ornaments, and they are sagacious, benevolent, virtuous, and skilled in wisdom.
Out of a desire to benefit others, they give everything away, never harboring even the slightest stinginess;
not for the sake of worldly livelihood or profit, but to benefit sentient beings, they seek awakening.
Fully cultivating and practicing pure merit, Performing immeasurable and supreme deeds,
Dedicating them to all classes of sentient beings, Yet not grasping at the solid characteristics of those actions.
The Bodhisattva was able to renounce the rank of a great king, along with the magnificent adornments of the capital and its various cities,
all things within and without the palace, and the gardens, groves, and various ponds for strolling and viewing.
For immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of kalpas, you have practiced giving with the unsurpassed mind;
awakening the world and showing it the further shore, you guide and transform all classes of living beings in accordance with their needs.

When a Bodhisattva sees those who come seeking, all arriving from worlds in other directions, he fulfills their wishes according to what each requires; great joy then suffuses the Bodhisattva’s entire body.
The Bodhisattva dedicates the merit of their giving to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
having perfected what they have studied, they reach the further shore, the realm of the Unsurpassed Teacher.
The Bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena: who is it that delivers sentient beings, and whom does he deliver to what destination?
Understanding emptiness, he does not abandon the mind of giving.
Because the bodhisattva dedicates for the sake of wisdom, The bodhisattva dedicates seeking the true Dharma,
And the bodhisattva dedicates to the profound meaning, They remain unattached to all phenomena.
The mind does not discriminate among any karmas, nor is it stained by or attached to the retributions of those karmas;
it thoroughly understands that bodhi arises from conditions, and thus does nothing to destroy the true nature of dharmas.
Having understood that one’s own body is without defilement or attachment, the mind is tranquil and has no basis;
through wisdom one discerns that there is no nature of karma, yet one skillfully understands that causes and conditions are not without karma.
Not falsely grasping at past phenomena, nor grasping at future phenomena,
one thoroughly understands that the present is non-existent, observing that all three periods of time are entirely empty and quiescent.
The Bodhisattva has reached the ultimate shore of form; feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise so.
Having forever crossed over all things to reach the other shore, his mind is humble, compliant, and ever pure.
Observing the five aggregates and the eighteen elements, and discerning the various sense bases as well as one's own body—
seeking awakening within all these phenomena, they are found to be entirely empty, quiescent, and ungraspable.
One does not grasp at the mark of the permanence of all phenomena, nor does one accept the mark of annihilation;
all phenomena are neither existent nor non-existent, for they arise through the harmonious conjunction of karmic causes and conditions.
There is no sentient being who attains enlightenment; all phenomena are entirely quiescent.
The mind is unstained by attachment to any buddha-field, and one thoroughly understands that the three periods of time are non-existent.
If one can understand the true Dharma in this way, they are just like all the Most Victorious Ones.
Although one seeks them and finds nothing at all, the conduct of the Bodhisattva is not in vain;
therefore, one seeks all phenomena within conditions, never contravening the path of all causes and conditions.
To analytically explain the traces of all karmas, desiring to bring all sentient beings to complete purity—
this is what is practiced by the wise, as taught by all Buddhas.
Following and reflecting upon this, one enters into the true meaning; One spontaneously awakens to the unsurpassed path:
that all phenomena are neither born nor extinguished, Neither coming nor going, not dying here to be reborn there.
Thus one deeply understands all the teachings of the Buddhas.
Thoroughly comprehending the true nature of all phenomena, they have no attachment within that dharmatā.
Forever free from the false appearances of all phenomena, such persons attain the vision of the Buddhas' wisdom;
they analytically understand the destinies of all phenomena—the various realms of sentient beings and the realm of the Buddha-lands.
All phenomena existing throughout the three periods of time, he knows them all completely without exception;
the dharmas awakened to by all Buddhas of the three periods, he is able to hear, receive, and uphold them all in their entirety.
All dharmas of the three periods of time that have been taught—such dharmas as these are all non-dharmas;
yet, while practicing in accordance with all dharmas, one does not destroy the characteristics of dharmas.
The Bodhisattva dedicates [merit] to all sentient beings, so that they may swiftly attain all-knowledge.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the seventh dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: the dedication of an impartial mind that accords with all sentient beings?
O Son of the Buddha!”
This bodhisattva mahāsattva increases inferior roots of goodness, middling roots of goodness, superior roots of goodness,
immeasurable roots of goodness, vast roots of goodness, diverse roots of goodness, unfathomable roots of goodness, inconceivable roots of goodness,
incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) roots of goodness, and boundless roots of goodness.
The roots of goodness of the faculties; the roots of goodness of the Buddha-realm; the roots of goodness of the Dharma-realm; the roots of goodness of the Saṅgha-realm;
the roots of goodness of the realm of spiritual friends; the roots of goodness of the realm of all sentient beings; the roots of goodness of the realm of skillful means;
the roots of goodness of the realm of cultivating the subtle and wondrous; the roots of goodness of the internal realm; and the external [realm].
The roots of goodness of the sphere; the roots of goodness of the sphere of immeasurable and distinct merits;
the roots of goodness of the sphere of practicing all forms of giving; the roots of goodness of the sphere of pure precepts;

the roots of goodness of the sphere of a bodhisattva’s internal self-composure and rectitude regarding all relinquishment and patience; and the roots of goodness of the sphere of non-regressive diligence.
...the roots of goodness for entering the various states of meditative concentration; the roots of goodness for practicing the wisdom-realms of the various stages (*bhūmi*);
the roots of goodness for discerning the mental states and objects of all sentient beings; the roots of goodness for accumulating immeasurable pure merit;
the roots of goodness for cultivating the realm of the bodhisattva’s practice of right mindfulness; and universally covering...
Regarding the roots of goodness within the spheres of all sentient beings,

when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice such immeasurable roots of goodness— cultivating them to perfection, accumulating and nurturing them, and having extensively developed their understanding— they are then able to abide securely in the power of patience,

closing the gates to the evil realms; they skillfully discipline their faculties, are fully endowed with dignified deportment, forever depart from inversion, and proceed resolutely toward the correct path.
They are capable of being vessels for the Dharma of all Buddhas and serve as supreme fields of merit for all sentient beings;

they are constantly protected by all Buddhas, giving birth to and nurturing the pure roots of goodness of all Buddhas; they accord with and fulfill the great vows of the Tathāgatas, deeply delighting in the Buddha-works, attaining mastery of mind, and becoming equal to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
they are able to universally make offerings to all Buddhas, perfecting the powers of all Tathāgatas, and are always praised by all Buddhas.

They do not seek rebirth in the heavens, do not crave gain or offerings, and do not cling to any conditioned phenomena. They dedicate all roots of goodness to serve as a treasury of merit for all sentient beings;

they are fully endowed with all paths and universally shelter all beings, pulling them out from within birth and death, teaching them to cultivate all roots of goodness, and dedicating them toward all realms without interruption;
they open the gate of omniscient bodhi, erect the banner of wisdom, and adorn and purify the Great Path.
He universally shows sentient beings how to abandon all worldly dust and defilements;

he bestows the merit of his mind, causing them to be born into the family of the Tathāgata. With pure merit fully perfected, they become unsurpassed fields of blessings; they do not cling to sentient beings nor rely upon the world.
He causes all sentient beings to become entirely pure, cultivating and gathering all roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, with a bodhicitta that is stainless and pure, gathers roots of goodness and forms this thought:

"These roots of goodness arising from bodhicitta, these roots of goodness contemplated by bodhicitta, these roots of goodness obtained through bodhicitta, these roots of goodness through the right aspiration of bodhicitta, and these roots of goodness of the single-minded bodhicitta—out of compassion for all sentient beings, they encompass the realm of all-knowledge, culminate in the realm of the ten powers, and accumulate the realm of the ten powers;
they are roots of goodness that do not destroy the dharma-realm, and roots of goodness that are non-retrogressive."
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

'If these roots of goodness have any fruit of retribution, I shall, until the end of the future, practice the bodhisattva conduct; because I do not abandon sentient beings, I shall cultivate great relinquishment and dedicate it to all sentient beings without exception:'"

May countless worlds be filled with precious jewels; may countless worlds be filled with precious garments; may countless worlds be filled with exquisite fragrances; may countless worlds be filled with ornaments; may countless worlds be filled with *maṇi* gems; may countless worlds be filled with supreme *maṇi* gems; may countless worlds be filled with various flowers of wondrous color; may countless worlds be filled with superior flavors; may countless worlds be filled with gold and silver; may countless worlds be filled with celestial couches, adorned with exquisite jewels and spread with celestial robes; and may countless worlds be filled with celestial crowns adorned with various jewels.
If there were a person who, throughout all future kalpas, constantly came to seek [these things], and one bestowed these precious objects upon them without ever becoming weary or tired—
just as with one sentient being, so it would be for all sentient beings.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice giving in this way, they do so with a mind of equanimity, a mind free from partiality, a mind that seeks no fame, a mind free from feverish distress, a mind free from regret, a mind solely seeking all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), a mind of the pure path, a mind of single-minded generosity, a mind of compassion, a mind of self-mastery, and a mind established in all-knowledge.
With their roots of goodness thus dedicated, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas constantly practice giving throughout all future eons.
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates his roots of goodness to all sentient beings without exception, thinking:

'I shall fill countless worlds with precious elephants, complete with seven limbs, possessing full six protuberances, adorned with great precious banners, decorated with pure gold, covered with nets of white jewels, and embellished with all kinds of miscellaneous gems, and offer them as a gift;
I shall fill countless worlds with pure precious horses, such as the king of horses, Bālāha, adorned with every kind of equestrian treasure, and offer them as a gift.'"
He gives in charity countless worlds filled with precious women, complete with all means of entertainment;
he gives in charity countless worlds filled with men and women;
he gives in charity countless worlds filled with his own body.
He fills countless worlds with his own body and head, giving them away with a mind free from negligence;
he fills countless worlds with his own eyes, giving them away as an offering;
he fills countless worlds with his own body, enduring bitter suffering and piercing his bones to extract his marrow, giving it all away as an offering.
He gave as alms countless worlds entirely filled with great thrones;
he gave as alms countless worlds entirely filled with servants and attendants.
Cultivating a mind of universal giving characterized by equanimity, one practices the bodhisattva path for the sake of a single sentient being throughout all future kalpas within a single world;
one likewise practices the bodhisattva path for the sake of a single sentient being throughout all future kalpas in all worlds;
and for the sake of all sentient beings, it is exactly the same.

Endowed with great compassion and far removed from all evils, he universally regards all beings and causes me to practice giving without ever regressing; when performing acts of generosity, he does not give rise to even a single thought of sorrow or regret.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"I practice such immeasurable giving with a mind free from attachment, a mind free from bondage, a mind of liberation, a great mind, a profound mind, a mind of gathering, a mind free from aversion and affection, a mind free from concern for life, a well-tamed mind, an undisturbed mind, a harmless mind, a mind established in all-knowledge, a mind whose light of wisdom universally illumines all phenomena, and a mind that enters into all-knowledge."
"The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness moment by moment, thinking:
'May all sentient beings be fully satisfied with wealth and treasures;
may all sentient beings be endowed with an inexhaustible treasury of great merit.'"
May all sentient beings attain peace and happiness;
may all sentient beings nurture the practice of the Bodhisattva Mahāyāna;
may all sentient beings fulfill the profound Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain non-retrogression in the vehicle of omniscience;
may all sentient beings behold all Buddhas; may all sentient beings universally regard all beings without making any distinctions.
May all sentient beings attain a pure and equanimous mind;
may all sentient beings leave behind all places of hardship and attain omniscience;
may all sentient beings bring benefit, peace, and happiness to immeasurable beings.
May all sentient beings universally attain a mind of equanimity toward all things;
may all sentient beings attain a mind of gentle generosity;
may all sentient beings embrace a mind of true and authentic giving.
May all sentient beings never lose the mind of giving;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the mind of giving and forever extinguish poverty;
may all sentient beings gather all the wonderful treasures of the world so that they lack for nothing.
May all sentient beings practice immeasurable giving;
may all sentient beings practice all-encompassing giving;
may all sentient beings, throughout all future kalpas, cultivate the practice of generosity with minds that never regress.
May all sentient beings completely relinquish everything without any regret in their hearts;
may all sentient beings practice giving in accordance with the Dharma to benefit other beings;
may all sentient beings practice supreme and vast generosity.
May all sentient beings practice various forms of adorned giving;
may all sentient beings practice unattached giving;
may all sentient beings practice impartial giving.
May all sentient beings practice the gift of the great power of the vajra;
may all sentient beings practice the gift of the radiance of the sun;
may all sentient beings attain the wisdom of the Tathāgata.
May all sentient beings fully perfect and complete their retinue of roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings bring forth the wisdom of their roots of goodness before them;
may all sentient beings attain an indestructible and upright mind.
May all sentient beings fully accomplish and perfect pure roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings awaken with wisdom from the slumber of afflictions;
may all sentient beings have their doubts entirely eliminated.
May all sentient beings attain the merit of pure, equalizing wisdom;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with merit such that none can destroy it;
and may all sentient beings be complete in the pure, unshakable samādhi.
May all sentient beings be endowed with the indestructible wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*);
may all sentient beings be fully possessed of the immeasurable, pure, and sovereign right practices of bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings cultivate unattached and pure roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings purify and correctly cultivate the right mindfulness of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may all sentient beings give rise to supreme, wondrous, and pure roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings eliminate all demons, demonic activities, and obstacles to the Dharma that hinder the Path.
May all sentient beings fully practice and fulfill immeasurable merits, giving rise to various samādhis that are pure and complete;
may all sentient beings constantly keep the Buddhas in mind, never forgetting them;
may all sentient beings always behold the Buddhas, causing them all to rejoice, never being separated from them for even a moment.
May all sentient beings open the gateways of the pure Dharma, give birth to roots of goodness, and fully possess all pure and white dharmas with equanimity;
may all sentient beings attain an immeasurable, impartial, and upright mind;
and may all sentient beings accomplish a mind of pure and impartial giving.
May all sentient beings fulfill the śīla-pāramitā of all Buddhas, becoming impartial and pure;
may all sentient beings possess the mahā-vīrya-pāramitā, never falling into indolence;
may all sentient beings attain the mahā-kṣānti-pāramitā.
May all sentient beings attain immeasurable meditative concentration and wisdom, and fully master the various supernormal powers through discernment;
may all sentient beings attain the Prajñāpāramitā that is free from the body regarding all phenomena, and achieve equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-realm, and achieve equal fulfillment.
May all sentient beings fully possess the pure, wondrous roots of goodness of the various supernormal powers;
may all sentient beings cultivate impartial conduct and be endowed with all wholesome dharmas;
may all sentient beings ultimately and forever cross over into the realm of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain equal purity in the actions of body, speech, and mind;
may all sentient beings attain equal purity in the retributions of their various karmic deeds;
may all sentient beings fully attain equal purity in all dharmas.
May all sentient beings fully attain the true meaning of the purity and equality of all phenomena;
may all sentient beings fully attain all pure, supreme, and wondrous practices;
may all sentient beings fully attain all the pure vows of Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings universally attain the wisdom of pure merit that is equal for all;
may all sentient beings dedicate their various roots of goodness toward the vehicle of *sarvajñā* (omniscience), attaining equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings manifest all adorned and purified Buddha-fields, attaining equal fulfillment.
May all sentient beings be enabled to behold all Buddhas, thereby eliminating and extinguishing all afflictions and ailments;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the primary and secondary marks of excellence, adorned with merit, and fulfilled in equanimity;
may all sentient beings attain the eightfold voice, adorned with hundreds of thousands of wondrous sounds, fully possessing the immeasurable, pure Brahma-voice of the Tathāgata’s infinite merits.
May all sentient beings be adorned with the ten powers and achieve an unimpeded, impartial mind;
may all sentient beings attain the inexhaustible light of the Dharma and immeasurable eloquence of all Buddhas, fulfilling them with equanimity;
may all sentient beings attain the supreme, fearless Great Lion’s Roar of the Hero among Men.
May all sentient beings attain all-knowledge and turn the non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma;
may all sentient beings give birth to all dharmas and achieve equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings purify their roots of goodness, never missing the proper time, and achieve equal fulfillment.
May all sentient beings achieve and equally fulfill the Dharma of the Pure Tamer of Men;
may all sentient beings equally fulfill the singular adornment, the immeasurable adornment, the great adornment, and the adornments of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings observe the three periods of time and discern them as equal.
May all sentient beings go to the abodes of all Buddhas, hear the Dharma, receive and uphold it, and fully realize its equality;
may all sentient beings possess a sense of shame and wisdom equal to those of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the wisdom of equality and contemplate all phenomena.
May all sentient beings attain the retribution of immovable karma, be free from all obstacles, and achieve equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings enter profound wisdom, fully discern and know the faculties of all beings, and achieve equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings attain non-conceptual, equalizing wisdom, become entirely uniform, and achieve pure fulfillment.
May all sentient beings follow and never tire of roots of goodness, discerning with equanimity so that they are all fully satisfied;
may all sentient beings attain mastery over great supernormal powers, with the spiritual power of Bodhisattvas equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings obtain the inexhaustible treasury of merit and wisdom of all Buddhas, reaching ultimate merit so that all are equal and one.
May all sentient beings attain freedom from falsehood regarding all phenomena, accord with equality, enter into all dharmas, and realize the bodhicitta;
may all sentient beings become supreme and wondrous fields of merit, fulfilled in equanimity;
may all sentient beings attain pure great compassion and universally become the most supreme fields of merit for the world.
May all sentient beings be firm and indestructible, and be equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings see the true Dharma, which is indestructible, and be equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings attain the most supreme mind, contemplate with correct observation, and be equally fulfilled.
May all sentient beings be freed from all fears, enter the profound Dharma, and reach the other shore;
may all sentient beings emit a single ray of light that universally illumines the ten directions, equally delivering all;
may all sentient beings fully attain the non-regressive diligence of Bodhisattvas, sharing the same practices and the same vows, and achieve equal fulfillment.
May all sentient beings, with a single utterance, attain equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings attain equal fulfillment in the bodhisattva’s straightforward mind;
may all sentient beings behold all spiritual friends and experience great joy in their hearts.
May all sentient beings fully possess all the practices of Bodhisattvas, taming sentient beings without ever resting, and be equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings attain uninterrupted eloquence, universally entering all sounds, and be equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings be able, with a single mind, to know all minds and all roots of goodness, and be equally fulfilled.
May all sentient beings cultivate various roots of goodness without falling back, and may they be established in pure wisdom;
may all sentient beings attain omniscience, impartial merit, and the pure Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings completely abandon ignorance, examine their roots of goodness, and achieve equal fulfillment.
May all sentient beings attain the single *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), achieve equal and perfect enlightenment, and be equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings leave behind all evil realms, give birth to the single path of all-seed knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*), and be equally fulfilled;
may all sentient beings attain the purity of a single assembly, being able to universally purify all assemblies and adorn them with equal wisdom.
May all sentient beings, within a single buddha-field, universally behold all the fields of all Tathāgatas, attaining equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings adorn all buddha-fields with every kind of adornment—inexpressible adornments, immeasurable adornments, and inexhaustible adornments—attaining equal fulfillment;
may all sentient beings discern and understand immeasurable dharmas and perceive their profound meaning, attaining equal fulfillment.
May all sentient beings attain the various noble practices and the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas, fulfilling them with equanimity;
may all sentient beings, being neither identical nor different, fulfill the various supernormal powers with equanimity;
may all sentient beings, in accordance with their roots of goodness, universally receive the consecration of ambrosia from all Buddhas.
"May all sentient beings possess a pure body of wisdom, fully and equally endowed with it.

Thus, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, out of compassion and for the benefit of sentient beings, and out of great pity and mindfulness for them, causes all sentient beings to become entirely pure; they leave behind the fetters of stinginess and envy, become fully endowed with immeasurable and boundless virtuous merits, always delight in the supreme Dharma, and remain free from the turbidity of anger and all obstacles."

His mind is supple, free from delusion, upright, and without crookedness; his conduct is firm and solid, incapable of being thwarted or destroyed. He has attained a non-regressive mind of equanimity and has fully accomplished the power of pure, white Dharma. He neither doubts nor loses faith, and he skillfully understands dedication (*pariṇāmanā*). He cultivates merit, tames sentient beings, and eradicates all unwholesome karma.

With single-minded diligence in ascetic practices, he universally instructs all, fully cultivating the roots of goodness of asceticism. For the sake of all sentient beings, he undergoes manifold sufferings; his eye of wisdom is pure as he observes these roots of goodness, and through the noble conduct of wisdom, he dedicates these roots of goodness to all sentient beings.

To cause all sentient beings to dwell securely in pure and subtle merit, to remain far removed from the burning afflictions, and to accomplish the dedication of roots of goodness through an impartial mind;
to cause all sentient beings to attain *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge) and practice dedication;
to gather all the roots of goodness of sentient beings, to bring them to equal fulfillment, and to fully accomplish the dedication of an impartial mind.
Dedicating such immeasurable roots of goodness to sentient beings:
may all sentient beings always attain peace and security;
may all sentient beings always attain purity.
May all sentient beings always attain peace and happiness;
may all sentient beings attain ultimate liberation;
may all sentient beings attain ultimate equality.
May all sentient beings attain sovereign spiritual powers;
may all sentient beings abide securely in the pure dharmas;
may all sentient beings obtain unobstructed eyes.
"May all sentient beings tame their faculties;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the ten powers to teach and transform other beings.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice such dedication, they do not cling to the dedication of karma, nor to the dedication of retribution, nor to the dedication of the body, nor to the dedication of gain and offerings, nor to the dedication of various lands, nor to the dedication of various directions, nor to the dedication of sentient beings, nor to a dedication that is apart from sentient beings, nor to the dedication of all things, nor to the dedication of dharmas.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they form this thought:

"May all sentient beings fulfill the Buddha-wisdom, attain a pure mind, possess discerning wisdom, have inner tranquility, remain undisturbed by external conditions, and be born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time."
"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice such dedication, they surpass all others; none can destroy them. All sentient beings together praise them, yet cannot exhaust their virtues.
They universally practice all bodhisattva deeds, reaching all lands with minimal effort and seeing all Buddhas without obstruction.

Furthermore, they see all the bodhisattvas in those lands cultivating various practices, attaining all skillful means, discerning all dhāraṇīs of the Dharma, expounding the sublime Dharma, and teaching and transforming sentient beings throughout all future kalpas without ever ceasing."
In every thought-moment, they manifest birth in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-worlds, like flashes of lightning;

in every thought-moment, they are able to purify and adorn unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-worlds, practicing the wisdom that adorns and purifies Buddha-fields without ever feeling weary or satisfied.

They cause unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to achieve purity and fulfillment, equally satisfying them; according to the roots of goodness in which they dwell, they enable all to fully complete the *pāramitās*, gathering in sentient beings, eliminating defilements, and accomplishing pure karma. They attain the unimpeded pure ear, whereby they hear and uphold the turning of the wheel of Dharma by Buddhas in unspeakably unspeakable worlds; regarding those Buddhas, they do not conceive thoughts of distance, nor for even a single snap of the fingers do they fail to hear the True Dharma.
They abide in non-existence, without dependence, without defilement, without attachment, and without activity, possessing the firm and indestructible spiritual power of a Bodhisattva.

In every moment of thought, within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all Buddha-fields, they manifest their bodies according to what is appropriate for each, practicing the conduct of Bodhisattvas, always engaging in activities with those who share their vision, never being in opposition to them.

"When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practices the Bodhisattva path, they accomplish such immeasurable and boundless pure merits that they can never be fully described; how much more so when they achieve unsurpassed Bodhi and attain supreme perfect enlightenment."

That is to say: the purity and equality of all buddha-fields; the purity and equality of all sentient beings; the purity and equality of all bodies; the purity and equality of all faculties; the purity and equality of all karmic retributions; the purity and equality of all retinues; the purity and equality of fulfilling all practices; the purity and equality of skillfully entering all dharmas; the purity and equality of fulfilling the dedication of all vows of the Tathāgatas; and the purity and equality of manifesting the sovereign mastery of the realms of all Buddhas.
“After the bodhisattva mahāsattva has thus dedicated these roots of goodness, they attain the dharma-gate of all pure merits and adorn themselves with those various merits.”
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice dedication in this way, they do not contradict any buddha-field, nor do the buddha-fields contradict sentient beings;
the buddha-fields do not contradict the karma of sentient beings, nor does the karma of sentient beings contradict the buddha-fields;
their thoughts do not contradict the mind, nor does the mind contradict their thoughts.
Volition does not conflict with the sphere of the mind, and the sphere of the mind does not conflict with volition;
karmic conditions do not conflict with retribution, and retributive conditions do not conflict with karma;
karma does not conflict with the traces of karma, and the traces of karma do not conflict with karma.
Dharmas do not contradict their characteristics, and characteristics do not contradict dharmas;
the arising of dharmas does not contradict their nature, and the nature does not contradict the arising of dharmas;
the equality of lands does not contradict the equality of sentient beings, and the equality of sentient beings does not contradict the equality of lands.
The equality of all sentient beings does not contradict the equality of all phenomena; the equality of all phenomena does not contradict the equality of all sentient beings.

The equality of the limit of detachment does not contradict the equality of the peaceful abiding of all sentient beings; the equality of the peaceful abiding of all sentient beings does not contradict the equality of the limit of detachment.
The past does not contradict the future, and the future does not contradict the past.
The past does not conflict with the future or the present; the future and the present do not conflict with the past.
The equality of the world does not conflict with the equality of the Buddha; the equality of the Buddha does not conflict with the equality of the world.
The conduct of a bodhisattva does not conflict with sarvajñā (all-knowledge); sarvajñā does not conflict with the conduct of a bodhisattva.
"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice such dedication, they attain impartial karma, attain impartial retribution, attain an impartial body, attain an impartial path, attain impartial vows,
attain an impartial mind toward all sentient beings, attain impartiality regarding all lands, and attain impartiality regarding all practices."
They attain impartial omniscience; they attain equality with all Buddhas of the three periods of time; they attain the vision of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
they attain all roots of goodness; they attain the fulfillment of all vows; they attain the accomplishment of all sentient beings;
they attain skillful discernment of all karmas; and they attain the vision of all virtuous knowledges.
They cause all sentient beings to be fully satisfied and joyful, attain a pure assembly, achieve the ultimate teaching of all Buddhas,
and accomplish the dedication of all pure, white dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha! This is the seventh dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: the dedication of an impartial mind that accords with all sentient beings.

Once a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has accomplished this dedication, they are able to subdue all enemies and adversaries; they can completely uproot all thorns of desire, attain the path of non-arising, and reach the state of non-duality. They become kings of immeasurable sovereign merit who rescue and protect sentient beings; their supernormal powers are unimpeded as they travel throughout all lands. They always delight in tranquility and attain mastery over all bodies. They are able to give rise to the great practices of a Bodhisattva, attain sovereign wisdom regarding all vows and deeds, discern and understand all phenomena, and are able to manifest universally in all Buddha-fields.”
They attain unimpeded ears, hearing all sounds throughout every buddha-field;
they attain the eye of pure wisdom, seeing all Buddhas cultivating various roots of goodness without ever ceasing, fully accomplishing all dharmas.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate these states of mind by conforming to all sentient beings, dedicating them toward all roots of goodness.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Bodhisattva fully practices all meritorious virtues, Profound, far-reaching, pure, and most subtle.”
Though the merits they perform may be slight, they are all able to dedicate them so as to become vast and immeasurable.
All the requisites for life possessed by Bodhisattvas—rare, wondrous, extraordinary, and priceless treasures;
elephants, horses, and precious royal chariots; various kinds of jeweled robes and manifold valuables—[they dedicate all].
One's own head, eyes, hands, and feet, Breaking the bones to extract the marrow and cutting the flesh,
Filling immeasurable worlds, All bestowed as gifts without greed or stinginess.
Thus, throughout immeasurable and boundless eons, they universally bestow all things without ever turning back;
dedicating all such merit, they do so for the sake of delivering immeasurable sentient beings.

The Bodhisattva benefits all sentient beings; through pure merit and sublime vows, he brings peace and happiness to the multitudes of beings within the three realms of existence, causing them all to ultimately realize enlightenment.
The Bodhisattva impartially makes great vows, Cultivating pure deeds in accordance with them;
Causing all sentient beings to attain equality, Yet remaining unattached within those vows.
Universally free from resentment toward the world, they are able to act in accordance with all vows;
they are able to dedicate [merit] to all classes of sentient beings, never contravening any of the worthy sages.
The sun of wisdom for all the world arises from pure generosity and ethical discipline;
through diligent cultivation and tireless effort, one never regresses from any aspiration.
The Bodhisattva dedicates merit to reach the other shore, Able to open the gateways of the pure and wondrous Dharma;
Attaining the supreme wisdom of the Two-Legged Honored One, He discerns the true meaning and reaches the other shore.
The Bodhisattva’s Brahma-voice is utterly perfected; Possessing steadfast and wondrous wisdom, He penetrates the True Dharma, free from all obstacles; The Bodhisattva has no attachment toward them.
The Bodhisattva’s mind is pure and does not create duality, nor does it create the dharma of non-duality;
having relinquished both dualistic and non-dual dharmas, they awaken sentient beings to the path of language.

The Bodhisattva awakens to the equality of the world: all minds, sounds, and all karmas, as well as all sentient beings, are like illusions, all turning according to the retribution of causes and conditions.
All that is created by the entire world, The infinite sounds of karma from the ten directions, All arise from the conditions of karma; One should extinguish that karma so that nothing remains.
The Bodhisattva observes all sentient beings, Whose physical, verbal, and mental actions are entirely equal;
He causes all beings everywhere to attain equality, Just like that which is equal to the unequaled.
The Bodhisattva dedicates all his wholesome karma, universally causing the physical forms of all sentient beings to be pure,
so that they may be fully endowed with all merits and become identical to the Unsurpassed Tamer of Men.
Most supreme among all assemblies, Possessing the wondrous Dharma-body of perfected merit,
I dedicate this ocean of merit entirely To benefit and bring peace and happiness to all living beings.
May all the merits I cultivate through my practice cause all beings everywhere to become completely pure;
may the purity of all Buddhas, which is peerless and beyond compare, likewise prevail throughout the entire world.
Dedicating all roots of goodness with equanimity, May all beings know the true meaning;
With sublime wisdom and merit fulfilled, May they become equal to all Tathāgatas.
The Bodhisattva contemplates all phenomena: the world is quiescent, empty, and without remainder;
there is no agent of action and no one who acts, yet he does not destroy the retribution of various karmas.
In that state, stillness and agitation are non-dual; with an entirely equanimous mind, one observes correctly.
The Bodhisattva truly understands the world and remains far removed from all delusions.
Such true sons of the Buddha, born through transformation from the Dharma of all Tathāgatas,
dedicate all immeasurable merits and completely eliminate all doubts and delusions.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Nineteen;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Seventh [Section] of the Twenty-first Chapter, "The Ten Dedications," of the Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva:
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the eighth dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the Dedication of the Suchness of Phenomena?"

O Son of the Buddha! This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes mindfulness and wisdom, dwelling therein immovably; free from delusion, with right mindfulness and a straightforward mind, he remains unshakable. He achieves firm and indestructible karma, attains non-retrogression within the realm of omniscience, and gains the courageous and fearless mind of the Mahāyāna. He cultivates inexhaustible roots of goodness, accumulates supreme and wondrous roots of goodness, practices pure and white dharmas, increases great compassion, and attains the jewel of rectitude. He is always able to maintain right mindfulness of the pure and white dharmas of all Buddhas, dedicating them so that his mind never regresses.

Delighting in seeking the Bodhisattva path, they employ skillful means to produce pure and firm roots of goodness. With right mindfulness, they cultivate the merit of wisdom and act as masters who discipline others. Fully producing all roots of goodness, wisdom, and skillful means, they dedicate them to sentient beings. Their eye of wisdom is pure, enabling them to observe all roots of goodness and nurture immeasurable varieties thereof:

roots of goodness that distinguish realms, roots of goodness that are complete, roots of goodness that are pure, roots of goodness that are single-minded, roots of goodness that are cultivated, roots of goodness that are practiced, roots of goodness that are contemplated, and roots of goodness that are extensively explained with equanimity.

The roots of goodness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva possess various gateways, various spheres, various characteristics, various matters, and various distinctions; they involve immeasurable practices and immeasurable paths of speech, giving rise to immeasurable conceptualizations. By cultivating these various adorned roots of goodness, they are fully able to correctly uphold the ten powers and all vehicles.
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas cultivate such various roots of goodness that they contemplate the realm of omniscience as one, without duality.
With such roots of goodness, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dedicate them toward fulfilling the unobstructed body while practicing the bodhisattva conduct;
they dedicate them toward purifying unobstructed verbal karma while practicing the bodhisattva conduct.”

Desiring to bring them to fulfillment in the unimpeded karma of the mind, to cause them to dwell securely in the Mahāyāna, to possess an unimpeded mind, and to make all bodhisattva practices entirely pure;
to attain a mind of immeasurable great generosity that fills all sentient beings;
and to attain a mind of mastery over the Dharma that illuminates all phenomena and universally reveals them to the world.

They attain the most supreme and indestructible mind; they attain the pure bodhicitta of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*); they universally illumine all right mindfulness; and they fully perfect the Buddha-remembrance samādhi (*buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*) of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Fulfilling a mind that is free from harm and upright, they remain far removed from enmity; sustaining all sentient beings, they pervade everything without ceasing.

They dwell securely within the wisdom of the ten powers, attain profound samādhis, and are able to travel throughout all worlds without attachment. Abiding in all lands, they never feel weary or satisfied.

They transform and deliver sentient beings without ever resting, giving rise to immeasurable skillful means, thought, and wisdom; they fully accomplish all the inconceivable wisdom of Bodhisattvas, attain the knowledge that is free from delusion, and are able to discern all worlds.

Within a single thought-moment, they are able to completely adorn and purify all Buddha-fields, attain mastery over all supernormal knowledges and wisdoms, enter into the true mark of all phenomena, and manifest the purification of all worlds.

Within a single land, one perceives all lands; possessing the ultimate indestructible wisdom, one is able to sustain all lands, adorning them with the ornaments of a bodhisattva, manifesting in response to all circumstances, and being fully capable of taming immeasurable sentient beings.
A single Buddha-world is as vast as the Dharma-realm; all worlds are likewise so. Having attained ultimate wisdom, he goes to all lands and universally sustains them all.

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness toward the Buddha-fields, dedicating them so as to fill them with sentient beings; he discriminates and upholds wisdom as if it were for his own person.
His dedication for the sake of sentient beings is likewise:
he causes all sentient beings to be forever separated from the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and King Yama.
May all sentient beings be able to eliminate all obstructive karma;
may all sentient beings attain an impartial mind and equal wisdom;
and may all enemies possess a heart of loving-kindness and pure wisdom.
May the wisdom of all sentient beings manifest before them, becoming perfectly complete and universally illuminating all;
may all sentient beings possess true knowledge, be free from defilement and upright, have immeasurable bodhicitta, and be fully satisfied with wisdom;
may all sentient beings manifest the equality of peace and the auspicious realms.
"When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate in this manner, they cultivate roots of goodness and all vows like a great rain cloud:
causing all sentient beings to become completely pure;
causing all sentient beings to become fields of merit for the accumulation of virtue."
May all sentient beings guard and uphold the inner treasury of bodhi;
may all sentient beings be free from all obstacles and dwell securely in the unobstructed, pure dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings fulfill the unobstructed wisdom of the various supernormal powers.
