May all sentient beings attain bodies of mastery, traveling throughout the ten directions and manifesting as appropriate;
may all sentient beings attain the roots of goodness free from delusion and the knowledge of all modes;
may all sentient beings embrace all things and cause them all to be purified.
May all sentient beings be led to distance themselves from obstructive and wrathful minds, ultimately accomplishing all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*).
"Furthermore, if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees delightful lands with forests, trees, flowers, and fruits;
or sees delightful fragrant incenses, exquisite garments, precious treasures, wealth, and various ornaments;"
Some see delightful parks, gardens, villages, towns, and royal capitals;
some see delightful sovereign emperors;
and some see delightful forest hermitages.

Having seen this, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates skillful means, giving rise to immeasurable pure and sublime merits; seeking the true meaning with joy for the sake of sentient beings, he remains free from negligence.

They are well able to cultivate all roots of goodness, which are as difficult to measure as the great ocean; their roots of goodness are fully endowed and inexhaustible, and they are completely satisfied in all merits. Furthermore, they do not discriminate among the various roots of goodness, but through skillful means, they perform pure dedications.
They manifest the roots of goodness of immeasurable practices, constantly mindful of all realms of sentient beings without ever forgetting them, such as the roots of goodness of equality.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this way, they cause all sentient beings to aspire to always joyfully behold immeasurable Buddhas, grasping nothing according to the Dharma; that the nature of phenomena is incalculable and that sentient beings are equally pure is likewise so.
They cause all sentient beings to fully attain the Buddhas’ fulfillment of their wishes and their joyful affection, serving them as attendants;
and they cause all Buddha-lands to eliminate and extinguish afflictions, becoming pure and delightful.

May all sentient beings fully attain the sight and hearing of immeasurable Buddha-dharmas, always delighting in them with their hearts; may they always joyfully protect and uphold the practices of all bodhisattvas, and joyfully observe spiritual friends with eyes of love;
may all sentient beings see the delightful Dharma;
and may all sentient beings joyfully uphold the True Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain delightful illumination within the Buddha-dharma;

May all Bodhisattvas attain the heart of joyful and great generosity; may they attain fearlessness regarding all dharmas; may they delight in analyzing and extensively expounding them for the sake of sentient beings; may they attain the Bodhisattva’s delightful samādhis and various dhāraṇīs; may they attain the wisdom of the predictions of enlightenment for all Bodhisattvas; may they attain that which is most beloved by all Bodhisattvas—the sovereign manifestation and the fulfillment of the Buddhas’ perfect preaching of the Dharma; may they attain delightful skillful means for analyzing and expounding the Dharma; may they attain delightful great compassion and give rise to the Bodhisattva mind; may their faculties be joyful and serene; may they attain the delightful families of all Tathāgatas and teach and transform sentient beings with a tireless mind; and may they attain the delightful and inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of Bodhisattvas, transforming and delivering sentient beings in every single world throughout immeasurable kalpas.
"In the presence of the present Buddhas, they have attained delightful and skillful means, and delightful and profound means, free from all obstructions and forever separated from ignorance;
they are endowed with the delightful, impartial, and desireless state, having severed all obstacles regarding all phenomena and definitively and deeply realized the non-dual Dharma-realm;

they are endowed with the delightful limit of detachment, equalizing all phenomena and entering the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), attaining the delightful Bodhisattva dharma of fulfillment through non-contention."
They are fully endowed with the delightful Vajragarbha-mind, possessing the courageous diligence of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*), which is pure and perfected;
they are fully endowed with delightful and pure roots of goodness, subduing enemies and extinguishing those dharmas that obstruct the path;
they are fully endowed with delightful, unsurpassed enlightenment (*anuttara-bodhi*), with all-encompassing wisdom constantly manifest before them, filling all sentient beings.

In this way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva nurtures roots of goodness and attains the clarity of pure wisdom. Constantly sustained and protected by spiritual friends, the sun of the Tathāgata’s wisdom shines brightly upon their mind, extinguishing the darkness of ignorance. They purely cultivate the true Dharma, enter into all activities of wisdom, and skillfully study the stages of wisdom. Discerning all roots of goodness within the dharma-realm, they are adept at dedicating the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ roots of goodness to its very source and foundation. Thus they achieve wisdom, penetrating deeply and firmly; they clearly understand roots of goodness and thoroughly comprehend all the perfections.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this manner, they do not cling to worlds nor cling to the realm of sentient beings; their minds have no point of reliance, being tranquil and undisturbed. They maintain right mindfulness of all phenomena, fully possessing the non-discriminative wisdom of all Buddhas. They do not contravene the gate of correct dedication of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, nor do they contravene all impartial and true Dharma. They do not destroy the marks of the Buddha, but observe the three periods of time with equanimity.

Realizing the emptiness of sentient beings, they have no place of reliance or abiding; following the path of the Tathāgata, they universally illumine all phenomena, comprehend the meaning of ultimate reality, and gradually advance through the stages.
He discerns all phenomena as they truly are; his wisdom is complete and perfect, firm and steadfast, never forgotten or lost.
He cultivates right action, constantly delights in tranquility, and correctly proceeds toward the state of detachment.

They realize that all phenomena are like illusions and transformations; they understand that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature; they contemplate all meanings and various practices without attachment to the path of language; they see that all dharmas arise from conditions. Contemplating the profound Dharma, they give rise to true wisdom and dedicate it;

they observe the cessation of all dharmas, entering them all through a single contemplation. Without contradicting the various distinct characteristics of all dharmas, they skillfully understand dedication: they dedicate the roots of goodness cultivated on the Bodhisattva path to gathering in sentient beings and to nourishing all the dedications of Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time.
"In this way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates roots of goodness with a mind free from fear toward all Buddha-dharmas;
dedicates roots of goodness with an immeasurable mind toward all sentient beings so that they may all become completely pure;
and dedicates roots of goodness with a mind free of self and what belongs to self toward the realms of the ten directions without any defiled attachment."
With roots of goodness from a mind free of remainder, they dedicate them toward being unstained by any realm or world;
with roots of goodness from practicing dharmas that transcend the world, they dedicate them toward attaining supramundane dharmas and not clinging to sentient beings;
they dedicate them toward seeing all supreme paths.
Dedicate toward the departure from false and illusory dharmas and the production of true roots of goodness;
dedicate toward the gates of the Dharma that reach all paths and immeasurable, boundless roots of goodness;
and likewise dedicate toward the roots of goodness of suchness.
Dedicating [merit] to sentient beings so that they may understand all phenomena—just as it is with their nature, so it is with the roots of goodness;
dedicating to the self-nature of all phenomena, which is the absence of self-nature—just as it is with their characteristics, so it is with the roots of goodness;
dedicating to the signless true characteristic of all phenomena—just as it is with the dharmas themselves, so it is with the roots of goodness.
Dedicating [roots of goodness] toward the Buddha-dharma so as not to regress is like the practice; the roots of goodness are likewise so.
Dedicating them toward the conduct of all Tathāgatas is like the sphere of experience; the roots of goodness are likewise so.
Dedicating them toward the fulfillment of the spheres of the Buddhas of the three periods of time is like their establishment; the roots of goodness are likewise so.
Dedicating [roots of goodness] to establish all sentient beings, just as the roots of goodness that accord with suchness are likewise;
dedicating them to the exhaustion of future kalpas, continuing without interruption in accordance with them, just as the roots of goodness that accord with measure and suchness are likewise;
dedicating them so that the minds of sentient beings are equal to space, just as the roots of goodness that fill space are likewise.
Dedicating a single thought so that it fills all worlds, just as the dwelling is long-lasting, so too is the root of goodness;
dedicating [the mind] to dwell apart from all worldly realms and to dwell in the ultimate dwelling, just as there is no birth, so too is the root of goodness;
dedicating [the mind] to non-arising so as to fulfill all Buddha-dharmas, just as it is firm and solid, so too is the root of goodness.
Dedicating [roots of goodness] to shatter and disperse all afflictions is like the suchness that is indestructible; roots of goodness are likewise so.
Dedicating them so that they cannot be destroyed by any sentient being is like the suchness of clarity; roots of goodness are likewise so.
Dedicating them to universally illuminate all things is like the suchness of all places; roots of goodness are likewise so.
Dedicating [merit] so as to reach the path that leads everywhere is like the suchness of all times;
the dedication that accords with all times is like the suchness of all roots of goodness;
dedicating [merit] so as to accord with the purity of all sentient beings is like the suchness of the equality of all things.
Dedicating all practices toward equality, just as the eye of all dharmas is, so too is the root of goodness;
dedicating so that all sentient beings may fully attain the Dharma-eye, just as indefatigability is, so too is the root of goodness;
dedicating to practicing the Bodhisattva path without weariness, just as profundity is, so too is the root of goodness.
They dedicate [these roots of goodness] to all supreme and profound dharmas; as there is nothing that exists, so too are the roots of goodness.
They dedicate them to the knowledge that all things are non-existent; as there is no emergence, so too are the roots of goodness.
They dedicate them to the state where nothing is manifested; as it is free from obscuration, so too are the roots of goodness.
They dedicate [these roots of goodness] toward the clarity of vision free from obscuration and purity, just as space is peerless, so too are these roots of goodness;
they dedicate them toward the peerless conduct of Bodhisattvas, just as tranquility is peerless, so too are these roots of goodness;
they dedicate them toward the eternal joy of universal tranquility, just as the rootless is peerless, so too are these roots of goodness.
They dedicate toward the ultimate rootless dharma; as the infinite and boundless is such, so too are their roots of goodness.
They dedicate toward all infinite and boundless sentient beings so that they may all become completely pure; as non-attachment is such, so too are their roots of goodness.
They dedicate toward the ultimate limit of non-attachment; as non-obstruction is such, so too are their roots of goodness.
Dedicating [merit] to eliminate all obstacles, just as non-worldly conduct is, so too are the roots of goodness;
dedicating [merit] to remain far removed from all worldly dharmas, just as being unbound is, so too are the roots of goodness;
dedicating [merit] to being unattached to all of birth and death, just as non-action is, so too are the roots of goodness.
Dedication is the distancing from all conditioned activities, just as it is with abiding; so too is it with roots of goodness that abide in suchness.
Dedication is abiding in all things within the state of abiding in suchness, just as it is with roots of goodness that bring all phenomena to fulfillment in suchness.
Dedication is the accomplishment of what sentient beings study, just as it is with roots of goodness that are equal to the suchness of all phenomena.
They dedicate [the roots of goodness] so as to possess impartial conduct toward all, just as all phenomena do not abandon suchness, so too are the roots of goodness;
they dedicate them so as not to abandon any sentient beings until the end of the future, just as all phenomena are inexhaustible, so too are the roots of goodness;
they dedicate them to all inexhaustible sentient beings, just as they do not contradict any phenomena, so too are the roots of goodness.
Dedicating [merit] to all sentient beings so as not to contradict the Buddhas of the three periods of time is like the suchness that encompasses all phenomena; the roots of goodness are also thus.
Dedicating [merit] to all sentient beings so as to encompass all roots of goodness without exception is like the suchness in which all phenomena are identical; the roots of goodness are also thus.
Dedicating [merit] so as to be entirely identical with the Buddhas of the three periods of time is like the suchness from which all phenomena do not depart; the roots of goodness are also thus.
The dedication encompasses both the mundane and the supramundane; as it is indestructible, so too are the roots of goodness.
The dedication to all sentient beings is irrepressible; as it is free from malice, so too are the roots of goodness.
The dedication to all sentient beings cannot be moved by any demonic activities; as it is unclouded, so too are the roots of goodness.
They dedicate [these roots of goodness] to all bodhisattva practices so that they are free from defilement, just as the Suchness is undisturbed, so too are the roots of goodness;
they dedicate them so that all sentient beings may be free from the confusion of dust, just as they are inexhaustible, so too are the roots of goodness;
they dedicate them so that they cannot be exhausted by any worldly dharmas, just as Bodhi is, so too are the roots of goodness.
Dedicating toward the awakening to all phenomena is like the suchness that is never lost; so too is the root of goodness.
Dedicating toward all sentient beings so that they do not lose their straightforward mind is like the illumination of suchness; so too is the root of goodness.
Dedicating toward all sentient beings so that they may universally illumine all things with the light of great wisdom is like the unspeakable suchness; so too is the root of goodness.
They dedicate [their roots of goodness] to all ineffable wisdom, just as they hold all sentient beings;
they dedicate them to upholding all bodhisattva practices, just as they accord with all languages;
they dedicate them to all wordless wisdom, just as they are free from all various phenomena.

They dedicate [their roots of goodness] by manifesting all Buddha-fields and all Tathāgatas attaining supreme perfect enlightenment, manifesting immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers; as they are free from falsehood, so too are these roots of goodness.
They dedicate them to the world so that it may be entirely free from falsehood; as their bodies pervade everywhere, so too are these roots of goodness.
They dedicate them to infinite bodies pervading all lands; as they do not undergo birth, so too are these roots of goodness.
Dedicating [roots of goodness] through the skillful means of non-arising while manifesting birth is like non-existence being as it is; so too are the roots of goodness.

Dedicating [them] to the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and to all lands, manifesting them within the body, is like night being as it is; so too are the roots of goodness.
Dedicating [them] to perform Buddha-works throughout all nights and attaining supreme illumination is like day being as it is; so too are the roots of goodness.

I dedicate [this merit] to all sentient beings during the day, so that they may all awaken well, behold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas, abide in the wheel of non-retrogression, and be purified of delusion; as the crescent moon and the full moon are, so too are these roots of goodness.

I dedicate [this merit] to all sentient beings abiding at all times, through skillful means, so that within a single thought-moment they may discern all seasons and periods; as the years and ages are, so too are these roots of goodness.

I dedicate [this merit] to receiving and upholding various kalpas, purifying the faculties and thoroughly understanding the faculties; as the formation and destruction of all kalpas are, so too are these roots of goodness.

They dedicate [these roots of goodness] throughout all kalpas to purify the dwelling of all sentient beings so they remain untainted, and to purify and subdue sentient beings; as it is with the future, so too are these roots of goodness.

They dedicate them to exhausting the limits of all future time to cultivate the pure and wondrous conduct of Bodhisattvas, fully satisfying immeasurable great vows; as it is with the world, so too are these roots of goodness.

They dedicate them to all sentient beings so that in a single thought-moment they may see all Buddhas, never for even a single thought-moment being separated from them; as it is with the path that reaches all places, so too are these roots of goodness.
Dedicating [these roots of goodness] so that all sentient beings may attain the indestructible path and transcend the triple world, just as space is suchness, so too are these roots of goodness;
dedicating them toward the purification of all realms of existence, knowing that nothing exists, just as purity is suchness, so too are these roots of goodness;
dedicating them toward the pure conduct of all bodhisattvas to produce the requisites for unsurpassed enlightenment, just as clarity and purity are suchness, so too are these roots of goodness.
They dedicate [their roots of goodness] to attaining the pure and luminous mind of all bodhisattva samādhis, just as the simile of being free from defilement is;
they dedicate them so that their pure minds are fulfilled and free from all stains, just as the simile of non-possession (*amama*) is;

they dedicate them to encompassing the pure mind that is free from self and what belongs to self, filling all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, just as the simile of equality (*samatā*) is.
Dedicating [roots of goodness] to attain inexhaustible omniscience and to forever leave behind delusion and craving, universally illuminating all things, just as the roots of goodness are infinite;
dedicating them to the power of the vehicle of omniscience, abiding in the cloud of Dharma of skillful means, universally covering all worlds, just as the roots of goodness abide in equanimity;
dedicating them to all sentient beings, fulfilling the bodhisattva practices and abiding in omniscience, just as one discerns the realms of all sentient beings through the roots of goodness.
They dedicate all roots of goodness so that they manifest before them, fulfilling unimpeded wisdom; as the speech of all sentient beings is, so too are their roots of goodness.
They dedicate them to understanding all modes of speech and dharma, never being apart from all sentient beings; as these are, so too are their roots of goodness.
They dedicate them to gathering in all sentient beings, perfecting roots of goodness and remaining far removed from birth and death; as the vastness [of space] is, so too are their roots of goodness.

They dedicate [their roots of goodness] toward receiving and upholding the teachings spoken by the Buddhas of the three periods of time, practicing the bodhisattva conduct that is free from delusion; as their non-ceasing is such, so too are their roots of goodness.

They dedicate them toward all kalpas, practicing the bodhisattva path without ever resting, establishing sentient beings securely in the Mahāyāna; as the supreme suchness of all phenomena is such, so too are their roots of goodness.
They dedicate them toward opening pure Dharma-gates with unimpeded pure mindfulness, encompassing all phenomena; as immeasurable praise is such, so too are their roots of goodness.
Dedicating [roots of goodness] to attain the practice of bodhisattvas with immeasurable praise and wisdom is like the analogy of being free from blazing fire;
dedicating them to the dharma that is free from blazing fire, extinguishing the blazing fires of sentient beings and causing them to attain purity, is like the analogy of the immovable [earth];
dedicating roots of goodness to abide immovably, fulfilling the vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, is like the analogy of the realm of all Buddhas.

They dedicate [their merit] toward the realm of wisdom for all sentient beings so that it may be entirely fulfilled; they eliminate the realm of all afflictions, and as it is indestructible, so too is their root of goodness.

They dedicate their roots of goodness so that they cannot be destroyed by any demonic activities and can subdue all heterodox outsiders; as it is neither something to be cultivated nor something not to be cultivated, so too is their root of goodness.
They dedicate [their merit] toward the departure from all cultivation and non-cultivation of falsehood, severing all delusion; as it is non-retrogressive, so too is their root of goodness.

They dedicate [their merit] toward constantly beholding all Buddhas without ever withdrawing from the cultivation of the bodhicitta adorned with excellence; as all speech is, so too are their roots of goodness.
They dedicate toward discerning all speech; as they are unattached to all phenomena, so too are their roots of goodness.

They dedicate toward being entirely without attachment to any sentient beings, causing all sentient beings to practice the conduct of Samantabhadra; as all stages are, so too are their roots of goodness.
Dedicating it so that all sentient beings may fully attain the stage of conforming wisdom and be adorned by Samantabhadra; as that which is indestructible, so too is this root of goodness.

Dedicating it so that within all dharmas they may attain fearlessness and non-interruption, such that all speech is pervasive, complete, and capable of extensive exposition; as that which is without outflows, so too is this root of goodness.

Dedicating it so that all sentient beings may be endowed with the root of goodness of outflow-free bodhicitta, attaining the wisdom of dharmas, understanding and discerning them; as that which is neither a dharma of arising nor a dharma of cessation, so too is this root of goodness.

They dedicate [their roots of goodness] toward awakening to all phenomena, so that in a single thought-moment they completely fill the infinite dharma-realms; as the past is not identical, the future is not original, and the present is not different, so too are these roots of goodness.

They dedicate [them] toward the arousal of ever-new bodhicitta vows to extinguish birth and death and purify sentient beings; as one does not grasp at falsehoods throughout the three periods of time, so too are these roots of goodness.

They dedicate [them] toward the complete purity of the past and future, and the manifestation of perfect enlightenment in every moment of the present; as all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are fully endowed with suchness, so too are these roots of goodness.

They dedicate [their merit] so that all sentient beings may be fully endowed with the Buddha-wisdom and the skillful means of great vows; as their roots of goodness are eternally pure and undefiled, so too is this dedication.
They dedicate it so that all sentient beings may completely eliminate afflictions and achieve the purity and fulfillment of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, it is because they equalize all buddha-fields by purifying all worlds;
they equalize all worlds by turning the indestructible, pure wheel of Dharma;
and they equalize all bodhisattvas by giving rise to the vows for all-knowledge."
They equally contemplate all Buddhas because they are non-dual;
they equally contemplate all phenomena because their intrinsic nature is indestructible;
and they equally contemplate the wisdom of skillful means regarding the three periods of time, thereby understanding the path of language.
Because they are able to dedicate all roots of goodness planted through the various practices of all bodhisattvas;
because they know all times and practice accordingly at the appropriate moments without abandoning the work of the Buddha;
and because all karmic retributions are equal, they do not cling to the world but give rise to roots of goodness that transcend it.
With sovereign mastery of spiritual powers, equal to all Buddhas, he accords with the world by equally manifesting the deeds of a Buddha.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the eighth dedication, the Dedication of the Nature of Suchness, of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in this dedication:

they attain immeasurable and boundless gates of pure Dharma; as heroes among men, they are fearless and let out the great lion’s roar; they bring to fulfillment immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattvas, never resting at any time;
and they attain the immeasurable and boundless fulfilled body of a Buddha, a single body that fills all worlds."
They attain the Buddha’s immeasurable, boundless, and perfect voice, such that when a single sound is uttered, there are no sentient beings who do not hear it;
they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable, boundless, and perfect power, being able to place all worlds within the path of a single hair;
they attain the Buddha’s immeasurable, boundless, and perfect sovereign spiritual power, being able to place all sentient beings within a single minute atom.

They attain the infinite and boundless fulfillment of liberation of all Buddhas, wherein within the body of a single sentient being they manifest all Buddha-lands and all Tathāgatas attaining supreme perfect enlightenment;

they attain the infinite and incalculable fulfillment of samādhi of all Buddhas, through the power of skillful means in right reception, whereby within a single samādhi they are able to give rise to all samādhis;

they attain the infinite and boundless fulfillment of eloquence of all Buddhas, such that by speaking a single phrase of Dharma, it remains inexhaustible throughout all future kalpas, completely removing the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings.

They attain the supreme dharmas of sentient beings that are infinite, boundless, and fully perfected by all Buddhas, manifesting for all sentient beings omniscience (*sarvajñā*), the ten powers (*daśabala*), and equal enlightenment (*samyaksambodhi*).
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the dedication of all roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas in accordance with the mark of Suchness.
At that time, Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Bodhisattva’s mind dwells in peace, free from delusion and always possessing right mindfulness;
through patience he is free from affliction and harm, cultivating and accumulating immeasurable virtues.
His mind is without resentment, upright, and ever pure.”
All karmas adorn the world, and one is able to discern them all well.
The Bodhisattva contemplates karma, which is manifold and immeasurable;
regarding those actions that benefit sentient beings, he cultivates and constantly practices them.
Skillfully conforming to the world, they cause all beings to rejoice;
according to the karma of sentient beings, the Bodhisattvas distinguish their practices.
Forever free from all anger and hindrances, they know both the phenomena and their meaning.
Abiding securely on the stage of the Tamer, they benefit all beings.
Awakening to all wholesome dharmas— immeasurable and beyond counting—
they are able to discern and know them all, dedicating this merit to the benefit of sentient beings.
By means of these profound skillful methods, they fulfill the wisdom of all stages,
extinguish all afflictions, and skillfully dedicate [merit] according to suchness.
Universally gathering all realms of existence, they abide securely in the Dharma of reality as it is.
Thus dedicating their karma, they cause all things to be free from attachment.
Deeply delighting in the path to the ultimate state, they cultivate the dharma of *tathatā* (suchness).
Being without intrinsic nature and without anything existing, those of brilliant virtue perform this dedication.
Day and night, as well as half-months, months, years, and even eons—all are entirely equal; their merit is likewise so.
As are the worlds and all lands, and all phenomena of sentient beings, [so too is this].
The destinations and non-destinations as they truly are— dedicating all these without exception;
the nature of suchness as it truly is— contemplating this very nature,
one dedicates all merits so that they entirely accord with True Suchness (tathatā).
Just as the nature of suchness is thus, so all phenomena are non-existent;
since suchness is devoid of intrinsic nature, the wise dedicate their karma accordingly.
Just as all marks are as they truly are, so too are all births.
As the suchness of self-nature is real, so too are all karmas;
as suchness is immeasurable, so are all karmas.
There is neither bondage nor liberation; all karmas are entirely pure.
Such true sons of the Buddha, dwelling securely and immovably,
have accomplished the power of wisdom and entered the treasury of the Buddha’s skillful means.
Having awakened to the Dharma of the Dharma King, they are neither bound nor attached.
The unimpeded and non-revolving mind likewise has nothing upon which to turn.
The activity encompassed by the Dharma-body accords with the characteristics of sentient beings;
it penetrates deeply into the mark of reality, yet even that mark is not a mark.
Such is the inconceivable; it cannot be exhausted by thought.
Deeply entering the inconceivable, thought and non-thought are both stilled.
Contemplating the Dharma in this way, one discerns all karmic actions.
Extinguishing all afflictions—this is called the King of Merit.
All the retributions of a Bodhisattva are sealed by inexhaustible wisdom;
they exhaust phenomena yet possess an inexhaustible nature, extinguished through inexhaustible skillful means.
The mind is neither within nor without, and the mind itself has no existence;
it is through false grasping that phenomena appear to exist, yet when there is no grasping, there is quiescent extinction.
O Son of the Buddha, know this: all phenomena are empty and lack intrinsic nature.
All phenomena lack self-mastery; the Supreme Awakened One realizes non-self.
As suchness is equal to all sentient beings, he awakens to the nature of phenomena as being thus.
He perceives that which is inconceivable; through signless wisdom, he is not deluded.
Thus practicing deeply, seeking only awakening,
their vows do not regress for the sake of benefiting sentient beings.
When Bodhisattvas relinquish this body, they are free from the false notion of death.
Understanding that the mind is like an illusion, they subdue all beings.
Observing how worldly karmic retributions arise according to right mindfulness,
the Bodhisattvas provide protection for all without exception throughout the three realms.
Understanding that all conceptual activities are entirely illusory,
the Bodhisattva knows them to be unreal, yet does not destroy the nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
Thus dedicating their wisdom and roots of goodness, they [attain] sublime excellence.
Out of compassion for all beings, he causes them to enter profound skillful means.
"O Son of the Buddha!
What is the ninth dedication of the mind of liberation—unbound and unattached—of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?

This bodhisattva mahāsattva does not give rise to a mind of contempt toward any roots of goodness; they do not despise the mind that seeks to transcend birth and death, nor the mind that gathers roots of goodness, nor the mind that single-mindedly seeks all roots of goodness. They do not despise the mind of repentance, nor the mind of sympathetic joy toward roots of goodness, nor the mind of paying homage to Buddhas in other directions, nor the mind of the practice of respectful salutation with palms joined. They do not despise the mind of the practice of reverently prostrating at stupas and temples, nor the mind of the practice of exhorting the Buddhas in other directions to turn the wheel of Dharma.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas always delight in gathering those roots of goodness, making them firm and indestructible;

they cause those roots of goodness to abide securely, reflect upon those roots of goodness, nurture those roots of goodness, remain unattached to those roots of goodness, and possess those roots of goodness endowed with an upright mind; they do not discriminate regarding those roots of goodness, but follow those roots of goodness that accord with the realm of all Buddhas, and by beholding those roots of goodness, they attain the power of mastery.
With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates those roots of goodness to fulfill the physical, verbal, and mental actions of Samantabhadra;
with a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they cultivate the courageous diligence of Samantabhadra;
and with a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they fulfill the dharani-door of Samantabhadra’s unimpeded voice, filling the ten directions.
With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they fulfill the Samantabhadra dhāraṇī for perceiving all Buddhas;
with a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they fulfill the Samantabhadra dhāraṇī of wondrous sound, discerning all voices and being able to expound immeasurable clouds of Dharma;
with a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they attain the Samantabhadra dhāraṇī for practicing throughout all kalpas, fully cultivating the practices of all Bodhisattvas in all worlds.

With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they manifest within the body of a single sentient being, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, the entirety of the sovereign spiritual powers of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; as it is with the body of one sentient being, so it is with the bodies of all sentient beings.

With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they fully attain the sovereign spiritual powers of Samantabhadra and manifest within the assemblies of all present Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, cultivating the practices of a Bodhisattva.

With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, they attain a single dharma-door of Samantabhadra and, throughout immeasurable and incalculable kalpas, manifest the inexhaustible sovereignty of all Buddhas, capable of delivering and liberating all sentient beings.

By means of the unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains mastery over the various dharma-gates of Samantabhadra; throughout immeasurable and innumerable eons, one manifests the inexhaustible mastery of all Buddhas and is able to deliver and liberate all sentient beings.

By means of the unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains the mastery of Samantabhadra; in every thought-moment, one causes immeasurable sentient beings to dwell securely in the ten powers, without ever feeling weary or satisfied.

By means of the unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains the mastery of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra; within the bodies of all sentient beings, one perceives the mastery of all Buddhas and cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra.

With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, one attains the sovereignty of Samantabhadra, such that within a single word, one is able to discern the voices and languages of all sentient beings, taming all beings and abiding in the stage of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge).

With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, one attains the sovereignty of Samantabhadra, such that within the body of a single sentient being, one can contain all sentient beings, each of whom perceives themselves as having attained the body of a Buddha.
With a mind of liberation, unbound and unattached, one attains the sovereignty of Samantabhadra, such that within a single flower, one causes all adorned and purified worlds to abide therein.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further reflects:

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, I shall produce the subtle and wondrous sounds of Samantabhadra, filling the Dharma-realm so that they are heard by all according to their needs throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this Samantabhadra’s unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may I, as Samantabhadra does, in every thought-moment behold all the Buddhas of the infinite and boundless worlds throughout the entirety of the past, hear the Dharma they preach, receive and uphold it without forgetting, and adorn the Buddha-family."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may I, like Samantabhadra, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, expound all dharmas in all worlds, reaching ultimate perfection."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may I attain supreme perfect enlightenment in all worlds and appear in the world.

By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may I be able to universally illumine all worlds throughout space with a single ray of light, and cultivate the conduct practiced by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains immeasurable and boundless wisdom, becomes able to accord with the spiritual powers of all stages, and accomplishes the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may they all attain the ultimate wisdom of the Tathāgata; may they expound the wisdom of the Tathāgata throughout all kalpas, such that even when all kalpas are exhausted, their wisdom remains inexhaustible, and may they be fully endowed with the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is able to cultivate all the practices of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas throughout the entire dharma-realm with body, speech, and mind, without indolence, just like Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may I attain the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Buddhas; may my body of meaning not contradict the Dharma-body; may my purity of eloquence and the stages be indestructible; may I possess the inexhaustible treasury of the eloquence of joyful exposition; may I subdue all sentient beings, and fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one enters each and every Dharma-gate, universally illuminating immeasurable and inconceivable worlds, exhausting the very source and bottom of all Dharma-gates, practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and attaining the ultimate stage of Sarvajñā (all-knowledge)."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, within each and every object, one fully discerns and understands all modes of knowledge with the wisdom of all modes; yet, as if never exhausted, one ultimately reaches the shore of Samantabhadra’s adornment, cultivates the bodhisattva practices, and fully accomplishes the Great King of Expedient Means."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, from this life until the end of the future, may I fulfill the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and attain the Dharma King who is free from delusion and possesses all-knowledge."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may I attain the light of Dharma that is free from obstruction, universally illumine all bodhisattva practices, constantly cultivate right action, and be fully endowed with the sovereign skillful means of Samantabhadra."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, they fully attain immeasurable skillful means:

inconceivable skillful means, bodhisattva skillful means, all-knowledge skillful means, skillful means for subduing bodhisattvas, skillful means for turning the immeasurable wheel of Dharma, skillful means for ineffably ineffable times, skillful means for various modes of teaching the Dharma, skillful means for boundless fearlessness, and skillful means for expounding all dharmas without exception. Attaining such wisdom of all conforming skillful means, they cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may they fulfill their physical actions so as to cause all sentient beings to rejoice; may they attain the pure roots of goodness of the non-regressive bodhisattva stage, and ultimately abide securely in all the deeds of Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains pure wisdom and is able to discern the languages of all sentient beings. All verbal karma becomes pure and adorned; one's voice and diction are subtle and wondrous, such that none can equal them, as they cultivate and uphold the conduct of Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is able to discern all Buddha-fields, all sentient beings, all phenomena, and all adornments; with a pure mind, one gives birth to the Dharma-treasury of all Tathāgatas, reaches the ultimate of all-knowledge, and is well able to accord with the conduct of Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, and with a pure and straightforward mind, one attains the unimpeded Dharma-body of all Buddhas, fulfills liberation, cultivates the Dharma of the Tathāgatas, gathers the merits of the Buddhas, dwells in the realm of the Buddhas, and the great wisdom shines universally. One practices the pure conduct of a Bodhisattva, accords with skillful means, and is fully able to discern all treasuries of the Dharma. One gives rise to immeasurable mastery of the Mahāyāna and is able to manifest the unsurpassed Great Way for all immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, fulfilling the dedication of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from a mind that is unbound, unattached, and liberated, one attains the faculty of clear and sharp wisdom; the faculty of well-tamed senses; the faculty of mastery over all phenomena; the faculty of inexhaustibility; the faculty of cultivating all roots of goodness; the faculty of equality regarding the realm of all Buddhas; the faculty of great diligence in receiving the prediction of non-retrogression for all Bodhisattvas; the faculty of discerning the Vajra-realm of all Buddha-dharmas; the faculty of the adamantine flame of the light-illumination of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas; the faculty of mastery in discerning all faculties; the faculty of causing all sentient beings to dwell securely in the faculty of omniscience; the faculty of immeasurability; the faculty of fulfilling all faculties; the faculty of unimpeded purity; and the faculty of impartially cultivating all vows."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains all the spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas:
the spiritual power of sustaining immeasurable bodies;
the spiritual power of the sphere of immeasurable wisdom;..."
Without leaving a single location, they possess the sovereign spiritual power to manifest all Buddha-fields;
the sovereign spiritual power of the Bodhisattvas that is unimpeded, uncontainable, and irresistible;
and the sovereign spiritual power to manifest the gathering of all Buddha-fields and place them within a single location.
The sovereign spiritual power of a single body filling all Buddha-fields;
the sovereign spiritual power of the Bodhisattva’s unimpeded liberation;
and the sovereign spiritual power of mastery in a single thought-moment through minimal means.
By relying on the sovereign spiritual power of non-existence,

they bind infinite worlds with a single hair and carry them all throughout the dharma-realm and buddha-fields, manifesting this to sentient beings so that they may attain the sovereign spiritual power of the gate of ultimate, wondrous wisdom and cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, in a single thought-moment, one can travel to immeasurable Buddha-fields;
within a single body, one can fully contain immeasurable Buddha-fields;

one attains the ground of profound and subtle wisdom, skillfully discerning the worlds of all Buddhas, attains the mind of non-arising, enters entirely into the Dharma-gates of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and gives rise to the practices of a bodhisattva."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is born into the family of the Tathāgatas and cultivates the bodhisattva practices;

one becomes fully endowed with immeasurable, incalculable, and inconceivable dharmas, and all immeasurable great vows are completely fulfilled; one discerns the entire dharma-realm and the dharma-realm of the three periods of time without indolence, accords with all the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and reaches the ultimate realm of wisdom."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one can, within a single hair-path, discern immeasurable and innumerable Buddha-fields, fully encompassing the entire Dharma-realm and the ultimate realm of space;

as it is with one hair-path, so it is with all hair-paths throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of space, opening the eye of wisdom through the pure Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one can take immeasurable, innumerable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas as a single thought-moment, and can take all the thoughts of all sentient beings as a single thought-moment; all such skillful means are brought to ultimate fulfillment through the profound resolve of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."
"By means of these roots of goodness from a mind that is unbound, unattached, and liberated, one is able to contain all immeasurable bodies within a single body;
as it is with one body, so it is with all bodies, fully endowed with the dedication of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, may they enter the spheres of all Buddhas; may they constantly behold the Buddhas’ pure Dharma-bodies, equal to the realm of space, adorned with the marks and signs, possessing sovereign spiritual powers, and endowed with subtle Brahma-voices as they extensively proclaim the unimpeded True Dharma. May they be able to receive and uphold all those Buddha-dharmas upon hearing them; yet regarding those Buddha-bodies, may they realize they are utterly non-existent. May they fully attain the immeasurable great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and forever leave behind the perversions of sentient beings' thoughts, conceptions, and views."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, they enter all worlds—entering inverted worlds and prostrate worlds—and within a single thought-moment, they are able to universally enter all Buddha-lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions. They discern the world-net如因那 (Indra's net), discern the entirety of the equal Dharma-realm, and cause diverse worlds to become a single form. Entering the profound Dharma-realm through immeasurable various worlds and immeasurable skillful means, they find it to be entirely like empty space, yet without destroying the nature of the worlds; thus they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and abide in the stages of Bodhisattvas."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is able to discern all conceptualizations:

the conceptualization of sentient beings, the conceptualization of phenomena, the conceptualization of Buddha-fields, the conceptualization of directions, the conceptualization of Buddhas, the conceptualization of worlds, the conceptualization of karma,
the conceptualization of conduct, the conceptualization of liberation, the conceptualization of faculties, the conceptualization of time, and the conceptualization of upholding."
the perception of afflictions, the perception of purity, the perception of maturation, the perception of seeing all Buddhas, the perception of turning the wheel of Dharma,
the perception of understanding the Dharma upon hearing it, the perception of subduing [sentient beings], the perception of the arising of various skillful means,
the perception of various stages, the perception of entering the bodhisattva path, the perception of cultivating the merits of a bodhisattva, and the bodhisattva’s three...

The perception of meditative absorption; the perception of a bodhisattva’s arising from samādhi; the perception of a bodhisattva’s sphere of activity; the perception of the formation and destruction of kalpas;
the perception of light; the perception of darkness; the perception of day; the perception of night; the perception of the changes of half-months, months, years, and seasons;
the perception of going; the perception of coming; the perception of sitting; the perception of standing; and the perception of waking.
He is able to fully comprehend all such perceptions as the perception of sleep within a single thought-moment;

his mind is free from falsehood and entirely detached from all perceptions, being unattached and far removed from obstacles. He is filled with the wisdom of all Tathāgatas and nurtures the roots of goodness of all Buddha-dharmas.

He perfumes his own body with the bodies of all Buddhas and is constantly sustained by the Buddhas. He never regresses from pure dharmas and is well-able to practice and study the dharma of Equal Perfect Enlightenment. Having reached the ultimate shore, he practices the conduct of Samantabhadra as performed by all Buddhas, fulfills all vows, receives the prediction of Buddhahood from the Tathāgata, and within a single thought-moment attains entry into the stage of skillful means and ultimate wisdom, remaining therein in full satisfaction.

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one contemplates immeasurable minds with each single mind; being free from all delusions and having no dependence, because the mind is not singular, its activities differ and the characteristics of karma vary, causing all sentient beings to be courageous and diligent, producing the jewel of Samantabhadra’s wisdom just like Samantabhadra himself."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is able to discern all immeasurable locations within a single location;
as it is with one location, so it is with all locations, definitively knowing and fulfilling the jewel of wisdom of Samantabhadra’s great vows."
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-one.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Eighth [Section] of the Twenty-first Chapter, "The Ten Dedications," of the *Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva*:

"By means of these roots of goodness from a mind of liberation that is unbound and unattached, one discerns within a single karma the various conditions that create immeasurable karmas as being like a single karma; all karmas are likewise so. Thus one cultivates the ground of wisdom for the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one fully discerns and knows all phenomena within a single phenomenon;
likewise, one knows a single phenomenon within all phenomena, discerning all phenomena without contradiction or attachment."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one thoroughly discerns and knows immeasurable sounds and voices within a single word, just like an echo;

as it is with all languages within a single word, so it is likewise—without any dependence or attachment to those sounds and voices, one abides in the accomplishment of the wisdom of bodhisattva conduct and attains the unimpeded, pure ear of Samantabhadra."

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is able to expound upon each and every dharma all the unspeakably unspeakable dharmas; one nurtures inconceivable roots of goodness, preaching the Dharma according to the occasion, and remaining liberated at all times."
They definitively discern the faculties of sentient beings and, according to what each should hear, the Buddhas’ sublime voices gladden immeasurable multitudes;
at the site of a single Tathāgata, the assembly of Bodhisattvas fills the Dharma-realm;
they thoroughly comprehend all conditioned activities and abide in the stage of Samantabhadra.
In every thought-moment, as described for entering the Dharma, they nurture an ineffable body of sublime wisdom;

throughout all kalpas of the future, in all worlds and at the abodes of all Buddhas, they are able to cultivate practices equal to space, being as courageous as Samantabhadra, cultivating great wisdom, perfecting all practices, and dwelling securely in the stage of Samantabhadra.

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, within each and every faculty, one thoroughly understands immeasurable faculties, incalculable intentions, inconceivable realms, and the faculties for the Dharma-gate of practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra."
“By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one fulfills the bodhisattva practices and gives rise to true, wondrous wisdom:

knowing the subtlety of form, the subtlety of the body, the subtlety of lands, the subtlety of eons, the subtlety of worlds, the subtlety of directions, the subtlety of time, the subtlety of numerical phenomena, the subtlety of karma, the subtlety of retribution, and the subtlety of purification—all such subtleties as these are fully understood within a single thought-moment;
following the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, one accomplishes the true wisdom of Samantabhadra.”

Free from fear, free from delusion, free from distraction, and free from confusion; with a mind that has subdued the sense faculties, a mind of single-minded meditative absorption, a mind that skillfully discerns all phenomena, and a mind that dwells securely in wisdom; practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra, one follows the mind of dedication of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one knows the subtleties of the destinies of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the death of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the birth of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the abodes of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the arising of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the categories of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the realms of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the conduct of sentient beings; one knows the subtleties of the grasping of sentient beings; and one knows the subtleties of the spheres of sentient beings.
All such subtleties as these can be fully understood in a single thought-moment; yet one practices the conduct of Samantabhadra without weariness."
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind,
[I] shall fully discern and know all the subtle practices of bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds, the subtleties of the bodhisattva’s stations,
the subtleties of the bodhisattva’s masteries, the subtleties of the bodhisattva’s wandering through immeasurable buddha-fields, and the bodhisattva’s Dharma..."
The subtlety of clarity; the subtlety of the pure eye of a bodhisattva; the subtlety of a bodhisattva’s possession of a profound mind;
the subtlety of a bodhisattva approaching the great assemblies of all Tathāgatas; the subtlety of a bodhisattva’s gates of knowledge of all dhāraṇīs;
and the subtlety of a bodhisattva’s skillful means in expounding all forms of eloquence on the stages of immeasurable and boundless fearlessness.
The subtle [nature of] the bodhisattva’s immeasurable and boundless samādhis; the subtle [nature of] the bodhisattva’s samādhi of seeing all Buddhas;
the subtle [nature of] the bodhisattva’s samādhi of adornment; the subtle [nature of] the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s samādhi of the dharma-realm;
and the subtle [nature of] the wisdom of the bodhisattva’s samādhi of mastery. The bodhisattva...
The subtlety of samādhi and wisdom; the subtlety of the samādhi and wisdom maintained by Bodhisattvas throughout the limits of the future;
the subtlety of the discernment of all Bodhisattva samādhis through the supreme and wondrous wisdom of Bodhisattvas;
and the subtlety of the thorough knowledge and discernment of the birth of all immeasurable and boundless Bodhisattva samādhis.
The Bodhisattva’s subtle entry into the presence of all Tathāgatas through the birth of samādhi and wisdom;

the cultivation of all Bodhisattvas’ vast, profound, and unobstructed samādhis; the ultimate realization of all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā); the attainment of the stage of skillful means, the stage of all supernormal powers, and the stage of discerning the true meaning; and the Bodhisattva’s wisdom free from delusion, which cultivates the subtle, immeasurable practices of Samantabhadra.
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, in a single thought-moment, they fully know the subtleties of all the bodhisattva abodes;
they fully know the subtleties of the bodhisattva stages; the subtleties of the various practices of the bodhisattvas;
the subtleties of the bodhisattvas' birth and dedication; and the bodhisattvas' attainment of all Buddhas..."
The subtlety of the *dharmadhātu*; the subtlety of the bodhisattva’s analytical wisdom; the subtlety of the bodhisattva’s mastery over the spiritual power of great vows;
the subtlety of expounding the bodhisattva’s samādhis; the subtlety of the bodhisattva’s skillful means and spiritual powers; the subtlety of the bodhisattva’s seals (*mudrā*);
the subtlety of the bodhisattva in their final birth before enlightenment (*ekajātipratibaddha*); and the subtlety of the bodhisattva’s birth.
The subtlety of the Tuṣita Heaven; the subtlety of the Bodhisattva dwelling in the celestial palace; the subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s adornment and purification of Buddha-fields;
the subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s observation of the human realm; the subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s emission of great radiance;
the subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s thorough comprehension of domestic laws; the subtlety of the Bodhisattva’s laws regarding retinues; the Bodhisattva...
The subtle nature of taking birth in all worlds; the subtle manner in which a single body of a bodhisattva manifests as all bodies at the time of death;
the subtle manner in which the body of a bodhisattva enters the mother’s womb; the subtle manner of the bodhisattva abiding in the womb;
the subtle manner of the sovereign spiritual power by which the bodhisattva within the womb manifests the Dharma-realm and a great assembly; the subtle [nature] of the bodhisattva...
While in his mother’s womb, the Bodhisattva manifested the subtle mastery of all Buddhas; the subtle manner of a Bodhisattva’s birth;
the subtle wisdom of fearlessness in the Bodhisattva’s seven steps; the subtle skillful means of the Bodhisattva’s presence in the royal palace;
and the subtle practice of the Bodhisattva’s renunciation, seeking the Way, subduing the sense faculties, and cultivating the Dharma.
The subtle method by which the Bodhisattva sits beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment; the subtle method by which the Bodhisattva subdues Māra and attains supreme perfect enlightenment;
the subtle radiance emitted by the Tathāgata while sitting upright at the site of enlightenment; the subtle illumination that universally shines upon all worlds in the ten directions;
and the manifestation of the Tathāgata’s immeasurable and boundless sovereign spiritual powers.
The subtlety of the Tathāgata’s lion’s roar of the Great Parinirvāṇa;
the subtlety of the Tathāgata’s teaching of all sentient beings without ever failing; the subtlety of knowing the Tathāgata’s adamantine bodhicitta;
the subtlety of manifesting the Tathāgata’s sustaining of all worlds; [and] throughout all worlds...
Subtly and ultimately performing buddha-works throughout future kalpas without rest;

subtly upholding all worlds, including the subtle realm of the dharma-dhātu and the realm of empty space, for the sake of transforming sentient beings by universally manifesting the buddha-body appearing in the world;
and subtly, from a single tathāgata-body, manifesting infinite bodies.
I shall fully know the subtle wisdom retinues of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as all such subtle merits;
having become perfected and reached the further shore, I shall manifest purity for all sentient beings.
In every moment of thought, their wisdom is all-pervasive and complete; they attain non-retrogression and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva;
they fulfill the ground of Samantabhadra’s merit of dedication and uphold all that is practiced by the Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas.

Without departing from the various gates of bodhisattva wisdom, all skillful means are entirely pure; they are able to universally bring peace and security to all sentient beings as they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva.

Fully endowed with the merits of all the bodhisattva stages, they attain the gate of the adamantine banner dedication, give birth to immeasurable treasuries of merit within the dharma-realm, and are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas.

They enter the profound and pure Dharma-gates of all bodhisattvas, expounding the subtle and wondrous meanings of all dharmas without error or omission, and are able to extend compassion and pity to all sentient beings.

In every moment of thought, they thoroughly and completely understand the treasuries of merit of both conceivable and inconceivable stages; from the inconceivable they bring forth the conceivable, manifesting various Dharma-gates that transcend the path of language, thereby attaining the stage of wisdom.
All Bodhisattvas are entirely equal, practicing the bodhisattva path throughout the limits of the future without ever resting.

They are endowed with the conduct of Samantabhadra, far removed from all worldly delusions and the pathways of language; they fully uphold the sovereignty of their great vows and practice the bodhisattva path without interruption.

“By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one enters into and, within a single thought-moment, knows as they truly are all the subtle aspects of the wisdom regarding the nature of all sentient beings: the subtle wisdom of entering the nature of all sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of discerning the nature of sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of fully expounding the nature of sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of the defiled attachment of sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of the immovable nature of sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of the moving nature of sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of the nature of sentient beings in immeasurable and boundless realms of rebirth; the subtle wisdom of the various activities and natures of inconceivable sentient beings; the subtle wisdom of the immeasurable afflictions of sentient beings; and the subtle wisdom of the immeasurable purity of sentient beings—in short, the subtle wisdom regarding the spheres of the nature of all such sentient beings.”
They tame and bring peace to all sentient beings, preaching the Dharma as appropriate without missing the proper time;
they constantly turn the wheel of Dharma to gather in sentient beings, expounding various Dharma-gates and cultivating the bodhisattva path;
endowed with perfect wisdom, they manifest infinite transformation bodies to bring peace to sentient beings and cause them all to rejoice.
The sun of wisdom shines universally; deeply entering the bodhicitta, one attains the sovereign wisdom of a bodhisattva and awakens to abide within the realm of bodhisattva wisdom;
cultivating the wisdom of the Mahāyāna, one brings the conduct of Samantabhadra to ultimate perfection.
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind,
one is able to fully discern the subtle wisdom of all worlds— equal to the space of the dharma-realm— including the subtle wisdom of small worlds,
the subtle wisdom of medium worlds, the subtle wisdom of impure worlds, and the subtle wisdom of pure worlds."
...the subtle wisdom regarding incomparable worlds, the subtle wisdom regarding diverse worlds,
the subtle wisdom regarding vast worlds, the subtle wisdom regarding narrow worlds, the subtle wisdom regarding unimpededly adorned worlds,
and the subtle wisdom regarding the manifestation of all-knowledge by all Buddhas appearing in all worlds, and the exposition of all...
The subtlety of the wisdom that fills a single body with all worlds; the subtlety of the wisdom that emits immeasurable light to universally illuminate all worlds;
the subtlety of the wisdom of the sovereign spiritual power manifested by all Buddhas in all worlds;
and the subtlety of the single wondrous voice heard throughout the ten directions.
The subtlety of knowledge regarding worlds; the subtlety of knowledge regarding all worlds currently surrounded by the great assemblies of Buddhas;
the subtlety of knowledge regarding the entire dharma-realm being manifested as a single buddha-field; the subtlety of knowledge regarding a single buddha-field being manifested as all buddha-fields;
the subtlety of knowledge regarding all worlds as being like a dream; [and] all worlds...
Just as the wisdom of lightning is subtle, so too does he discern and know the subtlety of the wisdom regarding all such worlds;
he thoroughly understands and penetrates that all the practices of Bodhisattvas are entirely like illusions.
They attain sovereign wisdom in the ultimate conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and achieve the clear contemplation of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
they practice all bodhisattva deeds without ceasing, completely free from all perversions.

They behold all Buddhas and the sovereign powers of the Buddhas; they attain an unimpeded body, their wisdom is without dependence, and they are unstained by any dharmas of the roots of goodness; as for the movements of their minds, they are entirely non-existent.
Having abandoned the firm marks of all directions and purified the marks of the bodhisattva’s conduct, they have never grasped at the mark of omniscience.
Unattached to sentient beings, they are adorned by samādhi;
their wisdom accords with the entire dharma-realm, and they cultivate the bodhisattva practices in all worlds.
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one deeply enters the subtlety of wisdom regarding the immeasurable dharma-realm;
the subtlety of wisdom in expounding all dharma-realms; the subtlety of wisdom in traversing the vast dharma-realm;
the subtlety of wisdom in discerning the inconceivable dharma-realm; and the discernment of all dharma-realms..."
The subtlety of wisdom that fills the entire dharma-realm in a single thought-moment; the subtlety of wisdom that contemplates the entire dharma-realm with equanimity;
the subtlety of wisdom that perceives the non-existence of any objective sphere within the entire dharma-realm;
the subtlety of wisdom that observes the entire dharma-realm without obstruction; and the understanding that the entire dharma-realm is unborn.
The subtlety of wisdom, the subtle wisdom that maintains mastery over all dharma realms within the body—
having brought all such subtleties of wisdom regarding the entire dharma realm to ultimate perfection, one accomplishes the conduct of Samantabhadra.
Upholding wisdom, they attain mastery over all phenomena and cause sentient beings to rejoice.
Without abandoning the body of meaning, they do not perceive a separate dharma-body;
they give rise to unimpeded, impartial wisdom and achieve unobstructed conduct.
They do not cling to any phenomena and are detached from all existence; they are truly undefiled.
They conform to the world by engaging in the conventions of speech, yet they always delight in tranquility and do not abandon the ultimate meaning.
Wisdom is pure, extinguishing all delusions; all that exists is entirely without solidity.
One awakens to the infinite dharma-realm of all phenomena, realizing that all worlds are equal and non-dual, and that all dharmas are likewise non-dual.
Without any dependence, one enters the practice-gate of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and ultimately achieves the wisdom of equality.

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one is able to discern the subtle wisdom of all kalpas: that immeasurable kalpas are the subtle wisdom of a single thought-moment; that a single thought-moment is the subtle wisdom of immeasurable kalpas; that incalculable (asaṃkhyeya) kalpas are the subtle wisdom of a single kalpa; that a single kalpa is the subtle wisdom of incalculable kalpas; that long kalpas are the subtle wisdom of short kalpas; that short kalpas are the subtle wisdom of long kalpas; entering the subtle wisdom of kalpas with Buddhas and kalpas without Buddhas; knowing the number of all kalpas without remainder through subtle wisdom; explaining that all kalpas are non-kalpas through subtle wisdom; and awakening within a single thought-moment to all kalpas of the past, future, and present limits without remainder through subtle wisdom."
All such eons as these are known by the Tathāgata’s wisdom within a single thought-moment.

He attained the mind that is the sovereign king of the perfection of all bodhisattva practices; he attained the mind of the ultimate practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; he attained the mind free from all falsehood; he attained the mind of non-regressing great vows; he attained the mind that manifests the pervasive presence of all Tathāgatas within the infinite and boundless network of worlds; he attained the mind that hears and retains the roots of goodness and bodhisattva practices of all Buddhas; he attained the mind of great fearlessness granted to all sentient beings; he attained the mind that manifests the appearance of all Buddhas in the world throughout all kalpas; he attained the mind that practices the bodhisattva path without rest in every single world until the end of the future; and he attained the bodhisattva body and mind filled with the physical activities of the Tathāgatas in all worlds.

"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one knows the subtlety of immeasurable, profound knowledge of dharmas; the subtlety of superior knowledge of dharmas; the subtlety of mixed knowledge of dharmas; the subtlety of adorned knowledge of dharmas; the detailed explanation of the subtlety of knowledge of all dharmas; the subtlety of knowledge that all dharmas are a single dharma; the subtlety of knowledge that a single dharma is all dharmas; the subtlety of knowledge that all dharmas entirely enter into non-dharmas; the subtlety of knowledge that non-dharmas enter into all dharmas without contradicting them;
and the subtlety of knowledge that enters the skillful means of all Buddha-dharmas without exception. All such subtle dharmas as these are fully understood through unobstructed wisdom."

They attain a mind in which all practices are of one and the same practice; they attain a mind that reaches the ultimate, immeasurable, and boundless realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); they attain a mind that discerns the teachings through the power of fearlessness; and they resolutely abide in all unimpeded practices.
With all-knowledge filling all the faculties, the skillful means of right mindfulness of the wisdom of all Buddhas are fully manifested;
they accomplish the vast merits of all Buddhas, filling the worlds.

They universally enter the bodies of all Tathāgatas, manifesting the bodily activities of all Bodhisattvas; they produce sublime sounds that pervade all Buddha-lands throughout the world; they attain the wisdom of mental activity endowed with majestic spiritual power; they give rise to immeasurable analytical skillful means and the knowledge of all modes; and by practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra, they attain non-retrogressive wisdom.
"By means of these roots of goodness from this unbound, unattached, and liberated mind, one attains the subtle wisdom that exhaustively knows the arising of all Buddha-fields;
the subtle wisdom that exhaustively knows the arising of the various supernormal powers and wisdoms of all sentient beings;
the subtle wisdom that exhaustively knows the arising of the karmic retributions of all phenomena; the arising of all..."
The subtle wisdom of generating a mind without remainder; the subtle wisdom of generating the teaching of the Dharma at all times without remainder;

the subtle wisdom of generating the discernment of the entire dharma-realm without remainder; the subtle wisdom of generating wisdom equal to the realm of empty space throughout the three periods of time without remainder;
and the subtle wisdom of generating all paths of linguistic expression of the Dharma without remainder.
The subtlety of wisdom that gives rise to all worldly phenomena without exception;
the subtlety of wisdom that gives rise to the phenomena that transcend worldly conduct without exception; the subtlety of wisdom that gives rise to all such things—this is the subtlety of wisdom.
The subtle wisdom that gives rise to the path of all Tathāgatas, the path of all Bodhisattvas, and the path of all sentient beings;

practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva and abiding in the conduct of Samantabhadra, they know all meanings and essences as they truly are—like a dream, like lightning, like an illusion, like an echo, and like a transformation;
they are quiescent within the entire Dharma-realm, for there is no reality therein and nothing to which they may become attached.
“[They] give birth to the equal wisdom of all Buddhas and bring it all to ultimate perfection; they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and give birth to subtle wisdom.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness from such an unbound, unattached, and liberated mind as follows:

they do not falsely grasp at the world or worldly phenomena; they do not falsely grasp at awakening or Bodhisattvas; they do not falsely grasp at Bodhisattva practices or the path that emerges from saṃsāra; they do not falsely grasp at all Buddhas or the Buddha-dharma; they do not falsely grasp at taming or untamed sentient beings; they do not falsely grasp at roots of goodness or dedication; they do not falsely grasp at themselves or others; they do not falsely grasp at the gift or the recipient; they do not falsely grasp at Bodhisattva practices or awakening; and they do not falsely grasp at phenomena or those who understand phenomena.

In this way, the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s unbound, unattached, and liberated mind are dedicated toward an unbound, unattached, and liberated body; an unbound, unattached, and liberated speech; unbound, unattached, and liberated action; unbound, unattached, and liberated retribution; unbound, unattached, and liberated worlds; unbound, unattached, and liberated buddha-fields; unbound, unattached, and liberated sentient beings; unbound, unattached, and liberated dharmas; and unbound, unattached, and liberated wisdom.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, it is equal to the dedication of all the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.

He accomplishes and dwells in the dedication of all bodhisattvas of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, attaining non-retrogression regarding the dedications of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
They accord with all the teachings of the Buddhas of the past, are fully endowed with all the teachings of the Buddhas of the future, and attain all the teachings of the Buddhas of the present;

they fulfill the impartial true Dharma of all Buddhas of the past, accomplish the impartial true Dharma of all Buddhas of the future, and turn toward the impartial true Dharma of all Buddhas of the present;
they practice within the realm of all Buddhas of the past, abide within the realm of all Buddhas of the future, and equalize the realm of all Buddhas of the present.

Their roots of goodness are no different from those of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; they abide where all Buddhas of the three periods of time abide; they share the same realm as all Buddhas of the three periods of time; and they do not contradict the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the ninth dedication of roots of goodness of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: the unbound and unattached liberation-mind.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in this dedication, all roots of goodness dedicated thereby cannot be destroyed by any diamond mountains; among all sentient beings, they are the most supreme.”
