They cannot be destroyed by any demons; they are able to utterly crush and eliminate the evil deeds of all demons, universally manifesting throughout all worlds as they practice the bodhisattva path.
Through skillful means, they extensively expound the various Buddha-dharmas for sentient beings, causing them to abandon ignorance and accord with the wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas.

Wherever the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is born, whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, he always obtains an indestructible retinue and attains pure mindfulness, such that he is able to hear and retain all the teachings of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
Throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, they practice the bodhisattva path without ever resting, yet remain free from attachment.

Attaining the conduct of Samantabhadra, their vows are fulfilled; they realize omniscience and perform the work of Buddhas, fully acquiring the immeasurable sovereign powers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Bodhisattvas never harbor a mind of pride; They are peerless and honored throughout all directions.
In accordance with the meritorious deeds they have cultivated from the beginning, They likewise do not give rise to a mind of contempt.”
Whatever merits one cultivates, not for oneself nor for others,
but with a mind free from bondage and attachment, one dedicates them to the benefit of all sentient beings.
Forever free from all aspirations for self-exaltation, And having likewise abandoned the mind of pride,
One performs bodily actions toward the Most Victorious One, Entreatying him to teach the Dharma through various practices.
All the immeasurable merits I have performed, To benefit all classes of sentient beings,
Abiding in the mind of liberation free from attachment, I dedicate them to all the Tathāgatas.
Regarding the countless classes of sentient beings in the world, With their various skillful means and diverse techniques,
And all matters that are supreme, wondrous, profound, and subtle— He is fully able to discern and know them all.
All the various bodies that exist in the world Are obtained through the karma of the body;
Awakening to the immeasurable practices of birth and death, One attains the gateway of non-retrogressive wisdom.
In all the infinite lands of the ten directions, including those subtle, supreme, and inverted worlds,
the Bodhisattva enters deeply into the gates of wisdom and fully understands them all within a single pore.
The immeasurable minds of all sentient beings, the wise understand them to be but a single mind;
the Bodhisattva awakens to this gateway of wisdom, yet does not abandon or increase their various karmic activities.
The various faculties of all sentient beings— superior, middling, and inferior, each distinct—
and all their most profound merits, the Bodhisattva fully understands according to their individual natures.
The various karmas of all sentient beings, With their distinct characteristics of superior, middling, and inferior grades— The Bodhisattva,
having deeply entered the power of the Tathāgata, Is able to fully and discerningly know them all.
Inconceivable and immeasurable eons, they can all be fully known within a single thought-moment;
the deeds performed throughout all the ten directions, the Bodhisattva awakens to with pure knowledge.

They are able to know the three periods of time in both forward and reverse order, discerning their respective characteristics as each being distinct, yet without contradicting the characteristic of equality; this is the practice of a bodhisattva who has abandoned delusion.
The immeasurable conduct of all sentient beings, And their various fetters of craving and pride,
each distinct— The Bodhisattva discerns these individual characteristics, Yet never abandons the contemplation of signlessness.
The Tathāgatas of the worlds in the ten directions, Fully manifesting great sovereign mastery,
Difficult to see, difficult to encounter, and inconceivable— Bodhisattvas are able to discern and know them all.
The Great Guide of Tuṣita Heaven, the peerless and most excellent Lion among Men,
whose merit is profoundly deep, vast, and pure, perceives the nature of all things exactly as they are.
Manifesting the descent of the spirit into the mother’s womb, With immeasurable, sovereign, and great supernormal transformations,
He attains Buddhahood, enters nirvana, and turns the wheel of Dharma— A wheel that no one in all the worlds can turn.
When the Lion among Men was first born, all the most excellent beings paid him homage and respect:
the celestial kings, Śakra, and Brahmā, as well as all those possessed of wisdom, attended upon him with reverence.
Throughout all the ten directions without exception, In immeasurable and innumerable dharma realms,
Without beginning, end, or middle, He manifests immeasurable powers of mastery.
Once the Honored Guide among Men has manifested his birth, he walks seven paces in each direction;
observing all classes of sentient beings, he awakens to all things through the unimpeded Dharma-gate.
Beholding sentient beings submerged in the five desires, the Lion among Men manifests a smile;
seeing them shrouded in blindness, darkness, and folly, I shall deliver them from the suffering of the three realms of existence.
With a great lion’s roar, he utters a wondrous sound: "I am the foremost honored one in the world;
I manifest the lamp of clear and pure wisdom to forever extinguish the darkness of ignorance within birth and death."
The Lion among Men has appeared in the world, emitting immeasurable great radiance;
he cuts off all evil realms, so that infinite sufferings are ultimately extinguished.
At times he manifests dwelling in palaces, and at times he manifests leaving home to practice the Way;
as a lion among men, he displays sovereign power for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
When the Bodhisattva first sat at the site of enlightenment, The great earth shook in six ways;
He universally emitted immeasurable, vast radiance, Illuminating all classes of sentient beings throughout the five realms of existence.
Shaking all the palaces of Māra, It awakens the minds of sentient beings throughout the ten directions;
Those who have had a karmic affinity with the Bodhisattva in the past All fully awaken to the meaning of ultimate reality.

Within a single hair-pore are immeasurable vehicles; throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, the paths and vehicles of sentient beings are limitless, as he manifests supreme and great spiritual transformations.
Thus, through skillful means, they accord with awakening;
whatever has been proclaimed by all Buddhas, and even that which the Tathāgatas have not spoken, they fully understand, discern, and know.
Extinguishing all the enmity of Māras, Universally covering the trichiliocosm,
Deeply entering all gates of non-obstruction, He is able to destroy all paths of Māra.
Whether the Tathāgata is in various Buddha-fields, Or manifests his presence in the palaces of the devas,
Or appears in the celestial mansions of Brahmā, The Bodhisattvas see him all without obstruction.

He turns the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma; the Tathāgata’s Dharma-body is without limit or boundary, and throughout all kalpas of the three periods of time, the Most Victorious One proclaims it without end.
The peerless lion thrones of all Buddhas completely fill the worlds of the ten directions;
adorned with various wondrous marks, the Buddha sits upon those seats, inconceivable.
Surrounded by all true sons of the Buddha, filling the entire dharma-realm without exception,
they proclaim the boundless conduct of Bodhisattvas, following the essential path that leads forth from all Buddhas.
The wise one, by means of a single skillful method, encompasses all Buddha-dharmas without exception;
with various adornments and most excellent dharmas, they completely fill the entire dharma-realm.
Incomparable, immeasurable, and wondrously sovereign, you manifest all manner of diverse bodies;
you further appear through infinite births in the various realms of existence, or manifest surrounded by a retinue of court ladies.
He manifests the practice of leaving home and studying the Way, desiring to make the faculties of all sentient beings sharp;
even manifesting parinirvāṇa, he distributes his relics and establishes stupas and temples.
Such various and immeasurable practices as these, the Tathāgata has expounded as the dwelling place of the Buddhas;
all the merits of all Tathāgatas he has fully and universally known, reaching the further shore.
Through such various and immeasurable practices, Without rest throughout all kalpas,
And never giving rise to a mind of sorrow or distress, The Bodhisattva skillfully dedicates them all.
The sovereign power of all Buddhas, And the immeasurable virtues of the Buddhas—
The Bodhisattvas understand them all in accordance with reality, And proclaim them universally for the sake of all sentient beings.
All such Kings of Dharma, according to those immeasurable realms,
awaken to them all within a single thought-instant, yet they do not abandon the bodhisattva practices.
All most supreme and profound dharmas, And the path of the true Dharma in all Buddha-fields—
In accordance with these, may I awaken to sublime conduct And ultimately dedicate it to reaching the other shore.
Whether kalpas are numbered or unnumbered, the Bodhisattva deeply understands them as a single instant;
fully cultivating the practices of a Bodhisattva, they do not regress from that supreme path.
Throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, whether they be pure and wondrous or defiled and impure,
as well as all those Tathāgatas therein, the Bodhisattva discerns and knows them all.
In every thought-moment, they clearly comprehend inconceivable and immeasurable eons;
thus understanding the eons of the three periods of time, they fully abide in ultimate practice.
Deeply penetrating the movements of the mind, Skillfully practicing all dharmas through expedient means,
The bodhisattva practices of all buddha-fields— They are able to clearly understand and discern them all.
It gives birth to immeasurable wisdom; it gives birth to sentient beings and all phenomena;
it gives birth to the power and mastery of bodhi—all of which are entirely without limit.
Profoundly penetrating all things without exception, they discern all sublime dharmas;
fully understanding both their common and distinct characteristics, they completely fulfill the vast cultivation of bodhisattva practices.
In all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, there are immeasurable and innumerable multitudes;
though their various natures are each different, the Bodhisattva is able to discern and know them all.
All Tathāgatas of the past, And all Guides of the future and present—
If one can thus understand dedication, Then one is equal to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
If one can know dedication in this way, Then it is equal to the most supreme merit,
Equal to the most supreme wisdom, And equal to the most supreme conduct.
Nothing in all the worlds can destroy them; they fully accomplish all that is to be learned;
they accord with all the Most Victorious Ones, and are well able to observe the world.
The conduct of the Bodhisattvas is immeasurable; they are fully endowed with infinite merit.
Firmly established in the practice of the Tathāgatas, they possess the power of analytical mastery.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the tenth dedication of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the immeasurable dedication equal to the Dharma-realm?
O Son of the Buddha!”

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has a stainless silk cloth bound upon his head; he has received the prediction of a Great Dharma Master, is able to extensively bestow the gift of Dharma and accomplish great compassion, establishes sentient beings in the bodhicitta, and benefits sentient beings without ever resting.

Nurturing roots of goodness through the bodhicitta, he acts as a guide for all sentient beings, showing them the path to omniscience. He serves as the sun of the Dharma-treasury for all sentient beings, the pure light of his roots of goodness universally illuminating everything;
with an impartial mind, he observes all sentient beings, desiring that they always practice roots of goodness without ever ceasing.

They increase pure and subtle wisdom, never abandoning the path of all roots of goodness; they act as great guides for all sentient beings to gather jewels of wisdom, revealing and showing the secure and correct path to all.
Taking all sentient beings as foremost, they practice all dharmas;
they cause all sentient beings to obtain indestructible, true spiritual friends and to nurture their roots of goodness.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice all wholesome dharmas such as the gift of Dharma, they embrace the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*) and, through ultimate right power, reach the further shore.
With firm and indestructible resolve for bodhicitta, they constantly delight in great vows and cultivate awakening.
Relying upon spiritual friends, they abandon a crooked mind and single-mindedly seek bodhi, discerning the boundless realms of the gates of all-knowledge.

“The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates those roots of goodness in a manner that is vast and without limit; even regarding a single phrase or a single flavor of the Dharma taught by the Buddha, if there are those who hear it, uphold it, or explain it, he dedicates these roots of goodness in such a way.”

With single-minded right mindfulness, one contemplates how the Buddhas of the three periods of time throughout worlds as vast and boundless as space practiced the bodhisattva path; dedicating these roots of goodness, may all Buddhas constantly guard and keep them in mind.
In a single world, throughout all future kalpas, one practices the bodhisattva path for the sake of a single sentient being;

as in that one world, so it is in all worlds—extending through space and the dharma-realm—throughout all future kalpas, one practices the bodhisattva path for the sake of a single sentient being, and likewise for the sake of all sentient beings.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they adorn themselves with the great adornments.

They do not give rise to the thought of being separated from the Buddhas and spiritual friends; because they have attained this thought, they constantly see all Buddhas of the present, never having been separated from even a single Buddha.

They have fully perfected the holy life praised by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; they practice the holy life without deficiency, possess the holy life without breach, and maintain the holy life that is untainted, stainless, non-retrogressive, and indestructible—the holy life praised by all Buddhas, the holy life without dependence, the holy life of non-appropriation, the holy life that is free from inversion, pure, and in accord with the conduct of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time; the holy life that is unimpeded, without grasping, without contention, and without discrimination; the holy life of peaceful abiding, incomparable, immovable, undisturbed, and free from anger.

Just as I practice the holy life (*brahmacarya*), may I cause all sentient beings to dwell securely in these various holy lives: practicing the holy life, fulfilling the holy life, purifying the holy life, cleansing the holy life of defilement, illuminating the holy life, removing dust from the holy life, clearing away the mist from the holy life, removing the fever from the holy life, leaving behind the entanglements of the holy life, leaving behind all doubt in the holy life, and leaving behind all affliction and harm in the holy life, until they reach the further shore.
"Why is this? It is impossible for a bodhisattva who does not personally cultivate the holy life to cause others to purely cultivate the holy life;
it is impossible for a bodhisattva who themselves regresses from the holy life to cause others to fulfill the holy life."
It is impossible for a bodhisattva to personally destroy the holy life while causing others to be established in the holy life;
it is impossible for a bodhisattva to personally depart from the holy life while causing others to stand in the path of the holy life;
it is impossible for a bodhisattva to personally extinguish the holy life while causing others to cultivate the holy life.
It is impossible for a bodhisattva who does not delight in the holy life to cause others to delight in practicing the holy life;
it is impossible for a bodhisattva who does not abide in the holy life to cause others to dwell securely in the holy life;
it is impossible for a bodhisattva who has not perfected the holy life to cause others to perfect the holy life.
It is impossible for a bodhisattva to abandon the holy life themselves while causing others not to abandon it and to abide in the holy life;
it is impossible for a bodhisattva to destroy and disperse the holy life themselves while causing others to embrace the holy life.
"Why is this? Because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice according to their words, remaining far removed from perversions and being able to extensively expound the Dharma that is free from perversion;
they speak truth and act with integrity, cultivating pure actions of body, speech, and mind, remaining free from all defilements, proceeding in unobstructed states, and extinguishing all hindrances."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva himself maintains a straightforward mind and causes others to adopt the dharma of a straightforward mind;
the Bodhisattva cultivates patience and, through various roots of goodness, tames his own mind, while causing others to cultivate patience and tame their minds through various roots of goodness;
the Bodhisattva himself is free from doubt and regret, and causes others to be free from all doubt and regret.
The bodhisattva personally attains joyful faith and causes others to attain indestructible faith;
the bodhisattva personally practices the steadfast Dharma and causes others to practice the steadfast Dharma;
such is the dedication of roots of goodness by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness from the gateways of Dharma-giving and other such virtues in this way:

'By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings fully attain the inexhaustible Dharma-gates of all Buddhas; may they analyze and explain the Dharma-gates of all Buddhas; may they destroy all the heterodox arguments of external paths; may they cause the opponents' words and logic to be exhausted and defeated;

and may they fully attain the ocean of teachings spoken by all Buddhas of the three periods of time. Regarding each and every dharma of arising, each and every dharma of expedient means, each and every dharma of language, each and every dharma of designation, each and every dharma of instruction, each and every dharma of exposition, each and every Dharma-gate, each and every dharma of entry, each and every dharma of certainty, and each and every dharma of abiding, may they all fully attain the immeasurable, boundless, and inexhaustible treasury of Dharmas.'"

Attaining the state of fearlessness, they enter deeply into the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) and extensively expound the subtle and wondrous Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, without exhaustion until the end of the future.
They perfect the upright mind, depart from all inversions, give rise to the unimpeded path, and speak without error; when sentient beings hear their Dharma, they all rejoice.

Understanding all the languages and sounds of sentient beings, they attain non-retrogression and the illumination of all dharmas; all sentient beings experience immeasurable joy and all come to dwell securely in the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Fully endowed with freedom from delusion and possessing clear, pure eloquence in the Dharma, they hear and retain all teachings and are able to discern all worlds.
They attain an immeasurable body equal to the dharma-realm, which in a single thought-moment can completely fill the entire dharma-realm;
their subtle and wondrous voice pervades the infinite and boundless dharma-realm, manifesting retinues that fill the dharma-realm.

They cultivate the pure karma of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm; they attain the immeasurable abodes of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm; they attain the immeasurable definitive dharmas equal to the Dharma-realm; they study the ultimate realization of immeasurable phenomena equal to the Dharma-realm; they abide in the immeasurable Bodhisattva practices equal to the Dharma-realm; and they dedicate themselves to the immeasurable internal dharmas of Bodhisattvas equal to the Dharma-realm.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this way, they cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with sarvajñā (all-knowledge) and to dwell securely in sarvajñā.
Furthermore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:

They behold infinite Buddhas equal to the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), tame infinite sentient beings equal to the realm of phenomena, purify infinite Buddha-fields equal to the realm of phenomena, attain the infinite wisdom of Bodhisattvas equal to the realm of phenomena, attain the infinite fearlessnesses equal to the realm of phenomena, attain the infinite profound and wondrous eloquence equal to the realm of phenomena, attain all the infinite *dhāraṇīs* of Bodhisattvas equal to the realm of phenomena, attain the infinite inconceivable Bodhisattva abodes equal to the realm of phenomena, become fully endowed with the infinite treasuries of merit equal to the realm of phenomena, and become fully endowed with the infinite roots of goodness of true meaning equal to the realm of phenomena.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further reflects:
"By means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings fully attain this Dharma and bring it to complete perfection, no different from myself;

may they be equal in all practices, equal in merit, equal in wisdom, equal in powers, equal in fearlessnesses, equal in masteries, equal in perfect enlightenment, equal in preaching the Dharma, equal in the meaning of reality as it is, equal in debate, and equal in all supernormal penetrations."
"In this manner, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
'Just as the dharma-realm is immeasurable, so too is the wisdom that arises from it.'"
As the dharma-realm is immeasurable, so too are the Buddhas they behold;
as the dharma-realm is immeasurable, so too are the Buddha-fields they visit;
as the dharma-realm is immeasurable, so too are the practices of the bodhisattvas.
Just as the dharma-realm is indestructible, so too is the attainment of all-knowledge;
just as the dharma-realm is equal and one, so too is the attainment of all-knowledge;
just as the dharma-realm is naturally pure, so too is the purification of all sentient beings.
Just as the Dharma-realm accords with and reaches all things, so too does it cause all sentient beings to practice the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
just as the Dharma-realm adorns all sentient beings, so too does it cause all sentient beings to attain the adornment of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
just as the Dharma-realm is indestructible, so too does it cause all sentient beings to attain indestructible roots of goodness.
"Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:

'May all buddhas and bodhisattvas be fully delighted; may all roots of goodness lead toward sarvajñā (all-knowledge); may all roots of goodness lead toward sarvajña (omniscience) and reach all paths; and may all sentient beings constantly behold all buddhas.'"
“Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate these roots of goodness in this way: they dedicate them because they see all Buddhas as being able to perform the works of a Buddha;

they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas do not give rise to a mind of attachment toward the works of a Buddha; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas cause all sentient beings to universally attain purity; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas are able to fully comprehend everything; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas are entirely without attachment; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas are able to discern the unimpeded Dharma; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas are endowed with the practices of Samantabhadra; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas never miss the proper time; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas give birth to the immeasurable powers of Bodhisattvas; they dedicate them because they see that all Buddhas do not forget their Dharma.”

With these roots of goodness, one should dedicate them in this way: understanding that the dharma-realm is unborn; understanding that the dharma-realm is without intrinsic nature; understanding that the dharma-realm is suchness; understanding that the dharma-realm is without dependence; understanding that the dharma-realm is without delusion; understanding that the dharma-realm is free from marks; understanding that the dharma-realm is quiescent; understanding that the dharma-realm has no location; understanding that the dharma-realm neither departs nor accumulates; and understanding that the dharma-realm is indestructible.
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness in this way:
'By these roots of goodness encompassed by this gift of Dharma, may all sentient beings become great Dharma masters, abiding in the immeasurable sovereignty of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings become unsurpassed Dharma masters, establishing all sentient beings in omniscience.'"
May all sentient beings become indestructible Dharma masters, such that no questioning or challenging can exhaust them;
may all sentient beings become unimpeded Dharma masters, fully endowed with the unhindered illumination of all dharmas;
may all sentient beings become Dharma masters who are treasuries of wisdom, skillfully using expedient means to expound all Buddha-dharmas.
May all sentient beings achieve the status of a Tathāgata-like sovereign Dharma-master, capable of skillfully expounding the wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
may all sentient beings become pure-eyed Dharma-masters, extensively proclaiming the true Dharma without depending on the instruction of others;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-masters who correctly uphold the Buddha-Dharma, preaching the teachings with complete perfection so as not to lose even a single flavor.
May all sentient beings become Dharma-preachers who have transcended signs, adorning themselves with all sublime marks and radiating immeasurable light to extensively expound all dharmas;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-preachers of the Great Body, filling countless Buddha-fields with a single body, raising great clouds of Dharma and raining down the Buddha-dharma everywhere;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-preachers who never lose the great ocean of the Buddha-dharma, such that no one in any world can destroy it.
May all sentient beings become Sunlight Dharma Masters who are fully perfected, emitting the light of Buddha-wisdom that can clearly illuminate all dharmas;
may all sentient beings become Dharma Masters of Responsive Questioning, skillfully and expediently expounding all dharmas extensively;
may all sentient beings become Dharma Masters who have reached the other shore through ultimate practice, skillfully and expediently opening the immeasurable treasuries of Dharma.
May all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who establish the True Dharma, analytically expounding the Tathāgata’s wisdom of the Way;
may all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who thoroughly comprehend all phenomena, praising their inexhaustible merits;
may all sentient beings become Dharma teachers who are free from falsehood, entering the profound, true, and wondrous limit of all skillful means.
May all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers who awaken others to the works of Māra, being able to utterly destroy and disperse all demons;
may all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers protected by all Buddhas, never for a moment giving rise to thoughts of "I" or "mine";
may all sentient beings become Dharma-teachers of the peaceful True Dharma, fully attaining all the powers of aspiration of the Bodhisattvas.
The bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this manner: they dedicate without selecting karma; they dedicate without selecting retribution;

they dedicate without selecting vows; they dedicate without selecting dharmas; they dedicate without selecting phenomena; they dedicate without selecting causes; they dedicate without selecting the accomplishment of dharmas; they dedicate without selecting the body of names, the body of phrases, or the body of syllables; they dedicate without selecting dedication itself; and they dedicate without selecting meanings.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-one;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Twenty-two.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Ninth [Section] of the Twenty-first Chapter, "The Ten Dedications," of the *Vajradhvaja Bodhisattva*:
"The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
he dedicates them because he does not cling to form;..."
One dedicates without attachment to sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects;
one dedicates without seeking rebirth in the heavens;
and one dedicates without seeking sensual pleasures.
One dedicates because of non-attachment to the realm of desire;
one dedicates because of not seeking a retinue;
one dedicates because of not seeking sovereignty.
They dedicate [their merit] because they do not seek the pleasures of birth and death;
they dedicate because they do not cling to birth and death;
they dedicate because they do not cling to dying here and being born there.
They dedicate [their merit] because they do not seek the pleasures of the three realms of existence;
they dedicate because they do not seek that which is associated with desire;
they dedicate because they do not seek places of worldly enjoyment.
One dedicates because of the absence of a poisonous mind;
one dedicates because of not destroying roots of goodness;
one dedicates because of not relying on the triple world.
They dedicate [their merit] because they do not relish or become attached to the various dhyānas, liberations, samādhis, or meditative attainments;
they dedicate because they do not seek to abide in the vehicles of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas;
and they dedicate solely because they desire to subdue all sentient beings and fulfill the ultimate, unobstructed knowledge of omniscience (sarvajñā).
They dedicate [their merit] because they wish to purify all roots of goodness so that they are unimpeded;
they dedicate it because they wish to cause all sentient beings to transcend birth and death and attain the wisdom of the Mahāyāna;
they dedicate it because they wish to fulfill the adamantine bodhicitta.
They dedicate [their merit] because they desire to ultimately accomplish the dharma of immortality;
they dedicate it because they desire to manifest the sovereignty of omniscience through immeasurable adornments of the Buddha-lineage;
they dedicate it because they desire to fulfill the sovereign power of the spiritual light of all bodhisattva dharmas.

They dedicate their merit because they wish to practice the conduct of Samantabhadra in all Buddha-fields, equal to the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, without ever turning back; because they adorn themselves with the great adornment of the diamond of freedom from delusion and abide in the stages of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;

and because they wish to practice the conduct of Samantabhadra throughout all future eons to liberate sentient beings, manifesting the ground of the conduct adorned by all Buddhas and abiding therein without interruption.
“The bodhisattva mahāsattva thus dedicates with a mind of equanimity;
dedicates with a mind of the dharma of equanimity;
and dedicates with an immeasurable mind toward all sentient beings.”
Dedication with a mind free from contention;
dedication with a mind that perceives nothing;
dedication with an undistracted mind.
The dedication of the mind that enters equally into the three periods of time;
the dedication of the mind toward the lineage of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
and the dedication of the mind that attains the deathless supernormal powers.
They dedicate [their merit] with the mind of the Tathāgata’s nirvāṇa;
they dedicate so that all sentient beings may leave behind the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and King Yama;
they dedicate so that all sentient beings may eliminate those dharmas that obstruct the Path.
They dedicate for the sake of causing all sentient beings to fully possess roots of goodness and to rejoice;
they dedicate because they wish not to lose the opportunity to turn the wheel of Dharma;
and they dedicate because they wish to cause all sentient beings to perfect the wheel of the ten powers and reach the other shore.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] because I wish to fulfill the immeasurable and boundless pure Dharma-vows of bodhisattvas;
because I wish to perfect the vessel of spiritual friends so that, by following all the teachings of spiritual friends, one may possess the jewel of the bodhicitta;
and because I wish to cause all beings to abide in the profound Dharma of the Buddhas, to uprightly cultivate all Buddha-dharmas, and to be endowed with the light of unsurpassed wisdom.
They dedicate [their merit] because they desire that the unimpeded wisdom and illumination of all bodhisattvas may always be manifest before them;
they dedicate it because they desire that all may constantly see the Buddhas manifest before them;
they dedicate it because they desire that all may attain the gates of pure and clear Dharma.
I dedicate [these roots of goodness] because I wish to cause all beings to be free from all terrors by means of the gate of the bodhicitta that is endowed with fearlessness;
I dedicate them because I wish to cause all beings to attain the gates of wisdom regarding the inconceivable stages of the bodhisattvas;
and I dedicate them because I wish to cause all beings to attain complete purity through the protection and rescue of great compassion.
They dedicate [their merit] because they wish to adorn all buddha-fields without exception;
they dedicate because they wish to eliminate all demonic activities, hooks, baits, and the clever stratagems of Māra;
and they dedicate because they wish to cause all beings to cultivate the bodhisattva practices without becoming attached to any buddha-field.
They dedicate [their roots of goodness] because they desire to cause all beings to cross over and attain all Buddha-dharmas, and because they desire to obtain the vast mind of omniscience.
By means of these roots of goodness, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate them because they desire to purify right mindfulness;
they dedicate them because they desire to achieve certainty.
They dedicate [their merit] because they wish to comprehend and fully understand all Buddha-dharmas;
they dedicate it because they wish to attain immeasurable, boundless, and unimpeded wisdom;
they dedicate it because they wish to attain a pure and upright mind.
They dedicate [their merit] so that all sentient beings may cultivate the mind of great loving-kindness;
they dedicate it so that they may cultivate the mind of great compassion;
and they dedicate it so that they may cultivate the mind of sympathetic joy.
They dedicate because they cultivate a mind of equanimity;
they dedicate because they attain the two kinds of unimpeded liberation and abide in roots of goodness;
they dedicate because they desire to discern all phenomena of dependent origination.
They dedicate [their merit] because they wish to discern the dharma of dependent origination and attain a mind of dharma-born transformation;
they dedicate it because they wish to attain a mind like a courageous banner;
they dedicate it because they wish to attain the treasury of the indestructible banner.
They dedicate [their merit] because they wish to destroy all Māras;
they dedicate because they wish to attain a mind that is entirely pure and unimpeded regarding all dharmas;
they dedicate because they wish to practice all bodhisattva deeds and attain a mind of non-retrogression.
One dedicates [merit] because of the desire to seek and attain a mind of supreme excellence;
one dedicates because of the desire to attain the joy of sovereign wisdom regarding all meritorious dharmas and to seek omniscience;

one dedicates because of the desire to fulfill all vows, extinguish all evils, receive the prediction of stainlessness, attain the sovereignty of a Buddha, and turn the non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.

I dedicate [these roots of goodness] because I desire that the sun-like light of the immeasurable wisdom of the Tathāgata’s various wondrous and supreme dharmas, adorned with the radiance of great knowledge, may universally illuminate the dharma-realm of all sentient beings;

I dedicate them because I desire to subdue all sentient beings so that they may all rejoice and fulfill their great vows, practicing the bodhisattva path throughout all future kalpas, extinguishing all afflictions, becoming stainless and pure, tearing asunder the net of craving, removing the darkness of ignorance, becoming fully endowed with the stainless and unimpeded Dharma, cultivating the non-retrogressive conduct of a bodhisattva, and attaining all-knowledge;
I dedicate them because I desire to cause all sentient beings to attain the body of unimpeded, unsurpassed, wondrous wisdom and to manifest the bodies of immeasurable Buddhas.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate their roots of goodness in this way, they do not cling to the five desires and do not rely upon the three realms. Why is this?
Because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas dedicate roots of goodness that are free from defilement.
Dedicating roots of goodness that are far removed from ill will;
dedicating roots of goodness that abandon delusion;
dedicating indestructible roots of goodness.
The dedication of roots of goodness through remaining far removed from arrogance;
the dedication of roots of goodness through eliminating flattery and crookedness;
and the dedication of roots of goodness through a straightforward mind.
Diligently cultivating roots of goodness and dedicating them.
When a bodhisattva mahāsattva thus dedicates, they attain great joy;
regarding the bodhisattva practices, they attain correct aspiration:
They proceed upon the path of the mahāsattvas, possess the lineage of the Buddhas, attain the wisdom of the Buddhas, and remain free from all evils;
they subdue all māras and are able to discipline all sentient beings, causing all spiritual friends to rejoice;
they bring to full completion all the vows they have cultivated and invite all sentient beings to partake in great assemblies of giving.
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness from this Dharma-giving in this way:

'May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the pure sound of Dharma; may they obtain a gentle voice, an agreeable and joyful voice, an inconceivable voice, a delightful voice, a voice that fills all Buddha-fields, a voice adorned with inconceivable merit, a voice that extinguishes loud and distracted sounds, a pure and wondrous voice that fills the Dharma-realm, and a voice that gathers in all sentient beings;
may all sentient beings obtain the wisdom of infinite voices.'"
May all sentient beings attain pure and wondrous voices;
may all sentient beings fully attain the wondrous wisdom of mastery over sound;
may all sentient beings attain voices adorned with every excellence.
May all sentient beings attain wondrous voices, such that sentient beings delight in hearing them without ever becoming weary;
may all sentient beings attain the voice of liberation and reach the other shore;
may all sentient beings attain the voice of joy.
May all sentient beings attain the pure speech and sounds of the Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain the voice of the Buddhas, possessing wondrous eloquence and remaining far removed from ignorance;

may all sentient beings attain the sublime *dhāraṇī* that adorns all phenomena, expounding infinite modes of practice for each and every dharma, with countless retinues filling the Dharma-realm, able to hear and retain the inconceivable Vajra True Dharma, explaining it in detail, and being able to fully proclaim the infinite treasuries of Dharma through immeasurable word-bodies and meaning-bodies, with various characteristics of phenomena, abiding in the state of non-attachment, and attaining the illumination of all dharmas.

May all sentient beings ultimately attain *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), encompassing all dharmas; may they obtain mastery over the sounds of the phonemes (*vyañjana-kāya*) and the meanings of all dharmas through the body of phrases (*pada-kāya*) and the body of syllables (*nirukti-kāya*), and reaching the further shore, may they possess mastery over unimpeded sound;

may they cause all sentient beings to obtain the voice of sorrowlessness, the voice of fearlessness, the voice of non-defilement, the voice of merit, the voice that causes their retinues to rejoice, the voice that accords with the Dharma, the voice of the speech of all Buddhas, the voice that swiftly eradicates the net of doubts of all sentient beings, the voice of uninterrupted eloquence, and the voice of supreme awakening for sentient beings.
"Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
'May all sentient beings attain the pure Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings attain pure and wondrous merit;'"
May all sentient beings be endowed with the primary and secondary marks;
may all sentient beings attain the retribution of pure karma;
may all sentient beings attain the pure mind of omniscience (sarvajñā-citta).
May all sentient beings attain the immeasurable, pure mind of bodhi;
may all sentient beings attain pure skillful means that enable them to discern the various faculties of all beings;
may all sentient beings attain the nature of purity.
May all sentient beings attain pure and unimpeded conduct that fulfills all vows;
may all sentient beings attain pure right mindfulness, wisdom, and uninterrupted eloquence.
“The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:

‘May all sentient beings attain such pure and wondrous bodies as these—namely, the luminously pure body, the body free from turbidity, the ultimately pure body, the purified body, the dust-free body, the body free from various kinds of dust, the stainless body, the radiant body, the delightful body, and the unimpeded body. With such bodies, may they universally respond to all worlds throughout the ten directions, manifesting all karmas and appearing before sentient beings; may they universally illumine everything and manifest all things like reflections in a mirror or the moon in clear water, so that all sentient beings may fully attain such pure and wondrous bodies.’”
They manifest to sentient beings the various practices of Bodhisattvas;
they manifest to sentient beings all profound and wondrous Dharmas;
and they manifest to sentient beings immeasurable merits.
They manifest the true path of reality to sentient beings;
they manifest sentient beings as being fully endowed with all dharmas;
and they manifest all great vows of sentient beings as abiding within a single kṣetra.
Manifesting the appearance of Tathāgatas in all worlds;
manifesting the sovereign power of the supernormal feats (*ṛddhi-vaśitā*) of all Buddhas;
and manifesting the upholding of the inconceivable liberations (*vimokṣa*) of Bodhisattvas.
Manifesting the universal conduct, vows, and wisdom of Samantabhadra,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates their roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings achieve the body of wisdom consisting of all meritorious virtues."
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates the roots of goodness gathered through this Dharma-giving in this way:
'May a single body pervade all worlds to practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva, such that all sentient beings who see it shall not do so in vain, but shall attain the non-regressive mind of Bodhi;
may all sentient beings accord with reality and attain an indestructible mind.'"
May all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and for as long as the future kalpas endure, practice the bodhisattva path without ever feeling weary or satisfied.
May they possess a great heart of compassion equal to the dharma-realm, teaching and transforming sentient beings without ever missing the proper time.

Discerning all faculties, one should keep the spiritual friend in mind; within a single thought-moment, one perceives all Buddhas of the present and never for a moment abandons the mindfulness of the Tathāgata.

They cultivate all roots of goodness without falsehood or deception; they establish sentient beings in omniscience; they fully attain the non-regressive, pure wheel of Dharma; they fully attain the illumination of all Buddha-dharmas; they receive and uphold the rain of all Buddha-dharmas, and practice the conduct of a bodhisattva.

Entering all sentient beings; entering all lands; entering all phenomena; entering all worlds; entering all three periods of time; entering the wisdom of the karmic retributions of all sentient beings; entering the wisdom of the skillful means of all bodhisattvas; entering the wisdom of the birth of all bodhisattvas; entering the wisdom of the pure realms of all bodhisattvas; entering the sustaining realms of all Buddhas; and entering all infinite and boundless dharma-realms to cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva and abide securely in all stages of dwelling—this is the dedication of the roots of goodness from the Dharma-giving of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
"Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva cultivates roots of goodness and dedicates them in this way:
'May all Buddha-fields be completely purified and adorned with immeasurable ornaments;
may each single Buddha-field be as vast as the Dharma-realm, and as it is for one Buddha-field, so it shall be for all Buddha-fields.'"
Having attained supreme perfect enlightenment in a single buddha-field, one manifests all buddha-fields; as it is with one buddha-field, so it is with all buddha-fields.
Each of those lands was adorned with various ornaments equal in extent to the dharma-realm:
they were adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* multitudes of jewels;
there were immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* pure jewel thrones, upon which exquisite jewel robes were spread.
There were immeasurable, incalculable canopies of exquisite jewels, adorned with all kinds of jeweled bells and hanging jeweled bands;
immeasurable jeweled parasols were spread above them;
and immeasurable jeweled clouds rained down every kind of jewel and scattered various jeweled flowers, such that those who beheld them could never tire.
It has railings made of immeasurable wonderful jewels and is adorned with exquisite jeweled pavilions;
immeasurable jeweled bells spontaneously proclaim the sublime Dharma of all Buddhas;
immeasurable jeweled flowers fill it everywhere, and it is further embellished with the colors of various wonderful jewels.
Immeasurable jewel trees fill that land, producing immeasurable exquisite jewels as flowers and fruits;
immeasurable exquisite jewels serve as palaces, and exquisite jewel towers and pavilions travel throughout all lands;
immeasurable exquisite jewels form railings, magnificently adorned with great treasures.
The pavilions were covered with immeasurable exquisite jewels and adorned with every kind of pure gem;
they featured immeasurable jeweled gates, embellished with various garlands of gems;
and they were decorated with immeasurable crescent-shaped ornaments of rare treasures, all fashioned from a multitude of jewels.
Adorned with immeasurable, incalculable, and inconceivable treasures, it arises from the roots of goodness and pure karma of all Buddhas;
adorned with immeasurable treasuries of jewels, which are further embellished by various precious gems;
it flows forth immeasurable rivers of pure jewels, constantly streaming the True Dharma without ever ceasing.
Infinite oceans of Dharma pervade that land, filled to the brim with the pure water of the True Dharma;
it is completely filled with infinite *asaṃkhyeya* jewel *puṇḍarīka* flowers, which spontaneously produce the melodic sounds of the flowers of the True Dharma;
it is adorned with infinite *asaṃkhyeya* precious Sumeru mountains, wherein the Sumerus of wisdom are all fully present.
Adorned with immeasurable asankhyeyas of exquisite eight-faceted jewels, with various precious necklaces hanging down as sashes;
adorned with immeasurable asankhyeyas of luminous and pure jewels, radiating the great light of wisdom that universally illumines the Dharma-realm;
adorned with immeasurable asankhyeyas of precious bells, spontaneously producing subtle and wondrous sounds.
It was adorned with stairways of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* precious jewels, filled entirely with the exquisite jewels of the bodhisattvas;
it was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* precious silk banners, established with inconceivable purity of precious colors;
it was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* precious victory banners, embellished with images of precious half-moons.
Adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel banners, they were able to rain down immeasurable jewel banners everywhere;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel silks that filled the worlds and decorated the void, they spread immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* fine, soft jewel garments as an adornment;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* swirling currents of various jewels, they manifested the pure eye of omniscience (*sarvajñāna*) of the bodhisattvas.
Adorned with immeasurable asaṃkhyeya jewel garlands, each jewel garland was further embellished by hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas;
adorned with immeasurable asaṃkhyeya palaces of various jewels, they were able to eliminate all attachment to specific locations;
and adorned with immeasurable asaṃkhyeya clusters of various jewels, they were further embellished with vajra-maṇi gems.
Adorned with immeasurable asankhyeya varieties of precious jewels, they manifest immeasurable pure and wondrous colors;
adorned with immeasurable asankhyeya vajra-rimmed mountains, they are pure, translucent, and without obstruction;

adorned with immeasurable asankhyeya exquisite fragrances, their scent universally perfumes all worlds, giving rise to immeasurable asankhyeya transformation bodies, each of which is equal to the dharma-realm and emits immeasurable asankhyeya rays of light from exquisite jewels.

From each and every light ray emerge all lights, with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* pure and radiant jewel-lights providing illumination, capable of generating the light of pure wisdom in sentient beings;
they emit immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* unimpeded jewel-lights, each light ray universally illuminating the Dharma-realm;
there are immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* adornments of various jewels, and within each individual jewel are contained all jewels.
Adorned with immeasurable asaṃkhyeya treasuries of jewels, they spontaneously expound the jewel-treasury of all dharmas;
adorned with immeasurable asaṃkhyeya jeweled banners, they establish the sublime banner of the Tathāgata’s wondrous wisdom;
adorned with immeasurable asaṃkhyeya noble jewels, they are fully endowed with the pure noble jewels of the Mahāyāna.
It was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel gardens, where the bodhisattvas’ samādhis were cool, refreshing, and joyful;

immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sounds of exquisite jewels spontaneously issued forth, and from each sound emerged the voice of the Tathāgata, filling the ten directions so that there was no one who did not hear it;
it was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* precious images, each image-body universally radiating immeasurable light of the Dharma-jewels.
Adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* multitudes of marks, yet adorned with the marklessness of all marks;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewels of majestic deportment, such that those who see them joyfully seek the Bodhisattva’s deportment;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* treasures nurtured for growth, producing all manner of sublime jewel treasuries.
It was adorned with the peaceful dwelling of immeasurable asankhyeya multitudes of jewels, embellished by all manner of precious gems;
it was adorned with immeasurable asankhyeya robes of precious materials, which universally covered and fully endowed the immeasurable samādhis of the bodhisattvas;

it was adorned with immeasurable asankhyeya exquisite garments, such that those who resolved their minds upon enlightenment immediately attained the *dhāraṇīs* of the bodhisattvas, such as the "Excellent Manifestation" (*Suvikrānta*).
They possess the adornment of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewels of cultivation, being able to discern all karmic jewels and their retributions with definitive purity;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* exquisite jewels of unimpeded knowledge and vision, such that whoever beholds them attains the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel celestial crowns, fully accomplishing the celestial crown of wisdom.
There were adornments of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel thrones, forming pure and precious lion seats for the attainment of Buddhahood;
immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* bright and pure jewel lamps were lit, fully possessing the lamps of brilliant and wondrous wisdom;
there were adornments of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* precious *tāla* trees, each and every *tāla* tree being decorated with precious necklaces.
It was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jeweled cooling terraces;
it was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel trees, upon which inconceivable birds gathered and emitted wondrous sounds;

it was adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* transformed flowers of exquisite jewels, and upon each flower sat immeasurable bodhisattvas in the full lotus posture, traveling everywhere throughout the Dharma-realm.
Adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* fruits, it possesses the fruit of the great wisdom of *sarvajñā*;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* clusters of various jewels, all have cultivated the pure and true Dharma;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel mansions, the streets and alleys of various jewels are filled with people.

There were immeasurable, incalculable royal capitals adorned with jewels, where those great kings, courageous and diligent, donned the great armor of the Dharma and remained firm and non-regressive in the unsurpassed path;
there were immeasurable, incalculable jewel mansions adorned with jewels, which eliminated all craving for dwellings;
and there were immeasurable, incalculable jewel robes adorned with jewels, which they enjoyed according to their will without any attachment.
It was filled with bodhisattvas who had abandoned their homes to leave the household life, adorned by immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel mansions;
it was adorned by immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewels that never weary, inspiring immeasurable joy in all who behold them;
it was adorned by immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel wheels, emitting inconceivable light of wisdom and turning the wheel of non-retrogression.
It was adorned with immeasurable, incalculable rows of trees made of wondrous jewels, embellished with pure *indranīla* gems;
it was adorned with immeasurable, incalculable jewel-grounds, manifesting inconceivable jewels in their distinct arrays;
it was adorned with immeasurable, incalculable musical instruments, which produced spontaneous sounds that filled the entire Dharma-realm.
Adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* musical instruments, they constantly produce the sounds of the Dharma until the end of the future, never ceasing;
adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* precious bodies, they fill those lands and are able to receive and uphold all the treasures of the Dharma;

adorned with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* pure precious mouths, they possess the treasure-trove of all merits and produce immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* pure precious sounds, constantly preaching immeasurable pure and wondrous Dharma-treasures.
Adorned with immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel-minds, they attain the jewel of rectitude, and all their vows for omniscience are completely fulfilled;
adorned with immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel-thoughts, they eliminate ignorance and attain the supreme jewel-king of omniscience;
adorned with immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel-approaches, they are able to fully embrace the jewels of the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
Adorned with the jewel of wisdom of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas, they possess definitive and excellent knowledge of all Buddha-dharmas;
adorned with the jewel of wisdom of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya non-negligence, they are entirely filled with the jewels of omniscience;
adorned with the jewel of the pure eye of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya, they encounter no obstruction regarding the jewels of all ten powers.
They possess the adornment of immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel ears, which are able to hear the subtle sounds of the entire dharma-realm without obstruction;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel noses, which never tire of smelling the fragrances of pure jewels;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel broad and long tongues, which skillfully expound all modes of speech and dharma.
They possess the adornment of immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel bodies, traveling through the ten directions without obstruction;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel minds, being able to fully cultivate all the great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable, incalculable, pure jewel voices, their subtle and wondrous sounds completely filling all worlds.
They possess the adornment of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel-like deeds of body, fully endowed with all jewel-like deeds of wisdom;
they possess the adornment of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* jewel-like deeds of speech, extensively expounding the wondrous jewels of immeasurable wisdom;
and they possess the adornment of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* pure jewel-like deeds of mind, reaching the ultimate in all unimpeded jewel-like wisdom.
“Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects in this way:
‘Within all those lands of the Tathāgatas—within a single Buddha-field, a single direction, or a single hair-pore—I shall accomplish immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable pure wisdom.’”

Great Bodhisattvas completely fill them all—just as it is for one buddha-field, one direction, or one hair-pore, so it is for the entirety of space and the dharma-realm; likewise, it is so for all buddha-fields, all directions, and all hair-pores.

This is the dedication of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva toward the wondrous jewel-adornments of all Buddha-fields; just as all Buddha-fields are adorned with jewels, so too are they extensively described as being adorned with incense, up to and including the ultimate, immeasurable, pure, and wondrous fragrance of the unimpeded jewel-like wisdom of mental action.
The detailed exposition of the adornment of flowers, up to the ultimate purity of the mental karma of the Flower-Intention Unhindered Jewel-Wisdom, is likewise.
The detailed exposition of garlands, ointments, powdered incense, robes, parasols, banners, and streamers, up to the hundredfold adornments, is likewise.
In this way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dedicates these roots of goodness gathered through such gifts of Dharma:

they dedicate them for the purpose of nurturing roots of goodness; they dedicate them for the purpose of adorning and purifying Buddha-fields; and they dedicate them for the purpose of bringing all sentient beings to purity and equality.
To cause all sentient beings to eliminate and extinguish anger and hatred;
to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the profound Buddha-dharma of equanimity;
and to cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with the power of indestructible, pure merit through equanimity.
May all sentient beings fully attain impartial, inexhaustible wisdom to transcend all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings fully attain impartial, pure Brahma-voices;
may all sentient beings fully attain impartial, unobstructed pure eyes, reaching the ultimate unobstructed wisdom equal to empty space and the dharma-realm.
May all sentient beings attain pure, impartial, and right mindfulness throughout all past kalpas;
may all sentient beings attain impartial and unimpeded wisdom, decisively and fully understanding all dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain impartial bodhi, filling the dharma-realm without any obstruction.
May all sentient beings fully attain equality in all sublime roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings fully attain equality in the actions of body, speech, and mind, being endowed with the adornments of merit and purity;
may all sentient beings fully attain equality in all the practices of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
May all sentient beings attain the equality of pure Buddha-fields;
may all sentient beings attain the equality of full endowment, deeply entering into the practices of omniscience;
may all sentient beings be free from all evils and fully attain the equality of dedicating their roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings attain the equality of all-knowing vision, such that they are all able to discern the mental activities of others;
may all sentient beings attain the equality of dwelling securely in pure dharmas (*śukladharma*);
may all sentient beings attain the equality of possessing all-knowledge within a single thought-moment, ultimately fulfilling unsurpassed bodhi.
May all sentient beings achieve all paths of equal practice, fully purified and complete.
With these roots of goodness, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva universally dedicates them for the sake of equality;
may all sentient beings attain the power of pure discernment regarding all dharmas, and he extensively explains this dedication for the sake of all beings.
“Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reflects thus:

‘By means of these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings cultivate the pure conduct of Bodhisattvas and attain immeasurable oceans of Dharma; within each and every ocean of Dharma, equal to the immeasurable realms of reality (dharmadhātu), may their pure wisdom universally illumine the realm of reality;
and may they cause all sentient beings to analyze and explain the meaning of all phrases.’”
May all sentient beings fully attain the Samādhi of the Illumination of All Dharmas, which universally shines light upon all phenomena;
may all sentient beings be completely endowed with the eloquence that accords with the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may all sentient beings attain the sovereign body of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
May all sentient beings attain unimpeded roots of goodness, give rise to love for the Buddha-dharma, never retreat from great compassion, and rescue and protect all beings;
may all sentient beings attain unimpeded wisdom and inconceivable dharmas, and be able to purify and bring joy to all assemblies;

may all sentient beings, within all buddha-fields—whether inverted, upright, prostrate, minute, vast, pure, or defiled—within all such buddha-fields, universally turn the pure and non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma.
May all sentient beings, in every thought-moment, attain inexhaustible and fearless eloquence, so that they may extensively expound the Buddha-dharma without end;
may all sentient beings always find joy, single-mindedly seeking the supreme Dharma, and attain sovereign wisdom regarding all phenomena;
may all sentient beings be filled with great delight and extensively expound all dharmas.
Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in the dedication of immeasurable roots of goodness within the dharma-realm;
the dedication of immeasurable physical actions within the dharma-realm;
and the dedication of immeasurable verbal actions within the dharma-realm.
Dedicating immeasurable mental karma throughout the dharma-realm;
dedicating immeasurable sublime forms throughout the dharma-realm;
dedicating immeasurable sublime sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness throughout the dharma-realm.
The dedication of the immeasurable equality of the dharma-realm aggregates;
the dedication of the immeasurable equality of the dharma-realm elements;
the dedication of the immeasurable equality of the dharma-realm sense-bases.
The impartial dedication within the immeasurable realm of phenomena;
the impartial dedication without the immeasurable realm of phenomena;
and the impartial dedication through the immeasurable vigor and diligence of the realm of phenomena.
The impartial dedication of the immeasurable, upright mind of the dharma-realm;
the impartial dedication of the immeasurable skillful means of the dharma-realm;
the impartial dedication of the immeasurable nature of the dharma-realm.
The dedication of the equality of the infinite faculties of the dharma-realm;
the dedication of the equality of the infinite three periods of time of the dharma-realm;
the dedication of the equality of the infinite karmic retributions of the dharma-realm.
The dedication of the infinite dharma-realm as pure and equal, free from all afflictions;
the dedication of the infinite dharma-realm to the equality of all sentient beings;
and the dedication of the infinite dharma-realm to the equality of all buddha-fields.
The dedication of all phenomena throughout the infinite dharma-realm with equanimity;
the dedication of all worlds throughout the infinite dharma-realm with equanimity;
and the dedication of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the infinite dharma-realm with equanimity.
The dedication of all bodhisattva practices and vows throughout the infinite dharma-realm with equanimity;
the dedication of the infinite path of equality of all bodhisattvas throughout the infinite dharma-realm;
and the dedication of the accomplishment of all roots of goodness by all bodhisattvas throughout the infinite dharma-realm.
The dedication of the equality and non-duality of all phenomena throughout the infinite realm of reality;
the dedication to the perfect fulfillment of the retinues of all Tathāgatas throughout the infinite realm of reality.
"When a bodhisattva mahāsattva dedicates in this way, they abide in immeasurable, pure bodily actions equal to the dharma-realm;
they abide in immeasurable, pure verbal actions equal to the dharma-realm;
they abide in immeasurable, pure mental actions equal to the dharma-realm."
They abide in immeasurable pure practices and vows equal to the dharma-realm;
they abide in immeasurable pure retinues equal to the dharma-realm;
and they abide in the immeasurable pure wisdom of all bodhisattvas equal to the dharma-realm, extensively expounding all dharmas.

Abiding in the immeasurable pure bodies that are equal to the *dharmadhātu*, they fill all worlds and the *dharmadhātu*. Having attained the clarity, purity, and fearlessness of all phenomena, they completely eliminate the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings with a single utterance, causing them all to rejoice. They discipline the faculties and establish them in the unsurpassed wisdom, the powers, the fearlessnesses, and the sovereign powers of all Buddhas—the supreme and wondrous Dharma of the immeasurable merits of the Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth dedication of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, the immeasurable dedication equal to the Dharma-realm.

Having dedicated all roots of goodness, such as this gift of Dharma, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva accomplishes the infinite and boundless practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; he is able to adorn and purify all buddha-fields throughout the infinite and boundless expanse of space and the Dharma-realm, causing all sentient beings to do likewise.”
Fully accomplishing immeasurable and boundless wisdom, they penetrate deeply into all phenomena, manifesting in every moment the appearance of countless and innumerable Buddhas throughout all worlds.
They all attain the sovereign mastery of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas;
they all attain the sovereign mastery of immeasurable and boundless Tathāgatas;
they all attain the sovereign mastery of immeasurable and boundless vastness.
They have all attained immeasurable, boundless, unimpeded mastery;
they have all attained immeasurable, boundless, unobstructed mastery;
they have all attained immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable mastery.
They all attain immeasurable and boundless mastery in purifying all sentient beings;
they all attain immeasurable and boundless mastery in sustaining all worlds;
they all attain immeasurable and boundless mastery in all that is ineffable.
They have all attained mastery over all times, which is immeasurable and boundless;
they have all attained mastery over the unimpeded knowledge of all supernormal powers, which is immeasurable and boundless;
they have all attained mastery over the extensive exposition of all dharmas that fills the dharma-realm, which is immeasurable and boundless.
They all attained the pure eyes of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, which are immeasurable, boundless, and fully satisfied;

they all attained the immeasurable, boundless pure ears of a bodhisattva, by which they hear and retain the true Dharma spoken by all Buddhas; they were able, with a single body sitting in the full lotus posture, to fill all worlds throughout the ten directions without causing any distress to sentient beings;
and they all attained immeasurable, boundless, and fully perfected wisdom that penetrates deeply into the three periods of time.
They have all attained the infinite and boundless purity of awakening, the purity of sentient beings, the purity of Buddha-fields, the purity of all Buddhas, and the purity of all sense bases;
they have all attained the infinite and boundless pure wisdom equal to space and the dharma-realm;

they have all attained the infinite and boundless pure wisdom of the languages and sounds of sentient beings, emitting great radiance that universally illumines all worlds in the ten directions; they have produced the pure wisdom of the practices of all Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time; and within a single thought-moment, they have fully perfected the pure wisdom of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, causing all sentient beings to become entirely pure, to be fully endowed with the accomplishment of impartial right contemplation and decisive wisdom, and to ultimately reach the other shore.
At that time, through the spiritual power of the Buddha, worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten million buddha-fields in each of the ten directions shook in six ways;

and through the spiritual power of the Buddha, and because such is the nature of the Dharma, clouds of celestial flowers rained down, as did celestial garlands, celestial powdered incense, celestial jeweled robes, celestial ornaments, celestial perfumes, celestial maṇi jewels, celestial aloeswood incense, celestial agalloch incense, celestial bālāgandha incense, celestial solid incense, celestial sandalwood incense, and celestial multicolored banners and canopies.
Inconceivable and subtle Dharma-sounds from immeasurable asaṃkhyeya celestial bodies, and inconceivable wondrous voices of the devas, praised the Tathāgata;
immeasurable asaṃkhyeya devas showered clouds of "Excellent! (Sādhu) praises;
and immeasurable nayuta devas paid reverent homage and prostrated themselves.
Immeasurable, incalculable, nayuta-devas rejoiced in mindfulness of the Buddha and cultivated the inconceivable merits of all Buddhas;
immeasurable, incalculable devas produced sounds of entertainment as an offering to the Tathāgata;

they emitted immeasurable, incalculable, vast radiances that surpassed those of all other devas, universally illuminating all buddha-fields throughout space and the dharma-realm, manifesting immeasurable, incalculable transformation bodies of the Tathāgatas with sovereign power that transcended all devas.

Just as in this world, in the Tuṣita Heaven of all four continents, within the palace of King Śāntatuṣita, this Dharma was taught; so too it was in the palaces of King Śāntatuṣita in all the Tuṣita Heavens throughout the worlds of the ten directions.

At that time, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, from each of the ten directions, across worlds as numerous as the atoms in a million buddha-fields, there came together clouds of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a million buddha-fields, all of whom spoke these words: "Excellent!
Excellent, O Son of the Buddha!
You are truly able to expound these great dedications.
We are all of one and the same name, Vajradhvaja.
We have come to this land from the world-system Vajraprabhā, from the presence of the Buddha Vajradhvaja.
By the spiritual power of the Buddhas in those various worlds, they too preach this Dharma.
The great assembly, its retinue, and the phrasing and flavor of the Dharma teachings are all entirely equal.
We have come from that land by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power to bear witness for you.

Just as I have come to this world to bear witness for you, so too do I go to bear witness in the same manner wherever such a Dharma is taught upon the mani-jewel palaces of the Tuṣita Heaven kings throughout all the four continents in every direction of the ten quarters.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions, his own retinue, and the entire dharma-realm; he contemplated all meanings, phrases, and expressions, cultivating an immeasurable and vast mind, with supreme great compassion universally covering all beings.

Their minds dwell securely in the lineage of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, fully perfecting the merits of all Buddhas and accomplishing the precious bodies of sovereign mastery of all Buddhas.
They are able to discern the hopes, inclinations, and mental activities of all sentient beings; they fully know the timing for each according to the roots of goodness they have planted;
and, in accordance with the Dharma-body, they manifest form-bodies.
Having observed this, he spoke in verse:
“The Bodhisattva receives these Immeasurable treasures of Dharma; He is a self-enlightened one, Prophesied as a Great Dharma Master.”

Acting as a teacher who tames and controls, he universally illuminates all dharmas; having skillfully awakened to the unobstructed path of supreme perfect enlightenment, this Bodhisattva, as a great master who tames and controls, is able to extensively expound the profound Dharma that is so difficult to encounter.
All the immeasurable multitudes throughout the ten directions are fully established in all the gates of the True Dharma.
The Bodhisattvas drink from the immeasurable oceans of Dharma, raise great clouds of Dharma, and rain down the rain of Dharma everywhere.
The sun of the Dharma shines with brilliance, universally illuminating the world; it proclaims the subtle and wondrous Dharma to benefit all sentient beings.
This patron of the Dharma is extremely difficult to encounter; they have fully accomplished the skillful means of all dharmas.
With the light of wisdom, they universally illumine their minds; being fearless in the world, they extensively expound the profound Dharma.
Skillfully able to cultivate the transformative mind, they are widely able to open and reveal all gates of the True Dharma.
Having accomplished all gateways, [he is] the most supreme ocean of Dharma; for the sake of the entire world, he beats the drum of ambrosia.
He is able to fully expound the wondrous Dharma so difficult to encounter, nourishing all merits through the Dharma.
The pure and true Dharma, the straight and upright Dharma, is manifested for sentient beings as a most profound treasury of teachings.
To those most excellent ones, he bestows the empowerment of the Dharma King; they fully accomplish the body that is a treasury of wisdom.
With the wondrous wisdom of signlessness, they contemplate the true nature of phenomena; thus do Bodhisattvas dwell securely in wholesome dharmas.
The Dharma-giving of Bodhisattvas is most preeminent, and all Buddhas together praise it.
In accord with all, the God among Gods, he is able to give birth to all Buddhas.
The Bodhisattva’s pure and subtle Dharma-body is entirely born through transformation from the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
The bright and pure lamp of Dharma benefits sentient beings; it expounds immeasurable teachings to eliminate sorrow and affliction.
The Bodhisattva’s giving is the pure and wondrous Dharma, which accords with and contemplates all roots of goodness.
The merit performed throughout immeasurable worlds, and all pure wisdom, are entirely dedicated.
May all the merits attained by all Buddhas cause all sentient beings to fully achieve and perfect them.
Discerning all pure merits, they bring to ultimate completion the adornments of the Buddhas on the other shore.
Throughout the ten directions, all the infinite and innumerable Tathāgatas likewise purify and adorn their Buddha-fields.
In this way, throughout all Buddha-lands without exception, the adornments of sentient beings are inconceivable.
All Tathāgatas cause all sentient beings to be completely pure and fully endowed with wisdom.
Just as Samantabhadra, with the adornments of a bodhisattva, causes all sentient beings to likewise become so;
fully accomplishing immeasurable mastery, filling all worlds without exception.
Throughout all the ten directions, without exception, all sentient beings abide entirely in those pure practices.
In the infinite Buddha-fields of the ten directions, all those Tathāgatas practice the bodhisattva path.
May all sentient beings throughout the ten directions ultimately achieve the supreme and victorious practice.
May all these sons of the Buddha cultivate the merits of a Buddha, which are immeasurable, boundless,
and beyond calculation.
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, discern and know all things, causing all sentient beings to fully achieve perfection.
The Bodhisattvas possess all supernatural powers and are able to skillfully learn everything that is to be learned.
Wandering through the ten directions and all worlds, they manifest immeasurable and sovereign spiritual powers.
Within a single thought-moment, these Bodhisattvas are able to see all Buddhas, as numerous as all sentient beings.
Within a single hair-pore, the Bodhisattva is able to see all the True Dharmas of all Buddhas;
all sentient beings and their immeasurable practices, as well as all that is most supreme,
