For example, just as space neither moves nor remains stationary, yet can manifest various modes of deportment, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: neither moving nor remaining stationary, yet able to discern all conditioned activities (*saṃskāra*).

For example, just as space is neither form (*rūpa*) nor formless, yet can manifest hundreds of thousands of forms, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: neither worldly form nor free from worldly form, yet able to manifest all forms.

Just as space neither abides for long nor abides for a moment, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: he neither approaches for long nor approaches for a moment, yet is able to extensively expound all the stages of dwelling and practice of Bodhisattvas.
Just as space is neither pure nor defiled, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: he is neither obscured by worldly hindrances, nor is he [intrinsically] pure.

Just as space is said by all the world to be present before them, yet in reality it is not present before them, so too is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: all dharmas appear before the Bodhisattva, yet for the Bodhisattva, nothing appears before him.
Just as space dwells in all places yet space has no boundaries, so too it is with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: he dwells in all phenomena, yet the bodhisattva’s mind has no boundaries.
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates their own roots of goodness as being like empty space:

the roots of goodness are pure, the roots of goodness are complete, the roots of goodness are equal, the roots of goodness are a single part, the roots of goodness are quiescent, the roots of goodness are of one flavor, the roots of goodness are of one measure, and the roots of goodness are as pure as the color of space. These roots of goodness lead to all paths, do not forget any dharmas, attain all indestructible dharmas, travel through all lands, and are endowed with all bodies, yet they remain entirely unattached to any of those bodies.
Throughout the ten directions, they are forever free from delusion and confusion; they fully accomplish indestructible power and fulfill all realms of merit;
they attain all modes of Dharma, attain profound delight in the Dharma, and attain adamantine roots of goodness equal to space;
they give rise to all manner of wondrous sounds.
Throughout all worlds, they constantly turn the wheel of Dharma, never missing the proper time.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth space-like patience of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
“If a bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes this patience, they attain a body that does not come, because it has no going;
they attain a body that is not born, because it is not subject to extinction;
they attain a body that is not accumulated, because it is without disintegration.”
They are endowed with an unreal body because it lacks true reality;
they attain a body of one mark because it is markless;
they attain an infinite body because the power of the Buddha is infinite.
They attain an impartial body because of the characteristic of suchness;
they attain an indestructible body because they contemplate the three periods of time with equanimity;
they attain a body that reaches all places because their pure eyes universally illumine without obstruction.
They attain the body of the limit of detachment from desire, because all phenomena are without conjunction or dispersion;
they attain the treasury of merit of the limit of space, because it is inexhaustible;
they attain the eloquence of the equal Dharma that is without end, because the nature of all phenomena is of a single character, like space.
They attain immeasurable, unimpeded, and subtle sounds, because they are unobstructed like space;
they attain the pure and complete skillful means of all bodhisattva practices, because all dharmas are unobstructed and pure like space;
they attain the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas, because they are indestructible like space.
They attain the upholding of all Buddha-fields, because they are as immeasurable as space and free from desire;
they attain sovereign mastery in manifesting all dharmas without ever ceasing, because they are as firm and stable as space;
they attain the indestructible and solid Dharma-body, because, like space, they can sustain all worlds.
They are fully endowed with indestructible vajra faculties, because they manifest the formation and destruction of all worlds;
they have attained perfect power, able to sustain all worlds, because they uphold wisdom that is like space.
“O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of patience of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, wishing to restate this meaning for the sake of all Bodhisattvas, spoke in verse:
"Just as there may be people in the world who, hearing of the location of a treasure trove,
experience great joy upon hearing it because that treasure can be obtained;
so too is this great wisdom for the Bodhisattva, the true son of the Buddha."
Having heard the Buddha’s profound and quiescent Dharma, they experience great joy.
Having heard that profound Dharma, their minds feel no terror;
they give rise to neither alarm nor fear, and they neither regress nor sink.
The Bodhisattva, turning toward enlightenment, hears this sound of tranquil extinction;
being able to endure the dharma of tranquility, he conceives no doubt therein.
"I shall become the All-Knowing One, the Honored Teacher of gods and humans."
Because they have heard the profound Dharma, their minds are capable of endurance.
Hearing the sound of quiescence, they leap for joy with great delight;
with single-minded devotion, they joyfully seek all the qualities of the Buddhas.
Cultivating the taming of the mind, seeking enlightenment with uprightness,
nurturing all roots of goodness, and not destroying the nature of phenomena;
being patient with the dharma of quiescence and conforming to those sounds.
Cultivating the bodhisattva practices, Abiding securely in the patience of sounds,
Seeking further the supreme and wondrous path, Giving rise to all wholesome dharmas,
With diligence that never regresses, One ultimately accomplishes *bodhi*.
Hearing this wondrous sound, the bodhicitta becomes pure;
one attains courageous and wholesome roots, causing all Buddhas to rejoice.
It is like a person of merit who discovers a great treasury of precious jewels.
Just as one fashions various ornaments according to what is suitable for the body,
so too is it with the wise: having heard the meaning of this profound Dharma,
they expand the ocean of their wisdom and seek all dharmas in accordance with it.
Resolutely conforming to the Dharma, one discerns that nothing exists;
conforming to suchness, one attains that true reality.
Having attained a pure and sovereign mind, one is brilliantly clear and filled with great joy.
Having understood that all phenomena arise entirely from a multitude of conditions,
one cultivates the dharma of equality; by discerning both existence and non-existence,
one does not destroy the treasury of the Buddha-dharma and perfectly awakens to all dharmas.
With an upright mind firm and steadfast, they adorn pure bodhi;
as immovable as Mount Sumeru, they seek the Buddha-way single-mindedly.
They cultivate profound samādhi, practicing with diligence and without indolence.
Having practiced for immeasurable eons, you have never experienced any decline or loss.
Like the most supreme and profound ocean, you have reached its ultimate further shore;
having exhausted the very source and bottom of all phenomena, you are far removed from all terrors.
Contemplating all phenomena with an impartial mind, as taught by the Peerless One,
one achieves the patience of compliance and fulfills the wisdom of equality.
Endowed with the gateway of compliant patience, one accords with what the Buddha has taught.
In accordance with true wisdom, one does not discriminate among the characteristics of phenomena. Among the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
those various sons of gods eat from a single precious vessel, yet what they consume differs for each.
The various foods of the devas do not come from the ten directions;
according to the karma they have cultivated, food appears naturally in their vessels.
So too it is with the Bodhisattva: observing all phenomena, [they perceive them as such].
All arise from causes and conditions; they neither arise nor cease.
If a phenomenon neither arises nor ceases, that phenomenon is inexhaustible.
Thoroughly understanding its formation and dissolution, it is pure and indestructible.
The ultimate reality is indestructible; all things are quiescent and suchness.
Through diamond-like vows, may there be benefit, endowed with the Buddha’s unimpeded wisdom.
Constantly mindful of the dharma of quiescence, their minds never depart from it.
Acting in accordance with the ways of the world, He nurtures the vow of great compassion.
Endowed with the power of all vows, Yet remaining unattached to the world,
He achieves profound wisdom And preaches the Dharma extensively in accordance with [the needs of beings].
This is called the patience of non-arising; understanding that all phenomena are inexhaustible, one realizes that they are entirely suchness, and that within the dharma-realm nothing arises.
When a bodhisattva abides in this patience, throughout all the worlds of the ten directions,
The immeasurable Buddhas of the present have all bestowed upon him this prediction:
He delights in contemplating the dharma of quiescence, and gives rise to all roots of goodness.
In a single thought-moment, he penetrates the three periods of time, taming and purifying sentient beings.
Observing all worlds, one understands them to be entirely like illusions;
being quiescent and devoid of existence, one has no attachment to them.
All forms are created from the mind, appearing just like magical illusions.
Space is not real; all things are like an illusion.
Just as a skilled magician manifests various forms at a crossroads, causing sentient beings to see them with joy, yet in reality nothing exists there.
The world is likewise thus: all things are like illusions.
Having realized that all phenomena, whether existent or non-existent, are entirely false and deceptive, one liberates all sentient beings, understanding them all to be like illusions.
They are well able to know with equanimity that sentient beings and illusions are no different.
Sentient beings and all Buddha-fields, all phenomena of the three times,
and the infinite worlds— all are understood to be in meaning like illusions.
Just as a skilled illusionist manifests various forms—
men, women, elephants, horses, oxen, gardens, flowers, fruits, and the like—
the illusion itself is free from attachment and has no place of abiding.
Illusory phenomena lack true reality; all that appears is entirely false.
So it is with the sons of the Buddha: when they observe all worlds and all phenomena—whether existent or non-existent—they realize them all to be like illusions.
Sentient beings and all Buddha-fields are created by various karmas;
awakening to their illusory nature, one has no attachment to them.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva always delights in the dharma of tranquility.
Deeply entering the ground of reality, Ultimately abiding in the dharma-realm,
Following and inclining toward the true Dharma, Born through transformation from the most supreme Dharma,
Skillfully understanding all perceptions, [He perceives] the nets that entangle the multitudes of sentient beings.
Perception is like a mirage in the heat, causing sentient beings to fall into error;
the Bodhisattva, skillfully understanding perception, is able to leave behind all such errors.
The worlds are each distinct, and their forms and types are entirely different.
The Son of the Buddha is skillfully clear and penetrating, understanding that appearances are not true reality.
All sentient beings throughout the ten directions are entirely shrouded by the net of conceptualization;
the Bodhisattva’s eye of wisdom is pure, clearly seeing the conceptualizations of the world.
The world is like a mirage; through false conceptualization, one grasps at the world.
If one can sever the perception of the world, one is then free from the three types of inversion.
Just as when it is hot, a mirage appears, and sentient beings see it from afar.
Deluded thoughts are taken to be water, yet in reality they are not true water.
Sentient beings are likewise; they falsely grasp at the world, their perceptions like a mirage in the heat, which is the unimpeded realm of the mind.
Discerning all perceptions, one accomplishes unimpeded wisdom;
while perceptions bind the multitudes of sentient beings, the courageous and steadfast are able to liberate themselves.
Far removed from negligence and pride, they eliminate worldly perceptions.
Ultimate exhaustion and non-exhaustion: non-exhaustion is skillful means.
He is able to understand that all phenomena in the world are like a dream;
the nature of a dream has no location, and the world is likewise so.
Understanding the Dharma frees one from delusion; in the state of cessation, the mind is without distinction.
Clearly comprehending the activities of the world, one sees that all three times are like a dream.
A dream is not the dharma of birth and death; it is neither existent nor non-existent.
The three realms of existence are all like a dream; in the mind of quiescent extinction, there is no bondage.
Understanding that the nature of the world is like a dream, one does not rely upon the world;
observing the world’s quiescent extinction, one is not defiled by or attached to the various destinies.
Clearly seeing all worlds, they do not give rise to false inversions;
skillfully understanding that phenomena are like dreams, they attain the patience of the dream-like.
Sentient beings see within their dreams various and diverse appearances.
Knowing fully that all is created from the mind, yet in reality nothing exists at all;
the Moon of Wisdom sees thus: all sentient beings are like a dream.
Having clearly understood them to be like a dream, one leaves behind all delusions.
Through the Bodhisattva’s skillful means of understanding, all phenomena are like dreams;
the nature of a dream lacks reality, being neither identical nor different.
So too are all phenomena of sentient beings and all karmic activities within the Buddha-fields.
The Bodhisattva fully understands that all things are like dreams.
According to all defilements and purities, they are able to know them as they truly are;
realizing that the world is like a dream, they do not grasp at false appearances.
The practices performed by Bodhisattvas and all their sublime vows—
understanding them clearly as being like dreams, they have no attachment to them.
They have attained definitive understanding of all phenomena as well as the entire world.
The Bodhisattva is able to know well that their nature is entirely like a dream.

Regarding the phenomena of arising and ceasing in the world, and the characteristics of the coming and going of sentient beings, they understand them to be pure like a dream; their nature is never forgotten or lost.
Acting in accordance with the dream-like state, yet not destroying the world;
thoroughly understanding all modes of conduct as being without reality, like length or shortness—
this is called the patience of the dream-like, through which one understands all phenomena.
Having accomplished unimpeded wisdom, they deliver all beings.
These Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, practicing immeasurable deeds extensively,
give rise to all the equal dharmas of perfect enlightenment.
Through various skillful means, they understand the true nature of phenomena;
all phenomena have neither coming nor going, and thus their minds are unattached to them.
Toward all classes of sentient beings and their immeasurable voices, [they remain equanimous].
The Bodhisattva awakens deeply, Realizing all things are like echoes.
The Bodhisattva knows that sounds Are neither internal nor external phenomena;
Thoroughly understanding all sounds, He sees they are all like echoes.
All sounds and voices are entirely illusory;
the Bodhisattva, knowing them to be unreal, has no attachment to them.
The Bodhisattva beholds all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Furthermore, one hears that Tathāgata preaching the Dharma with a Brahma-voice.
Those great guides extensively expound the sūtras;
hearing the sound of the Dharma, the bodhisattvas' minds remain unattached.
The sounds one hears are like echoes, coming from nowhere at all;
discerning all voices, they skillfully understand the indestructible nature of phenomena.
Discerning all sounds and voices, they skillfully understand all dharmas.
Understanding that sound is not sound, they emit immeasurable pure tones.
Observing all phenomena, they find them all entirely devoid of sound;
they are fully able to thoroughly comprehend the limits of all various forms of speech.
The Bodhisattva, regarding all sentient beings, understands them all to be like echoes;
thus able to penetrate deeply, [he perceives] all living beings.
The Bodhisattva skillfully accords with them, clearly mastering the paths of language.
They comprehend all worlds and their various sounds;
understanding the nature of sound, they always delight in the state of tranquility.
Clearly understanding all worlds, they know that everything is like an echo.
Just as the path of speech proclaims and clarifies various phenomena,
yet sentient beings delight in and become attached to these false sounds;
just as those sounds have such characteristics, so too is the world.
The mark of sentient beings is likewise so; the true sons of the Buddha possess clear awakening.
Such is the mark of reality: the power of patience of the wise brings their voice to pure and subtle refinement, understanding that all worlds are utterly quiescent.
Throughout the three periods of time, they thoroughly understand the path of speech;
they do not grasp at false sounds, for their minds are free from attachment.
With a tranquil and concentrated mind for the sake of the world, they single-mindedly and exclusively seek the Bodhi of the Buddha.
Never falsely grasping at the world, his mind always delights in the dharma of quiescence.
Observing that the world has nothing remaining— that it is entirely quiescent and devoid of intrinsic nature—
he single-mindedly seeks enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, fully endowed with the power of wisdom and great compassion.
Not receiving birth within any world, yet not being liberated from the world;
with nothing upon which to rely in any world, yet likewise not departing from reliance upon the world.
Understanding the nature of all phenomena in sentient beings, They do not cling to that very nature;
Having no dependence upon any sentient beings, They are pure, liberated, and unbound.

Knowing the true nature of all realms of existence, and the phenomena of the world’s cycle of birth and death, the Bodhisattva understands that these dharmas are non-dual; thus, they have no attachment to this non-duality.
Their minds do not abide within the various worlds, nor do they depart from the worlds;
their practice does not lie outside the world, for they thoroughly understand the true nature of all phenomena.
Just as the color of lightning in water, that color is neither internal nor external;
so too, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, the Bodhisattva proclaims that the world has no reality.
Sentient beings are neither bound nor liberated; the entire world is ineffable.
The world is neither internal nor external, like the reflection of lightning in water.
With such a pure and stainless mind, following profound and subtle practices,
possessing the light of the lamp of wisdom and the Dharma, they fulfill all vows without ever regressing.
The accomplishment of their wisdom is immeasurable; they are always able to benefit all beings, establishing them in the Dharma of fearlessness and eliminating all obstacles.
Cultivating the profound Dharma, they benefit all sentient beings;
this patience increases wondrous wisdom and fulfills the bodhisattva practices.
Deeply entering the dharma of quiescence, they clearly realize that all things are like illusions.
Manifesting immeasurable practices, yet in reality there is nothing practiced.
Cultivating bodhi on the supreme stages, one acts in accordance with that which is like an illusion;
as that which is like an illusion is eternally quiescent, so too is the practice of the Bodhisattva.
Fully understanding the classes of sentient beings and their immeasurable karmic actions, one sees them all as equal to illusions; liberation is likewise so.
Clearly comprehending the Buddhas of the three periods of time, one knows that they all are like illusions.
Through immeasurable original practices and vows, he manifests as all the Teachers.
Great compassion is all-pervasive; he transforms sentient beings into purity.
Purity itself is transformation; the power of transformation sustains his responsive manifestations.
The world is entirely illusory; the Bodhisattva understands it to be like a magical transformation.
The nature of all worlds is that of a transformation, adorned by various karmas.
Adorned with the treasury of transformations, they bring the Bodhisattva practices to ultimate completion.
Following the various karmic activities of the world, which are diverse and immeasurable, these transformations are illusory dharmas; from them arise illusory transformations.
Yet the dharmas practiced by Bodhisattvas are entirely free from illusion.
The ocean of transformative wisdom is definitive; the seal of transformation stamps the world.
Transformation is not a phenomenon of arising and ceasing, and wisdom is likewise so.
The tenth patience is clear observation, pure as space.
Space, sentient beings, and phenomena— Contemplating them equally, they are without distinction.
Wisdom is perfected like space, Eliminating all obstacles;
The nature of space is unmixed, And the world is likewise so.
Having accomplished the power of the patience of emptiness, it is like space, inexhaustible;
its sphere is like empty space, and it does not grasp at false appearances.
Space has no intrinsic nature, and space cannot be severed.
Space has no variety, and the power of wisdom is likewise so.
Just as the nature of space has no beginning, middle, or end,
and space has no distinct natures, so too is wisdom.
Thus correctly contemplating all phenomena, seeing them all as being like space—
without arising and without ceasing— one contemplates all phenomena with equanimity.
Abiding in the dharma of space, one extensively explains it throughout the ten directions.
The patience of skillful means regarding space subdues all māras.
Space has no intrinsic nature, and the world is likewise so;
phenomena with intrinsic nature and those without are equal like space.
First, the adornment of skillful means: observing the world as empty, they fully know that the phenomena of the three periods of time are like the nature of space.
The bodhisattva’s body of wisdom has a voice like space.
The nature of the body is also empty space; abiding in the wisdom of empty space, these are called the ten kinds of patience, which the sons of the Buddha fulfill in their practice.
With minds abiding in the power of patience, they extensively expound them throughout the ten directions.
True children of the Buddha learn well, transcending to achieve the power of wisdom.
Through the power of the Dharma and the power of concentration, they cultivate bodhi in accordance with reality;
deeply entering this gate of patience, they accomplish unimpeded knowledge.
Subduing all evils, he turns the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
Abiding securely in immeasurable dharmas, none are able to know him;
the Ocean of Wisdom of the Tamer of Men, the Bodhisattvas exhaust its very source and bottom.
Practicing the bodhi-path with humility, one attains this profound dharma-patience;
with a pure mind regarding the wondrous Dharma, all vows are completely fulfilled.
For all classes of sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, [this is accomplished].
One may calculate their number, yet the virtues of a Bodhisattva are difficult to know.
If there is a true son of the Buddha who accomplishes these ten kinds of patience,
no sentient being whatsoever can fathom their realm.

Chapter Twenty-Five: The Questions of Bodhisattva Cittarāja Regarding the Asaṃkhyeya.
At that time, Bodhisattva Cittarāja addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
That is to say:

asaṃkhyeya (incalculable), aprameya (immeasurable), aparicchinna (without limits), anavasthita (without pervasiveness), asaṃkhyeya (innumerable), atulya (incomparable), acintya (inconceivable), anabhilāpya (ineffable), and anabhilāpyānabhilāpya (ineffably ineffable).
“World-Honored One!
What is meant by ‘incalculable’ (*asaṃkhyeya*) up to ‘unspeakably unspeakable’?
The Buddha addressed Cittarāja Bodhisattva, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent! O son of good family!”

It is for the sake of benefiting sentient beings that you are able to inquire about this profound meaning of the realm of the Buddha’s wisdom, which belongs to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
O son of good family!
"Listen attentively now, and I shall explain it to you.
At that time, Bodhisattva Mind-King addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"Listen attentively.
The Buddha addressed Mind-King Bodhisattva, saying:
"A hundred times a hundred thousand is one *kuli*."
One *kuli* is called one "unchanging" (*avikāra*);
one "unchanging" is called one *nayuta*; one *nayuta* is called one *vibhava*.
Vipula-vipula is named "One Action";
action-action is named "Once-returner";
coming-coming is named "One Victory."
Ten *śreṣṭha-śreṣṭha* are called one *punar-punar*;
ten *punar-punar* are called one *apara*;
ten *apara-apara* are called one *vijaya*.
"Victory over victory" is called one "boundary";
"boundary after boundary" is called one "pervasion";
"pervasion after pervasion" is called one "measure."
Each measure is called one understanding;
each understanding is called this single understanding;
this understanding and that understanding are called one detachment from desire.
Detachment from desire and detachment from desire are called one relinquishment;
relinquishment and relinquishment are called one collection;
collection and collection are called one penetration.
All these together are called one *bimbiṣa*;
ten *bimbiṣas* are called one *jāla*;
ten *jālas* are called one *saṃtati*.
The various streams are all called "streams";
their emergence is called "emergence"; each part is called "a single portion"; and these portions are called "discrimination."
Discrimination and further discrimination are called one "designation" (chēng);
each designation is called one "retention" (chí);
each retention is called one "non-perversion" (bùdiānpǎo).
Non-inversion and non-inversion are called one non-fluttering;
non-fluttering and non-fluttering are called one correctness;
correctness and correctness are called one wisdom.
Wisdom and wisdom are named the one foremost;
the foremost and foremost are named the one awakening;
awakening and awakening are named the one supreme height.
One *parama-parama* is called one *sūkṣma*;
one *sūkṣma-sūkṣma* is called one *lava*;
one *lava-lava* is called one *hariva*.
One *hāri-vahāri* is called one liberation (*vimukti*);
one liberation is called one yellow (*pīta*);
one yellow is called one *hārinā*.
One *hāriṇa* is called one *hāriṇa*; one *hāriṇa-hāriṇa* is called one *bhadra-udaya*;
one *bhadra-udaya-bhadra-udaya* is called one *vibhūti-nimitta*.
One *ābhāsvara* is called one *māludha*;
one *māludha* is called one *kṣānti*;
one *kṣānti* is called one *śākhā*.
Each branch is called one *māluma*;
each *māluma* is equal to one *māluma*;
and each such equality is called one *vigatasaṃśaya*.
Freedom from doubt and freedom from doubt are called one kind;
various [forms] are called one heedfulness;
heedfulness and heedfulness are called one *mātrā*.
*Mata-ra mata-ra* means "one movement";
*dong-dong* means "one arrival";
*dao-dao* means "one teaching."
To speak of speaking is one "white";
white-white is one "discernment";
discernment-discernment is one "consummation."
Ultimate ultimate is called one *śītalā*;
*śītalā* *śītalā* is called one *ara*;
*ara* *ara* is called one *tara*.
One *cau* is called one *yu*;
one *yu* is called one *jiluo*;
one *jiluo* is called one *wei*.
One *rasa-rasa* is called one *ni-lo*;
one *ni-lo-ni-lo* is called one *khi*;
one *khi-khi* is called one *sra*.
One *sras-sro* is called a cluster of foam;
one cluster of foam is called a *mi-ra*;
one *mi-ra* is called a solid mass.
One *dhṛti-dhṛti* is called one *vāyu*;
one *vāyu-vāyu* is called one *pūrṇa*;
one *pūrṇa-pūrṇa* is called one *atulya*.
That which is immeasurable and immeasurable is called one root;
each root is called one subtle atom;
each subtle atom is called one lotus.
One padma is called a mahāpadma; one mahāpadma is called an asaṃkhyeya;
one asaṃkhyeya is called a hetu.
One *he-lou-he-lou* is called a single word;
one word is called a single *kalpa*;
one *kalpa* is called a single *baba*.
Baba-baba is named One Interval (eka-antara);
interval upon interval is named One Without Interval (anantara);
without interval upon without interval is named One Free from Defilement (vimala).
One *vimala* (stainless) is called one *vimalottara* (superior stainless);
one *vimalottara* is called one *mīlāvaraṇa*; one *mīlāvaraṇa* is called one *cāmara*.
Camaracāmara is the name for one dharma;
dharmadharma is the name for one paramārtha;
paramārthaparamārtha is the name for one certainty.
Certainty upon certainty is called a single "evolution";
evolution upon evolution is called a single "extensive exposition";
extensive exposition upon extensive exposition is called a single "inexhaustibility."
Inexhaustible and inexhaustible is called the one True Reality;
the one True Reality and the one True Reality is called the one Non-self;
the one Non-self and the one Non-self is called the one Aparānta.
Ananta, an Ananta is called one blue lotus;
a blue lotus, a blue lotus is called one counting;
a counting, a counting is called one direction.
One *gati-gati* is called one *vedanā*;
one *vedanā-vedanā* is called one *asaṃkhyeya*;
one *asaṃkhyeya-asaṃkhyeya* is called one *asaṃkhyeya-parivarta*.
An asaṃkhyeya multiplied by an asaṃkhyeya is called one immeasurable (apramāṇa);
an immeasurable multiplied by an immeasurable is called one immeasurable-multiplied (apramāṇāvarta);
an immeasurable-multiplied multiplied by an immeasurable-multiplied is called one limitlessness (anavasthāna).
Non-limit and non-limit is called "one turning of non-limit";
the turning of non-limit and the turning of non-limit is called "one universal pervasion";
non-pervasion and non-pervasion is called "one turning of universal pervasion."
One *asaṃkhyeya* is the name for a non-universal revolution (*aparivartana*) and a universal revolution (*parivartana*);
one *asaṃkhyeyaparivarta* is the name for a non-numbered [revolution] and a numbered [revolution];
one *anabhilāpya* is the name for a non-numbered revolution and a numbered revolution.
One "incalculable" (asaṃkhyeya) is called one "incalculable-turn" (asaṃkhyeyāvarta);
one "incalculable-turn" is called one "inconceivable" (acintya);
one "inconceivable" is called one "inconceivable-turn" (acintyāvarta).
An inconceivable revolution of an inconceivable revolution is called one immeasurable;
an immeasurable of an immeasurable is called one immeasurable revolution;
an immeasurable revolution of an immeasurable revolution is called one ineffable.
"An unspeakable number of unspeakables is called one 'unspeakable turn' (avaktavya-parivarta);
an unspeakable number of 'unspeakable turns' is called one 'unspeakable turn-turn' (avaktavya-parivarta-parivarta).
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse for the sake of the Bodhisattva Mind-King:
"Ineffable and beyond description, filling all that is ineffable,
throughout ineffable eons, one could not exhaustively describe what is ineffable."
All the unspeakable Buddha-fields, having been entirely ground down into atoms,
within each and every atom, they expound all that is unspeakable.
They are all able, within a single thought-moment, to expound unspeakable worlds throughout unspeakably many eons, explaining them in successive order, moment by moment.
Eons that cannot be described may yet come to an end, But that which cannot be described can never be exhausted;
Within every single atom, They analyze and expound that which is ineffable.
Eons beyond expression may yet come to an end, But that which is beyond expression can never be exhausted;
Within every single atom that cannot be described, There dwell sentient beings beyond all expression.
If all together were to praise the virtues of Samantabhadra, they could not exhaust them;
even if within the space of a single hair-tip there were unspeakably many Samantabhadras.
All those, such as Samantabhadra and the rest, could not exhaustively describe what is unspeakable;
just as it is in the space of a single minute hair-tip, so it is throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Upon each and every tip of a hair, one may place unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
though a hair-tip might exhaust the measurement of empty space, the Buddha-fields can never be exhausted.
Within each and every pore-path, there are various and immeasurable Buddha-fields;
those of similar type are unspeakably many, and those of different types are likewise unspeakably many.
Within each and every pore-path, there are unspeakably many pure Buddha-fields.
With unspeakably many ornaments, they adorn each and every Buddha-field;
from within each and every pore-path, they produce unspeakable sets of names,
and from each and every such set of names, they extensively proclaim the names of immeasurable Buddhas.
Within the body of each and every Tathāgata, there are unspeakably many transformed pores;
from within each and every pore, there arise unspeakably many diverse colors;
from within each and every diverse color, there radiate unspeakably many sublime rays of light.
Within each and every one of those rays of light, there emerge unspeakably many precious lotuses;
within each and every one of those precious lotuses, there are unspeakably many precious petals;
within each and every one of those precious lotus petals, there are unspeakably many subtle and wondrous colors.
Within each and every one of those exquisite forms, there arise unspeakably many lotuses;
within each and every one of those lotuses, there radiate unspeakably many rays of light;
within each and every one of those rays of light, there arise unspeakably many pure moons.
Within each and every one of those moons, there further emerge unspeakably many pure moons;
within each and every one of those pure moons, there emerge unspeakably many pure radiances;
within each and every one of those radiances, there emerge unspeakably many pure and bright suns.
Within each and every one of those days, there emerge unspeakable numbers of pure and wondrous colors;
within each and every one of those wondrous colors, there emerge unspeakable numbers of pure radiances;
and within each and every one of those pure radiances, there emerge unspeakable numbers of lion thrones.
Inexpressible ornaments of adornment emit inexpressible pure rays of light;
from within each and every ray of light, there emerge inexpressible varieties of wondrous colors;
from within each and every wondrous color, there emerge inexpressible, luminously pure jewels.
From each and every one of those luminous, pure jewels, there emerge unspeakably unspeakable numbers of vajra-treasure repositories like Mount Sumeru, pure, complete, and magnificently adorned.
Within that single Jewel Sumeru, there are unspeakably unspeakable numbers of subtle,
exquisite, and extraordinary Buddha-fields, pure, complete, and magnificently adorned.
Just as this single jewel Sumeru mountain, so too are all Sumeru mountains;
each possesses immeasurable and ineffable pure Buddha-fields in their entirety.
Inexpressible and beyond expression, all their distinctions are likewise inexpressible;
they encompass that which cannot be spoken of and manifest inexpressible radiance.
Within each and every ray of light, there arise inexpressible Buddhas.
All those Tathāgatas and the like Proclaim unspeakable verses of purity;
In every single thought-moment, those verses Proclaim unspeakable truths of reality.
They manifest throughout all future limits The inexhaustible wisdom of the Tathāgatas.
Each and every one of those Tathāgatas emits ineffable Brahma-sounds;
within each and every Brahma-sound, they turn the ineffable wheel of the pure Dharma;
within each and every wheel of the Dharma, they rain down ineffable sūtras.
Within each and every sūtra, the differentiation of all phenomena is ineffable;
within each and every phenomenon therein, the further explanation of all phenomena is ineffable;
and furthermore, within those very phenomena, the explanation of sentient beings' reliance upon them is ineffable.
Furthermore, within each and every pore-path, one may preach the True Dharma for unspeakable eons;
as it is in that single point of a fine hair-tip, so it is throughout all the ten directions.
The unimpeded mind is ineffable; the transformations of all Buddhas are ineffable.
Each and every transformed Tathāgata produces transformations that are ineffable;
all those who are thus transformed travel throughout Buddha-fields that are ineffable.
Inconceivable transformation bodies, adorned with various wondrous colors;
in those ineffable Buddha-worlds, they distinguish all sentient beings,
purify all classes of living beings, and deliver all multitudes of creatures.
The adornments of adornment are unspeakable; The accomplishment of spiritual powers is unspeakable;
Pure mastery is unspeakable; Manifesting in response to sentient beings is unspeakable;
Mastery over spiritual powers is unspeakable; The realm of wisdom is unspeakable.
Sustained by ineffable supernormal powers, they universally transform the world to make it pure.
With ineffable methods of purification, they expound unspeakable sūtras;
within each and every one of those sūtras, they encompass unspeakably many teachings of the Buddha-dharma.
Within each and every pure dharma, he further speaks of the unspeakable True Dharma;
within each and every such dharma, he speaks of the unspeakable definitive dharma;
within each and every such certainty, he speaks of the unspeakable refuge for sentient beings.
Inconceivable varieties of phenomena, inconceivable varieties of mind;
Inconceivable non-analogous phenomena, inconceivable non-analogous mind,
Inconceivable non-analogous faculties, inconceivable non-analogous speech.
In every thought-moment, they are able to tame unspeakably many sentient beings.
With unspeakably immeasurable powers of mastery, they manifest before unspeakably many sentient beings.
At those unspeakable times of responding through transformation, there may be those who are of the same kind or of different kinds.
The Bodhisattvas know and distinguish them all, such that no master of calculation can count them.
Within the space of a single hair-tip, the Bodhisattvas place unspeakably many Buddha-fields—some minute, some vast or narrow;
pure or defiled, they are immeasurable and beyond description.
Within each and every one of those buddha-fields, there are further unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields;
the bodhisattvas know them all through their discernment—such are the unspeakable buddha-fields.
Within the tip of a single hair there are immeasurable lands, yet they are not crowded therein;
nor does the minute tip of the hair become large, for it accommodates all vast Buddha-fields without causing them to become confused,
their forms and characteristics remaining as they were, without change.
Within a single buddha-field are immeasurable fields, and all buddha-fields are likewise so.
All are accommodated within the tip of a single hair, as are immeasurable fields equal to space.
The forms and characteristics of these buddha-fields are ineffable; within the tip of a single hair, each is distinct and different.
Entering into the space of a single hair-pore, they enter all in succession in ways that are ineffable;
the hair-pores encompass what is ineffable, yet even those hair-pores are never ultimately filled.
The sequential entry into eons is unspeakable; Constantly being able to gather in beings is unspeakable;
The various skillful means are unspeakable; The liberation of sentient beings is unspeakable.
Fully possessing these skillful means of gathering is unspeakable; The immeasurable realms are unspeakable.
The Bodhisattva’s profound penetration is ineffable; this is called “profound penetration that is ineffable.
The root of his intention is deep and vast, ineffable; he wanders everywhere through all directions, ineffable;
his courageous diligence is ineffable; he is fully endowed with sovereign mastery, ineffable.
Those great vows are unspeakable; The merit thereby attained is unspeakable;
Those various realms are unspeakable; The ability to ultimately deliver others is unspeakable.
The physical actions of the Bodhisattva are ineffable; The purity of their verbal actions is ineffable;
The purity of their mental actions is ineffable; Their pure liberation is ineffable;
Their pure wisdom is ineffable; Their subtle and marvelous excellence is ineffable.
Skillful means for profound entry are unspeakable; The eradication of doubt and confusion is unspeakable;
Valiant diligence is unspeakable; Profound entry into the True Dharma is unspeakable;
The most profound samādhi is unspeakable; Reaching the ultimate other shore is unspeakable.
All sentient beings are ineffable; all Buddha-fields are ineffable.
The bodies of all sentient beings are ineffable; the aspirations of sentient beings are ineffable.
Their various karmic retributions are ineffable; knowing the desires of sentient beings is ineffable.
The nature of sentient beings is ineffable; the differentiation of sentient beings is ineffable;
the time for their manifestation through transformation is ineffable; the places from which they emerge are ineffable;
the paths of skillful means are ineffable; and those who emerge are ineffable.
Unsurpassed wisdom is ineffable; The path of skillful means is ineffable;
All that is taught is ineffable; And all its manifestations are ineffable.
Thus accomplishing great compassion, He benefits all worlds.
The manifestation of physical forms is unspeakable; Wandering through all Buddha-fields is unspeakable.
The wisdom of Bodhisattvas is exceedingly bright and pure; Beholding the Buddhas of the ten directions is unspeakable.
The sublime Dharma they inquire about is unspeakable; The responsive answers of the Buddhas are unspeakable.
The manifestation of physical forms is unspeakable; Wandering through all directions is unspeakable;
Approaching the presence of the Buddhas is unspeakable; The display of sovereign mastery is unspeakable.
With unspeakable forms and appearances, they go to the abodes of unspeakable Tathāgatas;
with unspeakable articles of offering, they make offerings to unspeakable Tathāgatas—
unspeakably pure jewels and unspeakably many precious flowers.
With unspeakably wondrous flower garlands, they make offerings to unspeakably many Most Victorious Ones.
Their profound faith is unspeakable; their pure liberation is unspeakable;
their upright aspiration is unspeakable, as they reverently make offerings to all Buddhas.
The accomplishment of the mind of giving is unspeakable; The past mind of giving is unspeakable;
The practice of generosity is unspeakable; Giving both internal and external things is unspeakable;
The purity of the precepts is unspeakable; The purity of faith is unspeakable.
Praising the supreme is unspeakable; Giving rise to love for the sublime Dharma is unspeakable;
Being fully endowed with all patiences is unspeakable; Profoundly understanding non-arising is unspeakable;
Accomplishing cessation is unspeakable; Abiding in the stage of cessation is unspeakable.
The perfection of diligence is unspeakable; The wondrous mind of the past is unspeakable;
The mind of non-retrogression is unspeakable; The mind of forbearance is unspeakable;
All treasuries of dhyāna are unspeakable; The contemplation of all dharmas is unspeakable.
The tranquil concentration of mind is ineffable; The thorough knowledge of all dhyānas is ineffable;
The wisdom of the pāramitās is ineffable; The accomplishment of samādhi is ineffable;
The definitive understanding of phenomena is ineffable; The ultimate realization of all Buddhas is ineffable.
The bodhisattva’s gateways of practice are unspeakable; The fulfillment of all vows is unspeakable;
The realm of wisdom is unspeakable; The gateways of the pure Dharma are unspeakable;
The power of those various dharmas is unspeakable; The dharma of pure dwelling is unspeakable.
The right mindfulness of the bodhisattva is ineffable; those dharma-realms are ineffable;
the cultivation of wisdom is ineffable; the skillful training in wisdom is ineffable;
that body of wisdom is ineffable; the sustaining power of wisdom is ineffable.
That pure wheel of Dharma is ineffable; That wisdom of the Dharma is ineffable;
Those clouds of the sublime Dharma are ineffable; That rain of the sublime Dharma is ineffable;
Those various supernormal powers are ineffable; The understanding of the methods of skillful means is ineffable.
In every moment of thought, they are able to comprehend the ineffable, profound Dharma-realm;
They achieve ineffable dedications of merit; In every moment of thought, they travel throughout ineffable oceans of Buddha-fields; The Buddhas whom they visit are also ineffable.
The differentiation of Buddha-fields is unspeakable; Their various adornments are unspeakable;
Their pure adornments are unspeakable; Their subtle and pure colors are unspeakable;
Their various mixed colors are unspeakable; Their manifold ornaments are unspeakable.
Pure buddha-fields are unspeakable; Defiled buddha-fields are unspeakable.
The profound entry into sentient beings is unspeakable; The various realms of sentient beings are unspeakable.
Their various karmic retributions are unspeakable; The conduct of sentient beings is unspeakable.
The various faculties are ineffable; The delusions of sentient beings are ineffable;
The natures of sentient beings are ineffable; The desires and inclinations of sentient beings are ineffable;

The purity of sentient beings is unspeakable; the taming of sentient beings is unspeakable.
The spiritual power of the Bodhisattva is unspeakable; the manifested bodies he creates are unspeakable.
His conformity to all practices is unspeakable; his deliverance of sentient beings is unspeakable.
The manifestation of sovereign mastery is ineffable; The emission of great radiance is ineffable;
The wondrous colors of that radiance are ineffable; The purification of sentient beings is ineffable.
Within each and every tip of his hair, he emits unspeakable nets of light;
the colors of these nets of light are unspeakable; they universally illuminate unspeakable Buddha-fields;
his courageous vigor is unspeakable; and his accomplishment of fearlessness is unspeakable.
The samādhi of tranquility is ineffable; The taming of the world is ineffable;
The purity of physical action is ineffable; The purity of verbal action is ineffable;
The immeasurability of mental action is ineffable; The supreme conduct of purity is ineffable.
The accomplishment of the jewel of wisdom is unspeakable; Deep entry into the dharma-realm is unspeakable;
All dhāraṇīs are unspeakable; The bodhisattva’s skillful learning is unspeakable;
The purity of their voice is unspeakable; Wisdom that knows sounds is unspeakable.
True and correct mindfulness is ineffable; The speech that sustains sentient beings is ineffable;
The conduct of Bodhisattvas is ineffable; The purity of perfect enlightenment is ineffable;

The true sons of the Buddha are beyond description; Their pure conduct is beyond description;

those Bodhisattvas are unspeakable, their pure merits are unspeakable,
their various distinctions are unspeakable, and the places where they dwell are unspeakable.
The abiding in wisdom is ineffable; it cannot be described even in ineffable eons.
The joy in beholding all Buddhas is ineffable; the nurturing of wisdom is ineffable.
The eternal crossing over by means of the True Dharma is ineffable; the unimpeded True Dharma is ineffable.
The correct contemplation of the three times is ineffable; The wisdom of the three times is ineffable;
That which is measured and weighed is ineffable; The arising of wisdom is ineffable;
The supreme practices of the bodhisattvas are ineffable; The various aspirations are ineffable.
The purity of their vows is unspeakable; The perfection of bodhi is unspeakable;
The bodhi of all Buddhas is unspeakable; The arising of their wisdom is unspeakable;
The discernment of reality is unspeakable; The knowledge of all phenomena is unspeakable.
The purification of Buddha-fields is unspeakable; The various powers practiced are unspeakable;
That which they have cultivated is unspeakable; Awakening in a single thought-moment is unspeakable;
The extensive exposition of the True Dharma is unspeakable; The sovereign mastery of all Buddhas is unspeakable.
Leaping for joy is ineffable; manifesting in the world is ineffable;
turning the sublime wheel of Dharma is ineffable; being free from all fears is ineffable;
the True Dharma taught is ineffable; delivering sentient beings is ineffable.
Though one were to spend unspeakable eons praising all the virtues of the Bodhisattva,
those great eons might come to an end, yet the praise of his virtues would never be exhausted.
The Tathāgatas, beyond all measure, each possess infinite pure faculties;
even if one were to praise them for unspeakable eons, the merits of the Tathāgatas would still not be exhausted.
All sentient beings throughout the ten directions, may they all simultaneously attain perfect enlightenment;
each of those perfectly enlightened ones possesses an ineffable number of pure and wondrous bodies,
and each of those pure and wondrous bodies possesses an ineffable number of Tathāgata heads.
Upon each of that Tathāgata’s heads, there are tongues, broad and long, beyond all description;
from each of those broad and long tongues, there issue forth immeasurable, pure, and wondrous sounds.
With each of those wondrous sounds, one might praise the Buddha for unspeakable eons.
Even if one were to proclaim and praise the Buddha’s virtues for unspeakably many eons,
those unspeakable eons might come to an end, yet the praise of the Buddha’s virtues would never be exhausted.
Within a single minute mote of dust, there are unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
within each of those Buddha-fields, there are likewise unspeakably many Bhadrasris.
Within the world-system of each Bhadrasri Tathagata, there are again unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
Throughout the entire realm of phenomena without exception, within every single atom therein,
the formation and destruction of Buddha-fields are unspeakable;
within every single atom therein, the arrangement of Buddha-fields is unspeakable.
Setting aside unspeakable oceans of lands, and unspeakable distinctions of their directions and types—
within each and every one of those buddha-fields, there are Tathāgatas beyond all measure;
the lifespans of those Tathāgatas span unspeakably many great kalpas.
The conduct of all Buddhas is ineffable; The subtle and sublime True Dharma is ineffable;
The power of their majestic spiritual authority is ineffable; Wisdom free from all obstacles is ineffable;
Subtle and sublime wisdom is ineffable; Their realm, profoundly deep, is ineffable.
The merit of the ten powers is unspeakable; The Buddha’s awakening to bodhi is unspeakable;
His pure and profound penetration is unspeakable; The pure realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is unspeakable;
That treasury of wisdom is unspeakable; The analysis of his merits is unspeakable.
The Bodhisattva perfectly and correctly accords with them, Fully accomplishing unspeakable dedications;
Discerning infinite varieties of dedication, He dedicates them to all the Teachers.
Throughout unspeakably many great kalpas, they remain single-mindedly absorbed in various samādhis;
in the presence of unspeakably many Buddhas, their conduct is unspeakably pure.
They attain an ineffable, unimpeded mind, Traveling everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
The practices they cultivate are ineffable, Their spiritual powers and manifestations are ineffable,
Their discernment of Buddha-fields is ineffable, And the Buddhas appearing before them are ineffable.
Their courageous diligence is ineffable, and their ultimate wisdom is ineffable;
without ever leaving their single seat, they are able to travel throughout the realms of the ten directions.
Throughout unspeakably many great kalpas, They travel everywhere through the Buddha-fields of the ten directions.
Their wisdom and skillful means are unspeakable; Their wisdom of reality as it is is unspeakable;
Their transformation of pure wisdom is unspeakable; In every thought-moment they manifest manifestations that are unspeakable.
Within each and every single expression, one understands the Buddha’s wisdom, which is ineffable.
Sometimes awakening to bodhi at a single moment, sometimes awakening to bodhi at various times;
entering into the tips of all body hairs is ineffable, and entering into all subtle things is ineffable.
The extraordinary and supreme nature is ineffable; seeing all Tathāgatas is ineffable;
each and every skillful means is ineffable—thus one accords with and enters the nature of all Buddhas.
The nature of all Buddha-fields is ineffable, yet one can enter awakening in accordance with them all;
the indestructible dharma-realm is ineffable, and the Buddhas, sentient beings, and fields are ineffable;
that which is encompassed by the three periods of time is ineffable, and the ultimate state of the Bodhisattvas is ineffable.

Chapter 26: On Life Span The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Chapter Twenty-Six: On Life Span. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mind-King addressed the Bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
One kalpa in the realm of Śākyamuni Buddha in this Sahā world is a single day and night in the realm of Amitābha Buddha in the Land of Peace and Bliss (Sukhāvatī);
one kalpa in the Land of Peace and Bliss is a single day and night in the realm of Vajra Buddha in the world of Noble Robe Banner;
one kalpa in the world of Noble Robe Banner is a single day and night in the realm of the Buddha Pure Blossoming Radiance of Good Joy in the world of Wheel of Non-retrogressive Sound.
One eon in the world-system Avivartyasvaracakrā is a single day and night in the Dharmanetrabuddhakṣetra of the world-system Vimalā;
one eon in the world-system Vimalā is a single day and night in the Siṃhabuddhakṣetra of the world-system Sudīpa;
one eon in the world-system Sudīpa is a single day and night in the Rocanagarbhabuddhakṣetra of the world-system Suvimalaprabhā.
One eon in the world-system *Sukhābhāsa* constitutes one day and night in the Buddha-field *Dharmaprabhāsaviśuddhipraphullapadma* of the world-system *Abhyudgata*;
one eon in the world-system *Abhyudgata* constitutes one day and night in the Buddha-field *Sarvaprabhāsasamantaprabha* of the world-system *Vyūhamati*;
and one eon in the world-system *Vyūhamati* constitutes one day and night in the Buddha-field *Buddhacandra* of the world-system *Ādarśaprabhā*.
O Son of the Buddha!

Following this sequence, even up to a hundred thousand *asaṃkhyeya* worlds, the one kalpa of the final world constitutes a single day and night in the Buddha-field of Bhadrāśva in the world-system of Varapadma; therein, great bodhisattvas such as Samantabhadra Bodhisattva fill the space.

Chapter 27: The Abodes of Bodhisattvas. From the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Chapter Twenty-Seven: The Abodes of Bodhisattvas. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mind-King (*Cittarāja*) again addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!"
To the east there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Mount Ṛṣigiri, where past bodhisattvas have constantly resided;
therein currently dwells a bodhisattva named Vajravara, who stays among a retinue of three hundred bodhisattvas, constantly preaching the Dharma for them.
To the south there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Mount Victorious Pavilion, where all the bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided;
therein currently dwells a bodhisattva named Dharmamati, who has a retinue of five hundred bodhisattvas and constantly expounds the Dharma for them.
To the west there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Mount Vajrajvāla, where the bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided;
therein currently dwells a bodhisattva named Abhayasimhacaryā, who has a retinue of three hundred bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
In the north there is a dwelling place of bodhisattvas called Mount Gandhamādana, where all the bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided;
there currently dwells a bodhisattva named Gandhahastin, who has a retinue of three thousand bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
In the northeast there is a dwelling place of bodhisattvas called Mount Qingliang, where all bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided;
therein currently resides a bodhisattva named Mañjuśrī, who has a retinue of ten thousand bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
In the southeast there is a dwelling place of bodhisattvas called Firm Branches, where the bodhisattvas of the past have always resided;
there currently dwells a bodhisattva named Celestial Crown, who has a retinue of one thousand bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
In the southwestern direction there is a dwelling place of bodhisattvas called Mount Jyotiṣprabha; in the past, various bodhisattvas constantly resided therein.
There currently dwells a bodhisattva named Bhadramukha, who has a retinue of three thousand bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
In the northwest direction, there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Fragrant Wind Mountain, where the bodhisattvas of the past have always resided;
therein currently dwells a bodhisattva named Fragrant Radiance, who has a retinue of five thousand bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
Within the four great oceans there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas named Citra, where bodhisattvas of the past have always resided;
therein currently dwells a bodhisattva named Dharmodgata, who has a retinue of twelve thousand bodhisattvas and constantly preaches the Dharma for them.
In the ocean there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas named the Cave of Merit Adornments, where bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided.
To the south of the city of Vaiśālī, there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas named Good Abiding, where bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided.
In the city of Pāṭaliputra there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called the Kāñcanapradīpa Monastery, where the bodhisattvas of the past constantly resided.
In the kingdom of Mathurā there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Guṇavardhana, where the bodhisattvas of the past constantly resided.
In the kingdom of Kucenayā, there is a bodhisattva dwelling place named Dharma Seat (Dharmāsana), where the bodhisattvas of the past constantly resided.
In the kingdom of Viśuddhapāra, there is a bodhisattva dwelling place named Mucilinda-guṇa, where the bodhisattvas of the past constantly resided.
Within the region of Vāyu-bhūmi, there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Created by the Dragon King Anāvaraṇa, where past bodhisattvas have constantly resided.
In the land of Kambu, there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas called Supreme Compassion, where past bodhisattvas have constantly resided.
In the land of Zhendan, there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas named Mount Nārāyaṇa, where bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided.
In the land of the frontier tribes, there is a dwelling place for bodhisattvas named Ox-Head Mountain, where bodhisattvas of the past have constantly resided.
In the land of Kaśmīra, there is a bodhisattva dwelling place called Mount Uḍaśī, where the bodhisattvas of the past constantly resided.
In the city of Nandivardhana, there is a bodhisattva dwelling place called Tilabhoga, where the bodhisattvas of the past constantly resided.
In the country of Āmrapālī, there is a bodhisattva dwelling place named Rectifying the Crooked; past bodhisattvas have always resided therein.
In the country of Gandhāra, there is a bodhisattva dwelling place named Cave of Tranquility; past bodhisattvas have always resided therein.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Twenty-nine;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty.

Chapter 28: The Inconceivable Dharma of the Buddhas At that time, within the great assembly of bodhisattvas, there were bodhisattvas who formed this thought:

"The buddha-fields of all buddhas are inconceivable; the pure vows of all buddhas are inconceivable; the lineages of all buddhas are inconceivable; the appearance in the world of all buddhas is inconceivable; the dharma-body of all buddhas is inconceivable; the voices of all buddhas are inconceivable; the wisdom of all buddhas is inconceivable; the sovereign spiritual powers of all buddhas are inconceivable; the unimpeded abiding of all buddhas is inconceivable; and the liberation of all buddhas is inconceivable."

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas, immediately bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus the Buddha’s spiritual power, the Buddha’s wisdom, the Buddha’s eloquence, the Buddha’s merit, and the Buddha’s fearlessness, filling his body with them.

He brought him to the ultimate realization of all Buddha-dharmadhātus and the unobstructed practice within the sphere of the Buddha’s spiritual power; he caused him to discern the lineage of all Tathāgatas and the inconceivable skillful means of countless Buddhas.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Blue Lotus immediately entered the profoundly deep and unimpeded Dharma-realm to cultivate the bodhisattva practice of all unimpeded dharmas. He fulfilled the vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and, in accordance with all Buddhas, adorned himself with the Great Adornments. With great compassion, he universally surveyed all sentient beings, desiring to bring them to purity;

in a single thought-moment, he gave birth to the Tathāgata’s immeasurable great wisdom, accomplished the inexhaustible gates of the Tathāgata’s knowledge, and achieved all *dhāraṇīs* and the radiance of all eloquence, which universally illumines everything.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, addressed the Bodhisattva Lotus Treasury, saying:

"O Son of the Buddha! All Buddhas possess immeasurable and innumerable pure and wondrous abodes; all Buddhas dwell in immeasurable sovereignty; all Buddhas never miss the proper time regarding any matter; all Buddhas equally turn the pure wheel of Dharma; the four analytical knowledges of all Buddhas are inexhaustible in their exposition; all Buddha-dharmas are inconceivable; the pure voices of all Buddhas reach everywhere; all Buddhas are able to discern the infinite dharma-realms; the radiance of all Buddhas shines universally; and all that is spoken by all Buddhas enters the profoundly deep dharma-realm."
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of dharma-realms that are immeasurable and boundless. What are these ten?
The form-bodies (*rūpakāya*) of all Buddhas are pure, immeasurable, and boundless, transcending the world;
the unimpeded eyes of all Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, purifying and equally awakening to all phenomena;
the unimpeded ears of all Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, discerning the voices of all sentient beings.
The olfactory faculties of all Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, ultimately pure; all Buddhas have attained mastery and reached the further shore.
The broad and long tongues of all Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, emitting wondrous sounds that universally reach throughout the Dharma-realm.
The physical actions of all Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, manifesting the body of a Tathāgata in accordance with the needs of sentient beings.
The mental karma of all Buddhas is immeasurable and boundless, unimpeded throughout the three periods of time, and their Dharma-body is pure and indestructible;
the dharma-gate of unhindered liberation of all Buddhas is immeasurable and boundless, manifesting inexhaustible sovereign spiritual powers;
and the adornment of Buddha-lands in all worlds by all Buddhas is immeasurable and boundless, acting in accordance with sentient beings.

All Buddhas are immeasurable and boundless; they have fully perfected all bodhisattva practices, supreme vows, and sovereign spiritual powers, and are able to awaken to the true Dharma of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of infinite and boundless dharma-realms of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
In every thought-moment, all Buddhas are able to bring forth ten kinds of inexhaustible wisdom. What are these ten?
In a single thought-moment, they manifest the passing away from the Tuṣita Heaven in all worlds;
In a single thought-moment, they manifest the birth of Bodhisattvas in all worlds;
in a single thought-moment, they manifest the renunciation of Bodhisattvas in all worlds;
and in a single thought-moment, they manifest their proceeding to the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree in all worlds to attain perfect awakening.
In a single thought-moment, they manifest throughout all worlds the turning of the pure wheel of Dharma;
in a single thought-moment, they manifest throughout all worlds, guiding and transforming all sentient beings according to their needs so that all are brought to liberation;
in a single thought-moment, they manifest adorned bodies throughout all worlds in accordance with the capacities of sentient beings.
Within a single thought-moment, they manifest all the various adornments of all worlds—countless adornments that are the sovereign treasury of omniscience of the Tathāgatas;
within a single thought-moment, they manifest all pure sentient beings in all worlds;
and within a single thought-moment, they pervade all worlds, manifesting all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

Within a single thought-moment, for the sake of the various faculties, diligences, aspirations, and dispositions, they manifest the lineage of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, and guide all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is how all Buddhas give rise to ten kinds of wisdom in a single thought-moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of never-failing timing.
What are these ten?
All Buddhas attain equal and perfect enlightenment at a time that is never lost;
The karmic retribution of the roots of goodness of all Buddhas never misses its appointed time;
the bestowal of predictions upon Bodhisattvas by all Buddhas never misses its appointed time;
and the manifestation of spiritual powers by all Buddhas in accordance with the needs of sentient beings never misses its appointed time.
All Buddhas manifest the body of a Tathāgata without ever missing the proper time;
all Buddhas practice equanimity without ever missing the proper time;
all Buddhas enter cities and villages without ever missing the proper time.
All Buddhas gather in and gladden sentient beings without ever missing the proper time;
all Buddhas relinquish those sentient beings who are difficult to transform for the sake of their eventual subduing, never missing the proper time;
all Buddhas manifest inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers without ever missing the proper time.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which all Buddhas never fail their appointed time.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of incomparable and inconceivable realms.
What are these ten? First, they sit cross-legged, pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions.
With a single utterance of sound, they are able to expound all Buddha-dharmas;
emitting a single ray of light, they are able to universally illumine all worlds;
with a single body, they are able to manifest all bodies.
Without departing from their original place, they manifest themselves throughout all worlds;
having attained certainty in a single dharma, they encounter no obstruction among all dharmas;
and within a single thought-moment, they are able to fill all world-systems without exception.
Within a single thought-moment, they are able to manifest all the merits of the Buddhas;
within a single thought-moment, they are able to manifest all the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
and while teaching and transforming all sentient beings, they do not abandon the Buddhas’ samādhi of quiescent extinction, which is non-dual and without distinction.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of inconceivable, incomparable realms of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of wisdom for generating and maintaining [the teachings].
What are these ten? They are:
the wisdom of pure vows that can generate all dharmas despite their lack of any point of departure;
All dharmas are bodiless, yet they can give birth to the wisdom of the Dharma-body;
all dharmas are entirely non-dual, yet they give rise to perfect awakening and realize all dharmas;
all dharmas are entirely without self and without sentient beings, yet they can give birth to the wisdom that transforms sentient beings.
All dharmas are entirely without marks, yet they can give rise to the wisdom that discerns various marks;
all worlds are entirely without formation or destruction, yet they can give rise to the wisdom that discerns the formation and destruction of worlds;
all dharmas have no creator, yet they can give rise to the wisdom of karmic retribution.
All dharmas are ineffable, yet they can give rise to the wisdom that expounds the dharma-realm;
all dharmas are neither defiled nor pure, yet they can give rise to the wisdom of defilement and purity;
all dharmas are without arising or ceasing, yet they can give rise to the wisdom of dependent origination.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of wisdom for the birth and sustenance of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of immeasurable internal dharmas. What are these ten?
All Buddhas have internally pure bodies that accord with the three periods of time;
All Buddhas possess the inner dharma of the three wheels to teach and transform sentient beings;
all Buddhas possess the profound inner wisdom-dhāraṇī that discriminates all Buddha-dharmas;
all Buddhas possess the fourfold eloquence wheel within, turning the pure wheel of Dharma among the fourfold assembly.
All Buddhas possess within them great loving-kindness and great compassion, and are thus able never to abandon any sentient being;
all Buddhas are constantly in internal meditative concentration, skillfully observing sentient beings without ever missing the proper time;
all Buddhas possess within them skillful and subtle roots of goodness for the purpose of taming sentient beings.
All Buddhas internally abide within the entire dharma-realm in an unimpeded manner;
within a single thought-moment, all Buddhas are able to manifest the appearance of all Buddhas of the three periods of time in the world;
and within all Buddhas, there is the discernment that all incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*) of the three periods of time are but a single day.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of immeasurable internal dharmas of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of profound great dharmas. What are these ten?
All Buddhas are able to utterly destroy and disperse all Māras.
All Buddhas are able to subdue all non-Buddhists;
all Buddhas are able to manifest transformations for all sentient beings to cause them to rejoice;
all Buddhas are able to travel to all worlds to teach and transform sentient beings.
All Buddhas thoroughly discern and know the profoundly deep realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu);
all Buddhas pervade all worlds with various bodies, yet possess no differentiated bodies;
every single voice of all Buddhas is endowed with the four kinds of eloquence (pratisaṃvid) that never ceases.
All sentient beings who behold all Buddhas are caused to rejoice and receive benefit without fail;

from every single pore of all Buddhas, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of all worlds emerge in succession without interruption; within each and every atom, all Buddhas manifest Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of all worlds with their various adornments, constantly turning the wheel of Dharma to teach and transform sentient beings without interruption, yet the atoms do not enlarge and the worlds do not diminish, for they know with certainty that they abide in the Dharma-realm;

all Buddhas awaken to the darkness of ignorance regarding all phenomena and are endowed with the ten powers, extensively preaching the Dharma as it truly is for all sentient beings to eliminate the cataracts of delusion.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of profound great dharmas of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of merit that are pure through the abandonment of evil. What are these ten?
All Buddhas are, from the very beginning, pure through the abandonment of evil by cultivating all merits.
All Buddhas are born into the family of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, being pure through the departure from evil;
all Buddhas have minds that are unattached throughout the limits of the future, being pure through the departure from evil;
all Buddhas do not cling to any phenomena of the three periods of time, being pure through the departure from evil.
All Buddhas are free from all manner of delusions, adorning themselves with a single adornment, and are purified by being free from evil;
all Buddhas possess inexhaustible merit and dwell peacefully within the dharma-realm, equal and purified by being free from evil;

all Buddhas possess pure and wondrous form-bodies that are immeasurable and boundless, appearing universally in all worlds throughout the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings without ever missing the proper time, and are purified by being free from evil.

All Buddhas abide in the four fearlessnesses, free from all terrors, and amidst the assemblies of devas and humans, they roar the great lion’s roar, extensively expounding the Dharma to cause the multitudes to rejoice, abandon evil, and attain purity;

even those Buddhas who have entered parinirvāṇa throughout unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas—if there are sentient beings who hear their names, they will obtain a great fruit and reward, just as when a Buddha is present in person, causing them to abandon evil and attain purity;

and although all Buddhas dwell far away in worlds that are unspeakably unspeakable in number, if there are sentient beings who maintain single-minded right mindfulness, those Tathāgatas will immediately appear before them, causing them to abandon evil and attain purity.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of merit of all Buddhas that are pure through the abandonment of evil.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of ultimate purity. What are these ten? All Buddhas have ultimate purity in all their vows;

all Buddhas have ultimate purity in their pure conduct and prohibitive precepts; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in having completely abandoned all *upadhi*; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in their Buddha-fields; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in their retinues; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in their lineage; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in the marks and signs of their form bodies; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in their Dharma bodies; all Buddhas have ultimate purity in their unimpeded body of omniscience; and all Buddhas have ultimate purity in liberation—having completed what was to be done and forever crossed to the other shore.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of ultimate purity of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas perform ten kinds of Buddha-activities in all worlds at all times. What are these ten?
Whenever there are sentient beings who mindfully recollect them, all Buddhas appear before them.
All Buddhas constantly preach the Mahāyāna for the sake of sentient beings;
all Buddhas are always able to nurture the immeasurable roots of goodness of all sentient beings;
and all Buddhas fully discern and know whenever any sentient being first leaves birth and death and enters the stage of the True Dharma.
All Buddhas do not abandon sentient beings when teaching and transforming assemblies;
all Buddhas constantly traverse all worlds without obstruction;
all Buddhas, through great compassion, never forsake any sentient being.
The emanation bodies manifested by all Buddhas are never interrupted;
the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas have never ceased;
and all Buddhas universally and eternally abide within the pure dharma-realm, extensively expounding the teachings for the sake of all sentient beings.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of buddha-activities performed by all Buddhas in all worlds at all times.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of inexhaustible oceans of skillful means and wisdom.
What are these ten? They are:
the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of the Dharma-body of all Buddhas;
The inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of the merits of all Buddhas;
the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of the realm of the Buddha-eye of all Buddhas;
the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of the inconceivable roots of goodness of all Buddhas.
The inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas practicing all dharmas;
the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas raining down the nectar of the Dharma;
the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas praising the merits of all Buddhas.
The inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas’ original vows and various practices;
the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas who, throughout the limits of the future, constantly perform Buddha-work for the sake of all sentient beings without ever resting;
and the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of all Buddhas who know the mental activities and movements of every thought of sentient beings.
All Buddhas give birth to the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom that is the merit of all-knowledge.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of inexhaustible oceans of expedient wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of eternal dharmas. What are these ten?
