All Buddhas constantly practice all the *pāramitās*; all Buddhas are eternally free from delusion regarding all phenomena; all Buddhas are always endowed with great compassion; all Buddhas are always possessed of the immeasurable ten powers (*daśabala*); all Buddhas constantly turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma; all Buddhas constantly deliver all sentient beings; all Buddhas constantly bring all sentient beings to equal and perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*); all Buddhas constantly respond to and transform all sentient beings through their emanations; all Buddhas constantly practice the dharma of right mindfulness and non-duality; and having constantly transformed sentient beings, all Buddhas manifest *nirvāṇa*, yet the realms of the Buddhas have no boundaries.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten eternal laws of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of immeasurable gateways for teaching the Buddha-dharma. What are these ten?
All Buddhas universally teach the immeasurable gateway of the realm of sentient beings;
All Buddhas fully expound the various gateways of the immeasurable practices of sentient beings;
all Buddhas fully expound the immeasurable gateways of the karmic retributions of sentient beings;
all Buddhas fully expound the immeasurable gateways of skillful means for delivering sentient beings.
All Buddhas possess immeasurable gateways of pure conduct for maturing sentient beings;
all Buddhas possess immeasurable gateways for teaching and establishing all bodhisattvas in their practices;
all Buddhas expound immeasurable gateways of the supreme and wondrous vows of bodhisattvas.
All Buddhas fully expound the gateways of the formation and destruction of immeasurable worlds;
all Buddhas fully expound the immeasurable pure Buddha-fields, which are the gateways of the right aspirations of all Bodhisattvas;

all Buddhas fully expound the immeasurable worlds of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, who appear in succession throughout immeasurable eons, skillfully discerning these gateways of the Buddhas' wisdom.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of immeasurable gates for expounding the Buddha-dharma of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten dharmas by which they constantly perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
What are these ten? All Buddhas, through their form bodies (*rūpakāya*), constantly perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings;
The voices of all Buddhas constantly perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings;
all Buddhas accepting offerings constantly perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings;
all Buddhas not accepting offerings constantly perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
All Buddhas constantly perform the work of a Buddha by means of earth, water, fire, and wind;
all Buddhas, through the realm sustained by their spiritual power, constantly perform the work of a Buddha for the sake of sentient beings;
all Buddhas constantly perform the work of a Buddha for all sentient beings by means of their names and titles.
All Buddhas constantly perform buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings through the realm of the buddha-field;
all Buddhas constantly perform buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings through pure buddha-fields;
all Buddhas constantly perform buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings through silence.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of dharmas of all Buddhas, which they constantly employ to perform buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten qualities of the steadfast hero. What are these ten?
All Buddhas are firm in their vows and cannot be thwarted; as they speak, so they practice, for their words and deeds are in accord.
All Buddhas cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, their adornment of merit never being subject to fear;
for the sake of transforming all sentient beings, all Buddhas travel to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, teaching and transforming beings in all those worlds without any hindrance;
and all Buddhas regard with equal great compassion those sentient beings who have faith and those who do not, without any distinction.
From their first aspiration until their perfect enlightenment, all Buddhas have never at any point during that interval regressed from the mind of bodhi.
All Buddhas cultivate various merits and dedicate them entirely toward omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), seeking no worldly conduct.

Under the guidance of all Buddhas, they follow and train in the physical, verbal, and mental actions of those Buddhas; they forever distance themselves from the minds of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, single-mindedly and exclusively seeking unsurpassed bodhi. All the merits they cultivate are dedicated toward omniscience, as they seek the unsurpassed path to achieve equal and perfect enlightenment (*samyaksaṃbodhi*).

All Buddhas impartially and universally illuminate the infinite and boundless True Dharma of all Buddhas, purifying the bodhisattva mind and bringing it to ultimate fulfillment in all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

All Buddhas are able to relinquish all worldly pleasures; they take no delight in what the world seeks to enjoy, nor do they cling to the world. They cause all sentient beings to extinguish all suffering and attain the peaceful, equal happiness of nirvana.

For the sake of all sentient beings, all Buddhas undergo immeasurable suffering, desiring to establish the lineage of the Buddhas and causing all beings to joyfully seek Bodhi, transcend birth and death, and attain the ground of the Ten Powers.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of dharmas of the steadfast heroes of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of unobstructed abodes of Buddhahood. What are these ten?
All Buddhas are able to travel everywhere throughout all worlds; this is their first unobstructed abode.
All Buddhas are able to abide securely in all worlds through unobstructed dwelling;
all Buddhas abide securely in all worlds through unobstructed walking, standing, sitting, and reclining;
all Buddhas abide securely in all worlds through unobstructed preaching of the Dharma.
All Buddhas dwell without obstruction in the Tuṣita Heaven throughout all worlds;
all Buddhas dwell without obstruction within the dharma-realm of the three periods of time;
and all Buddhas dwell without obstruction as they teach the Dharma, their retinues filling the entire dharma-realm.
All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, fully know the mental activities of every sentient being and dwell without obstruction in taming them through the three wheels of teaching;
all Buddhas are able, with a single body, to dwell entirely within all the inconceivable dharma-gates of all Buddhas and dwell without obstruction;
all Buddhas distinguish and know all sentient beings and dwell without obstruction.
All Buddhas are able to discern all the unobstructed abodes of the Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of unobstructed abodes of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of most excellent and unsurpassed adornments. What are these ten?

All Buddhas possess the marks and signs of the form-body (*rūpakāya*), which are the most excellent and unsurpassed adornments; this constitutes the most excellent and unsurpassed adornment of the form-body of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess eight kinds of subtle and wondrous vocal tones; each individual tone is accompanied by five hundred attendant wondrous sounds, adorned with incalculable hundreds of thousands of sounds. These infinite and boundless wondrous vocal arts are entirely pure, universally able to expound the meanings and flavors of the true Dharma of all Buddhas. Being entirely free from fear, they abide in the fearless Great Lion’s Roar, causing all beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm to hear their voices and, according to their original practices and various roots of goodness, attain full understanding and liberation. This is the supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the verbal karma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess the adornment of the mental karma of the ten powers; they cause the flowers of the great samādhis of all Buddhas to bloom; their spheres of activity are adorned by the eighteen unique qualities (āveṇika-dharma) and are without obstruction; abiding on the stage of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu-bhūmi), they fully attain the very source and bottom of all Buddha-dharmas; the entire dharma-realm without exception is adorned; and within a single thought-moment, they discern and know all dharmas of the three periods of time and the mental activities of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm without remainder—this is the most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the mental karma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess the most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of light; they all universally radiate the treasury of great light, and each ray of light has countless nets of wondrous light as its retinue, universally illuminating the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, eliminating all darkness and obscurity of the world, manifesting the appearance of a Buddha in the world to perform the most supreme Buddha-activities of non-retrogression, and giving birth to immeasurable pure Dharma-bodies—this is the most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of light of all Buddhas.

Whenever all Buddhas smile, they emit from their mouths incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* billions of *nayuta* rays of light, each possessing various immeasurable and inconceivable colors, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions. They bestow upon immeasurable, innumerable, and *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. This is the supreme, unsurpassed adornment of universal illumination that manifests the departure from delusion for all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess an immeasurable Dharma-body, which is the unobstructed, pure, and boundless Dharmadhātu. It is far removed from the world, unstained by the world, and unattached to the world; it understands the reality of the world, practices supramundane dharmas, cuts off the path of speech, encompasses the limit of the ineffable, and is free from the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. This is the most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the Dharma-body of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess immeasurable, eternal, and wondrous radiance that universally illumines all worlds throughout the ten directions, adorned with unspeakably unspeakable varieties of exquisite colors. It shines everywhere upon the world without obstruction and gives rise to the treasury of all light; this constitutes the supreme, unsurpassed adornment of the eternal light of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas possess infinite wondrous forms: delightful wondrous forms, pure wondrous forms, wondrous forms that accord with all sentient beings, wondrous forms whose radiance eclipses the three realms, and supreme wondrous forms that have reached the ultimate other shore; these constitute the most excellent, unsurpassed, and infinite adornment of wondrous forms of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are naturally pure; born into the noble family of the Buddha-jewels of the three periods of time, they are free from all evils and practice all pure and supreme dharmas. Giving birth to all-knowledge, the lineage of the Tathāgatas is pure and unimpeded; this is the most supreme, unsurpassed adornment of the pure lineage of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are adorned with the power of great compassion; their bodies are naturally pure, far removed from all unwholesome thoughts and observations, and their bodily activities are eternally stilled. Those who behold them never tire of doing so. Their minds are pure and liberated, and they are fully endowed with great compassion. They are the foremost field of merit for all sentient beings and the unsurpassed recipients of offerings. Out of pity for sentient beings, they cause them all to be established in all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*). They bring forth an immeasurable treasury of jewels of merit and serve as a treasury of the roots of goodness, wisdom, and merit that nourish all sentient beings. This is the supreme, unsurpassed, ultimate treasury of jewels of the merit of great compassion and great pity, the pure adornment of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten most supreme and unsurpassed adornments of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of sovereign correct dharmas. What are these ten?

All Buddhas exercise sovereign mastery over all phenomena according to their will regarding the phrases and syllables; their eloquence is inexhaustible, and they expound all phenomena without obstruction—this is the sovereign correct dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas respond to sentient beings according to their needs, manifesting transformations without missing the proper time; they preach the Dharma according to their aspirations, never failing the opportune moment—this is the sovereign true Dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to cause the six kinds of earth tremors throughout the worlds of the ten directions without ever causing disturbance or confusion; within a single world as vast as space, filled with immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* varieties of adornments, whether they cause it to rise, fall, contract, or expand, in every single world and every single location, they do not disturb the minds of sentient beings nor cause them to give rise to thoughts of doubt or confusion—this is the sovereign true Dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to maintain all the various adornments of all worlds through their wisdom; within a single thought-moment, they manifest the various adornments of all worlds for incalculable, incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* eons, praising these ornaments without end. Forever free from the defilements of all worlds, they adorn every Buddha-field in the world-systems—this is the sovereign True Dharma of all Buddhas.

If all Buddhas see even a single sentient being who should be transformed, they shall sit in the full lotus posture for incalculable, incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas without their bodies becoming weary; with single-minded mindfulness, they never forget that person nor miss the proper time. For the sake of one sentient being, they maintain their life-span, sitting in the full lotus posture until the end of future kalpas without their bodies becoming weary, mindful of that sentient being without ever forgetting them. As it is with one sentient being, so it is with all sentient beings; this is the sovereign True Dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas travel without obstruction to the abodes of all Tathāgatas throughout every world-system; in each direction there are world-oceans equal to the Dharma-realm, and within each direction there are infinite networks of worlds and all world-oceans equal to the Dharma-realm, wherein they are able, in a single thought-moment, to universally turn the wondrous Wheel of Dharma without obstruction—this is the sovereign True Dharma of all Buddhas.

Because all Buddhas tame and transform all sentient beings, they attain equal and perfect enlightenment in every moment of thought. It is not that they have not previously awakened to the true Dharma of the Buddhas, nor do they attain perfect enlightenment while remaining on the stage of training. Having attained unimpeded mastery over all Buddha-dharmas, they do not relinquish their sovereign spiritual powers; with immeasurable wisdom and spheres of experience, they transform sentient beings—this is the sovereign true Dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to perform the Buddha-work through the sense-base of the eye as the sense-base of the ear; they are able to perform the Buddha-work through the sense-base of the ear as the sense-base of the nose; they are able to perform the Buddha-work through the sense-base of the nose as the sense-base of the tongue; they are able to perform the Buddha-work through the sense-base of the tongue as the sense-base of the body; they are able to perform the Buddha-work through the sense-base of the body as the sense-base of the mind. They are able to engage with all the various realms of all worlds—both mundane realms and supramundane realms—and within each and every realm, they are able to perform the Buddha-work. This is the sovereign True Dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are able to place all sentient beings within a single pore; the body of each and every sentient being is equal in size to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, yet there is no crowding among those beings. Each and every sentient being has a lifespan of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas and is able to travel throughout immeasurable worlds. Within those worlds, they see Buddhas appearing in the world and turning the pure wheel of Dharma, proclaiming and expounding countless dharma-gates, extensively teaching the incalculable dharmas of the past, as well as the incalculable dharmas of the future and the present. All sentient beings perform the four modes of deportment without any crowding; this is the sovereign true Dharma of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, manifest lion thrones of lotus-jewel treasuries; their Tathāgata-pure bodies are equal to the Dharma-realm, and seated upon those jewel thrones, they attain perfect enlightenment and manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of a Tathāgata. Just as they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment by a single Tathāgata within a single thought-moment, so too do they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment by as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in all worlds within a single thought-moment.
As it is within a single thought-moment, so it is within all thought-moments.

Just as he manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment upon a lion throne of lotus-jewel treasuries, so too are there inconceivable varieties of world-systems—pure Buddha-fields equal to the *dharmadhātu*, adorned with various arrays, and various realms—that cannot be described. These unspeakable Buddha-fields may possess common characteristics or differing characteristics; they could not be fully described even in unspeakably many *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas. The various thoughts and various times of immeasurable Buddhas are likewise inconceivable. Within a single thought-moment, all Buddhas manifest themselves to all sentient beings through slight expedient means in this very same way.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of sovereign dharmas of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas, having fully perfected ten kinds of inconceivable dharmas, have attained equal and perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*). What are these ten?
All Buddhas, each with their wondrous marks (*lakṣaṇa*) complete with the hundred merits (*śata-puṇya*), have attained equal and perfect enlightenment. All Buddhas... [text continues]

The Buddha is fully endowed with all Buddha-dharmas and has attained equal and perfect enlightenment; all Buddhas are fully endowed with all roots of goodness and have attained equal and perfect enlightenment;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with the cultivation of all meritorious practices and have attained equal and perfect enlightenment;
all Buddhas thoroughly know that the faculties of sentient beings have matured and have attained equal and perfect enlightenment. One.
All Buddhas have fully accomplished the indestructible, supreme Dharma and attained equal and perfect enlightenment;

all Buddhas have fully adorned and purified Buddha-fields and attained equal and perfect enlightenment; all Buddhas have fully perfected all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and attained equal and perfect enlightenment;
the physical bodies (*rūpakāya*) of all Buddhas are complete with the primary and secondary marks, such that those who behold them do not do so in vain.
They attain equal and perfect enlightenment; all Buddhas fully possess the equal and correct Dharma of all Buddhas and thereby attain equal and perfect enlightenment;
having fully accomplished all the Buddha-works of all Buddhas, they subsequently enter into nirvana without remainder.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten inconceivable dharmas that all Buddhas fulfill to achieve equal and perfect enlightenment.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of skillful means. What are these ten?
All Buddhas fully know that all phenomena have no ultimate end, yet they speak exhaustively of the roots of goodness of all Buddhas; this is the first skillful means of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas realize that all phenomena are entirely without anything seen; they are mutually unknowing, neither bound nor liberated, without grasping or accumulation, without fulfillment, without sovereignty, and without ultimateity. Yet, within those phenomena, all Buddhas truly know them to be without difference; they are free from all defilements and have attained mastery over all phenomena. Within the dharma of non-grasping, they do not destroy the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); having perfected their training, they abide in the stage of great mastery and perceive the entire dharma-realm, awakening to all-knowledge. This is the skillful means of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are free from the limits of all marks and do not abide in any mark, yet they discern and know all marks without confusing their own nature. All natures are devoid of self-nature, yet they can manifest incalculable pure form-bodies and various adorned, pure Buddha-lands with wondrous marks. The Buddhas are fully endowed with all-knowledge; their wisdom-body is luminous and pure, and the lamp of wisdom extinguishes the darkness of ignorance, universally manifesting themselves to all sentient beings—this is the skillful means of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas know the limit of sentient beings as neither past, nor future, nor present; it is the Dharma-realm, which is neither past, future, nor present, but the suchness of reality, free from all falsehood. They are thus able to expound upon the equal realm perceived by the Buddhas of the three periods of time; this is the subtle and skillful means of all Buddhas.

The physical, verbal, and mental actions of all Buddhas are without fabrication; they are ultimately non-abiding, transcending all numerical dharmas, and have reached the other shore. Yet they give birth to an immeasurable treasure-store of merit, analytically expound the mundane and supramundane dharmas, fully accomplish unimpeded wisdom, and manifest immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers to deliver all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm—this is the skillful means of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas fully know that all phenomena are without knowledge and without vision; they are neither one nor different, neither with marks nor without marks, neither adorned nor unadorned. All phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature, neither arising nor ceasing. Yet, within all these phenomena—both existent and non-existent—they do not destroy the conventional characteristics of the world. Those of all-encompassing wisdom perceive beings and manifest supreme, wondrous wisdom, freely and extensively expounding all phenomena, yet they do not eternally extinguish suchness (*tathatā*).

This is the skillful means of all Buddhas. All Buddhas are able, in a single moment, to discern and know all times, never abandoning the birth of the equal and true Dharma, which is not encompassed by any time; it is neither day nor night.
Neither for half a month nor a month, neither for one year nor a hundred years, neither during the formation of a kalpa nor its destruction,
neither apart from time nor not separated from time, he turns the pure wheel of Dharma throughout immeasurable time—
whether for a mere moment, or during the beginning, middle, and end of the day, or during the beginning, middle, and end of the night, or at...
For seven days, one month, one year, a hundred years, and even for inconceivable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas,
until the end of all future kalpas and at all times, they turn the pure wheel of Dharma without ever ceasing for a moment; this is the skillful means of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas know that the entire dharma-realm is neither apart from time nor not-time; all Buddhas are fully accomplished in immeasurable fearlessnesses, and are fully accomplished in incalculable eloquence, immeasurable eloquence, inexhaustible eloquence, indestructible eloquence, boundless eloquence, unshared eloquence, endless eloquence, and true eloquence. Through skillful means, they analytically expound all bodies of phrases and bodies of meanings, as well as the eloquence of all dharmas, extensively teaching unspeakably many billions of nayutas of sutras according to dispositions, faculties, and practices. Each and every one of those sutras is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, being perfectly and excellently taught—this is the wondrous and skillful means of all Buddhas.
The dharmadhātu of the perfect enlightenment of all Buddhas is without name, without intrinsic nature, without names for the three periods of time,
without names for sentient beings, without names for phenomena, without names for non-phenomena, without names for merit, without names for non-merit,
without names for bodhisattvas, without names for Buddhas, and without names for numbers, nor is it without names.
It is named "numberless," "unborn," "undying," "neither existent," "nor non-existent," "not one," and "not manifold.
The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is ineffable; it has no direction and no location.
It transcends sound, the path of speech is cut off, it reaches the ultimate further shore, and is free from falsehood.
Cultivating formless dharmas within the realm of experience, they eliminate all conceptualization and delusion;
without clinging to any worldly speech, they are able to give rise to all dharma-words and dharma-phrases—
this is the skillful means of all Buddhas.
All Buddhas know that all dharmas are non-arising and have no recipient;
they know that form is non-arising, and that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are non-arising. All dharmas are entirely quiescent;
there is no entering and no realm within the dharma-realm. While there is nothing whatsoever, they do not destroy the characteristics of any dharma—this is the one [reality].
All phenomena are without arising; they are entirely like space.

All phenomena are quiescent, without karmic retribution, without that which is learned, without accomplishment, without number, without non-number, neither existent nor non-existent, neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, without coming, and without going.

There is no going, nor is there any staying; there are no sentient beings, yet it is not that there are no sentient beings; there is no teaching or transformation, yet there is no lack of teaching or transformation;
there is no life-force, yet it is not that there is no life-force; there are no causes and conditions, yet it is not that there are no causes and conditions;

there is no dependent origination, yet it is not that there is no dependent origination—yet one skillfully discriminates between sentient beings who are fixed in the right, fixed in the wrong, or indeterminate.
To achieve the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, and the knowledge of all modes,
and to let out the great lion’s roar within the assembly in the realm of the Tathāgata— this is the skillful means of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of skillful means of all Buddhas.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Thirty.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll Thirty-One,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty,
Part Two of the Second Section of Chapter Twenty-Eight: The Inconceivable Dharmas of the Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas have ten kinds of Buddha-activities that are immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable; they cannot be measured by any gods or humans, nor can they be described by any Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas of the three periods of time, except through the spiritual power of a Buddha.”
What are these ten?

All Buddhas, throughout immeasurable and boundless empty space and the dharma-realm, as well as in all worlds, perform the work of a Buddha while practicing the bodhisattva path in the Tuṣita heavens.

With immeasurable exquisite forms, immeasurable merits, immeasurable radiances, immeasurable sounds, immeasurable pure voices, immeasurable samādhis, and immeasurable spheres of wisdom, they gather in all the worlds—including devas, humans, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and asuras—through the sphere of great kindness and unimpeded great compassion, peacefully gathering in sentient beings;
they cause some to be born in the heavens, cause others to cultivate the power of various merits, cause others to purify their faculties, or tame their minds, thereby gathering in sentient beings;
or they gather in sentient beings by means of the various pure vehicles.
Either by fulfilling the Mahāyāna to gather in sentient beings,
or by transcending birth and death to gather in sentient beings—
this is the foremost Buddha-activity of all Buddhas.
"All Buddhas descend from the Tuṣita Heaven into their mothers' wombs and cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva;

they contemplate all forms of existence as being like illusions, like transformations, like lightning, like dreams, like space, and like flames; they remain free from all contention, cultivate true and real wisdom, become pure through the departure from desire, and fulfill the treasury of great adornments; in their final birth, they perform the work of a Buddha;
they dwell within pavilions adorned with exquisite jewels and perform the work of a Buddha."

Some perform Buddha-work through supernatural powers; some perform Buddha-work through right mindfulness; some perform Buddha-work by manifesting the treasury of great sovereignty; some perform Buddha-work by means of the sun of perfected wisdom; some perform Buddha-work by being endowed with the vast realm of the Tathāgata; some perform Buddha-work by manifesting Buddhas who fill immeasurable and boundless worlds; some perform Buddha-work by entering immeasurable and boundless great samādhis and samāpattis; some perform Buddha-work by arising from those various samādhis; some perform Buddha-work from the first production of the thought of enlightenment, even unto the nirvana without remainder.
In this second stage, one ultimately manifests throughout all worlds;
or at the time of initial birth, one performs buddha-work throughout all worlds;
or during childhood, one performs buddha-work throughout all worlds.
Sometimes, while as a bodhisattva, he performs buddha-work for all the world;
sometimes, while renouncing the household life, or when attaining buddhahood, or when turning the wheel of Dharma, he performs buddha-work for all the world.

By means of various skillful expedients, they perform the work of a Buddha in all worlds without exception, perform the work of a Buddha throughout the entire network of directions, perform the work of a Buddha in all buddha-fields, and perform the work of a Buddha regarding all karmic retributions; or they perform the work of a Buddha among all sentient beings without exception, or within all cycles of birth and death, they perform the work of a Buddha by manifesting the dharma-gate of the transformation of right mindfulness.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the second buddha-activity of all Buddhas.
When all Buddhas were bodhisattvas, they accomplished all pure and supreme deeds within royal palaces and were well able to discern and know all forms of birth."

In accordance with sentient beings, he manifests dwelling in a royal palace; yet, desiring to cause all roots of goodness to be fulfilled, he does not cling to any forms, remains detached from all sounds, and contemplates that all existence is entirely quiescent.
With profound wisdom, he enters all realms, upholds all precepts, and is pure and complete.

With great compassion, he observes his inner retinue; with great kindness, he observes that sentient beings are empty and quiescent; with great joy, he observes that there is nothing in the world to be delighted in; and with great equanimity, he observes that the mind has attained mastery.
Able to transform at will, he ultimately realizes all-knowledge and all sublime merits, giving rise to the Dharma-body, which is equal to the Dharma-realm, pure, fulfilled, and free from attachment.
They cause all their retinues to become entirely pure; they are able to extensively preach the Dharma to them as appropriate, causing them to grow weary of the world;
they can utter all worldly sounds and manifest the retribution of karmic results according to the conduct of beings;
they produce immeasurable and diverse skillful means to tame and transform them according to what is required.
He brings to full maturity all those whose roots of goodness are not yet mature;
he enables those already matured to attain liberation;
he manifests immeasurable and non-regressive Buddha-activities, extensively expounding various Dharma gates to cause the minds of immeasurable sentient beings to become pure.
Raising the heavy clouds of great compassion, he universally rains down the immeasurable Dharma-rain of ambrosia;
with great kindness and equanimity, he manifests the three wheels to teach and transform sentient beings.
Although dwelling in the royal palace, he universally manifests all Buddha-activities;

throughout all worlds, he manifests Buddha-activities, giving rise to the unimpeded supernatural powers of all Buddhas, and is fully endowed with the three types of skillful means. His physical and vocal actions are ultimately pure, while his mental action is profoundly deep and ultimately unimpeded; having attained skillful means, he benefits all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the third buddha-work of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas, as rare treasures of the world, possess all manner of precious objects capable of dazzling and swaying the minds of people;
yet the Bodhisattvas renounce them all, leaving home for the homeless life to manifest within the world,
desiring to cause sentient beings not to become attached to the world.
Understanding that all things are subject to decay and destruction, and realizing they are entirely impermanent,
one abandons craving and attachment, practices the pure Dharma, benefits sentient beings, and attains the benefit of leaving the household life.

Manifesting in the world, he cast off secular attire and cultivated the dharma of non-contention; his original vows were fulfilled, and all his immeasurable merits were brought to complete perfection.
Endowed with wisdom, he removes the ignorance of the world and manifests himself to sentient beings as the unsurpassed field of merit.

If there are sentient beings who plant roots of goodness within this field of merit of the Buddha, he praises them, saying that they have already become fully possessed of all merits and profound wisdom, having realized the true meaning.
He causes all sentient beings to attain pure happiness and forever leave behind all evils through the gateway of the pure Dharma;
he extensively expounds the gateway of the True Dharma for the sake of sentient beings so that they may transcend birth and death;
and, desiring to establish the banner of omniscience, he leaves his home to enter the homeless life.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the fourth buddha-activity of all Buddhas.
All Buddhas cultivate immeasurable practices, single-mindedly and exclusively seeking sarvajñā (all-knowledge);"

Seated at the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, he attained perfect awakening and realized all dharmas; having shattered and dispersed the hosts of Māras, he possesses the indestructible treasury of the Dharma-body.
He is able to completely fill the entire Dharma-realm, transcending all marks, ultimately inexhaustible, and fully accomplishing immeasurable Dharma-gates.

Within the realm of omniscience, they exercise mastery in accordance with its meaning; having accumulated and perfected the merits of all-encompassing wisdom (*sarvākārajñatā*), they adorn all jewel thrones that pervade all lands.
All great bodhisattvas occupy these seats, having accomplished the supreme practices of a bodhisattva and being fully endowed with the most excellent great vows of a bodhisattva;
they are constantly revered and remembered by all bodhisattvas.
For the sake of all bodhisattvas, they turn the profound wheel of Dharma;
they encompass all bodhisattvas within the immeasurable realm of the Buddhas; they cultivate and adorn the practices of bodhisattvas;
and they cause the assembly of bodhisattvas to completely purify all the realms of the Buddhas throughout every world.
May all sentient beings cultivate roots of goodness that cannot be destroyed;
may they emerge from the stage of reality and dwell securely in the immeasurable stages of bodhisattva conduct, becoming fully endowed with all supreme and wondrous merits;

and may they thoroughly discern and know all worlds, all sentient beings, all buddha-fields, all dharmas, all bodhisattvas, all modes of maturation, all three periods of time, all methods of teaching and transforming, the sovereign awakening of all buddhas, and the nature of all sentient beings, thereby performing the work of a buddha.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the fifth buddha-activity of all Buddhas:
"All Buddhas turn the sublime wheel of Dharma because they are non-retrogressive."
The wheel of Dharma that is immeasurable, because it is known by all the worlds;
the wheel of Dharma of universal awakening, because it is the fearless great lion’s roar of the Great Teacher;
the wheel of Dharma that knows the treasury of all dharmas, because it reveals and manifests the clear and pure Dharma-gates to extinguish the darkness of ignorance.
The wheel of Dharma that is unattached, because wisdom is equal to empty space;
the wheel of Dharma that is unimpeded, because it contemplates all phenomena as being neither existent nor non-existent;
the wheel of Dharma that is a lamp for all worlds, because it purifies the Dharma-eye of all sentient beings.
They manifest the wheel of Dharma of omniscience in order to fill all worlds throughout the three periods of time;
they are the single wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas, for all Buddha-dharmas are not mutually contradictory.
In this way, these immeasurable and incalculable wheels of Dharma turn according to what is appropriate, performing inconceivable Buddha-works.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the sixth Buddha-work of all Buddhas.
"All Buddhas, whether entering villages, towns, or great royal capitals, are able to perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings;
or they enter the capitals of human kings;
or they enter the abodes of the kings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, and piśācas."
When entering the capital cities of all such kings, he is able to perform the work of a Buddha for the sake of sentient beings. That is to say:

when he enters the city gates, the entire earth shakes in six ways, and light shines everywhere; the blind gain sight, the deaf gain hearing, the insane regain their composure, the naked obtain clothing, and those in suffering find joy;
all musical instruments sound spontaneously without being struck, and all ornaments naturally produce subtle and wondrous sounds.
Such objects as these also spontaneously emit subtle and wondrous sounds.
The form-bodies (*rūpakāya*) of all Buddhas are pure; those who behold them never tire of doing so, as they universally perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
The physical marks and embellishments (*lakṣaṇavyañjana*) of all Buddhas are majestic and sublime, as they universally perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.

All Buddhas gaze with serene composure, never acting with haste; they observe all directions without losing their dignified deportment. In all spheres of experience, their faculties are tranquil and stilled; they restrain the mind from distraction and proceed directly toward Nirvana, universally performing the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
All Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings through the four modes of conduct;
all Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings either by preaching the Dharma or by remaining silent.
All Buddhas, by means of their supernormal powers, preach the Dharma and provide instruction, universally performing Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings;

all Buddhas, within the oceans of all worlds, for the various oceans of sentient beings who cultivate great roots of goodness, practice the samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha, and carry out the bodhisattva practices while contemplating all Buddhas without ever feeling weary or satisfied;
or they speak of the appearance of a Buddha as something difficult to encounter.

Having seen the Tathāgata, they give rise to all immeasurable wholesome dharmas, cultivate meritorious virtues, and practice the conduct of all Buddhas. When a Buddha appears in the world, they purify sentient beings, praise the immeasurable merits of all Buddhas, nurture the lineage of future Buddhas, and cultivate all roots of goodness. They cause all Buddhas to rejoice and understand the Tathāgata’s immeasurable wondrous forms; according to those who are to be transformed, they can universally manifest before them, enabling inconceivable numbers of sentient beings to behold the Tathāgata within all Buddha-fields.
All Buddhas, by means of such immeasurable roots of goodness, universally perform the work of a Buddha for the sake of sentient beings.

Those sentient beings may, some seeing the Buddha, rejoice; some prostrate; some join their palms; some offer praise; some entreat the Buddha; some receive his gifts; some see the Buddha smile; some practice mindfulness of the Buddha; and some see the Buddha’s joy—thus he universally performs the work of a Buddha for all sentient beings.
All Buddhas are able to perform buddha-work for sentient beings by manifesting immeasurable and diverse physical bodies;
all Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings everywhere with wondrous voices;
all Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings everywhere through such immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable matters.
Within all worlds, they teach and transform all sentient beings, causing them never to regress;

filled with great compassion, they do not forsake their original vows, fully accomplishing all powers of wisdom, and according to those who should be transformed, they cause them all to be tamed and subdued.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the seventh buddha-activity of all Buddhas.
All Buddhas may dwell in forest hermitages (āraṇya), or in places of solitude, or in seclusion..."
They perform Buddha-works while remaining in the realm of desire; or they perform Buddha-works while abiding in the abode of Buddhas;
or they perform Buddha-works while abiding in great samādhis; or they perform Buddha-works while abiding in solitary seclusion; or they perform Buddha-works without manifesting their physical form;
or they perform Buddha-works while abiding in profound wisdom; or they abide in that which is immeasurable... [and so forth].
They perform Buddha-works within the realm of the Buddhas, or perform Buddha-works according to what is appropriate,
or perform Buddha-works through the realm of celestial bodies, or through the realms of devas,
nāgas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, humans, non-humans, and all other such beings.
They perform Buddha-works: sometimes performing Buddha-works through the realms of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or bodhisattvas;
sometimes performing Buddha-works by means of preaching the Dharma; sometimes performing Buddha-works through silence;
sometimes performing Buddha-works by teaching that there is but one Buddha in the world; or sometimes by teaching that there are all Buddhas in the world.
They perform Buddha-works in various ways: sometimes they perform Buddha-works by teaching that the infinite vows and infinite practices of all bodhisattvas are one;
sometimes they perform Buddha-works by teaching that a single practice or a single vow is infinite;
sometimes they teach that the realm of the world is the realm of the Tathāgata; and sometimes they teach that the realm of the Tathāgata is the realm of the world.
Regarding their spheres of activity: they may perform Buddha-works by declaring that which is not a sphere of activity to be the sphere of the Tathāgata;
or they may perform Buddha-works while abiding for a single day, a single night, a half-month, a month, a year, or even for immeasurable, incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the eighth buddha-activity of all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are an inexhaustible treasury of merit; they are able to cause sentient beings to give rise to deep faith and to become fully endowed with purity. According to what is appropriate for each, they are able to transform and deliver them, perfecting their faculties, subduing sentient beings, and causing them all to rejoice.
To transform all sentient beings through the path of reality, awakening the entire assembly of bodhisattvas;
to cause all who have not yet resolved upon bodhicitta to resolve upon it,
and to cause those who have already resolved upon it to be endowed with wisdom and realize enlightenment independently of others.
Some manifest parinirvāṇa and perform buddha-work; some manifest the impermanence of the world and perform buddha-work;
some praise the purity of the dharmakāya and perform buddha-work; some speak of having completed what was to be done and perform buddha-work;
some speak of destroying all existence and perform buddha-work; or some speak of the root of the three realms of existence.
They perform Buddha-works through eternal exhaustion; they may teach sentient beings to cultivate weary detachment from the world in accordance with the Buddha-mind;
or they may speak to sentient beings of the brevity of life; or they may speak to sentient beings that there is nothing in all the worlds worth delighting in;
or they may speak to sentient beings of meeting all future Buddhas; or they may [speak] to sentient beings...

They proclaim that all Tathāgatas turn the sublime wheel of Dharma; they inspire sentient beings to give rise to the mind of the Buddha-realm, or teach them to practice pure mindfulness of the Buddha according to the occasion, so that they may behold the Tathāgata.
They eliminate all sufferings and cause all beings to become pure, single-mindedly seeking the path of the Buddha.
In all worlds, they gather in sentient beings and lead them into the profound realm of the Tathāgata.
Taking the body of the Tathāgata as the body of all, he gathers in sentient beings and those who are heedless, causing them all to be fully endowed with the three kinds of pure precepts.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the ninth buddha-work of all Buddhas:
"When all Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa, all sentient beings weep with sorrow, shedding tears like rain, distressed and tormented by grief."
Alas, how painful it is!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, always regards all sentient beings with great compassion;
as the Great Teacher, he pities and benefits all beings, providing protection for the world.
The one to whom devas and humans turn for refuge, so difficult to encounter, the unsurpassed field of merit, has now perished forever;
it is precisely because of such sentient beings that the Buddhas, moved by their sorrow, suffering, grief, and affliction, and inspired by their longing and devotion, perform the work of a Buddha.

In accordance with the needs of those to be transformed—including all devas, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others—he pulverizes his entire body to manifest śarīras (relics). This is because he desires to cause sentient beings to give rise to joy and perform offerings, to purify their upright and honest minds, and to tame, transform, and purify them;
because he desires to cause sentient beings to fulfill their merits;
and because he desires to cause sentient beings to erect stūpas for the Tathāgata and perform various kinds of offerings.
Throughout all worlds—in the palaces of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—they erected stupas to make offerings;
furthermore, they erected stupas to make offerings with their claws, teeth, and hair.
Upon seeing this, sentient beings will recollect the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, giving rise to a mind of reverence and making offerings; they may practice generosity or cultivate merit.

Having fulfilled these merits, they will be born either in the heavens or among humans, enjoying honor, nobility, wealth, and happiness; they will eliminate rebirth in the evil realms, proceed directly toward the Right Path, and attain the vision of all Buddhas.
Endowed with pure and white dharmas, they will accomplish the Right Path, transcend the Triple World, and have all their aspirations fully realized according to their wishes.
Constantly mindful of the Tathāgata, one recognizes his kindness and repays it;
for all Tathāgatas constantly act as protectors and refuges for sentient beings, and thus one takes refuge in the Tathāgata.
Although they have entered parinirvāṇa, they still serve as the unsurpassed field of merit and the inexhaustible field of merit for sentient beings.
They cause all sentient beings to nurture their roots of goodness and to fully accomplish all merits.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth buddha-work of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!

These ten kinds of buddha-activities are immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable; no devas or humans can know them, and they cannot be described by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas of the three periods of time, except through the spiritual power of a Buddha.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of non-differentiated dharmas of the Dharma King. What are these ten?
All Buddhas are identical in their granting of predictions;
all Buddhas are identical in fulfilling the aspirations of any sentient beings who practice mindfulness of the Buddha;
and all Buddhas are identical in that they possess no distinct bodies and are identical in their awakening to the meaning of all dharmas.
All Buddhas are no different in their wisdom regarding the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time;
all Buddhas universally know all phenomena of the three periods of time in every thought-moment, without any difference;
all Buddhas clearly understand and distinguish the Buddha-lands of the three periods of time, without any difference.
All Buddhas and all the words of the Buddhas are entirely without difference;
all Buddhas and their teaching and transformation of sentient beings are entirely without difference;
all Buddhas understand that all worldly dharmas and Buddha-dharmas are without difference.
The roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time are one and the same root of goodness; they are entirely without distinction.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of non-differentiated dharmas of the Dharma Kings of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of dharmas toward which they are directed. What are these ten?
All Buddhas abide in the awakening to the entire dharma-realm;
all Buddhas abide in great compassion;
all Buddhas abide in their original vows.
All Buddhas abide in never ceasing to teach and transform sentient beings;
all Buddhas abide in the dharma of non-reliance; all Buddhas abide in the dharma of non-falsity.
All Buddhas abide in the dharma of mindfulness without loss;
all Buddhas abide in an unobstructed mind;
all Buddhas abide in a concentrated mind, never becoming distracted.
All Buddhas abide entirely in the equality of all dharmas, without destroying the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten modes of abiding toward which all Buddhas are directed.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas know ten kinds of dharmas, leaving nothing out. What are these ten?
All Buddhas know all dharmadhātus of the past, without exception; all Buddhas know all dharmadhātus of the future, without exception;
all Buddhas know all dharmadhātus of the present, without exception.
All Buddhas know all paths of language without exception;
all Buddhas know the formation and destruction of all worlds without exception;
all Buddhas know all sentient beings and their wisdoms without exception.
All Buddhas know the superior, middling, and inferior characteristics of all bodhisattvas' roots of goodness, without exception;
all Buddhas know the perfected wisdom of all Buddhas, without exception;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena arise from conditions, without exception.
All Buddhas discern and understand all worlds without exception;
all Buddhas, through their wisdom, discern the entire dharma-realm as being like Indra’s net, without exception.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of dharmas known by all Buddhas, without exception.
O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of most excellent powers:

the power of great strength, the power of immeasurable strength, the power of great merit, the power of reverence, the power of non-retrogression, the power of firmness, the power of indestructibility, the power that cannot be conceived by any world, the power that cannot be destroyed by any sentient being, and the power of great might.
"The dharmas in which the Buddha Narayana-dhvaja abides—
what are these ten? First,
the body of every Buddha cannot be destroyed by any worldly calamities or misfortunes."
The life-faculty of all Buddhas cannot be harmed by any poisons in the world;
when the fire kalpa arises in all worlds, it cannot burn or scorch them;
when the water kalpa arises, it cannot drown them.
When the kalpa-ending winds arise, they cannot scatter or destroy it.

All the armies of Māra, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, piśācas, humans, non-humans, and all other sentient beings, might rain down vajras as vast as Mount Sumeru or the Vajra Encircling Mountains throughout the trichiliocosm; yet even such a rain falling upon the Buddha could not cause him to feel fear, nor would a single hair stand on end. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, his majestic deportment remains unchanged.
In whichever direction the Tathāgata dwells, the drops of the vajra rain ultimately cannot fall there; whether they wish to rain or not, it is according to the will of the Tathāgata.
Even the sentient beings sustained by the Buddha and the Buddha’s own mission cannot be harmed, let alone the Tathāgata himself.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the first great power of all Buddhas, the Nārāyaṇa Banner, the Dharma in which the Buddha abides.
"O Son of the Buddha!

All Buddhas, within all worlds equal to the entire dharma-realm—including Mount Sumeru, the Diamond Rim Mountains, the Great Diamond Rim Mountains, all great oceans, all mountains, and all sentient beings—can entirely contain and sustain them within a single pore.
Until the end of the future eons, all sentient beings do not know at all where they dwell; yet, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, a single hair-pore sustains all sentient beings."

Traveling throughout immeasurable worlds in the ten directions, whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, all Tathāgatas give rise to no thoughts of suffering, affliction, or weariness; their majestic deportment remains unchanged.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as space contains and sustains all worlds equal in extent to the entire dharma-realm without giving rise to a mind of suffering, distress, or weariness;
so too do all Buddhas likewise contain and sustain all sentient beings from all worlds without remainder within a single pore, without giving rise to a mind of suffering, distress, or weariness.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the second great power of all Buddhas, the Dharma-abode of the Tathāgata Nārāyaṇadhvaja.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas can, in a single step, traverse as many Buddha-lands as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable worlds;
and within a single thought-moment, they can take as many steps as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable worlds.
With such steps, one passes through as many eons as there are atoms in all worlds; in every thought-moment, one is able to pass through as many eons as there are atoms in all worlds.
A single Vajra-encircling mountain is equal in number to the atoms within all the Buddha-fields passed through during the aforementioned kalpas;
likewise, there are as many such Vajra-encircling mountains as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, all contained within a single pore, and it is the same for every pore.
The pores of the Tathāgata are equal in number to the pores of all sentient beings;

with such pores, taking such vast strides and with such swiftness, he travels through all worlds in the ten directions and throughout the entire realm of space, across all kalpas from the limits of the past to the limits of the future.

Though such kalpas might be exhausted, the bodies of the Tathāgatas suffer no weariness or decay, their minds do not falter or sink, and they never abandon their samādhis or any of their Buddha-activities.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the third great power, the Dharma-abode of the Tathāgata Nārāyaṇadhvaja.
O Son of the Buddha!"

All Buddhas eat but once, sitting in the full lotus posture; throughout all unspeakably unspeakable kalpas of the past and future limits, their bodies do not sway or move. Abiding in the inconceivable dwelling of a Buddha, they experience the bliss of nirvana, never failing even for a moment to transform a single sentient being.
To place all worlds and all sentient beings upon a single fingertip of a Tathāgata for as many eons as there are until the end of the future;
and for each and every one of those sentient beings, their bodies are as vast as unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields of micro-dust;
and for each and every one of those sentient beings, their bodies are as heavy as all worlds—yet the Tathāgatas experience no physical fatigue and no mental distress.
As it is with one fingertip, so it is with all fingertips;

entering each and every world, entering the realm of empty space, and entering the net of all directions— thus, throughout the entire realm of empty space in all places without exception, reaching the ultimate dharma-realm—
one uses a single hair-tip to measure all worlds.
Upon each and every tip of a hair, they sit in the full lotus posture throughout all kalpas from the past limit to the future limit.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the fourth great power, the Dharma-abode of the Tathāgata Nārāyaṇadhvaja.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas manifest within a single body heads as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
from each head, they manifest tongues as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.”

From each tongue, there issue sounds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, such that there are no sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm who do not hear them;
from each sound, there are preached Sūtras as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
and from each Sūtra, there are explained Dharmas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Within each and every dharma, he speaks of sentence-bodies (*padakāya*) and phoneme-bodies (*vyañjanakāya*) equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

He teaches the Dharma in this manner until the end of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas equal to the atoms within those Buddha-fields; furthermore, for another unspeakably unspeakable number of kalpas equal to the atoms within those Buddha-fields, he speaks of different sentence-bodies and phoneme-bodies. Even if one were to exhaust all kalpas equal to the atoms of all worlds, all kalpas equal to the thoughts of all sentient beings, and all kalpas throughout the limits of the future, the total number of these kalpas could still be exhausted.
The Tathāgata’s emanation-body preaches the Dharma and turns all dharmas, like a whirling firebrand; with sovereign wisdom, it expounds all dharmas;
it turns the wheel of the true Dharma to eliminate the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings;
it turns the wheel of the true Dharma to illuminate all dharmas.
Turning the wheel of the true Dharma, they fully open and reveal all treasuries of the Dharma;
turning the wheel of the true Dharma, they joyfully subdue and adorn all sentient beings;
turning the wheel of the true Dharma, they expound the various dharma-practices that adorn Bodhisattvas.
Turning the wheel of the sublime Dharma, may the sun of Mahāyāna wisdom be made perfectly complete and adorned;
turning the wheel of the sublime Dharma, may all sentient beings without exception be adorned by the wisdom of the Mahāyāna;
turning the wheel of the sublime Dharma, may all forms of eloquence be adorned with fearlessness.

Just as a single Tathāgata and a single emanation-body turn such clouds of wheels of Dharma beyond all analogy, so too do they pervade all realms of reality and worlds equal to the realm of empty space, measuring them entirely with the tip of a hair;

at each point of every hair-tip, in every moment of thought, they manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, continuing until the end of all future eons; and within each of these emanated Buddha-bodies, there are heads as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
and upon each head, there are tongues as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
From each tongue, there issue sounds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
from each sound, there are preached sūtras as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
and from each sūtra, there are explained dharmas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

Within each and every dharma, he speaks of as many collections of phrases (*padakāya*) and collections of syllables (*vyañjanakāya*) as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;

furthermore, for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, he speaks of different collections of phrases and collections of syllables, the sound filling the entire Dharma-realm so that there is not a single sentient being who does not hear it.
Throughout all future eons, he constantly turns the wheel of Dharma; the voice of the Tathāgata is without variation and without interruption, and can never be exhausted.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the fifth great power of all Buddhas, the Dharma-abode of the Narayana Banner Buddha.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas have accomplished the supreme and wondrous great adornment; the mark of the syllable *de* upon their chests is like a vajra, indestructible.

When the Tathāgata sat beneath that Bodhi tree, there were immeasurable hosts of Māra kings, equal in number to all sentient beings, with various evil forms and colors, most terrifying, capable of inciting madness and confusion, and able to strike fear into the entire world.

Such hosts filled the void, the Dharma-realm, and all worlds—possessing various evil forms and colors, most terrifying, capable of inciting madness and confusion, causing all sentient beings to tremble with fear, destroying all worlds, and harming all sentient beings.

Having seen this, the Tathāgata felt no fear in his heart; not a single hair stood on end, his countenance showed no change, and he did not give rise to even a single thought of the slightest sign of dread. His mind was peaceful and unmoving, his physical appearance remained unchanged, and he was far removed from discursive thought (*vitarka* and *vicāra*). His mind was constantly tranquil, ultimately free from all terror, and having extinguished all afflictions of craving and hatred;

he dwelt in the dwelling of the Buddhas, fully endowed with the power of unimpeded great loving-kindness, abiding in the dwelling of great compassion, with all faculties serene and forever free from fear.
The mark of the *śrīvatsa* upon his chest was indestructible, firm, and true.
When all the Māras and their retinues of Māra-devas behold the Tathāgata, they all take refuge in him.

Through the Tathāgata’s teaching by means of the three wheels, they are all brought to subdual; they give rise to the bodhicitta and become entirely non-retrogressive, even until they attain unsurpassed bodhi.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the sixth great power of all Buddhas, the Dharma-abode of the Narayana Banner Buddha.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas emit subtle and wondrous sounds that are free from obstruction, filling all worlds; according to those who are to be delivered, there are none who do not hear them.
The sounds emitted by those Tathāgatas cannot be obstructed by any mountains;
they cannot be obstructed by Sumeru, the king of mountains, by jewel mountains, by the Lesser Diamond Ring Mountains, or by the Greater Diamond Ring Mountains;
nor can they be obstructed by the palaces of devas, the palaces of nāgas, or any of the palaces of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Even the loud sounds throughout all worlds cannot obstruct them;
according to what is appropriate for each, they hear them all without any hindrance.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the seventh great power of all Buddhas, the Dharma-abode of the Narayana Banner Buddha.
"O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas have minds free from obstruction; throughout unspeakably unspeakable billions of nayutas of eons, their minds are ever pure."

The Buddhas of the three periods of time are free from defilement and pure; they share a single adornment, being detached from "I" and "mine. Regarding all phenomena, they have no dependence; they are neither internal nor external, neither arising nor non-arising.
They transcend all objective realms, being quiescent and without location, and without any conditioned activity.
Free from various marks, they eliminate all false grasping at signs, being naturally pure.
Detached from all objective spheres and free from recollection, he accords with the non-contentious Dharma that follows objective spheres;

pure through the abandonment of desire, he dwells in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) and teaches the limit of the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu). This dharma-realm is equal and inexhaustible, such that no sentient being is able to know it.
Forever free from all conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, having abandoned all realms of the path of verbal expression, they reach the ultimate, unobstructed, and inexhaustible Dharma-realm;
turning in accordance with wisdom, adorned with the ten powers, they purify all dharmas and practice skillful means;
they teach that the various characteristics of dharmas are identical to the single characteristic of dharma, such that all characteristics of dharmas do not contradict one another.
Without destroying the three periods of time within the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they attain ultimate mastery and reach the further shore;
they are fully endowed with the profound treasury of the Dharma of mastery and all skillful means (*upāya*);
possessing right mindfulness free from delusion, they dwell peacefully in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions without wavering.
Possessing the knowledge of immortality, having exhausted all outflows (*āsrava*), having reached the ultimate consummation of all phenomena, and having realized the state free from outflows;
with mind and wisdom liberated, having reached the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), dwelling in unimpeded abiding, ever in samādhi and undisturbed;
regarding the phenomena of the three periods of time, they are without obstruction.
Within a single thought-moment, they fully comprehend the mental activities of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the eighth great power of all Buddhas, the Dharma-abode of the Narayana Banner.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas are fully accomplished in the subtle and dense Dharma-body; the realm of the Buddhas’ Dharma-body is immeasurable.
It cannot be known by any in all the worlds, yet within the triple world it remains unstained. Responding to causes and conditions as appropriate, it manifests everywhere.”
Neither real nor unreal, it is equal and pure; neither departing nor arriving, it is unconditioned and indestructible, eternally abiding in purity.

It is the single mark and the markless—the mark of the Dharmakāya. Neither a location nor a direction, it is the body of all bodies, sovereign and infinite. Its wondrous form is infinite, encompassing all bodies and manifesting in various forms as bodies of expedient means. It universally illumines all things, possessing the treasury of wisdom, yet free from any manifold discrimination.

His body fills all worlds without exception, expounding the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). Though it moves, it is not subject to motion; this pure *dharmakāya* is neither existent nor non-existent, neither a skillful means nor not a skillful means. It manifests in accordance with the needs of sentient beings;
it is neither extinguished nor non-extinguished, yet it is not non-manifesting as it transforms sentient beings.
This body arises from the jewels of all merits and originates from the Buddha-nature of all phenomena; it is the *tathatā-dharmakāya*, naturally quiescent.

Regarding all phenomena, there is no obstruction; one accords with the entire realm of reality (*dharmadhātu*), purifies all worlds, and discerns all worlds. Being without movement or fluctuation and devoid of objective spheres, the liberation of the Tathāgata encompasses all-knowledge and accords with all bodies.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the ninth great power of all Buddhas, the Dharma-abode of the Narayana Banner Buddha.
O Son of the Buddha!"

All Buddhas are equal in their perfect enlightenment; they give birth to all bodhisattva practices, ensuring that what they perform is not in vain, fulfilling their profound vows, purifying bodhisattva conduct, and being fully endowed with the wisdom of all bodhisattva practices.

All Buddhas, while practicing the bodhisattva path, are entirely without difference; they skillfully discern and know all bodhisattva practices, fulfill the ocean of all great bodhisattva vows, leave behind all evils, give rise to all wholesome deeds, and cultivate the bodhisattva path until it is completely pure.

They accord with all Buddhas, remaining tranquil and free from negligence; they abide in the immeasurable realms of all samādhis and are able to teach all supreme paths while keeping one far removed from all evil paths.
Having reached the ultimate further shore, they are fully accomplished in the foremost power of wisdom;

they rain down the fearless rain of Dharma, providing excellent answers to whatever questions are asked. They skillfully employ expedient means to preach the Dharma, their wisdom being impartial, universally pure, and their actions of body, speech, and mind all entirely purified.

They abide in the dwelling of all Buddhas, belong to the lineage of all Buddhas, and perform the deeds of Buddha-wisdom, never regressing. They discern the immeasurable and boundless dwellings of all-knowledge; their illumination of omniscience accords with wisdom, being inconceivable and beyond the comprehension of all worlds.
Their wisdom is luminous and pure, knowing all phenomena; their subtle wisdom is immeasurable and boundless, skillfully able to discern all three periods of time.

Their wisdom is sublime, awakening all worlds, and they fully and perfectly know the meaning of the unsurpassed path. Throughout all worlds, they perform ineffable Buddha-works. Their wisdom never regresses, accomplishing the bodies of all Tathāgatas.

They enter the wisdom of calculation, definitively knowing all dharmas; they transcend words and sever the path of speech, yet are skillfully able to expound all syllables. They practice pure and wholesome dharmas, fulfilling the wisdom of Samantabhadra.

Within a single thought-moment, they are able to fully awaken to and comprehend all phenomena; according to the purity of sentient beings and according to the vehicle to which they should respond, they are able to bestow the gift of Dharma;
and with clear, pure wisdom, they understand the realm of all phenomena, the realm of all worlds, and the realm of all sentient beings.

Within a single thought-moment, they are able to fully know and see the dharma-realm of the three periods of time, the realm of the appearance in the world of all Tathāgatas, and the realm of all their teachings, never missing the proper time; reaching the realm of total purity, they awaken to all realms, all of which are ultimately perfected.

In a single thought-moment, one awakens to the fact that the mind, intellect, consciousness, and mental formations of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time are equal to those of all Buddhas;

and that sentient beings are boundless, worlds are boundless, the dharma-realm is boundless, the three periods of time are boundless, and the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas is boundless—to awaken to such things as these without any obstruction.

The wisdom of all Buddhas, the sovereignty of all Buddhas, and the turning of the wheel of the immeasurable and boundless abodes of all Buddhas; they dwell in the unimpeded dwelling, the dwelling of the unimpeded mind, and the dwelling of great compassion, extensively expounding the profound Dharma to teach and transform sentient beings with minds that never rest.
This is the tenth great power, the Dharma-abode of the Narayana-Banner Buddhas of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!

These are the ten kinds of great powers, the Dharma-abodes of the Narayana-Banner Buddhas of all Buddhas; they are immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable. All sentient beings of the three periods of time—whether Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas—cannot know them, except through the spiritual power of a Buddha."
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of fixed laws. What are these ten?
All Buddhas are certain to remain in the Tuṣita Heaven for the full duration of their lifespan;
all Buddhas are certain to manifest dwelling in the womb and give birth after ten months;
all Buddhas are certain to renounce their palaces and delight in practicing the life of a renunciant.
All Buddhas, seated in meditative concentration beneath the Bodhi tree, awaken to all dharmas;
all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, awaken to all Buddha-dharmas, universally manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata throughout all worlds;
all Buddhas, in meditative concentration, teach and transform according to the time, turning the wheel of the True Dharma.
All Buddhas certainly know that one has planted various roots of goodness according to the time, and thus bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment;
all Buddhas certainly act in accordance with the appropriate time, never failing in their Buddha-work;
all Buddhas certainly know that a Bodhisattva’s merits are fully perfected, and thus bestow upon them the prediction of enlightenment.
All Buddhas, in accordance with all the questions and challenges posed by sentient beings, are able to provide skillful answers within a single thought-moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of dharmas of certainty belonging to all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of dharmas; if there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata, they shall all swiftly attain ten kinds of retributive fruits.”
What are the ten? If there are sentient beings who see the Tathāgata, they will swiftly attain liberation from all evil realms;
if there are sentient beings who see the Tathāgata, they will swiftly attain the growth of all roots of goodness.
If there are sentient beings who see the Tathāgata, they will swiftly attain fulfillment in all roots of goodness;
if there are sentient beings who see the Tathāgata, they will swiftly attain rebirth in the pure and sublime heavens;
if there are sentient beings who see the Tathāgata, they will swiftly eliminate all doubts and delusions.

If there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata, those who have already resolved upon bodhicitta will swiftly attain the stage of non-retrogression, and those who have not yet resolved upon it will quickly give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

If there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata, those who have not yet attained the noble path that transcends birth will eliminate their views of existence and be swiftly led to correctly embrace the noble path that transcends birth.
If there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata, he will swiftly cause them to purify all worldly faculties and transcend all worldly states.
If there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata, they will swiftly attain the eradication of all obstacles;
if there are sentient beings who behold the Tathāgata, they will swiftly attain fearlessness and uninterrupted eloquence.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is how all sentient beings who behold the Buddhas shall all swiftly attain ten kinds of retributive fruits.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of pure dharmas that all bodhisattvas should constantly and correctly recollect. What are these ten?
All Buddhas possess past skillful means, which all bodhisattvas should constantly and correctly recollect.
All Buddhas possess pure and wondrous conduct; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant right mindfulness of this.
All Buddhas have fulfilled the pāramitās; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant right mindfulness of this.
All Buddhas have fulfilled their great vows; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant right mindfulness of this.
All Buddhas are the accumulation of merit; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant right mindfulness of them.
All Buddhas have practiced the holy life in the past; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant right mindfulness of them.
All Buddhas have attained equal and perfect enlightenment; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant right mindfulness of them.
All Buddhas possess immeasurable and boundless form-bodies; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant and correct mindfulness of this.
All Buddhas possess immeasurable and boundless realms of supernatural power; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant and correct mindfulness of this.
All Buddhas possess the ten powers and fearlessnesses; all Bodhisattvas should maintain constant and correct mindfulness of this.
"O Son of the Buddha!
