These are the ten kinds of pure dharmas of all Buddhas, which all Bodhisattvas should always maintain right mindfulness of.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of abodes of omniscience. What are these ten?
All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, fully know all the mental activities and mental states of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time across the entire dharma-realm.
All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, thoroughly and skillfully discern the various karmic retributions of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time;

all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, according to those among all sentient beings who are ready to be delivered, transform and teach them—whether by means of supernatural powers, or by means of exhortation and instruction, or by means of preaching the Dharma;

all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to skillfully grasp the mental states and characteristics of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions of the entire dharma-realm, manifesting the appearance of Tathāgatas in all worlds.

All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, according to the hopes, desires, and natures of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, cause those who are ready to be transformed and delivered to behold the Tathāgata;
all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, manifest for all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm the sovereign power of the Tathāgata’s sustaining spiritual authority;

all Buddhas, for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, speak of all Buddhas as being free from all burning afflictions, transforming and delivering sentient beings according to what is appropriate for them.
All Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, by means of the path that reaches all places, fully know all sentient beings within their various destinies throughout the entire dharma-realm;
all Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, cause all sentient beings throughout all directions and locations within the entire dharma-realm who call upon the Tathāgata to behold him;

all Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, according to the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm, cause them all to behold the physical form and color of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of abidings in omniscience of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of immeasurable and inconceivable samādhis. What are these ten?

All Buddhas are always in a state of meditative concentration regarding all phenomena without distraction; within a single thought-moment, they expound all phenomena for the sake of all sentient beings.

All Buddhas, regarding all dharma-realms and all sentient beings, are always in a state of concentration without distraction; within a single thought-moment, they analyze and expound for the sake of sentient beings the reality-limit of non-self.

All Buddhas, regarding all dharma-realms and the dharmas of the three periods of time, are always in a state of concentration without distraction; within a single thought-moment, they enter billions of samādhis.

All Buddhas, regarding all dharma-realms and the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, are always in a state of concentration without distraction; within a single thought-moment, they travel throughout and pervade all Buddha-lands.

All Buddhas, throughout the entire dharma-realm, universally manifest the various bodies of infinite and boundless Buddhas; they are constantly in samādhi and undisturbed, such that within a single thought-moment, there is no world in which they do not appear.

The physical, verbal, and mental actions of all Buddhas fill the entire dharma-realm; they are constantly in samādhi and undisturbed, such that within a single thought-moment, they discern and expound the desires and natures hidden within the minds of all sentient beings.

All Buddhas, throughout the entire dharma-realm and regarding the nature of all dharmas, are constantly in samādhi and undisturbed, such that within a single thought-moment, they are able to fully realize the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi) free from desire.

All Buddhas, regarding all dharma-realms and the dependent origination of all worlds, are eternally concentrated and undisturbed; within a single thought-moment, they analyze and expound all causes and conditions.

All Buddhas, regarding all dharma-realms and all mundane and supramundane phenomena, are eternally concentrated and undisturbed; within a single thought-moment, through infinite adornments, they universally manifest as all Buddhas for the sake of all sentient beings, without end.

All Buddhas, regarding all sentient beings and all dharma-realms, attain unimpeded meditative absorption, are eternally concentrated and undisturbed; within a single thought-moment, they reach the realm of all Buddhas, infinite liberations, and the ultimate further shore.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable samādhis of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
All Buddhas possess ten kinds of unimpeded liberation. What are these ten?
All Buddhas, within a single atom, are able to universally manifest the appearance in the world of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas.
All Buddhas, within a single atom, are able to universally manifest unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas turning the pure wheel of Dharma;
all Buddhas, within a single atom, teach and subdue unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings;
all Buddhas, within a single atom, universally manifest unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
All Buddhas, within a single atom, bestow the prediction of enlightenment upon unspeakably unspeakable numbers of bodhisattvas;
all Buddhas, within a single atom, universally manifest the appearance in the world of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
all Buddhas, within a single atom, universally manifest all Buddha-lands of the three periods of time.
All Buddhas, within a single atom, universally manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
all Buddhas, within a single atom, universally manifest all sentient beings of the three periods of time;
all Buddhas, within a single atom, universally manifest the Buddha-activities of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of unimpeded liberations of all Buddhas.
*The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Great Vaipulya*, Scroll Thirty-One.
The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Two, translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Twenty-Nine: The Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Marks. Chapter Twenty-Nine: The Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Marks.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Sons of the Buddha!
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well; I shall now describe for you the ocean of marks of the Tathāgata."

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of a great man called Radiant Purity, adorned with thirty-two kinds of jewels. It universally emits immeasurable nets of great light, illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions.

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of greatness called the Ocean of the Buddha’s Skillful Means of Universal Illumination. It is adorned with a perfect array of various jewels and embellished by diverse sovereign maṇi gems; arising from the world-realm of Vajra Radiance, it universally illumines the entire dharma-realm.

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of greatness called Cloud Filling the Dharma Realm; its wondrous jewel-light universally illumines all dharma realms, all worlds, the clouds of the Tathāgata’s ocean of merit and wisdom, and the clouds of the ocean of merit of the bodhisattvas throughout the seas of worlds in the ten directions.

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of greatness called Universal Illumination; it manifests all inconceivable Buddha-worlds with the wondrous light of diamond-maṇi jewels, which one can never tire of beholding, surging forth like a mass of various jewel-flowers, universally illuminating the Buddha-jewel light of the entire Dharma-realm.

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of greatness called the Lapis Lazuli Jewel, which universally illumines all dharma-realms with great sovereign clouds and the marks of the King of Maṇi Jewels. Adorned with various ornaments, it universally illuminates all worlds throughout the ten directions and extols the virtues of the Buddha. Arising from causes and conditions, it emits everywhere great clouds of the Tathāgata’s precious light, universally shining upon the bodhisattvas seated cross-legged at the tree of enlightenment. It universally manifests the sovereign spiritual powers of the bodhisattvas and awakens them to the power of the Tathāgata. Universally illuminating all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, it causes the earth to shake in six ways, and within the empty space of the great dharma-realm, it universally manifests immeasurable clouds of sovereign omniscience.

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of greatness called “Equanimity. It is a stainless jewel-ocean of clouds of lamps of the Tathāgata’s voice, which emits all manner of radiances that universally illuminate the oceans of merit of the bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions of the entire dharma-realm, and establishes the ocean of the banner of wisdom of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

Upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is a mark of greatness called the Vast Cloud of Buddha-Light. It is adorned with *ainara* jewels, wish-fulfilling king jewels, and *maṇi* king jewels, universally illuminating all worlds with clouds of radiant lamps of Dharma-realm Bodhisattvas, and universally illuminating the oceans of the wondrous forms and sounds of all Tathāgatas, as well as the oceans of worlds and the oceans of pure Buddha-powers.

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Perfect Radiance,’ adorned with various jewel flowers and the light of the sovereign *vaiḍūrya* maṇi-jewel. It praises the Dharma-body and all Bodhisattvas; throughout the oceans of worlds in all ten directions, it extols the stage of the Tathāgata, causing all sentient beings to incline toward the realm of the Tathāgata’s powers. It universally manifests the stainless, pure, and immaculate ground of the infinite and boundless Tathāgatas, emitting a great radiance that shines everywhere upon all Buddha-worlds.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Radiant Cloud of the Treasury of Bodhisattva Practices. Within immeasurable worlds, the Tathāgatas emit immeasurable rays of light from various kinds of jewels, universally illuminating all Buddha-lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm. They produce the sublime voices of immeasurable Tathāgatas, each clearly and distinctly expounding the profound Great Dharma of the Tathāgatas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Illumination,’ adorned with vaidūrya, indra-vajra jewels, and pure maṇi jewels of immeasurable colors. It radiates light the color of vaidūrya that universally illuminates all oceans, issues the infinite, subtle, and wondrous voices of the Buddha that fill all worlds of the ten directions, and universally manifests the infinite transformation bodies of the ocean of all Buddhas’ wisdom.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Awakening. The right side of the Buddha’s crown is adorned with the flames of various jewel-flowers; it adorns the sites of enlightenment in all worlds, purifies all dharma-realm worlds, causes all falsehoods to be completely liberated, and awakens to the pure dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Radiance. Adorned with the sovereign wish-fulfilling jewel of the ocean of mind, it embellishes the crown of the Tathāgata’s head and universally illuminates the clouds of bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions. It nurtures the supreme body of wisdom and the dharma-body, traverses the ocean of all Tathāgatas’ marks, and fulfills the clouds of the dharma-realm of all bodhisattvas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of All Adornments,’ which is universally illumined by vajra-lapis lazuli flowers and adorns the ocean of all dharma-realms. It is adorned with world-systems of various precious lotus flowers, filling the entirety of the dharma-realm; and the four kinds of bodhisattva practices and the sovereign lion’s roar fill the ocean of all dharma-realms.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Cloud of Ocean-like Practice of the Buddha’s Samādhi,’ which adorns the entire ocean of the dharma-realm; in every thought-moment, it universally manifests the adornments of immeasurable Tathāgatas, filling all inconceivable worlds of the dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Universally Illuminating the Ocean of Transformations. It is a wondrous jewel lotus like Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, which gives rise to an infinite ocean of jewel radiance. Arising from the intention of the Buddha and manifested by Vairocana, it brings forth an infinite ocean of all transformations.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Liberation of All Tathāgatas,’ adorned with stainless, supreme jewels. It universally illuminates and adorns the lion thrones of all Tathāgatas; within those thrones, it manifests the forms and images of all Tathāgatas, emitting great jewel-light and expounding the vast ocean of immeasurable Buddha-dharmas, thereby adorning the oceans of all Buddha-lands.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Awakening the Cloud of the Buddha-lineage. From sapphire flowers and golden jewel lotuses, he emits immeasurable clouds of light of the true Dharma-jewels, purifying the radiance of all Tathāgatas and universally manifesting throughout the entire pure Dharma-realm. This indestructible liberation of jewel-light enters everywhere into the profound ocean of all Dharma-realms, universally manifesting an ocean of immeasurable sovereign powers.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Wheel of Immeasurable Jewel Radiance,’ which manifests past pure roots of goodness, gives rise to the sun of pure wisdom, and universally illumines the ocean of the Dharma of wisdom throughout the ten directions.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Radiance and Sovereignty. From the jewel at the crown of the Tathāgata’s head, the exquisite flower of liberation and the lapis lazuli radiance universally illumine the ocean of all dharma realms and Buddhas, manifesting within them the oceans of all Buddha-lands, fully perfected with the wisdom of the Tathāgata.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Entering All-Pervading Illumination. This precious mark of the Tathāgata is pure and adorned, universally illuminating the treasury of wondrous wisdom of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas throughout the entire, infinite, and boundless Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Luminous Pure Cloud,’ which emits hundreds of thousands of immeasurable rays of light from precious flowers and lapis lazuli moons, universally illuminating all Buddha-fields throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, and universally manifesting all Tathāgatas of the ten directions.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Enlightened Radiance. All the jewel-lights universally illuminate all Buddha-realms throughout the entire Dharma-realm as the Buddhas turn the pure wheel of Dharma; they all emit the wondrous clouds of light of the Tathāgata, universally illuminating all worlds in the ten directions.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Universal Cloud Manifesting All Adornments,’ with immeasurable jewel radiance; in a single thought-moment, throughout the entire dharma-realm, it universally manifests all bodhisattvas sitting at their sites of enlightenment beneath the bodhi trees and attaining perfect awakening, and it can also universally manifest all Buddhas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud-Cause of the Dharma Realm,’ adorned with wish-fulfilling, wondrous jewels; one can never tire of beholding it, as it emits a vast net of great jewel-light, universally manifesting the ocean of karmic retributions of all sentient beings.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Cloud of the Pure Wheel of Dharma Shining Universally. It is able to purify the True Dharma of the Tathāgata, universally illuminating and adorning all Buddha-fields, and profoundly understanding the ocean of all inconceivable dharmas. It shines universally upon the dharma-realm of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, giving birth to immeasurable emanations of the Tathāgata.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Universal Illumination of the Ocean-Clouds of All Buddhas,’ by which he is entirely free from obstructions throughout the ocean-like seas of all worlds in the ten directions, and universally beholds the ocean-clouds of all Tathāgatas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Pure Lamp Cloud; through skillful means, he enters deeply into the inconceivable ocean-clouds of the dharma-realm of all sentient beings, all bodhisattvas, and all Tathāgatas, universally illuminating them with clouds of awakening throughout the entire dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Discerning the Dharma Realm. The wisdom of the Tathāgata shines extensively upon all the bodhisattvas of the Buddha-ground, the infinite oceans of Dharma, and the infinite Buddha-fields, causing all sentient beings to enter the realm of the Buddha and to become fully endowed with the vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, the equal wisdom of the Buddhas, and all forms of clear knowledge.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Illumination Abiding Peacefully Throughout All World-Oceans,’ which is a cloud of jewel-light radiance throughout all dharma-realms and the realm of space; one can never tire of beholding it, as it universally manifests the bodies of all bodhisattvas and all Tathāgatas at the sites of enlightenment, giving rise to immeasurable clouds of universal merit.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great person called ‘Cloud of Blazing Flames of All Jewels. From within this mark between the Buddha’s eyebrows, he produces immeasurable light from pure jewels that universally illumines all worlds in the ten directions, purely illuminating the practices of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. The light of the Dharma King universally illumines the Dharma-realm, fully able to nourish all lights and the adornments of light throughout the entire Dharma-realm. It universally illumines the oceans of all Bodhisattvas and the clouds of the Tathāgata’s powers, universally shining upon all Buddha-lands in the ten directions.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Adorned with All Dharma Realms. The cranial protuberance (uṣṇīṣa) of the Tathāgata gradually rises in succession, adorned with Jāmbūnada gold and various jewels, emitting manifold golden radiances. In every thought-moment, it universally manifests all Buddhas of all worlds, able to universally illumine all Buddha-fields and adorn the treasuries of merit of all Bodhisattvas. This cranial protuberance of the Tathāgata can fully adorn the thirty-two marks, and can also adorn the entire dharma realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Universal Illumination Cloud Pervading the Dharma Realm. This mark between the Buddha’s eyebrows is able to universally illuminate all wondrous jewels, all varieties of colors, all suns and moons, and all oceans of Buddhas; it gives rise to infinite oceans of light throughout the ten directions, adorns the bodies of all Tathāgatas, and proclaims the ocean of teachings of all Tathāgatas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Sovereign Cloud; the Buddha’s pure eye is adorned with various jewels, and his wisdom-eye is pure, being unobstructed throughout all dharma-realms, manifesting all things through clouds of auspicious radiance.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of the great person’s sublime and wondrous nose, adorned with pure and myriad jewels, covered by the exquisite colors of all precious gems. It is like a cloud of Buddha-jewel flowers, inconceivable to all Bodhisattvas, through which he fully knows the oceans of the Buddhas and all sentient beings.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of a great person’s broad and long tongue, which is able to completely cover all the oceans and clouds of the worlds in the ten directions. It is the fruit of all jewel-kings obtained through the cultivation of roots of goodness in the past; its pure radiance universally illuminates the mind of ethical discipline (*śīla*) throughout the entire Dharma-realm, and it also illumines all Buddhas of the three periods of time, fully adorning the entire Dharma-realm. It produces immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous sounds, adorned with inconceivable jewels, universally shining upon infinite oceans of light. The Buddha’s sublime voice completely fills all the world-oceans within the entire Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Dharma-realm Earth Cloud. His tongue and palms rest upon all manner of jewels as adornment; they abide in all dharmas and give rise to the perfect sounds of the Buddhas of the ten directions, capable of purifying all Buddha-fields and discerning the inconceivable ocean-clouds of the voices of all Buddhas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud Following the Dharma-realm. This sublime mark at the tip of his tongue is adorned with pure golden jewels, from which it issues forth immeasurable golden light that universally illumines the oceans of all Tathāgatas. He utters the great lion’s roar and vibrates with wondrous sounds that reach every single world; there are no sentient beings who do not hear them. Attained through cultivation over inconceivable eons, they universally manifest an ocean of all sounds and universally illuminate all sentient beings, who never tire of hearing them.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called the Cloud of the Dharma-Gate of Equality. This mark on the tip of the Buddha’s tongue makes immeasurable Buddha-lands entirely pure; it is adorned with wish-fulfilling wonderful jewels and produces immeasurable varieties of sounds that praise the dharma-realm of all Buddhas, universally manifesting the dharma-realm of all Bodhisattvas. Clouds of sublime merit universally cover all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, penetrating deeply into the teachings of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. It manifests all stainless, various jewel-adorned, pure Buddha-lands and is able to universally illuminate all Buddha-lands.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of the great person’s upper and lower jaws, adorned with the pure *indranīla* lapis lazuli jewel; within it lie all the grounds of the dharma-realm, completely filled by clouds of bodhisattvas. It produces the radiant light of stainless, wondrous jewels, universally illuminating various clouds of incense and various clouds of lamps throughout the ten directions. It shines upon the inner pavilions of the bodhisattvas, discerning the oceans of all Buddha-lands. Through the power of skillful means and sovereign spiritual authority, it universally manifests inconceivable clouds of the dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called the Buddha’s Great Tooth Cloud. On the lower right side of the Tathāgata’s face is the mark of the great tooth, adorned with various jewels, emitting great wheels of light that universally illumine the Dharma-realm and the bodies of all Buddhas;
it universally emits nets of light that illuminate the oceans of worlds and the oceans of sentient beings in the ten directions, adorned with exquisite wheels of peace and stability.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Jewel-Flame Sumeru-Treasury. On the upper right molar of the Tathāgata’s face, there is a treasury of the sovereign jewel-king of supreme fragrant-flame clouds that shines as an adornment; it emits precious light equal in extent to the Dharma-realm, and within each and every ray of light, there are universally manifested the sovereign powers of all Buddhas and the adorned sites of enlightenment of all Buddha-fields.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Illuminating Lamp-Cloud of All Jeweled Sumeru Mountains. On the lower left side of the Tathāgata’s face is the mark of his large tooth, which analytically explains all marks. It is adorned with a wonderful wheel of skillful means consisting of fragrant flowers and various jewels, emitting clouds of precious light that universally illumine all oceans of worlds and universally manifest before all Buddhas upon lion-thrones within lotus-treasury worlds, surrounded by a retinue of oceans of clouds of stainless Bodhisattvas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Universal Radiance of the Buddha-Cloud. On the left side of the Tathāgata’s face, the mark of the large upper tooth is adorned with pure multitudes of jewels and a network-wheel of Jambūnada gold flowers. It produces inconceivable and subtle sounds, universally manifests the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas, and accomplishes the merits of all Bodhisattvas. It universally illuminates all of space, as well as the dharma of language, inexhaustible clouds of dharma, the ocean of all dharmas, the voices of all Buddhas, and all jewels. It gives rise to the various wondrous voices that distinguish all Buddhas, filling the entire Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called *kanakamṛgaśīrṣa*. From between each of the Tathāgata’s teeth, there emerge clouds of gateways to infinite oceans of marks, with various colored jewels emitting great oceans of light in the color of Jambūnada gold, universally illuminating all worlds and all Tathāgatas throughout the entire Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of All Jewel Grounds. This mark on the Tathāgata’s right shoulder consists of the colors of all jewels, the color of pure lotuses, and the color of luminous, pure jewels; its blazing radiance universally illuminates the clouds of the inner Dharma-treasury of all Bodhisattvas, fully shining upon the oceans of Dharma of all Tathāgatas.”

The Tathāgata’s right shoulder is the mark of a great man, level and full, with the pure color of Jambūnada gold; it universally illumines the Dharma-realm of the Bodhisattva’s wheel of Dharma and shines upon all sovereign wish-fulfilling jewel kings.

The Tathāgata possesses the mark of a great man on his left shoulder, with the color of a Jambūnada lotus; adorned by the Tathāgata’s ocean of perfected merits, it universally emits infinite nets of light that fully illuminate all worlds and the Dharma-realm, manifesting clouds of the Tathāgata’s immeasurable and sovereign spiritual powers.

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Pervasive Universal Radiance. The mark on the Tathāgata’s left shoulder is adorned with various jewels and emits light of Jambūnada gold, which completely fills all dharma-realms, universally illuminating the oceans of all Tathāgatas, and adorns the oceans of all Buddha-fields with various precious fragrances.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Illumination and Adornment. Without shifting his right shoulder, he brings forth the immeasurable light of the Buddha-lamps and lets fall clouds of the Dharma-realm, filling the assembly of Bodhisattvas and universally illuminating and adorning the entire Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Ocean-Crest Cloud; upon the Tathāgata’s chest is the adornment of a sea of supreme and wondrous marks, soft, supple, and smooth, adorned with flaming wheels of various jewels, universally pure, and emitting the sounds of the ocean of profound Dharma.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Cloud of Universally Manifesting Supreme and Wondrous Continuity. The Tathāgata’s right flank is supremely wondrous and pure; the ground of the Dharma-realm wheel serves as its adornment, covered all over by a net of pure jewels, giving rise to immeasurable clouds of Tathāgata emanations that universally illumine the entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Universal Manifestation of the Tathāgata Cloud,’ which is a jewel crown of the merit-treasury of the Bodhisattva Supreme and Wondrous Merit Storehouse. It is a cloud of supreme radiance, free from defilement and utterly pure, universally manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions and revealing the ocean of pure practices of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; seated beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment, he has attained equal and perfect awakening.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Blooming Flowers,’ a manifestation of the Tathāgata’s continuous succession of supreme and wondrous merits. Adorned with wheels of various exquisite jewel-flowers, it emits light of fragrant flames, universally manifesting all worlds in the forms and colors of lotuses.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Delightful Golden Cloud,’ which is a continuous succession of the most sublime and wondrous merits from the treasury of all jewel-kings. It emits wheels of light from mani-jewels from the heart-treasury of all jewels; stainless and pure, it is exceedingly lofty and prominent, universally illuminating the treasury of internal skillful means and merits of all Buddhas, and universally illuminating the entire dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Supreme Ocean Cloud; it emits the fragrance-light of supreme space-jewels that universally illumines all places of enlightenment throughout the ten directions, and is filled with complete lapis lazuli jewel incense-lamp garlands pervading the ten directions.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Lightning-Light. Below it is the second supreme merit: the mark of the level ground where lotuses swirl to the right; upon these pure lotus flowers sit the assembly of Bodhisattvas, who radiate the light of the Buddha-treasury, universally illuminating the ocean of the Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Universally Manifesting the Dharma Realm,’ the third ocean of supreme marks; it fully accomplishes and perfects all oceans of jewel-adorned lands, universally illuminating and revealing the infinite dharma realms of bodhisattvas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Universal Illumination of the Supreme Cloud,’ the fourth ocean of supreme marks. It emits an ocean of stainless light from various jewels that universally illuminates all dharma-realms, all Tathāgatas, the adornments of all worlds, and the ocean of all sentient beings.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Wondrous Sounds that Turn All Wheels of Dharma. This superior mark of the lower body is stainless and pure; it is the radiant light of the fragrance of the path of all true dharmas, which illumines the ocean of marks within the hearts of all Buddhas throughout the entire dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Adornment,’ the tenth supreme mark. It proclaims the pure conduct, awakening, stainless purity, and radiance of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions; it reveals the ocean of all-knowledge of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and it adorns the ocean of all Buddha-lands.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of a great man’s palm, complete with a jeweled wheel of a thousand spokes, adorned with various kinds of precious gems. It emits a great radiance that universally illumines the Dharma-realm; it turns the Wheel of the True Dharma, universally shining upon the oceans of all Tathāgatas, filling the oceans of all Buddha-merits, and adorning the Dharma-realm with various wondrous jewels.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Ocean-Illuminating Cloud; the Tathāgata’s precious hands are adorned with various jewels, universally emitting clouds of flames of pure moonlight that adorn the oceans of worlds of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas throughout space, and extol the ocean of Bodhisattva practices.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Adornment. The Tathāgata’s wondrous hands are adorned with *indranīla* and *vaiḍūrya* jewel flowers, which universally illuminate all dharma-realms and all worlds. They cause the Bodhisattva Lotus-Womb to dwell securely within the treasure-trove, adorning all sites of enlightenment throughout the ten directions, and universally illuminating the ocean-clouds of all Buddhas and their pure Dharma-bodies.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Illumination of the Stainless Lamp,’ which is the pure radiance of jewels. It emits nets of pure light that universally illuminate the ten directions, everywhere producing clouds of transformation-nets that adorn the pure jewel-light of Bodhisattvas, bringing them to the ultimate fulfillment of the ocean of all dharmic practices and reaching the further shore.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Ocean-Cloud Treasury of All Jewels Universally Manifesting as Clouds,’ which adorns the Tathāgata’s lotus, fills all jewel-lotuses, and emits clouds of precious light that universally illumine the entire Dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Pure Cloud of Universal Illumination. It emits an ocean of jewel-flame radiance that illumines the entire dharma-realm; it is adorned with the light-flames of all manner of fragrances, universally manifests jewel-flower flame-light, causes the entire network of Buddha-worlds to be completely purified and adorned, and universally illuminates all sites of enlightenment.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Sapphire Lamp Cloud; it universally illuminates and adorns the ground of all worlds with the colors of every kind of jewel, radiating the golden light of all Buddhas and being adorned with every form of ornamentation, manifesting all dharma-gates within a single thought-moment.”
“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of the Lamp of Wisdom; adorned with vajra-jewel flowers, it emits the golden light of Jambūnada, universally illuminating all worlds.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Abiding in the Lotus Light Cloud,’ adorned with exquisite flowers of various jewels, which emits a great net of light rays that covers all the Sumeru mountains throughout every world-system.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Tathāgata Cloud Filling the Dharma Realm. Adorned with stainless, pure jewels, it emits a great radiance that universally illumines all Buddha-worlds, wherein one sees the Tathāgata seated upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury.
Furthermore, it universally illumines the entire dharma realm, manifesting all marks:

the Tathāgata’s wondrous hand universally manifests all signs of mastery; its thousand-spoked wheels are perfectly pure and complete, adorned with various kinds of precious gems. This Buddha-hand fills all clouds of lands and universally illumines all clouds of the dharma realms.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Accomplishment of the Ocean-Clouds of Buddha-fields. From the jewel-mark on the right hand of the Buddha, there issues pure light from the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and pure flames; it shines everywhere like the moon in clear water, producing myriad jewel flowers and generating all manner of wondrous jewel sounds, universally manifesting the oceans of all Buddha-fields.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Abiding in All Jewel Clouds,’ which universally illumines the dharma-realm of the jewel-treasuries of all Buddhas. From the mark of his fingers, he produces clouds of sovereign wish-fulfilling jewels, adorned with various gems and emitting vast nets of great light. These illuminate the clouds of all dharma-realms and the clouds of all Buddhas; they universally illuminate and adorn the oceans of merit of all Bodhisattvas, and produce an ocean of sublime sounds of the pure conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, which is heard in every Buddha-field without exception.

Furthermore, they open and illuminate the minds of all Bodhisattvas, causing them to fully satisfy immeasurable great vows; they are adorned with sovereign maṇi-jewel kings, and various sun-discs universally illuminate the entire dharma-realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of the treasury of great beings’ horses; it is concealed on the right side, adorned with all manner of jewels, universally illuminating the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, adorning the ocean of the dharma-realm with every kind of jewel, and producing the subtle, wondrous sounds of the adornments of all Tathāgatas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Single Mark Manifesting an Ocean-Cloud of All Marks. When the Tathāgata sits upon the seat of the field of merit, adorned with all manner of jewels, he produces immeasurable, inconceivable, wondrous jewel-light that universally illumines all dharma-realms in the ten directions. It universally manifests and distinguishes all various marks, appearing as clouds of a single mark, illuminating and revealing the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of the Ocean of All Dharma Realms,’ which universally illumines the seats of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions, as well as the wheels of Dharma and the oceans of Dharma within all dharma realms, and is able to manifest clouds of all manner of forms.

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Universal Manifestation Cloud. The right thigh of the Tathāgata is adorned with various jewels and emits various fragrant lights of the sublime Dharma; dwelling in accordance with reality, it produces all manner of sounds and is adorned by all kinds of jewel-kings. In every thought-moment, it is able to manifest ocean-clouds of the mind-king.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Universal Illumination and Dedication to All Oceans. The left thigh of the Tathāgata is entirely filled with all oceans of jewels; it dwells in accordance with the adornments of the ocean of Dharma and emits an ocean of all radiances, which are able to universally illuminate the infinite oceans of Buddhas within all sentient beings.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of a great man: his right calf is like that of the Eṇeya deer. He emits the golden light of Jambūnada, which universally illumines all worlds, causes immeasurable Buddha-fields to tremble, and produces the voice of the Buddha, heard everywhere by all. He brings forth immeasurable emanations of Bodhisattvas that fill all Buddha-worlds and the realm of empty space; emitting pure and radiant light, they adorn and universally illuminate everything, causing all Buddha-fields to become utterly pure. The clouds of dharmas from the treasury of the Bodhisattva’s transformations pervade the entire dharma-realm, just like space.”

“The Tathāgata possesses the mark of a great man: his left calf is like that of an *aineya* deer, with a color like refined gold. It constantly emits the wondrous light of all jewels, filling immeasurable Buddha-worlds, opening up the Dharma-transformations of all Buddhas, and adorning the immeasurable oceans of the Buddhas' Dharma.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Manifestation of All Buddha-fields within the Tips of Hairs,’ wherein from a single pore he emits the treasury of all jewel-lights, universally illuminating all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions;
and from a single pore, he manifests clouds of the sovereign dharmas of all Tathāgatas across all dharma-realms.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Adorned by the Ocean of Bodhisattvas. From beneath the Tathāgata’s adamantine feet, which are the color of Jambūnada gold, he emits a net of light from all jewels that fills the clouds of Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions. He unfolds the Dharma-transformations of all bodhisattvas, gives rise to the infinite transformations of bodhisattvas, and emits the light of all precious fragrances. Abiding in the ocean of bodhisattvas, he is able to traverse all Buddha-fields in a single step.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Luminous Pure Cloud. The entire surface of the Buddha’s foot-sole is adorned with all manner of jewels, emitting wondrous jewel-light that manifests the great treasury of light of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, universally illuminating the clouds of immeasurable Tathāgatas.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Awakening, which universally covers the spaces between all the fingers of the Tathāgata. Adorned with the kings of all jewels, it emits various jewel lights; in every thought-moment, it manifests the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas, universally illuminating the infinite oceans of the Buddhas' teachings, manifesting all sites of enlightenment, and shining throughout all future kalpas to the furthest limits.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Ocean-Cloud Illuminating the Entire Dharma Realm. Beneath the Tathāgata’s feet is the wheel-mark with its thousand spokes, adorned in various ways, emitting hundreds of thousands of multicolored jewel lights that universally illuminate all world-oceans throughout the entire dharma realm. It is a treasury of exquisite adornments consisting of the flames of many jewel lamps, universally illuminating all Buddhas of the ten directions; adorned with immeasurable fragrant light, it universally illuminates the entire pure ocean of the dharma realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Manifesting the Ocean-Clouds of All Buddhas. It is as pure as space, illuminating the ocean of all dharmas and filling the ten directions. It gives rise to clouds of all bodhisattvas and clouds of wondrous sounds, adorned with clouds of various precious flowers, fragrances, lamps, and flames, manifesting a universal illumination of all worlds.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Sovereign Radiance,’ adorned with various jewels, manifesting the radiance of all Buddhas, purifying the ocean of the Dharma-realm and all sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). It constantly emits the wisdom-radiance of the Tathāgata; all manifold marks are entirely of a single mark, for the Dharma-realm is without confusion, yet adorned in myriad ways.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Sounds of the Ocean of the Dharma Realm. At the rear portion of the Tathāgata’s feet, adorned with various jewels, it universally illumines all oceans of the dharma realms; it is the sovereign adornment of all Buddhas, universally entering the wheel of transformation and covering all dharma realms. From each and every body, it produces clouds of wondrous sounds of the dharma realm.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Profound Treasure Source,’ adorned with myriad jewels, emitting Jambūnada-golden light, a perfect radiance that universally illuminates the Dharma-realm of the worlds of the ten directions, manifesting all manner of adornments of the site of enlightenment.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud Illuminating the Dharma Realm, Adorned with the Treasury of Indranīla Jewels and the Radiance of All Jewel Moons,’ which, in every thought-moment, is able to manifest the ocean of the Tathāgata’s teachings.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called the Universal Cloud Treasury Right-Space Jewel Cloud; its supreme jewel radiance illuminates the treasury of all Buddhas’ sites of enlightenment and thrones, manifesting the adornment of *vajra-indranīla* jewels.”

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘Cloud of Equal Radiance,’ adorned with exquisite flowers of various jewels. It produces the sounds of the profoundly deep Dharma-realm, pervading all Dharma-realms and the realm of empty space. Within each and every mark, it universally illumines the oceans of all Tathāgatas, entering the Buddha’s profound mastery and the ocean of the Bodhisattva Dharma-realm, expounding that which is inexhaustible.”

The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called Cloud of Manifesting Adornments. It is adorned with various jewels of pure Jambūnada gold and universally emits various kinds of wondrously colored light, illuminating all adorned Buddha-lands. Clouds of Buddhas fill immeasurable worlds, adorning the ocean of the Bodhisattvas' sovereign dharmas, universally illuminating the merits of all Buddhas and the treasuries of liberation of all Bodhisattvas, thereby adorning the Dharma-realm.

“The Tathāgata possesses a mark of a great man called ‘The Cloud of Universal Manifestation of the Sovereignty of All Buddhas. It turns the wheels of all jewels, is adorned with myriad gems, and radiates the inconceivable light of the Tathāgata. Its sublime fragrance is universally perceived throughout all worlds and the infinite oceans of Buddhas; it produces the ocean of all Buddha-voices and manifests clouds of the sovereign power of Buddhas through the gateways of Bodhisattvas in all worlds.”
O Son of the Buddha!

Within the body of the Buddha, there are such great marks of a Buddha as these, numbering as many as the atoms in ten oceans of Lotus Treasury worlds; all his limbs and joints are adorned with various kinds of wondrous jewels.

Chapter 30: The Merit of the Radiance of the Minor Marks of the Buddha The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Great Vaipulya, Chapter Thirty: The Merit of the Radiance of the Minor Marks of the Buddha. At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, saying:

“The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha possesses a secondary mark of excellence called ‘Ocean King. It emits a radiance named ‘Luminous Purity,’ which has seven million asaṃkhyeya rays as its retinue.”

Furthermore, when the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is in the Tuṣita Heaven, he emits a great radiance called "Banner King" (Dhvaja-rāja), which universally illumines lands as numerous as the atoms within ten worlds. It shines everywhere upon the sentient beings in the hells there, extinguishing their suffering and pain, and causing the ten faculties—eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—and all the karmic activities of those beings to become entirely pure. Once those sentient beings behold this light, they all experience great joy; at the end of their lives, they are all reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
Having been born in the heavens, they hear a celestial wondrous sound called "Inconceivable Joy. This voice speaks to the sons of gods, saying:

"Because of non-negligence, because of having planted roots of goodness in the presence of the Buddhas, because of meeting spiritual friends, and by the majestic spiritual power of Vairocana Buddha, you have ended your lives in the hells and been born here in the heavens."

Beneath the feet of the Tathāgata, within the thousand-spoked wheels, there is a wondrous radiance named Universal Illumination King. From the various beautiful parts of that Ocean King’s body, forty vast radiances are emitted; the first is named Pure Merit. It universally illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms in sixty billion nayutas of Buddha-fields, according to the spheres of sentient beings, according to the roots of goodness they have planted, and according to the inclinations of their minds, even extending its light to the Avīci Hell. All sentient beings therein, upon the end of their lives, are reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
Having been born in the heavens, they hear the wondrous sounds of the devas and speak these words:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"O sons of gods!
The Bodhisattva Vairocana now dwells in the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement; you should pay him reverent homage and mindfulness.
At that time, having heard these subtle and wondrous words of exhortation from the devas, the sons of gods then thought to themselves:
"How marvelous! How marvelous!
By what cause has this subtle and wondrous sound emerged?"
At that time, the voice addressed the devaputras, saying:
"This celestial voice of mine is accomplished through various virtuous merits. O devaputras!"

Just as I speak of a "self" yet do not cling to a self or to what belongs to a self, so too it is with all Buddhas: they themselves declare themselves to be Buddhas, yet they do not cling to a self or to what belongs to a self.
O sons of the gods!
Just as my voice does not come from the east, nor from the south, west, or north, nor from the four intermediate directions, nor from above or below—O sons of the gods!
The attainment of Buddhahood through karmic retribution is likewise so: it does not come from the ten directions. O Sons of Heaven!

It is just as when you were formerly in the hells—you did not come from the ten directions; rather, because you were bound by inverted views and delusion, you obtained bodies in hell, yet fundamentally there was no place of origin. Just as the light of King Universal Radiance does not come from the ten directions, so too my celestial voice does not come from the ten directions. It is merely through the power of the roots of goodness of samādhi that such subtle and wondrous sounds are produced, and through the power of the Prajñāpāramitā that such sovereign spiritual powers are manifested.
"O sons of the gods!

For example, the various exquisite palaces and manifold instruments of pleasure belonging to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven on Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, do not come from the ten directions; my celestial voice is likewise so."
"O sons of the gods!

Suppose one were to grind into dust as many worlds as there are atoms in a hundred billion nayutas of Buddha-fields; suppose there were as many sentient beings as there are such atoms, and I were to preach the Dharma to them, causing each to rejoice according to their needs. Yet, toward them, I would give rise to no mind of aversion, no mind of weariness, no mind of negligence, and no mind of pride."
"O sons of the gods!

It is likewise with the Bodhisattva Rocana, who dwells in the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement. From within the secondary marks upon his right palm, he emits a single ray of light that gives rise to immeasurable powers of sovereign spiritual mastery, which cannot be known by any sentient beings, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas."
"You all should go to the Bodhisattva Vairocana, pay him respectful homage, and do not become attached to the five desires which obstruct all roots of goodness.
O sons of the gods!"
Just as at the end of a kalpa, the fire consumes Mount Sumeru until it is entirely extinguished, so too, O sons of the gods,

when the five desires that entangle the mind are eliminated through the cultivation of the Buddha-remembrance samādhi (buddhānusmṛti-samādhi), they are all utterly destroyed. Therefore, O sons of the gods, you should know how to repay this kindness, and with single-minded devotion, pay reverent homage to the Bodhisattva Vairocana.
"O sons of the gods!
Those sentient beings who do not know how to repay kindness, after casting off this body, will enter the three evil realms.
O sons of the gods!"
In the past, while you were in hell, you received the grace of this light; having abandoned that hell, you have now been reborn in this heaven, and you ought to nurture those roots of goodness.
"O sons of the gods!
It is like me, the Devī; though neither male nor female, I am able to give birth to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of inconceivable dharmas.
O sons of the gods!"

Just as the sons of gods, daughters of gods, the five objects of sensual pleasure, and the palaces and gardens are all like me—neither arising nor ceasing—so too are form, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness. If one knows them thus, this is called being able to enter the ocean of the profound samādhi of non-attachment.

At that time, when the sons of the gods heard these sounds, they were filled with immeasurable joy. They all manifested ten thousand clouds of flowers, ten thousand clouds of incense, ten thousand clouds of music, ten thousand clouds of banners, ten thousand clouds of canopies, and ten thousand clouds of praises. Having created these manifestations, they proceeded to the palace where the Bodhisattva Vairocana resided; there they paid respectful homage and offerings, standing to one side, yet they did not see the Bodhisattva Vairocana.
At that time, there was a son of heaven who spoke these words:
"This Bodhisattva has now passed away and been born into the house of King Śuddhodana; riding upon a sandalwood palatial tower, he dwells within the womb of Queen Māyā."

At that time, the sons of the gods, using their divine eyes, beheld the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vairocana being reverently honored and made offerings to by the Brahmakāyika devas and the various devas of the desire realm.
At that time, the sons of the gods spoke these words:

"If we do not first go to pay our respects and make offerings to Rocana Bodhisattva, even for the duration of a single thought-moment, remaining in Tuṣita Heaven with a mind of attachment and delight, then that would be improper for us."
At that time, each of the devaputras, together with a retinue of ten nayutas of devaputras, desired to descend from heaven to Jambudvīpa to go to where the Bodhisattva was.
Then, the Deva Subhāṣita said to the devaputra:
"The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva does not pass away from this life to be reborn in that realm; rather, according to those who are to be transformed, he causes them all to see him there."
"O sons of the gods!

Just as I am now not seen by the eye yet am able to produce sounds, so too it is with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abiding in the Samādhi of Freedom from Defilement: he is not seen by the eye, yet he manifests death and rebirth in various places; he abandons falsehood, eliminates pride, and remains free from all attachment."
Therefore, O sons of the gods!

You should swiftly resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, purify your minds, and abide in the precepts of dignified conduct (*īryāpatha*). You should repent of all karmic obstructions, afflictive obstructions, retributive obstructions, and obstructions of false views. By means of virtuous actions of body, speech, and mind as vast as the Dharma-realm, the realm of space, and the realm of sentient beings—and by means of bodies, heads, and tongues as numerous as the realm of sentient beings—you should repent of these four obstructions.
At that time, having heard these words, all the devaputras were filled with great joy; their minds became supple and gentle, and they asked the celestial voice:
"How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva repent of his transgressions?"
At that time, by the power of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s samādhi and the power of the devas’ roots of goodness, the celestial voice replied to the sons of the gods, saying:

"The karmic obstructions and other sins do not come from the east, the south, the west, or the north, nor from the four intermediate directions, nor from above or below, to accumulate within the mind."
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that these karmas arise from inversion and do not give rise to doubt or confusion.
O sons of the gods!

Just as my celestial voice speaks of conduct according to karmic retribution, according to precepts, according to joy, according to meditative concentration, and according to cessation—so too it is when the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas speak of the karma of sentient beings' greed, anger, and delusion; in reality, there is no self and nothing belonging to a self. It is exactly like this.
All the karmic actions performed cannot be found even if sought throughout the ten directions.
O sons of the gods!
Just as my celestial voice cannot be heard by sentient beings of meager merit—except for those sentient beings in the hells who are destined to receive transformation—so it is with these matters.
O sons of the gods!
Sound is neither born nor extinguished; all karmic actions are likewise neither born nor extinguished, yet one receives their retribution in accordance with the performance of those actions.
"O sons of the gods!
Just as the sounds I produce cannot be exhausted throughout immeasurable kalpas,
so it is, O sons of the gods!"
If one claims that sounds come and go, one falls into extreme views; all Buddhas do not speak of annihilation or permanence, except as a skillful means for teaching sentient beings.
"O sons of the gods!

Just as my celestial voice is heard throughout the worlds of the ten directions by all those who are ready to be transformed, so too it is with all Buddhas: they are seen by all those who are ready to be delivered."
"O sons of the gods!

It is as if there were a bright, pure mirror of glistening gold and crystal, equal in size to ten worlds. Within that mirror, one would see immeasurable lands—all mountains and rivers, all sentient beings, the hells, and the hungry ghosts—whether beautiful or ugly, their various forms and appearances all appearing therein."
"O sons of the gods!
What do you think? Do those various reflections come and enter into the mirror? They replied:
"No. "O sons of the gods! All karmic retributions are likewise;
though they have no place from which they come or to which they go, they are nevertheless able to produce the fruits and rewards of roots of goodness."
For example, just as a magician can delude the eyes of people, one should know that all karmas are likewise so.
To know them in this way is called pure and true repentance.

When this Dharma was being spoken, within worlds as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, the sons of the Tuṣita Heaven all attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). Immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sons of the gods from the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) all resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Among the six heavens of the desire realm, all the goddesses abandoned their female bodies and became men, attaining the non-retrogressive mind of enlightenment.
At that time, the sons of the gods, having heard extensively of Samantabhadra’s dedication of roots of goodness, all attained the ten stages (*bhūmi*),
were adorned with the various powers (*bala*), and were fully endowed with samādhis. They all accomplished wholesome actions of body, speech, and mind equal to the realm of sentient beings,
extinguished all hindrances, and attained complete purity, seeing hundreds of thousands of millions [of buddhas].
There were lotus flowers made of the seven precious gems, as numerous as the atoms within billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields.
Upon each flower, a bodhisattva was seen sitting in the full lotus posture, emitting great radiance.

From within every one of those bodhisattvas' secondary physical marks (anuvyañjana), light was emitted equal in number to the realms of sentient beings; within that light, the realms of sentient beings were perceived.
Equal to all Buddhas, they sit in the full lotus posture and preach the Dharma according to those who are to be saved,
yet they are still unable to perceive even a small portion of the Samādhi Free from Defilement.

"At that time, from each and every pore, the sons of the gods manifested clouds of exquisite fragrant flowers equal in number to the realms of sentient beings, making offerings to Vairocana Buddha. Having scattered these fragrant flowers, within each flower they beheld all the Tathāgatas. At that moment, those clouds of fragrance universally perfumed the sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the dust motes of immeasurable Buddha-fields. Those who were touched by the fragrance experienced physical and mental bliss, like a bhikṣu entering the fourth dhyāna."

If there are sentient beings who hear this fragrance, all their karmic obstructions of evil deeds will be completely extinguished. Within the objects of form, sound, fragrance, taste, and touch, there are five hundred afflictions; likewise, there are five hundred afflictions externally, as well as twenty-one thousand afflictions of sensual desire, twenty-one thousand afflictions of aversion, twenty-one thousand afflictions of delusion, and twenty-one thousand afflictions of equal distribution. All these afflictions will be completely extinguished, and those sentient beings will be endowed with various pure fragrances, sovereign radiance, and roots of goodness.

If there are sentient beings who see this cloud-canopy, those sentient beings have planted roots of goodness equal to those of one *gaṅgā*-sands of universal wheel-turning kings, such as the Wheel-Turning King Pure White Jewel Net and others.

When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwell securely in such a station of a wheel-turning monarch, they transform and guide sentient beings within worlds as numerous as the atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields. This is like the case of the World-Honored One Candrarāja Tathāgata in the world Vimaladarśana: throughout immeasurable lands in the ten directions, among the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, there is not even one who, for so much as a single thought-moment, does not manifest a transformation body to come before that Buddha and listen to the Dharma. That Buddha constantly expounds the sutras and dharmas extensively, even preaching the Jātaka tales in detail; upon hearing the name of that Buddha, all shall be reborn in his land after their lives end.

It is likewise for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who dwells in the station of the Universal Monarch of the Pure White Jewel Net: he emits the sovereign light of the *maṇḍarava* flower. If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they all attain the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of a Bodhisattva. One should know that these sentient beings have all, in previous lives, cultivated the power of roots of goodness; just as one who attains the first dhyāna sees the Brahma-heaven and experiences the bliss of Brahma even before their life has ended, so too those who successively attain the various dhyānas experience that bliss even before their life has ended.

Thus, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in the station of the Universal Monarch of the Pure White Jewel Net, they emit a great radiance called *Cūḍāmaṇi*. If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they all attain the ten stages (*bhūmi*) of a Bodhisattva; they all obtain the immeasurable radiance of wisdom and achieve the ten kinds of pure karmic actions of the eye, up to the ten kinds of pure karmic actions of the mind. They fully accomplish the Samādhi of Pure Power, and thus achieve the purity of the physical eye (*māṃsa-cakṣus*).

For example, suppose a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes up with his left hand as many atoms as there are in a billion nayuta Buddha-fields and travels eastward, passing through as many worlds as there are atoms in a billion nayuta Buddha-fields, dropping a single atom. Continuing in this manner to the east until all these atoms are exhausted, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to fully comprehend the number of those atoms, as well as recognize the original fields from which they came and the specific fields where each atom was dropped; and it is likewise so for all ten directions.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva can again gather all these atoms to form a single Buddha-field, and within that Buddha-field, he also discerns and knows them all.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, saying: "What do you think?
Is such a buddha-field vast and inconceivable?"
The Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Such buddha-fields are immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable.”
World-Honored One!
How marvelous! How marvelous!
"If one hears this exhortation, such a person is rare; and those who hear it and believe it are likewise rare.
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi: "So it is, so it is.
If there are good sons or good daughters who hear it and believe it, I grant them this prediction: they shall swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and realize all-knowledge (sarvajñatā)."
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, saying:

"Suppose there were worlds as numerous as the atoms in a thousand billion buddha-fields, as previously described; if all these fields were ground into atoms, each of those atoms would be equal in number to the atoms in all buddha-fields."

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva takes these atoms and multiplies them successively up to eighty times; from each of those individual atoms, fruits are produced, all equal in number to the atoms within all worlds.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s karmic retribution is pure; with the fleshly eye, they discern and see all things, and in every thought-moment, they behold as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi, saying:

“It is like a *dīpaṃkara* crystal gem that illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten buddha-fields; this gem was produced by the roots of goodness of the Universal Monarch Śveta-vimala-ratna-jāla.”
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Thirty-two and Volume Thirty-three,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-one: The Conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
At that time, the Mahāsattva Samantabhadra Bodhisattva addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What has been stated above is but a brief explanation. Why is this? All Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas preach the Dharma according to the needs of those to be converted.

Fools and ignorant sentient beings are entangled by various fetters; they conceive of "self" and "what belongs to self," cling to the view of a personal identity, constantly follow after perversions, give rise to the delusions of false views, and produce erroneous and vain thoughts. Bound by their own bonds, they wander through birth and death and remain far from the path of the Tathāgata. It is for the sake of such sentient beings that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas appear in the world.
“O Son of the Buddha!
If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives rise to even a single thought of anger, among all evils, there is none that surpasses this evil. Why is this?
O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to a mind of anger, they encounter hundreds of thousands of dharma-gates of obstruction. What are these hundreds of thousands?
They are as follows:
The obstacle of not perceiving awakening; the obstacle of not hearing the true Dharma; the obstacle of being born in an impure land; the obstacle of being born in the evil realms;
the obstacle of being born in the eight states of no leisure; the obstacle of having many illnesses; the obstacle of being frequently slandered and reviled;
the obstacle of being born in a dull-witted state; the obstacle of losing right mindfulness; the obstacle of having little wisdom; [the obstacles of] the eyes and ears...

Obstacles regarding the nose, tongue, body, and mind; obstacles of associating with evil spiritual friends (*pāpamitra*); obstacles of associating with evil companions; obstacles of associating with evil persons;
obstacles of dwelling together with evil persons; obstacles of not delighting in working together with the virtuous and noble;
obstacles of distancing oneself from right view (*samyagdṛṣṭi*); obstacles of being born into non-Buddhist sects; and obstacles of departing from the Buddha’s true teaching.
The obstacle of entering the realm of Māra; the obstacle of not seeing spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); the obstacle of [failing to cultivate] all roots of goodness;
the obstacle of increasing unwholesome dharmas; the obstacle of being born into an evil family; the obstacle of being born in a border region;
the obstacle of being born among wicked people; the obstacle of being born as a poor deva; and the obstacle of being born as various nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, or asuras.
...obstacles among the *garuḍas*, *kiṃnaras*, *mahoragas*, and *rākṣasas*;
obstacles of having no delight in the Buddha-dharma; obstacles of practicing the teachings of the ignorant; obstacles of delighting in the *hīnayāna*; obstacles of not delighting in the *mahāyāna*;

obstacles of frequently giving rise to fear and terror; obstacles of delighting in birth and death (*saṃsāra*); obstacles of attachment to the three realms; and obstacles of failing to provide protection.
The obstacle to the Buddha-dharma; the obstacle of not delighting in hearing of the Buddha’s sovereign spiritual powers; the obstacle to the purification of the bodhisattva’s faculties;
the obstacle of being separated from bodhisattva conduct; the obstacle of being separated from the bodhisattva’s profound aspiration;
the obstacle of failing to maintain right mindfulness; the obstacle of failing to generate the mind of omniscience; the obstacle of impure practice of giving; and the obstacle of impurity.
The obstacle of karma; the obstacle of impure retribution; the obstacle of failing to develop the various powers; the obstacle of severing the root of wisdom;
the obstacle of not upholding the various practices of a bodhisattva; the obstacle of slandering the Buddha-dharma; the obstacle of distancing oneself from bodhi;
the obstacle of not entering the realm of the Buddhas; the obstacle of falling into the realms of Māra; and the obstacle of being unable to seek the Buddha-dharma.
The obstacle of generating terror upon hearing of the great adornments of the bodhisattvas; the obstacle of not delighting in dwelling together with bodhisattvas;
the obstacle of not delighting in seeking the karmic roots of the bodhisattvas; the obstacles of wrong views, hindrances, and doubt; the obstacle of increasing ignorance;
the obstacle of abandoning the bodhisattva precepts and conforming to broken discipline; and the obstacle of lacking faith in the Tathāgata’s precepts.
The obstacles are: the obstacle of generating a mind of anger upon hearing the Buddha praise those who uphold the precepts;
the obstacle of abandoning the joy of patience and being constantly indolent; the obstacle of slandering bodhisattvas who do not regress in their diligence;
the obstacle of abandoning samādhi and wisdom; the obstacle of reviling the skillful means of the *prajñāpāramitā*; and the obstacle of not knowing what is possible and what is impossible.
The obstacle of skillful means; the obstacle of not knowing the skillful means for liberating sentient beings; the obstacle of not entering the various profound wisdoms of bodhisattvas;
the obstacle of not giving rise to the various paths of bodhisattvas; the obstacle of being born blind regarding the ten kinds of eyes of bodhisattvas;
the obstacle of being unable to give rise to the unimpeded flow of dharmas regarding the teachings of bodhisattvas; and the unimpeded ear.
The obstacle of the nose; the obstacle of being incomplete in the marks and signs; the obstacle of an unimpeded tongue; the obstacle of being unable to distinguish the voices of sentient beings;
the obstacle of giving rise to a mind of indolence toward sentient beings; the obstacle of deranged karma; the obstacle of being separated from the three types of precepts;
the obstacle of being obstructed regarding the unhindered sense bases; and the obstacles of the four verbal transgressions and the evil karma of the mind.
The obstacle of giving rise to increased greed, anger, and wrong views; the obstacle of not seeking the true Dharma;

the obstacle of a mind of indolence regarding the bodhisattva-dharmas; the obstacle of a mind of doubt regarding the bodhisattva’s dharma of diligence; the obstacle of abandoning the bodhisattva’s definitive dharmas;
the obstacle of diminishing the gateway to bodhisattva wisdom; and the obstacle of diminishing right mindfulness.

They distance themselves from obstacles to the Buddha-dharma; they do not practice the obstacles to the bodhisattva’s way of transcending birth; they possess the obstacle of a humble mind toward bodhisattvas;

they distance themselves from the obstacles to the śrāvakas’ and pratyekabuddhas’ way of transcending birth; and they do not accord with the obstacles of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to a single thought of anger, they encounter such hundreds of dharma-gates of obstruction, even up to hundreds of thousands of dharma-gates of hindrance.
Why is this? O Son of the Buddha!
I do not see any single evil dharma that surpasses a bodhisattva’s single thought of anger.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to swiftly fulfill the bodhisattva practices should cultivate ten kinds of right dharmas. What are these ten?

That is to say: not abandoning any sentient being; conceiving the thought of the Tathāgata toward all bodhisattvas; never slandering any Buddha-dharma; attaining inexhaustible wisdom regarding all Buddha-fields; reverently honoring and delighting in the conduct of bodhisattvas; not forsaking the bodhicitta that is equal to space and the dharma-realm; discerning the ultimate power of a Buddha within enlightenment and reaching the further shore; cultivating all the eloquences of a bodhisattva; teaching and transforming sentient beings with a mind free from weariness; and manifesting birth in all worlds without attachment or delight therein.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these ten kinds of true dharmas, they are able to grasp ten kinds of pure dharmas. What are the ten?

That is to say: purity through ultimate clarity regarding the profound Dharma; purity through drawing near to spiritual friends; purity through being able to protect the true Dharma of all Buddhas; purity through being able to fully discern the realm of space; purity through skillfully entering the Dharma-realm; purity through wisdom that thoroughly understands all mental activities; purity through causing the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas to be pure; purity through a mind that is always unattached to any eon; purity through wisdom that observes the three periods of time; and purity through accomplishing the lineage of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in such pure and correct Dharma, they are able to fulfill ten kinds of correct knowledge. What are these ten?

That is to say: the wisdom that discerns the mental activities of the hearts of sentient beings; the wisdom that discerns the various karmic retributions of sentient beings; the wisdom that universally illumines all Buddha-dharmas; the wisdom that attains the sequential skillful means regarding all Buddha-dharmas; the wisdom that is fully endowed with all dhāraṇī-doors; the wisdom that accomplishes all eloquence in written characters; the wisdom that skillfully knows all the languages of sentient beings; the wisdom that manifests bodies in all worlds; the wisdom that is fully endowed with the universal illumination of all sentient beings; and the attainment of all-knowledge within all realms of existence.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these ten kinds of correct knowledge, they enter into ten kinds of skillful conformative entries. What are the ten?
That is to say:
all worlds enter into a single hair-pore, and from a single hair-pore emerge inconceivable lands;
the bodies of all sentient beings entirely enter into a single body, and from that one body emerge immeasurable bodies.
Inconceivable eons are entirely contained within a single thought-moment, and a single thought-moment is made to enter inconceivable eons;
all Buddha-dharmas are entirely contained within a single dharma, and a single dharma is made to enter all Buddha-dharmas;
all sense-bases (*āyatana*) enter into a single sense-base, and a single sense-base is made to enter all sense-bases.
All faculties enter into a single faculty, and a single faculty causes all faculties to enter;
all faculties enter into that which is not a faculty, and that which is not a faculty enters into all faculties;
all characteristics entirely enter into a single characteristic, and a single characteristic enters into all characteristics.
All vocal sounds enter into a single vocal sound, and a single vocal sound enters into all vocal sounds;
all three periods of time entirely enter into a single period of time, and cause a single period of time to enter into all three periods of time.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas discern these ten kinds of entry into the Dharma, they are able to dwell securely in ten kinds of straightforward mind. What are these ten?

That is to say: the straightforward mind that abides in the dharma of all worldly languages and non-languages; the straightforward mind that abides in right mindfulness toward all sentient beings; the straightforward mind that abides in the realm of empty space; the straightforward mind that abides in the infinite and boundless dharma-realm; the straightforward mind that abides in accordance with the true dharma of all Buddhas; the straightforward mind that abides in profound, wholesome dharmas and the indestructible true dharma; the straightforward mind that abides in the eradication of all doubts and delusions; the straightforward mind that abides in the equal contemplation of the dharmas of the three periods of time; the straightforward mind that abides in the equality of all Buddhas of the three periods of time; and the straightforward mind that abides in the immeasurable power of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these ten kinds of straightforward mind, they attain the ten kinds of skillful means of all Buddhas. What are the ten?
That is to say:
attaining skillful means to universally illumine the profound Dharma of all Buddhas;
attaining skillful means to give birth to the most profound and supreme Dharma of all Buddhas;
They attain skillful means to analytically expound all the dharmas of the adornments of all Buddhas;
they attain skillful means to enter deeply into the equal dharma of all Buddhas;
they attain skillful means to analytically distinguish the individual characteristics of all Buddha-dharmas.
