That bodhisattva mahāsattva, out of reverence and making offerings to spiritual friends, gives rise to ten kinds of mind.
What are these ten? They are as follows:

One should develop toward spiritual friends a mind of service, a non-opposing mind, a compliant mind, a joyful mind, a mind free from seeking profit, a single-minded devotion, a mind sharing the same roots of goodness, a mind sharing the same vows, a mind like that of a Tathāgata, and a mind sharing the fulfillment of practice.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mind that a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva should arouse toward a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
O Son of the Buddha!"
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to these ten kinds of mind, they will attain ten kinds of purity.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
The mind of integrity is pure, for it is ultimately never lost;
the physical body is pure, for there is nothing that cannot be seen according to those to be transformed;
the voice is perfect and pure, for it ultimately encompasses all modes of speech and dharma.
Their eloquence is pure, for they skillfully employ expedient means to expound the inconceivable teachings of all Buddhas;
their wisdom is pure, for it eradicates all darkness of ignorance;
their birth is pure, for they are fully endowed with the sovereign power of Bodhisattvas.
The retinue is pure, because it accomplishes the roots of goodness of all sentient beings who practiced together in the past;
the retribution is pure, because it eliminates all karmic obstructions;
the vows are pure, because they are identical to those of all bodhisattvas.
All conditioned phenomena are pure, because they ultimately fulfill the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of purity of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva. "O Son of the Buddha! [he continued].
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of pāramitās.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
The dāna-pāramitā, because it relinquishes all existence;
the śīla-pāramitā, because it purifies the Buddha’s precepts;
the kṣānti-pāramitā, because it fulfills the Buddha’s forbearance;
The perfection of diligence, because it does not regress at any time;
the perfection of meditation, because right mindfulness is undisturbed;
the perfection of wisdom, because one contemplates all phenomena as being entirely suchness.
The perfection of wisdom, because it penetrates deeply into the powers of the Buddhas;
the perfection of aspiration, because the vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva are fulfilled;
the perfection of spiritual power, because all supernatural powers are manifested.
The perfection of Dharma, because it encompasses all dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten perfections of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, ultimate wisdom-pāramitā.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of conformative awakenings and realizations for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.”
What are these ten? They are:
conforming to the awakened knowledge of all worlds;
They accordingly awaken to the inconceivability of all sentient beings;
they accordingly awaken to the fact that all phenomena are neither identical nor different;
and they accordingly awaken to the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
They accordingly awaken to and know all realms of space;
they accordingly awaken to and know all worlds entering the past;
they accordingly awaken to and know all worlds entering the future.
They accordingly awaken to the knowledge that all worlds enter the present age;
they accordingly awaken to the knowledge that all Tathāgatas are fully endowed with vows and practices within a single thought-moment;
and they accordingly awaken to the knowledge that the Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely identical in their conduct.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of compliant awakening and knowledge of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain mastery over all dharmas, universally illumine them, and fulfill their vows according to their will.
In a single thought-moment, they awaken to the unsurpassed path, and all Buddha-dharmas appear before them.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of definitive knowledge."
What are these ten? They are:
definitively knowing all dharmas within a single thought-moment;
They decisively know all phenomena through unimpeded wisdom;
they decisively know the mental activities and states of mind of all sentient beings;
and they decisively know that all sentient beings possess identical faculties.
They definitively and thoroughly know the afflictions, habitual tendencies, and various activities of all sentient beings;
they definitively and thoroughly know the mental impulses and activities of all sentient beings;
and they definitively and thoroughly know the wholesome and unwholesome actions of all sentient beings.
They definitively know all the vows and practices of bodhisattvas;
they definitively know the mastery of spiritual powers, transformations, and sustenance;
and they definitively know how all Tathāgatas accomplish the ten powers.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of definitive wisdom of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the skillful means for all dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of power. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the power of penetrating deeply into all dharmas;
and the power of understanding that all dharmas are like magical transformations.
The power to understand that all phenomena are like illusions;
the power to cause all phenomena to enter into the Buddha-dharma;
and the power to remain unstained by and unattached to all phenomena.
The power of single-mindedly seeking all wholesome and wondrous dharmas;
the power of consistently revering and making offerings to all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*);
and the power of bringing all roots of goodness to ultimate completion through the attainment of unsurpassed wisdom.
The power of deep-seated faith and understanding that does not disparage any Buddha-dharma;
and the power of the ultimate, non-retrogressive mind of omniscience.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten powers of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides securely in these powers, they will be able to fulfill the unsurpassed ten powers of a Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of equality for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the equality of all sentient beings;
the equality of all phenomena;
The equality of all buddha-fields;
the equality of all buddha-vehicles;
the equality of all roots of goodness;
All bodhi is equal; all vows are equal; all pāramitās are equal.
All conditioned phenomena are equal; all Buddhas are equal.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of equality of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in this equality, they will be fully endowed with the unsurpassed equality of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of skillful means regarding the phrases of the Buddha-dharma for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
explaining all phenomena through the phrases of the Buddha-dharma as skillful means of discourse;
that all phenomena are like illusions;
All phenomena are like lightning;
all phenomena are dependently originated;
all phenomena are pure karma.
All phenomena are words;
all phenomena are the limit of reality;
all phenomena are signless.
The true meaning of all phenomena;
the dharma-realm of all phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten skillful phrases of the Buddha-dharma for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme skillful means of omniscience.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of Dharma-teachings for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
preaching the profound Dharma;
preaching the sublime and wondrous Dharma;
They teach the Dharma of various adornments;
they teach the Dharma of omniscience;
they teach the Dharma that accords with the perfections.
He expounds the Dharma of the powers of the Tathāgata;
he analyzes and explains the Dharmas of the three periods of time;
and he expounds the Dharma of the non-regressive Bodhisattvas.
He spoke on the teaching that praises all the qualities of the Buddhas;
he spoke on all the practices of the Bodhisattvas, the equality of all Buddhas, and the dharmas of the realm of all Tathāgatas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of Dharma-teachings of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these Dharma-teachings, they will attain the unsurpassed Dharma-teaching of the Tathāgata."
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of upholding for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
upholding all roots of goodness and merits;
and upholding all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas.
They uphold all parables; they uphold all gates of expedient means;
they uphold all gates of dhāraṇīs that bring forth [wisdom].
He upholds all dharmas that eliminate doubt;
he upholds all dharmas that perfect the qualities of a bodhisattva;
he upholds the dharma-gate of the samādhi of equality taught by all Tathāgatas.
They uphold all dharmas that universally illumine;
they uphold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of upholding for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme wisdom of upholding the Dharma.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of eloquence for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the eloquence that does not falsely grasp any phenomena;
the eloquence that has no activity regarding any phenomena;
The eloquence of non-attachment toward all phenomena;
the eloquence of the universal emptiness of all phenomena;
the eloquence of being free from darkness and obstruction regarding all phenomena.
The eloquence sustained by the Buddha regarding all phenomena;
the eloquence that realizes all phenomena without depending on others;
and the eloquence of skillful means in explaining all phenomena through phrases and syllables.
They possess the eloquence to speak of all phenomena as sentient beings;
they possess the eloquence to cause joy by observing all sentient beings with an impartial mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of eloquence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in this eloquence, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed eloquence of skillful means.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of supreme dharmas for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the supreme dharma that brings all sentient beings to maturity;
and the supreme dharma that universally illuminates all phenomena.
The supreme dharma of cultivating all roots of goodness and all practices;
the supreme dharma of Mahāyāna wisdom;
and the supreme dharma of being fully endowed with unattached pure precepts.
The supreme dharma of dedicating all roots of goodness toward enlightenment;
the supreme dharma of diligent cultivation through tireless vigor;
and the supreme dharma of subduing all māras.
The supreme dharma of freely roaming after having resolved upon bodhicitta;
the supreme dharma of manifesting the attainment of bodhi through transformation according to the times.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten supreme dharmas of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme dharma of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of non-attachment for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
non-attachment toward all worlds;
non-attachment toward all sentient beings;
Non-attachment to all phenomena;
non-attachment to all activities;
non-attachment to all roots of goodness.
They are unattached to all places of birth;
they are unattached to all vows;
they are unattached to all conditioned activities.
They are unattached to all bodhisattvas;
they are unattached to all buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of non-attachment of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas, they will be able to swiftly transform all conceptualizations and attain pure, unsurpassed, and unattached wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of impartial minds of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the mind of equanimity that nurtures all merits;
the mind of equanimity regarding all verbal teachings; and so forth.
A mind of equanimity toward all sentient beings;
a mind of equanimity regarding the karmic retribution of all sentient beings;
and a mind that enters into the equality of all phenomena.
A mind of equanimity toward all buddha-fields, whether pure or defiled;
a mind of equanimity toward the nature of all sentient beings, whether beautiful or ugly;
and a mind of equanimity toward all practices, without making any distinctions.
They enter the impartial mind of the powers and fearlessnesses of all Tathāgatas;
they enter the impartial mind of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of impartial minds of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these minds, they will attain the unsurpassed impartial mind of a Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of wisdom that arise for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
entering the nature of all sentient beings and giving rise to wisdom;
entering all buddha-fields, seeing them as neither one nor different, and giving rise to wisdom;
Entering the discernment of the ten directions and all networks of worlds, they give rise to wisdom;
entering all worlds that are upright, inverted, or turned upside down, they give rise to wisdom;
through skillful means entering all phenomena as being neither one nor different, they give rise to wisdom.
Entering into all various and diverse bodies, they give birth to wisdom;
entering into the nets of delusion and inversion of all worlds, remaining entirely unattached, they give birth to wisdom;
entering into all phenomena and reaching the ultimate One Vehicle, they give birth to wisdom.
Entering all dharma-realms, they give rise to wisdom through sovereign spiritual power;
entering the buddha-lineages of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, which are never interrupted, they give rise to wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give birth to wisdom;
if Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide securely in these dharmas, they will attain the inexhaustible treasury of the Dharma.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of transformations. What are these ten?
That is to say:

the transformation of sentient beings, the transformation of the body, the transformation of Buddha-fields, the transformation of offerings, the transformation of sounds, the transformation of practices and vows, the transformation of taming and maturing sentient beings, the transformation of enlightenment, the transformation of preaching the Dharma, and the transformation of sustaining the teachings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of transformations of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain all supreme methods of transformation.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of upholding for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:

the upholding of the Buddha, the upholding of the Dharma, the upholding of sentient beings, the upholding of karma, the upholding of vows, the upholding of practice, the upholding of the realm, the upholding of the sublime, the upholding of goodness, and the upholding of wisdom.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of upholding of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells securely in these modes of upholding, they will attain sovereign upholding over all phenomena.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of great, correct aspirations of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"Throughout the entirety of future ages, whenever all Buddhas appear in the world, I shall follow and practice their teachings, causing them all to be joyful, and thereby attain great and correct aspiration."
I shall honor all those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with unsurpassed reverence and offerings, thereby attaining great and authentic hope.
Having reverently made offerings to those Buddhas, they will surely fully instruct me in the True Dharma;
having heard the True Dharma, may I obtain all the merits produced on all the stages by Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, and attain great, authentic hope.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates this thought:
"For unspeakably unspeakable eons, I shall cultivate the bodhisattva practices, never being separated from the Buddhas and the various bodhisattvas, thereby attaining great and correct aspiration."
A bodhisattva mahāsattva generates this thought:
"I shall proceed directly toward enlightenment, free from all fears, namely:
the fear of lacking a livelihood, the fear of ill repute, the fear of death, the fear of the evil realms, and the fear of assemblies."
"I shall distance myself from such fears as these;
having brought to rest and extinguished all demons and non-Buddhists, they shall be unable to destroy me, and I shall attain great, correct hope."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates this thought:
"May all sentient beings ultimately achieve unsurpassed bodhi and abide securely in bodhi;
once they have attained bodhi, I shall, for as long as my life lasts, cultivate the bodhisattva practices before those Buddhas and reverently make offerings to those Tathāgatas."

After those Tathāgatas have entered parinirvāṇa, I shall collect all their relics and erect immeasurable stūpas to make offerings to them; I shall uphold and protect the teachings of those Buddhas and attain great, authentic aspiration.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"May all worlds in the ten directions be adorned with unsurpassed adornments; may they be equally pure, abide in the mastery of supernatural powers that sustain and produce [wonders], undergo the six kinds of earth-tremors, and attain great, correct hope."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates this thought:

"May all sentient beings completely eliminate doubt and confusion, attain a pure and straightforward mind, eradicate afflictions, forever close the gates to the evil realms, open the doors to the good destinies, achieve the light of wisdom to illuminate and dispel the darkness of ignorance, subdue all Māras, establish themselves in a place of peace and security, and obtain great, correct hope."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:
"Throughout immeasurable and incalculable kalpas, a Tathāgata is difficult to encounter and the True Dharma is difficult to hear, like the udumbara flower;
yet I desire to see the Buddha and listen to the True Dharma, and thus I shall see and hear them the very moment I think of it."

In the presence of those Buddhas, their minds were upright and pure, free from all flattery and crookedness; having abandoned the dharma of illusion and falsehood, they constantly beheld the Buddhas, revering them with single-minded devotion, and attained great, correct aspiration.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates such a mind:

"I shall beat the great Dharma drum, rain down the nectar of the Dharma, perform the great gift of Dharma, and with purity and fearlessness, let out the great lion’s roar; fulfilling my great vows, I shall abide in the Dharma-realm;

throughout immeasurable and incalculable kalpas, I shall constantly preach the True Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, abiding in great compassion, never wearying in the actions of body, speech, and mind, and attaining great and correct hope."
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of great, correct aspirations of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the great, correct aspiration for unsurpassed wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of profound entry into the Buddha-dharma for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; what are these ten?
That is to say:
that all worlds enter the past is the first profound entry into the Buddha-dharma;
that all worlds enter the future is the second profound entry into the Buddha-dharma.

To cause all worlds to enter into the number of worlds, the movements of worlds, the descriptions of worlds, the purification of worlds, and the wisdom regarding worlds existing in the present age, such that they all enter the present age—this is the third profound penetration into the Buddha-dharma.
To cause all worlds to be individually and distinctly entered into all worlds—this is the fourth profound penetration into the Buddha-dharma.
To individually and distinctly enter into the karmic retributions of all sentient beings—this is the fifth profound penetration into the Buddha-dharma.
To thoroughly discern and enter into all bodhisattva practices is the sixth profound entry into the Buddha-dharma;
to know all past Tathāgatas in their proper sequence is the seventh profound entry into the Buddha-dharma;
to know all future Buddhas appearing in the world in their proper sequence is the eighth profound entry into the Buddha-dharma.

To fully know all Buddha-fields throughout the present worlds of the ten directions, including the Buddhas and their retinues, as they preach the Dharma to transform sentient beings within the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—this is the ninth profound entry into the Buddha-dharma.

To know worldly dharmas, to know the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, and to know the dharmas of the Tathāgata; to realize that among those various dharmas there is neither identity nor difference, yet to speak of identity and difference regarding those dharmas; to enter entirely into the Dharma-realm because there is nothing to be entered; and to explain according to the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā) without any defilement or attachment—this is the tenth profound entry into the Buddha-dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas deeply penetrate the Buddha-dharma;
if Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will be able to deeply penetrate the profound wisdom of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of reliance for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; relying upon these, Bodhisattvas practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva. What are the ten?
That is to say:
practicing the bodhisattva conduct by relying on spiritual friends;
practicing the bodhisattva conduct by relying on all roots of goodness;
They practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on pure buddha-fields;
they practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on not abandoning any sentient beings;
they practice the bodhisattva conduct by relying on deeply entering all perfections.
One practices the bodhisattva conduct by relying on the fulfillment of all the vows of all bodhisattvas;
one practices the bodhisattva conduct by relying on the immeasurable bodhicitta;
one practices the bodhisattva conduct by relying on the enlightenment of all buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of reliance for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
relying upon these, Bodhisattvas practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of fearless minds generated by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
to extinguish all karmic obstructions and give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
and after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, to uphold and protect the true Dharma and give rise to a mind of fearlessness.
They give rise to a fearless mind by subduing all Māras;
they give rise to a fearless mind by not begrudging their own bodies or lives;
they give rise to a fearless mind by subduing all non-Buddhists in accordance with the Dharma.
May all sentient beings be filled with joy and give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
may the entire great assembly be filled with joy and give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
and may all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas be tamed and give rise to a mind of fearlessness.
They distance themselves from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, enter the profound Dharma, and give rise to a fearless mind;
for unspeakably unspeakable eons, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices without weariness of heart, giving rise to a fearless mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give rise to a mind of fearlessness;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these minds, they will attain the Tathāgata’s great wisdom and mind of fearlessness.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of ways by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas eliminate all doubts and give rise to a mind free from uncertainty. What are these ten?
That is to say: the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"I shall gather in all sentient beings through giving; I shall gather in all sentient beings through precepts, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity. He does not give rise to doubt; for it is impossible that he would give rise to doubt. This is called the first [stage]: the eradication of all doubts and the development of a mind free from doubt.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"When all future Buddhas appear in the world, I shall serve, revere, and make offerings to them; I shall not give rise to doubt or confusion regarding them, for it is impossible that such doubt would arise. This is the second [practice]: eliminating all doubts and giving rise to a mind free from uncertainty.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates such a mind:

"May all worlds be adorned with various ornaments and emit great nets of light that universally illuminate everything; may no doubt or uncertainty arise regarding this, for it is impossible for doubt to arise. This is the third [practice]: eliminating all doubts and generating a mind free from uncertainty.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"I shall, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, cultivate the bodhisattva practices—practices that are immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, boundless, and unspeakably unspeakable, beyond the reach of all calculation;

for all sentient beings equal in extent to the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, I shall provide supreme instruction and discipline them to maturity, without weariness of mind and without giving rise to doubt. It is impossible that such doubt should arise; were it to arise, it could not be so. This is the fourth [practice]: eliminating all doubt and giving rise to a mind free from doubt."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates this thought:

"I shall fulfill all vows, practice the bodhisattva conduct, give birth to all-knowledge, and abide in all-knowledge; I shall not give rise to doubt or perplexity regarding these, for it is impossible that such doubt should arise. This is the fifth [stage]: eliminating all doubt and perplexity and generating a mind free from doubt.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates this thought:

"I shall, for the sake of all worlds, practice the bodhisattva conduct and act as a great lamp to universally illumine the Buddha-dharma; I shall not give rise to doubt or confusion regarding it, for it is impossible that such doubt would arise. This is the sixth [perfection]: eliminating all doubts and generating a mind free from uncertainty.
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"I shall proclaim that all dharmas are entirely the Buddha-dharma, for the sake of transforming all beings according to their needs. He does not give rise to doubt or perplexity regarding this; it is impossible for such doubt to arise. This is the seventh [practice]: eliminating all doubt and perplexity and giving rise to a mind free from doubt.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to this thought:

"I shall attain the dharma-gate of non-obstruction, eliminate all hindrances, and ultimately achieve unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; regarding this, I shall not give rise to doubt or confusion, for it is impossible that such doubt should arise. This is the eighth [practice]: eliminating all doubts and giving rise to a mind free from uncertainty.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva generates this thought:
"I shall know that all worldly dharmas are themselves supramundane dharmas, thereby severing all inversions;

adorning myself with a single adornment, which is itself non-adornment; awakening not through another, nor giving rise to doubt therein—were such doubt to arise, it would be impossible. This is the ninth [perfection]: the elimination of all doubts and the generation of a mind free from uncertainty."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates this thought:
"I shall attain equal and perfect enlightenment and obtain all-knowledge (sarvajñā), forever extinguishing all inversions and doubts;

I shall achieve the wisdom of a single thought-moment, non-dual wisdom, the wisdom of non-existence, unimpeded wisdom, unconditioned wisdom, unattached wisdom, and the wisdom of the ineffable realm of reality (bhūtakoṭi). Regarding these, I shall not give rise to doubt or confusion; for it is impossible that such doubt should arise. This is the tenth [practice]: the elimination of all doubts and the generation of a mind free from uncertainty.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas eliminate all doubts and give rise to a mind free from doubt;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain a mind free from doubt regarding all Buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of inconceivability for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
all roots of goodness are inconceivable; all vows are inconceivable.
To understand that all phenomena are like illusions and inconceivable;

to resolve for bodhicitta and cultivate the roots of goodness of the bodhisattva path without relying on or dwelling in anything, yet without losing them, and without becoming stained by attachment—this is the fourth inconceivable.
To profoundly understand all dharmas yet not enter parinirvāṇa because all vows have not yet been fully accomplished—this is the fifth inconceivable.

To practice the bodhisattva path, manifesting conception in a womb, birth, renunciation, asceticism, proceeding to the site of enlightenment, subduing the hosts of Māras, attaining supreme perfect enlightenment, and turning the wheel of the true Dharma;
to attain mastery over all dharmas and manifest great parinirvāṇa, yet without abandoning the great vow to rescue and protect sentient beings through great compassion—this is the sixth inconceivable.

To manifest the sovereign power of the Tathāgata’s ten strengths, yet without abandoning the mind of equality that is coextensive with the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu), thereby teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity—this is the seventh inconceivable [quality].
Understanding all phenomena:
that the signless is with signs, and that which has signs is signless;
that what is not an eon is an eon, and that an eon is not an eon.
That which is non-existent is existent, and that which is existent is non-existent;
that which is non-practice is practice, and that which is practice is non-practice;
that which is non-explanation is explanation, and that which is explanation is non-explanation—this is the eighth inconceivable.
To understand that the arousal of the bodhicitta is equal to bodhi;
to understand that bodhi is equal to the arousal of the bodhicitta;
and to understand that the initial arousal of the bodhicitta and bodhi are equal to all sentient beings.
Furthermore, they do not give rise to perversions of mind, perversions of perception, or perversions of view; this is the ninth inconceivable quality.
In every thought-moment, they enter the meditative attainment of the samādhi of cessation, extinguishing all outflows (*āsrava*) without yet realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*);
moreover, they do not exhaust their roots of goodness associated with outflows, for they know that all phenomena are without outflows, and they also know the extinction of those outflows.

They know that all Buddha-dharmas are worldly dharmas; within the Buddha-dharmas, they do not grasp at the characteristics of the world, and within worldly dharmas, they do not grasp at the characteristics of the Buddha-dharmas;
for all dharmas enter the Dharma-realm, yet there is nothing to enter.
To understand that all phenomena are entirely non-dual because they are unchanging—
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth inconceivable quality of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these teachings, they will attain the inconceivable Dharma of the Tathāgata.
"Sons of the Buddha!
Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of skillful means and esoteric speech."
What are these ten? They are:
skillful means regarding the subtle and secret language of all sūtras;
The subtle, secret language of skillful means regarding all places of rebirth;
the subtle, secret language of skillful means regarding the awakening to the sovereign spiritual powers of all bodhisattvas;
and the subtle, secret language of skillful means regarding the karmic retributions of all sentient beings.
Regarding the defilement and purification of all sentient beings, there is the subtle, secret language of skillful means;
regarding all phenomena, there is the subtle, secret language of skillful means concerning the gate of ultimate non-obstruction;

regarding every single direction within the entirety of the realm of space, there is the subtle, secret language of skillful means that manifests in every world-system undergoing formation and disintegration.

Throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), in all directions and even in the most subtle of places, they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment; they see the Tathāgatas filling the entire realm of phenomena and even manifesting great parinirvāṇa—all through the skillful means of subtle and secret speech.

They understand that all sentient beings are identical to nirvāṇa because they are unchanging, yet they do not abandon their great vows until they ultimately fulfill the vow for omniscience—all through the skillful means of subtle and secret speech.

They understand all phenomena through their own awakening without depending on others, yet they do not distance themselves from spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*); they revere the Tathāgatas, follow spiritual friends, and cultivate all roots of goodness.

Dedicating roots of goodness, abiding in roots of goodness, continuity of roots of goodness, uniformity of roots of goodness, a single path of roots of goodness, and a single accomplishment of roots of goodness—these are the subtle and secret words of skillful means.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of skillful means and esoteric speech of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed skillful means and esoteric speech.
The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Seven and Scroll Thirty-Eight,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.

Chapter Thirty-Three: The Threefold Departure from the World, Part Three. “O Son of the Buddha! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of skillful means of analytical wisdom. What are these ten? They are as follows: 1. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-arising of all phenomena; 2. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-ceasing of all phenomena; 3. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-abiding of all phenomena; 4. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-dwelling of all phenomena; 5. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-coming of all phenomena; 6. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-going of all phenomena; 7. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-birth of all phenomena; 8. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-death of all phenomena; 9. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-attachment of all phenomena; 10. Skillful means of analytical wisdom regarding the non-liberation of all phenomena. These, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten kinds of skillful means of analytical wisdom possessed by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
What are these ten? They are:
the wisdom of skillful means for entering all Buddha-fields through discernment;
The analytical wisdom of skillful means that enters the abodes of all sentient beings;
the analytical wisdom of skillful means that enters the mental activities of the minds of all sentient beings;
and the analytical wisdom of skillful means that enters the faculties of all sentient beings.
The wisdom of skillful means that discerns the karmic retributions of the various activities of all sentient beings;
the wisdom of skillful means that discerns the practices of all śrāvakas;
and the wisdom of skillful means that discerns the practices of all pratyekabuddhas.
The wisdom of skillful means that discerns all bodhisattva practices;
the wisdom of skillful means that discerns all worldly dharmas;
and the wisdom of skillful means that discerns all Buddha-dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of skillful means of discerning wisdom of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme skillful means of discerning wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of samādhis of correct reception for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the samādhi of entering meditative absorption in all worlds;
the samādhi of entering meditative absorption in the bodies of all sentient beings;
The samādhi of the correct reception of all dharmas; the samādhi of seeing all Buddhas;
the samādhi of skillfully abiding in and maintaining all kalpas.
The samādhi of the birth of inconceivable bodies through skillful means;
the samādhi of the body of all Tathāgatas;
and the samādhi of the equal realization of all sentient beings through skillful conformity and awakening.
In a single thought-moment, they correctly enter all bodhisattva samādhis;
in a single thought-moment, with unimpeded wisdom, they fully accomplish all bodhisattva practices, never abandoning their great vows, while skillfully employing wisdom to correctly enter samādhi.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of samādhis of right reception for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in these samādhis, they will attain the samādhi of right reception of the unsurpassed wisdom of skillful means of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of ‘all-pervasive spheres. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the abodes of all sentient beings;
the abodes of all buddha-fields;
The locus of the nature of all sentient beings;
the locus of all fire calamities;
the locus of all water calamities.
The locus of all Buddhas;
the locus of the manifestation of all adornments;
the locus of the immeasurable merits of all Tathāgatas.
It is the locus for all conceptual explanations of the Dharma;
it is the locus for all various offerings made to all Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten universal bases of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these bases, they will attain the unsurpassed state of all great wisdom of the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of Dharma-gates for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the dharma-gate of a single body filling all worlds;
and the dharma-gate of manifesting the various and immeasurable forms within all worlds.
The dharma-door of all worlds entering into a single Buddha-field;
the dharma-door of sustaining all sentient beings;
and the dharma-door of the Tathāgata’s adorned body filling all worlds.
The Dharma-door of pervading all worlds;
the Dharma-door of traveling through all worlds in a single thought-moment;
the Dharma-door of manifesting the appearance of all Tathāgatas in a single Buddha-field;
The dharma-door of a single body filling the entire dharma-realm;
the dharma-door of manifesting the spiritual powers of all Buddhas within a single thought-moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten dharma-gates of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharma-gates, they will attain the unsurpassed dharma-gate of the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). What are these ten?
That is to say:
the supernormal power of the wisdom of skillful means for producing the recollection of past lives;
and the supernormal power of the wisdom of skillful means for producing unimpeded divine hearing.
The supernormal power of skillful knowledge that gives birth to the realization of the inconceivable mental states and mental factors of all sentient beings;
the supernormal power of skillful knowledge that gives birth to the unimpeded divine eye for observing sentient beings;
and the supernormal power of skillful knowledge that gives birth to the manifestation of inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers for sentient beings.
The skillful wisdom and supernormal power that manifests a single body to appear in inconceivable worlds;
the skillful wisdom and supernormal power that, within a single thought-moment, travels to unspeakable numbers of worlds;
and the skillful wisdom and supernormal power that produces inconceivable ornaments to adorn all worlds.
The power of skillful means and wisdom that manifests an unspeakably unspeakable number of transformation bodies for the sake of sentient beings;
and the power of skillful means and wisdom that manifests inconceivable attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in unspeakably many worlds for the sake of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of supernormal powers of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these powers, they will attain the supreme, great power of skillful means and wisdom, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of clarity. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the light of wisdom of skillful means that gives rise to knowledge of the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
and the light of wisdom of skillful means that gives rise to knowledge of the realms, liberations, quiescence, and pure minds of all sentient beings.
The light of wisdom and skillful means that gives birth to entry into all realms, all sentient beings, and the non-existence of all various determined phenomena;
the light of wisdom and skillful means that gives birth to inconceivable, pure, and wondrous sounds, which are heard everywhere throughout immeasurable worlds;
and the light of wisdom and skillful means that gives birth to insight that eradicates all harm, affliction, and attachment.
The light of wisdom regarding the skillful means of taking birth and not taking birth;
the light of wisdom regarding the skillful means of transforming all sensations and perceptions within all objective realms;

and the light of wisdom regarding the skillful means of attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* by knowing that all phenomena are without intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*) and without non-nature, without characteristics (*alakṣaṇa*) and without non-characteristics, because they are of a single nature which is no-nature, while preaching the Dharma in various ways throughout immeasurable eons and cultivating roots of goodness.

He knows the birth of all sentient beings and also knows their non-birth; he knows the cessation of all sentient beings and also knows their non-cessation. He knows causes and knows conditions; he knows phenomena and knows objects; he knows conduct and knows arising and ceasing. He knows the speech of sentient beings; he knows delusion and knows freedom from delusion; he knows perversion and knows the absence of perversion; he knows defilement and knows purity; he knows saṃsāra and knows nirvāṇa; he knows existence and knows non-existence; he knows attachment and knows non-attachment; he knows firmness and knows detachment; he knows revolution and knows non-revolution; he knows origination and knows non-origination; he knows destruction, he knows the path, he knows accomplishment, and he knows faculties—because he knows how to transform sentient beings according to their capacities and dispositions.
While transforming and teaching sentient beings, they never forget or lose sight of the practices of a bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings;

therefore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas constantly transform sentient beings without losing their bodhisattva practice, their bodies never weary, they do not oppose any sentient being, and they observe the wisdom-light of skillful means regarding dependent origination.

They do not cling to various lands, nor do they give rise to a mind of clinging; they do not cling to various Buddhas, nor do they give rise to a mind of clinging; they do not cling to all phenomena, nor do they give rise to a mind of clinging; they do not cling to worlds, nor do they give rise to a mind of clinging; they do not cling to sentient beings, nor do they give rise to a mind of clinging. They do not perceive sentient beings, do not transform sentient beings, do not discipline sentient beings, and do not preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings; yet they do not abandon the bodhisattva practices and vows, they nurture great compassion, and they behold all Buddhas and listen to and receive the true Dharma.

Never forgetting or losing [this resolve], they attain the seeds of all roots of goodness that are the fruits of reliance upon the Buddha; they do not abandon the mind of reverence and making offerings toward the Tathāgata, but rather increase that mind of reverence and making offerings. They fully accomplish a mind equal to the Dharma-realm, possessing sovereign spiritual powers that cause inconceivable and immeasurable worlds to shake in six ways. They know various methods of teaching the Dharma, know the number of sentient beings, know the various types of sentient beings, know the arising of suffering, know the cessation of suffering, and know the suffering inherent in all conditioned formations (*saṃskāra-duḥkha*). Knowing that all conditioned formations are like flashes of lightning, they practice the bodhisattva path, forever severing the root of all birth and death, and are able to rescue and protect all sentient beings. Practicing the bodhisattva path without being defiled by anything, they never sever the lineage of all Tathāgatas.

They give rise to the mind like Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, which cannot be shaken; they eliminate all inverted and manifold conceptions, so that the gates of omniscience appear before them in their entirety. Unmoving and indestructible, they attain equal and perfect enlightenment, possessing the clear wisdom of skillful means to ferry all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of clarity of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these clarities, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed clarity of wisdom in skillful means.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of liberation. What are these ten?
That is to say:
liberation from afflictions;
liberation from false views;
The liberation of blazing radiance;
the liberation of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases;
and the liberation of transcending the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
The liberation of the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena;

the liberation of dwelling in the station of immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas without clinging to any buddha-fields, any sentient beings, or any dharmas, while remaining detached from all bodhisattva practices and abiding in the stage of the Tathāgata;
and the liberation of being able to fully comprehend all dharmas of the three periods of time within a single thought-moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of liberation of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells in these liberations, they are able to universally perform the unsurpassed buddha-work for the sake of all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of groves for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the garden of birth and death, because one practices the bodhisattva path without giving rise to anxiety or affliction;
the garden of teaching and transforming sentient beings, because one never tires of sentient beings.
The groves of all kalpas, because they encompass all the great practices of bodhisattvas;
the groves of pure worlds, because their nature is free from attachment;
the groves of all the palaces of Māra, because they are the realm for subduing Māra.
The garden of hearing and receiving the True Dharma, because of observing with right mindfulness;
the gardens of the six pāramitās, the four methods of attraction, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, because of cultivating the realm of the Compassionate Father.
Because they do not dwell upon any other dharmas, [the Bodhisattvas] manifest the groves of all Buddha-dharmas, from the ten powers and four fearlessnesses up to all Buddha-dharmas.
They manifest the groves of the power and spiritual transformations of all immeasurable and boundless merit, turning the pure wheel of Dharma to subdue and transform sentient beings.

In every thought-moment, he manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment for the sake of all sentient beings; his Dharma-body is like space, for it pervades all worlds through the realization of equality.
O Son of the Buddha!

These are the ten kinds of groves of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in these groves, they will attain the unsurpassed grove of joy free from sorrow belonging to the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of palaces for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the palace of generating the bodhicitta,
because of not forgetting it.
The palace of merit and wisdom consisting of the ten paths of wholesome action,
for the purpose of teaching and bringing to maturity the sentient beings of the desire realm;
and the palace of the four divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*).
Because they bring to maturity and transform sentient beings in the realm of form,
they take birth in the palaces of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens;
because no afflictions can defile them.
The palace for taking birth as a deva in the formless realm;
the palace for descending to take birth in an impure world in order to eliminate the obstacles and difficulties of sentient beings.
In order to cause sentient beings to sever all afflictions,
he manifests dwelling in a deep palace, surrounded by court ladies, wives, children, sensual pleasures, and palaces; and in order to teach, transform,
and bring to maturity those sentient beings with whom he shared common practices in the past.
They manifest as the palaces of the Kings of the Four Continents, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Śakra, and Brahmā;
this is for the sake of taming those sentient beings whose minds are autonomous.
The palaces of the sovereign power over life and conduct through the spiritual transformations of all bodhisattvas;
the palaces of receiving the prediction of supreme sovereignty as the King of All-Knowledge from all Buddhas, due to mastery over all meditations, liberations, samādhis, and wisdom.
Adorned with the ten powers, they perform the deeds of the Sovereign Dharma-King who has mastery over all phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of palaces of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the sovereign dharma of receiving the prediction of all Dharma Kings.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of joy."
What are the ten? They are:
delighting in tranquility, because of being undistracted;
They delight in clear wisdom, because they skillfully discern all phenomena;
they delight in visiting the abodes of all Buddhas, because they hear the Dharma in their presence and receive it with devotion;
they delight in all Buddhas filling the ten directions.
They delight in the sovereign spiritual powers and immeasurable Dharma-gates of Bodhisattvas, for they manifest bodies for the sake of sentient beings;
they delight in samādhi, for from a single gate of samādhi they give birth to all gates of samādhi;
they delight in the gates of dhāraṇī, for they uphold all Dharmas to teach and transform sentient beings without forgetfulness.
They delight in eloquence, for they can expound upon a single phoneme (*akṣara*) or a single flavor (*rasa*) without exhaustion throughout unspeakable eons;
they delight in awakening, for by means of immeasurable Dharma-gates, they manifest bodies equal in number to all sentient beings to attain perfect enlightenment;
and they delight in turning the wheel of Dharma, for they subdue all non-Buddhists in accordance with the Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of joy of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these joys, they will attain the unsurpassed Dharma-joy of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of adornments for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the adornment of power, because it is indestructible;
the adornment of fearlessness, because it gives rise to no terror.
Adornment of meaning, because the inexhaustible dharma-gates of the ineffable meaning are expounded;
adornment of Dharma, because the eighty-four thousand treasuries of Dharma are expounded without forgetfulness;
adornment of vows, because all bodhisattva vows and undertakings do not regress.
The adornment of conduct, because one brings the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to ultimate fulfillment;
the adornment of Buddha-fields, because one sustains all Buddha-fields as a single Buddha-field;
the adornment of sublime voice, because one rains down the great nectar of the Dharma to fill all Buddha-fields.
The adornment of upholding [the Dharma] is because one practices the bodhisattva deeds without interruption throughout all kalpas;

the adornment of transformation is because, within the body of a single sentient being, one manifests bodies equal in number to all sentient beings, such that no sentient being fails to know or see them, as they single-mindedly seek the ten powers and never regress from omniscience.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of adornments of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme adornment of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of unshakable resolve generated by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the unshakable resolve that is able to relinquish everything that exists;
and the unshakable resolve that gives birth to all the true dharmas of the Buddhas.
The unshakable resolve to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas;
the unshakable resolve to observe all sentient beings with an impartial mind;
and the unshakable resolve to gather in and sustain all sentient beings.
They develop an unshakable resolve by single-mindedly and exclusively seeking all Buddha-dharmas without ever resting;
they develop an unshakable resolve by practicing the bodhisattva conduct for as many eons as there are sentient beings;

they develop an unshakable resolve by achieving rooted faith, unclouded faith, stainless faith, clear and pure faith, faith that reverently makes offerings to all Buddhas, non-retrogressive faith, and indestructible faith.
They develop an unshakable resolve to fully accomplish ultimate omniscience;
they develop an unshakable resolve to accomplish all the practices of bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of unshakable resolve generated by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme, unshakable resolve for all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*).
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of non-abandonment of the profound mind by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the profound resolve never to abandon the awakening to the bodhi of all Buddhas;
and the profound resolve never to abandon the teaching and maturing of all sentient beings.
The deep resolve never to sever the lineage of all Buddhas;
the deep resolve never to abandon the service of spiritual friends;
and the deep resolve to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas in all Buddha-fields.
The profound resolve never to abandon the exclusive pursuit of the Mahāyāna and all meritorious qualities;
the profound resolve never to abandon the practice of pure conduct and the maintenance of pure precepts in the presence of all Buddhas;
and the profound resolve never to abandon the gathering of all bodhisattvas.
They hear and uphold all Buddha-dharmas without abandoning their profound resolve;
they cultivate all bodhisattva practices and vows, single-mindedly and exclusively seeking all Buddha-dharmas without abandoning their profound resolve.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of non-abandonment of the profound mind of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the true dharma of the non-abandonment of the profound mind of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of intellectual observation for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the wisdom that skillfully discerns and examines all phenomena;
and the wisdom that examines all roots of goodness throughout the three periods of time.
With wisdom, they observe the sovereign spiritual powers of all bodhisattva practices;
with wisdom, they observe the skillful means of all dharmas;
with wisdom, they observe the sustaining power of all Buddhas.
With wisdom they observe all dharani-doors;
with wisdom they observe the constant preaching of the True Dharma throughout all worlds;
with wisdom they observe the profound penetration into all dharma-realms.
Wisdom observes the inconceivable nature of all worlds in the ten directions;
wisdom observes all Buddha-dharmas;
and wisdom observes unobstructed knowledge.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of wisdom-observations of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom-observation.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of analytical discernment of phenomena for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
discerning that all phenomena arise entirely from conditions;
and discerning that all phenomena are entirely like illusions.
He discerns that all phenomena are entirely without contention;
he discerns that all phenomena are immeasurable and boundless;
he discerns that all phenomena have no basis of reliance.
He discerns that all phenomena are entirely like vajras;
he discerns that all phenomena are entirely the Tathāgata;
he discerns that all phenomena are utterly tranquil.
To discern that all phenomena are entirely the right path;
to discern that all phenomena are entirely of one characteristic and one meaning.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of discernment of phenomena for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these teachings, they will attain skillful means and be able to discern all phenomena.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of stainlessness for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the stainlessness of the profound mind;
the stainlessness of having eliminated doubt and confusion;
Freedom from the stain of wrong views;
freedom from the stain of objective spheres;
and freedom from the stain of desiring to attain all-knowledge.
The stainlessness of all eloquences;
the stainlessness of fearlessness;
the stainlessness of the abodes of all bodhisattvas;
All Bodhisattvas possess the stainless samādhi of right reception;
they are adorned with the thirty-two marks and the hundred merits, have accomplished all pure and white dharmas, and have ultimately attained the stainless state of unsurpassed bodhi.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of stainlessness of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain all the unsurpassed, stainless dharmas of the Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten seals of wisdom for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:

when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva understands the suffering of suffering, the suffering of change, and the suffering of conditioned formations, they do not give rise to indolence, but cultivate the bodhisattva practices, single-mindedly and exclusively seeking unexcelled bodhi; they are without fear, terror, alarm, or dread, and do not abandon their great vows;
their bodhicitta is firm and non-retrogressive, culminating in anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi—this is the first seal.

All ordinary sentient beings possess afflictions and are deluded by inverted views; yet when those beings address the Bodhisattva with coarse, vulgar, and evil words of abuse, or even inflict harm upon him with knives, staves, tiles, or stones, the Bodhisattva at that time feels no sorrow or distress.
He cultivates the practices of a Bodhisattva, proceeds directly toward Bodhi, practices the dharma of patience, and attains the realization of the stage of non-arising. This is the second seal.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva hears the profound Buddha-dharma and praises all-knowledge, and having heard it, believes and understands it with single-minded resolve, this is the third seal.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"I have resolved for bodhicitta and shall ultimately achieve unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
All sentient beings wander through the five realms of existence, undergoing immeasurable suffering;
I shall cause them all to experience great joy, diligently practicing with vigor, cultivating roots of goodness, crossing the stream of birth and death, and attaining eternal peace and happiness.
This is the fourth seal.
A bodhisattva-mahāsattva understands that the Tathāgata’s wisdom is immeasurable and boundless, yet they are not yet equal to the Tathāgata;
from the Tathāgata, they hear of immeasurable and boundless wisdom.
To analytically understand and comprehend within the midst of words that one is equal to the Tathāgata—this is the fifth seal.

That a bodhisattva-mahāsattva achieves a virtuous aspiration, an indestructible aspiration, a profound aspiration, a superior aspiration, a meritorious aspiration, an adorned aspiration, an incomparable aspiration, an unsurpassed aspiration, a firm aspiration, and an aspiration for the ultimate and correct seeking of unsurpassed bodhi—an aspiration that all Māras, non-Buddhists, and their retinues cannot destroy, and an aspiration for non-retrogression from unsurpassed bodhi—this is the sixth seal.

Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas do not begrudge their bodies or lives and are free from all fear; they cultivate the bodhisattva practices, resolve for bodhicitta, and advance toward omniscience, thereby attaining the light of wisdom of all Buddhas.
They do not forsake the Buddha’s bodhi, nor do they forsake spiritual friends—this is the seventh seal.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva—whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family—who studies the Mahāyāna, nurtures the roots of goodness of all Buddhas, dwells securely in those roots of goodness, and embraces all-knowledge with a mind that does not regress from Bodhi, this is the eighth seal.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva causes all sentient beings to abide in a mind of equanimity, cultivates omniscience, and preaches the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, ensuring that they all do not regress from unexcelled bodhi and nurturing great compassion; this is the ninth seal.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas accord with the Buddhas of the three periods of time, continuing the lineage of the Buddhas through all roots of goodness and giving rise to all-knowledge, this is the tenth seal.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten seals of wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these seals, they will swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and become fully endowed with the unsurpassed seal of wisdom of the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of light of wisdom for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s light of wisdom that is certain regarding unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment;
and the light of wisdom for beholding all buddhas.
The light of wisdom that perceives all sentient beings dying here and being born there;
the light of wisdom that awakens all sentient beings, causing them all to correctly seek the Dharma of the Sūtras;
and the light of wisdom that, by relying on spiritual friends, gives rise to the bodhicitta and nurtures the roots of goodness.
The light of wisdom that manifests the wisdom of all Buddhas;
the light of wisdom that transforms all sentient beings, causing them all to reach maturity and dwell securely in the ground of Buddhahood;
and the light of wisdom that analytically explains the inconceivable Dharma.
The light of wisdom of skillful means and sustaining power through the spiritual authority of all Buddhas;
the light of wisdom that fulfills all perfections.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of light of wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed light of wisdom of all buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of immeasurable abodes of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas that cannot be measured by any sentient beings, nor by Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
What are the ten? They are as follows:

A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in the dwelling of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), yet does not realize it because all their vows have not yet been fully accomplished; this is the first Bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva plants roots of goodness as pure as the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), yet remains unstained by and unattached to those roots of goodness; this is the second bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva understands that the bodhisattva practice is like a magical transformation; all dharmas are entirely quiescent, and he gives rise to no doubt or confusion regarding the Buddha-dharmas. This is the third bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, having detached from the mind of saṃsāra, cultivates the bodhisattva practices throughout unspeakable eons, fulfilling all great vows without ever giving rise to a heart of weariness or indolence; this is the fourth bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in all dharmas without any basis of reliance; they are entirely quiescent, yet do not realize nirvāṇa because the path to omniscience has not yet been fully perfected. This is the fifth bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that all kalpas are not kalpas, yet he speaks of all kalpas as they truly are; this is the sixth bodhisattva abode, which is immeasurable.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that all dharmas are not [objects of] practice, yet does not abandon the practice of the Way, correctly seeking the Buddha-dharma; this is the seventh bodhisattva abiding, which is immeasurable.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva understands that the mind is the triple world and that the mind is the three periods of time; he thoroughly knows that this mind is immeasurable and boundless. This is the eighth bodhisattva dwelling, which is incalculable.
For the sake of a single sentient being, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva path for unspeakable eons, desiring to establish them on the ground of all-knowledge;
as it is with one sentient being, so it is with all sentient beings, yet they do not give rise to a mind of weariness—this is the ninth bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.
Although a bodhisattva mahāsattva fulfills all the practices of a bodhisattva, they do not take up perfect enlightenment.
Why is this? The bodhisattva mahāsattva forms this thought:

"I practice the bodhisattva path not for the sake of receiving perfect enlightenment myself, but so that immeasurable sentient beings throughout immeasurable eons may all be established in unsurpassed bodhi."
This is the tenth bodhisattva dwelling, which is immeasurable.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides securely in this dharma, they will attain the supreme, great wisdom of all buddha-dharmas, the immeasurable dwelling.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of generating the mind free from indolence for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"I shall subdue all māras and their retinues," and thus gives rise to a mind free from indolence.
They give rise to a mind free from indolence in order to subdue all non-Buddhists in accordance with the Dharma;
they give rise to a mind free from indolence in order to preach the profound and wondrous Dharma so that all sentient beings may be filled with joy;
and they give rise to a mind free from indolence in order to fulfill all the pāramitās equal to the entire dharma-realm.
I shall cause all sentient beings to accumulate and fulfill the treasury of all merits, and resolve to never give rise to a mind of indolence;

I shall resolve to never give rise to a mind of indolence as I cultivate the Bodhisattva practices to fully achieve the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Tathāgatas—a vast and great undertaking that is exceedingly difficult to accomplish;
and I shall resolve to never give rise to a mind of indolence as I teach and discipline all sentient beings with the unsurpassed Dharma, causing them all to reach full maturity.
In all worlds, he achieves perfect awakening through various colors and immeasurable adornments, giving rise to a mind free from indolence.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to such a thought:

"When I practice the bodhisattva path, if there are sentient beings who come to seek my body, or to seek my hands, feet, ears, nose, blood, flesh, bones, marrow, wife, children, elephants, horses, or kingdoms—if they seek any such things as these—I am able to relinquish them all. Even so much as a single thought of regret does not arise; I am able to bestow them as gifts to benefit and bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings, seeking no karmic reward, with great compassion as my primary guide, giving rise to a mind free from indolence."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

within a single moment of mind, by means of wisdom corresponding to that single moment, they fully and distinctly perceive all phenomena—namely, all Buddhas of the three periods of time, all Buddha-dharmas, all sentient beings, all lands, all worlds, all realms of space, all dharma-realms, all realms of conventional linguistic designations, and all realms of quiescent nirvāṇa.

They clearly understand and cultivate them, distinguish and cultivate them, and know their wisdom, abandonment, and realization. Regarding all phenomena, they do not grasp at falsehood; there is neither unity nor difference, no conceptual discrimination, and nothing to be cultivated. There is no objective sphere and nothing that exists.
The wisdom of non-duality awakens to all dualities;
the wisdom of signlessness awakens to all signs;
the wisdom of no kalpas awakens to all kalpas.
The wisdom of non-differentiation awakens to all distinctions;
the wisdom of radiance awakens to the realm of light throughout all worlds;
the wisdom of progression awakens to all world-systems.
The wisdom that transcends the world awakens to all worlds;
the wisdom of the stage of sentient beings awakens to the entire realm of sentient beings;
and unattached wisdom brings the practice of non-attachment to ultimate fulfillment.
With wisdom that is not fixed, one awakens to all that is fixed;
with undefiled wisdom, one awakens to all afflictions;
with wisdom that has no limit, one awakens to all limits.
The wisdom equal to the dharma-realm manifests its body in all worlds;
the wisdom detached from all speech and sound gives birth to all subtle and wondrous sounds;
the wisdom of single nature expounds the dharma of non-nature.
The wisdom of a single object manifests various diverse realms;
the wisdom that awakens to all ineffable phenomena manifests immeasurable, great sovereign spiritual transformations;
the wisdom that awakens to all stages manifests the great sovereign spiritual transformations.
Through the sovereign spiritual transformations of omniscience, they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity, giving rise to a mind free from indolence.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give rise to a mind free from indolence.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in this mind, they will attain the unsurpassed and tireless Dharma of all buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva mahāsattvas have ten kinds of upright minds that are like the king of mountains, Sumeru."
What are these ten? They are as follows:

A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva constantly cultivates right mindfulness of the dharmas of omniscience; this is the first determination for Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, the upright mind of Sumeru, the King of Mountains.

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva contemplates that all phenomena are empty and that all phenomena are non-existent, this constitutes the second determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*: the upright mind of Sumeru, the king of mountains.

For immeasurable and incalculable eons, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva conduct, generating the resolve through all-encompassing pure and white dharmas. He definitively understands the immeasurable wisdom-dharmas of the Tathāgata and proceeds toward the accumulation of all pure and white dharmas; this is the third determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the upright mind of Sumeru, the King of Mountains.

For the sake of all Buddha-dharmas, a bodhisattva mahāsattva reverently makes offerings to spiritual friends with an impartial mind, giving rise to no doubt and seeking no gain or sustenance; furthermore, they remain far removed from any intention to steal the Dharma, but instead give rise to a supreme, respectful, and all-encompassing mind of giving. This is the fourth determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*: the upright mind of Sumeru, the King of Mountains.

If all sentient beings should revile, scold, or insult a bodhisattva mahāsattva, causing them every kind of suffering, even unto the taking of their life, the bodhisattva mahāsattva shall not, because of this, abandon the mind of enlightenment;

his mind shall remain undistracted, he shall not give rise to a heart of anger, and he shall not forsake the adornment of great compassion toward all sentient beings, but shall instead nurture that great compassion.
Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have accomplished the relinquishment of all dharmas according to their suchness (tathatā),
and because they have definitively and fully realized the Great Patience (mahākṣānti) of the Tathāgata.
This is the fifth determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*: the upright mind of Sumeru, King of Mountains.

A bodhisattva mahāsattva accomplishes superior merit as a deity, superior merit as a human, superior merit in physical form, superior merit in power, superior retinues, superior desire, superior royal dharma, superior sovereignty, and superior wisdom;
yet that bodhisattva does not cling to the pleasure of flavors, does not cling to the pleasure of desires, does not cling to the pleasure of wealth, and does not cling to the pleasure of retinues.
They single-mindedly seek the truth of the true Dharma, fulfill the truth of the true Dharma, discern the true Dharma, and reach the ultimate consummation of the true Dharma;

they turn toward the lamp of the true Dharma, toward the protection of the true Dharma, toward refuge in the true Dharma, toward the path of the true Dharma, and toward the meaning of the true Dharma. Delighting in seeking the true Dharma and delighting in dwelling in the dharma of tranquility, although these Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas achieve all such joys, they remain entirely far removed from the realms of Māra.

Why is this? Because in past lives, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have given rise to such a mind, causing all sentient beings to remain far removed from the realms of Māra and to dwell within the realm of the Buddha; this is the sixth determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the upright mind of Sumeru, the King of Mountains.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas diligently cultivate vigor and rightly seek Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, practicing the bodhisattva path for incalculable eons (asaṃkhyeya-kalpa), they still think:

"I have only now first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Their minds are neither startled, nor terrified, nor afraid as they practice the bodhisattva path; though they could swiftly achieve perfect enlightenment, for the sake of transforming sentient beings, they cultivate the bodhisattva path throughout immeasurable eons.
"This is the seventh determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the upright mind of Sumeru, King of Mountains.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that all sentient beings are difficult to subdue and difficult to guide; they are ungrateful and do not know how to repay kindness. For the sake of those sentient beings, they don the great armor of adornment to adorn themselves, desiring to cause the minds of all sentient beings to attain mastery and to dwell within their own realms of experience without giving rise to evil thoughts or afflictive states of mind toward others. This is the eighth determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the upright mind of Sumeru, King of Mountains."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"I shall not rely on others to resolve upon Bodhicitta or to cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva; there is no one at all who assists me in practicing these Bodhisattva deeds. Yet, by myself alone, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, I shall practice the austerities of a Bodhisattva;
I shall accumulate all the true dharmas of the Buddhas and realize Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
