One’s own body is pure, and one causes all sentient beings to be pure;
one knows one's own realm and knows the realms of others;
I shall fully accord with the realms of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
"This is the ninth determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, the upright mind of Sumeru, the King of Mountains.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas perceive and see in this way, they do not find a single dharma that cultivates the bodhisattva practice, nor a single dharma that fulfills the bodhisattva practice; they do not find a single dharma that tames sentient beings, nor a single dharma that transforms and delivers sentient beings.

They do not perceive a dharma that reverently makes offerings to all Buddhas; they do not perceive a dharma that attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the past, nor a dharma that will attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the future, nor a dharma that attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the present."
There is not a single dharma that speaks of the past, speaks of the future, or speaks of the present; there is not a single dharma that is able to speak.
Furthermore, as for dharmas, there is no dharma that can be spoken. Yet, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not abandon the great vow-mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Why is this? Because a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva thus gives birth to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, deeply penetrating all profound dharmas and practicing the practice of non-existence; yet this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva cultivates and accumulates wholesome karma and roots of goodness, purifies all remedial dharmas, and brings wisdom to full completion, being able in every thought-moment to collect and nurture all dharmas of the roots of goodness.
If all dharmas were non-existent, for what purpose would I seek the unsurpassed path?
Therefore, one does not give rise to a mind of fear, alarm, or dread; this is the tenth determination for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*: the upright mind of Sumeru, the King of Mountains.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of upright mind like Sumeru, the King of Mountains, belonging to Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these minds, they will attain the unsurpassed wisdom of all Buddhas—the upright mind like Sumeru, the King of Mountains.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten ways in which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas deeply enter the great ocean of wisdom and thereby attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
What are the ten? They are as follows:
entering the infinite realms of all sentient beings; this is the first profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva enters all worlds without grasping at what is false, this is the second profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby they achieve anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all space-realm spheres are equal, entering all worlds in the ten directions without any obstruction; this is the third profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one accomplishes Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva skillfully enters the Dharma-realm; he enters non-obstruction, enters non-interruption, enters non-permanence, enters the immeasurable, enters the unarisen, enters the undestroyed, and enters the knowledge of all things. This is the fourth profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one accomplishes Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva [dedicates] the roots of goodness planted toward all Buddhas, bodhisattvas, Dharma-preachers, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all sentient beings of the past, future, and present;

the roots of goodness by which the Buddhas of the past have already attained unsurpassed awakening; the roots of goodness by which the Buddhas of the future will attain unsurpassed awakening; the roots of goodness by which the Buddhas of the present are now attaining unsurpassed awakening; and the roots of goodness by which the Buddhas of the past, future, and present teach the Dharma, transform, subdue, and bring to maturity sentient beings through their preaching.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas all rejoice in these matters, nurturing and accumulating all such roots of goodness with a mind that never knows satiety; this is the fifth way of deeply entering the great ocean of wisdom to achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
In every thought-moment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva enters the past and observes unspeakable eons.

Within a single eon, there may appear in the world ten billion Buddhas, or a hundred billion Buddhas, a hundred thousand billion Buddhas, immeasurable Buddhas, asaṃkhyeya Buddhas, inconceivable Buddhas, unfathomable Buddhas, limitless Buddhas, boundless Buddhas, unspeakably unspeakable Buddhas, or Buddhas beyond the reach of calculation or analogy appearing in the world.

Regarding those Tathāgatas and their retinues—the assembly of Bodhisattvas, the community of Śrāvakas, their preaching of the Dharma and edification, their lifespans and sustenance, and the various abidings of the Dharma—as it is within one eon, so it is likewise in all eons.
If there are sentient beings in kalpas devoid of Buddhas who have planted roots of goodness for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, he fully knows them all;

furthermore, observing sentient beings who plant roots of goodness through seeing a Buddha and thus encounter immeasurable Buddhas of the future—he contemplates all past kalpas in this manner without ever becoming weary. This is the sixth profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one accomplishes anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters the future world and observes all kalpas; he knows which kalpas have Buddhas and which kalpas have no Buddhas, and he knows how many Buddhas appear in each of those kalpas;
he knows the names of the Tathāgatas of those worlds, as well as the number of sentient beings to be delivered, and he also knows the length of the Tathāgatas’ lifespans.

Thus entering all kalpas of the future, he discerns and understands them without ever becoming weary; this is the seventh profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one accomplishes Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva enters the present age and observes all worlds throughout the ten directions;

within immeasurable, boundless, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, he beholds all Tathāgatas who have left home to study the Way, proceeded to the site of enlightenment, sat cross-legged upon the bodhi-grass beneath the tree of awakening, and subdued the hosts of Māra;

having attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they arise and enter cities and towns, ascend to celestial palaces, preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma, turn the wheel of the True Dharma, and tame and transform immeasurable sentient beings.

Manifesting the immeasurable and sovereign supernatural powers of a Tathāgata, he entrusted them with anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, even unto the relinquishing of his life and entry into nirvana without remainder;
after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, the great assembly gathered universally to compile the scriptural collections, protect and uphold the True Dharma so that it might long abide in the world,
and for the sake of the relics, they erected immeasurable stupas, adorned in various ways, and paid them respectful offerings.

Furthermore, they transform sentient beings, causing them to behold all Buddhas, hear and receive the True Dharma, recollect and uphold it, and investigate it with wisdom; they nurture superior rebirths, filling their profound resolve throughout the immeasurable Dharma-realm, remaining without error regarding any Buddha-dharma.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas know that all Tathāgatas are entirely like dreams, yet they are able to go to the abodes of all Buddhas to pay respect and make offerings. They do not cling to their own bodies, they do not cling to the bodies of the Buddhas, they do not cling to worlds, they do not cling to great assemblies, they do not cling to hearing the Dharma, and they do not cling to kalpas, as they see the Buddhas and hear the Dharma;

they observe the worlds and comprehend all kalpas without ever feeling weary or satisfied. This is the eighth profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one accomplishes Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For unspeakably unspeakable eons, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva reverently makes offerings to immeasurable Buddhas;
within each and every eon, he reverently makes offerings to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas;
and he manifests passing away from this life and being born in that, thereby transcending the three realms.
With various articles of offering, they made offerings to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, the great assemblies, and the Sangha of Śrāvakas;
after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddhas, they honored their relics with unsurpassed offerings;
they extensively practiced great giving, fulfilling the aspirations of all sentient beings, and the great giving they performed was inconceivable.
Seeking no karmic reward, yet out of compassion and for the benefit of sentient beings, they reverently make offerings to all Buddhas throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons;

they uphold the True Dharma, transform and deliver sentient beings, and achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* without ever feeling weary or satisfied—this is the ninth profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one achieves *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, in the presence of all Buddhas, all bodhisattvas, and all Dharma-preachers, single-mindedly and exclusively seek the teachings for bodhisattvas, the bodhisattva’s deportment, the bodhisattva’s conforming dharmas, the bodhisattva’s pure dharmas, the bodhisattva’s nurturing dharmas, the bodhisattva’s taming dharmas, the bodhisattva’s equalizing dharmas, and the path of the bodhisattva’s emergence; they uphold the bodhisattva *dhāraṇī* gates;

they gather in all sentient beings and preach the Dharma for them, taming and ripening them, causing unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to resolve upon the mind of omniscience, attain non-retrogression, and abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

To practice in accordance with all Buddha-dharmas and to teach and transform sentient beings without ever becoming weary—this is the tenth profound entry into the great ocean of wisdom, whereby one attains Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas deeply enter the great ocean of wisdom and realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
if Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the great ocean of the supreme wisdom of all Buddhas.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Eight;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Nine.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-Three: The Chapter on Transcending the World, Part Four.
“O Sons of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of jewels possessed by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, by abiding in which they realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).”
What are these ten? They are as follows:

A bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas in immeasurable, incalculable worlds to pay respect, prostrate, draw near, and make offerings. This is the first treasure of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by abiding in which they shall achieve unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva hears the Dharma from inconceivable Tathāgatas, receives and upholds it, maintains it with right mindfulness without forgetting, discerns it with wisdom, nurtures superior destinies, gives birth to wisdom, and fills the ten directions—this is the second treasure of the bodhisattva mahāsattva, by abiding in which one accomplishes anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva does not depart from this land, yet manifests birth in other realms; his mind remains undeluded regarding all Buddha-dharmas. This is the third treasure of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, by abiding in which he attains Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to the distinct characteristics of a single dharma and discriminatively knows all dharmas; because all dharmas ultimately have no sense of being one or different, this is the fourth treasure of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, by abiding in which they achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows how to pacify afflictions, knows how to depart from afflictions, and knows how to sever afflictions; yet they skillfully abide in and cultivate all bodhisattva practices, not realizing the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) prematurely, while ultimately reaching the further shore of that limit of reality. Having skillfully studied and accomplished subtle and wondrous expedient means (upāya), their original vows are fulfilled, and their minds are free from weariness or fatigue. This is the fifth treasure of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by which they abide and achieve unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that the minds of all sentient beings have no location, yet he speaks of the minds of sentient beings as having a location; being without attachment and without activity, he cultivates the bodhisattva practices to transform and deliver sentient beings. This is the sixth treasure of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, by abiding in which he attains Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva knows that all dharmas have a single nature, namely:

they are without nature, without unity, without difference, without coming, without going, immeasurable, beyond praise, and entirely devoid of a real nature; whether sought through unity or difference, they cannot be apprehended.

Furthermore, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva definitively knows that "this is the Buddha-dharma, this is the bodhisattva-dharma, this is the pratyekabuddha-dharma, this is the śrāvaka-dharma, this is the dharma of ordinary persons; this is wholesome dharma, this is unwholesome dharma; this is mundane dharma, this is supramundane dharma; this is defiled dharma, this is undefiled dharma; this is outflowing dharma, this is non-outflowing dharma; and so on, up to conditioned dharma and unconditioned dharma. This constitutes the seventh treasure of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by abiding in which they achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva seeks the Buddha and finds him unobtainable; seeks the bodhisattva and finds him unobtainable; seeks the Dharma and finds it unobtainable; seeks sentient beings and finds them unobtainable. Yet, they do not abandon their original vow, but rather transform and guide all sentient beings to achieve the unsurpassed path. Why is this?

The roots of goodness cultivated by a bodhisattva are intended to cause all beings to achieve the unsurpassed path; they skillfully know the roots of goodness of sentient beings, skillfully know the realms of sentient beings, skillfully know how to teach and transform sentient beings, and skillfully know the nirvana of all sentient beings. Cultivating the bodhisattva practices with the desire to fulfill all great vows—this is the eighth treasure of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by abiding in which one attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, according to what is appropriate for each, skillfully teaches the Dharma to subdue them;
through skillful means he manifests *nirvāṇa*, knowing it to be real, not false, and not inverted, while dwelling securely in the true Dharma of the Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.

He does not depart from suchness (*tathatā*), nor does he dwell in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); furthermore, he perceives no sentient beings, nor does he perceive sentient beings who have been transformed, are being transformed, or will be transformed.

To understand that my practice is not false or vain; to comprehend that there is not even a single dharma to be found, because there is neither arising nor ceasing; and for the vows of a bodhisattva to be entirely non-empty while having no point of dependence—this is the ninth treasure of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, by abiding in which one achieves *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, in the presence of each of the inconceivable Buddhas, hears the dharma of the prediction of enlightenment— which is unspeakably unspeakable—
in which the names and titles differ and the number of kalpas varies.
From hearing the Dharma sequentially throughout a single kalpa, up to hearing and receiving the prediction of enlightenment throughout unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas;
having heard this Dharma, they are not startled, not terrified, and not afraid, as they practice the bodhisattva path with a mind free from doubt or confusion.

They understand that the wisdom of the Tathāgata is inconceivable, and that what the Tathāgata speaks is without duality. With their original vows fulfilled, they transform beings according to their needs, leading them to achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, fulfilling all aspirations, and thoroughly penetrating the Dharma-realm. This is the tenth treasure of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, abiding in which they shall achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the great jewel of supreme wisdom—the anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten ways in which Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas generate the adamantine mind to adorn the Great Vehicle. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"All dharmas have no boundaries and cannot be fully exhausted"—the bodhisattva gives rise to such a mind—thinking, "I shall awaken to all dharmas of the three periods of time, without exception."
This is the first adamantine mind-generation that serves as the adornment of the Mahāyāna for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"Upon the tip of a single hair there are immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable Bodhisattvas; how much more so throughout the entire Dharma-realm!"—the Bodhisattva generates such a mind: "I shall generate the great adornment to adorn myself, transform and deliver all sentient beings so that they all attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and enter Parinirvāṇa through the Great Parinirvāṇa."
This is the second adamantine resolve that adorns the Mahāyāna of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"The worlds of the ten directions are immeasurable and boundless, without limit; yet the Bodhisattva makes such a great vow: 'I shall adorn all these worlds with unsurpassed, pure adornments, and all those adornments shall be real and not false.'"
This is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s third generation of the adamantine mind as an adornment of the Mahāyāna.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"Sentient beings are immeasurable and boundless, without limit and inexhaustible—the Bodhisattva generates such a mind, thinking: 'I shall dedicate all roots of goodness to all sentient beings, and with the light of supreme, great wisdom, I shall universally illumine all sentient beings.'"
This is the fourth adamantine resolve of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva that adorns the Mahāyāna.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:

"All buddhas are immeasurable and boundless, and cannot be exhausted. A bodhisattva generates such a mind: "I shall dedicate the roots of goodness I have planted to offer and provide for all buddhas; only after that shall I attain equal and perfect enlightenment."
"This is the fifth adamantine resolve of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva that adorns the Mahāyāna.

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva sees all buddhas and hears the Dharma they teach, they give rise to a mind of great joy, yet they do not cling to their own body or the body of the Tathāgata. They understand that the Buddha-body is neither real nor unreal, neither existent nor non-existent, neither having a nature nor lacking a nature, neither form nor formless, neither with marks nor markless, and neither arising nor ceasing.
They understand that the Tathāgata truly has nothing whatsoever, yet they do not destroy the appearance of existence. Why is this?"
Because they embrace all;
this is the sixth adamantine resolve that adorns the Mahāyāna of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

If there are sentient beings who revile, scold, or insult the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, or who cut off his hands, feet, ears, or nose, or gouge out his eyes, or sever his head, the Bodhisattva does not, on account of these things, give rise to a mind of anger or malice. For unspeakably unspeakable kalpas, he cultivates the bodhisattva practices, embracing sentient beings, never abandoning them in mind.
Why is this? Because a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in the non-dual dharma, having well trained in the pure and upright mind that is the Bodhisattva’s training;

they harbor no malice toward any sentient being, endure all sufferings with patience, and do not seek retribution, being able to personally undergo all manner of suffering. This is the seventh adamantine-mind adornment of the Mahāyāna for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:

"The kalpas of future worlds are immeasurable and boundless, without limit and inexhaustible—such is the mind the Bodhisattva generates: 'I shall, throughout all kalpas of the future Dharma-realm, the space-realm, and so forth, practice the Bodhisattva path in a single world to transform sentient beings; as it is in one world, so it shall be in all worlds throughout the entire Dharma-realm and space-realm.'"
The mind is neither startled, nor terrified, nor afraid as one practices the bodhisattva conduct.
Why is this? Because it is the nature of a bodhisattva to thus cultivate the bodhisattva conduct for the sake of all sentient beings.
This is the eighth adamantine resolve that adorns the Mahāyāna of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"Anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi has the mind as its root; because the mind is pure, one is able to accumulate and fulfill all roots of goodness."

If one attains mastery over the mind, then one can accomplish unsurpassed bodhi, practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, fulfill all vows, and ultimately bring all sentient beings to spiritual maturity.
This is the ninth generation of the adamantine mind by which a bodhisattva mahāsattva adorns the Mahāyāna.

The bodhisattva mahāsattva knows that the Buddha is unapprehendable, awakening is unapprehendable, the bodhisattva is unapprehendable, all phenomena are unapprehendable, sentient beings are unapprehendable, the mind is unapprehendable, conduct is unapprehendable, the past is unapprehendable, the future and the present are unapprehendable, all sentient beings are unapprehendable, the conditioned and the unconditioned are unapprehendable. Thus the bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in tranquility, abides in profundity, abides in cessation, abides in non-contention, abides in the ineffable, abides in non-duality, abides in the peerless, abides in reality, abides in accomplishment, abides in liberation, abides in nirvāṇa, and abides in the limit of reality.

Yet they do not abandon any of their great vows; they do not abandon the arousal of the mind of omniscience; they do not abandon the cultivation of bodhisattva practices; they do not abandon the teaching and transforming of sentient beings; they do not abandon the respectful making of offerings to all Buddhas; they do not abandon the preaching of the Dharma; and they do not abandon the adornment of all worlds.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give birth to great vows, they thoroughly understand the characteristics of such dharmas; they nurture immeasurable merit through great compassion, embracing sentient beings and never abandoning them.
"All dharmas lack any true reality, yet ordinary, ignorant beings neither know nor perceive this;
all Buddhas abide in quiescent extinction, proclaiming the True Dharma to teach and transform sentient beings;
they do not abandon great compassion, for as long as all sentient beings have not attained Bodhi, the Buddha-dharma is not yet sufficient, and their great vows are not yet fulfilled."
I have originally invited all sentient beings to be the donors of the unsurpassed great Dharma; I utter words of truth, not false speech, the words of the lineage of all Buddhas;

I have resolved my mind upon the gateway of great vows, resolved my mind upon benefiting all sentient beings, resolved my mind upon nurturing all roots of goodness, resolved my mind upon abiding in skillful means, resolved my mind upon inwardly embracing all sentient beings, and resolved my mind upon equality toward all sentient beings, so as to cause the aspirations of all sentient beings to be fulfilled. How could I abandon great compassion before all sentient beings have been delivered?
This is the tenth adamantine resolve of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva that adorns the Great Vehicle.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of adamantine resolves of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva that adorn the Great Vehicle.
If Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme Vajra Wisdom-illumination of all Buddhas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of great undertakings initiated by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas; this is the first great undertaking of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
To nurture all the roots of goodness of bodhisattvas—this is the second great undertaking of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
After the parinirvāṇa of all Tathāgatas, to collect their relics and erect immeasurable stūpas, adorning them with various kinds of exquisite jewels;

and to make offerings to them with every kind of flower, every kind of garland, every kind of incense, every kind of unguent, every kind of powdered incense, every kind of robe, every kind of parasol, every kind of banner, and every kind of pennant; and to uphold and protect the true Dharma of all Buddhas—this is the third great undertaking of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
To teach and transform all sentient beings, bringing them to maturity so that they may attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi—this is the fourth great undertaking of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva.
To adorn all worlds with the unsurpassed, pure adornments of the buddha-fields—this is the fifth great undertaking of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva forms this thought:
"For the sake of even a single sentient being, I shall practice the bodhisattva conduct in every world throughout the succession of incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas until the end of the future;

as I do for one sentient being, so shall I do for all sentient beings, giving rise to great compassion and causing all sentient beings to dwell securely in Bodhi, never conceiving even a single thought of weariness."
"This is the sixth great undertaking of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
'I shall, for inconceivable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, reverently make offerings to those Tathāgatas'—this is the seventh great undertaking of a bodhisattva mahāsattva."
After those Tathāgatas have entered parinirvāṇa, I shall collect all their relics and erect stūpas and temples;
those stūpas shall be so high and vast as to equal unspeakable numbers of worlds;
and I shall fashion images of the Tathāgatas, towering and magnificent, like inconceivable worlds.
Throughout inconceivable eons, they make offerings with various exquisite jewels, banners, pennants, silk canopies, flowers, and incense, never giving rise to even a single thought of rest;

they teach and transform sentient beings, uphold and protect the True Dharma, and praise it, likewise without a single thought of rest—this is the eighth great undertaking of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

Cultivating those various roots of goodness, they achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and become equal in all respects to all Tathāgatas; they attain the stage of all Tathāgatas—this is the ninth great undertaking of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

Once I have attained Bodhi, throughout unspeakable eons in all worlds, I shall preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma and manifest the inconceivable, sovereign spiritual transformations of a Tathāgata;

yet my body, speech, and mind shall never for a moment give rise to thoughts of weariness or exhaustion. Instead, I shall give rise only to a mind single-mindedly intent on the True Dharma, a mind with the power of a Tathāgata, a mind that fulfills the vows of all sentient beings, a mind of great compassion, and a mind that observes the reality of all phenomena; I shall abide in truthful speech and realize the dharma of quiescent extinction.

All sentient beings are entirely ungraspable, yet this does not contradict any karmic actions; it accords with all Buddhas of the three periods of time, reaching the ultimate limits of the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space. One observes that all phenomena have the characteristic of non-existence, being neither born nor extinguished, and fully accomplishes the supreme great vows of all Buddhas. Performing the great deeds of all Buddhas, one is able to transform and deliver all sentient beings; this is the tenth great undertaking of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of great undertakings of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed wisdom of all Buddhas and never sever the practices of all Bodhisattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of ultimate great tasks for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the ultimate great matter of reverently making offerings to all Tathāgatas;
and the ultimate great matter of delivering and liberating all sentient beings according to their requests.

The ultimate great task of single-mindedly seeking the true Dharma of all Buddhas; the ultimate great task of nurturing all roots of goodness; the ultimate great task of giving birth to the teachings of all Tathāgatas; the ultimate great task of fulfilling all pure great vows; the ultimate great task of practicing all bodhisattva deeds; the ultimate great task of reverently serving all spiritual friends; the ultimate great task of proceeding to the abodes of the Buddhas in all worlds; and the ultimate great task of hearing and upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas while penetrating deeply into the assemblies of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of ultimate great deeds of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the ultimate wisdom of great deeds of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of indestructible faith for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?

That is to say: indestructible faith in all Buddhas; indestructible faith in all Buddha-dharmas; indestructible faith in the noble Saṅgha; indestructible faith in all Bodhisattvas; indestructible faith in all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra); indestructible faith in all sentient beings; indestructible faith in all the great vows of Bodhisattvas; indestructible faith in all the practices of Bodhisattvas; indestructible faith in reverently making offerings to all Buddhas; and indestructible faith in the skillful means of Bodhisattvas for teaching and transforming all sentient beings so that they achieve perfection.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of indestructible faith of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas, they will attain the indestructible faith in the unsurpassed wisdom of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of prophecy for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?

That is to say: the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who exclusively seek liberation; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas whose roots of goodness consist of the fulfillment of truth and the eloquence of truth; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who extensively practice the immeasurable practices of Bodhisattvas; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas in their presence; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas through secret means; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who attain awakening by virtue of their own minds; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who have attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*); the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who teach and bring sentient beings to maturity; the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who exhaust all kalpas; and the prediction of enlightenment for Bodhisattvas who practice with mastery over all things.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of prophecies for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they shall receive prophecy from all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?

That is to say: dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the vows of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the upright mind of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the conduct of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the roots of goodness of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to accord with the roots of goodness of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the right mindfulness of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the purity of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the abiding of spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the entry into the fulfillment of equality by spiritual friends; dedicating all roots of goodness to be identical to the indestructible profound resolve of spiritual friends. If one is thus identical, there is no difference in that identity.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of dedication of roots of goodness of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain all unsurpassed dedications of roots of goodness.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain wisdom. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the wisdom of mastery over all giving;
and the wisdom of mastery over liberation through delighting in all Buddha-dharmas.
The sovereign wisdom that deeply penetrates the immeasurable and boundless wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
the sovereign wisdom that can answer whatever is asked and extinguish all doubts;
and the sovereign wisdom that profoundly understands the true meaning.
They understand the skillful means of all Tathāgatas and penetrate the sovereign wisdom of liberation of all Buddhas;

they understand that even a small root of goodness planted under any Buddha will inevitably fulfill all pure and white roots of goodness, giving rise to the sovereign wisdom of the Tathāgata’s omniscience;
and they are fully endowed with the sovereign wisdom of the inconceivable abodes of Bodhisattvas.
In a single thought-moment, they are able to travel to the abodes of unspeakably many Buddhas with sovereign wisdom;

they awaken to the enlightenment of all Buddhas, penetrate deeply into all dharma-realms, hear and retain all Buddha-dharmas, and enter deeply into the sovereign wisdom of the adorned speech of all Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas attain wisdom;
if Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed, sovereign wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of immeasurable, boundless, and vast resolve generated by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
to give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind directed toward all Buddhas;
and to give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind for the purpose of delivering all sentient beings.
They give rise to immeasurable, boundless, and vast minds, causing all sentient beings, all worlds, and all lands to enter the Dharma-realm;
they give rise to immeasurable, boundless, and vast minds to contemplate all phenomena as being like empty space;
they give rise to immeasurable, boundless, and vast minds to observe all the practices of Bodhisattvas.
They give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind that maintains right mindfulness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind that thoroughly understands the inconceivable karmic fruits and retributions;
they give rise to an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind that adorns and purifies the lands of all Tathāgatas.

They give rise to immeasurable and boundless expansive minds, entering deeply into the great assemblies of all Tathāgatas; they give rise to immeasurable and boundless expansive minds, contemplating the wondrous voices of all Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of immeasurable and boundless expansive minds generated by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these minds, they will attain the ocean of immeasurable and boundless wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of treasuries for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
discerning and knowing all treasuries of dharmas;
bringing forth all treasuries of dharmas;
The treasury of dharanis that universally illumines all;
the treasury of eloquence that analytically explains all dharmas;
and the treasury of skillful means that awakens to the ineffable nature of all dharmas.
The treasury of great spiritual transformations that manifests the sovereign power of all Buddhas;
the treasury of skillful means that gives rise to equality regarding all phenomena;
and the treasury that never departs from the constant vision of all Buddhas.
The treasury of skillful means that enters inconceivable eons, all of which are like illusions;
and the treasury of joyful reverence toward all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten treasuries of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these treasuries, they will attain the great treasury of wisdom of all buddhas and be able to deliver and liberate all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of discipline for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
being disciplined by not slandering any of the Buddha-dharmas;
and being disciplined by having indestructible faith in all Buddhas.
It is the discipline of honoring and revering all bodhisattvas;
the discipline of drawing near to all spiritual friends;
and the discipline of distancing oneself from all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
It is the discipline that nurtures all samādhis of a bodhisattva;
it is the discipline of impartially observing all sentient beings;
it is the discipline of ultimately bringing all roots of goodness to full completion.
They are able to subdue all māras and bring them to harmony;
they fulfill all pāramitās and bring them to harmony.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of taming and compliance of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the taming and compliance of unsurpassed great wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery. What are these ten?
That is to say:
mastery over lifespan, because they maintain their lifespan for immeasurable, boundless, and ineffable eons;
and mastery over the mind, because they give rise to incalculable samādhis and enter profound wisdom.
Mastery over adornment, because one is able to adorn all lands with great adornments;
mastery over karma, because one receives retribution according to the time;
mastery over birth, because one manifests birth in all lands.
Mastery of liberation, because one perceives all worlds as filled with Buddhas;
mastery of vows, because one attains enlightenment at any time and in any land;
mastery of spiritual power, because one manifests all great miraculous transformations.
Mastery over phenomena (*dharmavaśitā*), because they manifest immeasurable and boundless dharma-gates;
mastery over wisdom (*jñānavaśitā*), because in every thought-moment they manifest the awakening to the ten powers and fearlessnesses of a Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the ultimate fulfillment of all-knowledge mastery shared by all Buddhas and bodhisattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery. What are these ten?

They are: mastery over sentient beings, mastery over lands, mastery over dharmas, mastery over bodies, mastery over vows, mastery over spheres of experience, mastery over wisdom, mastery over supernormal powers, and mastery over powers.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
What is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s mastery over sentient beings?
Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of mastery over sentient beings possessed by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are the ten? They are:
mastery in liberating all sentient beings;
Mastery over the perception of all sentient beings;
mastery over teaching the Dharma to all sentient beings without ever missing the proper time;
and mastery over the transformation of all sentient beings.
The mastery of placing all sentient beings upon the path of a single hair-pore without crowding;

the mastery of manifesting as a king among all worlds and all sentient beings; the mastery of manifesting as Śakra or Brahmā among all sentient beings; the mastery of manifesting the unshakable deportment of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas among all sentient beings; the mastery of manifesting the practice of the bodhisattva path among all sentient beings; and the mastery of awakening through the power of omniscience by manifesting the Buddha’s body adorned with the primary and secondary marks among all sentient beings.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery over sentient beings of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery over buddha-fields.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The mastery of making all lands into a single land; the mastery of causing all lands to enter into a single hair-pore;
the mastery of deeply penetrating inexhaustible skillful means within all lands;
the mastery of manifesting a single body seated in the full lotus posture to fill all lands; and the mastery of causing all lands to appear as entering into one's own body.
He possesses mastery in using spiritual power to shake all buddha-fields without causing sentient beings to feel fear;

he possesses mastery in manifesting the adornments of all fields as the adornment of a single field; he possesses mastery in manifesting the adornments of a single field as the adornment of all fields;
and he manifests the body of a single Tathāgata, together with its entire retinue, filling them all completely.
He possesses mastery in manifesting to sentient beings throughout all Buddha-fields—
whether small fields, medium fields, large fields, vast fields, deep fields, inverted fields, downward-facing fields,
upward-facing fields, or level fields— manifesting to sentient beings with such mastery over these various fields.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery over buddha-fields of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery over dharmas. What are the ten?
They are as follows:
All phenomena are but a single phenomenon, and a single phenomenon is all phenomena, yet they do not contradict the sovereign mastery over the characteristics of sentient beings' phenomena;
the Prajñāpāramitā gives birth to all phenomena, awakening all sentient beings with sovereign mastery such that there is nothing they do not understand;
regarding all phenomena, they are entirely free from the conceptualization of phenomena, universally causing sentient beings to enter the supreme Dharma with sovereign mastery.
All phenomena enter into a single skillful means, yet they possess the mastery to analyze and explain them through immeasurable skillful means;
all phenomena transcend the path of language, yet they possess the mastery to expound immeasurable Dharma-gates;
regarding all phenomena, they possess the mastery to turn the inexhaustible wheel of the universal door through skillful means.
All phenomena enter into a single gateway of Dharma; one possesses the mastery to analyze and explain them exhaustlessly throughout unspeakable eons;
all phenomena entirely enter the Buddha-Dharma, possessing the mastery over superior sentient beings;
and all phenomena manifest as infinite and boundless, possessing such mastery.
All phenomena are unimpeded, the limit of reality, immeasurable and boundless like a net of illusions; throughout immeasurable eons, they possess the mastery to teach sentient beings without end.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery over dharmas of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery over the body.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The mastery of causing all sentient beings to enter one's own body;
the mastery of manifesting one's own body as the bodies of all sentient beings;
and the mastery of manifesting the bodies of all Buddhas as the body of a single Buddha.
The mastery of manifesting all Buddha-bodies from within a single Buddha-body;
the mastery of placing all lands within one’s own body;
and the mastery of manifesting to sentient beings a single Dharma-body that pervades the three periods of time.
The mastery of entering samādhi with a single body and arising from samādhi with immeasurable bodies;
the mastery of attaining supreme perfect enlightenment in a single body and manifesting to sentient beings as bodies equal in number to them;
and the mastery of making the bodies of all sentient beings into the body of a single sentient being while manifesting the bodies of all sentient beings.
The physical bodies of all sentient beings manifest as the Dharma-body, and the Dharma-body manifests with mastery as the physical bodies of all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery over the body of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery over vows. What are these ten?
That is to say:
all the vows of all bodhisattvas are their own vows, which is mastery over vows;
through the power of the vows and enlightenment of all Buddhas, they manifest to sentient beings, which is mastery over vows.
According to what is appropriate for each, they cause all to achieve the mastery of vows for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
the mastery of vows that remain uninterrupted throughout incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas;
and the mastery of vows to manifest all bodies while remaining detached from the body of consciousness and abiding in the body of wisdom.
The mastery of vows to fulfill all the affairs of others without abandoning one's own;
the mastery of vows to teach and mature all sentient beings, causing them never to regress;
and the mastery of vows to practice the bodhisattva conduct throughout all incalculable eons without ever interruption.

Attaining perfect enlightenment within the space of a single hair-pore, their power of vows fills all Buddha-fields; for each and every sentient being, they manifest the sovereign power of vows across unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds.

By uttering a single phrase of Dharma, clouds of Dharma universally cover the entire Dharma-realm, thundering the lightning of the true Dharma, flashing the brilliant light of liberation, and pouring down the rain of nectar-like Dharma, fulfilling the heart’s aspirations of all sentient beings through the sovereign power of their vows.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery over vows of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mastery over their spheres of activity.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The Bodhisattva dwells within the realm of the Dharma-dhātu while manifesting within the realms of sentient beings;
dwells within the realm of the Buddhas while manifesting within the realms of Māras; dwells within the realm of nirvāṇa without departing from the realm of saṃsāra;
dwells within the realm of omniscience without departing from the realm of the bodhisattva; and dwells within the realm of quiescent extinction...

Abiding in the realm of non-abandonment while amidst the realm of distracted sentient beings; abiding in the realm detached from all false constructs while not departing from the realm of false constructs;
abiding in the realm of the power of adornment while manifesting what is not the realm of omniscience;
and abiding in the realm of the reality-limit where no sentient beings exist while not abandoning the transformation and liberation of all sentient beings.
While abiding in the realm of the various dhyānas, samādhis, liberations, supernormal powers, and the wisdom of detachment from desire,
they manifest birth in all worlds; while abiding in the realm of the Tathāgata’s conduct and the adornments of bodhi,
they manifest the tranquil deportment of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery over spheres of activity for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of mastery over knowledge.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
Mastery over inexhaustible eloquence and wisdom;
mastery over the wisdom of all dhāraṇīs that brings no confusion;
and mastery over the wisdom that knows the faculties of all sentient beings through the fixed nature of phenomena.
In a single thought-moment, by means of unimpeded mental wisdom, they possess mastery over the knowledge that fully knows the minds and mental factors of all sentient beings;
they possess mastery over the knowledge of the methods for treating illnesses according to the specific afflictions, latent tendencies, and habitual energies within the minds of all sentient beings;
and in a single thought-moment, they penetrate deeply into the mastery of the Tathāgata’s ten powers of wisdom.
The mastery of wisdom that knows the liberation of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time according to their timing through unimpeded knowledge;
the mastery of wisdom that manifests the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment within a single thought-moment for all sentient beings;
and the mastery of wisdom that, by understanding the mind of a single sentient being, thoroughly comprehends the karmic actions of all sentient beings.
The mastery of wisdom that manifests the voices of all sentient beings through the voice of a single sentient being—
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth mastery of wisdom of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of mastery over supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). What are these ten?
That is to say:
manifesting bodies in all worlds; mastery of the supernormal power of the sphere of a single body;

and while sitting among the great assembly of a single Tathāgata to hear and receive the True Dharma, possessing mastery of the supernormal power to hear, retain, and comprehend the teachings of the assemblies of all Buddhas.

The mastery of penetration that, within the mental state of a single sentient being in a single thought-moment, accomplishes unspeakably many unsurpassed enlightenments, such that there is not a single sentient being who does not know it;

the mastery of penetration that, by emitting a single sublime sound, is able to pervade all worlds and produce all various distinct sounds, such that there is not a single sentient being who does not attain understanding;

the mastery of penetration that, within a single thought-moment, manifests the entirety of past eons, such that there is not a single sentient being whose karmic fruits and retributions are not known.
The mastery of supernormal power that causes all worlds to be entirely adorned;
the mastery of supernormal power that observes the equality of the three periods of time;
and the mastery of supernormal power that gives birth to the bodhi and vows of all Buddhas and sentient beings, emitting the great radiance of the Dharma.

All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, and Brahmā, as well as all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, all pay him respectful homage and honor; he is well able to protect and uphold the powers of all Tathāgatas, and his all roots of goodness are universally sovereign.
O Son of the Buddha!
To speak briefly, this is the Bodhisattva’s universal mastery in the equal observation of all phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of mastery of spiritual power (*ṛddhi*)."
What are these ten? They are:
the sovereign spiritual power to cause unspeakably many worlds to enter into a single minute atom;
The sovereign power of spiritual mastery that manifests all Buddha-fields, equal in extent to the entire Dharma-realm, within a single atom;

the sovereign power of spiritual mastery that can contain all great oceans within a single pore and travel through all worlds while ensuring that sentient beings feel no fear or anxiety in their minds;
and the sovereign power of spiritual mastery that can manifest all manner of phenomena within one's own body by encompassing all worlds therein.

With the supernatural power of mastery over the mind, they bind the inconceivable Diamond Ring Mountains with a single hair and carry them all about through every world without causing sentient beings any fear;
they manifest unspeakable eons as a single eon, and manifest a single eon as unspeakably many eons of formation and destruction, without causing sentient beings any fear;
and they manifest the formation and destruction of all worlds through the calamities of water, fire, and wind, without causing sentient beings any fear.
He possesses mastery over spiritual powers such that, when all worlds are destroyed by the calamities of water, fire, and wind, he can sustain all the necessities of life for all sentient beings;

he possesses mastery over spiritual powers such that he can place inconceivable worlds within his palm and cast them far away beyond unspeakable numbers of worlds without causing sentient beings any fear or anxiety;
and he possesses mastery over spiritual powers such that he causes all sentient beings to understand that all Buddha-fields are like empty space.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of sovereign spiritual powers of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of mastery of power.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
Mastery over the power of sentient beings, because they do not abandon sentient beings, but rather teach, transform, and subdue them;
mastery over the power of Buddha-fields, because they manifest and adorn all Buddha-fields with unspeakable ornaments;
mastery over the power of dharmas, because they cause all bodies to enter the bodiless state.
Mastery over the power of eons, because it does not interrupt any bodhisattva practice;
mastery over the power of the Buddhas, because it awakens sentient beings who have long been asleep in the cycle of birth and death;
mastery over the power of conduct, because it encompasses all bodhisattva practices.
The Tathāgata possesses mastery of power because he delivers all sentient beings;
he possesses mastery of the power of teacherless wisdom because he has spontaneously awakened to all phenomena;
and he possesses mastery of the power of all-knowledge because the wisdom of the Omniscient One has awakened him.
The mastery of the power of great compassion, because of not abandoning any sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery of power of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mastery of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, beginning with mastery over sentient beings.

If a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these ten kinds of mastery, whether they wish to attain unexcelled bodhi or do not wish to attain unexcelled bodhi, they possess mastery according to their will.
Although they have attained bodhi, they nevertheless do not cease the various practices of a bodhisattva. Why is this?
Because bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give rise to great vows, they skillfully employ expedient means to manifest immeasurable gateways of sovereign dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of playful supernatural powers (*abhijñā-vikrīḍita*) of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:

when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva manifests the body of a buddha-field within the bodies of sentient beings, yet does not destroy the bodies of those sentient beings, this is the first supernatural power of playful mastery;

when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva manifests the body of sentient beings within the body of a buddha-field, yet does not depart from the body of that buddha-field, this is the second supernatural power of playful mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests the bodies of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas within the body of a Buddha, yet does not diminish the body of a Tathāgata; this is the third supernatural power of mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests the body of a Tathāgata within the bodies of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, yet does not increase the bodies of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; this is the fourth supernatural power of mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests the body of unsurpassed Bodhi within the body of a Bodhisattva, yet does not abandon the practices of a Bodhisattva; this is the fifth supernatural power of mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests a bodhisattva body within the body of unsurpassed enlightenment, yet does not diminish that body of enlightenment; this is the sixth supernatural power of mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests the continuous succession of birth and death within the realm of nirvāṇa, yet does not cling to the realm of nirvāṇa; this is the seventh supernatural power of mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests the realm of nirvāṇa within the realm of birth and death, yet does not enter the ultimate nirvāṇa without remainder; this is the eighth supernatural power of mastery.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, while in the samādhi of correct reception (*samyaksamādhi*), manifests all dignified postures—walking, standing, sitting, and reclining—yet does not relinquish that samādhi of correct reception; this is the ninth sport of supernatural power (*abhijñā-vikrīḍita*).

Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva hears and upholds the Dharma from a single Buddha, yet is able to travel to the abodes of unspeakably many Buddhas to listen to and receive the True Dharma; yet he does not leave his original seat, nor does he divide his body, nor does he arise from samādhi. In every thought-moment, within each and every door of the samādhi-body, he produces unspeakably unspeakable doors of the samādhi-body. While all kalpas may come to an end, the production of the doors of the samādhi-body by the Bodhisattva can never be exhausted; this is the tenth sport of supernatural power.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of playful supernatural powers of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed great wisdom of all Buddhas—the playful supernatural power.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of supreme practices for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the supreme conduct of universally manifesting to sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm by means of infinite gates of skillful means;
and the supreme conduct of universally manifesting to sentient beings by adorning all worlds with infinite adornments.
The supreme practice of knowing that the arising of all realms of sentient beings is entirely like a magical transformation;
the supreme practice of producing the body of a bodhisattva from the body of a Tathāgata, and producing the body of a Tathāgata from the body of a bodhisattva;
and the supreme practice of producing world-systems within the realm of empty space, and producing the realm of empty space within world-systems.
The supreme practice of giving rise to the realm of nirvana from within the realm of birth and death, and giving rise to the realm of birth and death from within the realm of nirvana;
the supreme practice of giving rise to the sounds of all Buddha-dharmas from the voice of a single sentient being;
and the supreme practice of manifesting a single body through immeasurable gateways of bodies, and manifesting the differentiation of all bodies through the gateway of a single body.

The supreme practice of pervading all worlds with a single body; the supreme practice of causing all sentient beings in a single thought-moment to give birth to immeasurable and boundless Dharma gates and attain equal, perfect enlightenment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of supreme practices of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these practices, they will attain the supreme practice of the unsurpassed great wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of power. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the power of the straight mind, because it is free from attachment to all worlds;
the power of the profound mind, because it does not destroy any of the Buddha-dharmas.
The power of skillful means, because it brings all bodhisattva practices to ultimate fulfillment;
the power of wisdom, because it knows the mental activities of all sentient beings;
the power of vows, because it causes the vows of all sentient beings to be fulfilled.
The power of practice, because it remains uninterrupted throughout all future kalpas;
the power of the vehicle, because it gives birth to and universally manifests all vehicles without ever turning away from the Great Vehicle;
and the power of the play of supernormal knowledges, because within a single hair-pore it manifests all pure worlds and the appearance of all Tathāgatas in the world.
The power of awakening, because one awakens to the equality of the thought of enlightenment with that of all sentient beings;
and the power of turning the wheel of Dharma, because within a single phrase of the Dharma one explains the various faculties and aspirations of all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten powers of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these powers, they will attain the supreme ten powers of the omniscience of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of fearlessness. What are these ten?
That is to say:
Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are able to hear and retain all inquiries and challenges, forming this thought:

"If there should be anyone from any world throughout the ten directions who comes to question me, it is impossible that I would be unable to answer; indeed, I do not perceive even the slightest sign of fear."
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, the Bodhisattva ultimately attains all forms of fearlessness and dwells securely in fearlessness;
for all sentient beings, he completely cuts through their doubts and delusions according to whatever they ask—this is the first fearlessness.

Regarding all speech and sounds, as well as all written characters, the Tathāgata bestows upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva unimpeded eloquence that reaches the ultimate further shore. Thus he reflects:

"Should any sentient beings from the worlds of the ten directions come to challenge me with difficult questions, it is impossible that I would be unable to answer them; I do not perceive even the slightest sign of fear."
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he is able to utterly extinguish all doubts and hesitations and dwells securely in fearlessness; this is the second fearlessness.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all dharmas are empty, being devoid of self and what belongs to self, without an agent or one who causes action, without a knower, without a life-principle, without a nourisher, and without a *pudgala*. He is detached from the aggregates, elements, and sense bases, and free from all false views. With a mind like space, he reflects thus:
"It is impossible for any sentient being to cause me to give rise to evil in body, speech, or mind."
Why is this? Because a bodhisattva is always free from the notions of "self" and "what belongs to self";
it is impossible for them to give rise to fear, nor do they perceive even the slightest sign of fear.
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, his practice of the bodhisattva path cannot be thwarted; this is the third fearlessness.

Protected by all Buddhas, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes the powers of a Tathāgata, practices the conduct of a Tathāgata, and never deviates from the majestic demeanor of a Tathāgata. He forms this thought:
"It is impossible for anyone to come and censure my majestic demeanor," and thus he does not perceive even the slightest sign of fear.
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma amidst the great assembly; this is the fourth fearlessness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s body, speech, and mind are pure, and being far removed from all evils, he reflects thus:
"It is impossible for anyone to come and reproach me for faults of body, speech, or mind; indeed, I do not perceive even the slightest sign of fear."
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he is able to teach and transform all sentient beings; this is the fifth fearlessness.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are constantly followed and guarded by Vajrapāṇi, as well as by all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, and Brahmā, who constantly follow and guard him with reverence and offerings. All Buddhas constantly protect and keep him in mind. The Bodhisattva reflects thus:

"It is impossible that any Māras, their retinues, or various non-Buddhists, upon seeing sentient beings come to me, could obstruct my unsurpassed bodhi; such a thing cannot occur, nor does he perceive even the slightest sign of fear."
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he dwells securely in fearlessness and joyfully practices the bodhisattva deeds; this is the sixth fearlessness.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, free from delusion and possessing right mindfulness, is born in accordance with the Tathāgatas and achieves the foremost faculty of mind (*manas-indriya*). He forms this thought:

"Regarding all the True Dharma taught by all Buddhas—the bodies of phrases and the bodies of flavor that accord with enlightenment—it is impossible that I should be unable to receive and uphold it according to the Dharma, nor do I perceive even the slightest sign of fear."
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he upholds and protects the True Dharma of the Tathāgata; this is the seventh fearlessness.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, fully endowed with skillful means and wisdom, having reached the ultimate shore of all the powers of a bodhisattva, possesses a pure and straightforward mind. He teaches and transforms sentient beings, making the great vow for bodhi.

Because he gives rise to great compassion toward sentient beings, he manifests birth within the turbid world of afflictions and manifests the enjoyment of the five desires, maintaining a wife, children, and various kinsmen. For the sake of transforming sentient beings, the Bodhisattva further reflects:
"Although I am here, I shall not give rise to delusion or confusion that obstructs the dharma-gate of eloquence regarding bodhi, liberation, and samādhi;
it is impossible for me to create such an obstruction."
Why is this? Because the bodhisattva has attained mastery over all dharmas and reached the ultimate other shore;
practicing the bodhisattva conduct, they abide securely in bodhi.
He cannot be disturbed by the delusions arising from birth within all worlds;
it is impossible for him to be so disturbed, and he does not perceive even the slightest sign of fear.
Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he manifests birth in all worlds; this is the eighth fearlessness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abandons delusion and realizes all-knowledge;
he abides in the bodhisattva path and mounts the Great Vehicle.
Abiding by the power of the mind of omniscience, he manifests as a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha without altering his majestic deportment. The bodhisattva forms this thought:
"I shall never realize the path of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha; it is impossible for me to undergo such realization, nor do I perceive even the slightest sign of fear."

Because he perceives not even the slightest sign of fear, he dwells securely in fearlessness and is able to manifest all vehicles in their full perfection, culminating in the ultimately equal Mahāyāna; this is the ninth fearlessness.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes all pure and white dharmas, accumulates roots of goodness, fulfills all aspirations, and attains universal illumination; firmly abiding in bodhi, they fully perfect all bodhisattva practices.
Having received from all Buddhas the Tathāgata’s prediction of omniscience upon their crowns, they teach and transform sentient beings without abandoning the bodhisattva path, thinking thus:

"If there are sentient beings who should be transformed, it is impossible that I would fail to manifest the realm of a Tathāgata to them at the appropriate time, nor do I perceive even the slightest sign of fear."

Because they do not perceive even the slightest sign of fear, they abide in fearlessness; according to those who are to be transformed, they universally manifest the realm of the Tathāgata, yet they never sever their bodhisattva vows and practices—this is the tenth fearlessness.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of fearlessness of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed fearlessness of all Buddhas, yet without ever abandoning the fearlessness of a bodhisattva.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Thirty-Nine and Scroll Forty,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-Three: The Fifth Part of the Chapter on Transcending the World.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of unshared dharmas of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas."

What are these ten? They are as follows: the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the six pāramitās without relying on the awakening of others; they give with an impartial mind, free from all stinginess; they maintain pure precepts, remaining far removed from evil conduct; they achieve patience such that the mind cannot be shaken; they diligently cultivate vigor, never regressing throughout all kalpas; they enter deeply into meditative concentration, free from all distraction; and they give birth to wisdom, remaining far removed from false views.
This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the six pāramitās, following the path of the pāramitās, which is the foremost unshared dharma realized without depending on others.

“The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva gathers in all sentient beings and benefits them, constantly providing the gift of Dharma; he maintains a gentle countenance and speaks with loving words toward all sentient beings, remaining far removed from harsh speech; he always gives rise to a joyful mind for all sentient beings and brings them true benefit, causing all sentient beings to realize and awaken to bodhi and remain far removed from evil thoughts; he fully accomplishes the meaning of equality and reality. This is the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s gathering of sentient beings, the path of compliant gathering, which is realized through no other—this is the second unique quality.”

"Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are skilled in dedication; they do not seek karmic retribution, but dedicate in accordance with the bodhi of all Buddhas. They do not cling to any worldly samādhis, but dedicate toward Buddha-wisdom to benefit sentient beings. This is what is meant by a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva being skilled in dedication: single-mindedly seeking the roots of goodness and unsurpassed wisdom of all Buddhas to benefit sentient beings, awakening through no other means—this is the third unique quality."
"Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, having attained mastery in skillful means and reached the ultimate further shore, accord with the world and associate with the world without weariness."

They are correctly oriented toward noble conduct, remaining far removed from all the paths of deliverance belonging to the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; they teach and bring to maturity all sentient beings without attachment to their own pleasure;
they skillfully know all dhyānas, liberations, samādhis, and meditative attainments (samāpattis), and having arisen from these various samādhis, they attain mastery over them.
Within the cycle of birth and death, their minds are free from weariness; they traverse saṃsāra as if visiting a garden or a pleasure grove.
They dwell securely within all the palaces of Māras, manifesting as Śakra, Brahmā, and other deities of infinite sovereignty.
Amidst all births and deaths, the light of their wisdom is pure and radiant, illuminating and dispelling the darkness of ignorance.
Among all the multitudes, they renounce the household life to become monastics, remaining unattached to divergent views.

They manifest mastery in all worldly scripts, recitations, discourses, speech, arithmetic, methods of sealing, and all forms of entertainment; appearing in female form, their skillful arts and talents are able to transform the minds of others.
Regarding worldly dharmas and supramundane dharmas, they are able to provide answers to all questions and have reached the ultimate further shore;
regarding worldly matters and supramundane matters, they likewise have completely reached the further shore;
they constantly observe sentient beings, manifesting themselves as all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas without altering their majestic deportment, never forgetting the Mahāyāna.

In every moment of thought, they manifest the realization of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed bodhi, yet they do not cease the practices of a bodhisattva; this is the fourth unshared quality of a bodhisattva mahāsattva, wherein they have fully cultivated skillful means, reached the other shore, and attained awakening without depending on another.

“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas skillfully know the samādhi of simultaneous transformation and the samādhi of overturning; they sport with wisdom and the supernormal powers, reaching the ultimate further shore of wisdom.”
Constantly abiding in nirvana while manifesting the gateway of birth and death; knowing there is no limit to the realm of sentient beings, yet teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity;
constantly abiding on the ultimate shore of quiescent extinction, yet manifesting as dwelling amidst the blazing fires of affliction;
constantly abiding in the single, wondrous diamond-like Dharma-body, yet manifesting the infinite gateways of the bodies of sentient beings. Constantly...
They are able to correctly enter various dhyānas and samādhis while manifesting the five sensual pleasures for the entertainment of sentient beings;
they constantly delight in tranquility and remain detached from the triple world while teaching and transforming all beings to nurture their roots of goodness;

they constantly delight in the True Dharma while manifesting themselves surrounded by hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens who enjoy their company, their bodies adorned with the marks and signs of a hundred merits.
Though manifesting in the form of the poor, lowly, and base, they constantly distance themselves from all evils and cultivate wholesome karma;
yet while manifesting birth in all evil realms, they ultimately reach the further shore of Buddha-wisdom without ever abandoning the bodhisattva’s body of wisdom.
When a bodhisattva accomplishes such immeasurable wisdom as this, no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas are able to know it, let alone all ignorant sentient beings.
This is the fifth unique quality of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"The physical, verbal, and mental actions of a bodhisattva mahāsattva are preceded by wisdom; all their deportments and activities are pure."
Having accomplished great loving-kindness, they are forever free from the intent to kill;

even unto being far removed from wrong views and fully endowed with right view—this is the sixth unique quality of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, wherein their actions of body, speech, and mind follow wisdom.

"Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having accomplished great compassion, do not abandon any sentient beings, but undergo on behalf of all sentient beings the sufferings of the hells, animals, hungry ghosts, and King Yama."
To benefit sentient beings with a mind free from weariness or fatigue, liberating the entire realm of all living beings;
to have no defiled attachment toward any sensual pleasures;
and to constantly extinguish the aggregates of suffering for sentient beings without abandoning great compassion—this is the seventh unique quality of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
"The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is loved and respected by all sentient beings; Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings, and others all revere and make offerings to him.
All sentient beings always delight in seeing him, never feeling satiated."

Why is this? Because the bodhisattva’s original practice of the path is characterized by a mind free from attachment and entirely pure, and because his deportment is fully perfected, all sentient beings delight in beholding him without weariness; this is the eighth unique quality of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
"The mind of omniscience of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is firm and upright, adorned with great adornments;

even when entering difficult places, the abodes of wicked people, or the realms of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, he never regresses from or loses the pure and wondrous jewel of the mind of omniscience."

For example, there is a water-jewel called Pure Light; although it remains in turbid water, its precious nature remains unchanged, and it is able to make that turbid water entirely clear. The Bodhisattva is also like this:

though situated amidst various hardships, among evil people, or among Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, he never abandons the pure jewel-mind of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
