He causes all sentient beings to eliminate false views and the turbidity of afflictions, and to abide in the pure jewel-mind of omniscience. This is the ninth unique quality of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

“The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains the perfection of the Dharma of self-awakened wisdom, receives the prophecy of no-teacher, and is crowned upon the head with the fillet of the stainless Dharma; he does not abandon the mind of reverence and making offerings toward the Tathāgata, nor does he forsake spiritual friends—this is the tenth unique quality of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.”
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of uncommon dharmas of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain all the Buddhas' supreme and great uncommon dharmas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of karma for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the karma of worlds, because it is able to thoroughly adorn and purify all worlds;
the karma of Tathāgatas, because it serves and makes offerings to all Buddhas.
The karma of a bodhisattva’s spiritual friends, because their roots of goodness are identical;
the karma of sentient beings, because of teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity;
and the karma of future lives, because of gathering in all [beings] throughout the limits of the future.
The karma of supernormal power, because they are able to travel through all worlds without leaving their original place;

the karma of pure light, because they emit immeasurable and boundless rays of colored light, at the tip of each ray of which there are pure lotuses made of the seven treasures, and upon each lotus pedestal there is a bodhisattva sitting in the full-lotus posture, all of whom are clearly manifested;
and the karma of ensuring the non-interruption of the Three Jewels, because after all Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa, they uphold and protect the Buddha’s True Dharma.
The karma of transformation, for the purpose of traveling through the ten directions to preach the Dharma and transform sentient beings;
and the karma of maintenance, for the purpose of manifesting before sentient beings according to their aspirations so that they may fulfill all great vows.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of activities of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these activities, they will attain the supreme, great activity of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of bodies. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the bodhisattva’s non-coming body, because it does not undergo birth in any realm of existence;
the bodhisattva’s non-going body, because it cannot be found by seeking in any realm of existence.
The Bodhisattva’s body is not unreal, for it is as that which is attained by all worlds;
the Bodhisattva’s body is not empty, for he understands the reality of all worlds;
the Bodhisattva’s body is inexhaustible, for it cannot be severed until the end of the future.
The Bodhisattva’s firm body, because no māras whatsoever can destroy it;
the Bodhisattva’s immovable body, because no māras or heterodox teachers whatsoever can move it;
the Bodhisattva’s mark-body, because he manifests the pure marks of a hundred merits.
The Bodhisattva’s formless body, because the characteristics of phenomena are ultimately devoid of all marks;
the Bodhisattva’s universally reaching body, because it is entirely equal to the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of bodies of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these bodies, they will attain the supreme and inexhaustible body of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of physical actions (*kāyakarman*). What are these ten?
That is to say:
the bodhisattva’s physical action of filling all worlds with a single body;
and the bodhisattva’s physical action of manifesting his body before all sentient beings.
The physical activity of manifesting birth in the bodies of bodhisattvas within every realm of existence;
the physical activity of traveling through all worlds;
and the physical activity of approaching the presence of all Buddhas and their great assemblies.
The physical karma of a Bodhisattva that is able to universally cover all worlds with a single palm;
the physical karma of a Bodhisattva that can grind all the Diamond Ring Mountains (Vajra-prakāra-parvata) with the hand until they are like fine dust;
and the physical karma of a Bodhisattva that manifests within their own body all sentient beings and the formation and destruction of all Buddha-lands.
The bodhisattva’s physical action that is able to pervasively cover all sentient beings with a single body;

and the bodhisattva’s physical action that universally manifests within one's own body all adorned and purified buddha-fields and all sentient beings, ultimately accomplishing unsurpassed enlightenment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of physical actions of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these actions, they will attain the supreme Great Dharma of all Buddhas and be able to awaken all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of bodies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the body of the pāramitās, because it is correctly directed toward bodhi;
the body of the four means of integration, because it does not abandon sentient beings.
The body of great compassion, because it undergoes immeasurable suffering on behalf of all sentient beings without weariness;
the body of great kindness, because it rescues and protects all sentient beings;
the body of merit, because it benefits all sentient beings.
The body of wisdom, because it is the vajra-body of all Buddhas;
the pure dharma-body, because it is far removed from birth and death within the various realms of existence;
the body of skillful means, because it is able to manifest universally to all sentient beings.
The body of spiritual power, because it manifests all sovereign powers;
the body of awakening, because it realizes awakening at all times.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of bodies of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these bodies, they will attain the unsurpassed body of great wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of speech. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a gentle mouth, for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
an ambrosial mouth, for the sake of cooling all sentient beings.
The mouth is not in vain, because it speaks what is true;
the mouth acts according to reality, because it utters no false words even in dreams;
the mouth is honored, because all Śakras, Brahmās, and the Four Great Kings show it reverence and respect.
The profound mouth, because it manifests the true Dharma;
the firm mouth, because it expounds immeasurable teachings that can never be exhausted;
the upright mouth, because all its sounds are endowed with eloquence.
The mouth of adornment, because it universally manifests according to the time and according to karmic retribution;
the mouth of omniscience, because it delivers sentient beings according to what is appropriate for them.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of speech of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in this speech, they will attain the supreme, pure, and wondrous speech of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of pure actions by which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas adorn their verbal karma. What are these ten?
That is to say:
delighting in hearing the pure voice of the Tathāgata purifies the bodhisattva’s vocal karma;
delighting in hearing the pure voice of the bodhisattvas purifies the bodhisattva’s vocal karma.
Not speaking words that all sentient beings do not wish to hear purifies the bodhisattva’s verbal karma;
being free from the four faults of speech in past lives purifies the bodhisattva’s verbal karma;
and joyfully praising the Tathāgata purifies the bodhisattva’s verbal karma.
To praise the Buddha’s true merits with a loud voice at the stupas and temples of the Tathāgata purifies the bodhisattva’s verbal karma;
to single-mindedly and universally bestow the True Dharma upon sentient beings purifies the bodhisattva’s verbal karma;
and to praise the Tathāgata with music and song purifies the bodhisattva’s verbal karma.
To listen to and receive the true Dharma from the Buddhas without sparing one’s own body or life is to purify the bodhisattva’s verbal karma;
to never abandon the bodhisattva Dharma-preacher while listening to and receiving the true Dharma, serving and making offerings to them, is to purify the bodhisattva’s verbal karma.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of pure actions by which a bodhisattva mahāsattva purifies the verbal karma of a bodhisattva and gives rise to the pure verbal karma of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!"
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas produce such pure verbal karma, they attain ten kinds of protection.
What are these ten? They are as follows:

It is protected by all the celestial kings and the various devas who act as guardians; by the dragon kings, yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, Brahmā kings, and the various Brahmā devas; and it is protected by all the Buddhas, the Dharma Kings.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is how a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to pure verbal karma and attains ten kinds of protection;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to such pure verbal karma and attains these ten kinds of protection, they will then be able to accomplish ten great tasks.
What are these ten? They are:
causing all realms of sentient beings to be entirely filled with joy;
There is no realm of lands that is not heard and known;
they are able to activate all faculties;
and they are able to purify all natures and realms.
They uproot the realm of all afflictions;
they distance themselves from the realm of all habitual tendencies;
and they clarify and purify the realm of all straightforward minds.
It nurtures the realm of all profound intentions;
it fills the realm of the nature of all phenomena;
and it illuminates the realm of great parinirvāṇa.
These are the ten.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mind."
What are the ten? They are as follows:
a mind like the great earth, because it sustains all the roots of goodness of all sentient beings;
A mind equal to the great ocean, because it upholds the great dharma-ocean of the immeasurable and boundless wisdom of all Buddhas;
a mind equal to Sumeru, the king of mountains, because it causes all sentient beings to dwell securely in unsurpassed roots of goodness;
a mind like a mani jewel, because it is free from afflictions and possesses a pure and upright heart.
The Vajra mind, because it definitively knows all phenomena;
the mind of the solid Vajra-encircling mountain, because no māras or non-Buddhists can destroy it;
the Lotus-like mind, because no worldly dharmas can defile it.
A mind like the udumbara flower, for it is difficult to encounter in all kalpas;
a mind like the pure sun, for it eliminates the cataracts, obscurations, and darkness of ignorance in all sentient beings;
a mind like space, for it cannot be measured by any sentient being.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mind of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these minds, they will attain the supreme, pure, great mind of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of arousal of the mind for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
they resolve to deliver all sentient beings;
they resolve to uproot the afflictions of all sentient beings.
They give rise to the mind that eliminates all habitual tendencies;
they give rise to the mind that eliminates all doubts and delusions;
they possess a pure mind free from doubt.
They resolve to generate the mind that eliminates the suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings;
they resolve to generate the mind that eliminates all hardships and calamities of the evil realms;
they resolve to generate the mind that accords with the teachings of all Buddhas.
They give rise to the mind that studies all that is to be learned by all bodhisattvas;
they give rise to the mind that awakens to the bodhi of all buddhas and manifests for all sentient beings a state that is not entered by the ordinary or the foolish;
they give rise to the mind that beats the great dharma drum so its sound is heard throughout all worlds, universally illuminating the faculties of all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mental resolve of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these resolves, they will attain the unsurpassed mental resolve of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of fulfilled minds of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
filling all realms of empty space, because sentient beings are boundless;
filling all dharma-realms, because they penetrate deeply into the immeasurable and the limitless.
It fulfills all three periods of time, because it attains complete liberation within a single thought-moment;

it fulfills all Buddhas, because it clearly understands their descent into the womb, conception, birth, renunciation of the home, attainment of the Way, turning of the wheel of the sublime Dharma, and even their Great Parinirvāṇa;
it fulfills the realms of all sentient beings, because it definitively knows their aspirations, habitual tendencies, and faculties.
It fulfills the light of wisdom, because it accordantly understands the entire dharma-realm;
it fulfills the immeasurable and boundless, because it realizes that all phenomena are like an illusory net;
it fulfills non-arising, because all phenomena lack intrinsic nature.
They are fulfilled in non-obstruction, because there is no hindrance regarding their own minds or the minds of others;
they are fulfilled in mastery, because they manifest the attainment of Bodhi in every thought-moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which the mind of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is fulfilled;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these states of mind, they will be able to fully accomplish all the unsurpassed and immeasurable adornments of the Buddha-dharma.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of faculties (*indriya*). What are these ten?
That is to say:
the faculty of joy, because one’s faith in all Buddhas is indestructible;
the faculty of delighting in bodhisattvas, because one awakens to the bodhi of all Buddhas.
The root of non-retrogression, because it brings all tasks to ultimate completion;
the root of abiding, because it dwells securely in all bodhisattva practices;
the profound root, because it awakens to the skillful means of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
The unceasing faculty, because it brings all matters concerning sentient beings to ultimate completion;
the diamond-like faculty, because it definitively and thoroughly knows all phenomena;
the diamond-light-flame faculty, because it universally illumines the realms of all Buddhas.
It is the root of non-confusion, for all Tathāgatas possess a single body;
it is the root of the unobstructed limit, for it penetrates deeply into the ten powers of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten faculties of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these faculties, they will attain the unsurpassed pure faculties of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of straightforward mind for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a straightforward mind that is untainted by any worldly dharmas;
a straightforward mind that is untainted by the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
A straightforward mind that accords with enlightenment;
a straightforward mind that does not deviate from the path to omniscience;
and a straightforward mind that cannot be thwarted or destroyed by any demons or externalists.
The direct mind that is unstained, perfect, pure, wise, and straightforward;
the direct mind that is able to grasp and uphold all teachings heard exactly as they were taught;
and the direct mind that makes no selection regarding any place of rebirth.
The straightforward mind that penetrates deeply into subtle wisdom;
the straightforward mind that skillfully cultivates all Buddha-dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of straightforward mind of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these minds, they will attain the unsurpassed, pure, and straightforward mind of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of profound resolve for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the profound mind of non-retrogression, because it nurtures all wholesome dharmas;
the profound mind free from doubt, because it understands the subtle and secret teachings of all Buddhas.
They correctly maintain the profound mind because they do not abandon the great vows and practices of a bodhisattva;
they possess the unsurpassed, upright, and profound mind because they have deeply entered all the teachings of the Buddhas;
they possess the penetratingly realized profound mind because they have attained mastery over all the teachings of the Buddhas.
The profound mind of excellence, because it penetrates deeply into various skillful means;
the foremost profound mind, because it reaches ultimate perfection regarding all objective realms;
the sovereign profound mind, because it adorns all sovereign samādhis without interruption.
They are fully endowed with the profound mind because they have embraced their original great vows;
they do not abandon the profound mind because they teach and transform all classes of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of profound resolve of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in these resolves, they will attain the unsurpassed, pure, and profound resolve of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of skillful means. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the skillful means of giving, which consists in relinquishing everything without seeking recompense;
and the skillful means of learning all that is to be learned, upholding all precepts, and fully practicing the dhūtas with pure deportment, without disparaging others.
They are free from all entanglements, inversions, ill-will, and pride, through the skillful means of enduring all the evils of sentient beings;
they possess the skillful means of non-retrogressive diligence, because they never forget any object as they bring to ultimate completion the actions of body, speech, and mind;
and they possess the skillful means of all dhyānas, samādhis, liberations, and supernormal powers, because they remain far removed from all five desires and all afflictions.
The skillful means of right-directed wisdom nourish all merits because the mind never knows satiety;
the skillful means of great compassion teach that all sentient beings are non-existent as sentient beings;
and the skillful means of not abandoning great compassion involve undergoing all manner of suffering on behalf of all sentient beings because one understands that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature.
The skillful means of awakening through the ten powers consist of the definitive, unimpeded wisdom that manifests for all sentient beings;
the skillful means of turning the non-regressive wheel of Dharma consist of turning it so as to reach the minds of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of skillful means of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme, great wisdom and skillful means of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of joyful cultivation for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
they delight in cultivating the most supreme by honoring all roots of goodness through skillful means;
they delight in cultivating adornment by giving rise to all manner of adornments.
They delight in cultivating vast undertakings because their minds are increasingly expansive;
they delight in cultivating quiescence because they have deeply entered the methods of profound skillful means;
they delight in cultivating the boundless because they give rise to immeasurable resolve.
They delight in cultivating wholesome retention, for they are protected and remembered by all Buddhas;
they delight in cultivating the indestructible, for no demonic activities can destroy them;
they delight in cultivating certainty, for they understand all karmic retributions.
They delight in cultivating the present, because they are able to manifest great transformations through sovereign spiritual powers at will;
they delight in cultivating listening and receiving, because they receive the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas;
and they delight in cultivating mastery, because they attain Bodhi according to their wish and at any time.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of joyful cultivation of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this cultivation, they will attain the unsurpassed joyful cultivation of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of liberation through which Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas deeply penetrate the worlds. What are these ten?
That is to say:
all worlds entering into one world; and one world entering into all worlds.
A single lotus seat and a single Tathāgata body fill all worlds;
they manifest that all worlds are entirely empty;
and with the adornments of all Buddhas, they adorn all worlds.
A single bodhisattva body fills all worlds;
all worlds are placed within a single pore;
and all worlds enter the body of a single sentient being.
A single Buddha’s place of enlightenment and a single Bodhi tree fill all worlds;
a single sublime sound fills all worlds, such that according to their capacities, there are none who do not hear and understand it, and all are brought to joy.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of liberation through which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter deeply into worlds;
if Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme liberation of all Buddhas for manifesting Buddha-lands.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten ways in which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas enter into the nature of sentient beings. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the entire realm of sentient beings enters into the nature of bodilessness;
the entire realm of sentient beings all enters into the body of a single sentient being.
The entire realm of sentient beings enters the body of a bodhisattva;
the entire realm of sentient beings enters the nature-treasury (dharmatā-garbha) of the Tathāgata;
the entire realm of sentient beings enters the realm of a single sentient being.
The entire realm of sentient beings enters the vessels of the Buddhadharma;
the entire realm of sentient beings enters the realms of Śakra and Brahmā, universally manifesting according to the forms and types of sentient beings;
the entire realm of sentient beings manifests entry among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas without altering their dignified deportment.
The realm of all sentient beings enters into the adornment of the bodhisattva’s merits, thereby adorning all sentient beings;
the realm of all sentient beings enters into the adornment of the Tathāgata’s marks and signs, wherein the form-body is tranquil and majestic deportment is manifested for sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas enter the nature of sentient beings;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide securely in this nature, they will attain the supreme sovereign nature of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of habitual tendencies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?

They are as follows: the habitual tendencies of the bodhicitta; the habitual tendencies of roots of goodness; the habitual tendencies of teaching and transforming sentient beings; the habitual tendencies of seeing Buddhas; the habitual tendencies of taking birth in pure lands; the habitual tendencies of the bodhisattva practices; the habitual tendencies of great vows; the habitual tendencies of the perfections; the habitual tendencies of giving rise to the dharma of equality; and the habitual tendencies of various differentiated realms.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of habitual tendencies of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;

if Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will be able to eliminate all habitual tendencies of affliction in all sentient beings and attain the habitual tendencies of the Buddha’s unsurpassed great wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of blazing in Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
it is to blaze forth throughout all realms of sentient beings, in order to teach and transform them until they reach ultimate maturity;
and it is to blaze forth throughout all worlds, in order to completely adorn and purify them.
The Tathāgata is ablaze because he has brought all bodhisattva practices to ultimate completion;
he is ablaze with roots of goodness because he has accumulated the various marks and signs of a Tathāgata’s merit;
he is ablaze with great compassion because he eradicates the suffering of all sentient beings.
Blazing with great compassion, because it causes all sentient beings to dwell securely in the unsurpassed bliss of the Tathāgata;
blazing with the perfections (*pāramitā*), because it accumulates all the adornments of a bodhisattva;
blazing with skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), because it manifests in every appropriate manner.
The bodhicitta is blazing because it attains unimpeded wisdom;
in brief, all bodhisattvas are blazing with respect to all phenomena because they clearly penetrate and fully understand all phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of blazing of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;

if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will be able to ultimately never sever the various practices of a bodhisattva, extinguish all the blazing of afflictions, and attain the unsurpassed blazing of the True Dharma of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of inclinations for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?

That is to say: tending toward the perfections; tending toward training; tending toward wisdom; tending toward the true meaning; tending toward the sublime Dharma; tending toward the production of roots of goodness; tending toward seeing the Buddhas; tending toward the various gateways of bodhisattva practices; tending toward unexcelled enlightenment; and tending toward turning the wheel of Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten modes of approach for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides in these modes, they will attain the unsurpassed Dharma of the modes of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten things by which a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva can fully accomplish all the Buddha-dharmas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
having deep faith that spiritual friends are fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma;
and having deep faith that the Buddha’s teachings are fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma.
Not slandering the true Dharma, they are endowed with the Buddha-dharmas;
being free from heedless conduct, destroying arrogance, and skillfully dedicating their roots of goodness, they are endowed with the Buddha-dharmas;
having deep faith that the realm of all Buddhas is immeasurable, they are endowed with the Buddha-dharmas.
They penetrate all worlds and are fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma;
they abide in the dharma-realm and are fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma;
they leave behind all realms of Māra and are fully endowed with the Buddha-dharma.
They maintain right mindfulness of all Buddhas as being fully endowed with the Buddha-dharmas;
they have deep faith that the Tathāgatas have accomplished the ten powers and are fully endowed with the Buddha-dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten matters by which a bodhisattva mahāsattva can fulfill all Buddha-dharmas;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the fulfillment of the supreme, great wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of loss of the Buddha-dharma that Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should distance themselves from. What are these ten?
That is to say:
giving rise to a mind of arrogance toward spiritual friends causes one to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma;
fearing the suffering of birth and death causes one to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma.
To weary of bodhisattva practice is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma;
to weary of taking birth is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma;
to delight in and cling to samādhi is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma.
To give rise to doubt and uncertainty regarding all roots of goodness is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma;
to slander the true Dharma is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma;
to sever the bodhisattva practices is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma.
To seek after the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma;
to give rise to a mind of anger is to lose the path of the Buddha-dharma—one should remain far removed from these.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which a bodhisattva-mahāsattva falls away from the Buddha-dharma;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva remains far removed from these states, they will attain the correct orientation toward non-arising, the noble conduct, and the right path of all bodhisattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of transcendence from birth for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the bodhisattva’s transcendence of birth, which consists in giving rise to the *prajñāpāramitā*;

and the bodhisattva’s transcendence of birth, which consists in observing all sentient beings, remaining far removed from all false views, severing all bonds, and delivering all sentient beings across [samsara].
The bodhisattva’s liberation from birth consists in not dwelling on any signs, yet not abandoning sentient beings who are attached to signs;
it consists in not being attached to the three realms, yet also not being attached to any world-system;
and it consists in being forever free from afflictions, yet remaining close to sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva’s birth of detachment consists in attaining the dharma of freedom from desire amidst all phenomena;
the Bodhisattva’s birth of detachment consists in manifesting residence among a retinue while delighting in tranquility;
the Bodhisattva’s birth of detachment consists in being free from birth in the world, yet manifesting death here and birth there while practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva.
The bodhisattva’s transcendence of birth consists in performing all worldly affairs without being defiled by worldly dharmas;
the bodhisattva’s transcendence of birth consists in definitively realizing unsurpassed enlightenment while yet not abandoning the bodhisattva’s practices and vows.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of transcendence from birth by which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are forever separated from the world;
they are the sublime Dharma of the Great Sages, not shared with any sentient beings, nor with Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the ten kinds of definitive dharmas of all bodhisattvas.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
Born into the lineage of all Tathāgatas;
deeply entering the realm of all Tathāgatas;
profoundly understanding all bodhisattva practices.
They are correctly directed toward all the pāramitās;
they give birth to all the roots of goodness of all Buddhas;
and they abide securely within the supreme lineage of all Tathāgatas.
Abiding securely in the pure power of all Buddhas;
conforming to the enlightenment of all Tathāgatas;
and being of one body with all Buddhas.
They dwell together with all Buddhas without any distinction.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of definitive dharmas of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of dharmas that give birth to the path of the Buddha for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the dharma that gives birth to the path of the Buddha by following spiritual friends, because their roots of goodness are identical;
and the dharma that gives birth to the path of the Buddha through deep faith in all Buddha-dharmas, because of the joyful seeking of the Tathāgata’s inexhaustible sovereignty.
The dharma for giving birth to the path of the Buddha by attaining correct aspiration for all great vows, because of cultivating a vast mind;
the dharma for giving birth to the path of the Buddha through the certain knowledge of one's own roots of goodness, because all actions performed are without falsehood;
and the dharma for giving birth to the path of the Buddha by practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout all kalpas, because of being free from weariness until the end of the future.
The Dharma for generating the path to Buddhahood by taking birth in various places throughout incalculable worlds, in order to skillfully transform and guide all sentient beings;
the Dharma for generating the path to Buddhahood through the uninterrupted cultivation of the bodhisattva’s conduct, in order to nurture great compassion;
and the Dharma for generating the path to Buddhahood with an immeasurable mind, which fills the entirety of the realm of empty space in a single thought-moment.

The Dharma that gives birth to the path of Buddhahood by deeply entering all profound great vows and practices, because it ensures that originally cultivated roots of goodness are neither destroyed nor lost;

the Dharma that gives birth to the path of Buddhahood by skillfully upholding and guarding the lineage of all Tathāgatas, causing all sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta, constantly and joyfully aspiring for unsurpassed Bodhi, and nurturing all roots of goodness.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of dharmas for generating the path of the Buddha for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will obtain the ten titles of a good son.
What are the ten? They are as follows:
the name of a bodhisattva, because it is the body of the wisdom of enlightenment;
He bears the title "Mahāsattva" because he abides in the Great Vehicle;
he bears the title "Paramasattva" because he possesses the supreme, uninterrupted path of the Dharma;
he bears the title "Vijayasattva" because he has awakened to the supreme Bodhi.
He bears the name Peerless Being because his wisdom is peerless;
he bears the name Supreme Being because his diligence is supreme;
he bears the name Unsurpassed Being because he reveals and manifests the unsurpassed Dharma.
He bears the name *Balasattva* because he extensively knows the ten powers;
he bears the name *Asamasattva* because no sentient being is his equal;
he bears the name *Acintyasattva* because he awakens to bodhi in accordance with the inclinations of their minds.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten titles of a virtuous son attained by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of paths.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The first path is the bodhisattva path, because it does not abandon the bodhicitta.
The second path is the bodhisattva path, because it gives birth to wisdom and skillful means.
The third path is the bodhisattva path, because through the samādhis of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, one remains undefiled by the three realms.

The four practices constitute the bodhisattva path: repenting transgressions to eliminate offenses, rejoicing in merit, reverently entreating the infinite Buddhas, and skillfully knowing how to dedicate [merit].

Cultivating the five faculties is the path of a bodhisattva. Abiding in the faculty of faith, they become indestructible; they exert great diligence, bringing all matters to completion without regressing; they dwell securely in right mindfulness, eliminating distracted thoughts through samādhi; and through skillful discernment, they decisively understand the realm of wisdom by means of expedient means.
Mastery of the six supernormal powers is the path of the bodhisattva:
with the divine eye, they see all sentient beings possessing form throughout all worlds as they die here and are reborn there;
with the divine ear, they hear all the sutras and teachings spoken by all Buddhas, being able to receive and uphold them and extensively explaining them for the sake of all sentient beings.
He is born with the unimpeded knowledge of others' minds, fully knowing the mental thoughts of all sentient beings;
through the supernormal power of recollecting past lives, he fully knows all incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*) of the past;
and through the mastery of the supernormal power of the body that nurtures roots of goodness, he manifests great spiritual transformations according to what is appropriate for each being.
The supernormal power of the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows consists in knowing and seeing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), so that the path of the bodhisattva remains uninterrupted.
These seven recollections are the path of the bodhisattva:
recollection of the Buddha, wherein one perceives within a single pore all Buddhas teaching and transforming sentient beings;

Mindfulness of the Dharma: not departing from the assembly of a single Tathāgata, one is able to receive and uphold the Dharma heard directly in the presence of all Buddhas, and delivers sentient beings according to their various faculties and aspirations; mindfulness of the Saṅgha:
beholding the great assembly of non-retrogressive Bodhisattvas, one causes all sentient beings to constantly see this great assembly of Bodhisattvas;
mindfulness of practice: performing the giving of all Bodhisattvas, one nurtures the merit of Bodhisattva giving through right mindfulness.
He recollects the precepts, never departing from the bodhicitta and dedicating all roots of goodness to sentient beings;
he recollects the heavens, specifically the Bodhisattvas in their final birth in the Tuṣita Heaven;
and he recollects all sentient beings, employing skillful means and wisdom to teach and transform them, so that they may all be established in peace and accord with unsurpassed bodhi.
The eightfold path is the bodhisattva path, namely:
right view, which is to remain far removed from wrong views;
and right intention, which is to maintain right mindfulness of all-knowledge and remain far removed from falsehood.
Right speech conforms to the noble teachings and is free from the four faults of verbal conduct;
right action benefits and transforms all sentient beings without ever missing the proper time;
right livelihood abides securely in the four noble lineages, accomplishes the merits of dhūta practices, maintains pure deportment, and remains far removed from all evils.
Right Effort: Diligently practicing all the ascetic austerities of a bodhisattva, one cultivates the ten powers of a Buddha without any obstruction;
Right Mindfulness: Being able to fully remember and maintain all sounds, one eliminates all worldly discursive thoughts;
Right Concentration: Through skillful means, within a single samādhi, one gives rise to all the inconceivable dharma-gates and all samādhis of a bodhisattva.
The nine successive concentrations are the path of the bodhisattva, namely:
the cause for departing from desire and unwholesome states;
and the arising of applied and sustained thought such that all verbal karma is without obstruction.

They preach the Dharma to transform and edify all sentient beings, causing them to attain the joy of omniscience; they cause them to remain far removed from the joy of regressing toward faults and to rest in sublime joy;
they cause them to transcend worldly suffering and pleasure and to constantly behold all Buddhas;
and they cause them to attain the bliss of unsurpassed Bodhi.
The Immovable Samādhi gives rise to the four formless attainments;
yet it does not involve being born in the desire realm or the form realm.
It correctly enters the samādhi of the cessation of perception and feeling, yet it does not cease the bodhisattva practices.
The ten powers of the Tathāgata constitute the path of the bodhisattva, namely:
skillful means that correctly know what is possible and what is impossible;
and correctly knowing the retribution of the causes and effects of the karma of all sentient beings in the past, future, and present.
They skillfully know the various faculties of all sentient beings and preach the Dharma according to those faculties;

they skillfully know the immeasurable natures of sentient beings and skillfully know the various inclinations and desires of all sentient beings, preaching the Dharma in accordance with what is appropriate;

the pure bodies of these Bodhisattvas completely pervade all sentient beings, all lands, all worlds, and all eons, universally manifesting the complete majestic deportment of a Tathāgata while never abandoning the skillful means practiced by Bodhisattvas.
They know the arising of all dhyānas, samādhis, and liberations, both defiled and pure;
they know how to produce the immeasurable Dharma-gates of bodhisattvas according to the proper and improper times;
and they skillfully know the deaths and rebirths of all sentient beings as they pass from this life to that.
In a single thought-moment, they skillfully know all incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*) of the three periods of time;
they skillfully know how to eliminate all afflictions, fetters, and habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of all sentient beings, yet they do not abandon the practices of a bodhisattva.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten paths of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these paths, they will attain the path of the supreme skillful means of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have immeasurable paths, immeasurable path-equipments, immeasurable path-cultivations, and immeasurable path-adornments.”
Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of immeasurable paths. What are these ten?

That is to say: the immeasurability of the realm of space; the immeasurability of the dharma-realm; the inexhaustible and immeasurable realm of sentient beings; the boundless and immeasurable realm of worlds; the inexhaustible and ultimate immeasurability of incalculable eons; the immeasurability of the languages and dharmas of sentient beings; the immeasurability of the body of the Tathāgata; the immeasurability of the Buddha’s voice; the immeasurability of the powers of the Tathāgata; and the immeasurability of all-knowledge.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of immeasurable paths of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
For what reason?
As the realm of space is immeasurable, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for enlightenment;
as the dharma-realm is immeasurable and boundless, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for enlightenment;
as the realm of sentient beings is inexhaustible and immeasurable, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for enlightenment.
Just as the worlds are boundless and immeasurable, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for awakening;
just as the calculation of all kalpas can never be exhausted, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for awakening;
it cannot be exhausted even by the collective calculations of all sentient beings.
Just as the languages of all sentient beings are infinite, so too are the various linguistic dharmas of wisdom produced by the Bodhisattva through the accumulation of the requisites for practice;
just as the body of the Tathāgata is infinite, so too does the Bodhisattva, through the accumulation of the requisites for practice, fill all sentient beings, all lands, all worlds, and all eons;

just as the voice of the Buddha is infinite, such that a single utterance completely fills the entire Dharma-realm and there are no sentient beings who do not hear and know it, so too is the Bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for practice.
Just as the power of the Tathāgata is immeasurable, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for awakening that nurtures the power of the Tathāgata;
just as all-knowledge is immeasurable, so too is the bodhisattva’s accumulation of the requisites for awakening.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of requisites for a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the immeasurable and boundless wisdom of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of cultivation of the path for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the cultivation of non-attachment and non-emergence, because there is no forgetfulness of body, speech, or mind;
the cultivation of neither increase nor decrease, because of knowing the reality of all phenomena.
They cultivate neither existence nor non-existence, because they enter into the nature that is neither existent nor non-existent;

they cultivate that which is like an illusion, like a dream, like lightning, like an echo, like a reflection in a mirror, like a mirage, and like the moon in water, because they have no attachment to any phenomena;
they cultivate emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, because they perceive the three realms yet do not abandon the nurturing of all roots of goodness.
Cultivation that is ineffable, because it does not cling to the designations of phenomena;
cultivation that does not destroy the dharma-realm, because it definitively and thoroughly knows all phenomena;
and cultivation that is indestructible like the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), because it reaches all things with the equality of suchness and the limit of space.
The bodhisattva’s cultivation of wisdom does not abandon the power of courageous diligence;
it is the equal cultivation of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and all-knowledge, because it completely eliminates doubt regarding all phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas cultivate the path;
if Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme, all-knowing wisdom and the skillful means of cultivation of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of adornments of the path for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:

a bodhisattva-mahāsattva does not depart from the desire realm, yet is fully able to correctly enter the meditative concentrations, liberations, and absorptions of the form and formless realms; furthermore, they do not take birth there because of these attainments. This is the first path of adornment.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva enters the path of the śrāvakas, yet does not depart from the triple world by means of this path, this is the second adornment of the path.
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva enters the path of the pratyekabuddhas, yet does not abandon great compassion, this is the third adornment of the path.

Although a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva may be surrounded by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens—each of whom is exceptionally beautiful and distinguished, peerless in countenance, fully skilled in all arts, and adept in music—the Bodhisattva, upon hearing these exquisite sounds, never for a moment abandons his various dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis; this is the fourth adornment of the path.

When a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva provides various musical performances for all sentient beings to enjoy together, yet does not abandon the various dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis for even a single thought-moment, this is the fifth adornment of the path.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva does not cling to any phenomena of the world; having ultimately reached the further shore of the world, he delivers sentient beings—this is the sixth path of adornment.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells securely in right wisdom and cultivates the right path;

though he proceeds toward the wrong paths, it is with the intent to cause sentient beings to distance themselves from those wrong paths. He does not grasp at any mark of true reality or purity regarding these wrong paths. This is the seventh adornment of the path.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva remains far removed from the unwholesome karma of body, speech, and mind, constantly upholding pure precepts, and single-mindedly seeking the pure precepts of the Tathāgata. He manifests the observance of precepts and dignified conduct for all ordinary, foolish, and ignorant sentient beings in order to teach and bring to maturity those who have transgressed the precepts.

The Bodhisattva fully perfects all pure merits and correctly proceeds toward the Bodhisattva path, yet he manifests birth in the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, King Yama, and other difficult destinies in order to cause those sentient beings to leave behind the evil paths; however, in reality, the Bodhisattva does not take up those destinies. This is the eighth way of adornment.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, regarding all Buddha-dharmas, attains awakening independently of others; they obtain unimpeded eloquence and clear, pure wisdom that universally illumines the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
they dwell securely in the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas and share in the pure Dharma-body of all Buddhas; they fully accomplish all firm and clear, pure true Dharmas of great beings;
they dwell in all equal vehicles and turn toward the Dharma-gates of the realm of all Buddhas, being worthy of the praise, reverence, and offerings of all sentient beings.

Acting as the unsurpassed teacher for all sentient beings, he single-mindedly seeks the True Dharma without ever abandoning it; he manifests doubt regarding the Dharma and shows himself receiving respectful offerings from his preceptors (*upādhyāya*) and instructors (*ācārya*), yet in reality, he is the unsurpassed Dharma Master for all devas and humans.

Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas skillfully know the means (upāya) and abide in the Bodhisattva path, manifesting through skillful means according to what is appropriate; this is the ninth adornment of the path.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is fully endowed with profound wisdom and has perfected all the unsurpassed practices of a bodhisattva; all Tathāgatas have conferred upon him the empowerment of the nectar-like Dharma upon his crown, and he has reached the ultimate shore of mastery over all phenomena.

With a crown of pure, stainless, and unobstructed Dharma-scarves upon their heads, they universally manifest the Tathāgata’s unimpeded Dharma-body throughout all worlds, turning the indestructible, pure wheel of Dharma;
their pure Dharma-bodies reach every place in all worlds,
having reached the ultimate shore of mastery over all dharmas, and being fully accomplished in all the sovereign qualities of Bodhisattvas.
Through skillful means, they manifest birth in all lands; they share a single realm with the Buddhas of the three periods of time while never ceasing their bodhisattva practices.

They do not abandon the bodhisattva-dharma, do not turn back from bodhisattva-karma, and do not forsake the bodhisattva-path. They have never discarded the bodhisattva’s deportment, nor have they abandoned their fervent zeal, nor their skillful means, nor remained apart from bodhisattva activities.
Cultivating the bodhisattva-practices, their minds are free from weariness, and they do not depart from the bodhisattva’s practice of upholding the Dharma.

Why is this? Because a bodhisattva mahāsattva desires to swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they do not abandon the bodhisattva practices and observe sentient beings; this is the tenth path of adornment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of adornments of the path for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in this path, they will attain the adornment of the supreme jewel of the path of all Buddhas, yet without forsaking the Bodhisattva path.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-one.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Sixth Part of the Thirty-third Chapter on Transcending the World:
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of feet."
What are these ten? They are:
the foot of pure precepts, because it accumulates and fulfills all great vows;
The feet of diligence, for they accumulate all branches of enlightenment until reaching the stage of non-retrogression;
the feet of supernormal powers, for they bring joy to sentient beings according to their wishes;
the feet of physical supernormal power, for they are able to reach all Buddha-fields without leaving a single seat.
The limb of profound resolve, because it brings all supreme and wondrous dharmas to ultimate fulfillment;
the limb of firm vows, because all sought-after matters are completely perfected;
the limb of embracing the right dharma, because one does not contravene any reverent instruction.
They are never weary of hearing the Dharma, for they hear and uphold all that the Buddhas have taught without fatigue;
they are fully provided with the requisites for living according to the Dharma, for they enter among all assemblies with faculties that are undifferentiated;
and they are established in the correct practice of the Bodhisattva path, for they are free from all evil.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of feet of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;

if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells securely in these feet, they will attain the supreme, unsurpassed feet of all Buddhas, by which they can, with a single lift of their foot, reach every world-system throughout the universe.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of hands. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the hand of faith, because it single-mindedly believes in and ultimately upholds all the true Dharma spoken by all Buddhas;
the hand that does not cling to material gifts, because it causes those who come to beg to be joyful.
The hand of first intending to come and inquire with greetings, because it manifests the mark of the right palm;
the hand of reverently making offerings to all Buddhas, because it nurtures immeasurable merit without weariness;
the hand of skillfully understanding extensive learning, because it removes all doubts and delusions of all sentient beings.
The hand that is far removed from the three realms and possesses the tranquility of detachment, for it uproots sentient beings from the mire of desire;
the hand that establishes others on the further shore, for it rescues sentient beings drowning in the four currents;
the hand that is free from stinginess regarding the Dharma, for it is fully capable of expounding all teachings.
The hand of wisdom that transcends all worldly discourses of the world, because it eradicates all diseases of body and mind;
the precious hand of wisdom, because it eliminates the darkness of all afflictions and delusions and manifests the light of all ineffable teachings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of hands of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these hands, they will attain the supreme hand of all Buddhas, capable of covering all worlds throughout the ten directions with a single palm.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of bellies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a belly free from flattery and crookedness, because the mind is upright and pure;
a belly free from illusion and hypocrisy, because the actions of body, speech, and mind are all genuine.
The belly that does not harbor affairs, because it is free from the concealment of evil;
the inexhaustible belly, because it has no attachment to any phenomena;
the belly that extinguishes afflictions, because its wisdom is luminous and pure.
The belly of a pure mind, because it is free from all evil;
the belly that contemplates all perceptions of food, because it maintains right mindfulness of the true Dharma;
the belly that contemplates all formations, because it skillfully awakens to dependent origination.
It is the womb that perfectly awakens to all paths, because it is fully endowed with and accomplished in right aspiration;
it is the womb that is free from all afflictions and false views, because it causes all sentient beings to attain the womb of the Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of bellies of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells securely in these bellies, they will attain the unsurpassed belly of all Buddhas, which is fully capable of containing and receiving all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of treasuries for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the Bodhisattva-piṭaka is that which does not sever the lineage of the Tathāgata, for it extensively expounds the Buddha-dharma to nurture immeasurable wholesome dharmas;
the Bodhisattva-piṭaka is that which receives, upholds, and protects the True Dharma of the Tathāgata, for it reveals the light of great wisdom to sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva-piṭaka nourishes the Jewel of the Saṃgha, for it gathers in those who do not regress from the wheel of the True Dharma;
it awakens sentient beings established in right concentration, for it delivers sentient beings without missing the proper time;
it teaches and matures sentient beings of indeterminate nature, for it ensures that the continuity of the causes of their roots of goodness is never severed.

The Bodhisattva-piṭaka is that which gives rise to the mind of great compassion to rescue and protect those beings fixed in wrong determination, because it establishes the causes and conditions for their future roots of goodness;

the Bodhisattva-piṭaka is that which fulfills the ten powers of the Tathāgata so they cannot be destroyed, because it subdues all Māras and brings to full completion the non-retrogressive roots of goodness;
the Bodhisattva-piṭaka is that which dwells in the four fearlessnesses and utters the great lion’s roar, because it causes all sentient beings to rejoice.
Attaining the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, for there is no wisdom that it does not encompass;
awakening equally to all sentient beings, all lands, all dharmas, and all Buddhas is the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, for it penetrates deeply into equality within a single thought-moment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten treasuries of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these treasuries, they will attain the treasury of supreme roots of goodness and great wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of mind. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a courageous mind, because all undertakings initiated are brought to completion;
a tireless mind, because one accumulates the various roots of goodness that constitute the primary and secondary marks of a Buddha.
A mind of courageous strength, because it subdues all evil Māras;
a mind of right reflection, because it eliminates all defilements of affliction;
a mind of non-retrogression, because it proceeds to the site of enlightenment to realize ultimate Bodhi.
The mind of intrinsic purity, because it awakens to the fact that the mind reaches nowhere and clings to nothing;
the knowledge of the minds of sentient beings, because it causes them to awaken and attain liberation in accordance with their natures;

the entry into the abiding of the Great Brahma Heaven and the dwelling in the mind of the Buddha-dharma, because it universally protects and saves all varieties of sentient beings according to their natures.
The mind of emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and non-action, because it is far removed from signs and views and does not cling to the triple world;
the adamantine-adorned mind, because even Māras equal in number to all sentient beings cannot move a single hair of it.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of mind of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these minds, they will attain the supreme Vajra-treasury mind of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of adornments of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the adornment of great loving-kindness, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings;
the adornment of great compassion, for the sake of enduring all suffering;
Adorned with great vows, for all the vows they have made are brought to ultimate fulfillment;
adorned with dedication, for they establish the wondrous adornments of the merits of all Buddhas;
adorned with merit, for they bring benefit to all sentient beings.
The adornment of the pāramitās, for the sake of delivering all sentient beings;
the adornment of wisdom, for the sake of eliminating the darkness of afflictions and ignorance in all sentient beings;
the adornment of skillful means, for the sake of producing all roots of goodness from the universal gate;
It is adorned with the firm and undisturbed resolve for omniscience, because one does not delight in other vehicles;
it is adorned with certainty, because one eliminates doubt within the True Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of adornments of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme adornment of all Buddhas and subdue all Māras.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of weapons. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the support of the mind of generous giving, which distances one from stinginess by eliminating all stains of avarice;
the support of upholding the precepts, which uproots all forms of immoral conduct.
The staff of impartial observation of all phenomena, because it is far removed from all false and illusory dharmas;
the staff of wisdom, because it eliminates the various afflictions of sentient beings;
the staff of right livelihood, because it remains far removed from all forms of wrong livelihood.
The support of skillful means, because it manifests all things;
the support of greed, anger, and delusion—the entirety of all afflictions—in brief, because one transforms sentient beings through the gateway of afflictions;
and the support of birth and death, because one does not sever the bodhisattva practice while teaching and transforming sentient beings.
It is the support for teaching the true Dharma, because it is entirely free from attachment;
it is the support for the gateway to omniscience, because it does not depart from the gateway of bodhisattva practice.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of weapons of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;

if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva abides securely in these dharmas, they will be able to eliminate all the afflictions, fetters, and habitual tendencies accumulated by sentient beings throughout the long night.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of heads. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the head of nirvāṇa, because its crown cannot be seen;
the head of reverence and respect, because it is honored and made offerings to by all the world, including devas and humans.
Gambhīramatiśiras, because you are the foremost among all the trichiliocosms;
Sarvakuśalamūlaśiras, because you are worthy of the offerings of all sentient beings within the three realms;
Sarvasattvadhūrakaśiras, because you have attained the unsurpassed Vajra-peak.
The head of immeasurability and boundlessness, because it encompasses all supreme dharmas;
the head of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*), because it delights in the Dharma of the Dharma-King;
the head of skillful means (*upāya*), because it manifests the equality of all sentient beings.
He is foremost in teaching and maturing all sentient beings, for he is the unsurpassed teacher of all sentient beings;
he is foremost in protecting the True Dharma of the Tathāgata, for he ensures that the Three Jewels are never interrupted.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of heads of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these dharmas, they will attain the unsurpassed crown of wisdom of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of eyes. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the fleshly eye, because it sees all forms;
the divine eye, because it sees all sentient beings dying here and being reborn there.
The wisdom-eye, because it perceives the faculties of all sentient beings;
the dharma-eye, because it perceives the true nature of all phenomena;
the buddha-eye, because it perceives the ten powers of the Tathāgata.
The eye of wisdom, because it discriminates all phenomena;
the eye of clarity, because it beholds the light of all Buddhas;
the eye that transcends birth and death, because it perceives nirvana.
The Unobstructed Eye, because it sees all phenomena without hindrance;
the Universal Eye, because it perceives the Dharma-realm through the gateway of equality.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of eyes of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these eyes, they will attain the unsurpassed great wisdom-eye of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of ears of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
upon hearing sounds of praise, one cuts off craving;
upon hearing sounds of disparagement, one cuts off anger.
Upon hearing the sounds of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, they do not give rise to a seeking mind;
upon hearing the sound of the bodhisattva path, they give rise to a heart of joy and wonder;

and upon hearing the voices of suffering and poverty in all difficult states—such as those of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, King Yama, and asuras—they give rise to the adornment of great compassion to adorn themselves.
Hearing the sublime and wondrous sounds of the realms of devas and humans, they contemplate that all phenomena are entirely impermanent;
hearing the sounds of the Buddha’s merits, they diligently cultivate vigor to ultimately fulfill all merits;

hearing the sounds of the *pāramitās*, the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*), the bodhisattvas, and the scriptural collections (*piṭaka*), they give rise to the ultimate resolve to reach the other shore.
They hear all sounds throughout the worlds of the ten directions and understand them all to be like echoes.

From their first aspiration until they reach the site of enlightenment, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas constantly maintain the right concentration of the Dharma-ear, yet they do not abandon the teaching, transforming, and maturing of all sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of ears of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes these ears, he shall attain the unsurpassed, great wisdom-ear of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of noses. What are these ten?
That is to say:
when smelling a foul odor, one contemplates it as being non-foul;
when smelling a fragrant scent, one contemplates it as being non-fragrant.
When smelling fragrances and odors, one observes them with equanimity;
when smelling that which is neither fragrant nor foul, one observes with detachment;

and when smelling the fragrance of clothing, bedding, mattresses, and the limbs of the body, one knows that person’s afflictions are of the "equal-part" type, consisting of greed, hatred, and delusion.
Upon smelling the fragrance of the various medicinal herbs from the great treasure storehouse, they are able to fully comprehend all treasure stores;

upon smelling the fragrance of sentient beings from as low as the Avīci Hell to as high as the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception, they are able to fully comprehend all their fundamental practices;
upon smelling the fragrance of sound, the fragrance of giving and precepts, and the fragrance of wisdom, they abide in the mind of omniscience without ever becoming distracted.
They smell the fragrance of all bodhisattva practices, thereby encompassing the ground of the Tathāgata’s wisdom;
they smell the fragrance of the realm of all Buddhas’ wisdom, never ceasing the conduct performed by bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of noses of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these noses, they will attain the infinite, boundless, and unsurpassed pure noses of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of tongues. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the tongue that analytically explains the inexhaustible conduct of all sentient beings;
the tongue that analytically explains inexhaustible dharmas;
The tongue that praises the inexhaustible merits of all Buddhas;
the tongue of inexhaustible eloquence;
the tongue that expounds the inexhaustible Mahāyāna Dharma.
Tongues that universally cover the realms of empty space in the ten directions;
tongues that universally illumine all Buddha-worlds;
tongues that impartially praise all sentient beings;
The tongue that accords with all Buddhas and causes them joy;
the tongue that subdues all Māras and non-Buddhists, eliminates all afflictions of birth and death, and causes all sentient beings to reach nirvana.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of tongues of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these tongues, they will attain the supreme great vajra-tongue of all Buddhas, which universally covers all worlds.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of bodies. What are these ten?
That is to say:
a human body, for the purpose of teaching and bringing all people to maturity;
a non-human body, for the purpose of teaching and bringing those in the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, and the realm of King Yama to maturity.
The celestial body, for the purpose of teaching and bringing to maturity the sentient beings of the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm;
the body of one in training (*śaikṣa*), for the purpose of manifesting the stage of training;
and the body of one beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), for the purpose of manifesting the stage of an arhat.
The body of a pratyekabuddha, for the purpose of teaching and transforming others so that they may enter the stage of a pratyekabuddha;
the body of a bodhisattva, for the purpose of accumulating the Mahāyāna;
the body of a Tathāgata, for the purpose of bestowing the prediction of Tathāgata-knowledge.
The *maṇu-ma* body, because it skillfully gives rise to immeasurable merit through expedient means;
the untainted *dharma*-body, because it universally manifests the bodies of all sentient beings through minimal expedient means.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of bodies of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a Bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these bodies, they shall attain the supreme Dharma-body of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of intention. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the foremost intention, because it gives birth to all roots of goodness;
the intention that accords with the Buddha’s teaching, because one practices according to what has been taught.
The mind that penetrates deeply, because it understands all Buddha-dharmas;
the inward mind, because it penetrates deeply into the aspirations of sentient beings;
the undisturbed mind, because it is not disturbed by afflictions.
The mind is pure, for it is not defiled by stains;
the mind is well-tamed, for it does not miss the proper time;
the mind is characterized by right reflection on karma, for it remains far removed from all evil.
The mind that subdues the sense faculties, because the senses do not run wild amidst their objects;
the mind of profound concentration, because the Buddha’s samādhis are immeasurable.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of intentions of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva accomplishes these intentions, they will attain the unsurpassed intention of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of practices for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the practice of hearing the Dharma, because one delights in listening to and receiving the Dharma;
and the practice of expounding the Dharma, because it benefits sentient beings.
They do not act out of attachment, aversion, delusion, or fear, because they have tamed their own minds;
they practice within the realm of desire, because they teach and bring to maturity the sentient beings of the desire realm;
and they practice the samādhis of the form and formless realms, because they cause [those beings] to swiftly turn toward awakening.
The practice of the Dharma according to its meaning, because it swiftly accomplishes pure wisdom;
the practice of all realms of existence, because it transforms and educates sentient beings;
and the practice of all Buddha-fields, because it reverently pays homage to and makes offerings to all Buddhas.
The practice of nirvana, because it severs the continuity of birth and death;
the practice of fulfilling the deeds of all Buddhas, because it does not interrupt the bodhisattva practices.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of practices of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva accomplishes these practices, they will attain all the practices of the Buddhas, non-practices, and the practices of the Tathāgatas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of abodes for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
dwelling in the bodhicitta, because it is never forgotten;
dwelling in the pāramitās, because one never tires of their merits;
He dwells delighting in hearing the true Dharma because his wisdom is luminous and pure;
he dwells in forest hermitages because he has accomplished the great samādhis;
and he dwells in accordance with the ascetic practices (*dhūta*), the dignified conduct, and the four noble lineages because he has few desires and is content.
The dwelling of conformity, because it accords with the True Dharma;
the dwelling of intimacy with the Tathāgata, because it brings the majestic deportment of a Buddha to fulfillment;
the dwelling of all illuminations, because it satisfies great wisdom;
They abide in the patience of non-arising because they have fulfilled the reception of the prediction;
they abide in the enlightenment of the site of awakening because they have fulfilled all Buddha-dharmas, including the powers and the fearlessnesses.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten abodes of a bodhisattva mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells securely in these abodes, they will attain the supreme abode of all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of sitting for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the seat of the wheel-turning king, because he promotes the ten wholesome paths of action;
the seat of the four heavenly kings, because he desires to attain mastery over the true Dharma of all Buddhas in all worlds.
The seat of Śakra, because he is the foremost among all sentient beings;
the seat of Brahmā, because he has attained mastery over his own mind and the minds of others;
the lion’s seat, because he analytically expounds the most profound meanings.
The seat of the True Dharma, because it seeks to clarify the various powers and eloquence of dhāraṇī;
the seat of steadfast samādhi, because it brings the great vows to ultimate fulfillment;
the seat of great compassion, because it causes all sentient beings with malicious minds to rejoice.
The Great Compassion Seat, because it is able to endure all sufferings and afflictions;
the Vajra Seat, because it subdues all Māras and non-Buddhists.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of seats of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these seats, they will attain the unsurpassed seat of honor of all Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of reclining for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
reclining in tranquility, because the body and mind are serene;
reclining in meditative concentration, because one contemplates all phenomena with right mindfulness and reflection.
They sleep in various samādhis because their bodies and minds are supple;
they sleep as Brahmās because they do not afflict themselves or others;
they sleep contemplating their karma because their minds will have no regrets hereafter.
One lies down in accordance with the True Dharma because one cannot be shaken;
one lies down on the Right Path because of awakening through spiritual friends;
one lies down with sublime vows because of skillfully knowing dedication (*pariṇāmanā*).
He lies down when all affairs are concluded, because what was to be done has been brought to completion;
he abandons expedient means when lying down, because the fundamental task has been finalized.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of reclining of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide securely in these dharmas, they will attain the supreme path of reclining of all Buddhas and will be able to awaken all sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of abodes for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
dwelling in great loving-kindness, because one observes all sentient beings with an impartial mind;
dwelling in great compassion, because one does not treat those who have not yet studied with contempt.
Abiding in great joy, because it extinguishes sorrow and affliction;
abiding in great equanimity, because conditioned and unconditioned phenomena are entirely equal;
abiding in all the pāramitās, because the bodhicitta is their foremost principle.
They dwell in the emptiness of all aspects because they skillfully understand all phenomena;
they dwell in signlessness because they have attained the realization of non-arising and are irreversible;
they dwell in wishlessness because they have relinquished rebirth.
They abide in mindfulness and wisdom because they have perfected the dharma of patience;
they abide in the equality of all dharmas because they have attained the dharma of receiving the prediction of enlightenment.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten abodes of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas;
if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva dwells securely in these abodes, they will attain the supreme, unimpeded abode of all buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of practices for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the practice of right mindfulness, because it fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness;
the practice of all realms of existence, because it correctly awakens to the destination of phenomena.
The practice of wisdom, because it accords with all Buddhas;
the practice of the perfections, because it fulfills all-knowledge;
