When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva first enters the womb, he remains far removed from delusion, contemplating with right mindfulness, eliminating distracted thoughts, and accomplishing mindfulness and wisdom; his mind never becomes disordered—this is the third matter demonstrating his dwelling in the womb.

When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in the mother’s womb, he constantly preaches the Dharma; bodhisattvas from the worlds of the ten directions, as well as Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings, come to visit the Bodhisattva, and the Bodhisattva immediately expounds the Dharma extensively for them.

He manifests the sovereign spiritual powers of a Bodhisattva; because the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has fully accomplished immeasurable and boundless wisdom, he manifests such extraordinary and marvelous deeds. This is the fourth matter, the manifestation of dwelling in the womb.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is within the mother’s womb, it is for the sake of transforming sentient beings and to cause their original vows to be fulfilled; this is the fifth matter of manifesting the dwelling in the womb.

Because a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains enlightenment among human beings and should manifest birth according to the laws of humanity, this is the sixth matter: the manifestation of dwelling in the womb.

While the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is within the mother’s womb, the sentient beings of the trichiliocosm all see the Bodhisattva residing in the womb, as clearly as seeing one's own reflection in a bright mirror.

At that time, the great-minded devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others all go to the Bodhisattva to pay homage and make offerings; this is the seventh matter: the manifestation of dwelling in the womb.

When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in his mother’s womb, those in other world-systems who are in their final birth before Buddhahood (ekajātipratibaddha) and dwelling in their mothers’ wombs all together discourse upon the inexhaustible treasury of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom; this is the eighth matter of manifesting the dwelling in the womb.

When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva first enters the womb, he correctly attains the *vimala-samādhi* (stainless samādhi); all the Tuṣita palaces and all the implements of offering and adornment enter the mother’s womb through the power of this samādhi.
He causes his mother’s body to be free from all suffering and affliction; this is the ninth matter, the manifestation of dwelling in the womb.
O Son of the Buddha!

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in the mother’s womb, because he has fully accomplished an immeasurable and boundless treasury of merit, all the offerings from every world in the ten directions are used to make offerings to all Tathāgatas. Those Tathāgatas, for the sake of this Bodhisattva, expound immeasurable and boundless Dharma-gates of the Dharma-realm; this is the tenth manifestation of dwelling in the womb.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this dharma-gate, they are able to manifest the ten kinds of subtle inclinations of a bodhisattva.
What are these ten? They are as follows:

When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in the mother’s womb, he manifests the initial arousal of the mind of enlightenment, up to the stage of the consecration with nectar and the bestowal of the prophecy;
while remaining in the mother’s womb, he further manifests dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven;
and while in the mother’s womb, he manifests birth.
Within the mother’s womb, he manifests the stage of childhood;
within the mother’s womb, he appears amidst the sensory pleasures of the palace;
within the mother’s womb, he manifests the renunciation of the household life.
Manifesting the practice of asceticism within the mother’s womb; proceeding to the site of enlightenment and attaining perfect awakening;
manifesting the turning of the wheel of Dharma within the mother’s womb;
and manifesting the Great Parinirvāṇa within the mother’s womb.
Within the mother’s womb, he manifested all subtle phenomena, all bodhisattva practices, and the immeasurable gateways of practice through the sovereign spiritual powers of all Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten subtle gateways of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva;
if a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in these gateways, they will attain the supreme wisdom of all Buddhas, the great subtle gateway.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-two;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-three.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-three, Part Eight: The Chapter on Transcending the World.
“O Sons of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of birth for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
What are these ten? They are:
birth free from delusion;
They emit great nets of light, universally illuminating the three thousandfold world-system;
they eliminate all future births in their final bodies;
they are the birthless birth.
They give rise to the knowledge that all kalpas of the three realms are like illusions;
they give rise to the manifestation of bodies throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
and they give rise to the body of omniscience, fully perfected.
The birth of the body that universally illumines through the radiance of all Tathāgatas and awakens all sentient beings;
the birth of the body of great wisdom, mastery, and various dhyānas and samādhis—
O Son of the Buddha!

When the Bodhisattva was born, all Buddha-fields shook in six ways; all sentient beings attained liberation; all evil realms were entirely extinguished; the radiance of all Māras was eclipsed, appearing like a mass of ink; and immeasurable Bodhisattvas gathered there from all directions like clouds.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of births of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; desiring to transform and deliver the various classes of sentient beings, they manifest these births.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas adorn themselves with ten kinds of great adornments.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva forms this thought:
"All the world is submerged in the mud of the five desires; with the exception of myself alone, there is no one capable of rescuing them. Knowing this, he dons the great armor to adorn himself.

The afflictions and ignorance shroud the eyes of sentient beings, leaving them all blind and sightless; I, now possessing sovereign wisdom, shall universally guide and open the eye of wisdom for all beings, causing it to be entirely purified, and adorning myself by donning the great adornment.
By means of this provisional body of name, I have now attained the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, pure Dharma-body, which fills the three periods of time and adorns itself with great adornments.

With unimpeded, pure eyes, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva thoroughly observes all the abodes of the Brahmā heavens throughout the ten directions, up to the abode of Maheśvara; these sentient beings all say of themselves:
"I have accomplished the power of sovereign wisdom."
The Bodhisattva is fully able to crush and eliminate that mind of self-conceit, adorning himself by donning the great armor.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees sentient beings who, having planted various roots of goodness in past lives, now wish to fall back and sink away, he causes those sentient beings to dwell in the stage of non-retrogression, adorning himself by donning the great armor.
They desire to cause sentient beings to plant even a small root of goodness and obtain immeasurable fruit, adorning themselves by giving rise to great adornment.
Seeing the Buddha’s immeasurable and sovereign spiritual powers, they give rise to great adornment and adorn themselves.

Observing that bodhisattvas who practiced together in the past became attached to other matters and failed to achieve perfect enlightenment, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dons the great armor to adorn himself.
Seeing that gods and humans are exhausted, weary, and have retreated from their right aspirations, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva dons the great armor to adorn himself.
Because the bodhisattva-mahāsattva is touched by the light of all Tathāgatas, he nurtures all great and correct aspirations, and having generated the great adornment, he adorns himself with it.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of great adornments of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas; for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings, they give rise to these adornments to adorn themselves.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten reasons why Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas walk seven steps. What are these ten?
That is to say:
he walked seven steps to manifest the power of a bodhisattva;
he walked seven steps to manifest the seven treasures.
He took seven steps because he fulfills the vows of the earth deities;
he took seven steps because he manifests the sign of transcending the triple world;
he took seven steps because he manifests the most supreme gait of the great elephant king, the bull king, and the lion king.
He took seven steps because he manifested the characteristics of the vajra-ground;
he took seven steps because he wished to bestow strength upon sentient beings;
he took seven steps because he manifested the signs of the seven jewels of awakening.
He took seven steps because he had fully accomplished all the Buddha-dharmas and did not attain awakening through another;
he took seven steps because he wished to declare: "I am the most supreme and peerless in the world."
O Son of the Buddha!
It is for these ten reasons that the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva takes seven steps;
he manifests this display for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten matters by which Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas manifest the stage of a youth. What are these ten?
That is to say:
because he manifests these activities through writing, mathematics, calculation, seal-carving, and skillful means, he manifests the stage of a youth;
because he manifests riding elephants, horses, and chariots, as well as archery and various martial arts, he manifests the stage of a youth.
Because he wishes to learn all the skillful discourses and various amusements of the world, he manifests the stage of a youth;
because he has abandoned all evil karma of body, speech, and mind, he manifests the stage of a youth;
and because he manifests the direct path toward parinirvāṇa and the full attainment of samādhi that pervades all worlds, he manifests the stage of a youth.

Because he manifests the power of a bodhisattva that surpasses that of devas, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā, and the four heavenly kings, he manifests the stage of a youth; because he manifests a sublime and exquisite form that exceeds all those of Śakra, Brahmā, and the four heavenly kings, he manifests the stage of a youth;
because he desires to cause sentient beings to distance themselves from the five desires and to always delight in the True Dharma, he manifests the stage of a youth;
and because he manifests reverence for the True Dharma and makes offerings to all Tathāgatas in all worlds, he manifests the stage of a youth.
Always delighting in the True Dharma, because they universally manifest the upholding of all the True Dharma, they manifest the Stage of the Youth.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is for these ten reasons that Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas manifest the Stage of the Youth.
“O Son of the Buddha!
After the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has manifested the stage of a youth, he manifests his dwelling within the inner palace for ten reasons. What are these ten?
That is to say:
he manifests dwelling in the inner palace in order to cause those who practice the same path to increase their roots of goodness;
he manifests dwelling in the inner palace in order to clarify all the roots of goodness of the Bodhisattvas.
He dwells in the inner palace because he manifests there for the sake of those devas who are attached to pleasure;
he dwells in the inner palace because he manifests there in accordance with the needs of beings in this world of five turbidities;
and he dwells in the inner palace because he enters into samādhi within the deep chambers, desiring to clarify the power of the Bodhisattva’s meritorious virtues.
In order to fulfill the original vows of sentient beings who practiced together with him in past lives, he manifests dwelling in the inner palace;
in order to fulfill the original vows of his parents and kinsmen, he manifests dwelling in the inner palace;
and in order to offer music and song as the sublime sound of the Dharma to all Buddhas, he manifests dwelling in the inner palace.

Because the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva enters profound samādhi within his palace, attains equal and perfect enlightenment, and even manifests great parinirvāṇa, he manifests as dwelling in the inner palace;
because he accords with and protects the Dharma, he manifests as dwelling in the inner palace.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is for these ten reasons that the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests dwelling within the inner palace; and for these reasons, the Bodhisattva in his final birth manifests the act of leaving the home life.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten matters by which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas manifest the act of leaving the household life. What are these ten?
That is to say:
in order to cause sentient beings to feel weary of and renounce the household life, he manifests leaving home;
for the sake of sentient beings who are attached to the household life, he manifests leaving home.
Because he wishes to manifest conformity with the path of all noble ones, he manifests leaving the household life;
because he wishes to proclaim and praise the dharma of leaving the household life, he manifests leaving the household life;
because he wishes to cause sentient beings to abandon the two views, he manifests leaving the household life.
He manifests renunciation because he wishes to cause sentient beings to leave behind sensual pleasure and the pleasure of self;
he manifests renunciation because he wishes to manifest the appearance of transcending the three realms;
he manifests renunciation because he wishes to demonstrate that his awakening is attained through his own mastery and not by depending on another.
In order to conform to the Tathāgata’s ten powers and four fearlessnesses, he manifests the act of leaving the household life;
because it is the natural law for all Bodhisattvas in their final birth, he manifests the act of leaving the household life.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten reasons for which Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas manifest the act of leaving the household life in order to transform sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!"
For ten reasons, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas manifest ascetic practices.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
The Bodhisattva-mahāsattva manifests ascetic practices in order to teach and bring to maturity sentient beings of narrow minds;
he manifests ascetic practices to uproot sentient beings who cling to false views;
and he manifests ascetic practices for those sentient beings who hold the false view that there is no karmic retribution, desiring to cause them to understand the law of karma and its results.
He manifests ascetic practices in order to accord with the sentient beings of the world of five turbidities;
he manifests ascetic practices for the sake of indolent sentient beings;
and he manifests ascetic practices because he desires to cause sentient beings to joyfully seek the Dharma.
He manifests ascetic practices for the sake of sentient beings who are attached to sensual pleasures and self-indulgence;
he manifests ascetic practices to demonstrate the extraordinary conduct of a bodhisattva;
and he manifests ascetic practices with the desire to inspire diligence in future sentient beings.
Because the faculties of gods and worldlings have not yet matured, and they must wait for those faculties to ripen, the Bodhisattva manifests ascetic practices.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten reasons for which a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva manifests ascetic practices.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten reasons why Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas proceed to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). What are these ten?
That is to say:
they proceed to the site of enlightenment in order to universally illumine all worlds;
they proceed to the site of enlightenment in order to cause all worlds to tremble.
They proceed to the site of enlightenment because they wish to manifest their bodies universally in all worlds;
they proceed to the site of enlightenment for the sake of awakening all bodhisattvas, all sentient beings, and all those who practice in concert with them;
and they proceed to the site of enlightenment to manifest the adornments of the site of enlightenment.
They proceed to the site of enlightenment in order to manifest the adornments of the Bodhi tree according to the needs of those to be converted;
they proceed to the site of enlightenment desiring to behold all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions;

and they proceed to the site of enlightenment desiring to enter, at every thought-moment as they lift and lower their feet, immeasurable doors of samādhi and meditative absorptions, thereby attaining perfect and complete awakening.

They proceed to the site of enlightenment in order to receive the respectful offerings of all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and even Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings, so that each may remain unaware of the others;

and they proceed to the site of enlightenment desiring to universally observe all worlds with the unimpeded eye of wisdom, to maintain right mindfulness of all Buddhas, and to manifest the attainment of Buddhahood in all lands.
"O Son of the Buddha!
For these ten reasons, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva proceeds to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas sit at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) for ten reasons.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
He sits at the site of enlightenment because he causes all lands to tremble in various ways;
he sits at the site of enlightenment because he universally illumines all worlds;
he sits at the site of enlightenment because he eliminates all evil realms.
They sit at the site of enlightenment because they transform all lands into vajra;
they sit at the site of enlightenment because they observe the lion’s roar of all Buddhas;
they sit at the site of enlightenment because they are free from all falsehood, their minds being as pure as space.
He sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) because he manifests conduct in accordance with the purity of his body;
he sits at the site of enlightenment because he accords with the perfection of the vajra-samādhi;
he sits at the site of enlightenment because he receives the pure seat of all Buddhas.
Because they are able to fully receive and uphold all sentient beings through the power of their own roots of goodness,
the sons of the Buddha,
these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas sit at the site of enlightenment for ten reasons. For these ten reasons, they sit at the site of enlightenment.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), there are ten kinds of extraordinary and unprecedented phenomena. What are these ten?
That is to say:

when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), all Buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions behold this Bodhisattva and, raising their right hands, praise him, saying:
"Excellent! (Sādhu!)"
"Excellent! O Unsurpassed Teacher!
This is a marvelous and unprecedented phenomenon.

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas provide protection and support; this is the second extraordinary and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment, all Bodhisattvas who were his companions in past lives gather like clouds and respectfully make offerings with various kinds of ornaments; this is the third extraordinary and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment, all grasses, trees, forests, and non-sentient entities throughout all worlds in the ten directions bend their bodies in homage toward the site of enlightenment; this is the fourth extraordinary and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), he enters the samādhi named "Thoroughly Knowing the Dharma-Dhātu" (*dharmadhātu-suvijñāna*); because he attains this samādhi, he brings all the practices of a Bodhisattva to ultimate completion—this is the fifth marvelous and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment, he attains a dhāraṇī named "Stainless, Supreme, and Wondrous Ocean-Treasury" (*vimala-viśeṣa-samudragarbha*); because the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in this dhāraṇī, all Buddhas bestow the nectar of the Dharma (*amṛta-dharma*) which rains down upon this Bodhisattva—this is the sixth marvelous and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment, he reverently makes offerings to all Buddhas through his supernormal powers (*abhijñā*)—this is the seventh marvelous and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), they enter the dharma-gate of unsurpassed wisdom and, through skillful means (upāya-kauśalya), fully know the faculties of all sentient beings;

this is the eighth rare and unprecedented quality. When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment, they enter the samādhi called "Excellent Awakening" (Sujñāna); having entered this concentration, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains a pure Dharma-body that fills the realm of empty space and all three periods of time; this is the ninth rare and unprecedented quality.

When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment, their physical actions (kāyakarman) are purified, and they grasp the unimpeded wisdom of the three periods of time, universally illuminating everything; this is the tenth rare and unprecedented quality.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of extraordinary and unprecedented dharmas attained by a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva when sitting at the site of enlightenment.
O Son of the Buddha!"
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sits at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), there are ten reasons for manifesting the subduing of Māra.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
In this world of the five turbidities, sentient beings delight in mutual warfare; therefore, in order to manifest the power of the Bodhisattva’s merit, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
To completely extinguish the doubts of devas and humans, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
Because he wishes to transform and deliver the retinue of Māra, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
For those among the devas and people of the world who delight in military conquest, he manifests the subduing of Māra in order to assemble them for transformation;
once the devas and humans have assembled, he manifests the indestructible power of the Bodhisattva’s merit in order to tame sentient beings, thus manifesting the subduing of Māra;
and he manifests the subduing of Māra in order to inspire the strength within all sentient beings.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings of the future, he manifests the subduing of Māra;
because he is able to transcend all realms of Māra even when Māra’s activities appear at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), he manifests the subduing of Māra;
and because he reveals that the power and force of afflictions are weak and inferior while the power of the roots of great compassion is exceedingly strong, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
In accordance with the sentient beings of the five turbid ages, he manifests the subduing of Māra.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten meanings for which a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva manifests the subduing of Māra when sitting at the site of enlightenment.
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten kinds of awakening to the powers of the Tathāgata for Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these ten?
They are as follows:”
They transcend all the activities of Māra and eliminate afflictions; they bring to ultimate completion all bodhisattva practices and awaken to the power of the Tathāgata;
they attain mastery over all bodhisattva samādhis and awaken to the power of the Tathāgata;
they fully accomplish all bodhisattva dhyānas and samādhis and awaken to the power of the Tathāgata.
The power of awakening that fulfills all pure and wholesome dharmas;
the power of awakening that discerns wholesome dharmas and subdues worldly dharmas;
the power of awakening that fills all lands with the pure Dharma-body;
The pure sounds they produce are entirely equal to the minds of all sentient beings; this is awakening to the power of the Tathāgata.
They are able to receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas; this is awakening to the power of the Tathāgata.

They attain equality with the body, speech, and mind of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, and within a single thought-moment, they know the dharmas of the three periods of time; this is awakening to the power of the Tathāgata.

They attain the Samādhi of Excellent Awakening and are endowed with the ten powers of a Buddha—namely, the knowledge of what is possible and what is impossible, up to the knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows—thereby awakening to the powers of a Tathāgata.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten ways in which a bodhisattva-mahāsattva awakens to the powers of the Tathāgata; because a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is endowed with these powers, they receive the name "Tathāgata."
“O Son of the Buddha!
Having thus attained the state of a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, one is able to turn the tenfold wheel of the pure Dharma. What are these ten?
First, they are fully endowed with the four kinds of pure fearlessness;
second, they produce the four analytical knowledges and pure, wondrous voices;
third, they clearly understand the four noble truths.
Fourth, they accord with the unimpeded Dharma-gates of all Buddhas;
fifth, their minds are pure and impartial, capable of universally encompassing all sentient beings;
sixth, what they teach is not in vain, as they resolutely deliver sentient beings from the limits of suffering.
Seventh, they are sustained by the great compassion of past lives;
eighth, they fill the world with the sublime sound of the Dharma so that all sentient beings hear and know it without exception;
ninth, for incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*), they constantly preach the True Dharma without ever ceasing for even a moment.
Tenth, they transform the powers of the faculties, the factors of enlightenment, the liberations, and all meditative concentrations and samādhis, maintaining them in uninterrupted continuity.
O Son of the Buddha!
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha turns the wheel of Dharma of these ten practices and immeasurable other practices.
“O Son of the Buddha!

The wheel of the pure Dharma of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, because of ten kinds of pure dharmas, enters the minds of sentient beings, gives rise to the signless, and is certain and not in vain.”
What are the ten? They are:
by virtue of the power of past vows;
Because they are sustained by great compassion;
because they do not abandon sentient beings;
and because, possessing mastery of wisdom, they preach the Dharma according to what is appropriate for each.
Because they never miss the proper time;
because they neither increase nor decrease according to the capacity of those who are vessels for the Dharma;
and because they possess the definitive knowledge that discerns the three periods of time.
Because his physical conduct is most excellent;
because his verbal conduct is never false;
and because his mental conduct awakens to all sounds as they arise.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is because of these ten kinds of pure dharmas that one is able to turn the wheel of Dharma and enter the minds of sentient beings, giving rise to the signless, which is certain and not in vain.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha has brought his buddha-activities to ultimate completion, he manifests Great Parinirvāṇa through ten kinds of meanings.”
What are the ten? They are:
understanding that all conditioned phenomena are entirely impermanent;
It clarifies that all conditioned phenomena are not secure;
it clarifies that parinirvāṇa leads to the ultimate security;
and it clarifies that parinirvāṇa is far removed from all fears.

Because devas and humans are attached to the form-body (*rūpakāya*), [the Buddha] clarifies that the form-body is impermanent and subject to decay and destruction, in order to cause them to seek the eternally abiding pure dharma-body (*dharmakāya*);
he clarifies that the power of impermanence is so strong it cannot be overturned;
and he clarifies that conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛtadharma*) do not follow the course of desire and lack self-mastery.
It clarifies that all phenomena of the three realms are like unbaked clay vessels, for they lack solidity;
it clarifies that parinirvāṇa is the most real, for it is indestructible;
and it clarifies that parinirvāṇa is far removed from saṃsāra, for it is neither arising nor ceasing.
O Son of the Buddha!
For these ten reasons, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha manifests Great Parinirvāṇa.
O Son of the Buddha!

The Dharma of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas is likewise: their vows have been fulfilled, they have turned the wheel of Dharma, and all those who were to be delivered have been delivered;
they have bestowed the noble prediction upon the Bodhisattvas, and having brought all Buddha-activities to ultimate completion, they abide immutably, manifesting Great Parinirvāṇa.
"O Son of the Buddha!
It is for these ten reasons that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha manifests Great Parinirvāṇa.
O Son of the Buddha!"
This is the great and wondrous Dharma-gate of the pure and supreme conduct of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.

It elucidates the immeasurable and profound meanings taught by all Buddhas, causing all those possessed of wisdom to rejoice, bringing all the great vows of Bodhisattvas to ultimate fulfillment, and ensuring that their practices never cease.
O Son of the Buddha!
If there are sentient beings who hear this sutra and, with pure faith, do not give rise to slander but practice according to what is taught, those beings will swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Why is this? Because Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas practice according to what they have taught.
O Son of the Buddha!
Therefore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas should practice according to what has been taught, single-mindedly revering, believing in, and upholding this sutra.
O Son of the Buddha!

This sutra gives birth to all the merits of the various practices of Bodhisattvas; it is the flower of profound and wondrous meaning, penetrating deeply into wisdom, encompassing all dharma-gates, and remaining far removed from the worldly dharmas of Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and those not shared with any sentient beings. It is able to universally illumine all dharma-gates, nurture roots of goodness, and deliver sentient beings.
Therefore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas should listen to and receive this sutra with a single-minded focus, and protect and uphold it.

If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva upholds this sutra, they will be able to give rise to all vows; through minimal expedient means, they will swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. This [sutra] explains the flowers of the profound and wondrous meaning—the merit of giving rise to all the practices of bodhisattvas—penetrating deep wisdom and encompassing all dharma-gates. It is a quality not shared by worldly beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or any other sentient beings. It is able to universally illumine all dharma-gates, nurture roots of goodness, and deliver sentient beings over time. By the spiritual power of the Buddha and because the Dharma of this sutra is thus, immeasurable asaṃkhyeya worlds in the ten directions tremble in six ways, and a great light shines everywhere.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions gazed face-to-face at Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and joyfully praised him,
saying: "Excellent,
O Son of the Buddha!"

It is indeed able to expound this Sūtra which gives birth to all the merits of the practices of Bodhisattvas, a flower of profound and wondrous meaning, which penetrates deeply into wisdom, encompasses all dharma-gates, and is a teaching not shared by worldly beings, Śrāvakas, or Pratyekabuddhas; it can universally illumine all dharma-gates, nurture roots of goodness, and deliver sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
You have already well studied this Dharma, well understood this Dharma, and eloquently expounded this Dharma; we Buddhas likewise expound this Dharma, and all Buddhas do so as well.
Therefore, O Son of the Buddha!
"We shall all together protect this sutra, so that future bodhisattvas who have not yet heard it may hear it.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the entire great assembly and the entire dharma-realm, and spoke in verse:
"Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, He diligently practiced all manner of ascetic austerities."
Having made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, one is born as a true son of the Buddha.
Having transformed and delivered immeasurable multitudes, establishing them in the unsurpassed path—
listen well and attentively as I speak of the peerless conduct of the Bodhisattvas.
Making offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, they remain entirely free from attachment;
they transform and deliver all beings, yet do not give rise to the notion of "sentient beings.
Constantly seeking the merits of the Buddha, their minds have no point of reliance.
He expounds those supreme and wondrous practices, causing all the multitudes to rejoice.
Having subdued all Māras and extinguished the afflictions of the three realms,
and having already perfected the noble merits, he manifests the stage of a youth.
Having extinguished evil afflictions and delusion, their minds are ever tranquil;
manifesting immeasurable practices, I shall proclaim their merits.
Having distanced themselves from all evils, they have ultimately reached the further shore.
Amidst immeasurable sentient beings, He manifests various transformations.
Knowing the arising, abiding, and ceasing of the mind, He demonstrates all manner of deeds;
Proclaiming those wondrous merits, He causes all the assembly to rejoice.
Seeing the sentient beings within the three realms of existence, Oppressed by immeasurable suffering,
wandering through birth and death, And with the fires of affliction blazing fiercely;
Desiring to bring them liberation, I seek enlightenment with single-minded resolve.
Briefly explaining those pure virtues, listen well with a single-minded focus:
Through generosity, ethical discipline, patience, and diligence, And through mastery of meditative concentration,
Possessing wisdom and skillful means, Great compassion delivers all sentient beings.
Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, they joyfully cultivated compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;
I shall now describe their merits, which you, O virtuous ones, should listen to with careful attention.
With countless bodies that have become withered and emaciated, they have constantly and correctly sought awakening.
Not sparing even his own life, he has perfected the unsurpassed path.
Always acting for the benefit of sentient beings, he seeks no personal peace or happiness.
To that Muni of compassion and mercy, I shall describe his supreme conduct.
Even in immeasurable and countless eons, one could not exhaustively describe even a small portion [of it].
One might measure the void, or count the drops of the ocean waters;
yet the ocean of a bodhisattva’s merit is beyond all analogy.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, I have briefly explained but a small portion.
Upholding the roots of goodness of sentient beings, nurturing pure and white dharmas,
remaining far removed from a mind of arrogance, they seek the Dharma without ever being satiated.
Causing the multitude to dwell in peace, Nurturing the tree of wisdom,
The Bodhisattva’s mind is like the earth, Benefiting all beings.
With the root of supple and compassionate heart, And the trunk of unsurpassed great compassion,
The leaves of merit and the flowers of wisdom, with the fragrance of upheld precepts,
The Tathāgata’s light of pure insight causes the bodhisattva flowers to bloom;
Unstained by the waters of conditioned existence, it brings universal joy to all sentient beings.
The upright mind is the seed; compassion is the root and sprout;
wisdom and skillful means are the stem; the five perfections are the branches;
dhyāna is the leaf and the various insights are the flowers; and omniscience is the fruit.
The Dharma-tree of supernatural power is a bird that universally covers the three worlds;
with the true truths as its feet, the pure white dharmas as its body,
right mindfulness as its neck and crown, wisdom as its head, and liberation as its crest.
With eyes of compassion, clarity, and purity, you emerge from the deep valley of ultimate truth.
A Bodhisattva, a lion among Dharma-teachers, you subdue all demons;
for you, birth and death are a vast wilderness, and the afflictions are the various evil paths.
The view of extremes is a perilous thief; the blind through ignorance lose the right path.
The Bodhisattva, the Great Guide, seeing those who are lost in darkness, reveals the true path to them and leads them to the place of peace and security.
The afflictions of greed and hatred constantly torment and harm sentient beings;
through immeasurable suffering and calamity, they are oppressed throughout the long night.
Seeing their suffering, the Bodhisattva gives rise to great compassion.
He fully expounds the eighty-four thousand [teachings], delivering beings through their respective remedies.
The Bodhisattva is a Dharma King; transforming sentient beings through the Right Path, he causes them to distance themselves from evil and cultivate all manner of goodness, seeking only toward Bodhi.
In the presence of all Buddhas, they receive the prediction of sovereign wisdom;
They extensively bestow the treasures of the noble ones, causing others to possess the jewels of the seven factors of enlightenment.
With pure precepts as the hub and diligence as the spokes,
With the rim of samādhi and right concentration, he turns the pure wheel of Dharma three times.
With the shield of a pure mind and the sharp sword of brilliant wisdom,
he crushes and destroys all afflictions, as well as the various externalists and demonic adversaries.
The ocean of profound wisdom, with the water of the single flavor of the True Dharma, is filled with the jewels of dhyāna and awakening; none are able to fathom it.
With a straightforward mind, its purity expands ever wider, and omniscience serves as its tide.
The ocean of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom Is inexhaustible in its exposition.
Supreme and unsurpassed in the world, He remains unattached therein;
A mountain of dhyāna, clarity, and wisdom, Firm and upright, it does not waver.
If there are those who draw near, they will swiftly attain wisdom equal to his;
dwelling upon the summit of the Sumeru of knowledge, they universally observe all worlds.
Their profound mind is like a vajra; all things are entirely firm and solid.
The Triple Gem and all-encompassing wisdom— faith in these cannot be destroyed.
Subduing all Māras and extinguishing all afflictions,
one dwells securely in fearlessness to deliver all living beings across.
Raising the great cloud of loving-kindness, it universally covers all;
flashing the lightning of great compassion, it thunders with the vast sound of the Dharma.
From its fourfold eloquence it pours down the rain of the Dharma, the nectar-water of the Eightfold Noble Path.
Extinguishing the fires of affliction, one dwells securely in all that is meaningful.
With pure and white dharmas as its city and wisdom as its walls,
it possesses a pavilion of unsurpassed knowledge and a deep moat of shame and remorse.
The three gates of liberation through emptiness, with right mindfulness as their defense;
the four paths as the correct way— traversing these, one exits the triple world,
erects the unsurpassed Dharma banner, and utterly destroys all Māras.
The Dharma-body garuḍa has the four bases of psychic power as its feet, And the clear, pure eyes of compassion; it dwells upon the tree of all-knowledge.
The Bodhisattva, king of garuḍas, [soars] within the great ocean of birth and death.
Seizing and gathering devas, humans, and nāgas, he establishes them on the shore of nirvāṇa.
With the sun of perfected pure precepts and the radiance of pure wisdom,
with supernormal powers as his swift gait, he dries up the waters of craving and desire.
Awakening sentient beings through the long night, nourishing them with the medicines of the faculties and powers,
the Bodhisattva is a bright and pure sun that leaves nothing unilluminated.
The moon of the perfected Dharma-realm is such that sentient beings never tire of beholding it.
Outshining the two vehicles, which are like the fireflies of small wisdom,
The Bodhisattva’s cool moon travels through ultimate emptiness.
Hanging down its light to illuminate the three realms, there is no mental phenomenon that does not appear.
Sovereign King of all Dharmas, whose body is adorned with the color of merit, possessing the pure eye of wisdom through skillful means, you dwell securely in the supreme and wondrous Dharma.
Your body is graced by the primary and secondary marks; all who behold it never tire of looking.
That King of Dharma Sovereignty governs sentient beings according to the Dharma;
having eradicated the afflictions of desire and transcended the three realms,
he constantly delights in diligently practicing the dharmas of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
The Bodhisattva, Great Brahma King, universally manifests various bodies and utters pure,
wondrous sounds that are heard throughout the three realms without exception.
Having distanced himself from all conditioned activities, his sphere of experience is ever pure.
Having attained non-retrogressive wisdom, they are fully endowed with mastery over the Dharma.
Forever departing from the paths of the two vehicles, they receive the predictions of all Buddhas;
mounting the Unsurpassed Vehicle, they ultimately realize all-encompassing knowledge.
The mind is pure like space, forever free from all existence;
though engaged in worldly affairs, the mind has no dependence.
Having perfected the practice of total purity, they likewise cause all sentient beings to be so.
The wisdom of the Bodhisattva is ever more expansive, Pure as the vast expanse of space.
Upon the ground of immeasurable skillful means, They bring benefit to all living beings;
With the cool waters of compassion, They extinguish the blazing afflictions.
The fierce and blazing fire of wisdom Completely incinerates the habitual tendencies of affliction;
Racing like the wind, it travels through the ten directions, Extensively performing the deeds of all Buddhas.
The Bodhisattva is a wish-fulfilling jewel, Eliminating the poverty and suffering of all beings.
Wisdom like a vajra destroys all false views;
adorned with immeasurable virtues, it brings joy to all sentient beings.
Having perfected the supreme practice, one dwells securely in the state of the Tathāgata.
The Bodhisattva’s flowers of merit cause the seven factors of awakening to bloom;
with vows as jeweled garlands, they adorn the crown of the world.
The fragrance of the Bodhisattva’s pure precepts keeps all evil conduct at a distance.
With the fragrance of this pure precept, they anoint and perfume all beings.
The Bodhisattva’s unsurpassed canopy universally covers all worlds;
establishing the banner of wisdom, they destroy the banners of all Māras.
The Bodhisattva’s adorned conduct, The banner of pure and wondrous wisdom,
And the robe of the merit of shame and remorse, Universally cover all beings.
The Bodhisattva’s unsurpassed vehicle— Riding upon it, one transcends the triple world.
With a mind well-tamed and compliant, he dwells securely upon the king of precious elephants.
The Bodhisattva, a great dragon king, endowed with sovereign power,
universally showers the nectar of the Dharma, moistening and nourishing all living beings.
Bodhisattvas are extremely difficult to encounter, just like the udumbara flower;
they subdue all māras and extinguish all afflictions.
Regarding the wheel of Dharma turned by the Buddha, they are able to turn it in accordance with it.
The lamp of wisdom dispels all darkness, causing all to see the true path.
The river of the Bodhisattva’s merit flows in accordance with the true path;
it is a constant bridge across birth and death, ferrying beings without rest.
The Bodhisattva’s vessel of the True Dharma sails upon the ocean of all vows;
with wisdom fully perfected, he ferries beings to the other shore.
The Bodhisattva purifies the groves and gardens, truly delighting in bringing joy to sentient beings.
The flowers of liberation from the True Dharma, the palace of luminous and pure wisdom—
upon the summit of the Bodhisattva’s Snowy Mountain, the King of Medicinal Trees grows forth;
it eradicates the disease of afflictions and causes all beings to rejoice.
The Bodhisattvas are equal to the Tathāgatas; awakening all sentient beings and eliminating the darkness of ignorance, they attain perfect enlightenment.
From whence the Most Victorious One comes, from such a place do the Bodhisattvas come.
Having attained the wisdom of equality, they have ultimately reached the further shore.
The Bodhisattvas, great teachers, transform and guide all sentient beings;
they spontaneously realize perfect enlightenment, the realm of omniscience.
Endowed with immeasurable power, which none can destroy,
Abiding securely in fearlessness, knowing all phenomena and fully understanding sentient beings.
Even throughout the entire realm of form, among all sentient beings that exist—
All sounds of every language, he can follow and accord with them all.
Transcending the realm of form to reach the formless, he manifests all those various phenomena;
though all sentient beings were to speak of them, they could never exhaustively describe them.
The Bodhisattva fully accomplishes such virtues as these;
understanding both existence and non-existence, as well as all that exists and all that does not exist,
he is endowed with true wisdom and eliminates all bonds.
Having perfected all-knowledge, their minds are free from attachment.
They expound those profound practices, causing all beings to rejoice;
they thoroughly comprehend all phenomena as being entirely like illusions and transformations.
Arousing the skillful means of compassion, All Buddhas protect and uphold them;
Giving birth to the gateways of wisdom-transformations, They universally manifest immeasurable deeds.
You virtuous ones, listen attentively To the various merits of the Bodhisattvas.
The single body is without limit, universally manifesting infinite bodies.
Neither mind nor the objects of the mind, it appears in response to all beings;
from it issues a single wondrous sound, the ultimate dharma of speech.
He fully encompasses all classes of sentient beings and all languages and sounds;
having distanced himself from the body of afflictions, he manifests bodies according to what is appropriate.
With bodies of immeasurable skillful means, he preaches the Dharma in every voice.
Their minds are ever in tranquil extinction, pure as empty space.
Adorning the lands with their minds, they manifest before all multitudes;
displaying various bodies, they remain unattached to them.
Distant from all birth, yet not destroying its causes;
Following all realms of existence, taking birth without attachment.
Realizing the body is like space, manifesting according to what is appropriate.
The Bodhisattva manifests such immeasurable and boundless deeds;
he reverently makes offerings to that most supreme among two-legged beings with ointments,
powdered incense, flowers, banners, canopies, pennants, and music.
With supreme articles of offering, they offer with a straightforward mind to all Buddhas;
never departing from the assembly of a single Buddha, they are universally present before all Buddhas.
Skillful in posing difficult questions, they listen to and receive the profound and wondrous Dharma.
By hearing this True Dharma, they attain all samādhis.
Within each and every samādhi, they give rise to immeasurable gates of concentration;
furthermore, they are able to universally manifest the arising of immeasurable samādhis.
Through wisdom and skillful means, they have reached the ultimate further shore;
awakening to all phenomena as being entirely like illusions and transformations,
they manifest various bodies and produce immeasurable sounds.
Entering the net of conceptions regarding sentient beings, their minds remain free from attachment.
At times they manifest as sentient beings, conforming to worldly purposes;
at other times they demonstrate the practice of bodhi, which is immeasurable and boundless.
Practicing generosity and maintaining pure precepts, Cultivating patience, diligence,
concentration, wisdom, and the four immeasurables, And practicing the four means of integration.
Whether manifesting through the completion of conduct, Or attaining the forbearance of the non-arising of phenomena,
Some receive the prediction of empowerment, while others are in their final birth before Buddhahood;
some manifest as followers of the Śrāvaka vehicle, and others again appear as Pratyekabuddhas;
though they enter nirvana in immeasurable lands, they do not abandon the bodhisattva practices.
Sometimes he manifests as Śakra, sometimes as Brahmā;
surrounded by celestial maidens, or again, alone in silent contemplation;
or he manifests in the form of a bhikṣu, pure in precepts and with senses subdued.
Sometimes appearing as a Sovereign King, sometimes appearing as one who has entered the Net of Dharma;
sometimes appearing as a woman skilled in arts, or appearing as one practicing asceticism;
sometimes appearing amidst the five desires, or again, abiding in meditative concentration.
Sometimes manifesting parinirvāṇa, or again manifesting birth;
sometimes manifesting as a youth, or again manifesting as an aged person—
if anyone should attempt to conceive of these, their mind will become confused and driven mad.
Sometimes in celestial palaces, sometimes manifesting his final descent to be born;
sometimes manifesting dwelling in the mother’s womb, or attaining Buddhahood and turning the wheel of Dharma;
sometimes manifesting birth, or manifesting parinirvāṇa.
Sometimes they manifest the arts of a youth, or again they manifest leaving the home life;
sometimes they manifest sitting at the site of enlightenment, or achieving the unsurpassed path;
or again they manifest turning the sovereign wheel of the true Dharma.
Sometimes they manifest seeking the True Dharma, sometimes they manifest as the body of a Buddha.
Filling immeasurable lands, they do not regress from the Bodhisattva practice;
penetrating deeply into immeasurable eons, they ultimately reach the other shore.
Immeasurable eons are a single thought-moment; a single thought-moment is immeasurable eons.
All eons are not eons, yet they manifest as eons for sentient beings.
Without coming and without accumulation, they manifest the events of all eons.
Within a single mote of dust, one universally beholds all Buddhas;
among all classes of sentient beings, there is no place where a Buddha does not exist;
so too with all Buddha-fields and the realms of sentient beings.
They are able to discern and know all the seals of all dharmas;
though all kalpas may come to an end, the seals of dharma are inexhaustible.
Thus they know sentient beings to be immeasurable and boundless.
That single sentient being possesses immeasurable hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, and millions of bodies; the causes and conditions are likewise so.
As it is with that one sentient being, so it is with all others as well.
Thus having attained ultimate knowledge, he causes all to learn as well;
he fully knows the faculties of sentient beings—their differences of superior, middling, and inferior.
He understands that the various faculties are in constant flux, and he discerns who is a fit vessel and who is not.
The single faculty and all faculties Mutually depend upon one another.
The subtle wisdom of the Bodhisattva Discerns and knows them all;
it likewise knows the nature of all desires And the various stains of affliction.
Having fully understood the mental activities of the past, the future, and the present,
he knows the conduct of all sentient beings and has reached the ultimate further shore.
Knowing that there is no practice in the practice of knowing, he expounds the sublime Dharma for the sake of the multitude.
Thus knowing the mental activities, both defiled and pure, the Bodhisattva,
within a single thought-moment, attains all-knowledge;
he penetrates deeply into the mind of the Tathāgata, which is ultimately inconceivable.
In a single thought, they are able to know the supreme wisdom of all Buddhas,
the ultimate wisdom of spiritual power, and the possession of all supernormal faculties and clarities.
Within a single thought, they can travel to all lands throughout the ten directions.
Thus they travel swiftly through immeasurable and incalculable eons,
yet without leaving their original seats, they abide securely in the profound Dharma.
Just as a skilled illusionist manifests various forms and colors, so do they appear.
Neither form nor formless, like an illusion it has no existence;
the Bodhisattva is likewise, deeply understanding vast skillful means,
manifesting all manner of transformations that fill all worlds.
Just as the bright and pure sun appears in the world,
Able to dispel all darkness and leaving nothing unilluminated,
So too is the sun of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom, Brilliantly pure and perfectly full.
Emerging from the sphere of the pure mind, it universally illuminates all phenomena.
Just as when a person in a dream performs various deeds,
though immeasurable eons might pass, the nature of the dream remains inexhaustible.
In a single thought-moment, the Bodhisattva manifests phenomena such as dreams;
though immeasurable eons might come to an end, their wisdom has no limit.
They always delight in dwelling among mountains and marshes, remaining far removed from worldly speech.
Having reached the ultimate end of the path of language, their minds are free from attachment.
The Bodhisattvas fully comprehend the true nature of all phenomena;
they universally speak in the voices of sentient beings without giving rise to false conceptualizations.
Just as in the spring months, when sentient beings see a mirage,
the foolish take it for water and pursue it with increasing thirst;
so too does the Bodhisattva perceive that sentient beings are shrouded by afflictions.
Like a mirage that increases thirst, he seeks liberation with single-minded resolve.
Knowing that sentient beings lack substantial reality, his great compassion increases all the more;
he contemplates form as a mass of foam and sensation as a bubble upon the water.
Perception is like a springtime mirage; all conditioned phenomena are like the plantain tree.
The mind is like a skilled illusionist, manifesting all manner of things;
skillfully discerning the five aggregates, the mind remains unattached.
All sense-bases (*āyatana*) are entirely empty and quiescent, far removed from the affairs of self-mastery;
the elements (*dhātu*) have no substantial nature, yet they manifest the divisions of the realms of sentient beings.
This is the foremost, ultimate truth, the definitive nature of cessation.
Extensively expounding and analyzing the Dharma, yet the mind remains unstained and unattached.
The Bodhisattva knows that the five aggregates have no past, future, or present;
driven by afflictions and karma, they revolve in this wheel of the three sufferings.
He expounds the Dharma of dependent origination, which is neither existent nor non-existent;
having deeply understood the true meaning, he is unattached to it.
With pure wisdom, the Bodhisattva explains the phenomena of the three periods of time.
Manifesting to all living beings, That they are all but a single thought;
In the realms of desire, form, and formlessness, He manifests the affairs of sentient beings,
The precepts and liberation of the Three Vehicles, And ultimate omniscience.
Knowing what is possible and what is impossible, knowing karma and the faculties,
the nature of desire and the various afflictions, and all paths leading to every destination;
with the knowledge of past lives and the divine eye, he utterly extinguishes all afflictions.
They know the ten powers of the Buddha, yet they have not yet reached the ultimate;
they accord with all Buddha-dharmas and deeply understand the emptiness of all phenomena;
they completely extinguish all afflictions, yet do not exhaust their outflows.
Extensively entering the profound path, they teach and transform all sentient beings;
these sons of the Buddha dwell in fearlessness, never abandoning the bodhisattva practices.
Without error or omission, they likewise do not forsake right mindfulness.
Vigor, aspiration, and samādhi, Wisdom without diminution—
these three are ever pure. Thoroughly penetrating the three periods of time,
With great compassion mindful of sentient beings, There is no obstruction whatsoever.
Deeply entering the various gateways of the Dharma, they are fully endowed with such practices.
I have spoken but a small portion of the meaning of their adorned merits;
even in immeasurable and incalculable eons, one could not exhaustively describe them.
What I have spoken is but a small portion, like a single mote of dust upon the great earth.
Constantly relying on the Tathāgata’s wisdom, yet having nothing upon which to rely;
constantly cultivating extraordinary thoughts, because of the firmness of great compassion.
Abiding securely in pure precepts, always diligently cultivating vigor,
they teach and transform all sentient beings and bestow upon them the prediction of true Buddha-sons.
Reaching the ultimate fulfillment of Buddha-virtues, they know the lands and they know sentient beings.
Discerning the kalpas of the three periods of time, their minds never grow weary.
Possessing the power of dhāraṇī, they deeply understand the true meaning;
contemplating the peerless Dharma, they attain the unsurpassed path.
All sublime merits are sought through the aspiration for bodhi;
by the power of the causes and conditions of compassion, bodhi is made pure and supreme.
Endowed with the pāramitās, one accords with them until their perfect consummation.
Through the power of wisdom that determines all things, one awakens to the unsurpassed path.
Having accomplished the wisdom of skillful means, one delights in expounding the profound Dharma;
by following and constantly guarding it, one attains the station of the Dharma King.
Abiding securely in the supreme and wondrous Dharma, they are unattached to it;
giving rise to the transformation of wisdom, they awaken to supreme Bodhi.
Abiding throughout all kalpas, these Bodhisattvas attain the correct aspiration.
Abiding securely in the profound Dharma, he eliminates the doubts of sentient beings.
Cultivating profound wisdom, he is skillfully able to discern all phenomena;
reaching the ultimate realm of concentration and insight, he awakens to all-encompassing knowledge.
Wisdom enters all liberations, reaching the ultimate further shore;
Possessing all supernormal powers and clear insights, one dwells in the stainless, cool garden.
Fully endowed with pure and white dharmas, one manifests various modes of conduct.
The Dharma of universal manifestation and adornment is entirely beyond conceptualization.
Skillfully knowing the minds of sentient beings, he is able to preach so that they reach the ultimate;
with the seal of pure bodhi, the light of his wisdom illuminates all.
Nothing can measure it; far removed from the dharma of indolence, it abides like the king of mountains, possessing an ocean of merit and wisdom.
This sublime vajra-jewel dharma abides in great adornment.
Having brought all great matters to ultimate completion, nothing whatsoever can destroy them.
Having received the prediction of enlightenment (*bodhy-avyākaraṇa*), they abide in a vast mind;
having attained the Buddha’s inexhaustible treasury, they awaken to all phenomena.
Worldly wisdom is ever sovereign, sporting in all supernormal powers;
within the realm of all phenomena, it is free and without obstruction.
Sovereign in body, vows, and conduct, wisdom likewise is sovereign.
Countless billions of sovereign powers are manifested in all things.
Fully endowed with all masteries, they sport through various supernormal powers;
Deeply entering the realm of the Buddhas, nothing whatsoever can destroy them.
Adorned with wisdom, possessing the fearless qualities unique to the Buddhas,
these sons of the Buddha practice their noble deeds and remain far removed from all evil.
Their physical actions are pure, and their verbal actions are pure.
Because they are protected by all Buddhas, they accomplish the ten great deeds.
As mind and mental factors arise and abide, they manifest unsurpassed matters;
dwelling in the concentration of the faculties, they attain the most excellent faculties.
With a pure and upright mind, far removed from all guile and crookedness,
they penetrate deeply into the nature of sentient beings and manifest all manner of deeds.
Having eradicated the habitual tendencies of afflictions, they have reached the ultimate, unsurpassed practice.
Endowed with profound wisdom, they attain all-knowledge.
Having distanced themselves from all evils, they skillfully proceed toward nirvana.
Giving birth to the path of merit, they have well-mastered all trainings.
The realm of mind of the immeasurable path, Cultivated without attachment,
abiding in profound wisdom, Manifesting the adornments of the path.
From hands, feet, heart, and belly, The treasury of unsurpassed wisdom.
His mind is like a vajra, with wisdom as his weapon;
with the peak of wisdom-observation, he enters deeply into the practice of bodhi.
With pure precepts as his nose, he extinguishes all burning afflictions.
With the four analytical knowledges and a broad, long tongue, his body reaches everywhere;
with a mind of pure and wondrous wisdom, he practices all virtuous deeds.
Dwelling securely at the site of enlightenment, he takes the lion’s throne as his seat.
The Brahma-abodes serve as a peaceful bed; the unimpeded ultimate truth is the goal.
Contemplating the wisdom of the Sugata, it shines universally upon all things;
observing the conduct of sentient beings, it reveals their manifold and wondrous virtues.
Taking this as valorous exertion, freedom from greed is pure giving;
freedom from pride is pure morality; immovability is pure patience;
non-retrogression is pure diligence; and mastery is pure meditation.
Not practicing the wisdom of folly, one universally rescues others with the compassion of space.
Not being distressed by sorrow is kindness (*karuṇā*); the pure Dharma is joy (*muditā*).
Being free from all afflictions is equanimity (*upekṣā*); tranquility is the profound meaning.
Taking the objective realm as the True Dharma, one possesses the merit of dedication;
wisdom is like a sharp sword, universally illuminating as a great light for all beings.
To hear the Dharma without weariness or satiety—this is the correct seeking of the Dharma.
Not begrudging one's body or life—this is the illumination of the True Dharma.
Following the teachings of all Buddhas, one eradicates the paths of all Māras;
with a pure and upright mind, one gathers the karmic deeds of all Buddhas.
Far removed from the deeds of Māra, they nurture all forms of wisdom;
Far removed from that which is sustained by Māra, they dwell securely in the sustenance of all Buddhas.
Ultimately attaining the sustenance of the Dharma, they abide in the wisdom of non-abiding.
Having completed his karmic tasks, he passed away and descended by spirit into his mother’s womb.
He manifested the subtle transition, and again manifested birth;
he manifested being proclaimed the most supreme, and manifested taking seven steps.
He manifests as a youth, and again manifests dwelling in a deep palace;
he manifests leaving home to study the Way, adorning all sites of enlightenment.
Universally emitting immeasurable light, he awakens all living beings.
Subduing all māras, he attains the unsurpassed path.
Manifesting the turning of the pure Dharma wheel, he reveals the stage of the Tathāgata;
increasing the pure and white dharmas, he manifests great parinirvāṇa.
The practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas are immeasurable and boundless;
as I have previously explained, I have here briefly cited but a small portion of them.
Having practiced for immeasurable eons, they cause all beings to abide in Bodhi.
Regarding the practices of all sentient beings and all phenomena, they remain unstained by them.
Thus, through the perfection of such practice, they achieve mastery over power;
by means of immeasurable lands, they place them within the path of a single hair.
Holding infinite lands in his palms, he travels throughout all worlds,
yet returns them to their original places so that sentient beings feel no fear.
With everything at his disposal, the Bodhisattva adorns and purifies all Buddha-fields.
Placed within a single pore, sentient beings cannot fail to see it.
Able to receive all oceans within a single pore,
the great ocean neither increases nor decreases, and no harm comes to sentient beings.
Manifesting all such phenomena and signs,
he grinds infinite adamantine mountains into fine dust with his hand;
with all these particles, he scatters them throughout all the Buddha-fields.
Furthermore, taking the atoms from the lands below, And spreading them throughout all other worlds,
One might know the number of all those atoms, But the wisdom [of the Buddha] can never be exhausted.
From within a single pore, He radiates forth pure light.
Universally illuminating all worlds, it completely eclipses the light of the sun and moon;
the radiance of jewels, fire, and celestial deities is obscured and does not appear.
It extinguishes the suffering of the evil realms and preaches the unsurpassed Dharma for all.
From a single word and sound of the Bodhisattva, all sounds are produced;
among all sentient beings, there is not one who does not hear them.
By hearing this Dharma-sound, they all attain great joy.
Fully and extensively proclaiming all that the Buddhas have taught,
they place all past eons within the future and the present, and transpose future and present eons into the past.
In all lands throughout the ten directions, The processes of formation and destruction are all clearly manifested;
By means of all sentient beings, They are placed within the path of a single hair-pore.
All Tathāgatas of the past and the present—
Possessing the power of mastery, they manifest it all within their own bodies.
Deeply understanding the dharma of transformation, they are skillfully able to respond to what is appropriate,
universally manifesting infinite bodies while remaining entirely unattached to them.
The body of Śakra and Brahmā, the bodies of the Four Great Kings,
the pure bodies of all devas, the bodies of all sentient beings,
the bodies of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and the pure body of the Tathāgata.
Universally manifesting all bodies, they skillfully cultivate the bodhisattva practices.
Appearing to enter the web of various perceptions— whether superior, middling, or inferior—
all are sustained by omniscience, universally manifesting Buddhas and their lands.
Possessing profound wisdom, they eliminate the web of all conceptualizations;
manifesting the conduct of a bodhisattva, they ultimately achieve enlightenment.
They manifest such immeasurable powers of mastery.
Nothing exists that is not manifested, yet throughout the world none can know it.
Manifesting while having nothing to manifest, ultimately unsurpassed,
he accords with sentient beings and teaches them the definitive practice.
The purified body is equal to space; Sublime sounds fill the world.
Pure precepts serve as unguents; The raiment of shame and remorse covers all.
The silk of the stainless True Dharma, And the *maṇi* jewel of omniscience.
With a body adorned by merit, you are enthroned as the Unsurpassed King.
The pāramitās are your golden wheel; the various supernormal powers are your elephant-treasure;
the bases of psychic power are your horse-treasure; and pure wisdom is your unsurpassed jewel.
Sublime conduct is the jewel of the queen; The four means of integration are the treasure-minister;
Skillful means is the general-jewel; He is the unsurpassed Wheel-Turning King.
The city of supreme and wondrous samādhi, The exquisite palace of the contemplation of emptiness.
Great adornment of compassion, with wisdom as a sharp sword;
The bow of firm and right mindfulness, with clear and keen faculties as arrows;
The parasol of the Buddhas' protection, establishing the banner of wisdom.
Directly entering the armies of Māra, they utterly destroy them with the power of patience;
the level ground of dhāraṇīs, the flowing waters of pure and wondrous conduct,
the gushing spring of profound wisdom, and the cool grove of pure insight.
Emptiness is a clear and pure pool, where the wondrous flowers of the seven factors of enlightenment bloom.
Spiritual power serves as adornment, samādhi as recreation,
the Dharma gates as songs of praise, and contemplation of the True Dharma as the maiden.
The food of the nectar-like Dharma, with the flavor of liberation as its drink,
they drive the well-tamed Three Vehicles and sport in the unsurpassed garden.
These various supreme practices, along with other unsurpassed dharmas—
Having practiced and studied for immeasurable eons, their minds never grew weary.
They made offerings to all Buddhas and purified all lands,
universally causing all sentient beings to dwell securely in omniscience.
The atoms of all lands may all have their numbers known;
The entire realm of empty space may all be measured;
The minds of all sentient beings may have their counts known in every thought-moment.
The virtues of the Buddha’s heirs are inexhaustible to describe.
Those who wish to possess these virtues and other sublime, wondrous dharmas;
those who wish to extinguish all suffering and bring peace and happiness to all living beings—[should study this].
Desiring to be equal in body, speech, and mind to all Tathāgatas,
one should give rise to the adamantine mind and bring this supreme practice to ultimate completion.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle 43.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha of Great Extensive Meaning, Scroll Forty-four.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-four: Entering the Dharma Realm, Part One. Chapter Thirty-four: Entering the Dharma Realm, Part One.
At that time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, in the Greatly Adorned High-Pavilion Lecture Hall, together with five hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
with Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva as their leaders; [and] Rātriketu Bodhisattva, Meruketu Bodhisattva, Ratnaketu Bodhisattva,
Asaṅgaketu Bodhisattva, Puṣpaketu Bodhisattva, Vimalaketu Bodhisattva, and Sūryaketu Bodhisattva.
...the Bodhisattva Right Banner, the Bodhisattva Banner Free from Dust, the Bodhisattva Radiant Pure Banner, the Bodhisattva Earthly Majestic Adornment,
the Bodhisattva Jewel Majestic Adornment, the Bodhisattva Great Wisdom Majestic Adornment, the Bodhisattva Vajra-Knowledge Majestic Adornment,

The Bodhisattva Resplendent Mountain of Merit, the Bodhisattva Resplendent Light of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Resplendent Universal Sublime Virtue,

The Bodhisattva, the Bodhisattva Vimalagarbha, the Bodhisattva Nābhigarbha, the Bodhisattva Padmagarbha,
the Bodhisattva Sukhadarśana, the Bodhisattva Samantadarśana, the Bodhisattva Viśuddhacakṣus,
the Bodhisattva Vimalacakṣus, the Bodhisattva Asaṅgacakṣus, the Bodhisattva Samantacakṣus, and the Bodhisattva Sudarśanacakṣus.

...the Bodhisattva Celestial Crown Producing the Treasury of All Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Celestial Crown Supreme in All Worlds,
the Bodhisattva Radiant Pure Celestial Crown, the Bodhisattva Immeasurable Jewel Celestial Crown,
the Bodhisattva Celestial Crown Receiving the Lion Throne of All Tathāgatas, and the Bodhisattva Celestial Crown Universally Illuminating the Dharma-realm and Space.
The Bodhisattva Brahmā-Śikhin, the Bodhisattva Nāga-Śikhin, the Bodhisattva Universal Buddha-Emanated Radiance-Śikhin,
the Bodhisattva Maṇḍala-Śikhin, the Bodhisattva Universal Vow-Ocean Sound Maṇi-Jewel King-Śikhin,
and the Bodhisattva Tathāgata-Light-Born Multitude of Jewels Sovereignty-Śikhin.
The Bodhisattva Maṇi-rāja-cūḍa Who Adorns All Space, the Bodhisattva Maṇi-rāja-jāla-sarvātma-tathāgata-vaśitā-prabhā-dhvaja Who Universally Covers All with a Net,
the Bodhisattva Cakra-pravartana-sarva-buddha-ghoṣa-cūḍa, the Bodhisattva Tryadhva-jñāna-ghoṣa-cūḍa, and the Bodhisattva Mahāprabha.
The Bodhisattva Vimalaprabha, the Bodhisattva Ratnaprabha, the Bodhisattva Virajaprabha, the Bodhisattva Rātriprabha,
the Bodhisattva Dharmaprabha, the Bodhisattva Śāntiprabha, the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabha,
the Bodhisattva Vaśitāprabha, the Bodhisattva Devaprabha, the Bodhisattva Guṇaketurāja, and the Bodhisattva Jñānaketurāja.
Dharmadhvaja Bodhisattva, Sarvābhijñādhvaja Bodhisattva, Prabhādhvaja Bodhisattva, Puṣpadhvaja Bodhisattva, Maṇidhvaja Bodhisattva,
Bodhidhvaja Bodhisattva, Brahmādhvaja Bodhisattva, Samantaprabhādhvaja Bodhisattva, Brahmaghoṣa Bodhisattva, Sāgaraghoṣa Bodhisattva, and Mahāpṛthivīghoṣa Bodhisattva.
Bodhisattva Sound of the Lord of the World, Bodhisattva Sound of Colliding Mountains, Bodhisattva Sound Filling All Dharmadhātus,
Bodhisattva Thunderous Sound of the Ocean of All Dharmas, Bodhisattva Sound Subduing All Māras,
Bodhisattva Cloud-Thunder Sound of Great Compassionate Expedient Means, and Bodhisattva Comforting Sound that Extinguishes All Suffering.
Bodhisattva Dharmottara, Bodhisattva Jayottara, Bodhisattva Jñānottara, Bodhisattva Guṇasumerūttara,
Bodhisattva Guṇapravālottara, Bodhisattva Yaśottara, Bodhisattva Samantaprabhottara,
Bodhisattva Mahāmaitryuttara, Bodhisattva Jñānasāgrottara, and Tathāgatagotra-samudgata.
The Bodhisattva Uttama, the Bodhisattva Prabhāsa-guṇa, the Bodhisattva Jyotir-guṇa, the Bodhisattva Uttama-guṇa,
the Bodhisattva Vimala-prabhāsa-guṇa, the Bodhisattva Dharma-guṇa, the Bodhisattva Candra-guṇa,
the Bodhisattva Gaganaguṇa, the Bodhisattva Ratna-guṇa, and the Bodhisattva Guṇadhvaja.
The Bodhisattva Wisdom-Supreme Virtue, the Bodhisattva King of the Śāla Forest, the Bodhisattva Dharma-King,
the Bodhisattva King of Sentient Beings, the Bodhisattva Brahma-King, the Bodhisattva Mountain-King, the Bodhisattva Jewel-King,
the Bodhisattva King Free from Birth, the Bodhisattva Tranquility-King, the Bodhisattva Immovable-King, and the Bodhisattva Sage-King.
Bodhisattva Satya, Bodhisattva Jayarāja, Bodhisattva Śāntasvara, Bodhisattva Anāvaraṇasvara,
Bodhisattva Mahāpṛthivīnirghoṣa, Bodhisattva Mahāsāgaranirghoṣa, Bodhisattva Meghasvara,
Bodhisattva Dharmaprabhāsasvara, Bodhisattva Gaganasvara, and Bodhisattva Sarvasattvakuśalamūlanirghoṣa.
...the Bodhisattva Enlightened by Past Vows, the Bodhisattva Perfect Sound of the Path, the Bodhisattva Wisdom Sumeru Sound,
the Bodhisattva Space-Awakened, the Bodhisattva Stainless-Awakened, the Bodhisattva Unobstructed-Awakened, the Bodhisattva Virtuous-Awakened,
the Bodhisattva Universally Illuminating the Three Times-Awakened, and the Bodhisattva Vast-Awakened.
Samantaprabhābodhisattva, Dharmadhātuprabhābodhisattva, and five hundred such bodhisattvas as these.
All these bodhisattvas had fully brought forth the conduct of Samantabhadra; their spheres of activity were unimpeded, for they filled all buddha-fields.
They maintain immeasurable bodies, for they are able to go to all Buddhas;
they are endowed with unimpeded pure eyes, for they see the sovereign brilliance of all Buddhas;
they reach immeasurable places, for whenever all Buddhas attain perfect enlightenment, they are able to go there and behold the Buddhas face-to-face without ceasing.
The light of immeasurable wisdom universally illumines the ocean of all phenomena;
it is inexhaustible throughout immeasurable eons due to the purity of its eloquence;
and it reaches the ultimate limit of the realm of empty space because the sphere of its wisdom is entirely pure.
Because they have no basis of reliance, yet manifest form-bodies according to what is appropriate;
because they eliminate the cataracts of ignorance and skillfully discern and know the realms of sentient beings;
and because their space-like wisdom emits great nets of light that universally illumine all dharma-realms.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by five hundred great śrāvakas, all of whom had awakened to the ultimate truth, realized the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), deeply penetrated the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and departed from the ocean of birth and death;
they dwelt securely in the space-like realm of the Tathāgata, were free from the bonds of the fetters (*saṃyojana*), clung to nothing, wandered through space,
had extinguished all doubts and delusions regarding the Buddhas, and had deeply entered the great ocean of faith and inclination toward the Buddhas.

Furthermore, together with the various celestial kings, they have all already reverently made offerings to the Buddhas of the past; throughout the long night, they have benefited all sentient beings, their minds constantly practicing compassion without ever forgetting it;
they protect all living beings, enter the gate of supreme wisdom, and do not abandon any sentient being;

they give birth to the realm of the Buddhas' true Dharma, protect the Buddha-dharma, uphold the Buddha-nature, are born into the family of the Tathāgatas, and single-mindedly seek the gates of all-knowledge.
At that time, all the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, devas, humans, and their retinues had this thought:
“The Tathāgata’s conduct, the Tathāgata’s realm of wisdom, the Tathāgata’s retention, the Tathāgata’s powers,
the Tathāgata’s fearlessnesses, the Tathāgata’s samādhis, the Tathāgata’s abodes, and the Tathāgata’s supreme and wondrous merits— ”
The body of the Tathāgata, the wisdom of the Tathāgata, and the Dharma of the Tathāgata cannot be known by any gods or humans;
they cannot be fathomed, cannot be attained, cannot be received,
cannot be contemplated, cannot be scrutinized, cannot be analyzed, cannot be revealed, and cannot be clearly elucidated.
To explain this to others as it truly is, by means of the power of the Buddha’s sustaining, the power of mastery, the power of majestic spiritual authority,
