the power of the Tathāgata’s original vows, the power of past roots of goodness, the power of associating with virtuous friends,
the power of skillful means through pure faith, the power of seeking the supreme and wondrous Dharma, and the power of pure and upright bodhi.
The power of the mind, the profound mind, and the power of the vow for omniscience;

furthermore, the various intentions, various desires, various understandings, various languages, various stages, various faculties, various skillful means, various mental objects, and various inclinations toward the Tathāgata’s merits of the great assembly;
and how the World-Honored One, in the past, made the vow for omniscience and sought all-knowledge—such are the pure vows of the Bodhisattvas.
The perfection of purity, the various stages of the bodhisattva, the fulfillment of the bodhisattva’s practices, the adornment of the bodhisattva,
the adornment of the bodhisattva’s skillful means, the adornment of the bodhisattva’s path, the adornment of the ocean of skillful means born of the bodhisattva,
the adornment of the bodhisattva’s mastery, the ocean of the bodhisattva’s past lives, and the gateways to enlightenment.
The Ocean of Sovereignty: the Tathāgata’s sovereignty in turning the wheel of Dharma; the Tathāgata’s sovereignty in the purification of Buddha-fields;
the Tathāgata’s adornment of the realm of sentient beings through skillful means; the Tathāgata’s Dharma as the King of Dharma;
the Tathāgata’s path-light universally illuminating all things; the Tathāgata’s sovereignty in entering the abodes of all sentient beings; and the Tathāgata acting as one.

All sentient beings act as the supreme field of merit; the Tathāgata proclaims the merits and *dakṣiṇā* for all sentient beings, transforming and delivering the entire multitude of living beings through the three wheels of purity.
“I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion and kindness, will fully manifest [this teaching].

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the great assembly, entered the Lion’s Boundless Prowess Samādhi through his body of great compassion, the gateway of great compassion, with great compassion as the foremost, and by means of the skillful methods that accord with great compassion, so as to cause all sentient beings to delight in the pure Dharma.

Having entered into samādhi, at that moment the Great Adorned High Hall suddenly became vast and expansive, immeasurable, boundless, and indestructible. The ground of diamond-jewels was pure and magnificent; all kinds of *maṇi*-jewel kings were spread across the ground, strewn with immeasurable jewel-flowers and wondrous various gems. Columns of lapis lazuli were adorned with bright, pure jewels; the various precious ornaments were so densely arrayed as to be without gaps, and the pavilions were made of Jambūnada gold.
There were railings of various jewels, battlements, and watchtowers, decorated with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) railings;
and the treasures of the heavenly kings and solid precious substances further adorned it.

A net of mani jewels covered it from above; various precious banners were erected, and pennants and canopies were suspended, emitting a great web of light that universally illumines the entire dharma-realm.
Furthermore, its exterior was adorned with unspeakably many varieties of exquisite jewels, and the stairways on all four sides were composed of various precious gems.

At that time, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, the Jeta Grove suddenly became vast and expansive, equal in extent to worlds as numerous as the atoms within unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; it was adorned with various jewels, with unspeakable numbers of gems spread across its ground, and with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels forming its perimeter walls.
Ratna-tāla trees were planted in rows along the sides of the path;

immeasurable fragrant rivers flowed gently and filled to the brim, with waves formed of all kinds of precious flowers that all turned to the right, proclaiming all Buddha-dharmas with inconceivable sounds.
Pundarīka lotuses were all in full bloom, spreading across the surface of the water;
various precious flower-trees stood tall and lush along its banks;
and inconceivable pavilions were covered above by nets of maṇi jewels.
Adorned with incalculable exquisite jewels, its radiance shines everywhere; the ground is embellished by incalculable sovereign maṇi-jewels, which emit a multitude of wondrous fragrances.

They were adorned with immeasurable banners of mani-kings: banners of incense, banners of robes, banners of pennants, banners of silken streamers, banners of flowers, banners of ornaments, banners of garlands, banners of jeweled pendants, banners of various precious canopies, great mani-banners, universally illuminating mani-jewel banners, banners emitting the voices of Buddhas, lion-king jewel banners, banners manifesting the ocean of all Buddhas' past lives, banners of the entire dharma-realm, and banners of the king of mani-jewels.

At that time, in the space above the Jeta Grove, inconceivable clouds of celestial jewel palaces, inconceivable clouds of various fragrant trees, and unspeakable clouds of Mount Sumerus adorned the sky.
Inexpressibly inexpressible clouds of various precious musical instruments played sublime Dharma sounds, chanting praises of the Tathāgata.

Inexpressible clouds of jewel trees completely covered the void, and inexpressible clouds of various precious thrones were draped with jeweled robes; Bodhisattvas sat upon them, extolling the virtues of the Buddha.

It was adorned with clouds of unspeakably many celestial jewel images; it was adorned with clouds of unspeakably many nets of pure white pearls; it was adorned with clouds of unspeakably many pavilions of liberation; and it was adorned by clouds and rains of unspeakably many musical performances of sublime liberation.
Why is this? Because the roots of goodness of the Tathāgata are inconceivable;
because the pure and white dharmas of the Tathāgata are inconceivable.
Because the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata is inconceivable;
because the single body of the Tathāgata pervades all dharma-realms with sovereign mastery, which is inconceivable;
and because the adornments of all buddha-fields enter into the body of a single Buddha, which is inconceivable.
Because within a single atom all Buddhas appear, for the sake of the inconceivability of the entire dharma-realm;
because within a single pore all Tathāgatas appear in succession throughout the limits of the past, for the sake of its inconceivability;
and because a single ray of light is emitted to illuminate all lands, for the sake of its inconceivability.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, clouds of transformation bodies as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-fields emerge, filling all worlds, because this is inconceivable;
from a single pore of the Tathāgata, the formation and destruction of all Buddha-fields are manifested, because this is inconceivable.
In this same way, just as the Jetavana Anāthapiṇḍada-ārāma is seen as a purified Buddha-field, so too are all dharma-realms, the realm of empty space, and all worlds seen as purified.

The Tathāgatas arrived in a full assembly at the Jeta Grove; the Bodhisattvas filled the ocean-like great assemblies of all Tathāgatas and dwelt in peace, universally raining down clouds of all manner of exquisite adornments;
raining down clouds of light from all kinds of jewels that universally illumined clouds of all *maṇi* kings;
raining down clouds of all canopies and clouds that adorned the bodies of all devas.
They rained down clouds of all kinds of flowering trees and clouds of all manner of variegated robes for adornment;
they rained down clouds of all kinds of garlands and clouds of flowing, adorned *maṇi* jewel-kings for adornment;
they rained down clouds of various fragrances for the bodies of all sentient beings.

Clouds of precious flower-rain and clouds of celestial maidens each held exquisite jewels that revolved in the void, adorning all manner of treasures; lotus flowers and various jewel lion-thrones adorned the sky.

At that time, to the east, beyond as many oceans of worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, there was a world named Adorned by the Pure Lamp of Vajra-Cloud Radiance; its Buddha was named King of Pure and Wondrous Virtue.
Within that great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Light of Pure Vows, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, came toward this land.
They raised various clouds to adorn the void;
that is to say:

they raised clouds of celestial flowers, scattered clouds of celestial powdered incense, hung down clouds of celestial garlands and ribbons, rained down clouds of celestial jewels, clouds of celestial ornaments, clouds of celestial jewel-canopies, clouds of celestial jewel-robes, and clouds of celestial banners and canopies. Filling the void with delightful adornments of myriad treasures, they approached the place where the Buddha was, prostrating and making offerings.
Immediately, in the eastern direction, he manifested a pavilion adorned with every ornament and a lion throne within a treasury of precious lotuses;
with his body covered by a net of wish-fulfilling jewels, he sat cross-legged together with his retinue.
To the south, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, there is a world named Vajragarbha; the Buddha there is named Samantāvabhāsa-guṇarāja.
Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named Akṣayavīryavegarāja, who, together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, has come toward this land.
All of them carried every kind of exquisite incense, which, sustained by their supernatural power, universally perfumed all the oceans of Buddha-worlds;

they held up nets of all kinds of mani-jewels, flower garlands, necklaces, precious robes, jeweled images, and various ornaments of wondrous virtue and light, adorned with all manner of exquisite lion-jewels;
sustained by their supernatural power, these filled all the Buddha-worlds as they came to the presence of the Buddha to pay homage and make offerings.
Immediately to the south, he manifested a white, pure, and wondrous jeweled pavilion, which universally illuminated the lion thrones of the Jewel Lotus Treasury throughout the ten directions;
thereupon, he sat cross-legged, his body covered by a net of precious flowers.
To the west, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, there is a world named Jewel Lamp Sumeru Banner; the Buddha there is named Dharma Realm Wisdom Lamp.

Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named Supreme Universal Sublime Virtue King, who, together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, has come toward this land.
He manifested clouds of Mount Sumerus made of various colors and fragrances, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, filling the entire Dharma-realm;
clouds of Mount Sumerus made of various colored scented waters, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, filling the entire Dharma-realm;
and clouds of Mount Sumerus made of various colored mani-jewel kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-lands, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
Clouds of Sumeru mountains of jewel banners adorned with light rays of various colors, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, filled the entire Dharma-realm;
clouds of Sumeru mountains of *vajra-garbha* mani-jewel kings of various colors, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, filled the entire Dharma-realm;
clouds of Sumeru mountains of Jāmbūnada-jewel banners, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, filled the entire Dharma-realm.
Clouds of Sumeru mountains of mani-jewel kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, which universally illumine all dharma-realms, cover all Tathāgatas throughout space;

clouds of Sumeru mountains of mark-and-sign mani-jewel kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, which shine everywhere, fill the spheres of experience of all sentient beings;
and clouds of Sumeru mountains of practices performed by all Tathāgatas when they were bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, fill the entire dharma-realm.

All the Tathāgatas manifested adornments for their sites of enlightenment equal in number to the atoms within unspeakable Buddha-fields; they came to the place where the Buddha was, prostrating and making offerings.

Then, in the western direction, they conjured forth celestial pavilions made of all kinds of kingly fragrances, covered above with nets of genuine jewels, and sat cross-legged upon lion thrones of precious lotus-treasury like the banners of Śakra;
golden jewel-nets covered their bodies.

With the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels as the bright pearl in his topknot, he came from the northern direction, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields. There is a world named Jewel-Raiment Radiant Banner, where the Buddha is named Wondrous Virtue of the Dharma-Domain and Space;

from within that great assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Unobstructed Treasury of Wondrous Virtue, who, together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, came toward this land.
With clouds of silken banners made of all kinds of jewels adorning the void, sustained by their supernatural power, they filled the sky;

with clouds of variegated jewel garments, clouds of garments perfumed with various incenses, clouds of sun-banner maṇi-jewel garments, clouds of exquisite golden garments, clouds of garments with nets of various jewels, clouds of garments adorned with Jāmbūnada gold, clouds of pure white jewel garments, clouds of garments of brilliant and pure jewel-kings, clouds of garments of exquisite light-jewels, and clouds of jewel-kings adorned like the ocean—they adorned the void;
sustained by their supernatural power, they completely filled all of space and came to the place where the Buddha was, prostrating and making offerings.
Immediately, in the northern direction, he manifested a pavilion made of the great ocean’s mani-jewel kings, and sat cross-legged upon a lion throne within a treasury of lapis lazuli lotuses;
his body was draped with a net of exquisite jewel-kings,
and a pure jewel-king served as the bright pearl at the center of his topknot.
To the northeast, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is a world named Radiant Net of Joy Free from Defilement; its Buddha is named Unobstructed Eye.

Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named King of the Moon of Wishes for Skillful Transformation in the Dharma-realm, who, together with a multitude of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, has come toward this land.
Clouds of jewel pavilions arose, completely filling all worlds;

clouds of incense pavilions, clouds of incense smoke pavilions, clouds of flower pavilions, clouds of sandalwood pavilions, clouds of diamond pavilions, clouds of maṇi-jewel pavilions, clouds of gold pavilions, clouds of precious robe pavilions, and clouds of padma-lotus pavilions—all of these universally covered all buddha-fields, coming to the place of the Buddha to pay homage and make offerings.

Immediately, in the northeast, he manifested a jeweled mountain pavilion that was a gateway to all dharma realms, and sat cross-legged upon a lion throne within a treasury of precious lotuses of unspeakable fragrance-kings;
his body was draped with nets of mani flowers,
and he wore as a celestial crown a mani-jewel king of the treasury of wondrous adornments.
To the southeast, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, there is a world named Fragrant Cloud Adorned Banner; the Buddha there is named Dragon Sovereign King.
Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named Dharma-Meaning Wisdom Flame King, who, together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of that world, has come toward this land.
They manifested immeasurable clouds of perfect golden light, which universally covered the void; immeasurable clouds of perfect light in the colors of jewels;

clouds of perfect light from the Tathāgata’s *ūrṇā-kośa*; clouds of perfect light in various colors of diverse jewels; clouds of perfect light from the treasury of jewel lotuses; clouds of perfect light from the flowers of jewel trees; clouds of perfect light from the Tathāgata’s invisible crown-mark (*uṣṇīṣa*); clouds of perfect light in the color of Jāmbūnada gold; clouds of perfect light like the sun; and clouds of perfect light like the moon. These universally covered the void as they approached the Buddha’s dwelling to pay homage and make offerings.
Immediately, in the southeast direction, he manifested a pavilion made of luminous and pure mani-jewel kings and a lion throne within a treasury of vajra-jewel lotuses;
there he sat in the full lotus posture, his body covered by a net of jewel-flame light.

To the southwest, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is a world named Light Treasury; the Buddha there is named King of Wisdom Universally Illuminating the Dharma Moon.

Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named King of the Wisdom Banner that Scatters All Māras, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a world-system, comes toward this land.
From each and every pore, clouds of jewel-flame blossoms as vast as the realm of empty space arose, universally illuminating all worlds;

they emitted clouds of fragrant flames, clouds of various jewel flames, clouds of vajra flames, clouds of fragrant smoke flames, clouds of great dragon-sovereign lightning-light flames, clouds of brilliant mani-jewel flames, clouds of golden jewel flames, and clouds of exquisite virtue-treasury mani-jewel king-net flames.

From each and every pore, oceans of Tathāgata light-clouds as vast as the realm of empty space were emitted, universally illuminating the three periods of time, as they came to the presence of the Buddha to prostrate and make offerings.

Thereupon, in the southwestern direction, he manifested a jeweled pavilion made of mani-gems, its lattice of light from gates in all directions universally illuminating the dharma-realm; upon a lion throne within a lotus treasury of fragrant lamps and blazing jewels, he sat cross-legged;

his body was covered by a wondrous net of light from the king of mani-jewel treasuries, and he wore a crown of the sovereign mani-jewels that emits the sound of the liberation-seeking voices of all sentient beings.

To the northwest, beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields, there is a world named Pure Vow Maṇi Jewel Treasury; its Buddha is named Universal Radiance Pure Wondrous Virtue Sumeru King.
Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named Bright Pure Vow Wisdom Banner King, who, together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in a world-system, has come toward this land.

In every moment of thought, from all the primary and secondary marks and from every pore, clouds of bodies of all Buddhas of the three periods of time emerge, filling the entirety of the realm of empty space.

Furthermore, there issued forth clouds of the bodies of all bodhisattvas; clouds of the bodies of the retinues of all Tathāgatas; clouds of the emanation-bodies of all Tathāgatas; clouds of the birth-bodies of all Tathāgatas; clouds of the bodies of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; clouds of the bodhi-trees at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; clouds of the sovereign powers of all Tathāgatas; clouds of the bodies of all world-kings; and clouds of all adorned and purified Buddha-fields. In every thought-moment, from all their marks and signs of excellence and from every pore, such clouds as these issued forth, filling the void and approaching the presence of the Buddha to pay homage and make offerings.

Then, in the northwest, he manifested a pavilion of exquisite mani-jewels, pure in all directions; upon a lion throne of mani-jewel lotus-treasury that purifies all sentient beings, he sat cross-legged;
his body was draped with a net of firm, radiant, true jewels, and he wore a mani-jewel crown that universally covered his head.

Below, past worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is a world named Perfectly Pure Radiance of All Tathāgatas; the Buddha there is named Sovereign Banner of Unobstructed Space-Wisdom.

Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named Sovereign Power of Wisdom that Shatters and Dispels All Obstructions, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a world-system, has come toward this land.

From every pore, there issued forth clouds of sounds from the ocean of the voices of all sentient beings; clouds of sounds from the ocean of the practices of Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time; clouds of the sounds of the vows of all Bodhisattvas; clouds of the sounds of the fulfillment of the pure *pāramitās* of all Bodhisattvas; clouds of the wondrous sounds of the practices of all Bodhisattvas; clouds of the sounds of the sovereign accumulation of all Bodhisattvas that fill all worlds; clouds of the sounds of the sovereignty of all Bodhisattvas proceeding to the site of enlightenment, subduing the hosts of Māras, and attaining supreme perfect awakening; clouds of the sounds of the *sūtras* of the true wheel of Dharma turned by all Buddhas; clouds of the sounds of skillful means for converting and delivering sentient beings according to their needs; and clouds of the sounds of skillful means that enable all sentient beings to attain wondrous wisdom and roots of goodness at the appropriate times. These came to the presence of the Buddha to pay homage and make offerings.
Immediately below, he manifested various Buddha-palaces adorned with the treasury of jewel-light and lion-thrones within lotus-treasury jewels;
there he sat cross-legged, with a crown-jewel of the sovereign mani-gem that universally illumines the site of enlightenment.

Above, passing through worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, there is a world named Expounding the Inexhaustible Awakening; the Buddha there is named Perfect Universal Wisdom Light-Sound.

Within that great assembly, there is a bodhisattva named King of the Penetrating Wisdom that Discerns the Dharma Realm, who, together with bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, came toward the place where Śākyamuni Buddha was in the Sahā world.

From within all the marks and signs of excellence, all the pores, all the limbs and joints, all the members of the body, all the ornaments, and all the garments, there emerge Vairocana and all the Buddhas of the past, all those of the future who have already received their prediction, and those who have not yet received it, as well as all the Buddhas of the present in all worlds throughout the ten directions along with their clouds of retinues—all of whom are fully manifested.
The practice of the perfection of giving (dāna-pāramitā) in the past, as well as those who received the gifts, all appear clearly;
the cultivation of the perfection of ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā) in the past, wherein his observance of the precepts was pure;
and the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā) in the past, wherein his mind remained undisturbed even when his limbs were severed.
In the past, they cultivated the perfection of vigor;
in the past, they cultivated the ocean of the perfection of meditation of all Tathāgatas;
in the past, they cultivated the turning of the pure wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas.
In the past, he completely relinquished all things and was unattached to the life-span;
in the past, he joyfully sought the path of all bodhisattvas;
in the past, he gave birth to the pure and great vows of adornment of a bodhisattva.
They were fully endowed with all the powers of the bodhisattvas of the past and all the perfected wisdoms of the bodhisattvas of the past.
Emitting clouds of such sovereign powers that filled the entire dharma-realm and manifested everywhere, they came to the place where the Buddha was, prostrating and making offerings.
Immediately above, he manifested a pavilion adorned with vajras and a lion throne within a treasury of blue-vajra-jewel lotuses, whereupon he sat in the full lotus posture;
his body was draped with nets of every kind of jewel,
and the name-mantras of the Buddhas of the three periods of time were the mani-jewel kings that formed the bright pearls of his topknot.
These bodhisattvas and their retinues are all fully endowed with the practices and vows of Samantabhadra;
they have accomplished the pure eye of wisdom of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
and they turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas.
They embrace the ocean of sūtras of the supreme and wondrous voices of all Buddhas;
they are fully endowed with the ultimate perfection of all bodhisattva masteries.

In every thought-moment, they go before all Tathāgatas and manifest their power of mastery, filling all worlds with a single body, and able to manifest pure bodies within the assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
Within a single atom, they are able to manifest all worlds, maturing sentient beings according to their needs for transformation without ever missing the proper time.

From a single pore, they emit the thunderous sound of the sublime Dharma of all Buddhas; they know that the realms of sentient beings are entirely like illusions, that all Buddhas are like flashes of lightning, that all states of existence are like dreams, that all karmic retributions are like reflections in a mirror, that all births are like mirages, and that all worlds are like magical transformations.
They fully accomplish the ten powers and the dharmas of fearlessness of the Tathāgatas.
Within the great assembly, they can roar the lion’s roar, deeply entering the inexhaustible ocean of all eloquence;
they definitively understand and know the ocean of the languages and dharmas of all sentient beings;
they practice unimpeded conduct within the pure dharma-realm, knowing that all phenomena are entirely without contention.
Endowed with the wondrous wisdom of the various supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, they diligently cultivate vigor to subdue all māras;
they dwell securely in the supreme and wondrous wisdom of the three periods of time, remaining free from all attachment;
through their pure and wondrous conduct, they attain the stage of all-knowledge adorned by the Buddhas.
Knowing that all that exists is entirely non-existent;
deeply entering the ocean of wisdom of all dharma-realms; entering all worlds with indestructible wisdom;
and manifesting sovereign presence throughout all worlds.
They manifest birth in all worlds;
they know the various forms and colors of all worlds, manifesting vast Buddha-fields through subtle realms,
and manifesting subtle realms through vast Buddha-fields.

In a single thought-moment, they abide in the dwelling of all Buddhas, attain the wisdom-body sustained by all Buddhas, and obtain pure intelligence, thereby comprehending the ocean of all lands in the ten directions;
in a single thought-moment, they are able to manifest infinite masteries, pervading the oceans of all worlds throughout the ten directions.
All these bodhisattvas have fully accomplished such immeasurable merits; that the entire Jeta Grove is filled with them is due to the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.

At that time, the great śrāvakas—Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Revata, Subhūti, Aniruddha, Nanda, Kambala, Kātyāyana, and Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra—along with all such great śrāvakas, while staying in the Jeta Grove, could not perceive at all the Tathāgata’s sovereignty, the Tathāgata’s adornments, the Tathāgata’s realm, the Tathāgata’s transformations, the Tathāgata’s lion’s roar, the Tathāgata’s wondrous merits, the Tathāgata’s sovereign conduct, the Tathāgata’s power, the Tathāgata’s sustaining power, or the pure buddha-field; none of these things did they see.

Furthermore, he did not see the inconceivable great assembly of bodhisattvas, nor the sovereign transformations within the bodhisattvas' realms; nor the lion thrones adorned with exquisite jewels that appeared in every direction from which the bodhisattva retinues had come; nor the bodhisattvas' palaces and their mastery of samādhi as they observed all things; nor the bodhisattvas' vigorous exertion and diligent practice as they made offerings to the Buddhas; nor the bodhisattvas' receiving of predictions and the nurturing of their roots of goodness; nor the bodhisattvas' assumption of bodies—the pure dharma-body, wisdom-body, vow-body, and form-body—with their marks and signs, immeasurable radiance, and perfect adornments; nor the emission of great nets of light and clouds of transformation-bodies; nor the bodhisattvas filling the entire network of all directions; nor the bodhisattvas' various practices being fully perfected.
Such matters as these were entirely unseen by all the śrāvakas and great disciples.
Why is this? Because they have cultivated various distinct roots of goodness;
they did not originally cultivate the roots of goodness that enable one to see the sovereign power of the Tathāgata, nor did they cultivate the purification of Buddha-fields.
Furthermore, they do not praise the merits obtained through the Buddha’s sovereign power;
they do not teach and transform sentient beings within birth and death to cause them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
nor do they establish sentient beings in the Buddha’s bodhi, nor do they protect the lineage of the Tathāgatas so that it remains unbroken.
They do not gather in all sentient beings, nor do they accomplish the various *pāramitās*;
they do not praise the ground of the supreme, wondrous eye of wisdom for the sake of sentient beings, nor do they cultivate the practices of omniscience;
they do not seek the world-transcending roots of goodness of the Buddhas, nor do they bring forth pure lands of mastery, nor do they seek them.

The Bodhisattva’s various supernormal powers and the eye of clear vision do not cultivate the Bodhisattva’s realm, nor do they destroy roots of goodness, yet they do not give rise to the Buddha-powers.

They abide in and uphold the great vows of a Bodhisattva; furthermore, they do not perceive all phenomena as being like illusions, nor do they perceive the assemblies of Bodhisattvas as being entirely like dreams, nor do they practice the noble state of the Bodhisattva’s transcendence of birth.
In their minds as they practice, they do not attain the pure eye of wisdom of Samantabhadra.
These merits are not shared with śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas;

for this reason, the great disciples do not see them, do not hear them, do not enter them, do not know them, do not awaken to them, do not contemplate them, cannot universally observe them, and do not even give rise to thoughts of them.

Why is this? This is the sphere of wisdom of the bodhisattvas, not the sphere of wisdom of the śrāvakas. Therefore, while the great disciples were in the Jeta Grove, they did not perceive the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual power;

nor did they possess the pure eye of wisdom of samādhi that perceives phenomena in their subtlest aspects. They lacked the sphere of the spiritual power of the dharma-gates, nor the supreme and wondrous merit of the [ten] powers, nor the knowledge of what is possible and impossible (sthānāsthāna-jñāna), nor the eye of wisdom capable of seeing, hearing, perceiving, knowing, or forming mental conceptions regarding it. They took no pleasure in speaking of it, could not praise it, could not manifest it, could not bestow it, and were unable to exhort and establish sentient beings within that sublime Dharma.
Why is this? Because those of the Śrāvaka vehicle have transcended the triple world.
Furthermore, because they fulfill the path of the śrāvaka and abide in the fruit of the śrāvaka, they are unable to fully realize the wisdom of non-existence.
Abiding in the ultimate truth, they constantly delight in tranquility; being far removed from great compassion, they always discipline themselves alone and abandon sentient beings.
Therefore, although they sit face-to-face with the Tathāgata, they are unable to perceive his sovereign spiritual transformations.

For example, it is like a hungry ghost who is naked, famished, and parched, with his entire body burning and tormented by tigers, wolves, and other venomous beasts; he goes to the Ganges River seeking water to drink, yet he sees it either dried up or as ashes and charcoal.
Why is this? It is entirely due to the obstructions of karmic offenses from past actions.
All śrāvakas are likewise the same.
Although they were at the Jetavana, they did not behold the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual powers. Why was this?
Because the obscuration of ignorance covered their pure eyes.

For example, suppose there is a person at a great assembly who, while fast asleep, dreams of various celestial cities and palaces of Śakra, with gardens, groves, and flowing streams adorned with all kinds of jewels;
strewn with various flowers and lined with jeweled trees, covered above with exquisite garments, where celestial men and women sport and play.

They enjoy themselves with natural, wondrous sounds and experience celestial bliss; the person beholds this for himself as he dwells securely there, seeing the celestial palaces adorned with immeasurable splendor, while the rest of the great assembly neither knows nor sees it.
Why is this? Because awakening and dreaming are different.
All Bodhisattvas who are kings of worlds are likewise; as in that dream, there is nothing they do not see.
Because they have deeply entered the sublime Dharma-gate of the bodhisattvas;
because they have accumulated roots of goodness and brought forth the vows for omniscience;
and because they have attained certain and clear understanding of the Buddha’s merits.
Because they are correctly directed toward the bodhisattva’s path of great vows;
because they fulfill all-knowledge;
and because they fulfill the various practices and vows of Samantabhadra.
Because they have attained the complete stages of all bodhisattvas;
because they have attained mastery over all bodhisattva samādhis;
and because they practice the unimpeded wisdom of all bodhisattvas.

Therefore, all the great Bodhisattvas behold the Tathāgata’s inconceivable realm of spiritual transformations; they penetrate deeply with clear understanding to the ultimate other shore, something that none of the Śrāvaka great disciples can know.
For example, on the Snowy Mountains there are various medicinal herbs that a wise and skilled physician can distinguish and know completely;
yet though hunters, herdsmen, and others may dwell upon those mountains, none of them can know them at all.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: fully endowed with all-knowledge, he gives rise to all the sovereign powers of a Bodhisattva and clearly understands the miraculous transformations of the Tathāgata’s spiritual feet;
yet although the great assembly of Śrāvaka disciples reside within the Jeta Grove, none of them perceive or know of these things.
Why is this? Because they constantly seek their own peace and do not extensively save others.

It is like various treasures hidden within the earth that only those with incantations can discern and identify; having recorded these treasuries, they use them to provide for themselves, support their parents, relieve their kinsmen, and rescue the poor and destitute.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise thus: with the eye of pure wisdom, they enter the inconceivable realm of the Buddha’s sovereign spiritual power; they universally enter the great ocean of immeasurable skillful means and the oceans of all samādhis; they reverently make offerings to all Buddhas, protect the true Dharma, and gather in sentient beings through the four methods of attraction.
Although these great śrāvakas reside in the Jeta Grove, they do not behold the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual transformations;
they are like blind people who, having reached a great island of jewels, walk, stand, sit, and lie down there, yet do not see the various treasures.

These śrāvakas are just the same: though situated in the Jeta Grove, that great island of the Dharma-treasure, and personally attending upon the World-Honored One, they do not behold the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual transformations nor the assembly of bodhisattvas.
Why is this? Because they have not attained the pure eye of a bodhisattva, they are unable to realize the dharma-realm in its successive stages.

It is like a person who uses a clear and bright medicinal ointment to treat their eyes; in the darkness of night, while standing amidst a great multitude, they can see everyone in the crowd walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, yet other people do not see them.

The Tathāgata is likewise; having attained the unimpeded, pure eye of wisdom, he is able to know and see all worlds, manifesting immeasurable sovereign spiritual transformations along with the assembly of bodhisattvas.
The great śrāvakas did not behold the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual transformations, nor the assembly of bodhisattvas.
It was like a bhikṣu in a great assembly who enters the meditative concentration of "pervading all places"—

namely, earth, water, fire, wind, devas, sentient beings, and objective realms— such that the rest of the great multitude could not see the earth, water, fire, wind, or even the objective realms of all those various places.
The manifestations of the Tathāgata are inconceivable; all Bodhisattvas see them, whereas the great Śrāvakas neither know nor see them.

It is, for example, like a person who applies a medicine that obscures the body to his own eyes: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, no one else can see him, yet only that person himself can perceive everything.
The Tathāgata is likewise: forever transcending the world, he cannot be seen by anyone; he is the domain of the omniscient Bodhisattvas alone, and is not something that the Śrāvakas can know.

From birth, a person is constantly attended and guarded by two kinds of devas: the first is called "co-natal" (sahaja), and the second is called "same-name" (samānanāman). These devas always see the person, but the person does not see the devas.
The supernatural transformations of the Tathāgata are likewise thus: they cannot be known or seen by any śrāvakas, but only bodhisattvas are able to behold them.

It is like a bhikṣu who, in the midst of a great assembly, enters the meditative absorption of cessation (nirodhasamāpatti); he does not abandon his sense faculties, nor has he entered final nirvāṇa, yet he neither knows nor sees the affairs of the great assembly.
Why is this? It is because of the power of the concentration of cessation (*nirodha-samādhi*).

All the great śrāvakas were likewise; though they were present within the great assembly in the Jeta Grove with their sense faculties fully manifest, they did not behold the Tathāgata’s supernatural transformations. They did not enter into them, did not know them, did not perceive them, did not attend to them, and no mental activity regarding them arose.
Why is this? The realm of the Tathāgata is profoundly deep and vast; it is difficult to know, difficult to see, and its ultimate source is difficult to fathom, being without limit or measure.
It is far removed from the world, inconceivable, and indestructible; it is not the realm of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Radiance of Pure Vows, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Behold the steadfast one! Awakening is inconceivable;
It manifests within the Jeta Grove As infinite, sovereign dharmas.”
Sustained by the Tathāgata’s spiritual power, he manifests immeasurable virtues;
yet the world is entirely deluded, not knowing the teachings of the Buddhas.
The Dharma of the Dharma King is profoundly deep, immeasurable, and inconceivable.
Manifesting great transformations, they cannot be fathomed by any;
The adorned marks of the Tathāgata are beyond exhaustive praise.
Because phenomena are without marks, all Buddhas are proclaimed and revealed.
The Most Victorious One, within the Jeta Grove, manifested his sovereign power;
it is profoundly deep and inconceivable, transcending the path of language.
Observing his immeasurable virtues, a multitude of bodhisattvas gathered like clouds.
Coming from inconceivable lands, they make offerings to the Most Victorious One;
having fulfilled all great vows, they constantly cultivate unimpeded conduct,
such that no one in any world can know their minds.
All the pratyekabuddhas and the immeasurable great śrāvakas are entirely unable to know the sphere of the bodhisattva’s practice.
The great wisdom of the bodhisattva cannot be destroyed by anything at all.
Far removed from all discursive thoughts, he has reached the ultimate ground of profound wisdom.
This person of supreme renown enters deeply into immeasurable concentrations;
manifesting his sovereign power, he fills the entire realm of phenomena.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of Indestructible Vigorous Power, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Behold the true sons of the Buddha, Treasures of merit and wisdom,
Who have perfected the bodhisattva path And bring peace and security to all worlds.”
Immeasurable wisdom clearly discerns; the mind of meditative concentration is unmoving.
Wisdom is exceedingly deep and vast; its sphere cannot be fathomed.
In the secluded and tranquil Jetavana Grove, there is immeasurable and wondrous adornment.
Bodhisattvas fill [the space], all dwelling in reliance upon perfect awakening.
An ocean-like assembly of immeasurable beings, entirely free from attachment,
has gathered here from the ten directions, seated upon lion thrones of flowers.
Eliminating all delusions, they remain entirely unstained;
with a stainless and unimpeded mind, they reach the ultimate limit of the dharma-realm.
They raise the banner of wisdom, as immovable as a vajra.
All phenomena are without transformation, yet they manifest infinite transformations.
To all worlds throughout the ten directions, across immeasurable billions of Buddha-fields,
they are able to go everywhere, yet without dividing their bodies.
Beholding the Lion of the Śākyas, Of infinite power and mastery,
By the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, The great assemblies from the ten directions have gathered.
The Sons of the Buddha have fully perfected All paths of speech and expression.
The Buddha-dharma is indestructible, abiding securely in the ground of the Dharma-realm.
The nature of phenomena is indestructible; the profound Dharma of the Muni—its phrases and its meanings—is analyzed without end.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Unsurpassed Universal Wondrous Virtue King, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“Behold the steadfast person, Whose wisdom is vast and perfect;
Well-knowing the timely and the untimely, He expounds the Dharma for the sake of the multitudes.”
Distant from all non-Buddhist paths, he subdues all disputants;
according to those who are to be transformed, he manifests his sovereign power.
Perfect Awakening is neither a finite dharma nor an infinite dharma.
The Muni has completely transcended all phenomena, whether finite or infinite.
Just as the bright, pure sun dispels all darkness,
so too is the wisdom of the Guide, universally illuminating the dharmas of the three periods of time.
Just as on the fifteenth day, the full moon is perfectly bright and pure,
so too is the Most Victorious One, perfected in the pure and white dharmas.
Just as in the midst of space, the sun shines with radiant light, so too is the Buddha.
Universally illuminating all things, the Buddha’s sovereignty is likewise so.
Just as the nature of space is entirely without obstruction,
the Lamp of the World is similarly sovereign and unobstructed.
Just as the nature of the great earth is able to support all living beings,
so too is the Wheel of Dharma, the Lamp of the World, able to support them.
Just as the nature of a great wind blows swiftly without obstruction, [so too is the power of this teaching].
The Buddha-dharma is likewise, swiftly pervading all worlds.
Just as the great wheel of water is that upon which the world rests,
so too is the wheel of wisdom the support for the Buddhas of the three times.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Unobstructed Treasury of Wondrous Virtue, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Just as a great mountain of jewels Benefits all living beings,
So too does the mountain of the Tathāgata’s merit Benefit them in the same way."
Just as the waters of the great ocean are cool and translucent,
so too is the Tathāgata, able to remove the feverish thirst of craving.
Just as Mount Sumeru stands firm and towering within the great ocean, [so does the Tathāgata stand amidst the world].
The mountain of the Tathāgata is likewise, abiding securely within the deep ocean of the Dharma.
Just as all manner of jewels can emerge from the great ocean, so too is the untaught wisdom:
that which is difficult to awaken to is awakened to without difficulty.
The Guide’s profound wisdom is immeasurable and beyond counting;
he manifests sovereign powers that no one can conceive.
Just as a skilled illusionist displays all manner of phenomena, so does he appear.
The Buddha’s wisdom is likewise, manifesting all powers of mastery.
Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel can satisfy every desire,
so too does the Most Victorious One completely fulfill all pure vows.
Just as a bright and pure jewel can illuminate everything,
so too is the wisdom of the Guide, universally illuminating all phenomena.
Just as a jewel that follows its direction appears wherever it is situated in the various quarters, so too does the wisdom of the Buddha manifest throughout all directions.
The Lamp of Non-obstruction is likewise: all phenomena appear within it.
Just as a water-purifying jewel clarifies turbid waters, so too is seeing the Buddha: all faculties become completely pure.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King Moon of Vows for the Skillful Transformation of the Dharma Realm, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Just as a blue jewel can turn all colors blue, so too,
those who behold the Buddha all become one with Bodhi."
Within each and every atom, the Most Victorious One manifests sovereign power;
he is able to purify all the infinite and boundless bodhisattvas.
They attain the most profound Dharma and various forms of sublime adornment.
This is the realm of the Bodhisattvas alone, which no one in the world can fathom.
Endowed with all adornments, the Tathāgata’s pure and wondrous conduct brings the Bodhisattva path to fruition and leads to a profound penetration of all dharma realms.
The inconceivable lands manifested by the Perfectly Awakened One are entirely filled with present Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The Lion of the Śākyas has accomplished the immeasurable dharmas of mastery.
He manifests great supernormal transformations, immeasurable and boundless.
The various practices of the bodhisattvas are likewise immeasurable and boundless;
through the Tathāgata’s power of mastery, they are all fully revealed.
The Buddha’s heirs, having skillfully practiced and studied, Penetrate the profound realms of all phenomena;
Having accomplished unimpeded wisdom, They clearly understand all dharmas.
Through the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual power, They turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of the multitudes.
Born with supreme merit, he causes the entire world to be completely purified.
The Tathāgata’s pure realm is profound and perfect wisdom;
the Great Nāga King of True Wisdom delivers all sentient beings across.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dharmārthajñānārcirāja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
“The Most Victorious One of the three times— Even all the śrāvaka disciples Are utterly unable to know The manner in which the Tathāgata lifts his foot.”
All the Pratyekabuddhas of the past, future,
and present are likewise unable to know the act of the Tathāgata lifting his foot;
how much less so can ordinary worldlings, who are bound and fettered by the afflictions?
How could one whose pure eyes are shrouded by the darkness of folly know the Teacher?
Possessing supreme and immeasurable virtues and endowed with all wisdom, he transcends the path of language; none are able to know him.
Just as the bright and pure moon, whose radiance is beyond comprehension, so too is the Guide; his merits are inconceivable.
Through a single skillful means, the Tathāgata gives rise to immeasurable emanations.
Though one were to calculate for incalculable eons, one could not know even a small fraction [of it].
A single skillful means of the Tathāgata gives birth to immeasurable virtues;
none at all can fully know the True Dharma of the All-Knowing One.
If there are those who seek enlightenment and cultivate the bodhisattva practices,
this is their sphere, which they are able to discern and know.
Through inconceivable skillful means, they cross over the ocean of birth and death.
If one extinguishes the mind of "I" and "mine," Then one is able to reach the ultimate.
With a pure and immeasurable mind, All great vows are fully accomplished;
One attains the Bodhi of the Buddhas, The most supreme state.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Forty-four and Volume Forty-five.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Part Two of the Thirty-fourth Chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Wisdom Banner King Who Scatters All Maras, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The body of great wisdom is unimpeded; It is no-body, inconceivable.
The Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body cannot be fathomed by anyone;
through inconceivable karmic deeds, he has given rise to this pure body,
adorned with immeasurable wonders, untainted by the three realms.
Universally illuminating all things, purifying all dharma realms,
opening the gateways to bodhi, and giving birth to profound samādhi and wisdom;
forever free from all defilements, eliminating and extinguishing all obstacles.
The bright and pure sun of the world universally radiates the light of wisdom.
Forever severing the stream of birth and death, it causes all three realms to be purified;
Fully endowed with the virtues of a bodhisattva, one achieves the enlightenment of a Buddha.
Manifesting immeasurable forms, yet remaining unstained by them;
all those various forms that appear cannot be conceived by thought.
With supreme wisdom, the King of Men, within every moment of thought, can [manifest them].
Possessing immeasurable bodhi, which none can know;
Endowed with inexhaustible wisdom, which none can destroy;
Within a single thought-moment, they clearly penetrate the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Discerning all karma, one contemplates awakening with right mindfulness;
yet in this contemplation there is no contemplation, for the nature of contemplated phenomena is quiescent.
It is profoundly deep and inexpressible, transcending the path of language.
"The Tathāgata arises from this; the Buddha’s deeds are inconceivable.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Banner of Wisdom and Vows of Radiant Purity, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"With pure mindfulness free from delusion, He hears and upholds all dharmas."
With profound wisdom they can discern the inexhaustible ocean of all Buddhas;
with a resolute mind, these Bodhisattvas cultivate the Bodhisattva practices,
giving birth to most profound knowledge and eliminating all doubts.
Their minds are free from weariness, having distanced themselves from indolence;
always diligently cultivating vigor, they bring all Buddha-dharmas to ultimate completion.
Endowed with faith and wisdom, they abide securely and immovably.
Always delighting in profound wisdom, They observe all things without attachment.
Throughout immeasurable and boundless eons, They have accumulated all manner of merit;
With single-minded devotion, they constantly dedicate it To the profound Dharma of all Buddhas.
Though dwelling within birth and death, their minds are free from defilement and attachment;
they abide securely in all Buddha-dharmas and always delight in the conduct of the Tathāgatas.
Regarding all that exists in the world—the aggregates, the elements, and all such phenomena—
Fearlessness completely eliminates [all obstacles], as they dwell securely in the Buddha’s true Dharma.
Amidst the world’s inverted delusions and the constant turning of the wheel of birth and death,
they cultivate unimpeded conduct and truly benefit sentient beings.
The conduct of the Bodhisattva is difficult to praise; none are able to know it fully.
It extinguishes all suffering and brings peace and happiness to all living beings.
Having awakened well to the wisdom of Bodhi, it shines universally upon all worlds.
"Eliminating the darkness of ignorance, he delivers all beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Power of Wisdom Who Shatters and Dispels All Obstructions, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, the Buddha’s voice is difficult to hear."
How much more so for those who personally behold him, Who eliminates all doubts and delusions.
The Tathāgata, the lamp of the world, Who has perfected all dharmas,
Is the unsurpassed and supreme field of merit, Causing all beings to become utterly pure.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body Is beyond the reach of thought by all;
Even after contemplating it with earnest focus for immeasurable eons, The mind never reaches satiety.
O Son of the Buddha, observe well: The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body.
Eliminating all hindrances, one ultimately achieves bodhi.
The Tathāgata’s wondrous form-body produces pure and subtle sounds and unimpeded eloquence, widely opening the gateway to bodhi.
Universally illuminating all multitudes, Immeasurable and inconceivable,
He establishes the wisdom of the Mahāyāna And bestows upon them the prediction of Bodhi.
On the day his merit is perfected, He appears in the world to illuminate it.
Nurturing all worlds, his body is composed of immeasurable merit.
Should anyone encounter such a Tathāgata, they will leave behind all evil realms,
extinguish all suffering, and become fully endowed with the body of wisdom.
If there are those who behold the Tathāgata, they can give rise to the immeasurable mind,
nurture countless wisdoms, and encounter all the Teachers.
If there are those who behold the Tathāgata, they shall attain the samādhi of the bodhicitta.
"One can know with certain resolve: 'I shall surely attain Bodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva King of the Supernatural Power of Discerning the Dharma-Domain, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
"The Bodhisattva beholds the Tathāgata’s Immeasurable and pure merits."
All are perfectly dedicated toward the ultimate attainment of omniscience.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, the Tathāgata appears in the world;
endowed with great compassion, he turns the wheel of Dharma for the sake of the world.
No one at all can repay the Great Sage’s universal kindness and grace,
for throughout inconceivable eons he has endured suffering on behalf of all beings.
Throughout immeasurable billions of eons, he has undergone the torments of the various hells.
Never abandoning any being, they cause all to behold the Buddha;
universally able to take upon themselves on behalf of sentient beings all immeasurable sufferings,
their minds never wearying, for the sake of delivering all.
Throughout all the worlds, wherever there is suffering in the evil realms,
the Tathāgata constantly dwells therein, causing all beings to hear the True Dharma.
He remains in each and every hell for inconceivable eons.
Undergoing immeasurable suffering, they never depart from the Buddhas.
Thus, throughout immeasurable kalpas, they constantly remain in the three evil realms,
desiring to nurture and develop the wisdom of all living beings.
When sentient beings behold the Tathāgata, All their sufferings and afflictions are extinguished;
They are established in great wisdom, The realm of all Buddhas.
If there are those who see the Buddha, All their obstacles are eliminated.
Nurturing the treasury of merit, they ultimately achieve Bodhi.
The Tathāgata is able to eliminate all doubts and delusions of the world;
according to those who should be transformed, he fulfills their great vows in their entirety.
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva surveyed the entire assembly, wishing to further expound, manifest, and illuminate [the teaching];
by means of expedient means equal to the Dharma-realm, he extensively explained the Lion’s Vigorous Stride Samādhi (Siṃhavikrīḍita-samādhi).

He extensively explained the Lion’s Vigorous Stride Samādhi for the sake of all bodhisattvas through ten aspects: [equality with] the Dharma-realm; equality with the realm of space; equality with the three periods of time; equality with the realm of all sentient beings; equality with all kalpas; equality with the nature of all karma; equality with the aspirations of sentient beings; equality with the desires of sentient beings; equality with the light of the Dharma; and equality with the timely instruction and transformation [of beings], as well as equality with the faculties of all sentient beings.
"What are these ten? They are as follows:
extensively expounding how, throughout the entire dharma-realm, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands arise in succession in the world and proclaim the True Dharma;..."
Extensively explaining that throughout all Buddha-fields, equal in extent to the realm of space, all Buddhas will speak for as long as all future kalpas;
extensively explaining that throughout all Buddha-fields, all Tathāgatas manifestly attain perfect enlightenment;

and extensively explaining that throughout all Buddha-fields, equal in extent to the realm of space, Buddhas sit at the site of enlightenment surrounded by their retinues, with great assemblies of bodhisattvas all approaching them.
It is explained extensively that within a single thought-moment, all Buddhas of the three periods of time manifest transformation bodies that fill the entire Dharma-realm;
it is explained extensively that a single body fills all oceans of worlds and all oceans of Buddha-lands, equally illuminating and sustaining them;
and it is explained extensively that within each and every state, there are manifested the stages of the sovereign merits of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

It extensively describes how, within each and every atom, there appear the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas throughout the three periods of time, as numerous as the atoms of all Buddha-lands;

it extensively describes how, from each and every pore, there issue forth the sounds of the ocean of great vows of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, awakening and guiding all Bodhisattvas throughout all future kalpas;

and it extensively describes how they occupy lion thrones equal to the Dharma-realm, surrounded by great assemblies, adorning the sites of enlightenment, and turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma in their respective places without interruption throughout all future kalpas.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Lion’s Rush Samādhi has such extensive expositions as these, numbering as many as the atoms within unspeakably many Buddha-fields; it is solely the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, wishing to further elucidate the Lion’s Exertion Samādhi, relied upon the Buddha’s spiritual power to contemplate the Tathāgata;
he contemplated the great assembly;
and he contemplated the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgata.
Contemplating the samādhis of all Buddhas;
contemplating inconceivable worlds; contemplating inconceivable wisdom.
They contemplate all phenomena as being entirely like illusions;
they contemplate the inconceivable equality of all Buddhas;
and they contemplate the infinite and boundless paths of all sounds and languages.
He spoke in verse:
Within each and every pore, The most supreme ocean is universally manifested;
The Buddha sits upon the Tathāgata’s seat, Surrounded by a multitude of Bodhisattvas.
Within each and every pore, there are oceans of immeasurable Buddhas;
seated upon flower thrones at sites of enlightenment, they turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma.
Within each and every pore, there are as many lands as there are atoms.
In the supreme full-lotus posture, he expounds the conduct of Samantabhadra.
Seated upon a single world-system, he fills the realms of the ten directions;
infinite clouds of bodhisattvas come to the presence of the Buddha.
In immeasurable billions of Buddha-fields, Bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms have gathered;
surrounding the Tathāgata, they listen as he expounds the various dharma-realms.
He manifests all Buddha-fields and enters the ocean of wisdom of the dharma-realm.
Abiding securely in the conduct of Samantabhadra, fulfilling the practices of all Buddhas;
Abiding securely in the state of the Tathāgata throughout all worlds,
Deeply entering the bodhisattva practices, one delights in hearing the clouds of the sublime Dharma.
In each and every buddha-field, infinite and immeasurable, they cultivate all practices for billions of eons;
having cultivated those practices, they reach the ultimate depths of the ocean of profound Dharma,
fulfilling the ocean of great vows and dwelling securely in the stage of the Tathāgata.
Born into the most supreme Dharma, Endowed with the practices of Samantabhadra,
Accomplishing an ocean of merit, Attaining immeasurable mastery,
The cloud-like bodies of the Tathāgatas Envelop all Buddha-fields.
"Universally raining down the Dharma of ambrosia, Causing all beings to abide in the Buddha-way.

At that time, wishing to cause all bodhisattvas to dwell securely in the Lion’s Vigorous Stride Samādhi (*siṃhavikrīḍita-samādhi*), the World-Honored One emitted from between his eyebrows a ray of light called "The Door of Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm of the Three Times.
This light was accompanied by a retinue of rays equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many worlds, universally illuminating all oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions.

At that time, the great assembly of bodhisattvas gathered like clouds throughout the Jeta Grove all beheld all Buddha-fields within the entire dharma-realm and space-realm—various in color, various in purity, various in their foundations, and various in form;
likewise, they saw all the great bodhisattvas in such worlds sitting upon the site of enlightenment, surrounded by bodhisattvas and honored by devas, as they attained perfect awakening.

In some instances, he saw [the Buddha] amidst retinues as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, emitting wondrous sounds that filled the dharma-realm and turning the pure wheel of Dharma;
or he saw him in celestial palaces, in the palaces of nāgas, and in the palaces of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, as well as humans and non-humans;

or he saw him in human villages, towns, and royal capitals, manifesting various bodies, various names, various complexions, various halos, various nets of light, various eloquences, various retinues, various upholds, various teachings upheld, and various voices, thereby preaching the Dharma for them.
Just as here the Tathāgata manifests the miraculous transformations of profound samādhi for the sake of all bodhisattvas,

so too in all world-oceans throughout the ten directions— in the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of space— he manifests bodies of lands and bodies of sentient beings arising from various karmas;
even within a single pore, he manifests everything in this same manner.
Without destroying the three periods of time, and without destroying sentient beings;
universally illuminating the minds of all sentient beings with a pure form-body according to those who are to be transformed;
appearing before all classes of sentient beings to reveal and teach the wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas.
He tames sentient beings, manifesting the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata.
Any sentient beings who see, hear, recollect, or know the sovereign supernatural powers of the Tathāgata have all been his virtuous spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) in past lives;

they have all cultivated the roots of goodness of the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), single-mindedly seeking unsurpassed enlightenment, gathering all roots of goodness, accomplishing skillful means, and attaining the inconceivable sovereign samādhi of the Tathāgata, which is equal to the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
Some attain the Dharma-body;
some attain the form-body;
some attain the Bodhisattva’s fulfillment of all practices.
Some attain the purification of the various pāramitās;
some attain the bodhisattva’s perfect pure conduct;
and some attain the various stages (bhūmis) of the bodhisattvas.
Some attain mastery over bodhi;
some attain the indestructible samādhi of the Tathāgata;
and some attain the Tathāgata’s power of knowledge regarding all modes of conduct.
Or they may attain the unimpeded eloquence of a Tathāgata.
These bodhisattvas attain such marvelous merits as these—ten times the number of atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields—namely:

various paths, various gates, various entries, various crossings, various skillful means, various arrivals, various directions, various radiances, various merits, various endowments of merit, and various masteries.
They deeply enter the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis, namely:
the bodhisattva samādhi of universally adorning the dharma realm;
the samādhi of universally illuminating the three periods of time without obstruction; and so forth.
The samādhi of unimpeded wisdom regarding the dharma-realm;
the samādhi of entering deeply into the realm of the Tathāgata according to the occasion;
and the samādhi of universally illuminating space.
The samādhi of practicing the powers of the Tathāgata;
the samādhi of the lion’s majestic stride adorned with the fearlessnesses of the Tathāgata;
and the samādhi of the treasury of skillful means for the entire dharma-realm.
The Samādhi of the Pure Moon of the Unobstructed Dharma-realm;
the Samādhi of the Dharma-Cloud Adorned with Purity;
and the Samādhi of the Dharma-King’s Banner that Eliminates the Obstructions of Ignorance.
Within each and every realm, there is the Samādhi of Perceiving the Ocean of All Buddhas;
the Samādhi of the Banner of Wisdom of Pure Radiance from the Indestructible Body of All Worlds;
and the Samādhi of Profoundly Entering the Indestructible Buddha-Body.
The samādhi of conforming to all world-treasuries;
the samādhi of all phenomena being traceless and without dependence;
and the samādhi of the perfect illumination of universal quiescence.
The samādhi of non-existence, skillful transformation, universal transformation, and pervasive illumination;
the samādhi that sustains and upholds all buddha-fields;
and the samādhi that adorns all buddha-fields and manifests the attainment of enlightenment.
The samādhi of practicing all royal laws;
the samādhi of unimpeded practice within the spheres of all sentient beings;
and the samādhi of giving birth to all Buddhas.
The samādhi of ultimately perfecting the ocean of all Buddha-virtues;
the samādhi of producing, in every single state of realization, virtues that extend to the end of the future;
and the samādhi of understanding the ocean of all Tathāgatas' past lives.
The samādhi of sustaining the lineage of all Tathāgatas throughout the limits of the future;
the samādhi that purifies all oceans of Buddha-fields in the ten directions of the present;
and the samādhi that universally illumines the abodes of all Buddhas within a single thought-moment.
The samādhi of penetrating all realms while remaining far removed from obstacles;
the samādhi of causing all lands to enter into a single Buddha-land;
and the samādhi of manifesting all the transformation bodies of Buddhas.
The Samādhi of Entering the Ocean of All Faculties as the Vajra King of Decisive Wisdom;
the Samādhi of Abiding in the Single Body-Treasury that Sustains the Bodies of All Buddhas Without Differentiation;
and the Samādhi of Inexhaustible Skillful Means that Abides in the Dharma-realm of All Buddhas within a Single Thought-moment.
The samādhi of manifesting nirvāṇa within all dharma-realms and buddha-fields;
the samādhi of abiding in the unsurpassed stage;
and the samādhi that causes all sentient beings in all worlds to see his body as being without distinction.
The samādhi of the manifestation of the wisdom of all Buddhas before one;
the samādhi of knowing the true mark of all dharmas;
and the samādhi of possessing the discerning knowledge of the three periods of time within a single thought-moment.
In a single thought-moment, [he attains] the samādhi of knowing the treasury of all dharma-realms;
the samādhi of following and knowing the lion-like conduct of the Tathāgata’s wisdom;
and the samādhi of the perfection of the eye of wisdom regarding all objective spheres.
The samādhi of the sphere of the ten powers and so forth;
the samādhi that manifests with the eye of equality regarding all spheres;
and the samādhi that produces all exquisite forms, which sentient beings never tire of beholding.
The Samādhi of the Immovable Treasury;
the Samādhi of One Dharma Encompassing All Dharmas;
and the Samādhi of Universally Proclaiming All Sounds with a Single Utterance.
The samādhi of the non-dual dharma of all Buddhas;
the samādhi of detachment from the three periods of time;
and the samādhi of indestructible wisdom that discerns all kalpas.
The samādhi of subtle skillful means within the ten powers;
the samādhi of the uninterrupted production of bodhisattva practices throughout all eons;
and the samādhi of the universal manifestation of clouds in all ten directions.
The samādhi of sovereign bodhi and unimpeded dharma-realm;
the samādhi of discerning all awakenings, correct aspirations, and the banner of peace and security;
the samādhi of all adornments that adorn empty space.
In every thought-moment, they give rise to the Samādhi of Emanating Clouds;
the Tathāgata Moonlight Samādhi, which is free from defilement like space;
and the Samādhi of Sustaining All Buddhas Like Space.
The Samādhi of the Radiance of Dharma Adorned with All Dharmas;
the Samādhi of Opening the Lamp of the Meaning of All Dharmas;
the Samādhi of the Perfect Light of the Ten Powers; and so forth.
The samādhi of the banner of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
the samādhi of the single treasury of all Buddhas being identical;
and the samādhi of initiating the ultimate fulfillment of all tasks in every thought-moment.
The samādhi of the inexhaustible treasury of merit;
the samādhi that manifests the infinite and boundless realms of all buddhas;
and the samādhi of abiding in all dharmas upon the vajra lion throne.
The samādhi of manifesting the births and transformations of all Tathāgatas, wherein there is nothing not known or seen;
the samādhi of recollecting all Tathāgatas as the sun;
and the samādhi of awakening to the three periods of time in a single day.
The samādhi of natural quiescent liberation;
the samādhi of beholding all Buddhas;
and the samādhi of the definitive wisdom of the entire dharma-realm, adorned with padma flowers.
The Samādhi of Non-attachment to All Dharmas and the Pure Eye of Space;
the Samādhi of Gathering the Oceans of the Ten Directions into One Direction;
and the Samādhi of Profoundly Entering the Bottomless Dharma-realm.
The Samādhi of the Ocean of All Dharmas;
the Samādhi of the Tranquil Body Emitting All Radiance;
and the Samādhi of the Vow to Produce All Supernormal Powers and Clarities in a Single Thought-moment.
The samādhi of attaining enlightenment at all times and in all places;
the samādhi of entering the entire dharma-realm into a single adornment;
the samādhi of the sustaining power of all Buddhas;
The Samādhi of the Wisdom-Light of the Supreme Ground of All Sentient Beings;
the Samādhi of a Single Body Filling the Dharma Realm in a Single Thought-Moment;
and the Samādhi of Manifesting the Pure Dharma Realm within a Single Body.
The Samādhi of Manifesting Great Adornments by Universally Entering the Dharma Realm;
the Samādhi of Abiding in the Wisdom-Wheel that Perfects All Buddha-Dharmas;
and the Samādhi of the Adornment of the Single Expedient Means of All Dharmas.
The Indra’s Net Samādhi that gathers in the realms of sentient beings; the Samādhi of Abiding in All Vows and Diligence;
the Samādhi of Discerning the Cycles of All Worlds;
and the Samādhi of Sovereign Wonderfulness of the Lotus.
The samādhi of discerning the bodies of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of manifesting before the bodies of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of discerning the ocean of all sounds; and—
The samādhi of knowing the stages of all sentient beings;
the samādhi of the indestructible treasury of great compassion;
and the samādhi of all Buddhas entering the limit of the Tathāgata.
The samādhi of cultivating all gates of the Buddha-dharma;
the samādhi of observing the lion’s boundless prowess of the Bodhisattva.

Through such inconceivable gates of samādhi, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, they enter the ocean of the Tathāgatas and enter the samādhi of the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas.
In every moment of thought, they fill the Dharma-realm.

Each of those bodhisattvas possesses a sublime lion throne equal in extent to ten Buddha-worlds; they manifest great sovereign and profound wisdom, having attained the clear and pure wisdom of all stages (*bhūmi*).
Universally observing all things as arising from the nature of wisdom, they single-mindedly seek omniscience, fully accomplishing it with the eye of wisdom that is free from delusion.
They act as guides and teachers for all sentient beings;

they practice the impartial, true Dharma of all Buddhas, decisively and fully understanding all realms, discerning and knowing all worlds, delighting in the dharma of cessation, remaining detached from the world, and always preferring solitude and stillness;
they travel through all Buddha-fields without any defilement or attachment.
Regarding all phenomena, the mind has no point of dependence;
dwelling securely within the majestic palace of the sublime Dharma, they teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they manifest Buddha-fields, fully accomplishing the gateway to unsurpassed wisdom.
Following the limit of detachment from desire, they attain the body of wisdom and dry up the ocean of all conditioned phenomena;
for the sake of all sentient beings, they manifest the true reality-limit, and with the light of wisdom from the ocean of Dharma fully perfected, they all dwell securely in steadfast samādhi.
With a heart of great compassion, they constantly keep sentient beings in mind;
they understand that all sentient beings are entirely like dreams;
and they perceive all Tathāgatas as being like flashes of lightning.
All sounds and voices are entirely like echoes;
all phenomena are fully understood to be like magical transformations.

They fulfill all vows, perfect the bodhisattva practices, achieve universal wisdom, and possess pure skillful means. Their minds delight in tranquility, and they bring to completion the realm of wisdom of all dhāraṇīs.
Endowed with the ten powers, they are far removed from fear and dwell securely in the realm of reality (*dharmadhātu*),

possessing the pure eye of Dharma; having attained the gate of the non-existence of all phenomena, they practice the great ocean of immeasurable wisdom, reaching the ultimate further shore of wisdom, fully acquiring the power of the *prajñāpāramitā*, accomplishing the *abhijñāpāramitā* to ferry across the ocean of sentient beings,
and attaining complete mastery over the *samādhipāramitā*.
They thoroughly know all-knowledge without error; through skillful means, they reveal the treasury of the Dharma;
they are endowed with eloquence and have accomplished great vows;
they possess all powers, and their clouds of Dharma are inexhaustible.
Within the great assembly, he can roar the lion’s roar without fear;
he constantly seeks the true Dharma with a mind free from attachment.
With the eye of pure wisdom, he extinguishes the darkness of ignorance.
The moon of wisdom is full, illuminating the arising and ceasing of the world; it perfects wisdom and radiates great light;
it illumines all truths through skillful means.
The Vajra Mountain of Wisdom and Merit transcends all Dharma-kings of the three periods of time; he awakens to the banner of wisdom and merit that is free from fear;
he extinguishes the banners of all Māras and establishes the banner of perfect wisdom through diligence;
he is fully endowed with the accomplishment of the unsurpassed body and attains unimpeded wisdom regarding all phenomena.
Having fully awakened to the true limit of inexhaustible wisdom, they dwell securely in that true limit and practice the samādhi of definitive signlessness.

Through skillful means, they give rise to all bodhisattva practices and possess non-dual wisdom. They clearly perceive the realms and various destinies of the world, universally illuminating the buddha-fields without any attachment;

they eliminate the darkness of ignorance regarding all phenomena, bring ultimate wisdom to complete perfection, and radiate the pure light of the Dharma to illuminate the worlds of the ten directions.
For the sake of all sentient beings, he acts as an unfailing field of merit;
those who see or hear him shall have their aspirations fulfilled.
He is the Sumeru of merit for all the world, far removed from fear, and subdues all heterodox teachers.
With subtle and wondrous voices, they pervade all lands;

constantly beholding all Buddhas, their minds never grow weary or satisfied; they accomplish the Tathāgata’s sovereign Dharma-body and transform and deliver beings according to what is appropriate for them;
they are able, with a single body, to fill all lands.

By means of slight expedient means, they fully possess pure and sovereign spiritual powers, traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions without obstruction; their wisdom is perfected, universally illuminating the entire dharma realm.
Acting as a brilliant, pure sun illuminating all beings, he praises their virtues according to what is appropriate for them;
