he fully understands the faculties and aspirations of all sentient beings;
and regarding all phenomena, he has attained the realm of non-contention.
They discern and understand the intrinsic nature of all phenomena and how they encompass one another in their various scales.
They definitively realize the profound stage of the Tathāgata, expounding the phrases and the body of flavors—the profound meanings of all phenomena—without end;
within a single word, they universally proclaim the ocean of all sūtras and exhaustively master all dhāraṇīs.
They expand the body of wisdom, attaining the ultimate *dhāraṇī* of immeasurable eons.
Within a single thought-moment, they definitively and thoroughly know unspeakable numbers of eons;
within a single thought-moment, they penetrate the *dhāraṇī* of the phenomena of the three periods of time, universally illuminating the ocean of the teachings of immeasurable Buddhas.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they give rise to pure wisdom and turn the wheel of the true Dharma, which none can destroy;
they achieve the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, constantly enter the samādhi of "well-manifested" (sudarśana), remain far removed from obstacles, and penetrate deeply into all phenomena.
Regarding all phenomena, they attain sovereign mastery over supreme wisdom, purifying and adorning all spheres of experience;
they penetrate deeply into the profound dharma-realm of the ten directions and encompass the entirety of the dharma-realm throughout the ten directions.
Within each and every atom, he manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment;
within the nature of formlessness, he manifests all forms;
and with a single direction, he encompasses all directions.
Those bodhisattvas were fully endowed with such immeasurable treasuries of merit and wisdom that they were constantly praised by all the Buddhas;
even if one were to describe their merits through the bodies of words and phrases, one could never reach the end, and they had all gathered together in the Jeta Grove.
At that time, those bodhisattvas entered deeply into the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits.

Having entered, by the power of joy in the Dharma and by the power of the inconceivable, within the bodies of the bodhisattvas, within the pavilions, within the ornaments, and within the lion thrones;
In every thought-moment, they each emit immeasurable clouds of light that universally illumine the Dharma-realm and awaken sentient beings.
These include:
clouds of light of all precious incenses, which praise the merits of the Buddhas of the three periods of time with subtle and wondrous sounds that fill the ten directions;

They emit clouds of all sentient beings, with the radiance of their spheres of experience, proclaiming the pure karmic retributions of all sentient beings; their subtle and wondrous voices fill the ten directions.
They emit clouds of light adorned by the vows and practices of all bodhisattvas, proclaiming the merits of the vows and practices of all bodhisattvas.
They emit clouds of the transformation bodies of all buddhas, with the subtle and wondrous voices of all Tathāgatas, filling the ten directions.

They emit clouds of the bodies of all bodhisattvas, adorned with the primary and secondary marks, who throughout all buddha-fields praise all buddhas with subtle and wondrous voices, filling the ten directions;

they emit clouds of the adorned sites of enlightenment of the buddhas of the three periods of time, manifesting the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment by all buddhas, filling the ten directions;
within all realms, they emit clouds of dragon kings, raining down all kinds of incense, filling the ten directions.
They emit clouds of the bodies of all Buddhas, extolling the conduct of Samantabhadra and filling the ten directions;
they emit clouds of pure light from all Buddha-fields and the sounds of all Tathāgatas turning the wheel of Dharma, filling the ten directions.
At that time, by the spiritual power of the bodhisattvas and by the power of this Dharma, there emerged clouds such as these, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.

Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and, wishing to praise the immeasurable adornments within the Jeta Grove, spoke in verse:
"Observing within the Jeta Grove, The sovereign power of the Tathāgata..."
From all realms emerge clouds of immeasurable merit;
With infinite pure and wondrous forms, Adorned in manifold ways,
they shine forth universally Throughout the Buddha-lands of the ten directions.
From the pores of the Buddha-sons’ bodies, clouds of the Buddha’s voice emerge, adorned with various jewels, filling the lands of the ten directions.
Their bodies are like those of Brahmā kings; their majestic deportment is ever serene and still.
Traveling throughout the lands of the ten directions, they produce wondrous sounds.
From the pores of the Tathāgata emerge inconceivable bodies,
all like Samantabhadra, adorned with myriad sublime marks.
The Bodhisattvas have universally accomplished oceans of merit throughout the three periods of time;
filling the void of space, they produce clouds of adornment.
Within this Jeta Grove, they emit wondrous sounds.
Universally proclaiming to all assemblies the pure karmic retribution of deeds;
within each and every realm, he manifests oceans of Buddha-fields and the immeasurable powers of mastery of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
Within the pores of the Tathāgata, all worlds—
Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms— are all distinctly manifested.
From within every realm, clouds of Buddhas emerge.
With immeasurable skillful means, they deliver all sentient beings.
Clouds of flowers, clouds of fragrant flames, pure maṇi jewels,
and clouds of various adornments fill the ten directions.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time, Adorning their wondrous places of enlightenment,
Are all fully manifested here in this Jeta Grove,
Along with Samantabhadra and other sons of the Buddha, With infinite varieties of adornment.
"Throughout kalpas as numerous as all sentient beings, the lands they have cultivated and purified—
all such worlds as these are now manifested within this Jeta Grove.

At that time, because they were illuminated by the Tathāgata’s samādhi, each and every one of those bodhisattvas attained incalculable dharma-gates of great compassion, equal in number to the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields, whereby they benefited and brought peace and happiness to sentient beings, gathering them into the fold.
From each and every pore of those bodhisattvas, there issued forth as many rays of light as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
from the tip of each ray of light, there emerged as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
Their bodies are honored and most preeminent among all worlds;
they manifest everywhere according to what is appropriate, filling the entire Dharma-realm;
they teach and transform sentient beings, delivering those not yet delivered and liberating those not yet liberated.
He manifested celestial palaces as numerous as the atoms within unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, displaying the signs of impermanence and death;
he taught that all phenomena are entirely like dreams, praised the site of enlightenment, and expounded upon the gateways of the great vows of all Bodhisattvas.
In some cases, they manifest birth in all worlds to extensively demonstrate for all sentient beings the gateway of the *dāna-pāramitā*;
in others, they manifest the fulfillment of the merit of pure precepts of all Buddhas, the gateway of the *śīla-pāramitā*;
and in others, they manifest the severing of all limbs and members, the gateway of the *kṣānti-pāramitā*.
In some instances, they manifest the gateway of the *vīrya-pāramitā* by diligently cultivating vigor;
in others, they manifest the gateway of the continuous liberation through all bodhisattva meditative concentrations and samādhis.

The Tathāgata’s light of perfect wisdom seeks exclusively all Buddha-dharmas; for the sake of the meaning of each and every word-body (*pada-kāya*) and phoneme-body (*vyañjana-kāya*), he is able to relinquish immeasurable and incalculable bodies.

He approaches the abodes of all Buddhas to inquire about immeasurable dharma-gates, skillfully knowing the proper time and assembly, and manifests the Dharma according to what is appropriate for them.
They cause all sentient beings to abide in omniscience, attain the ocean-gate of the light of skillful means wisdom, and be able to make offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
they subdue all Māras, restrain all non-Buddhists, and are able to manifest the gate of Bodhisattva power;

they know the ground of pure and clear wisdom regarding all arts and crafts, and desiring to cause sentient beings to obtain the supreme and wondrous Dharma, they are fully able to understand the faculties of sentient beings, their afflictions and habitual tendencies, their various karmic retributions, and the ground of wisdom.
By means of such dharma-gates as these, numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakable Buddha-fields, they teach and transform sentient beings:

sometimes manifesting celestial palaces, sometimes manifesting dragon palaces, or the palaces of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth; sometimes manifesting Brahma palaces, sometimes human palaces, sometimes the palace of King Yama, or the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals. Their great compassion, wisdom, and various great vows are indestructible;

they gather in sentient beings without abandoning skillful means—whether by teaching through their name, or by teaching through mindfulness, or by teaching through their voice, or by teaching through perfect radiance.

Or they may teach and transform through networks of light, appearing before each being according to their needs; manifesting various adornments everywhere, yet never departing from the presence of the Buddha, nor leaving their own pavilion seat, while appearing universally throughout the ten directions.
Some emit clouds of transformation bodies;
some manifest non-dual bodies, traveling throughout the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings;
and some manifest the physical forms of śrāvakas.
Sometimes they manifest the physical form and color of Brahmā;
sometimes they manifest the physical form and color of those who practice all manner of asceticism;
and sometimes they manifest the physical form and color of a skilled physician.
Sometimes they manifest in the form of merchants;
sometimes they manifest in the form of those who live by right livelihood;
and sometimes they manifest in the form of courtesans.
Sometimes they manifest the forms and images of celestial beings;
sometimes they manifest the forms and images of all crafts and skills;
and sometimes they manifest the forms and images of all cities, villages, and capitals.
According to what is appropriate, they go to those places.
They may manifest various physical forms and voices to teach and transform sentient beings;
or they may manifest various languages and dharmas, various modes of deportment, various bodhisattva practices, various skillful arts, and the illumination of all-knowledge.

Acting as a lamp for the world, they universally illumine the adornments of the karmic retributions of sentient beings; distinguishing all directions, they fully practice all the bodhisattva deeds and manifest in all cities, villages, and capitals to transform and deliver sentient beings.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī emerged from the Pavilion of Excellent Abiding, accompanied by all his fellow bodhisattvas;
the Vajrapāṇi spirits constantly followed him, attending and protecting him.
The Heaven of the Fulfillment of Original Vows;
the Heaven of the Ground Delighting in Hearing the Dharma;
and the Heaven of the Quadrangle of the Spring-Pool of Constant Practice in Great Compassion.
The Night Goddess who Eliminates Ignorance;
the Day Goddess who Gives Birth to the Buddhas;
and the River Goddess of Space who Adorns the Realm of the True Dharma.
The devas who ferry sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death;
the devas who nurture all roots of goodness on the mountain of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge);
the devas who adorn the bodies of all sentient beings, fulfill all vows, and make offerings to the bodies of all Buddhas; and the devas who protect the cities of all sentient beings.
The Yakṣa King who protects all sentient beings;
the Gandharva King who causes all sentient beings to rejoice;
and the Kumbhāṇḍa King who eliminates all realms of hungry ghosts.
A king of garuḍas who rescues sentient beings from the ocean of birth and death;
a king of asuras who correctly seeks omniscience (*sarvajñā*);
and a king of mahoragas who, upon seeing the Buddha, rejoices without ever being satiated.
The various heavenly kings who are ever weary of birth and death,
and the Brahmā heavenly kings and others who constantly pay reverent homage to the Buddha,
all went together to the place where the Buddha was. Having bowed their heads at his feet in prostration and made various offerings, they took their leave to travel toward the south.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, saw the youth Mañjuśrī—adorned with the ornaments of a bodhisattva—departing from the Jeta Grove and traveling toward the south.
Having seen him, he thought to himself:
"I shall now go together with the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, surrounded by a retinue of six thousand bhikṣus, emerged from his own cell and approached the Buddha. He prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, took his leave, and set out toward Mañjuśrī.
These six thousand bhikṣus are the fellow-disciples of Śāriputra; they have all recently left the household life. Their names are:

the bhikṣu Sāgarajñāna, the bhikṣu Mahāsusaṃvigna, the bhikṣu Guṇaprabha, the bhikṣu Mahākumāra, the bhikṣu Vidyutprabhotpāda, the bhikṣu Viśuddhacaryā, the bhikṣu Divyasumati, the bhikṣu Indrajñāna, the bhikṣu Brahmā, and the bhikṣu Śāntamati.
These six thousand bhikṣus, and others like them, have already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past.

Having planted various roots of goodness under all Buddhas, they delight by nature in purity; their faith is clear and penetrating, and they practice great vows. They contemplate the realm of the Buddhas, comprehend the true reality of dharmas, and benefit sentient beings; they always delight in single-mindedly seeking the merits of all Buddhas.
These bhikṣus are all those who have been transformed and delivered by Mañjuśrī.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra surveyed the great assembly and addressed the bhikṣu Samudramati:

"You should observe the pure body of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, which no devas or humans can conceive. His radiance is perfect and complete, causing immeasurable sentient beings to give rise to hearts of joy. He emits a great net of magnificent and wondrous light, extinguishing the immeasurable sufferings and afflictions of sentient beings."
He observes their retinue, seeing how they have accomplished roots of goodness;
he observes their gait, seeing how their deportment is composed and dignified, and how the ground where they travel becomes naturally level and even, unimpeded throughout the ten directions;
he observes the paths upon which their merit travels, seeing that along both sides there are various wonderful treasuries of jewels that spontaneously emerge.
He observed that as offerings were made to the Buddhas of the past, the fruits of those roots of goodness emerged from the various forest trees as treasuries of adornments;
he observed all those great celestial kings paying respectful homage and raining down clouds of offerings.

Sāgarajñāna! Observe how Mañjuśrī and all the Tathāgatas emit immeasurable light from the tuft of hair between their eyebrows as they proclaim the teachings of the Buddhas, and how it all enters through the crown of his head.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra praised Mañjuśrī to the bhikṣus, extolling his immeasurable merits and great adornments.
Having heard this praise, those bhikṣus were all filled with joy;
their minds became pure and free from all defilements, their bodies grew supple, their faculties were subdued,
and they were far removed from all hindrances.
They directly behold all Buddhas as they truly seek enlightenment; they attain the pure faculties of a Bodhisattva;
they possess the powers of a Bodhisattva, nurture great compassion, enter the various *pāramitās*, and give rise to vast vows, seeing the oceans of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions.
Then, the bhikṣus addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying: "Indeed,
O Great Teacher!"
"May we all go together to visit Mañjuśrī.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, together with the bhikṣus, went to where he was;
having arrived, he addressed Mañjuśrī:
"These bhikṣus have all newly gone forth and wish to see you, O Venerable One.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī immediately manifested the sovereign power of a bodhisattva, looking back at the bhikṣus as a king of elephants turns its head.
At that time, the bhikṣus prostrated with their heads at his feet, withdrew to stand to one side, and stood with palms joined, thinking thus:
"By the merit of this prostration, may we come to know the true reality of dharmas just as the Upādhyāya Śāriputra and the World-Honored One Śākyamuni do;
and may we attain a pure body, with the marks and signs, a melodious voice, and sovereign spiritual powers, just like Mañjuśrī."
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the bhikṣus:
"You should know, sons of good family and daughters of good family, if you accomplish ten kinds of great resolve, you will attain the stage of a Buddha, let alone the stage of a bodhisattva.
What are these ten?"
That is to say:
they give rise to the vast mind, nurturing all roots of goodness to ultimate non-retrogression, with no weariness or satiety;
they behold all Buddhas, reverently making offerings to them, with no weariness or satiety.
They seek all Buddha-dharmas with a mind that never knows satiety;
they practice all the pāramitās of a bodhisattva with a mind that never knows satiety;
they fulfill all bodhisattva samādhis with a mind that never knows satiety.
They have no weariness or satiety in the transmigration through all three periods of time;
they have no weariness or satiety in adorning and purifying Buddha-fields that fill the ten directions;
they have no weariness or satiety in teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity.
Throughout all lands and throughout all eons, they practice the conduct of a bodhisattva with a mind that never knows satiety;

they give rise to the vast mind and cultivate all the pāramitās, as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields, liberating all sentient beings and perfecting the ten powers of a buddha, their minds never knowing satiety.

If good sons or good daughters accomplish these ten kinds of great dharmas, they will be able to nurture all roots of goodness; they will leave behind the realms of birth and death and transcend the natures of all worldly states; they will surpass the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;

they will be born into the family of the Tathāgata, fully accomplish the great vows of bodhisattvas, practice the conduct of bodhisattvas, dwell in the stages of bodhisattvas, achieve the power of the Tathāgata’s merits, subdue all māras, and restrain all heterodox teachers.
Having heard this Dharma, those bhikṣus all attained the Samādhi of the Unobstructed Pure Eye;
they beheld all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions along with their retinues and immeasurable sentient beings;
they also saw the various forms and types of worlds, the palaces made of myriad jewels, and all atoms of dust.
They perceive everything within the range of the ten eyes of the Tathāgatas.
They hear and understand all the oceans of Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas through various bodies of phrases and syllables, diverse forms of eloquence, and subtle, wondrous sounds.
In that world, he fully understands the mental inclinations and faculties of all sentient beings;
he knows the births of those beings in various realms throughout the past and future;
and he is further able to know the events of ten eons each in both the past and the future.

They know that Tathāgata’s ten kinds of past lives, ten kinds of mastery in achieving enlightenment, ten kinds of turning the wheel of Dharma, ten kinds of spiritual powers, ten kinds of instructions, ten kinds of preaching the Dharma, and ten kinds of eloquence.
When attaining this samādhi, one fully accomplishes ten kinds of the bodhicitta of the ultimate reality;
ten thousand samādhis, ten thousand pure pāramitās, and the perfect radiance of great wisdom; and the ten clarities of a bodhisattva, abiding in the bodhicitta.
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva exhorted the bhikṣus to cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and abide in the practices of Samantabhadra.
Those bhikṣus gave rise to an ocean of great vows;
having given rise to this ocean of great vows, their bodies and minds became pure, and they attained the supernormal power of immortality.
Having attained this illumination, without leaving this place, one gives birth to the Dharma-body of all Tathāgatas, filling the ten directions and becoming fully endowed with all Buddha-dharmas.
At that time, after Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva had established those bhikṣus in the bodhicitta, he proceeded southward together with his retinue.
He proceeded to the eastern part of the city of Bodhimaṇḍa and stayed in the Śāla grove of the Adorned Banner, at the site of a great stūpa,
a place where the Buddhas of the past had dwelt and where, when those same Buddhas were bodhisattvas, they had practiced ascetic austerities.
This place is constantly honored by all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, humans, non-humans, and others.
At that time, Mañjuśrī immediately preached the Sūtra on Universally Illuminating the Entire Dharma Realm at this very spot; it had one hundred trillion sūtras as its retinue.
While he was preaching this Dharma, immeasurable thousands of billions of dragon kings, together with their retinues, came from the great ocean to visit Mañjuśrī.
Having heard this Dharma, they grew weary of and renounced the dragon realm, seeking rightly the path of the Buddha;
after casting off their dragon bodies, they were reborn among gods and humans;
and ten thousand dragon kings attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the people of the city of Vairambhya heard that Mañjuśrī was in the Śāla Grove of the Banner of Adornment, at the site of the great stūpa;
having heard this, the upāsakas, upāsikās, boys, and girls all went to visit Mañjuśrī.
At that time, there was an upāsaka named Mahāmati, who, together with a retinue of one thousand upāsakas—
namely, the upāsakas Sudatta, Vasudatta, Guṇaprabha, Yaśodeva, Śāntideva, Nandideva, Sumati, Mahāmati, Bhadra, and Bhadraguṇa— approached him.
With their heads bowed at his feet, they withdrew and sat to one side.
Furthermore, there were five hundred upāsikās, namely:

the upāsikā Mahāprajñāprabhā, the upāsikā Suprabhā, the upāsikā Sukāya, the upāsikā Rucitakāya, the upāsikā Bhadrā, the upāsikā Bhadraguṇā, the upāsikā Bhadraprabhā, the upāsikā Prabhāketudhvajā, the upāsikā Guṇaprabhā, and the upāsikā Sunetra.
Together with these five hundred upāsikās, they bowed their heads at his feet in salutation and withdrew to sit to one side.
Furthermore, there were five hundred youths, whose names were:

the youth Sudhana, the youth Sucarita, the youth Suśīla, the youth Susampannavṛtta, the youth Suvīrya, the youth Sucitta, the youth Sumati, the youth Sambodhi, the youth Sunetra, the youth Subāhu, and the youth Suprabhājaya;
together with these five hundred youths, they prostrated themselves at his feet and withdrew to sit to one side.
Furthermore, there were five hundred young maidens, whose names were:

the maiden Sudarśanā, the maiden Bhadrā, the maiden Priyamukhī, the maiden Dṛḍhamati, the maiden Guṇavatī, the maiden Jyeṣṭhakāyā, the maiden Brahmadattā, the maiden Guṇaprabhā, and the maiden Suprabhā.
Together with these five hundred maidens, they bowed their heads at his feet in prostration and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, Mañjuśrī, knowing that the great assembly had gathered in the city of Saṃjñā, employed the power of great loving-kindness according to their needs to bring them refreshing coolness;
manifesting great compassion, he was about to preach the Dharma for them;
and with profound wisdom, he discerned their minds and preached the Dharma through the power of great eloquence.
He observed Sudhana, considering by what causes and conditions he was named Sudhana:
when this youth first entered the womb, within his residence there were seven great treasuries;

from those treasuries emerged seven-jeweled pavilions, naturally complete in every detail—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, pearl, musaragalva, and agate—and from these seven jewels, seven kinds of sprouts grew forth.
At that time, this boy remained in the womb for ten months; upon his birth, he was handsome with all limbs complete.
His sprouts of the seven kinds of jewels were two fathoms high and seven fathoms wide.
Furthermore, within his home there were naturally present five hundred precious vessels filled with various treasures:
gold vessels containing silver;
silver vessels containing gold;
Vajra vessels were filled with various fragrances;
fragrant vessels were filled with precious garments;
and vessels of jade and stone were filled with food of the finest flavors.
Maṇi vessels were filled with various jewels;
diverse precious vessels were filled with ghee, oil, honey, and clarified butter, as well as articles for sustaining life.
Vessels of lapis lazuli were filled with many kinds of gems.
Crystal vessels were filled with conch shells;
conch shell vessels were filled with crystal;
agate vessels were filled with red pearls.
A vessel of red pearls contained agate;
a vessel of fire-pearls contained water-purifying pearls;
and a vessel of water-purifying pearls contained fire-pearls.
In this manner, five hundred precious vessels naturally formed in rows.
Furthermore, a rain of various jewels fell, filling all the treasuries.
Because of these events, among the Brahmins there was a master of physiognomy, well-versed in the arts, named Sudhana.
This youth has already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past, deeply planted roots of goodness, and always delighted in purity;
he has drawn near to spiritual friends, purifying his body, speech, and mind;
and he cultivates the bodhisattva path, seeking all-encompassing wisdom.
Cultivating all Buddha-dharmas, his mind is as pure as space, and he is fully endowed with the practices of a bodhisattva.
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva turned like an elephant king, surveyed Sudhana, and said to him:
"I shall now expound for you the subtle and wondrous Dharma."
He then analyzed for them the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
the Dharma of the successive appearance of all Buddhas in the world;
and the Dharma of purifying one's retinue.
The method for turning the Brahma-wheel;
the dharmas of the physical bodies of all Buddhas, adorned with the marks and signs of purity;
and the dharmas of the dharma-body possessed by all Buddhas.
The Dharma of the wondrous adornment of the voices of all Buddhas;
the teaching of the equal and true Dharma of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, Mañjuśrī knew that the entire assembly, including Sudhana and the others, having heard this teaching of the Dharma, were all filled with great joy and resolved their minds upon Bodhicitta.
Having manifested his past roots of goodness and not forsaking his original seat,
and having appropriately transformed and delivered the sentient beings of Vārāṇasī,

he traveled toward the south. At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from Mañjuśrī these various sublime merits of the Buddha, sought enlightenment with single-minded devotion and followed after Mañjuśrī, speaking in verse:
“The three realms of existence are its city walls; Arrogance is its garden ramparts;
The various destinies are its defensive towers; And craving is its deep moat.
Enveloped by the darkness of ignorance, The three poisons burn perpetually.”
With Māra as their sovereign, the ignorant dwell in dependence;
ensnared by craving, they ruin right conduct through deceit and crookedness.
Hindered by doubt, the eye of wisdom is obscured, and they wander through various false paths.
Bound by stinginess and envy, they head toward the perils of the hungry ghosts;
oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death, the ignorant revolve through the wheel of existence.
You possess perfect, unsurpassed compassion, the sun of pure wisdom.
Having exhausted the ocean of afflictions, may you deign to look upon us with a moment’s reflection.
Perfecting unsurpassed compassion, the light of wisdom brings peace to all beings;
shining upon everything without exception, O King of Moons, may you shine upon me.
Sovereign of the entire realm of phenomena, With the pure Dharma as your fourfold army, You constantly turn the wheel of the true Dharma; I pray that you transform me through the sublime Dharma.
Fully endowed with the vow for enlightenment, You have accumulated a treasury of merit.
Benefiting all beings, O Great Teacher, may you deliver me.
With the armor of patience adorning your body and wielding the sword of wisdom,
rescue me from the perilous and evil paths of Māra and free me from all calamities.
Abiding on the summit of the Sumeru of Dharma, served by celestial maidens of wondrous concentration, you subdue the asuras; Śakra observes me.
Possessing the power of complete freedom from defilement, you discern all that exists.
Lamp of clarity and purity for the world, I pray you show me the right path.
May I leave behind all evil realms And purify all auspicious destinies.
Open for me the gate of liberation To transcend all worldly hardships.
Attached to permanence, bliss, self, and purity, They are deluded within birth and death;
O you with the eye of pure wisdom, I pray you open the gate of liberation.
Far removed from all inversions, Fearless, you know the true path.
Thoroughly comprehending all right paths, you manifest my enlightenment.
Abiding on the ground of right view, the tree of the Buddhas' merits constantly rains down the flowers of perfect awakening; may you show me the way to enlightenment.
The sun that illuminates the world, the Tathāgatas of the three times,
coming and going according to the Dharma— may I behold them all.
May I discern all karma and deeply understand the nature of all phenomena.
The vehicle of decisive wisdom, you have shown me the Mahāyāna.
All wheels of aspiration are fulfilled; your great compassion is inexhaustible.
Adorned with pure and wondrous virtues, establish me in the vehicle of Bodhi.
Fully endowed with the pure dharma-realm, Observing with great compassion,
adorned with the flowers of merit, Grant me the foremost vehicle.
Dwelling securely upon the seat of brahma-conduct, Attended by the women of samādhi.
The music of the subtle and wondrous Dharma shows me the royal path of the Dharma.
The inexhaustible treasury of the four means of attraction, adorned with merit and wisdom,
its radiance illuminating all— I pray that you swiftly show me the supreme path.
With the perfect radiance of bestowed benefits, Your body anointed with the sandalwood of precepts,
And the great adornment of patience— I pray you, swiftly reveal the true path.
Deeply entering various meditative concentrations, You transform and guide all classes of sentient beings.
Possessing the vehicle of skillful means, establish me in the supreme Dharma-vehicle.
With the wheel of perfected vows, forever severing the wheel of birth and death,
and endowed with the power of sustaining wisdom, establish me in the wondrous Dharma-vehicle.
All things are entirely sublime; with great compassion, you observe all sentient beings.
Having perfected the most excellent and wondrous conduct, you establish me in the vehicle of true wisdom.
Abiding in adamantine insight, you have reached the ultimate of all-knowledge.
Eliminating all obstacles, establish me in the vehicle of the sages and saints.
Your compassion is exceedingly vast; bring peace and happiness to all living beings.
With eyes as pure as the Dharma-realm, establish me in the Unsurpassed Vehicle.
Extinguishing the aggregates of manifold suffering, The wheel of all karma and afflictions;
Subduing all Māras, You establish me in the vehicle of the True Dharma.
Your wisdom illuminates the ten directions, Adorning all realms of phenomena.
Fulfilling the vows of sentient beings, establish me in the supreme, wondrous vehicle.
With a mind as pure as space, eliminating false views and craving,
benefiting all multitudes, establish me in the supreme vehicle of the Dharma.
Abiding like a wind-wheel, universally supporting all lands,
causing all beings to dwell in the stage of concentration, establish me in the supreme vehicle.
Abiding like the great earth, fully endowed with the power of great compassion.
Wisdom benefits sentient beings, establishing me in the most supreme vehicle.
With the light of the four means of integration perfected, you bring benefit to all classes of living beings;
with the pure light of dhāraṇī, show me the bright and clear sun.
He has developed the pure eye of wisdom and is the sovereign of wondrous knowledge;
crowned with the unsurpassed crown, the Dharma King looks upon me with compassion. *The Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 45.

At that time, Mañjuśrī turned like an elephant king and gazed at the youth Sudhana, saying these words:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son! You are indeed able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi,
seeking spiritual friends and drawing near to spiritual friends."
Questioning on the conduct of a bodhisattva and seeking the path of a bodhisattva:
O son of good family!
This is the first treasury of a bodhisattva, which possesses all-knowledge; namely:
One should seek out spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), drawing near to them, honoring them,
and making offerings to them. Therefore, noble son,
you should seek out spiritual friends, draw near to them, honor them, and make offerings to them with a single mind, never becoming weary or satisfied.
Question on the Bodhisattva Practice:
How does one cultivate the bodhisattva path?
How does one fulfill the bodhisattva practice?
What is the pure bodhisattva practice?
What is the ultimate bodhisattva practice?
What is the generative bodhisattva practice?
What is right mindfulness of the bodhisattva path?
What is the path that takes the bodhisattva’s sphere as its object?

"How does a bodhisattva fulfill the conduct of Samantabhadra?
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the youth Sudhana in verse, saying:

Generating a vast and great heart of compassion, I single-mindedly seek the unsurpassed path.
First I have made the great vows To eliminate the suffering of sentient beings;
Having perfected the bodhisattva practices, I shall accomplish the unsurpassed path.
If there are bodhisattvas who do not weary of the suffering of birth and death,
and who fulfill the practices of Samantabhadra, none shall be able to destroy them.

Truly seeking the conduct of Samantabhadra to benefit all beings,
In the presence of the Buddhas throughout immeasurable and boundless worlds,
I hear the preaching of the Cloud of Pure Dharma, And receive and uphold it without ever forgetting.
Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, they universally behold immeasurable Buddhas;
having fulfilled the ocean of all vows, they are fully endowed with the practices of a bodhisattva.
Having perfected the ocean of skillful means, they dwell securely in the stage of the Tathāgata.
Following the teachings of all Buddhas, one attains omniscience.
Throughout all worlds, the Dharma King has practiced for accumulated eons;
having perfected the path of Samantabhadra, he has reached the ultimate awakening of a Buddha.
Throughout oceans of all lands and eons, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva,
fulfill all great vows, and achieve the vehicle of Samantabhadra.
All immeasurable sentient beings who hear his name—

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard the Dharma from Mañjuśrī, was filled with joy; he prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and gazing up at him with longing and affection, departed with tears in his eyes.
Gradually traveling south toward the country of Sukhāvatī, he ascended Mount Saṃyuta;
there, within that mountain, he observed all ten directions with a single-minded focus, searching for where the Great Teacher might be.
He continued this search in this manner for as long as seven days.

At that time, Sudhana saw the bhikṣu on the mountain peak, walking in meditation while reflecting in stillness. Having seen him, he hurried toward him, prostrated with his head at the bhikṣu’s feet, circumambulated him to the right, and stood before him, saying:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Great Master is well able to proclaim the Dharma; I only pray that you will deign to show compassion and explain it fully.
Then, that bhikṣu said to Sudhana: "Excellent!"
Excellent, son of good family!
That you are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva.
"Good son! Such a matter is the most difficult among difficulties, namely:

being able to inquire about the conduct of Bodhisattvas, cultivating the Bodhisattva path, entering the realm of Bodhisattvas, giving birth to the pure path of Bodhisattvas, and seeking the pure and vast mind of a Bodhisattva."
Fulfilling all vows, they accord with those in the world who are ready for transformation, seeking the gateway to liberation within the cycle of birth and death;
regarding the conditioned and the unconditioned, their minds remain unstained by attachment.

Some see one Buddha, two Buddhas, ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten million, a hundred million, a billion, or a hundred thousand billion Buddhas in the eastern direction;

others see immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya, inconceivable, incomparable, limitless, boundless, unfathomable, ineffable, and even ineffably ineffable numbers of Buddhas.

some see Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of the four continents;

or they see Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in three thousand great thousandfold worlds.
It is likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
With various forms and colors, various masteries, and the playful exercise of supernormal powers;
adorned with various retinues, they radiate great nets of light;

I behold all Tathāgatas amidst great assemblies, uttering the lion’s roar. Good son!
I know only this Samādhi of Universal-Gate Radiance for Observing Right Mindfulness of All Buddhas.
How could one possibly fathom the perfectly pure conduct of wisdom of the Bodhisattvas?

These great Bodhisattvas have attained the Samādhi-door of Universal Illumination through Mindfulness of the Buddha, by which they are able to behold all Buddhas and their retinues, as well as their adorned and purified Buddha-lands;

they have attained the Samādhi-door of Mindfulness of the Buddha that Causes All Sentient Beings to Depart from Perversion, by which they cause all sentient beings to become pure according to their respective needs.
They attain the gate of the Samādhi of Recollecting the Buddha through the Ultimate Attainment of All Powers, wherein they practice the ten powers of all Buddhas with right mindfulness;

they attain the gate of the Samādhi of Recollecting the Buddha with a Mind Free from Inversion regarding all Dharmas, whereby they behold the clouds of all Buddhas and hear, receive, and uphold the Dharma in their presence;
they attain the gate of the Samādhi of Recollecting the Buddha by Discerning All Tathāgatas of the Ten Directions, whereby they see the oceans of all Tathāgatas within the ocean of all worlds.
They attain the gate of the *nien-fo samādhi* (buddhānusmṛti-samādhi) that is invisible and unenterable, wherein they perceive the sovereign realm of all Buddhas within subtle objects;
they attain the gate of the *nien-fo samādhi* that is non-perverted throughout all eons, wherein they constantly see all Buddhas at all times without ever being separated from them;
they attain the gate of the *nien-fo samādhi* according to the occasion, wherein they constantly see all Buddhas at every moment.

They attain the gate of the *nien-fo samādhi* (Buddha-recollection samādhi) of the Adorned and Pure Buddha-fields, whereby they give rise to all Buddha-fields that cannot be destroyed and universally behold all Buddhas;
they attain the gate of the *nien-fo samādhi* of non-inversion throughout the three periods of time, whereby they see all Buddhas of the three periods of time along with their retinues;
they attain the gate of the *nien-fo samādhi* of the indestructible realm, whereby they see all Buddhas within every realm.
They attain the gate of the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha of Quiescence, wherein in a single thought-moment they see all Tathāgatas manifesting parinirvāṇa in all worlds;
they attain the gate of the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha Free from Months and Free from Time, wherein in a single day they see all Tathāgatas traveling and teaching;
they attain the gate of the Samādhi of Vast Mindfulness of the Buddha, wherein they see the body of a single Buddha sitting cross-legged, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
They attain the gate of the subtle *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*, wherein they see all Buddhas attaining perfect enlightenment within a single pore;
they attain the gate of the adorned *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*, wherein they see all Buddhas in a single thought-moment attaining perfect enlightenment in all worlds with sovereign spiritual powers;
they attain the gate of the pure-object *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*, wherein they see all Buddhas with their light of wisdom universally illuminating as they turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma.
They attain the gate of the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha through the Pure Mind, clearly seeing all Buddhas within their own minds;
they attain the gate of the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha through Pure Action, seeing the various karmas of all sentient beings like images in a mirror;
they attain the gate of the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha through Sovereignty, seeing all adorned realms of the Dharma-realm filled with Buddhas.
He attained the gate of the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* equal to space, whereby he beheld the body of the Tathāgata universally illuminating the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
At that time, the bhikṣu Guṇamegha said to Sudhana:
