To the south there is a land called Sāgaramukha;
there dwells a bhikṣu named Sāgaramegha.
You should go to him and inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva.

"Good son! That bhikṣu is able to analytically explain the roots of goodness—possessing the roots of goodness of causes, the roots of goodness of the great earth, and the roots of goodness of great power;
he is able to praise the causal conditions of bodhi, extensively expound the Mahāyāna, increase the power of the pāramitās, and manifest the ocean of all bodhisattva practices."
"He is well able to purify and fulfill great vows, enabling the birth of the pure Universal Gate, the Adornment Dharma-gate, and the power of great compassion.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard the Dharma from the bhikṣu Meghashri, was filled with joy; he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and looking up at him with longing and affection, took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, with single-minded right mindfulness, contemplated the instructions of the spiritual friends, the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the light of wisdom, and the bodhisattva samādhis;
he observed the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ skillful means and their perfected merits;
his heart constantly delighted in beholding all bodhisattvas and recollecting all Buddhas who have successively appeared in the world and whose merits are pure.
Gradually proceeding toward the southern land of Samudramukha, he went to the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha;
prostrating with his head at the bhikṣu’s feet and circumambulating him to the right, he withdrew to stand to one side and said:
"O Great Sage!

I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to cross the great ocean of all wisdom; yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva may leave the nature of birth and death and attain non-retrogression;
how they may be born into the family of the Tathāgata, cross the ocean of birth and death, and reach the ocean of the Tathāgata’s all-encompassing wisdom;
how they may abandon the stage of ordinary beings and attain the stage of the Tathāgata.
They sever the stream of birth and death and enter the stream of bodhisattvas;
they extinguish the wheel of the various realms of existence and fulfill the wheel of all vows;
they subdue all demons and perfect the merits of a Buddha.
They exhaust the ocean of craving and desire, and expand the ocean of great compassion;
they close off all evil paths and open the gates of liberation—the paths of devas and humans;
they emerge from the city of the triple world and reach the city of omniscience.
"Having renounced all objects of pleasure and amusement, you have made great vows to gather in sentient beings.
At that time, the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha said to Sudhana:
"O son of good family!
“Have you already resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
He replied, “Indeed, I have.”

“Good son! If one does not deeply plant roots of goodness, one cannot give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, nor obtain the roots of goodness of the Universal Gate and the Dharma-door of Universally Illuminating Radiance;
nor can one nurture the light of wisdom of the Samādhi of the Right Path, or bring forth the ocean-treasury of various merits.”
They cultivate long-standing, pure dharmas without ever falling back;
they draw near to spiritual friends, honoring and making offerings to them, not begrudging even their own bodies or lives, and possessing no hoarded stores;
they are free from all arrogance, their minds remaining unshakable like the great earth.
With great compassion, they take pity on all living beings and distance themselves from all gates of birth and death.
Those who delight in the realm of the Buddha are able to give rise to the bodhicitta.
The mind of great compassion, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings;
the mind of great loving-kindness, for the sake of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
the tireless mind, for the sake of extinguishing all the sufferings and afflictions of all sentient beings.
A mind of benefit, because it extinguishes all unwholesome dharmas of sentient beings;
a fearless mind, because it eliminates all afflictions and harms;
an unimpeded mind, because it extinguishes all obstacles.
A vast mind, because it fills the entire dharma-realm;
a boundless mind, because it is equal to the realm of empty space;
a broad mind, because it beholds all Tathāgatas.
The pure mind, because its wisdom regarding the phenomena of the three periods of time is non-contradictory;
the wisdom mind, because it reaches the ultimate depths of the ocean of all-knowledge. "Good son!
I have resided in this country of Sāgaradvāra for twelve years, observing the great ocean that constitutes its domain.
I contemplate the great ocean as being immeasurable and boundless;
I contemplate the great ocean as being profoundly deep and difficult to fathom to its source or bottom.
Contemplating the great ocean as gradually becoming deep and vast;
contemplating the great ocean adorned with immeasurable wondrous jewels;
contemplating the great ocean as an immeasurable mass of water.
One contemplates the great ocean, with its various colors of water that are inconceivable;
one contemplates the great ocean as the place where beings of massive bodies take refuge;
one contemplates the great ocean as the abode of the watery realm.
Contemplate the great ocean as being completely covered by vast clouds;
contemplate the great ocean as never having increased or decreased. Good son!
While I was reflecting in this way, I further thought:
"Is there perhaps any other phenomenon in the world that is more vast than this great ocean, deeper than this great ocean, or more magnificent than this great ocean?"
Having formed this thought, he immediately saw a wondrous jewel lotus spontaneously emerge from the boundary of the water-circle at the bottom of the ocean.
It had sapphire for its stem, Jāmbūnada gold for its petals, aloeswood for its pedestal, and agate for its filaments, covering the great ocean entirely.
A million asura kings all together upheld it;
a million nets adorned with maṇi jewels were spread over its top;
and a million dragon kings rained down fragrant water.
A million Garuḍa kings held exquisite jeweled silk ribbons in their beaks, hanging them down in adornment;
a million Rākṣasa kings gazed upon him with hearts of compassion;
and a million Yakṣa kings paid him reverent homage.
A million gandharva kings offered praise and worship;
a million celestial kings rained down clouds of celestial fragrant flowers, powdered incense, banners, pennants, and exquisite jewel-encrusted robes;
and a million Brahma kings prostrated themselves in reverent salutation.
A million Śuddhāvāsa devas, having each paid their respects, stood with palms joined;
a million wheel-turning kings, adorned with the seven treasures;
and a million sea-king deities, emerging from the great ocean, paid respectful homage.
A net of light from a million luminous jewels shines universally upon all;
it is adorned with a million pure jewels and a million brilliantly clear jewels;
and from a million jewel-treasuries, immeasurable light issues forth, illuminating all things everywhere.
A million Jambūnada jewels were established as a magnificent adornment;
a million vajra-siṃha jewels were indestructible and pure as an adornment;
and a million sun-treasury jewels were brilliantly radiant, universally illuminating all.
A million indestructible maṇi jewels, which give rise to and nurture all virtuous deeds;
a million wish-fulfilling jewels, providing inexhaustible adornment.

That jewel lotus was produced from the unsurpassed roots of goodness of the Tathāgata; it causes all the vows of every bodhisattva to be fulfilled and manifests throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
It gives rise to the realization that all dharmas are like illusions, born of pure dharmas and adorned with the skillful means of non-contention.
Its practice is like the dharma of dreams, the seal of unconditioned dharmas, ultimately reaching the skillful means of non-obstruction.

Universally covering all dharma realms throughout the ten directions, this is solely the realm of the Buddhas; even if one were to follow along with the world for immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, it could never be fully extolled.

Upon that flower, he saw a Tathāgata sitting cross-legged; the pure body of that Buddha extended upward as far as the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception, filling it entirely without exception.
He saw that Tathāgata seated upon this adorned precious lotus throne, surrounded by an inconceivable assembly; he saw the adornment of inconceivable, perfect radiance;
he saw the adornment of inconceivable marks and signs; he saw the mastery of inconceivable spiritual powers;
he saw the inconceivable sublime form of the Tathāgata; and he saw the inconceivable mark of the invisible crown of the head.
One beholds the inconceivable mark of the broad and long tongue; one recollects the inconceivable pure voice;
one contemplates the inconceivable perfect voice; one beholds the inconceivable powers of the Tathāgata;
one understands the inconceivable pure fearlessnesses; and one understands all that is inconceivable.
Through various eloquences, they remember the original practices of Bodhisattvas throughout inconceivable great kalpas of the past;
they behold inconceivable mastery over enlightenment; they behold inconceivable clouds of the True Dharma;
they behold inconceivable bodies adorned with universal gates; they behold inconceivable majesty and symmetry on the left and right of the body.
He discerns all inconceivable matters to benefit sentient beings.
At that time, that Tathāgata extended his right hand, rubbed the crown of my head, and preached the *Puyan Sūtra*.

This is solely the domain of the Tathāgata, wherein he gives rise to all pure practices of Bodhisattvas, universally illumines the entire Dharma-realm, encompasses and perfects the entire Dharma-realm, universally illuminates all adorned and purified Buddha-lands, subdues all demons and followers of external paths, causes all sentient beings to rejoice, universally illuminates the conduct of all sentient beings so that nothing remains unmanifested according to their needs, and universally illuminates the faculties of all sentient beings.

"Good son! From the Buddha I have heard this *Puyan jing* (Universal Eye Sutra), which I have received and upheld in its entirety, recited until it was mastered, and contemplated with right mindfulness. Good son!"

Even if someone were to use ink as vast as the great ocean and pens as numerous as Mount Sumeru to transcribe this sutra—writing out the meaning and flavor of each chapter, each dharma-gate, each skillful means, each sequential dharma-gate, and each single phrase—it still could not be exhausted.
"Good son! For twelve hundred years at the place of the Buddha, I have heard and received this sutra;
in each and every day, I have received incalculable chapters (*asaṃkhyeya-pada*) by the power of the light of the *dhāraṇī* of great learning."
The chapter on the ultimate incalculable [qualities], by the power of the light of the hundred-gate dhāraṇī;
the chapter on the gathering of the incalculable [qualities], by the power of the light of the immeasurable-turning dhāraṇī;
the chapter on the differentiation of the incalculable [qualities], by the power of the light of the dhāraṇī that accords with the differentiation of the various stages (*bhūmi*).
The chapter on Purifying the Incalculable, through the power of the light of the Dhāraṇī of Sublime Adornment;
the chapter on Producing the Incalculable, through the power of the light of the Dhāraṇī of Ornamentation According to Exhortations;
the chapter on Explaining the Incalculable, through the power of the light of the Dhāraṇī of Clear and Pure Sound;
The chapter on "Illuminating the Asaṃkhyeya" is due to the power of the radiance of the Gaganagañja Dhāraṇī;
the chapter on "Extending the Asaṃkhyeya" is due to the power of the radiance of the Drumasamudgata Dhāraṇī;
the chapter on "Accomplishing the Asaṃkhyeya" is due to the power of the radiance of the Sāgaragarbha Dhāraṇī.
There were the various devas and deva-kings, nāgas and nāga-kings,
yakṣas and yakṣa-kings from the ten directions;
Gandharvas and Gandharva kings; asuras and asura kings; garuḍas and garuḍa kings;
Kinnaras and Kinnara kings; humans and human kings;
Brahmās and Brahmā kings.
If anyone comes to question me, I shall immediately expound, reveal, analyze, and praise it for them, causing them all to dwell securely in this *Puyan jing* (Universal Eye Sutra).
O son of noble family!
I know only this single dharma-gate; how could I possibly know exhaustively all the practices of the bodhisattvas?
Why is this? Because the bodhisattvas have perfected all practices to their ultimate limit.
They have perfected the ocean of great vows, for they remain uninterrupted throughout all oceans of eons;
they enter the ocean of sentient beings, for they accord with all who are ready to be transformed;
they penetrate deeply into the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, giving rise to the light of wisdom of the Tathāgata’s ten powers.
Because they fully know the faculties of all sentient beings and, according to those who are to be transformed, do not miss the proper time;
because they enter the ocean of all Buddha-fields and give rise to firm vows regarding those Buddha-fields;
and because, through the power of their great vows, they ultimately pay respectful homage and make offerings to the ocean of all Buddhas.
They cross the ocean of all dharmas because of their wisdom of liberation;
they enter deeply into the ocean of merit because they practice according to what they have taught;
and they cross the ocean of the languages of all sentient beings because they turn the wheel of Dharma in the lands of the ten directions.
"Good son! Travel sixty yojanas to the south; there is a land called Sāgaratīra.
There dwells a bhikṣu named Susthita."
"I should go to him and ask how a bodhisattva cultivates pure conduct. Then,
the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times,
and with boundless reverence and longing, took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness of the instructions of the spiritual friend and right mindfulness of the *Samantanetra Sūtra*, contemplated the sovereign spiritual powers of that Buddha and received and upheld the clouds of Dharma in the words and meanings of that Buddha’s teachings.
Cultivating the True Dharma, they enter the profound ocean of the Dharma;
exhausting the source and bottom of the Dharma, they grasp the supreme teachings;
eliminating the cataracts of ignorance, they fully comprehend the island of Dharma-treasures.
Arriving at the coastal kingdom, he searched throughout the ten directions for the Great Teacher, asking, "Where is he now?
He saw that bhikṣu walking upon the void, surrounded by a retinue of asaṃkhyeya devas.
At that time, for the sake of making offerings to the bhikṣu Susthita, the hosts of devas scattered various celestial flowers in the void;
they performed manifold music, producing subtle and wondrous sounds;
and incalculable jeweled banners adorned the sky.
At that time, for the sake of making offerings, the dragon kings raised inconceivable clouds of aloeswood incense that filled the entirety of space;
the kinnara kings, for the sake of making offerings, performed various musical performances and produced wondrous sounds that pervaded the void;
and the kings of the ocean deities, for the sake of making offerings, emitted harmonious and elegant tones.

For the sake of making offerings, the Asura King raised inconceivable clouds of jewels to adorn the void, emitting inconceivable radiance that universally illumined all things, and using inconceivable precious playthings to adorn the void.
Inconceivable kinnara kings filled the void, free from any intent to harm, reverently making offerings to the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita;
inconceivable rākṣasa kings, surrounded by their retinues of rākṣasas and piśācas of hideous form, filled the void through the power of the great compassion of the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita;
and inconceivable yakṣa kings, together with hosts of yakṣas, filled the void, surrounding him on all sides to protect the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita.
Inconceivable Brahma kings stood in the void with palms joined in reverent salutation, praising that bhikṣu in human voices as they remained to one side;
inconceivable Śuddhāvāsa devas, together with their palaces, approached the bhikṣu Susthitamati for the sake of making offerings.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, seeing such offerings in the sky, joined his palms in reverent salutation to the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita and said to him:
"O Great Sage!..."

I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva correctly directs oneself toward the Buddha-dharma, single-mindedly seeks the Buddha-dharma, reveres the Buddha-dharma, cultivates all Buddha-dharmas, nurtures the Buddha-dharmas, accumulates the Buddha-dharmas, perfumes and practices the Buddha-dharmas, purifies all Buddha-dharmas, universally purifies the Buddha-dharmas, and reaches the Buddha-dharmas.
I have heard that the Great Sage is well able to instruct all bodhisattvas in the Dharma;
how does a bodhisattva cultivate the Buddha-dharma so as to constantly see all Buddhas and never be separated from them,
and to constantly see bodhisattvas and share their roots of goodness?
They do not depart from the Buddha-dharma, their wisdom being fully perfected;
they do not abandon their great vows for all sentient beings, bringing those matters to ultimate completion;
throughout all kalpas, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices with minds free from weariness, never forsaking the buddha-fields.
They are universally able to adorn all worlds and are fully capable of knowing and seeing the sovereign powers of all Buddhas;
without departing from the conditioned, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, thoroughly understanding them all to be like illusions as they enter every realm of existence;
they manifest the experience of birth and death yet remain free from arising or ceasing, constantly hearing the True Dharma and never being separated from it.
"How can one fully receive and uphold the clouds of the Buddhas' Dharma, never depart from the light of wisdom, and universally illumine the three periods of time?
At that time, the bhikṣu Susthita said to Sudhana: "Excellent!"
Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!
That you are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and are able to inquire about the Buddha-dharma, the dharma of omniscience, and the dharma that requires no teacher.
"Good son! I have already accomplished the bodhisattva’s unimpeded dharma-gate; I have cultivated the discernment of clarity and attained the light of unimpeded, pure wisdom."
Having attained the light of wisdom, one observes the mental activities of all sentient beings without obstruction;
one observes all sentient beings dying here and being born there without obstruction;
and one possesses unobstructed knowledge of past lives.
He is without obstruction regarding knowledge of the future;
he is without obstruction regarding his knowledge of all sentient beings in the present world;
and he is without obstruction regarding the languages and dharmas of all sentient beings.
If all sentient beings come to pose difficult questions, one is able to respond to them all without any hindrance;
one knows the faculties of all sentient beings without any hindrance;
and one teaches and transforms sentient beings without any hindrance.
They discern and understand all *kṣaṇas*, *lava-s*, and *muhūrta-s* without obstruction;
they are without obstruction regarding the ocean of the three periods of time;
and their own bodies fill the Buddha-fields of the ten directions without obstruction.
Why is this? Because they rely on non-existence and possess the power of unconditioned supernormal knowledges. Good son!
By virtue of having attained this power of supernatural faculties, I move, stand, sit, and lie down within the void; I soar and travel through the ten directions;
and in a single thought-moment, I reach everywhere throughout one Buddha-world in the eastern quarter, and even a hundred Buddha-worlds.
They behold all the Buddhas and their retinues within worlds numbering one thousand, one hundred thousand, and immeasurable Buddhas;

even up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-worlds, as many worlds as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, and even up to worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

Within all these worlds, they see every Buddha and his retinue, and they make offerings to those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas with every kind of flower, incense, powdered incense, ointment, precious garlands, banners and streamers, variegated silk canopies, various exquisite jewel nets, and all manner of images.
Whatever those Tathāgatas have revealed, manifested, proclaimed, and praised, I hear and receive it all, discerning and penetrating it;
I likewise remember all the pure lands of those Buddhas in the past,
as well as those in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
If there are sentient beings who manage to see me, they shall all be destined for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Just as I perceive all sentient beings—whether great or small, beautiful or ugly, suffering or happy—for the sake of transforming and delivering them, I manifest a body identical to theirs according to what is appropriate for each.
If there are sentient beings who come to me, I cause them all to dwell securely in this True Dharma. Good son! I know only this single unimpeded dharma-gate;

how could I possibly explain the Bodhisattva’s precepts of great compassion, the precepts of the various pāramitās, the precepts of mounting the Great Vehicle, the precepts of not abandoning the Bodhisattva path, the precepts for extinguishing obstacles, the precepts of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, the precepts of not abandoning the bodhicitta, the precepts of the profound resolve for all Buddha-dharmas, the precepts of mindfulness of omniscience without forgetfulness, the precepts like space, the precepts of non-reliance upon any world, the indestructible precepts, the incomparable precepts, the unclouded precepts, the unmixed precepts, the precepts free from doubt, the pure precepts, the dust-free precepts, and the stainless pure precepts?
"Good son! A bodhisattva possesses such immeasurable merits as these; how could I possibly know them or explain them according to reality? Good son!"
To the south of here, there is a land called Vaśavartin, and a city named Mantrauṣadhi;
in that place there is a skilled physician named Megha.
"Go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva proceed toward the conduct of a bodhisattva?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of the bhikṣu Supratiṣṭhita and, having paid his respects, departed to travel south.
At that time, the youth Sudhana focused his mind with single-minded right mindfulness on the Dharma-door of the Light of Dharma, becoming fully endowed with the power of the Dharma;

he maintained right mindfulness of all Buddhas, never severing the Three Jewels; he praised the nature of detachment from desire, recollected spiritual friends who universally illumine the three periods of time;
and he recollected his great vows to bring all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm to ultimate fulfillment.
Regarding all conditioned phenomena, the mind has no attachment;
observing that all dharmas are impermanent, they are able to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields with a mind free from indolence;
regarding all Buddhas and their retinues, the mind has no attachment.
Gradually arriving at that country, he entered the City of Mantra-Medicine and sought the eminent physician Megha, asking, "Where is he now?

At that time, the youth saw the eminent physician seated upon a lion throne in the Hall of Right Dharma, surrounded before and behind by a great assembly of ten thousand people, as he was expounding for them the *Sūtra of the Radiant Adornment of the Wheel-Syllable*.
Then, the youth Sudhana went to the physician Megha, prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him to the right, and withdrawing to one side, joined his palms and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should proceed toward the bodhisattva practice,
nor how one should train in the bodhisattva practice.
How can one, amidst birth and death, always remain without losing the bodhicitta?
How can one attain a mind of equanimity that has no fixed destination?
How can one reach a firm and upright mind that nothing in all the worlds can destroy?
How does one give rise to the power of great compassion while remaining free from sorrow and affliction?
How does one realize the power of the pure *dhāraṇī* of the universal gate?
How does one generate the light of wisdom to eliminate the darkness of ignorance regarding all phenomena?
How does one realize the powers of eloquence and discern the true treasury of all phenomena?
How does one attain the power of right mindfulness to receive and uphold all wheels of the pure Dharma, never forgetting them?
How does one attain the power of pure destinies, so as to universally illuminate all phenomena across every realm of existence?
How does one attain the power of wisdom, so as to achieve definitive knowledge regarding all phenomena and realize their true meaning?
At that time, the skilled physician said to Sudhana: "Noble son,
have you already previously resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?"
He replied, "So be it.
At that time, the excellent physician descended from his lion throne, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and paid homage to Sudhana.

Having completed the prostrations, they scattered exquisite golden flowers, various miscellaneous jewel flowers, priceless *maṇi* gems, superior powdered sandalwood, and priceless precious robes, covering him with them;
with such a multitude of wondrous offerings, they made this offering,
honoring and praising him while speaking these words:
“Excellent! Excellent, son of good family!”
One is thus able to give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Good son!
If there are those who can give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they are thereby protecting the *buddha-dhātu* (buddha-nature) of all beings.
To purify the nature of all Buddha-fields;
to transform the nature of sentient beings;
and to expound the Dharma according to the nature of reality for the sake of all sentient beings.
The nature of conforming to all karmic actions;
the nature of fulfilling all bodhisattva practices;
and the nature of never severing any great vows.
They realize the nature of detachment;
their wisdom is luminous and pure, universally illuminating the nature of all phenomena throughout the three periods of time;
they establish the nature of liberation;
They are sustained by the protection of all Buddhas;
all Buddhas constantly guard and mind them;
and they are well able to accord with all Bodhisattvas.
All worthy and holy ones universally rejoice;
all Brahmā deities pay him respectful homage;
and all devas offer him veneration and support.
It was established by all the yakṣa kings;
it was reverently honored and made offerings to by all the rākṣasa kings;
and it was borne upon the crowns of all the nāga kings.
All the Kinnara kings praised him with reverent hearts;
all the kings of the worlds remembered him with respect.

He brought comfort to all sentient beings, extinguishing the three evil realms and causing them to distance themselves from all hardships. He rescued all from the root of poverty and established them in the blissful abodes of devas and humans.
They encountered spiritual friends and never remained far from them;
they heard the wondrous Dharma of the Buddha and gave rise to the bodhicitta.
By means of the branch of the pure bodhicitta, they attained clear and radiant light that illumines the bodhisattva path, accords with bodhisattva wisdom, and abides upon the bodhisattva stages.
"Good son! You should know that Bodhisattvas are able to perform extremely difficult tasks for the sake of all sentient beings—tasks that are hard to encounter and hard to see;
they act as parents for all sentient beings and adorn them."
They encompass all devas and people of the world, eliminating the immeasurable sufferings and hardships of sentient beings;
they protect sentient beings, keeping them far removed from grief and affliction.
The Bodhisattva acts as a great wind-wheel, securely supporting sentient beings so that they do not fall into the three evil realms.
The Bodhisattva is the great earth, for he causes all roots of goodness to grow; the Bodhisattva is the great ocean, for he is fully endowed with an inexhaustible treasury of merit;
the Bodhisattva is the sun, for with the light of his pure and clear wisdom, he universally illumines the world and extinguishes the darkness of delusion;
the Bodhisattva is Sumeru, the king of mountains, for his roots of merit and goodness are loftiest and greatest.
The Bodhisattva is like the moon, for he brings refreshing coolness to all sentient beings;
the Bodhisattva is like a great general, for he is able to subdue all Māras;
the Bodhisattva is a virtuous man, for he serves as the sovereign within the city of the Dharma.
The Bodhisattva is fire, for he can burn away the various cravings of sentient beings;
the Bodhisattva is a cloud, for he rains down the nectar-like Dharma;
the Bodhisattva is right view, for he is able to nurture all the sublime faculties.
"Bodhisattvas are the compass, for they reveal the ocean of Dharma;
Bodhisattvas are the bridge, for they enable all sentient beings to cross the ocean of birth and death.
At that time, having praised and extolled Sudhana and the other bodhisattvas, the skilled physician emitted from his mouth a great cloud of light that universally illuminated the trichiliocosm.
Having been thus illuminated, the great powerful devas of the trichiliocosm, up to and including the various Brahmā devas, all went to the skilled physician.
At that time, the physician, employing skillful means in accordance with their needs, analyzed, extensively expounded, and revealed the *Cakrākṣaravyūhaprabhāsasūtra*.
When that great assembly had heard this sūtra, they attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having performed what was to be done, he returned to his original seat and addressed Sudhana, saying: "Good son!

I have accomplished the Dharma-door of 'the non-falsity of one's word' and have clearly distinguished and understood the languages of all the devas, as well as the languages of all the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans within the trichiliocosm."
As it is with this trichiliocosm, so it is with the immeasurable, boundless, and unspeakably unspeakable numbers of trichiliocosms throughout the ten directions.
"Good son! I know only this bodhisattva dharma-door of 'the non-falsity of speech. How could I possibly explain the practices of all bodhisattvas?"

Those bodhisattvas, in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of all characteristics of sentient beings; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of all designations of sentient beings; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of all names and titles; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of all languages; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of the continuity of all phrases; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of the sequence of all explanatory phrases; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of the continuity of the sequence of all explanatory phrases; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of all Tathāgatas; in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of the differentiation of all phrases; and in accordance with and deeply entering the ocean of all the languages of sentient beings—they attain all perfect adornments and subtle, wondrous voices, giving rise to the wheel of the differentiation of all written characters.
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a land called Vanavāsin; in it dwells an elder named Vimukta."
"Go to him and ask: How does a bodhisattva turn toward the bodhisattva path, cultivate the bodhisattva path, accomplish the bodhisattva path, and contemplate the bodhisattva path?

Then, at the abode of the excellent physician, Sudhana heard this Dharma-gate; he gave rise to deep and pure faith, revered the Dharma with reverence, attained certain knowledge and vision, and through the spiritual friend, gained omniscience (*sarvajñā*).
He prostrated his head at the physician's feet, and finally took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, Sudhana the youth correctly recollected the Bodhisattva’s teaching on the Dharma-gate of non-emptiness: entering the ocean of Bodhisattva speech; recollecting the ocean of subtle skillful means for all sentient beings;

contemplating the various defiled and pure dharmas of Bodhisattvas; giving rise to the radiance of Bodhisattva roots of goodness; purifying and cultivating the Bodhisattva’s gate of skillful means for teaching and transforming sentient beings; clarifying and purifying the Bodhisattva’s wisdom for gathering in sentient beings; strengthening the Bodhisattva’s power of upright mental resolve; nurturing the power of the Bodhisattva’s profound mind; purifying and cultivating the Bodhisattva’s various powers of aspiration; and, with a Bodhisattva’s mind of faith, remaining far removed from all evils.

With a firm resolve, they adorn themselves with great ornaments; their minds are free from weariness, and through courageous diligence, their hearts never regress. Possessing the power of an indestructible pure faith that even Vajra Nārāyaṇa cannot shatter, they embrace the instructions of all spiritual friends, and their unimpeded spheres of experience become entirely pure.
In this stainless sphere, the wondrous mind manifests before them.
They attain the stage of the *dhāraṇī* of the light of skillful means of the universal eye; they realize the stage of the dharma-realm, with the mind constantly manifest before them;
they know the stage of equality is no stage, being adorned and pure, without attachment to "mine";
they dwell in the non-dual realm and attain pure, unobstructed wisdom.
They thoroughly understand the ground of phenomena as being without obstruction;
they know the grounds of all directions and do not regress;
and they analytically understand all grounds of karma.
They manifest the pure and majestic ground of all Buddhas;

they attain the wheel of wisdom to discern the three periods of time; they reach the Samādhi of Universal Bliss and Radiance, which illuminates body and mind, and proceed in accordance with all stages of the realms.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom universally illumines all realms, giving rise to the waves of all-encompassing wisdom;
his body is never separated from the power of the Buddha-dharma and is sustained by the protection of all Tathāgatas;
his mind is entirely equal to that of all Buddhas, and in accordance with wisdom, it universally illumines all things.
His body filled all the networks of lands, he had accomplished his great vows, and his own person encompassed the entire dharma-realm.
Having reflected thus, he traveled by stages for twelve years until he reached the country of Vṛkṣaprasāda,
where he searched everywhere for the elder Vimokṣa.
Having seen him, he prostrated at his feet, stood to one side, and thought to himself:
“I have gained a great benefit in seeing a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).

It is difficult for a spiritual friend to appear in the world; it is difficult to reach their presence; it is difficult to encounter them; it is difficult to see and know them; it is difficult to draw near to them; it is difficult to dwell together with them; it is difficult to win their favor; and it is difficult to act in accordance with them.”
Having reflected thus, he said: "Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, desiring to encounter all Buddhas."
Desiring to see all Buddhas;
desiring to attain the intentions of all Buddhas;
desiring to know the minds of all Buddhas.
Desiring to attain the samādhis of all buddhas;
to accord with all the great vows of all buddhas;
and desiring to fulfill all the great vows of all buddhas.
They desire to seek the light of wisdom of all Buddhas;
they desire that all Buddhas emerge from within their own bodies;
and they desire to attain the various illuminations that know the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
Desiring to purify all the powers and fearlessnesses of the Buddhas;
desiring to hear all the Buddha-dharmas with a mind never weary or satisfied;
desiring to receive all the Buddha-dharmas.
Desiring to uphold all Buddha-dharmas;
desiring to discern all Buddha-dharmas;
desiring to protect all Buddha-teachings;
I desire to be one with all bodhisattvas; I desire to have as spiritual friends those bodhisattvas who share the same roots of goodness;
I desire to fulfill all the pāramitās of a bodhisattva.
Desiring to fulfill all bodhisattva practices;
desiring to give rise to the pure great vows of a bodhisattva;
and desiring to obtain the treasury of the causal dharmas of all buddhas and bodhisattvas.
They desire to attain the light of wisdom of the immeasurable Dharma-treasury of all bodhisattvas;
they desire to attain the treasury of all bodhisattva samādhis;
they desire to bring forth the treasury of all bodhisattva supernormal powers and clarities.
They wish to bring forth the treasury of great compassion to teach and transform sentient beings without end;
they wish to discern and know the treasury of playful supernatural powers;
and they wish to discern and know the treasury of mastery.
Desiring mastery over the treasury of sovereignty, his mind attained mastery;
desiring to purify the ten kinds of treasuries, he sought these various merits with single-minded devotion and went to the place of the elder;
desiring to fulfill all his vows.
Desiring to transcend birth and death;
desiring to attain the dharma of mastery;
desiring to be endowed with the gateway of reverence;
Desiring to perfect the gates of skillful means;
desiring to distance oneself from all defilements;
desiring to achieve pure adornment.
"I desire that my body and mind be supple;
I desire to subdue the sense faculties. He said:
"I have heard that the Great Sage skillfully teaches the bodhisattvas the correct path of expedient means, which universally illumines all things and manifests the wondrous Dharma;
it shows the way across the ford, opens the gate of the True Dharma,
eliminates inversions, and extracts the thorns of doubt and confusion."
The mind is freed from the defilement of delusion, illuminating and dispelling the dense darkness;
detached from all afflictions, it forever attains refreshing clarity;
casting aside flattery and crookedness, it transcends birth and death.
They abandon the unwholesome roots and nurture the wholesome roots;
they distance themselves from all realms of existence without any attachment;
they extinguish all hindrances and seek sarvajñā (omniscience).
Upon reaching the City of the Dharma King, their minds abide securely in great loving-kindness and great compassion;
they are taught the bodhisattva practices and cultivate various samādhis;
their minds abide securely in the dharma-gates of accordance, giving rise to the vast mind.
Endowed with all powers, you illuminate the minds of all living beings.
I pray that the Great Sage will analyze and explain for me how a bodhisattva proceeds toward the bodhisattva path and cultivates the bodhisattva path;
and having cultivated it, how one may swiftly purify the bodhisattva conduct and fully accomplish the perfect, pure conduct of a bodhisattva?
At that time, by the power of his past roots of goodness, the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, and Mañjuśrī’s power of mindfulness, the householder Vimukta entered a gate of bodhisattva samādhi;
this gate of samādhi was named the "Dhāraṇī of the Infinite Revolutions that Encompasses All Buddha-fields."
Having entered, he attained a pure body;

within that body, he saw in each of the ten directions as many Buddhas as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds, along with their adorned and purified lands and all the past deeds of the great assemblies.
Those Tathāgatas possess sovereign spiritual power and are endowed with all great vows and merits;

they adorn the Right Path through various pure practices, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, turn the pure wheel of Dharma, transform and guide sentient beings, and bring all dharmas to ultimate fulfillment.
Within his body, all these appear clearly without confusion or mutual obstruction;
they abide in their original forms, with diverse shapes and colors, adorned in various ways.
Surrounded and graced by a great assembly of bodhisattvas, he manifests the sovereign power of all Buddhas, proclaims the gates of various vows, and displays immeasurable powers of mastery.
In some lands, he performs buddha-work while dwelling in the Tuṣita Heaven;
in some lands, he manifests the end of his life;
or he manifests entering the womb.
Sometimes he manifests dwelling in the womb to display his sovereign power;
sometimes he manifests birth;
and sometimes he manifests residing in the inner palace.
Some manifest leaving the household life;
some manifest proceeding to the adorned site of enlightenment;
and some manifest subduing Māra.
Sometimes they manifest as attaining Buddhahood;
sometimes they manifest as being surrounded by a great assembly in the palaces of devas, yakṣas, gandharvas, or kings of various worlds, being requested to turn the wheel of Dharma;
or they manifest as turning the wheel of Dharma themselves.
Sometimes they manifest entering the various realms of existence;
sometimes they manifest parinirvāṇa;
and sometimes they manifest the distribution of their relics.
Or they manifest various adornments for stupas.

Those Tathāgatas, for the sake of various sentient beings—that ocean of sentient beings—employ various skillful means according to their various faculties and various habitual tendencies of affliction;
or they manifest a great assembly from within a small assembly, namely:

To assemblies of one *yojana*, he manifested assemblies of ten *yojanas*, and even up to assemblies of as many *yojanas* as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, and for them he preached the Dharma.
Sudhana heard and received all the true Dharma spoken by those Tathāgatas with their subtle and wondrous voices;
furthermore, he beheld the sovereign spiritual powers of those Buddhas and the inconceivable samādhis of the Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the householder Vimokṣa rose from samādhi and said to Sudhana,
“Son of good family!
I have already accomplished the Dharma-door of the Tathāgata’s Unobstructed Adornment.”

Having attained this Dharma-gate, he beheld in the eastern direction the world-system of Jambūnada-prabhā, where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Star-King (Jyotirāja), together with the Bodhisattva Bright Pure Treasury (Vimalagarbha) and the entire great assembly, were present;

furthermore, he saw in the southern direction the world-system of All Powers (Sarvabala), where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Universal Fragrance (Samantagandha), together with the Bodhisattva Mind-King (Cittarāja) and the entire great assembly, were present;

and furthermore, he saw in the western direction the world-system of Fragrant Light (Gandhaprabhā), where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sumeru Lamp King (Sumerupradīparāja), together with the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Mind (Anāvaraṇacitta) and the entire great assembly, were present.

Furthermore, he saw in the northern direction, in the world called Holy Robe Banner, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Sovereign Spiritual Power Unassailable, together with the entire assembly including the Bodhisattva Sovereign Might;

he also saw in the northeastern direction, in the world called All Joyful Jewels, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Unobstructed Eye, together with the entire assembly including the Bodhisattva Unobstructed Transformation;

and he also saw in the southeastern direction, in the world called Fragrant Flame Light, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Fragrant Wisdom, together with the entire assembly including the Bodhisattva Sovereign Wisdom Flame Light.

Furthermore, in the southwestern direction, he saw the world called Sun of Universal Radiance Wisdom (*Samantābhāsajñānasūrya*), where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Banner of the Dharma-Wheel (*Dharmadhātucakraketu*) was presiding over a great assembly including the Bodhisattva Dispenser of All Transformation Banners (*Sarvanirmāṇaketudāyin*) and others;

in the northwestern direction, he saw the world called Universally Pure Manifestation (*Samantaviśuddhābhāsa*), where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Supreme Banner of All Buddha-Jewels (*Sarvabuddharatnānuttaradhvaja*) was presiding over a great assembly including the Bodhisattva King of the Dharma-Banner (*Dharmadhvajendra*) and others;

and in the zenith, he saw the world called Infinite Buddha-Nature (*Akṣayabuddhagotra*), where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Perfect Banner of Immeasurable Wisdom-Light (*Anantajñānaprabhāparipūrṇaketu*) was presiding over a great assembly including the Bodhisattva King of the Ground-Banner of the Dharma-Dhātu (*Dharmadhātubhūmiketendra*) and others.

Furthermore, he saw below, in the world-system called Light of Liberation, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Unobstructed Wisdom Banner, together with the entire assembly, including the Bodhisattva King of the Banner of All Sentient Beings' Worlds.
"Good son! I see Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in ten thousand Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions;
yet those Tathāgatas do not come here, nor do I go there."
"Good son! If I wish to see the world of peace and happiness and the Buddha Amitāyus, I see them at will.
Likewise, I see the world of wondrous joy and the Tathāgata Akṣobhya."
In the world Suṣaṃsthita is the Tathāgata Siṃha;
in the world Suparipūrṇaprabhāsa is the Tathāgata Candramati;
in the world Ratnasiṃhavyūha is the Tathāgata Vairocana.
"Good son! All such Buddhas as these can be seen at will.
Those Tathāgatas do not come here, nor do I go there."
They know that all Buddhas come from nowhere and that they themselves go nowhere;
they know that all Buddhas and their own minds are entirely like dreams;
they know that all Buddhas are like flashes of lightning, and they clearly understand their own minds to be like reflections in water.
They know that all Buddhas are entirely like illusions, and their own minds are likewise;
they know that the voices of all Buddhas are like echoes, and their own minds are likewise.
Knowing thus, understanding thus, and entering thus. Good son,
you should know that Bodhisattvas all attain all Buddha-dharmas through their own minds, cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva, and purify all lands.
They transform and guide sentient beings, giving rise to great vows;
they sport within the city of omniscience through inconceivable gateways of supernatural powers;
and regarding the Bodhi of all Buddhas, their universal sovereignty and unimpeded realm are all derived from their own minds, as they possess profound wisdom and fully comprehend all phenomena.
Therefore, son of good family!
By increasing your own mind with all roots of goodness, you shall rain down the Dharma of ambrosia to moisten that mind;
within the sphere of sensory objects, you shall cause the mind to be pure and diligently cultivate vigor.
They cause the mind to be firm and steadfast, focusing its mindfulness on the True Dharma;
they cause the mind to be undisturbed, so that wisdom becomes bright and pure, and one remains far removed from mental defilements.

With the light of bright and pure wisdom, they examine their own minds, giving rise to a mind of mastery and a vast, expansive mind, equal to the ten powers of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, thereby illuminating the mind.

"Good son! I have only cultivated this Dharma-gate of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded nature; how then could I possibly explain the various practices of Bodhisattvas, their unobstructed wisdom, and their unimpeded pure conduct?
How could I describe their abiding in the samādhi that contemplates the Buddhas of the present, or their attainment of the samādhi of non-nirvāṇa?"
They are fully endowed with the True Dharma of the equality of the three periods of time;
they skillfully know the ground of the realm of the samādhi of equality;
they are fully endowed with a purified body, abiding in the indestructible realm where all Buddhas abide.
The gateways and spheres of all dharmas are perfected through the gateway of wisdom;

with wisdom they observe and universally illumine all things within their own bodies, manifesting the formation and destruction of all worlds therein, yet giving rise to no dualistic notions regarding their own bodies or those worlds;
having brought all practices to ultimate completion, they are fully endowed with merit.
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a land called Adorned Summit of Jambudvīpa;
therein dwells a bhikṣu named Sāgaradhvaja."
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva advances toward the bodhisattva path and cultivates the bodhisattva practices.
Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the elder Vimokṣa by touching his head to them; having circumambulated him to the right, he praised his immeasurable, incalculable merits.
Gazing up at him with longing and observing him, his heart could not be satiated, and he wept with tears streaming down.
One should single-mindedly attend to the spiritual friend, follow the spiritual friend, and contemplate the spiritual friend; it is through the spiritual friend that one attains all-knowledge.
Toward the spiritual friend, one should remain free from flattery and crookedness;
one should regard the spiritual friend with the heart of a compassionate mother, because they cause one to distance oneself from all unbeneficial dharmas.
Regarding spiritual friends, he conceived the thought of them as compassionate fathers, for they are able to give birth to all wholesome dharmas;
then, taking his leave, he traveled south.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll Forty-six.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha of Great Extensive Meaning, Scroll Forty-Seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Part Four of the Thirty-Fourth Chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm."
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness, reflected upon the instructions of the elder Vimokṣa;
he recollected the inconceivable Dharma-gates of the bodhisattvas, contemplated the inconceivable light of wisdom of the bodhisattvas,
followed along and entered deeply into the inconceivable and profound realm of reality (dharmadhātu), and grasped the inconceivable purity of the bodhisattvas.
With wondrous merit, he manifested the inconceivable sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata;
he understood the inconceivable adornments of the Buddha-fields; he discerned and knew the inconceivable realms of the Buddha’s sustaining power, adornment, and abiding;
and he contemplated the inconceivable adornments of the samādhis of the bodhisattva realms.
They attain ultimate unimpeded discernment regarding inconceivable worlds,
turn toward the firm and pure karma of inconceivable bodhisattvas, and with deep resolve, uphold inconceivable vows of pure karma.
Gradually proceeding toward the south, he arrived at the country of Adorned Jambudvīpaśikhara, where he searched everywhere for the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja;
he saw him in a secluded place, sitting cross-legged, absorbed in samādhi, with his inhalation and exhalation extinguished, his body peaceful and unmoving, silent and without perception.

From beneath his feet, there emerged incalculable numbers of householders and incalculable numbers of brahmins, all wearing celestial crowns adorned with various jewels. Each carried exquisite treasures and the finest delicacies, as well as all manner of precious garments, perfumes, flowers, jeweled garlands, powdered incense, and unguents—requisites for life—to gather in the poor, comfort and welcome them, and rain down a multitude of precious objects;
causing all sentient beings to rejoice greatly, filling the ten directions.
From his two knees, there emerged Kṣatriyas and Brahmins, all of whom were wise;
their physical forms, dignified deportment, and ornamental attire were each distinct.

With subtle and wondrous voices, they instructed and guided sentient beings, leading them to abandon evil and cultivate goodness, to abide in the meaning of ultimate reality, and to expound the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), causing all beings to rejoice and filling the ten directions.
From both sides of his waist, there emerged as many five-attainment rishis as there are sentient beings;
some wore garments of grass, others wore garments of tree bark, all holding water jars and carrying triple-staffs, their deportment composed and orderly, without any change.

They traveled through the void, praising the Triple Gem and preaching pure Brahma-conduct for the sake of sentient beings. They subdued the sense faculties, expounded the true meaning, and gathered in the world, causing all sentient beings to enter the ocean of wisdom. Furthermore, they expounded various worldly treatises, leading them to abide successively in all roots of goodness and filling the ten directions.
From his two flanks issued forth inconceivable numbers of nāgas and inconceivable numbers of nāga maidens, manifesting inconceivable sovereign powers over all nāgas to gather in sentient beings;

they rained down inconceivable clouds of fragrant adornments, clouds of flower adornments, clouds of garland adornments, clouds of precious parasol adornments, clouds of precious banner adornments, clouds of various jewel adornments, clouds of priceless maṇi-jewel adornments, clouds of precious necklace adornments, clouds of precious throne adornments, clouds of precious palace adornments, clouds of precious lotus-flower adornments, clouds of precious crown adornments, clouds of celestial male forms adornments, and clouds of celestial female forms adornments.

Raining down such clouds as these, each inconceivable, they universally illumine all worlds throughout the ten directions, making offerings to all Tathāgatas and causing all sentient beings everywhere to experience great joy, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
From the syllable *De* on his chest, there emerged immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) asura kings, manifesting the inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers of asura kings;

they caused all the waters of the great oceans and hundreds of thousands of worlds to tremble, made all the kings of mountains collide with one another, shook all the celestial palaces, and eclipsed the radiance of all demons so that it appeared entirely like a mass of ink;
they subdued all demonic armies and eliminated the negligence and arrogance of sentient beings.
Free from anger and harmful intent, they extinguish unwholesome dharmas, shatter the mountains of affliction, and abandon strife;

furthermore, by means of their spiritual powers, they awaken sentient beings, causing them to weary of and leave all evils behind, forever severing birth and death, and remaining unattached to the various realms of existence;

they cause all beings everywhere to always delight in quiescent extinction, abide in the bodhicitta, purify the conduct of a bodhisattva, dwell in the various pāramitās, reach the ultimate bodhisattva stages, illuminate all dharmas, universally illumine the skillful means of all Buddhas, and fill the entire dharma-realm.
From his back emerge incalculable numbers of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, for the purpose of transforming sentient beings through the two vehicles:
those who cling to the view of self are taught the contemplation of impurity;
those with excessive desire are taught the contemplation of loving-kindness.
For those with an abundance of hatred, he teaches the contemplation of dependent origination;
for those with an abundance of delusion, he teaches skillful wisdom to observe all phenomena;
and for those with equal proportions of these afflictions, he expounds the Dharma of non-attachment.
For those attached to objective realms, they explain the realm of sublime vows;
for those who delight in quiescence, they teach entry into the various realms of existence;
and they benefit sentient beings, filling the entire dharma-realm.

From his two shoulders emerged incalculable numbers of yakṣa kings and rākṣasa kings with various evil bodies of diverse heights, forms, and colors, riding upon various vehicles and each surrounded by their own retinues.

For any sentient beings capable of practicing virtue, as well as for the assembly of noble sages and bodhisattvas—whether they were treading the right path or had attained the realization of the fruits—they all provided defense and protection. Some acted as Vajrapāṇi heroes to protect the Buddhas and the Buddha’s dwelling places;
and if there were sentient beings who encountered various terrors, they also protected them, causing them all to be free from fear.
May all who are afflicted by disease attain healing;
may all who are in distress be completely liberated;
may untimely deaths be eliminated and all fevers and afflictions be dispelled; and may sentient beings be transformed and taught so that they may obtain true benefit.
They shatter the wheel of birth and death, praise the wheel of Dharma, and crush the wheels of external paths, filling the entire dharma-realm.
From their bellies emerge hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kinnara kings, each surrounded by retinues of hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya kinnara queens;
they also emerge hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya gandharva kings, each surrounded by retinues of hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya gandharva queens.

They emitted hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya celestial sounds of entertainment, preaching the Dharma of the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*), praising all Buddhas, extolling bodhi and the practices of bodhisattvas, lauding the gates of bodhi, entering the gates of the wheel of Dharma (*dharmacakra*), delighting in all gates of sovereign mastery, expounding all gates of parinirvāṇa, upholding all gates of the Buddha-teachings, gladdening all sentient beings, purifying all buddha-fields, lecturing on all gates of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), eliminating all obstacles, and proclaiming and illuminating all gates of wholesome roots, filling the entire dharma-realm.

From his mouth, there emerged hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* wheel-turning sage-kings (*cakravartin*), fully endowed with the seven treasures and surrounded by the fourfold army. They emitted light of non-avarice and rained down *maṇi* jewels, causing all who were poor and suffering to become wealthy and joyful;
those who lacked the means for giving were enabled to practice charity.

For the sake of all living beings, they praised the dharmas of abstaining from killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct; they cultivated a mind of loving-kindness, constantly spoke words of affection, and brought benefit to sentient beings.
Eliminate false speech and distance oneself from harsh words;
gather in sentient beings and distance oneself from divisive speech;
speak words that promote harmony and abandon meaningless speech.
They preach the profound Dharma, causing all sentient beings to remain far removed from verbal transgressions;
they praise great compassion, causing sentient beings to rejoice and abandon hearts of anger;
they discern all correct dharmas of the world, observe causes and conditions, and illuminate the ultimate truth.

He extracts the poisonous thorns of false views from all sentient beings, eliminates doubt and confusion, and leaves behind all hindrances; he clarifies the true meaning of the Dharma, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
From his two eyes, he emits hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* suns that universally illuminate the ten directions, extinguishing all darkness;
he causes all sentient beings to eliminate defilement and obscurity, and to remain far removed from the bitter poisons of all evil realms.

They cause those who are cold to obtain warmth; in defiled buddha-fields, they emit bright and pure light, extensively illuminating all worlds—including those of gold, silver, and lapis lazuli—as well as all classes of sentient beings.
They eliminate the heavy darkness of the minds of sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice;
they are able to accomplish the immeasurable tasks of sentient beings, adorning the sublime realm of all worlds, filling the entire dharma-realm.
From between his eyebrows, there emerged hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya Indras, kings of the gods, adorned with immeasurable varieties of jewels;
they upheld the laws of the Śakra kings, universally illuminating all celestial palaces and shaking all Sumeru Kings of Mountains.

They caused all the devas within their celestial realms to give rise to a mind of weary detachment, to praise the power of merit, the power of clear wisdom, to arouse a mind of direct resolve, to increase a deep mind of resolve, to purify the power of mindfulness, and to make the bodhicitta firm. They led them to distance themselves from sensual pleasures, to praise the joy of beholding all Buddhas, and not to praise the joy of worldly realms.
They praise the joy of hearing the Dharma, which transcends worldly pleasure and is the joy of wisdom that observes all phenomena;
they are free from the terrors of battle with the asuras, extinguish the armies of afflictions, distance themselves from the fear of death, and vow to subdue the hosts of Māra;

they raise the mountain of the sublime Dharma and proclaim vast Dharma-phrases equal to Mount Sumeru, capable of discerning the immeasurable activities of sentient beings and filling the entire Dharma-realm.
From his forehead, there emerged immeasurable Brahmā deities, of exquisite and majestic appearance, peerless in the world;
their deportment was dignified and orderly as they produced sublime sounds to praise all Buddhas and entreat them to preach the Dharma;
they caused sentient beings to rejoice and were even able to accomplish the immeasurable tasks of sentient beings, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
From their heads emerged incalculable multitudes of bodhisattvas, with various forms and colors, their bodies adorned with the primary and secondary marks;
they emitted infinite nets of light, manifesting the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*), praising generosity, and remaining far removed from stinginess and attachment;

they adorned all worlds, extolled pure precepts, and distanced themselves from immoral conduct; they established sentient beings in the bodhisattva discipline, praised the Mahāyāna precepts, and brought forth the treasury of the merits of great compassion; they taught that all existing things are entirely like dreams, declared that the pleasures of the five desires have no true flavor, established sentient beings in the dharmas for leaving affliction behind, and praised and extolled the golden body-karma.
They praised the mind of loving-kindness, encouraging the abandonment of killing to extinguish rebirth in the animal realm;
they extolled the power of extensive learning, establishing sentient beings in the power of patience;
and they praised universal illumination and mastery, urging the abandonment of negligence and establishing sentient beings in heedfulness.
He praised the dhyāna-pāramitā, whereby the mind attains mastery and the thorns of false views are extracted;

he extolled the right-view prajñā-pāramitā, which delights in the mastery of wisdom, praises conformity with the world while remaining far removed from birth and death, and enables one to take birth at will within the various realms of existence;
he praised the fulfillment of the power of vows, which brings forth the supernormal powers, clarities, mastery, and longevity.
They praised the power of all dhāraṇīs, the arising of the power of vows, and the power of pure samādhi that manifests sovereign birth;
they praised wisdom, which universally illumines the faculties of all sentient beings, discerns and expounds upon all mental states and activities, and illuminates the knowledge of the ten powers;
they praised the sovereignty of sarvajñā (omniscience), which fills the dharma-realm.

From the crown of his head, there emerged hundreds of thousands of asaṃkhyeya Buddhas, their bodies complete and adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, like mountains of gold illuminating all things;
they emitted wondrous sounds that filled the entire Dharma-realm.
Manifesting immeasurable and boundless mastery of spiritual powers, they universally rain down clouds of all ambrosial Dharma:
for Bodhisattvas seated at the site of enlightenment, they rain down clouds of the Dharma of equality;
for Bodhisattvas who have received empowerment, they rain down clouds of the Dharma of universal gates.
For Bodhisattvas of Deep Patience, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of Universal Adornment;
for Bodhisattvas of the Stage of Youthful Truth, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of the Solid Mountain;
for Bodhisattvas Who Never Retreat, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of the Ocean Treasury.
For Bodhisattvas who have achieved a straightforward mind, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of universal realms;
for Bodhisattvas on the path of skillful means, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of the sounds of their own fundamental nature;
for Bodhisattvas born of noble lineage, he rains down the Dharma-cloud that accords with the world.
For bodhisattvas who are practicing, they rain down the dharma-cloud of renunciation;
for bodhisattvas who have purified the stages, they rain down the dharma-cloud of the treasury of nourishing dharmas;
for bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds, they rain down the dharma-cloud of diligence.
For those who practice through faith, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of the inexhaustible gate;
for sentient beings of the form realm, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of inexhaustible equanimity;
for the Great Brahma heavens, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of the universal treasury.
For the Mahāśvara devas, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of the method for generating power;
for the Māra kings, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of the mind-banner;
for the Nirmāṇarati devas, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of pure mindfulness.
For the Tuṣita Heaven, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of pure intention;
for the Yāma Heaven, they rain down the Dharma-cloud of joy;
for the Śakra Heaven, they rain down the Dharma-cloud that adorns space.
As a yakṣa king, he rains down the dharma-cloud of joy;
as a gandharva king, he rains down the dharma-cloud of sovereign perfection;
as an asura king, he rains down the dharma-cloud of the great realm.
As a king of the garuḍas, he rains down clouds of Dharma upon immeasurable worlds;
as a king of the kiṃnaras, he rains down clouds of the supreme wisdom that benefits sentient beings;
as a king of men, he rains down clouds of the Dharma of non-delight.
For the dragon kings, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of the Banner of Joy;
for the mahoraga kings, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of Quiescence;
for the sentient beings in the hells, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of the Adornment of Undistracted Mindfulness.
For the sake of all animals, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of wisdom;
for the realm of King Yama, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of fearlessness;
for the realm of hungry ghosts, he rains down the Dharma-cloud of correct aspiration.
They cause all sentient beings to turn toward the gate of the noble ones, filling the entire Dharma-realm.

From each and every pore of those Tathāgatas, they each emit incalculable nets of pure light, incalculable exquisite colors, incalculable adornments, and incalculable realms, performing incalculable deeds that fill the ten directions.
At that time, Sudhana single-mindedly observed the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, recollecting his dharma-gate of samādhi;
he contemplated the inconceivable realm of the bodhisattvas;
and he contemplated the immeasurable, effortless, present adornment of the universal gate dharma-gate.
They contemplate the wisdom that adorns the dharma-realm;
abiding by the Buddha-wisdom, they manifest the power of bodhisattvas, establish the power of bodhisattva vows, and expand the various practices of bodhisattvas.
Observing in this manner correctly for one day and night, up to seven days and nights;
for half a month and one month, up to six months and six days;
after this had passed, the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja arose from samādhi.
At that time, Sudhana marveled at what he had never before experienced; joining his palms, he said:
"How extraordinary!
O Great Sage!"
This samādhi is the most profound; this samādhi is the most vast;
this samādhi has immeasurable spheres of experience.
This samādhi possesses inconceivable mastery of supernatural power; this samādhi is immeasurable;
this samādhi is pure with the radiance of wisdom.
This samādhi is adorned with incalculable adornments;
this samādhi has an indestructible sphere of activity;
this samādhi is without regression.
This samādhi universally illumines all worlds throughout the ten directions;
this samādhi possesses immeasurable meanings and skillful means.
O Great Sage!

When there are bodhisattvas who enter this samādhi, they are able to eliminate all suffering for all beings, forever severing the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals, as well as all torments and poisons; they remain far removed from all calamities;
they cause the realms of devas and humans to attain complete tranquility;
they cause sentient beings to rejoice and always delight in the profound realm of meditative concentration, becoming weary of and detached from the conditioned, and transcending the triple world.
They give rise to the bodhicitta, nurturing the causes and conditions for the merit of wisdom; they nurture and expand the unsurpassed great compassion;
they generate the power of great vows to illuminate the path of the bodhisattvas;
they adorn the great pāramitās with wisdom, ultimately giving birth to the realm of the Mahāyāna.
With wisdom that shines universally upon the conduct of Samantabhadra, one attains the light of wisdom of the various bodhisattva stages;
endowed with all the pure vows and practices of a bodhisattva, one realizes the realm of omniscience.
“Great Sage! What is the name of this samādhi? “Good son!”
This samādhi is named "Universal Eye of Renunciation and Attainment," and it is also named "The Sphere of Pure Radiance Prajñāpāramitā," and it is also named "Pure Adornment of the Universal Gate."
"Good son! By practicing the Prajñāpāramitā, one attains this samādhi;
upon attaining this samādhi, one immediately attains ten million asaṃkhyeya samādhis."
“Great Sage! Does this samādhi possess only these meritorious spheres of activity, or are there others? “Good son!”
This samādhi discerns all worlds without obstruction; it exhaustively penetrates all worlds without obstruction;
it traverses all worlds without obstruction.
Adorning all worlds without obstruction; cultivating and purifying all worlds without obstruction;
making all worlds pure and serene without obstruction.
They behold all buddhas without obstruction;
they contemplate the merits of all buddhas without obstruction; they know the sovereign spiritual powers of all buddhas without obstruction;
and they exhaustively realize the powers of all buddhas without obstruction.
They cross the great ocean of the merits of all Buddhas without obstruction;
they rain down the pure and wondrous Dharma-clouds of all Buddhas without obstruction;
they master all Buddha-dharmas without obstruction.
They attain the wisdom of all Buddhas for turning the wheel of Dharma, which is indestructible and without obstruction;
they attain the source and depth of the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas, which is without obstruction;
and they accordingly and universally enter the worlds of the ten directions, which is without obstruction.
He observes the Buddha-dharma of the ten directions in accordance with reality without obstruction;
he gathers in sentient beings of the ten directions through great compassion without obstruction;
and his great loving-kindness fills the worlds of the ten directions without obstruction.
They behold the Buddhas of the ten directions with a mind that never tires or becomes weary, remaining free from all obstructions;
they follow and enter the great ocean of sentient beings in accordance with their needs, remaining free from all obstructions;
they thoroughly understand the entire ocean of the faculties of sentient beings, remaining free from all obstructions.
I discern the oceans of all sentient beings without any obstruction.
Good son, I know only this Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Pure Radiance of Prajñāpāramitā; how could I possibly explain the ultimate practices of the great Bodhisattvas?
All these great Bodhisattvas have deeply entered the great ocean of wisdom and are well able to discern the pure Dharma-realm;
their wisdom reaches the ultimate destination of all phenomena, and the light of their insight is immeasurable, filling all things;

they have attained the sovereign radiance of great dharanis, and all their samadhis are perfectly pure; they give rise to all sovereign supernormal powers and clarities, deeply enter the inexhaustible ocean of eloquence, and with a thunderous resonance that vibrates through all stages, they are fully able to rescue and protect all sentient beings.
I cannot even describe their conduct, much less their merits?

How could I reveal their sphere, explain their sphere, illuminate their dharma-gates, clarify their accumulated treasuries of merit, or speak of the streams of samādhis and the impartial wisdom of their true path?
"Noble son! To the south of here, there is a dwelling place named Sea Tide;
there is a grove there named Universally Adorned."
"There is a laywoman named Śreṣṭhadattā.
Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva cultivates the bodhisattva path and purifies the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the youth Sudhana was filled with immeasurable joy; in the presence of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, he attained firmness within what was previously unstable.
Within the unreal, they attain the real;
reaching the realm of the ultimate treasury of merit, they obtain clear and pure wisdom that universally illumines all things;
they attain the radiance of profound samādhi and reach the liberation of purity.
He skillfully observed all worlds, purifying the gateways to the Dharma;
with clear and pure wisdom, he shone universally throughout the ten directions.
Prostrating his head at [the Buddha’s] feet, he circumambulated him countless times, gazing up at him with veneration before taking his leave and traveling south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana contemplated the bhikṣu Sāgaramegha with right mindfulness, never ceasing in his thoughts; he delighted in seeing him without weariness, yearning for the sage’s voice and visualizing his compassionate countenance.
With right mindfulness, he contemplated the scope of his mind, the scope of his samādhis, and the scope of his vows and practices;
with right mindfulness, he contemplated his luminous and pure wisdom, revered the spiritual friend, turned toward the spiritual friend, and recollected the teachings of the spiritual friend.
One should give rise to love and reverence toward spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra),
and further reflect:
"It is by means of spiritual friends that one is able to see all Buddhas."
A spiritual friend reveals and manifests all Buddha-dharmas;
a spiritual friend is a marvelous dharma, for they enable people to perceive the dharmas of all Buddhas;
a spiritual friend is a bright and pure eye, enabling people to see the Buddhas as vast as space.
"A spiritual friend is a virtuous ferry that enables people to reach the source and bottom of the Buddha’s lotus pond.
Gradually traveling south, he arrived at the place where the ocean tides meet and saw the Universally Adorned Garden;
it was surrounded on all sides by walls made of the seven treasures.
Various exquisite jewel trees stood in rows, forming a magnificent adornment;
all the flower trees rained down blossoms like clouds, scattering them across the ground;

Garland-trees hung down garlands, and jewel-trees rained down jewels, adorning everything everywhere;

It was adorned with such various precious playthings as these.
Within this grove, there were ten thousand lecture halls composed of many jewels,

There were ten thousand palaces, adorned with the Vaiḍūrya-vairocana treasure-trove;

The water of eight virtues is serene and fills it to the brim;

Ratna-tāla trees stand in rows all around;
wild ducks, geese, mandarin ducks, peacocks, and sorrowful pheasants— various species of birds— sport within them,

The wind arose spontaneously, producing subtle and wondrous sounds;
canopies of various jewels were set up, and jeweled trees surrounded them on all sides.

Black sandalwood mud solidified and accumulated at the bottom of the pond;

from those lotuses, a great radiance issued forth, universally illuminating all things.
Within that grove of trees, there is a great palace named Adorned Banner;

and its lapis lazuli pillars are exquisitely adorned, towering and lofty like a mountain of gold.
All sentient beings who see them experience nothing but joy and delight.
There are incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) pure maṇi-jewels that universally illuminate all things;
they emit natural fragrances, namely:

the radiance of night-light *maṇi*, the radiance of the pure jewel of sun-treasury *maṇi*, the radiance of the wondrous jewel of moon-banner *maṇi*, the radiance of fragrant flames, the radiance of the wondrous treasury *maṇi* jewel, the radiance of *padma*, the radiance of the pure jewel of night-light *maṇi*, the radiance of the pure jewel of great lamp *maṇi*, and the radiance of the *maṇi* that universally illuminates all directions.
Furthermore, ten kinds of great fragrant lightning-flashes issued forth, raining down ten kinds of clouds that surpassed those of all the devas; namely:
