She always delights in hearing the Dharma.
At that time, the laywoman Śroṇā sat upon a golden-treasury seat, her body draped with a net of jewel-adorned ocean-treasury ornaments;
adorned with kinnara ornaments, she surpassed all the devas.
A great net of mani-jewels adorned his head;
lion-shaped jewel-pearls and immeasurable wish-fulfilling pure mani-gems embellished his body;
surrounded by a multitude of immeasurable billions who paid him respectful homage, they stood with palms joined.

Countless sentient beings from the eastern direction—Brahmā kings, Mahābrahmās, Brahmā-purohitas, Paranirmita-vaśavartin kings, and so forth, including humans and non-humans, as well as all various kings—came to his presence;
the same was true for the southern, western, and northern directions, the four intermediate points, and the zenith and nadir.
Whoever beholds this upāsikā shall have all their various ailments completely healed;
their minds will become pure and free from defilement, they will extract the thorns of wrong views, eliminate obstacles, and purify the stage of non-obstruction.

Within that stage, they nurture roots of goodness and bring the faculties to fulfillment. Through skillful means, they encompass all-knowledge; all doors of dhāraṇī and all doors of samādhi appear before them. They give rise to all doors of vows, perfect all doors of practice, and produce all doors of purity.
Their minds are vast, giving birth to all things; they attain an unobstructed body that reaches everywhere.
At that time, the youth Sudhana entered the Universally Adorned Garden and surveyed it thoroughly. There he saw the laywoman Śrīprabhā seated upon a golden throne;
he approached her, prostrated himself at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and said to her:
"O Noble One!"

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path; I only pray that you will explain this fully for me.
He replied: "Good son!
I have accomplished but a single dharma-gate; for those who see, hear, remember, know, or draw near to me, none shall go in vain."

"Good son! If there are sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness, who do not draw near to spiritual friends, and who are not protected and remembered by the Buddhas, those sentient beings are unable to see me."
"Good son! If there are sentient beings who are able to see me, they shall attain non-retrogression regarding Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
The Buddhas of the eastern direction constantly come to my place, sit upon jeweled lion thrones, and preach the Dharma for me;
likewise, all the Buddhas of the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir, all come to my place, sit upon jeweled lion thrones, and preach the Dharma for me.
"Good son! I constantly see all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; I have never been separated from them. Good son!"
In this great assembly of mine, there are eighty-four thousand billion bodhisattvas, all my fellow practitioners who have attained non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
likewise, all the members of this entire gathering in the Universally Adorned Garden have also attained non-retrogression from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Sudhana said: "O Great Sage!
How long has it been since you first resolved to attain Bodhicitta?"
He replied, "Good son! I recall that in the past,
at the place of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I left the household life to seek the Way, purely cultivated the Brahma-faring, paid respectful offerings, and heard and upheld the Dharma."
Next, in the presence of the Buddha Vigatamala, he left the household life to seek the Way, purely cultivating the Brahma-faring, reverently making offerings, hearing the Dharma, and upholding it;
subsequently, he did so in the presence of the Buddhas Citradhvaja, Guṇakīrti, Guṇagarbha, Vairocana, Samantacakṣus, Brahmapāla, Vaśavartin, and Sudeva.

"Good son! In the presence of as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in thirty-six Ganges Rivers, I left the household life to seek the Way, purely cultivated the Brahma-faring, paid respectful offerings, heard and upheld the Dharma, and fully understood the wisdom of all Buddhas."
At the initial arousal of the bodhicitta, they fill the dharma-realm, embracing sentient beings with immeasurable great compassion;

they give rise to the immeasurable great vows of all bodhisattvas, reaching the ultimate limits of the dharma-realm throughout the ten directions, universally covering all sentient beings with immeasurable great compassion.

Throughout all lands and throughout all eons, they cultivate the immeasurable practices of bodhisattvas and the power of immeasurable samādhis, never abandoning nor turning back from the true path of bodhisattvas;
they possess the immeasurable power of bodhisattva dhāraṇīs, skillfully able to protect and sustain all sentient beings;
and they possess the immeasurable power of pure wisdom, using skillful means and right mindfulness to universally illumine the three periods of time.
By means of the power of the bodhisattva’s immeasurable supernormal knowledges and clarities, they travel throughout all networks of worlds;
by means of the power of the bodhisattva’s immeasurable eloquence, they are able to gladden all assemblies with a single word.
“Good son! I possess the bodhisattva’s immeasurable power of sovereign spiritual transformations, by which I am able to fill all lands with a single body. Sudhana said:
“Great Sage! How long will it be before you shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi? “Good son!
A bodhisattva does not resolve upon awakening (bodhicitta) for the sake of teaching and transforming a single sentient being;
nor for the sake of teaching and transforming a hundred sentient beings, up to and including an unspeakably unspeakable number of times more sentient beings;
as explained at length in the *Asaṃkhyeya-parivarta*, they do not resolve upon awakening for the sake of teaching and transforming the sentient beings of a single world-system.
Furthermore, they do not resolve upon *bodhicitta* for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds;

nor do they resolve upon *bodhicitta* for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings equal in number to the atoms of Jambudvīpa, nor for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings equal in number to the atoms of a trichiliocosm, nor even for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings equal in number to the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of trichiliocosms;
nor does a Bodhisattva resolve upon *bodhicitta* for the sake of honoring and making offerings to a single Tathāgata.
They do not generate the bodhicitta for the sake of honoring and making offerings to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Tathāgatas;
the Bodhisattva does not generate the bodhicitta for the sake of purifying a single buddha-field,
nor even for the sake of purifying unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields.
A bodhisattva does not resolve upon awakening for the sake of purifying as many lands as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa;
nor do they resolve upon awakening even for the sake of purifying as many lands as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of trichiliocosms;
nor does a bodhisattva resolve upon awakening for the sake of protecting and upholding the Dharma of a single Buddha.

As explained in detail above, a bodhisattva does not resolve to attain bodhicitta for the sake of fulfilling a single vow; nor for the sake of adorning a single buddha-field; nor for the sake of knowing the retinue of a single Buddha;

nor for the sake of upholding a single teaching of the Buddha; nor for the sake of knowing the ocean of the minds of a single sentient being; nor for the sake of crossing over the ocean of the faculties of a single sentient being; nor for the sake of knowing the sequence of the formation and destruction of kalpas in a single world-system; nor for the sake of knowing the afflictions and habitual tendencies of a single sentient being; nor for the sake of severing the afflictions of a single sentient being; nor for the sake of fulfilling the practices of a single sentient being.
Rather, one resolves to attain bodhicitta because of the desire to teach and transform all sentient beings.

One generates the bodhicitta because one wishes to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas; because one wishes to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields; because one wishes to protect, uphold, and maintain all Buddha-dharmas; because one wishes to fulfill all great vows; because one wishes to know all the retinues of the Buddhas; because one wishes to know the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings; because one wishes to know the mental activities and movements of the minds of all sentient beings; because one wishes to know the wheels of the faculties of all sentient beings; because one wishes to know the sequence of the formation and destruction of all worlds throughout all kalpas; because one wishes to know the afflictions and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings; because one wishes to sever the afflictions of all sentient beings; and because one wishes to fulfill the practices of all sentient beings.

"Noble son! Briefly stated, there are as many as ten million asaṃkhyeya skillful means (upāya-mukha) such as these belonging to bodhisattvas; a bodhisattva should thoroughly understand them all and accord with wisdom.
They should ultimately cultivate the equal practices of a bodhisattva, purify all buddha-fields, and remain free from mental delusion."
"Good son! For this reason, I have made this vow: to purify all buddha-fields, and my vow shall then be fulfilled;
to sever the afflictions and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings, and my vow shall then be fulfilled."
“Great Sage! What is the name of this Dharma-gate? “Good son!”
This dharma door is named "Banner of Freedom from Sorrow and Peaceful Stability.
I know only this single dharma door; as for the great bodhisattvas whose minds are like the ocean and who are able to contain all Buddha-dharmas, how could I possibly know their conduct?
The minds of all bodhisattvas are firm and upright, like Mount Sumeru;
these great bodhisattvas are like medicinal herbs for vision—if anyone beholds them, their afflictions are extinguished;
these great bodhisattvas are like the pure sun, dispelling the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings.
The great Bodhisattvas are like the great earth, for they are able to support and sustain all sentient beings;
the great Bodhisattvas are like the wind of wisdom, for they nurture the true meaning of all sentient beings;
the great Bodhisattvas are like sovereign lords, for they universally illumine all things with the light of pure wisdom.
The great Bodhisattvas are like auspicious clouds, raining down the Dharma of ambrosia according to the needs of beings;
the great Bodhisattvas are like the pure moon, emitting nets of light from all their merits;
the great Bodhisattvas are like Śakra, capable of protecting all sentient beings.
"How shall I be able to know his conduct? Good son,
to the south of here, there is a land called Sāgaratīra."
“There is a seer there named Vimalatara, who is well able to explain the various practices of Bodhisattvas; you should go to him and ask.

Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and gazed upon him without weariness. Weeping with tears of compassion, he reflected with right mindfulness:

“It is difficult to attain Bodhi; it is difficult to encounter a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra); it is difficult to dwell together with such a superior person; it is difficult to obtain the faculties of a Bodhisattva; it is difficult to fulfill the upright mind of a Bodhisattva; it is difficult to meet a spiritual friend of like-minded intent; it is difficult to contemplate reality; it is difficult to receive the correct teaching according to the Dharma; it is difficult to give birth to the wondrous mind; it is difficult to keep omniscience in mind; and it is difficult to nurture the light of the Dharma.”
Having formed this thought, he took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana contemplated and followed the true teachings of the Bodhisattvas, purifying the Bodhisattva practices, and his mind was able to nurture the power of Bodhisattva virtues;
his mind beheld all Buddhas.
The mind desires Bodhi;
the mind is able to initiate and nurture great vows;
the mind illuminates all dharmas throughout the ten directions.
The mind perceives the reality of phenomena;
the mind covers all things without distraction;
the mind is pure wisdom, contemplating the dharma-realm and extinguishing the darkness of ignorance.
With a mind pure and upright, he eliminated all obstacles;
his mind was able to subdue all Māras.
Traveling by degrees, he reached the kingdom of Sāgaratīra and searched everywhere for the seer Vimalacitra.
At that time, that seer was in a great forest;
this forest was adorned with incalculable trees, covered everywhere with precious leaves,
and constantly embellished by various flowering and fruit-bearing trees.
Jeweled trees rained down treasures, scattering them everywhere across the ground;
great sandalwood trees stood in rows all around;
and various aloeswood trees constantly emitted exquisite fragrances.
Nyagrodha trees and Jambūnada trees rained down sweetly fragrant fruits;
and Utpala, Padma, and Puṇḍarīka lotuses served as adornments.
At that time, Sudhana saw the seer in this forest, wearing garments of tree bark, with matted hair and seated upon grass;
ten thousand seers were his retinue, like a sandalwood grove surrounded by sandalwood trees.
He went to where [the spiritual friend] was and prostrated himself with his five limbs in reverence, saying:
"I call to mind the spiritual friend, who can open for me the gateway to *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge);
I call to mind the spiritual friend, who manifests the true path."
I reflect upon the spiritual friend, who can establish me on the ground of all-knowledge;
I reflect upon the spiritual friend, who kindles the jewel-lamp of wisdom, whose pure and radiant light of insight nourishes the luminous wisdom of the ten powers;
the path of the spiritual friend is the inexhaustible treasury of all-knowledge.
A spiritual friend is a lamp, for it illuminates the realm of all-knowledge;
a spiritual friend is a bridge, for it carries one across birth and death;
a spiritual friend is a parasol, for it generates the power of great compassion to cover all beings.
"A spiritual friend is not in vain, for they illuminate the true nature of all phenomena;
a spiritual friend is like the ocean tide, for they fulfill great compassion.
Having formed this thought, he circumambulated him countless times, stood with palms joined, and said:

At that time, the seer surveyed the great assembly and spoke these words:
"You should know that this youth has already resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; he invites all sentient beings to universally bestow fearlessness and benefits all sentient beings;
he is directed toward the ocean of profound wisdom, desiring to drink the rain of the Dharma of all Buddhas."
Desiring to exhaust the source and bottom of the ocean of all phenomena;
desiring to accomplish the great ocean of worldly wisdom;
desiring to raise the heavy clouds of great compassion;
They desire to rain down the Dharma-rain of ambrosia;
they desire the world-transcending, luminous, and pure moon of wisdom;
they desire to extinguish the darkness of all worldly afflictions.
"I wish to nurture the roots of goodness in all sentient beings.
At that time, the great assembly each took various kinds of exquisite golden flowers, whose fragrance was most delightful, and scattered them over the boy;
they prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, circumambulated him with bowed bodies in reverence, and spoke these words:
"This youth is fully capable of protecting and delivering all sentient beings; he extinguishes the three evil realms and frees them from all the perils of the realm of Yama;
he dries up the ocean of desire, eliminates the aggregates of suffering, abandons the darkness of ignorance, and severs the bonds of craving;

he can ascend the Vajra-encircled mountain of merit and establish the Sumeru of wisdom in the world; he brings forth the bright and pure sun of knowledge in the world, illuminating all dharmas of the roots of goodness and guiding the world to clearly discern what is wholesome and what is unwholesome."
At that time, the seer addressed the great assembly, saying:
"If there are those who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they shall obtain all-knowledge and purify the ground of all Buddha-merits."
Then, that rishi said to Sudhana: "Noble son!
I have attained the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the wisdom of the indestructible banner."
Sudhana said: "O Great Sage! As for that Dharma-door, what is its sphere of activity?"
Then, that rishi extended his right hand and stroked Sudhana’s head;
having done so, he took Sudhana’s hand.

At that very moment, Sudhana saw himself before Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-worlds of the ten directions. He beheld those Buddhas, adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, and their lands were adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) precious jewels and playthings.

Furthermore, they see the great ocean-like assembly of that Buddha’s retinue; the Dharma they hear from them they are able to receive and uphold entirely, not losing even a single phrase or a single flavor. They discerningly uphold the Brahma-wheel of the True Dharma, receive the clouds of all dharmas, enter the great vows of the Buddhas, purely cultivate the various powers, purify their vows and practices, and bring the treasuries of all merits to ultimate fulfillment.
He beholds those Buddhas, transforming and delivering all sentient beings according to their needs; he beholds all Buddhas as a pure and perfect great net of light.
Having seen this, he accords with the unimpeded light of wisdom and reaches the ultimate power of the Buddhas;
or he sees his own body before a single Buddha for one day and one night.
Or again, they may see themselves in the presence of other Buddhas for seven days and seven nights.
In this manner, they proceed sequentially through the presence of other Buddhas for half a month, one month, one year, a hundred years, a thousand years;
or for a hundred thousand years, or even a hundred thousand *koṭis* of years.
Or for ten billion nayutas of years;
or for half an eon, one eon, a hundred eons, a thousand eons, or a hundred thousand eons;
or for ten billion nayutas of eons, even up to unspeakably unspeakable nayutas of eons.
For as many eons as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, even up to eons equal to the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds,
at that time, because he was illumined by the dharma-gate of indestructible-banner wisdom, Sudhana attained the samādhi of the luminous pure treasury;
and because he was illumined by the samādhi of the inexhaustible dharma-gate, he attained the light of the dhāraṇī for roaming through all directions.

Because the Dharma-gate of the Perfect Radiance of Vajra illumines, one attains the Samādhi of the Pavilion of the Discerning Wisdom-Mind and dwells in the Treasury of Dharma Adorned by the Level Ground;
because the diligence of Prajñāpāramitā illumines, one attains the radiance of the Buddha’s Gaganagañja Samādhi;
because the radiance of the Samādhis of the Dharma-wheels of all Buddhas mutually illumines, one attains the inexhaustible radiance of the perfect wisdom of the three periods of time.
Then, that rishi released Sudhana’s hand;
at that moment, Sudhana saw himself returned to his original place. Then, the rishi asked Sudhana:
"Do you remember? He replied, "Indeed, I do."
"It is by the power of the Great Sage, the Good Spiritual Friend. "Good son!
I know only this Dharma-door of the wisdom of the indestructible banner of the bodhisattva; how could I possibly know the conduct of the great bodhisattvas?"
All these great Bodhisattvas have attained the Samādhi of Sovereignty over All Sentient Beings and have gained mastery over the wheel of all times;
they give birth to the inexhaustible wisdom of all Buddhas, realize all Buddhas, and purify the lamp of wisdom;
within a single thought-moment, they comprehend the events of the three periods of time.
Throughout all worlds, they manifest bodies of pure wisdom that fill the dharma-realm; according to the needs of sentient beings, they appear before them all.
They thoroughly understand the conduct of all sentient beings, which is perfectly pure and entirely delightful.

How could I possibly know the conduct of the great bodhisattvas, their wondrous merits and vows, their adornment and purification of buddha-fields, their skillful examination of the capacities of beings, and the sphere of their wisdom;
their profound samādhis, their sovereign spiritual powers, and the realm of their liberation;
their playful exercise of supernormal faculties, the sounds of their dharma-body, and their ultimate wisdom?
Matters such as these are not within my sphere of experience. Good son!
To the south of here, there is a land named Jinqiu (Seeking Progress).
"There is a brahmin named Upāyendrayaśas.
Go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva advance toward the bodhisattva path and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

At that time, the youth Sudhana was filled with immeasurable joy; having paid his respects with reverence, he circumambulated him countless times, gazing up at him with deep observation, and then took his leave to travel south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana was illuminated by the dharma-gate of indestructible banner-like wisdom; he decisively realized the inconceivable sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas and thoroughly understood the inconceivable dharma-gates of Bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, by illuminating their minds with the inconceivable samādhi and wisdom of bodhisattvas, they attain the radiance of samādhi at all times, the radiance of the realm of samādhi in all its aspects, and clear, pure knowledge.
May all sentient beings attain supreme and wondrous states;
may they attain the Dharma-gate of the path leading to all destinations;
and may they act in accordance with the ways of the world, their minds free from duality.
Illuminating all spheres with clear and pure wisdom, they attain the treasury of clear and pure patience of all śrāvakas;
they attain the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and know the true reality (*dharmatā*) of phenomena;
they constantly practice the bodhisattva deeds, never forsaking the bodhisattva mind, and increase the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñā-citta*).
They attain the light of the ten powers, which universally illumines all;
they delight in the sublime sound of the Dharma, their minds never wearying of it;

they practice according to the teaching, abide in *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), and reach the ultimate realm of omniscience; they give rise to the immeasurable ornaments of the bodhisattva mind and fulfill the pure great vows of a bodhisattva.
In a single moment of thought, they reach all the networks of Buddha-fields, teaching and bringing to maturity an ocean of infinite sentient beings without weariness of mind;

they see the entire range of the immeasurable practices of Bodhisattvas, clearly discerning and seeing all worlds, and beholding the various adornments of all Buddha-fields, being able to place infinite worlds within even the most subtle of realms.
Furthermore, they are able to see their various adornments and can fully discern the countless worlds and all systems of language therein.

They also know the inclinations and desires of immeasurable sentient beings and understand the infinite conduct of those beings; using immeasurable skillful means, they teach and transform sentient beings, being well-versed in diverse regions and delivering them according to what is appropriate for each, while remaining mindful of spiritual friends.
Gradually traveling on, he arrived at the kingdom of Jinqu (Seeking Progress) and searched everywhere for that brahmin.

At that time, the brahmin was practicing various ascetic penances in his quest for omniscience; around him were masses of fire like great mountains, and in their midst stood a mountain of blades, towering and infinitely steep.
From that mountain, he threw himself into a mass of fire.
At that time, Sudhana went to the brahmin, prostrated with his head at his feet, stood with palms joined, and said:
"O Great Sage!"

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice or cultivate the bodhisattva path; I pray that you will explain this to me.
He replied: "Good son!
If you can now ascend this mountain of blades and cast yourself into this mass of fire, all the practices of a bodhisattva will be completely purified."

At that time, Sudhana thought to himself: "It is difficult to obtain a human body; it is difficult to be free from all calamities; it is difficult to attain a state free from calamities; it is difficult to encounter the pure Dharma; it is difficult to meet a Buddha in the world; it is difficult to possess all the sense faculties; it is difficult to hear the Buddha’s teachings; it is difficult to encounter a spiritual friend; it is difficult to dwell together with one; it is difficult to hear the true instruction; it is difficult to obtain a righteous livelihood; and it is difficult to proceed in accordance with the True Dharma."
"Is this not Mara, or one sent by Mara?
Is this not someone who is not a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) appearing in the guise of one, but rather a wicked bodhisattva?
For now he creates obstacles for my life-span, obstacles for my roots of goodness, and obstacles for all-knowledge (sarvajñatā); this is surely no orthodox teaching, but a perilous and evil path."
“The dharma-gate of distancing oneself from all Buddha-dharmas, such as omniscience (*sarvajñā*) and the like.
While he was thinking this, one hundred thousand Brahmā devas in the midst of the sky spoke these words: “O noble son!
Do not harbor such thoughts;
do not harbor such thoughts.
This is a Great Sage, fully endowed with the radiance of adamantine wisdom, possessing non-retrogressive diligence, having completely perfected all realms.
They wish to exhaust the great ocean of craving and attachment of all sentient beings;
they wish to tear asunder the net of all false views;
they wish to incinerate the afflictions of all sentient beings, eliminate the darkness of ignorance, and universally illuminate all things.

"May all sentient beings be freed from the perils of birth and death; may the darkness of ignorance throughout the three periods of time be extinguished; and may pure radiance be emitted to universally illumine all.
At that time, the Brahmā deities, the Īśvara deities, the Prajāpati deities, and the various deities of false views spoke thus:
"I created sentient beings; I am the most excellent in all the world; I am the highest; I am the foremost."
When these devas saw the brahmin practicing such great asceticism— tormenting his body with the five fires—
and having seen this, they found no further relish in their respective meditative absorptions and came to where he was.
At that time, the brahmin, through his power of mastery, preached the Dharma for them, causing them to extinguish false views and abandon the notion of self;
he inspired great compassion to universally cover all sentient beings and nurtured the upright mind of bodhi.
They open four kinds of paths to seek the Buddha’s Dharma-body;
according to those who are to be transformed, they are able to manifest the Buddha’s subtle and wondrous voice, which all hear without any obstruction.
Furthermore, ten thousand māras were in the sky, scattering various maṇi-jewel flowers over the brahmin and addressing Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!
"By the power of his ascetic practices, this brahmin emitted such great radiance that all the ornaments of my palace became like a mass of ink.
I no longer took pleasure [in them], and so, surrounded by an immeasurable retinue of heavenly maidens and celestial beings, I went to where he was.
He preached the Dharma for me, and I attained the stage of non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
Furthermore, ten thousand gods from the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations were in the sky, each holding celestial flowers to offer with reverence, saying these words:
"O son of good family!
By the power of his ascetic practices, this brahmin emitted a great radiance that rendered all the ornaments of my palace as dark as a mass of ink.

I no longer took pleasure [in them], and so I went with my retinue to where he was. He preached the Dharma for me, causing me to attain mastery over the mind, mastery over the afflictions, mastery over rebirth, mastery in the elimination of obstacles, mastery in all samādhis, mastery in ornaments, mastery in the span of life, and even mastery in all Buddha-dharmas.
Furthermore, ten thousand gods of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven were in the air, making offerings with celestial music and performing this speech:
"O Son of Good Family!
This brāhmaṇa, performing the austerity of scorching his body with the five fires, emitted a great radiance that illuminated my palace and its ornaments.

Having shone upon them, it caused all of us to take no pleasure in the five desires and to seek no sensual gratification; our bodies and minds became supple, and together with our retinues, we came to where he was.
He preached the Dharma for us, [inducing] a pure mind, a luminously pure mind, a virtuous and extraordinary mind, a supple mind, and a joyful mind.
...until they attain the pure ten powers, nurture the state of transcendence, and give birth to immeasurable, pure bodies;
until they attain the Buddha’s pure Dharma-body;
and attain a pure mouth with subtle and wondrous voices that reach everywhere without obstruction.
"Up until the attainment of all-knowledge.

Furthermore, ten thousand Tuṣita devas, together with their retinues, were in the midst of the sky, raining down clouds of all kinds of powdered incense as a respectful offering, and spoke these words:
"O Son of Good Family!
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five heats, I, within my palace, found no joy for even a moment and came to his side;

he expounded for me the Dharma of non-attachment, the practice of few desires and contentment, the cultivation of roots of goodness, the arousal of the bodhicitta, and everything up to the ultimate realization of all Buddha-dharmas.

Furthermore, ten thousand devas from the Trāyastriṃśa heaven and the asuras, together with their retinues, were in the midst of the sky, raining down clouds of māndārava flowers and clouds of mahāmāndārava flowers, making offerings with reverence and saying these words:
"O son of good family!
When this Brahmin was performing the austerity of scorching his body with the five fires, I felt no attachment to celestial pleasures for even a moment and went to where he was.
He preached the Dharma to me, teaching me to remain far removed from sensual pleasures;
he even taught me the Dharma of impermanence—that all things change and do not abide—and thereby caused me to sever all heedlessness and arrogance, while nurturing and giving rise to the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, noble son!
When I saw this brahmin, the summit of Mount Sumeru shook in six ways;
at that time, my heart was filled with great terror, and I single-mindedly sought all-knowledge.
Furthermore, there were ten thousand great nāga kings, such as Airāvaṇa, Nanda, and Upananda, who raised clouds of black sandalwood incense;
the daughters of these nāga kings produced exquisite musical sounds and rained down clouds of celestial flowers and celestial fragrant waters, making offerings with reverence and saying:
"O Noble Son!..."
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, he emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated all the palaces of the dragon kings;
it caused the dragon kings to be freed from the suffering of hot sand and the fear of the garuḍas, extinguished the heat of their anger, cooled their bodies, and gave rise to hearts of joy.

Having aroused a mind of joy, he preached the Dharma for him; [the nāga] came to loathe the nāga realm, sincerely repented his transgressions, eliminated his karmic obstructions, and resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, even unto dwelling in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
Furthermore, there were ten thousand yakṣa kings who made various offerings to this brahmin and to Sudhana, saying these words:
"O son of good family!
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, I, along with the rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others, all gave rise to a mind of great compassion toward sentient beings and ceased all harm;
by the power of that compassionate mind, we took no pleasure in our palaces and came together with our retinues to visit him.
That brahmin, with his mind of great compassion, sheltered and protected us, causing us to rejoice, making our bodies and minds supple, and bringing us peace, stability, and happiness.
Preach the Dharma for me, even to the point of causing immeasurable yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, and others to resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, ten thousand gandharva kings were in the air, saying these words: "O noble son!
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, he emitted a great radiance that illuminated our palaces, causing all of us to attain inconceivable bliss."
Come to where I am and preach the Dharma for me, even to the point of causing me to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and attain the stage of non-retrogression.
Furthermore, ten thousand asura kings were in the air, kneeling on their right knees with palms joined in single-minded devotion, making offerings with reverence and speaking these words:
“O Son of Good Family!
When this Brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, all the palaces of the asuras, the great earth, and the vast oceans were utterly shaken;
at that time, we cast aside our prideful hearts and came to where he was.

He preached the Dharma for us, causing us to distance ourselves from all deceitful and illusory minds, to attain profound *dharmakṣānti*, to abide immovably, and to become fully endowed with the ten powers.

Furthermore, there were ten thousand *garuḍa* kings, such as Vīryadhara and others, who transformed themselves into the youths of non-Buddhist sects and, remaining in the midst of the sky, spoke these words:
"Even for our sake, he preaches the Dharma, establishing us in great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), praising great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), and delivering us from the ocean of birth and death;

for those submerged in the mud of the five desires, he extols the gateway of pure and upright mind, causing them to grow the wings of wisdom and skillful means (*upāya*), and thus transforms and delivers them all according to their respective needs."
Furthermore, ten thousand kinnara kings in the sky spoke these words: "O noble son!

When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, from within our precious tala trees, our nets of golden bells, our precious necklaces, our various jewel trees, and our diverse musical instruments, there spontaneously issued forth subtle and wondrous sounds: the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṃgha of bhikṣus, the sound of non-retrogressive bodhisattvas, and the sound of the bodhicitta."

In such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a country, there is a certain Bodhisattva who has resolved upon Bodhicitta, practices asceticism, cultivates great generosity, adorns the site of enlightenment, proceeds to that site, and attains the sound of perfect awakening.
"Good son! Upon hearing this sound, I was filled with great joy and went to that place;
he preached the Dharma for me, causing immeasurable sentient beings to attain non-retrogression in their progress toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Furthermore, immeasurable devas of the desire realm were in the sky, making offerings and paying respect, saying these words:
"O son of good family!
When this brahmin scorched his body with the five fires, he emitted a great radiance that even shone throughout the Avīci Hell, extinguishing its agonizing pains."
If there are sentient beings who see this light, at the end of their lives they will be reborn in the heavens;
because they understand the principle of repaying kindness, they abandon the pleasures of the five desires and come to where [the Buddha] is, gazing upon him with insatiable delight.
He preaches the Dharma for them, even causing immeasurable sentient beings to resolve to attain Bodhicitta.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard this extraordinary Dharma, was filled with great joy. In the presence of the brahmin, he gave rise to a mind of true spiritual friendship;
bowing his head at the brahmin’s feet, he spoke thus:
“I previously doubted the holy teachings and contravened the instructions of my spiritual friend.”
“I only pray that the Great Sage will accept my confession of transgression.
Then, the brahmin spoke these verses for the sake of the youth Sudhana:
“Those who seek awakening Should follow the instructions of their spiritual friend.”
Eliminating all doubts and delusions, With single-mindedness, always maintaining reverence,
Cultivating the true path, And knowing the true nature of phenomena,
Abiding securely in the site of enlightenment, One accomplishes the Bodhi of the Buddha.

At that time, the youth Sudhana ascended the mountain of blades and threw himself into the mass of fire; before he had even reached the middle, he attained the bodhisattva samādhi called "Abiding in Peace," and once he reached the flames, he further attained the bodhisattva samādhi called "Tranquil, Blissful Illumination."
Having attained samādhi, he said:
"How marvelous!
O Great Sage!"
"Even when my body touches such mountains of knives and great masses of fire, I experience peace and happiness.
Then, the brahmin said to Sudhana: "Noble son!"
I have only accomplished this inexhaustible dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva.
It clarifies and purifies the practices of all Bodhisattvas under the Dharma-King, fulfilling all vows;
it completely extinguishes the afflictions and false views of sentient beings, attaining a non-regressive and inexhaustible mind, free from sloth, and possessing fearlessness in all things.
They attain the Vajra-Nārāyaṇa treasury and reach the ultimate great realm without ever becoming weary;
they remain far removed from all defilements, as immovable as a wind-wheel; with unflagging diligence, they adorn themselves with the great ornaments to bring benefit to all sentient beings.
"How could I possibly know or expound such a Dharma-gate?
Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Siṃhavikrīḍita."
"There is a young maiden named Maitrāyaṇī.
Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva trains in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazing upon her without weariness, and took his leave to travel south.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-seven and Scroll Forty-eight,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Fifth Part of the Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm, Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Five. At that time, the youth Sudhana gave rise to a mind of inconceivable reverence;

delighting in the pure Dharma and single-mindedly directed toward the Mahāyāna, he sought the wisdom of all Buddhas, drew near to the Tathāgatas, and contemplated the realm of phenomena without obstruction. He was resolved in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and dwelt in the realm of reality; reaching the limit of the three periods of time, he understood that the three periods are like the limit of space. He decisively and fully knew the limit of the phenomena of the three periods, yet did not construct a limit of phenomena; he dwelt in the unobstructed limit and did not contradict the limit of karma. He decisively and fully knew that the limit of the Buddha is no limit, and he dwelt in the dwelling of the Tathāgata.
Having extinguished all false conceptualizations, he was not attached to any Buddhas, any retinues, or any worlds.
Knowing that all sentient beings are without self and lack substantial reality, that all sounds are beyond the path of speech, and understanding that all forms are like flashes of lightning,
he gradually traveled south until he reached that city, where he inquired everywhere as to the whereabouts of the maiden Maitrāyaṇī.
At that time, someone replied,
"She is currently within the palace of King Siṃhadhvaja.
Having heard this, he went immediately to the gate and sought an audience with her.
At that time, a vast multitude of people all entered the palace,
and Sudhana asked them, "Where are you all going now? They replied:
"We wish to go to the maiden Maitrāyaṇī to listen to and receive the True Dharma.
At that time, Sudhana thought to himself:
"This palace gate allows one to enter and exit with complete freedom and without any obstruction."

Sudhana entered and saw that woman situated in a Dharma Hall of Radiant Pure Treasures. Its floor was the color of crystal, its pillars were of lapis lazuli, and its walls were of diamond. It featured railings and windows of Jāmbūnada gold, with light shining everywhere, adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) maṇi jewels.
Furthermore, there were thousand-treasury maṇi mirrors, perfectly adorned and pleasing to all sentient beings, embellished with bright, pure, and exquisite gems.
Moreover, it was covered above by an incalculable net of maṇi jewels, from which hundreds of thousands of golden bells emitted subtle and wondrous sounds.
With such inconceivable arrays of various precious ornaments, the lecture hall was adorned.
There he saw that woman, her body like pure gold, her eyes and hair deep blue, seated upon a lion throne made of fragrant jewels amidst pure water;
it was covered with a golden net, spread with garments of many jewels, and surrounded by a great multitude as she preached the Dharma with a Brahma-like voice.
Having seen him, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence.
He addressed him, saying: "Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
He replied: "Good son! Observe closely this adornment of the Dharma Hall."

At that time, Sudhana saw within each and every lapis lazuli pillar, each and every diamond wall, each and every mani mirror, each and every image, each and every jewel, each and every ornament, each and every small bell, each and every jewel tree, each and every precious image, and each and every precious necklace, all the Tathāgatas throughout the entire dharma-realm—from their first generation of the mind of enlightenment, through their cultivation of bodhisattva practices, the fulfillment of their great vows, their adornment of merit, their attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment, their turning of the pure wheel of Dharma, and even unto their manifestation of nirvana without remainder—just as one sees the reflection of the moon in clear water.

Within the ornaments adorning all realms, the youth Sudhana likewise beheld all Buddhas from their initial generation of the mind of enlightenment until their manifestation of final nirvana without remainder; this was entirely due to the power of the fruit of that woman’s past roots of goodness.
At that time, Sudhana, maintaining right mindfulness of all Buddhas, joined his palms in reverence and said:
"O Great Sage! What is this Dharma-door?"
He replied: "Good son! This Prajñāpāramitā is the Dharma-gate of Universal Adornment."

I have cultivated this dharma-gate in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of thirty-six Ganges Rivers; those Tathāgatas each, by means of different approaches, enabled me to enter this Prajñāpāramitā Dharma-gate of Universal Adornment.
Sudhana said: "O Great Sage! As for this Dharma-door, what is its sphere of activity?"
He replied, “Good son!

When I entered this Dharma-door and, through right mindfulness, reflection, discernment, and upholding, gave rise to equanimity, I attained the Samantamukha Dhāraṇī and ten million asaṃkhyeya dhāraṇī-doors as my retinue.”
That is to say: the dhāraṇī door of buddha-fields, the dhāraṇī door of buddhas, the dhāraṇī door of dharmas,
the dhāraṇī door of sentient beings, the dhāraṇī door of the past, and the dhāraṇī door of the future.
The present dhāraṇī gateway, the gateway of abiding in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) dhāraṇī,
the merit dhāraṇī, the gateway of the possession of merit dhāraṇī, the wisdom dhāraṇī, the gateway of the possession of wisdom dhāraṇī,
the gateway of all vows dhāraṇī, and the gateway of the discernment of all vows dhāraṇī.
The dhāraṇī-door of practice, the dhāraṇī-door of the cultivation and accumulation of practice, the dhāraṇī-door of pure practice,
the dhāraṇī-door of the fulfillment of practice, the dhāraṇī-door of karma, the dhāraṇī-door of non-contradiction with karma, the dhāraṇī-door of the flow of karma,
the dhāraṇī-door of what is produced by karma, and the dhāraṇī-door of detachment.
The dhāraṇī gateway of evil karma, the dhāraṇī gateway of turning toward right action,
the dhāraṇī gateway of mastery over karma, the dhāraṇī gateway of virtuous conduct, the dhāraṇī gateway of the samādhi of virtuous conduct,
the dhāraṇī gateway of samādhi, the dhāraṇī gateway of conforming to samādhi, and the dhāraṇī gateway of discerning samādhi.
The dhāraṇī gate of the *dhāraṇīs*, the dhāraṇī gate of the indestructible samādhi, the dhāraṇī gate of the various supernormal powers and clarities,
the dhāraṇī gate of the ocean of mind, the dhāraṇī gate of the various minds, the dhāraṇī gate of the pure ground of mind,
the dhāraṇī gate of universally illuminating the heavy evils of the mind, and the dhāraṇī gate of the joyful mind of the Tamer of Men.
The dharani-door of eloquence, the dharani-door of initiating sentient beings, the dharani-door of afflictions, the dharani-door of habitual tendencies,
the dharani-door of the skillful means regarding afflictions, the dharani-door of desire,
the dharani-door of the conduct of sentient beings, and the dharani-door of the various karmic actions of sentient beings.
The gate of the intrinsic nature of the world of sentient beings, the gate of the characteristics of sentient beings,
the gate of directions, the gate of expounding the Dharma, the gate of great compassion, the gate of great loving-kindness, the gate of quiescent extinction, and the gate of all paths of speech.
the *dhāraṇī* gate, the *dhāraṇī* gate of skillful means and non-skillful means,
the conforming *dhāraṇī* gate, the analytical *dhāraṇī* gate, the encompassing *dhāraṇī* gate, the unimpeded reality-limit *dhāraṇī* gate,
the *puṭa-dhāraṇī* gate, the Buddha-dharma *dhāraṇī* gate, and the Bodhisattva-dharma...
The dharani-door of the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharani-door of the dharmas of śrāvakas,
the dharani-door of mundane dharmas, the dharani-door of the arising of worlds, the dharani-door of the cessation of worlds,
the dharani-door of the forms and colors of worlds, and the dharani-door of purifying worlds.
The gate of dhāraṇīs for impure worlds; the gate of dhāraṇīs for manifesting defiled lands within pure worlds;
the gate of dhāraṇīs for manifesting pure lands within defiled worlds; the gate of dhāraṇīs for purely pure worlds;
the gate of dhāraṇīs for purely defiled worlds; and the gate of dhāraṇīs for equalized worlds.
The dharani-door of the gates of the *niraya* hells, the dharani-door of overturning worlds, the dharani-door of causing worlds to dwell in subjection,
the dharani-door of entering Indra’s net, the dharani-door of revolving worlds, the dharani-door of abiding in signs,
the dharani-door of placing the great within the small, and the dharani-door of placing the small within the great.
The dharani-door of the differentiation of the Buddha-body; the dharani-door of emitting the net of light of the Buddha’s adornments;
the dharani-door of differentiating the Tathagata’s perfect voice; the dharani-door of the Buddha’s true wheel of Dharma;
the dharani-door of generating the Buddha’s wheel of Dharma; the dharani-door of differentiating the Buddha...
The Dharma-wheel dhāraṇī gateway; the indestructible Buddha-dharma-wheel dhāraṇī gateway; the Buddha’s eloquence dharma-wheel dhāraṇī gateway;
the dharma-wheel dhāraṇī gateway directed toward the Buddhas; the dhāraṇī gateway capable of performing the Buddha-work;
the dhāraṇī gateway directed toward the assemblies of all Buddhas; and the dhāraṇī gateway that distinguishes the great assemblies of all Buddhas.
The dharanī-door of the inexhaustible great ocean-like retinue of all Buddhas, the dharanī-door of the universal illumination of the Buddha’s power,
the dharanī-door of the Tathāgata’s samādhi, the dharanī-door of the sovereign mastery of the Tathāgata’s samādhi-power,
the dharanī-door of the ultimate fulfillment of buddha-works, and the dharanī-door of abiding in the presence of the Buddhas.
The dhāraṇī-door of abiding, the dhāraṇī-door of the Buddha’s upholding, the dhāraṇī-door of the Buddha’s transformation,
the dhāraṇī-door of the Buddha’s knowledge of the mental activities and states of sentient beings, the dhāraṇī-door of the Buddha’s sovereign spiritual power,
the dhāraṇī-door of abiding in the Tuṣita Heaven, and so forth, up to the manifestation of entry into parinirvāṇa.
The gate of dhāraṇīs; the gate of dhāraṇīs that benefit immeasurable sentient beings; the gate of dhāraṇīs of all profound dharmas;
the gate of dhāraṇīs of all adorned dharmas; the gate of dhāraṇīs of skillful means regarding the form of the bodhicitta;
the gate of dhāraṇīs of the arising of the form of the bodhicitta; the gate of the form of vows...
The *dhāraṇī* gate of the doors of liberation, the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of practice, the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of penetrating clarity,
the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of transcending birth and death, the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of pure knowledge, the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of pure wisdom,
the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of immeasurable bodhi, and the *dhāraṇī* gate of the color of the purity of one’s own mind.
...the *dhāraṇī* gateways. Good son!

I know only this Dharma-gate of the Universal Adornment of the Prajñāpāramitā. The minds of the great Bodhisattvas are like space; they enter the profound realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), their merits are fully perfected, they dwell securely in supramundane dharmas, and they remain far removed from worldly conduct.

Fully endowed with purity, possessing the eye of wisdom free from delusion, having definitively realized the immeasurable realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), their wisdom is as infinite as space; they have attained the unobstructed eye, remaining unhindered in all spheres of experience, dwelling in the treasury of non-obstruction, universally illuminating all things, skillfully discerning the meaning of all dharmas, and being incapable of being defeated by any in the world; they perform worldly activities without attachment, employing skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) to benefit and gather in all sentient beings, manifesting in whatever way is appropriate for them, and turning the wheel of the true Dharma at all times with sovereign mastery.
How could I possibly know or describe such merits?

"Noble son! To the south of here is a land called Jyotir-dāna (Saving). There dwells a bhikṣu named Subhūti. Go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to travel south.

At that time, Sudhana reflected with right mindfulness upon the profound dharma-gate; he reflected upon the profound realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); he reflected upon the profound stage of phenomena (*dharmabhūmi*); he reflected upon the profound nature of sentient beings; he reflected upon the profound nature of all conditioned activities (*saṃskāra*); he reflected upon the profound flow of the minds of sentient beings; he reflected upon the profound luminosity of sentient beings; he reflected upon the profound nature of all dharmas; he reflected upon the profound linguistic conventions of sentient beings; he reflected upon the profound and perfect adornment of the realm of phenomena; he reflected upon the profound planting of various karmic actions; and he reflected upon the profound adornments produced by worldly karma.

Traveling by degrees, he arrived at the country of Saṃtāraṇa; throughout its capital cities, towns, villages, market towns, hermitages, mountain forests, and wildernesses, he searched everywhere for the bhikṣu Subhūti.
He saw that bhikṣu walking in meditation within the forest; his physical form was upright and majestic, his countenance was beautiful and exquisite.

His hair curled to the right like a deep blue-black color, and he possessed a fleshy protuberance on the crown of his head (*uṣṇīṣa*). His body was the color of purple-gold, and his eyes were long and wide like blue lotuses. His lips were crimson like the *bimba* fruit; his neck was rounded, straight, and proportionate in length. Upon his chest was the auspicious *śrīvatsa* mark, most wonderfully adorned, and his seven parts were full and even.

His arms were slender and long, his fingers joined by a web and adorned with golden wheels; his calves were firm like those of a deer, while his waist and abdomen were unobtrusive. With the upper body of a lion, he resembled a deity of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven.

His body was perfectly complete like the king of *nyagrodha* trees; adorned with the primary and secondary marks like the king of the Snowy Mountains; producing all excellent medicines; with a halo extending one fathom; his faculties were fully subdued; his gaze was calm and steady; and his wisdom was unimpeded, like the great ocean.
His mind was unmoving, indestructible by anything in the entire world, and he was respectfully surrounded by the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas.

When that bhikṣu was walking in meditation, the Earth-Deva sustained the ground; the Step-Devas produced precious lotus flowers to follow and cover his footprints; the Inexhaustible Perfection Deva dispelled all darkness; the Awakening Deva rained down clouds of various flowers; the Immovable Treasury Deva manifested various treasuries of jewels; the Universal Radiance Surpassing Space Deva adorned the void; the Wondrous Virtue Ocean Deva scattered jewels as an offering; the Stainless Treasury Sumeru Deva joined his palms in reverent service and made offerings with respect; the Unobstructed Power Deva raised clouds of fragrant flowers and winds to make offerings; the Night Deva paid homage with her five limbs in a body adorned with ornaments; and the Constantly Awakened Sun Deva held a bright, pure jewel banner to adorn the void and dispel the gloom.
At that time, Sudhana went to his place, prostrated himself at his feet, and said:

"O Great Sage! I am seeking the conduct of a bodhisattva for the sake of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. I have heard that you, Great Sage, are well able to guide others in the path of all bodhisattvas; how does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path? I pray that you will explain this in detail."
He replied: "Good son!

My years are few and my time since leaving the household life is short. Since my birth, I have purely cultivated the brahma-faring in the presence of Buddhas as numerous as the sands of thirty-eight Ganges Rivers; or in the presence of a single Buddha, I have purely cultivated the brahma-faring for seven days and seven nights; or in the presence of other Buddhas, for half a month, a month, a year, a hundred years, a billion nayutas of years, even up to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of years; or for a small kalpa, a half-kalpa, a full kalpa, or for asaṃkhyeya kalpas, even up to unspeakably unspeakable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, I have purely cultivated the brahma-faring."

In the presence of those Buddhas, he heard the Dharma and received it with devotion, never contravening their teachings; he adorned all his vows and ultimately purified the various practices of a bodhisattva, fully perfecting the six pāramitās.

They know the realm of Bodhi and know the various wheels of Dharma; they protect the Buddha-dharma until the extinction of the True Dharma; they purify all Buddha-worlds through the power of their great vows arising from samādhi;
they bring to ultimate completion all the pure practices of a bodhisattva through the power of all bodhisattva practices and vows;
and they purify all the pāramitās of all Buddhas through the power of the practices of Samantabhadra.
"Good son! Without leaving this place where I walk, I see all the ten directions because my wisdom is unimpeded;
the entire dharma-realm appears before me, for in a single thought-moment I traverse unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds."
In a single thought-moment, one purifies unspeakably many Buddha-worlds through the power of generating great vows;

unspeakably unspeakable gates of skillful means for sentient beings all appear before one, as one possesses the wisdom of the ten powers through the power of generating the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;

and one beholds unspeakably unspeakable Buddhas all appearing before one, reverently making offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable worlds through the power of the vow to reverently make offerings to the Tathāgatas.
Because of the power of the *dhāraṇī* of the Wheel of Dharma, they are able to hear, receive, and uphold the clouds of the Buddhas' teachings, which are unspeakably unspeakable;

they discern and understand the courses of incalculable dharmas, and bring forth all bodhisattva practices before them, such that all practices are entirely pure, due to the power of the vows of the Indra’s Net of Bodhisattva practices, which are unspeakably unspeakable;

and because of the power of generating all samādhis from a single samādhi, unspeakably unspeakable oceans of samādhis all appear before them, and all samādhis are completely purified and perfected within one samādhi.

Inexpressibly inexpressible oceans of faculties all appear before them, because they give rise to and abide in the power of vows regarding the limits of all faculties that accord with the wheel of time;

inexpressibly inexpressible wheels of time all appear before them, because they are able to turn the pure wheel of Dharma at all times, giving rise to the power of vows for the ultimate liberation of sentient beings;

and the entire ocean of the three periods of time all appear before them, because they discern the three periods of time in all worlds, giving rise to the power of vows for the light of wisdom that accords with reality.

"Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the Lamp of Accordance with Bodhisattvas, by which the Vajra-lamp Bodhisattvas are born into the families of all Buddhas; they fully accomplish the immortal life-force and inexhaustible wisdom;
they achieve an indestructible body, complete in its limbs and members, capable of manifesting itself in every appropriate form."
Possessing exquisite form and color, peerless in the world, he cannot be harmed by poison, blades, or fires;
his body is like a vajra, indestructible, subduing all māras and restraining all heterodox teachers;

his body is the color of pure gold, transcending the world, and there is nothing he does not hear or see according to what is appropriate for beings, as he universally surveys the world and rains down the Dharma of ambrosia.

It universally illumines all things and extinguishes all obstacles; those who behold it never tire of the sight. It uproots all unwholesome roots and gives rise to sublime wholesome roots; it is difficult to encounter and difficult to see.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
Son of good family!
To the south of here there is a land called Sūna; there dwells a youth named Śakranātha. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva trains in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.

At that time, the youth Sudhana single-mindedly sought the path adorned by the bodhisattvas; he cultivated practice with his mind illuminated by the various powers of the bodhisattvas, perfected the indestructible and inexhaustible meritorious deeds of the bodhisattvas, and fulfilled the firm great vows of the bodhisattvas. Adorning himself with great adornments, he was fearless in all things, possessing a firm, upright, and non-regressive mind. He received and upheld the clouds of all bodhisattva practices and received and upheld the clouds of the bodhisattvas' true Dharma without ever becoming weary. He revered all the merits of the bodhisattvas, gathered in all sentient beings, and constantly desired to transcend the wilderness of birth and death. He delighted in seeing, hearing, revering, and attending upon spiritual friends, his heart never growing weary or fatigued.
He prostrated with his head at [the Buddha's] feet, paid immeasurable respect, followed the instructions, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, surrounded by a great assembly of followers including devas and nāgas, arrived in the kingdom of Śūṇa and searched everywhere for the youth Śakrādhipati.
At that time, various devas and nāgas in the void spoke to him, saying:
"Good son! This boy is by the side of the river outside the gate of the City of Excellence."

At that time, Sudhana saw the Lord of the Śakras playing with ten thousand youths, making sand castles as they played. He immediately went to where they were, prostrated himself at their feet, circumambulated them countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence. He addressed them, saying:
"O Great Sage!..."

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices and cultivate the bodhisattva path; I only pray that you will explain this for me.
He replied: "Good son!
Mañjuśrī taught me the methods for interpreting marks, the methods of calculation, and the methods of seals; it is because I have learned these three kinds of methods that..."
I have attained the Dharma-gate of wisdom in all skillful arts.

Good son! By means of this Dharma-gate, I know the methods of divination, calculation, and seals; I am able to completely eliminate and subdue illnesses, poisoning, possession by ghosts, and the influence of various demons.

I fully understand the establishment of great and small cities, capitals, towns, and villages; the characteristics of good and evil; the characteristics of agricultural lands, businesses, and all the limbs and joints of sentient beings; and the characteristics of the karmic actions leading to the happy realms or the miserable realms. I know which sentient beings belong to the happy realms and which belong to the miserable realms; I know the various skillful means of the stages of the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, and the Tathāgatas. Having thoroughly understood such matters as these, I cause all sentient beings to cultivate and study this Dharma.
Furthermore, good son! I also fully understand the method of calculation for bodhisattvas, which is as follows:

one hundred thousand makes one lakṣa; one hundred thousand lakṣas make one koṭi; one hundred thousand koṭis make one nayuta; as explained at length in the "Chapter on the Incalculable" (Asaṃkhyeya-parivarta).
"Good son! If there were great heaps of sand, hundreds of yojanas in measure, I could distinguish and calculate their number. Good son!"

Just as mathematics can calculate a heap of sand, so too can it calculate all the worlds in the eastern direction, and likewise in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.

He calculates and knows all kalpas, all Buddhas, all dharmas, all bodhisattvas, and all karmas within all worlds; he likewise calculates and fully understands all the names and designations of the Four Noble Truths within all worlds.

“Good son! I know only this dharma-gate of skillful artifice and wisdom. The great bodhisattvas have deeply entered all dharma-gates of calculation; they calculate all dharmas and deeply enter the methods of calculating the three periods of time;

they calculate all sentient beings, calculate all dharmas, calculate all Buddhas, calculate all the names of all Buddhas, calculate all bodhisattvas, and calculate all the bodhisattvas who turn the wheel of mastery.”

How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct, illuminate their spheres of experience, praise their powers, manifest their upright minds, speak of their endowment with virtues, declare their great vows, reveal their pure perfections, or explain their treasuries of merit and sublime wisdom?

"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Sāgarāvāsā, where there is an upāsikā named Īśvarī. Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path."

At that time, having heard the instructions of the spiritual friend, the youth Sudhana rejoiced immeasurably. He attained a rare, extraordinary, upright, and precious jewel of a mind; his heart became vast and expansive, universally covering all sentient beings. He attained the sovereign dharma-gate of calculating the sequential appearance of all Buddhas in the world, whereby his purity of dharma was perfected and his wisdom brought to ultimate completion. He clearly discerned and manifested all realms of existence, remaining unimpeded within the spheres of the three periods of time. He gave birth to a mind like an inexhaustible ocean of merit and attained the sovereign light of great wisdom, thereby severing the bonds of the triple world.
He prostrated himself at [the teacher's] feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, the youth Sudhana was never satiated with his mind toward spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), just as the great ocean receives and contains all streams.

The sun of the spiritual friend, with its bright and pure light of wisdom, opened his mind, just as a lotus flower unfolds to nurture the sprouts, stalks, nodes, branches, and leaves of the great tree of all roots of goodness (kuśalamūla).
The moon of the spiritual friend, through the light of the cooling teachings, removed the heat of all afflictions.
A spiritual friend is like the Snowy Mountains in summer, a place where all creatures gather in joy;
the mind of a spiritual friend is like the great ocean, filled with all manner of treasures;
the teaching of a spiritual friend nurtures the Dharma-body, like the Jambu tree, fully endowed with flowers and fruit, in which the mind always delights to dwell.
The teaching of the spiritual friend is like a dragon king, who possesses sovereign mastery over miraculous transformations in the midst of space;
the teaching of the spiritual friend raises up a great mountain of jewels, manifesting all things;
by surrounding oneself with the teaching of the spiritual friend, one is invincible, just as Śakra cannot be defeated when he descends upon the asuras.
Gradually traveling on, he arrived at the city of Samudrapratisthita and searched everywhere for the laywoman Īśvarī;
at that time, someone said:
"O noble son!..."
"This upāsikā is within the inner palace of this city.
Having heard this, Sudhana went to the palace gate and stood there with a reverent heart;
the place where that upāsikā resided was vast and magnificently adorned, surrounded on all sides by walls made of various jewels.
It was provided with four gates, adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels.
Sudhana entered and saw the laywoman seated upon a lion throne; she was in the prime of her youth, her countenance was exceptionally beautiful, and those who gazed upon her could never tire.

With the exception of her ornaments, she wore plain garments and had her hair loose; the radiance of her body’s complexion surpassed all others, such that none except Buddhas and Bodhisattvas could equal it.
Within that palace, ten billion couches were spread out, surpassing those of devas and humans, fashioned through the karmic deeds performed by the Bodhisattva in his past lives;
with clothing, food, drink, and various wonderful precious objects and ornaments, the four gates were always open to provide for all beings without end.

Surrounded by a retinue of ten thousand women, their countenances and dignified deportment were entirely like those of the devas; they were like majestic trees adorned with various exquisite jewels. Their mouths constantly produced the wondrous sounds of the heavens as they reverently and joyfully gazed upon this upāsikā, prostrating before her and making offerings.

The bodies of those women constantly emit a wondrous fragrance that perfumes the entire great city. Any who smell it all attain the non-retrogressive mind of bodhi, a mind free from anger or harm, a mind free from enmity, a mind free from stinginess or jealousy, a mind free from illusion or deceit, a mind free from flattery or crookedness, a mind free from greedy attachment, a mind free from malice, a mind free from indolence, an immeasurable mind, an impartial mind, a mind of great compassion, a mind intent on benefiting sentient beings, a mind of pure upholding of the precepts, and a mind free from seeking desires. Upon hearing their voices, all are filled with joy; their bodies and minds become supple, and all who see them attain freedom from desire.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that upāsikā, circumambulated her to the right with a reverent heart, and standing to one side, addressed her, saying:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
He replied, “Good son!

I have accomplished the Dharma-door of the Adornment of the Treasury of Inexhaustible Merit. With a single vessel of food, I bestow it upon a hundred beings, and according to their desires, they all obtain full satisfaction. Whether it be a thousand beings, a hundred thousand beings, a billion beings, ten billion beings, a hundred thousand billion beings, a nayuta of beings, a hundred nayutas of beings, a hundred thousand nayutas of beings, or even unspeakably unspeakable numbers of beings—beings as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa, or even beings as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields—I satisfy them all according to their desires, yet there is no depletion.”
Furthermore, he bestowed upon them exquisite and delicious food, palanquins, garments, flower garlands, wonderful incense, powdered incense, ointments, and precious ornaments.

Furthermore, they provide couches, seats, vehicles, exquisite parasols, banners, and streamers—such various articles as these, fulfilling whatever they desire, so that all may be filled with great joy.

"Good son! In worlds to the east—ranging from a single world to unspeakably unspeakable worlds, from as many worlds as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa to as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields—all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, having eaten my food, shall fully realize the fruit of the Way."

Furthermore, throughout worlds in the eastern direction as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, Bodhisattvas in their final birth before Buddhahood, having partaken of my food, subdue Māra and attain the Way;
the same is true for the southern, western, and northern directions, the four intermediate points, and the zenith and nadir.
"Good son! Do you see these ten thousand women who are my retinue? "Indeed, I see them."
“Good son! These one million asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas are all my companions in practice, companions in aspiration, companions in roots of goodness,
companions in the path of cultivation, equal in their inclinations, equal in their pure right mindfulness, and equal in their pure destinies.”
They share the same immeasurable bodhi; they share the attainment of the various faculties; they share the same fruit resulting from the reliance upon the mind;
they share the same objective sphere; they share the same correct departure from birth; they share the same ultimate reality; they share the same illumination of the true Dharma;
they share the same pure and wondrous physical form of a bodhisattva; they share the same immeasurable power; they share the same firm diligence; and they share the same sound of the true Dharma.
They share the same path of speech; they share all merits; they share pure karma; they share pure retribution;
they share pure great compassion that rescues and protects all; they share pure karma that does not contradict causes and conditions;
they share pure verbal karma in that they preach the Dharma for all assemblies of Buddhas according to what is appropriate; and they share the same reverence.
Having reverently made offerings to all Buddhas, they have attained identical, definitive knowledge of all dharmas and equally realized the pure stages of the Bodhisattvas.
These Bodhisattvas take my vessel of food and, in a single moment of thought, travel throughout the ten directions to make offerings to all Śrāvakas,
Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Buddhas, as well as to bestow it upon the hungry ghosts.
I cause all the hungry ghosts to be fully satisfied, yet the food in my vessel is not diminished. Noble son!
Just as I cause all the devas to be filled according to their needs with the food from this vessel, it is likewise when I bestow it upon humans.
"Good son! Wait but a moment, and you shall see for yourself.

Sudhana then saw immeasurable multitudes of people entering through the four gates; that upāsikā had them all sit down comfortably and satisfied them all according to their respective desires and pleasures.

“Good son! I have attained only this Dharma-door of the Adornment of the Treasury of Inexhaustible Merit. As for the great Bodhisattvas, their ocean-like treasury of inexhaustible merit is like space; they perfume and cultivate their minds with immeasurable merit so that they are like wish-fulfilling jewels, satisfying the vows of all sentient beings; they are cities of great merit that utterly extinguish all poverty and suffering; they are Sumerus of merit that rain down various treasures; they are treasuries of great merit that open the gates of the city of Dharma; they are lamps of merit that dispel the darkness of poverty; they are parasols of great merit whose supreme and wondrous roots of goodness cover all sentient beings.
How could I possibly know or speak of their meritorious conduct?”

"Noble son! To the south of here, there is a city named Mahodaya. There dwells an elder named Amṛtāśikhin; go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and, recollecting him without letting him go from his mind, took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, Sudhana attained the Dharma-door of the Radiance of Inexhaustible Merit; with right mindfulness, he contemplated that ocean of merit, observed those virtues of space, entered that accumulation of merit, ascended that mountain of merit, gathered that treasury of merit, reached the bottom of that ocean of merit, crossed that sea of merit, purified those perfect merits, universally observed all those virtues, followed that treasury of merit, upheld those teachings of merit, and purified that nature of merit.
Gradually traveling on, he arrived at the city of Daxing, where he searched everywhere for the elder Amṛtaśikhin, desiring to seek out a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).

He permeated his body and mind with the influence of the spiritual friend, gave rise to a mind of straightforwardness toward the spiritual friend, and contemplated the spiritual friend without ever becoming weary. He emulated the spiritual friend’s courageous diligence, sought all the roots of goodness of the spiritual friend, and shared in all the roots of goodness of the spiritual friend. Free from any heart of resentment toward the spiritual friend, he fulfilled the treasury of merit and studied the various skillful means of the spiritual friend.

Although they do not attain awakening through others, they constantly draw near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), nurture their roots of goodness, and purely cultivate the upright mind of bodhi; they increase all the faculties of a bodhisattva, accomplish all roots of goodness, and fulfill their great vows.
They give rise to vast compassion, draw near to all-knowledge, and never depart from the Buddhas;
they increase the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and the light of the Tathāgata constantly illumines their minds.

At that time, Sudhana saw Amṛtadhvaja within that city, seated upon a lion throne made of seven precious gems inside a hall of seven jewels. The feet of the throne were made of *vajra-aindra-rāja* gems, adorned with stainless jewel-treasures, and embellished with five hundred precious images. Various jeweled banners were erected, precious silk streamers hung down, and canopies of many jewels were spread above, all covered by an immeasurable net of jewels.

Some held canopies of Jāmbūnada gold with poles of lapis lazuli; others stood in attendance at their sides holding stainless jewel-whisks, while they were perfumed by various exquisite incenses. Clouds of celestial flowers rained down, and five hundred kinds of sublime musical performances were performed for their entertainment.

Within the city, a great assembly of ten thousand people surrounded him on all sides; their countenances were exquisite and peerless among gods and humans. Having perfected the bodhisattva’s straightforward mind, they adorned sentient beings and constantly followed the teachings of the Ambrosial Summit, for they had cultivated various roots of goodness together throughout past lives.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself at [the Bodhisattva’s] feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying:
"O Great Sage!
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, I have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, namely:
