to extinguish the suffering and affliction of all sentient beings, to cause them to dwell in peace and security, to bring about ultimate happiness, to cross the ocean of birth and death, to reach the island of the Dharma-treasure, to dry up craving and attachment, to cultivate the mindfulness of great compassion, to eliminate the thirst for the five desires, to delight in all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), to cause them to ultimately cross the wilderness of birth and death, to always rejoice in the merits of all Buddhas, to transcend the triple world and reach the city of *sarvajñā*. Yet, I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, cultivate the bodhisattva path, and gather in all sentient beings.
The householder replied: “Excellent! Excellent!”
"O youth! That you are able to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is rare;
that one who can resolve their mind to study the bodhisattva path and cultivate the bodhisattva practices is even more difficult to find."
One seeks spiritual friends, beholds spiritual friends, and draws near to them with reverence;
regarding spiritual friends, one’s mind never regresses and one never feels weary or satisfied. Good son!
"Do you see these ten thousand members of my retinue?

"Indeed, I do. "I originally taught them various dharmas to cause them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, to be born into the family of the Tathāgata, to cultivate pure and white dharmas, to fulfill the immeasurable *pāramitās*, and to be endowed with the ten powers of a Buddha."
He leaves behind worldly lineages and establishes the lineage of the Tathāgata;
he destroys the wheel of birth and death and turns the pure wheel of Dharma;
he extinguishes the three evil realms and establishes the path of the True Dharma.
"Good son! You should know that a bodhisattva is fully capable of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings. Good son!"

I have accomplished this Dharma-gate of the Jewel-Treasury of Sovereign Merit, which fulfills all their wishes according to what they require. That is to say, I bestow upon them all manner of things—various jewels, vehicles, elephants and horses, servants, clothing, food and drink, incense, flowers, powdered incense, lamps, medicinal decoctions, banners and streamers, silk canopies, retinues according to their desires, celestial crowns, precious ornaments, all kinds of rare playthings, and the necessities of life; I give these all away as gifts, even extending to the extensive bestowal of the Dharma upon sentient beings.
"Good son! Wait but a moment, and you shall see it for yourself.
Immediately, Sudhana saw that from all directions—countries, cities, towns, and villages—all sentient beings came to his place, and he bade them all sit down.
At that time, Amṛtakuṇḍala looked up into the void; whatever was required by all those gathered there descended from the sky, fulfilling their wishes.

Once their wishes were satisfied, he preached the True Dharma for them, causing them all to nurture the treasury of all merits, to extinguish the craving of birth and death, and to thirst with longing for the Buddha-dharma, even until they were fully endowed with the marks of the great man’s taste-in-taste.

He extinguished the suffering of poverty, enriched them with the wealth of nectar, and subdued the hosts of Māras so that none could destroy them, bringing them to the accomplishment of the ten powers and unsurpassed wisdom.
Having thus fulfilled their vows, all these beings were filled with great joy and returned to their respective abodes from whichever direction they had come.

"Good son, I know only this Dharma-door of the Jewel Treasury of Sovereign Merit. As for the great Bodhisattvas, who are endowed with all sovereign merits and have perfected the 'Jewel Hand' that covers all lands, raining down clouds of the infinite; [I do not know their ways]."
That is to say:

clouds of various jewels, clouds adorned with various colors, clouds of various colored celestial crowns, clouds of various colored garments, clouds of various sublime sounds, clouds of various flowers, clouds of various *cūḍāmaṇi* jewels, clouds of various colored fragrances, clouds of various colored parasols, and clouds of various colored banners and pennants—all completely filling all worlds, all Buddha-fields, and all Buddhas together with their retinues—in order to teach and transform all sentient beings and cause them to make offerings to all Buddhas.
How could I possibly know or describe those bodhisattva practices, or manifest their sovereign mastery?
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Siṃhala-kūṭāgāra;
in it dwells an elder named Dharmaratna-cūḍa."
"Go to him and ask: how does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

At that time, the youth Sudhana, filled with joy and exultation, prostrated himself with his head at [Maitreya’s] feet, circumambulated him countless times, and paid homage according to the manner of a disciple.
They form this thought:

"It is by means of a spiritual friend that one attains all-knowledge; toward the spiritual friend, one gives rise to an indestructible mind; hearing the instructions of the spiritual friend, one is able to follow them entirely and subdue the sense faculties."
Having formed this thought, he took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana maintained the dharma-gate of the treasury of jewels of the merit of right mindfulness; he guarded that treasury of merit, purified that Sumeru King of Merits, reached the source and bottom of that ocean of merit, opened that treasury of merit, contemplated that treasury of merit, brought that treasury of merit to complete purity, gathered that treasury of merit, and generated and nurtured the power of that treasury of merit.

Traveling by degrees, he arrived at that city and searched everywhere for the elder Dharmarāṣṭrapāla. Meeting him on the road, he prostrated with his head at the elder's feet, joined his palms in reverence, stood to one side, and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Then, that elder took Sudhana by the hand and led him back to his home, saying:
"Noble son! Behold my home for a moment."
At that time, Sudhana looked all around the residence; it was entirely the color of Jāmbūnada gold, with walls made of the seven treasures surrounding it on all sides.

It was adorned with lapis lazuli, with pillars of mother-of-pearl, and featured lion thrones of red *cintāmaṇi* jewels. Lion-treasure banners were erected, and lapis lazuli canopies were spread above, covered by nets of wish-fulfilling jewels and adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) gems.
There were agate treasure ponds, filled to the brim with water possessing the eight virtues.
It was surrounded on all sides by trees made of every kind of jewel, and the residence was vast, consisting of ten stories with eight gates.
At that time, Sudhana saw that on the lowest story, various delicacies were prepared and bestowed as gifts upon all;
he saw that on the second story, various jeweled garments were given away.
He saw that the third tier was adorned with all manner of precious ornaments bestowed as gifts;
he saw that the fourth tier consisted of inner retinues who had all practiced virtuous conduct and were skillful in speech;

he saw that the fifth tier was filled with bodhisattvas from the first to the fifth stages who had gathered therein to compile the True Dharma, who were detached from worldly pleasures, and who produced all treatises, dhāraṇīs, samādhis, and dharma seals, discerning the light of the wisdom of samādhi.

He saw that the sixth level was filled with Bodhisattvas who had attained the *prajñāpāramitā*. Possessing profound wisdom, they had attained the stage of the treasury of tranquil and luminous wisdom and the dharma-gate of non-obstruction. They had transcended the realms of the three existences without hindrance, contemplated the non-dual Dharma, and compiled and expounded the gates of *prajñāpāramitā*, namely:

the gate of *prajñāpāramitā* of the treasury of quiescence, the gate of *prajñāpāramitā* of discerning all sentient beings, the gate of *prajñāpāramitā* of immovability, and the gate of *prajñāpāramitā* of universal illumination through the departure from desire.
the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the treasury of non-retrogression, the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the indestructible treasury,
the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the pure eye of all sentient beings, the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the ocean-treasury,
the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the universal eye, and the Prajñāpāramitā gateway of the ocean of all inexhaustible skillful means.
The gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* that universally illumines in accordance with sentient beings without obstruction;
the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the gradually descending auspicious clouds— compiling such hundreds of thousands of *asaṃkhyeya* gates of *prajñāpāramitā*,
those assemblies of bodhisattvas were adorned with unspeakable adornments.

He saw that the seventh level was filled with Bodhisattvas of the Stage of Resonance-Patience, who had produced the wisdom of skillful means and were able to hear and retain all the clouds of the Buddhas' teachings;

In the eighth tier, he saw Bodhisattvas of the stage of perpetual abiding filling it; endowed with all supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), they pervaded all lands, illuminating all sentient beings and the entire Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*). Possessing the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*), they proceeded to all Buddhas without obstruction and were able to receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas. In the ninth tier, he saw Bodhisattvas in their final birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*) filling it. In the tenth tier, he saw all Tathāgatas filling it; from their first aspiration, they had cultivated the Bodhisattva practices, transcended birth and death, fulfilled their great vows, and attained mastery over spiritual powers. In all Buddha-lands and their retinues, they turned the pure wheel of Dharma, transforming and delivering sentient beings, and manifested their sustaining presence.
At that time, having witnessed such extraordinary and marvelous events, Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!
I have never before seen such a pure assembly. In what place did they plant various roots of goodness in the past, so as to now obtain such a supreme and wondrous retribution?"

“Good son! I recall that in the past, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān named Immeasurable Radiance Dharma-realm Universal Adornment King appeared in the world.”
When that Buddha entered the city, I made offerings to him with incense, flowers, and music;
having made these offerings, I dedicated this root of goodness toward three goals:
namely, to eliminate poverty and suffering, to always see the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends, and to constantly hear the True Dharma—thereby obtaining this retribution.

"Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of Fulfilling Great Vows. As for those Bodhisattvas of the great oceans of jewels who have attained the indestructible pure Dharma-body; whose indestructible Dharma-clouds universally cover all things; who are fully accomplished in indestructible merit; whose indestructible great web of merit universally covers all things; who enter the realm of indestructible samādhi; who are endowed with the indestructible roots of goodness of Bodhisattvas; who dwell in the indestructible wisdom of the Tathāgatas' dwelling, ultimately penetrating the three periods of time; who dwell through all kalpas without weariness; and who dwell in the stage of the indestructible realm of the Universal Eye—how could I possibly know or speak of their meritorious conduct?"
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a land named Śrīkūṭa and a city named Samantamukha. There dwells an elder named Samantanetra-gandhottama;
go to him and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva practice and cultivates the bodhisattva path."
At that time, the youth Sudhana, having prostrated his head at the feet of Dharmadhātu-keśara, took his leave and traveled south.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 48;
*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Scroll 49.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Six: The Dharma-Domain of the Six Entrances.

At that time, the youth Sudhana contemplated the immeasurable dharma-gates of all Buddhas, attained the immeasurable practices of Bodhisattvas, and the immeasurable, wondrous paths of skillful means of Bodhisattvas, which universally illumined his body and mind.

They joyfully seek immeasurable gates of expedient means, accomplishing the pure liberation of Bodhisattvas, the immeasurable purity of the Bodhisattva faculties, and the immeasurable purity of the Bodhisattva powers;

their minds follow the immeasurable practices of Bodhisattvas, giving rise to the immeasurable power of the Bodhisattva’s great vows, and attaining the indestructible banner of wondrous wisdom of Bodhisattvas that universally illumines all.
Gradually traveling on, he reached that country and sought the city of Samantamukha with an unwearied mind, practicing with diligence and without retreat.

He kept the spiritual friend in mind, praised the spiritual friend, and followed the spiritual friend; his faculties were single-mindedly directed toward the Dharma-gate of Universal Doors, remaining far removed from all heedless conduct, opening the eye of pure wisdom, and crossing the ocean of birth and death.

He saw the city of Samantamukha, surrounded on all sides by hundreds of thousands of smaller cities that were lofty, steep, and secure, exquisitely crafted beyond compare, and adorned with various ornaments;
he saw the elder Sugandhakūṭa, the Wondrous Fragrance, sitting upon a seat of many fragrances within this city.
He went to where [the Buddha] was, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and with palms joined in reverence, stood to one side and said: "Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice or cultivate the bodhisattva path."
He replied, "Excellent! Excellent!"
"O son of good family!
You are indeed able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O son of good family!"

I know all the illnesses of sentient beings: diseases of wind, cold, and heat; various miscellaneous ailments; madness and violent afflictions; possession by spirits; toxic diseases; and diseases caused by various incantations. All such categories of illness, I fully understand;
according to what is appropriate for each, I am able to cure them all.
"Good son! All sentient beings of the ten directions who come to me with various ailments, I am able to treat them all.

Once their afflictions have been removed, I bathe them with fragrant water and adorn them with fragrant flowers, necklaces, famous garments, and superior robes; I provide them with delicacies and food as offerings, and bestow upon them immeasurable precious treasures. Only then do I preach various Dharma gates for them."
For those with an abundance of greed, teach the contemplation of impurity;
for those with an abundance of hatred, teach the contemplation of loving-kindness;
for those with an abundance of delusion, teach the contemplation of the characteristics of phenomena.
For those who practice with equal parts of the afflictions, one teaches the sublime Dharma-gate;

because they praise and extol the merits of all Buddhas and resolve upon Bodhicitta, one speaks of nurturing great compassion, so that their minds do not weary amidst the sufferings of immeasurable births and deaths;
and because they nurture immeasurable pure wisdom, one analytically and extensively explains the various pāramitās.
He speaks of the various great vows in order to teach and bring all sentient beings to maturity;
he speaks of the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva to manifest the perfection of pure ethical discipline (śīla-pāramitā);
and he speaks of the inconceivable merits of the Tathāgata to manifest the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā).
It is said that the Tathāgata possesses an indestructible and pure *dharmakāya*, which manifests the *vīryapāramitā*;
it is said that the Tathāgata has no equal, which manifests the *dhyānapāramitā* of the Tathāgata;

it is said that the *dharmakāya* is pure, which manifests the *prajñāpāramitā*; and it is said that the entirely pure *dharmakāya* is beheld by all sentient beings, which manifests the *upāyapāramitā*.
It speaks of abiding for all kalpas within birth and death to manifest the perfection of vows;
it speaks of adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields to manifest the perfection of powers;
and it speaks of purifying the Dharma-body so that, according to what is appropriate, all may be brought to joy to manifest the perfection of wisdom.
I preach that the pure Dharma-body is eternally joyful to behold, for it is far removed from all unwholesome dharmas. Good son!
By means of such various gifts of Dharma as these, I cause all to be fully satisfied and they return with joy.
"Good son! I also well know the methods for compounding various incenses, namely:

the incense of King Incomparable, the incense of the Indus River, the incense of Victory, the incense of Awakening, the incense of Radiant Signs, the incense of Aquilaria, the incense of Firmness, the incense of Sandalwood, the incense of Clouds, and the incense of Immovable Faculties; I know all such incenses as these."
When burning this incense, one should direct the mind single-mindedly toward the Buddha and give rise to the great vow-mind to fulfill all aspirations, namely:
to rescue and protect all sentient beings, to adorn and purify all buddha-fields, and to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas;
even when burning a single pellet of incense, it fills the entirety of the ten directions and all dharma-realms, reaching all Tathāgatas and their retinues.

Fragrant canopies adorn the entire Dharma-realm; fragrant palaces, fragrant walls, fragrant towers, fragrant railings, fragrant battlements, fragrant windows, fragrant crescents, fragrant parasols, fragrant banners, fragrant pennants, fragrant nets, fragrant images, fragrant radiance, fragrant ornaments, and fragrant clouds and rains adorn all the Dharma-realms of the ten directions, as well as all Buddhas and their retinues.
"Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the Universal Gateway that causes all sentient beings to rejoice; it is seen by the Great Medicine King Bodhisattvas who behold the bodies of all Buddhas.
If there are those who hear of it, see it, draw near to it, recollect it, or uphold its name, none of these shall be in vain."

Those who behold it have all their afflictions extinguished; they attain the fundamental source of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas, eliminate the aggregate of suffering, and forever leave behind all fears of birth and death. They obtain fearlessness, possess all-knowledge, shatter the lofty mountains of immeasurable saṃsāra, and dwell securely in the True Dharma.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
Son of good family!
To the south of here, there is a city named Pūrṇadhvaja and a king named Pūrṇabhadra. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the elder Viśvapadmasupratiṣṭhita with his head, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, Sudhana successively recollected all his spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), reflecting with right mindfulness upon their instructions;
he further thought to himself:
“Virtuous friends are able to gather me in and protect me, causing me not to regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Thinking thus, one attains a heart of great joy, a heart of immeasurable joy, a pure heart, a heart of quiescence, a vast heart, an adorned heart, an unattached heart, an unimpeded heart, a heart of emptiness, a heart that beholds all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, a sovereign heart, a heart that accords with all dharmas, a heart that fills all Buddha-fields in a single thought-moment, a heart that beholds the Tathāgata, a heart that recollects the Ten Powers, and a heart that does not abandon the Buddhas and virtuous friends.”
Gradually passing through crowds of people, cities, towns, and villages,
he arrived at the city of Pūrṇadhvaja and asked, "Where is King Pūrṇa now? Someone replied:
"Currently, I am in the main hall, exercising the royal law to transform and guide sentient beings.
Those who should be gathered in are gathered; those who should be punished are punished; those who should be disciplined are disciplined;
and for all those with disputes, I resolve their litigation."
To those who have fear, he bestows fearlessness;
he praises non-killing, non-stealing, non-sexual misconduct, non-lying, non-slander, non-harsh speech, non-frivolous speech, and freedom from greed, hatred, and delusion.

At that time, Sudhana saw from afar that king seated upon a diamond lion throne, adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels and embellished with immeasurable precious images; it was universally perfumed by various clouds of incense, and immeasurable precious garments were spread upon it.
Furthermore, immeasurable jeweled banners were erected, with countless jeweled pennants hanging down on all sides, and a canopy of many jewels was stretched above.
He wore a crown of wish-fulfilling *maṇi* jewels, adorned with a crescent moon of Jāmbūnada gold.
His hair was deep blue-black, and his ears hung down long and full; he wore upon his body priceless *maṇi* necklaces, over which were spread nets of hundreds of thousands of jewels;

there was a parasol of Jambūnada gold with bells made of various gems that constantly emitted wondrous sounds, and a staff of lapis lazuli with a nocturnal luminous treasure that shone universally in all directions.
That King Paripūrṇa possessed great power; free from all enemies, he enjoyed immeasurable sovereignty.
Ten thousand ministers each occupied their permanent posts, attending to the affairs of state, while ten thousand brave generals stood guard with weapons at the ready.

At that time, Sudhana saw immeasurable sentient beings who had violated the king’s laws and were subjected to corporal punishment: their bodies bound with the fivefold fetters; some having their hands and feet cut off, others having their ears and noses severed, others having both eyes gouged out, others having their bodies or heads decapitated, or being cast into boiling ashes;
or else being wrapped in layers of cloth, doused with oil, and set ablaze;
they were thus tormented by such immeasurable and agonizing sufferings.
At that time, Sudhana thought to himself:

"For the sake of all sentient beings, I study the conduct of a bodhisattva and cultivate the path of a bodhisattva; yet now I see this king practicing great evil and perversity, various unwholesome dharmas.
This is the most evil among evils, the foremost of wicked men."
While he was reflecting thus, a deva in the sky addressed him, saying:
"O son of good family!
You should recollect the instructions of the spiritual friend Universal Eye Wondrous Fragrance."
Sudhana immediately looked up into the sky and replied to him, saying,
"I constantly keep it in mind!
The deva spoke again, saying:
"If you constantly maintain mindfulness, why do you harbor such doubt and wonder?

Good son! The skillful means of a bodhisattva are inconceivable; the wisdom of a bodhisattva is inconceivable; the gathering of sentient beings is inconceivable; the taming of sentient beings is inconceivable; the teaching and transforming of sentient beings is inconceivable; the compassionate regard for sentient beings is inconceivable; and the liberation of sentient beings is inconceivable."
At that time, having heard the celestial instruction, Sudhana went to the place where the king was, prostrated himself at his feet, and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, King Pūrṇa, having finished his royal duties, took Sudhana by the hand and led him into the palace. He had him take a place upon a precious lion throne and addressed him, saying: "Noble son!
"Observe my home," [she said].
Sudhana immediately beheld vast and boundless walls made of the seven treasures surrounding it on all sides;
within were lecture halls of the seven treasures, adorned with hundreds of thousands of immeasurable towers and pavilions made of various jewels.
It was even covered above by an inconceivable net of mani-jewels;
five hundred handmaidens, as beautiful and dignified as celestial beings, were there, just as described above.
“Good son! Do you see the karma that is the cause of this retribution of mine? He replied:
“I have seen it.
“Good son! I have accomplished the bodhisattva’s dharma-gate of illusory transformation.”

In this land of mine, there are sentient beings who commit killing, stealing, and even hold wrong views; they cannot be taught to abandon these evil deeds. To subdue them and bring them to liberation, I manifest as various people and subject them to diverse forms of suffering, so that they may renounce the ten unwholesome paths and all evils, become fully endowed with the ten wholesome paths, attain ultimate bliss, resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and perfect all-encompassing wisdom.
"Good son! You should know that my body, speech, and mind do not give rise to thoughts of harm even toward an ant, let alone toward a human being.
A human is a field of merit, from which all roots of goodness grow."
"Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of illusory transformation.
The great Bodhisattvas, having attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), know that all realms of existence are entirely like illusions."
They know that the practices of bodhisattvas are entirely like magical transformations;
all worlds are entirely like flashes of lightning;
and all phenomena are entirely like dreams.

They have deeply entered the unimpeded Dharma-realm and are endowed with the sublime practices of Bodhisattvas; their spheres of experience are unobstructed, they encompass all modes of conduct, and they have attained mastery over the infinite *dhāraṇīs* of revolving.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?

Good son, to the south of here there is a city named Suprabha and a king named Mahāprabha; you should go to him and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the king’s feet, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, Sudhana maintained single-minded, right mindfulness of that king’s Dharma-door of the magical manifestation of wisdom.

Contemplating that all phenomena are entirely like illusions, they discern various karmas and single-mindedly seek the True Dharma; with one-pointed mind, they contemplate the transformations of that king as he rescues and delivers sentient beings.

Contemplating that everything in the world is like an illusion, they discern and understand that the vows and practices of the three periods of time are all like illusory manifestations, thereby entering the pure realm of reality (*dharmadhātu*).

Gradually passing through crowds of people, villages, towns, cities, and the hardships of wildernesses, his mind remained free from weariness until he reached the city of Suprabha, where he asked the people,
"What is the name of this city?"
He replied, "Sukhāloka. At that time, Sudhana thought to himself:
"My spiritual friend is in this city; today I shall certainly see my spiritual friend and hear of the bodhisattva conduct, the true Dharma of the bodhisattvas, and all the Dharma-gates.

The merit of the bodhisattvas is inconceivable, their sphere of activity is inconceivable, their mastery is inconceivable, their Dharma-gate of equality is inconceivable, and their power of valor is inconceivable; today I shall surely hear of the ultimate sphere of the bodhisattvas."
Having formed this thought, he entered the city of Suprabha.

He saw that the city was adorned with immeasurable arrays of the seven precious jewels, surrounded on all sides by seven tiers of deep moats filled with water possessing the eight virtues; its bottom was strewn with golden sand, and it was completely covered with *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers.
There were walls made of the seven treasures, surrounding it in seven tiers, namely:

walls of adamantine lions, indestructible adamantine walls, adamantine walls of diligence, indestructible adamantine walls of diligence, bottomless adamantine walls, walls of pure nets, and adamantine walls of desire-free purity;
these seven tiers of walls were adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels.
That city was extraordinary, lofty, steep, and vast, with ten billion streets and alleys;
in each street and alley, there were immeasurable billions of nayutas of asankhyeyas of people.
There were incalculable pavilions of Jāmbūnada gold, covered above by nets of lapis lazuli jewels;
inconceivable pavilions of white silver, covered above by nets of red pearls;
and inconceivable pavilions of lapis lazuli, covered above by nets of maṇi-jewels from the Treasury of Adornments.
Inconceivable crystal pavilions were covered by nets of stainless maṇi-jewel treasuries;
inconceivable bright and pure jewel pavilions were covered by nets of sun-treasury maṇi jewels;
incalculable indranīla jewel pavilions were covered by nets of exquisite jewel radiance.
There were asaṃkhyeya pavilions of solid jewels, covered by nets of flaming noctilucent gems;
inconceivable pavilions of vajra, covered by nets of indestructible banner-maṇi jewels;
and inconceivable pavilions of aloeswood and sandalwood, covered by nets of mahāmandārava flowers.
Such innumerable, ineffable pavilions of exquisite jewels were covered above by various kinds of nets:
inconceivable nets of exquisite jewels, inconceivable nets of golden bells, inconceivable nets of incense, inconceivable nets of flowers, and inconceivable nets of garments, all draped over them.

Furthermore, inconceivable canopies of exquisite jewels were spread out, inconceivable precious and wonderful jewel parasols were placed over them, and inconceivable banners and streamers of various jewels were erected to adorn them.
Within this city there was a tower named "Inexhaustible Delight for All Beings to Behold," adorned with incalculable *maṇi* jewels;
King Mahāprabha constantly resided therein.
At that time, Sudhana was free from any attachment to these various magnificent and exquisite adornments;

with a single-minded longing to see the spiritual friend, he beheld King Mahāprabha seated upon a precious lion throne in the Dharma Hall. He sat cross-legged, adorned with various jewels and draped in precious garments, further embellished by ten thousand *asaṃkhyeya* precious images, while being entertained by all manner of musical performances.
He is adorned with the twenty-eight marks of a great man and the eighty secondary characteristics.
His body is of a true golden color, like the bright, pure sun that universally illumines all;
like the full moon, he is the most luminous among the host of stars.
Like the Brahma King dwelling amidst the great assembly;
like the many precious treasures within the great ocean;
like the various excellent medicines produced from the Snowy Mountains.
Like a great dragon king, he thunders the sound of the true mark of all dharmas;
like space, he is pure and untainted by dust or defilement;
like Mount Sumeru with its four kinds of precious colors, he universally illumines the ocean of the natures of sentient beings.
It was like a jewel island, filled with the treasures of wisdom.
Before the king’s palace and throughout the streets and alleys, as well as outside the four gates of the city, heaps of various rare jewels and precious garments were placed everywhere.

There were immeasurable billions of nayutas of court ladies, whose appearances and adornments were dignified and majestic; they possessed peerless qualities of the five desires, with such exquisite beauty and skill that they could captivate both gods and humans, and there was not one of the sixty-four arts that they did not fully master.
There were immeasurable milch cows with horns of golden hue, whose milk was sweet and fragrant, yielding one *shí* from each milking.

Furthermore, there were immeasurable various ornaments, diverse delicacies of a hundred flavors with sweet fragrances, immeasurable music, as well as medicinal decoctions and all manner of requisites for sustaining life.
In each and every street and lane, there were twenty billion bodhisattvas on either side, who bestowed all these requisites for life;

they did so for the sake of gathering in sentient beings, for the sake of gladdening sentient beings, for the sake of purifying the minds of sentient beings, for the sake of extinguishing the afflictions of sentient beings, for the sake of causing all sentient beings to understand the true meaning, for the sake of establishing sentient beings in omniscience, for the sake of causing sentient beings to leave behind evil thoughts, for the sake of pulling out the thorns of false views from sentient beings, and for the sake of purifying the paths of karma of sentient beings.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself before King Mahāprabha with his five limbs, circumambulated him to the right once, stood to one side, and said:
"O Great Sage!

"I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice or cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Great Sage is well able to explain this; I only pray that you will expound it for me."
He replied, "Good son!
I have accomplished the pure and complete fulfillment of the Bodhisattva’s practice of the Banner of Great Compassion."
In the presence of immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I have heard this sublime Dharma, observed it with purity, and cultivated its adornments.
"Good son! Abiding in this practice, I rule the country according to the Dharma; I observe sentient beings and act in accordance with the world.
I teach and transform sentient beings according to the Dharma, gathering them in, establishing them, and benefiting them."
They perfume sentient beings according to the Dharma and teach sentient beings according to the Dharma, causing them to cultivate roots of goodness and contemplate the reality of all phenomena.

They cause all sentient beings to attain a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of great loving-kindness, a mind of the power of great loving-kindness, a mind of benefiting others, a mind free from fear, a mind that gathers in sentient beings, and a mind that does not abandon sentient beings; they inspire them to give rise to great vows to extinguish all suffering.

They bring peace and security to sentient beings, causing them to attain happiness; their bodies and minds become supple, they distance themselves from mental defilements, and they renounce the pleasures of birth and death. They constantly delight in the True Dharma, eliminate the stains of afflictions, and attain a pure mind.
By perfuming the minds of sentient beings with all that is wholesome, they sever the flow of birth and death, enter the deep ocean of the Dharma, and extinguish all realms of existence;
they give rise to an unimpeded mind, attain all-knowledge, purify the ocean of their own minds, and possess a power of faith so firm that none can destroy it.
"Noble son! Abiding thus in this practice, I ruled the kingdom according to the Dharma, causing all the people to be free from every fear.
When those who were impoverished came to me, I would always open my treasuries for them according to their needs and tell them: "
"Take as you please, but do not commit any evil.

The sentient beings within this city all incline toward the Mahāyāna; each perceives this city differently: some see it as defiled, others see it as pure; some see it made of wood and stone, others see it as lapis lazuli; some see it surrounded on all sides by indestructible banners and walls;
others see inconceivable multi-storied pavilions adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels.

By cultivating all roots of goodness with an upright mind and seeking omniscience in the presence of all Buddhas, those who were gathered by me in past lives and are now practicing the bodhisattva path behold this city as adorned and pure with various jewels; others see it as defiled and impure.

"Good son! When the sentient beings of this city dwell in an age of the five turbidities and practice various unwholesome deeds, I take pity upon them and enter the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Great Compassion Foremost and Accordant with the World.
When I enter this concentration, the evil minds, vexed minds, contentious minds, and harmful minds of those sentient beings are all completely extinguished. Why is this so? "
This is the power of this samādhi; such is the nature of dharmas. Good son!
Wait but a moment, and you shall see it for yourself.

At that time, the king immediately entered the "Great Compassion as the Foremost Accordance with the World" Samādhi. Having entered it, the great city of Suprabha shook in six ways; from the jeweled walls, towers, palaces, railings, windows, battlements, crescent-shaped ornaments, jeweled bells, and lattices, as well as from all the various jeweled images, wondrous sounds issued forth, praising that king.
All the people within and without the city were filled with great joy; with single-minded palms joined, they paid homage to the king.
Even the animals, facing one another with hearts of loving-kindness, likewise paid homage to the king.
The mountains, plains, and forests all bowed their forms toward that king;
the rivers, ponds, springs, and streams all flowed toward him;
ten thousand dragon kings raised dark and heavy clouds, with thunder rolling and lightning flashing, raining down a multitude of fragrant waters.

Ten thousand Śakra-devānām-indras, Yāma-devānām-indras, Suyāma-devānām-indras, Nirmāṇarati-devānām-indras, Paranirmita-vaśavartin-devānām-indras, and others, produced in the void the sounds of billions of nāyutas of musical instruments;

incalculable celestial maidens sang with various wonderful melodies and hymns, raining down incalculable clouds of flowers, clouds of incense, clouds of powdered incense, clouds of garlands, clouds of parasols, and clouds of multicolored garments; and incalculable jeweled banners, pennants, and parasols adorned the void as they made offerings to that king.

The Dragon King Enapana spread a great lotus flower that universally covered the void; it hung with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) exquisite silk ribbons, was adorned with incalculable jewels, and filled the void with incalculable jewel garlands, necklaces, celestial ornaments, and various wonderful flowers and fragrances as an offering to that king;
incalculable celestial maidens filled the void, praising that king.

Innumerable rākṣasa demons and others, who constantly dwell in the great ocean and Jambudvīpa, drinking blood and eating flesh, as well as the malevolent beasts of water and land that perpetually harm sentient beings, all attained a mind of loving-kindness and a mind of tranquility. They gained clear faith in future lives, distanced themselves from all evils, and with hearts of great joy, prostrated themselves on the ground with their five limbs to pay homage to that king; they all attained immeasurable physical and mental happiness.

It was likewise so for innumerable piśāca demons and those who poison and harm sentient beings throughout the four continents, as well as those who poison and harm sentient beings within the trichiliocosm and even throughout ten million billion nayutas of worlds in the ten directions.

Then, King Mahāprabha arose from samādhi and said to Sudhana: "Good man! I know only this Bodhisattva samādhi called the Banner of Great Compassion Practice; [I do not know the practices or the realms of the Bodhisattvas who have perfected the conduct of all Buddhas, nor The great Bodhisattvas, with the great canopy of universal compassion, universally cover and protect all sentient beings; regarding those of superior, middling, and inferior capacities, they view them all equally without distinction.
Their compassion is like the great earth, bearing and nourishing all beings;
the Bodhisattva is like the full moon, emitting the light of merit to dispel the heat of all afflictions.
The Bodhisattva is a pure sun, whose light of wisdom shines universally upon all;
the Bodhisattva is a bright lamp, which extinguishes the dense darkness;
the Bodhisattva is a water-purifying jewel, which eliminates the defilements and turbidity of the ocean of afflictions in the minds of sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva is like a wish-fulfilling jewel, satisfying all sentient beings according to their inclinations;
the Bodhisattva is like a swift wind, rapidly causing sentient beings to practice samādhi and enter the city of omniscience.

How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct, praise or measure that mountain of merit, contemplate those virtues, understand the wind-circle of great vows, attain the stage of reality, discern and comprehend the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and his various samādhis as he adorns the Mahāyāna, or extol the clouds of his great compassion?

"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Anvaya; in it dwells a laywoman named Acalā. Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"
Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage to that king, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to travel south.

At that time, Sudhana reflected with right mindfulness upon the instructions of King Mahāprabha; he contemplated the practice of the Bodhisattva’s Banner of Great Compassion, the samādhi of conforming to the world with great compassion as its foremost principle;
and he brought forth the inconceivable power of merit and vows, thereby nurturing the inconceivable, steadfast wisdom of a Bodhisattva.

He contemplates the unique qualities of the bodhisattvas; he contemplates the inconceivable true nature of all phenomena; he contemplates the inconceivable retinue of the bodhisattvas; and he contemplates the inconceivable manifold activities of the bodhisattvas.

Having reflected thus, he attained a mind of joy, a mind free from desire, a mind of extreme exultation, a humble mind, a stainless mind, a clear and pure mind, a firm mind, a fearless mind, and an inexhaustible mind.
As he was thinking this, tears flowed from his eyes in sorrowful weeping. He further thought:

"Upon seeing a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), one is able to give birth to all merits, initiate the bodhisattva practices, and attain the *dhāraṇī* of pure right mindfulness. One gives birth to the radiant light of the bodhisattva samādhis, beholds all Buddhas raining down clouds of Buddha-dharma, and discerns and explains the various vows of the bodhisattvas. One gives birth to the inconceivable radiance of bodhisattva wisdom and nurtures the firm faculties of a bodhisattva."
To mind the spiritual friend is to be able to leave behind perilous paths;
to mind the spiritual friend is to be shown the correct path;
to mind the spiritual friend is to accord with the dharma of equality.
Mindfulness of spiritual friends reveals the Mahāyāna;
mindfulness of spiritual friends brings to ultimate fulfillment the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
mindfulness of spiritual friends manifests the city of omniscience.
Mindfulness of the spiritual friend crosses the ocean of all dharma-realms;
mindfulness of the spiritual friend universally illumines the ocean of all dharmas throughout the three periods of time;
mindfulness of the spiritual friend nurtures and increases all pure and white dharmas.
"By recollecting spiritual friends, one brings to fulfillment all the dharmas of the worthy and noble ones.
As Sudhana was thus recollecting with a heart of compassion, a celestial messenger of the Tathāgata, a follower of the Bodhisattva-devas, spoke to him from mid-air:
"O son of good family!
Those who comply with the instructions of spiritual friends bring joy to all Buddhas!
Those who comply with the instructions of spiritual friends draw near to omniscience!
Because their minds never grow weary of the instructions of spiritual friends, all meanings manifest before them.
“Good son! Go to the laywoman Acalā in the city of Anupama-vyūha; she is your spiritual friend, and you shall see her before long.
At that time, Sudhana arose from the samādhi of the light of wisdom and gradually traveled on foot until he reached the city of Anupama-vyūha, where he inquired about her whereabouts.
“Where is the upāsikā Acalā now?
At that time, someone said: “Good son!
The laywoman Acalā was within her home, protected by her parents and surrounded on all sides by her kin and attendants, as she expounded the True Dharma for an immeasurable multitude.
At that time, Sudhana was filled with immeasurable joy; he immediately went to her gate and entered her house.
He beheld her palace, its golden radiance shining everywhere, such that those who touched this light found their bodies and minds becoming supple and serene.
At that time, when the light of Good Wealth touched his body, he immediately attained five hundred gates of samādhi, namely:

the gate of samādhi called Awakening to All, the gate of samādhi called Extraordinary Banner, the gate of samādhi called Tranquility, the gate of samādhi called Far Removed from All Sentient Beings, the gate of samādhi called Universal Eye, and the gate of samādhi called Tathāgatagarbha.
Having attained these five hundred gates of samādhi, his body and mind became as supple as a seven-day-old embryo.
Furthermore, he smelled a wondrous fragrance surpassing that of devas and humans; he proceeded to where [the Buddha] was, joined his palms in reverence, and observed with single-minded concentration.

Beholding her form and appearance, she is beyond the reach of the gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as all the female attendants; among all women in the worlds of the ten directions, there is none equal to her.
Her countenance and complexion are exquisitely transcendent and peerless throughout the ten directions—how could there be anyone superior?
Except for the Buddhas,
there is none in the worlds of the ten directions whose palaces and their adornments can equal theirs;
there is none in the worlds of the ten directions whose mouth emits such wondrous fragrance as theirs.
As for his ornaments, there are none equal to them in the worlds of the ten directions;
as for his retinue, there are none equal to them in the worlds of the ten directions, let alone any who surpass them.
Excluding the assembly of the Tathāgata,
such supreme excellence does not cause sentient beings to give rise to thoughts of defiled attachment;
rather, for those who behold it, afflictions are extinguished, just as when the Brahmā King appears, the afflictions of the desire realm do not manifest before one.

Whoever obtains the sight of this upāsikā has all afflictions completely extinguished; the sentient beings of the ten directions delight in beholding her without weariness, with the sole exception of those who have already attained the perfection of knowledge and conduct.

At that time, Sudhana beheld that woman’s inconceivable Dharma, her inconceivable samādhi, her inconceivable and peerless exquisite form, and her immeasurable net of light, which was entirely unobstructed; he observed her inconceivable benefit to sentient beings and her inexhaustible ocean of retinues, and he gazed upon her inconceivable body without ever feeling satiety.
At that time, Sudhana spoke in verse:
"Always upholding the pure precepts, Diligently cultivating patience,
He is like the full moon at its peak, Shining alone among the stars."
At that time, having praised him with verses, Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!

I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path. I have heard that the Great Sage is well able to explain this; I pray that you will expound it for me."
At that time, she replied to Sudhana with kind and affectionate words:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! You are indeed able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

I have accomplished the Bodhisattva’s indestructible Dharma-gate, cultivated and studied the Bodhisattva’s firm conduct, attained the *dhāraṇī* of the stage of equality of all dharmas, attained the Dharma-gate of the equality of all dharmas, and attained the Samādhi of Adornment Free from Existence."
Sudhana said: “What is the Bodhisattva’s indestructible dharma-gate, up to the sphere of the samādhi called ‘Adornment Beyond Existence’? “Noble son!
"This matter is difficult to know and difficult to explain! Sudhana said,
"I only pray that the Great Sage, relying on the Buddha's spiritual power, will explain it for me."
"By means of spiritual friends, I shall come to know through faith, discern with right mindfulness, observe with single-minded compliance, distance myself from falsehood, and understand equality."
At that time, the upāsikā replied: "Good son!
In a past age, during the Vimala Kalpa, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Dīrabhuja, who appeared in the world."
At that time, there was a king named Vidyutprabha, and I was his daughter.
During the silence of midnight, when the music had ceased, my five hundred handmaidens were all fast asleep.
I was on the upper floor, gazing up at the constellations;
there I saw that Tathāgata in the midst of space, like a king of jewel mountains,

respectfully surrounded by an inconceivable multitude of great bodhisattvas, including devas and nāgas— the eight classes of beings— as they emitted a vast net of great radiance that universally illumined the ten directions.
From the pores of that Buddha’s body, a subtle and wondrous fragrance issued forth;

upon smelling this fragrance, my body became supple and my heart was filled with great joy. With reverence and prostration, I joined my palms in single-minded devotion and gazed up at that Buddha; yet I could not see the mark of his crown, nor could I perceive his limits when looking at the left and right sides of his body—his marks and signs were so majestic and adorned that I never grew weary of beholding them.
"Good son! At that time, I had this thought:

'What kind of karma must be cultivated to produce such a body, to nourish such a body, to perfect such a body, to purify such a body, and to master such a body—with its radiance, retinue, various ornaments, merit, wisdom, samādhis, dhāraṇīs, and the treasury of all eloquence, which is beyond all analogy?'"
"Good son! At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing my thoughts, addressed me, saying:
'You should give rise to an indestructible mind to eliminate and extinguish the afflictions;'"
They give rise to the supreme and wondrous mind, remaining unattached to all that exists;
they give rise to the mind of indefatigable diligence, following and deeply entering the methods of skillful means;
they give rise to the mind of forbearance, subduing the ocean of all evil minds among sentient beings.
They give rise to a mind free from delusion, remaining far removed from all realms of birth and death;
they give rise to a tireless mind, never wearying in their vision of all Buddhas;
they give rise to a mind of insatiable aspiration, drinking in the clouds of the Dharma of all Buddhas.
They give rise to a mind of tranquility, conforming to the world through the skillful means of all Buddhas;
they give rise to a mind of protection, upholding the Dharma wheel of all Buddhas;
and they give rise to a mind of discernment, expounding the treasure of the Dharma as appropriate for each being to bring them all joy.

"Good son! At that time, having heard this Dharma teaching and the gate of pure Dharma from that Tathāgata, I sought all-knowledge, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the non-falsity of his speech, the adornment of light, the pure Dharma-body, the adornment of the marks and signs, the retinue of a Tathāgata, the purification of Buddha-fields, the majestic deportment of a Tathāgata, and the lifespan of a Tathāgata.
When I gave rise to this mind, it could not be destroyed by any afflictions, nor by Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or even by the adamantine mountains."
"Good son! Since I gave rise to this mind, for as many eons as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, I have not given rise to thoughts of desire, much less engaged in such acts.
During those same eons, I have not given rise to a single thought of anger toward my own kinsmen, much less toward others."
Throughout those kalpas, he did not give rise to a mind of self-view, much less a mind of "mine-ness.
Throughout those kalpas, he did not give rise to a mind of delusion, nor a neutral (avyākṛta) mind; even while in the womb, he constantly maintained right mindfulness, let alone at other times.
Throughout all those kalpas, they see all Buddhas even within their dreams, let alone when beholding them with the ten eyes.

Throughout all those kalpas, they hear and uphold the clouds of Dharma of all Buddhas without ever forgetting a single word; they do not forget even worldly speech, let alone the words of the Tathāgata.

Throughout those kalpas, they drink from the ocean of all Buddhas' teachings, even discerning and knowing worldly dharmas; they give birth to all gates of expedient samādhis, their minds being free from falsehood.

Throughout those kalpas, they uphold the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas, not losing a single dharma within that wheel, nor possessing dualistic knowledge, except for the sake of transforming sentient beings.
Throughout those kalpas, they behold the oceans of all Buddhas and their emanated Buddhas, and in the presence of those Buddhas, they fulfill their great vows.
Throughout those kalpas, in the presence of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, I shall fully bring forth the ocean of pure Bodhisattva practices;
throughout those kalpas, if there are sentient beings who behold me, they shall all resolve their minds upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, never giving rise to even a single thought of the two vehicles;

throughout those kalpas, regarding all Buddha-dharmas, even down to a single phrase or a single flavor, I shall not give rise to doubt or confusion, nor harbor dualistic notions, false conceptions, diverse notions, notions of defiled attachment, notions of beauty or ugliness, or notions of love or hatred.

"Good son! Since I first resolved to attain enlightenment, I have constantly seen all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends; I have heard of the great vows of the Buddhas, cultivated the practices of a Bodhisattva, and realized the wisdom of the various pāramitās and the inexhaustible Dharma-treasury of the stages.
I have universally entered all infinite and boundless worlds and have discerned the realms of infinite sentient beings."
Never departing from the light of pure wisdom, they extinguish the afflictions of all sentient beings;
they nurture and inspire the roots of goodness in sentient beings, manifesting in every way appropriate to their needs;
never abandoning sublime sounds, all who hear them are filled with joy.

"Good son! I have entered this indestructible dharma-gate and observe the *dhāraṇī* of the equality of all dharmas, manifesting immeasurable sovereign spiritual transformations; do you wish to see them?"
“Yes, indeed, we wish to see it!
At that time, the laywoman Acalā entered ten thousand gates of samādhi and observed with right mindfulness, namely:

the gate of samādhi of seeking to adorn the True Dharma with a mind free from weariness; the gate of samādhi of the adornment of freedom from delusion; the gate of samādhi of the ten powers; and the gate of samādhi of the Buddha’s inexhaustible treasury.
While dwelling in such gateways of samādhi, worlds as numerous as the atoms within ten unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields shook in six ways and became as pure as lapis lazuli.
Within each and every world, one beheld ten billion Tathāgatas, each surrounded by a great assembly, emitting vast radiance that universally illumined the ten directions;
some appeared in the Tuṣita Heaven, while others appeared in all worlds, turning the pure wheel of Dharma with wondrous voices, even manifesting the Great Parinirvāṇa.
Then, the upāsikā arose from samādhi and said to Sudhana: "Good man, do you see this?"
“Yes, indeed, I have seen it. “Noble son!
I have only accomplished this indestructible dharma-gate, whereby I preach the subtle and wondrous Dharma for all sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice.”
The great Bodhisattvas travel throughout the ten directions without obstruction;

like the king of golden-winged birds, they reach the very depths of the great ocean of sentient beings, and if they see a being possessing the cause for Bodhi, they extract them from the sea of birth and death and establish them in Bodhi.

Just as a merchant enters a great island of jewels seeking exclusively the great treasure of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, they traverse the sea of birth and death to teach and transform sentient beings, eliminating their afflictions.
Like the bright, pure sun, it dries up the waters of craving and causes the lotuses of all sentient beings to bloom;
like a swift wind blowing through the ten directions, it destroys the branches of the trees of false views and afflictions of all sentient beings;
like the great earth, it nurtures the roots of goodness of all sentient beings.
"Just as a Wheel-Turning King gathers sentient beings through the four methods of attraction,
how could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct? Good son!"

To the south of here, there is a land named Incomparable and a city named Contentment. There dwells a renunciant non-Buddhist practitioner named Accordant with All Sentient Beings; go to him and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva practice and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, Sudhana maintained single-minded, right mindfulness:
"That laywoman is my true spiritual friend."

One should mindfully recollect that sublime teaching, that which was spoken, that which was brought forth, that which was opened up, that which was manifested, that which was praised, that which was clarified, that which was extensively expounded, and that which was practiced;
one should cultivate contemplation in accordance with these, universally cultivating tranquility and cessation, illuminating and observing them.
Gradually passing through cities and villages, at sunset he entered the city of Saṃtuṣṭa and searched everywhere, asking:
"Where is the non-Buddhist teacher Sarvasattvanugata now?"
During the middle watch of the night, he saw a great mountain to the north of that city, its radiance shining like the rising sun.

At that time, Sudhana left the city at dawn and ascended the mountain, where he saw from afar an ascetic practicing walking meditation in a hermitage for non-Buddhists; his wondrous form surpassed even that of Brahmā, and he was surrounded by a retinue of ten thousand Brahmās.
He went to where he was, prostrated himself at his feet, stood to one side, and said: "Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
He replied, “Excellent! Excellent!”
"O son of good family!
You are indeed able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
O son of good family!"

I have already established myself in the bodhisattva practice that reaches all places, having accomplished the dharma-gate of the Samādhi of Universal Observation, and possessing the supernormal power (*ṛddhi*) of non-reliance and non-action. By means of the light of the *prajñāpāramitā* of equality, I observe and discern all realms of existence (*gati*), seeing all sentient beings die here and be born there, transmigrating through various states of being—of diverse kinds, with various forms and colors, beautiful or ugly, with various desires and pleasures, and taking birth in the various realms, namely:
devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, the realm of King Yama, humans, and non-humans.
Those sentient beings may be attached to false views, or prefer the Two Vehicles, or delight in the Mahāyāna; [the Buddha] benefits them through wondrous wisdom and various skillful means.
Some teach the various worldly arts and crafts, desiring to cause sentient beings to attain the *dhāraṇī* gates of all skillful techniques;
some employ the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) to gather in sentient beings, desiring to cause them all to attain *sarvajñatā*;
or some praise the various *pāramitās*, desiring to cause sentient beings to attain the dedication toward omniscience.
Some praised the arousal of the bodhicitta, wishing to ensure that sentient beings could not be thwarted in their roots of goodness;
some praised the practices of Bodhisattvas, wishing to cause sentient beings to adorn and purify Buddha-fields, fulfill great vows, and transform sentient beings;
some spoke of the Dharma of wearying detachment, wishing to cause sentient beings to know the fruits of evil conduct and the sufferings of the three miserable realms.

In some instances, he speaks of the pure Dharma and aspiration, desiring to cause sentient beings to give rise to a heart of joy, plant the roots of all virtues before the Buddhas, and attain the fruit of omniscience;
in other instances, he extols the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, desiring to cause sentient beings to give rise to great vows and single-mindedly seek the pure Dharmakāya;
and in yet others, he extols the merits of the Tathāgata, desiring to cause sentient beings to single-mindedly and joyfully seek the indestructible body of the Buddha.
Or they may praise the incomparable, wondrous Dharma of the Tathāgata, desiring to cause sentient beings to attain all the indestructible merits of a Buddha.
Furthermore, good son!

Within this city of Saṃtuṣita, among all the people—men and women, old and young—I have transformed and delivered them all according to their respective capacities, yet those sentient beings do not know who I am.
In this Jambudvīpa, there are ninety-six kinds of heterodox paths and false views; for all of them, I have preached various teachings to sever those false views.

Likewise, throughout the trichiliocosm and even in all worlds of the ten directions, I use various gates of wisdom and skillful means, diverse matters, forms, and sounds to transform, deliver, and benefit the ocean-like multitude of sentient beings. It is exactly thus.
"Good son! I know only this bodhisattva dharma-gate of reaching all places.

The bodies of the great bodhisattvas are as numerous as the count of all sentient beings; they have all attained the samādhi that distinguishes the bodies of all sentient beings, produce wheels of transformations, travel everywhere through all worlds and all realms of existence, and manifest universally before all sentient beings throughout the ten directions."
Those who behold them find joy in gazing upon them without weariness, and they are able to nurture all roots of goodness.

Abiding through all kalpas, they do not forsake their great vows; they attain the practice of the *indranīla* jewel-like radiant adornment, remaining unattached to anything while single-mindedly seeking the true meaning. They accord with sentient beings, viewing the three periods of time as equal, illuminating the realm of non-self, and being fully endowed with the inexhaustible treasury of great compassion.
"How could I possibly know or describe the merit, wisdom, and pure conduct of that [bodhisattva]?

Good son, to the south of here there is a land named Amṛtarasa. There dwells an elder named Utpalagandha; go to him and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of that non-Buddhist teacher with his head, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, Sudhana did not spare his own body or life, nor was he attached to wealth or treasures; he remained far removed from the burning fires of worldly passion.

He was unattached to the various realms of existence, unattached to the pleasures of the five worldly desires, and unattached to the power and sovereignty of his retinue. He constantly delighted in transforming and liberating all sentient beings, purifying all Buddha-worlds, and reverently making offerings to all Buddhas without ever feeling weary or satisfied. He understood the true nature of all phenomena and desired to attain the vast ocean of all bodhisattva merits, fulfilling his great vows.

Throughout all kalpas, they cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva; they visit the oceans of all Buddhas and their retinues, enter all bodhisattva samādhis, and are able to manifest all the sovereign spiritual powers of bodhisattvas.
Within a single pore, they behold all Buddhas without ever feeling weary or satisfied;
they hear and uphold the clouds of the true Dharma wheels of all Buddhas without ever feeling weary or satisfied, single-mindedly seeking all such merits of bodhisattvas and Buddhas.

Traveling gradually, he arrived at the country of Amṛtarasa and went to the residence of the householder Nīlotpala-gandha. He prostrated with his head at the householder's feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood to one side, saying:
"O Great Sage!"

I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, turning toward the unsurpassed path with the intent to seek the wisdom of all Buddhas; I desire to fulfill the great vows of all Buddhas, to purify the form-bodies (*rūpakāya*) of all Buddhas, to behold the dharma-bodies (*dharmakāya*) of all Buddhas, and to know the wisdom-bodies (*jñānakāya*) of all Buddhas. I desire to purify and complete all bodhisattva practices, to illumine all gates of bodhisattva samādhis, to accomplish all bodhisattva dhāraṇīs, to utterly eliminate all obstacles, and to travel throughout all Buddha-worlds. Yet, I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, cultivate the bodhisattva path, and give rise to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).
He replied, "Excellent! Excellent!"
"O son of good family!
You are indeed able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
O son of good family!"
I am able to thoroughly know all kinds of fragrances: all blended perfumes, all incense for burning, all unguents, all powdered incenses, all king-of-fragrances, and all celestial scents;
as well as those of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and so forth.
The fragrance of mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth; the fragrance that eliminates all diseases of sentient beings; the fragrance that extinguishes grief and affliction;
the fragrance that gives rise to all joy and happiness for sentient beings; the fragrance that nurtures the various afflictions;
the fragrance that eliminates the various afflictions; the fragrance of delighting in the conditioned; and the fragrance of wearying of and renouncing the conditioned.
I fully understand such fragrances as: the fragrance of incense, the fragrance of heedlessness, the fragrance of non-heedlessness, the fragrance of mindfulness of all Buddhas,
the fragrance of conformity to the True Dharma, the fragrance of noble sages, the fragrance of the discernment of all Bodhisattvas,
the fragrance of all Bodhisattva stages, and the fragrance of all Bodhisattva abodes.

He thoroughly understands the arising, the range of activity, the accomplishment, the fulfillment, the purification, the peace, the skillful means, the objective sphere, the conduct, and the root of those fragrances.

"Good son! Among humans there is a fragrance named Great Elephant Treasury (Mahāgajagarbha), which arises from the combat of dragons. If one pellet is burned, it raises a great cloud-net of light that covers the Land of Ambrosial Flavor (Amṛtarasā), raining down fragrant water for seven days and seven nights.
If it is applied to the body, the body becomes golden in color."
If they wear clothing, or dwell in palaces and towers, these too shall all be golden in color;

if there are sentient beings who catch this fragrance, for seven days and seven nights they will be filled with joy and delight, all illnesses will be extinguished, they will be free from madness and violence, they will distance themselves from hearts of fear and harm, and they will single-mindedly turn toward great compassion, universally mindful of all sentient beings.
Having known them thus, I preach the Dharma for them, causing immeasurable sentient beings to attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Forty-nine and Scroll Fifty.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Seventh Part of the Thirty-Fourth Chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm. "Good son!
Furthermore, there is a fragrance named Gośīrṣa-candana, which arises from the King of Mountains, Vimala. If it is applied to the body, fire cannot burn it;..."
Furthermore, there is a fragrance named Indestructible, which arises from the great ocean; if it is applied to the body, it produces wondrous sounds that subdue enemies and adversaries.

Again, there is a fragrance named Lotus-Black Aloeswood, which grows on the four shores of Lake Anavatapta; if a single pellet is burned, it can universally perfume the entire Jambudvīpa realm, and if any sentient beings catch the scent of this fragrance, they will leave all evils behind and become endowed with pure precepts.

Again, there is a fragrance named Radiant Appearance, which arises from the King of Snow Mountains; if any sentient beings hear this fragrance, they will be freed from all defilements and their minds will attain purity. One then preaches the Dharma for them, causing them all to attain the Bodhisattva Samādhi of Stainless Perfection.

Furthermore, there is an incense named Ocean Treasury (*Sāgaragarbha*), produced in the land of the rākṣasas; it is fit for a wheel-turning king (*cakravartin*), and if one pellet is burned, it causes the fourfold army to stand arrayed in the void.

Furthermore, there is an incense named Pure Adornment (*Vimalavyūha*), produced in the Hall of Good Dharma (*Sudharmā*); if one pellet is burned, it enables all the devas to attain the Buddha-remembrance samādhi (*buddhānusmṛti-samādhi*).

Furthermore, there is an incense named Pure Treasury (*Vimalagarbha*), produced in the Yāma Heaven; if one pellet is burned, it causes all those devas to gather like clouds and proceed to the King of the Yāma Heaven to hear and receive the True Dharma.

Furthermore, there is an incense named Saindhava, which originates from Tuṣita Heaven and constantly remains before the seat of a Bodhisattva in his final birth. If a single pellet is burned, it raises a great cloud of fragrance that universally covers all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, raining down immeasurable adornments as offerings to all Buddhas and their retinues.

Furthermore, there is an incense named Mind-Transforming, which originates from the Nirmāṇarati Heaven. If a single pellet is burned, for seven days and seven nights in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, it rains down a rain of adornments.
"Good son! I know only this fragrance.

As for the great Bodhisattvas who have distanced themselves from all unwholesome habitual tendencies, who have forever abandoned the five desires, extinguished the afflictions, subdued the hosts of Māras, severed all bonds, and departed from the three realms of existence; who adorn themselves with the wondrous fragrance of wisdom, remain unstained by anything in all worlds, and fully accomplish the fragrance of unimpeded precepts; who eliminate obstacles and whose sphere of wisdom is unhindered and penetrating; whose minds are always equanimous—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct, their gates of pure precepts, or how their actions of body, speech, and mind are free from all evil?"

"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Kūṭāgāra. There dwells a maritime navigator named Īśvara. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of that elder, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to travel south.

At that time, Sudhana proceeded toward the city of Kūṭāgāraśālā; he observed the right path, sought the right path with single-minded devotion, and contemplated paths that were level or rugged, defiled or pure, and secure or perilous.
Again, he reflects:
"By means of spiritual friends, one attains the path of the bodhisattvas and the paths of the various pāramitās;
one gathers in sentient beings and leads them into the unobstructed dharma-realm; one accords with all sentient beings and extinguishes all the blazing afflictions and all false views."
They uproot all thorns of unwholesomeness, cross the ocean of all birth and death, and will certainly reach the city of omniscience.
Why is this? Because by means of a spiritual friend, one attains all roots of goodness.
"Through a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one attains all-knowledge.
Having formed this thought, he gradually traveled on until he reached the city of Kūṭāgāra, where he searched everywhere for the master mariner Svayambhūsamudra.

I saw him dwelling at a seaport where ships were moored, surrounded by a hundred thousand merchants and an immeasurable multitude who, desiring to hear the supreme Dharma, had gathered to listen to the Dharma of entering the great ocean and the Dharma of the ocean of the Buddha’s merits.
He went to where he was, prostrated with his head at his feet, and standing to one side, addressed him, saying: "Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
He replied, “Excellent! Excellent!”
"Good son! You are indeed able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;

you are able to inquire of me regarding the wondrous jewel of the Mahāyāna, which crosses the ocean of birth and death to reach the continent of all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*), attains the indestructible Dharma of the Mahāyāna, leaves behind the perils of the two vehicles, dwells in the bliss of cessation, and stays far removed from the swirling abysses of the currents of birth and death. You have attained the *dhāraṇī*-wheel of the path to the ultimate destination of Bodhisattvas, the path adorned by Bodhisattvas, the waves of the path to *sarvajñā*, and have perfected the gateway of universal Dharma. Thus, you are without obstruction regarding all phenomena and cross the ocean of all-knowledge."

"Good son! I have accomplished the Dharma-door of the Pure Practice of the Banner of Great Compassion. Here, within this city of pavilions on the seashore, I perform various ascetic practices for the sake of the poor, desiring to cause all their wishes to be fully satisfied according to their desires. Having done so, I extensively preach the Dharma to bring them all joy, causing them to arouse roots of goodness and nurture the treasury of merit and wisdom;

sharpening the faculties of Bodhisattvas, inspiring the Bodhi-mind, purifying the Bodhisattva’s straightforward mind, increasing the Bodhisattva’s profound resolve, giving birth to and nurturing the power of great compassion, removing the suffering of birth and death, wandering through the ocean of birth and death without weariness, gathering in the ocean of sentient beings, causing them to dwell in the ocean of merit, attaining the light of the ocean of wisdom of all dharmas, beholding the ocean of all Buddhas, and crossing over the ocean of all-knowledge."
"Good son! Abiding in this city, I contemplate in this way and maintain right mindfulness in this way for the benefit of sentient beings. Good son!"
I know all the jewel islands in the ocean, all the characteristics of jewels, all produced jewels, and all pure as well as impure jewels;
I know the value of all jewels and all jewel vessels;
and I know how all jewels are to be applied according to their respective uses.
They know how to produce all jewels;
they know the spheres of all jewels;
they know the radiance of all jewels.
They know all the palaces of the nāgas and extinguish all calamities caused by nāgas;
they know all the palaces of the rākṣasas and extinguish all calamities caused by rākṣasas;
they know all the palaces of large-bodied beings and extinguish all calamities caused by large-bodied beings.
He knows the currents and knows how to abandon the eddies, fears, and terrors; he is able to leave behind the waves.
He knows the characteristics of the water’s color, knows the sun, moon, and constellations, and knows all forms of calculation. He knows day and night, and knows the *kṣaṇa*, *lava*, and *muhūrta*.
He knows going and staying, and the dharmas of security and peril.

I know the method for determining whether a ship on the ocean is secure or not; I clearly observe the signs of the winds to steer it accordingly and understand the destination to be reached. Good son!

Having accomplished such wisdom for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, I enter the great ocean to preach the Dharma for them, causing them all to rejoice, to leave behind the fear of birth and death, to enter the ocean of omniscience, to exhaust the ocean of craving and desire, to attain the ocean of wisdom that illuminates the three periods of time, to cross the ocean of all suffering, to purify the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, to adorn and purify the ocean of all Buddha-lands, and to travel everywhere through the ocean of all worlds in the ten directions without any obstruction.

He knows the ocean of faculties and vows of all sentient beings; he accords with the ocean of practices of all sentient beings; and he knows the ocean of what is appropriate for each sentient being. Good son!
I have accomplished this Dharma-door of the Pure Conduct of the Banner of Great Compassion;
for anyone who sees, hears, or remembers me, none of it shall be in vain.
O son of good family!
