I know only this Dharma door; as for the great Bodhisattvas who traverse the great ocean of birth, death, and afflictions without being stained by them, who leave behind the ocean of false views and enter the ocean of true reality, who gather in the ocean of sentient beings through skillful means and abide in the ocean of all-knowledge, who extinguish the ocean of all sentient beings' heedlessness, who skillfully discern the oceans of proper and improper timing, and who skillfully employ expedients to transform sentient beings without ever missing the right moment—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

“Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Sukhāvatī. In it dwells an elder named Anuttarajaya. Go to him and ask: ‘How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?’”
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and with tears flowing from his sorrowful weeping, took his leave and traveled south.

At that time, Sudhana’s great loving-kindness and great compassion increased and expanded; he was moistened and nurtured by the adornments of merit and wisdom. Free from the defilement of afflictions, he entered the dharma of equality, and his mind became free from negligence.

He pulled out the thorns of unwholesomeness, extinguished all hindrances, and with firm diligence cultivated the inconceivable samādhis of a bodhisattva. The light of his wisdom shone everywhere; he dwelt in tranquil bliss within a pond of merit where the flowers of liberation bloomed. Having fulfilled his great vows, he pervaded the entire dharma-realm without obstruction, heading toward omniscience and single-mindedly seeking the true path of the bodhisattvas.
Traveling gradually, he arrived at the city of Sukhāvatī and searched everywhere for the supreme elder Anuttaravara.
To the east of the city was a forest named Viśokābhirati-suvyūha-dhvaja;

at that time, the elder was in this forest, surrounded on all sides by immeasurable elders, adjudicating state affairs while preaching the Dharma. He had abandoned the notions of "I" and "mine" as well as all forms of existence, and being far removed from envy, his ocean-like mind was pure. Abiding in a purified mind, he constantly beheld all Buddhas, attained the power of stainless faith, received the teachings of all Buddhas, gave rise to the power of a bodhisattva, and practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva. He brought forth the power of all bodhisattva samādhis, manifested the power of all bodhisattva wisdoms, expounded the power of a bodhisattva’s right mindfulness, and delighted in generating the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment.
At that time, Sudhana went to the place where the elder was and, out of reverence for the Dharma, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground. After a long while, he rose and said:
"O Great Sage!

I am Sudhana, I am Sudhana. I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct, cultivate the bodhisattva path, and teach and transform sentient beings; nor how one may constantly behold all Buddhas, inquire about the true Dharma, and fully receive and uphold the clouds of the Buddhas' teachings; nor how one may single-mindedly turn toward all gates of skillful means, practice the bodhisattva conduct throughout all worlds and all eons, know the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, be sustained by the support of all Buddhas, and attain the power of all Buddhas.
Then, that elder said to Sudhana: "Excellent! Excellent!"
"O son of good family!
You are indeed able to resolve upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
O son of good family!"

I have accomplished the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas Reaching All Destinations, and the power of the spiritual footprints that are non-reliant and non-active. Good son,
what is this Dharma-gate of the Adornment of Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas Reaching All Destinations?

"Good son! Within this trichiliocosm, there are all the worlds of the asuras; all the worlds of the garuḍas, hell-beings, hungry ghosts, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, gandharvas, humans, and non-humans; the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, up to the Māra Heaven;

and all the realms of rebirth, all celestial palaces, and all dragon palaces inhabited by those in the world’s desire realm, including the abodes of all yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas."
He teaches the Dharma within the lands, cities, towns, and villages of the human realm;

he eliminates disputes and all hearts of malice and harm, completely releasing those in bondage and causing them all to emerge from prison. He frees them from all terrors, extinguishes unwholesome karma, and brings an end to the killing of sentient beings, as well as to wrong views, royal affairs, and state matters.
Keeping them far from unwholesome dharmas, he causes all sentient beings to eradicate every evil, instructing them in skillful arts and various treatises to benefit all and cause them all to rejoice.
He accords with all the various groups of non-Buddhists, manifesting supreme and wondrous wisdom;
he remains far removed from false views and delights in the Buddha-dharma,
even preaching the Dharma extensively up to the Brahma Heaven.

In this way, throughout this trichiliocosm and even across unspeakably unspeakable billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within them, he extensively expounds the True Dharma—namely:

the Buddha-dharma, the Bodhisattva-dharma, the dharma of sentient beings, the Śrāvaka-dharma, and the Pratyekabuddha-dharma; he speaks of the dharmas of the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and Yama;
he manifests the suffering of the evil paths and speaks of the heavenly realms, manifesting the bliss of the heavens; he speaks of worldly dharmas and the dharmas that transcend the world.

It reveals the Bodhisattva path, brings about liberation from the evils of birth and death, and expounds the sublime merits of omniscience; it extinguishes the suffering of ignorance and all obstacles;

and it seeks to enable sentient beings to attain transcendence from worldly pleasures, to depart from all falsehoods, to understand the true Dharma, to distance themselves from evil karma, to extinguish all afflictions, and to turn the pure wheel of the Dharma.
Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the Adornment of Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas Reaching All Destinies, and the power of spiritual penetrations that are without dependence or fabrication.

These great Bodhisattvas are fully endowed with the accomplishment of all supernatural powers (*abhijñā*), illuminations (*vidyā*), and bodies equal to Buddha-fields; they have attained the stage of the Universal Eye (*samantacakṣur-bhūmi*), know the path of language, possess sovereign spiritual power, and are complete in wisdom. Free from all contention, they have attained the mark of the broad and long tongue of a Great Man, emitting a subtle and wondrous sound that none can destroy. They discern all Buddhas of the three periods of time without dualistic thought, and their clear and pure wisdom illumines the dharmas of the three periods. Their realm is immeasurable and as pure as space. How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Good son! To the south of here, there is a land called Dussaha and a city named Kaliṅgapati. There dwells a bhikṣuṇī named Siṃhavijṛmbhitā. Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that elder, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with longing and reverence, took his leave, and traveled southward.
At that time, the youth Sudhana gradually traveled until he reached that city, where he inquired everywhere for that bhikṣuṇī.
Then, a great multitude of men and women replied to Sudhana:
"This bhikṣuṇī is currently in the Sunlight Grove within the royal park, benefiting all sentient beings with the Dharma."
At that time, Sudhana went to that grove and surveyed it thoroughly. He saw a great tree named Pūrṇacandra (Full Moon), which emitted a great radiance that illuminated a hundred yojanas.
He also saw a great tree named Samantacchādana (Universal Canopy), shaped like a parasol, emitting blue light.
He further saw a flower tree named Kusumagarbha (Flower Treasury), as high as the Snowy Mountains, raining down clouds of various flowers like Śakra’s Pārijātaka tree.
Furthermore, he saw a great tree named Soft and Supple, its radiance shining everywhere and always bearing fruit;
he also saw a great tree named Bright and Pure, adorned with incomparable *mani* jewels that produced incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) pure and wondrous gems;
and he also saw clothing trees, which yielded treasuries of incalculable wondrous jewel garments.
Furthermore, he saw trees of joy that spontaneously produced subtle and wondrous sounds;
he also saw trees of universal adornment and incense that emitted all manner of fragrances, which perfumed the ten directions without obstruction;

he further saw the springs, streams, and deep ponds of that garden, surrounded on all sides by rows of sandalwood trees and adorned with railings of the seven treasures. At their bottoms, black sandalwood mud settled and pooled, while golden sand was spread across them. The waters of eight virtues filled them completely, and blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), night-blooming water lilies (*kumuda*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*) flourished in vibrant profusion, covering the surface entirely.

Jeweled trees surrounded the area, majestic and exquisite; beneath each tree were spread countless lion thrones, draped with precious garments, perfumed with various incenses, and covered with canopies of many jewels. Pure white jeweled nets overspread them from above, and within the nets of golden bells, wondrous sounds issued forth.

In some places beneath the trees were spread lion thrones of lotus-treasury; in some, thrones of fragrance-treasury; in some, thrones of dragon-adorned treasury; in some, lion thrones of jewel-aggregate; in some, thrones of luminous and pure universal illumination-treasury; and in some, lion thrones of joy-treasury.

Each of those individual seats was surrounded by a retinue of one hundred thousand precious lion-thrones; they were adorned with immeasurable ornaments, strewn with countless jewels, and filled within like a treasure island in the ocean.
Jeweled robes were spread upon the ground, soft and exquisite; when stepped upon, they sank to the ankle, and when lifted, they returned to their original state.
Various kinds of birds emitted harmonious and elegant sounds, surpassing the Garden of Joy of Śakra;
various flowering trees constantly rained down clouds of blossoms, excelling the Illuminating Garden of Śakra.
Exquisite fragrances waft everywhere, surpassing those of Śakra’s Hall of Good Dharma;
the jeweled trees and music trees produce subtle and wondrous sounds that exceed the singing voices of the goddesses of the Heaven of Good Oratory;
and the adornments of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of pavilions never tire the beholder, surpassing even Śakra’s Great City of Sudarśana.
All the ornaments of this garden were like those of the Brahma palace, which sentient beings delighted in beholding.

At that time, Sudhana saw that this grove was entirely formed by the karmic practices of Bodhisattvas, arisen from roots of goodness transcending all worlds, obtained through making offerings to inconceivable Buddhas, and incapable of being destroyed.

All of these were produced by the roots of goodness nurtured within the treasury of merit by the Bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā, who realized that all phenomena are like illusions; thus, the gods, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, and immeasurable sentient beings of the trichiliocosm could all enter this garden without it becoming crowded.
Why is this? It is because of the inconceivable power of this bhikṣuṇī’s majestic spiritual authority.
At that time, Sudhana saw the bhikṣuṇī seated upon lion thrones made entirely of jewels; she was upright, dignified, and exquisite in appearance, her deportment composed and orderly.
His mind is tranquil and his faculties are subdued, like a noble elephant; he is like a clear, deep pool or a wish-fulfilling gem;
unstained by the five desires, he is like a lotus flower;
his mind is fearless, like a lion king.
Abiding securely in pure precepts, they are unshakable like Mount Sumeru;
they extinguish the heat of the afflictions of sentient beings like the king of cooling incenses;
and they eliminate all maladies like the king of excellent medicines.
Those who see him do not do so in vain, just as with the god Vairōcana;
he nurtures roots of goodness, like a fertile field.
He was seen seated upon a throne, surrounded by a retinue of gods from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, expounding for them the inexhaustible Dharma-gate.
Furthermore, he saw [the Buddha] seated on a throne, surrounded by the Brahma-hosts such as the Joyful Brahmās, preaching for them the Dharma-gate of Universal Wondrous Sound;

he also saw [the Buddha] seated on a throne, surrounded by the retinues of immeasurable kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, including sons and daughters of gods, preaching for them the Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva’s Pure Sovereignty;

he also saw [the Buddha] seated on a throne, surrounded by the retinues of kings of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, including sons and daughters of gods, preaching for them the Dharma-gate of Purifying All Adornments.

Furthermore, I saw him seated on a throne, surrounded by a retinue of gods and goddesses, including the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, for whom he was expounding the Dharma-gate of the Revolving Heart-Treasury;
I also saw him seated on a throne, surrounded by a retinue of gods and goddesses, including the King of the Yāma Heaven, for whom he was expounding the Dharma-gate of Immeasurable Adornments;

and I also saw him seated on a throne, surrounded by a retinue of gods and goddesses, including the King of the Śakra Heaven, for whom he was expounding the Dharma-gate of Worldly Disgust and Renunciation.

Furthermore, I saw the Dragon King Sāgara, the Dragon King Daśaraśmi, the Dragon Kings Nanda and Upananda, the Dragon King Manasvin, the Dragon King Erapattra, the Dragon King Anavatapta, and others, surrounded by their retinues of dragon sons and dragon daughters, teaching them the Dharma-gate of skillful means for the protection and salvation of sentient beings;
I also saw the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and others, surrounded by their retinues of male and female gandharvas, teaching them the inexhaustible Dharma-gate;

and I also saw the Mahoragas, the Asura kings, and their retinues, surrounding [the Buddha] on their seats, teaching them the Dharma-gate of the adornment of the wisdom of skillful means regarding the dharma-realm.
Furthermore, he saw [the Buddha] seated, surrounded by a retinue of powerful Garuḍa kings, teaching them the Dharma-gate of Fearlessness within the Ocean of Birth and Death;
he also saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of Tumburu Kiṃnara kings, teaching them the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of the Buddha’s Conduct;
and he also saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of Meghaśaila Mahoraga kings, teaching them the Dharma-gate of the Buddha’s Joy.
Furthermore, I saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of immeasurable men, women, boys, and girls, teaching them the Dharma-gate of the Supreme Destinations;
I also saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of Rākṣasa kings and others who constantly seize the lives of beings, teaching them the Dharma-gate of giving rise to Great Compassion;
and I also saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of those who delight in the Śrāvaka vehicle, teaching them the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Supreme Wisdom.

Furthermore, he saw [the Buddha] seated, surrounded by a retinue of those who delight in the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Radiance of the Tathāgata’s Pure Merits;
he also saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of those who delight in the Mahāyāna, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Wisdom Radiance of the Universal Gate Samādhi;
and he also saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds on enlightenment, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Great Vows of all Buddhas.
Again, I saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of second-stage bodhisattvas, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Stainless Samādhi;
again, I saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of third-stage bodhisattvas, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of Tranquil Adornment;
again, I saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of fourth-stage bodhisattvas, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Sphere of the Power of All-Knowledge.
Furthermore, he saw [the Buddha] seated, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the fifth stage, expounding for them the Dharma-door of the Pure Mind Flower Treasury;
again, he saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the sixth stage, expounding for them the Dharma-door of the Clearly Pure Treasury;
and again, he saw him seated, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the seventh stage, expounding for them the Dharma-door of the Universal Ground Treasury.

Furthermore, he saw [the Buddha] seated on a throne, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the eighth stage, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the realm of the Dharma-realm and the Dharma-body;
he also saw him seated on a throne, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the ninth stage, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the adornment of non-existence and non-attachment;
and he also saw him seated on a throne, surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the tenth stage, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of unimpeded samādhi.
Furthermore, he saw himself seated upon a throne, surrounded by a retinue of Vajrapāṇi spirits, expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Wisdom-Vajra.
He saw himself in such seats as these, amidst all realms of existence and surrounded by the retinues of all sentient beings.
For those who have planted roots of goodness, he preaches the roots of goodness;

for those whose roots of goodness have grown, he preaches the increase of all roots of goodness. He teaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate for each, until they attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Why is this? Because this bhikṣuṇī has accomplished one million asaṃkhyeya gates of the *prajñāpāramitā*, namely:

the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the Universal Eye; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* that expounds all Buddha-dharmas; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* that discerns the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*); the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* that shatters and disperses all obstacles; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* that gives birth to and nurtures the wholesome dharmas of all sentient beings; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of supreme adornment; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the unobstructed treasury; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the perfection of the dharma-realm; the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the treasury of the pure mind; and the gate of the *prajñāpāramitā* of the treasury of the joy of all sentient beings.
He attained as many as one million asaṃkhyeya gates of prajñāpāramitā such as these.
Within this garden, all sentient beings attained non-retrogression from anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi.
At that time, Sudhana beheld the various extraordinary wonders of the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā; namely:

her groves and gardens, her requisites for life, her modes of walking and deportment, her precious lion throne, her great assembly of followers, her manifold sublime virtues, her sovereign supernormal powers, and her exquisite voice—all such extraordinary wonders as these.
Furthermore, they heard subtle and pure sounds proclaiming and praising the inconceivable Dharma.

Moistened by immeasurable clouds of Dharma, their bodies and minds became supple; prostrating themselves with their five limbs touching the ground in reverent worship, they were about to circumambulate when they saw bhikṣuṇīs filling every seat.
They saw themselves and the immeasurable multitude, as well as the trees and groves, all turning to the right and circling countless times.
Having seen this, he joined his palms in reverence, stood to one side, and said:
"O Great Sage!

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices or cultivate the bodhisattva path. I only pray that the Great Sage will explain this for me."
“Good son! I have accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the foundation of all-knowledge. “O Great Sage!”
"What is the essential nature of this dharma-gate?
"Good son, this dharma-gate is the Adornment of Wisdom-Light; in a single thought-moment, it universally illumines the three periods of time."
“Great Sage! What is the sphere of this Dharma-gate of the Adornment of Wisdom-Light? “Good son!

Upon entering this Dharma-door and manifesting the Samādhi of the Forest of All Dharmas before one's eyes, from each and every Buddha residing in the Tuṣita Heaven throughout all worlds in the ten directions, he emanates from his own body as many *maṇi* bodies as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands, and pays them respectful homage and prostrations.

Furthermore, they brought flowers, incense, necklaces, various exquisite jewel garlands, powdered incense, ointments, robes, parasols, banners, and pennants—as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields—in the form of clouds of various precious flowers, up to clouds of all manner of ornaments, including jeweled nets, jeweled canopies, and decorative lattices, as well as various precious thrones. With such offerings, they made worship to the Tathāgata, just as the offerings were presented in the Tuṣita Heaven: at the descent into the mother’s womb, at birth, at the residence in the palace, at the renunciation of home to study the Way, at the arrival at the Bodhi tree, at the attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment, at the turning of the pure wheel of Dharma, and even at the entry into parinirvāṇa among gods, humans, and non-humans; their offerings were likewise performed in this same manner.
If there are sentient beings who know that I am making offerings, they shall all attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
and whenever there are sentient beings who come to my presence, I shall immediately expound the Prajñāpāramitā for them.
I do not give rise to the notion of sentient beings;
I do not grasp at the marks of sentient beings;
and though I know all languages, I am not attached to language.
They behold all Buddhas, yet do not grasp at the marks of a Buddha, for they deeply understand the Dharma-body;
they receive and uphold the Dharma-wheels of all Buddhas, yet do not grasp at the marks of the Dharma-wheel, for they comprehend the true nature of all Buddhas;
in every thought-moment they are able to fill the entire Dharma-realm, yet do not grasp at the marks of the Dharma-realm, for they realize that all phenomena are like illusions.
"Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva Dharma-gate of the Foundation of All-Knowledge.
The great Bodhisattvas have reached the ultimate limit of the Dharma-realm and are entirely unattached; with a single body sitting cross-legged, they fill the entire Dharma-realm."
Within one's own body, one can manifest all Buddha-fields;
in a single thought-moment, one can travel to the presence of all Buddhas;
within one's own body, one can manifest the spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
One is able to lift unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-worlds with a single hair;
within a single pore, one manifests the formation and destruction of unspeakably unspeakable worlds;
and within a single thought-moment, one gathers in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings.
Within a single thought-moment, they encompass unspeakably unspeakable eons;
how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? Good son!

To the south of here, there is a land called Durga, and a city named Ratnavyuha. There dwells a woman named Vasumitra; go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of the bhikṣuṇī, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with longing and contemplation, and took his leave to travel south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana’s mind was illuminated by the light of great wisdom; he fully cultivated all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), contemplated the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena with single-minded focus, established the treasury of *dhāraṇīs* of all languages, and extensively practiced and maintained the *dhāraṇī* of all wheels of Dharma (*dharmacakra*). Acting as a refuge for sentient beings through the power of great compassion, he skillfully observed all-knowledge and fulfilled pure great vows equal to the dharma-realm. With the light of clear and pure wisdom, he universally illumined the sentient beings of the ten directions, and the power of all adornments and supernormal knowledges filled all worlds throughout the ten directions, ultimately bringing to completion all the karmas of a bodhisattva.
Gradually traveling on, she arrived at the city of Ratnavyūha in the country of Durgama and inquired:
"Where is the woman Vasumitrā now? At that time, there were some who did not know of her profound wisdom and thought to themselves:

"This youth now possesses dignified and composed deportment; his mind is tranquil, his faculties are subdued, and he is far removed from negligence, perversion, and confusion. Mindfulness and wisdom are present before him; his gaze is careful and discerning, and his voice is harmonious and elegant. He is unattached to forms and colors, contemplating the profound characteristics of phenomena with right mindfulness. Free from weariness, his mind is like the great ocean. This is no man of defiled desire or perversion;

he has no thoughts of sensual passion, does not sink into the mire of desire, and does not follow the dictates of his senses. His conduct has transcended the realm of Māra; he does not indulge in the five desires and is not bound by any of the Māras. Since he is already able to refrain from what ought not to be done, for what purpose does he seek this girl?"
Among them, some who had previously known that the girl possessed wisdom spoke thus:
"Excellent! This youth has attained a great and wholesome benefit in that he is able to seek out a woman of profound wisdom."

"Young man, you should know that you seek the Buddha with single-minded devotion, desiring to gather in all sentient beings, to extract the thorns of desire, and to shatter and disperse the notion of purity. Good son!"
"Now this woman is within the inner palace of this city.
At that time, having heard these words, Sudhana was filled with great joy and went to her gate.

He saw that palace and residence, magnificent and vast, surrounded on all sides by ten layers of precious walls. Ten rows of precious *tāla* trees were planted in succession, and there were ten layers of deep moats filled with water possessing the eight virtues; their bottoms were strewn with golden sand, and wonderful jewel lotuses—*utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka*—bloomed in lush profusion, covering the surface of the water and emitting a subtle fragrance capable of transforming the human mind and preventing the arising of defilement.
The palace halls were made of various jewels, with terraces, pavilions, and towers adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) gems;
the ground of deep-blue lapis lazuli was sprinkled with scented water, perfumed with agallochum, and anointed with sandalwood, all covered by nets of jewels;
bells made of Jambūnada gold hung down, emitting harmonious and elegant sounds.
Various precious flowers were scattered like falling clouds;
their exquisite adornments are beyond description.
Within the residence, a treasury of genuine jewels such as diamond-maṇi pearls was filled, and it was adorned with ten kinds of groves and gardens.

At that time, Sudhana saw that woman seated upon a precious lion throne; her countenance was upright and majestic, endowed with wondrous marks. Her body was like pure gold, and her eyes and hair were deep blue. She was neither tall nor short, neither too fair nor too dark; her physical form was perfectly complete, such that there was no one equal to her in all the desire realm, let alone anyone superior.
His speech and voice were elegant and exquisite, peerless in the world;
he was skilled in the wheels of syllables (*akṣaracakra*) and all treatises on the arts and crafts, having perfected the bodhisattva’s skillful means of illusory wisdom (*māyājñāna*);
his body was adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels, covered by a net of gems, and crowned with a celestial tiara.
Surrounded by a great assembly, all of whom cultivate goodness and share in his vows and conduct;
who have perfected roots of merit that cannot be thwarted or destroyed;

who possess a treasury of inexhaustible jewels of virtue; whose bodies emit radiance that universally illumines all things—those who touch this light experience joy and delight, their bodies and minds become supple, and the fever of afflictions is extinguished.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated with his head at [the Bodhisattva’s] feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying:
“O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should study the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
He replied, “Good son!
I have already accomplished the Dharma-gate of the purity of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) that is free from desire.”
If a deva sees me, I appear as a celestial maiden;
if a human sees me, I appear as a human maiden;
and even if a non-human sees me, I appear as a non-human maiden.
My physical form is exquisite and wondrous, and my radiant appearance is incomparably sublime.
If there are sentient beings who are bound by desire, they come to me, and for their sake I preach the Dharma; they all become free from desire and attain the samādhi of the state of non-attachment.
If there are those who see me, they attain the samādhi of joy.
If there are sentient beings who speak with me, they shall attain the Samādhi of Unobstructed Wondrous Sound;
if there are sentient beings who grasp my hand, they shall attain the Samādhi of Reaching All Buddha-fields;
if there are sentient beings who share a night’s lodging with me, they shall attain the Samādhi of the Radiance of Liberation.
If there are sentient beings who gaze upon me with their eyes, they shall attain the Samādhi of the Quiescence of All Conditioned Phenomena;
if there are sentient beings who see me stretching my limbs, they shall attain the Samādhi of the Dispelling and Destruction of Non-Buddhists;
if there are sentient beings who contemplate me, they shall attain the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Realm of All Buddhas.
If there are sentient beings who say "āliyi me," they shall attain the Samādhi of Gathering All Sentient Beings;
if there are sentient beings who say "a-jung-vi me," they shall attain the Samādhi of the Secret Treasury of All Merits;
and for all such classes of sentient beings who come before me, they shall all attain the Dharma-gate of the Reality-limit Free from Desire.
Sudhana said: "O Great Sage!
In what place did you plant these roots of goodness in the past, and what kind of practices did you cultivate to attain this Dharma-gate?"
He replied, "Good son!
In the past, there was a Buddha named Constant Abiding Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who appeared in the world."

Out of compassion and for the benefit of all living beings, that Buddha entered the City of Peace and Bliss; as his feet crossed the threshold of the gate, the great earth immediately shook in six ways. That city spontaneously became wondrous, vast, and expansive, adorned with various jewels and strewn with diverse flowers. It naturally produced sounds of entertainment and emitted great radiance, while all the devas filled the void of space, manifesting extraordinary wonders as extensively described in the *Buddha-praveśa-nagara-sūtra*.

"Good son! At that time, I was the wife of an elder, named Shan-nü (Good Woman). Witnessing such extraordinary and marvelous events, I went out from my husband the elder onto the road and alleyway to offer that Tathāgata the wondrous jewel celestial crown."
At that time, Mañjuśrī was the Buddha’s attendant; he expounded the Dharma for me, causing me to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
O son of good family!

I know only this Dharma-gate of the reality-limit that transcends desire; as for the great Bodhisattvas who have accomplished immeasurable skillful means and wisdom, who are vast treasuries of knowledge, and whose sphere of wisdom cannot be destroyed by any, how could I possibly know or speak of their meritorious conduct?

"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Śubhapāla. There dwells an elder named Anala who constantly makes offerings to a sandalwood stūpa of the Buddha. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of that woman and departed southward.
At that time, Sudhana gradually traveled until he reached that city and approached the householder’s dwelling, where he spoke thus: “O Noble One!”
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
He replied: "Good son!
I have already accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the limit of non-extinction."
Abiding in this Dharma-gate, one universally perceives that throughout all worlds in the ten directions, there are no Buddhas of the past, future, or present who enter nirvana;
they only manifest passing into extinction through skillful means in order to transform sentient beings.

"Good son! When I opened the door of the Candana Buddha-stūpa, in every thought-moment I entered the samādhi-gate of the inexhaustible Buddha-nature, and within each thought-moment I attained immeasurable and boundless, supreme, wondrous dharmas."
He addressed [the Buddha], saying: "Great Sage!
What is the sphere of this samādhi?"
He replied, “Good son!
When I entered this samādhi, I saw in this world-world the Buddhas Kāśyapa, Kanakamuni, Śikhin, Vipaśyin, Tiṣya, Puṣya, Anuttarajaya, and Anuttarapadma.”
He beheld such Buddhas as these—inexpressibly inexpressible numbers, as many as the atoms of Jambudvīpa, even unto as many as the atoms of inexpressibly inexpressible Buddha-fields.

He beholds all these Buddhas from their initial generation of the mind of enlightenment, through their sovereign spiritual powers, all their great vows, their pure and wondrous practices, and their various *pāramitās*; he sees them successively accomplish the bodhisattva stages, attain profound *dharmakṣānti*, subdue all Māras, nurture and perfect sovereign enlightenment, purify all Buddha-fields, assemble various congregations, teach and transform sentient beings, radiate great light, turn the pure wheel of Dharma, and manifest spiritual transformations—all of which he fully upholds and contemplates with right mindfulness.

With wisdom, he discerns the teachings of those Buddhas to manifest them for sentient beings; he perceives and knows all future Buddhas such as Maitreya, and likewise all present Buddhas such as Vairocana.

Just as it is with this world, so too is it with the seeing and knowing of all Buddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time. Good son!

I know only this Bodhisattva Dharma-gate of the Limit of Non-extinction. All great Bodhisattvas, in a single thought-moment, fully know all phenomena of the three periods of time; they perceive the limits of thought as equal and non-dual.
Abiding where the Buddhas abide, they have no perception of "kalpas" throughout all kalpas.
They accord with the equal and true Dharma of all Buddhas, such that the Tathāgatas, myself, and all sentient beings are equal and without distinction.
With pure and adorned wisdom, they illuminate the three worlds and accomplish the unshakeable majestic deportment of all Buddhas, discerning the spheres of all dharma-realms;
how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Noble son! To the south of here, there is a mountain named Prabhāsa. There dwells a bodhisattva named Avalokiteśvara. Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."

Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of that elder, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with longing admiration, and took his leave to travel south.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Fifty, and Volume Fifty-one,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
In the eighth part of the thirty-fourth chapter, "Entering the Dharma Realm," at that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness, contemplated the instructions of that elder;

he followed the treasury of the bodhisattva’s liberation, maintained right mindfulness of the various powers of recollection of the bodhisattvas, sequentially distinguished all Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas, and with a single mind maintained right mindfulness of the flow of the Buddha-dharmas. He recollected and upheld those Buddha-dharmas and the Buddha-adornments, nurtured enlightenment, and contemplated with right mindfulness the inconceivable activities of all Buddhas.

Gradually traveling on, he reached Mount Prabhāsa and ascended its peak, searching everywhere until he saw Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva dwelling on the western slope of the mountain. There were flowing springs and bathing pools everywhere, the forest trees were lush and dense, and the ground was covered with soft grass. The Bodhisattva sat cross-legged upon a diamond-jeweled throne, surrounded by immeasurable bodhisattvas who paid him respectful homage, as he expounded the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* to universally gather in all sentient beings.
Having seen this, he leaped for joy, unable to contain himself; joining his palms, he gazed intently at him without blinking for a moment, thinking:
"A virtuous friend is indeed a Tathāgata."
A spiritual friend is the cloud of all dharmas;
a spiritual friend is the treasury of all merits;
a spiritual friend is the wondrous jewel of the ten powers.
A spiritual friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter;
a spiritual friend is an inexhaustible treasury of wisdom;

a spiritual friend is a king of mountains of merit; a spiritual friend opens and guides one through the gates of all-knowledge, enabling all beings to enter the ocean of sarvajñā (omniscience) and ultimately attain the purity of unsurpassed bodhi.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara saw Sudhana from afar and addressed him, saying:
"Welcome, young man!
You who single-mindedly seek the Mahāyāna, who embrace all sentient beings, and who possess a straightforward mind, a profound mind, and a joyful longing for the Buddha-dharma."
They nurture great compassion to rescue and protect all beings; they turn toward the conduct of Samantabhadra and purify and fulfill all great vows.

They desire to hear and uphold the teachings of all Buddhas and all clouds of Dharma, increasing their roots of goodness without ever feeling weary or satisfied. They follow spiritual friends and do not contravene their instructions. Arising from the ocean of wisdom and merit of Mañjuśrī, they accomplish roots of goodness and attain the power of the Buddhas, the samādhi of radiance, and freedom from the mind of indolence. They single-mindedly seek the True Dharma, constantly behold all Buddhas, remain far removed from all evils, cultivate all virtuous practices, and bring wisdom to full completion, as pure as space.
At that time, Sudhana went to Avalokiteśvara, prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
He replied, "Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! You are indeed able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Noble son!"
I have already accomplished the practice of the light of the Dharma-gate of Great Compassion, teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity.
I constantly abide in the presence of all Buddhas, appearing universally before them according to those who are to be transformed.

They gather in sentient beings through the practice of giving, up to gathering them through the practice of cooperation; they gather in sentient beings by manifesting wondrous bodies of inconceivable form.

They radiate great nets of light to extinguish the heat of the afflictions of sentient beings, produce subtle and wondrous sounds to transform and deliver them, and employ majestic deportment, the preaching of the Dharma, sovereign spiritual powers, and skillful means to awaken them;
they manifest transformation bodies and appear in forms identical to those of their kind, even dwelling together with them to gather in and sustain sentient beings.

"Good son! When I was practicing the luminous conduct of the Dharma-gate of Great Compassion, I made a great vow called 'Gathering in All Sentient Beings,' desiring to cause all beings to be free from the terrors of perilous paths,

the terrors of feverish affliction, the terrors of ignorance, the terrors of bondage, the terrors of slaughter, the terrors of poverty, the terrors of being unable to survive, the terrors of litigation, the terrors of large assemblies, the terrors of death, the terrors of the evil realms, the terrors of the various destinies, the terrors of disagreeable things, the terrors of the liked and disliked, the terrors of all evils, the terrors of bodily oppression, the terrors of mental oppression, and the terrors of grief and anxiety."
Furthermore, good son!

Because I have brought forth the Dharma-gate of the Wheel of Names—the Dharma-gate of the present mindfulness—I manifest various skillful means in bodies equal to all sentient beings. According to what is appropriate for each, I eliminate their terrors and preach the Dharma, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and attain non-retrogression, never missing the proper time.
"Good son! I know only this bodhisattva practice of the light of the gate of great compassion.

As for the great bodhisattvas, they have fulfilled all the great vows of Samantabhadra and have ultimately accomplished the conduct of Samantabhadra; they do not sever the flow of any roots of goodness, nor do they sever the flow of any bodhisattva samādhis; throughout the flow of all eons, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices without ever ceasing."

Flowing in accordance with the three periods of time, they skillfully know all successions of rise and fall; they flow through all worlds, severing the flow of all unwholesome roots in sentient beings, giving birth to the flow of all wholesome roots in sentient beings, and extinguishing the flow of all birth and death. How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
At that time, there was a bodhisattva from the eastern direction named Samantagāmin who came to this land.
He stayed atop Mount Vajra, and when he arrived at this mountain, the Sahā world shook in six ways; it was adorned with various jewels that emitted a great radiance, eclipsing the sun and the moon.

The Śakras, Brahmās, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings all saw their radiance become like a mass of ink; it shone universally upon the hells, the hungry ghosts, the animals, and the realm of King Yama, extinguishing all sufferings and severing afflictions as well as all ailments.
They rained down a universal rain of jewels that filled the Buddha-fields, even raining down clouds of all manner of adornments as offerings to the Tathāgata.
Manifesting their bodies according to what was appropriate for each being, they then proceeded to the place where Avalokiteśvara was.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara said to Sudhana:
"Good man, do you see this Bodhisattva Samantagāmin in this assembly?"
He replied, “Indeed, I have seen it. “Good man!
“Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.

Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of Avalokiteśvara with his head, circumambulated him countless times, gazing upon him without weariness. Mindfully reflecting on the holy teaching and deeply entering the ocean of wisdom, he took his leave and went to Samantagupta. He prostrated with his head at Samantagupta’s feet, circumambulated him to the right, and standing to one side with palms joined in reverence, addressed him, saying:
“O Great Sage!”
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
“Good son! I have already accomplished the Bodhisattva Dharma-door of Universal Gate Swift Practice. He replied:
“Great Sage! Under which Buddha did you obtain this Dharma-gate?
From what realm did you come, and how far is it from here?”
"How long has it been since it was sent? He replied,
"O son of good family!"
This place is difficult to know;
it cannot be comprehended by any devas, humans, or non-humans.

Only those who are diligent and never retreat, who draw near to spiritual friends, who are protected by the Buddhas, who are fully endowed with roots of goodness, whose minds are pure and upright, who have attained the faculties of a bodhisattva, who have opened the eye of wisdom, and who have heard much and possess extensive knowledge of the bodhisattva realm, can understand it.
“I only pray that the Great Sage will explain this for me!
I shall, by relying on the Buddha’s spiritual power and the power of a virtuous friend, attain faith and understanding. He replied:
“Good son! The land from which I have come is named Wondrous Treasury (Guna-garbha), and the Buddha there is named Wondrous Virtue (Guṇakūṭa).
I obtained this Dharma-door from that Buddha; it has been an unspeakable number of kalpas, equal to the dust motes of Buddha-lands, since I departed from there.”
In a single thought-moment, they take steps equal in number to the atoms of unspeakably many Buddha-fields;
with each step, they pass through worlds as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
In all the lands they traverse, Buddhas are currently present, and they make offerings to them with every kind of offering requisite for Bodhisattvas.

They are able to fully comprehend the ocean-like multitudes of sentient beings within those worlds; they discern their various faculties and preach the Dharma to them according to what is appropriate for each. They emit great nets of light that universally illuminate the ten directions, and produce wondrous sounds to expound the True Dharma, thereby benefiting and liberating all those sentient beings; this extends even to the ten directions in the same manner.
"Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva Dharma-door of the Swift Practice of the Universal Gate.
As for the great Bodhisattvas, they go everywhere throughout the ten directions; their spheres of activity are immeasurable and none can destroy them."

The pure Dharma-body fills the Dharma-realm; it discerns and understands the paths of all sentient beings, pervades all lands, accords with all dharmas, contemplates the three periods of time equally, and proclaims the dharma of equality. It conforms to the world yet does not cling to the Buddha-way, reaching universally into all paths without attachment or obstruction. How could I possibly know or describe such meritorious conduct?
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Pāṭaliputra;
in it dwells a deity named Mahādeva."
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.

Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the Bodhisattva Samantagāmin with his head, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him in veneration, and taking his leave, traveled southward.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness, contemplated the unobstructed conduct of bodhisattvas; he pursued it single-mindedly, correctly directed toward the realm of bodhisattva wisdom, giving rise to all the merits of the realm of supernormal powers and clear insights. His diligence was firm and his joy immeasurable; he attained inconceivable playful mastery of spiritual powers and gained definitive knowledge of the stages of all merits, the stages of all samādhis, the stages of dhāraṇīs, the stages of all great vows, the stages of all eloquence, and the stages endowed with all powers.
Gradually traveling on, he arrived at that city and inquired,
"Where is Mahādeva now? At that time, someone said:
“Good son! Within this city, atop the Great Dharma Hall, he has manifested his body, surrounded by a great assembly, preaching the Dharma.

Thereupon, Sudhana went to that place, prostrated himself at the feet of Mahādevī with his head, circumambulated her countless times, and standing to one side with palms joined in reverence, addressed her, saying:
“O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.”

At that time, Mahādeva extended four long arms, took up the waters of the four oceans, and washed his face. Having finished washing, he took various golden flowers and scattered them over Sudhana, speaking these words:
"O son of good family!
The Bodhisattva is difficult to hear of and difficult to see; he is a most extraordinary phenomenon in the world.

Among all men, he is a *puṇḍarīka* flower, a refuge for sentient beings. He gathers and benefits them, nourishing and supporting them; he shines universally upon all, manifesting the true path and causing them to distance themselves from ignorance.
He is the teacher of sentient beings and the protector of the True Dharma.
Acting as leaders for sentient beings, they provide protection, rescue, and peace.
They cause all to reach the city of omniscience, fully accomplishing the purification of bodily and verbal karma, and forever remaining free from all evils;
toward the various classes of sentient beings, they always employ kind speech, appearing before each according to their needs, never missing the proper time.
"Good son! I have already accomplished the Bodhisattva Cloud-Net Dharma-gate. He replied:
“Great Sage! What is the scope of this Dharma-gate?
At that time, Mahādeva piled up a heap of celestial gold before Sudhana, like a king of mountains.

White silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, mother-of-pearl, agate, stainless night-luminous treasury jewels, luminously pure jewels, maṇi jewels of various skillful means, cūḍāmaṇi jewels, necklace jewels, keyūra armlet jewels, hair-adornment jewels, youth-adornment jewels, mīḍhara-adornment jewels, mukuṭa crown jewels, red pearl jewels, and jewels that adorn all the limbs and joints, as well as wish-fulfilling jewels—all these were gathered together in heaps like the king of mountains.

All kinds of flowers, all kinds of incense, all kinds of unguents, all kinds of powdered incense, all kinds of garlands, all kinds of robes, all kinds of parasols, all kinds of banners, all kinds of pennants, and all kinds of entertainments—possessing the objects of the five desires—such as these were accumulated in heaps as vast as the King of Mountains.
Furthermore, there appeared an incalculable multitude of young maidens who said to Sudhana:
"Son of good family!

Take these various objects to make offerings to the Tathāgata, bestow them as gifts upon all, and gather in sentient beings, causing all beings to practice the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), to study the perfection of giving, and to relinquish everything."

"Good son! I teach you this act of giving; I teach all sentient beings in the same way, so that all may universally permeate their bodies and minds with the wholesome root of non-attachment, draw near to spiritual friends, reverently make offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, give birth to and nurture all wholesome roots, and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi."
Furthermore, good son!
If there are sentient beings who crave the five desires, I manifest impure realms for them.

If they are prone to anger, negligence, arrogance, or contention—like rākṣasa demons who drink blood and eat flesh—I instruct them all to cultivate great compassion, causing them all to forever leave behind anger, negligence, and the like.
If there are those who are indolent, [the Buddha] manifests for them the perils of water and fire, thieves, wicked kings, enemies, and so forth. Good son!

For such evil beings as these, through various skillful means, he causes them to extinguish their unwholesome roots and nurture their wholesome roots; he eliminates all obstacles and adversaries to the *pāramitās*, brings the *pāramitās* to full completion, enables them to transcend all hindrances, and causes them to attain the unimpeded Dharma.
"Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva Cloud-Net Dharma Door, which causes all great Bodhisattvas, Śakras, and celestial kings to extinguish all afflictions and the calamities of the asuras."
The water of all bodhisattvas extinguishes the fire of afflictions;
the fire of all bodhisattvas can burn away the craving of all sentient beings;
the wind of all bodhisattvas can disperse all minds of defiled attachment.
The Bodhisattva Vajra has utterly destroyed all notions of self.
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
O son of good family!
Within this Jambudvīpa, there is a land named Magadha;
there is a site-of-enlightenment ground deity named Anvaya.
Go to her and ask: how does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in reverence at the feet of that Great Goddess, and after taking his leave, he proceeded toward the kingdom of Magadha to visit the earth goddess Ananyagāminī at her place of practice.
At that time, ten thousand earth-dwelling devas each spoke these words:
"This youth who has come here is able to gather in sentient beings; he is the very treasury of the Buddhas.

He can shatter the shell of ignorance of all sentient beings, be born into the family of the Dharma King, remain free from defilement and unimpeded, wear a precious silken turban upon his crown, and with the treasure-trove of wisdom, crush the wheels of the heterodox."

At that time, ten thousand earth-dwelling devas, including those of the Abhirati-bhūmi, rained down various fragrant waters to sprinkle the ground, adorned it by sweeping with fragrant winds, and emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated the trichiliocosm.

Adorned with various jewels, all the flowering trees bloomed in lush profusion, and all the fruit trees bore their fruit. All springs, rivers, and ponds flowed into one another in a continuous cascade, producing the sounds of manifold music for entertainment. The celestial mansions were adorned with myriad precious gems, and birds of diverse species were filled with joy, uttering harmonious and plaintive songs. Immeasurable treasuries of jewels spontaneously welled forth.
At that time, the earth goddess Anuvartinī addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Welcome, young man!
Do you wish to see for yourself the fruits and rewards of the roots of goodness you have previously planted in this very place?"
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that earth goddess, joined his palms in reverence, stood to one side, and said: "O Noble One!
"Indeed, I wish to see them.
At that time, the earth deity pressed the ground with her toe, and immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) nayutas of treasure troves opened up and became manifest.
“Good son! This treasure store has come to you through the roots of goodness and their karmic fruits that you planted in the past; it is at your disposal according to your will. Good son!”

I have already accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the indestructible treasury. Since the time of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I have constantly protected bodhisattvas as they cultivate the bodhisattva practices, entering deeply into the realm of wisdom to exhaust its very source and bottom. My great vows have been fulfilled, my bodhisattva conduct purified, and all the supernormal powers and clarities of a bodhisattva have been brought forth. I am fully endowed with the merits of a bodhisattva’s various powers and have accomplished the indestructible dharmas of a bodhisattva.

They travel through all Buddha-fields, hear the teachings of the predictions bestowed by all Buddhas, and turn all wheels of Dharma; with the clouds of Dharma from all sūtras and the great light of the Dharma, they teach and transform sentient beings, and receive and uphold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
"Good son! In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was an eon named Adornment and a world named Moon Banner, where the Buddha was named Good Eye."

Having attained this Dharma-gate from that Buddha, I cultivated, nurtured, and purified it; during that interval, I constantly encountered Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. I went before all those Tathāgatas at their sites of enlightenment and beheld them with my own eyes through their sovereign spiritual powers, cultivating and accumulating roots of goodness in the presence of these Buddhas.
"Good son! I know only this Dharma-door.

The great Bodhisattvas are always able to attend upon all Buddhas, hearing and receiving all those Buddhas' teachings, and entering deeply into the secret instructions of the Buddhas. In every thought-moment, they manifest pure Dharma-bodies equal to all Buddhas and the hidden treasury of all Buddha-reflections; they manifest the unimpeded practice of all Buddha-dharmas. How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?"
"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa there is a city named Kapilavastu;
therein dwells a night goddess named Vāsavadattā."
"Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the earth goddess Sthāvarā with his head, circumambulated her countless times, took his leave, and departed for that city.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness and reflection, dwelt in the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the indestructible treasury taught by the goddess; he cultivated various samādhis, clarified various samādhis, and observed the rules and rituals of the bodhisattvas. He observed the sovereign play of the bodhisattvas' supernatural powers, observed all the pure dharmas of the bodhisattvas, and deeply entered the profound wisdom of the bodhisattvas. He reached the ultimate limit of the indestructible dharma-gates of the bodhisattvas, followed in accordance with the indestructible dharma-gates of the bodhisattvas, and deeply entered the ocean of all the bodhisattvas' dharma-gates.
Gradually traveling on, he arrived at that city and entered through the eastern gate, staying in the center of the city.

At that time, not long after the sun had set, Sudhana, in accordance with the instructions of all the bodhisattvas, single-mindedly desired to see the night goddess Vāsantī. Regarding the spiritual friend as a Tathāgata, the realm of the Universal Eye appeared before him; the wisdom of all directions reached him, all realms became pure, and his Dharma-eye universally beheld the ocean of all dharma-realms.
With the eye of great wisdom, he surveyed the ten directions and saw that Night Goddess dwelling in the void above that city;

seated upon a fragrant lotus throne within a jeweled pavilion, her body was like pure gold and her eyes and hair were deep blue; she was so upright, dignified, and exquisite that those who beheld her never grew weary of the sight.
He was dressed in crimson robes and adorned with various jewels; his hair was tied in a topknot like that of Brahmā.
Upon his body appeared all the constellations, and through their radiance, he transformed and delivered sentient beings across immeasurable worlds, causing them to leave the evil realms far behind.

Within a single pore, they behold all the sentient beings being transformed: some are born in the heavens, some attain the stages of Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha, and others cultivate the bodhisattva path; through various skillful means, physical forms, voices, and the methods of speech, they preach the Dharma to correctly teach and deliver sentient beings.

Throughout all successive eons, these bodhisattvas teach and transform sentient beings, causing them all to practice the various conducts of a bodhisattva; they cultivate various samādhis and gateways of spiritual power with courage and diligence, utilizing the realm of a bodhisattva’s sovereign spiritual powers, the dwelling place of a bodhisattva, the radiance of a bodhisattva, the prowess of a bodhisattva, and the Dharma-gates of a bodhisattva to transform sentient beings.
Within a single pore, he saw and heard everything.

At that time, having seen and heard this, Sudhana was filled with great joy; he prostrated his head at the feet of that Night Goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and standing to one side with palms joined in reverence, addressed her, saying:
"O Celestial Deity!"

I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and I believe and understand that one attains all Buddha-dharmas through spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). I only pray that the celestial deity will reveal and manifest the path to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); if any bodhisattva proceeds toward this path, they shall attain the stage of the ten powers (*daśabala-bhūmi*).
At that time, the Night Goddess said to Sudhana:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son! Revere spiritual friends and follow their instructions.
If there are bodhisattvas who follow their instructions, they will swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Good son! I have already accomplished the Bodhisattva’s Radiance that Universally Illuminates All Dharmas and Dispels the Ignorance of Sentient Beings. Good son!"

I give rise to a mind of great loving-kindness toward evil sentient beings; I give rise to a mind of great compassion toward sentient beings who engage in unwholesome karma; I give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward sentient beings who cultivate goodness; I give rise to a mind of non-duality toward sentient beings who are both good and evil; I give rise to a mind of purity toward defiled sentient beings; I give rise to a mind of the right path toward sentient beings on deviant paths; I give rise to a mind that delights in purity toward sentient beings who delight in impurity; I give rise to a mind that accords with the Wheel of Dharma toward sentient beings who delight in birth and death; and I give rise to a mind that establishes all in the path of omniscience toward sentient beings who delight in the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
"Good son! I constantly contemplate and teach sentient beings in this way:

during the darkness of night when people are quiet and ghosts, spirits, thieves, and bandits roam; when bhikṣus have departed from their proper deportment; when heavy clouds, smoke, and dust obscure the sky so that the sun and moon cannot be seen; and for any sentient beings in cities, towns, mountain crags, wildernesses, the eight directions, or the great ocean—even including all beings of water and land—I employ various skillful means to extinguish their fear."

If there are sentient beings who encounter perils at sea—such as clouds, mountains, great winds, and turbulent eddies—or who are confused by waves and lose their way, unable to see the shore, and meet with various such maritime calamities, I at that time may manifest in the form of a ship, or in the forms of a horse king, an elephant king, a dog king, an asura king, or a sea god king; manifesting in such forms, I employ skillful means to deliver these sentient beings from their maritime perils.

For the sake of sentient beings on land, he may manifest as the pure moon, various constellations, torches, lightning, the radiance of various jewels, the light from celestial bodies, or the light of Bodhisattvas; through such immeasurable skillful means, he protects and delivers sentient beings.
They give rise to this thought:
"I shall always act as a refuge for all sentient beings, eliminating their afflictions;
I shall enable those who fear death to attain the Dharma of fearlessness."
"May those who are impoverished all attain wealth and happiness.
For the sake of sentient beings dwelling in the mountains, he may become fruit trees, flowing springs, or kalaviṅka birds that emit wondrous sounds;
or he may become mountain deities or level plains. Through such immeasurable skillful means as these, he delivers and liberates sentient beings.
He gives rise to this thought:
"May all sentient beings be freed from these mountain perils, and may they all transcend the mountain of birth and death.

For the sake of sentient beings in the wilderness, he employs various skillful means to bring them joy and cause them to enter the path of right view, eliminating their hunger and thirst. Having thus rescued sentient beings from such immeasurable hardships, he further reflects:
"May all sentient beings swiftly extinguish their manifold sufferings and ultimately attain the path of all-pervading peace and wisdom.

Seeing sentient beings who delight in and are attached to lands undergoing various forms of suffering and affliction, he employs diverse skillful means to eliminate their attachment, forming this thought:
"May all sentient beings remove their attachment to the five aggregates and abide in the realm of the *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge) of all Buddhas."

Seeing sentient beings attached to villages and towns suffering various afflictions, he employs diverse skillful means to preach the Dharma for them, causing them to feel weary of and detach from such attachments, and gathering them in through the Dharma. He further reflects:
"May all sentient beings leave behind the empty village of the six sense bases, transcend birth and death, and ultimately enter the city of omniscience."
"Furthermore, good son!

If there are sentient beings who are confused regarding the ten directions—taking east for west and west for east, even taking above for below and below for above—for the sake of these sentient beings, one employs immeasurable skillful means to sever their delusions."
If they wish to go forth, he opens and shows them the gateway;
if they have lost their way, he points out and guides them along the correct path;
if they wish to cross over, he shows them the ferry and the crossing.
To those who lack boats or oars, he provides them;
to those who do not know the regions, he shows them the blissful land.
Through such immeasurable skillful means as these, he manifests and opens the path to deliver them.
They give rise to this thought:
"I have already illuminated and dispelled the darkness of the long night; there is no matter in the world that I do not proclaim and explain.

Furthermore, I cause sentient beings to forever extinguish the gloom of ignorance and attain the pure eye, becoming free from the perception of a self among sentient beings and all false views, and realizing permanence, bliss, self, and purity."
"Fixated upon sentient beings, persons (*pudgala*), the aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), and sense bases (*āyatana*), they fail to understand cause and effect.
They practice unwholesome paths, killing living beings, and even holding wrong views;
they are unfilial toward their parents, do not make offerings to śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas, stray from the right path, perform unwholesome deeds, and slander..."
Those who slander the true path, seek to destroy the Wheel of Dharma, disparage the assembly of Bodhisattvas, harbor hatred for the Mahāyāna, do not praise bodhi,
revile the worthy and holy ones, practice the ways of evil persons, and commit the five heinous crimes— such wicked beings as these,
I shall dispel their ignorant darkness with the light of my clear and pure wisdom, and cause them to...
Having resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they bring to ultimate fulfillment the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
they open the way of the ten powers, remain far removed from birth and death, and manifest the city of all-knowledge.

They dwell within the realm of all Buddhas and the spiritual powers of all Buddhas, fully endowed with all the powers, manifesting the power of maintaining the Dharma, and abiding securely in all [virtues].
The Buddha’s impartial True Dharma manifests all Buddhas as being entirely one and the same body.
Furthermore, good son,
when I see sentient beings who are poor, suffering, old, or sick, I rescue and relieve them through various skillful means.
Again, he forms this thought:

"I shall gather those sentient beings with the unsurpassed Dharma, extinguish their afflictions, and cause them to attain liberation, freeing them from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, distress, and the various hardships of the evil realms."

By associating with virtuous friends, they enter deeply into the Dharma-realm, leave behind all evil karma, purify the Buddha-Dharmakāya, and establish themselves in the eternal Dharma-realm, free from old age, sickness, and death.
"Furthermore, son of good family!

I see various evil sentient beings who have abandoned the right path and entered upon deviant tracks; they are attached to inverted views, deluded by falsehoods, and fully engage in unwholesome conduct. Their actions of body, speech, and mind are variously dissolute; they rely upon evil dharmas, perceiving what is not true awakening as true awakening, and perceiving what is true awakening as not true awakening."

Having associated with evil associates, they undergo various sufferings and afflictions; having witnessed this, I employ immeasurable skillful means to eliminate their false delusions, establish them in right view, and cause them to become most preeminent among devas and humans.
Furthermore, they form this thought:

"May all sentient beings attain the supramundane, unsurpassed right path and never again regress; may they fulfill the great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva regarding omniscience, attain omniscience itself, yet never depart from the various bodhisattva stages, and never destroy the nature of sentient beings."

At that time, the Night Goddess, wishing to further proclaim and clarify the meaning of this Dharma-door, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and spoke these verses for Sudhana:
“The wondrous Dharma I have accomplished Is the ground of the various gates of knowing the proper time;
It illuminates and dispels the darkness of ignorance, Universally observing all phenomena.”
Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, I have constantly cultivated great loving-kindness,
universally covering all living beings; Sudhana should quickly fulfill this and achieve the ocean of great compassion,
giving birth to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Having extinguished all suffering, Sudhana swiftly reaches the ultimate goal.
The Son of the Buddha rejoices in his heart; far removed from worldly evils, he transcends the sufferings of the three realms and experiences the bliss of the worthy and the sages.
Far removed from conditioned evils, With the wisdom and liberation of the śrāvakas,
And the fulfillment of the Tathāgata’s powers— The Son of the Buddha should bring these to ultimate completion.
With my pure divine eye, I universally observe the lands of the ten directions.
In those worlds, one beholds the Buddhas dwelling at their sites of enlightenment;
their bodies adorned with the marks and signs, surrounded by immeasurable multitudes,
they radiate oceans of great light, universally illuminating and transforming sentient beings.
Beholding all classes of sentient beings, dying here and being born there,
circulating through the five realms of existence and constantly undergoing immeasurable suffering;
with the pure celestial ear of the ocean, he universally hears the sounds throughout the ten directions.
The entire ocean of all languages, they are able to receive and uphold it all.
The immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous voices of all Tathāgatas,
and the pure wheels of Dharma they turn, they hear them all and are able to receive and uphold them.
By means of my purified nose faculty, I am unimpeded within the ocean of Dharma;
able to enter all dharma-gates, Sudhana should reach the ultimate.
I have attained the marks of a great man, with a pure and broad tongue.
One should expound the sublime Dharma as appropriate; the sons of the Buddha should bring this to ultimate completion.
The pure and sublime Dharma-body is equal to suchness throughout the three periods of time;
according to those who are to be transformed, there is nothing that does not manifest.
My mind is unstained, pure as space; it universally encompasses all Buddhas, yet remains without attachment.
I thoroughly understand the infinite lands and the ocean of minds of all living beings.
Discerning all faculties and remaining far removed from all delusions,
I travel throughout immeasurable lands by the power of my spiritual penetrations,
universally sheltering all beings and taming every sentient being.
Wisdom is like space, an incomparable and inexhaustible treasury;
It makes offerings to all Tathāgatas and benefits all sentient beings.
With pure and vast wisdom, it discerns the ocean of all dharmas.
To eliminate the delusions of sentient beings, the sons of the Buddha should reach ultimate perfection.
Mastering the dharmas of the three periods of time and entering deeply into the ocean of all Buddhas, they clearly comprehend all phenomena; none are able to fathom them.
Within each and every atom, one sees entirely oceans of Buddha-fields, and beholds all Tathāgatas; this is the stage of Universal Power.
One sees Vairocana Buddha attaining perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening.
"In the lands of the ten directions, as numerous as motes of dust, you have everywhere turned the wheel of the True Dharma.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said, "O Deva!"
"How long has it been since you first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
How long has it been since you obtained this Dharma-door,
that you are now able to benefit sentient beings in such a way?"
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!
In the distant past, more than as many eons ago as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was a world named Ratnaguṇa and an eon named Śānta."
Five hundred billion buddhas appeared in the world; at that time, there was a great city named Padmaprabhā.
There was a wheel-turning sage king named Sudharmatīrtha, who, according to the dharma of a sage king, possessed the seven treasures.
To the east of the city there is a forest named Wondrous Virtue;
within this forest is a bodhi tree called All-Buddha-Sovereign-Light.
At that time, the Buddha Thunder-King of All Dharmas sat beneath this tree and attained equal and perfect enlightenment, emitting a great radiance that universally illuminated the world.
The noble lady’s precious name was Dharmamati-candra-padmaprabhā.
Within that city there was a night goddess named Viśuddhacandrā, who at the hour of midnight produced a subtle and wondrous sound and addressed this noble lady:

"You should know that the Buddha Sarvadharma-nirghoṣa-rāja has appeared in the world. You should extol and praise the virtues of that Buddha, manifest the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual powers, resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and praise all the vows and practices of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra."
At that time, the King’s jade maiden made offerings to that Buddha, as well as to the various bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas.
Good son! At that time, was this jade maiden named Dharmamati-candrapadmaprabhā anyone other than [yourself]?
"I am that very person. Good son!

By the power of the roots of goodness I planted under that Buddha, for as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, I did not fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, or the domain of King Yama; nor was I born into a lowly family. My faculties were complete, and all sufferings were extinguished."

They shall always be preeminent among gods and humans, never parting from spiritual friends, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas; they shall not be born during the kalpas of the five turbidities, but rather, in the presence of those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they shall increase their roots of goodness. For as many eons as there are atoms in eighty Mount Sumerus, they shall abide in peace and happiness, yet they will not have fully perfected the faculties of a Bodhisattva.
"Furthermore, son of good family!

After the passing of kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, and after further passing ten thousand kalpas, there will be a kalpa named Free from Sorrow (*vītaśoka*) and a world named Stainless Excellence (*vimalavijaya*).
Therein, five hundred Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, beginning with the Tathāgata Sumeru-Śāntanetra, will appear in the world."
That buddha-field may be either pure or defiled; within that world-system there is a four-continent world called Vimala, and its city is named Vyūha.
At that time, I was the daughter of the elder Vimalajaya, named Jñānaprabhā; I was upright and exceptionally beautiful.
That deity Candraprabha, through the power of his original vows, was born in this city and further became a night goddess named Viśuddhanetra.

At that time, that night goddess again came to my house during the middle watch of the night, manifesting a wondrous form and praising the Tathāgata; she further exhorted me to go to that Tathāgata, emitting a great radiance as she led the way before me.

At that time, together with my parents and their retinue, I went to the presence of the Tathāgata Sumeru-śāntanetra, where I made offerings and paid him respect. Listening to the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma, I attained a bodhisattva samādhi called "Beholding the Buddha."

He transforms and teaches sentient beings with the light of pure, clear wisdom that universally illumines the three periods of time. Having attained this samādhi, he recollects all the Buddhas he beheld throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, and he hears the sūtras and teachings spoken by those Buddhas.
