He attains the illumination that shines upon all dharmas and the dharma-gate that shatters the ignorance of sentient beings; emitting a great radiance, it illuminates worlds as numerous as the atoms of ten buddha-fields.

He saw that within those lands, all Tathāgatas went to their respective places; knowing the various languages, dharmas, mental faculties, inclinations, and natures of those sentient beings, they acted as spiritual friends for them, manifesting their bodies according to what was appropriate for each.

In every moment of thought, one nurtures this dharma-gate, filling worlds as numerous as the atoms within a single body, and even filling oceans of worlds as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds.

I saw within all those oceans of worlds, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, all the Tathāgatas proceeding to their respective abodes; I heard and retained all the teachings those Buddhas proclaimed, and I discerned and understood the oceans of past deeds and vows of those Tathāgatas. Furthermore, I purified the Buddha-fields that those Tathāgatas had adorned and purified, and I likewise adorned and purified them myself.

In those worlds, he manifests his body according to what is appropriate for each, transforming and delivering sentient beings; in every thought-moment, he nurtures this Dharma-gate, making it equal to the Dharma-realm.
"Good son! I know only this dharma-door of the Universal Radiance that Illumines All Dharmas and Dispels the Ignorance of Sentient Beings.

As for the great Bodhisattvas who have reached the ultimate in the immeasurable and boundless practices of Samantabhadra, who enter deeply into the ocean of the Dharma-realm, who erect the banner of wisdom, who attain all samādhis, who sport with supernatural powers, whose great vows are fulfilled, and who protect and uphold all the Buddha-dharmas of the worlds in the ten directions—I do not know their ways."
In every thought-moment, they are able to adorn and purify all Buddha-fields, fulfilling the ocean of merit;

in every thought-moment, they teach and transform the ocean of all sentient beings. As the pure sun of wisdom, they universally illumine all worlds throughout the three periods of time; as the stainless, pure moon, they teach and transform all sentient beings, extinguishing the feverish afflictions, doubts, and the darkness of ignorance of all beings.
With minds free from attachment amidst the ocean of all existence, they produce pure and perfect sublime sounds that fill all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.

Within each and every atom, all sovereign spiritual powers are manifested, and the luminous rays of pure wisdom universally illuminate the three periods of time; how could I possibly know or describe such meritorious conduct?

"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, in the kingdom of Magadha, there is a night goddess named Gambhīra-guṇa-vimala-prabhā. Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path."
At that time, Sudhana praised that night goddess with these verses:
"I behold your pure body, Adorned naturally with the marks and signs of excellence;
Like Mañjuśrī, And like the king of jewel mountains."
Fully endowed with the pure Dharma-body, equal throughout the three periods of time,
universally gathering all living beings, their minds are free from attachment.
They radiate pure light, illuminating all realms of existence.
Within a single pore, one sees all the constellations;
with a stainless and pure mind, like space filling the ten directions,
they embrace the Kings of Dharma, possessing bright, pure, and profound wisdom.
From each and every pore, He emits immeasurable light,
Reaching the abodes of all Buddhas in the ten directions, Universally raining down clouds of merit.
From each and every pore, He manifests various transformation bodies.
Pervading the realms of the ten directions, he delivers sentient beings through skillful means.
When he was originally a bodhisattva, he purified inconceivable lands;
within every single pore, all these manifestations are clearly revealed.
Should there be any who see or hear [this], they shall all obtain the benefits of merit;
Dedicating themselves solely to the Bodhisattva path, they shall achieve the Buddha’s Bodhi.
Should there be any who see or hear [this], they shall give rise to a heart of great joy.
Far removed from the perils of the evil realms, All afflictions are eradicated.
Even if one were to praise their virtues For as many eons as there are atoms in a thousand lands,
Those eons might come to an end, But the virtues would never be exhausted.

Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazing up at her with longing and contemplation, his heart never wearying of the sight; he then took his leave and traveled toward the kingdom of Magadha.
At that time, the youth Sudhana single-mindedly contemplated how that night goddess had first resolved her mind upon the Way, bringing it to full and pure completion.

Having reflected thus, he immediately attained deep entry into the treasuries of all bodhisattvas, gave birth to the ocean of all great bodhisattva vows, purified the path of the bodhisattva perfections (*pāramitā*), reached the perfect stages of the bodhisattvas, dwelt in the perfect practices and deeds of the bodhisattvas, exhausted the ocean of the bodhisattva’s path of advancement, and became skillfully able to enter deeply into the ocean of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
He brought protection and salvation to all sentient beings, nurtured and increased the vast clouds of great compassion, and brought forth the great vows and practices of Samantabhadra in all lands.
Gradually traveling on, he arrived at the place of the night goddess Gambhīraśrīvirajaprabhā;
he prostrated with his head at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying: "O Devī!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva practices the bodhisattva conduct and fulfills the various stages (*bhūmi*).
He replied: "Excellent! Excellent!"
That you, young man, are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, inquire about the bodhisattva practices, and fulfill all the stages (*bhūmi*)!
Well done, son of good family!
If a bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas, they will be able to fulfill the practices of a bodhisattva. What are these ten?
First, attaining the samādhi of presence before one's eyes and seeing all buddhas.
Second, they attain the pure eye, seeing all Buddhas with their bodies adorned by the primary and secondary marks.
Third, they analytically understand the boundless and infinite great ocean of merit of all Buddhas.
Fourth, there is an immeasurable and boundless ocean of Buddha-light that is able to universally illumine the entire Dharma-realm.
Fifth, from a single pore, he emits an ocean of great light rays equal in number to all sentient beings, delivering and liberating them according to their respective needs.
Sixth, within each and every pore, they see an ocean of the blazing flames of all jewels.

Seventh, in every thought-moment, they manifest oceans of the transformations of all Buddhas, filling the Dharma-realm and reaching the ultimate bounds of the spheres of all Buddhas, teaching and transforming sentient beings without obstruction.
Eighth, they produce the ocean of the wondrous sounds of all Buddhas and turn the pure wheel of Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Ninth, they expound the clouds of all sūtras, reaching the ultimate Buddha-voice, and deeply entering the ocean of all Tathāgatas.
Tenth, he manifests the inconceivable sovereign spiritual powers of a Buddha to transform and deliver sentient beings.
Son of good family!
If a bodhisattva is endowed with these ten dharmas, they will fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva.

Good son! I have already accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of quiescence, meditative bliss, and diligence, whereby I see all Buddhas and their oceans of retinues, as well as the infinite and boundless oceans of the spiritual powers of the Buddhas, within all the adorned and pure Buddha-lands of the three periods of time.

They discern and know the ocean of the Buddhas' names and the ocean of their turning of the wheel of Dharma; they know that the lifespans of those Buddhas are immeasurable, their voices are subtle and wondrous, and their Dharma-bodies are pure and pervade the entire Dharma-realm, yet they do not cling to any of the marks of a Tathāgata.
Why is this? The Tathāgata is not of the past, for he has eliminated all worldly grasping;
the Tathāgata is not of the future, for there is nothing that arises from him.
The Tathāgata is not present, because he has no body of birth;
the Tathāgata is not extinguished, because he is beyond the path of language;
the Tathāgata is not real, because he manifests illusory dharmas.
The Tathāgata is not false, for he appears in the world to benefit all sentient beings;
the Tathāgata goes nowhere, for he extinguishes death here and birth there;
the Tathāgata is indestructible, for the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is indestructible.
The Tathāgata has a single nature, because he is beyond the path of language;
the Tathāgata has no nature, because he is the ultimate dharma-nature. Good son!

Thus I have thoroughly understood all Tathāgatas, who have opened up, expanded, and illuminated the bodhisattva gateways of quiescence, meditative bliss, and diligence; who have entered deeply into the realms of conformity, equality, and steadfastness;

who have discerned and understood the transcendence of falsehood; who have given rise to great compassion to gather in sentient beings, never abandoning them; and who, with a single mind in tranquil concentration, have correctly attained the first dhyāna.
Eliminating mental karma and attaining the power of tranquil wisdom, they gather in sentient beings with joy and delight, entering the second dhyāna.
Abandoning birth and death for the sake of the tranquility of nirvana, they contemplate the nature of sentient beings and cultivate the third dhyāna.
They extinguish all the afflictions and sufferings of all sentient beings and cultivate the fourth dhyāna.

They increase the vows of the bodhicitta of omniscience, give birth to the ocean of all bodhisattva samādhis, and through skillful means, they reach the ultimate limit of the ocean of all bodhisattva dharma-gates. They accomplish the playful supernormal powers of bodhisattvas, give rise to the sovereign conduct of bodhisattvas, and with clear and pure wisdom, they penetrate deeply into the universal gate of the dharma-realm.
"Good son! In this way, I cultivate the bodhisattva’s dharma-gate of quiescence, meditative bliss, and diligence, employing various skillful means to deliver and liberate sentient beings."

For those householders who are heedless and possessed by craving, may they cultivate the perception of impurity, the perception of lack of delight, the perception of distress, the perception of oppression, the perception of bondage, the perception of rākṣasas, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, the perception of emptiness, the perception of non-mastery, and the perception of old age and death; may they cause those beings to distance themselves from the five desires, always delight in the True Dharma, have faith in leaving the household life for the homeless state, renounce home to study the Path, practice seated meditation through contemplation, eliminate obstructing and distracting sounds, and remove the fear of malevolent spirits.
If, during the middle watch of the night, one wishes to go forth, [the light] shall open the gates and doors, illuminate the path, and dispel all darkness.
One shall praise the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṃgha, and spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), and further extol the practice of associating with spiritual friends.

To cause all sentient beings to employ skillful means so that unarisen unwholesome states do not arise, to employ skillful means so that arisen unwholesome states are extinguished, to employ skillful means so that unarisen wholesome states arise, and to employ skillful means so that arisen wholesome states are increased and expanded.
Practicing the bodhisattva path, cultivating the pāramitās, fulfilling great vows, and giving birth to all-knowledge;
practicing great compassion with the desire to cause sentient beings to attain the bliss of humans and devas, eliminating deluded thoughts, increasing wholesome dharmas, and conforming to sarvajñatā.
"Good son! I only know this bodhisattva dharma-gate of quiescence, meditative bliss, and diligence.

As for the great bodhisattvas who fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra, who are fully endowed with the practices of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who have ultimately attained liberation from the darkness of delusion within the dharma-realm, who possess all roots of goodness, who have accomplished the light of the Tathāgata’s power of wisdom, who are unimpeded within the realm of the Buddhas, who dwell amidst birth and death with minds unstained, who are fully perfected in the vow for *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), who enter deeply into the ocean of all Buddha-lands, who encompass the great oceans of all Buddhas, who receive the ocean of the subtle Dharma-clouds of all Buddhas, who extinguish the dark ocean of birth and death for all sentient beings, and whose light of *sarvajñā* illuminates the night of birth and death; [I do not know their ways]."
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Good son! Not far from here, on the right side of the Tathāgata, there is a night goddess named Joyful Eyes Who Observes Sentient Beings.
“Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva trains in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the Night Goddess Profound and Sublime Virtue Free from Defilement Radiance, wishing to further clarify the meaning of this Dharma gate, spoke in verse:
“Entering into the samādhi of presence, Universally beholding the Buddhas of the three periods of time,”
With stainless, pure eyes, they discern the oceans of all Buddhas.
Observing the bodies of the Buddhas, adorned with the primary and secondary marks,
they see their infinite power in a single thought-moment, sovereignly filling the entire Dharma-realm.
Vairocana Tathāgata, having attained perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening,
turns the pure wheel of Dharma throughout the entire realm of phenomena.
With supreme knowledge of the characteristics of dharmas, he abides in quiescence where duality does not exist.
Adorned with wondrous marks and signs, appearing before all multitudes;
the Buddha’s body is inconceivable, filling all dharma realms,
manifesting everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions according to the needs of beings.
In a single thought, they emit radiance, Equal in number to the atoms of all lands,
With infinite and subtle colors, Universally illuminating all dharma realms.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, They emit inconceivable light.
Universally illuminating all living beings, He extinguishes their manifold afflictions.
From a single pore of the Tathāgata, An inexhaustible ocean of emanations issues forth,
Filling the entirety of the Dharma-realm, And manifesting before all classes of sentient beings.
The Tathāgata’s single wondrous voice fills all dharma-realms,
universally raining down the nectar of the Dharma to cause the arousal of the bodhicitta.
Having practiced for immeasurable eons, he gathers in and protects all living beings.
Universally beholding all Buddha-fields, All of which are like flashes of lightning;
The Tathāgata appears in the world, Manifesting universally among the various classes of beings;
The natures and realms of sentient beings— He is able to discern and know them all.
All the dharma-gates in which all bodhisattvas abide,
they are able to discern and know them all within a single pore of the Buddha.
Not far away is a night goddess named Joyful Eye Contemplation.
"Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva practice?

Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and with deep reverence and longing, took his leave and proceeded toward the night goddess Rativīkṣaṇasarvasattva.
The Flower Adornment Sutra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifty-one and Scroll Fifty-two,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
The Ninth Part of the Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm, Thirty-Fourth, Part Nine.
At that time, the youth Sudhana sought exclusively for spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), reflecting that all wholesome dharmas arise from spiritual friends;
for spiritual friends are difficult to see and difficult to encounter.
By seeing a spiritual friend, all distracted thoughts are extinguished;
by seeing a spiritual friend, all entanglements and obstacles are eliminated;
by seeing a spiritual friend, one attains the radiant wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñā*).
By seeing spiritual friends, one enters deeply into the ocean of the Buddhas;
by seeing spiritual friends, one attains the dharani of the Dharma-cloud of right mindfulness and receives and upholds the clouds of the pure Dharma-wheels of all Buddhas;
by seeing spiritual friends, one becomes endowed with the ocean of great compassion to rescue and protect all sentient beings.
Upon seeing the spiritual benefactor (kalyāṇamitra), whose wisdom was bright and pure, capable of universally illuminating the entire ocean of all dharma realms,

the night goddess Joyful Eye Observing Sentient Beings then used her majestic spiritual power to empower the youth Sudhana, praising the spiritual benefactor, instructing him to approach the spiritual benefactor, and to pay respectful homage and offerings;
for the spiritual benefactor is indeed Bodhi.
A spiritual friend is diligence; a spiritual friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter;
a spiritual friend is an indestructible power.
By means of spiritual friends, one travels throughout the ten directions, cuts off the flow of birth and death, and is able to accomplish all great undertakings;
one adorns the right path, attains the Dharma-door of universal entry, and becomes entirely unimpeded;
yet, upon seeing a spiritual friend, one does not leave one's original place, while simultaneously reaching the abodes of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
At that moment, Sudhana immediately understood that by seeing a spiritual friend, he would fulfill an immeasurable ocean of great vows;
attain all-knowledge to benefit sentient beings;
eliminate the suffering of immeasurable kalpas in the future; and adorn himself with the great ornaments.
Within each and every atom, they cultivate all the dharmas of the entire dharma-realm;
they behold the oceans of the ten directions and know the languages and practices of bodhisattvas throughout future eons, bringing all bodhisattva practices to ultimate completion;
in every thought-moment, they attain omniscience, sovereign spiritual powers, and the paths of all adornments.
They are the flow from the pure Dharma-realm of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
without departing from the sphere of the Dharma-realm, they are able to go to and reach the presence of spiritual friends who fill the Dharma-realm.

At that time, Sudhana went to visit the Night Goddess Joyful Eyes Observing Sentient Beings and saw her at the site of the Tathāgata, seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses within the great assembly.
The Bodhisattva Samādhi-Pratilabdha-Samantaprabhāsa-Ratnaketu entered the Dharma-gate of Universal Radiance and Joyful Banner, and from all his pores issued forth clouds of myriad wonders.
Those who beheld them were filled with joy and never grew weary, for these were what were known as:
clouds of the practice of wisdom that benefit sentient beings, remaining free from contention and non-attached to any phenomena;

With a mind of equanimity, they universally gather in all sentient beings, manifesting the practice of giving by Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time; they completely relinquish all things, both internal and external, that are difficult to give away, so that all sentient beings of the ten directions may behold them.
Furthermore, from every single pore, clouds of transformation bodies of Bodhisattvas, equal in number to all sentient beings, emerge and fill the Dharma-realm, appearing before all living beings;
they manifest the samādhi of immovable meditative absorption to awaken sentient beings who take no pleasure in the three realms.
Distant from the mundane world and extinguishing birth and death, they manifest the various successes and failures among devas and humans;
they teach all sentient beings to practice the contemplation of impurity to eliminate the perversion of perceiving the pure as pure;
and they explain that conditioned phenomena are impermanent, subject to change, and of the nature of suffering.
They cause all sentient beings to enter deeply into the Buddha’s precepts, never departing from them even for a moment, as they receive and uphold the pure prohibitions of all Buddhas;
they manifest the precept of non-doubt and the fragrance of the precepts, universally perfuming all sentient beings.

Furthermore, from every single pore, clouds of sublime physical bodies as numerous as all sentient beings emerge, manifesting to all beings that they are able to endure the amputation of their limbs and joints, and are capable of undergoing all manner of suffering;
they fully tolerate all forms of reproach and foul abuse.
Toward those sentient beings, one does not give rise to a mind of anger, nor does one give rise to a mind of attachment while showing reverence and praise;
toward all sentient beings, one does not give rise to pride, but manifests the patience regarding the intrinsic nature of all phenomena and manifests the inexhaustible wisdom-mind of bodhicitta;
one eliminates the afflictions of all sentient beings, cultivates the dharma of patience, and practices the conduct of a bodhisattva.
He manifests the pure vajra-body and manifests the pure, unsurpassed form-body (*rūpakāya*) of the Tathāgata, teaching and transforming sentient beings according to their needs.
Furthermore, from every pore, clouds of various physical bodies belonging to all realms of existence emerge; through courageous diligence, they manifest omniscience;
through courageous diligence, they manifest the realm of enlightenment without ever regressing;
and through courageous diligence, they subdue all Māras.
With courageous diligence, they are able to rescue and deliver all sentient beings from the ocean of birth and death;
with courageous diligence, they eliminate all hardships of the evil realms;
with courageous diligence, they shatter the mountain of ignorance.
With courageous diligence, they reverently make offerings to all Tathāgatas with minds free from weariness;
with courageous diligence, they receive, uphold, and protect the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas;
with courageous diligence, they shatter and disperse all mountains of obstacles.
With courageous and diligent effort, they adorn and purify all the buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas, attain the pure diligence of all the Tathāgatas, and teach and liberate all sentient beings.

Furthermore, from every single pore, they emit clouds of various physical bodies; through diverse skillful means, they eliminate the sorrow, grief, and afflictions of sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice;
they cause them to loathe the five desires, praise shame and remorse, subdue the sense faculties, and practice the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-conduct;
and through the virtues of body, speech, and mind, they manifest that all worldly desires are ultimately not to be relished.
They establish sentient beings so that they may delight in the True Dharma, giving rise to the nine successive meditative attainments;
they eliminate all afflictions of sentient beings, manifesting the ocean of bodhisattva samādhis and the sphere of sovereign spiritual powers of clear illumination;
they cause all sentient beings to be filled with joy, making their bodies and minds supple, extinguishing the heat of afflictions, attaining cool and refreshing bliss, and nurturing the True Dharma.

Furthermore, from every single pore, clouds of various bodies belonging to all realms of existence emerge, proceeding to all lands where Buddhas, teachers, and spiritual friends reside, reverently making offerings to them with a mind free from weariness.
Upholding the wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas;
reaching the ultimate depths of the ocean of all Buddhas;
manifesting the ocean of all phenomena;
Manifesting the true reality of all phenomena;
manifesting all gateways of samādhi and pure wisdom;
discerning the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings through vajra-wisdom.
They shatter the mountains of all sentient beings' false views and give birth to the sun of perfect, luminous, and pure wisdom.
In a single thought-moment, they are able to utterly extinguish the darkness of ignorance for all sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice and attain *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge).
Furthermore, from every single pore, clouds of bodies as numerous as all sentient beings emerge, manifesting various physical forms and inconceivable bodies;
according to what is appropriate for each, they appear before them all, and with immeasurable voices, they expound for all sentient beings the treasury of worldly merits.
All worldly activities within the three realms are entirely unworthy of delight;

one should praise the departure from all evil and false views of the three realms, distance oneself from deviant paths, and turn toward omniscience, thereby transcending the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Regarding the conditioned and the unconditioned, the mind has no attachment;
it turns its back on birth and death and proceeds directly toward nirvāṇa,

yet it does not abandon wandering through the various realms of existence, nor does it abandon the arousal of the bodhicitta, the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment, the teaching and transforming of sentient beings, or the realization of all-knowledge.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there emerge clouds of transformation bodies as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, appearing before all sentient beings to cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra, fulfill the vows of Samantabhadra, and praise the ultimate fulfillment of all great aspirations.
In every thought-moment, they adorn and purify all oceans of worlds;
in every thought-moment, they reverently make offerings to all Buddhas;
in every thought-moment, they are fully able to receive and uphold all oceans of teachings.

In every thought-moment, within each and every atom, they bring forth oceans of all world-systems and oceans of skillful means as numerous as atoms throughout the Dharma-realm; they sustain all lands and all eons, purifying the path of all-knowledge without ever resting.
In every thought-moment, they enter the powers of all Tathāgatas, reaching the ultimate ocean of skillful means across the three periods of time.
In all lands, he manifests his power of mastery, causing all sentient beings to cultivate the bodhisattva practices, fulfill their great vows, and attain all-knowledge.

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issue forth clouds of bodies equal in number to the minds of all sentient beings, appearing before all beings and manifesting the infinite power of the Tathāgata’s wisdom—power that is inexhaustible and indestructible.

They cultivate the various practices of non-regressive Bodhisattvas; their minds remain unstained by the phenomena of birth and death; they subdue all Māras, extinguish the power of afflictions, shatter the power of all mountains of obstacles, and are endowed with the power of great compassion.

Throughout all kalpas, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices with a mind free from weariness; they shake all Buddha-worlds, bringing joy to sentient beings, turning the pure wheel of Dharma, establishing the banner of Dharma, and subduing all heterodox teachers;
by cultivating the power of the *pāramitā* of bodhisattva practice, they attain all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).

Furthermore, from each and every pore, there issue forth clouds of various physical bodies equal in number to the minds of all sentient beings, filling the infinite realms of sentient beings. According to what is appropriate for them, they manifest the conduct of Bodhisattvas;

with the power of wisdom and diligence, they ferry across the ocean of sentient beings, discerning and understanding the ocean of the mental activities of all sentient beings, the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings, and the ocean of the practices of all sentient beings.
They teach and transform sentient beings without ever missing the proper time, possessing clear and pure wisdom that reaches the ultimate nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).

In every thought-moment, their bright and pure wisdom fills the dharma-realm; they thoroughly understand the formation and destruction of all worlds, as well as their adornments and sovereign spiritual powers;
they go to the abodes of all Buddhas to pay respectful homage and offerings, and to protect, uphold, and maintain the clouds of the wheel of the true Dharma.
Thus manifesting the perfection of wisdom, they cause all sentient beings to experience great joy, radiance, and delight, with bodies and minds made supple;

they eliminate feverish afflictions, distance themselves from sorrow and grief, abandon all evils, subdue their faculties, attain liberation of mind, and achieve non-retrogression regarding omniscience.
Just as they manifest the various *pāramitās* to transform and deliver sentient beings,
so too do they manifest all the merits of a bodhisattva to transform and deliver sentient beings.

Furthermore, from every single pore, there appeared the Night Goddess Joyful Eyes Surveying Sentient Beings, manifesting the merits she had cultivated since first resolving her mind: seeking spiritual friends, approaching all Buddhas, reverently making offerings, and practicing roots of goodness.
Practicing the *dānapāramitā*, he is able to give what is difficult to relinquish;
practicing the *śīlapāramitā*, he abandons the world, palaces, and retinue to leave home and study the Way, purely cultivating the prohibitive precepts;
practicing the *kṣāntipāramitā*, he is able to endure all sentient beings who address him with harsh words and subject him to immeasurable oppression.
Practicing the *vīrya-pāramitā*, they cultivate various ascetic practices and single-mindedly seek bodhi, their minds firm and unretrogressive;

practicing the *dhyāna-pāramitā*, through various skillful means, they fulfill the pure *dhyāna-pāramitā*, attaining mastery over all samādhis, and reaching the ultimate depths of the ocean of all samādhis in continuous succession without interruption;

practicing the *prajñā-pāramitā*, they purify the perfect wisdom of a bodhisattva, bringing forth the bright and pure sun of wisdom from the inexhaustible treasury of wisdom, reaching the ultimate ocean of knowledge.

They practice the *pāramitā* of skillful means (*upāya*), giving birth to all bodies of skillful means, the merit of skillful means, the purity of skillful means, and the fundamental matters of skillful means;

they practice the *pāramitā* of vows (*praṇidhāna*), giving birth to all pure bodies of vows, fulfilling all vows, acting in accordance with their vows as appropriate, and [explaining] the fundamental matters of the *pāramitā* of vows;

they practice the *pāramitā* of power (*bala*), [explaining] the causal merit of the *pāramitā* of power, the ocean of skillful means of the *pāramitā* of power, and analytically expounding the fundamental matters of the *pāramitā* of power.

The practice of the perfection of wisdom, the birth of the perfection of wisdom, the purification of the body through the perfection of wisdom, the teaching of the perfection of wisdom, the sphere of the perfection of wisdom, that which is subsumed by the perfection of wisdom, the radiance of the perfection of wisdom, the fundamental basis of the perfection of wisdom, the analytical practice of the perfection of wisdom, the profound penetration of the perfection of wisdom, and the comprehensive grasping of all dharmas through the perfection of wisdom;

In accordance with these, they know phenomena, know karma, know lands, know eons, know the three periods of time, know the appearance of Buddhas in the world, know the wisdom of Buddhas, know Bodhisattvas, know the wisdom of Bodhisattvas, know the abodes of Bodhisattvas, know the merits of Bodhisattvas, know the dedications of Bodhisattvas, know all great vows, know the turning of the wheel of Dharma, know the differentiation of phenomena, know the entry into the ocean of phenomena, know the ocean of skillful means, know the whirlpools of phenomena, and know the destinations of all phenomena;
such as these, all the perfections of omniscience are manifested from every single pore, transforming and delivering sentient beings.

Furthermore, from every pore, there issued forth immeasurable clouds of bodies, namely: clouds of bodies of Akaniṣṭha devas; clouds of bodies of Śuddhāvāsa devas; clouds of bodies of Sudarśana devas; clouds of bodies of Atapa devas; clouds of bodies of Bṛhatphala devas; clouds of bodies of Śubhakṛtsna devas; clouds of bodies of Apramāṇaśubha devas; clouds of bodies of Parīttaśubha devas; clouds of bodies of Śubhakṛtsnaphala devas; clouds of bodies of Apramāṇaśubhaphala devas; clouds of bodies of Parīttaśubhaphala devas; clouds of bodies of Ābhāsvara devas; clouds of bodies of Apramāṇābhāsvara devas; clouds of bodies of Parīttābhāsvara devas; clouds of bodies of Mahābrahmā devas; clouds of bodies of Brahmapurohita devas; clouds of bodies of Brahmakāyika devas;
and clouds of bodies of the King of the Paranirmitavaśavartin devas, as well as the sons and daughters of the Paranirmitavaśavartin devas.
Clouds of bodies of the King of the Heaven of Mastery over Transformations, along with the sons and daughters of the gods of that heaven;
clouds of bodies of the King of Tuṣita Heaven, along with the sons and daughters of the gods of that heaven;
and clouds of bodies of the King of the Yāma Heaven, along with the sons and daughters of the gods of that heaven.
Clouds of the bodies of the thirty-three heavenly kings, as well as the sons and daughters of the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three;
clouds of the bodies of the heavenly king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, as well as all male and female gandharvas;
and clouds of the bodies of the heavenly king Virūḍhaka, as well as all male and female kumbhāṇḍas.
The celestial king Virūpākṣa and clouds of the bodies of all male and female nāgas;
the celestial king Vaiśravaṇa and clouds of the bodies of all male and female yakṣas;
and the kinnara kings and clouds of the bodies of all male and female kinnaras.
The mahoraga kings and clouds of the bodies of all male and female mahoragas;
the garuḍa kings and clouds of the bodies of all male and female garuḍas;
the asura kings and clouds of the bodies of all male and female asuras;
The cloud-bodies of King Yama and all the male and female forms of the kings of the hells;
the cloud-bodies of human kings;
and the cloud-bodies of men, women, boys, and girls.
From these [bodies] emerge clouds of bodies for all realms of existence:
clouds of bodies of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and rishis;

and clouds of bodies of earth, water, fire, and wind deities; sea deities, river deities, mountain deities, forest deities, tree deities, grain deities, flavor deities, medicinal herb deities, garden and pavilion deities, city-wall deities, maṇḍala deities, night deities, day deities, space deities, directional deities, road deities, bodily-form deities, and Vajrapāṇi deities. Such clouds of all these bodies emerge, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.

For the sake of all sentient beings, she manifests as the Night Goddess Joyful Eyes Who Observes Sentient Beings. From her initial resolve, she has practiced meritorious deeds, accumulated immeasurable *pāramitās*, and undergone successive births—dying here and being born there—including their respective names, her proximity to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), her encounters with various Buddhas, her hearing and upholding of the True Dharma, her practice of the bodhisattva path, and her attainment of various samādhis. She has successively beheld all Buddha-fields and the Tathāgatas throughout the succession of eons;
she has attained pure wisdom, deeply entered the Dharma-realm, observed sentient beings, and known the ocean of sentient beings as they die here and are born there.
Having attained the pure divine ear, they hear all sounds in successive order;
possessing the knowledge of others' minds, they thoroughly understand the mental activities of sentient beings in successive order;
and through the basis-less supernormal power, they freely pervade the ten directions in successive order.

They attain the sequential dharma-gates of all bodhisattvas, reaching the ultimate ocean of all bodhisattva dharma-gates, the sovereignty of bodhisattvas, the diligence of bodhisattvas, and the realization of the correct course by bodhisattvas; they are free from the notion of sentient beings, the notion of bodhisattvas, and the notions of the supreme, wondrous, and pure merits of bodhisattvas.
All such categories of merit as these, that cloud of transformation bodies fully explains, analyzes, reveals, and manifests for the sake of sentient beings through various sounds; namely:

The sound of the wind-circle, the sound of the water-circle, the sound of the flames, the sound of the great ocean, the sound of the great earth quaking, the sound of mountain kings colliding, the sound of celestial cities shaking, the sound of celestial jewels, the sounds of all the devas, the sounds of the nāga kings, the sounds of the yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, and so forth; the sounds of human kings, the sounds of Brahmā kings, the sounds of celestial maidens singing hymns, the sounds of celestial music, the sounds of the king of maṇi jewels, the sounds of the Tathāgata, the sounds of the bodhisattvas, and the sounds of the Tathāgata’s transformation bodies.

With these and various other such sounds, for the sake of all sentient beings, he analytically expounded upon the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā and all her merits from the time she first resolved to attain enlightenment.

When each of those clouds of bodies preached this Dharma, in every thought-moment, in every direction, they purified unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-worlds; immeasurable and boundless sentient beings were made to extinguish the suffering of the evil realms; immeasurable and boundless sentient beings attained celestial bliss; immeasurable and boundless sentient beings crossed the ocean of birth and death; immeasurable and boundless sentient beings were established in the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; immeasurable and boundless sentient beings attained the Bodhisattva dharma-gate of the Sovereign Banner of Inconceivable Joy; and in every thought-moment, immeasurable and boundless sentient beings dwelt in the stage of the Tathāgata.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld and heard all these aforementioned extraordinary events; he reflected upon them with right mindfulness, examined and discerned them, entered deeply into meditative wisdom, and dwelt in equanimity.

Why is this? Because they have previously practiced together with those night goddesses; because they are protected by the mindfulness of the Buddhas; because they have accomplished inconceivable roots of goodness; because they are endowed with the faculties of a bodhisattva; because they are born into the family of the Buddhas; because they have obtained the power of spiritual friends; because they are sustained by the spiritual power of all Buddhas; because of the power of the original vows of Vairocana Buddha; because their roots of goodness are matured; and because they are capable of receiving the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

At that time, Sudhana attained the Bodhisattva’s ocean of pure light of joy, obtained the power of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions, and attained that night goddess’s dharma-gate of the Banner of Undefiled Joy. He then joined his palms in reverence and praised the night goddess with these verses:
“Throughout immeasurable and countless eons, You have deeply studied the most supreme Dharma;
According to the needs of those to be transformed, You manifest a wondrous form-body.”
Fully understanding that all living beings are deluded by ignorance and inversion,
he employs various bodily skillful means to deliver and liberate the multitudes of sentient beings.
With his pure and wondrous Dharma-body, he extinguishes the fever of their afflictions.
Though non-dual, they manifest as dual for the sake of transforming sentient beings.
Regarding the aggregates, sense bases, and elements, they are entirely without attachment;
through their practice and their physical bodies, they liberate all multitudes.
Unattached to internal or external phenomena, He has crossed over the ocean of birth and death.
With the light of clear and pure wisdom, He universally illumines all things.
The Deva of Joyful Eyes is unattached, Extinguishing all that is false and delusive.
For sentient beings who delight in and cling to the world, you manifest the power of the Buddha-dharma.
By the power of unimpeded samādhi, from every single pore you emit clouds of transformation bodies to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
In every thought-moment, they bring forth the power of skillful means of all Buddhas,
gathering in all sentient beings and bringing all dharmas to ultimate completion.
They observe the ocean of all realms of existence, their bodies adorned by the traces of karmic actions.
He expounds the unimpeded Dharma in order to purify all beings.
Adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, his body is like that of Samantabhadra;
according to those who are ready to be transformed, he manifests infinite bodies.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had praised her with these verses, he said: "O Deva,
how long has it been since you first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi?"
"How long has it been since this Dharma-gate was attained?
At that time, the Night Goddess replied in verse:
"I recall past ages, as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable lands."
At that time there was an eon named Silent Sound (Śāntasvara).
There was a capital city named Fragrant Water (Gandhodaka), and its king was named Wisdom (Jñāna).
It comprised twelve billion hundred thousand nayutas of four-continent worlds.
That noble Wheel-Turning King possesses a pure and wondrous physical form,
complete with the thirty-two marks and adorned by the eighty secondary characteristics.
His sublime body is a treasury of purity, the color of Jāmbūnada gold.
His radiance illuminates all things as he strides with measured gait through the void.
That king has a thousand sons, valiant and of handsome form;
he has ten million ministers, all of whom are wise and sagacious.
He has ten billion court ladies, as beautiful and dignified as celestial queens;
with great compassion and gentle hearts, they attend upon and serve the King.
That holy Wheel-Turning King always governs by means of the True Dharma.
Ruling over all mountainous lands throughout the four continents,
I was then a precious woman, endowed with pure Brahma-voices;
from my body issued golden light that illuminated forty thousand li in every direction.
When the sunlight has already set, and the midnight is tranquil and still,
at that time, divine portents shall descend as auspicious dreams:
I shall see a Buddha appearing in the world, named Guṇasāgara (Ocean of Merit).
Manifesting sovereign power, they fill the realms of the ten directions.
Emitting oceans of great radiance, equal in number to the atoms of all lands,
their infinite bodies of mastery fill the ten directions.
The great earth shook in six ways, And wondrous sounds issued forth spontaneously;
As the Tathāgata arose in the world, Gods and humans all rejoiced.
From every single pore, An ocean of the Buddha’s transformation bodies emerged.
Filling the realms of the ten directions, He teaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate.
I saw this in a dream, The sovereign power of the Tathāgata;
Hearing him preach the profound and wondrous Dharma, My heart was filled with great joy.
Ten thousand night deities, filling the void of space, praised that Tathāgata;
having heard this, I immediately attained awakening.
Those deities spoke to me, saying:
"O wise woman, arise quickly! A Buddha has appeared in your land, one difficult to encounter even in oceans of kalpas.
Hearing these words with joy, she immediately beheld a bright and pure light.
Observing whence it came, she saw it was from beneath the King of Trees at the site of enlightenment."
At that time, seeing the body of the Tathāgata, Like the king of jewel mountains,
From every single pore, He emitted a great ocean of radiant light.
Beholding the Buddha’s power of mastery, His heart was filled with great joy.
I immediately made a great vow, praying that I might attain such merit.
At that time, I awakened the Great King and his entire retinue;
seeing the radiance of that Buddha, their hearts were filled with immeasurable joy.
At that time, together with that king and his retinue of immeasurable nayutas of the fourfold army, I went to where the Tathāgata was.
For twenty thousand years, I made offerings to that Tathāgata.
The seven treasures and the four continents— All these were offered as gifts.
At that time, the Tathāgata preached The *Sūtra of the Universal Cloud of Merit*,
Adorned by an ocean of great vows, To deliver sentient beings according to their needs.
I made this vow: "In a future life, may I become a night goddess and cause all those who are heedless to be entirely free from such negligence.
At that time, I first gave rise to the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment.
Within the conditioned realm of birth and death, he never once forgot [the Dharma].
From that time forward, he made offerings to ten billion nayutas of Buddhas;
enjoying happiness within the ocean of birth and death, he brought benefit to all living beings.
First was the Buddha Guṇasāgara; second, Guṇapradīpa;
third, Ratnadhvaja Buddha; fourth, Gaganajñāna; fifth, Padmagarbha; sixth, Asaṅgaghoṣacandra.
The seventh was King Dharmacandra; the eighth, Perfect Wisdom Lamp;
the ninth, Jewel Flame Buddha; the unsurpassed Honored One of Gods and Men;
and the tenth, Transformed Sound—I have made offerings to them all.
Such Buddhas as these, numbering ten billion nayutas,
had not yet attained the eye of wisdom to reach the ultimate end of the ocean of birth and death.
Following this, there was another eon named Divyavimalajaya.
In the world named Ratnaprabhā, five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world:
the first was Pūrṇacandra, the second Vimalasūrya, the third Prabhāsa, and the fourth Sumerurāja.
The fifth was Padmajvālāsamudra; the sixth, Jñānasāgara;
the seventh, Dīpaṃkara Buddha; the eighth, Devaguṇagarbha;
the ninth, Prabhāsarājadhvaja; and the tenth, Samantajñānarāja.
All such Buddhas as these, I have already made offerings to all;
yet they had not yet abandoned the attachment to the five aggregates, perceiving pleasure where there is no pleasure.
Following this, there was another eon named Adorned Brahma-Sound.
At that time there was a world named Lotus Lamp Cloud;
therein were immeasurable Buddhas along with their great retinues,
all of whom I have fully made offerings to, hearing and upholding their True Dharma.
The first Buddha was Sumeru; the second, Guṇasāgara;
the third, Dharmadhātusumerudhvaja; the fourth, Dharma-sumeru;
the fifth, Dharmadhvaja Buddha; and the sixth, Dharmabhūmi Buddha.
The seventh was Dharma-power Buddha, the eighth Space-wisdom,
the ninth Flame-mountain, and the tenth Illumination-mountain;
all such Buddhas as these I have fully made offerings to.
Still not having realized the truth, they have not yet reached the ultimate ocean of all dharmas.
Subsequently, there was another eon named Joyful Virtue;
at that time, there was a world named Banner of Merit.
In that kalpa, there were eighty nayutas of Buddhas,
to whom he offered immeasurable articles of worship.
First was the Gandharva King, and second was the King of the Longevity Tree.
The third was Meru-guṇa, the fourth was Ratnanetra Buddha,
the fifth was Vairocana, the sixth was Prabhāsa-alaṃkāra,
the seventh was Dharmajaya Buddha, and the eighth was Vimalaśrī.
The ninth was the Lord of the World, and the tenth was the King of All Dharmas;
to all such Buddhas as these I have made offerings,
yet I have not yet attained the wondrous wisdom that deeply enters the ocean of the Dharma-realm.
Next there was another eon, named Silent Wisdom;
at that time there was a world named Universal Radiant Cloud,
where a thousand Buddhas appeared in the world, adorned with immeasurable virtues.
Having eliminated the defilements of affliction, all beings were purified.
The first Buddha was named Araṇa (Free from Strife); the second was Anāvaraṇabala (Power of Non-obstruction);
the third was Dharmadhātuprabha (Radiance of the Dharma-realm); and the fourth was Sarvapradīparāja (King of All Lamps).
The fifth was Bharadvāja; the sixth was Sattvāśraya;
the seventh was Kṣāntiparipūrṇapradīpa; the eighth was Dharmasampannapradīpa;
the ninth was Prabhāsavyūhasāgara; and the tenth was Prabhāsarāja.
I have made offerings to all such Buddhas as these, yet I have not yet understood the True Dharma; thus I have wandered through all lands.
Following this, there was another kalpa.
At that time there was a world named Pure Arising,
where one hundred million Buddhas appeared in the world, adorning and purifying all kalpas;
the Dharma taught by those Buddhas, I heard it all and received and upheld it.
The first Buddha was Immeasurable Renown; the second, Dharma-Ocean Buddha;
the third, Valiant King; the fourth, Virtue-Dharma King;
the fifth, Supreme Dharma-Cloud; and the sixth, Celestial Crown Buddha.
The seventh was Jñānārci Buddha, the eighth Gaganasvara,
the ninth Samudgataśreṣṭha, and the tenth Guṇaprabhāsa;
having made offerings to those Buddhas, he accomplished the Eightfold Noble Path.
Next there was another eon, named Pure and Firm Brilliance;
at that time there was a world named Jewel Banner King,
wherein five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world— those Tathāgatas and their equals.
I have made offerings to them all, seeking the unimpeded Dharma-gate:
The first Buddha, Perfect Virtue; the second, Silent Sound;
the third, Ocean of Merit; and the fourth, Sun King Buddha.
The fifth was Guṇarāja, the sixth Sumerudhvaja,
the seventh Dharmarāja Buddha, the eighth Guṇarāja,
the ninth Sumeru, and the tenth Prabhāsa-rāja.
All such Buddhas as these, I have already made offerings to;
I have purified all their most supreme paths,
yet I have not yet fully attained the ultimate profound dharma-patience.
Next there was another eon, named Victorious Lord;
at that time there was a world named Silent Sound,
where eighty nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world.
I have made offerings to them all, practicing the Right Path under them:
The first Buddha was named Puṣpaketu; the second was Sāgaragarbha;
the third was Guṇasambhava; and the fourth was Deva-keśara.
The fifth was Maṇigarbha; the sixth, the Buddha Suvarṇaparvata;
the seventh, the Buddha Ratnarāśi; the eighth, Śāntadhvaja;
the ninth, the Buddha Dharmadhvaja; and the tenth, the Buddha Jñānarāja.
Such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings to all of them.
Following that, there was another eon named Thousand Merits;
at that time, there was a world named Banner-Lamp of Skillful Transformation.
Six hundred million nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world;
I have made offerings to all of those Tathāgatas.
The first Buddha was Śāntadhvaja, and the second was Prajñādhvaja.
The three hundredth Buddha was Caturguṇamegharāja;
the fourth was Śāntaprabharāja; the sixth was Vimalasūrya;
the seventh was Dharmapradīpa; and the eighth was Arciṣmanta.
The Ninth is the Treasury of Merit, and the Tenth is the Lamp of Wisdom;
to all such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings in their entirety.
Yet I had not yet attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas, nor reached the ultimate depths of the ocean of all phenomena.
Next there was another eon, named Adornment of Non-attachment;
at that time there was a world named Immeasurable Supreme Radiance,
wherein thirty-six nayutas of Buddhas appeared.
Such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings to them all:
First was Guṇasumeru, second was Śūnyatācitta, Third was Vyūhajñāna, and fourth was Vyūhagarbha.
Fifth is Dharmasvarasāgara; sixth is Dharmadhārasvara;
seventh is Nirmāṇasvara; eighth is Guṇasāgara; ninth is Guṇasāgarapradīpa; tenth is Guṇadhvaja.
I have encountered all those Tathāgatas. When the Tathāgata Guṇaketurāja appeared in the world,
I was Guṇadharā, and I made offerings to that Most Victorious One.
At that time, the Buddha explained to me how to receive and uphold the ocean of great vows,
the dhāraṇīs, and the power of mindfulness; I attained the clear and pure eye, as well as samādhi and dhāraṇī.
In every single thought-moment, they behold the most supreme ocean;
Giving birth to the treasury of great compassion, they enter deeply into clouds of skillful means.
With minds as pure as space, they fully attain the powers of all Buddhas.
Observing all sentient beings, who are inverted by the notions of permanence, bliss, self, and purity;
shrouded by the darkness of ignorance, they give rise to delusions through afflictions.
With false views, craving, and the like, they commit immeasurable evil karmas.
Throughout all realms of existence, one fully experiences the retribution of unwholesome deeds;
throughout all realms of existence, one receives a body through various karmas,
beset by the afflictions of birth, old age, sickness, and death, and oppressed by immeasurable suffering.
I have resolved upon the unsurpassed mind, to bring peace and happiness to those sentient beings,
leading them to the presence of all Buddhas and enabling them to fulfill the powers of the Tathāgatas.
May I satisfy the clouds of great vows and constantly behold all Buddhas.
Cultivating the true path, they are fully endowed with all merits.
Single-mindedly and extensively seeking the clouds of immeasurable merit,
the Dharma-gates, and the perfections (pāramitās), they fill all realms of phenomena (dharmadhātu).
O Son of the Buddha, at that time, I immediately attained the conduct of Samantabhadra;
I discerned the profound Dharma-realm and gathered up all phenomena.
I fulfilled all the stages and mastered the ocean of skillful means throughout the three periods of time.
Cultivating unimpeded conduct, one possesses Buddha-wisdom in a single thought-moment.
"Good son! At that time, was the Wheel-Turning King Wisdom anyone else? It was none other than myself."
This is the youth Mañjuśrī; he succeeds to the lineage of the Wheel-Turning Kings and ensures that the seed of all Tathāgatas is never severed.
At that time, the virtuous and wise Jewel-Woman was my own self; and the night goddess who awakened me then was a transformation of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.

At that time, I first gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Having resolved upon the path, for as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, I did not fall into the evil realms, but was constantly born among gods and humans, beholding various Buddhas. Eventually, at the place of the Buddha Guṇadhvaja, I attained this Dharma-door of the Banner of Universal Radiance and Joy. Having attained this Dharma-door, I have benefited and brought to liberation immeasurable sentient beings.
“Good son! I know only this Dharma gate. As for the great Bodhisattvas, in every thought-moment they go before all Tathāgatas and fully accomplish the great ocean of vigor;
in every thought-moment, they fulfill the great ocean of all vows.”
In every moment of thought, they bring forth all the practices of Bodhisattvas throughout all future eons;
within each and every Bodhisattva practice, they manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands, and each of those bodies fills the oceans of all Dharma-realms;
within each and every Dharma-realm, they manifest all Buddha-lands, appearing in Bodhisattva practices according to what is appropriate for each being.
Within each and every buddha-field, they exhaustively realize oceans of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields;

at the site of each and every Buddha, they exhaustively realize the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgatas, which are equal to the entire dharma-realm; at the site of each and every Tathāgata, they discern the past kalpas and practice the bodhisattva path;
at the site of each and every Tathāgata, they protect and uphold all wheels of Dharma, and exhaustively master the ocean of skillful means of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
"How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

Good son, within this assembly of the Buddha, there is a night goddess named *Guṇarati-sattvatrāṇa* (Savior of Beings through Wondrous Virtue). Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva conduct, fulfills the bodhisattva conduct, and purifies the bodhisattva conduct."
Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā with his head, took his leave, and departed.

At that time, Sudhana, with right mindfulness, contemplated the Dharma-door of the Banner of Universal Radiance and Joy; he analyzed it, entered into it deeply, and brought it forth into manifestation.
Following the instructions of spiritual friends, they single-mindedly and exclusively seek to see them; with their bodies, minds, and all faculties, they travel everywhere in every direction.
Seeking spiritual friends and contemplating the path of spiritual friends, they attain the opportunity to meet them through courageous and diligent effort;
they share in all the roots of goodness of the spiritual friends and fully accomplish profound and wondrous skillful means.

Relying upon spiritual friends, one gives birth to and nurtures all roots of goodness and gives rise to great vows; throughout all kalpas, one never leaves spiritual friends and proceeds to the presence of the Night Goddess Wondrous Virtue Who Protects and Saves Sentient Beings.

At that time, the Night Goddess manifested for the youth Sudhana the realm of the Bodhisattva’s Dharma-door for teaching all worlds; her body was adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, and from the white tuft of hair between her eyebrows, she emitted a great light called "Pure Banner of the Lamp of Universal Wisdom Flames," with immeasurable rays of light as its retinue, universally illuminating all worlds.
Having illuminated them, the light entered the crown of Sudhana’s head and filled his entire body.
At that time, Sudhana immediately attained the Bodhisattva samādhi called "Stainless Perfection.

Having attained this samādhi, within every atom of earth, water, fire, and wind; within atoms of various jewels, atoms of fragrance, atoms of diamond, atoms of mani-gems, atoms of pulverized powder, atoms of all ornaments, and atoms of all objective realms—in each and every such atom, he beheld the formation and destruction of worlds as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field.

The wind-circle, water-circle, vajra-circle, and earth-circle, adorned with various ornaments; surrounded by numerous mountains and immeasurable great oceans; the palaces of the devas and various jewel-trees, all magnificently arrayed;

the palaces of the nāgas, and the cities and palaces of the yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans; and the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and the realm of King Yama—therein he saw all sentient beings of the five destinies, dying here and being born there.
He discerns and understands those various worlds: some worlds are pure, some are impure;

some worlds tend toward purity, some tend toward impurity; some worlds are both pure and impure, some are both impure and pure; some worlds are exclusively pure; some worlds are level and even in shape, some are shaped like a reclining figure, and some are square in shape.
Within all such worlds and all realms of existence, he sees that Night Goddess appearing at all times before all sentient beings, liberating them according to their respective needs.
For the sake of sentient beings in the hells, he extinguishes all their agonizing torments;
for the sake of animals, he extinguishes their fear of affliction and harm;
for the sake of sentient beings who are hungry ghosts, he removes the suffering of hunger and thirst.
For the sake of the nāgas and others, he extinguishes all fears;

for the sake of sentient beings in the desire realm, he removes the sufferings of the desire realm; and for the sake of all human beings, he eliminates the fear of darkness, the fear of inability to subsist, the fear of ill repute, the fear of assemblies, the fear of evil destinies, the fear of death, the fear of losing roots of goodness, the fear of losing the bodhicitta, the fear of associating with evil friends, the fear of losing virtuous friends, the fear of the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, the fear of saṃsāra, the fear of disagreeable circumstances, the fear of taking birth at an improper time, the fear of being born into an evil family, the fear of performing evil deeds, the fear of karmic obstructions, the fear of afflictive obstructions, the fear of maturational obstructions, the fear of various attachments, and the fear of various fetters—extinguishing all such terrors as these.

Furthermore, they teach and transform sentient beings of the four modes of birth—namely, those born from eggs, those born from wombs, those born from moisture, and those born by transformation—as well as those with form and those without form, those with perception and those without perception, and those with neither perception nor non-perception; they constantly manifest before them to instruct and transform them.
Because of the fulfillment of the power of great vows; because of the power of the bodhisattva’s samādhis; because of the power of the various supernormal knowledges and clarities;
because of the power of producing the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; because of producing and nurturing the ocean of great compassion;
because of covering all sentient beings with unimpeded great kindness; because of bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings; and because of gathering them in...
For the sake of all sentient beings; because they have deeply entered the dharma-gate of the bodhisattva’s realm of mastery;
because they universally manifest within all Buddha-fields to adorn and purify them; because they possess wisdom and awakening amidst all dharmas;
because they reverently make offerings at the abodes of all Buddhas; and because they protect and maintain all Buddha-dharmas.
Because of the True Dharma, they dwell within the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings to deliver and liberate them;
they dwell within the faculties of all sentient beings to discipline those faculties;
they dwell within the ocean of desires of all sentient beings to remove obstacles and attain purity; and they arise within the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings.

Because of the light of omniscience, at that time, Sudhana beheld the sovereign spiritual power of that night goddess—the inconceivable realm of a bodhisattva, her sovereign spiritual power in teaching and transforming sentient beings across all worlds, and her mastery over all bodhisattva dharma-gates. Overcome with immeasurable joy, he prostrated himself at her feet, joined his palms in reverence, and stood to one side, contemplating her with single-minded focus.

At that time, the Night Goddess cast off her body of exquisite adornment with its primary and secondary marks and manifested in the form of a night goddess, yet she did not relinquish her sovereign spiritual power.
Then, Sudhana spoke in verse:
"Sudhana stood with palms joined, Gazing intently without weariness."
Beholding his immeasurable spiritual powers, my heart was filled with great joy.
I beheld the Honored One’s wondrous body, adorned naturally with the marks and signs;
it is as pure as space, and nothing can destroy it.
The extraordinary light he emits is equal in number to the atoms of immeasurable lands;
with various subtle and wondrous colors, it shines universally throughout the ten directions.
From every single pore, he emits radiance as numerous as all sentient beings.
At the tip of each ray of light, precious lotus flowers emerge.
From these flowers, transformation bodies appear to extinguish the suffering of sentient beings.
They emit rays of fragrant light that universally pervade the realms of the ten directions.
Raining down clouds of immeasurable flowers, they make offerings to all the Most Victorious Ones;
emitting immeasurable jewel-lights, each as vast as Mount Sumeru,
they universally illumine all beings and eliminate the darkness of ignorance.
From his mouth he emits pure radiance, like immeasurable suns;
it universally illumines the realm of Vairocana, that immeasurable sphere.
From his eyes he emits pure radiance, like immeasurable moons.
Universally illuminating all classes of sentient beings, He eradicates the cataracts of ignorance and delusion.
With sublime marks equal to those of all beings, He brings forth an ocean of transformation bodies.
Pervading all dharma realms, He delivers and liberates them from the ocean of the three realms of existence.
Your pure and wondrous body is seen by all without exception;
Far removed from the perils of water, fire, thieves, And kings and all other hardships—
O Deva of the Joyful Eye, observe me And instruct me to go to the presence of the Honored One.
Beholding the World-Honored One’s mark of the white tuft of hair,
It emits bright and pure light that universally illuminates the oceans of the ten directions, Extinguishing all darkness.
Manifesting the power of sovereign mastery, It enters through the crown of my head.
Once the light has entered the body, the entire frame becomes supple and blissful;
one immediately attains the stainless samādhi and perceives the Buddhas of the ten directions everywhere.
One is able to discern and know all the subtle atoms without exception.
Within each and every atom, one universally beholds the lands of the ten directions:
some are pure worlds, while others are impure lands;
within those impure worlds, sentient beings undergo all manner of suffering.
In impure worlds, because sentient beings suffer,
he manifests the forms of the three vehicles and goes to rescue and deliver them.
In pure buddha-lands, adorned with immeasurable jewels, he likewise appears.
The Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas Always delight in dwelling therein.
Within each and every atom, One universally beholds oceans of pure lands,
Which Vairocana, over the course of accumulated kalpas, Has caused those lands to become pure.
In all Buddha-fields, manifesting seated beneath the Bodhi tree,
they have attained supreme perfect enlightenment and turn the pure wheel of Dharma.
I see the Deva Wondrous Virtue approaching those adorned and pure lands.
"I shall reverently make offerings at the abodes of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, having praised with these verses, Sudhana said: "O Deva!"
How marvelous! How extraordinary!
This Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva is most profound;
What is the name of this dharma-gate?
How long has it been since one attained this dharma-gate?
What practices did you originally cultivate to bring it about?
“Good son! This place is profoundly deep; it cannot be known by any humans, devas, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas. Why is this?
The realm of the practitioner of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
the realm of the Great Compassion Bodhisattva Treasury;
the realm of the Bodhisattva who protects and delivers all sentient beings.
The bodhisattva realm of eliminating all hardships and calamities of the evil destinies;
the bodhisattva realm of protecting all Buddha-dharmas within all buddha-fields so that they are never interrupted;
and the bodhisattva realm of cultivating bodhisattva practices throughout all kalpas to fulfill the ocean of great vows.
Fully accomplishing the light of clear and pure wisdom, it extinguishes the dark obscurations of ignorance for all sentient beings and universally illumines the spheres of all bodhisattvas;
within a single thought-moment, with clear and pure wisdom, it universally illumines the ocean of skillful means throughout the three periods of time—the sphere of the Bodhisattva.
“Good son! Listen attentively! Listen attentively!”
"I shall now, by the Buddha's spiritual power, explain this for you.
Son of the Buddha!
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system, there was an eon named Stainless Perfection and a world named Banner of Radiant, Pure, and Wondrous Virtue."
There appeared in the world Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru.
Their Buddha-worlds were composed of the seven treasures and adorned with various jewels;
those lands were perfect, stainless, and pure, covered by nets of jewels and surrounded on all sides by the Diamond Mountains.
There are ten trillion nayutas of four-continent worlds:
some worlds are pure and their sentient beings are also pure;
some worlds are impure and their sentient beings are also impure.
In some worlds there is a mixture of purity and impurity, and the sentient beings therein are likewise mixed;
in some worlds there is total purity, where all sentient beings are fully endowed with roots of goodness and free from all ailments;
and in some worlds there is sublime and magnificent purity, inhabited solely by bodhisattvas.
At the eastern limit of that world, near the Diamond Mountains, there is a set of four continents named Flower Lamp Banner;
there, exquisite jewel pavilions, towers, palaces, and the finest foods and drinks are spontaneously provided in abundance.
Campa flower trees universally covered everything;
various incense trees emitted clouds of exquisite fragrance;
jewel-garland trees rained down clouds of garlands everywhere; and various miscellaneous flower trees rained down inconceivable clouds of myriad wonderful flowers.
From the various powder-incense trees, clouds of powdered incense rained down;
from the various king-of-incense trees, clouds of exquisite fragrance rained down;
and from the mani-jewel trees, various kinds of jewels rained down.
The various trees of musical instruments, stirred by a gentle breeze, produced harmonious and elegant sounds that filled the void;
the sun and moon were bright and pure, and the radiance of wondrous jewels shone universally upon all things.
In those four continents, there were hundreds of billions of nayutas of royal capitals.

In each capital city, there were a thousand canals whose gentle currents reflected one another; they were covered everywhere with various flowers that spontaneously produced the sounds of celestial music.
Precious trees were planted along the banks in solemn rows, and the ground was composed of various jewels.
Between each of the waters, there are ten billion cities;
each of those cities is surrounded by ten trillion nayutas of villages;
and each of those cities and each of those villages is adorned with immeasurable billions of nayutas of exquisite jewel pavilions.
In that Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Ratnapuṣpadīpa;
it was peaceful, prosperous, and joyful, with a flourishing population, and these sentient beings therein fully practiced the ten paths of wholesome action.
“At that time, in that city, there was a wheel-turning monarch named Pure Radiance Jewel-Treasury Wondrous Virtue;
he was a great Dharma King who ruled by the True Dharma, born from a lotus, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, and possessed of the seven treasures.”

The king had a thousand sons, handsome and valiant; he had a billion ministers; and the king had a precious queen named Perfected Wondrous Virtue, who was upright, dignified, and exquisite, with deep blue eyes and hair, and a body like celestial gold.
His Brahma-voice was pure, and his body emitted a radiance that illuminated a thousand yojanas.

He had a daughter named Wondrous Virtue Eye (*Guṇalocanā*), who was fully endowed with all noble qualities; she was so exceptionally beautiful and upright that those who beheld her never grew weary of the sight. She was attended by ten billion nayutas of hundreds of thousands of court ladies, all of whom shared the same roots of goodness and conduct as the holy king. Their bodies were of a true golden color, and from every pore issued a wondrous fragrance; adorned with various jewels, they surpassed even the celestial maidens.

"At that time, the lifespan of sentient beings was immeasurable; some were indefinite, while others met with untimely death. Their physical forms and complexions varied, as did their heights, names, voices, roots of goodness, diligence, and skillful means—all of which were entirely different. Some were handsome and some ugly; some were praised and some were reviled."
At that time, one person said to another:
"My physical form is handsome and dignified, while your appearance is base and ugly.
Having thus mutually insulted and disparaged one another, they committed evil karma; consequently, their lifespan, physical vigor, and the pleasures they experienced were all utterly diminished.
At that time, to the north of that city, there was a bodhi tree named Universal Radiance;

it was a banner of the sublime Dharma’s sound, with roots made of various jewels that none could destroy. Its trunk, nodes, branches, and leaves were all composed of various jewels and were perfectly symmetrical. It emitted clouds of various jewels that universally covered everything, radiated light of various jewels that universally illuminated the ten directions, and produced sublime sounds to proclaim the Tathāgata’s sovereign spiritual powers.
In front of that tree, there was a pond of fragrant water named Jewel Flower Radiance True Dharma Sound Cloud;
its banks were made of various jewels, and it was surrounded by ten billion hundred thousand nayutas of jewel trees.
Each of those trees—such as the Bodhi tree and the jewel-garland trees—hung down all around, adorned with pure and wondrous jewels;
and countless, immeasurable jeweled pavilions were spread everywhere throughout the site of enlightenment.
Within that fragrant pond, there is a lotus flower named Cloud of the Adorned Realms of All Buddhas of the Three Times.

At the very beginning, the Buddha Wondrous Virtue Banner attained equal and perfect enlightenment upon that flower; for the sake of transforming sentient beings, he emitted a great radiance called "Ten Thousand Years.
When sentient beings see it, they know that ten thousand years hence, a Buddha shall appear in the world.
"Next, he emitted a light called 'Lamp of Joy Free from Defilement for All Sentient Beings';
those sentient beings who saw it knew that in nine thousand years, a Buddha would appear in the world."
Thereafter, he emitted a light named "Stainless Lamp of the Wondrous Virtue Treasury";
all sentient beings who saw it beheld exquisite colors and knew that eight thousand years hence, a Buddha would appear in the world.
Thereafter, he emitted a light named "The Sound of the Karmic Retribution of All Sentient Beings";
those sentient beings who saw it clearly discerned their own karmic retributions and knew that in seven thousand years, a Buddha would appear in the world.
Next, he emitted a light named "Sound Arising from All Roots of Goodness";

if there were sentient beings with incomplete faculties who touched this radiance, they would all become fully endowed with them, and they knew that for six thousand years the Buddha was about to appear in the world.
Thereafter, he emitted a light called "The Sound Manifesting the Inconceivable Realms of All Buddhas";
all sentient beings who saw it attained a mind of luminous purity and mastery, and knew that in five thousand years a Buddha would appear in the world.
Thereafter, he emitted a light called "Adorning and Purifying All Buddha-fields";
those sentient beings who saw it beheld all the Tathāgatas adorning and purifying the Buddha-fields, and they knew that after four thousand years, a Buddha would appear in the world.
Thereafter, he emitted a light named "The Pure Lamp of the Indestructible Realm of All Buddhas";
sentient beings who saw it knew that the Buddha’s sovereign power reaches everywhere, and they knew that in three thousand years, a Buddha would appear in the world.
Thereafter, he emitted a light named "Universal Illumination of the Sounds of the Original Deeds of All Buddhas of the Three Times.
Sentient beings who saw it came to know the immeasurable oceans of the past original deeds of all Tathāgatas, and they knew that in two thousand years, a Buddha would appear in the world.
Thereafter, he emitted a light named "The Pure Lamp of the Tathāgata Wisdom Free from the Obscuration of Delusion.

Any sentient beings who saw it attained the pure eye of equanimity, whereby they universally beheld all adorned and purified Buddha-fields, all Tathāgatas, and all sentient beings; they knew that in one thousand years, a Buddha would appear in the world.
Next, he emitted a light named "All Sentient Beings Beholding the Tathāgatas Cultivate Their Roots of Goodness";
those sentient beings who saw it knew that in seven days the Buddha would appear in the world.
Next, he emits a light named "Sound of Joy for All Sentient Beings";
those sentient beings who see it become single-mindedly joyful and desire to behold the Tathāgata.
“O Son of the Buddha!

During those ten thousand years, that Buddha emitted such immeasurable rays of light to transform sentient beings. When the seven days were completed, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, all worlds shook in six ways.”
At that time, in every moment of thought, sentient beings saw all Buddha-lands as entirely pure and adorned with various jewels.
Then, the sentient beings of that world all proceeded to the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa);
[they beheld] all the Diamond Ring Mountains, Sumeru the King of Mountains, all other mountains, all transformations, all sounds, the entire great earth, and all cities, walls, and palaces.
All such things as these produced subtle and wondrous sounds, singing praises and extolling the Buddha.
