Furthermore, they issued forth clouds of all kinds of incense, clouds of the radiance of all jewels, clouds of the forms of all jewels, clouds of all jewel garments, clouds of all flowers, clouds of all powdered incense, clouds of all jewel ornaments, clouds of the perfect light of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the voices of the great vows of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the sublime voices of all Tathāgatas, clouds of the various marks and signs of excellence of all Tathāgatas, and clouds manifesting the inconceivable auspicious omens of the Tathāgatas;
issuing forth all such wonderful clouds, they made offerings to the Tathāgata.

At that time, from the clouds of the adorned realms of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, which were surrounded by lotuses, there emerged as many precious lotus flowers as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds;
upon the filaments of each of those lotuses was a lion throne made of a treasury of precious lotuses;
and upon each of those lion thrones sat as many Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds.
"At that time, the Buddha Wondrous Virtue Banner, throughout all worlds, turned the pure wheel of Dharma according to what was appropriate for each;
he caused immeasurable sentient beings to leave behind the sufferings of the evil realms,
and immeasurable sentient beings to be reborn among humans and devas."
They established immeasurable sentient beings in the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
they established immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of courageous diligence;
they established immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of the Stainless Banner of Diligence.
They establish immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of the light of the Dharma;
they establish immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of the pure faculties;
they establish immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of the equal powers.
They established immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of single-mindedly seeking entry into the city of the True Dharma;
they established immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of sovereign mastery over indestructible spiritual powers that reach all places;
and they established immeasurable sentient beings in the bodhisattva practice of all skillful means.
They establish immeasurable sentient beings in the birth of bodhisattva samādhis and cause them to dwell securely in bodhi;
they establish immeasurable sentient beings in the cultivation of all pure practices and cause them to dwell securely in bodhi;
they establish immeasurable sentient beings in the arousal of the bodhicitta.
He established immeasurable sentient beings on the bodhisattva path;
he established immeasurable sentient beings in the purification of the various pāramitās;
he established immeasurable sentient beings in the first stage of the bodhisattvas.
He established immeasurable sentient beings in the ten stages of a bodhisattva;
he established immeasurable sentient beings in the sublime practices of the great vows of a bodhisattva;
and he established immeasurable sentient beings in the pure vows and conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because the Tathāgata turns the inconceivable wheel of sovereign Dharma;

in every thought-moment, according to what is appropriate for each, he delivers and liberates immeasurable sentient beings through various bodies, various skillful means, and various teachings of the Dharma.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, knowing that the sentient beings in the royal capital city of Ratnapuṣpadīpa were arrogant regarding their own physical appearance and looked down upon others, manifested a wondrous body of extraordinary and sublime beauty.
He proceeded to that city, emitting a great radiance that universally illuminated all things.

At that time, the bodily radiance of that holy king, the radiance of the various jewels, the radiance of the precious women, the radiance of the precious trees, and the radiance of the sun, moon, and stars were all completely eclipsed, appearing like a heap of ink;
likewise, the bodily color and radiance of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva eclipsed all those lights, just as a mountain of pure gold outshines them.
"At that time, sentient beings each had this thought:
'Now this radiance completely obscures us so that we no longer appear;
is this the light of Brahmā or of the various devas?'"
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Fifty-two;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Volume Fifty-three.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
In the tenth part of the "Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm," the thirty-fourth:
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was above the precious palace of that holy king, and from within the void, he addressed him, saying: "Great King!
"You should know that a Buddha has appeared in the world, now dwelling beneath the Bodhi tree named Banner of the Wondrous Sound of Universal Radiance.

At that time, those sentient beings, seeing the marks and signs adorning the body of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, his immeasurable radiance, and hearing his wondrous voice, were filled with boundless joy and made this vow:
"May the roots of goodness we have cultivated enable us to obtain such a wondrous body, adorned with marks and signs, with deportment no different [from his], and with sovereign spiritual powers."
To eliminate the ignorance and darkness of all sentient beings and awaken them all;
whenever a Buddha appears in the world and takes birth in every realm of existence, may I never be separated from this spiritual friend.

Then, that holy king, together with his precious queen, his retinue, his thousand sons, his ministers, and the fourfold army, ascended into the void and emitted a great radiance that illuminated the four continents. For the sake of all sentient beings, he spoke in verse:
"The Tathāgata has appeared in the world, Universally rescuing all living beings.
You all should quickly arise And go to where the Teacher dwells."
Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, there may be Buddhas who appear in the world,
expounding the profound and wondrous Dharma to benefit all beings.
Universally beholding all living creatures, [he sees them] deluded by ignorance and inverted views.
Circulating through the suffering of birth and death, He gives rise to great compassion for them.
Throughout immeasurable and innumerable kalpas, He cultivates the bodhisattva practices;
For the sake of transforming sentient beings, He initiates unsurpassed compassion.
Head, eyes, hands, feet, and the like— All that is difficult to relinquish, he was able to give away.
Throughout immeasurable and innumerable kalpas, He sought exclusively for the Bodhi of the Buddha.
In immeasurable and boundless kalpas, A Tathāgata is difficult to encounter.
For all who see or hear this, nothing shall be in vain. The Tathāgata,
at the site of enlightenment, seated upon the Buddha’s seat of true Dharma,
has subdued all Māras and attained supreme perfect awakening.
Observing the body of the Tathāgata, It radiates immeasurable light of various subtle and wondrous colors, Extinguishing all darkness.
From each and every pore, It emits inconceivable rays of light.
Dispelling the cataracts of ignorance, they caused all beings to rejoice.
Each prepared various offerings and, generating a mind of great diligence,
they all went to where the Tathāgata was and reverently presented their offerings.

At that time, after the Wheel-Turning Sage King had praised the Buddha, he raised ten kinds of clouds through the roots of goodness and merit of his sovereignty as a wheel-turner, which universally covered the void as he proceeded to the site of enlightenment to make offerings to the Tathāgata. These were:

clouds of all kinds of jewels, clouds of all kinds of flowers, clouds of all kinds of robes, clouds of all kinds of precious robes, clouds of all kinds of jewel-nets with golden bells, clouds of all kinds of solid fragrances, clouds of all kinds of wish-fulfilling gems, clouds of all kinds of exquisite jewel-banners, clouds of all kinds of jewel-palaces, and clouds of all kinds of adornments. Universally covering the entire adorned void, they made offerings to the Tathāgata as he approached the Buddha’s dwelling.
She prostrated with her head at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and withdrew to sit upon the seat of the Universal Radiance Jewel Treasury.
At that time, the girl Wondrous Virtue Eye removed all the ornaments from her body and scattered them as an offering to the Tathāgata.

At that time, the ornaments in the void transformed into a precious canopy, adorned with various jewels, equal in splendor to all the celestial palaces; it was upright, majestic, and orderly, embellished with ten kinds of jewels, and surrounded on all sides by the Diamond Ring Mountains.
Its form was like a bright and pure pavilion, adorned with myriad jewels, held up together by countless dragon kings, encircled by jewel trees, and permeated everywhere with exquisite fragrance.
Within that canopy, there was a Bodhi tree with flourishing branches and leaves, universally covering the entire Dharma-realm and adorned with immeasurable ornaments.

He saw Vairocana Buddha sitting beneath this tree, together with as many great bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields; all of them were fully endowed with every practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, abiding in the bodhisattva stages, such that none could destroy them.
Furthermore, they saw all the kings of every world surrounding the Tathāgata;
they also saw the sovereign spiritual power of those Buddhas;
and they saw the succession of all kalpas and the formation and destruction of worlds.
Furthermore, they saw all Buddhas appearing in the world one after another;
and they saw Samantabhadra Bodhisattva at the abodes of all Buddhas, reverently making offerings and teaching and transforming sentient beings.

Furthermore, within each of those worlds, he saw as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field, with various modes of abiding, various adornments, various purities, various eons, various Tathāgatas appearing in the world, various periods of the three times, various lands, various dharma-realms, various paths, various entries into the dharma-realm, various spaces, various sites of enlightenment, various Buddha-rays, various lion-thrones adorned by the Buddhas, various retinues of Tathāgatas, various skillful means of the Tathāgatas, various turnings of the wheel of Dharma, various sublime voices of the Tathāgatas speaking, various oceans of sounds speaking, and various clouds of sūtras.
At that time, having seen and heard this, the woman was filled with immeasurable joy.

Then, amidst the great assembly, the Buddha Wondrous Virtue Banner preached a sūtra titled "The Sublime Sound of the Dharma-Wheel of All Tathāgatas," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in ten buddha-worlds serving as its retinue.

At that time, having heard this sutra, the woman immediately attained ten thousand samādhis; her body and mind became supple and pliant, like one newly conceived in the womb, like a sentient being first receiving the retribution of superior karma, or like a sturdy and auspicious tree first sprouting from the ground.

They are: the samādhi of seeing all Buddhas of the present; the samādhi of universally illuminating all Buddha-fields; the samādhi of deeply entering the three periods of time; the samādhi of the sublime voice of all Tathāgatas turning the wheel of Dharma; the samādhi of knowing the ocean of vows of all Buddhas; the samādhi of extinguishing the suffering and affliction of birth and death for all sentient beings; the samādhi of extinguishing the darkness of ignorance of all sentient beings and fulfilling the adornment of great vows; the samādhi of extinguishing all sufferings of all sentient beings; the samādhi of causing all sentient beings to be fully endowed with happiness; the samādhi of teaching and transforming all sentient beings with a mind free from weariness; the samādhi of the unimpeded banner of all Bodhisattvas; and the samādhi of the Bodhisattva’s descent into the mother’s womb and its adornments.
He attained these and ten thousand other such samādhis; furthermore, he attained the samādhi of the pure mind,
the immovable mind, the joyful mind, the mind of right aspiration, the vast mind, the mind that accords with the instructions of spiritual friends,
the mind of profound *sarvajñatā*, the mind that follows the ocean of skillful means, and the mind of total non-attachment.
The mind that has abandoned all worldly spheres; the mind that reaches the ultimate sphere of the Tathāgata;
the mind that universally illumines the ocean of all forms; the mind that extinguishes anger; the mind of loving-kindness;
the mind of equanimity; the tireless mind; the non-retrogressive mind; the mind free from indolence; and the mind that contemplates the tranquility of all phenomena.
A mind that accords with the ocean of all phenomena; a mind that accords with the discernment of all phenomena;
a mind that discerns the ocean of all sentient beings; a mind that rescues and protects all sentient beings; a mind that universally illumines all worlds;
a mind that fulfills the ocean of great vows of all Buddhas; and a mind that shatters and disperses all mountains of obstacles.
A mind that accumulates mountains of immeasurable merit; a mind directed toward the ten powers of the Buddha;
a mind that universally illuminates all bodhisattva realms; a mind that nurtures all the virtues of all bodhisattvas;
a mind that fills the oceans of all ten directions; a mind that gives rise to equanimity; and a mind that brings to fulfillment as many buddha-fields as there are atoms.
The mind of the ocean of vows; the mind that purifies the lands of all Tathāgatas.
From such minds as these, there arise Dharma-gates as numerous as the atoms within ten Buddha-worlds, namely:
the Dharma-gate of teaching and transforming all sentient beings;
The dharma-gate of discerning all dharma-realms;
the dharma-gate of reaching the ultimate depths of the ocean of all dharmas;
and the dharma-gate of generating the practices of bodhisattvas throughout all worlds for as long as all future kalpas endure.
The dharma-gate of abiding in the bodhisattva practices throughout all worlds for as long as all future kalpas;
the dharma-gate of proceeding to the presence of all Buddhas;
and the dharma-gate of encountering all spiritual friends.
The dharma-door of reverently making offerings to all Buddha-dharmas;
the dharma-door of generating all-knowledge in every thought-moment without ceasing the practices of a bodhisattva;

and the generation of as many such dharma-doors as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds, giving rise to the vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva while single-mindedly seeking all-knowledge.
At that time, that woman attained the initial vows of aspiration of all Tathāgatas. "Good son!

Furthermore, ten great kalpas prior to this, there was a world named Sun-Disk Radiance, where the Buddha was named Indra-Supreme-Virtue-Banner. Because of the spiritual friend Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, this woman, Wondrous-Virtue-Eye, fashioned an image of Lotus-Tathāgata adorned with various jewels and gave rise to the bodhicitta."
"Good son! At that time, was the noble cakravartin king Vimalanetra-guṇa not someone else?
He is none other than the present Bodhisattva Maitreya."
At that time, the maiden Ratnāśrī, who had perfected her virtues, was the Night Goddess Śāntasvarā;
the maiden Ratnanetrā was my own self.

"Good son! Because I made offerings to the Tathāgata Wondrous Virtue Banner with these ornaments, I beheld the Buddha’s immeasurable and sovereign spiritual powers and heard him preach the True Dharma. Having heard the True Dharma, I immediately attained the Dharma-door for teaching and transforming all sentient beings. I reverently made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, and having heard the sūtras and teachings spoken by those Buddhas, I received and upheld them all. In a single thought-moment, I saw all those buddha-fields, as well as all the Tathāgatas and their assemblies of bodhisattvas."
“Good son! Thereafter, there was an eon named Great Radiance, and a world named Various Adornments, in which five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world; I reverently made offerings to them all.”
Among these Tathāgatas, the first Buddha was named Mahākāruṇikadhvaja; at that time, I was a night goddess and made offerings to him with reverence.
The next Tathāgata was named Vajranārāyaṇadhvaja; at that time, I was a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) and made offerings to him with reverence.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Sarvatathāgatagotrābhyudaya*, with as many auxiliary sūtras as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds.
Thereafter, there was a Tathāgata named Unobstructed Wondrous Virtue Abiding; at that time, I was a Cakravartin King and reverently made offerings to him.

That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled "Universally Illuminating the Faculties of All Sentient Beings," with as many sūtras as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru serving as its retinue, all of which I heard, received, and upheld.
Thereafter, there was a Tathāgata named Vimalajvālāguṇaparvatavyūha; at that time, I was a householder and made offerings to him with reverence.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Samantāvabhāsatriyadhātugarbha*, which had as many ancillary sūtras as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, all of which I heard, received, and upheld.
Thereafter, there was a Tathāgata named Sarvadharmanidhānasamudgatarāja. At that time, I was an asura and paid him respectful homage and offerings.
That Buddha preached a sūtra for me titled *Vibhaṅga-sarvadharmadhātu*, with five hundred sūtras as its retinue; I heard them all and received them into my keeping.
Thereafter, there was a Tathāgata named Gambhīradharmanayasāgaraprabha. At that time, I was a dragon girl; I rained down clouds of wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels as an offering of reverent worship.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Saṃvardhanaprītisāgara*, with a hundred trillion sūtras as its retinue, all of which I heard, received, and upheld.
After that, there was a Tathāgata named Ratnajvālāguṇaparvatapradīpa. At that time, I was a sea spirit, and I offered reverent worship by raining down clouds of various precious flowers.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra called the *Dharmadhātuprayogārṇava*, with as many auxiliary sūtras as there are atoms in a world-system; I heard them all and received and upheld them.

Subsequently, there was a Tathāgata named Guṇasāgaraprabhāparipūrṇasudarśana. At that time, I was a rishi dwelling in the Snowy Mountains together with sixty thousand other rishis; we went to visit that Buddha and made offerings of reverent respect by raining down clouds of precious flowers.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named *Dharmapradīpāsaṅga*, with sixty thousand sūtras as its retinue, all of which I heard, received, and upheld.

Subsequently, there was a Tathāgata named Vimalasudarśanaguṇagarbha. At that time, I was a terrestrial deity named Rātripratimaṇḍalārtha, and together with immeasurable deities, I went to that Buddha and made offerings of reverence, raining down clouds of all kinds of jewels, all kinds of jewel treasuries, and all kinds of ornaments.
That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *Sarvatathāgatajñānakośasamudgama*, with immeasurable sūtras as its retinue, which I heard in their entirety and received and upheld.
"O Son of the Buddha!
Thus, these five hundred Tathāgatas appeared in the world in succession; the last of these Buddhas was named Dharma-realm Space-Jeweled Mountain Sublime Virtue Lamp.
At that time, I was a courtesan named Good Mouth."
When that Buddha entered the city, I was in the air and praised the Tathāgata with one thousand verses.

At that time, from the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows of the World-Honored One, a great light was emitted called "Adornment Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm," which shone throughout the ten directions;
having shone, it entered my body, and I immediately attained the Dharma-door of the Non-retrogressive Treasury of Skillful Means of the Dharma Realm.
O Son of the Buddha!
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within such worlds, I have reverently made offerings to all the Buddhas who appeared in the world;
I have heard, received, and upheld all the true Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas, never forgetting a single word or a single flavor.
At each and every Buddha’s abode, they attain the pure Dharma-body of the profound Dharma-realm of the three periods of time;
with the light of omniscience, they universally illumine all things and embrace the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
In every thought-moment, they see immeasurable and boundless Buddhas and attain immeasurable and boundless light of pure wisdom that universally illumines all.
That which they had previously not attained and not realized—the conduct of Samantabhadra—they now fully accomplish and perfect. Why is this?
"Because it is said to be immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, the Night Goddess Maitrīyaśas, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
"Sudhana, listen attentively To this profound and difficult-to-see Dharma."
Universally illuminating the three periods of time, He discerns the profound realm of reality (*dharmadhātu*).
Just as I first resolved my mind, Solely seeking the unsurpassed path,
According to the Dharma-gates I have attained, Listen attentively as I now speak.
In the distant past, eons as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field,
there was at that time an eon named Vimalapūrṇa. At that time, there was a world named Vimalasubhatejodhvaja.
As numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, Tathāgatas appeared in the world.
The first Buddha was Citraguṇadhvaja; the second was Samantaprajñājvālā;
the third was Dharmadhvajaguṇasumeru; and the fourth was Siṃha Buddha.
The fifth was King of Tranquility; the sixth was named Eliminator of Evil;
the seventh was Accumulation of Merit; the eighth was Sumeru Mountain;
the ninth was Buddha Wondrous Virtue; and the tenth was Bright Pure Moon.
Thus these ten Tathāgatas appeared in the world at the beginning of that kalpa.
Following them, there were another ten Buddhas: first, Ākāśopāya;
second, Samantaprabha; third, Sarvadigvyavasthita.
The fourth was Guṇasāgara; the fifth, Anuttara; the sixth, Varapuṣpa; the seventh, Guṇabuddhi;
the eighth, Arciḥparvata; and the ninth, Padmabuddhi.
The tenth is the Transformation of the Dharma-realm; this is the twentieth.
First was King of the Radiant Banner, second was the Buddha Wisdom, third was the Buddha Meaning of Mind, and then Indramati.
The fifth was Buddha Wondrous Heaven; the sixth, King of Valor;
the seventh, Virtue of Wisdom; the eighth, Banner of Radiance;
the ninth Tathāgata was named Transcending All Worlds.
The tenth was Padmabuddha; this was the thirtieth.
The first was Arciṣmatparvata, the second Guṇasāgara, the third Dharmaprabhāsa, and the fourth Suvimalapadma.
The fifth is Sattvākṣa; the sixth is Gandhaprabha;
the seventh is Ratnagiriśrī; the eighth is Gandharvarāja;
the ninth is Vimalajñāna; and the tenth is Śāntavarṇa.
The first was Buddha Prabhāprajñā; the second, Ratnārcis;
the third, Gaganagunavyūha; the fourth, Laksanottama Buddha;
the fifth, Pūrṇaguṇaprabhāsa; and the sixth, Nārāyaṇa.
The seventh was Sumeru-vimala, the eighth Guṇa-ratna-cakra,
the ninth Abhedyarāja, and the tenth Ratnaparvata-buddha.
The first Buddha was Śālarāja, and the second was Guṇakara-garbha.
The third was King of Radiance; the fourth, Arising of Reality;
the fifth, Virtue of Light; the sixth, Virtue of Dhāraṇī;
the seventh, Profound Radiance; and the eighth, Buddha Sound of the Dharma Ocean.
The ninth was Sumeruketu, the Buddha Prabhāsamati; Ratnārcis Tathāgata was the tenth Buddha.
The first Buddha was Brahmarci, The second was Gaganasvara.
The third is Dharmadhātuprabha; the fourth is Paripūrṇaprabha;
the fifth is Vibhaktiprabha; the sixth is Prabhāketudhvaja;
the seventh is Gaganapradīpa; and the eighth is Sukhasudarśana.
The ninth is Vimalaprabhā, the Tathāgata of Wondrous Merit;
the tenth is Śāntaguṇa, the Tathāgata of Clouds of Great Compassion.
The first Buddha is Balaprabhājñāna, the second is Sattvābhimukha.
The third was Anuttarapuṇya, the fourth was Varalakṣmīprabha;
the fifth was Dharmodaya Buddha, the sixth was Vāyuvegavaralakṣmī;
the seventh was Śuddhadhvaja Buddha, and the eighth was Ratnacchattra Buddha.
The ninth was the Buddha Wondrous Virtue; the tenth was Universal Illumination of the Three Times.
The first Buddha was named Ocean of Vows; the second was Radiant Virtue;
the third was Diamond Body; the fourth was Sumeru Wondrous Virtue.
The fifth was Samyak-smṛti-buddha; the sixth, Dhvajendra-viśuddhaguṇa;
the seventh, Prajñā-pradīpa; the eighth, Amita-ratna;
the ninth was named Upāya; and the tenth, Viśuddha-dharmadhātu-buddha.
The tenth was named Dharma-Sea, Of Clear, Pure Wisdom and Wondrous Virtue.
The first Buddha was named Dharma-Jewel, The Wheel-Turning King of Merit;
The third was Merit-Cloud, And the fourth was Lamp of Forbearance.
The fifth was Śāntasvara, the sixth Śāntadhvaja,
the seventh Sattvapradīpa, the eighth Mahāpraṇidhāna Buddha,
the ninth Tathāgata named Abhedya-dhvaja-rāja.
The tenth was named Wisdom; the Buddha was Jvalanottamaśrī.
The first Buddha was named Dharma King; the second, Unobstructed Wisdom.
The third was Illuminator of the Ocean of Speech; the fourth, Wondrous Sound.
The fifth is Subhāṣitaghoṣa, the sixth is the Buddha Vaśavartin; the seventh is Sarvadiśāmabhimukha,
the eighth is Samacitta, and the ninth is the Tathāgata Anuttara.
The tenth was Svayambhū, the most excellent of those with noble and wondrous virtue.
All such Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru— those Tathāgatas I have all made offerings to.
Throughout eons as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field,
I have reverently made offerings to all the Tathāgatas who appeared; having attained this Dharma-gate,
I have practiced it for immeasurable eons until I realized this Dharma-gate.
Upon hearing and reflecting on this, Sudhana should quickly bring it to ultimate completion:
"O noble son! I know only this bodhisattva dharma-door for teaching and transforming sentient beings;..."

All these great Bodhisattvas have ultimately accomplished the infinite and boundless conduct of Bodhisattvas, all arising from the ocean of various natures; with various upright bodies and minds, they fulfill the ocean of sense-faculties, are endowed with all gateways of great vows, practice immeasurable gateways of samādhi, fully accomplish immeasurable spiritual powers, and cultivate immeasurable practices of wisdom, entering into various knowledges and the radiance of all dharmas to universally illumine everything.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?

"Good son! Not far from me here at this site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Silent Sound, seated upon a lion throne of precious banners and lotus treasuries, surrounded by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of asankhyeyas of devas."
“Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva practice and cultivates the bodhisattva path.

Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of the Night Goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā, circumambulated her countless times, and withdrew with a heart full of reverence.

At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the place where the night goddess Praśāntarutasvarā was, prostrated himself at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying:
"O Celestial Being!

I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Relying upon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), I study the bodhisattva conduct, enter the bodhisattva conduct, enter the stages of bodhisattva conduct, and abide in the stations of bodhisattva conduct;
I only pray that the devas will explain this for me.
At that time, the Night Goddess said to Sudhana:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Noble son! You are indeed able to seek the bodhisattva path by relying on spiritual friends. Noble son!"
"I have accomplished the Bodhisattva Dharma-gate of the Adornment of Immeasurable Joy.
He addressed [the deity], saying: "O Deva!"
What is the function of this dharma-gate?
What is its sphere of activity?
And what are its skillful means?
"What kind of practices does it entail? He replied, "Good son!
I am able to purify the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings;
I eliminate defilements and dust, never severing the mind of pure adornment;
I attain the firm mind of the non-retrogressive realm and the immovable mind.
A mind that decisively realizes the mountain of jewels of merit and is adorned with non-attachment;
a mind that constantly manifests to protect all sentient beings;
and a mind that never tires of beholding the ocean of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The mind of the pure bodhisattva’s power of uprightness;
the mind that universally illumines the ocean of all wisdom. Good son!

For the sake of sentient beings, I shall eliminate their grief and affliction, as well as their immeasurable sufferings, causing them to forever leave behind all evil forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects (*dharmas*). I shall eradicate for sentient beings the suffering of being separated from what is loved, the suffering of encountering what is hated, and all other evil causes and conditions; I shall destroy the great suffering of decay, the suffering of dwelling in birth and death, and the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, and despair, so that they may attain the unsurpassed bliss of the Tathāgata.

I shall protect and deliver all sentient beings in every city and village, enabling them to attain peace and happiness; I shall extensively preach the Dharma for them, instructing them to gradually seek the knowledge of all modes.
If he sees sentient beings dwelling in palaces and mansions with hearts attached to them, he preaches the Dharma for them to enable them to know the true nature of all phenomena;
if he sees sentient beings joyfully feasting and gathering with their parents and brothers, he preaches the Dharma for them to enable them to assemble together with the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;

if he sees sentient beings happily reunited with their wives and children, he preaches the Dharma for them to enable them to exhaust the ocean of craving and desire within birth and death, to be fully endowed with great compassion, and to view all things with equanimity.
If he sees sentient beings dwelling in royal palaces, he preaches the Dharma for them so that they may all attain the bliss of the noble ones;
if he sees sentient beings attached to sensory realms, he preaches the Dharma for them so that they may attain the profound realm of the Tathāgata;
if he sees sentient beings giving rise to anger, he preaches the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Tathāgata’s pāramitā of kṣānti (patience).
For those who are indolent, he expounds the true Dharma to enable them to attain the Bodhisattva’s pure *vīrya-pāramitā*;
for those with distracted minds, he expounds the true Dharma to enable them to attain the Tathāgata’s *dhyāna-pāramitā*;
for those who are deluded by error, he expounds the true Dharma to enable them to attain the *prajñā-pāramitā*.
For those attached to the three realms, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to transcend the three states of existence;
for those who delight in inferior teachings, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to fulfill their great vows for Bodhi;
for those seeking personal peace, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to possess great vows and benefit all beings.
For those with inferior resolve, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of power;
for those lacking wisdom, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of wisdom;
for those without form, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the Tathāgata’s pure form-body.
For those with fragile and brittle bodies, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to attain the unsurpassed, pure Dharma-body;
for those of unwholesome appearance, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to attain the Tathāgata’s pure and wondrous form;
for those who suffer and are distressed, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to attain the unsurpassed bliss of the Tathāgata.
For those who are impoverished, he expounds the True Dharma, causing them to attain the various pure treasuries of a bodhisattva;
for those in gardens and parks, he expounds the True Dharma, causing them to seek exclusively the wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas;
for those on the road, he expounds the True Dharma, causing them to attain the path to omniscience.
For those who are villagers, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to transcend the triple world;
for those who are of the nation, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to pass beyond the stages of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, and to abide in the stage of the Tathāgata;
for those who are in cities and walled towns, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to enter the city of the Dharma King and universally illumine all things.
For those situated in the intermediate corners, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the wisdom of equality throughout the three periods of time;
for those situated in the cardinal directions, he expounds the True Dharma to cause all-knowledge to be ever present before them as they contemplate all phenomena;
for those with excessive greed and desire, he expounds the True Dharma to lead them to contemplate impurity and extinguish their craving for birth and death.
For those with an abundance of hatred, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the ultimate ocean of great compassion;
for those with an abundance of delusion, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain wisdom and contemplate the ocean of all phenomena;

for those with equal proportions of the three poisons, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to discern the ocean of supreme vows, to leave behind the pleasures of birth and death, to extinguish the sufferings of birth and death, to manifest the Buddha’s True Dharma, not to cling to the five aggregates, and to constantly practice the sublime Dharma.
For those who are indolent, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the adornment of the supreme path;
for those who are arrogant, he expounds the True Dharma to cause them to contemplate the equality of all phenomena;
for those who are deceitful and crooked, he expounds the True Dharma to enable them to attain the pure and straightforward mind of a bodhisattva.

"Good son! By means of such immeasurable Dharma-gifts as these, I gather in sentient beings, extinguishing the sufferings of the evil realms and establishing them in the joys of devas and humans. Causing them to forever leave the triple world and be endowed with all merits, I transform and deliver them through various skillful means, with immeasurable joy."
"Furthermore, good son!

I constantly observe the various vows and practices, various purified bodies, various purified radiances, various flames of light, and various paths of the Bodhisattvas' great ocean; how they proceed toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and enter the ocean of various samādhis;
and how they manifest various sovereign spiritual powers."
They give birth to oceans of various wondrous sounds, various wondrously adorned bodies, and various skillful means for entering the ocean of Tathāgatas;
they travel to oceans of various Buddha-fields;
and they reach the ultimate depths of oceans of various Tathāgatas.
They deeply enter the various oceans of eloquence;
they universally illumine the various realms of the Tathāgatas;
and they accomplish the various oceans of wisdom.
They cross over the various oceans of samādhi-seals;
they dwell securely in the various gateways of playful mastery;
and through various gateways, they proceed toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
Adorning the space of the dharma-realm in various ways;
clouds of various adornments universally covering the void;
observing the oceans of various great assemblies.

From all lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions, at the abodes of all Tathāgatas, the bodhisattva retinues universally rained down clouds of various kinds of wondrous adornments; they all came together for this assembly, sat upon various adorned seats, deeply entered the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s skillful means, traversed the ocean of all dharmas, and crossed over the ocean of various wisdoms.
Having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy, equal to the power of the Buddha.
"Furthermore, noble son, the inconceivable,
pure form-body of Vairocana Buddha is adorned with the primary and secondary marks."
Having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.
Within every thought-moment, Vairocana Buddha emits light equal to the Dharma-realm, universally illuminating all oceans of the Dharma-realm;
having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.

In every thought-moment, Vairocana Buddha emits from each and every pore rays of light equal in number to the atoms of immeasurable Buddha-lands; each ray of light has as its retinue rays of light equal in number to the atoms of immeasurable Buddha-lands, universally illuminating all things and filling the Dharma-realm, extinguishing all the sufferings and afflictions of sentient beings.
Having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.

In every thought-moment, Vairocana Buddha emits from his crown and his two shoulders clouds of jewel-luminous mountains, as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields; they universally illuminate everything, filling the entire dharma-realm.
Having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.
From every single pore of Vairocana Buddha, clouds of fragrance as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields are emitted, universally perfuming all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions;
having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.
Within each and every mark of Vairocana Buddha, there emerge marks as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-lands, filling all oceans of worlds;
having seen this, I give rise to immeasurable joy.

From every single pore of Vairocana Buddha, there emerge clouds of sovereign power equal in number to the atoms within all buddha-fields, as well as the pure perfections beginning with the first aspiration for enlightenment, which adorn the various stages of the bodhisattvas;
having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.

From every single pore of Vairocana Buddha, in every moment of thought, there emerge bodies of dragon kings as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, so that those who see these dragon bodies may be transformed;

furthermore, there emerge bodies of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, so that those who see such bodies may be transformed.
Having seen this, I gave rise to immeasurable joy.

From each and every pore of Vairocana Buddha, there emerge clouds of bodies of Cakravartin kings, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, perfected with the seven treasures and possessing sovereign spiritual powers, filling the entire Dharma-realm;
because sentient beings receive transformation upon seeing those bodies, I, having seen this, give rise to immeasurable joy.

From every single pore of Vairocana Buddha, there emerge clouds of bodies of Brahmā kings, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. They emit pure Brahmā-sounds to preach the Dharma for sentient beings, so that those who see or hear them may be transformed.

Having seen this, in every thought-moment I give rise to immeasurable joy, which is equal to the *sarvajñatā* (omniscience) of the Dharma-realm. That which arises does not arise; that which is attained is not attained; that which is seen is not seen; that which enters does not enter; that which is delivered is not delivered; that which is fulfilled is not fulfilled; and that which is heard is not heard.
Why is this? Because they analytically understand the nature of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), and because they comprehend that all phenomena of the three periods of time are of a single nature.
O Son of the Buddha!
This Bodhisattva’s Dharma-gate of Adornment with Immeasurable Joy possesses such immeasurable realms as these.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This Dharma-gate is infinite and boundless, for it is the ocean of all dharmas through ultimate skillful means."
This Dharma-gate cannot diminish omniscience (*sarvajñā*), for the mind is indestructible;
this Dharma-gate cannot exhaust the deluded imaginings of sentient beings, for they are inexhaustible;
this Dharma-gate is the most profound realm of tranquil wisdom.
This dharma-gate is the most vast, for it is the realm of all Buddhas;
this dharma-gate cannot be destroyed, for it is that which is known by the wisdom of Bodhisattvas;
this dharma-gate is immeasurable and indestructible, for it fills the entire Dharma-realm.
This dharma-gate is the Universal Gate, for within a single characteristic it encompasses all powers of mastery;
this dharma-gate is the foremost dharma, for all dharmas are bodiless and their practice is non-dual;
this dharma-gate does not give rise to any dharmas, for they are all like illusions.
This Dharma-door is like lightning, for it gathers all the great vows of omniscience;
this Dharma-door is like a magical transformation, for it is skillfully able to transform the practices of bodhisattvas;
this Dharma-door is like the wheel of the great earth, for it benefits all sentient beings.
This Dharma-gate is like a great wheel of water, for it moistens sentient beings with vast compassion;
this Dharma-gate is like a great wheel of fire, for it dries up and exhausts the various cravings of sentient beings;
this Dharma-gate is like a great wheel of wind, for it establishes all sentient beings in *sarvajñā* (omniscience).
This Dharma-gate is like the great ocean, for it adorns all sentient beings with meritorious virtues;
this Dharma-gate is like Mount Sumeru, for it arises from the ocean of all merits;
this Dharma-gate is like a great city, for it is adorned by the streets and alleys of all dharmas.
This Dharma-gate is like space, for it is the sovereign, most unsurpassed state of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
this Dharma-gate is like a celebratory cloud, for it universally rains down the nectar-like Dharma upon sentient beings;
this Dharma-gate is like the bright sun, for it universally illumines all things and extinguishes the darkness of ignorance.
This Dharma-gate is like the full moon, for it fulfills the ocean of merit of sentient beings;
this Dharma-gate is suchness, for it reaches all things;
this Dharma-gate is like a reflection, for it is skillfully able to manifest in response to the retributions of various karmas.
This Dharma-gate is like an echo, for it preaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate;
this Dharma-gate is like a flash of lightning, for it illuminates and brings full knowledge according to what is appropriate;
this Dharma-gate is like the king of trees, for it bears the wondrous flowers of all Buddhas' merits and produces the fruit of omniscience.
This Dharma-gate is like a vajra, for no one in all the worlds can destroy it;
this Dharma-gate is like the king of wish-fulfilling jewels, for it gives rise to immeasurable powers of mastery;
this Dharma-gate is like a stainless jewel, for it discerns and knows all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
This Dharma-gate is like a precious banner, for it emits the sublime sounds of the wheel of Dharma of equality of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!
These various metaphors are not metaphors, yet they are used as metaphors.
At that time, Sudhana said to the night goddess Śāntamati,
"By practicing what dharmas does a bodhisattva attain this dharma-door? She replied:
“O Son of the Buddha!
Because Bodhisattvas practice ten sublime dharmas, they attain this Dharma-gate. What are these ten?
That is to say:
the Bodhisattva practices generosity, causing the ocean of all sentient beings to be entirely filled with joy;
he practices pure precepts, bringing to full completion the great ocean of the merits of all Buddhas.
Cultivating patience, one thoroughly understands the true nature of all phenomena;
cultivating diligence, one remains firm and non-regressive toward omniscience (*sarvajñā*);
cultivating meditative concentration, one eradicates the afflictions of all sentient beings.
They practice wisdom, discerning and understanding the ocean of all phenomena;
they practice skillful means and instruction, bringing the ocean of all sentient beings to maturity;
and they practice great vows, cultivating the conduct of a bodhisattva throughout all oceans of buddha-fields for as long as all future eons endure.
Cultivating the various powers, they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment in all lands within every moment of thought;
cultivating inexhaustible wisdom, they comprehend the phenomena of the three periods of time without any obstruction.
O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten sublime dharmas;

when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice these dharmas, give rise to these dharma-gates, attain these dharma-gates, purify these dharma-gates, and perfect these dharma-gates, they cause them to grow and expand, becoming indestructible.
Sudhana said, "Divine being,
how long has it been since you first resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in two buddha-fields, there was an eon named Universal Illumination Banner;”
To the east of this Lotus Treasury Adorned Ocean of Worlds, beyond ten oceans of worlds, there is an ocean of worlds named Stainless Array of Various Jewels.
Within that ocean of worlds, there is a world-system named Sound of the Vows and Light of All Buddhas;
within that world-system, there is a world named Stainless Light.

Adorned with golden splendor and embellished by clouds of every kind of jewel, its ground was composed of various gems, firm and immovable. Its form was like that of the King of All Fragrant and Wondrous Virtues; its adorned pavilions were entirely pure, and the celestial palaces of the devas filled their midst.

There is a royal capital there named Universal Fulfillment Wondrous Virtue Treasury King; there is a site of enlightenment there named Moonlight Adorned with All Jewels Treasury, where the Buddha named Non-retrogressive Dharma-realm Wondrous Sound attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, I was a bodhi-tree deity named Boundless Light Banner of Merit-Lamp. I beheld that Buddha as he attained equal and perfect enlightenment, manifesting immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers.
At that time, I resolved my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and in the presence of that Buddha, I attained a samādhi called Universally Illuminating the Ocean of the Buddha’s Merits.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there subsequently appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Dharma-Tree Merit Mountain (*Dharmavṛkṣaguṇaparvata*).

After that bodhi-tree goddess passed away, she was reborn in this very place as the Night Goddess of the Bodhi Tree, named Wondrous Virtue Wisdom Merit Radiance (*Sugandhamatiguṇaprabhā*). Hearing that Tathāgata turn the wheel of the true Dharma, she again attained immeasurable joy and the samādhi called Universally Illuminating All Realms (*Sarvaviṣayavyāpi-prabhāsvara-samādhi*).
Upon that site of enlightenment, there subsequently appeared in the world a Tathāgata named King of the Wondrous Sound of the Ocean of All Dharmas;
encountering that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called Accomplishing the Ground of All Dharmas.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there appeared in succession a Tathāgata who arose in the world, named Ratnārciḥpradīpadhvajarāja;
encountering that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called Sarvavibhakta-samantāvabhāsa-megha.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there appeared next a Tathāgata who arose in the world, named Guṇasumeruprabharāja;
encountering that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called Illuminating the Ocean of All Buddhas.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there appeared next a Tathāgata who arose in the world, named King of the Sublime Sound of the Dharma-Cloud;
encountering that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called Lamp of the Ocean of All Dharmas.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there next appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Wisdom Torch Pure Brightness Lamp King;
at that time, I was a celestial maiden who, encountering that Tathāgata, further attained a samādhi called Pure Brightness Lamp, which extinguishes the suffering of sentient beings.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there next appeared a Tathāgata in the world named Dharma-Vīrya-Dhvaja-Suvimala-Śrī;
encountering that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called the Universal Illumination Treasury of the Buddhas of the Three Times.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there next appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Dharmapradīpavīryajñānasiṃha.
Encountering that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called "Luminous Pure Wisdom," which universally illumines all things without any obstruction.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there next appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Jñānabalaśailendrarāja;
meeting that Tathāgata, he further attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating the Faculties, Conduct, and Actions of All Beings Throughout the Three Times."
“O Son of the Buddha!

In that world-system called Stainless Radiance Golden Adornment within the eon known as Universally Shining Banner, there appeared in succession as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in ten Buddha-worlds, arising in the world.”
At that time, whether I was a king of devas, a king of nāgas, a king of yakṣas, a king of gandharvas, a king of asuras, a king of garuḍas, a king of kinnaras, or a king of mahoragas;
or whether I was a king of humans, a Brahmā king, a man, a woman, a boy, or a girl—I encountered all those Tathāgatas, reverently making offerings to them;
and when those Buddhas preached the Dharma, I heard it all and received and upheld it.

In that Buddha-field, for as many eons as there are atoms in two Buddha-worlds, she cultivated the bodhisattva practices, undergoing births as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field. Finally, at the end of her life, she was born here in this Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean, within the Sahā world, as a night goddess of the site of enlightenment. There she encountered Tathāgata Krakucchanda and attained a samādhi called "Stainless Light of the King of All Fragrances.
Next, she encountered Tathāgata Kanakamuni and again attained a samādhi called "Universally Illuminating All Oceans of Lands in Accordance with Reality.
Next, she encountered Tathāgata Kāśyapa and again attained a samādhi called "Ocean of Wondrous Sounds," which discerns the ocean of sounds of all sentient beings.

Now, having again encountered Vairocana Buddha, seated beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment, he has attained equal and perfect awakening; in every thought-moment, he manifests an ocean of immeasurable sovereign powers and further attains the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the adornment of immeasurable joy.
Having attained this dharma-gate, they enter deeply into the ocean of skillful means within the dharma-realm, which is as vast as the atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable oceans of worlds.

By means of this ocean of skillful means within the dharma-realm, within every single atom of all buddha-fields—within each and every atom—they see worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakably unspeakable oceans of buddha-fields, as well as those Buddhas and the True Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas; they hear them all and receive and uphold them.

Furthermore, I see the Buddha Vairocana, in every thought-moment, in all worlds, sitting at the site of enlightenment and attaining perfect awakening; he manifests immeasurable powers of sovereign spiritual mastery, each power of which fills the ocean of the Dharma-realm. I go to each of those places where he preaches the True Dharma, and I hear, receive, and uphold it all.

Furthermore, he saw that from every single pore of all those Buddhas, oceans of transformation bodies emerged, filling the ocean of the Dharma-realm. They manifested various sovereign spiritual powers, turning the wheel of the True Dharma as appropriate for each being among the oceans of all Buddha-lands, the natures of all worlds, all worlds, all realms of existence, and all sentient beings.

By means of my diligence and the dharani of hearing and retaining, I am able to receive and uphold all [teachings], contemplate them with right mindfulness, know their flavor and their meaning, clarify the treasury of wisdom, and achieve perfect purity. I discern and understand the ocean of all dharmas, observe the equality of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, and give rise to all gates of expedient means.
From each and every expedient means, I produce clouds of all sutras;
from each and every cloud of sutras, I bring to fulfillment the ocean of all true dharmas.
Each ocean of dharmas encompasses all revolving dharmas;
each revolving dharma universally produces clouds of all sublime dharmas;
each cloud of dharmas gives rise to waves of all dharmas.
Each and every wave attains the ocean of all dharmas of joy;
each and every ocean of dharmas of joy gives birth to the ground of all merits;
each and every ground of merit gives birth to the ocean of all samādhis.
In each ocean of samādhi, one sees oceans of all Buddhas;
at each Buddha’s abode, one attains oceans of all radiances;

each ocean of radiance universally illumines the three periods of time, attaining the ground of perfect wisdom that shines throughout the ten directions, knowing the oceans of past practices of immeasurable Buddhas and illuminating the oceans of the infinite original deeds of all Buddhas.

They are able to give what is difficult to relinquish; they maintain immeasurable pure precepts; they practice immeasurable patience; they nurture the pure vigor of a bodhisattva; and they purify the immeasurable oceans of meditative concentration.
They thoroughly understand the ocean of the Tathāgata’s *prajñāpāramitā*; they universally illumine the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgata’s skillful means;
they thoroughly understand the Tathāgata’s perfection of the power of merit and wisdom that nurtures all; and they discern the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgata’s ocean of *jñānapāramitā*.
Samantaprabha Tathāgata universally illumines the immeasurable bodhisattva stages and immeasurable buddha-stages of the past, possessing sovereign power over spiritual transformations;

throughout immeasurable kalpas, he has cultivated and brought forth the purification of the immeasurable past bodhisattva stages of the buddhas, practiced the immeasurable past wisdom stages of the buddhas, and illuminated the various stages of wisdom of the immeasurable buddhas.

They know the continuous succession of roots of goodness of immeasurable Buddhas when they were bodhisattvas; they know the bodhisattva practices cultivated by immeasurable Buddhas throughout all oceans of kalpas and all oceans of Buddhas during their time as bodhisattvas;

and they know how immeasurable Buddhas, while acting as bodhisattvas, brought forth oceans of Buddha-fields, filling the Dharma-realm with immeasurable bodhisattva practices and teaching sentient beings through various gates of skillful means.
It universally illumines the oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions, manifesting sovereign power for the sake of all sentient beings;

it universally illumines the ground of the Tathāgatas’ omniscience, turning the pure wheel of Dharma, fully hearing and upholding all clouds of Dharma, and manifesting the immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas;

it universally illumines the oceans of marks, the oceans of practices, and the oceans of powers of all Buddhas, and in every thought-moment, it knows those Buddhas from their initial resolve until their final nirvana without remainder and the subsequent extinction of their bequeathed teachings.

"Good son! Regarding your question as to how much time has passed since I first resolved my mind [for enlightenment], it is as previously described: even up to my coming to be born in this realm to make offerings to Rocana Buddha—just as in this world I made offerings to Krakucchanda Buddha and so forth up to Rocana Buddha; likewise, making offerings to all future Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa is also thus;
and just as I have made offerings to the Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, making offerings to all future Buddhas in all worlds is also thus."
Furthermore, that world called Stainless Radiance Golden Adornment still exists today.
Therefore, noble son, you should cultivate this Dharma-gate with a single-minded focus.
At that time, the night goddess Śāntamati, wishing to clarify once more the meaning of this Dharma-gate, spoke in verse:
“Sudhana, listen attentively as I explain this Dharma-gate;
you should give rise to a heart of joy and cultivate it diligently to reach its ultimate fulfillment.”
Throughout oceans of immeasurable kalpas, They cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva;
With minds as pure as space, They enter the city of all-knowledge.
Hearing the Buddha-dharma of the three periods of time, They joyfully seek it with single-minded devotion.
In the presence of those Tathāgatas, I cultivated all manner of meritorious virtues.
I beheld the Buddhas of the past, revering and making offerings to them all;
hearing the Buddhas preach the True Dharma, my joy was immeasurable.
Having also fully and respectfully made offerings to their parents,
they single-mindedly delight in seeking exclusively to bring this Dharma-gate to ultimate completion.
For those who are old, sick, or impoverished, and for those whose faculties are incomplete—
I shall eliminate their suffering and distress, causing them all to attain peace and happiness.
Whether they face the perils of water, fire, officials, or bandits; the terrors of enemies;
or various dangers within the great ocean—I shall rescue and deliver them all.
Sentient beings, through their afflictions and karma, undergo various sufferings as retribution;
may you shatter the mountain of birth and death and rescue and protect all living creatures from the immeasurable, agonizing pains of all the evil realms.
The pains of birth, old age, sickness, and death— these I shall entirely eliminate.
For immeasurable kalpas, I vow to bring peace and security to all beings,
to constantly behold all Buddhas, and to extinguish the suffering of birth and death.
“Good son! I have only accomplished this Dharma-door of the Adornment of Immeasurable Joy;

as for the great Bodhisattvas who have deeply entered the ocean of Dharma, who discern all kalpas, and who well know the matters of the formation and destruction of all oceans of worlds—how could I possibly know or speak of their meritorious conduct?”
"Good son! Here in this place of enlightenment, within the assembly of the Tathāgata, there is a night goddess named Guṇakāraṇḍavyūhā-rakṣāpurī;
go to her and ask how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path."
At that time, Sudhana praised the Night Goddess Silent Sound with these verses:
"Following the instructions of my spiritual friend, I have come to the abode of the celestial goddess.
I behold her immeasurable, pure body, Resting serenely upon a throne of celestial jewels."
Grasping at false appearances and becoming stained by attachment to all phenomena,
ignorant sentient beings such as these are unable to know the realm.
As for the pure and wondrous form-body, all the hosts of devas—
Contemplating with earnest attention for immeasurable eons, his mind never grew weary or satisfied.
Having distanced himself from the five aggregates and being entirely free from attachment,
he transcended worldly doubts and manifested the power of mastery.
Untainted by internal or external phenomena, with an unimpeded and unmoving mind,
one possesses the clear and pure eye of wisdom, seeing the Buddha’s power of mastery.
The body is the treasury of the True Dharma, and the mind is unimpeded wisdom.
The light of the Buddha’s wisdom universally illuminates all sentient beings.
He analyzes and explains the activities of the mind, adorning all worlds;
knowing the intrinsic nature of mental activity, he manifests bodies equal in number to all living beings.
Knowing that the world is entirely like a dream, Understanding that the Buddha is like a flash of lightning,
And that all phenomena are like echoes, They cause the multitude to be free from attachment.
Moment by moment, they completely eliminate The delusions of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time.
Without grasping at the characteristics of the three periods of time, they are able to expound the Dharma.
Regarding the ocean of all buddha-fields, the ocean of all Buddhas,
and the ocean of immeasurable sentient beings, they practice the gateway of the Dharma without attachment.
Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in reverence at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and withdrew with a heart of respect.

At that time, Sudhana, maintaining right mindfulness and reflection, discerning with wisdom, and proceeding in accordance with the correct path, cultivated the vast body of realization and attained the Dharma-door of the Adornment of Infinite Joy; he then proceeded to the place where the night goddess Vimaladattā, who protects all cities, resided.

He saw that Night Goddess dwelling in a place that universally illumines all palaces and precious lion-thrones, surrounded by unspeakably many celestial retinues; her body appearing according to every direction, manifesting before the bodies of all sentient beings as their own forms—her body that is everywhere present before all sentient beings, her body that is unattached to all sentient beings, her body that is the very body of all sentient beings, her body that is the supreme body of all sentient beings, her body that accords with and teaches all sentient beings;

her body that travels through the ten directions, her body that reaches all ten directions, her body that is the ultimate Buddha-body, and her body that ultimately teaches and transforms all sentient beings.

Having seen this body, Sudhana was filled with immeasurable joy; he prostrated himself at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying: "O Devī!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva path to benefit sentient beings;
nor how, by means of the supreme methods of gathering, one should embrace sentient beings, accord with the deeds of the Tathāgata, and draw near to the Dharma King.
At that time, the night goddess addressed Sudhana, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
O Son of the Buddha!
For the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, you ask about the conduct of Bodhisattvas;

for the sake of adorning and purifying all Buddha-lands, making offerings to all Buddhas, abiding through all kalpas, rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, guarding the lineage of all Tathāgatas, and attaining the mind of equality throughout the ocean of all dharma-realms in the ten directions to fill them all completely.

Having heard and upheld all the wheels of Dharma turned by all Buddhas, and because they rain down the nectar-like Dharma according to what is appropriate for each, they inquire about the conduct of Bodhisattvas.
O Son of Good Family!
I have already accomplished the dharma-gate of the Sovereign Sound of Profound and Sublime Virtue;
therefore, O Son of the Buddha,
I am a supreme great Dharma-master, free from all obstructions.

Regarding all phenomena, their minds are without attachment; they discern the entire treasury of the Tathāgata’s teachings and abide in the great loving-kindness and great compassion of the Tathāgata.
They establish sentient beings in the bodhicitta, attain all benefits, do not abandon the bodhicitta, and nurture all roots of goodness.
He is the Great Teacher who tames and guides all sentient beings, for he establishes them upon the path to omniscience.
In all worlds, he is the bright and pure sun, for he illuminates the immeasurable roots of goodness of all sentient beings.

Observing all sentient beings with an impartial mind, never abandoning any sentient being, giving birth to and nurturing all roots of goodness and profound wisdom, contemplating the purity of the *jñeya* (objects of knowledge), severing all unwholesome karma, performing all wholesome deeds, rescuing and protecting sentient beings, manifesting all Buddha-worlds, practicing the purification of all fundamental undertakings, establishing pure roots of goodness for all sentient beings, causing them to encounter all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) who cannot be thwarted, and establishing all sentient beings in the true teaching of the Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha!

I always take the gift of Dharma as primary, giving birth to and nurturing all pure and white dharmas. My mind of omniscience is firm and immovable, like the Vajra-treasury, incapable of being destroyed;

my mind constantly relies upon the power of the Buddhas, the power of Māras, and the power of spiritual friends. My mind shatters the mountains of all fetters and karmic actions; my mind is able to single-mindedly seek omniscience, thereby fulfilling the dharma-gate of unimpeded pure dharmas and the knowledge of all modes.
O Son of the Buddha!
By means of such light of wisdom, I purify the immeasurable wholesome dharmas of all sentient beings and benefit them all.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!
I observe the dharma-realm through ten practices, accord with the dharma-realm, and encompass the dharma-realm.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
They know that the dharma-realm is immeasurable because their wisdom is immeasurable;
they know that the dharma-realm is immeasurable and boundless because they see all Tathāgatas;
they know that the Buddha-dharma-realm is immeasurable and boundless because they travel to all lands to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas.
They know that the dharma-realm has no boundaries, because they practice the bodhisattva conduct throughout all oceans of worlds;
they know that the dharma-realm is indestructible, because they possess the ultimate, unassailable, and perfect wisdom of the Tathāgata;
they know that the dharma-realm is the single wondrous voice of the Tathāgata, because there are no sentient beings who do not hear it.
They know that the dharma-realm is naturally pure in order to teach and transform all sentient beings and fulfill the vows of the Buddhas;
they know that the dharma-realm reaches everywhere among sentient beings in order to enter deeply into the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
and they know that the dharma-realm encompasses all adornments of the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, as they are sovereignly adorned.
Knowing that the roots of goodness of all-knowledge, which cannot be extinguished within the dharma-realm, fill the dharma-realm in order to cause all sentient beings to become completely pure.
O Son of the Buddha!
By means of these ten practices, I observe the dharma-realm, increase my roots of goodness, and know the wondrous and extraordinary realm of the Buddhas, which is inconceivable.
O Son of the Buddha!
Thus, with right mindfulness and reflection, I preach the Dharma for sentient beings by means of ten thousand dhāraṇīs; namely:

The *dhāraṇī* of perfect mastery over all phenomena, the *dhāraṇī* of upholding all phenomena, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect thunderous resonance of the clouds of all phenomena, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect arising and abiding of all Buddhas, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect wheel of the names of all Buddhas, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect exposition and analysis of the ocean of great vows of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect gathering of the ocean of all vehicles, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect lamp-treasury illuminating the ocean of the karma of all sentient beings, the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect valiant revolving-flow of all phenomena manifesting before one,
and the *dhāraṇī* of the perfect valor of omniscience— with these ten thousand *dhāraṇīs*, he expounds the Dharma for all sentient beings through detailed analysis.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifty-three;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifty-four.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
[The Thirty-fourth Chapter of the Entry into the Dharma Realm, Part Eleven] "Furthermore, Sons of the Buddha!
I may, for some sentient beings, teach the Dharma of the wisdom derived from hearing; or, for some sentient beings, I may teach the Dharma of the wisdom derived from reflection; or..."
For the sake of sentient beings, he teaches the Dharma of cultivating wisdom; or he speaks of a single existence, or of the ocean of all existences;
or he speaks of the ocean of a single Buddha, or of the ocean of the names of all Buddhas;
or he speaks of a single world-system, or of the ocean of all world-systems; or he speaks of the bestowing of a single prediction, or of the bestowing of all [predictions].
The ocean of records—some speak of the ocean of the retinue of a single Buddha, some speak of the ocean of the retinues of all Buddhas;
some speak of the wheel of Dharma of a single Buddha, some speak of the ocean of the wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas;
some speak of a single sūtra, some speak of the ocean of the sūtras of all Buddhas; or some speak of a single assembly, or speak of...
Within all oceans of assemblies, he may speak of the single mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), or speak of the ocean of all bodhicittas,
or speak of the Single Vehicle (*ekayāna*), or speak of the ocean of all vehicles.
"O Son of the Buddha!
By means of such immeasurable skillful expedients, for the sake of all sentient beings, you have expounded the ineffably ineffable Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha!"

I have deeply entered this indestructible dharma-realm and have fully realized the true Dharma of the Tathāgata; through the unsurpassed gift of Dharma, I gather in all sentient beings and shall practice the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva throughout all kalpas of the future.
O Son of the Buddha!
I have already accomplished this profound and wondrous dharma-gate of the Sovereign Sound of Virtue; in every thought-moment, I am able to nurture all dharma-gates, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
At that time, Sudhana said to the Night Goddess:
"How wonderful! O Devī!"
"This Dharma gate is most profound; how long has it been since you attained this Dharma gate?
He replied, "O Son of the Buddha!

In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system, there was an eon named Stainless Radiance (*vimalaprabhā*). At that time, there was a world named Dharma-realm Exquisite Virtue Cloud (*dharmadhātusuvimalamegha*), adorned with fragrant Mount Sumerus as numerous as the atoms in four continents.

From within the lotus, there issued forth the wondrous sounds of the vows of all Buddhas, arising from the pure karma of all sentient beings. It was composed of various jewels, shaped like a lotus, pure and stainless. It was surrounded on all sides by multitudes of exquisite jewel trees as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, and adorned with multitudes of exquisite jewel incenses as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.
There were worlds adorned with the four continents as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru; in each of these four continents, there were unspeakably unspeakable numbers of cities.
In that world, there is a set of four continents named Adorned Banner;
in those four continents, there is a royal capital city named Universal Jewel Flower Light;
outside that city, there is a site of enlightenment named Radiance of the Dharma King’s Palace.
Upon that site of enlightenment, there appeared as many Buddhas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru;
the first of these Buddhas was named King of the Radiance of the Thunderous Sound of the Dharma-Ocean.
At that time, there was a wheel-turning king named Vimalaprabha, who, in the presence of that Buddha, protected the true Dharma and heard and upheld the ocean of sūtras of the true Dharma.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, he left the household life to study the Way.

When the True Dharma was about to perish, during a great kalpa in which a degenerate kalpa had arisen, afflictions blazed fiercely and sentient beings were filled with rage; they fought one another with mutual hatred and poison. The assembly of bhikṣus turned their backs on merit and benefit, their hearts delighting in negligence; they constantly took pleasure in discourses on kings, bandits, women, nations, oceans, and worldly matters, finding enjoyment in such various kinds of talk.
At that time, the bhikṣu King had this thought:
"The Tathāgata, over immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, cultivated and gathered the sublime Dharma; how is it that these bhikṣus together seek to destroy it?"

That King-Bhikṣu immediately ascended into the void and emitted great clouds of light in immeasurable varieties of color, universally illuminating all worlds in the ten directions. He extinguished the afflictions of all sentient beings, established immeasurable beings in unsurpassed Bodhi, and further caused the True Dharma to flourish for sixty-five thousand years.
At that time, there was a bhikṣuṇī named Dharma-cakra-vikurvita-prabhā, who was the daughter of that Cakravartin king and had a retinue of one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs.

Upon seeing the miraculous manifestation of light of his father-king, the Bhikṣu, he immediately resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and attained the samādhi of the Lamp-Light of All Buddhas, as well as the Dharma-gate of the Sovereign Sound of Profound and Sublime Virtue.

Having attained these, his body and mind became supple; through the sovereign spiritual power of the Buddha King of the Thunderous Sound of the Ocean of Dharma and Light, all merits were fully manifested before him.
“O Son of the Buddha!
At that time, was the Universal Monarch who followed that Tathāgata to turn the wheel of the true Dharma and cause the Dharma to flourish anyone else?
It was none other than the present Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra.”
The bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakrapravartanaprabhā was none other than myself.
At that time, I protected the Buddha-dharma and established a community of one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs who attained the stage of non-retrogression;

furthermore, I caused them to grasp all the Tathāgatas' dharma-gates and samādhis, such as the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Dharma-Wheel, and I further established for them the skillful means and the Prajñāpāramitā for entering the ocean of all dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha!
Next, there appeared a Tathāgata in the world named Vimaladharmaparvata, whom I encountered;
next, there was a Tathāgata named Dharmapūrṇaprabhācūḍa.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharmanidhāna-suvimala-guṇamegha;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharmasāgara-vibhaṅga-svararāja;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharmadivākara-paripūrṇapradīpa.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-transformation Banner Cloud;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-flame Mountain Banner King;
next there was a Tathāgata named Profound Dharma Sublime Virtue Moon.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Wisdom Universal Radiance Treasury;
next there was a Tathāgata named Awakening Sentient Beings through the Sphere of Universal Wisdom;
next there was a Tathāgata named Wondrous Virtue Mountain King.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Gate Samantabhadra Sumeru Mountain;
next there was a Tathāgata named Banner of Diligence in All Dharmas;
next there was a Tathāgata named Jewel Flower Sublime Virtue Cloud.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Śānta-gambhīra-prabhā-keśarāja;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-jvālā-mahāmaitrī-prabhā-candra;
next there was a Tathāgata named Arciṣmat-suśīla-sāgara.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Wisdom Sun Universally Illuminating All;
next there was a Tathāgata named Perfect Universal Wisdom;
next there was a Tathāgata named Supreme Wisdom Enlightenment Radiant King.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Guṇajvālāpuṣpadīpa;
next there was a Tathāgata named Prajñāsiṃhadhvajarāja;
next there was a Tathāgata named Samantādityaprabharāja.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Sumeru-Phase Adornment;
next there was a Tathāgata named Valiant Sun Universal Radiance;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Network Awakened Wondrous Virtue Moon.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-padma-vyūha-sukhaguṇa-manojña-ghoṣa;
next there was a Tathāgata named Lakṣaṇa-divākara-samanta-prabhāsa;
next there was a Tathāgata named Samanta-prabha-sugata-saddharma-ghoṣa.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Fearless Wondrous Virtue Nārasiṃha;
next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Wisdom Resolute Banner;
next there was a Tathāgata named Body of the Spread Dharma Lotus.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Guṇakusuma-sudharmasāgara;
next there was a Tathāgata named Bodhimaṇḍa-bodhisudharma-candra;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharmolkā-sudharma-candra.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Radiance Crest;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma Banner Lamp;
next there was a Tathāgata named Wondrous Virtue Ocean Banner Cloud.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Renowned Mountain Wondrous Virtue Cloud;
next there was a Tathāgata named Sandalwood Wondrous Virtue Moon;
next there was a Tathāgata named Radiant and Pure Universal Wondrous Virtue Flower.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Illumination King of Sentient Beings;
next there was a Tathāgata named Wondrous Merit Treasury of Padma Flowers;
next there was a Tathāgata named Fragrant Flame Radiance King.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Padmahetu;
next there was a Tathāgata named Vimalalakṣaṇaparvata;
next there was a Tathāgata named Samantaguṇakīrtidhvaja.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Gate Radiance Sumeru;
next there was a Tathāgata named Wondrous Virtue Dharma-City Radiance; next there was a Tathāgata named Bright and Pure Mountain of Merit;
next there was a Tathāgata named Supreme Mark Wondrous Virtue.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-power Valiant Banner;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-wheel Radiance Wondrous Sound;
next there was a Tathāgata named Merit-flame Pavilion Wisdom-light.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Anuttara-dharmacakra-candraprabha;
next there was a Tathāgata named Vimala-dharma-padma-bodhidhvaja;
next there was a Tathāgata named Ratna-padma-prabhā-kośa.
