Next there was a Tathāgata named Ratnaśikhicandrapradīpa;
next there was a Tathāgata named Jñānabodhikusuma;
next there was a Tathāgata named Citrārciḥsutejaḥsumerugarbha.
Next there was a Tathāgata named King of Perfect Radiance and Wondrous Virtue;
next there was a Tathāgata named Adorned Light of Clouds of Merit;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Mountain Cloud Banner.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Radiance Pure Merit Mountain;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Sun Cloud Lamp King;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Cloud Renowned Sovereign King.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharmapūrṇamegha;
next there was a Tathāgata named Suprabodhaviśuddhajñānadhvaja;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharmapūrṇasuprabodhasudharmacandra.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Golden Mountain Worthy;
next there was a Tathāgata named Radiant Pure Worthy Sublime Virtue Sumeru Mountain;
next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Wisdom Cloud Sublime Sound.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-power Wondrous Virtue Pavilion;
next there was a Tathāgata named Fragrant Flame Wondrous Virtue King;
next there was a Tathāgata named Golden Maṇi Mountain Wondrous Sound.
Next there was a Tathāgata named White Tuft Treasury of All Dharmas Perfect Radiance;
next there was a Tathāgata named Bright and Pure Wheel of Dharma;
next there was a Tathāgata named Unsurpassed Pure Mountain of Śīla.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Universal Vigor Torch-Illuminating Cloud;
next there was a Tathāgata named Vast Samādhi Ocean Celestial Crown Radiance;
next there was a Tathāgata named Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue King.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Torch Jewel Canopy Wondrous Sound;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Cloud Void Radiance Lion;
next there was a Tathāgata named Marks-and-Minor-Marks Adorned Banner Moon.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Flame-Mountain-Electricity-Cloud;
next there was a Tathāgata named Unobstructed-Space-Dharma-Light;
next there was a Tathāgata named Joyful-Wisdom-Blossom.
Next there was a Tathāgata named World-Ruler Radiance Wondrous Sound;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Samādhi Radiance Wondrous Voice;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Sound True Treasure-Treasury.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-Radiance-Flame-Splendid-Voice-Ocean;
next there was a Tathāgata named Banner of Signs Universally Illumining the Three Times;
next there was a Tathāgata named Mountain Radiance of Perfect Dharma.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-realm Lion Radiance;
next there was a Tathāgata named Dharma-realm Lion Flame;
next there was a Tathāgata named Luminous Pure Sublime Virtue Sumeru Mountain.
Next there was a Tathāgata named Lion of the Ocean of All Samādhis;
next there was a Tathāgata named Lamp of Universal Wisdom Light.
O Son of the Buddha!

Within the eon called Stainless Radiance, as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru appeared in the world; the last of these Buddhas was named Lamp of Pure Wisdom of the Dharma-realm City.
I have reverently made offerings to all those Tathāgatas, heard and upheld their Dharma, left the household life to study the Way, and protected the Buddha-dharma;

under those Buddhas, through various skillful means, I entered this profound and wondrous Dharma-door of Sovereign Sound of Virtue, and by means of various skillful means, I transform the ocean of sentient beings.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, there have been Buddhas appearing in the world, all of whom I have likewise reverently honored and made offerings to.
Therefore, O Son of the Buddha!

All sentient beings sleep forever within birth and death; I alone have awakened, and I am further able to awaken all sentient beings, guarding the city of the mind, departing from the city of the triple world, and entering the unsurpassed city of the Dharma of all-knowledge.

"Good son! I have only accomplished this profound and wondrous Dharma-door of Sovereign Sound of Virtue, which extinguishes the verbal transgression of double-tongued speech among sentient beings and causes them to purify their truthful words."

These great Bodhisattvas have definitively mastered the paths of all sentient beings' languages; in a single thought-moment, they awaken to the minds of all sentient beings. They enter deeply into the ocean of the sounds and languages of sentient beings, skillfully knowing the linguistic conventions established by them. They discern and understand the ocean of all phenomena, entering deeply to grasp the ocean of *dhāraṇīs* of all dharmas.

Through skillful means, they bring forth clouds of all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings, ultimately delivering all sentient beings. They gather in sentient beings, establish unsurpassed karma, and accord with pure wisdom. Discerning the treasury of karma, they are able to roar the lion’s roar, bestow the gift of Dharma upon all, attain the stages of all dharmas, and perfect the *dhāraṇīs*.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Good son, within this assembly of the Buddha, there is a night goddess named Puspakūṭa (Flower-Blossoming Tree).
"Go to him and ask: How does a bodhisattva train in all-knowledge and establish sentient beings in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*)?
At that time, the Night Goddess Guptasarā, wishing to further clarify the meaning of this Dharma-gate, spoke in verse:
"The profound Dharma-gate of the Buddha’s son, The nature of space and suchness,"
Discerning the Buddhas of the three periods of time, And the immeasurable realms of phenomena;
Giving rise to infinite gateways, And inconceivable dharmas;
Nurturing unimpeded wisdom, One thoroughly understands the dharmas of the three periods of time.
After passing through kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, there was a kalpa named Vimalaprabhā;
the world was named Suvimalagunamegha, and its city was named Ratnakusumaprabhā.
In that kalpa, there appeared Buddhas in succession, as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru.
The first Buddha was named Dharma-Ocean, King of Thunderous Sound and Radiance;
The latter Buddha was Dharma-Domain City, Lamp of Pure and Clear Wisdom.
I made offerings to them all, And hearing the Dharma, I rejoiced greatly.
He beheld the Tathāgata King of Radiance, Dharma-Ocean Thunder-Sound,
adorned with myriad wondrous marks like Mount Sumeru.
Upon seeing the Buddha, he immediately resolved his mind, single-mindedly seeking all-knowledge.
The mind is as vast as space, its nature identical to suchness.
It pervades the three periods of time; the assembly of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, with their great compassionate heart, universally covers all sentient beings in every land.
The pure and wondrous Dharma-body pervades all Buddha-fields;
according to those who are to be transformed, it manifests its body for them all.
When I first resolved my mind, I caused all lands to tremble.
He transformed all living beings, causing them all to rejoice greatly.
Next he encountered the second Buddha; hearing the Dharma, he made offerings and immediately beheld Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within ten oceans of lands.
In this manner, meeting Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru in succession,
he reverently made offerings to all those Tathāgatas.
Hearing the Dharma, he received and upheld it all, and thereby attained this Dharma-gate.
Universally delivering all sentient beings, may they ultimately reach the other shore.
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, whenever Buddhas arise in the world,
may I go to them all, reverently making offerings.
"Hearing the Dharma, I receive and uphold it all; I purify this Dharma-gate.

At that time, Sudhana attained this profound and wondrous Dharma-gate of Sovereign Sound of Virtue, entered the ocean of the infinite and boundless samādhis of bodhisattvas, gave birth to the ocean of infinite and boundless dhāraṇīs, obtained the brilliant radiance of the supernormal powers and insights of bodhisattvas, entered the ocean of eloquence, and nurtured the ocean of all profound Dharmas.
Desiring to praise the Night Goddess Guarding the City of Wondrous Virtue, he spoke in verse:
The ocean of wisdom is fully perfected, forever crossing the sea of birth and death;
the treasury of long life and wisdom shines universally throughout the ten directions.
Having thoroughly realized all internal and external phenomena, they are seen to be entirely like empty space.
With unimpeded and pure wisdom, they have reached the ultimate realization of the three periods of time.
In every thought-moment, they are able to discern all infinite and boundless realms, yet their minds remain free from attachment.
With a mind of immeasurable great compassion, they deliver the ocean of sentient beings;
with the clear and pure eye of wisdom, they realize that sentient beings have no inherent nature.
They enter deeply into the ocean of the Buddha-dharma, exhausting its very source and bottom.
Through various skillful means, they transform and deliver all living beings.
Universally regarding all phenomena, they thoroughly comprehend their true nature;
practicing for omniscience (*sarvajñā*), they cause all multitudes to become completely pure.
The Celestial One is the Teacher who Subdues, Having exhausted all-encompassing wisdom,
He fills the entire Dharma-realm, Expounding the Dharma to transform sentient beings.
In accordance with the vows of Vairocana, He delivers sentient beings without obstruction.
Abiding securely on the path to the ultimate destination, they see the Buddhas of the ten directions everywhere.
The celestial mind is profoundly subtle; it extinguishes the fever of afflictions, is pure like space, and is free from defilement and attachment.
Encompassing the three periods of time, all the Tathāgatas of the Buddha-fields,
the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas, and all classes of living beings—
[the Buddha] discerns and knows them all in a single thought-moment, within a kṣaṇa and a lava.
Day and night, for half-months, and even throughout immeasurable eons,
[he] knows the deaths and births of all beings in the ten directions— those with form and those without form, those with perception and those without perception, and so forth.
Eliminating all the false and inverted perceptions of the multitudes,
Skillfully knowing the laws of speech, he manifests the path to Bodhi.
Emerging from the vows of Vairocana, he reveals the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas.
"With unimpeded dharma-body and mind, you manifest before sentient beings according to their needs.
Then, having praised that Night Goddess with these verses, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and withdrew with a heart of reverence.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, reflecting with right mindfulness upon the Dharma-door of the Sovereign Sound of Profound and Wondrous Virtue’s Expansion, went to where the night goddess Kiṃśukrapuṣpābhijñā was.
He saw that night goddess within a pavilion of various precious fragrant trees, seated upon a lion Dharma-throne made of the sprouts of jewel-trees, surrounded by a retinue of a million devas.

At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times with palms joined in reverence, and standing to one side, addressed her, saying: "O Devī!"
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; how should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva practice, cultivate the bodhisattva path, and proceed toward *sarvajñā*?
"I only pray that the celestial deity will explain this for me. He replied,
"O son of good family!
When the sun sets, my *utpala* and *padma* flowers all close;
when the crowds of people who have been wandering through the gardens and viewing the sights abandon their indulgence and return to their homes, I emit light for them;
and for those on perilous paths, I illuminate the level road, causing them to single-mindedly seek the path to omniscience.

If they are in mountain crags, deep waters, or vast wildernesses—in such various places of hardship—he emits light everywhere to cause them to escape all suffering and attain peaceful, secure happiness.
Furthermore, good son!

If there are sentient beings who are negligent regarding the five desires, he manifests for them the sufferings of old age, sickness, and death, causing them all to behold these and abandon negligence while cultivating roots of goodness;
for those who are stingy and greedy, he praises generosity.
If there are those who violate the precepts, he establishes them in pure morality;
for those who harbor malice, he praises great compassion and establishes them in patience;
and for those who are indolent, he instructs them to practice the diligence of a bodhisattva.
If there are those with distracted minds, he teaches them to practice the various dhyānas and samādhis;
if there are those who are ignorant, he causes them to enter deeply into the Prajñāpāramitā;
and for those who delight in inferior teachings, he instructs them in the Mahāyāna.
For those attached to the three realms, he causes them to abide in the bodhisattva’s perfect and unattached *pāramitās*;
for those sentient beings whose merit is weak and who are oppressed by various fetters and karmic actions, he causes them to abide in the bodhisattva’s *bala-pāramitā*;
for those who follow ignorance, he causes them to abide in the bodhisattva’s *jñāna-pāramitā*, so that they may abandon the darkness of delusion.
"Good son! I have already accomplished the dharma-gate of the light of immeasurable joy and contentment. Sudhana said:
“Devaputra! What is the sphere of this dharma-gate? He replied:
“Good son! The Tathāgata’s light of skillful means gathers in and sustains sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!

If there are sentient beings who experience happiness, they all receive it through the power of the Buddha and the power of his various radiances; by following the Tathāgata’s teachings and the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power;
by acceding to the Buddha-way, hearing the Buddha’s true Dharma, and entering the Buddha’s roots of goodness;

and because the Tathāgata’s perfect, bright, and pure sun of wisdom, as well as the Tathāgata’s inherently pure karmic power, universally illumines all, and by virtue of receiving such powers of merit, they cause all sentient beings everywhere to experience all forms of happiness.
O Son of the Buddha!

When I entered this dharma-gate, through right mindfulness and contemplation, I deeply penetrated the ocean of bodhisattva practices performed in the past by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana.

"Good son! When I know that a bodhisattva has first resolved upon the mind of the bodhisattva stages, I see all sentient beings attached to 'self' and 'what belongs to self,' shrouded by ignorance, entering into various false views, following along with craving and attachment, bound by desire and anger, their minds distracted and inverted, entangled by stinginess and jealousy, oppressed by poverty, undergoing manifold sufferings within birth and death, and failing to encounter the Buddhas."

Having seen this, he gives rise to a heart of great compassion, gathering in sentient beings, removing their various sufferings and afflictions, and universally benefiting them so that they may attain a mind free from all attachment;
regarding all things given, he does not seek karmic retribution, and he thoroughly understands all causes and conditions and the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena;
he fully accomplishes great kindness and great compassion, perfects the canopy of the Dharma, and universally covers all sentient beings.

By means of the dharma of contentment, one nurtures the elephant of wisdom, shatters all mountains of affliction, and brings peace and happiness to sentient beings; according to their needs for transformation, one rains down the nectar-like Dharma.

Bestowing the benefits of the noble Dharma equally upon all beings, one attains the unsurpassed bliss that is the fruit of the ten powers, achieves the sovereign mastery of the bodhisattva’s supernormal powers, and fills the entire Dharma-realm.

They manifest before all sentient beings, raining down all manner of things to bring them universal joy and satisfy their every wish. They rescue and protect sentient beings, extinguishing the suffering of birth and death without seeking any reward for their kindness. They purify the jewel-like minds of all sentient beings, making them identical to the roots of goodness of all Buddhas. They increase *sarvajñā* (omniscience), teaching and maturing all sentient beings, and purifying all Buddha-fields with the unsurpassed pure Dharma.
In every moment of thought, they fill the entire dharma-realm;
with luminous and pure wisdom, they discern the three periods of time, pervading all of space;

at all times, they turn the pure wheel of Dharma to teach and transform sentient beings, causing them to give birth to all-encompassing wisdom, purify all dhāraṇīs, awaken to the bodhi of all Buddhas, and discern all future kalpas.
Throughout all eons, they practice the conduct of a bodhisattva with a mind free from duality;
they are able to travel everywhere throughout all worlds, their bodies encompassing the entire ocean of lands, and they fully embrace all worlds within themselves.
One analytically explains all world-systems— their various forms and colors, their various adornments,

and their various modes of abiding; whether they are impure or pure, pure or impure, purely clean or purely defiled, vast or narrow, great or small, inverted or upright— and within such oceans of world-systems,
one generates the conduct of a bodhisattva and realizes the conduct of a bodhisattva.

In every thought-moment, they give rise to the various sovereign practices of Bodhisattvas; in every thought-moment, they manifest for sentient beings the pure Dharma-body of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha!

In past ages, when Vairocana Buddha was practicing the bodhisattva path, he saw that all living beings lacked the merit of wisdom; they were shrouded by ignorance, attached to the self and what belongs to the self, obscured by the veil of nescience, and engaged in improper reflection.
They enter into various false views and fail to recognize cause and effect;
they follow the karma of afflictions and do not cultivate the Noble Path;
having attained a state of non-action, they constantly wander through the perilous paths of birth and death, undergoing all manner of suffering.
They give rise to great compassion, causing all sentient beings to produce the immeasurable practices of a bodhisattva and cultivate all the pāramitās;
they establish firm and sublime roots of goodness, eliminate all sufferings, and expand the treasury of merit;
they thoroughly understand cause and effect, do not contradict the retribution of karma, and know the reality of all phenomena.

They fully discern and know the inclinations and desires of sentient beings as well as all buddha-fields; they protect and uphold all Buddha-dharmas so that they are never interrupted, extinguish unwholesome dharmas, and fulfill omniscience (*sarvajñā*).
O Son of the Buddha!

By means of such immeasurable gifts of Dharma, you gather in sentient beings, causing them to seek exclusively the dharma of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), to practice the various *pāramitās* of a bodhisattva;
to possess the benefits of the noble ones, to increase *sarvajñā*, to fulfill the ocean of roots of goodness, and to manifest the immeasurable sovereignty of the Tathāgata.

By means of such various skillful methods, they gather in sentient beings, manifesting the immeasurable merits of the Tathāgata, and establishing sentient beings in the wisdom of the bodhisattva's various means of gathering.
Sudhana said: "O Deva!
How long has it been since you first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?"
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!
This matter is difficult to know, difficult to believe, difficult to enter, difficult to explain, and difficult to attain."
This is unknown to all devas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas, except through the Buddha’s spiritual power.
By relying on a virtuous friend, one brings good roots to fulfillment, purifies the upright mind, remains far removed from flattery and crookedness, and extinguishes all defilements.

One attains the illuminating light of universal wisdom, takes pity on sentient beings, subdues all māras, and uproots the tree of afflictions. With the resolve to surely achieve all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), one eliminates the ocean of birth-and-death, grief, lamentation, and distress; attains the bliss of the Tathāgata, enters the ocean of the Buddha’s merit and vigor, dwells securely in the stage of a Buddha, fulfills the Tathāgata’s power of all-knowledge, and reaches the ultimate ten powers.
Such persons as these are able to believe and understand, able to know, able to enter, able to explain, and able to attain. Why is this?

This realm of the Buddha cannot be known by any sentient beings or even by all the bodhisattvas; yet, relying upon the Buddha’s spiritual power, for the sake of taming sentient beings, with a straightforward and pure mind, having extensively cultivated roots of goodness and attained a profoundly deep mind, and delighting in hearing this Dharma—for such individuals as these, I shall provide detailed explanations according to their respective capacities.
At that time, the Night Goddess, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, contemplated the realm of the Buddhas of the three periods of time and spoke in verse:
"O Son of the Buddha, this Dharma gate Is the profound realm of the Buddhas;
Even in inconceivable eons as numerous as the atoms of lands, One could not exhaustively describe it."
Those possessed by greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as those arrogant beings,
are all unable to know the most supreme and quiescent Dharma.
Those whose minds are stingy, envious, and crooked, and who are shrouded by afflictions and karma— [cannot know it].
None can know the profound realm of the Buddha; Attached to the aggregates,
sense bases, and elements, And giving rise to the view of a self,
With thoughts and views that are inverted, They do not know the Dharma of the Buddha’s realm.
Pure and free from delusion, the profound realm of the Tathāgata cannot be known by those who dwell within the cycle of birth and death;
yet for those born into the family of the Tathāgatas, all Buddhas constantly provide protection.
Upholding the treasury of the Buddha’s Dharma, the realm of the eye of wisdom;
drawing near to spiritual friends, fulfilling pure and white dharmas;
reaching the ultimate power of all Buddhas—one hears this Dharma and rejoices.
With a pure mind free from delusion, like the nature of empty space,
the lamp of wisdom dispels the darkness of ignorance— this is their realm.
With a heart of great compassion, they universally cover all sentient beings.
Observing all with an impartial mind—this is their sphere of activity.
Their minds are filled with great joy as they impartially observe the various classes of sentient beings;
having relinquished all attachments, they abide in the stainless sphere.
With a pure mind, one leaves all evils behind; Fearing even the slightest transgression, one follows the teachings of all Buddhas, Abiding in the realm free from defilement.
Dwelling securely in the dharma of patience, One’s mind cannot be shaken.
In accordance with reality, not contradicting karma, The realm of the inexhaustible mind.
With courageous and diligent vigor, Abiding securely in a non-regressive mind,
One reaches the ultimate *sarvajñā* (omniscience), The realm of subduing [all afflictions].
Entering the mind of tranquil meditative absorption, he extinguishes the heat of afflictions;
deeply entering the ocean of wisdom, he gives rise to the realm of stillness.
He thoroughly understands the various classes of sentient beings and the true nature of all phenomena.
The realm of the profound Dharma is the dharma-gate of the lamp of wisdom.
Awakening the nature of sentient beings so they do not cling to the ocean of existence,
and universally illuminating all minds— this is the dharma-gate of the Teacher.
All arise from the Buddhas of the three periods of time, born of the nature of pure vows;
throughout all lands, until the end of future kalpas,
they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva— this is the Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra.
Entering the ocean of all skillful means, Universally observing the ocean of all lands,
With unimpeded and profound wisdom, They fully know the formation and destruction of lands.
Within every single atom, they see All Buddhas seated at the site of enlightenment.
To attain Buddhahood and transform sentient beings, This is the unimpeded eye dharma-gate.
When Sudhana comes to my abode, He shall attend upon spiritual friends,
Hear this most profound Dharma, And practice it with diligent vigor.
This realm of Vairocana is profound and inconceivable;
receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, I shall explain it to you in detail for you.
"O Son of the Buddha!
In ages past, beyond kalpas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, there was an ocean of worlds named Bright Pure Mountain.
Therein appeared a Tathāgata in the world, titled Wisdom Dharma-realm Mountain;
he was the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King of Universal Illumination in Quiescence of All Directions.
When that Buddha was a bodhisattva, he purified that world-ocean;
within that world-ocean, there were world-systems as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field;
and within each of those world-systems, there appeared in the world Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a world.
Each and every Tathāgata preaches as many sūtras as there are atoms in a world-system;

within each and every sūtra, they bestow predictions of enlightenment upon as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a buddha-field, manifesting the various supernatural powers and immeasurable skillful means of the Tathāgatas,
and teaching sentient beings through various vehicles.
O Son of the Buddha!
Within that ocean of worlds, there is a world-system named Universal Gate Adornment;
within that world-system, there is a world named Wondrous Virtue of All Jewel Colors, which universally illumines an ocean of all jewel flowers as its adornment.

With various jewels as its substance, it is shaped like a celestial city; pure and magnificently adorned, it universally illuminates all the bodhimandas of the Buddhas, manifesting the transformative radiance of all Buddhas.
In that world, there are four continents as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru;
among those four continents, there is one four-continent system named Jewel Mountain Banner;
in that four-continent system, there is a Jambudvīpa, ten thousand yojanas in length and breadth.
Within that Jambudvīpa, there were one hundred thousand great cities;
among those cities was a royal capital named Cloud-Lamp Adorned with Solid Jewels, surrounded by ten thousand cities, where the lifespan of the people was ten thousand years.

At that time, there was a great king named Sarvadharmanirdeśasiṃhanādacchatramanojñaghoṣa, who had five hundred ministers, sixty thousand court ladies, and seven hundred princes, all of whom were handsome, brave, and strong.
At that time, the majesty and virtue of that king pervaded the entire Jambudvīpa, and he had no enemies.
During that great kalpa, a degenerate kalpa arose, and the five corruptions blazed fiercely.

At that time, the people practiced the ten unwholesome deeds and abandoned the ten wholesome ones; upon death, they entered the evil realms. Their lifespans were short, their physical forms were coarse and ugly, and they were poor, lowly, and base. They experienced much suffering and little joy, engaging in mutual litigation and slander, alienating one another’s kin, and falling deeply into false views.

Because they acted unlawfully out of various attachments and cravings, the winds and rains did not come at their proper times; the grasses, trees, forests, and all the hundred grains and sprouts withered away entirely.
At that time, the people, afflicted by famine and disease, all flocked to the royal capital and cried out with loud voices.

Then, an immeasurable and countless multitude of people surrounded the royal city; some raised both hands, others joined their palms, some wailed toward heaven and struck the earth, some threw themselves prostrate, some knelt on their right knees, and some wore tattered rags. Their eyes were devoid of luster as they cried out in mournful tones, all saying: "Great King!"
We are now in great suffering! Great suffering!
Starving, parched, frozen, and afflicted by disease and peril, we have no place of refuge and no one to rescue us.

"As if in prison, oppressed by all manner of sufferings and treading the path toward death," he uttered such words of immeasurable agony and bitter pain, appealing with a mournful voice for his own preservation, safety, and happiness.

The Great King is a treasure-trove for sentient beings and a pool of refreshing clarity; through the Dharma of skillful and upright governance and the Great Vehicle of great wisdom, he serves as a great island of jewels, providing true benefit and bestowing the bliss of gods and humans upon all sentient beings.

At that time, when the great king heard these sounds of sorrowful suffering and bitter agony, he immediately attained ten million *asaṃkhyeya* dharma-gates of great compassion; with single-minded contemplation, he then uttered ten words of great compassion.
What are these ten?
They are as follows: "Alas! How painful!"
All sentient beings have fallen into the bottomless, deep pit of birth and death, having no place of refuge; I shall act as their refuge and cause them all to attain the stage of the Tathāgata.
Alas for sentient beings, who are distracted by afflictions and have no one to provide relief; I shall act as their protector and establish them all securely in all wholesome deeds.
Alas for sentient beings, who suffer from birth, old age, sickness, and death and have no one to provide protection; I shall act as their protector and eliminate all suffering of body and mind.
Alas for sentient beings! They are beset by various terrors and lack any protection; I shall act as their protector, causing them to dwell in the secure and peaceful state of omniscience.

Alas for sentient beings! They are shrouded and obscured by the view of a self and by doubt; I shall act as a bright and pure lamp for them, universally illuminating all things and manifesting clear, pure wisdom.
Alas for sentient beings! They are covered by ignorance; I shall act as a great, brilliant torch for them, revealing the city of the True Dharma of omniscience.

Alas for sentient beings! Their minds are turbid and confused by stinginess, envy, flattery, crookedness, illusion, and falsehood; I shall cause them all to attain the unsurpassed, pure Dharma-body. Alas for sentient beings!
They are adrift and submerged in the long current of birth and death; I shall cause them to cross the ocean of birth and death and reach the Buddha’s other shore.
Alas for sentient beings! From birth they have been blind and sightless; I shall cause them to see the true meaning, becoming equal to all Buddhas.
Alas for sentient beings, whose faculties are unsubdued! I shall cause them to subdue their faculties, eliminate all obstacles, and attain omniscience.

At that time, the Great King uttered these ten kinds of words of great compassion, beating the drum to proclaim to all sentient beings: "Be at peace and do not fear; whatever you require, I shall provide for you all."

Immediately, he issued a decree throughout Jambudvīpa, to all cities, great and small, capitals, towns, and villages, to open their treasuries and storehouses, releasing gold, silver, rare jewels, clothing, delicacies, incense, flowers, necklaces, couches, mats, bedding, quilts, palaces, and dwellings;
as well as various exquisite jeweled banners, night-luminous jewel banners, and mani-jewel banners;
and physicians' decoctions and medicines, along with all kinds of vessels filled with various miscellaneous treasures.
Various adamantine vessels were filled with manifold exquisite incenses;
various types of incense containers held diverse garments;
and there were various vehicles, along with banners, silken streamers, standards, and canopies.

Furthermore, he struck the drum and issued a proclamation throughout all the cities, capitals, towns, and villages of the world: "I now bestow upon you my kingdom, cities, towns, and villages, as well as my wife, children, head, eyes, teeth, tongue, heart, liver, blood, flesh, intestines, stomach, hands, feet, and all my limbs."
At that time, outside the eastern gate of the city, there was a great assembly site named Pure Radiance Maṇi Sublime Virtue.
Its ground was level and even, vast and pure, free from all impurities;
it was made of various jewels, strewn with diverse precious flowers, and perfumed with manifold fragrances, such that clouds of every kind of incense filled the void of space.

Surrounded by jewel trees, with immeasurable nets of flowers and various nets of jewels spread over them, they spontaneously produce immeasurable billions of nayutas of musical sounds for entertainment;
adorned with such immeasurable, rare, and wonderful things, all of which are the karmic fruits of the pure deeds of bodhisattvas.

In that assembly, at the place where the king resided, the ground was made of ten kinds of jewels and surrounded by railings of ten kinds of jewels; ten types of jewel trees encircled it on all sides.
Its form and color were adamantine and indestructible.

Adorned with various treasures, precious banners were suspended from it, and its surface was covered by nets of pure white jewels, nets of golden bells, nets of various flowers, nets of *maṇi* jewels, and nets of various garments.
Perfumed with sublime incense, it spontaneously produced immeasurable sounds of exquisite and subtle songs.
At that time, the Great King sat upon the lion throne, majestic and most wonderful, endowed with the marks of a great man;
his limbs were perfectly formed, and his body was like that of Nārāyaṇa, indestructible.

Born into the royal lineage, he governed the kingdom with righteousness; regarding wealth, mind, and the Dharma, he attained complete mastery. His merit was immeasurable, and there were none who disobeyed his commands.
A multitude of exquisite jeweled canopies covered its summit;
these canopies constantly emitted immeasurable light of Jambūnada gold, and were further draped with nets of pure and wondrous maṇi jewels.
Golden bells, made of various precious gems, produced harmonious and elegant sounds, proclaiming virtuous deeds.
"At that time, immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* beings within Jambudvīpa all came to take refuge and praised the Great King, saying:
'The King is a man of wisdom, foremost in the world;
his merit is like Mount Sumeru, and his merit is bright and pure, like the full moon.'"
"Having attained the Bodhisattva mind, one regards all sentient beings with equanimity and bestows gifts universally upon them.

At that time, having seen this, the King was filled with immeasurable joy; amidst that great assembly, he gave rise to a heart of great compassion and a heart toward spiritual friends, satisfying everyone according to their requests and thereby gathering them in.

At that time, the king immediately attained immeasurable bliss, which could not be equaled by the various pleasures experienced by Śakra Devānām Indra, up to and including the King of the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations, for immeasurable hundreds of billions of nayutas of kalpas;
nor could it be equaled by the various pleasures experienced by the King of the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations for inconceivable kalpas;
nor even by the Great Brahmā King’s dwelling in the bliss of the Brahma-abodes for unspeakable kalpas.
Even the gods of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, who dwell in the bliss of tranquility for incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*), cannot equal it.
Furthermore, son of good family!
It is like a person who is profoundly kind and filial, yet encounters worldly difficulties and is separated from his parents; after many years have passed, he suddenly meets them again.
Beholding the countenance of his parents, he was filled with such joy and exultation that he could not contain himself.
At that time, when the Great King saw those who came to him seeking aid, his heart rejoiced greatly in the same way;
his faith became firm and steadfast, nurturing his bodhicitta.
Why is this? Because these bodhisattvas single-mindedly seek all-knowledge (sarvajñatā) to bring benefit, advantage, and peace to all sentient beings;
they fulfill their great vows, distance themselves from unwholesome dharmas, and practice all forms of goodness.
To rescue and protect sentient beings, opening the gate of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge);
to encompass all-encompassing wisdom and fulfill the vows of sentient beings;
to enter the ocean of all merits of all Buddhas, to destroy the mountains of all afflictions, demonic activities, and karmic obstructions, and to accord with the teachings of all Tathāgatas.
Entering the stream of profound wisdom, they do not deviate from the true path; emerging from the flow of all phenomena, they fulfill their great vows.
Abiding in the dharma of great beings, they satisfy the treasury of universal roots of goodness;
remaining free from all evil, their minds are unstained as they thoroughly comprehend that all phenomena are like space.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, the Great King beheld all sentient beings and conceived toward them the thought of them as his only son, the thought of them as his parents, the thought of them as fields of merit, the thought of their kindness being difficult to repay, the thought of them as teachers, and the thought of them as Buddhas; he encompassed them all with a heart of great compassion.

According to their needs, he provided clothing, food and drink, flowers, incense, powdered incense, ointments, garlands, parasols, banners, and streamers—all manner of ornaments—as well as couches, seats, bedding, dwellings, palaces, gardens, bathing pools, vehicles, litters, elephants, horses, various jewels, the palaces where they resided along with their retinues, and the inner treasuries, cities, and villages.
All these things he gave away entirely to sentient beings, causing them all to be fully satisfied.
At that time, there was a young girl in that assembly named Ratnaprabhā;

she was upright and exquisite, with peerless countenance, a body like pure gold, and eyes and hair of deep blue. Her mouth produced wondrous sounds and her body emitted a sublime fragrance. Adorned with various jewels, she was always possessed of a sense of shame and remorse, maintained right mindfulness without distraction, and was composed and dignified in her deportment, showing reverence and respect toward her teachers and elders.
Their faculties are tranquil and composed; mindfulness and wisdom are present before them; they are able to retain and understand all the teachings they hear.

Having cultivated immeasurable roots of goodness and all manner of sublime, virtuous dharmas over many lifetimes, their bodies are moistened and nourished by them. They draw near to spiritual friends, delight in the Mahāyāna, and their minds are like space. Bringing peace to themselves and others, they always rejoice in seeing the Buddhas and seek omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
Together with sixty young maidens, they stood not far from the king, with single-minded reverence, palms joined, and thought to themselves:
"We have gained a great benefit; we have seen a virtuous friend and encountered a virtuous friend."
Toward that king, he conceived the thought of him as a Great Teacher, the thought of him as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), and the thought of him as a person of compassion.
When these thoughts arose, his joy was immeasurable; he removed his ornaments, placed them before the king, and made this aspiration:
"May this great king bring peace and security to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings; may I also be thus in a future life."

"The Great King’s wisdom, the Great King’s right path, that which the Great King rides, the Great King’s marks and signs, and the Great King’s treasures—none can destroy them; may I also be thus in a future life."
"Wherever you are born, I shall also be born there.
Then, the Great King said to this woman, "I now relinquish all that is precious, both internal and external; take whatever you desire."
At that time, the woman’s joy redoubled, and she spoke in verse:
“Before the Great King arose in this world, The firm and magnificent capital was entirely devoid of delight, Like the dwelling place of hungry ghosts.”
Sentient beings harm one another; they steal, indulge in lustful excess, engage in double-tongued speech and untruths, and utter meaningless, coarse, and evil words.
They covet the wealth and possessions of others, harboring anger and a malicious intent to do harm.
Those with wrong views and unwholesome conduct fall into evil realms at the end of their lives.
Such beings, shrouded by ignorance, perform all manner of evils;
thus, the heavens remain parched and do not send down rain.
Because there was no seasonal rain, all the hundred grains failed to grow;
the grasses and trees withered away, and even the springs and streams ran dry.
Before Your Majesty arose in this world, all the rivers and ponds—
All things have become parched and dried up, like a vast wilderness.
Yet when Your Majesty was first born, the heavens sent forth auspicious, heavy clouds;
rain fell and spread its bounty everywhere, until rivers and ponds were all filled to overflowing.
All evils are extinguished, And all terrors are cast far away;
The people are filled with joy, Because the Great King has been born into this world.
In times past, all living beings Harmed one another in turn.
They who once devoured the flesh and blood of others now all cultivate a mind of loving-kindness.
In the past, the hundred grains did not grow, and all plants and trees withered away;
oppressed by hunger and thirst, they underwent manifold sufferings and afflictions.
Once the Great King had appeared in the world, non-glutinous rice grew spontaneously and trees produced exquisite garments;
this was because the world turned its allegiance to the King.
In former days, people vied for meager profits, and the strong oppressed and plundered the weak.
Now, with all manner of adornments, it is like the Garden of Nanda belonging to Śakra.
In the past, people were heavy with craving and engaged in various acts of heedlessness;
they violated the wives and beauty of others, and thus brought harm upon one another.
Today all these people, adorned with various precious jewels,
are pure and free from sexual misconduct, just like those in the Tuṣita heaven.
In the past, sentient beings spoke falsehoods and unrighteous words.
Though they may utter meaningless words with their mouths, acting with flattery and crookedness to win over others' hearts,
may all living beings today distance themselves from such evil speech;
may they look upon sentient beings with eyes of affection and let forth gentle sounds from their mouths.
In former times, various sentient beings, practicing all manner of wrong views,
would join their palms in reverent prostration to cattle, sheep, dogs, and swine. Now,
having heard the King’s True Dharma, they have distanced themselves from all such false views.
He well understands that the phenomena of suffering and pleasure all arise from causes and conditions.
When the Great King utters his wondrous voice, there is no one who does not find it delightful;
even the voices of Brahmā and Śakra cannot equal it.
The Great King’s many precious canopies hang suspended in the midst of space;
covered with nets of various jewels, they emit a pervasive fragrance of wondrous incense.
From golden bells, there spontaneously issues the harmonious and elegant voice of the Tathāgata.
Proclaiming the profound Dharma, they eliminate all afflictions.
Furthermore, they extensively expound upon all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions,
and within all kalpas, the Tathāgatas and their retinues.
Furthermore, he speaks in succession of all the Tathāgatas and their retinues throughout every eon in the lands of the ten directions of the past;
again, they emit subtle and wondrous sounds that fill the world beneath heaven.
The Brahma King and all living beings All hear the retribution of karma.
Having heard these sounds, the beings Know for themselves the treasury of their own karmas;
They leave evil behind and cultivate all manner of goodness, Dedicated solely to seeking the unsurpassed path.
The father’s name was Pure Light, and the mother was named Lotus Radiance;
in this world of five turbidities, the father ruled the realm with the True Dharma.
There were five hundred lotus ponds, all surrounded by precious trees.
The bottom is spread with golden sand, and precious flowers bloom in full profusion.
Upon the banks of those ponds are various sublime Dharma halls,
with railings made of many jewels and adorned with all kinds of precious ornaments.
When evil dharmas arise in the final age, no rain shall fall for many years;
ponds and streams all dry up, and all plants and trees are scorched by fire.
Then the King of Seven Days shall be born, first manifesting auspicious and supernatural signs.
All people saw him and rejoiced; he was the protector who appeared in the world.
At that time, during the middle of the night, the great earth shook in six ways, and a wondrous light spontaneously radiated, like the bright and pure sun.
There are five hundred bathing pools, filled with water of merit;
all the various jewel trees are as flourishing as they were originally.
The rivers, springs, and sources are all completely full.
The spiritual grace universally moistens and nourishes, drenching all of Jambudvīpa.
Trees and various groves, diverse flowers and manifold medicinal herbs,
as well as the sprouts and crops of the hundred grains— all grow and flourish with universal abundance.
The various high mountains with their crags and precipices, the remote, deep, and perilous valleys,
and all the lands therein, become naturally level and even.
The mountains, hills, and all vegetation, along with the gravel, pebbles, and various impurities—
In a single thought-moment, all were transformed into various precious gems.
Seeing this marvel, people spoke with joy: "How wonderful!
What great and virtuous benefit! We have attained the pond of cool clarity."
At that time, King Pure Light, together with his inner retinue and all his ministers, joyfully went to roam through the park.
Among the five hundred bathing pools, there was one named Joy.
Upon the pond stands the Hall of Sublime Dharma, where the King and his retinue dwell and rest.
At that time, the King spoke to his consort: "My vows are all fulfilled;
the land has become rich and joyful, and the people are everywhere at peace."
At that time, within that bathing pool, a thousand-petaled jewel lotus arose,
universally emitting pure light that shone brilliantly upon the summit of Mount Sumeru;
its stem was of clear, pure vajra, and its petals were composed of various jewels.
Upon a pedestal of Jambūnada gold, with exquisite fragrances for its filaments, a young boy was born within that lotus;
his body adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, all the devas paid him homage.
The King, seeing this, was filled with great joy; he entered the pool and took him up, placing him upon the Queen’s lap. "Your son should rejoice! he said.
Then treasure-troves surged forth everywhere, and from the jewel-trees grew exquisite garments.
Celestial music played wondrous sounds, filling the void of space.
At that time, all those people joined their palms in reverent salutation and, filled with joy, spoke these words: "This is the refuge of the world."
The body emits a great radiance, universally illuminating all;
should anyone encounter this light, all outflows (āsravas) are completely extinguished.
All evil spirits and ghosts who harm and injure classes of sentient beings—
Having completely abandoned unwholesome thoughts, compassion arises spontaneously.
Ill repute, the loss of wholesome benefits, and being possessed by disease-demons—
all such manifold sufferings are extinguished, and everyone is filled with joy.
Toward all living beings in the world, May they regard one another as parents;
Leaving behind evil and cultivating a mind of loving-kindness, They shall single-mindedly seek all-encompassing wisdom.
May they distance themselves from all miserable realms And widely open the path for devas and humans.
Manifesting the unsurpassed path, you deliver all sentient beings.
We have gained a great benefit in meeting such a great donor;
for sentient beings who have lost the true path, the Guide has now appeared in the world.

At that time, after the maiden Ratnaprabhā had praised the king with these verses, she prostrated herself at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence.
The king praised the girl, saying: "Excellent! Excellent!"
To be able to believe in and know the merits of others is itself rare;
yet there are those who are foolish and do not know how to repay kindness, lacking wisdom, with turbid minds and false views—
beings such as these, who possess unrighteousness, neither know nor believe in the pure merits of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, which are the realm of omniscience.
"You now single-mindedly seek unsurpassed bodhi, cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva to gather and bring peace and security, benefiting all sentient beings.
After the king had praised the girl, he personally bestowed upon her a priceless robe and said to her,
"Put this on yourself."
Then, that woman knelt upon the ground, paid her respects with palms joined, and received and wore it upon her head.
At that time, the king further gave robes to sixty women; having put on the robes, they departed together with their retinue after circumambulating him and taking their leave.
From within the garments of all these women, the light of all the constellations issued forth; when the multitude saw this, they all sighed in admiration, saying:
"These women are all perfectly beautiful, like the clear night sky adorned with the stars."
"Good son! At that time, was the King of the Wondrous Sound of the Perfect Canopy, the Lion’s Roar of All Dharma-Masters, anyone else?
It was none other than the present Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vairocana."
King Pure Light was King Śuddhodana; Lady Lotus Light was Lady Māyā;
and the people of that country were the present great assembly.
They have all attained non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
some abide in the first stage (*bhūmi*) up to the tenth;
they have fulfilled their great vows, dwell in various Dharma-gates, cultivate the path of skillful means, seek all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and abide in various liberations.
At that time, the night goddess Vikasitapushpa, wishing to further clarify this meaning, spoke in verse:
“I possess the pure eye, Which perceives the entirety of the ocean of worlds;
Amidst the five realms of birth and death, Sentient beings are in constant flux.”
I see all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas proceeding to the Bodhi tree,
attaining the Way, turning the wheel of Dharma, and transforming and delivering all sentient beings.
With my pure divine ear, I perceive the realm of all sounds.
I hear all the teachings spoken by the Buddhas and joyfully uphold them.
Possessing the non-dual wisdom that is equal to all that is peerless,
I am able, within a single thought-moment, to fully comprehend the ocean of the minds of sentient beings.
I have attained the knowledge of past lives, recollecting all oceans of eons;
regarding myself and others, I discern and fully comprehend them all.
In a single thought-moment, I know the eons as numerous as the atoms within oceans of lands.
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and all classes of sentient beings within the five realms:
those Buddhas first made their vows, single-mindedly seeking the Bodhi of a Buddha;
they have ultimately brought to full completion the immeasurable practices of a Bodhisattva.
Having realized equal and perfect enlightenment through various skillful means,
you turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma, manifesting the ocean of all vehicles.
For the sake of the multitudes, you expound the Dharma, delivering and liberating all beings.
Even unto the time when the Dharma remains, I shall know it all in a single thought.
Having cultivated this dharma-gate throughout immeasurable kalpas,
true sons of the Buddha should swiftly bring this dharma-gate to ultimate completion.
“O Son of the Buddha!
I know only this Dharma-door of the Light of Infinite Joy and Contentment of Bodhisattvas;
as for the great Bodhisattvas, who practice the ocean of all Buddhas’ deeds in the presence of all Buddhas...”
Seeking all-knowledge, they purify and fulfill all great vows;
within a single bodhisattva stage, they practice the ocean of all bodhisattva stages;
within a single bodhisattva practice, they encompass the ocean of all bodhisattva practices.
Within a single dharma-gate, they exercise mastery over the cultivation and integration of all dharma-gates.
How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
O Son of the Buddha!
In this place of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Vīryapraṇidhānābhāsarakṣasattvā.
Go to her and ask: how does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path;
how does one bring sentient beings to maturity for unsurpassed bodhi and purify all buddha-fields?
"May I encounter all Buddhas and cultivate the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in reverence at the feet of that Night Goddess, circumambulated her, and took his leave.
