At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the place of the Night Goddess named Protecting Sentient Beings with the Radiance of Vow-Valiance. He saw that Night Goddess seated upon a lion throne of the treasury of the universally illuminating king of mani-jewels amidst a great assembly. A net of the king of mani-jewels covered her body, and her radiance shone universally throughout all dharma realms. She took as her body the light of all suns, moons, and stars, and within it appeared the forms, types, colors, and images of all sentient beings;
furthermore, she manifested bodies like oceans of all forms, bodies of all modes of conduct, and bodies in all directions, responding to [the needs of beings].
The body that manifests before all sentient beings; the body of sovereign power that wanders through the ten directions;
the body that appears before all beings at all times without missing the proper occasion; the body that approaches the abodes of all Buddhas to pay them homage;
the body that nurtures all roots of goodness; and the body that upholds the clouds of the true Dharma of all Buddhas without ever forgetting it.
The body that fulfills all bodhisattva vows; the body that universally illumines all worlds;

the body of a pure, bright lamp that universally illuminates and extinguishes the darkness of ignorance; the body that realizes all phenomena through deep wisdom free from defilement, knowing them to be like illusions;
the body that awakens all beings and manifests everywhere according to their minds; the body free from the burning heat [of afflictions]; and the body that does not...
This body is destructible, yet it is the body sustained by the Buddha’s practice, which has no basis for dwelling; it is the undefiled, pure Dharma-body.
Having seen this, Sudhana prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and gave rise to as many thoughts as there are atoms in a Buddha-world, contemplating that celestial body.
After a long while, he rose, joined his palms in reverence, and contemplated with single-minded attention; from the spiritual friend, he attained ten kinds of mind.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
They attain the mind of self-mastery, for they are able to receive and uphold all-knowledge through courageous diligence;
they attain the mind that possesses the qualities of omniscience, for they accord with all paths of the true teachings;
they attain the mind of intentional rebirth, for they dwell securely in the gateways of the unsurpassed True Dharma.
They attain the mind of shared practice, because they share in all the deeds and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
they attain the mind that is a treasury of all merits, because they nurture all pure and white dharmas;
they attain the courageous mind, because they nurture the great vigor of all Buddhas.
They attain a mind fully endowed with all roots of goodness, because they have brought all great vows to fulfillment;
they attain a mind capable of accomplishing all great benefits, because they are complete in the sovereign powers of a bodhisattva.
This is how one attains ten kinds of mind regarding spiritual friends.
At that time, Sudhana, having single-mindedly observed that night goddess, attained as many common dharmas of Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in a world-system; namely:
The commonality of right mindfulness, because one mindfully recollects all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time;
the commonality of great wisdom, because one discerns and understands the ocean of all dharmas;
the commonality of all realms of existence, because the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas is indestructible.
The commonality of awakening: wisdom like space, because it universally illumines the ocean of all skillful means throughout the three periods of time;
the commonality of the faculties: through clear and pure wisdom, because it universally illumines the ocean of all faculties of sentient beings;
the commonality of the pure mind: cultivating the bodhisattva path, because one attains the adornment of the unimpeded merit of all-knowledge.
The commonality of the sphere of experience, because clear and pure wisdom illuminates the realm of the Buddhas;
the commonality of conforming to skillful means, because one ultimately reaches the ocean of all-knowledge skillful means and universally illumines all things;
the commonality of knowing meaning, because one knows the true nature of all phenomena.
The common quality of fearlessness regarding the Dharma, because it disperses and destroys all enemies;
the common quality of the pure form-body, because it manifests a pure body according to what is appropriate;
the common quality of the powers, because one does not regress from omniscience (*sarvajñā*);
The shared quality of fearlessness, because the pure and upright mind is like space;
the shared quality of diligence, because one practices the bodhisattva conduct throughout all kalpas without ever turning back;
the shared quality of eloquence, because with clear and pure wisdom one penetrates deeply into all phenomena and illuminates them all.
The common quality of incomparability, because no sentient being is able to surpass them;
the common quality of eloquence, because they preach the pure and wondrous Dharma amidst the great assembly without fear;
the common quality of sublime voice, because they can roar the lion’s roar, emitting a subtle and wondrous sound that fills the ocean of all dharmas.
The commonality of pure sound, because all sentient beings delight in hearing it;
the commonality of pure virtue, because it causes all sentient beings to become completely purified;
the commonality of the ground of wisdom, because one receives the wheel of Dharma from all Buddhas.
The shared quality of the holy life (*brahmacarya*), because it causes one to dwell securely in the realm of all Buddhas;
the shared quality of great loving-kindness (*maitrī*), because in every thought-moment it universally covers the ocean of all sentient beings;
the shared quality of great compassion (*karuṇā*), because it rains down the Dharma of ambrosia to rescue all sentient beings.
The commonality of physical action, because it accords with the deeds performed for all sentient beings;
the commonality of verbal action, because it discerns all methods of speech;
the commonality of mental action, because it establishes in all sentient beings the mind of *sarvajñā* (omniscience).
The common dharma of adornment, for the purpose of purifying all Buddha-fields;
the common dharma of approaching all Buddhas, for the purpose of beholding all Buddhas appearing in the world;
the common dharma of exhortation, for the purpose of requesting all Tathāgatas to turn the wheel of Dharma;
The commonality of making offerings, because one makes offerings to all Tathāgatas;
the commonality of teaching and transforming, because one delivers and liberates all sentient beings;
the commonality of radiance, because it illuminates all dharmas.
The shared quality of samādhi, because it attains immovability within the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings;
the shared quality of fulfillment, because the sovereign spiritual powers of all bodhisattvas fill all buddha-fields;
and the shared quality of the bodhisattva dharma-gates, because they give rise to the sovereign power of bodhisattvas.
The commonality of retinues, because they delight in dwelling together with Bodhisattvas;
the commonality of profound entry, because they discern all worlds;
the commonality of understanding the mind, because they extensively purify Buddha-fields;
The common dharma of conformity, because it enters the ocean of all Buddha-worlds;
the common dharma of fulfilling skillful means, because it discerns and understands all worlds;
the supreme common dharma, because it universally manifests in all Buddha-fields.
The common quality of non-retrogression, because one wanders through the ten directions without obstruction;
the common quality of eliminating all ignorance, because one attains the perfect wisdom of all Buddhas;
the common quality of non-arising, because one becomes a member of the retinue of all Buddhas.
The commonality of fulfilling the networks of all Buddha-fields by reverently making offerings to all Buddhas;
the commonality of definitive wisdom by discerning and understanding the ocean of all phenomena;
and the commonality of practicing according to the teachings by entering in accordance with all gateways of the Dharma.
They single-mindedly seek the shared dharmas, desiring to attain all pure dharmas;
they purify the shared dharmas by adorning their body, speech, and mind with the merits of all Buddhas;
they purify the shared dharmas of the mind by bringing wisdom to full perfection regarding all dharmas.
The shared quality of valor, because it brings all undertakings to completion and fulfills roots of goodness;
the shared quality of pure conduct, because it brings all bodhisattva practices to fulfillment;
the shared quality of non-obstruction, because it discerns and thoroughly understands the characteristics of all phenomena.
The commonality of skillful means, because it is the dharma-gate of fulfilling sovereign wisdom;
the commonality of pure entry, because it manifests realms according to what is appropriate;
the commonality of the bodhisattva gate, because it practices all the dharmas of the Buddhas.
The shared dharma of protection and maintenance, because it is protected and maintained by all Buddhas;
the shared dharma of transcending birth, because one successively attains the bodhisattva stages;
the shared dharma of peaceful abiding, because one peacefully abides in all bodhisattva dwellings.
The commonality of expounding the Dharma, because of thoroughly understanding the dharma of the Buddhas' bestowal of predictions;
the commonality of meditative concentration, because of entering all samādhis within a single thought-moment;
the commonality of arising from samādhi, because of the various manifestations of all Buddha-activities.
The common dharma of pure mindfulness, because it knows all thoughts;
the common dharma of bodhisattva practice, because one practices the bodhisattva path without interruption throughout all future kalpas;
the common dharma of pure faith, because it increases the joy of the Buddha’s wisdom.
The shared quality of nurturing, because it eliminates all obstacles;
the shared quality of non-retrogressive wisdom, because it is equal to the wisdom of all Buddhas;
the shared quality of taking birth, because it manifests through transformation for all sentient beings at the appropriate time.
Abiding in the commonality of dharmas, because one abides in omniscience;
the commonality of the objective sphere, because the objective sphere is the dharma-realm;
the commonality of non-attachment, because the mind is not defiled by or attached to any existence.
They thoroughly know the commonality of the characteristics of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇasādhāraṇatā*), because they observe all phenomena with an impartial mind;
they accept the commonality of phenomena, because within their own bodies they receive and uphold all the Buddha-dharmas;
they possess the commonality of penetrating clarity, because they analytically understand all worlds.
The shared quality of spiritual powers, by which one traverses all oceans of Buddha-fields through slight means;
the shared quality of dhāraṇīs, by which one universally illumines all oceans of dhāraṇīs;
and the shared quality of upholding all Buddhas' wheels of Dharma, by which one is able to receive and maintain all sūtra teachings.
The common dharma of profound entry, because it understands all phenomena to be like space;
the common dharma of pure light, because it universally illumines all worlds;
the common dharma of brilliant purity, because it manifests to sentient beings according to their needs.
The shared quality of causing tremors shakes all Buddha-fields in order to manifest sovereign power for the sake of all sentient beings;
the shared quality of non-futility ensures that for those who see, hear, or remember it, nothing is in vain;
and the shared quality of the noble path fulfills all vows through the wisdom of the ten powers.
He attained such common dharmas of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.

At that time, having entered into these common dharmas of Bodhisattvas, Sudhana attained an immeasurable and boundless pure and upright mind toward his spiritual friend. Baring his right shoulder and joining his palms in reverence, he praised that Night Goddess with these verses:
"With a supreme mind, I seek exclusively the Bodhi of the Buddhas."
Now, regarding the spiritual friend, one should give rise to the thought that they are oneself.
By distancing oneself from all evil karma and accomplishing pure conduct,
through seeing the spiritual friend, one attains inexhaustible white dharmas.
Having seen my spiritual friend, my mind is adorned with merit;
throughout all lands and kalpas until the end of the future, I shall practice the bodhisattva path.
I only pray that the spiritual friend will take pity on me and accept me.
Reveal them all to me: the true Dharma of the authentic teaching.
Close off all evil destinies and widely open the path for devas and humans;
reveal to me the entire path of the Buddha’s omniscience.
Recalling that spiritual friend, the treasury of all merit,
In every thought-moment I attain an ocean of merit as vast as space.
He bestows upon me the *pāramitās* and inconceivable virtues.
Nurturing all wholesome merits, the silken cloth of wisdom is swiftly bound upon the crown of the head.
I mindfully reflect upon the spiritual friend, the path to omniscience;
by relying upon the spiritual friend, one fulfills all pure and white dharmas.
Fully endowed with all manner of beneficial virtues, His merit is universally perfected;
having reached the ultimate realization of all phenomena, He has accomplished omniscience (*sarvajñā*).
Taking the wise as his great teacher, He establishes the unsurpassed Dharma.
"Even through immeasurable and incalculable eons, one could not repay their kindness.
At that time, after Sudhana had finished praising her with these verses, he said:
"O Celestial Being, as for this inconceivable dharma that you have just manifested, what is the name of this dharma-gate?"
"How long has it been since you first resolved to attain the Way?
How much longer will it be before you realize unsurpassed bodhi? He replied:
“Good son! This Dharma gate is named ‘Awakening Sentient Beings According to Their Needs and Nurturing Their Roots of Goodness. Good son!”

Having entered this Dharma-door, I have awakened to the equality of all phenomena and known the true mark of all phenomena. Remaining far removed from the world, I am free from all attachment; I understand that all forms are neither one nor different, and I realize that form is no-form while being able to manifest immeasurable varieties of form.
These are: various forms, pure forms, adorned forms, forms that radiate all adornments, and universal...
Manifesting forms; forms identical to those of all sentient beings; forms appearing before all worlds; universally illuminating forms;
forms that one never tires of beholding; forms pure with the primary and secondary marks; forms free from evil; forms manifesting valor; profound forms;
forms that no one in any world can exhaust; forms praised as inexhaustible; and various [forms].

The color of various clouds, the color of all forms and images, the color of manifesting immeasurable sovereign power, the color of being lovely and delightful, the color of the arising of all that is wholesome,
the color of appearing in accordance with [the needs of beings], the color of appearing according to how sentient beings are to be delivered,
the color of universal illumination without obstruction, the color of freedom from defilement, the color of the indestructible pure body, and the inconceivable...
The color of the light of skillful means in deliberating the Dharma; the color of wondrous transcendence that is neither comparable nor incomparable;
the color that is neither bright nor dark; the color that extinguishes all darkness; the color produced by the accumulation of all pure and white dharmas;
the color born from the great ocean of merit; the color born from past cultivation and reverence; the color like a pure and upright mind.
The color of space; the color of supreme vastness; the color of being uninterrupted and inexhaustible; the color of oceanic radiance;
the indestructible color upon which all worlds have no dependence; the unimpeded color that fills all ten directions;
the color of every thought-moment; the color of the ocean; and the color that causes all sentient beings to experience great joy.
The color that encompasses the solid forms of all sentient beings; the color of the lion’s roar of the Tathāgata’s virtues from every pore;
the color that purifies the deep minds of all sentient beings; the color that manifests the meaning of all dharmas;
the color of unimpeded, perfect radiance; the color equal to the stainless void; and the color that does not rely on defilement.
The color of radiant attachment; the color of the universally illuminating, stainless Dharma-realm; the color of the ineffable; the color seen by the eye; the color that illuminates all directions;
the color that manifests according to the time to respond to sentient beings; the color of tranquility; the color that extinguishes all afflictions;
the color of the light of the field of merit for the virtues of all sentient beings; and the color of non-seeing.
The color of emptiness; the color of the light of great wisdom; the color of the unimpeded Dharma-body that fills all forms;
the color of manifesting majestic deportment without falsehood; the color of the accumulated ocean of great compassion; the color of the Mount Sumeru of perfected merit;
the color that universally illuminates all realms of existence; the color of pure great wisdom; and the color of right mindfulness toward all worlds.
The color of all jewel-lights; the color of the pure treasury of jewels; the color of the indestructible purity of sentient beings;
the color of the inclination toward *sarvajñā* (omniscience); the color that delights the eyes of sentient beings; the color of the supreme radiance of all jewel-adornments;
the color of neither grasping nor abandoning any sentient being; the color that is neither determinate nor ultimate; the manifestation...
The color of manifesting sovereign powers of retention; the color of all sovereign spiritual transformations (*ṛddhi*); the color of the Buddha-lineage;
the color of being far removed from all evils and filling the dharma-realm; the color of reaching all the great assemblies of Buddhas and illuminating all things;
the color of accomplishing all oceans [of merit]; the color of the fruit resulting from reliance on virtuous conduct; the color of bestowing according to transformation; the first...
The color of all worldly sights that never causes weariness; the color of various radiances shining everywhere;
the color manifesting all things of the three periods of time; the color manifesting all oceans; the color emitting an ocean of all radiances; the color of various lights;
the color surpassing all fragrant lights of every world; and the color manifesting perfect fulfillment.
The color of the sun’s clouds; the color of clouds of perfectly pure full moons; the color of clouds of exquisite flowers from Mount Sumeru;
the color of clouds emitting various garlands; the color of clouds manifesting all kinds of *padma* lotuses;
the color of clouds of all manner of incense images filling the Dharma-realm; the color of clouds scattering all powdered incense; and the manifestation of one...
The pure vow-body colors of all Buddhas, the Dharma-realm ocean colors produced by all sounds as the lion’s roar,
and the pure body colors of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva— such colors as these appear in every thought-moment,
filling the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings.
Some attain liberation through seeing or through mindfulness;
some manifest the turning of the wheel of Dharma;
and some manifest timely responses.
Sometimes they manifest as being in close attendance;
sometimes they manifest as awakening;
and sometimes they manifest as sovereign spiritual powers.
They may manifest various transformations;

or they may manifest inconceivable, sovereign supernatural powers and transformations to deliver sentient beings, extinguish unwholesome dharmas, establish wholesome dharmas, fulfill great vows, and—by the power of omniscience and the power of the bodhisattva dharma-gates—perfectly accomplish great loving-kindness and great compassion.
O Son of the Buddha!

Abiding in this Dharma-gate, I manifest immeasurable physical bodies, discerning and thoroughly comprehending all oceans of forms. I release immeasurable and boundless clouds of Dharma, universally illuminating all Buddha-worlds; I manifest immeasurable and boundless Buddhas and display immeasurable and boundless sovereign spiritual powers. I awaken sentient beings and nurture their roots of goodness, so that in every thought-moment, inconceivable numbers of beings attain non-retrogression in their progress toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“O Son of the Buddha!
Regarding your question as to how long it takes to attain this Dharma-gate,
I shall now explain it for you by receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power.”
O Son of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva’s perfection of wisdom is free from all falsehood; its intrinsic nature is pure. Possessing the knowledge of all modes, it transcends all mountains of obstacles and universally illumines all according to those who are to be transformed.
O Son of the Buddha!
It is like the nature of the sun, which possesses no darkness;
yet once the sun has set, the world becomes dark, and when it rises, there is great illumination.
In the same way, the Bodhisattva’s sun of perfected, luminous wisdom is likewise free from all falsehood, universally illuminating all things and transforming sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
For example, when the pure sun rises over Jambudvīpa, it shines universally upon all the mountains and trees of the world, and its reflection appears in everything;

the great oceans, rivers, ponds, and all classes of sentient beings behold it without exception, yet the sun does not actually enter these pools or streams. The sun of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom is likewise: it emerges from the ocean of the three realms of existence and moves within the empty space of the Buddha’s true Dharma. Abiding in quiescent extinction (*śānti*), it manifests in response within all destinies and places of birth, assuming forms identical to those of sentient beings to transform and deliver them. Yet in reality, it does not undergo birth and death; it is free from defilement and attachment, detached from all falsehood, and devoid of notions of long or short.
Why is this? Sons of the Buddha!

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are free from all inversions; they understand that all worlds are entirely like dreams and illusions. Having realized the true Dharma, they perceive that no sentient beings exist; yet, perfecting great compassion, they manifest before all sentient beings to teach and transform them.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as a great ship does not rely on this shore, does not delight in the other shore, and does not cling to the middle of the stream, yet ferries sentient beings across the great ocean;

so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who, by means of the ship of the power of the *pāramitās*, ferries sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death. Without relying on this shore and without delighting in the other shore, they deliver sentient beings, cultivating the practices of a Bodhisattva throughout all kalpas without giving rise to the notion of a kalpa, nor perceiving any distinction of length or brevity within a kalpa.
O Son of the Buddha!

It is, for example, as if space were to transcend all worlds within the dharma-realm; though those worlds undergo formation and destruction, that space is by nature pure, unstained, indestructible, and free from all fear and obstacles, yet it can universally sustain all buddha-fields throughout all future kalpas.

The mind of a bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: adorning the mind with wisdom as vast as space, they give rise to the wind-circles of all great vows to support all sentient beings, causing them to extinguish the evil realms and be born in the various happy destinies. With a mind free from anxiety or joy, they establish sentient beings on the path of omniscience, eliminating the afflictions and the calamities of birth and death.
O Son of the Buddha!

For example, a conjured person has no substantial form and is free from the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, death, hunger, thirst, and so forth. The wisdom born of the Bodhisattva is likewise indestructible; their wondrously colored Dharma-body is also like this. Throughout all kalpas and amidst all cycles of birth and death, they transform and deliver sentient beings without attachment, without fear, without greed, and without anger. They extinguish all burning afflictions, and their minds do not crave or delight in any realm of rebirth.
“O Son of the Buddha!

Although the wisdom of bodhisattvas is thus profoundly deep and difficult to fathom, I shall, relying on the Buddha’s spiritual power, explain it for you, so that the bodhisattvas of future ages may fulfill their great vows and achieve all the powers.”
O Son of the Buddha!
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, and further beyond that number, there was an eon named Good Light; in that eon, there was a world named Jewel Light.

In that kalpa, ten thousand Tathāgatas appeared in the world; the first Tathāgata was named Dharma-cakra-ghoṣa-gaganapradīpa. In that Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital called Ratnavyūha, and within it was a great forest named Sugandhaprabhāsa.
Within this forest, there is a site of enlightenment called Good Flower;
upon that site of enlightenment is a lion throne of precious lotuses, and at that time, the Tathāgata attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi upon this throne.

At that time, the lifespan of human beings was ten thousand years, and they practiced the ten unwholesome paths, such as killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, frivolous speech, covetousness, malice, and wrong views.

During those hundred years, that Tathāgata sat at the site of enlightenment and preached the Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas, the celestial kings, and those among the inhabitants of Jambudvīpa who had planted roots of virtue in the past; as for the remaining sentient beings, he waited until their roots of goodness had matured.

At that time, there was a king named Prabhāsa. Then, the people of that realm practiced the ten unwholesome paths; they were greedily attached to the five desires and committed various evils. They remained far removed from wholesome dharmas, were unfilial toward their parents, and showed no respect for śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas. Countless sentient beings violated the laws of the king’s governance, were imprisoned in dungeons, and endured all manner of tortures and agonies.

“At that time, that king had a crown prince named Shanfu (Well-Subdued), who was exceptionally handsome and possessed of exquisite beauty, endowed with twenty-eight of the marks of a Great Man. While staying in the inner palace surrounded by court ladies, he heard the cries of suffering and torment from those prisoners; having heard them, he became distressed and gave rise to a heart of great compassion.”

Entering that prison, he saw the various offenders—naked, with disheveled hair, bound and flogged, wailing in grief with streaming tears, enduring immeasurable and bitter agony. Having seen this, the Prince gave rise to a heart of great compassion and comforted them, saying:
"Do not fear!"
"Do not fear!
I am now able to bring you all liberation.
Thereupon, the Prince went to the King's presence and said:
"Great King! May you grant fearlessness to the offenders within the prison; out of compassion, we pray that you will graciously show them mercy and pardon.
At that time, the Great King summoned his ministers and deliberated together on how this matter should be handled.
The ministers replied:

"Those criminals have stolen official property, plotted to assassinate Your Majesty, and violated the palace women; having committed such crimes, they must certainly be executed. If one were to rescue them, the penalty for that offense should likewise be death."
At that time, because the Prince’s great compassion was profound and reached its limit in his desire to rescue and protect them, he spoke these words:

“I shall take upon myself the various tortures for the sake of these prisoners. I pray that you punish me with suffering; for I would not spare my own body or life in order to save them, desiring that all these offenders may attain complete liberation. Why is this? Because—”
If I do not rescue these sentient beings, how can I deliver those within the prison of the triple world?

All sentient beings within the prison of birth and death are entangled by craving and attachment, obscured by ignorance, and undergo various sufferings. Their physical forms are base and ugly, their minds are constantly dissolute, and they are unable to know the path to liberation. Lacking the light of wisdom, they are attached to the various realms of phenomena; devoid of merit and insight, they are far removed from true knowledge. Bound by the defilements of fetters and stains, they are confined in the dark prison of suffering, following along with evil Māras. Constantly oppressed by the anxieties of birth, old age, sickness, and death, how shall I cause them to attain liberation?
"I should now sacrifice my own life to rescue them.
At that time, the five hundred ministers all raised their voices and said:
"Great King!..."

"You should know that according to the Prince's intent, releasing the prisoners from jail would destroy the royal law and endanger us; if the Prince is not punished, the kingdom will not stand for long!"

Upon hearing these words, the king immediately gave vent to his wrath and ordered the prince to be executed. When the queen heard of this, she disfigured her appearance and humbled herself; accompanied by a thousand court ladies, she rushed to the king’s presence, prostrated herself at his feet, and entreated him thus:
"Great King!..."
"You should know that the Crown Prince has committed an offense; I pray you will show compassion and grant him his life!
At that time, the Great King summoned the Crown Prince. Once the Prince had arrived, he spoke again to the King, saying:
"I pray you will graciously pardon those prisoners suffering in jail; if you do not show mercy, I shall suffer in their stead."
The King said, "As you wish!

At that time, the Prince immediately entered the prison, released all the criminals, and took their agonizing punishments upon himself. He never once felt regret; with single-minded right mindfulness, he took great compassion as his foremost principle for the benefit of all sentient beings through the knowledge of all modes.

The queen said to the king, "I pray that you will permit the prince to go abroad for half a month to practice giving and cultivate merit; thereafter, he may be subjected to lawful and rigorous punishment according to your will.
The king immediately granted his permission.

At that time, to the north of the capital city, there was a great forest named Sūryaprabha. The Prince went there and established a great assembly for giving; he gave food to those who needed food, clothing to those who needed clothing, and even vehicles, flower garlands, ointments, powdered incense, banners, streamers, silk canopies, and all other kinds of precious ornaments. When the set period had come to an end, [he continued his giving].
At that time, the king, along with his various ministers, elders, householders, men and women, great and small, as well as all the non-Buddhists, gathered together like clouds.
At that time, the Tathāgata Dharmacakra-ghoṣa-gaganapradīpa, knowing that the time had come to transform all sentient beings, was accompanied by a great assembly; surrounded by celestial kings,
honored by dragon kings, protected by yakṣa kings,
and praised by gandharva kings.
The asura kings paid homage and attended upon him;
the garuḍa kings, with pure minds, scattered various kinds of precious jewels;
and the kiṃnara kings joyfully offered praise and made offerings to the buddhas of the past.
The Mahoraga King, weeping with compassion, practiced right contemplation;
surrounded by such an immeasurable multitude of followers before and behind him, he came to that assembly.

At that time, the Prince and the great multitude saw from afar the Buddha approaching—dignified and extraordinary, his faculties serene and stilled, like a great elephant king whose spiritual mind was clear, pure, and bright.

Like a deep ocean, it manifests the sovereign realm of the Tathāgata, with supreme and wondrous merits, a body adorned with the primary and secondary marks, and perfect radiance that universally illumines all things and causes the infinite worlds of the ten directions to tremble.

From every pore, there universally issued subtle clouds of the Tathāgata’s fragrance and a universal rain of various clouds of adornments; practicing the majestic deportment of a Buddha, they extinguished the afflictions of all sentient beings.
At that time, having beheld the Tathāgata, the Prince was filled with immeasurable joy; prostrating himself with his five limbs touching the ground, he joined his palms and said:
"Welcome, World-Honored One!"
"Please take pity on me and accept me; I only pray that the World-Honored One will occupy this maṇi throne.
Then, the assembly of bodhisattvas all took their places upon the precious seats, surrounding him on every side.

When the Buddha had sat down, he extinguished the suffering and afflictions of all sentient beings, freeing them from all hindrances and obscurations so that they became worthy vessels for the Dharma of the Sages.
"At that time, the Tathāgata, knowing those among the sentient beings who were ready to be transformed, expounded for them the *Sūtra on the Perfect Causes and Conditions*.

Then, having heard the True Dharma, eighty nayutas of sentient beings in that great assembly all gave rise to the stainless, pure Dharma-eye and attained the stage of No-More-Learning (*aśaikṣa*). Ten thousand sentient beings attained the Mahāyāna path, fulfilling the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; they beheld the Buddhas of the ten directions turning the wheel of the True Dharma and manifested sovereign power. Sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within a hundred Buddha-worlds became endowed with the Mahāyāna, extinguishing the suffering and hardships of the evil realms for immeasurable sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions, and causing them to be reborn in the realms of gods and humans."
At that time, that prince attained the Dharma-door of awakening and nurturing the roots of goodness in sentient beings through appropriate transformation.
O Son of the Buddha!
At that time, could that prince have been anyone else?
I am that very person!
Toward all sentient beings, I have given rise to great compassion to universally benefit them;

I do not cling to the triple world, nor do I seek fame or karmic rewards. I have abandoned arrogance and do not look down upon others; I do not inflict evil upon them, nor do I crave wealth or profit. Having distanced myself from the three realms of existence (*tridhātu*), I adorn the Mahāyāna, open the gateway to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and universally practice the immeasurable deeds of a bodhisattva.
“O Son of the Buddha!
At that time, I attained this Dharma-gate.
Those who were the ministers at that time are now these five hundred wicked men, the followers of Devadatta.”

The Buddha has taught and transformed all those people, causing them to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; after passing through future eons as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, they shall attain equal and perfect enlightenment.
The worlds in which they dwell shall all be named Jewel Light (*Ratnaprabhā*);

yet their realms’ adornments, their parents and lineages, their conception and birth, their renunciation of home to study the Way, their proceeding to the site of enlightenment, their turning of the wheel of the true Dharma, their preaching of sūtras, their speech and voices, their radiance, their retinues, their lifespans, the duration of their teachings, and even their names, shall all be entirely different.
The first of those Buddhas was named Moon of Benefit;
the second Buddha was named Great Compassionate Lion;
the third Buddha was named Savior and Protector of Sentient Beings.
Finally, the Tathāgata was named the Great King of Physicians.
"O Son of the Buddha!

You should know that those original sinners whom I saved were none other than the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, beginning with Krakucchanda, as well as millions of asaṃkhyeya great Bodhisattvas. At the place of the Buddha Immeasurable Diligence, Wondrous Virtue, and Wisdom, they resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. They are all currently present in the lands of the ten directions, practicing the bodhisattva path and cultivating it ever more extensively. It is these ones who, manifesting transformations according to the needs of beings, awaken sentient beings and nurture the roots of goodness through this Dharma-gate."
O Son of the Buddha!
The King Victorious Light of that time is none other than the great master of debate, Saccaka Nigaṇṭhaputta, who is present here now.

Those who were the king’s palace attendants and kinsmen at that time are these sixty thousand disciples of the Nigaṇṭhas who came together with their teacher to debate the Dharma with the Buddha; they were all subdued by him and received the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
"These people shall all attain perfect enlightenment; the names of their worlds, eons, and titles will all be different. Son of the Buddha!

At that time, after I had saved those who were subject to retribution, my parents permitted me to renounce my kingdom, wife, children, and kinsmen. I went forth from home to study the Path under the Buddha Dharmacakra-nirghoṣa-gaganapradīpa. For five hundred years, I purely cultivated the Brahma-conduct. During this interval, I attained ten thousand samādhis, ten thousand dhāraṇī-doors, ten thousand vidyās, ten thousand dharma-treasuries, ten thousand instances of courageous and diligent *sarvajñatā*, ten thousand doors of pure patience, ten thousand gates of tranquil extinction (*śamatha*), and ten thousand skillful means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, each manifesting before me throughout the ten directions."

They behold ten thousand Tathāgatas and give birth to ten thousand great vows of Bodhisattvas; they nurture ten thousand powers of Bodhisattvas and attain ten thousand supernormal knowledges of Bodhisattvas.
In every thought-moment, they travel individually through ten thousand Buddha-fields in the ten directions;
in every thought-moment, they individually recollect ten thousand oceans of Buddhas in the ten directions.
He saw that Tathāgata’s ocean of ten thousand emanations traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings;

in every thought-moment, he saw the sentient beings of ten Buddha-worlds passing from death here to birth there within the various realms of existence—whether handsome or ugly, whether going to good destinations or entering evil paths—and he clearly and thoroughly understood the minds of those beings, their mental factors, the activities of their thoughts and intentions, as well as the oceans of their faculties, their karmic actions, and their roots of goodness.
“O Son of the Buddha!
At that time, after my life had ended, I was immediately reborn within a royal palace in that same Jambudvīpa as a wheel-turning monarch.”
After the Tathāgata Dharmacakranirghoṣagaganapradīpa had entered parinirvāṇa, I protected the True Dharma at that time;
subsequently, I encountered the Buddha Dharmagaganasumateśvara;
and later, as a king of the Śākya clan, I encountered the Buddha Devagarbha at that very place of enlightenment.
Next, he became the King of the Yama Heaven, where in that world he encountered the Buddha Mountain of Great Earth Merit;
he further encountered the Buddha King of the Sound of the Dharma-Wheel’s Radiance;
next, he became the King of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, where in that world he encountered the Buddha King of Wisdom-Lamp of Space.
Next, he became a king of the asuras, where in that world he encountered the Buddha King of the Thunderous Roar of All Dharmas;
next, he became a king of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods, where in that world he encountered the Buddha Indestructible Power Banner;
next, he became a Brahma king, where in that world he encountered the Buddha Universal Radiance of the Wheel-Dharma Transformation.
"O Son of the Buddha!
In that world of Jewel Light, during the eon called Good Light, ten thousand Tathāgatas appeared in the world, all of whom I encountered.
Following that, there was another eon named Sunlight, in which sixty billion Buddhas appeared in the world."

At that time, I was a king named Mahāprajña; I encountered the Buddha Lakṣaṇaguṇaparvata at the very beginning, and later encountered the Buddha Susvara. Next, as a great minister, I encountered the Buddha Vimalakumāra; next, as an asura king, I encountered the Buddha Vikrāntavīrya, and later encountered the Buddha Pariniṣṭhitalakṣaṇa. Next, as a merchant, I encountered the Buddha Vimalabāhu; next, as a city goddess, I encountered the Buddha Siṃhagati; next, as the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, I encountered the Buddha Devamaulī; next, as a gandharva king, I encountered the Buddha Dharmottaranāman; and next, as a kumbhāṇḍa king, I encountered the Buddha Prabhāsamukuṭa, to whom I paid homage and made offerings.
O Son of the Buddha!
I have received bodies in various realms of existence to make offerings to sixty billion such Buddhas;
at the abode of each and every Buddha, I have taught and transformed immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.

At each and every Buddha’s abode, I attained various gates of samādhi, various gates of dhāraṇī, and became fully endowed with all forms of eloquence, various wisdoms, and various lights of Dharma that illuminate the oceans of the ten directions and the oceans of all Buddha-fields. I beheld the oceans of Buddhas as if they were within a single kalpa;
I encountered those Buddhas and paid them respectful offerings.

Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of worlds, whenever Buddhas appeared in all worlds, I encountered them all, paid them respectful offerings, heard their teachings and received them, protected the True Dharma, and likewise cultivated this Dharma-gate in the presence of those Buddhas.
At that time, the Night Goddess Praṇidhānavīryaprabhā-rakṣā-sattva, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
"With a heart of joy and reverence, you have been able to inquire about the profound Dharma;
I shall now, relying on the power of the Buddha, explain it to you in detail."
Beyond the inconceivable, through kalpas as numerous as the atoms within oceans of worlds,
there was at that time a kalpa named Fine Light. At that time, there was a world named Jewel Light.
In that world, ten thousand Buddhas appeared in the world.
I encountered all those Buddhas, revering and making offerings to them all;
in the presence of those Tathāgatas, I practiced this Dharma-gate.
At that time there was a royal capital named Lovely and Delightful;
it was vast, entirely level and regular, and adorned with all manner of wonders.
Sentient beings arose with diverse conducts, and the world contained both purity and defilement.
At that time, those sentient beings practiced unwholesome dharmas in great measure.
Then there was a great king named Prasenajit,
who ruled the world with the True Dharma and maintained an impartial mind toward all.
That king had a crown prince named Shanfu (Well-Subdued),
who was upright, dignified, and exceedingly beautiful, his body adorned with the marks of excellence.
At that time, among the people, there were those who had violated the king’s laws.
Imprisoned within the jail, the Prince rescued them all.
At that time, the ministers together addressed the Great King, saying:
"The Prince intends to bring harm to Your Majesty; it is fitting that he be subjected to severe punishment."
At that time, the king followed his minister’s words and punished the crown prince according to the law.
The ministers escorted the prince to the place of execution.
Having heard this, the queen came before the great king and said:
"I pray that you grant me fifteen days to practice giving and cultivate merit.
The King immediately granted his permission, allowing him to perform meritorious deeds;
he provided him with all that he desired, including fine foods and vehicles.
The appointed day having ended, as he was about to be led to the place of execution,
all the multitude at that time were moved with grief and wept aloud.
Then the Tathāgata Ākāśapradīpa, with a voice like the sound of the Wheel of Dharma, [spoke].
Knowing that the faculties of the assembly were mature, he went to where the great multitude was gathered.
Manifesting his power of mastery, he expounded the Perfect Sūtra;
to immeasurable sentient beings, he bestowed the prediction of their future enlightenment.
At that time, the prince immediately resolved his mind upon Bodhi, vowing:
"May I fully deliver and liberate all living beings.
He made offerings to that Tathāgata and then followed the Buddha forth from home.
With the power of courageous diligence, they single-mindedly seek the unsurpassed path.
Endowed with this Dharma-door, they regard sentient beings with great compassion;
knowing the true nature of phenomena, they cultivate bodhi for oceans of kalpas.
All the Teachers who have appeared in succession throughout the world,
I have honored them all with reverence, making offerings and upholding the Dharma.
Throughout all kalpas, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of lands, I have done so.
When the Tathāgata appeared in the world, I venerated and made offerings to him all with reverence.
It was I who was "Well-Subdued," who cultivated the mind of great compassion, and who,
disregarding my own body and life, rescued and protected those suffering people.
Having attained this Dharma-gate, I have constantly practiced it throughout oceans of kalpas;
in every thought-moment, immeasurable merits have fully increased.
Whatever supreme beings I have encountered, they have skillfully explained [this] for me.
Having heard it, I immediately practiced this dharma-gate of quiescence.
Having cultivated this inconceivable dharma-gate for immeasurable eons,
I have drunk in its entirety the ocean of nectar that the Buddha has rained down.
Relying upon this dharma-gate, one travels universally through the realms of the ten directions,
discerning in a single thought all the buddha-fields of the three periods of time.
By means of this dharma-gate, one beholds the ocean of Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Before all the Most Victorious Ones, they manifest their bodies like flashes of lightning.
By virtue of this dharma-gate, they go everywhere to the Buddhas of the ten directions,
each manifesting great supernormal powers and the sublime, wondrous methods of majestic deportment.
By relying on this Dharma-gate, one is able to pose inquiries as vast as the ocean,
and hear and uphold what is taught by the inconceivable Buddhas.
By relying on this Dharma-gate, throughout the worlds of the ten directions...
Within the great assemblies of all Buddhas, they manifest spiritual transformations with sovereign ease.
By means of this Dharma-gate, they manifest various form-bodies;
within a single body, they can manifest the bodies of all Buddhas.
By virtue of this Dharma-gate, from each and every pore,
he emits a great ocean of light, removing the afflictions of sentient beings.
By virtue of this Dharma-gate, from each and every pore...
Manifesting immeasurable bodies of transformation, The rain of Dharma saves all sentient beings.
This Dharma is inconceivable; It is that which Bodhisattvas cultivate and study.
Abiding by this Dharma-gate, They practice throughout all future kalpas.
Eliminating all false views, they transform sentient beings according to their needs,
causing them all to dwell securely in the ground of all-knowledge.
Manifesting various bodies within inconceivable realms, they appear in manifold forms.
According to those who are to be transformed, he expounds the Dharma for them. "O Son of the Buddha! I have only accomplished this Dharma gate;

yet the great Bodhisattvas transcend the world, universally illuminating all realms of existence, and are able to thoroughly exhaust all spheres of experience. They shatter the mountains of obstacles, penetrate the characteristics of phenomena, and through skillful means, distinguish all dharmas. Having realized the selflessness of phenomena, they gather and transform sentient beings, delivering them across. They fully comprehend the dharma-realm of the three periods of time and are well-versed in the ocean of all paths of language. How could I possibly enter such a great ocean of wisdom, the sovereign Dharma gate of samādhi and liberation within the realm of great wisdom?"
"Good son! In this Jambudvīpa, there is a grove named Lumbinī, where there is a goddess named Guṇakāraṇḍavyūhā.
Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva practice the bodhisattva conduct?'"
Are you born into the family of the Tathāgatas?
Are you a lamp for the world?
Will you cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all future kalpas with a mind free from weariness?
Then, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in reverent salutation at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her, and took his leave.

At that time, Sudhana reflected with right mindfulness upon the instructions of that night goddess; he practiced and cultivated the dharma-gate for awakening sentient beings according to their needs and nurturing their roots of goodness.

Traveling by stages, he arrived at that forest and searched everywhere for the Forest Deity Perfectly Endowed with Wondrous Virtue. He saw her seated atop a pavilion made of various jewels, surrounded by twenty thousand nayutas of devas, preaching the Sutra of the Ocean of Bodhisattva Births, which causes one to be born into the family of the Tathāgatas and nurtures the merits of a bodhisattva.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself at her feet and said: "O Devī!
I have already set my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. How should a bodhisattva practice the conduct of a bodhisattva?"
"Are you born into the family of the Tathāgata?
Are you a lamp for the world? He replied:
“O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten ways for Bodhisattvas to take birth.

If there are Bodhisattvas who practice these methods, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas; in every thought-moment, they nurture their roots of goodness, remaining without regression, without fear, without affliction, without distraction, without indolence, and without regret, until they reach all-knowledge, accord with the Dharma-realm, and cultivate the path of liberation.”

Within a single thought-moment, one nurtures all the pāramitās, abandons the mundane world, and becomes fully endowed with the fierce and powerful wisdom of the Buddha-stage; the Buddha-dharma manifests before them, they accord with the true meaning, and they fulfill sarvajñā.
What are these ten? They are as follows:
the method for the birth of Bodhisattvas through the treasury of vows as vast as space, which consists in making offerings to all Buddhas;
The method for the birth of the Bodhisattva Śākhākośaparipūrṇabodhicitta;
the method for the birth of the Bodhisattva Gaganagarbha-vyavalokana-pratyakṣopāya-śānti;
and the method for the birth of the Bodhisattva Tryadhvakośa-samantāvabhāsa-viśuddhārjava-citta.
The method for the birth of the Bodhisattva Universal Illumination of All Treasuries;
the method for the birth of the Bodhisattva Treasury of Birth in the Family of the Tathāgata;
the method for the birth of the Bodhisattva Treasury of the Power of the Buddha’s Radiance;
The method for the birth of Bodhisattvas who possess the treasury of the gateways to the discernment of omniscience (*sarvajñā*);
the method for the birth of Bodhisattvas who possess the treasury of the adornments manifested throughout the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
and the method for the birth of Bodhisattvas who, through courageous diligence, reach the ground of the Buddhas.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the method for making offerings to all Buddhas, the skillful means of the treasury of vows as vast as space, and the dharma of taking birth?
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva makes such a vow:”

I shall reverently make offerings to all Buddhas; with immeasurable joy, I shall behold the Buddhas without weariness, possessing indestructible faith, accumulating merit, and making offerings to the Buddhas with a mind that knows no satiety.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the method for the first birth, which serves as the initial gateway to *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge) for the purpose of nurturing the roots of goodness.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the dharma of taking birth within the treasury of branches that fulfill the bodhicitta?
It is when this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings through the arousal of great compassion;
and encounters the Buddha-mind by constantly seeing the Buddhas.
Because they seek the True Dharma without any sense of惜 (regret or attachment);
because their mind of great adornment is directed toward *sarvajñā* (omniscience);
and because they give rise to a mind of great compassion that universally covers and gathers in all sentient beings.
The mind that does not abandon any sentient being, because it is adorned with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) and is indestructible;
the mind free from flattery and crookedness, because it attains true wisdom;
the mind that acts according to what is taught, because it attains the path of the bodhisattva.
The mind that does not deceive any Buddha, because it fulfills the great vows of all Buddhas;
the mind that resolves upon great vows for the sake of *sarvajñā* (omniscience), because it teaches and transforms all sentient beings of the future—
through the fulfillment of such branches of the bodhicitta, as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, one is born into the family of the Tathāgata.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the second method of taking birth.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the method for manifesting birth within the Dharma-realm of the Treasury of Space through the observation of cessation?
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva observes with a mind that contemplates the ocean of all dharmas as cessation;
with a tireless mind that ultimately fulfills the path to omniscience;
A mind that is the ocean of karma of right mindfulness toward wholesome dharmas;
a pure mind that is the ocean of all bodhisattvas’ samādhis;
a mind endowed with all the virtues of all bodhisattvas.
The mind that gives birth to the path of adornment for all bodhisattvas;
the tireless mind of courageous diligence throughout immeasurable eons;
and the mind that gives birth to the conduct of Samantabhadra to transform all sentient beings.
Skillfully training in majestic deportment and abiding in the virtues of a bodhisattva, one realizes that all states of existence are entirely without a mind.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the third dharma for taking birth.
“O Son of the Buddha! What is the method of taking birth by universally illuminating the treasury of the three periods of time with a pure and upright mind?

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva illuminates the Buddha’s bodhi with the realm of a pure and upright mind, deeply entering the ocean of the Bodhisattva’s methods of skillful means. With a profound mind as indestructible as a diamond, he turns his back on all realms of existence within the cycle of birth and death and turns toward all Buddhas. Possessing sovereign power, he proceeds upon the various supreme paths, increasing the faculties of a Bodhisattva. His stainless, pure mind is immovable; he nurtures great vows and is constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas. He shatters and disperses all mountains of obstacles, acting as a refuge for all sentient beings.”
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the fourth dharma of taking birth.
"O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the dharma of taking birth that universally illumines all treasuries? This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is fully endowed with skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings;

they do not crave wealth or profit, but relinquish everything with a pure mind. They maintain immeasurable pure precepts, abide in the realm of the Buddhas, and are fully endowed with the dharma of patience, attaining the patience of all Buddhas. With the light of the dharma, they are courageous and diligent, reaching the ultimate limit of the realm of all-knowledge. They cultivate the various *dhyānas* and are fully endowed with the wisdom of the pure, perfect, and universal gate *samādhi*. With the bright sun of clear wisdom, they universally illumine the *dharmadhātu*; they obtain unimpeded eyes and behold the oceans of all Buddhas. They penetrate deeply to the very source of all dharmas, are praised by the wise, cause sentient beings to rejoice, cultivate the true Dharma, and perceive the mark of reality.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the fifth dharma of taking birth.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the method for taking birth in the treasury of the Tathāgata’s family?

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is born into the family of the Tathāgatas and, following the teachings of all Buddhas, becomes fully endowed with all profound Dharma-gates. They share the same great vows as all Buddhas of the three periods of time, the same roots of goodness as all Buddhas of the three periods of time, and the same Dharma-body as all Buddhas of the three periods of time. Having distanced themselves from the world and turned toward the supramundane path, they nurture pure and white dharmas, abide in the Dharma-gate of great merit, attain the Buddha-sustaining samādhi, and behold all Tathāgatas. According to those who should be transformed, they purify all sentient beings; they do not abandon their great vows, and having heard the Dharma, they receive and uphold it.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the sixth dharma of taking birth.
"O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the dharma for taking birth through the treasury of the power of the Buddha’s light?

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva penetrates deeply into the powers of the Buddha and travels throughout the ten directions, making offerings to all Buddhas without weariness of mind. They know that all phenomena are like illusions and dreams, that form is like a flash of lightning, and that they are accomplished as transformations; they possess mastery over the supernormal powers and clear insights.
They know that all births and destinies are like shadows.
To know that all the wheels of Dharma turned by all Buddhas are entirely like echoes, and to exhaustively expound the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the seventh dharma of taking birth.
“O Son of the Buddha!
What is the method of taking birth through the treasury of the gateways for discerning the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñatā*)?
This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, while in the body of a youth, dwells in the Bodhisattva-abodes and contemplates *sarvajñatā*, observing each and every gateway of wisdom throughout immeasurable eons.”

Eons may yet come to an end, but the gateways of all wisdom can never be exhausted. Ultimately, within the sovereign realm of the Bodhisattva’s various samādhi-gateways, in every thought-moment they reach the abodes of the Buddhas of the ten directions. They enter the realm of the indestructible samādhi—the boundless realm of indestructible dharmas and indestructible wisdom—thereby attaining that which is no-realm, yet fully possessing even the slightest realm. They attain the ineffable stage; within the immeasurable, they attain measurable dharmas. They know that all worldly names are merely provisional designations, and they discern all phenomena of speech.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the eighth dharma of taking birth.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the dharma of taking birth in the treasury of the adornments manifested from the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*)?

This bodhisattva mahāsattva adorns immeasurable buddha-fields with various ornaments; as a Buddha who has perfected the transformation bodies for the sake of sentient beings, he relies on neither the response body nor the transformation body, but manifests through the pure transformation of the Dharma. He traverses the entirety of the unobstructed realm of phenomena, manifesting his form before those who are ready to be transformed, teaching them the various practices of bodhisattvas, and skillfully giving rise to the gateway to omniscience—the treasury of pure wisdom—which is free from all obstacles. Thus he teaches and transforms sentient beings, never missing the proper time.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is the ninth dharma of taking birth.
O Son of the Buddha!"
What is the dharma of taking birth through the courageous diligence that reaches the treasury of the Buddhas?

This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva receives the dharma of empowerment from all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; they are without obstruction regarding the spheres of all worlds. The Bodhisattva fully knows the deaths and births of sentient beings throughout the three periods of time as they pass from one life to another, and practices the conduct of a Bodhisattva. They know the sequential arising of the minds of all sentient beings;
they know the sequence of the successive attainment of perfect enlightenment by the Buddhas of the three periods of time; and through skillful means, they know the sequence of the dharmas.

They know the sequential formation and destruction of all kalpas, manifesting adornments according to the needs of sentient beings; they manifest the sequence of attaining equal and perfect enlightenment, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, and teaching and transforming immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
This is the tenth method of taking birth.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in these dharmas, they adorn all Buddha-fields for immeasurable billions of kalpas; they teach and transform sentient beings through immeasurable oceans of dharma and immeasurable realms; they awaken to the infinite currents of the various Dharma-realms; they manifest the inconceivable, space-like, profound Dharma-realms of all Buddhas; they gather in sentient beings through immeasurable practices; they manifest the turning of the wheel of Dharma; they protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma in all worlds; and throughout all realms, with subtle and wondrous voices, they proclaim unspeakable clouds of the Buddhas' true Dharma. Abiding in all Dharma-gates, they proceed toward the path of non-obstruction; adorning the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) with all dharmas, they manifest as Buddhas appearing in the world according to those who are to be saved, teaching and maturing boundless sentient beings.
At that time, the deity of that forest, wishing to clarify this meaning further,
spoke in verse: "With a pure and upright mind, First making such a vow,
One sees all Buddhas everywhere, Making offerings without ever being satiated."
All the Buddha-fields of the three periods of time are completely pure and adorned;
with a mind adorned by vows, they deliver all living beings.
They cultivate the dharma of quiescent extinction, yet their minds never know satiety.
Unobstructed throughout the three periods of time, with body and mind like empty space;
deeply entering the ocean of great compassion, with a mind as upright as Mount Sumeru;
exhausting the ocean of great wisdom—such a one is a hero among men.
Great compassion covers all, expanding the ocean of the various perfections;
teaching and transforming all living beings—this is the Unsurpassed One.
Knowing the true nature of phenomena, he is born into the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Having reached the ultimate ocean of all dharmas, such a one is a possessor of wisdom.
With a pure and wondrous Dharma-body, their mind is free from obstruction;
their own body fills the ten directions, fully endowed with the powers of a Tathāgata.
Within profound wisdom, they have attained the power of mastery;
single-mindedly seeking all-knowledge, they reach the ultimate ocean of samādhi.
They adorn and purify all Buddha-fields and transform and guide all sentient beings.
Manifesting sovereign power— this is called adornment.
Entering deeply into the supreme powers, nurturing all-knowledge (sarvajñā),
And being unobstructed within the dharma-realm (dharmadhātu)— such a one is a true son of the Buddha.
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are endowed with these ten dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgatas and become lamps for the world.
O Son of the Buddha!”
"I have accomplished this Dharma-gate of sovereign mastery over immeasurable realms. At that time, Sudhana said, "O Deva!"
"What is the scope of this dharma-gate? He replied:
"O Son of the Buddha!..."

I have fully perfected all the great vows for the rebirths of Bodhisattvas; therefore, by the power of my original vows, I have come to be born in this forest, maintaining right mindfulness of the Dharma of the Bodhisattva’s rebirth.
A hundred years later, when the Bodhisattva descended from the Tuṣita Heaven to take birth, there were ten kinds of auspicious signs within this grove at that time. What are these ten?
First, this forest suddenly became vast and expansive, its ground as level as the palm of a hand.
Second, the earth, stones, and various impurities were transformed into vajra, adorned with myriad wonders.
Third, rows of precious sāla trees stand in circumference around it.
Fourth, at that time, the powdered aloeswood incense within this grove surpasses all the various adornments of the devas.
Fifth, all manner of exquisite flower garlands and precious ornaments are completely filled [with light].
Sixth, from within the various jewel trees, all kinds of wondrous jewels naturally flow forth.
Seventh, lotus flowers emerged from within the waters of all the ponds.

Eighth, at that time, the various devas of the desire and form realms, as well as nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas of this Sahā world, paid respectful homage and stood with palms joined.
Ninth, the daughters of the devas, up to the daughters of the mahoragas, bearing articles of offering, stood to one side with palms joined in reverent salutation.

Tenth, from the uṣṇīṣas of all Buddhas in the ten directions, a light was emitted called "The Sovereign Lamp of the Bodhisattva’s Birth," which universally illuminated this grove; within each and every one of those lights, there appeared the sovereign power of all Buddhas’ births, the sovereign power of their renunciation, and the sovereign power of all bodhisattvas’ merits, while further issuing forth the subtle and wondrous voices of the Tathāgatas.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of auspicious signs in the grove.
When these signs appear, the celestial kings and others know that a Bodhisattva will surely descend to be born; seeing these omens, my joy is immeasurable."
“O Son of the Buddha!
When Lady Māyā departed from the city of Kapilavastu and entered this grove to give birth to the Prince, ten kinds of radiance spontaneously appeared;
because of these lights, all sentient beings attained the light of the Dharma.”
What are the ten? They are:
Jewel Sprout Treasury Light;
The light of all fragrances;
the light of the *padma*;
the light that issues forth subtle sounds praising the excellence of birth;
The light of the initial resolve of Bodhisattvas in the ten directions;
the light of the sovereign dharmas for all Bodhisattvas to enter the various stages;
and the light of great wisdom regarding all the pāramitās of all Bodhisattvas.
The light of the immeasurable wisdom-vows of the birth of Bodhisattvas;
the light of wisdom that skillfully transforms and delivers sentient beings;
and the light that universally illumines all Buddhas throughout the entire Dharma-realm—receiving conception and birth, renouncing home to study the Way, and attaining perfect enlightenment.
"O Son of the Buddha!
These are the ten kinds of light; these lights universally illumine the minds of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!"
While Queen Māyā was seated beneath a Pārijātaka tree in this grove, she manifested ten kinds of mastery over birth as a bodhisattva.
What are these ten?

At that time, all the celestial kings, sons, and daughters of the desire realm, as well as the devas of the form realm, along with nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, together with their retinues, all gathered like clouds in order to make offerings to that bodhisattva.

"At that time, Lady Māyā emitted a wondrous light of sublime color born of great merit, which universally illumined all things; all other lights were eclipsed and did not appear, becoming like a mass of ink. It extinguished all the afflictions of sentient beings and all the sufferings of the evil realms. Furthermore, from every pore she emitted a great radiance that universally illumined the ten directions without obstruction; this is the Bodhisattva’s first mastery of birth."
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

Within the womb of Lady Māyā, the entire trichiliocosm can be fully accommodated, and she can further manifest ten billion sets of four continents. Within those ten billion Jambudvīpas, the royal capitals, imperial cities, and the gardens where they dwell each have different names;
Lady Māyā sits everywhere throughout them, surrounded by the devas, manifesting inconceivable mastery of wisdom. This is the Bodhisattva’s second mastery of birth.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

Within each and every pore of Lady Māyā, there appear the Tathāgatas as they were practicing the bodhisattva path in past lives, reverently honoring, respecting, and making offerings to all Buddhas. The true Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas is heard entirely within her pores, just as the images of the sun and moon are seen in a clear mirror or in the water of a pure pond.

It is likewise with the pores of Lady Māyā: the Tathāgatas appearing as they practiced the bodhisattva path in past lives, reverently honoring, respecting, and making offerings to all Buddhas, and the true Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas—all are heard therein. This is the third mastery of birth of a Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

Within each and every pore of Lady Māyā, there appear the Tathāgatas throughout all worlds of the past—in cities, villages, mountain forests, rivers, ponds, and all such places—performing the practices of a bodhisattva. All matters such as the Buddhas encountered during those various kalpas, their pure roots of goodness, their lifespans, their names, and their spiritual friends are all clearly manifested. At the time of each of those births, Lady Māyā constantly serves as their mother; this is the Bodhisattva’s fourth mastery over birth.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

Within each and every pore of Lady Māyā, there appear the physical forms, characteristics, karmic deeds, dignified deportment, and the various experiences of pleasure and pain of the Tathāgata when he was a bodhisattva in past lives. This is the fifth mastery of birth of a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

Within each and every pore of Lady Māyā, there appeared the Tathāgata’s acts of giving when he was practicing as a bodhisattva in past lives. His body, hands, feet, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, bones, teeth, marrow, brain, heart-blood, skin, flesh, wife, children, kinsmen, cities, villages, palaces, precious objects, and all internal and external things, together with all those who received them, were all clearly manifested; furthermore, the sounds of the voices of those who requested these things were heard. This is the sixth mastery of birth of a bodhisattva.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

From within the body of Lady Māyā, there universally emerge all the Buddhas of the past when they were in their final birth as Bodhisattvas. The adornments of those Buddha-fields—beings, groves, flower garlands, various incenses, ointments, powdered perfumes, and sovereign maṇi jewels for entertainment and praise—all such things fill this forest; they are all heard and seen. This is the seventh mastery of the Bodhisattva’s taking birth.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

From within the body of Lady Māyā, there further emerged the palaces of the various devas, as well as those of the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and humans—all adorned with myriad jewels, permeated by exquisite fragrances, and indestructible. Surpassing all other celestial realms, they filled this grove for the purpose of making offerings to that Bodhisattva. This is the Bodhisattva’s eighth mastery of birth.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

From within the body of Lady Māyā, there further emerge as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten unspeakably many billions of nayutas of worlds. Their bodies are adorned with physical forms, marks, and signs; their radiance is sovereign, and they and their retinues are all identical to that Rocana Buddha. Once these great beings have emerged, they praise the Bodhisattva. This is the ninth mastery of birth of the Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!

At the time of the Bodhisattva’s birth, within the diamond-wheel upon the ground before Lady Māyā, a great lotus flower arose. Its stem was made of diamond; it possessed jewel petals as numerous as the atoms of ten worlds, with a sovereign *maṇi* jewel serving as its calyx. It was draped above with fragrant garlands of various jewels and *asaṃkhyeya* nets of gems, which all the heavenly kings held up together.
All the *gandharva* kings universally rained down clouds of incense, praising the merits of the Buddhas of the past.
All the yakṣa kings surrounded and protected him, whereupon various wondrous jewel-flowers and delightful sounds spontaneously arose;
all the asura kings were completely subdued and paid homage with their heads at his feet; all the garuḍa kings adorned the void with precious silk banners;
and all the kiṃnara kings gazed upon him with joyful devotion, never wearying of their hearts, as they praised and sang hymns of the Bodhisattva’s virtues.
All the mahoraga kings, filled with joy and leaping for gladness, universally rained down clouds of various precious ornaments; this is the bodhisattva’s tenth mastery of birth.
O Son of the Buddha!

When Queen Māyā gave birth to the Bodhisattva, it was like the appearance of a bright, pure sun in the sky, like the flash of lightning, like clouds rising from a mountain, or like a lamp in the darkness. At that time, although the Bodhisattva manifested his birth, he fully understood and realized that all phenomena are like lightning and dreams—neither coming nor going, neither arising nor ceasing.
O Son of the Buddha!
Within a single thought-moment, I fully know the bodhisattvas' mastery over taking birth and mastery over manifesting birth here in this Jambudvīpa;
I likewise know their mastery over taking birth and mastery over manifesting birth throughout ten billion Jambudvīpas.

They also know the Buddha-fields equal in number to the atoms of a trichiliocosm, and the Buddha-fields equal in number to the atoms of ten Buddha-worlds, and even know all Buddha-fields equal in number to the atoms of all worlds; their mastery over the taking of birth and their mastery over manifestation as Bodhisattvas are likewise thus.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Part Thirteen of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter, the Thirty-fourth, Part Thirteen.
At that time, Sudhana said to the goddess Pūrṇaśrī:
"Goddess, how long has it been since you attained this bodhisattva dharma-door of mastery over birth?"
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred million buddha-fields, there was an eon named Pleasing Delight, and in that time there was a world named All Jewels."
In that kalpa-world, eighty nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world; the first of these Buddhas was named Invincible Sovereign Banner King (Abhedyasvairadhvajarāja).
In that world, within a single Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Adorned Banner; the king’s name was Foremost Jewel Flame Eye Light, and his queen’s name was Good Joyous Light.
Just as Lady Māyā was the mother of Vairocana Buddha in this world, so too was Lady Sukhaprabhā the mother of the primordial Tathāgata in that world.

When the noble lady Supriyaprabhā gave birth to the Bodhisattva, she went with a retinue of two million nayutas of female attendants to the Golden Grove; there, grasping a branch of a precious tree, she gave birth to that Tathāgata.
At that time, there was a nurse named Vimalaprabhā.

The various heavenly kings bathed the Prince with a mixture of fragrant waters and then carried him to present him to the nurse. The nurse received him with reverence and immeasurable joy, and she immediately attained the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Universal Eye Realm.
Having attained this samādhi, one sees the Buddhas of the ten directions without obstruction and further attains the bodhisattva dharma-gate of mastery over taking birth.
O Son of the Buddha!
Just as the initial consciousness at the moment of conception is swift and unimpeded, so too is it with the attainment of this dharma-gate: one knows the mastery of all Buddhas in taking birth.
O Son of the Buddha!
What do you think?
Could that wet nurse have been anyone other than this person?
I am that very person.

Since that time, in every thought-moment, I have constantly seen Bodhisattvas attaining mastery over the ocean of dharmas regarding their births, as well as the sovereign spiritual powers of Vairocana Buddha in his transformation and teaching of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!

In every thought-moment, I attain as many pure eyes of wisdom as there are atoms in a trichiliocosm, by which I constantly see all lands as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, as well as those Buddhas, and I know how those Tathāgatas manifest their births through sovereign power.
Furthermore, they clearly understand the initial great vows made by Vairocana Buddha, and likewise know the initial great vows made by all Buddhas of the ten directions in the same manner.
