"I also reverently made offerings to those Tathāgatas; I heard all the Dharma they preached and received, upheld, and practiced it.

At that time, the Deva of the Forest, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions. Desiring to further clarify the meaning of this "Dharma-gate of the Sovereign Birth of Bodhisattvas in All Realms," he spoke in verse:
"O Son of the Buddha, as for what you have asked— The most supreme realm of quiescence..."
Listen with single-minded attention as I now explain the causal conditions.
Beyond eons as numerous as the atoms in a billion lands, there was an eon named Pleasing Delight;
during that time, eighty nayutas of Tathāgatas appeared in the world.
The first name of the Tathāgata was Invincible Sovereign Banner.
At that time, I saw that Buddha born within a grove of golden trees;
his nursing mother was Stainless Radiance, who is none other than my own self today.
The Prince’s body is golden-hued; the Heavenly King cradled him and handed him to me.
Receiving this Unsurpassed One with reverence, I gazed upon him but could not see the crown of his head.
His perfect form is inconceivable; one never tires of beholding it.
With a stainless and pure body, adorned naturally with the marks and signs,
I beheld this wondrous jewel-image; my joy was immeasurable,
as I contemplated this inconceivable being who nurtures an ocean of merit.
Beholding that power of mastery, I have resolved upon Bodhicitta;
I seek exclusively the merits of the Buddhas, to fulfill the ocean of all vows.
I shall adorn and purify all worlds, and remain far removed from the three evil realms.
Throughout all worlds, I made offerings to all Buddhas.
Single-mindedly seeking the ocean of great vows to eliminate the suffering of sentient beings,
I heard that first teaching of the Buddha and accomplished this Dharma gate.
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of billions of lands,
I have cultivated the bodhisattva practices to adorn and purify this Dharma-gate.
All the Buddhas within those kalpas, I have made offerings to them all.
Guarding their True Dharma, they purify an ocean of dharma-gates.
For eons as numerous as the atoms within billions of lands, whenever Buddhas appear in the world,
they uphold their wheels of True Dharma and cultivate inconceivable dharma-gates.
In a single thought, they fully comprehend all the atoms of every land;
within each and every atom, they behold infinite oceans of lands.
When those Buddhas first take birth, they manifest their sovereign power.
Within a single thought-moment, I perceive them all distinctly:
inconceivable lands where those bodhisattvas dwell,
some residing in the Tuṣita heaven, single-mindedly seeking the Buddha’s enlightenment.
Within oceans of immeasurable lands, he sees those who have attained mastery over birth,
surrounded by immeasurable multitudes as they preach the Dharma for them.
Within a single thought-moment, he perceives entirely these oceans of immeasurable lands.
All the Bodhisattvas, having left the household life and proceeded to the site of enlightenment,
attained supreme perfect awakening in inconceivable lands;
manifesting various skillful means, they eliminate the suffering of sentient beings.
Within each and every atom, The inexhaustible wheel of Dharma is turned;
From an ocean of infinite sublime sounds, The nectar-like Dharma rains down everywhere.
In every single thought-moment, one sees them all, Within each and every atom.
Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in billions of lands manifest parinirvāṇa;
I see infinite oceans of lands where Tathāgatas first take birth;
At the abode of each and every Buddha, I make offerings with infinite bodies.
In inconceivable oceans of lands, for immeasurable multitudes of sentient beings,
I employ various skillful means to preach the nectar-like Dharma.
O Son of the Buddha, you should know this inconceivable gateway to the Dharma.
"Throughout immeasurable kalpas, one could never finish praising it.
'O Son of the Buddha!

I know only this Dharma-door of the Bodhisattva’s Sovereignty over Rebirth. The great Bodhisattvas are able to take all kalpas as a single thought-moment treasury, manifesting all manner of wondrous skillful means, making offerings to all Buddhas, fulfilling their great vows, awakening to all the true teachings of the Buddhas, and manifesting rebirth in all realms of existence. They are born in the presence of all Buddhas, teaching and transforming sentient beings without ever missing the proper time. For the sake of sentient beings, they manifest sovereignty over rebirth and appear as clouds of sovereign power throughout all Buddha-lands, always being born into the families of all Tathāgatas.'"
How could I possibly know or describe those virtues?
Son of the Buddha!
In the city of Kapilavastu, there is a Śākya woman named Gopī.
"Go to him and ask: How does a bodhisattva wander within the cycle of birth and death to teach and transform sentient beings?
Then, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the goddess Vanavāsī with his head, circumambulated her, took his leave, and departed for that city.

With right mindfulness, he contemplated and expanded this Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva’s mastery over birth, which is luminous and pure; gradually traveling on, he arrived at the Hall of Adorned Discourses where the assembly of bodhisattvas gathered, to the place of the goddess Viśoka-suvimala-śrī.
At that time, ten thousand devas, with that deva as their retinue, came to welcome Sudhana and said to him:
"Welcome, O person of great wisdom!"

They cultivate the inconceivable Dharma-gate of Bodhisattvas, fulfilling great vows with a pure and upright mind, extensively practicing the conduct of Bodhisattvas, heading toward the city of the True Dharma, and perfecting the immeasurable skillful means of Bodhisattvas.

I observe that you, O virtuous one, are courageous and diligent in cultivating the bodhisattva path, with a mind free from weariness, your deportment composed and your faculties subdued. Before long, you will surely attain supreme purity, adorning the Buddha’s body, speech, and mind; your body will be graced by the primary and secondary marks, and your mind will be adorned with the wisdom of the ten powers, as you travel through the ten directions to teach and transform sentient beings.

Observing your courageous and diligent power in practice, I am certain that you shall behold the Buddhas of the three periods of time, receive all the clouds of Dharma from the Tathāgatas, cultivate the bodhisattva gateways of meditative concentration and the dharma of quiescence, and enter the profound gateway of the Tathāgata’s Dharma.

Why is this? Because they approach spiritual friends, attend upon and make offerings to them, and contemplate their instructions with right mindfulness, never giving rise to a mind of regression or weariness.
"To eliminate obstacles, subdue all māras, remain indestructible by any, and cause all sentient beings to attain joy.
Sudhana replied, "As the deva has said, such is my vow!"
Desiring to cause all sentient beings to rejoice, to eliminate afflictions and all unwholesome dharmas, and to become fully endowed with wholesome dharmas so as to attain peaceful happiness;

seeing that all sentient beings, due to their various evil karmas, afflictions, and fetters, enter the three evil realms and undergo immeasurable suffering, the Bodhisattva gives rise to a heart of sorrow and compassion.

It is, for example, as if there were a man who had an only son whom he loved with deep affection; suddenly, someone comes and cuts his body, severing his limbs, joints, hands, and feet. Upon seeing this, the compassionate father feels profound sorrow and piteous grief.

If a bodhisattva sees sentient beings who, due to the conditions of their own evil karma and the fetters of afflictions, enter the three evil realms and undergo immeasurable suffering, having seen this, his heart is pained with compassion and his thoughts are likewise.

If a bodhisattva sees sentient beings who, by virtue of having performed various wholesome deeds of body, speech, and mind, are born among gods and humans and experience physical and mental bliss, and having seen this, feels immeasurable joy—why is this?

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva does not seek omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) for his own sake; he does not crave birth-and-death or the pleasures of the five desires; he does not follow mental conceptions, various inverted views, the fetters and bonds, or the craving of false views; he does not cling to the various perceptions of pleasure among sentient beings, nor does he cling to the flavor of dhyāna; thus, he is not obstructed by fetters as he transmigrates through birth-and-death.
The Bodhisattva perceives only that within the ocean of all existence, all sentient beings undergo immeasurable suffering; thus, they give rise to the vow of great compassion to gather them in.
Constantly, by the power of great compassion and great vows, they practice the bodhisattva path, making offerings to all Buddhas and seeking *sarvajñā* (omniscience);

desiring to cause sentient beings to distance themselves from afflictions, purify Buddha-fields, and subdue all sentient beings with evil minds, so that all may fully possess pure body and mind and practice the bodhisattva path without weariness.
If there are bodhisattvas who practice in this way, they are able to adorn all sentient beings, because they give rise to and nurture the happiness of devas and humans;
because they act as parents, causing all to be established in the bodhicitta;
and because they act as nurturers, causing all to ultimately perfect the bodhisattva path.
They act as guardians, causing all to remain far removed from the three evil realms;
they act as great captains, causing all to cross over the ocean of birth and death;
they act as refuges, causing all to abandon the terrors of demons and afflictions.
They act as guides, so that all may reach the state of cool serenity;
they act as those who know the crossings, so that all may be ferried across the ocean of Buddha-fields;
they act as ministers of the treasury, so that all may enter the island of the Dharma-jewels.
They are pure and exquisite flowers, because they cause the flowers of all Buddhas' merits to bloom;
they are great radiances, because they universally emit the light of merit and wisdom;
they are joy, because they render all things upright, dignified, and most sublime.
They are honored by all, because they have distanced themselves from all evil karma;
they are Samantabhadra, because they are fully endowed with all merits;
they are lamps of light, because they constantly radiate the pure and wondrous light of wisdom.
They are like auspicious clouds, for they constantly rain down all the nectar-like Dharma. O Devaputra!
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas practice in this way, all sentient beings love and cherish them, because they delight in the True Dharma.

At that time, as Sudhana was about to ascend the Dharma Hall, the goddess Viśokābhijñā, together with her retinue of one million, each carrying exquisite incense, flower garlands, and various miscellaneous jewels, scattered them over Sudhana and spoke in verse:
"In immeasurable and innumerable eons, A Lamp of the World may occasionally appear;
For the sake of all sentient beings everywhere, He rightly seeks the Bodhi of the Buddha."
Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, difficult to see and difficult to encounter,
the sun of merit has now risen, shining to dispel the darkness of the world.
Seeing all classes of sentient beings, shrouded by folly, delusion, and ignorance, [he brings forth compassion].
Extensively giving rise to the mind of great compassion, Dedicatedly seeking the teacherless Way;
With a pure and upright mind, Not begrudging body or life,
Drawing near to spiritual friends, Dedicatedly seeking the Bodhi of the Buddhas.
All things are without dependence, Not attached to the world;
With a stainless and pure mind, Unimpeded like space.
Practicing all bodhisattva deeds, Fully endowed with wondrous merit.
Emitting the great light of wisdom, It universally illumines all worlds.
Without departing from the world, Yet without being attached to the world,
It moves through the world without obstruction, Like the wind wandering through space.
Just as when a great conflagration breaks out, nothing can extinguish it,
so too is the fire of courageous diligence in seeking the Way.
With courageous and great diligence, nothing whatsoever can destroy it.
The Lion of Vajra-Wisdom wanders fearlessly;
within the ocean of all dharmas, amidst the ocean of all Buddhas,
by drawing near to spiritual friends, one swiftly beholds those Buddhas.

At that time, having praised with verses, the goddess Viśokābhijñā, out of reverence for the Dharma, ascended together to the Dharma Hall. Having ascended the Dharma Hall, she searched everywhere for that daughter of the Śākyas.

He then saw [the Bodhisattva] seated upon a lion throne within a treasury of precious lotuses, surrounded by eighty-four thousand women, all of whom were daughters of noble kings. They had all practiced various deeds under that same Bodhisattva in the past and shared all his roots of goodness. Constantly employing generosity and kind speech to gather in sentient beings, they sought omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), benefiting all, and causing all beings to attain the same enlightenment as the Buddha.
With great compassion as their foremost quality, they regard all sentient beings with the thought that each is like an only child; they cultivate great loving-kindness, which universally covers all.

In the past, they have already cultivated inconceivable, supreme, and wondrous wisdom under various bodhisattvas, attained non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and fully perfected all the *pāramitās*. Their minds are free from attachment, and their straightforward mind and wisdom are entirely pure.
Seeking *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge), they leave behind the net of hindrances and obscurations, transcend all difficulties, and attain the pure *dharmakāya*.
Practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra, they nurture all the powers of a bodhisattva and bring to fulfillment the perfect sun of pure wisdom.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself on the ground to pay homage to Gopā; having finished his prostration, he stood to one side with palms joined and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva may course within birth and death without being defiled.
How does one realize the true nature of all phenomena, transcend the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, abide in the stage of the Tathāgata, yet never abandon the practices of a bodhisattva?

How does one cultivate the bodhisattva practices without departing from the Buddha-ground, transcend the mundane world, perfect the Dharma-body, take birth in accordance with the world, and universally manifest various bodies of skillful means?
How do you know that phenomena have no intrinsic nature, yet manifest the bodies of all sentient beings; how do you understand the profound Dharma and preach it with wondrous sounds;
and how do you know that sentient beings are empty, yet are able not to abandon the transformation of all worlds?
How do they know that all Buddhas are neither born nor extinguished, yet are able to make offerings to them with minds that never regress?
How do they know that there is no karmic retribution, yet they practice wholesome deeds without ceasing?
At that time, Gopī spoke these words: “Excellent! Excellent!”
"Noble son! You are able to ask about the dharmas practiced by all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; you who cultivate the various practices and vows of Samantabhadra are indeed able to ask in this manner."
Listen attentively!
Listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well!
I shall now, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, explain this for you. Noble son,
if a bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas, they will be able to fulfill the bodhisattva practice of the Indra’s Net of Universal Wisdom Light.
What are these ten? They are: relying upon spiritual friends;

extensively making immeasurable and vast vows; cultivating purity, excellence, subtlety, and rectitude; aspiring to accumulate the merit of all-knowledge; experiencing immeasurable joy upon hearing of a Buddha’s appearance in the world; constantly delighting in dwelling in the presence of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; following along with all great Bodhisattvas; being protected and sustained by all Buddhas; possessing pure great compassion; and remaining far removed from birth and death. These are the ten dharmas.
If there are bodhisattvas who accomplish this dharma, they will be able to fulfill the bodhisattva practice of the Indra’s Net Universal Wisdom Radiance.
O Son of the Buddha!

If bodhisattvas are courageous and diligent, with minds that never regress, they will give rise to and cultivate the inexhaustible dharmas of the Buddhas because they encounter virtuous spiritual friends.
O Son of the Buddha!
There are ten dharmas by which a bodhisattva encounters virtuous spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). What are these ten?

They are as follows: not begrudging one's body or life; not seeking worldly pleasures; knowing the characteristics of all phenomena without abandoning them; the vow for omniscience; observing the dharma-realm; leaving behind the ocean of the three realms of existence; having no place of dependence or abiding; deeply entering all the vows of bodhisattvas; universally illuminating all Buddha-worlds; and purely cultivating the perfect wisdom of a bodhisattva. These are the ten dharmas for encountering a spiritual friend.
At that time, Gopī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
“Without flattery toward spiritual friends, With wisdom vast and immeasurable,
Dedicatedly seeking the Buddha’s enlightenment, One brings benefit to all sentient beings.”
Revering spiritual friends with a mind that regards them as Buddhas,
With the power of courageous diligence, one fulfills the conduct of Indra’s Net.
The mind of liberation expands and broadens, Its measure equal to empty space.
Encompassing the three periods of time, The Buddha-fields and all sentient beings;
With a mind as straight as space, Far removed from the stains of affliction;
Giving birth to the merits of a Buddha— This is the practice of the cloud-body.
With inconceivable wisdom, they have accumulated an ocean of merit;
as treasuries of pure karmic fortune, they remain unstained by the world.
In the presence of all Buddhas, they hear the Dharma without ever feeling satiated.
The lamp of wisdom shines universally; this is the practice of illuminating the world.
In a single thought-moment, one can reach the Buddhas throughout the ocean of lands in the ten directions;
hearing the Dharma and discerning it with knowledge—this is the practice of compliance.
Beholding the ocean of the Buddha’s retinue, And the ultimate ocean of samādhi,
Fulfilling all great vows— This is the practice of Indra’s Net.
Cultivating through future kalpas, One is protected and remembered by all Buddhas.
Universally illuminating all worlds—this is the practice of the light of Dharma.
Beholding sentient beings with great compassion, the sun of wisdom rises in the world;
The light of Dharma dispels the darkness of delusion—this is the practice of the sun of wisdom.
Beholding sentient beings in the various realms, Whirling in the currents of birth and death,
To turn for them the pure wheel of Dharma— This is the conduct of Samantabhadra.
With a body of wisdom that is immeasurable, He manifests in accordance with what is appropriate.
Universally throughout all realms of existence, They deliver and liberate all sentient beings.
Arousing great compassion, It universally covers all and shines upon every being,
Causing them to attain the Bodhi of the Buddhas.
“Good son! I have already accomplished the dharma-gate of the ocean-like samādhis for the analytical observation of all bodhisattvas. Sudhana said:
“Great Sage! What is the sphere of this Dharma-gate? He replied:

“Good son! Having entered this Dharma-door, I know all the good and evil of the sentient beings in this Sahā world throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field: their deaths here and births there; their performance of wholesome and unwholesome deeds and their reception of various retributions; those who wander in the path of birth and death; those of the right determination, the wrong determination, and the indeterminate; those with latent roots of goodness that are present and those with latent roots of goodness that are absent; those whose roots of goodness are complete and those whose roots of goodness are incomplete; unwholesome roots of goodness; how roots of goodness encompass unwholesome roots and how unwholesome roots encompass roots of goodness; and how they are produced from roots of goodness or produced from unwholesome roots. I fully and completely understand all such things.”
Throughout those eons, I have fully known all the Buddhas who appeared in the world;
I know how those Buddhas first resolved their minds on enlightenment, practiced the conduct of Bodhisattvas, and gave rise to the ocean of all great vows.

He knows that those [beings] make offerings to all Buddhas, fulfill the bodhisattva practices, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, turn the wheel of the true Dharma, manifest sovereign powers, and transform and deliver sentient beings.

He knows the practices of those kinsmen—śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—their cultivation of all roots of goodness in the past, their attainment of clear and pure wisdom, their accomplishment of the dharma-gate of mastery in quiescence, and their manifestation of various sovereign spiritual powers as they teach and transform sentient beings before entering parinirvāṇa.
He knew those assemblies of bodhisattvas who had first resolved their minds on the Way,
cultivated roots of goodness, brought forth various great vows and practices, and had fully accomplished the perfections;
he knew their various adornments of the bodhisattva path, the sovereign powers of the bodhisattva stages, and their dwellings within the bodhisattva stages.
Distinguishingly cultivating all bodhisattva stages, purifying the bodhisattva stages, practicing the bodhisattva stages,
the characteristics of the various bodhisattva stages, the wisdom of the various bodhisattva stages, the wisdom of the various bodhisattva integrations,
the skillful means of bodhisattvas for teaching and transforming sentient beings, the various abodes of bodhisattvas, and the complete purification of the conduct of bodhisattvas.
The sovereign conduct of bodhisattvas, the ocean of bodhisattva samādhis, and the skillful means of bodhisattvas— in every thought-moment,
they fully know the oceans of all bodhisattva samādhis, the knowledge of all modes, the lightning-flash Dharma-cloud,
the attainment of the various dharmic patiences, and the reaching of the very bottom of all-knowledge.
I fully understand all such matters as these: knowing those bodhisattvas' oceans of Buddha-lands and their ultimate oceans of Dharma;
knowing the ocean of sentient beings; and practicing all bodhisattva dharma-gates, fulfilling great vows, and manifesting various sovereign spiritual powers.

In this way, regarding the nature of worlds, world-oceans, world-circles, world-perfections, world-differentiations, world-rotations, world-turnings, world-lotuses, world-Sumerus, and the phenomena within the characteristics of worlds throughout the ten directions in this Sahā world, it is likewise so.
By the power of the original vows of Vairocana Buddha, I have deeply entered into and discerningly known them all. Why is this?
Because this Dharma-gate thoroughly knows the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings;
it knows the accumulation of roots of goodness by all sentient beings.
He knows that all sentient beings have both defilement and purity;
he knows the nature of all sentient beings;
and he knows the dharma-gates of the sovereign samādhis of all śrāvakas.
"I know the dharma-gates of mastery over samādhi belonging to all pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and buddhas; such matters as these, I know them all through detailed discernment.
Sudhana said, "O Great Sage!"
"Since you first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, how long has it been?
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!"
In the distant past, beyond eons as numerous as the atoms of worlds, there was an eon named Supreme Radiance.
At that time, there was a world named Free from Fear.
In that world there are four continents; within Jambudvīpa, there is a royal capital named Mount Sumeru of the Wondrous Virtue Tree, which is the most preeminent among eighty such royal capitals.
There was a king there named Sarvaratnādhipati.
He had sixty thousand court ladies, five hundred ministers, and five hundred princes, all of whom were handsome, brave, and strong, capable of subduing enemies.
The king’s crown prince was named Sovereign Lord of Increasing Merit (*Vardhamāna-guṇādhipati*).

His countenance was exceptionally sublime, and his body was adorned with the marks and signs of excellence. Accompanied by ten thousand court ladies, carrying exquisite banners and parasols, scattering various precious flowers, performing all kinds of music, and riding in a magnificent jeweled chariot, he went to Mount Fragrant Sprout (*Gandhāṅkura*) to sport in its groves and gardens.

At that time, the road was level and smooth, adorned in various ways; it was strewn with many exquisite flowers, lined with rows of jewel trees, and covered above by canopies of diverse wonderful gems.

By the side of that road, he piled up various treasures and gathered diverse kinds of jewels, garments, ornaments, and prepared delicacies and food; such things as these were all provided and bestowed according to whatever was required.

At that time, there was a woman named Bhadrottamā who was leading a young girl named Vimalaguṇā. She was upright, beautiful, and exquisite; her height and proportions were perfectly balanced, and her countenance was peerless. Her eyes and hair were deep blue, and her lips and teeth were crimson and white. Her voice issued from her mouth as the Brahma-sound; she was skillful in talent and eloquent in speech. Having cultivated a heart of loving-kindness, those who saw her never grew weary of the sight. With little greed, anger, or delusion, she was always possessed of a sense of shame and remorse, and her mind was free from flattery or crookedness. Riding in a magnificent jeweled chariot, surrounded by handmaidens, she followed her mother on an excursion.
Previously, when the Crown Prince went to the Incense Sprout Garden, he saw her and gave rise to a mind of defiled attachment. He spoke to his mother, saying:
"I wish to marry this virtuous woman to be my wife."
The mother said to her daughter, "The prince now wishes to seek you as his consort; what is your intention?
The daughter replied to her mother:
"If you wish to make me your consort, you must first bring about my own death.
The mother replied to her daughter,
"Do not speak such words!"

Why is this? This prince has now fully possessed all the marks of a Wheel-Turning King and will surely become a holy sovereign; he will have the precious jewel of a jade woman, and at that time you will be unable to serve him. This place is honorable and superior; do not harbor any thoughts of resistance.
At that time, outside that garden, there was a site of enlightenment named Dharmameghaprabha.
There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suprabhāsa appeared in the world and attained the unsurpassed path at that site of enlightenment.

At that time, the girl saw the body of that Tathāgata in a dream. Upon awakening from the dream, a deva in the sky addressed her, saying: "The one you saw in your dream is the Buddha Victorious Sunlight (Jaya-sūryaprabha).

It has been only seven days since he attained enlightenment, and he is currently at the site of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa), surrounded by a great assembly of immeasurable bodhisattvas. In that Buddha’s assembly, all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as ghosts and spirits—even the immeasurable devas of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, along with the earth deities, wind deities, ocean deities, fire deities, mountain deities, tree deities, and deities of groves, medicinal herbs, and city walls—all have gathered like clouds to pay homage to the World-Honored One and listen to the true Dharma."
At that time, having heard these words, the woman went to the Prince’s location, stood with palms joined, and addressed him in verse:
“My beauty is supreme in the world; My wisdom is without peer;
My talent is exquisite and my speech eloquent; Those who behold me can never tire.”
"O Prince, you should know that my mind is virtuous and pure;
my aspirations are noble and my heart is upright, stainless and undefiled.
I am far removed from anger, as well as from craving and delusion."
With a heart that is truly pure and upright, you bring benefit to all living beings.
I beheld the Prince’s body, adorned with its own marks and signs of excellence;
having seen him, my joy was immeasurable, and all my faculties were fully subdued.
His wondrous body is like pure gold; his hair is beautiful, the color of deep blue.
His forehead is broad and his eyes are clear and penetrating; he will surely become a sovereign king.
His body surpasses a mountain of gold, adorned naturally with the marks and signs of excellence.
I now stand before the Crown Prince, palms joined in reverent salutation.
His eyes are pure, long, and wide; his broad chest is like that of a lion.
Those who gaze upon him never tire of doing so; may he grant me an audience with his wondrous voice.
The mark of his tongue is broad, long, and wondrous, Like the color of refined red copper;
He utters the Brahma-voice, Which brings leaping joy to all who hear it.
His mouth is square, his tusks deep-set and firm, And his teeth are white, even, and closely set.
Should anyone behold him, all will be filled with joy.
With a stainless and pure body, endowed with the thirty-two marks—
having achieved these wondrous signs, he shall surely become a Wheel-Turning King.
At that time, the prince said to her: "Whose daughter are you?
By whom are you protected?"
"If she previously belonged to another, it would be improper for me to give rise to defiled and lustful thoughts.
At that time, the Prince spoke in verse, asking:
"With a body of pure merit, beholders can never tire of seeing it."
Who are your parents, and by whom are you protected?
If you already belong to another, I shall not give rise to desire;
should I harbor lustful thoughts toward what is not my portion, I shall fall into the evil realms at the end of my life.
One should not, for the sake of noble status, wealth, or various pleasures,
give rise to such states of mind as negligence, greed, and agitation. One should not produce various false views,
nor engage in illusions, deceptions, and all manner of flattery and hypocrisy.
Having thus committed various evils, one wanders through the world.
Toward parents and teachers, one should give rise to a heart of reverence;
with compassion that covers all extensively, one should protect every living being.
In all places, toward those from whom one hears the Dharma,
one should give rise to a mind of reverence, for they are able to produce all that is wholesome.
Toward all the Teachers and the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the True Dharma, one should likewise act.
The ocean of merit of the noble Saṃgha is entirely worthy of reverence.
Cultivating all virtues and remaining far removed from every evil,
they abide securely in the True Dharma and extensively practice the Bodhisattva path.
If there are those without refuge, one should give rise to a mind of great loving-kindness;
toward all those in the three evil realms, one should arouse thoughts of great compassion.
Within the entire realm of phenomena, whatever comes into being must inevitably perish.
Contemplate with an equanimous mind of renunciation; do not follow the demons of affliction.
You should resolve upon bodhicitta to awaken all sentient beings, practicing for immeasurable eons without giving rise to thoughts of weariness.
Then, her mother spoke in verse, saying:
"May the Prince deign to listen: From the time this girl was born Until she has now reached full maturity, I shall recount all the causes and conditions."
On the day the Prince was born, a daughter was born from a lotus flower;
her eyes were pure, long, and wide, and all her limbs and joints were perfectly formed.
Once, during the spring months, I went to stroll through the Śāla grove.
Beholding the various grasses and trees, with their manifold flowers in full and lush bloom;
seeing the eight hundred women who accompany him, all of whom are perfectly dignified and graceful in appearance,
and who have already mastered every skill and artful method.
In that garden there was a bathing pool named Samalaṃkṛtā;
seated upon its bank, surrounded by a host of court ladies,
a thousand-petaled lotus flower emerged from within that pool.
With precious petals and lapis lazuli stems, A pedestal of Jambūnada gold,
And filaments of various wondrous jewel-fragrances, It radiates pure light everywhere,
Illuminating all of Jambudvīpa, Like the sun first rising.
At that time, seeing this jade maiden born from that lotus, all who beheld her thought to themselves: "This is the retribution of virtuous karma.
Her eyes and hair are a deep azure-blue, and her body is like purple-gold.
Adorned with various jewels, those who behold him never tire of the sight.
Stainless, pure, and free from defilement, his limbs and joints are perfectly complete;
like a statue of pure gold, he dwells peacefully upon a precious lotus flower.
Sandalwood fragrance from every pore universally perfumes all;
from his mouth issues the scent of lotuses as he utters wondrous Brahma-sounds.
This is the Jewel of the Woman, rare and precious throughout the world.
Your physical marks are fully perfected, adorned with every kind of sublime ornament.
You have reached the ultimate mastery in all arts and techniques, as well as the worldly methods of discourse; we pray that you will compassionately accept us.
This is the Jewel of the Woman: her physical form is perfectly complete, adorned with every merit, obtained through the fruits of past deeds.
She thoroughly understands the maladies of sentient beings and the origins from which those afflictions arise.
Furthermore, knowing the methods of remedy, he eliminates all doubts and delusions.
Throughout the entire Jambudvīpa, regarding the languages and dialects of sentient beings and the sounds of various musical performances, there is nothing he does not skillfully master.
This woman has cultivated merit and distanced herself from the ways of women;
she is able to transform the minds of sentient beings—only pray that you will compassionately accept her.
Having abandoned the mind of jealousy, she is not intoxicated by the five desires.
Without giving rise to a mind of anger, you cultivate patience and wisdom;
with diligence you uphold the pure precepts and are able to accomplish all tasks.
Seeking exclusively after all merits, O Prince, we pray that you will accept us.
If one sees those who are impoverished, Or those oppressed by the many sufferings of old age and illness,
Having no one to rely upon, One should regard them with great compassion and universal kindness.
Always desiring to benefit sentient beings, Without seeking one's own peace or happiness.
With a body adorned by merit, he benefits all beings.
Amidst all modes of conduct, he constantly practices heedfulness;
cultivating all wholesome dharmas, those who see him are without fail delighted.
Universally adorned with merit, far removed from defiled minds,
they constantly seek out spiritual friends, revering them and delighting in making offerings.
Cultivating the dharma of great compassion, they cast aside hearts of enmity and resentment.
"Your wisdom is peerless; I only pray that you will compassionately accept me.
At that time, the Prince replied:
"O virtuous woman!"

I have already first resolved to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, desiring to practice the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons, to accumulate all merit and wisdom, to purely cultivate all the pāramitās, to reverently make offerings to all Buddhas, to protect and uphold the true Dharma, to adorn and purify all Buddha-worlds, to ensure that the lineage of the Tathāgatas continues without interruption, to teach and transform sentient beings, to extinguish the suffering of birth and death, and to abide in ultimate bliss.
I wish to cause sentient beings to purify their eye of wisdom, to abide in the Bodhisattva path, to cultivate the Bodhisattva practices, and to fulfill all the stages of a Bodhisattva.

To cause the minds of all sentient beings to rejoice greatly, I shall practice the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) throughout all future kalpas, relinquishing all kingdoms, cities, wives, children, limbs, hands, feet, head, eyes, marrow, and brain; whether practicing giving as a householder or cultivating the Way as one who has left the home life, at that time you must not create obstacles or destroy my resolve for the Path.
At that time, the Prince spoke again to her in verse:
“Out of compassion for all sentient beings, I have resolved upon bodhicitta;
through immeasurable and innumerable eons, I have accumulated the merit of wisdom.”
Throughout an ocean of immeasurable kalpas, you have cultivated all great vows,
extensively practiced the bodhisattva deeds, and perfected all the stages.
In the presence of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, you have studied the six pāramitās.
Hearing the Dharma, they are able to practice it, Dedicated solely to seeking the Bodhisattva path.
In the defiled lands of the ten directions, I shall cause them all to be adorned and purified,
And eliminate for all living beings The sufferings and afflictions of the three evil realms.
By means of various powers of skillful expedients, they extensively deliver all sentient beings;
having eliminated the darkness of ignorance, they abide in the path of omniscience.
They make offerings to oceans of Buddhas and purely cultivate all the stages.
Arousing great compassion, I renounce all things, both internal and external.
If I give away my wife, children, and various kinsmen—
whether they be laypeople or those who have left the home life— you must not create any obstacles.
"If you can do as I have said, I shall accept you. At that time, the woman replied, "I respectfully follow your instruction;
even regarding my going forth into homelessness, I dare not harbor any obstruction."
He then spoke in verse:
"Throughout all oceans of kalpas, May my body be scorched by the fires of hell;
If you would only accept me with affection, I would willingly endure such suffering."
May all bodies born of birth and death be ground into fine dust;
if you would graciously accept me, I shall willingly endure this suffering.
For immeasurable eons, I shall carry upon my head all the vajra mountains.
If you would graciously accept me, I shall willingly endure this suffering.
Throughout the entire ocean of birth and death, I shall give myself away without regret;
should I attain the station of the Dharma King, I pray that I may likewise be so.
For immeasurable and incalculable eons, he practiced the bodhisattva path;
whenever anyone came to seek from him, he joyfully vowed to bestow it upon them.
Seeing the manifold sufferings of sentient beings, the Prince gave rise to the bodhicitta.
With immeasurable great compassion, you encompass all sentient beings and me.
I do not seek wealth or status, nor do I crave the pleasures of the five desires;
I only wish to practice the Dharma together with you as the consort of the Prince.
Cultivating eyes that are vast, clear, and pure, He gazes upon all sentient beings with compassion;
Without giving rise to defiled thoughts, He will surely attain the path of Bodhi.
When the Prince wanders abroad, The earth brings forth various precious flowers.
These marks leave no room for doubt; you shall surely become a Wheel-Turning King.
In the past, I saw in a dream the Perfectly Awakened One, Sunlight of Excellence, sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, surrounded by a great assembly.
In a dream I beheld that Buddha, who stroked the crown of my head with his hand;
having awakened, I was filled with great joy, leaping for boundless delight.
At that time, there was a deity in the sky named Pure Body.
That deva spoke for me: "A Buddha has arisen in the world at the site of enlightenment.
I then gave rise to this thought: "If I see the Prince, I shall explain it clearly for him—that the Buddha Sunlight of Victory has appeared."
“The aspirations I formed in the past have now all been fulfilled.
I pray that you will come with me to pay homage to that Tathāgata.

At that time, hearing that the Tathāgata had appeared in the world, the Prince was filled with great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight. Desiring to see that Buddha, he scattered five hundred jewels over the woman and gave her the pure *cūḍāmaṇi* jewel named Wondrous Virtue Radiant Treasury, along with exquisite garments.
Then, her mother spoke these verses for the sake of the Prince:
"This jewel among women, Her body adorned with merit—
That which I aspired to in the past, That wish is now fulfilled."
Upholding the precepts without negligence, her wisdom and all her virtues are supreme and peerless throughout all worlds.
This woman was born from a lotus; her lineage is beyond reproach.
Far removed from all that is unwholesome—such was the aspiration shared by the Prince.
This maiden’s body is supple, like celestial silk or cotton;
those who receive the touch of her hand find all their afflictions utterly extinguished.
The fragrance emitted from the pores is incomparably sweet;
if sentient beings should smell it, they shall all abide in pure precepts.
Their bodies are pure and stainless, like images of genuine gold.
Should anyone behold them, they will leave behind harm and possess a compassionate heart.
From their mouths issue subtle and wondrous sounds, such that there are none who do not delight in hearing them;
should anyone listen to these sounds, they will remain far removed from all evil karma.
With a mind pure and free from blemish, straightforward and without guile,
one practices according to the Dharma as it has been heard.
One shows reverence to spiritual friends and those who are worthy of respect.
Having distanced her mind from desire, she sought exclusively the True Dharma.
This woman’s heart relied on nothing; though born from a lotus of exquisite form, she sought only the Unsurpassed Way amidst all the worldly glories and pleasures.

At that time, the prince, together with this woman and ten thousand court ladies, departed from the Fragrant Sprout Garden. Each mounted a precious chariot and proceeded toward the site of enlightenment. There, they alighted from their vehicles and advanced on foot. From afar, they beheld the Tathāgata, his body adorned with the marks and signs of excellence; his mind was as clear and pure as a mirror or a deep, still pool, and his faculties were as perfectly disciplined as those of a lordly elephant. Their hearts were filled with great joy, and they leaped for joy beyond measure.

Accompanied by a multitude of court ladies, they proceeded to where the Buddha was, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, and made offerings with reverence. They circumambulated him countless times, each holding five hundred varieties of exquisite jewel-flowers which they scattered as offerings over the Buddha, and erected for that Tathāgata five hundred pavilions adorned with various precious gems.

At that time, that Tathāgata preached for him the *Sūtra of the Lamp of Universal Gate Illumination*. Having heard this discourse on the sūtra, he attained oceans of samādhis within all dharmas, namely:

the samādhi of the ocean of vows of all Buddhas; the samādhi of the light-treasury that universally illumines the three periods of time; the samādhi of directly beholding all Buddhas; the samādhi of universally illuminating all sentient beings; the samādhi of the light of the lamp of pure wisdom that universally illumines the oceans of worlds; the samādhi of the light of wisdom that universally illumines the ocean of the faculties of sentient beings; the samādhi of the cloud of light that protects and rescues sentient beings; the samādhi of the manifest lamp of wisdom that teaches and transforms sentient beings; the samādhi of hearing and upholding the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas; and the samādhi of the pure cloud of the conduct of Samantabhadra. Within all dharmas, he attained such oceans of samādhis as these.
"At that time, that jade maiden attained the dharma-gate of indestructible tranquility among all dharmas, and she became non-retrogressive in her progress toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

At that time, the prince, together with his retinue, paid homage to that Tathāgata, circumambulated him countless times, and taking his leave, returned to the palace. He went to where his father, the king, was, prostrated himself in respectful salutation, and said:
"Great King!..."
"On that site of enlightenment, the Buddha Supreme Sunlight has just attained perfect awakening.
The King asked the Prince:
"From whom did you hear this?"
He replied, "I heard it from the girl Vimalaguṇā. When the king heard this,
he was filled with immeasurable joy, like a poor man who has found a great treasure, and he thought to himself:

"The Buddha, the unsurpassed jewel, is difficult to encounter and difficult to meet; he can extinguish the evil realms and the suffering of poverty for sentient beings, acting as the unsurpassed physician.
With the Dharma of skillful counteraction, he eliminates the afflictions and maladies of sentient beings, acting as the excellent guide.
Within the ocean of birth and death, he delivers sentient beings and establishes them in the state of nirvana."
Having formed this thought, he summoned the minor kings, the various ministers, as well as the brahmins, kṣatriyas, and householders; when they had all assembled, he addressed them, saying:
"I have heard the supreme and auspicious words of the crown prince, saying that the Buddha Victorious Sunlight has appeared in the world."
Having heard this, I was filled with immeasurable joy; unable to repay it in kind, I now relinquish the royal throne and bestow it upon the crown prince.

Having thus abdicated the throne, the king, together with his retinue, went to the site of enlightenment where the Buddha Victorious Sunlight (Jyotirāja) resided. He prostrated himself at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to sit at one side.

At that time, the Tathāgata observed the king and his retinue, and from within the mark of the white tuft between his brows, he emitted a great light called "The Lamp of the Minds of All Sentient Beings. It shone universally throughout immeasurable worlds in the ten directions, manifesting the inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata to all kings. For those who were ready to be transformed, he caused their minds to become pure; they became endowed with inconceivable merit, transcending the world, and their bodies became purified. With a subtle and wondrous voice, he preached for the great assembly the *Dhāraṇī Door of the True Lamp of the Dharma Free from the Obscurity of Delusion*, with as many dhāraṇīs as there are atoms in a buddha-field serving as its retinue.

Upon hearing this, that king immediately attained the vast radiance of wisdom. Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa obtained this dhāraṇī; sixty nayutas of people attained the exhaustion of all outflows (āsrava-kṣaya); ten thousand sentient beings all attained the stainless, pure Dharma-eye; and immeasurable sentient beings all resolved their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Furthermore, by means of inconceivable and sovereign supernormal powers, he transforms and delivers sentient beings throughout the lands of the ten directions through the Dharma of the Three Vehicles.
At that time, the king had this thought:
"These various merits cannot be accomplished unless one leaves the household life; I should now go forth under the Tathāgata to practice the Way."
He stepped forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I now wish to leave the household life and study the Path under the World-Honored One.
The Buddha replied to the king:
"Know that this is the time.

Thereupon, the king immediately went forth with ten thousand attendants to practice the Way, and they all attained the Dharma-true-lamp-dhāraṇī-gate of being free from the mist of delusion, as well as dhāraṇīs equal in number to the atoms of the world-systems.

Furthermore, they attain the ten clarities of a bodhisattva, as well as an immeasurable eloquence and a pure, unimpeded body. They visit the abodes of all Buddhas, hearing and upholding the true wheel of Dharma of the Buddhas in their entirety. Acting as great Dharma masters, they employ their supernormal powers to pervade all worlds, manifesting bodies for those according to their needs for transformation.

They praised the Buddha-dharma and the various past bodhisattvas' practices of the Jātaka tales, and further extolled the Buddha's immeasurable, boundless, and sovereign spiritual powers as he protected the True Dharma.
"At that time, on the fifteenth day of the month, when the King attained the Way, the Crown Prince was in his main hall surrounded by court ladies, and the seven treasures arrived spontaneously."
First is the gold wheel-treasure, named Supreme Sovereignty;
second is the elephant-treasure, named Green Mountain;
third is the dark-blue horse-treasure, named Brave Swift Wind.
The fourth precious jewel of the divine horse was named Cloud of Light-Treasury;
the fifth, the precious minister of the treasury, was named Great Wealth;
and the sixth, the precious jade woman, was named Pure and Sublime Virtue.
The seventh is the precious minister of the army, named Vimalanetra.
Having obtained these seven treasures, when he acts as a wheel-turning king over Jambudvīpa, he possesses a thousand sons who are handsome, courageous, and capable of subduing enemies.

At that time, the population was flourishing, and there was abundance, joy, and sovereignty. In the eighty thousand royal cities, five hundred multi-storied pavilions were established within each city, along with great monasteries adorned with various jewels. Within each monastery, vast stupas were erected, all of which were embellished with every kind of precious gem and offered worship with incense, flowers, silken canopies, and parasols.
In each royal city, the Buddha was invited in succession, and the Tathāgata was honored with inconceivable and exquisite offerings.

At that time, as the Buddha entered the city, immeasurable sentient beings were filled with great joy; they nurtured their roots of goodness and gave rise to the bodhicitta. Through vast compassion, he benefited all beings, seeking the Buddha-dharma correctly, knowing the true meaning, and observing the dharmas of the three periods of time with equanimity. With clear and pure wisdom, he universally illumined the three periods of time, knowing the successive appearances of the Buddhas of the three periods as they gather in sentient beings, directing them toward the Bodhisattva path, performing the Bodhisattva practices, and dwelling securely in the equal and correct Dharma of the Bodhisattvas. Having attained the Tathāgata’s wheel of Dharma, his light of wisdom deeply entered the ocean of Dharma; he was able to perceive all lands within his own body, skillfully knew the faculties of others, and through the ocean of his great vows, attained all-knowledge.
At that time, as the Tathāgata successively accepted the invitations of those kings, he thus benefited immeasurable sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha!
At that time, was the Prince Sovereign of Increasing Merit anyone else? [He was none other than myself.]
The present Śākyamuni Buddha is he.
At that time, King Ratnapati was the Buddha Ratnakusuma; the Tathāgata Ratnakusuma is now residing in the eastern direction.
Beyond world-oceans as numerous as the atoms within world-oceans, there is a world-ocean named Dharma-realm Space-Light Cloud;
within it is a world named Buddha-Perfect-Light Sublime Virtue Lamp;
therein is a site of enlightenment named All Heavenly Kings Light Banner.

When that Buddha first attained perfect enlightenment, he was surrounded by a great assembly of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields as he preached the Dharma. When that Buddha Ratnakusuma was a bodhisattva, he purified that ocean of worlds; all the Buddhas of the three periods of time who appeared in that ocean of worlds had been taught and inspired by Ratnakusuma while he was a bodhisattva to resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the girl’s mother, Sunakṣatrā, was my own mother, Sunetra;
and those who were the king’s retinue were the great assembly present before that Tathāgata.

They have fully perfected all the practices of Samantabhadra and accomplished their great vows. With their pure Dharma-body, they universally illumine the world; their minds are indestructible, and they have attained all the gateways of bodhisattva samādhi. With their pure eyes, they behold all Buddhas and all Tathāgatas face-to-face. Through clouds of wondrous voices equal to space, they turn the wheel of the True Dharma, hearing and upholding it all. Having attained sovereign power over all dharmas, they traverse all Buddha-worlds in the mere interval of a single inhalation and exhalation.

Using subtle and wondrous sounds, they preach the Dharma for sentient beings, yet they never depart from the presence of any Buddha. Until the end of future kalpas, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices, manifesting their bodies in accordance with those who are to be transformed.
At that time, I myself was the precious maiden Vimalaguṇavati who, together with the wheel-turning king Adhikaguṇendra, made offerings of the four requisites to the Buddha Jyotissūryaprabha.
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, sixty hundred thousand koṭi-nayuta Buddhas appeared in that world. The first of these was named Vimalavapu;
the next was named Viśuddhacandraprabhāsamantajñāna;
the next was named Jñānavilokitadhvaja.
Next is named King of the Radiance of Vast Wisdom;
next is named Nārāyaṇa of the Vajra of Diligence;
next is named Indestructible Wisdom.
Next is named Wisdom Universally Objectifying;
next is named Cloud of Pure Virtue and Wisdom;
next is named Lion-like Wisdom Light.
Next is named Cūḍāprabha; next is named Guṇaprabhaketu;
next is named Jñānasūryaketu.
Next is named Opening the Precious Lotus Body;
next is named Merit Light;
next is named Wisdom Light Cloud.
Next is named Universal Radiance Pure Moon;
next is named Adorned Canopy Wondrous Sound;
next is named Lion’s Valiant Wisdom Illumination.
The next was named Wisdom-Moon of the Dharma Realm;
the next was named Lightning Flash in the Sky of Sentient Beings' Minds;
the next was named Exquisite Fragrance of the Virtuous Nose.
Next is named Silent Extinction Resonance;
next is named Amṛta Mountain;
next is named Dharma Ocean Thunder Sound.
Next is named Unbreakable Sound of Wisdom;
next is named Topknot of Awakened Lightning-Light of Emptiness;
next is named Cloud of the White Urna-Hair Mark of Moonlight.
Next is named Pure Wisdom of the Perfect Face;
next is named Light of the Flower of Good Awakening Wisdom;
next is named King of Sublime Virtue on the Mountain of Jewel Flames.
Next is named Vast Virtue Night-Light;
next is named Wondrous Jewel Moon Banner;
next is named Endowed with the Body of Samādhi.
Next is named King of Supreme Jewel Light;
next is named Manifesting Universal Wisdom Light;
next is named Lamp of the Flame-Ocean Gate.
Next was named King of Stainless Wondrous Sound;
next was named Peerless Virtue;
next was named Victorious Banner.
Next was named Bhujabala;
next was named Mūlapraṇidhānaviśuddhacandra;
next was named Tattvajñānapradīpa.
Next was named Dharma-uttara-svara;
next was named Vimala-prabhāsa-sudharmagarbha-rāja;
next was named Yāna-dhvaja.
The next was named Dharma-Ocean Lotus.
O Son of the Buddha!

During that eon, sixty hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* Buddhas appeared in succession in the world; I approached, honored, and made offerings to them all. The last of those Buddhas was named Vast Light of Liberation, and from that Buddha, I attained the eye of pure wisdom.
“O Son of the Buddha!

At that time, when that Buddha had first attained perfect enlightenment and entered the city to teach and transform others, I was the queen of that great king. Together with the great king, I reverently made offerings to him. I heard that Buddha preach the *Tathāgatagotrodayapradīpa-sūtra*; having heard it, I attained the eye of pure wisdom and further attained the dharma-gate of the ocean-like samādhis for observing bodhisattvas.”
O Son of the Buddha!

Having attained this Dharma-gate, I have upheld and practiced it for as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system. Throughout those eons, I encountered immeasurable Buddhas appearing in the world, all of whom I reverently honored and made offerings to.
O Son of the Buddha!
In some cases, during a single eon, I may encounter one Tathāgata appearing in the world, whom I honor and make offerings to; or two, or three, or an unspeakable number.

Or, during a single eon, I may encounter as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a world appearing in the world, all of whom I honor and make offerings to. Yet, I am still unable to know the physical dimensions and features of these great Bodhisattvas, nor their bodily actions, mental activities, wisdom, or the spheres of their samādhis.
"O Son of the Buddha!

If I see one who practices the bodhisattva path, I feel immeasurable joy; I respectfully make offerings to them and gather them in through various skillful means, so that they may attain non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
O Son of the Buddha!
Throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of worlds, I have encountered all the Buddhas, reverently making offerings to them; I have heard all the Dharma they taught and have received and upheld it.

At that time, those Buddhas each taught this Dharma-gate to me by means of various sūtras. Having heard them, I cultivated this Dharma-gate in the oceans of Buddha-lands throughout the three periods of time, in the presence of all Tathāgatas and their retinues; furthermore, I practiced the conduct of Bodhisattvas and the ocean of great Bodhisattva vows, cultivating this Dharma-gate within various Dharma-doors. Yet, even so, I was still unable to fully know the Dharma-gate practiced by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Why is this?
O Son of the Buddha!

The Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra is as immeasurable and boundless as space; it is likewise as immeasurable and boundless as sentient beings, the ocean of the three periods of time, the ocean of lands in the ten directions, and all dharma-realms.
O Son of the Buddha!
The Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is equal in extent to the realm of the bodies of all Buddhas.
Even if I were to contemplate the body of this Bodhisattva for as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system, my mind would never grow weary or satisfied. Why is this?

Within each and every pore of the Bodhisattva, in every thought-moment, I see immeasurable and boundless worlds of adornment; therein, Buddhas sit at the site of enlightenment, attain equal and perfect awakening, and amidst great assemblies, turn the wheel of the true Dharma with subtle and wondrous voices, preaching various sūtras, various vehicles, and various forms of purity.
Furthermore, Sons of the Buddha!
Within each and every pore of my body, in every thought-moment, I see the oceans of sentient beings, each with their respective abodes and spheres of influence, and their diverse faculties;

I see them throughout the three periods of time as they resolve for Bodhicitta, practice the conduct of Bodhisattvas, fulfill the ocean of great vows, purify the infinite and boundless oceans of Bodhisattva perfections (*pāramitā*), and manifest the oceans of the Bodhisattvas' past lives and the infinite and boundless oceans of great compassion.
They embrace all sentient beings and cause them all to rejoice, even to the point that they see all bodhisattvas dwelling within inner palaces, surrounded by retinues of court ladies.
O Son of the Buddha!
Within each and every pore of the Bodhisattva, I behold all such matters as these. O Son of the Buddha! I know only this Dharma-door;

yet the great Bodhisattvas have all reached the ultimate depths of the ocean of all skillful means. They manifest bodies equal in number to all sentient beings and accord with the ways of the world. From every single pore, they universally radiate the light of the ocean of all marks. They realize that all phenomena lack inherent nature, and that all classes of sentient beings are equal to empty space. In all places they reach, everything is the very Suchness (Tathatā). They manifest spiritual transformations, attain the power of mastery over all Dharma-realms, and sport within the ocean of Dharma-doors of the universal gate of all stages.
"How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
At that time, Gopā said to Sudhana,
"O son of good family!

In this city of Kapilavastu, there is Lady Māyā; go to her and ask: how does a bodhisattva cultivate all practices without being defiled by worldly dharmas, and how does one make offerings to the Buddhas and attain non-retrogression in the bodhisattva conduct?
May they eliminate all obstacles and awaken through their own realization rather than by depending on others; may they enter all Dharma-gates and be able to constantly manifest before all Buddhas?

May they gather in sentient beings and, throughout all future eons, cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva without regressing, ultimately fulfilling all Mahayana vows and nurturing the roots of goodness in all sentient beings?
At that time, Gopī, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, spoke in verse:
“I see those who delight in practice, The bodhisattvas engaged in various deeds;
With immeasurable hearts of joy, I embrace them all.”
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred buddha-fields,
there was an eon named Pure and a world named Radiant.
At that time, within that eon, there were sixty hundred thousand billion [Buddhas].
Ten billion buddhas appeared in the world;
the last among them was the Samyaksaṃbuddha named Dharmadhvajapradīpa.
After that buddha had entered parinirvāṇa, there was a king named Jñānaparvata.
By the power of great sovereignty, he ruled over Jambudvīpa and was able to thoroughly subdue all enemies.
He had five hundred princes, whose bodies were upright, handsome, and exquisite.
Their essence is pure and perfect, such that those who behold them never tire of doing so.
With deep faith in all the Buddha-dharmas, they revere and make offerings to them;
they protect the treasury of the True Dharma, upholding it and delighting in its cultivation.
That king had a crown prince named Sugandhara;
his body was adorned with the thirty marks, and he brought benefit to all living beings.
Together with five billion people, he left the household life to practice the Way.
Through the power of courageous diligence, he shall protect and uphold that Buddha’s Dharma.
The royal capital is named Wisdom Tree, surrounded by one hundred million cities;
there is a grove named Tranquil Virtue, adorned with trees of various jewels.
The One of Excellent Radiance dwells in this forest, extensively expounding the Buddha’s True Dharma;
with inexhaustible eloquence, he causes all beings to be completely purified.
Or, for the sake of seeking alms, he enters that royal capital city.
With dignified decorum in the monastic schools, all who see him are filled with joy.
His gait is like that of a lion; his will is ever calm and steadfast.
All his faculties are thoroughly subdued, and mindfulness and wisdom are ever present before him.
At that time there was an elder named Harṣadhvaja;
I was the daughter of that elder, named Anugatalocanā.
Then, within the city, I encountered Subhāprabha.
His body was adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, and his joyful mind was immeasurable.
Next, he came to my door to beg for alms; with a mind of attachment, I offered him ornaments of mani jewels, casting them into his bowl of excellent radiance.
Although with a mind of stained attachment, he made offerings to those sons of the Buddha for two hundred and fifty eons, he did not pass through the three evil realms.
He was always born among gods and humans, within noble and wealthy royal families.
Constantly beholding the excellent radiance of his body adorned with wondrous marks,
after two hundred and fifty subsequent eons had passed,
he was born into the family of the woman Bhadraśrī, named Vimala-guṇa-śrī.
Seeing the Victorious Sovereign, I gave rise to a mind of offering;
disregarding my own body and life, I bestowed whatever was requested.
At that time, together with the Prince, I went to behold the Buddha Jyotiṣprabha.
With immeasurable joy, I gave rise to the bodhicitta.
In the final eon, there appeared in the world a Buddha named Vistīrṇavimuktiprabha; I encountered him and made offerings to him all.
From that final Buddha, I attained the pure eye of wisdom;
I thoroughly understood the characteristics of all phenomena and eradicated false and inverted views.
I attained the Bodhisattva Samādhi-ocean Dharma-door of Contemplation.
In a single thought, they behold entirely inconceivable lands;
seeing those various Buddha-fields, whether pure or defiled,
they feel no attachment to the pure and no aversion toward the defiled.
Universally seeing all worlds, the Tathāgatas sitting at the site of enlightenment;
in a single thought-moment seeing all Buddhas and their inconceivable oceans of light.
One also sees the Buddha’s retinue and all samādhis.
All gateways of the Dharma are entirely without obstruction;
furthermore, they know those karmic actions, the stages in which they abide,
and the oceans of their great vows, all fully comprehending them in a single thought-moment.
Within the body of a bodhisattva, I see all the bodhisattvas who have practiced for immeasurable eons; none can fathom them.
Within each and every pore, I see lands throughout incalculable eons.
The wind-circle, the water-circle, and the fire-circle, The entire earth-circle,
and all that upon which they depend; The shapes and characteristics of the world-systems,
All manner of exquisite ornaments, And the diverse bodies of sentient beings.
Furthermore, I see oceans of worlds, all the various worlds throughout them,
where Buddhas appear in the world, preaching the Dharma to deliver sentient beings.
For immeasurable eons, I have cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva.
"Even now I do not know the bodhisattva’s physical actions, mind, wisdom, and insight.
At that time, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in reverent salutation at the feet of Gopā, circumambulated her, and took his leave.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifty-six;
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifty-seven.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Fourteen: Entering the Dharma Realm.
At that time, the youth Sudhana had this thought:
"How shall I see the spiritual benefactor?"

A spiritual friend dwells far removed from the world yet has no fixed abode; they do not cling to the sense bases, transcend all obstacles, and proceed upon the unimpeded path. They possess the pure Dharma-body, virtuous karma, and transformation bodies; with clear and pure wisdom, they contemplate all worlds, fulfill their great vows, uphold the Buddha-dharma, and their bodies are as they wish.
The Dharma-body is not a body of birth and extinction, not a body of coming and going, not a body of emptiness or reality, and not a body of aggregation or dispersion.
All phenomena, in their various marks, are but a single mark.
The body is free from extreme views; the body is without attachment; the body is inexhaustible; the body extinguishes all false delusions.

Like a flash of lightning, like an illusion or a dream, like a reflection in a mirror, like the pure sun, this body fills all directions; its emanations remain indestructible throughout the three periods of time.
The Dharma-body is the body that is not a body; such bodies as these cannot be seen by anyone in all the worlds.
They are seen only by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, who perceives the unimpeded conduct of those spiritual friends. How could I possibly see them, draw near to them, or know their characteristics?
Having formed this thought, "How shall I hear and uphold the Dharma?",

there was then a city goddess named Ratnanetra, surrounded by her retinue, who appeared in the midst of the sky. She manifested a body of exquisite adornment for Sudhana and, making offerings of celestial jewels and precious crown ornaments, spoke these words to him:
“Good son! You should guard the city of the mind, for it is free from birth and death;
you should adorn the city of the mind, for it attains the ten powers.”
One should purify the city of the mind by remaining far removed from stinginess, envy, and all forms of deceit;
one should extinguish the fiercely blazing flames of the city of the mind by attaining mastery through the continuous application of the gateways of dhyāna and samādhi;
and one should illuminate the city of the mind by constantly using the light of the prajñāpāramitā to illumine the ocean of the Tathāgatas and their retinues.
One should cultivate the city of the mind, in order to embrace the skillful means of all Buddhas;
one should fortify the city of the mind, in order to give birth to the various practices and vows of Samantabhadra;
one should refine the city of the mind, so that no māras, their subjects, or other adversaries can destroy it.
One should clarify the city of the mind, because one attains the light of wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
one should cultivate the indestructible city of the mind, because it can receive the clouds of the Tathāgata’s true Dharma;
one should perfect the city of the mind, because one’s own mind fully receives the ocean of merits of all Tathāgatas.
One should broaden the city of the mind, because great loving-kindness universally covers all sentient beings;
one should roof the city of the mind, because the Dharma universally covers and obstructs that which is unwholesome;
one should advance the city of the mind, because immeasurable great compassion rescues all sentient beings.
One should open the city gates of the mind, because one must maintain right mindfulness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;

one should reach the citadel of the mind, because one must fully know the causes and conditions of the turning of the wheel of the true Dharma by all Buddhas and the *sūtra* gateways of the Dharma arising from dependent origination;
one should know the path of the city of the mind, because one must reveal and manifest the path of all-knowledge.
One should maintain the city of the mind, for it is fully endowed with the ocean of vows of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
one should know the power of the city of the mind, for it nurtures the power of merit within the Dharma-realm;
one should relax the city of the mind, radiating light everywhere to know the faculties, desires, natures, karmic bonds, habitual tendencies, and all defilements and purities of all sentient beings.
One should know that the sovereign power of the city of the mind encompasses all realms of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
one should polish the city of the mind by abiding in the mindfulness of the Buddha;
and one should know the true mark (*lakṣaṇa*) of the city of the mind by thoroughly comprehending that all phenomena lack an intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*).
One should know that the city of the mind is like an illusion, because it enters the city of the True Dharma of omniscience.
If a bodhisattva-mahāsattva understands the cities of all minds in this way, they will be able to accumulate all roots of goodness. Why is this?
Because they eliminate immeasurable obstacles, namely: the obstacle to seeing the Buddha,
the obstacle to hearing the Dharma, the obstacle to making offerings to the Buddha, the obstacle to gathering in sentient beings, and the obstacle to purifying Buddha-fields.
O Son of the Buddha!
If a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva possesses such an unobstructed mind, they can, through minimal expedient means, perceive all spiritual friends and ultimately achieve all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā).

At that time, there was a goddess named Dharmavicitraguṇā who, dwelling in the midst of the sky, praised Lady Māyā with a sublime voice and emitted nets of light of various colors, which shone extensively throughout immeasurable Buddha-worlds.
At that time, Sudhana saw a net of light illuminating the bodies of all Buddhas; after it had circled them once, it returned and entered the crown of Sudhana’s head, filling his entire body.
At that time, Sudhana immediately attained the stainless, pure eye of light, which extinguished all obscurations of the darkness of ignorance;
he attained the eye free from cataracts, through which he clearly understood the true nature of all sentient beings;
and he attained the stainless eye, with which he contemplated the nature of all phenomena.
They attain the eye of pure wisdom and contemplate the nature of all lands;
they attain the eye of pure light and behold the Buddha’s Dharma-body;
they attain the eye of universal illumination and contemplate the inconceivable form-body of the Tathāgata.
They attain the eye of unimpeded light, observing the formation and destruction of all worlds;
they attain the eye of pervasive light, seeing all Buddhas turning the wheel of the true Dharma and giving birth to the sūtras;
they attain the eye of universal scope, observing the spiritual powers of immeasurable Buddhas as they teach and transform sentient beings, thereby attaining the eye of universal vision.
Contemplating how all worlds arise according to causes and conditions,
at the time when the Buddhas appear in the world, there was a rākṣasa king named Sunetra who guarded the Dharma Hall of the Bodhisattvas;
accompanied by his wife and children and surrounded by a retinue of ten thousand rākṣasas, he stood in the midst of space, scattering various exquisite flowers, and spoke to Sudhana:
“Good son! If a bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas, they will be able to draw near to spiritual friends.
What are these ten?
That is to say:
the purity of the straightforward mind, which is far removed from flattery and crookedness;
and unbroken great compassion, which gathers in and sustains all sentient beings.
Observing that sentient beings lack true reality, they do not regress from the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*);
they attain the power of firm faith within the great assembly of the Buddha;
and with the eye of pure wisdom, they contemplate the nature of all phenomena (*dharma-svabhāva*).
With indestructible great compassion, they universally cover all sentient beings;
with the light of clear and pure wisdom, they illuminate all dharma-realms;
through skillful remedial dharmas, they rain down clouds of nectar to eliminate the suffering of birth and death.
He follows virtuous friends;
with clear and pure eyes, he observes the nature and characteristics of all phenomena as a continuous succession.
When a bodhisattva accomplishes these ten dharmas, he is able to draw near to virtuous friends.
"Furthermore, O Son of the Buddha!
When a bodhisattva accomplishes ten gates of samādhi, they are then able to behold all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
What are these ten?..."
They are: the samādhi of the perfect fulfillment of the space of pure dharmas;
and the samādhi of observing the ocean of all directions.
The samādhi of discerning all objective realms;
the samādhi of directly beholding the Buddhas of the ten directions;
and the samādhi of nourishing the ocean-treasury of merit.
The samādhi of never abandoning spiritual friends moment by moment;
the samādhi of directly beholding the merits of all Tathāgatas as spiritual friends;
and the samādhi of approaching spiritual friends.
They constantly attain the samādhi of never being separated from all spiritual friends,
and the samādhi of reverently making offerings to spiritual friends without fault. Good son!
When a bodhisattva accomplishes these thirteen samādhi-gates, they are able to behold all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
Furthermore, they attain the samādhi-dharma-gate of the subtle and wondrous voices of all spiritual friends turning the wheel of the true Dharma;
if a bodhisattva dwells in this dharma-gate, they fully know the equality of all Buddhas and are constantly able to behold all spiritual friends.
At that time, Sudhana replied to the rākṣasa, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
Out of compassion, please skillfully instruct me on how to see spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
I pray that you will tell me: how should I go to the place where spiritual friends dwell?
In which direction, in what city, town, or village should I seek a spiritual friend?
He replied, "Good son!
Pay homage to the spiritual friends sought throughout the ten directions; with right mindfulness, contemplate all objective realms while seeking spiritual friends."
With courageous mastery, they travel throughout the ten directions in search of spiritual friends;
knowing that the body and conduct are like dreams and like lightning, they approach the spiritual friends.
At that time, following his instructions, Sudhana immediately beheld a great jewel lotus springing forth from the earth.

Its stem was of diamond, its petals were of mani-jewels, its pedestal was of pure gems, and its filaments were of various exquisite fragrances; it was covered above by a net of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) mani-jewel ornaments.
Upon the lotus pedestal there was a tower named "The Comprehension of the Square Treasury of the Dharma Realm.

Its floor was made of vajra, and the tower had a thousand pillars composed of all kinds of *maṇi* jewels and various ornaments. It was hung with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) exquisite gems and necklaces, and incalculable jewels served as its railings.
At that time, Sudhana saw within the tower a lion throne made of maṇi jewels,
adorned with various precious gems and surrounded by railings of diverse jewels.
Spreading various exquisite robes;
covering them above with jeweled nets;
and erecting jeweled banners and canopies.
From within the golden bells, wondrous sounds issued forth, raining down exquisite fragrant flowers;
from within the various jeweled bells, the sounds of the vows and practices of all bodhisattvas emerged;
and from within the jewel-moon banners, the transformation bodies of Buddhas appeared.
