Within pure maṇi jewels, the successive births of the Tathāgatas appear;
from sun maṇi jewels, immeasurable light is emitted, illuminating the lands of the ten directions;
and from the light-bannered maṇi-jewel kings, the perfect radiance of all Buddhas is emitted.

From within the luminous and pure jewels emerge various articles of offering; from the wish-fulfilling jewels, the clouds of the Buddha’s True Dharma—the lamp for all sentient beings—arise moment by moment, manifesting the sovereign power of Samantabhadra to fill the entire dharma-realm;
and from within the Sumeru banners issue forth celestial, wondrous sounds, praising the Tathāgata.
At that time, Sudhana beheld this inconceivable, magnificently adorned high throne, surrounded by an inconceivable retinue;

he saw Lady Māyā seated upon that throne, upright and exquisite, possessing a pure physical body, a physical body that transcends the three worlds, a physical body manifested before all worlds, a physical body detached from all realms of existence, a physical body that teaches according to what is appropriate, a physical body unstained by any sentient beings, a vast physical body, a physical body equal to all sentient beings, a physical body unequaled by any sentient beings, and a physical body whose sight is never in vain for any sentient beings.

There are various bodies of form that manifest according to those who are to be transformed: the body of manifested form; the body of infinite images and forms; the body of universal-gate images and forms; the body manifested before all sentient beings; the body adorned with the gate of vast sovereignty; the body that transforms and teaches all sentient beings; the body of descending forms manifested before all sentient beings; the body of various indestructible forms manifested at all times; and the body that sustains all sentient beings whether their state is ultimate or non-ultimate.
It is a body that does not depart, for it is not extinguished in any realm of existence; it is a body that does not come, for it is not born in any realm of existence.
The form-body does not arise, because it neither originates nor manifests;
the form-body does not cease, because it is beyond all worldly paths of language;
the form-body is not empty, because it accords with what is attained.
The physical body is non-deceptive, for it accords with the world;
the physical body has no destination, for it is neither born nor does it die;
the physical body is indestructible, for the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is indestructible.
The form-body of signlessness, because all speech regarding the three periods of time has been severed;
the form-body of the single mark, because it skillfully explains the mark of signlessness;
the form-body like lightning, because it accords with the minds of all sentient beings as appropriate.
The illusory body, because it is perfected by the illusion of wisdom;
the mirage-like body, because it sustains the perceptions of sentient beings;
the shadow-like body, because the original vows of all sentient beings continue in uninterrupted succession.
The dream-like form-body, because it is indestructible in accordance with the needs of sentient beings;
the ultimate dharma-realm form-body, because it is as pure as space;
the manifested great compassion form-body, because it brings all sentient beings to fulfillment.
The form-body that manifests unimpeded gates, because it fills the Dharma-realm in every thought-moment;
the infinite and boundless form-body, because it purifies all worldly gates and transcends the path of language;
the form-body without dependence, because its vow for the ultimate transformation of sentient beings is fulfilled.
The abiding physical body, because it is able to accomplish all matters for sentient beings;
the non-arising physical body, because illusory vows are fulfilled;
the incomparable physical body, because it transcends the world.
The body that conforms to circumstances, because it accords with those to be saved;
the unmixed body, because it continues in accordance with karma;
the wish-fulfilling jewel body, because it fulfills the vows of all sentient beings.
The body free from false conceptualization, because all sentient beings arise from false conceptualization;
the body free from applied and sustained thought, because all sentient beings are incapable of contemplative investigation;
the non-ultimate body, because it eliminates birth and death.
The pure form-body, because it is free from the Tathāgata’s discursive thought and reflection;
such form is non-form, because form is like lightning;
sensation is non-sensation, because worldly painful sensations have been extinguished.
They are free from all conceptualizations, because they discern the conceptualizations of all sentient beings;
they give rise to both conditioned conduct and non-conduct, because all karmas are like illusions;
they transcend the realm of consciousness, because they fulfill the vows of bodhisattva wisdom.
It is empty and non-existent, for all the verbal expressions of sentient beings have been severed;
yet it is the accomplishment of a form-body, for its wondrous color does not perish.

At that time, Sudhana saw Lady Māyā manifesting such various and immeasurable form-bodies according to the needs of sentient beings—some seeing her as the daughter of the King of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, and so on, down to the daughter of the Four Heavenly Kings.
In some places he saw the daughters of dragon kings, and even the daughters of human kings.

At that time, Sudhana beheld such various physical forms as these, which nurture the roots of goodness in all sentient beings, practice the indestructible perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*), universally contemplate all sentient beings with great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), and give rise to the immeasurable merits of the Tathāgata.

With courageous diligence, they seek omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), knowing that all phenomena possess the mark of quiescence; they enter the ocean of profound patience, become fully endowed with indestructible meditative concentrations (*dhyāna-samādhi*), cultivate the spheres of all samādhis, attain the perfect meditative concentration of the Tathāgata, and extinguish the ocean of all afflictions of sentient beings.

They completely purify and adorn all dharma-realms, discerning and understanding the wheels of the Dharma of all Buddhas; with clear and pure wisdom, they contemplate the ocean of all dharmas, beholding all Buddhas with hearts that never know satiety.
Successively observing the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, they open the gates of all Buddhas and behold the Buddhas of the three periods.

Successively appearing in the world to purify the Buddha-way, their precepts are suchness, like emptiness; they gather in and transform all sentient beings, attaining the pure Dharma-body and purifying all Buddha-fields.
Having brought all great vows to ultimate fulfillment, they transform and deliver all sentient beings.
In a single thought-moment, they pervade the realms of all Buddhas and give rise to the sovereign spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas.

They manifest immeasurable bodies of pure form, subdue all demonic powers, increase the power of merit, give rise to the power of wholesome dharmas, attain the power of all Buddhas, possess the power of Bodhisattvas, and generate the power of omniscience.
The Tathāgata’s wisdom shines universally upon all things, fully knowing the ocean-like minds of immeasurable sentient beings and clearly understanding their various faculties, desires, and natures.

His single body fills the infinite and boundless Buddha-fields of the ten directions, discerning and knowing the formation and destruction of those fields. Opening the eye of pure wisdom, he beholds the ocean of the three periods of time and the ocean of the Buddhas' teachings, which give birth to the merits of all Tathāgatas. He knows the merits cultivated by all Bodhisattvas—from their first aspiration until their ultimate fulfillment—and nurtures the roots of goodness in all sentient beings. Throughout all worlds, he praises the merits of all Buddhas and brings to completion the vows of the mothers of all Bodhisattvas.

At that time, Sudhana beheld such unprecedented wonders as these, equal in number to the atoms of Jambudvīpa, within the body of Lady Māyā; he immediately transformed his own body so that it became equal in size to Lady Māyā’s body, joined his palms in reverent salutation, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, and instantly attained immeasurable and boundless gateways to samādhi.
Cultivating right mindfulness, he discerned and observed, giving rise to and attesting to [the realization] in accordance with it.
Having realized it, he arose from samādhi;
having arisen, he circumambulated Queen Māyā and her retinue with reverence, and standing to one side with palms joined in respect, he addressed them, saying:

“Great Sage! In the past, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva instructed me to resolve my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, to seek spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), and to draw near to and make offerings to them.”
"I have gradually sought my way to the presence of the Great Sage; I pray that you will explain for me how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!
I have already accomplished the Dharma-gate of the Great Vow and Wisdom-illusion.
Because I have attained this Dharma-gate, I am the mother of the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Here in the city of Kapilavastu in Jambudvīpa, within the palace of King Śuddhodana, I gave birth from my right side to Prince Siddhārtha, manifesting inconceivable and sovereign spiritual powers.

"Good son! When the Bodhisattva passes away from the Tuṣita Heaven, he emits from every single pore a great radiance named 'The Perfect Merit of the Birth of All Tathāgatas. This light manifests the adornments of the births of Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields, universally illuminating all worlds.
Having illuminated them, it comes to touch the crown of my head and enters everywhere into all the pores of my body."

Having entered, he universally beheld Bodhisattvas taking birth, adorned with sovereign mastery; he further saw them renounce the world, proceed to the site of enlightenment, and attain equal and perfect awakening, surrounded by assemblies of Bodhisattvas, devas, and humans, who reverently made offerings as they turned the wheel of the true Dharma.
In past ages, those Tathāgatas practiced the bodhisattva path, reverently made offerings to various Buddhas, gave rise to the bodhicitta, and purified the Buddha-fields.
Innumerable transformation bodies fill the Dharma-realm, teaching and transforming sentient beings, even manifesting the Great Parinirvāṇa; all such matters are clearly perceived.
Furthermore, good son!

When that wondrous light entered my body, my body at that time transcended the world and became equal to space; yet it did not exceed the dimensions of a human body, for it was fully capable of containing the bodhisattvas from the ten directions and their adorned palaces.

At that time, when the Bodhisattva descended from the Tuṣita Heaven, he was accompanied by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields; all of them shared the same great vows, were adorned with roots of goodness, possessed mastery over the wisdom of dharma-gates, had purified all the stages (bhūmis), attained the immeasurable Dharma-body, perfected the form-body (rūpakāya), and were entirely equal in the vast vows and practices of Samantabhadra.

Thus, the Bodhisattva was surrounded by his retinue and accompanied by eighty thousand nāga kings, such as Sāgara Nāgarāja, as well as yakṣas and the eight classes of divine beings, who paid him reverent homage and made offerings.
When descending to manifest in this world, he emits a great radiance that universally illumines the world;
he manifests his sovereign power to eliminate all sufferings of the evil realms;
and through skillful means, he teaches and transforms inconceivable numbers of sentient beings, causing them all to know their karmic actions from past lives.

To cause all bodhisattvas to cultivate heedfulness, remain free from attachment, and rescue and protect sentient beings, I have caused them all to behold this bodhisattva’s body manifesting such extraordinary wonders:

together with a great assembly, he enters my womb; within my womb, those bodhisattvas move about with sovereign ease, sometimes taking the three-thousandfold world system as a single step, and sometimes taking as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields as a single step.

Furthermore, in every moment of thought, within all worlds of the ten directions, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of bodhisattva retinues at the abodes of all Buddhas, as well as the Four Heavenly Kings, the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, up to the Brahmā Kings—all such celestial kings enter my womb desiring to see the Bodhisattva, to pay homage and make offerings, and to hear and receive the True Dharma. I accommodate all such multitudes, yet the womb neither expands nor becomes cramped. While manifesting such supernatural transformations in this world, I likewise do so in all Jambudvīpas throughout the ten directions; without dividing my body into various emanations, I act as the mother of a bodhisattva according to what is appropriate for each.
Why is this? Because they have cultivated this dharma-gate of the great vow and the wisdom-illusion.
O son of good family!
I am the mother of Vairocana Buddha, and [the mother] of Krakucchanda Buddha,

O Son of the Buddha!

All the Buddhas of this Bhadrakalpa who have attained perfect enlightenment in this world, I have been the mother of each and every one; likewise, I have taught and transformed sentient beings in all worlds throughout the ten directions.
At that time, Sudhana said: "O Great Sage!
How long has it been since you attained this Dharma-door?"
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!

In the distant past, beyond inconceivable and incalculable eons that exceed the sphere of the penetrating clarity of all Bodhisattvas, there was an eon named Pure Radiance and a world named Wondrous Virtue Sumeru King."
That land is pure and free from all defilements; composed of various jewels, it is adorned in manifold ways, such that those who behold it never grow weary.

Within that world are ten billion sets of four continents (*cāturdvīpaka*). Among these four-continents, there is one set of four continents; within that set of four continents, there are eight billion royal capitals. Among those royal capitals, there is one capital named Jñānaketu, where a wheel-turning king (*cakravartin*) named Vikramatejas resides.
To the north of that royal capital was a site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) named Moonlight, and the deity of that site was named Compassionate Wondrous Virtue.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva named Stainless Banner who sat at the site of enlightenment; as he was about to attain perfect awakening, an evil Māra named Vajra Radiance arrived at the bodhisattva’s location together with his retinue to disrupt his spiritual practice.
Then, King Courageous Prowess, fully endowed with the sovereign power of a bodhisattva’s spiritual faculties, manifested an army that outnumbered the host of Māras and utterly defeated them.
At that time, that bodhisattva attained perfect enlightenment;
seeing this event, the deity of the site of awakening was filled with immeasurable joy and made this vow:
"From the time this Wheel-Turning King attained Buddhahood until he reached that state, I was his mother. Good son!
I once made offerings to ten nayutas of Buddhas at that very site of enlightenment."
"Good son! As for that deity of the site of enlightenment, could he be anyone else?
It was my very self."
The Wheel-Turning King was none other than Vairocana Buddha. Good son!

From the time I first made that vow until now, throughout Vairocana Buddha’s practice of all bodhisattva deeds, his teaching and transforming of sentient beings, and even up to his final birth, I have always been his mother.
Furthermore, good son!

As for the immeasurable and boundless Buddhas of the present, the past, and the ten directions who emit great radiance to shine upon my body, palace, and dwelling place—I have been their mother in their final birth.
"Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the Illusory Power of Great Vow Wisdom.

As for the great Bodhisattvas, who possess the treasury of great compassion, they teach and transform sentient beings with minds that never grow weary; having attained the dharma of mastery, they manifest within each and every pore the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas."
"How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
At that time, Lady Māyā addressed the youth Sudhana, saying: "Noble son!
In this world, in the Heaven of the Thirty-three, there is a king named King Right Mindfulness and a maiden named Celestial Lord Light.
Go to her and ask: how does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

Then, the youth Sudhana respectfully received his instruction, prostrated himself with his head at [the teacher's] feet, circumambulated him countless times, and, gazing up at him with longing and veneration, withdrew while walking backward.
He then went to the celestial palace to see that young woman; having prostrated at her feet and circumambulated her, he stood before her with palms joined and said: "Noble Lady!
I have already set my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
"I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. The goddess replied, "O son of good family!
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called "Pure Adornment of Unimpeded Mindfulness.
Son of good family!
I recall that in the past there was a most excellent eon named Blue Lotus.
During that eon, I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River.

From the time those Tathāgatas first left the household life until their passing, I attended to, protected, and made offerings to them all, constructing monasteries and providing all necessary requisites.

Furthermore, regarding all those Buddhas—from the time they were Bodhisattvas dwelling in their mothers’ wombs, at the time of their birth, when they took seven steps, when they uttered the Great Lion’s Roar, while residing as youths in the palace, when they proceeded toward the Bodhi tree and attained Perfect Enlightenment, and when they turned the Wheel of the True Dharma, manifested the supernatural transformations of a Buddha, and taught and tamed sentient beings—I clearly remember all such deeds performed from their first resolution until the end of the Dharma, without exception; they are ever present before me, held in my mindfulness without being forgotten.
Furthermore, I recall a past kalpa named Good Ground (*Sudhara*), in which I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in ten Ganges Rivers.
Again, in a past kalpa named Wondrous Virtue (*Suguna*), I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a single Buddha-world.
Furthermore, there was an eon named Anupalabdha, during which I made offerings to eighty-four billion hundred thousand nayutas of Tathāgatas.
There was also an eon named Sugata, during which I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa.
Furthermore, there was an eon named Immeasurable Light, during which I made offerings to Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of twenty Ganges Rivers.
Moreover, there was an eon named Virtue of Diligence, during which I made offerings to Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of one Ganges River.
Furthermore, there was an eon named Subhāṣita (Good Compassion), in which I made offerings to as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as there are grains of sand in eighty Ganges Rivers.
Furthermore, there was an eon named Vijaya-vihāra (Victorious Roaming), in which I made offerings to as many Buddhas, Tathāgatas, as there are grains of sand in sixty Ganges Rivers.
Furthermore, there was an eon named Sublime Moon (*Candraprabhā*), during which I made offerings to as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas as there are grains of sand in seventy Ganges Rivers.
Son of good family!

Thus I recall eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; throughout them, I have never abandoned the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas. From all those Tathāgatas, I heard this Bodhisattva liberation called "Pure Adornment of Unobstructed Mindfulness," which I have received, upheld, practiced, and entered into in accordance with it, without ever interrupting my efforts.

Thus, regarding all the Tathāgatas of previous kalpas—from their initial stage as Bodhisattvas until the exhaustion of the Dharma—I have, through the power of my liberation of Pure Adornment, clearly recalled and brought before me all their supernatural transformations; I have maintained them and followed them in practice, never once becoming weary or negligent.

"Good son! I only know this liberation of pure, unimpeded mindfulness. As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, they have emerged from the night of birth and death; they are brilliantly clear and penetrating, forever free from the darkness of delusion, never falling into昏沉 (torpor) or sleep, their minds free from all hindrances, their physical conduct light and tranquil, possessing pure awakening regarding the nature of all phenomena, having accomplished the ten powers, and bringing enlightenment to all living beings."
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct?
Good son, in the city of Kapilavastu there is a teacher of youths named Viśvāmitra.
"Go to him and ask how a bodhisattva trains in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.

At that time, because he had heard the Dharma, the youth Sudhana’s body and mind were filled with joy; his inconceivable roots of goodness flowed forth and expanded. He prostrated himself at the feet of Indraketudhvaja, circumambulated him countless times, and then took his leave with longing and veneration.

Descending from the celestial palace, he gradually approached that city and arrived at the place where Samantabhadra was. He prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him, and with palms joined in reverence, stood to one side and said: "Noble One!"
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. Viśvāmitra replied, "Noble son!..."
"Here is a youth named Śāriputra, who studies the bodhisattva’s knowledge of letters.
You should question him; he will explain it for you.
At that time, Sudhana went to his place, prostrated himself with his head at his feet in reverence, stood to one side, and said:
“Noble One! I have already set my mind upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.”
"I have heard that the Holy One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. Then, the youth addressed Sudhana, saying:
"O son of good family!
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called "Skillfully Knowing All Arts.

I constantly chant and maintain the fundamental syllables for entering this liberation. When I chant the syllable *A*, I enter a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Distinctive Spheres of Bodhisattva Majestic Power.
When I chant the syllable *Ra*, I enter a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Supreme and Boundless Equality of One Flavor."
When pronouncing the syllable *pa*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Non-differentiated Aspect of the Dharma Realm.
When pronouncing the syllable *ca*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Universal Wheel that Severs Differentiation.
When pronouncing the syllable *ta*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Attaining the Supportless and Unsurpassed."
When pronouncing the syllable *ra*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Stainless Detachment from Reliance";
when pronouncing the syllable *ṭa* (pronounced as *tu* with the *ga*-reversion), one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Practice of Non-retrogression";
when pronouncing the syllable *ba*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Diamond Field."
When pronouncing the syllable *ḍa*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Universal Wheel";
when pronouncing the syllable *śa*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Ocean Treasury";
when pronouncing the syllable *tha*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Universally Born and Peacefully Abiding."
When pronouncing the syllable *na*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Perfectly Full Light";
when pronouncing the syllable *na*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Accumulation of Distinctions";
when pronouncing the syllable *ṣṭra*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Universal Radiance," which extinguishes all afflictions.
When pronouncing the syllable KA, one enters a door of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Single Flavor of Differentiation.
When pronouncing the syllable SA, one enters a door of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Torrential Rain of Dharma.
When pronouncing the syllable MA, one enters a door of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Great Currents Rushing Forward, with All Peaks Standing Side by Side."
When pronouncing the syllable *ga*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Universal Establishment on High";
when pronouncing the syllable *stha*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Treasury of Suchness, Pervasive Equality";
when pronouncing the syllable *ja*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Entering the Purification of the Ocean of Worlds."
When pronouncing the syllable *śi*, one enters a gate of the perfection of wisdom called "The Adornment of Right Mindfulness of All Buddhas";
when pronouncing the syllable *ṭa*, one enters a gate of the perfection of wisdom called "Contemplating the Perfect Accumulation of Dharmas";
when pronouncing the syllable *śa*, one enters a gate of the perfection of wisdom called "The Light of the Wheel of Instruction of All Buddhas."
When pronouncing the syllable *kha*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Treasury of Manifest Wisdom for Purifying the Ground of Practice.
When pronouncing the syllable *kṣa*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Treasury that Stills the Ocean of All Karmas.
When pronouncing the syllable *stā*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Dispelling All Obscurations of Delusion to Reveal Pure Radiance."
When pronouncing the syllable *raṅ*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Cause for Awakening to the World.
When pronouncing the syllable *pha*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Wheel of Wisdom that Severs Birth and Death.
When pronouncing the syllable *ba*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Complete Adornment of All Palaces."
When pronouncing the syllable *cha*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "The Fulfillment of Each Individual Treasury of Precepts through Practice";
when pronouncing the syllable *sama*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Manifestly Beholding All Buddhas Throughout the Ten Directions";

when pronouncing the syllable *hassa*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Observing All Conditionless Beings and Gathering Them In Through Skillful Means to Cause Them to Arise in the Ocean-Treasury."
When pronouncing the syllable *ha*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "Practicing the Entry into the Ocean of All Merits.
When pronouncing the syllable *ga*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "The Firm Ocean-Treasury that Sustains the Clouds of All Dharmas.
When pronouncing the syllable *ṭha*, one enters a gate of the Prajñāpāramitā called "All Buddhas of the Ten Directions Appearing Before One According to Their Vows."
When pronouncing the syllable *ṇa*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Assembly of Billions of Syllables in the Immutable Syllable-Wheel.
When pronouncing the syllable *spha*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Ultimate Place for Transforming Sentient Beings.

When pronouncing the syllable *ska*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Radiant Wheel of Liberation that Universally Illuminates the Fulfillment of All Stages, Being Unattached and Unobstructed."
When pronouncing the syllable *ja*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "Proclaiming the Realm of All Buddha-Dharmas.
When pronouncing the syllable *ta-sa*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Universal Roar of the Thunder of All Space-like Dharmas.
When pronouncing the syllable *ṭha* (pronounced with a retroflex *ṭ*), one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Bright Lamp that Illuminates All Deluded Consciousnesses as Being Without Self."
When pronouncing the syllable *ḍha*, one enters a gate of Prajñāpāramitā called "The Treasury from which All Dharma Wheels Are Born.

Noble son, when I pronounce such fundamental syllables for entering all liberations, with these forty-two gates of Prajñāpāramitā as the foremost, one enters immeasurable and innumerable gates of Prajñāpāramitā.

"Good son! I know only this bodhisattva liberation of 'Skillfully Knowing All Arts. As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, they are able to reach the further shore through the power of their wisdom regarding all mundane and supramundane skillful dharmas."
He thoroughly mastered various regions and diverse arts without exception;
he possessed profound understanding of scripts and mathematics;
and through medicine and incantations, he was skilled at curing all manner of ailments.

There are sentient beings who are possessed by ghosts and spirits, afflicted by resentment and curses, or beset by the portents of malevolent stars, pursued by wandering corpses, or suffering from various ailments such as epilepsy and emaciation; he is able to rescue them all and cause them to recover completely.

Furthermore, he is skilled in discerning the origins of all treasures—such as gold, silver, pearls, shells, coral, lapis lazuli, mani-jewels, conch shells, and kṣāra—and their differing varieties and respective values.

Whether it be villages, towns, and districts; large or small capital cities; palaces, gardens, and groves; or rocky cliffs, springs, marshes, and wetlands—in short, wherever any multitude of people dwells, the Bodhisattva is able to provide protection and guidance accordingly.

Furthermore, he skillfully observed celestial phenomena and terrestrial geography, the auspiciousness or misfortune of human physiognomy, the cries of birds and beasts, the appearance of clouds and mists and seasonal shifts, the abundance or scarcity of annual harvests, and the security or peril of nations; thus, there were no worldly arts and crafts that he did not master thoroughly, having exhausted their very sources and foundations.

Furthermore, he is able to discern the supramundane dharmas, correctly defining their names and clarifying their meanings; he observes their essential natures and characteristics and practices in accordance with them. His wisdom enters into them without doubt or hindrance, without ignorance or darkness, without dullness, without sorrow or affliction, without sinking, and without anything that is not directly realized.
How then could I know or describe his meritorious conduct? Good son!
In this kingdom of Magadha there is a village, and within it is a city named Pāṭalī.
"There is an upāsikā named Bhadrottamā.
Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva learns the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of Viśvāmitra, circumambulated him countless times, and departed with longing and reverence.
He went toward the village city to the place where Bhadrajyotis was, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him, and with palms joined in reverence, stood to one side and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind on anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Holy One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. Bhadrajaya replied, "Noble son!..."
I have attained a bodhisattva dharma-gate called the "Dharma-Seat of Non-Reliance," which I have both understood for myself and expounded to others.

Furthermore, I have attained the Inexhaustible Samādhi, which is not a dharma of that samādhi; it is inexhaustible because it can give rise to the inexhaustible eye of the nature of all-knowledge, and it is also inexhaustible because it can give rise to the inexhaustible ear of the nature of all-knowledge.
Furthermore, it can give rise to the nature of omniscience because the nose is inexhaustible;
it can give rise to the nature of omniscience because the tongue is inexhaustible;
and it can give rise to the nature of omniscience because the body is inexhaustible.
Furthermore, it can give birth to the inexhaustible nature of omniscience through the mind;
it can give birth to the inexhaustible various illuminations of wisdom of the nature of omniscience;
and it can give birth to the inexhaustible pervasive supernormal powers of the nature of omniscience.
Furthermore, it can give rise to the nature of all-knowledge, for its immeasurable merits are inexhaustible like the waves of the ocean;
furthermore, it can give rise to the nature of all-knowledge, for its light pervading the world is inexhaustible.

"Good son! I know only this Dharma-gate of the Place of Enlightenment Without Dependence; as for the meritorious practices of non-attachment in all their aspects, which belong to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, I do not know them."
How could I possibly know and explain them all?
Good son, to the south there is a city named Kṣetravatī.
"There is a householder there named Dṛḍhamukti.
You should go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Bhadrasena, circumambulated him countless times, and looking up at him with longing and devotion, took his leave and traveled south.
Arriving at that city, he went to the householder’s residence, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, saying: "Noble One!"
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Holy One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. The elder replied, "Noble son!
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called "Unattached Pure Mindfulness.
Since I first attained this liberation, my aspirations for the Dharma have been fulfilled, and I no longer harbor any further desires regarding the Buddhas of the ten directions.

"Good son! I know only this liberation of pure mindfulness. As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the fearless great lion’s roar and dwell securely in the vast and lofty accumulation of merit and wisdom—"
How could I possibly know or describe his meritorious conduct? Good son!
In this very city there is an elder named Moon of Wondrous Virtue; the residence of that elder is constantly filled with radiance.
“Go to him and ask: ‘How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Dṛḍhamati, circumambulated him countless times, took his leave, and departed.
Approaching Candracchattra, he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him, and with palms joined in reverence, stood to one side and said: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."
"I have heard that the Noble One is well able to provide instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. Candracchattra replied, "Noble son!
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called "Pure Wisdom Radiance. Noble son!

I know only this liberation of the light of wisdom; as for the immeasurable gates of liberation realized by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son! To the south of here, there is a city named Utpala. There dwells an elder named Ajitasena.
Go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"
At that time, Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Candracchattra, circumambulated him countless times, and departed with longing and reverence.
Gradually heading toward that city, he arrived at the householder’s residence, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him, and stood to one side with palms joined in respect, saying: "Noble One!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Holy One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. The elder replied, "Noble son!"
I have attained a bodhisattva liberation called "Inexhaustible Aspect.
Having realized this bodhisattva liberation, I see immeasurable Buddhas and obtain an inexhaustible treasury.
"Good son! I know only this liberation of the inexhaustible mark; as for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained infinite wisdom and unimpeded eloquence, I do not know their ways."
How then could I know or describe his meritorious conduct? Good son!
To the south of this city there is a village named Dharma.
In that village there is a brahmin named Śivipravara.
Go to him and ask: "How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?"
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at the feet of Anābhibhūsenāpati, circumambulated him countless times, and departed with longing and reverence, traveling south by stages.
Upon reaching that village, he saw Śibi Uttamasena; he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him, and standing to one side with palms joined in respect, addressed him, saying:
"Noble One!..."
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
"I have heard that the Noble One is skilled at providing instruction;
I pray that you will speak for me. The Brahmin replied, "Good son!"
I have attained a bodhisattva dharma-gate called "Speech of Sincere Vows.

Because of this speech, bodhisattvas of the past, present, and future never regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; they have not regressed in the past, do not regress in the present, and shall not regress in the future.
"Noble son! Because I abide in speech of truthful resolve, whatever I do according to my will is never not fully accomplished. Noble son!"

I know only this Dharma-gate of truthful speech; as for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, their words of sincere vows accord with their conduct, their speech is invariably truthful and never false, and immeasurable merit arises therefrom.
How could I possibly know or explain this?
Good son, to the south of here there is a city named Sumanāmukha.
There is a youth there named Śrīsaṃbhava, and there is also a maiden named Guṇavatī.
Go to them and ask: how does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?
At that time, the youth Sudhana, out of deep reverence for the Dharma, prostrated at the feet of the brahmin, circumambulated him countless times, and departed with longing and veneration.
Traveling south by stages, he reached that city and beheld the boy and girl; he prostrated at their feet.
Having completed the circumambulation, they joined their palms before him and spoke these words: "Noble One!
We have already set our minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet we do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice or cultivate the bodhisattva path."
"We only pray that you will compassionately explain this for us!
Then the boy and girl said to Sudhana: "Noble son!
We have realized the bodhisattva liberation called "Abiding as an Illusion.
By means of this pure wisdom, we observe that all worlds abide as illusions because they arise from causes and conditions;
we observe that all sentient beings abide as illusions because they are produced by karma and afflictions.
All phenomena abide as illusions, for they arise through the successive conditions of ignorance, craving, and so forth;
all the three realms abide as illusions, for they are produced by inverted cognition;

and the birth and death of all sentient beings, as well as their birth, aging, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and affliction, all abide as illusions, for they are produced by false discrimination.
All lands are illusory abodes, for they are manifested by the inversion of perception, the inversion of mind, the inversion of view, and ignorance;
all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are illusory abodes, for they are constituted by the discrimination of knowledge and abandonment;
all bodhisattvas are illusory abodes, for they are constituted by the superior wisdom-mind and various vows and practices capable of self-subduing and transforming sentient beings.

All the transformations, taming activities, and deeds performed by the assembly of all bodhisattvas abide as illusions, for they are accomplished through being encompassed by vows and wisdom. Good son!
The intrinsic nature of illusory manifestations is inconceivable. Good son!
We two can only know this liberation of a bodhisattva; as for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who skillfully enter the illusory net of infinite phenomena, we do not know them.
"How can we know or speak of those meritorious practices?

At that time, after the boy and girl had spoken of their own liberation, by the power of their inconceivable roots of goodness, they caused Sudhana’s body to become supple and radiant, and he spoke of his own original vows.
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll 57 and Scroll 58,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Fifteen: Entering the Dharma Realm, Chapter Thirty-Four, Part Fifteen.
Furthermore, he spoke these words: "Good son!
To the south of here, there is a land called Sāgaramegha; therein is a grove named Mahāvyūhagarbha;

and within that grove is a great tower named Vyūhaviśuddhigarbha, which has arisen from the bodhisattva’s past roots of goodness, his sovereign power of vows, his wisdom of the various supernormal knowledges, his skillful means, and his dharma-gates of merit and great compassion.
In that garden dwells a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Maitreya.
He constantly transforms his parents, relatives, kinsmen, and fellow practitioners;
furthermore, he nurtures the roots of goodness in countless other sentient beings, causing them to abide in the Mahāyāna.

I also wish to manifest for you the Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva’s skillful means; I wish to clarify the Bodhisattva’s mastery over taking birth; I wish to appear before all sentient beings to teach and transform them, causing them to grow weary of all realms of existence; I wish to proclaim and elucidate the power of the Bodhisattva’s great compassion; I wish to awaken them to the signless Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva; and I wish to clarify that all realms of existence are entirely devoid of intrinsic characteristics.

Go to him and ask: how does a bodhisattva purify the bodhisattva path? How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva precepts? How does a bodhisattva purify the bodhisattva mind? How does a bodhisattva give rise to the great vows? How does a bodhisattva accumulate the equipment of merit? How does a bodhisattva attain the bodhisattva stages? How does a bodhisattva fulfill all the pāramitās? How does a bodhisattva attain the various dharmas of patience? How does a bodhisattva abide in meritorious conduct? How does a bodhisattva draw near to spiritual friends? For what reason?

That bodhisattva mahāsattva has brought all bodhisattva practices to ultimate completion; he discerns and thoroughly understands the mental activities of sentient beings and teaches them through skillful means and wisdom;
he fulfills all the pāramitās, dwells in the bodhisattva stages, and attains the various gates of patience;
he realizes the bodhisattva’s dharma of transcendence from birth and receives the prediction of enlightenment from the Buddhas.
They sport with sovereign mastery in the bodhisattva-dharmas and uphold the upholding of all Buddhas;
immeasurable Buddhas anoint their crowns with the nectar of the true Dharma of omniscience.
“Good son! That Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva can show you the way to true spiritual friends, strengthen your bodhicitta, nurture your roots of goodness, and cause you to abide in an upright mind;

he manifests the faculties of a Bodhisattva, expounds the unimpeded Dharma and the equality of all stages, praises the path from which Bodhisattvas are born, is endowed with the merits of all Bodhisattva vows and practices, and is able to extensively expound the conduct of Samantabhadra.”
"Good son! You should not give rise to the thought of contentment regarding even a single root of goodness;
nor should you be satisfied with a single ray of light, a single practice, a single vow, a single prediction of enlightenment, the gate of dharma-patience, or the six pāramitās."
Regarding the bodhisattva stages, the buddha-fields to be purified, and the proximity to spiritual friends—
one should give rise to the thought of contentment with respect to these matters. Why is this?
"Noble son! A bodhisattva mahāsattva should single-mindedly seek immeasurable roots of goodness and accumulate immeasurable requisites for enlightenment."
Accumulating immeasurable causes and conditions for enlightenment;
practicing immeasurable great dedications;
teaching and maturing immeasurable sentient beings; and thoroughly knowing the minds, faculties, inclinations, and various conducts of immeasurable sentient beings.
They eliminate the afflictions, karmic bonds, and habitual tendencies of immeasurable sentient beings;
they eliminate the various defiled minds of wrong views of immeasurable sentient beings;
and they cause immeasurable pure minds to arise.
They extract the countless thorns of suffering and affliction;
they dry up the immeasurable ocean of craving and desire;
and they distance themselves from the boundless darkness of ignorance.
They shatter the immeasurable mountains of great pride;
they untie the immeasurable fetters of birth and death;
and they cross over the immeasurable torrents of afflictions and existence.
They dry up the boundless source of the ocean of rebirth;
they rescue and extricate beings from the mire of immeasurable craving and desire, delivering them from the hardships and sufferings within the prison of the three realms;
they cause all to be established securely in the eight branches of the Noble Path, and universally cause the blazing fires of the three poisons to be extinguished.
They sever the countless hooks and baits of Māras;
they distance themselves from the countless evil deeds of Māras;
and they purely cultivate the countless bodhisattvas’ straightforward minds.
They nurture the immeasurable skillful means of bodhisattvas;
they give birth to the immeasurable faculties of bodhisattvas;
and they purely cultivate the immeasurable aspirations and dispositions of bodhisattvas.
They deeply enter the immeasurable and equal dharmas of bodhisattvas;
they cultivate the immeasurable and supreme practices of bodhisattvas;
and they purify the immeasurable merits of bodhisattvas.
They purely cultivate the immeasurable dignified conducts of bodhisattvas;
they manifest the immeasurable ways in which bodhisattvas accord with the world;
and they give rise to immeasurable indestructible faith.
They initiate immeasurable power of great diligence;
they purely cultivate immeasurable powers of right mindfulness;
and they bring to fulfillment immeasurable powers of samādhi.
They develop immeasurable powers of great wisdom;
they consolidate immeasurable powers of aspiration and nature;
and they accumulate immeasurable powers of merit.
They nurture immeasurable powers of pure wisdom;
they initiate the immeasurable powers of bodhisattvas;
and they bring to fulfillment the immeasurable powers of all Tathāgatas.
They fully discern and know immeasurable dharma-gates;
they universally enter the immeasurable directions of all dharmas;
and they purely cultivate immeasurable dharma-gates.
They give rise to immeasurable illumination of the Dharma, illuminating immeasurable teachings and immeasurable faculties;
they thoroughly understand the immeasurable diseases of affliction;
and they accumulate immeasurable medicines of the sublime Dharma, using skillful means to heal the diseases of the various fetters.
They cultivate the immeasurable nectar-like True Dharma;
they travel to all Buddha-fields to reverently make offerings to immeasurable Tathāgatas;
they enter everywhere to the very depths of the great assemblies of Bodhisattvas to protect and uphold the immeasurable True Dharma of the Tathāgatas.
They do not revile the transgressions of immeasurable sentient beings;
they eliminate the various hardships of immeasurable evil realms;
and they cause immeasurable sentient beings to be reborn among devas and humans.
They encompass all immeasurable classes of sentient beings;
they purely cultivate immeasurable dharani-gates;
and they bring to fulfillment immeasurable great vows and practices.
They cultivate the power of immeasurable great compassion and vows;
they do not begrudge their own lives as they seek immeasurable teachings;
and they cultivate the power of immeasurable dharma of quiescent extinction.
They give birth to immeasurable pure wisdom, supernormal powers, and clarities;
they know the births of immeasurable sentient beings across various realms of existence and accordingly manifest immeasurable transformation bodies;
and they know the myriad languages and dharmas of immeasurable minds.
They fully enter the immeasurable practices of bodhisattvas and cultivate the bodhisattva-dharma;
they observe the profound dharma-gates of bodhisattvas;
and they awaken to the difficult-to-comprehend realms of bodhisattvas.
They reach the realms where bodhisattvas find it difficult to arrive;
they uphold the courageous virtues of bodhisattvas;
and they realize the pure, wondrous, and difficult-to-attain dharma of the bodhisattva’s birth in the stage of non-arising.
They awaken to the various adorned practices of bodhisattvas;
they manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of bodhisattvas in all places;
and they receive and uphold the indestructible dharma-clouds of bodhisattvas.
They expand the immeasurable and boundless practices of pure wisdom of bodhisattvas;
they bring to ultimate fulfillment the immeasurable perfections (pāramitās) and receive immeasurable predictions of enlightenment (vyākaraṇa);
and they enter deeply into the immeasurable gates of patience (kṣānti) of bodhisattvas.
They cultivate and refine the various gates of the true Dharma of the inconceivable stages of Bodhisattvas;

throughout immeasurable eons, they adorn themselves with great vows, making offerings to all Buddhas, purifying unspeakable Buddha-worlds, and giving rise to unspeakable Bodhisattva aspirations and practices.
“Good son! Briefly stated, the Bodhisattva’s teaching and transformation of all sentient beings consists in practicing the Bodhisattva conduct throughout all kalpas.”
One should manifest birth in all realms of existence;
with clear and pure wisdom, one fully understands the three periods of time;
one purifies all lands, fulfills all vows, and makes offerings to all Buddhas.
Together with all bodhisattvas, they cultivate vows and practices in common and draw near to all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra).
Therefore, son of good family, you should single-mindedly seek out spiritual friends; whenever you see or hear the Dharma, you should honor and make offerings to it.
Do not harbor suspicion or weariness of body and mind toward spiritual friends;
cause all spiritual friends to feel great joy in their hearts. Why is this?
Through spiritual friends, one brings all bodhisattva practices to ultimate fulfillment;
one accomplishes all bodhisattva merits, all bodhisattva great vows, all bodhisattva roots of goodness, and all bodhisattva factors conducive to enlightenment;
and one gives birth to all bodhisattva dharmas.
They clarify and purify all bodhisattva dharma-gates;
they purely cultivate all bodhisattva precepts, all bodhisattva dhyānas and samādhis, the firm and unsurpassed bodhicitta of all bodhisattvas, and the dhāraṇīs and eloquence of all bodhisattvas;
and they purify the treasury of all bodhisattva merits.
They harmonize with the great vows of all bodhisattvas;
they understand all the secret teachings of the bodhisattvas and the dharma-jewels of all bodhisattvas;
and they nurture all the faculties of the bodhisattvas.
Accumulating all the wisdom of bodhisattvas;
gathering and protecting the treasury of all the meritorious qualities of bodhisattvas;
and purifying all the births of bodhisattvas.
They hear and uphold all the clouds of Dharma of the bodhisattvas;
they give birth to all the right paths of the bodhisattvas;
and they initiate the bodhicitta of all bodhisattvas.
To accomplish the bodhi of all Buddhas and all the practices of all Bodhisattvas;
to thoroughly understand all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions;
and to praise the merit of the straightforward mind of all Bodhisattvas.
They give rise to the power of the great compassion of all bodhisattvas;
they gather in the immeasurable roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas;
and they attain all the factors of the path of all bodhisattvas.

They attain the mind that benefits all sentient beings like all Bodhisattvas; they remain far removed from the evil realms, abide securely in the Mahāyāna, cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva, and distance themselves from evil associates.

Regarding the Dharma of Bodhisattvas, their minds never regress; they transcend all worldly states of ordinary persons, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas. Their minds are free from delusion and confusion, untainted by any attachments, and they extensively cultivate the immeasurable practices of a Bodhisattva.
They nurture all virtuous merits and eliminate afflictions, such that no Māras whatsoever can obstruct or destroy them.
It is by means of spiritual friends that one is able to accomplish such matters as these. Why is this?
Because spiritual friends are able to cause all obstacles to be eliminated.

They distance themselves from unwholesome dharmas, leave behind evil associates, extinguish the darkness of ignorance and the bonds of all false views, and transcend birth-and-death and the entire world;

they sever the hook and bait of Māra, pull out the thorns of suffering and affliction, emerge from the perilous difficulties of ignorance and the mountain ravines of delusion, and cross over the stream of existence and all evil, heterodox paths;
they show and guide the pure, correct path of Bodhi, teach the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas, and cultivate the four paths and the bright, pure eye of wisdom.
They establish omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), increase the bodhicitta, and expand great compassion;
they cultivate the perfections (*pāramitā*), abide on the bodhisattva stages (*bodhisattvabhūmi*), and attain profound dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*);
they purify all roots of goodness, accumulate all bodhisattva merits, and bestow all bodhisattva merits upon others.
Beholding all Buddhas, their hearts were filled with great joy; they upheld the pure precepts and understood the true meaning;

they emerged from the gateways of the True Dharma, departed from all heterodox paths, and manifested the gateways of illumination that universally shine upon all things; they heard and retained the clouds of the teachings of immeasurable Buddhas;
they extinguished all afflictions, increased all-encompassing wisdom, and dwelt in all Buddha-dharmas.
"Furthermore, noble son,
a spiritual friend is like a compassionate mother, for they give birth to one within the family of the Buddhas;
A spiritual friend is like a compassionate father, for they benefit sentient beings through immeasurable deeds;
a spiritual friend is like a nurturer and protector, for they cause one to refrain from all evils;
a spiritual friend is like a great teacher, for they instruct and transform others to lead them to study the Bodhisattva precepts.
A spiritual friend is a guide, for they teach and transform others so that they may reach the path to the other shore;
a spiritual friend is a skilled physician, for they treat and cure the affliction of all defilements;
a spiritual friend is the Snowy Mountains, for they nurture the medicine of clear and pure wisdom.
A spiritual friend is like a valiant general, for they protect one from all terrors;
a spiritual friend is like a sturdy ship, for they enable one to cross over the ocean of birth and death;
a spiritual friend is like a helmsman, for they lead one to the island of the jewel-treasure of omniscience.
Therefore, son of good family!
You should approach a spiritual friend with such correct mindfulness and reflection.
Furthermore, son of good family!
They approach spiritual friends, generating the mind of the great earth because they sustain all things without weariness;
they generate the adamantine mind because it is firm, upright, and indestructible;
they generate the adamantine mountain mind because no suffering or affliction can destroy it.
One generates the mind that is without self-will, because one follows the intentions of others;
one generates the mind of a disciple, because one does not contravene any instruction;
one generates the mind of a servant, because one does not grow weary or resentful of any arduous labor.
They give rise to a mind of nurturing, because they do not fear being defiled by afflictions;
they give rise to a mind of service, because they do not oppose or contradict whatever instructions they receive;
they give rise to a mind of humility, because they remain far removed from self-importance and overweening pride.
They develop the mind of maturation, because they skillfully know the proper and improper times;
they develop the mind of a noble steed, because they are free from the unruly and untamed state of mind;
they develop the mind of a great carriage, because it carries all beings.
One should develop the mind of a great elephant, because it subdues the sense faculties;
one should develop the mind of a great mountain, because no winds of evil can move it;
one should develop the mind of a small dog, because it is free from anger.
One should generate the mind of a candāla, because of being free from arrogance;
one should generate the mind of a broken-horned ox, because of being free from haughty power;
one should generate the mind of a great wind, because of having no attachments.
One should develop the mind of a great ship, for it travels tirelessly back and forth between this shore and the other;
one should develop the mind of a bridge, for it carries across the instructions of the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra);
one should develop the mind of a filial son, for one never tires of seeing the spiritual friends.
One should give rise to the mind of a prince, for the sake of complying with the sovereign’s instruction. Furthermore, good son,
one should conceive the perception of sickness and suffering toward one's own body.
One should conceive of the spiritual friend as a king of physicians;
one should conceive of the teachings they expound as excellent medicine.
Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a traveler on a long journey.
One should conceive of the spiritual friend as a guide;
one should conceive of the teachings they expound as the correct path.
Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as one who is proceeding toward the further shore.
Toward the spiritual friend, one should conceive the thought that they are a savior;
toward the Dharma they teach, one should conceive the thought that it is a cooling pool.
Furthermore, regarding oneself, one should conceive the thought of being a farmer.
Regarding the spiritual friend,
one should conceive the thought of him as a dragon king;
regarding the Dharma he teaches, one should conceive the thought of it as seasonal rain.
Regarding the practice of following instructions, one should conceive the thought that they bring about maturation;
furthermore, regarding oneself, one should conceive the thought of being impoverished;
and regarding the spiritual friend, one should conceive the thought of them being Vaisravana, the King of Treasures.
Regarding the teachings thus expounded, one should conceive of them as rare jewels;
regarding oneself, one should conceive of oneself as a disciple;
and regarding the spiritual friend, one should conceive of them as the Great Teacher.
Regarding the Dharma being taught, one should conceive the thought of practicing and training;
furthermore, regarding oneself, one should conceive the thought of timidity and inferiority;
regarding the spiritual friend, one should conceive the thought of courage and strength.
Regarding the Dharma that is taught, one should conceive of it as a weapon;
furthermore, regarding oneself, one should conceive of oneself as a merchant;
and regarding the spiritual friend, one should conceive of them as a guide.
Regarding the Dharma that is taught, one should conceive of it as a rare treasure; following what is heard and practicing accordingly, one should conceive of it as a supreme jewel.
Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a child and of the spiritual friend as a compassionate father.
Regarding the Dharma that is taught, one should conceive of it as one's own home;
regarding oneself, one should conceive of oneself as a prince;
and regarding spiritual friends, one should conceive of them as ministers.
Regarding the Dharma that is taught, one should cultivate the thought that it is the instruction of a king.
Son of good family!
When approaching a spiritual friend, you should maintain right mindfulness and give rise to such a thought.
Why is this? Because by means of a pure and upright mind, one encounters spiritual friends;
by following their instructions, one increases one's roots of goodness, just as various medicinal herbs grow by relying on the Snowy Mountains.
To be a vessel for the Buddha-dharma is like the ocean swallowing all streams;
to give rise to all supreme virtues is like the ocean producing jewels;
to purify the bodhicitta is like refining true gold.
Transcending the world, like Mount Sumeru rising from the ocean;
unstained by the world, like a lotus in the water;
not submerged by evils, like a corpse in the sea.
He causes the pure dharmas to grow long, like the moon at its full;
he universally illumines the dharma-realm, like the sun radiating its brilliance;
he causes the bodies of bodhisattvas to grow, like a mother nourishing her child.

Good son! Briefly stated, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can comply with the instructions of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), they will attain ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of merits;
and they will clarify ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of pure, upright, and profound minds.
They increase the faculties of ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas;
they purify the dhāraṇīs of ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas;
and they eliminate ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of obstructive dharmas.
They transcend the karmic activities of more than ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of evil Māras;
they enter more than ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Bodhisattva Dharma-gates;
and they fulfill more than ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sublime merits.
They cultivate the practices of ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas;
they are endowed with ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great bodhisattva vows.

"Good son! Briefly stated, it is because of spiritual friends that Bodhisattvas bring to ultimate fulfillment all bodhisattva practices, all bodhisattva perfections, all bodhisattva stages, all bodhisattva patiences, all bodhisattva dhāraṇīs, all bodhisattva gateways of samādhi, all bodhisattva supernormal knowledges, wisdoms, and masteries, all bodhisattva dedications, and all bodhisattva great vows."
"Good son! All such dharmas as these have the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) as their root:

they arise depending on the spiritual friend, are produced depending on the spiritual friend, are grasped depending on the spiritual friend, are initiated depending on the spiritual friend, grow depending on the spiritual friend, abide depending on the spiritual friend, and are attained depending on the spiritual friend."
At that time, Sudhana, having heard such praises of spiritual friends, the various bodhisattva practices, and the True Dharma of the Tathāgata,
was filled with great joy and leaped for immeasurable delight, as he mindfully contemplated the conduct of the bodhisattvas.
Gradually traveling on, he headed toward the country of Samudravetāḍī;
by the power of his physical karma cultivated in past ages, as well as his pure mind, he remained far removed from evil conduct and transcended the world’s false delusions and inversions;
seeking the true meaning of the Buddha-dharma, he nurtured his faculties, fulfilled his great vows, and was endowed with the power of diligence.
Not sparing even their own bodies or lives, they benefit sentient beings, cultivate the bodhisattva practices, and accumulate the Buddha-dharma;
they behold all Tathāgatas, purify all buddha-fields, make offerings to Dharma masters, and protect and uphold the True Dharma;
they accomplish the pure vow-bodies of bodhisattvas, skillfully understand dependent origination, and cultivate inconceivable roots of goodness.
Having formed this thought, they cultivate a pure mind of faith and reverence toward all bodhisattvas, regarding them as they would the World-Honored One;
they practice the faculties so that their minds are not inverted, maintaining right mindfulness and respect while remaining free from worldly conceptions;
they fulfill all vows, manifesting immeasurable transformation bodies of bodhisattvas, and extolling the Dharma-gates of all Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
Through wisdom and awakening, Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas possess the sovereign spiritual powers that reach all places;

even within a single pore, the bodies of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas completely fill it. With unimpeded eyes of wisdom, they contemplate the dharma-realm of the ten directions, the realm of empty space, and all phenomena throughout the three periods of time.
At that time, Sudhana, having thus paid respectful homage and made offerings, was fully endowed with all vows and patience;
with immeasurable wisdom, he contemplated the ground of the objective realm.
Then, Sudhana prostrated himself with his five limbs before that lofty and pure treasury tower, and formed this thought:
"This is where all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as all spiritual friends, reside;
this is a stūpa of the Buddhas;
this is an image of the Tathāgata; and this is the dwelling place of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the Dharma Jewel."
These are the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and they are also their stūpas;
these are the multitude of sages, as well as parents, and also the field of merit;
these are the realm of all dharmadhātus.
Having formed this thought, he further contemplates with equanimity that it is like space;
he contemplates with equanimity that it is like the dharma-realm, being without obstruction;
he contemplates with equanimity that it is like the limit of reality, reaching all places.
They contemplate all things as being like the Tathāgata, eliminating all delusions and remaining free from attachment;
they contemplate them as being like shadows, dreams, lightning, and echoes—all arising from conditions, neither existent nor non-existent—thus believing and understanding with profound resolve.
One receives retribution according to the causes of various karmas; one knows that through faith, one achieves equal and perfect enlightenment.
By understanding the Buddha’s merits, one makes offerings to all Buddhas;
by means of a heart of reverence, one brings forth the emanations of the Buddha.
Through the cultivation of roots of goodness, all Buddha-dharmas arise;
through the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), all perfections arise;
and through firm vows, all Buddha-dharmas arise.
Through various dedications, one initiates all bodhisattva practices.
Regarding the dharma-realm of the sphere of omniscience, one understands dedication to be neither eternal nor annihilated, neither arising nor ceasing, and not produced without cause.
They abandon the view of existence and all inverted delusions—namely, the notion that all phenomena arise from a sovereign creator;
they realize that there is an original, real nature that emerges in succession;
and, being free from the notions of self and what belongs to self, they profoundly penetrate dependent origination.
Entering into all dharma-realms, one perceives conditioned phenomena as being like reflections in a mirror.
Free from views of existence and non-existence, they are neither born nor extinguished;
having eliminated false delusions and ignorance, one realizes that all dharmas are empty and entirely lack independent sovereignty.

Transcending all marks, they enter the limit of the markless, yet do not contradict the law by which seeds give rise to sprouts; they fully know that all things arise from causes and conditions, just as a seal-image arises because of a seal, or like a reflection in a mirror, like lightning, like a dream, like an echo, like a magical illusion—each existing according to its respective cause.
All phenomena are likewise thus: they receive retribution according to karma, and through skillful means, they moisten and nourish all dharmas.
At that time, while Sudhana was prostrating and had not yet risen, he realized that dharmas are such as this and attained inconceivable roots of goodness;
with a supple body and mind, having completed his prostrations, he respectfully circumambulated him ten times and, with palms joined, gazed at him intently.
Again, he thought: "This is the dwelling place of those who have realized emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
it is the dwelling place of those who have departed from falsehood."
Those who dwell in the dharma-realm;
those who understand that sentient beings do not truly exist;
and those who know non-arising.
One who knows all worlds without attachment;
one who skillfully discriminates among all sentient beings;
one who is entirely without dependence.
One who is free from all signs;
one who knows that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature;
one who does not falsely grasp at any action;
One who thoroughly understands the characteristics of all mind, thought, and consciousness;
one who knows that all paths neither emerge nor do not emerge;
one who abides in all profound and great *prajñāpāramitā*.
One who fulfills the universal Dharma-realm through skillful means;
one who brings all afflictions of sentient beings to cessation;
one who, through wisdom, severs views, craving, and pride.
Those who sport in all meditative concentrations, liberations, samādhis, and supernormal powers;
those who cultivate the spheres of all bodhisattva samādhis;
and those who dwell securely in the presence of all Tathāgatas.
To take one eon as all eons, and all eons as one eon;
to take all lands as one land, and one land as all lands, yet without destroying the characteristics of those lands;
to take one dharma as all dharmas, and all dharmas as one dharma, yet without destroying the characteristics of those dharmas.
To regard a single sentient being as all sentient beings, and all sentient beings as a single sentient being, thereby understanding that there is no distinction among sentient beings;
to regard a single Buddha as all Buddhas, and all Buddhas as a single Buddha, thereby understanding that all Buddhas are non-dual;
and to regard the three periods of time as a single thought-moment, and a single thought-moment as the three periods of time.
Those who, in a single thought-moment, travel to all lands;
those who universally illuminate and benefit all sentient beings;
and those who have attained entry into all [realms].
They transcend all sentient beings for the sake of teaching and transforming them, yet they do not abandon them;
they do not rely on any particular land, yet they travel through and adorn all worlds to make offerings to the Buddhas;
they approach all Buddhas without any defiled attachment.
Relying on spiritual friends, they do not savor worldly dharmas;
dwelling in all the palaces of Māra, they take no pleasure in desire;
entering into all signs, they do not abandon omniscience.
They thoroughly understand the bodies of all sentient beings as being without self, without sentient beings, and without dualistic perception;
they contain all worlds within their own bodies without violating the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);
and throughout all kalpas of the future, they cultivate various vows and practices without grasping at the characteristics of the length or brevity of those kalpas.
Those who, without departing from the tip of a single hair, manifest all worlds and universally preach the True Dharma for the sake of sentient beings;
those worthy of veneration;
those who understand the profound Dharma.
One who has realized non-duality; one who has thoroughly understood the absence of intrinsic nature;
one who is skilled in remedial counteraction.
Those who realize the emptiness of phenomena;
those who abide in compassion;
and those who remain far removed from the stages of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
One who has transcended all realms of Māra;
one who is unstained by any worldly realm;
one who has reached the ultimate consummation of all bodhisattva dharma-gates.
Those who accord with all gateways of the Buddha-dharma;
who weary of all birth and death yet do not realize the fruit of a śrāvaka, remaining detached from the dharma of arising;
who know that all dharmas are unarisen, yet do not give rise to the view of non-arising.
Contemplating the phenomena of impurity, yet not realizing the state of detachment from desire;
cultivating great loving-kindness, yet not seeking to extinguish the phenomena of hatred;
contemplating dependent origination, yet remaining free from delusion regarding all phenomena.
Abiding in the four dhyānas without being reborn there;
abiding in the four immeasurables without being born in the formless realms, for the sake of teaching and transforming sentient beings;
practicing śamatha and vipaśyanā without realizing final liberation, in order to transform sentient beings.
Abiding in the samādhi of emptiness, they eliminate the view of non-existence;
abiding in the samādhi of signlessness, they do not abandon signs in order to transform sentient beings;
abiding in the samādhi of wishlessness, they do not abandon any of the bodhisattva’s vows.
Among all afflictions and karmas, they have attained the power of mastery; for the sake of teaching and transforming others, they manifest in conformity with afflictions and karma;
though detached from birth and death, they manifest taking birth for the sake of teaching and transforming others;
though detached from all realms of existence, they manifest entering those realms to transform sentient beings.
One cultivates great compassion, yet does not follow after craving;
one cultivates sympathetic joy, yet remains ever sorrowful upon seeing the suffering of sentient beings;
one cultivates equanimity, yet does not abandon the work of benefiting others.
They attain the nine successive concentrations, yet do not weary of or seek to escape birth in the desire realm;
they are detached from all sensations, yet do not realize the limit of reality;
they abide in the three gates of liberation, yet do not realize the liberation of the śrāvakas.
Those who contemplate the Four Noble Truths yet do not realize the various fruits;
those who contemplate dependent origination yet remain free from extreme views;
and those who cultivate the Eightfold Path yet do not permanently transcend the hardships of birth and death.
Transcending the stage of ordinary beings without falling into the stages of the two vehicles;
observing that the aggregates are ablaze without extinguishing the five aggregates forever;
departing from the paths of the four māras without permanently abandoning the awakening of all māras;
They abandon the obstacles of the six sense bases while manifesting as those who experience them;
they contemplate the marks of true thusness (*tathatā*) without realizing the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*);
they manifest as students of all vehicles (*yāna*) without forsaking the Mahāyāna.
"A pavilion such as this is the dwelling place of those who abide in all virtues.
At that time, Sudhana spoke in verse:
"Abiding in a heart of great compassion, Maitreya, the Mahāsattva,"
Endowed with wondrous merits, they benefit all living beings.
Abiding on the stage of consecration, as the eldest sons of all Buddhas,
they contemplate the realm of the Buddhas and dwell peacefully within this Dharma hall.
All the sons of the Buddhas, Constantly practicing the Mahāyāna path,
Wandering through all dharma realms, Dwell securely in this Dharma Hall.
Generosity, precepts, patience, diligence, Meditation, wisdom, skillful means, and vows—
Those who have reached the ultimate further shore dwell in this Dharma Hall.
With unimpeded wisdom like space, they universally illumine the phenomena of the three periods of time;
those who fully comprehend all things dwell in this Dharma Hall.
Having understood that all phenomena are truly without the mark of arising,
like a bird soaring through the sky, they dwell securely in this Dharma hall.
Having extinguished greed, hatred, and delusion, as well as all inversions, [they abide here].
Those who always delight in tranquility dwell in this Dharma hall.
Those who contemplate the path of the three gates of liberation, the aggregates, the sense bases, the elements, and dependent origination,
and who have distanced themselves from the evil realms, dwell in this Dharma hall.
Deeply penetrating unimpeded wisdom, Equally observing sentient beings and lands,
Those who know that phenomena have no inherent nature Dwell securely in this Dharma Hall.
