The phenomena of the three times are unimpeded, Just like the wind in the sky.
Those who are free from all attachment dwell in this Dharma hall.
Seeing sentient beings suffering and having no place of refuge,
those who universally rescue them with great compassion dwell in this Dharma hall.
Seeing sentient beings in blindness and darkness, who have abandoned the right path to enter dangerous ways,
you dwell in this Dharma hall as one who shows the true path.
Seeing all within conditioned existence (*saṃskāra*) oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death, [you remain here].
Those who cause others to be free from fear dwell in this Dharma Hall.
Seeing the afflictions of sentient beings, they accumulate the medicine of wisdom;
these compassionate physicians, kings of healing, dwell in this Dharma Hall.
Beholding immeasurable sentient beings Drifting and drowning in the ocean of birth and death,
The Great Compassionate One who delivers them with his boat Dwells securely in this Dharma Hall.
Having plunged deep into the ocean of birth and death, He destroys and extinguishes the dragons of affliction.
Those who gather the jewel of the Buddha’s wisdom dwell securely in this Dharma hall.
May those with the compassionate eyes of the Earth-goddess look upon the ocean to deliver sentient beings—
those who are like the golden-winged garuḍa— dwell securely in this Dharma hall.
Moving through the void of the dharma-realm, like the pure sun and moon,
those who radiate the light of wisdom universally abide in this Dharma Hall.
For the sake of every single sentient being, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, they remain.
Those who bear all sufferings dwell in this Dharma Hall.
Those of adamantine diligence, who have practiced throughout every kalpa within each and every buddha-field, dwell in this Dharma Hall.
Hearing and retaining all teachings in a single sitting, never weary of the teachings of all Buddhas—
those who possess the great ocean of wisdom dwell here in this Dharma Hall.
They travel throughout the oceans of worlds and the oceans of great assemblies.
Those who make offerings to the ocean of Buddhas dwell in this Dharma hall.
Those who, throughout the ocean of all kalpas, cultivate oceans of vows and practices and give birth to oceans of merit dwell in this Dharma hall.
Within each and every pore, those with unimpeded vision behold the Buddha-fields, eons, and sentient beings, dwelling securely in this Dharma Hall;
in a single thought-moment, they enter throughout unspeakable numbers of eons.
Those who know thoughts to be unimpeded dwell in this Dharma hall.
Those who have generated vows as numerous as the atoms of all lands and the drops of water of all sentient beings dwell in this Dharma hall.
Those who have practiced for immeasurable eons, possessing the dhāraṇīs, meditative concentrations, vows,
and the gates of liberation— such as these dwell in this Dharma Hall.
All the sons of the Buddhas, who give birth to immeasurable virtues, [dwell here].
Those who benefit sentient beings dwell in this Dharma hall.
Those who have accomplished unimpeded wisdom, possess penetrating clarity and skillful means,
and manifest births according to what is appropriate, dwell in this Dharma hall.
From the first arousal of the mind for enlightenment, He brings all practices to ultimate completion;
His transformation bodies fill the Dharma-realm, Manifesting the power of sovereign mastery.
In a single thought-moment he attains perfect awakening, Entering into immeasurable activities of wisdom.
Those who cannot be measured, who dwell securely in this Dharma hall;
those with the power of unimpeded, pure wisdom, who traverse all dharma realms;
those who observe with stainless knowledge, they dwell securely in this Dharma hall.
Having accomplished the bases of supernormal power, being entirely unattached to anything,
and realizing that the realms have no duality, they dwell securely in this Dharma hall.
Contemplating all phenomena of quiescence, they see them all to be like empty space.
Those whose realm is free from defilement dwell in this Dharma hall;
With great compassion they observe sentient beings oppressed by all manner of sufferings.
Those who rescue and benefit them dwell in this Dharma hall.
Without leaving their single seat, they manifest universally before all sentient beings;
like the bright and pure sun and moon, they eliminate the hooks and bait of Māra.
The Sons of the Buddha dwelling in this hall take pity upon all living beings.
They manifest immeasurable transformation bodies, filling all dharma realms.
The Buddha-sons dwelling in this hall travel throughout all worlds,
to the abodes of all Tathāgatas, for immeasurable and countless eons.
Without reliance, one enters this hall; weighing the realm of the Buddha, for immeasurable and innumerable kalpas, the mind never grows weary.
The Son of the Buddha dwells in this hall, entering various meditative concentrations in every thought-moment.
Each and every gate of samādhi manifests the realm of the Buddha.
The sons of the Buddha dwelling in this hall awaken to all lands,
All kalpas of the three periods of time, and the names of sentient beings and Buddhas.
The Buddha-sons dwelling in this hall take all kalpas as a single thought-moment;
far removed from delusive conceptualizations, they accord with the needs of sentient beings.
The Buddha-sons dwelling in this hall cultivate and practice all samādhis.
Within each and every thought-moment, they thoroughly comprehend the dharmas of the three periods of time.
Sons of the Buddha dwelling in this hall sit cross-legged in a single place,
yet universally manifest throughout all lands and within all realms of existence.
The Sons of the Buddha dwell in this hall, Drinking deeply from the ocean of the Buddha-dharma;
They enter deeply into the ocean of wisdom And cross over the ocean of merit.
With unimpeded wisdom they contemplate The countless lands of the three periods of time.
Throughout all kalpas and all Tathāgatas, and among the countless classes of sentient beings—
when the sons of the Buddha dwell in this hall, they constantly, within a single thought-moment,
fully comprehend the three periods of time and the formation and destruction of all Buddha-fields.
Skillfully knowing all the Most Victorious Ones, The various practices and vows they have cultivated,
As well as the faculties of all sentient beings, They practice within the realm of the Buddhas.
Within every single atom, They see all kalpas and lands.
The Buddhas and their retinues, and all classes of sentient beings—
when the sons of the Buddha dwell in this hall, they constantly contemplate all phenomena:
that sentient beings, lands, worlds, and eons are all entirely devoid of intrinsic nature.
Observing that sentient beings are equal, dharmas are equal,
Tathāgatas are equal, vows are equal, and worlds are equal— all three times are entirely equal.
The Son of the Buddha dwelling in this hall transforms and teaches all living beings.
Making offerings to all Tathāgatas, Contemplating the realms of all phenomena,
With the karma of immeasurable wisdom, Fulfilling all great vows—
Expounding them for countless eons, One could never reach their end.
To all the sons of the Buddhas, Who are endowed with immeasurable virtues And dwell securely in this Dharma hall, I join my palms in reverent salutation.
The eldest son of all Buddhas, Maitreya, whose conduct is unimpeded—
"I now join my palms in prostration; I only pray that you will look upon me with compassion and pity.
At that time, having praised the various bodhisattvas of the tower, Sudhana joined his palms in reverence and made offerings;
having finished his prostrations, he stood at the gate, desiring to see Maitreya Bodhisattva.

At that time, he saw from afar Maitreya Bodhisattva approaching from outside, surrounded by a great assembly of immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
Possessing supreme majesty and virtue, they universally illumine all things;
unstained by worldly dharmas, they transcend all realms of Mara within the world;
having extinguished all obstacles, they enter deeply into the realm of the Tathagatas and Bodhisattvas.
Making offerings to all Buddhas, they equalize the Dharma of all Buddhas;
wearing the pure and wondrous celestial crown of the silk ribbon of liberation, they abide in the great net of wisdom;
and in the presence of all Buddhas, they attain omniscience.
"The nectar-consecration gives birth to all Buddha-dharmas and brings about the attainment of sarvajñā (all-knowledge).
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself with his head at [the teacher's] feet, joined his palms with single-minded devotion, and said:
"O Great Sage!"
How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

Having trained and cultivated it, they become endowed with all Buddha-dharmas; according to the requests of sentient beings, they cause them all to be delivered and liberated, fulfilling their great vows;
they bring to ultimate completion all that is practiced by bodhisattvas and provide consolation to all devas and worldlings.

May you not betray your original resolve, nor violate the Triple Gem; may you not deceive devas and humans, nor delude sentient beings; may you not sever the lineage of the Buddhas, but uphold the family of Bodhisattvas and the True Dharma of the Tathāgata.
Regarding such matters as these, we only pray that you will expound them for us.
At that time, Maitreya surveyed the great assembly and, pointing to Sudhana, said:
"Do you all see this youth who has inquired about the conduct of Bodhisattvas and is fully endowed with all merits?"

This youth is courageous and diligent, seeking exclusively the true meaning with an upright mind; he has attained non-retrogression and constantly cultivates the supreme Dharma without satiety. Like one whose head is on fire, he seeks out spiritual friends, attending upon and making offerings to them, hearing the Dharma, and receiving it with devotion.

This youth, in the past, at the city of Bhṛgukaccha, received the instruction of Mañjuśrī to seek spiritual friends; he traveled successively through one hundred and ten spiritual friends, inquiring about the conduct of Bodhisattvas without weariness of mind, and has now come to my presence.

Thus, young man, those who study the Mahāyāna are exceedingly rare; they fulfill their great vows, are able to accomplish the great task, and possess great adornment. With constant great compassion, they rescue and protect sentient beings; they give rise to the perfection of great vigor, guide the great multitude, and board the great Dharma-ship to cross the ocean of birth and death. They cause others to abide in the Great Way, obtain the great Dharma-treasure, and nurture great wisdom.
Such a person is difficult to encounter or behold; it is likewise difficult to draw near, dwell with them, or practice together with them. Why is this?

This youth has resolved his mind to rescue and protect all sentient beings, to eliminate their manifold sufferings, the hardships of the evil realms, the perilous paths of wrong views, and the darkness of ignorance; he has transcended birth and death, shattered the wheel of all destinies, and crossed beyond the realm of Māra, remaining unstained by anything in all worlds.

Emerging from the mire of desire, loosening the bonds of greed, removing perverse delusions, toppling the banner of pride, uprooting the thorns of the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*), abolishing the hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*), tearing asunder the net of craving, extinguishing ignorance, drying up the stream of existence (*bhava-srotas*), departing from flattery and illusion,

purifying the stains of the mind, and resolving doubts; crossing the ocean of non-wisdom, wearying of the suffering of birth and death, boarding the great ship of the Dharma, rescuing others from the current of the four floods,
building a bridge of wisdom across the great river of attachment, and lighting the lamp of wisdom in the darkness of folly:
On the path of birth and death, he shows the correct way;
to those afflicted by the disease of afflictions, he causes them to take the medicine of the Dharma;
to those subject to birth, old age, and death, he bestows the nectar-like Dharma.
For those in whom the three poisons are rampant, he extinguishes them with the water of meditative concentration, causing them to attain refreshing coolness;
to all who are afflicted by sorrow and fear, he bestows fearlessness;
and for those imprisoned within the three realms of existence, he opens the gateway of wisdom.
For those bound by wrong views, he cuts them with the sword of wisdom;
for those dwelling in the city of the triple world, he opens the gate of liberation;
for those in peril, he shows the place of peace and security.
To those who fear the thieves of the fetters, he bestows fearlessness;
to those who have fallen into the moats of the three evil realms, he reaches down to receive them and cause their deliverance;
and for those harmed by the latent thieves of the defilements, he establishes them in the city of Nirvana.
For those attached to sentient beings, he demonstrates the Eightfold Noble Path;
for those dwelling in the empty village of the six sense bases, he rescues them with the light of wisdom;
and for those who have lost the essential ford, he shows them the correct ferry.
For those who associate with evil friends, cause them to become close to virtuous companions;
for those who delight in ignorance, lead them by means of the sublime Dharma;
for those who take pleasure in dwelling within the house of birth and death, cause them universally to transcend and enter the city of omniscience.

They rescue and protect all classes of sentient beings without abandoning their purity; they seek the bodhicitta and accumulate the Mahāyāna without weariness of mind; they drink the rain of the True Dharma without ever being satiated;
they courageously bring all meritorious deeds to completion, purify all dharma-gates, and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva without fatigue or indolence;
they do not retreat from skillful means, give rise to great vows, and encounter spiritual friends with a joyful and insatiable heart.
"Whatever is required for their service, I shall comply with their instructions without regarding it as a hardship.
'O sons of good family!

Those in the world who are able to give rise to the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment are extremely rare; even rarer are those who, having given rise to that mind, seek the Buddha-dharma with such diligence.'"

With such aspiration, they purify the bodhisattva path and fulfill the bodhisattva practices; they do not begrudge their own bodies or lives as they seek spiritual friends and never disobey their instructions.
They accumulate the factors of enlightenment, do not crave gain or offerings, and do not abandon the upright mind of a bodhisattva.

They do not cling to household affairs, are untainted by the five desires, and harbor no attachment to parents or kinsmen, but delight solely in the dedicated cultivation of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
Such persons are even more rare.
O sons of good family!

If there are bodhisattvas who train in this way, they will be able to bring to ultimate completion the conduct of a bodhisattva, fulfill their great vows, draw near to the Buddha’s bodhi, and purify all buddha-fields.
They transform and guide sentient beings, penetrate deeply into the Dharma-realm, and fulfill all the *pāramitās*;
they expand the bodhisattva practices, perfect their fundamental nature, and emerge from the works of Māra;
meeting all spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), they are able to embody all the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva within a single lifetime.
This youth has entered the ocean of majestic deportment and the ocean of all wisdom;
he has cultivated the ocean of bodhi and the ocean of bodhisattva practices;
and he has brought to full completion the ocean of all buddhas' vows.
They go to oceans of lands;
they behold oceans of Buddhas;
they enter oceans of retinues.
Performing oceans of offerings;
hearing oceans of the true Dharma;
drinking oceans of the sublime Dharma;
They fulfill the ocean of all bodhisattva powers and manifest clouds of all sovereign powers, such that there are no sentient beings who do not see them;
they extinguish the locus of all afflictions.
Entering the abode of all Buddhas;
entering the abode of all Dharma-gates;
entering the abode of all samādhis;
They abide in the spheres of the supernormal knowledges and clarities;
they traverse the realm of phenomena;
and like the rising of the sun and moon, they illuminate all sentient beings.
Not relying on any signs, like a bird in the sky;
always delighting in tranquility, they possess the indestructible dharma-gate;
they travel everywhere through worlds of Indra’s net and all Buddha-worlds, unimpeded like the wind, deeply penetrating the dharma-realm.
Appearing before all worlds, they behold the Buddhas of the three periods of time; their hearts are filled with great joy and they leap for immeasurable delight.
Following the teachings of all Buddhas, they become vessels for the holy Dharma;
they attain all dharma-gates, fulfill the practices of Bodhisattvas, and manifest sovereign power.
“Sudhana! You have now attained the greatest benefit;
that which has been difficult to hear or see throughout immeasurable eons, you have heard and seen it all, and you know those merits.”
That is to say:
they behold Mañjuśrī, who has accumulated immeasurable virtues, remains far removed from all perilous and evil paths, and dwells securely in the True Dharma;

having transcended the stage of ignorance, he abides in the stages of the bodhisattvas' merits, possesses the stage of wisdom, attains the stage of the Buddhas, and navigates the ocean of bodhisattva practices.
They bring to fulfillment the treasury of the Buddhas' wisdom, which is equal to space; they single-mindedly seek immeasurable and wondrous merits without weariness of mind.
If one can possess such a firm and upright mind, one will be able to joyfully seek spiritual friends and fulfill the bodhisattva practices;
one will teach and transform sentient beings and possess inconceivable, pure faith.

"O Sudhana! You have now attained great and excellent benefit, for you shall successively behold the true sons of all Buddhas— those who possess all wondrous virtues and the meaning of the True Dharma."

Whatever was attained through their own vows and practices as they themselves described them, you have fully acquired all of that upon hearing it. Such a practice would be difficult to accomplish over immeasurable kalpas;
for this reason, O sons of the Buddha, you have heard and seen all that which others find difficult to hear or see, as it has been explained to you in succession.
Having heard the Dharma from him, he manifests sovereign power, is protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas, and is embraced by Bodhisattvas;
following his teachings, he attains great and wholesome benefits, nurtures the nature of all Bodhisattvas, studies all merits, and ensures that the lineage of the Buddhas is never severed;

he is constantly consecrated with the nectar of immortality by all Buddhas and will before long become equal to the sons of the Buddhas; according to the sentient beings before him, he causes them all to obtain supreme and wondrous fruits of retribution through their cultivation of goodness.
"Good Wealth!
You should give rise to great joy, for before long you shall attain the great fruit of retribution;
for immeasurable bodhisattvas have cultivated the bodhisattva practices throughout incalculable eons."
That you have now attained all these things in a single lifetime is entirely due to the power of your upright mind and diligence.

Anyone who wishes to attain such dharmas should practice and learn as Sudhana did; they will then reach the ultimate fulfillment of all bodhisattva practices, satisfy all vows, and penetrate all dharmas.
They will be like a celebratory cloud, which, wherever it covers the land, is able to bring down sweet rain.
In accordance with wisdom and vows, the fulfillment of the bodhisattva practices is likewise so. Sudhana!
You should know that all that I have manifested and explained is the practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; you should understand this and draw near to spiritual friends.
The Buddhas of the past, single-mindedly seeking bodhi, cultivated this practice;

throughout immeasurable kalpas amidst all conditioned phenomena, they endured immeasurable suffering, yet still did not encounter the Buddhas of the past unless they were fully endowed with this practice.
"Sudhana! You have now achieved all these things: hearing the teachings of all Buddhas and practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Any sentient beings who hear of this practice will obtain great and wholesome benefit."
Fulfilling great vows, drawing near to all Buddhas, becoming true sons of the Buddhas, and surely attaining the Buddha-way;
with pure liberation, eliminating all evils, distancing oneself from all sufferings, and accumulating a mass of merit;
with the pure Dharma-body, wandering through the ten directions, beholding all Tathāgatas and the great assemblies of Bodhisattvas, nurturing roots of goodness like a lotus flower in water.

"Encountering all Buddhas, hearing and upholding the True Dharma, dwelling securely in the Buddha-way, fulfilling the vows of all Buddhas, and reaching the ultimate shore of the merits of all Buddhas.
At that time, Maitreya said to Sudhana:
"You should go to Mañjuśrī and inquire about the various dharma-gates, the realm of wisdom, and the conduct of Samantabhadra."
"He shall explain this in detail for you.
When Sudhana heard these words, he wept with tears streaming down his face;
Mañjuśrī immediately extended his arm and reached across to bestow upon Sudhana a jeweled necklace of flowers.
Having received them, Sudhana joyfully scattered them as an offering over Maitreya Bodhisattva;
Maitreya Bodhisattva then stroked Sudhana’s head with his right hand and praised him, saying: "Excellent!
Excellent, Son of the Buddha! You,
too, shall before long be equal to us.
At that time, Sudhana leaped for joy immeasurably and spoke in verse:
“Throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, One who is difficult to encounter or behold—
I have now attained the fortune to pay homage to The unsurpassed spiritual friend.”
“Mañjuśrī is my honored one, who has reached the ultimate shore of merit;
having encountered this spiritual friend, I pray that I may quickly return to attend upon him.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated himself with his five limbs before Maitreya Bodhisattva and, joining his palms, said:
“O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.”
"O Great Sage!
You have now been granted the prediction of one more birth by all the Buddhas; you have realized the Bodhisattva’s Dharma of Transcending Birth and abide in the Bodhisattva dwelling;
you have perfected all the pāramitās and are fully endowed with all the gates of dharmakṣānti."
They accomplish all the stages of a bodhisattva, sporting with mastery in all dharma-gates;
they attain all samādhis and reach the destinations wherever a bodhisattva may go;
they acquire all dhāraṇīs and eloquence, the light of skillful means, and fully accomplish the sovereignty of a bodhisattva.
They have accumulated all factors conducive to enlightenment; they sport with skillful means and wisdom;
they have attained all supernormal powers and clarities;
and regarding whatever they have practiced and studied, they have brought all bodhisattva practices to ultimate perfection.
Possessing all vows, he knows the gateways of all vehicles, maintains the empowerment of the Tathāgatas, embraces the bodhi of the Buddhas, and guards the Dharma-treasury of all the Buddhas;
he gives rise to the jewels of wisdom and the merits of Bodhisattvas, and as the secret teaching of the Tathāgata, he constantly serves as the foremost leader among the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
For those oppressed by the thieves of affliction, he uses the power of his valor to crush and destroy them, bringing them peace and security;
for those lost on the straight path in the wilderness of birth and death, he shows them the correct way;
and for those afflicted by the maladies of affliction, he acts as a skilled physician to treat them.
The Honored One among all sentient beings is the God among Gods, the Unsurpassed Sage.
As one who has transcended the ocean of birth and death of the two vehicles, he acts as their guide to deliver them;
he spreads the great net of the Teaching across the ocean of birth and death, gathering in those to be tamed, nurturing their roots of goodness, and establishing them as Bodhisattvas.
Within the unimpeded vehicle, having brought all the affairs of bodhisattvas to ultimate completion, they dwell in the presence of all Buddhas.
I only pray that the Great Sage will expound for me how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva conduct and cultivates the bodhisattva path.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya surveyed Sudhana, pointed him out to the great assembly, and praised his meritorious virtues,
speaking in verse: "The youth Sudhana, with pure and upright mind and wisdom,
Dedicated solely to seeking the bodhisattva practices, Has come into my presence."
Welcome, Great Compassion Cloud, who can rain down the Dharma of ambrosia;
endowed with the three pure eyes, you never tire of the bodhisattva practice.
Welcome, you of upright mind, whose diligence is never weary.
All faculties fully subdued, Dedicated solely to seeking the bodhisattva practices;
Welcome, you of unbreakable conduct, Who constantly seek out spiritual friends,
Thoroughly comprehend all dharmas, And transform and guide all living beings.
Welcome to the pure path; dwelling securely in the treasury of merit, through the power of courageous diligence, you have attained the most supreme stage.
Welcome, O rare-to-be-seen one, son of the merits of all Buddhas!
Increasing all roots of goodness, They enter deeply into immeasurable realms.
Welcome, you who are equanimous! Regarding gain and loss, defamation and praise, And the worldly dharmas of suffering and pleasure, Your mind remains unstained.
Welcome, O you who dwell in peace and bliss; with a straightforward mind free from flattery and crookedness, you have eliminated pride, anger, and the dharma of heedlessness.
Welcome, O most excellent treasury, who observes all beings.
Nurturing the treasury of merit, their minds never grow weary.
Welcome, O Wisdom of the Three Times, who fulfills all dharma-realms;
having realized the treasury of the Buddha’s merit, your mind never grows weary.
Welcome, O Sublime Lotus, you who increase the clouds of renown!
Come, O sons of the Buddhas, as I show you the unobstructed path.
You have perfected the web of wisdom and thoroughly realized the inconceivable.
Extensively cultivating the bodhisattva practices, they transform and guide all sentient beings.
Single-mindedly seeking the Buddha’s bodhi, they practice the stainless conduct;
hearing and upholding all great vows, they reach this state without weariness.
The Buddhas of the past, future, and present— The various deeds and practices they have accomplished— Sudhana wishes to cultivate and learn; Therefore, he has come to my place.
He seeks with resolve a true Dharma Master To expound the teachings of the Right Path.
Those who skillfully instruct bodhisattvas have therefore come to my presence.
Sons of the Buddha who cultivate wisdom and are fully endowed with enlightenment have approached good spiritual friends; thus they have come to my presence.
The compassionate parents of all sentient beings, who nurture all virtues and bring them to the ultimate path of Bodhi, have therefore come to my presence.
They are the unsurpassed, supreme King of Physicians for those subject to birth, old age, sickness, and death.
The Śakra of sentient beings rains down the medicinal nectar of the Dharma;
the bright and pure sun of sentient beings universally illuminates all right paths;
the pure moon of sentient beings is so named because its merits are perfectly full.
Just as Mount Sumeru remains unmoved by the hearts of enemies or kin,
And like the waters of the great ocean, which never increase or decrease;
Like a master mariner of the sea, he delivers and liberates immeasurable multitudes.
Being entirely free from attachment, they have come to my presence.
With the power of courageous diligence, they rescue all sentient beings,
causing them all to attain peace and happiness, while single-mindedly seeking out virtuous friends.
They raise the banner of the True Dharma, manifesting the virtues of the Buddha;
they eliminate the suffering of the evil realms and open the gates to all auspicious destinies.
They are able to approach the various Guides and behold the wondrous body of the Buddha.
Having heard and upheld that secret teaching, you sought exclusively for a wise teacher.
Desiring to be endowed with wondrous wisdom and a noble form,
and wishing to be born into a lineage of high birth to perfect all merits, you have therefore come to my presence.
With a peerless and upright mind, you drew near to spiritual friends;
hearing the teachings they proclaimed, you were able to practice them all.
By virtue of your past immeasurable merits, Mañjuśrī caused you to resolve your mind upon enlightenment.
In accordance with his instructions, he single-mindedly sought the Bodhi of the Buddha.
Abandoning his celestial palace, family, parents, and all kinsmen,
as well as every worldly pleasure, he humbly endured hardships to seek out a spiritual friend.
Having thus practiced these pure deeds, at the end of this life,
one attains various supreme and wondrous fruits and ascends into the Hall of the Buddha-Dharma.
Sudhana beholds sentient beings suffering from birth, old age, sickness, and death.
Having given rise to the mind of great compassion, he single-mindedly sought the Bodhi of the Buddha.
Seeing beings revolving in the five realms of existence, oppressed by manifold sufferings,
he cultivated the wheel of wisdom-vajra to shatter and disperse the wheel of the miserable destinies.
The field of sentient beings is overgrown with weeds;
With greed, anger, and wrong views as its thorns, To cultivate it for purification, One must single-mindedly seek the plow of sharp wisdom.
Sentient beings dwell in the darkness of ignorance, Blind and bewildered, having lost the true path.
Sudhana acts as the guide, The light of wisdom reveals the true path.
With patience as his secret armor, Wielding the sharp sword of wisdom,
He mounts the three gates of liberation To crush and destroy the thieves of affliction.
With the courageous power of Sudhana, he universally acts for the sake of all beings in the three realms,
eliminating all terrors and establishing them in a place of peace and security.
Sudhana acts as a maritime captain, constructing the great ship of the Dharma.
Having crossed the ocean of ignorance, he causes others to dwell upon the pure jewel-island.
For the sake of all beings, Sudhana is the pure sun within the dharma-realm;
with the light of his vows and wisdom, he shines universally upon all classes of sentient beings.
Sudhana is the moon of awakening, In whom the wondrous Dharma is entirely perfected;
With the cool light of the samādhi of compassion, He extinguishes the heat of all afflictions.
Sudhana is the support for the ocean of wisdom, The adamantine ground of the straightforward mind.
As the Bodhisattva’s practice gradually deepens, the precious jewels of the sublime Dharma are brought forth.
The Dragon King of the Bodhicitta ascends into the void of the Dharmadhātu,
raising clouds that rain down nectar, nourishing the pure and white fruits.
With pure faith as the wick, compassion as the fragrant oil,
and right mindfulness as the precious vessel, one kindles that lamp which illuminates the world.
The mind of the Way is the *kalala*, and compassion is the *arbuda*.
The limbs and joints of the factors of enlightenment nourish the Tathāgatagarbha;
they augment the treasury of merit, the treasury of pure wisdom,
the treasury of blazing wisdom, and bring to fulfillment the treasury of all vows.
Such is this great adornment, which protects and delivers all living beings;
among all devas and humans, it is difficult to hear of and difficult to behold.
Such is the tree of wisdom, its roots so deep that it cannot be shaken.
Using skillful means as a lush canopy, they bring abundant benefit to all living beings.
Desiring to hear all dharmas, to eliminate all doubts and delusions,
and to be fully endowed with wondrous merit, they single-mindedly seek out virtuous friends.
Crushing the demon of afflictions, Extinguishing the defilement of perverse craving,
Causing all to attain liberation— For those who single-mindedly seek wisdom;
Abiding securely on the path of merit, Ultimately extinguishing the three miserable realms.
Revealing all favorable realms of rebirth, Causing one to be endowed with the path to nirvāṇa;
Manifesting the eightfold noble path, Eliminating all false views,
Tearing asunder the web of afflictions, And drying up the ocean of craving and desire.
The virtuous seeker, a bright and pure sun, Shines universally upon all classes of living beings;
Able to act as a charioteer of men, He rescues and delivers the multitudes within the three realms of existence.
Awakening all beings, He forever brings them forth from the mire of the five desires.
Eliminating false and deluded thoughts, He opens the gate of liberation.
Discerning all dharma-realms, He adorns and purifies the Tathāgata’s lands;
Having perfected all dharmas, Sudhana should rejoice.
Bravely practicing skillful means, with indestructible faith,
one accumulates sublime merit and fulfills all great vows.
Before long, one shall behold the Buddhas and thoroughly comprehend all phenomena.
Purifying all Buddha-fields, Accomplishing the Bodhi of Buddhas;
Conforming to the ocean of majestic deportment, Reaching the ultimate end of the ocean of all practices;
Delivering and liberating all The immeasurable oceans of sentient beings.
Giving birth to all wholesome dharmas, Possessing perfect and wondrous merit,
Equal to the sons of the Buddhas, They fulfill the dharma of liberation.
Bringing all great vows to completion, They subdue all māras.
Fully endowed with pure karma, he eliminates all afflictions.
Having accomplished all-knowledge and thoroughly realized the profound Dharma,
he eradicates the afflictions and manifold sufferings of all living beings.
The wheel of all sentient beings revolves within the cycle of birth and death;
to turn the pure wheel of Dharma, one must eliminate the wheel of manifold sufferings.
One shall protect the lineage of the Buddhas and purify the lineage of the Dharma.
Embracing the lineage of the Saṃgha, He fully understands the lineages of the three periods of time.
He brings to fulfillment the net of great vows, And destroys the net of false views;
He tears asunder the net of all cravings, And decisively breaks through the net of manifold sufferings.
Accomplishing the nature of straightforward mind, Possessing the nature of perfect wisdom,
Adorning and purifying the nature of the world, And liberating the nature of all sentient beings.
May Sudhana cause all Immeasurable multitudes of living beings—
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are filled with great joy.
The light of Sudhana’s pure wisdom universally illuminates the dharmas of all lands;
all classes of sentient beings behold immeasurable Buddhas.
Illuminating all dharma-realms, purifying the realms of sentient beings,
causing them to leave behind all evil paths, and extinguishing the suffering of the three realms of existence;
I cause the multitudes to depart from false paths and manifest all virtuous paths.
Cultivating the Eightfold Noble Path, He establishes the way to liberation.
May he cause all living beings everywhere To cross over the ocean of birth and death,
Extinguish all afflictions, And dwell securely in the ocean of merit.
They exhaust the ocean of afflictions and enable others to cross the ocean of the three realms of existence;
all their faculties are thoroughly subdued, and they remain unstained by the world.
— *The Flower Ornament Sutra of the Great Vaipulya*, Scroll 58
The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Mahāvaipulya, Scroll Fifty-Nine,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty,
Part Sixteen of Chapter Thirty-Four: Entering the Dharma Realm.

At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva, having praised Sudhana’s various sublime virtues in this manner and inspired immeasurable sentient beings to resolve their minds upon the Way, addressed Sudhana, saying: "Excellent!
Excellent, young man!
That you are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, single-mindedly seeking all Buddha-dharmas to benefit all the world and to rescue and protect all sentient beings.
"Noble son! You have gained a great benefit through this human body and life span; you have encountered the Buddhas and been able to see the great spiritual friend Mañjuśrī.

You are a vessel for the Dharma, your roots of goodness are moistened and flourishing, you cultivate pure and white dharmas, and you possess a nature of sublime aspiration. You are gathered under the protection of spiritual friends and are held in the mindful care of all Buddhas."
Why is this? The bodhicitta is the seed of all Buddhas, for it is able to give birth to all the Buddha-dharmas;
the bodhicitta is a fertile field, for it nurtures the pure and white dharmas of sentient beings.
The bodhicitta is like the great earth, for it can support all worlds;
the bodhicitta is like pure water, for it washes away the stains of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a great wind, for it is unobstructed throughout all worlds.
The bodhicitta is like a blazing fire, for it can incinerate all false views and attachments;
the bodhicitta is like the pure sun, for it universally illumines all classes of sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like the bright moon, for all pure and white dharmas are therein brought to full completion.
The bodhicitta is a pure lamp, for it universally illuminates all realms of phenomena;
the bodhicitta is a pure eye, for it is able to perceive both the deviant and the correct paths;
the bodhicitta is the Great Way, for it causes all to enter the city of omniscience.
The bodhicitta is the correct ferry, for it causes all to reach the place of ultimate liberation;
the bodhicitta is the Great Vehicle, for it accommodates and carries all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is the gateway, for it causes entry into all bodhisattva practices.
The bodhicitta is a palace, for it is where one dwells securely while practicing the dharmas of samādhi;
the bodhicitta is a pleasure grove, for therein one sports and experiences the joy of the Dharma;
the bodhicitta is a supreme abode, for it is that upon which all sentient beings rely.
The bodhicitta is the foundation, for it is the cause by which all bodhisattva practices are cultivated;
the bodhicitta is the protector, for it can fulfill all the great vows of the bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is the compassionate mother, for it nurtures and increases all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is a nurturer, for it protects and sustains all bodhisattvas;
the bodhicitta is a spiritual friend, for it brings one away from all evils and terrors;
the bodhicitta is a great king, for it surpasses the minds of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
The bodhicitta is supreme, for it brings to full completion all peerless vows;
the bodhicitta is like a great ocean, for it can contain all meritorious qualities;
the bodhicitta is like Sumeru, the king of mountains, for its mind remains unmoved as it regards all sentient beings with equanimity.
The bodhicitta is like the Cakravāḍa mountain range, for it sustains all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like the Snowy Mountains, for it nurtures the cooling medicine of wisdom;
the bodhicitta is like the Fragrant Mountain, for it gives rise to the fragrance of all meritorious virtues.
The bodhicitta is like space, for its sublime virtues are boundless;
the bodhicitta is like a lotus, for it is unstained by any worldly phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like a precious elephant, for it is able to fully subdue all the sense faculties.
The bodhicitta is like a precious steed, for it keeps one far removed from all wicked and unruly dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a charioteer, for it is able to protect the Mahāyāna in its entirety;
the bodhicitta is like an excellent medicine, for it thoroughly cures the disease of all afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like the Wujiao (Wojiao) rock, for it consumes and exhausts all unwholesome dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a vajra, for it shatters and disperses all evil dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like blended incense, for it gives rise to the fragrance of all meritorious virtues.
The bodhicitta is like a wondrous flower, for it is cherished and delighted in by all the world;
the bodhicitta is like white sandalwood, for it extinguishes the feverish diseases of the five desires;
the bodhicitta is like a musical instrument, for its subtle and exquisite sounds are heard throughout the dharma-realm.
The bodhicitta is courageous and strong, for it destroys all enemies that are the afflictions;
the bodhicitta is a skilled tweezers, for it pulls out all thorns of the afflictions;
the bodhicitta is a sovereign lord, for no other can surpass it.
The bodhicitta is the King Vaiśravaṇa, for it causes one to abandon all poverty and suffering;
the bodhicitta is Mañjuśrī, for it adorns all meritorious qualities;
the bodhicitta is an ornament, for it decorates all bodhisattvas.
The bodhicitta is like a conflagration, for it incinerates all conditioned phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like the root of the indestructible medicinal king-tree, for it nurtures and develops all the qualities of a Buddha;
the bodhicitta is like a dragon-gem, for it eliminates the poison of immeasurable afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like a water-clearing gem, for it purifies the stains of the mind and the turbidity of afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling jewel, for it is fully endowed with all meritorious qualities and benefits;
the bodhicitta is like a celestial vase of virtue, for it satisfies all desires and aspirations.
The bodhicitta is like a tree at the beginning of an eon, for it gives birth to all ornaments;
the bodhicitta is like a garment of *haṃsa* feathers, for it is not defiled by any dust or grime;
the bodhicitta is right action, for its intrinsic nature is pure.
The bodhicitta is like a sharp plow, for it cultivates the fields of all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like a Nārāyaṇa arrow, for it can completely pierce through the armor of the view of a self-identity;
the bodhicitta is like weary detachment, for it definitively understands the characteristics of suffering and affliction.
The bodhicitta is like a sharp spear, for it can pierce all the thieves of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like a rain of nectar, for it can extinguish all the fires of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp sword, for it can sever and eliminate all the evils of affliction.
The bodhicitta is like a golden hammer, for it shatters and disperses all mountains of pride;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp sword, for it cuts through the armor of the seven latent afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a banner of valor, for it topples all the banners of Māra.
The bodhicitta is like an axe, for it hews down the trees of ignorance and all forms of suffering;
the bodhicitta is like a weapon, for it protects against all hardships;
the bodhicitta is like skillful hands, for it guards the body of all perfections (pāramitās).
The bodhicitta is the wondrous foot, for it establishes all meritorious virtues;
the bodhicitta is the medicinal ointment for the eyes, for it eliminates all the cataracts of ignorance;
the bodhicitta is the skillful extractor of thorns, for it can completely uproot the thorn of the view of a self-existent body.
The bodhicitta is a bed of security, for it eliminates the bed of all suffering within birth and death;
the bodhicitta is a virtuous friend, for it delivers one from the immeasurable hardships of birth and death;
the bodhicitta is a sublime benefit, for it keeps one far removed from all phenomena of decline and loss.
The bodhicitta is the teacher of gods and humans, for it skillfully knows the essential path by which Bodhisattvas emerge;
the bodhicitta is a treasury of jewels, for its immeasurable merits are inexhaustible;
the bodhicitta is a gushing spring, for its pure and cool wisdom is without end.
The bodhicitta is a pure mirror, for it manifests all dharma-gates;
the bodhicitta is a pure pool, for it washes away all defilements;
the bodhicitta is a great river, for it leads forth the perfections and the four means of integration.
The bodhicitta is like a dragon king, for it can universally rain down the nectar of the Dharma;
the bodhicitta is the life-faculty, for it sustains the bodhisattva’s dharma of great compassion;
the bodhicitta is nectar, for it enables one to abide in the deathless dharma.
The bodhicitta is like a net, for it ensnares all those who are to be transformed;
the bodhicitta is like a fine snare, for it gathers in all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like a hook and bait, for it fishes out sentient beings dwelling in the abyss of birth and death.
The bodhicitta is like the agada medicine, for it eradicates all evils and afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like the pratibimba medicine, for it is able to cure the poisons of the five desires;
the bodhicitta is like the great earth, for it eliminates the waters of immeasurable false conceptions.
The bodhicitta is like a wind-circle, for it disperses and destroys all hindrances and obscurations;
the bodhicitta is like a jewel-island, for it gives birth to the jewels of the qualities of the factors of enlightenment;
the bodhicitta is like a seed-lineage, for it nurtures and develops all pure and wholesome dharmas.
The bodhicitta is a dwelling, for it receives all the jewels of merit;
the bodhicitta is a great city, for it is the abode of the bodhisattva-merchants;
the bodhicitta is a golden elixir, for it eliminates the stains of affliction and brings about purity.
The bodhicitta is like fragrant honey, for it is fully endowed with the flavor of all merits;
the bodhicitta is the correct path, for it leads one into the city of omniscience;
the bodhicitta is a precious vessel, for it contains and receives all pure and white dharmas.
The bodhicitta is like seasonal rain, for it is able to completely eliminate the dust of afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a secure dwelling, for it gives birth to the abodes where Bodhisattvas reside;
the bodhicitta is like the practice of longevity, for it does not adopt the various liberations of the Śrāvakas.
The bodhicitta is like lapis lazuli, for its nature is pure and subtle, being unstained by defilements;
the bodhicitta is like an indranīla gem, for it surpasses the wisdom of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
the bodhicitta is like the Dharma drum, for it awakens sentient beings who have long slumbered in the afflictions.
The bodhicitta is like pure water, for its nature is pure and free from turbidity;
the bodhicitta is like Jāmbūnada gold, for it makes all conditioned virtues appear like a heap of ink;
the bodhicitta is like the king of mountains, for it transcends all worlds.
The bodhicitta is a refuge, for it is able to protect all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is the ultimate reality, for it is far removed from all false and illusory phenomena;
the bodhicitta is the unsurpassed jewel, for it causes all to rejoice and attain fulfillment.
The bodhicitta is a great assembly, for it satisfies and gladdens beings according to their needs;
the bodhicitta is a venerable elder, for among all sentient beings there is no equal to it;
the bodhicitta is a precious treasury, for it upholds all the teachings of the Buddhas.
The bodhicitta is like Indra’s net, for it gathers in all the asuras of the afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like the wind of Vairūṇa, for it vibrates and awakens the minds of sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like Indra’s fire, for it incinerates all habitual tendencies of the afflictions.
The bodhicitta is the unsurpassed stūpa, for it is to be venerated by all devas and humans.
O Son of the Buddha!
The bodhicitta thus accomplishes immeasurable merits; it is entirely equal to the merits of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Why is this? Because it is by means of the bodhicitta that all practices of the bodhisattvas are produced, and the Buddhas of the three periods of time attain perfect enlightenment. "Good son!
For example, suppose there is a person who obtains a medicine of mastery and is freed from five kinds of terrors. What are these five?
They are as follows:
Fire cannot burn it, water cannot sweep it away, poison cannot affect it, blades cannot wound it, and smoke cannot harm it.
It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: having resolved upon bodhicitta and embraced sarvajñā (all-knowledge), they are free from the five fears.
What are these five? They are:

not being burned by the fire of desire; not being swept away by the flowing waters of existence; not being struck by the poisonous venom of anger; not being wounded by the sharp blades of affliction; and not being harmed by the smoke of perverse thoughts and reflections.
“Good son! For example, if a person obtains the medicine of liberation, they will never die an untimely death.
It is the same for a bodhisattva mahāsattva: having obtained the medicine of the sublime wisdom of the bodhicitta, they cannot be harmed by the afflictions of birth and death.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains the medicine of a dragon king; if any venomous insects smell its fragrance, they immediately flee far away.

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having obtained the great dragon-king medicine of the bodhicitta, all the venomous insects of the afflictions and evils, upon smelling its fragrance, are entirely dispersed and extinguished.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains an indestructible medicine; no enemy whatsoever can find an opportunity against them.
So it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: having obtained the indestructible medicinal drug of the bodhicitta, they cannot be destroyed by any afflictions, māras, or enemies.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who obtains the *piṅgala* medicinal herb, which is able to extract thorns of poison.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is also like this: having obtained the *piṅgala* medicinal herb of the bodhicitta, they are able to extract the thorns of the three poisons and all false views.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who obtains the king of medicines, Sudarśana, which extinguishes all diseases.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtains the king of medicines, the Bodhicitta, which extinguishes all the diseases of the afflictions of all sentient beings.”
“Good son! It is like the great medicinal king-tree, Śāntana; if there are sentient beings who remain within its shade, all the malignant sores upon their bodies will be healed and cured.”

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise thus: having obtained the sandalwood tree of the bodhicitta, any sentient beings who rely on the shade of this tree shall have all their sores of afflictions and unwholesome karma completely healed.
“Good son! It is like the medicinal king-tree named Unbreakable Root, which, by its power, nurtures and causes all the trees of Jambudvīpa to grow.”
The tree of the bodhicitta is likewise; by its power, it nurtures all the roots of goodness of both śaikṣa and aśaikṣa bodhisattvas.
"O son of good family!
For example, there is a medicinal herb named āmlavetasa; if it is applied to the body, the body becomes supple and lustrous, and the mind is freed from all evils.
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva obtains the āmlavetasa medicine of the bodhicitta, which causes the various wholesome karmas of body, speech, and mind to grow.
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains the medicinal herb of mindfulness; whatever Dharma they hear, they never forget.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: having obtained the medicinal herb of the mindfulness of the bodhicitta, they hear and uphold all Buddha-dharmas without forgetting.”
“Good son! It is like a medicine called ‘Lotus,’ which, when consumed by anyone, enables them to live for an eon.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who consumes the lotus-medicine of the bodhicitta attains mastery for incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.”
“Good son! It is like a person who possesses a medicine that renders the body invisible, whom no sentient beings can see.
In the same way, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has obtained the medicine that renders the body invisible through the bodhicitta cannot be seen by any of the Māras.”

“Good son! It is like the great ocean, which possesses a maṇi jewel named ‘Accumulation of All Jewels. Unless it is taken to another realm, even if a fire calamity should arise, it is impossible for it to evaporate even a single drop of the ocean water.

The bodhicitta, which accumulates a multitude of precious jewels, is also like this: when it abides within the ocean of the bodhisattva’s straightforward mind, there is no possibility that one would forget or lose even a single root of goodness dedicated toward *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge); yet *sarvajñā* remains unstained by attachment and is never separated from those roots of goodness.
“Good son! It is like a mani jewel named Pure Radiance; if someone adorns their body with it, it eclipses the light of all other jewels, making them appear like a mass of ink.”
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: by adorning his body with the maṇi-jewel necklace of the bodhicitta, he outshines the mind-jewels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
“Good son! It is like a water-clearing gem: when placed in turbid water, the water immediately becomes clear.
The jewel of the bodhicitta is likewise; it eliminates all the defilements and turbidity of the afflictions.”
“Good son! For example, suppose there is a person who possesses a water-abiding jewel and adorns their body with it; when they enter deep water, they do not drown.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva likewise possesses the water-abiding jewel of the bodhicitta; when they enter the ocean of birth and death, they do not sink.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a great dragon-jewel and goes to where the dragons dwell; the dragons will not harm him.
In the same way, a bodhisattva-mahāsattva who obtains the great dragon-jewel of the bodhicitta enters the desire realm and cannot be harmed by the evil dragons of the afflictions.”
“Good son! For example, Śakra possesses a maṇi jewel with which he adorns his body, and thus he is honored among the devas.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wears the jeweled necklace of the bodhicitta is honored above all within the three realms.”
“Good son! It is like a person who obtains a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), which eliminates all poverty and suffering.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtains the wish-fulfilling jewel of the bodhicitta, which eliminates all the poverty and suffering of wrong livelihood (*mithyājīva*).”
“Good son! For example,
just as a fire-gem produces fierce flames when stimulated by the light of the sun,
so too does the bright and pure fire-gem of the bodhicitta produce the fire of wisdom when stimulated by the light of great insight.
“Good son! For example, just as the moonstone produces cool water when touched by the light of the moon, so too is the pure moon-jewel of the bodhicitta;
once it has been moved by the moonlight of those roots of goodness dedicated for the sake of others, it gives rise to the water of great vows consisting of roots of goodness.”
“Good son! For example, when a dragon king wears a crown of wish-fulfilling jewels, he is free from all fear.

In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva wears the crown of the wish-fulfilling jewel of great compassion and the bodhicitta, thereby remaining far removed from all the hardships of the evil realms.”
“Good son! It is like the maṇi-jewel that is the treasury for adorning all sentient beings; it can completely fulfill all wishes without any diminution, thereby attaining the bodhicitta.”
"The Maṇi-jewel of the Treasury of Sublime Adornments fulfills the desires, wishes, and aspirations of bodhisattvas and other sentient beings without any diminution. Good son!"
For example, when a wheel-turning monarch possesses a maṇi jewel, it illuminates the palace universally and extinguishes all darkness.
It is the same for a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has obtained the maṇi jewel of the bodhicitta; they are able to illuminate the palaces of the five destinies everywhere and extinguish all darkness.
“Good son! It is like a person who, when touched by the light of a deep blue jewel, immediately becomes the same color as that jewel.

In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who obtains the deep blue jewel-light of the bodhicitta observes all phenomena and dedicates their roots of goodness, becoming identical in color to sarvajñā (omniscience).”
“Good son! Just as a lapis lazuli gem remains unstained even after dwelling amidst impurities for hundreds of thousands of years, so too is the bodhicitta, which is like a pure lapis lazuli gem;
though it dwells within the desire realm for hundreds of thousands of kalpas, it is not defiled by the five desires, because its nature is pure.”
“Good son! Just as the stainless-light pure maṇi jewel produces all other jewels,
so too is the bodhicitta like the stainless-light jewel, giving birth to the precious jewels of the merits of ordinary beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and all buddhas.”
“Good son! For example, just as a great maṇi jewel can completely eliminate all darkness, so too is the jewel of the bodhicitta; it eliminates all the darkness of ignorance.”
“Good son! It is like the great ocean, which contains jewels of priceless value; when a merchant’s ship or carriage carries them into the city, no other mani-jewels can equal them.”

The bodhicitta, a priceless jewel, is likewise: dwelling within the ocean of birth and death, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva carries it aboard the ship of great vows into the city of liberation, a state that cannot be matched by the jewels of merit belonging to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
“Good son! It is like a great, stainless maṇi jewel that, while situated in Jambudvīpa, can illuminate the palaces of the sun and moon for forty thousand yojanas, making them all clearly manifest.”

The jewel of the bodhicitta is likewise: though it dwells within the cycle of birth and death, it illuminates the emptiness of the dharma-realm, causing the palatial abodes of the Buddha-realms to appear in their entirety.
“Good son! It is like the Maṇi Wind King, which can sustain all varieties of fragrant flowers within the realm illuminated by the sun and moon.

The maṇi wind-king of the bodhicitta is likewise able to sustain and uphold all objects illuminated by the knowledge of all modes (sarvākārajñatā), as well as all devas and humans, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, buddhas, and bodhisattvas, along with all tainted and untainted roots of goodness.
“Good son! For example, there is a mani-jewel in the ocean called ‘Ocean-Treasury,’ which manifests all the various adornments within the sea.
The jewel of the ocean-treasury of the bodhicitta is likewise; it manifests all the various adornments of the realm of omniscience.”
“Good son! For example, Jāmbūnada gold, with the exception of the wish-fulfilling jewel, surpasses all other jewels.
The Jāmbūnada gold of the bodhicitta is likewise; with the exception of omniscience, it surpasses all other merits.”
“Good son! It is like a person who is skilled in incantations for dragons and attains mastery over all dragons.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has obtained the dharma of the excellent incantation of the bodhicitta attains mastery over all the dragons of affliction.”
“Good son! It is like a valiant warrior who, having donned armor and taken up weapons, cannot be defeated by any enemy.
In the same way, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having donned the great ornaments of the bodhicitta, cannot be defeated by any afflictions or the enemies that are the māras.”
“Good son! For example, if one *zhu* of udaka-sāra sandalwood is burned, its fragrance pervades a small chiliocosm;
even the treasures of a trichiliocosm cannot equal it.
The incense of the bodhicitta is likewise: with its sublime merits, it universally perfumes the entire dharma-realm, such that the merits of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot equal it.
“Good son! For example, when white sandalwood is applied to the body, it removes all afflictive heat and brings about the bliss of coolness.

The incense of the bodhicitta is also like this: it extinguishes the heat of discursive thought and the afflictions of greed, anger, and delusion, causing the body of wisdom to attain complete coolness and bliss.”
“Good son! For example, among the various classes of sentient beings, those who draw near to Mount Sumeru all become the same color as that mountain.
The mountain of the bodhicitta is likewise; if there are those who draw near to it, they all attain the same color as that sarvajñatā.”
“Good son! For example, the fragrance of the flowers of the pārijātaka tree cannot be matched by any of the vārṣika or campaka flowers within Jambudvīpa.”

The incense of the bodhicitta is likewise: its fragrance of sublime merit cannot be matched by that of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, nor by their untainted morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, or the knowledge and vision of liberation.
“Good son! For example, when the flowers of the pārijātaka tree have not yet blossomed, their fragrance pervades all within Jambudvīpa, such that it cannot be equaled by any other flower fragrance.”
The flower of the bodhicitta is likewise; it cannot be equaled by the fragrant flowers of the merit—whether with outflows or without outflows—of all devas and humans. "Good son!

For example, if a garment is perfumed with the flowers of the pārijātaka tree for a single day, it cannot be matched by the fragrance of kovidāra or vārṣika flowers, even if they have been used to perfume it for a thousand years.

The flower of the bodhicitta is likewise; the merit perfumed by it in a single day reaches the abodes of the Buddhas throughout the ten directions, such that all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, even with their untainted minds perfuming various merits over hundreds of thousands of kalpas, cannot equal it.
“Good son! For example, the nālikera tree—from its roots, trunk, branches, and leaves, down to its flowers and fruits—benefits all sentient beings.

The tree of the bodhicitta is likewise: arising from the cause of a bodhisattva’s great compassion, it constantly benefits all sentient beings from the first generation of the mind of enlightenment until the ultimate realization of all Buddha-dharmas.”
“Good son! It is like a single *tola* of *āroṣa* medicine that transforms a thousand *tolas* of copper into pure gold, yet without causing any diminution within the portion of that medicine itself.”

The medicine of the bodhicitta is likewise: it gathers the wisdom of dedication, eliminates all afflictions and karmic obstructions, purifies all phenomena, and becomes identical in form to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); thus, afflictions and evil karma cannot diminish it.
"Just as a small fire blazes more fiercely the more it consumes its fuel, so too is the fire of the bodhicitta:
the fire of wisdom grows ever more intense according to the dharmas upon which it takes its object."
"Just as a single lamp may light hundreds of thousands of other lamps without being diminished, so too is the lamp of the bodhicitta;
it lights the wisdom-lamps of all Buddhas of the three periods of time without being diminished."
"Just as a bright lamp entering a large, dark room is able to illuminate and dispel all darkness, so too is the lamp of the bodhicitta.
Entering the dark chamber of the mind, it is able to utterly extinguish the ignorance accumulated over immeasurable eons, bringing to full perfection the clear and pure wisdom of a bodhisattva."
"Just as the light of a lamp wick corresponds to its quality—whether fine or coarse—and increases further when more oil is added, so too is the wick of the bodhicitta.

In accordance with one's original vows, it emits the light of wisdom that universally illumines the dharma-realm; by increasing the oil of great compassion, it transforms sentient beings, purifies buddha-fields, and carries out all the works of a Buddha without end."
"It is, for example, like the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, who wears a natural celestial crown of Jambūnada gold that cannot be destroyed by any of the gods of the desire realm."
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: wearing the celestial crown of the great vow of bodhicitta, they cannot be destroyed by Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
"For example, when the Great Lion roars, the young lions who hear it all become courageous and vigorous, while all other birds and beasts flee far away and hide in concealment."

When the Buddhas roar the lion’s roar and the bodhisattvas hear it, they praise the sound of the bodhicitta, which nurtures the dharmakāya; thus, sentient beings with false views lie hidden and retreat in dispersion.
"It is like a person who uses a lion’s sinew to make the strings of a lute; once the sound is played, all other strings snap and break.

Likewise, when the sound of the merit of the bodhicitta issues forth from the body of the perfections (*pāramitā*) of all Tathāgatas, those who delight in the five desires or the teachings of the Two Vehicles will find them entirely severed and extinguished upon hearing it."

"It is like the milk of cows, horses, and sheep mixed together in a single vessel; if lion's milk is poured into that vessel, the other milks are completely consumed, and it passes through directly without obstruction."

The lion-like milk of the Tathāgata’s bodhicitta, when placed within the milk of the karmas and afflictions accumulated over immeasurable eons, completely dissolves and exhausts them all, so that one no longer dwells within the dharmas of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
"Just as when the kapinjala bird is still within its shell, it possesses great power that other birds cannot match;

so too is it with the bodhisattva-mahāsattva: while within the shell of birth and death, the power of the merit generated by the aspiration for enlightenment (bodhicitta) is such that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot equal it."
"For example, when the golden-winged bird (garuḍa) is first born, its eyes are clear and bright, and it possesses great power that no other birds, whether large or small, can equal."

The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: having been born into the family of the Tathāgata and having resolved upon bodhicitta, their eye of wisdom is clear and pure, and they possess great power;
that which śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot reach, even after practicing wisdom for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
"Just as a powerful warrior, using a sharp vajra arrow of Nārāyaṇa, shoots through a dense and firm armor, passing straight through without obstruction;

so too is it with the bodhisattva mahāsattva, who, using the sharp arrow of the wisdom of the bodhicitta, shoots through the dense armor of all false views and afflictions, piercing right through without obstruction."
"Just as when a mighty hero, a Mahānāga, rouses his awesome wrath, no one among the people of Jambudvīpa can defeat him;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: having aroused great compassion and cultivated the bodhicitta, he cannot be defeated by any of the hosts of Māras in all the worlds, nor by afflictions or karma."
"Just as when a person studies a great craft, although they have not yet reached its ultimate perfection, they cannot be surpassed by any other skillful arts;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: although they have not yet perfected their training in the vow of the bodhicitta, they cannot be surpassed by Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or any other sentient beings."
"Just as a person who studies the art of archery first establishes their own stance, so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
training in the stage of all-knowledge, they first establish the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), and will thereby certainly attain all Buddha-dharmas."
"Just as a magician first studies the arts of illusion and subsequently manifests all manner of illusory phenomena, so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
having first resolved upon the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta), they subsequently manifest all the true dharmas of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
"Just as a magical illusion manifests forms where there are no forms, so too is the characteristic of the bodhicitta: it manifests the adornments of the merits of the dharmadhātu.
It is like a person wearing ornaments of Jāmbūnada gold; they outshine everything else, making all other things appear like a mass of ink."
In the same way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattva, by means of the ornaments of the bodhicitta, eclipses all the merits of sentient beings, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas.
"Just as a small portion of ayas-kānta iron can destroy all other iron, including hooks, chains, and bonds, so too is the bodhicitta:
it severs all wrong views, afflictions, and the fetters of craving."
"Just as a swift wind moves without obstruction, so too is the wind of the bodhicitta;
wherever it goes, it eliminates all afflictions without any hindrance, and does not abide in the liberation of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas."
"Just as a person who skillfully enters the great ocean does not drown and cannot be harmed by the makara fish, so too is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva:

entering the ocean of birth and death with the bodhicitta, they are not defiled by birth and death, nor do they realize the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) as śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, and thus they cannot be harmed by the makara fish."
"Just as when a person consumes ambrosia (*amṛta*), they cannot be harmed by any ailment, so too it is with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva:
having consumed the ambrosial dharma-medicine of bodhicitta, they do not fall into the stages of the Śrāvaka or Pratyekabuddha, but cultivate great compassion and fulfill their vows and practices."
"Just as if there were a person who used an ointment for invisibility to anoint their eyes and traveled about at will, such that no one could see them;
so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: having attained the Bodhicitta and fulfilled the great vows, they travel at will, entering the realm of Māra, yet cannot be seen by any of the Māras."
"Just as a person who relies upon a great king has no fear of others, so too is it with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva:
relying on the Dharma King of the Great Power of the Bodhicitta, they eliminate hindrances and obscurations, and have no fear of the evil realms."
"Just as a person dwelling within deep water does not fear being burned by fire, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
dwelling within the waters of the roots of goodness of the bodhicitta, they cannot be burned by the fires of the liberation of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas."
"Just as a person who relies upon a valiant general has no fear of enemies, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: by relying on the bodhicitta, they have no fear of any evils."
"Just as Śakra, Lord of the Devas, wields the vajra to subdue all the asuras, so too does the bodhisattva mahāsattva: wielding the bodhicitta, he destroys all māras and other non-Buddhists."
"Just as there is a person who, having taken the *arasa* elixir, does not grow thin or old, and whose life is extended infinitely;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who, having taken the *arasa* elixir of the bodhicitta, dwells within birth and death for immeasurable eons, practicing the bodhisattva conduct without being stained or attached."
"Just as the arśa medicinal herb must first be treated with pure water, so too is the medicine of the bodhicitta; among all the practices cultivated by bodhisattvas, it is the foremost."
"Just as, among all the faculties, the life-faculty is the foremost, so too it is with the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva: among all the true dharmas of the Buddhas, the bodhicitta is the most foremost."

"Just as a person whose life-faculty has been severed is unable to benefit their parents or kinsmen, so too it is with a bodhisattva mahāsattva: separated from the bodhicitta, they cannot bring benefit to all sentient beings."
"Just as the great ocean cannot be destroyed by anything, so too is the ocean of the bodhicitta; śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot obstruct or destroy it."
"Just as the light of the sun cannot be eclipsed by the light of the various stars and constellations, so too is the sun of the bodhicitta;
its radiant light of wisdom and the fulfillment of great vows cannot be eclipsed by the untainted wisdom-light of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
"Just as a crown prince, upon his very birth, is already held in high esteem by the great ministers, so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
once he has resolved upon Bodhicitta, he is universally honored by all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas because he cultivates great compassion."
"Just as a prince, though young in years, is saluted by all the ministers, so too it is with a bodhisattva mahāsattva:
having resolved upon bodhicitta, they are saluted by all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas."
"Just as a prince, though not yet possessing sovereign power, has already fully attained the marks and characteristics of a king;
so too is it with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: although he is still shrouded by the karmic obstructions of afflictions, he has fully attained the marks of the bodhicitta."
"Just as one with a cataract in the eye perceives a truly pure jewel as impure, so too it is with the jewel of the bodhicitta:
those lacking wisdom and faith give rise to the notion that it is impure."
"Just as a medicinal mantra—if sentient beings see it, hear it, or dwell together with it—all their various illnesses are entirely cured.

The medicine of the bodhicitta is likewise: it nurtures the roots of goodness, gathers the medicine of wisdom, and fulfills the body of bodhisattva-intelligence born of great vows. If sentient beings see it, hear it, or dwell together with it, and practice right mindfulness, all the diseases of their afflictions are entirely eradicated."
"Just as a garment with the *haṃsa* motif does not receive dust or grime, so too is the garment of the bodhicitta; it likewise does not receive any of the dust or grime of saṃsāra."
"Just as if there were a person who constantly held ambrosia, focusing their mindfulness without distraction and being able to discern all dharmas;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who holds the ambrosial True Dharma of Bodhicitta, maintaining right mindfulness without distraction, and is thus able to teach and transform all sentient beings, causing them to fulfill great vows and achieve the body of wisdom."
"Just as a plow that lacks a yoke is unfit for use, so too is the bodhicitta:
apart from an upright mind, it possesses no real significance within the Dharma of the Tathāgata."
"For example, a wheel-turning monarch possesses a sublime celestial crown named Elephant Treasury;
when that crown is washed, the fourfold army travels through the void."

The crown of the bodhicitta is likewise: it purifies all the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas, distances them from the three realms of existence, and proceeds through the space of the unconditioned realm of Tathāgata wisdom.
"Just as diamond is produced from the nature of gold and not from other jewels,
so too is the jewel of the bodhicitta produced from the nature of great compassion that protects sentient beings, and not from any other virtues."
"Just as there might be a tree that does not grow from a root, yet is able to nurture branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit;
so too is the tree of the bodhicitta. Without any point of dependence, it is able to nurture all-knowledge (sarvajñā), the superknowledges (abhijñā), and great vows, universally covering the world."
"Just as a diamond cannot be manifested by all types of vessels, nor can it be contained within all types of vessels, so too is the jewel of the bodhicitta:
the vessel of a small mind, bound by stinginess and lacking wisdom, cannot manifest it; nor can it be contained within the vessel of sentient beings who are deceitful and hold wrong views."
"Just as a vajra can shatter all manner of jewels, so too is the bodhicitta: it definitively and thoroughly knows all dharmas.
Just as a vajra can shatter all mountains..."
The bodhicitta is likewise; it shatters and disperses all mountains of false views.
"For example, although a diamond may be broken and no longer whole, no other precious jewel can surpass it."
The mind of enlightenment is also like this: even if it is slightly lax, its various jewels of merit cannot be surpassed by those of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
"It is like a fragment of diamond that can still eliminate all poverty and suffering."
The bodhicitta is likewise; even if one slightly falters in dignified deportment or the approach to the Dharma, it is still able to eliminate all sufferings of poverty.
"It is like a small diamond, which can destroy all other things."
The bodhicitta is likewise: by taking even a small object as its condition, it can shatter all ignorance, delusion, and confusion.
"It is like a vajra, which cannot be obtained by ordinary people."
The bodhicitta is likewise; it cannot be attained by sentient beings of inferior resolve.
"It is like a vajra, which those lacking wisdom and skill cannot recognize."
The bodhicitta is likewise such that it cannot be recognized by sentient beings who lack wisdom.
"Just as a vajra cannot be destroyed, so too is the bodhicitta; no phenomena whatsoever can exhaust or destroy it."
"Just as no sentient beings, even up to the mahānāgas, can wield a vajra weapon, except for those with the strength of Nārāyaṇa."
The bodhicitta is likewise; śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are unable to receive and uphold it, with the exception of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
"It is like a vajra weapon, which penetrates everything without exception, something that no other weapon can achieve."

The bodhicitta is likewise: observing the three periods of time and teaching and transforming sentient beings, it undergoes immeasurable suffering for incalculable eons, something that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas cannot attain.
"Just as nothing else can support a vajra except for the vajra-ground, so too is the bodhicitta:
it gives birth to the merit of a bodhisattva’s practices and vows, and cannot be supported by śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, except by those who possess the upright mind of sarvajñā (omniscience)."
